name: MonarchAccordion
title: Accordion
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.clickable, androidx.compose.animation.AnimatedVisibility, androidx.compose.material3.HorizontalDivider
summary: Stacked sections whose content opens under each header, one at a time or any number, with headers that are headings and buttons.
whenToUse: For a set of related sections people scan by title and open one by one: FAQs, settings groups, the details of a record.
whenNotToUse: For one section on its own use MonarchCollapsible. For content people need to compare side by side, show it open or use tabs. For navigation to other screens use list rows.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAccordion(items: List<MonarchAccordionItem>, expanded: Set<String>, onExpandedChange: (Set<String>) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, multiple: Boolean = false, collapsible: Boolean = true, enabled: Boolean = true, trailingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, expandedLabel: String? = null, collapsedLabel: String? = null, content: @Composable ColumnScope.(item: MonarchAccordionItem) -> Unit)
class MonarchAccordionItem(id: String, title: String, enabled: Boolean = true)

options.name: items
options.description: The sections in order: id, title and whether the section can be opened.

options.name: expanded
options.description: The ids of the open sections.

options.name: onExpandedChange
options.description: Called with the new set of open ids when a header is activated.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the accordion.

options.name: multiple
options.description: Lets any number of sections stay open (the web's type multiple). Without it opening one closes the others.

options.name: collapsible
options.description: One-at-a-time only: lets the open section's header close it again (the web's collapsible).

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether any section can be opened or closed.

options.name: trailingIcon
options.description: An icon at the end of each header, such as a chevron; it turns half a turn while open. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: expandedLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in state "Expanded" (monarch_accordion_expanded).

options.name: collapsedLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in state "Collapsed" (monarch_accordion_collapsed).

options.name: content
options.description: The content of a section, in the muted body style.

options.name: headerTrailing
options.description: Content at the end of a header, such as a count; part of the header button.

options.name: MonarchAccordionItem.subtitle
options.description: A second line under the title, read after it.

states.name: collapsed
states.description: Only the header; its state is "Collapsed" and it offers the expand action.

states.name: expanded
states.description: The content under the header; the trailing icon turned half a turn; the state "Expanded" and the collapse action when the section can be closed.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The header in the disabled text color; it does not open or close.

appearance: Headers use the strong body style in the default text color and the trailing icon in the muted text color; content uses the body style in the muted text color. Lines in the default border color sit above the first section and under each section. Disabled headers use the disabled text color. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Material 3 has no accordion, so Monarch builds one; iOS styles the system DisclosureGroup instead and ships no accordion type. The web Accordion is Radix Accordion with separate Item, Trigger and Content parts and headingAs; here the sections are data (MonarchAccordionItem) and the content a lambda per item, and every header is a heading without levels (Compose has one heading property). Arrow-key, Home and End movement between headers is not offered; focus and TalkBack move header by header. The web is controlled or uncontrolled; here state is hoisted as a set of ids for both modes. The header is built here rather than with MonarchCollapsible because MonarchCollapsible's header cannot be marked as a heading; the behavior (button role, state, expand and collapse actions, reduced motion) is the same. The chevron is a slot because Monarch bundles no icons. Closed content leaves the composition, as in MonarchCollapsible and on iOS.
accessibility: Each header is one element with the Button role and the heading property, so TalkBack's heading navigation reaches it.
Each header has the state description "Expanded" or "Collapsed" and the expand or collapse accessibility action; an open section that cannot be closed offers no collapse action.
Headers are at least 56dp high and span the width, so the touch target is well over 48dp.
Closed content leaves the composition, so TalkBack does not reach it.
Content grows into place, or appears at once when animations are off.
The title wraps at font scale 2.0 and the trailing icon stays at the end in both layout directions.
edgeCases: With multiple, ids that are not in items are kept in the reported set; one at a time, opening a section replaces the whole set with its id.
With collapsible false and nothing open, any header opens its section; the open one then stays open until another is opened.
State inside closed content is lost; hoist it.

examples.title: Single, collapsible
examples.template:
MonarchAccordion(

}

title: AccountMenu
wrapsNative: MonarchIconButton with MonarchAvatar as its content, MonarchMenu with MonarchMenuItem, MonarchRadio and MonarchDivider, MonarchThemeToggle; or MonarchBottomSheet on phones
summary: A recipe, not a component: the signed-in person's menu, an avatar button that opens a menu (or a sheet on phones) with who is signed in, Profile and Settings, a workspace switcher, the color scheme and Sign out.
whenToUse: At the end of the top app bar, or at the foot of a navigation rail or drawer, as the one place for the person's account, workspace and appearance.
whenNotToUse: For a screen of account settings, use a settings screen with MonarchSwitchRows and sections. For switching workspaces as the main task of a screen, use a list of workspaces.
api: IconButton(onClick = { open = true }, modifier = Modifier.semantics { contentDescription = "Account menu for …" }) { MonarchAvatar(image = …, name = …, size = MonarchAvatarSize.Sm, decorative = true) }

DropdownMenu(expanded = open, onDismissRequest = { open = false }) { …; DropdownMenuItem(text = { Text("Profile") }, onClick = …); …; MonarchThemeToggle(scheme = scheme, onSchemeChange = { scheme = it }, size = MonarchThemeToggleSize.Sm); DropdownMenuItem(text = { Text("Sign out") }, onClick = …, colors = MenuDefaults.itemColors(textColor = MonarchTheme.colors.dangerStrong)) }
ModalBottomSheet(onDismissRequest = { open = false }) { …; MonarchThemeToggle(scheme = scheme, onSchemeChange = { scheme = it }); MonarchButton("Sign out", …, variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Danger) }

states.name: closed
states.description: The avatar, with a presence dot when given a status, as the icon button that opens the menu.

states.name: open (menu)
states.description: A Material 3 menu: the name and email, Profile and Settings, the workspaces as radio items with the current one checked, the theme toggle, and Sign out in the strong danger color.

states.name: open (sheet)
states.description: On phones, the same choices in a modal bottom sheet with full-width buttons and the segmented theme toggle, which leaves room at the largest font scale.

appearance: The trigger is MonarchAvatar in its initials or picture colors inside a 48dp icon button. The menu is the Material 3 menu on the raised background role with Monarch's medium radius; the header uses the strong body and muted caption text roles; Sign out uses the strong danger role. The sheet uses the Material 3 sheet surface. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web ships AccountMenu as one component with user, workspaces, theme and callback props, and renderLink for router links. On Android it is a recipe, as on iOS: a MonarchIconButton and MonarchMenu already give the trigger, focus, keyboard and TalkBack behavior, so no Monarch type is added. The theme choice is MonarchThemeToggle bound to the app's MonarchScheme; apply it with MonarchTheme(scheme = …) at the root and persist it with MonarchThemeToggleStorage. The web's "sheet on phones" option is the second example: a MonarchBottomSheet, where a dropdown menu at the largest font scale would scroll. The web's workspaceSlot and items props are the app's own menu items; navigation is the app's (onClick). Monarch bundles no icons, so the menu items carry no glyphs unless the app adds leadingIcon.
accessibility: The icon button is named "Account menu for <name>"; the avatar inside is decorative so the name is read once.
The header's name and email are one element.
Workspace items carry the radio button role and the selected state, so the current workspace is announced, not only shown by the radio mark.
"Switch workspace" is a heading, so TalkBack users can jump to it.
MonarchThemeToggle reads its options and the selected scheme; Sign out is a word, not only a color.
Material 3 gives each menu item a row at least 48dp high; the icon button is 48dp.
edgeCases: With one workspace, leave the switcher out.
A long name or email wraps in the header; at the largest font scale prefer the sheet.
Keep the scheme with rememberSaveable or the app's settings store so it survives a restart, through MonarchThemeToggleStorage.

examples.title: Workspaces, theme and sign out
The same choices in a sheet on phones
examples.setup:
var open by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
var scheme by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(MonarchScheme.System) }

name: MonarchActionEditor
title: ActionEditor
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of outlined action cards; MonarchSelect (androidx.compose.material3.ExposedDropdownMenuBox) for the type and single options, MonarchTextField (androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedTextField) for text, messages and numbers, MonarchMultiSelect (androidx.compose.material3.ModalBottomSheet) for several options and tags, MonarchCheckboxRow (androidx.compose.material3.Checkbox) for yes or no, MonarchInlineNotice for warnings, MonarchButton for move, remove and add
summary: Edits the ordered actions of a rule: each action has a type and the parameters that type defines, with validation and reordering.
whenToUse: For the "then do this" part of routing rules, automations and macros, where the kinds of action and their parameters are data the app defines.
whenNotToUse: For the "when" part of a rule use MonarchConditionEditor. For a fixed form with known fields, compose MonarchTextField and MonarchSelect directly.
api: @Composable fun MonarchActionEditor(value: List<MonarchRuleAction>, onValueChange: (List<MonarchRuleAction>) -> Unit, actionTypes: List<MonarchActionType>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, ordered: Boolean = true, maxActions: Int = 20, showErrors: Boolean = false, defaultType: String? = null, enabled: Boolean = true, createId: (() -> String)? = null, removeIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, addIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, emptyContent: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchActionEditorLabels = MonarchActionEditorLabels())

data class MonarchRuleAction(id: String, type: String, parameters: Map<String, MonarchActionValue> = emptyMap()) { fun problems(actionTypes: List<MonarchActionType>): List<MonarchActionProblem>; companion object { fun create(id: String, type: MonarchActionType?): MonarchRuleAction; fun problems(actions: List<MonarchRuleAction>, actionTypes: List<MonarchActionType>): Map<String, List<MonarchActionProblem>> } }

class MonarchActionType(key: String, label: String, description: String? = null, group: String? = null, parameters: List<MonarchActionParameter> = emptyList(), defaults: Map<String, MonarchActionValue> = emptyMap(), enabled: Boolean = true, disabledReason: String? = null, validate: ((parameters: Map<String, MonarchActionValue>) -> String?)? = null, editor: (@Composable (parameters: Map<String, MonarchActionValue>, onParamsChange: (Map<String, MonarchActionValue>) -> Unit) -> Unit)? = null)

class MonarchActionParameter(key: String, label: String, kind: MonarchActionParameterKind, options: List<MonarchSelectOption<String>> = emptyList(), required: Boolean = false, description: String? = null, placeholder: String? = null, emptyLabel: String? = null, min: Double? = null, max: Double? = null, visibleWhen: ((parameters: Map<String, MonarchActionValue>) -> Boolean)? = null) { fun isVisible(parameters: Map<String, MonarchActionValue>): Boolean }
enum class MonarchActionParameterKind { Text, TextArea, Number, Select, MultiSelect, Tags, Boolean }

sealed interface MonarchActionValue { val isEmpty: Boolean; data class Text(text: String); data class Number(text: String) { constructor(number: Double); val parsed: Double? }; data class Flag(checked: Boolean); data class Values(values: List<String>) }
sealed interface MonarchActionProblem { data class Missing(param: String); data class OutOfRange(param: String); data class Invalid(message: String) }

class MonarchActionEditorLabels(label: String? = null, action: ((position: Int) -> String)? = null, type: String? = null, remove: String? = null, removeItem: ((position: Int) -> String)? = null, moveUp: String? = null, moveDown: String? = null, moveUpItem: ((position: Int) -> String)? = null, moveDownItem: ((position: Int) -> String)? = null, moved: ((type: String, position: Int, count: Int) -> String)? = null, add: String? = null, empty: String? = null, choose: String? = null, required: ((label: String) -> String)? = null, outOfRange: ((label: String) -> String)? = null, unknownType: ((key: String) -> String)? = null, unavailable: String? = null, maxReached: ((max: Int) -> String)? = null)

options.name: value
options.description: The actions, in the order they run. Ids must be unique.

options.name: onValueChange
options.description: Called with the whole new list after every change: add, remove, move, type or parameter.

options.name: actionTypes
options.description: The kinds of action: label, description, group, parameters, defaults, availability, an extra validate and an optional custom editor.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the editor.

options.name: ordered
options.description: Actions run in order: each card gets Move up and Move down buttons, and each move is announced.

options.name: maxActions
options.description: The most actions. At this count the add button is replaced by a note.

options.name: showErrors
options.description: Shows empty required parameters and numbers out of range as the input's error, the type's own check under the inputs, and the danger border on the card.

options.name: defaultType
options.description: The key of the type new actions start as. The first enabled type when null or unknown.

options.name: enabled
options.description: When false every control is disabled; a type's custom editor is still shown but its changes are dropped.

options.name: createId
options.description: Makes the id of a new action. By default the first free action-<n>.

options.name: removeIcon
options.description: The icon of each remove button. Monarch bundles no icons; without it the button reads "Remove".

options.name: addIcon
options.description: An icon before the text of the add button.

options.name: emptyContent
options.description: Replaces "No actions yet."

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

states.name: empty
states.description: "No actions yet." above the add button.

states.name: actions
states.description: One outlined card per action: the heading "Action 1", a row of Move up, Move down and Remove, the type menu with the type's description, then one labelled input per visible parameter.

states.name: conditional parameter
states.description: A parameter with visibleWhen appears and disappears as other parameters change, and is validated only while shown.

states.name: custom editor
states.description: A type's editor replaces its parameter inputs.

states.name: unavailable type
states.description: A disabled type stays selected on existing actions, with a warning notice and its reason; it cannot be picked for others.

states.name: errors
states.description: With showErrors: "Fill in “Team”." or "Enter an allowed number for “Hours”." on the input, the type's message in a danger notice, and the danger border.

states.name: limit reached
states.description: The add button is replaced by a muted note.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Every control takes its disabled colors and does nothing.

appearance: Each action is a card on the surface fill with the subtle border (the danger border while it has problems) and a subheading title. Inputs, menus, sheets and checkboxes take their Monarch colors; warnings use the warning inline notice and the type's own problem the danger inline notice. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those roles.
platformNotes: The web reorders with ReorderableList (drag and keyboard); on Android the cards sit in a plain Column with Move up and Move down buttons, because a rule editor lives inside a scrolling form and MonarchReorderableList is a lazy list that cannot go inside one; buttons also work the same with TalkBack and Switch Access, and each move is announced in a polite live region. The web's NativeSelect, Combobox and TagInput are MonarchSelect and MonarchMultiSelect (free tags are created from the search text); the web's Textarea is a multi-line MonarchTextField. Parameter values are typed (MonarchActionValue) instead of JavaScript values; numbers keep the typed text. Problems are typed (MonarchActionProblem) and turned into text with labels, instead of the web's message strings. The web's render becomes editor, a composable slot. The web type's value is key here. The web moves focus after add and remove; Compose leaves focus to the system. Same name as iOS's plan; iOS has not built it yet.
accessibility: Each action title ("Action 1") is a heading.
Move and remove buttons are named with the position ("Move down: action 1", "Remove action 1") and have 48dp touch targets; Move up on the first and Move down on the last are disabled.
Each move is announced through a polite live region on an always-present node: "Close ticket moved to position 2 of 2."
Inputs keep their Material 3 roles and visible labels; a problem is set as the input's error text, not only as the border color.
A yes or no parameter is one checkbox row, read with its label and state.
edgeCases: Picking another type starts the action again with that type's defaults; parameters of the old type are dropped.
A stored type the list no longer has shows as "key (not available)" and is not validated.
A hidden parameter keeps its value in parameters; it is only skipped by validation.
Clearing an optional menu or a number removes the key from parameters.

name: MonarchActivityTimeline
title: ActivityTimeline
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn with LazyListScope.stickyHeader per day; MonarchAvatar, MonarchCollapsible, MonarchTag, MonarchLoadMore, MonarchSkeleton, MonarchEmptyState and MonarchInlineErrorRetry; android.icu.text.DateFormat and android.text.format.DateUtils.getRelativeTimeSpanString for times
summary: A vertical feed of events (actor, verb, target, time and a marker) grouped under sticky day headings, with expandable details and Load more.
whenToUse: For the history of a record, an audit trail in context or a project's activity: who did what, and when.
whenNotToUse: For a sequence of steps someone must complete, use MonarchStepper; for messages people exchange, a chat or comment thread; for notifications that need action, a notification list.
api: @Composable fun MonarchActivityTimeline(events: List<MonarchActivityTimelineEvent>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, groupByDay: Boolean = true, marker: MonarchActivityTimelineMarker = MonarchActivityTimelineMarker.Dot, density: MonarchActivityTimelineDensity = MonarchActivityTimelineDensity.Regular, expandedIds: Set<String>? = null, onExpandedChange: ((Set<String>) -> Unit)? = null, loading: Boolean = false, failed: Boolean = false, hasMore: Boolean = false, loadingMore: Boolean = false, loadMoreFailed: Boolean = false, now: Long? = null, timeZone: String? = null, state: LazyListState = rememberLazyListState(), contentPadding: PaddingValues = PaddingValues(), labels: MonarchActivityTimelineLabels = MonarchActivityTimelineLabels(), onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null, onLoadMore: (() -> Unit)? = null)

class MonarchActivityTimelineEvent(id: String, verb: String, time: Long, actor: MonarchActivityTimelineActor? = null, target: String? = null, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, tone: MonarchTone = MonarchTone.Neutral, tags: List<String> = emptyList(), body: String? = null, details: String? = null)
class MonarchActivityTimelineActor(name: String, image: Painter? = null, kind: MonarchActivityTimelineActorKind = MonarchActivityTimelineActorKind.Person, seed: String? = null)
enum class MonarchActivityTimelineActorKind { Person, Automation, System }
enum class MonarchActivityTimelineMarker { Dot, Avatar }
enum class MonarchActivityTimelineDensity { Regular, Compact }

class MonarchActivityTimelineLabels(list: String? = null, today: String? = null, yesterday: String? = null, automated: String? = null, details: String? = null, empty: String? = null, loading: String? = null, error: String? = null, loadMore: MonarchLoadMoreLabels = MonarchLoadMoreLabels())

options.name: events
options.description: The events, newest first or oldest first; the order is kept. Each has an id, a verb, a time (epoch milliseconds, UTC) and an optional actor, target, icon, tone, tags, body and details. The app filters them; put filter controls above the timeline.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the list. Give the feed a bounded height, or let it fill a screen or pane.

options.name: groupByDay
options.description: Groups events under Today, Yesterday and dates in timeZone.

options.name: marker
options.description: A dot in the event's tone, or the actor's avatar. An event's icon always wins.

options.name: density
options.description: Regular, or Compact for side panels.

options.name: expandedIds
options.description: The ids of events whose details are open. null lets the timeline keep its own set.

options.name: onExpandedChange
options.description: Called with the new set when details open or close.

options.name: loading
options.description: Shows three placeholder rows for the first page.

options.name: failed
options.description: Shows the error message, with Try again when onRetry is set.

options.name: hasMore
options.description: Shows Load more after the feed when onLoadMore is set.

options.name: loadingMore
options.description: Load more shows that the next page is loading.

options.name: loadMoreFailed
options.description: Load more shows that the next page failed, with a retry.

options.name: now
options.description: The reference time for relative times and day headings. The current time when null, refreshed every minute; pass a fixed time in tests and screenshots.

options.name: timeZone
options.description: The zone of day boundaries and dates. An IANA id such as Europe/Berlin; null, or an id the device does not know, is the device's zone.

options.name: state
options.description: The list's scroll state.

options.name: contentPadding
options.description: The padding around the feed inside the list, such as for a Scaffold's bars.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for Activity, Today, Yesterday, Automated, Details, the empty, loading and error texts and the Load more strings.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Retries the first page after a failure.

options.name: onLoadMore
options.description: Loads the next page.

states.name: default
states.description: Day headings that stick to the top while their events scroll, then each event: the marker on a line that joins the day's events, the sentence with the actor and target in bold, the relative time and tags, the body.

states.name: automated
states.description: Automation and system actors get an "Automated" tag after the time.

states.name: details open
states.description: The Details disclosure shows the event's details under it.

states.name: loading
states.description: Three placeholder rows, read as "Loading activity".

states.name: empty
states.description: MonarchEmptyState with "No activity yet".

states.name: failed
states.description: MonarchInlineErrorRetry with Try again, or the error text alone without onRetry.

states.name: more
states.description: MonarchLoadMore after the feed, with its loading and failed states.

appearance: Day headings are subheading text on the canvas color. Dots are 8dp with a surface ring and a subtle outline: neutral in the strong border color, other tones in their solid color; icon markers are tinted in the tone's strong color (muted text when neutral) inside a surface circle. The line is the subtle border color, the time muted caption text and tags small Monarch tags. Every color is a theme role, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes are covered.
platformNotes: Built on a LazyColumn with a stickyHeader per day, as the plan says, so long histories stay fast and headings stay in view; iOS uses a VStack so it can sit inside other scrolling content. As a result the Android timeline scrolls itself and needs a bounded height when it is placed inside a scrolling page; state and contentPadding are offered for that. The web takes rich content for the verb, object, meta, body and details; here they are strings, tags and an icon slot, and a link to the record belongs in the app's navigation. The web's object is target, because object is a Kotlin keyword. Times are epoch milliseconds in UTC and avatars a Painter, following the Monarch conventions. The web accent tone is MonarchTone.Accent. The filters slot is not offered: put the controls above the timeline. The web day heading level option has no meaning here: headings are headings. The web locale and timeZone options are the device locale and the timeZone parameter. Details use MonarchCollapsible, which says Expanded or Collapsed, instead of Show and Hide titles. iOS uses the same names, except target (iOS object), image (iOS avatarURL) and the Kotlin-style booleans (groupByDay, loading, failed, loadingMore, loadMoreFailed).
accessibility: Day headings are headings.

Each event's sentence, time, tags and body are one element read as the sentence, its absolute date and time, "Automated" for rules, its tags and its body, such as "Ana Ruiz moved Acme renewal, Mar 4, 2026, 2:00 PM, Negotiation". The relative time is visual.
Markers, avatars and the line are hidden from TalkBack.
Details are a MonarchCollapsible after the event: a control named "Details" with Expanded or Collapsed, at least 48dp high.
Loading is one element read as "Loading activity" with an indeterminate progress.
A feed that is not grouped by day is named "Activity".
Text wraps and scales with the font size.
edgeCases: Days appear in the order of their first event, so an oldest-first feed reads oldest day first.
Day boundaries follow timeZone (the device's zone by default); an event near midnight can move to another day in another zone.
Events from another year get the year in their day heading.
An event without an actor reads as its verb and target only.
Load more is hidden while the first page is loading or failed, and without onLoadMore.
Event ids must be unique: they are the list keys.
The sentence joins actor, verb and target with spaces; languages that need another order should pass the whole sentence as the verb.
Sticky headings use the canvas color; on another background they show as a band.
Relative times refresh every minute when now is null.

title: ActivityWidget
wrapsNative: MonarchWidget (a Monarch card on androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column with a Material 3 DropdownMenu and a View all button) holding a compact MonarchActivityTimeline (an androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn of event rows) with a bounded height
summary: A recipe, not a component: the recent-activity card of a dashboard, a MonarchWidget around a compact MonarchActivityTimeline of the latest few events, with View all leading to the full log.
whenToUse: On a dashboard or a home screen that shows what changed recently, when the full activity log is another screen.
whenNotToUse: For the full log or an audit trail, open a screen with MonarchActivityTimeline on its own. For the person's own notifications, use the notification center pattern.
api: MonarchWidget(title = …, onViewAll = …) { MonarchActivityTimeline(events = events.take(6), modifier = Modifier.heightIn(max = …), groupByDay = false, density = MonarchActivityTimelineDensity.Compact, loading = …, now = …, labels = MonarchActivityTimelineLabels(list = …, empty = …)) }

states.name: ready
states.description: The first events, newest first. Pass only the latest few (the web default is 6); View all opens the rest.

states.name: loading
states.description: Pass loading = true to the timeline so the card shows the timeline's own placeholder rows under the widget's title.

states.name: empty
states.description: The timeline shows its empty text; set labels.empty to "No activity yet" or the product's wording.

states.name: failed
states.description: Set the widget's state to MonarchWidgetState.Failed() with onRetry: the card shows the error with Try again instead of the timeline.

appearance: The widget's surface and subtle border with its title row, then the compact timeline: tone-coloured dots or avatars, the sentence in the default text color and the time in the muted text color. The same roles change with dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ActivityWidget is a component with a limit prop and its own "Recent activity" and "No activity yet" strings. On Android, as on iOS, it is a recipe of MonarchWidget and MonarchActivityTimeline: the app passes the first events (events.take(6)) and its own title, already localised, so Monarch ships no strings for it. The web view-all link is an href; on Android onViewAll is a callback the app uses to navigate to the full log. The Android timeline is a LazyColumn, unlike the iOS VStack, so inside a scrolling dashboard it needs a bounded height (Modifier.heightIn(max = …)); in a widget of a non-scrolling grid it can fill the space it is given. The web timeZone prop is the timeline's timeZone parameter.
accessibility: The widget title is a TalkBack heading, then each event is read as one sentence: actor, verb, target and time.
Automated actors carry the visible "Automated" tag from the timeline, so people and rules are told apart without color.
View all and Try again are Material 3 buttons with 48dp touch targets.
edgeCases: Keep the list short: pass five or six events and lead to the full log; more scroll inside the bounded height.
Pass now and timeZone from a fixed clock in tests and previews so relative times and day groups do not change between runs.
Ungrouped (groupByDay = false) reads better in a short card; grouped by day suits a taller widget.

name: MonarchAddressAutocomplete
title: AddressAutocomplete
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.ExposedDropdownMenuBox with a read-only androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedTextField that opens androidx.compose.material3.ModalBottomSheet with MonarchSearchBar and a androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn of suggestions; a form of MonarchTextField with androidx.compose.ui.autofill.ContentType address types and MonarchCountrySelect
summary: An address field with suggestions from the app's own provider: search, pick a suggestion, and the street, city, region, postal code and country fill in for review, with manual entry one step away.
whenToUse: For a postal address in checkout, billing, shipping or a profile, when the app has an address provider (its own endpoint, the Places SDK or android.location.Geocoder behind a suspending function).
whenNotToUse: Not for a place or point of interest on a map (use a map search), and not when no provider is available (use MonarchTextField fields with the address autofill content types, MonarchCountrySelect and MonarchRegionSelect).
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchAddressAutocomplete(address: MonarchAddressAutocompleteAddress, onAddressChange: (MonarchAddressAutocompleteAddress) -> Unit, search: suspend (query: String) -> List<MonarchAddressAutocompleteSuggestion>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, mode: MonarchAddressAutocompleteMode? = null, onModeChange: ((MonarchAddressAutocompleteMode) -> Unit)? = null, enabled: Boolean = true, allowManualEntry: Boolean = true, minQueryLength: Int = 3, debounceMillis: Long = 300L, locale: Locale? = null, helperText: String? = null, errorText: String? = null, fieldErrors: Map<MonarchAddressAutocompleteField, String> = emptyMap(), resolve: (suspend (MonarchAddressAutocompleteSuggestion) -> MonarchAddressAutocompleteAddress)? = null, onSuggestionSelect: ((MonarchAddressAutocompleteSuggestion, MonarchAddressAutocompleteAddress) -> Unit)? = null, searchIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, suggestionIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAddressAutocompleteLabels = MonarchAddressAutocompleteLabels())

@ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchAddressAutocompleteInline(address: MonarchAddressAutocompleteAddress, onAddressChange: (MonarchAddressAutocompleteAddress) -> Unit, search: suspend (query: String) -> List<MonarchAddressAutocompleteSuggestion>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, mode: MonarchAddressAutocompleteMode? = null, onModeChange: ((MonarchAddressAutocompleteMode) -> Unit)? = null, enabled: Boolean = true, allowManualEntry: Boolean = true, minQueryLength: Int = 3, debounceMillis: Long = 300L, locale: Locale? = null, helperText: String? = null, errorText: String? = null, fieldErrors: Map<MonarchAddressAutocompleteField, String> = emptyMap(), resolve: (suspend (MonarchAddressAutocompleteSuggestion) -> MonarchAddressAutocompleteAddress)? = null, onSuggestionSelect: ((MonarchAddressAutocompleteSuggestion, MonarchAddressAutocompleteAddress) -> Unit)? = null, searchIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, suggestionIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAddressAutocompleteLabels = MonarchAddressAutocompleteLabels())

data class MonarchAddressAutocompleteAddress(line1: String = "", line2: String = "", city: String = "", region: String = "", postalCode: String = "", countryCode: String? = null) { val isEmpty: Boolean }
class MonarchAddressAutocompleteSuggestion(id: String, label: String, description: String? = null, address: MonarchAddressAutocompleteAddress? = null)
enum class MonarchAddressAutocompleteMode { Search, Manual }
enum class MonarchAddressAutocompleteField { Line1, Line2, City, Region, PostalCode, Country }

class MonarchAddressAutocompleteLabels(label: String? = null, placeholder: String? = null, searching: String? = null, resolving: String? = null, empty: String? = null, searchFailed: String? = null, resolveFailed: String? = null, enterManually: String? = null, backToSearch: String? = null, filled: String? = null, cancel: String? = null, line1: String? = null, line2: String? = null, city: String? = null, region: String? = null, postalCode: String? = null, country: String? = null, optional: String? = null, tooShort: ((length: Int) -> String)? = null, results: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null)

options.name: address
options.description: The address. A pick replaces it; the form edits its parts.

options.name: onAddressChange
options.description: Called with the new address after a pick, a manual entry or an edit of the form.

options.name: search
options.description: Returns the suggestions for the trimmed text. Throw to show "Couldn’t search addresses." with Try again. Cancelled when the text changes or the sheet closes.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the component.

options.name: mode
options.description: The search field only, or with the form, when the app owns it. null keeps it inside, starting on the form when the address has a street line.

options.name: onModeChange
options.description: Called when the mode changes.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the field, the form and the buttons can be used.

options.name: allowManualEntry
options.description: Offers "Enter the address manually" under the field and at the end of the list.

options.name: minQueryLength
options.description: The characters needed before search runs.

options.name: debounceMillis
options.description: How long to wait after typing before search runs. A newer text cancels the wait and the older search.

options.name: locale
options.description: The language of the country names in the summary and the country field. null uses the first locale of the configuration.

options.name: helperText
options.description: Guidance under the search field.

options.name: errorText
options.description: An error under the search field; the field is in the error state.

options.name: fieldErrors
options.description: Errors of the form's fields, shown under each field.

options.name: resolve
options.description: Turns a picked suggestion without an address into one. Throw to show the resolve error. Without it such a suggestion fills only the street line.

options.name: onSuggestionSelect
options.description: Receives the picked suggestion and the address it gave.

options.name: searchIcon
options.description: An icon at the start of the search field. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: suggestionIcon
options.description: A decorative icon at the start of each suggestion, such as a pin, tinted muted.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

states.name: search, empty
states.description: The search field shows the placeholder, with "Enter the address manually" under it.

states.name: search, filled
states.description: The search field shows the address on one line, wrapping when long.

states.name: too short
states.description: The sheet asks for more characters and does not search.

states.name: searching
states.description: The sheet's search field shows its pending state and the status line says "Searching…".

states.name: suggestions
states.description: The sheet lists the suggestions under "2 addresses found", then the manual entry row.

states.name: no results
states.description: The sheet says "No addresses found" above the manual entry row.

states.name: search failed
states.description: MonarchInlineErrorRetry says "Couldn’t search addresses." with Try again, which reruns the same text.

states.name: resolving
states.description: A linear progress indicator labelled "Getting the address details…" shows under the field, and the field is disabled.

states.name: resolve failed
states.description: The resolve error is the field's error and is announced.

states.name: manual
states.description: The form shows street, apartment (optional), city, region, postal code and country, then "Search for an address".

states.name: disabled
states.description: The field, the form and the buttons take the disabled colors and nothing responds.

appearance: The search field and the form use MonarchTextField's colors: a surface fill with the input border, the danger strong color in error. The sheet is on the surface color; suggestion labels are the default text color and descriptions, icons and the status line the muted color; the manual entry and back buttons are ghost buttons. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Monarch adds no map or places SDK and makes no requests: search and resolve are the app's suspending functions, cancelled through coroutine cancellation instead of an AbortSignal (iOS uses async closures and task cancellation). MonarchAddressAutocomplete, as on iOS, opens the search in a bottom sheet; MonarchAddressAutocompleteInline lays it out as the web does, an editable field with the suggestions in a card under it. The form fields in both carry the platform's address autofill content types (AddressStreet, AddressAuxiliaryDetails, AddressLocality, AddressRegion, PostalCode); the country is a MonarchCountrySelect, which autofill does not fill. The field is a read-only exposed dropdown anchor, so TalkBack reads it as a control that expands, where iOS reads a button. The web's LocationFields adapter and idPrefix, and iOS's isRequired, are not offered; wrap the component in a form field for a required mark. The results count is shown as a visible status line as well as announced. Marked experimental, as a product composite, until a Rook app adopts it. The type names match iOS.
accessibility: The search field is a Material 3 exposed dropdown anchor named by its label ("Address"), whose value is the address on one line; the error is its error semantics.

In the sheet the title is a heading, and a status line that is always present is a polite live region: it reads "Searching…", the too-short hint, "No addresses found" or the number found as they change.
Each suggestion is one button, read as its label and description, at least 48dp high; the icon is decorative.
"Address filled in. Check the details." and the resolve error are announced through a polite live region that is always present.
The form fields are standard text fields named by their labels, with address autofill content types; the optional apartment line has "Optional" as helper text.
The manual entry, back, retry and Cancel controls are buttons at least 48dp high.
edgeCases: An answer that arrives after the text changed is dropped, because the coroutine that asked for it was cancelled.
A suggestion without an address and without resolve fills only the street line, for review.
Leaving the search for manual entry keeps an existing street line; otherwise the typed text becomes the street line.
Long addresses wrap in the search field; the form fields grow at font scale 2.0, so the component should sit in a vertically scrolling screen.
The country field lists the 249 ISO countries; a provider's code outside them is still shown.

name: MonarchAgendaList
title: AgendaList
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn with LazyListScope.stickyHeader, MonarchEventChip, MonarchEmptyState, android.icu.text.DateFormat
summary: Events grouped by day in a scrolling list: a pinned heading per day with the date, a Today marker and the number of events, all-day events first, longer events on each day they touch, and an empty state.
whenToUse: For the agenda view of a calendar, a bookings screen or a schedule tab, where people scan what is coming day by day and tap an event to open it.
whenNotToUse: For one day laid out in hours use a time grid. For a picker of dates use MonarchMiniMonth or the Material 3 DatePicker. For a feed of things that happened use MonarchActivityTimeline.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAgendaList(events: List<MonarchAgendaEvent>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, from: Long? = null, days: Int? = null, today: Long? = System.currentTimeMillis(), showEmptyDays: Boolean = false, timeZone: String? = null, dayNotes: Map<Long, List<String>> = emptyMap(), state: LazyListState = rememberLazyListState(), contentPadding: PaddingValues = PaddingValues(), labels: MonarchAgendaListLabels = MonarchAgendaListLabels(), onSelect: ((MonarchAgendaEvent) -> Unit)? = null)

class MonarchAgendaEvent(id: String, title: String, start: Long, end: Long? = null, allDay: Boolean = false, detail: String? = null, color: Color = Color.Unspecified, status: MonarchEventChipStatus = MonarchEventChipStatus.Confirmed)

class MonarchAgendaListLabels(today: String? = null, allDay: String? = null, count: ((Int) -> String)? = null, emptyTitle: String? = null, until: ((String) -> String)? = null, range: ((String, String) -> String)? = null)
typealias MonarchCalendarEvent = MonarchAgendaEvent

options.name: events
options.description: The events in any order, each with an id, a title, a start and optionally an end, allDay, a detail, a color and a status. Times are epoch milliseconds.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the list. Give it a bounded height, as for any LazyColumn.

options.name: from
options.description: Any time on the first day listed. By default the first day with an event. Events that started earlier and still run appear on it.

options.name: days
options.description: How many days to list from from. By default through the last event. At most 400 days.

options.name: today
options.description: Any time on the day marked Today, or null for no marker. Pass a fixed value in tests and previews.

options.name: showEmptyDays
options.description: Lists the days in the range that have no events and no notes, with "0 events".

options.name: timeZone
options.description: The zone days and times are read in; the web's timeZone. An IANA id such as Europe/Berlin; null, or an id the device does not know, is the device's zone.

options.name: dayNotes
options.description: Informational lines shown first in a day, such as time off or a holiday, keyed by any time on that day. A day with notes is listed even without events.

options.name: state
options.description: The scroll state, to scroll to a day from outside.

options.name: contentPadding
options.description: Padding around the content, for example for system bars.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for "Today", "All day", the count, "Nothing scheduled" and the spoken "until" and "to".

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Opens an event. Without it the events are labels, not buttons.

states.name: days
states.description: Each day has a heading pinned while its events scroll, with the date, a Today badge on today and the count; events are bar event chips.

states.name: multi-day
states.description: A timed event shows its start and end on its first day, "All day" on days it covers whole and "– 02:00" on its last day.

states.name: notes
states.description: Muted caption lines before the day's events.

states.name: empty
states.description: MonarchEmptyState titled "Nothing scheduled" when no day is listed.

states.name: event status
states.description: Tentative, cancelled and declined events use the event chip's dashed, struck-through and muted forms and say their status.

appearance: Headings sit on the surface color with a subtle divider; the date is in the default text color (the strong accent on today), the count in the muted color and Today in an info badge. Events keep the event chip's colors: the event color only as the bar and a light tint. High contrast themes use their stronger text and border roles.
platformNotes: The web AgendaList reads ISO days in an IANA zone, takes a renderEvent wrapper and moves focus between events with the arrow keys. On Android events are epoch milliseconds read in the zone of an IANA id, as on the web, TalkBack and hardware keyboards move through the list's items themselves, and a wrapper is not needed because the app handles onSelect. The web's headingLevel has no meaning in Compose; headings have the heading semantics. The web's hourCycle and locale come from the configuration's locale. The web's empty slot is not offered; the built-in empty state takes labels.emptyTitle. The web's accent Today marker is a MonarchBadge in the info tone, because MonarchTone has no accent tone; the date of today uses the strong accent role directly. iOS builds the same component with the same name.
accessibility: Each day heading is one element with heading semantics, read as "Wednesday, November 4, Today, 3 events", so TalkBack's heading navigation moves from day to day.
Each event is a MonarchEventChip read as one element: title, spoken time ("9:30 AM to 10:15 AM", "until 2:00 AM" or "All day"), status and detail.
With onSelect each event is a button with a 48dp touch target reserved in the layout; without it the events have no click action.
Today is a word in a badge, not only a color; statuses are words read by the event chip.
Text scales with the font size setting; the heading wraps instead of cutting the date.
edgeCases: An event that ends exactly at midnight does not appear on the next day.
An end before the start is treated as no end.
Ids must be unique; one event appears on several days with the same id, under different headings.
Give the list a bounded height; inside a vertically scrolling Column it needs Modifier.height.
Days and times are read in timeZone, so pass the zone of the place the events happen when it differs from the device.
today defaults to the time of composition; pass a fixed value for previews and tests.

name: MonarchAiActionLog
title: AiActionLog
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of entry rows with Material 3 HorizontalDivider, composing MonarchAiAgentAvatar, MonarchBadge, MonarchButton and MonarchEmptyState; android.icu.text.RelativeDateTimeFormatter for the times and androidx.compose.ui.text.LinkAnnotation for target links
summary: An audit list of what AI agents did: the agent, marked as an AI agent, what it did and to what, when, and Undo for actions that can be reversed.
whenToUse: On an agent's screen, in an assistant panel or in a record's history, where people check what agents changed on their behalf and reverse what they do not want.
whenNotToUse: For people's actions on a record, use MonarchActivityTimeline. For a single change the agent just made, offer undo with MonarchAiUndoBanner.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchAiActionLog(entries: List<MonarchAiActionLogEntry>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, now: Long? = null, pageSize: Int = 200, locale: Locale? = null, onUndo: (suspend (id: String) -> Unit)? = null, onOpenTarget: ((MonarchAiActionLogEntry) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiActionLogLabels = MonarchAiActionLogLabels())

data class MonarchAiActionLogEntry(id: String, date: Long, agent: MonarchAiAgentRef, action: String, target: String? = null, url: String? = null, undoable: Boolean = false, undone: Boolean = false, agentImage: Painter? = null)

class MonarchAiActionLogLabels(label: String? = null, actorKind: String? = null, undo: String? = null, undoLabel: ((description: String) -> String)? = null, undone: String? = null, undoneAnnouncement: ((description: String) -> String)? = null, undoFailed: ((description: String) -> String)? = null, openTarget: ((target: String) -> String)? = null, empty: String? = null, showMore: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null)

options.name: entries
options.description: The actions, in the order to show them, usually newest first: id, date (epoch milliseconds), agent, action, target, URL, whether it can be undone and whether it was.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the log.

options.name: now
options.description: The reference time for relative times, in epoch milliseconds. null follows the clock, refreshed every minute.

options.name: pageSize
options.description: How many entries show at first and how many Show more adds; at least one.

options.name: locale
options.description: The locale of the relative times. null uses the first locale of the configuration.

options.name: onUndo
options.description: Reverses an action, given its entry id. Shows Undo on undoable entries; the button shows progress while it runs. Throw to show and announce the failure.

options.name: onOpenTarget
options.description: Opens an entry's target. null opens its http or https URL through the system (LocalUriHandler).

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

states.name: entry
states.description: The decorative agent avatar, the agent's name in the strong body style with an outlined "AI agent" badge, the action and target, and the relative time.

states.name: link
states.description: A target with an http or https URL is an underlined link in the link color; other URLs show as plain text.

states.name: undoing
states.description: The entry's Undo button shows its spinner; pressing again does nothing.

states.name: undone
states.description: The action text turns muted, the time line adds "Undone" and Undo goes away; announced.

states.name: undo failed
states.description: "Could not undo: …" under the entry in the strong danger color; Undo stays; announced.

states.name: paged
states.description: A secondary Show more button says how many entries it adds.

states.name: empty
states.description: A small MonarchEmptyState, "No AI activity yet.".

appearance: Rows separated by subtle dividers on the surface behind the log. The name in default text, the badge outlined in neutral, the action in default text (muted once undone), the time in muted caption text, links in the link color and failures in the strong danger color. The same roles in dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: A product pattern, experimental until a Rook app adopts it, built only from Monarch parts. Names and parameters follow iOS: entries, now, pageSize, labels and one onUndo handler that receives the entry id (the web has an onUndo per entry); isUndoable and isUndone are undoable and undone, and onUndo is a suspending function, Compose's equivalent of async throws. The rows are a Column, not a LazyColumn, so the log can sit in a screen or a panel that scrolls, as on iOS; long logs page with Show more. The web's href is url; components do not navigate, so onOpenTarget lets the app route it and the default opens a safe URL through LocalUriHandler. The web marks the actor kind with visually hidden brackets; Android shows the "AI agent" badge and TalkBack reads it in brackets. The web moves focus to the first revealed row after Show more; Android leaves focus on the button's place. Relative times use android.icu.text.RelativeDateTimeFormatter in the given or configured locale; the web's locale prop is locale. Monarch bundles no icons, so the failure text has no icon. The agent's picture is agentImage: Painter? because Monarch loads no images.
accessibility: Each entry is one TalkBack element read as "Research agent (AI agent) added a summary to Quarterly report", built by a tested pure function, so the actor is never mistaken for a person.
The time, "Undone" and a failure are the entry's state description.
A target link is a named custom action, "Open Quarterly report".
The agent avatar is decorative.
Undo buttons are named per entry ("Undo: Research agent added a summary to Quarterly report") and keep a 48dp touch target.
A successful and a failed undo are announced through a polite live region that is always present, so nothing is announced when the log first appears.
The list is a traversal group named "AI activity".
edgeCases: A time in the future reads "now"; past times step from minutes to hours, days, weeks, months and years.
An entry that is undoable but already undone has no Undo.
A blank target is left out of the sentence; an unsafe URL such as javascript: keeps the target as plain text with no action.
pageSize below 1 counts as 1. A change of pageSize starts the paging over.
The undo state of an entry is kept by id while the log is on screen; the app should also set undone on its entry after a successful undo.

name: MonarchAiAgentAvatar
title: AiAgentAvatar
wrapsNative: MonarchAvatar (square shape) in an androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Box with Modifier.drawBehind drawing the state ring (DrawScope.drawRoundRect with a SweepGradientShader turned by rememberInfiniteTransition, or PathEffect.dashPathEffect), and a CircleShape badge
summary: The picture of an AI agent: a rounded square with an AI badge, so it is never taken for a person's round avatar, and a ring that shows whether the agent is working, waiting for someone or stopped with an error.
whenToUse: Wherever an agent appears as an actor: beside its messages, in a list of agents, on a task it owns.
whenNotToUse: Not for people, workspaces or apps (use MonarchAvatar). Not to show that a single answer is AI-generated (use MonarchAiGeneratedBadge).
api: @Composable public fun MonarchAiAgentAvatar(agent: MonarchAiAgentRef, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, image: Painter? = null, state: MonarchAiAgentState = MonarchAiAgentState.Idle, size: MonarchAvatarSize = MonarchAvatarSize.Md, showState: Boolean = false, decorative: Boolean = false, badgeIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiAgentAvatarLabels = MonarchAiAgentAvatarLabels())
public enum class MonarchAiAgentState { Idle, Working, Waiting, Error }
public class MonarchAiAgentAvatarLabels(kind: String? = null, state: ((MonarchAiAgentState) -> String)? = null)

options.name: agent
options.description: The agent from the conversation model: name names the avatar, codename feeds the initials, id picks the fallback color. avatar is a URL that the app loads itself and passes as image.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the avatar and its state text.

options.name: image
options.description: The agent's picture, loaded by the app. null shows the initials.

options.name: state
options.description: What the agent is doing: idle, working, waiting (needs a person) or error.

options.name: size
options.description: 24, 32 or 40dp before the font scale, as MonarchAvatar.

options.name: showState
options.description: Writes the state beside the picture.

options.name: decorative
options.description: Hides the avatar from TalkBack when the agent's name is written beside it; a state other than idle is still read.

options.name: badgeIcon
options.description: An icon inside the badge, for example a bot glyph, given the badge's content color. Monarch bundles no icons; without it the badge is a filled mark.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the kind ("AI agent") and the state names.

states.name: idle
states.description: No ring; the AI badge.

states.name: working
states.description: A ring in the AI strong and AI subtle colors that turns once every 1.6 seconds; a still AI strong ring when animations are off.

states.name: waiting
states.description: A dashed ring in the warning strong color.

states.name: error
states.description: A ring in the danger strong color and a danger solid badge.

states.name: no picture
states.description: Initials of the codename, else the name, on a color picked from the agent id; the color alone when there are no letters or digits.

appearance: A rounded square picture with a small round badge at the bottom end corner, filled with the AI solid color (danger solid on error) and ringed with the surface color. Rings use the AI, warning and danger strong roles. All colors are theme roles, so dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: Same states and labels as iOS. Sizes are MonarchAvatar's three sizes; the web's xs, xl and numeric sizes are not offered. The web draws a bot glyph and iOS an SF Symbol; Monarch for Android bundles no icons, so the badge is a filled mark and the app may pass badgeIcon. Following the Android image convention the picture is a Painter the app loads (iOS loads agent.avatar with AsyncImage), so there is one composable instead of iOS's two initialisers. The web's moving ring is a turning sweep gradient here too, and stands still when animations are removed.
accessibility: The avatar is one TalkBack element with the image role, read as "Research agent, AI agent", plus the state when it is not idle, such as ", Working", which is also its state description.
The state is always in words, so it never depends on the ring's color, dash or motion.
With decorative the avatar is hidden, except that a state other than idle is read on its own.
The visible state text is not read a second time.
When animations are removed the working ring stands still.
The picture and the badge grow with the font scale.
edgeCases: A name of emoji or symbols only shows the fallback color without initials.
A blank codename falls back to the name; a missing id picks the color from the name.
A long state text wraps beside the picture.

title: AiAgentBuilder
wrapsNative: MonarchTabs on phones and a Row of two panes at expanded width (androidx.compose.material3.adaptive.currentWindowAdaptiveInfoV2), with a verticalScroll Column of MonarchTextField, MonarchAiConnectorPicker and MonarchAiKnowledgeScope and a test pane of MonarchAiThread over MonarchAiPromptInput
summary: A recipe, not a component: a screen to define an AI agent (persona, instructions, tools and knowledge) and try the unsaved definition in a test chat.
whenToUse: Admin or builder screens where people create or edit an agent and want to test it before saving.
whenNotToUse: Picking an existing agent: use MonarchAiAgentPicker. Only choosing tools or knowledge for a conversation: use MonarchAiConnectorPicker or MonarchAiKnowledgeScope on their own.
api: if (currentWindowAdaptiveInfoV2().windowSizeClass.isWidthAtLeastBreakpoint(WindowSizeClass.WIDTH_DP_EXPANDED_LOWER_BOUND)) Row { form(Modifier.weight(1f)); VerticalDivider(); test(Modifier.weight(1f)) } else Column { PrimaryTabRow(selectedTabIndex = tab) { Tab("Configure"); Tab("Test") }; … }

form: Column(Modifier.verticalScroll(…)) { MonarchAiAgentAvatar(agent, size = MonarchAvatarSize.Lg, decorative = true); MonarchTextField(name, errorText = …); MonarchTextField(role, helperText = …); MonarchTextField(instructions, singleLine = false, helperText = "n / 8000 characters"); MonarchAiConnectorPicker(connectors, onConnectorsChange, title = "Tools", searchable = false); MonarchAiKnowledgeScope(sources, selection, onSelectionChange, expandIcon); MonarchButton("Save agent", variant = Primary) }

test: Column { MonarchAiAgentAvatar(agent, state = Working while streaming); MonarchButton("Restart test") { conversation.stop(); conversation.reset() }; MonarchAiThread(messages, Modifier.weight(1f), daySeparators = false); MonarchAiPromptInput(onSubmit = { conversation.send(it, body = mapOf("agent" to definition())) }) }

options.name: definition
options.type: App state: name, role, instructions, tool permissions (MonarchAiConnector list), knowledge ids
options.description: Held by the app and saved on Save agent; every edit clears the saved message, as the web's onChange does.

options.name: connectors
options.description: The tools the agent may use, grouped by connector with a permission per tool (allow, ask, never), shown by MonarchAiConnectorPicker. Destructive tools cannot be set to allow unless the app passes allowsDestructiveAutoApprove.

options.name: sources
options.description: Knowledge the agent can read, as a MonarchAiKnowledgeScope tree. Leave the section out without sources.

options.name: conversation
options.description: The test chat. Each test message is sent with the current definition in body under "agent", so the transport runs the unsaved agent. Leave the Test tab and pane out without it.

options.name: maxInstructions
options.description: Longest instructions; the field stops at it and its helper text counts characters.

options.name: save
options.description: Save agent checks the name, then the app saves; the status line is a polite live region that reads Agent saved.

states.name: phone
states.description: Configure and Test are two Material 3 primary tabs; the form scrolls in Configure and the test chat fills Test.

states.name: expanded width
states.description: From 840dp the form and the test chat show side by side with a vertical divider.

states.name: name missing
states.description: After Save agent with an empty name, the name field shows "Give the agent a name." as its error and nothing is saved.

states.name: saved
states.description: The status line reads Agent saved until the next edit.

states.name: testing
states.description: The avatar reads Working while the reply streams; Restart test stops and clears the test conversation.

states.name: empty test
states.description: The thread shows "Send a message to try the agent."

appearance: Every part is an existing component: MonarchTextField, MonarchAiConnectorPicker, MonarchAiKnowledgeScope, MonarchAiAgentAvatar, MonarchAiThread, MonarchAiPromptInput and MonarchButton, with Material 3 primary tabs and a subtle-border divider in the Monarch theme. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web ships AiAgentBuilder as one component with the form and the test chat side by side and stacked on narrow screens. On Android the phone form is two primary tabs, Configure and Test, so the test chat gets the whole screen and its lazy thread never sits inside the scrolling form; at expanded width (840dp, the Material window size class) the two show side by side. The web's tool checkbox list is MonarchAiConnectorPicker, which groups tools by connector and gives each an allow, ask or never permission, as the plan's dependency asks; the definition sends the allowed and asked tool ids. The web's avatar URL field is the app's own picker beside MonarchAiAgentAvatar, since Monarch loads no images. The web's save promise with progress and error is the app's own call; this recipe shows the saved state as a polite live region and the missing name as the field's error. The web moves focus to the name field when the name is missing; this recipe does not move focus. iOS has not covered this entry yet.
accessibility: Persona, Instructions and Knowledge are MonarchText headings; Tools is the connector picker's title.
The name field shows its error as text and reports it to TalkBack through MonarchTextField's error semantics.
The character count is the instructions field's helper text, read with the field.
The saved message is a polite live region, announced without moving focus.
Configure and Test are Material 3 tabs with the tab role and selected state.
The avatars are decorative; the agent's name is in the name field and the test messages.
edgeCases: Keep the test thread out of the scrolling form: on phones it is its own tab, at expanded width its own pane.
A test send while a tool call waits for approval is refused and the text comes back into the prompt input.
Edits after a save clear the saved message, so it never claims an unsaved edit was saved.
Long instructions stop at the limit; pasted text over it is cut to the limit.

name: MonarchAiAgentCard
title: AiAgentCard
wrapsNative: MonarchCard (androidx.compose.material3.Surface) with androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column and FlowRow, composing MonarchAiAgentAvatar and MonarchBadge
summary: What an AI agent is and what it may do: its name and role, a description, capabilities, the tools it can call, the data it can see and who owns it, with optional actions; a compact variant summarises it for lists.
whenToUse: On an agent's profile screen, in an agent directory, or in a picker where people choose which agent to work with and need to know what it can do and see before they trust it.
whenNotToUse: For the agent's face beside a message, use MonarchAiAgentAvatar. For a log of what the agent did, use MonarchAiActionLog.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchAiAgentCard(agent: MonarchAiAgentRef, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, image: Painter? = null, description: String? = null, capabilities: List<String> = emptyList(), tools: List<MonarchAiAgentTool> = emptyList(), dataAccess: List<String> = emptyList(), owner: String? = null, state: MonarchAiAgentState = MonarchAiAgentState.Idle, variant: MonarchAiAgentCardVariant = MonarchAiAgentCardVariant.Full, labels: MonarchAiAgentCardLabels = MonarchAiAgentCardLabels(), actions: (@Composable FlowRowScope.() -> Unit)? = null)
data class MonarchAiAgentTool(name: String, description: String? = null)
enum class MonarchAiAgentCardVariant { Full, Compact }

class MonarchAiAgentCardLabels(kind: String? = null, capabilities: String? = null, tools: String? = null, dataAccess: String? = null, owner: String? = null, toolCount: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null)

options.name: agent
options.description: The agent: name, role, codename and id. The name and role are written; the codename and id feed the avatar's initials and color.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the card.

options.name: image
options.description: The agent's picture, loaded by the app. null shows the avatar's initials.

options.name: description
options.description: One or two sentences on what the agent is for.

options.name: capabilities
options.description: Short capability phrases, shown as neutral badges, such as "Drafts replies".

options.name: tools
options.description: The tools the agent can call, each with what it does. The compact card shows only their count.

options.name: dataAccess
options.description: What data the agent can read, such as "Documents in this space". Full card only.

options.name: owner
options.description: Who owns or maintains the agent. Full card only.

options.name: state
options.description: What the agent is doing now, shown by the avatar's ring and read for a state other than idle.

options.name: variant
options.description: Every section and the actions, or the compact summary for lists and pickers.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for "AI agent", the section headings, "Owner" and the tool count.

options.name: actions
options.description: Buttons at the end of the full card, such as "Start a chat". They wrap onto new lines. Not shown on the compact card.

states.name: full
states.description: A 40dp agent avatar, the name and the role line, the description, then the sections that have content: What it can do, Tools, Data it can see, Owner, and the actions.

states.name: compact
states.description: A 32dp avatar, the name, the role line and a tool count ("3 tools"), the description and the capability badges; no other section and no actions.

states.name: idle, working, waiting, error
states.description: The agent avatar's ring and badge; a state other than idle is read by TalkBack. The working ring stands still when animations are off.

states.name: no role
states.description: The role line is "AI agent" alone.

appearance: MonarchCard's surface fill, default border and corners. The name in the strong body style and default text color, the role line and tool count in muted caption text, section headings in the subtle text color and label style, capability badges in the neutral subtle tone. The same roles in dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: A product pattern, experimental until a Rook app adopts it, built only from Monarch parts. Names and parameters follow iOS (MonarchAiAgentCard, MonarchAiAgentTool, MonarchAiAgentCardVariant, MonarchAiAgentCardLabels); the Android card also takes image: Painter? because Monarch loads no images, and actions is a trailing FlowRowScope slot. The web's headingLevel, as, nameId and descriptionId exist for HTML structure and for the web AiAgentPicker; on Android the name and role line are one heading and a picker builds its own rows. The web's owner can be any node, such as an avatar with a name; here it is text, as on iOS. The description is text rather than any node.
accessibility: The name and the role line are one TalkBack element with the heading property, read as "Research agent, Analyst · AI agent"; the role line always says "AI agent".
Section headings (What it can do, Tools, Data it can see) are headings.
Each tool is one element read as its name and what it does, built by a tested pure function.
The owner is read as "Owner, Sam Rivera".
The avatar is decorative; it is read only for a state other than idle, such as "Error".
On the compact card the capability badges are a traversal group named "What it can do".
Actions stay separate buttons with their own 48dp touch targets.
edgeCases: Sections with no content are left out; a card with only an agent shows the header alone.
A blank description, owner or tool description is treated as absent.
A long name or description wraps; nothing is cut at font scale 2.0.
The compact card ignores dataAccess, owner and actions, as on the web and iOS.

name: MonarchAiAgentPicker
title: AiAgentPicker
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.selection.selectableGroup of androidx.compose.foundation.selection.selectable rows, each a compact MonarchAiAgentCard with an androidx.compose.material3.RadioButton mark
summary: Chooses one AI agent from compact agent cards that show what each agent is for, what it can do and how many tools it has.
whenToUse: Starting a conversation or a task with one of a few agents, or setting the default agent of a space, when people should see what each agent does before choosing.
whenNotToUse: To choose a model rather than an agent, use MonarchAiModelPicker. For dozens of agents that need search, use MonarchCombobox with the agent names. For several agents at once, use checkbox rows.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchAiAgentPicker(agents: List<MonarchAiAgentPickerOption>, selected: String?, onSelect: (String) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, layout: MonarchAiAgentPickerLayout = MonarchAiAgentPickerLayout.List, enabled: Boolean = true, labels: MonarchAiAgentPickerLabels = MonarchAiAgentPickerLabels())

class MonarchAiAgentPickerOption(agent: MonarchAiAgentRef, description: String? = null, capabilities: List<String> = emptyList(), tools: List<MonarchAiAgentTool> = emptyList(), state: MonarchAiAgentState = MonarchAiAgentState.Idle, image: Painter? = null, enabled: Boolean = true) { val key: String }
enum class MonarchAiAgentPickerLayout { List, Grid }
class MonarchAiAgentPickerLabels(label: String? = null, empty: String? = null)

options.name: agents
options.description: The agents in display order: the agent, a description, capabilities, tools, its state, its picture loaded by the app, and whether it can be chosen.

options.name: selected
options.description: The chosen agent's key (agent.id, or agent.name without an id), or null for none.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Called with the key of the agent the person chooses. Not called for the chosen agent or an agent that cannot be chosen.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the group.

options.name: layout
options.description: One agent per row, or two columns on windows at least 640dp wide below font scale 1.5.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether any agent can be chosen.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the group name ("Choose an agent") and the empty message.

states.name: chosen
states.description: The chosen card has a 2dp AI accent border and its radio mark is filled.

states.name: not chosen
states.description: The card has its usual border and an empty radio mark.

states.name: unavailable
states.description: An option with enabled = false, or every option when the picker is disabled: the radio mark is disabled and the row is read as disabled; the card stays readable.

states.name: empty
states.description: With no agents, "No agents are available." in the muted text role.

appearance: Each option is the compact MonarchAiAgentCard (surface fill, default border, large radius) followed by the Material 3 radio mark. The chosen card is outlined with the AI solid role; the empty message uses the muted text role. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from the theme roles.
platformNotes: The web's AiAgentPicker is a radiogroup with roving focus and arrow keys; on Android each option is a selectable row inside selectableGroup, so TalkBack reads each as a radio button with its position, and a hardware keyboard moves with Tab. The web tints the chosen card with the AI subtle fill and puts a check in its corner; MonarchAiAgentCard has no fill option, so on Android the chosen card gets the AI accent border and the Material 3 radio mark sits after the card. The web dims an unavailable card with opacity; Monarch does not dim with alpha, so it is shown by the disabled radio mark and TalkBack's disabled state. The web's onChange also passes the option; on Android onSelect passes the key and the app looks the option up. The picture of an agent is a Painter the app loads. iOS has not built this component yet.
accessibility: Each agent is one TalkBack element with the radio button role: the agent's name and role line, its description, capabilities and tool count, and whether it is selected.
The group is named "Choose an agent".
An agent that cannot be chosen is read as disabled and does not react to a tap.
Each row is at least 48dp tall, so the whole card is the touch target.
The choice is shown by a filled radio mark and a heavier border, not by color alone.
In right to left the card is at the right and the mark at the left; text wraps at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: Agents without an id use their name as the key: keep names unique or give ids.
A selected key that matches no agent shows nothing chosen.
Choosing the chosen agent again does not call onSelect.
The grid falls back to one column on phones and at large font scales.
Many agents: the picker is a plain column; put it in a scrolling screen, not in a lazy list.
