name: MonarchAiAgentRunTimeline
title: AiAgentRunTimeline
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of clickable event rows with bars drawn on androidx.compose.foundation.Canvas, androidx.compose.material3.SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow for the view, and a table in Modifier.horizontalScroll; MonarchBadge, MonarchTabularNumber and MonarchButton
summary: The trace of one agent run: every model call, tool call and hand-off as a bar on a shared time axis, totals for time, tokens and cost, and details that open per event, with a table view of the same data.
whenToUse: In a developer or operator view of an agent: to see where a run spent its time, tokens and money, and to jump from an event to the conversation part it produced.
whenNotToUse: For the steps an assistant shows the person while it works, use MonarchAiChainOfSteps. For usage over a period, use MonarchAiUsageMeter or a chart.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchAiAgentRunTimeline(events: List<MonarchAiRunEvent>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, currency: String = "USD", now: Long? = null, mode: MonarchAiAgentRunTimelineMode? = null, onModeChange: ((MonarchAiAgentRunTimelineMode) -> Unit)? = null, initialMode: MonarchAiAgentRunTimelineMode = MonarchAiAgentRunTimelineMode.Timeline, onOpenPart: ((MonarchAiRunEvent) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiAgentRunTimelineLabels = MonarchAiAgentRunTimelineLabels())

public data class MonarchAiRunEvent(id: String, kind: MonarchAiRunEventKind, name: String, startedAt: Long, endedAt: Long? = null, inputTokens: Long? = null, outputTokens: Long? = null, costMicros: Long? = null, detail: String? = null, partId: String? = null, messageId: String? = null)
public enum class MonarchAiRunEventKind { Model, Tool, Handoff, Error }
public enum class MonarchAiAgentRunTimelineMode { Timeline, Table }

public class MonarchAiAgentRunTimelineLabels(label: String? = null, modeLabel: String? = null, mode: ((MonarchAiAgentRunTimelineMode) -> String)? = null, kind: ((MonarchAiRunEventKind) -> String)? = null, events: String? = null, totalDuration: String? = null, inputTokens: String? = null, outputTokens: String? = null, cost: String? = null, start: String? = null, duration: String? = null, eventColumn: String? = null, kindColumn: String? = null, running: String? = null, empty: String? = null, notAvailable: String? = null, openPart: String? = null, formatDuration: ((Long) -> String)? = null, formatOffset: ((Long) -> String)? = null)

options.name: events
options.description: The run's events in any order: kind, name, start and end in epoch milliseconds (end null while running), tokens, cost in micros, a detail text, and the conversation part or message it belongs to.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the trace.

options.name: currency
options.description: The ISO 4217 currency of costMicros. An unknown code is written after the number.

options.name: now
options.description: The end of events that are still running, in epoch milliseconds. Without it they end at the latest known time, so the trace never reads the clock.

options.name: mode
options.description: The view, timeline or table. Without it the component keeps the state.

options.name: onModeChange
options.description: Called when the person switches the view; set mode in it when the app holds the state.

options.name: initialMode
options.description: The first view when the component keeps the state.

options.name: onOpenPart
options.description: Adds "Show in conversation" to an open event that has a partId or a messageId.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, and the duration and offset formats.

states.name: timeline
states.description: A time axis (start, middle, end), then one row per event with its kind badge, name, duration and bar.

states.name: open event
states.description: Start offset, duration, the known tokens and cost, the detail in the code style, and Show in conversation.

states.name: running
states.description: "Running" instead of a duration, and a bar that fades into the AI thinking color.

states.name: error
states.description: The kind badge in the danger tone and a danger bar.

states.name: table
states.description: Event, kind, start, duration, input and output tokens and, when any event has one, cost; unknown values show "–". Scrolls sideways.

states.name: empty
states.description: "No events yet" under the totals.

appearance: Bars use the AI solid color for model calls, the AI tool color for tools, info solid for hand-offs and danger solid for errors, on a muted track. Totals are strong body text in tabular figures with muted captions. All colors are theme roles, so dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: Same parameters as iOS, with Android types: times are epoch milliseconds, counts and costs are Long, and the view is a nullable mode with onModeChange instead of a Binding. Bars are drawn on a Canvas inside each event's row, so the bar, the header and the details form one row for touch and TalkBack. The web draws a moving shimmer on running bars; Android draws a still gradient, so there is nothing to stop when animations are removed. The web's detail is any React node; on Android it is text. The axis shows three ticks instead of five, for phone widths. Costs below one unit keep up to four decimals, so a model call of a fraction of a cent does not read as zero.
accessibility: The trace is a traversal group named "Agent run"; the visible heading has the heading role.
Each total is one element, such as "Total time, 4.2 s".

Each event is one button read as its kind, name and duration, such as "Tool, search_invoices, 1.6 s", with an Expanded or Collapsed state and expand and collapse actions; a running event says "Running".
Bars and the axis are hidden, so nothing depends on their color or length.
Each fact of an open event is its own text; Show in conversation is a button with a 48dp touch target.
In the table each row is one element with every known value; unknown values are left out of what is read.
The view switch is a Material 3 segmented button row named "View".
edgeCases: Events are sorted by start; equal starts keep their order.
An event that ends before it starts is drawn with no length.
An instant event keeps a 2dp bar.
Long names wrap in the timeline and widen the table, which scrolls.

name: MonarchAiArtifactCanvas
title: AiArtifactCanvas
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.ModalBottomSheet (or a Column pane) with androidx.compose.material3.SecondaryTabRow, composing MonarchAiMarkdown, MonarchAiCodeBlock, MonarchCopyButton and MonarchButton; android.webkit.WebView through androidx.compose.ui.viewinterop.AndroidView for HTML
summary: The working surface for an artifact an assistant produced: title and version, Copy, Download and Save, an optional version stepper, and Preview and Code tabs, as a full-height sheet on phones.
whenToUse: When a reply produced a document, code, a table, a chart, an image or a web page the person opens, reads, copies or saves, usually from MonarchAiArtifactCard.
whenNotToUse: For a short snippet inside the reply, use MonarchAiCodeBlock or MonarchAiMarkdown in the message. For a file the person uploaded, use the file preview.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchAiArtifactCanvas(artifact: MonarchAiCanvasArtifact, open: Boolean, onDismissRequest: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, placement: MonarchAiArtifactCanvasPlacement = MonarchAiArtifactCanvasPlacement.Auto, tab: MonarchAiArtifactCanvasTab? = null, onTabChange: ((MonarchAiArtifactCanvasTab) -> Unit)? = null, image: Painter? = null, onCopy: ((MonarchAiCanvasArtifact) -> Unit)? = null, onDownload: ((MonarchAiCanvasArtifact) -> Unit)? = null, onSave: (suspend (MonarchAiCanvasArtifact) -> Unit)? = null, closeIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, versions: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, preview: (@Composable (MonarchAiCanvasArtifact) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiArtifactCanvasLabels = MonarchAiArtifactCanvasLabels())

data class MonarchAiCanvasArtifact(val id: String, val kind: MonarchAiArtifactKind, val title: String, val version: Int, val content: String, val language: String? = null)
enum class MonarchAiArtifactCanvasTab { Preview, Code }
enum class MonarchAiArtifactCanvasPlacement { Auto, Inline, Sheet }

class MonarchAiArtifactCanvasLabels(label: ((title: String) -> String)? = null, kind: ((MonarchAiArtifactKind) -> String)? = null, version: ((version: Int) -> String)? = null, preview: String? = null, code: String? = null, close: String? = null, copy: String? = null, copied: String? = null, download: String? = null, save: String? = null, frameTitle: ((title: String) -> String)? = null, sandboxNote: String? = null, imageUnavailable: String? = null, noPreview: String? = null)

options.name: artifact
options.description: The version shown: id, kind, title, version number, content as text and the language of the Code tab.

options.name: open
options.description: Whether the canvas is shown.

options.name: onDismissRequest
options.description: Called by the close button and, on a sheet, by the back gesture, a swipe down or a tap outside. Set open to false.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the sheet or the pane. Give a pane a bounded height.

options.name: placement
options.description: Auto is a full-height sheet below 640dp and a pane from 640dp, as on the web; Inline is always a pane; Sheet is always a sheet.

options.name: tab
options.description: The open tab. null lets the canvas keep it, starting on Preview; kinds without a preview show Code.

options.name: onTabChange
options.description: Called when the person picks a tab.

options.name: image
options.description: The picture of an image artifact, loaded by the app from the artifact's address. Without it the preview says the image is not available.

options.name: onCopy
options.description: Called after Copy put the content on the clipboard. Copy is always shown.

options.name: onDownload
options.description: Shows Download; the app produces the file.

options.name: onSave
options.description: Shows Save as the primary action. It shows progress until the call returns; taps meanwhile do nothing.

options.name: closeIcon
options.description: The close glyph. Without one the close button is a ghost text button "Close artifact" at the end of the toolbar, because Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: versions
options.description: A version stepper under the title, usually MonarchAiArtifactVersions with the app's versions.

options.name: preview
options.description: Replaces the built-in preview for every kind, such as a chart the app draws. Never render the content as HTML in it.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

states.name: document or table
states.description: Preview renders the Markdown with MonarchAiMarkdown; Code shows the Markdown source.

states.name: code or chart
states.description: No Preview tab unless preview is given; the source shows in MonarchAiCodeBlock with line numbers.

states.name: web page
states.description: Preview is a sandboxed WebView that fills the canvas, with "Sandboxed preview: scripts, forms and network requests are blocked." under it.

states.name: image
states.description: Preview shows the app's Painter at full width; without one, a warning line.

states.name: saving
states.description: Save shows the MonarchButton loading state until onSave returns.

states.name: sheet
states.description: A full-height Material 3 modal bottom sheet with its drag handle, announced by its pane title "Artifact: Q3 summary".

states.name: pane
states.description: The same content where the app places it, with the same pane title.

appearance: The title uses the heading style in the default text role with the kind and version under it in the muted caption; Copy and Download are small ghost buttons and Save a small primary button; the tabs are the Material 3 secondary tab row in the theme; the sandbox note is the muted caption and the image warning the warning strong role. The sheet uses the Material 3 sheet surface. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from the theme roles and the composed components.
platformNotes: The web shows a pane beside the thread and a full-screen sheet under 640px; Android does the same with a full-height ModalBottomSheet, so the system back gesture and the drag handle close it. The web closes its pane with Escape and returns focus to the opener; on Android the pane closes with its close button and the app's navigation keeps the back gesture. HTML renders in an android.webkit.WebView, the View the plan names, with JavaScript off, network, file and content access blocked, every navigation refused, a Content Security Policy with no network and no scripts, and scripts, frames, embeds, base, meta refresh and event attributes removed; the web uses an iframe with an empty sandbox. The web loads an image artifact from its URL; Monarch loads no images, so the app passes a Painter. The web's renderPreview can fall back per kind by returning undefined; Android's preview slot replaces the preview for every kind. The web's versions, onVersionChange and onCompare props are a versions slot where the app composes MonarchAiArtifactVersions with its icons. allowImages is not offered: Markdown images stay text, as the web's default. iOS has not built this component yet.
accessibility: The title is a TalkBack heading; the kind and version are read after it.
The sheet and the pane carry the pane title "Artifact: <title>", so TalkBack announces the canvas when it opens.
The tabs are Material 3 tabs, read as selected or not; each has a 48dp target.
The close button is named "Close artifact" and has a 48dp target; without an icon it is a text button at the end of the toolbar.
The web page preview is named "Preview of <title>" and the sandbox is said in words under it.
Copy announces the copy through MonarchCopyButton; Save is read as loading while it runs.
In right to left the close button is at the left; the title wraps at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: The content is untrusted model output: a web page never runs scripts or loads anything from the network, and the app's preview slot must not render it as HTML either.
Code and chart artifacts open on Code even when the tab asked for is Preview.
A pane needs a bounded height (fill a pane of a list-detail layout); in a vertically scrolling parent the inner scroll cannot be measured.
Long content scrolls inside the canvas; the header and the actions stay in place.
Several canvases: open one at a time; each keeps its own tab.

name: MonarchAiArtifactCard
title: AiArtifactCard

summary: The compact card a reply shows for an artifact it made, such as "Q3 summary · Document · v3", that opens the artifact.
whenToUse: In an assistant reply, for each artifact part of the message: a document, code, a table, a chart, an image or a web page the reply produced.

options.name: title
options.description: The title of the artifact.

options.name: kind
options.description: What the artifact is, which selects the kind name.

options.name: version
options.description: The version number.

options.name: onClick
options.description: Called when the card is activated. Open the artifact here.

options.name: part
options.description: The artifact part of a message, from MonarchAiConversation.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Called with the part when the card is activated.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the card.

options.name: description
options.description: Secondary text under the title.

options.name: active
options.description: Whether the artifact is the one currently on show.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the card can be activated.

options.name: icon
options.description: The kind's icon in a tile before the text. Monarch bundles no icons; without one there is no tile.

options.name: trailingIcon
options.description: An icon after the action, such as a chevron. Decorative.

options.name: kindLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in name of the kind.

options.name: versionLabel

options.name: actionLabel

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the press, focus and hover interactions.

states.name: resting
states.description: A surface-coloured card with the default border; the action text is in the strong AI color.

states.name: pressed
states.description: The Material 3 ripple.

states.name: active
states.description: The subtle AI fill, a 2dp AI border, "Showing" in place of "Open", and the selected state.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The subtle background and border and the disabled text color.

appearance: A card with 12dp corners. At rest the surface role with the default border; active, the subtle AI fill with a 2dp AI border. The title is default text, the kind and version line muted text, the action the strong AI role. The optional icon tile is the subtle AI fill with the strong AI color.
platformNotes: The web takes the artifact part of the conversation model; Android offers that overload and one that takes the title, kind and version, as iOS does. The parity map names MonarchCard; a card has no pressed, active or disabled colors, so the card is a Material 3 Surface with an onClick, drawn with MonarchCard's radius and border. The web draws its own kind glyphs and a chevron; Monarch for Android bundles no icons, so both are slots. The web's 28rem maximum width has no Monarch token on Android; constrain the width with the modifier. The web's hover state has no counterpart on touch.
accessibility: One button whose content description reads the title, the kind, the version in words, the description and the action.
The artifact on show has the selected state, reads "Showing" and has a heavier border, not color alone.
The icon and the trailing icon are inside cleared semantics and never read.
The card is at least 48dp high and its touch target at least 48dp.
Text grows with the font size setting and wraps; nothing is truncated.
A focus ring follows the card's shape for keyboard focus.
edgeCases: A long title wraps; nothing is truncated.
An empty versionLabel removes the version from the visible line and from what TalkBack reads.
The card does not open anything itself; onClick or onOpen does.

name: MonarchAiArtifactVersions
title: AiArtifactVersions
wrapsNative: MonarchAiMessageBranch (Material 3 IconButton) for previous and next, androidx.compose.material3.DropdownMenu with DropdownMenuItem behind a MonarchButton for the version menu, androidx.compose.material3.FilterChip for Compare, and MonarchDiffViewer for the changes; android.icu.text.DateFormat for the dates
summary: Steps through the versions of an AI artifact with previous and next buttons, the position, a menu to jump to any version and Compare with previous, which shows a diff of what changed.
whenToUse: Above a document, a reply or a piece of code that an AI model has rewritten several times, so people can go back to an earlier version and see what each rewrite changed.
whenNotToUse: For the regenerated versions of a chat reply, use MonarchAiMessageBranch alone. For the saved history of a document people edit, use MonarchVersionHistoryPanel.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchAiArtifactVersions(selection: Int, versions: List<MonarchAiArtifactVersion>, onSelectionChange: (Int) -> Unit, previousIcon: @Composable () -> Unit, nextIcon: @Composable () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, comparing: Boolean? = null, onComparingChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, granularity: MonarchDiffViewerGranularity = MonarchDiffViewerGranularity.Word, showCompare: Boolean = true, enabled: Boolean = true, locale: Locale? = null, timeZone: String? = null, menuIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiArtifactVersionsLabels = MonarchAiArtifactVersionsLabels())
data class MonarchAiArtifactVersion(version: Int, createdAt: Long, label: String? = null, content: String? = null)

class MonarchAiArtifactVersionsLabels(label: String? = null, position: ((version: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, previous: String? = null, next: String? = null, select: String? = null, versionTag: ((version: Int) -> String)? = null, versionName: ((version: Int) -> String)? = null, compare: String? = null, announce: ((version: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null)

options.name: selection
options.description: The version number shown. A number not in versions shows the newest.

options.name: versions
options.description: Every version, in any order; shown oldest to newest, one per number (the last given wins). Each carries its date in epoch milliseconds and its content for the diff.

options.name: onSelectionChange
options.description: Called with the chosen version number, from the buttons or the menu.

options.name: previousIcon
options.description: The previous button's icon, such as a chevron to the start with mirrorInRtl = true. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: nextIcon
options.description: The next button's icon, mirrored in the same way.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the stepper.

options.name: comparing
options.description: Whether the diff with the previous version shows, when the app owns it with onComparingChange. null keeps the state in the stepper.

options.name: onComparingChange
options.description: Called when Compare is toggled.

options.name: granularity
options.description: Whether the diff marks changed words (prose) or whole lines (code).

options.name: showCompare
options.description: Whether Compare with previous is offered.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the controls can be used, for example false while a new version streams.

options.name: locale
options.description: The locale of the dates in the menu. null uses the first locale of the configuration.

options.name: timeZone
options.description: The zone of the dates in the menu. An IANA id such as Europe/Berlin; null, or an id the device does not know, is the device's zone.

options.name: menuIcon
options.description: An icon after "Choose a version", such as a drop-down arrow. Decorative.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

states.name: middle version
states.description: Previous and next are enabled; the position reads "Version 2 of 4".

states.name: first or last
states.description: Previous (first) or next (last) is disabled.

states.name: single version
states.description: Both buttons are disabled; the position reads "Version 1 of 1"; there is no Compare.

states.name: menu open
states.description: A Material 3 drop-down menu lists every version as "v3 · Shorter intro · Nov 3, 2026, 2:05 PM"; the shown one is bold and selected.

states.name: comparing
states.description: Compare is selected (filled) and a MonarchDiffViewer from the previous version to this one shows under the controls, at most 384dp tall.

states.name: compare unavailable
states.description: No Compare when there is no previous version or either version has no content.

states.name: no versions
states.description: Nothing is shown.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Every control is disabled and the position uses the disabled text color.

appearance: Two icon buttons around the position in caption text, a ghost "Choose a version" button and a Material 3 filter chip in the colors MonarchTheme gives Material 3 (filled when selected), then the diff viewer on its own surface with added and removed lines in their success and danger colors and signs. The same roles in dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Names follow iOS; Binding<Int> and Binding<Bool>? become selection with onSelectionChange and comparing with onComparingChange, and showsCompare is showCompare. The stepper reuses MonarchAiMessageBranch for previous and next, so its icons are required slots (Monarch bundles no icons). The web's native select and the iOS Menu with an inline Picker are a Material 3 DropdownMenu, the platform's menu, behind a ghost button. The web's aria-pressed compare button and the iOS button-style Toggle are a Material 3 FilterChip, read as selected or not. As on iOS, the diff is MonarchDiffViewer shown by the component when Compare is on, where the web calls onCompare for the app to render an AiArtifactDiff, so each version carries its content; on Android the diff is a lazy list, so it is held to 384dp and the stepper can sit in a screen that scrolls. A change from the buttons is announced by the branch as "Version 3 of 5"; a change from the menu is announced as "Showing version 3 of 5". Dates use android.icu.text.DateFormat in the given locale and time zone (the configuration's locale and the device's zone by default).
accessibility: The controls are a traversal group; previous, the position and next are a group named "Versions" (MonarchAiMessageBranch).
Previous and next are named "Previous version" and "Next version", keep 48dp touch targets, and are disabled at the ends.
The position is visible text, "Version 3 of 5", from the labels or the built-in string.
The menu button is named "Choose a version"; in the menu the shown version is selected and bold, so it never depends on color.
Compare is a filter chip read with its selected state.

A change of version from the buttons is announced by MonarchAiMessageBranch; a change from the menu is announced politely as "Showing version 3 of 5" from a live region that is always present, so nothing is announced at first.
The diff is MonarchDiffViewer with "Version 2" and "Version 3" as the names of its sides; changes are marked with signs as well as color.
edgeCases: Versions can arrive in any order; two entries with the same number keep the last.
A selection that is not a version number shows the newest, and onSelectionChange is not called for it.
Choosing the version already shown in the menu does nothing.
An empty content is compared as an empty text; a null content hides Compare.
Without onComparingChange and comparing the compare state survives configuration changes (rememberSaveable).

name: MonarchAiAssistantPanel
title: AiAssistantPanel
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.ModalBottomSheet on phones, or a Column pane the app places (for example the supporting pane of androidx.compose.material3.adaptive.layout.SupportingPaneScaffold), composing MonarchAiThread, MonarchAiPromptInput, MonarchAiContextChips, MonarchAiWelcome, MonarchAiStarterPrompts and MonarchAiAgentAvatar
summary: The assistant surface any app mounts: a header with the agent and close, chips for what the assistant can see on the current screen, and a thread over a prompt input, as a bottom sheet on phones or a pane on wide windows.
whenToUse: A product adds a general assistant beside its screens. Hold the MonarchAiConversation above the navigation so the conversation survives moving between screens, and open the panel from MonarchAiLauncher.
whenNotToUse: A full-screen chat product: use the ai-chat-page recipe. A single AI action on a record: use the action's own button and show the result with MonarchAiSummaryCard or MonarchAiInlinePrompt.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchAiAssistantPanel(title: String, messages: List<MonarchAiConversationMessage>, open: Boolean, onOpenChange: (Boolean) -> Unit, onSend: suspend (String) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, placement: MonarchAiAssistantPanelPlacement = MonarchAiAssistantPanelPlacement.Auto, prompt: TextFieldState = rememberTextFieldState(), status: MonarchAiConversationStatus = MonarchAiConversationStatus.Idle, error: MonarchAiConversationError? = null, offline: Boolean = false, queuedCount: Int = 0, slow: Boolean = false, agent: MonarchAiAgentRef? = null, agentImage: Painter? = null, context: List<MonarchAiContextItem> = emptyList(), starters: List<MonarchAiStarterPrompt> = emptyList(), minimized: Boolean = false, onMinimizedChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, onStop: (() -> Unit)? = null, onRemoveContext: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, threadState: LazyListState = rememberLazyListState(), closeIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, removeContextIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = closeIcon, minimizeIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, headerActions: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null, toolbar: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, footer: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, empty: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, promptFocusRequester: FocusRequester? = null, labels: MonarchAiAssistantPanelLabels = MonarchAiAssistantPanelLabels())

@ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchAiAssistantPanel(conversation: MonarchAiConversation, title: String, open: Boolean, onOpenChange: (Boolean) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, placement: MonarchAiAssistantPanelPlacement = MonarchAiAssistantPanelPlacement.Auto, prompt: TextFieldState = rememberTextFieldState(), agent: MonarchAiAgentRef? = null, agentImage: Painter? = null, context: List<MonarchAiContextItem> = emptyList(), starters: List<MonarchAiStarterPrompt> = emptyList(), minimized: Boolean = false, onMinimizedChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, onRemoveContext: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, closeIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, removeContextIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = closeIcon, minimizeIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, headerActions: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null, toolbar: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, footer: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, empty: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, promptFocusRequester: FocusRequester? = null, body: Map<String, MonarchAiJSON> = emptyMap(), labels: MonarchAiAssistantPanelLabels = MonarchAiAssistantPanelLabels())
enum class MonarchAiAssistantPanelPlacement { Auto, Inline, Sheet }

class MonarchAiAssistantPanelLabels(close: String? = null, minimize: String? = null, expand: String? = null, inputLabel: String? = null, context: String? = null, welcome: String? = null, starters: String? = null, assistant: String? = null)

options.name: conversation
options.description: The conversation the panel shows and sends to. Its messages, status, error, connection, queue, slowness and agent are collected; sending calls send, and a refused send gives the text back to the prompt input; Stop calls stop.

options.name: title
options.description: The heading of the panel, such as "Assistant". It also names the pane (paneTitle) for TalkBack.

options.name: messages
options.description: The conversation, oldest first, shown by MonarchAiThread.

options.name: open
options.description: Whether the panel is shown.

options.name: onOpenChange
options.description: Called with false by the close button and, on a sheet, by the back gesture, a swipe down or a tap outside.

options.name: onSend
options.description: Sends the typed prompt or a chosen starter's prompt. Throw to give the typed text back to the prompt input.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the sheet or the pane. Give a pane a bounded height.

options.name: placement
options.description: Auto is a full-height bottom sheet on windows narrower than 640dp and a pane on wider ones; Inline is always a pane; Sheet is always a sheet.

options.name: prompt
options.description: The draft. It is kept while the panel is closed as long as the panel stays in the composition; hoist it to save drafts.

options.name: status
options.description: While Submitted or Streaming the avatar reads Working and Send becomes Stop; while a reply runs or a tool call awaits approval the starters are disabled.

options.name: error
options.description: The last turn's error, announced by the thread.

options.name: offline / queuedCount / slow
options.description: Passed to MonarchAiThread, which shows and announces its offline and slow notices.

options.name: agent
options.description: The agent in the header (name · role under the title) and in the welcome. Without one the avatar is named "Assistant" and no line is shown under the title.

options.name: agentImage
options.description: The agent's picture, loaded by the app; initials are shown without it.

options.name: context
options.description: What the assistant can see on the current screen, shown as MonarchAiContextChips above the thread.

options.name: starters
options.description: Suggested first prompts, shown under the welcome as a MonarchAiStarterPrompts list while the conversation is empty. Choosing one sends its prompt.

options.name: minimized
options.description: Collapses an inline pane to its header. Ignored on a sheet.

options.name: onMinimizedChange
options.description: Shows the minimize / expand button on an inline pane.

options.name: onStop
options.description: Stops the running reply, from the prompt input's Stop button and the Escape key of a hardware keyboard.

options.name: onRemoveContext
options.description: Lets the person remove a context chip by id.

options.name: threadState
options.description: The scroll position of the thread, kept while the panel is closed.

options.name: closeIcon / minimizeIcon
options.description: The app's glyphs (Monarch bundles no icons). With one, the button is a 48dp IconButton named by its label; without one, a small ghost button showing the label. The minimize glyph (a downward chevron) is turned up while collapsed.

options.name: removeContextIcon
options.description: The remove mark of the context chips, separate from the close glyph. It defaults to the close glyph, as before.

options.name: headerActions
options.description: Buttons before minimize and close, such as New conversation.

options.name: toolbar / footer
options.description: Passed to MonarchAiPromptInput: controls in its bar (a model picker) and content under it (MonarchAiDisclaimer).

options.name: empty
options.description: Replaces the whole empty state (the welcome and the starters).

options.name: promptFocusRequester
options.description: Moves focus to the prompt field, for example right after the app opens the panel. Passed to MonarchAiPromptInput.

options.name: body
options.description: Conversation overload only: extra request fields sent with each message from the panel, such as the selection the context chips show, merged over the conversation's own body. Read at each send.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings: close, minimize, expand, inputLabel, context, welcome, starters, assistant.

states.name: closed
states.description: Nothing is shown. The draft and the thread's scroll position stay in the panel's state.

states.name: sheet
states.description: A full-height Material 3 modal bottom sheet with its drag handle; the back gesture, a swipe down or a tap outside closes it. There is no minimize button.

states.name: pane
states.description: A column on the surface color where the app places it, with a divider under the header.

states.name: minimized
states.description: A pane shows only its header; the button reads Expand assistant.

states.name: empty
states.description: MonarchAiWelcome with the agent, "How can I help?" and the starters, scrolling when the panel is short.

states.name: running
states.description: The avatar reads Working, Send becomes Stop and the starters are disabled.

states.name: awaiting approval
states.description: The starters are disabled; a typed prompt that the conversation refuses comes back into the prompt input.

states.name: offline / slow / error
states.description: MonarchAiThread shows and announces its notice or the error.

appearance: Every part is an existing component: the header is the small agent avatar, the title in the subheading style in the default text color with the agent in the muted caption color, and muted icon buttons or ghost buttons; a pane fills with the surface color and has the border-coloured divider under the header; the sheet uses the Material 3 sheet colors of the Monarch theme. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those roles and components.
platformNotes: The web panel docks to the right or left edge of the window and becomes a full-screen modal sheet under 640px. On Android the phone form is a full-height ModalBottomSheet and the wide form is a pane the app places, usually the supporting pane of SupportingPaneScaffold; the web's side option is therefore not offered, because the scaffold decides the edge. The web's Escape closes the panel when nothing runs and stops a running reply; on Android the sheet closes with the back gesture, the drag handle or a tap outside, the inline pane leaves the back gesture to the app's navigation (as MonarchAiArtifactCanvas does), and Escape on a hardware keyboard still stops a running reply through the thread and the prompt input. The web moves focus to the input when the panel opens and returns it on close; on Android the input is not focused on open, so the keyboard does not cover the conversation, and the sheet's own focus handling returns focus. Minimize applies only to the pane: a sheet already has the platform's dismiss. The web takes the useAiConversation hook; Android offers an overload that takes MonarchAiConversation and one that takes plain state, as Compose hoists state. The web's context chips are label and value pairs; Android reuses MonarchAiContextItem (kind and label). The web's messageProps, threadProps and promptProps pass-throughs are not offered; an app that needs them composes MonarchAiThread and MonarchAiPromptInput itself. Starters use MonarchAiStarterPrompts in its list layout instead of plain buttons. The web's container query that switches AI components to their narrow layout has no Compose counterpart; the components inside already lay out for the width they get. iOS has not covered this entry yet.
accessibility: The title is a heading and the pane title of the sheet or the pane, so TalkBack names the panel when it appears.
The close and minimize buttons are named by their labels ("Close assistant", "Minimize assistant" or "Expand assistant"), with a 48dp touch target, whether they show an icon or text.
The avatar in the header is decorative; the agent's name and role are text under the title.
The prompt input is named "Message the assistant"; Send becomes Stop while a reply runs.
The thread announces new replies, errors and the offline notice through its polite live regions.
Starters are disabled, not hidden, while a reply runs or a tool call waits for approval.
The layout mirrors right to left: the close button sits at the start edge.
edgeCases: Give an inline pane a bounded height: the thread is a lazy list and cannot sit in a vertically scrolling parent.
Keep the panel in the composition with open = false (rather than removing it) to keep the draft and the scroll position.
A long title wraps at font scale 2.0; the buttons keep their size.
A starter that the conversation refuses (for example while a tool call waits for approval) is not sent and shows no error.
With no agent and no role, no line is shown under the title.

name: MonarchAiAttachmentTray
title: AiAttachmentTray
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyRow of MonarchAttachmentChip (MonarchFileTypeIcon, MonarchProgress, retry and remove buttons), with a polite live region for announcements
summary: The files attached to a message for an assistant, in a row that scrolls sideways, each with its type, name and size, upload progress, failure and retry, and a remove button.
whenToUse: Above the prompt field of an assistant's composer, for the files the person attached before sending.
whenNotToUse: For files already sent in a message, show MonarchAttachmentChip or MonarchFileCard in the message. For a long upload list, use an upload queue.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchAiAttachmentTray(files: List<MonarchAiAttachmentTrayFile>, onRemove: (String) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, onRetry: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, retryIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, removeIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiAttachmentTrayLabels = MonarchAiAttachmentTrayLabels())

public data class MonarchAiAttachmentTrayFile(id: String, name: String, sizeBytes: Long? = null, contentType: String? = null, progress: Float? = null, failed: Boolean = false, errorMessage: String? = null) { constructor(part: MonarchAiFilePart, id: String? = null, progress: Float? = null) }

public class MonarchAiAttachmentTrayLabels(label: String? = null, ready: ((String) -> String)? = null, removed: ((String) -> String)? = null, chip: MonarchAttachmentChipLabels = MonarchAttachmentChipLabels())

options.name: files
options.description: The attached files in the order they were added: name, size, MIME type, progress and failure (failed or an errorMessage). A conversation's MonarchAiFilePart converts with the secondary constructor.

options.name: onRemove
options.description: Removes a file by id; take it out of files.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the tray.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Disables the retry and remove buttons, for example while the message is sending.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Retries a failed upload by file id. Without it failed files have no retry button.

options.name: retryIcon / removeIcon
options.description: Icons for each chip's buttons. Monarch bundles no icons; without them the buttons show the words Retry and Remove.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the tray's name, the uploaded and removed announcements, and each chip's strings.

states.name: ready
states.description: Type icon, name and size.

states.name: uploading
states.description: The percentage under the name and a linear progress bar.

states.name: failed
states.description: The error message (or "Upload failed") in the danger color, with a retry button when onRetry is set.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Retry and remove are disabled.

states.name: empty
states.description: Nothing is drawn; only the empty live region stays, so the last removal is still announced.

appearance: A row of MonarchAttachmentChip tiles with the chip's control fill and border, each at most 240dp wide before the font scale, scrolling sideways. All colors are theme roles, so dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: Same parameters as iOS, with Android types: progress is a Float, the size is sizeBytes, and failed replaces isFailed. The web shows an image thumbnail for picture files; MonarchAttachmentChip has no thumbnail slot in the tray, so every file shows its type icon. The web moves keyboard focus to the next remove button after a removal; on Android the removal is announced and TalkBack focus is left to the system.
accessibility: The row is a traversal group named "Attachments".
Each file's name and the line under it are one element; the type icon is decorative.
Retry and remove are buttons named with the file name, such as "Remove report.pdf", with 48dp touch targets.
A finished upload ("photo.png uploaded") and a file removed with its button ("photo.png removed") are announced through a polite live region; a failure is announced by the chip.
edgeCases: Long names are shortened in the middle, so the extension stays visible.
A progress outside 0 through 1 is clamped; a progress of 1 counts as uploaded.
Several changes in one update are announced together, in one message.

options.name: state

options.name: suggestion

options.name: fieldName
options.description: The field's name, so the actions are read as "Accept suggested Company".

options.name: source
options.description: Where the value came from, shown as "From …" until the person edits it.

options.name: confidence
options.description: How sure the AI is, 0 through 1, shown as a MonarchAiConfidenceMeter badge while suggested.

options.name: lowThreshold / highThreshold
options.description: The confidence band edges, passed to MonarchAiConfidenceMeter.

options.name: confidenceExplanation
options.description: Why the AI chose the value, read with the confidence badge.

options.name: model / dateMillis
options.description: The model and the time in epoch milliseconds, read with the AI badge.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Disables Accept and Clear.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the badge texts, the action texts and names, the source and original lines and the announcements.

options.name: control
options.description: The form control, usually MonarchTextField.

states.name: suggested
states.description: A bar in the AI border color at the start edge; "AI suggested", the confidence badge, the source, and Accept and Clear.

states.name: accepted
states.description: "AI filled" and the source; no actions.

states.name: edited
states.description: "Edited by you" and "AI suggested: …" with the original value.

states.name: cleared
states.description: The control alone; the status line is gone.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Accept and Clear are disabled.

appearance: The status line uses the AI generated badge and the confidence badge as they are elsewhere, with the muted caption text. The marker bar uses the AI border role. All colors are theme roles, so dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: Same parameters as iOS with Android types (Float confidence, epoch milliseconds) and an added enabled. The web tints the input itself with the AI subtle background and border; a Compose control's inner field cannot be restyled from outside, so Android draws a bar in the AI border color at the start edge while suggested, as iOS does. The web notices typing through the input event and calls onEdit; Compose has no such event for any control, so the app sets edited in its own onValueChange (see the example). The web moves focus back to the control after Accept and Clear; Android announces the result instead.
accessibility: The control keeps its own label, value and role.
The status line is one merged TalkBack element read after the control, made of the badge, the confidence and the source text.
Accept and Clear are buttons named with the field, such as "Accept suggested Company", with 48dp touch targets.
After Accept or Clear, "Suggestion accepted" or "Suggestion cleared" is announced through a polite live region.
The suggested state is in words (the badge), so the marker bar's color is not the only signal.
edgeCases: A long source wraps onto its own line.
With no confidence and no source, the status line is the badge alone, followed by the actions.
If the app never sets edited, the field keeps saying "AI suggested" after the person types.

name: MonarchAiBackgroundTasks
title: AiBackgroundTasks
wrapsNative: MonarchButton with MonarchBadge counts opening androidx.compose.material3.ModalBottomSheet; task rows of androidx.compose.material3.Text, MonarchBadge, MonarchProgress (androidx.compose.material3.LinearProgressIndicator) and MonarchButton; android.icu.text.MeasureFormat and android.text.format.DateUtils for times
summary: A tray of the work agents do in the background: a button with running and waiting counts opens a sheet of tasks grouped into Needs you, Running and Finished, each with its status, progress, elapsed or end time and actions.
whenToUse: In an AI product, so long agent tasks stay visible after the chat is closed and the person can respond, retry, open or cancel them.
whenNotToUse: For one task in the conversation, use MonarchAiTaskProgress. For work that continues while the app is closed, post a system notification from onNotify; the tray only shows what the app reports.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchAiBackgroundTasks(tasks: List<MonarchAiBackgroundTask>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, inline: Boolean = false, now: Long? = null, onOpen: ((MonarchAiBackgroundTask) -> Unit)? = null, onCancel: ((MonarchAiBackgroundTask) -> Unit)? = null, onRetry: ((MonarchAiBackgroundTask) -> Unit)? = null, onRespond: ((MonarchAiBackgroundTask) -> Unit)? = null, onDismiss: ((MonarchAiBackgroundTask) -> Unit)? = null, onClearFinished: ((List<MonarchAiBackgroundTask>) -> Unit)? = null, onNotify: ((MonarchAiBackgroundTask) -> Unit)? = null, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, statusIcon: (@Composable (MonarchAiBackgroundTaskStatus) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiBackgroundTasksLabels = MonarchAiBackgroundTasksLabels())

data class MonarchAiBackgroundTask(id: String, title: String, status: MonarchAiBackgroundTaskStatus, agent: String? = null, progress: Float? = null, indeterminate: Boolean = false, step: String? = null, startedAt: Long? = null, endedAt: Long? = null, result: String? = null, error: String? = null)
enum class MonarchAiBackgroundTaskStatus { Queued, Running, NeedsInput, Succeeded, Failed, Cancelled }

class MonarchAiBackgroundTasksLabels(title: String? = null, runningCount: ((Int) -> String)? = null, queuedCount: ((Int) -> String)? = null, needsInputCount: ((Int) -> String)? = null, needsInputGroup: String? = null, runningGroup: String? = null, finishedGroup: String? = null, groupHeading: ((label: String, count: Int) -> String)? = null, status: ((MonarchAiBackgroundTaskStatus) -> String)? = null, elapsed: ((duration: String) -> String)? = null, ended: ((relative: String) -> String)? = null, progressLabel: ((title: String) -> String)? = null, open: String? = null, cancel: String? = null, retry: String? = null, respond: String? = null, dismiss: String? = null, clearFinished: String? = null, actionLabel: ((action: String, title: String) -> String)? = null, empty: String? = null, announce: ((title: String, status: String) -> String)? = null)

options.name: tasks
options.description: Every background task, in any order; the tray groups and sorts them.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the button, or of the panel when inline.

options.name: inline
options.description: Draws the panel in place, with no button and no sheet, for a side pane.

options.name: now
options.description: The reference time in epoch milliseconds; null follows the clock, refreshed every second while a task runs and the tray is visible.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Shows Open on every task.

options.name: onCancel
options.description: Shows Cancel on queued, running and waiting tasks.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Retry on failed tasks.

options.name: onRespond
options.description: Shows Respond on tasks that need input.

options.name: onDismiss
options.description: Shows Dismiss on finished tasks.

options.name: onClearFinished
options.description: Shows Clear finished while there are finished tasks; called with them.

options.name: onNotify
options.description: Called when a task succeeds, fails or starts needing input, so the app can post a system notification.

options.name: icon
options.description: The button's decorative leading icon.

options.name: statusIcon
options.description: A decorative icon before each task; the status is always also a word.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

states.name: button
states.description: The title with an info badge "2 running" (or a neutral "1 queued") and a warning badge "1 needs you".

states.name: needs you
states.description: Tasks waiting on the person, longest waiting first, with a warning Needs your input badge and Respond.

states.name: running
states.description: Running tasks (oldest first) then queued ones, with the agent, Running for 3 min 12 sec, the current step and a progress bar, determinate when a figure is known.

states.name: finished
states.description: Most recently ended first, with Done, Failed (the error in danger text) or Cancelled and Ended 5 minutes ago.

states.name: empty
states.description: "No background tasks".

states.name: announced
states.description: A change into Done, Failed or Needs your input is announced and passed to onNotify; the first show is not.

appearance: A small secondary button with tone badges; the sheet uses the raised surface. Task titles in strong body text, the status as a tone MonarchBadge, meta and steps in muted caption text, errors in danger-strong text, progress bars in the tone of the status (accent while running), and small primary, secondary and ghost buttons. All are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web opens a popover from the trigger; on a phone the tasks are a modal bottom sheet, as the plan names, and inline draws the panel in place. The web's controlled open state and align are not offered. The web's useAiRunNotifications hook (browser notifications) has no counterpart: work that outlives the app is a system notification, which the app posts from onNotify (needing POST_NOTIFICATIONS), as the plan notes. As on the web, a running task's status badge uses the AI tone and its progress bar the accent; the other statuses use their own tone for both. Dismiss is a text button: Monarch bundles no close glyph. The web's headingLevel and locale are not offered: headings are semantics headings and times use the device locale (MeasureFormat, DateUtils). Times are epoch milliseconds, not ISO strings. With removed animations the elapsed time is read once instead of every second. The web moves focus to the panel when an action removes its button; Android leaves focus to the system. There is no iOS AiBackgroundTasks yet. Experimental: an AI product composite that waits for a Rook app to adopt it.
accessibility: The panel title and the group headings ("Running (2)") are headings; the panel is a traversal group.
Each task's title, status word, agent, times and detail are read as one element; the status is always a word, never color alone.
Each progress bar is named "<title> progress".
Each action is a separate button named with the task, such as "Open: Summarize contracts", with a 48dp touch target.
Changes into Done, Failed and Needs your input are announced once from an always-present polite live region; nothing is announced on first show.
Icons are decorative and hidden.
edgeCases: Tasks without a start or end time go last in their group, in the given order.
A progress above 1 or below 0 is clamped; indeterminate or NaN shows the moving bar.
A waiting or queued task shows a bar only with a known figure.
Several changes in one update are announced together, joined by a period.
A task that first appears already finished is not announced.

examples.title: Trigger and popover
examples.template:
@OptIn(ExperimentalMonarchApi::class)
MonarchAiBackgroundTasks(
    initiallyOpen = true,
    tasks = tasks,
    now = {{now|millis}},
    onOpen = {},
    onCancel = { task -> tasks = tasks.filterNot { it.id == task.id } },
    onRetry = {},
    onRespond = {},
    onDismiss = { task -> tasks = tasks.filterNot { it.id == task.id } },
    onClearFinished = { finished -> tasks = tasks.filterNot { t -> finished.any { it.id == t.id } } },
)

    onCancel = { task -> tasks = tasks.filterNot { it.id == task.id } },
    onRetry = {},
    onRespond = {},
    onDismiss = { task -> tasks = tasks.filterNot { it.id == task.id } },
    onClearFinished = { finished -> tasks = tasks.filterNot { t -> finished.any { it.id == t.id } } },
)

name: MonarchAiChainOfSteps
title: AiChainOfSteps
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of step rows with androidx.compose.material3.CircularProgressIndicator for the running step, folded into MonarchCollapsible
summary: The steps an assistant is working through, as an ordered list that updates live and folds under a summary such as "4 steps" when every step has finished.
whenToUse: In an AI answer, to show the plan or the chain of actions the assistant is running, with the state of each step.
whenNotToUse: For the hidden reasoning of a model use a reasoning part in MonarchAiConversation. For a multi-step form the person fills in use MonarchStepper.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiChainOfSteps(steps: List<MonarchAiPlanStep>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, details: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(), collapsible: Boolean = true, initiallyExpanded: Boolean = false, announces: Boolean = true, stateIcon: (@Composable (MonarchAiPlanStepState) -> Unit)? = null, expandIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiChainOfStepsLabels = MonarchAiChainOfStepsLabels())

class MonarchAiChainOfStepsLabels(label: String? = null, state: ((MonarchAiPlanStepState) -> String)? = null, summary: ((count: Int, failed: Int) -> String)? = null, started: ((label: String, position: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, failedStep: ((label: String) -> String)? = null, finished: ((count: Int, failed: Int) -> String)? = null)

options.name: steps
options.description: The steps in order, for example from MonarchAiPlanPart. Update each state (Todo, Active, Done, Skipped, Failed) as the assistant works.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the list.

options.name: details
options.description: An optional detail under a step, such as a result or an error, by step id. Already localised.

options.name: collapsible
options.description: Whether the list folds under a summary once every step has finished.

options.name: initiallyExpanded
options.description: Whether the folded list starts open.

options.name: announces
options.description: Whether starts, failures and completion are announced to TalkBack. Turn it off when the thread announces progress itself.

options.name: stateIcon
options.description: An icon for every state but the running one, tinted by the state. Without it a drawn mark is shown: open for not started and skipped, filled for done and failed.

options.name: expandIcon
options.description: The chevron of the folded summary, passed to MonarchCollapsible.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the list name, the state names, the summary and the announcements.

states.name: todo
states.description: An open mark in the subtle text color; muted label.

states.name: active
states.description: A small CircularProgressIndicator in the AI strong color, or a still filled mark when animations are removed.

states.name: done
states.description: A filled mark in the success strong color.

states.name: failed
states.description: A filled mark in the danger strong color and the word "Failed" under the label.

states.name: skipped
states.description: An open mark, a struck-through muted label and the word "Skipped".

states.name: folded
states.description: Once every step has finished, a MonarchCollapsible with the summary ("3 steps, 1 failed").

appearance: Marks take the AI strong, success strong, danger strong or subtle text roles by state; labels the default or muted text role; details the muted text role. The summary uses MonarchCollapsible. All colors are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The step model is the shared MonarchAiPlanStep, whose not-started state is Todo (pending on the web). As on iOS, details are a map by step id because the shared step model has no detail field. The web draws a shimmer on the running label and iOS shows SF Symbols per state; Monarch for Android bundles no icons, so the marks are drawn shapes that differ by fill as well as color, failed and skipped are also written, and stateIcon lets the app pass its own icons. The web announces through a live region; Android uses a polite live region on an always-present node. The folded state is kept inside the component with rememberSaveable, as on iOS.
accessibility: The list is a traversal group named "Steps".
Each step is one TalkBack element: the label, with the state name and the detail as its state description, so the state does not depend on the mark or color.
Failed and skipped steps also show their state in words.
A step that starts or fails, and the end of the run, are announced once through a polite live region; the state at first appearance is not.
The folded summary is the MonarchCollapsible header: a button with an Expanded or Collapsed state and a 48dp touch target.
When animations are removed the running step shows a still mark instead of a spinner.
edgeCases: Long labels and details wrap at every font size.
An empty list shows nothing and never folds.
Several changes in one update are announced together, joined by full stops.
Step ids should be unique; the last state of a repeated id is used for comparisons.

MonarchAiChainOfSteps(

        MonarchAiPlanStep({{steps.0.id}}, {{steps.0.label}}, MonarchAiPlanStepState.{{steps.0.state|pascal}}),
        MonarchAiPlanStep({{steps.1.id}}, {{steps.1.label}}, MonarchAiPlanStepState.{{steps.1.state|pascal}}),
        MonarchAiPlanStep({{steps.2.id}}, {{steps.2.label}}, MonarchAiPlanStepState.{{steps.2.state|pascal}}),
        MonarchAiPlanStep({{steps.3.id}}, {{steps.3.label}}, MonarchAiPlanStepState.{{steps.3.state|pascal}}),
    ),

)

MonarchAiChainOfSteps(

title: AiChatPage
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.adaptive.navigation.NavigableListDetailPaneScaffold with MonarchAiConversationList in the list pane and a Column of MonarchAiConversationHeader, MonarchAiThread and MonarchAiPromptInput in the detail pane
summary: A recipe, not a component: the full chat screen of an assistant app, with the conversation history beside the open conversation on wide windows and as its own screen on phones.
whenToUse: An app whose main screen is a chat with an assistant and a history of conversations.
whenNotToUse: An assistant beside other screens: use MonarchAiAssistantPanel. A single conversation without history: compose MonarchAiThread over MonarchAiPromptInput.
api: NavigableListDetailPaneScaffold(navigator = rememberListDetailPaneScaffoldNavigator<String>(), listPane = { AnimatedPane { MonarchAiConversationList(conversations, onSelect = { active = it; conversation.reset(stored); navigator.navigateTo(ListDetailPaneScaffoldRole.Detail, it) }, activeId = active, onNew = …) } }, detailPane = { AnimatedPane { Column { … } } })
MonarchAiConversationHeader(title, agent = conversation.agent, onRename = …, navigationIcon = back to the history while one pane shows)
MonarchAiThread(messages, Modifier.weight(1f), status, error, onStop = conversation::stop, empty = { MonarchAiWelcome(…) { MonarchAiStarterPrompts(…) } })
MonarchAiPromptInput(label = "Message the assistant", state = prompt, onSubmit = { check(conversation.send(it)) }, busy = …, onStop = conversation::stop, footer = { MonarchAiDisclaimer() })
MonarchAiArtifactCanvas(artifact, open, onDismissRequest) for an artifact a reply produced: a sheet on phones, the scaffold's extraPane on wide windows

options.name: conversation
options.description: The open conversation. Switching history entries calls reset with the stored messages of the chosen one, as the web's onSelectConversation does.

options.name: conversations
options.description: The history, shown by MonarchAiConversationList with search, pinning, rename and delete.

options.name: active
options.description: The open conversation's id, marked current in the list and passed to the navigator as the detail key.

options.name: onNew
options.description: Adds New conversation at the top of the list; the recipe adds an untitled entry, resets the conversation and opens it.

options.name: title
options.description: Shown by MonarchAiConversationHeader, which renames in place with onRename.

options.name: empty
options.description: The thread's empty content while the conversation has no messages.

options.name: toolbar / footer
options.description: MonarchAiPromptInput's toolbar (a model picker) and footer.

options.name: artifact
options.description: An artifact to show in MonarchAiArtifactCanvas: a full-height sheet on phones (its Auto placement), the scaffold's extraPane on wide windows.

states.name: two panes
states.description: On a wide window the history and the conversation show side by side.

states.name: one pane
states.description: On a phone the history is a screen; choosing or starting a conversation opens it, and the system back gesture or the header's back button returns to the history.

states.name: empty
states.description: The thread shows MonarchAiWelcome with starters; choosing one sends it.

states.name: running
states.description: Send becomes Stop; the thread shows thinking, streams the reply and announces it.

states.name: error / offline
states.description: MonarchAiThread shows and announces the error or the offline notice.

appearance: Every part is an existing component: the Material 3 list-detail scaffold, MonarchAiConversationList, MonarchAiConversationHeader, MonarchAiThread, MonarchAiPromptInput and MonarchAiDisclaimer in the Monarch theme. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web ships AiChatPage as one component: a history rail beside the chat from 768px, the history in a start-edge sheet below it, and the artifact canvas as a third column. On Android it is a recipe on the list-detail pattern: NavigableListDetailPaneScaffold shows the history and the chat side by side on a wide window and as two screens on a phone, with the system back gesture and predictive back, instead of a drawer-like sheet. The navigator starts on the history, as Android list-detail screens do; an app that opens straight into the last chat passes initialDestinationHistory with the list and the detail entries. The artifact canvas is MonarchAiArtifactCanvas, a sheet on phones and the scaffold's extraPane on wide windows. The web's messageProps wiring (regenerate, feedback, branches, tool approval) is the default MonarchAiMessage of MonarchAiThread plus the app's own calls on MonarchAiConversation. The web focuses the prompt after New conversation; this recipe does not move focus, so the keyboard does not open by itself. iOS has not covered this entry yet.
accessibility: MonarchAiConversationList is named "Conversation history" by its label and marks the open conversation as selected.
The conversation title is a heading in MonarchAiConversationHeader; the back button to the history is named "Conversation history".
MonarchAiThread announces replies, errors and the offline notice through polite live regions.
MonarchAiPromptInput is named "Message the assistant"; Send becomes Stop while a reply runs.
The scaffold's panes follow the system back gesture on phones.
edgeCases: The history list and the thread are lazy lists: give the scaffold a bounded height and never put it in a vertically scrolling parent.
A new conversation has an empty title until the app names it; MonarchAiConversationList and MonarchAiConversationHeader show their untitled text.
Deleting the open conversation: pick another active id or start a new one, and reset the conversation.
A send that the conversation refuses (while a tool call waits for approval) throws in onSubmit, so the prompt input gives the text back.

examples.title: Chat page with history and canvas
examples.webExample: Chat page with history and canvas

parityExceptions.reason: The web page shows the conversation list beside the chat. On a phone the list and the chat are two screens of a list-detail pattern: the example opens the chat, and the list is the screen behind its back button. The docs preview is recorded in an 840dp tablet window, where both panes show side by side, as on the web; the exception applies to a compact phone window only.
parityExceptions.convention: list-detail navigates between panes on a compact window (Material adaptive)

name: MonarchAiCitation
title: AiCitation
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.clickable on a MonarchText marker, MonarchPopover (androidx.compose.ui.window.Popup) for the card, MonarchFavicon, MonarchButton and MonarchLink
summary: A [1] marker after a sentence of an AI answer that opens a card with the cited source's title, its kind and site, the quoted passage and a way to open it.
whenToUse: After a sentence of an AI answer that rests on a source part of the message, so the person can check where it came from without leaving the answer.
whenNotToUse: For the full list of sources under an answer, list the source parts with MonarchLinkCard or MonarchSearchResultItem. For a footnote in ordinary text, write the reference in the text.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiCitation(index: Int, source: MonarchAiSourcePart, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, quote: String? = null, image: Painter? = null, expanded: Boolean? = null, onExpandedChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, onOpen: ((MonarchAiSourcePart) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiCitationLabels = MonarchAiCitationLabels(), interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)
object MonarchAiCitationDefaults { fun sourceNumbers(parts: List<MonarchAiPart>): Map<String, Int> }

class MonarchAiCitationLabels(marker: ((index: Int, title: String) -> String)? = null, card: ((index: Int) -> String)? = null, open: String? = null, visit: String? = null, kind: ((MonarchAiSourceKind) -> String)? = null)

options.name: index
options.description: The number shown in the marker; 1 shows [1]. Number a message's sources with MonarchAiCitationDefaults.sourceNumbers.

options.name: source
options.description: The cited source part of the message.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the marker.

options.name: quote
options.description: The passage the answer relies on, from the citation part. Shown in the card.

options.name: image
options.description: The source's favicon, loaded by the app from source.favicon. null shows a letter tile.

options.name: expanded
options.description: Whether the card is open, to control it from outside. null lets the marker keep its own state.

options.name: onExpandedChange
options.description: Called when the marker, Open source or a dismissal asks to open or close the card.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Opens the source inside the app. Shows Open source in the card, which closes the card first. Without it the card links to the source's http, https or mailto address.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces the marker's spoken name, the card heading, Open source, Visit page and the kind names.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The interaction source of the marker.

states.name: closed
states.description: The marker [n] in the link color in the caption style.

states.name: open
states.description: A MonarchPopover card on the raised background with the heading, the favicon and title, the meta line (kind, site, product), the quote on the subtle background with a strong start bar, and the action.

states.name: open source
states.description: With onOpen, a small secondary MonarchButton Open source that closes the card and calls back.

states.name: visit page
states.description: Without onOpen and with an http, https or mailto address, an external MonarchLink Visit page that opens it with the platform URI handler.

states.name: no action
states.description: Without onOpen and without a safe address the card has no button or link.

appearance: The marker is caption text in the link color. The card is MonarchPopover's raised surface with its border and shadow, the heading in the subheading style, the title in the strong body style, the meta line in the caption style in the muted text color, and the quote on the subtle background with a bar in the strong border color. All colors are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: Same names as iOS, except that iOS's isPresented binding is expanded with onExpandedChange. The web opens the card on hover and focus after a delay and pins it on click; a phone has no hover, so a tap opens and closes it and openDelay and closeDelay are not offered. A Compose Text cannot contain a control, so the marker sits after the sentence in a Row or FlowRow instead of inside the text run. The favicon is a Painter the app loads (Monarch has no image loader); without it a letter tile is shown where iOS shows a kind symbol, because Monarch bundles no icons. Relative addresses, which the web resolves against the page, are not opened.
accessibility: The marker is one element with the button role named "Source <n>: <title>"; the brackets are not read.
The marker has a 48dp touch target, reserved in the layout, although it draws as small text.
The card is a popup that takes focus, named by its heading (pane title), and the back gesture or a tap outside closes it.
The card's heading has the heading semantics; the favicon is decoration and hidden from TalkBack.
Visit page is an external MonarchLink, read with "opens in the browser"; Open source is a MonarchButton with a 48dp target.
edgeCases: A source repeated in a message keeps its first number in sourceNumbers.
A javascript:, file: or relative address is neither opened nor shown as the site.

api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchAiClaimSources(claims: List<MonarchAiClaim>, sources: List<MonarchAiClaimSource>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, expandedIds: Set<String>? = null, onExpandedChange: ((Set<String>) -> Unit)? = null, filter: MonarchAiClaimSourcesFilter? = null, onFilterChange: ((MonarchAiClaimSourcesFilter) -> Unit)? = null, selectedClaimId: String? = null, onSelectClaim: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, onOpenSource: ((MonarchAiClaimSource, MonarchAiClaimEvidence) -> Unit)? = null, onFlag: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, onVerify: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, onCopyQuote: ((MonarchAiClaimEvidence) -> Unit)? = null, supportIcon: (@Composable (MonarchAiClaimSupport) -> Unit)? = null, expandIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiClaimSourcesLabels = MonarchAiClaimSourcesLabels())

options.name: claims
options.description: The claims of the answer, in the order the answer makes them.

options.name: sources
options.description: The sources the passages point at. MonarchAiClaimSource(part) builds one from a MonarchAiSourcePart of the message.

options.name: modifier

options.name: expandedIds
options.description: The ids of the open claims, when the app keeps them. Kept in the view, all closed at first, when null.

options.name: onExpandedChange
options.description: Called with the new set of open claim ids when a claim opens or closes.

options.name: filter
options.description: The filter, when the app keeps it. Kept in the view, starting with All, when null.

options.name: onFilterChange
options.description: Called when the person changes the filter.

options.name: selectedClaimId
options.description: The selected claim, such as the sentence the person tapped in the answer. When null the view selects the last claim the person opened or closed.

options.name: onSelectClaim
options.description: Called with a claim's id when the person opens or closes it, so the app can highlight that sentence in the answer.

options.name: onOpenSource
options.description: Opens a passage's source in the app, for example in MonarchAiSourcePreview. Without it, Open source shows only for an http, https or mailto address and opens it outside the app.

options.name: onFlag
options.description: Shows Report a problem in every open claim; called with the claim's id.

options.name: onVerify

options.name: onCopyQuote

options.name: supportIcon
options.description: An icon for a support level, shown in its badge and hidden from TalkBack. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: expandIcon
options.description: An icon at the start of each claim's header, such as a chevron that points down; it points down while the claim is open and to the end while it is closed.

options.name: labels

states.name: closed claims
states.description: Each claim shows its text, its support level as a toned badge in words and the number of passages.

states.name: open claim
states.description: A note for a claim that is not fully supported, the passages as quotations with the source title, kind, location, publication date and stance, and Open source and Copy quote for each.

states.name: selected
states.description: The selected claim's header has the accent subtle fill and an accent bar at its start, and is marked selected for TalkBack.

states.name: needs checking
states.description: The filter shows only the claims that are not fully supported; "Showing 1 of 5 claims" is announced.

states.name: nothing needs checking
states.description: Needs checking with every claim supported says so in words.

states.name: no claims
states.description: The summary reads "No claims", the filter is hidden and a line says there are no claims to check.

appearance: The heading in the subheading style with a muted summary, Material 3 segmented buttons for the filter, claim headers in the strong body style with success, warning, danger or neutral badges, and passages as quotations on the subtle fill with a bar in the success or danger border color by stance. Stance words use the success or danger strong color. All are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The parity map names a LazyColumn of claims; the claims are a plain Column, because the view sits under an answer inside the app's scrolling conversation or in a sheet, where a LazyColumn without a fixed height cannot be measured. Each claim is a disclosure with MonarchCollapsible's semantics (button, Expanded or Collapsed, expand and collapse actions), drawn by the component because MonarchCollapsible's header takes only a text label and the support badge must stay visible while the claim is closed. The web filter is its SegmentedControl with counts; Android uses the Material 3 segmented buttons with the count in the label. The web opens a safe link in a new tab and lets onOpenSource prevent it; Android opens the address outside the app only when there is no onOpenSource. The web's arrow, Home and End keys between claims are TalkBack's own navigation here. The web's controlled and uncontrolled pairs (expandedIds, filter, selectedClaimId) are nullable values that the view keeps when null. publishedAt is publishedMillis in epoch milliseconds, formatted in the device locale in UTC; the web's locale prop is the device locale. Monarch bundles no icons, so the support and expand icons are slots. iOS has no AiClaimSources yet. The composable is experimental: an AI panel that waits for a Rook app to adopt it.
accessibility: The heading has the heading semantics; the claims are a traversal group named by the heading, and each claim's passages a group named "Passages for: <claim>".

Each claim header is one button that reads the claim, its support level and its number of passages, with the state Expanded or Collapsed, the expand and collapse actions and a touch target of at least 48dp.
The selected claim is marked selected, not only coloured.
Support levels and stances are words; the badge colors and quote bars only repeat them.
Open source and Copy quote are named with the source, such as "Open source from Q3 report", so the actions of each passage are told apart.
A filter change is announced through a polite live region; the first filter is not announced.
Text wraps at the largest font size; the support and expand icons are hidden from TalkBack.
edgeCases: A passage whose source is not in sources shows "Unknown source" and no Open source button.
A source address that is not http, https or mailto (javascript:, file:, relative) is never opened.
An open claim without passages shows its note, or "No passages were provided for this claim." when it is supported.
Check again shows only on unchecked claims.
A claim id missing from claims but present in expandedIds is ignored.
