name: MonarchAiCodeBlock
title: AiCodeBlock
wrapsNative: MonarchCodeBlock with a androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow of MonarchButtons
summary: Code written by an assistant: MonarchCodeBlock with copy, wrap, diffs and line numbers, plus optional Apply and Insert actions that hand the code back to the app.
whenToUse: For code in an assistant's answer that the person may copy, apply to a file or insert into an editor.
whenNotToUse: For code in documentation or settings that nobody applies, use MonarchCodeBlock. For a short value to copy, use MonarchCopyField.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiCodeBlock(code: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, language: String? = null, title: String? = null, diff: Boolean? = null, highlighted: Boolean = true, showLineNumbers: Boolean = false, showWrapToggle: Boolean = true, copyable: Boolean = true, incomplete: Boolean = false, wrapped: Boolean? = null, onWrappedChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, onCopy: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, onInsert: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, onApply: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiCodeBlockLabels = MonarchAiCodeBlockLabels(), actions: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null)

class MonarchAiCodeBlockLabels(apply: String? = null, insert: String? = null, actionLabel: ((action: String, name: String) -> String)? = null, incompleteHint: String? = null, codeBlock: MonarchCodeBlockLabels = MonarchCodeBlockLabels())

options.name: code
options.description: The code, exactly as it should be copied, applied and inserted.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the block.

options.name: language
options.description: A language id that picks the highlighter and the header text; "diff" or "patch" turns on the diff mode.

options.name: title
options.description: The header text, such as a file name (the web's filename). It also names the code for TalkBack and the action buttons.

options.name: diff
options.description: Forces the diff mode on or off.

options.name: highlighted
options.description: Syntax colouring.

options.name: showLineNumbers
options.description: Line numbers before the lines, not read by TalkBack.

options.name: showWrapToggle
options.description: The wrap toggle in the header.

options.name: copyable
options.description: The copy button in the header.

options.name: incomplete
options.description: The code is still arriving: Apply and Insert are disabled, with a hint saying why. Copy stays available.

options.name: wrapped
options.description: Controls wrapping; without it the block keeps the state itself, starting unwrapped.

options.name: onWrappedChange
options.description: Called with the new wrap state when the toggle is pressed.

options.name: onCopy
options.description: Runs with the copied code after each copy.

options.name: onInsert
options.description: Adds a secondary Insert button that hands over the code.

options.name: onApply
options.description: Adds a primary Apply button that hands over the code.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for Apply, Insert, the spoken action names, the incomplete hint and the code block's own strings.

options.name: actions
options.description: App controls placed in the action row before Insert and Apply.

states.name: ready
states.description: The code block, then a row aligned to the end with the app's controls, Insert (secondary) and Apply (primary).

states.name: incomplete
states.description: Insert and Apply are disabled while the code streams in, and "Available when the code is complete" shows under them; Copy works on what has arrived.

states.name: diff
states.description: Added and removed lines with markers and the diff colors of MonarchCodeBlock.

states.name: no actions
states.description: Without onApply, onInsert or actions there is no action row: the block is a plain MonarchCodeBlock.

appearance: MonarchCodeBlock's subtle container and header, with small buttons under it: Apply in the primary style, Insert in the secondary style, and the hint in the caption style in the muted color. All are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: Same parameters as iOS, with Kotlin names (diff, highlighted, showLineNumbers, showWrapToggle, copyable, incomplete, wrapped with onWrappedChange). On the web Apply and Insert sit in the block's header; MonarchCodeBlock has no slot for extra header controls, so on Android, as on iOS, they are in a row under the code. iOS gives the reason for disabled actions as an accessibility hint; Android has no hint, so the reason is a visible line under the buttons. The web re-tokenises streaming code incrementally; Android re-tokenises the whole code on each update. The web names the header text filename; Android calls it title, as MonarchCodeBlock does. The composable is experimental: an AI panel that waits for a Rook app to adopt it.
accessibility: The code is read as MonarchCodeBlock reads it: a region named after the title or language, line by line, with added and removed lines named.
Apply and Insert are MonarchButtons named with the code, such as "Apply server.ts", with 48dp touch targets.
While the code is incomplete they are disabled and a visible line says "Available when the code is complete".
The action row wraps onto more lines at large font sizes.
edgeCases: Empty code still shows the header and one empty line.
Apply and Insert receive the code as given, including a trailing newline.
With several blocks in one answer, give each a title so the actions are told apart.

options.description: Whether the compact log shows; null lets the view keep it, starting hidden.

options.name: onLogExpandedChange
options.description: Called when the person shows or hides the compact log.

options.name: announceIntervalMillis
options.description: The shortest time between two action announcements; actions in between are announced together.

options.name: visibleActions
options.description: How many of the newest actions the log shows before "Show earlier".

options.name: locale
options.description: The locale of the times.

options.name: timeZone
options.description: The zone of the times. An IANA id such as Europe/Berlin; null, or an id the device does not know, is the device's zone.

options.name: live
options.description: A live picture of the screen from the app, such as its video renderer; it replaces the screenshot and gets the same privacy rules.

options.name: liveSensitive
options.description: The live picture may show private information: it is never shown.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string; the ones that name the surface take it.

states.name: starting, working
states.description: The status, an info banner "The assistant is controlling this browser", Take over, Pause and Stop.

states.name: paused
states.description: Resume replaces Pause; no control banner.

states.name: waiting for you
states.description: A warning banner with "The assistant needs you to continue" and the reason; Take over is the primary button.

states.name: taken over
states.description: A neutral banner "You are controlling this browser" and Hand back.

states.name: done, failed, stopped
states.description: The status in the success, danger or default text role, no control buttons.

states.name: stop confirmation
states.description: Stop is replaced by the question, a danger Stop now and Keep going.

states.name: screenshot
states.description: The picture at its aspect ratio with the last action's point as an AI ring, the selected action's point as an accent ring with a dot, and the pointer as a dot; the capture time under it. A tap opens it in MonarchLightbox.

states.name: no screenshot or hidden
states.description: A muted box with "No screenshot yet", "Screenshot unavailable" or "Screenshot hidden: it may show private information".

states.name: log
states.description: Each action with its kind and time, its label, and its detail or "Hidden"; the selected one has the accent fill and a bar at its start.

appearance: The status uses the strong body style, coloured by the success, danger or warning strong role where it has one and always written out. The banners are MonarchCalloutBanner in the info, neutral and warning tones; the controls are small MonarchButtons (Take over or Hand back primary when they are the expected step, Stop danger). The screen box has the muted fill and default border; markers use the AI solid and accent solid roles and the pointer the default text role outlined with the surface role. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from the theme roles.
platformNotes: The web shows the screen beside the log on wide screens; on a phone the controls come first so they stay in reach, then the screen, then the log. The web zooms nothing; Android opens the screenshot in MonarchLightbox (pinch, double tap and zoom buttons), the native pattern for a picture to inspect, without the markers. The web forwards the person's pointer and keys to the remote screen while taken over (onPointer, onKey, role application); Android offers no remote input surface, because a pixel-level target has no TalkBack equivalent: the app shows its own remote-control screen when the person takes over. The web plays a MediaStream in a video element; Android takes the live picture as a slot. Screenshots are Painters the app loads, times are epoch milliseconds. The web moves focus to the button that replaced the one used; Android leaves focus to TalkBack, which reads the new button. The parity map lists ai-action-log as a dependency; MonarchAiActionLog is a product-wide audit list with undo, so this view has its own log with kinds, points, privacy and selection, as the web does. iOS has not built this component yet.
accessibility: The view is a traversal group named "Assistant browser view" (or computer).
The status and who is in control are written in words; color only repeats them.
The screen is one image element whose description is the screenshot's text and the latest action, with "View larger" as its action when a picture shows; without a picture it says why first.
Each logged action is one element read as kind, label, detail or "Hidden", and time; with onSelectAction it is selectable and read as selected.
The compact log button is read with "Expanded" or "Collapsed".

Status changes are announced once in a polite live region; a failure or a wait for the person in an assertive one. New actions are announced politely, several together, at most once per announceIntervalMillis. Private actions are announced as "Private action".
Every button and logged action has a 48dp target; markers are decorative and hidden from TalkBack.
In right to left the controls start at the right; the address stays left to right; text wraps at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: A private screenshot, the screenshot after a private action and a private live picture are never shown, and the lightbox cannot open them.
Typed text is withheld unless showTypedText; a private action's label and detail are never shown, whatever else is set.
Points outside the screenshot are drawn on its edge; points without a frame size are not drawn.
Long sessions: only the newest visibleActions actions are composed until "Show earlier".
The actions present at first are not announced; announcements restart if the view leaves the composition.
The view is a plain column: put it in a scrolling screen, not in a lazy list item that must stay small.

name: MonarchAiConfidenceMeter
title: AiConfidenceMeter
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.LinearProgressIndicator (bar); androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row on a Monarch surface (badge)
summary: How sure the AI is about a value, as low, medium or high, always in words, in a compact badge or a labelled bar.
whenToUse: Next to a value the AI extracted or suggested, so people know which ones to check.
whenNotToUse: For progress of a task use MonarchProgress. For marking content as AI-written use MonarchAiGeneratedBadge.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiConfidenceMeter(value: Float, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchAiConfidenceMeterVariant = MonarchAiConfidenceMeterVariant.Badge, size: MonarchAiConfidenceMeterSize = MonarchAiConfidenceMeterSize.Md, explanation: String? = null, lowThreshold: Float = 0.6f, highThreshold: Float = 0.85f, showValue: Boolean? = null, icon: (@Composable (MonarchAiConfidenceLevel) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiConfidenceMeterLabels = MonarchAiConfidenceMeterLabels())

enum class MonarchAiConfidenceLevel { Low, Medium, High; companion object { const val DEFAULT_LOW_THRESHOLD: Float; const val DEFAULT_HIGH_THRESHOLD: Float; fun of(value: Float, lowThreshold: Float = 0.6f, highThreshold: Float = 0.85f): MonarchAiConfidenceLevel } }
enum class MonarchAiConfidenceMeterVariant { Badge, Bar }
enum class MonarchAiConfidenceMeterSize { Sm, Md }
class MonarchAiConfidenceMeterLabels(low: String? = null, medium: String? = null, high: String? = null, meter: String? = null, valueText: ((label: String, percent: String) -> String)? = null)

options.name: value
options.description: The confidence from 0 to 1. Values outside the range are clamped; not-a-number counts as 0.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the meter.

options.name: variant
options.description: A compact badge, or a labelled bar.

options.name: size
options.description: Sm has tighter padding, a thinner track and caption text in the bar.

options.name: explanation
options.description: Why the model is or is not confident. Shown under the bar; for the badge it is read by TalkBack after the value.

options.name: lowThreshold
options.description: The edge under which confidence is low.

options.name: highThreshold
options.description: The edge from which confidence is high.

options.name: showValue
options.description: Whether the percentage is shown. By default only the bar shows it.

options.name: icon
options.description: An icon before the band label. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the band labels, the bar name and the spoken value.

states.name: low
states.description: "Needs check" in the low-confidence color on a danger-subtle capsule; the bar fill in the low-confidence color.

states.name: medium
states.description: "Medium confidence" in the medium-confidence color on a warning-subtle capsule.

states.name: high
states.description: "High confidence" in the high-confidence color on a success-subtle capsule.

appearance: The badge is a capsule with the subtle fill and border of the danger, warning or success role and the confidence role of the band for the icon and label; the percentage is in muted text. The bar is a muted track filled with the confidence role of the band, with the label above and the explanation in muted text below.
platformNotes: The web shows the badge's explanation in a tooltip on hover and focus; touch has no tooltip, so for the badge the explanation is only read by TalkBack. Use the bar when sighted people must read it. The web draws its own band glyphs; Monarch for Android bundles no icons, so the icon is a slot and the band is always in words. The web's small badge uses an 11px size; Android uses the caption role at both sizes and tightens the padding, as iOS does. The web's aiConfidenceLevel function is MonarchAiConfidenceLevel.of. Built-in strings are replaced through one labels value. The value is a Float, as Material 3 progress is.
accessibility: The badge is one TalkBack element read as "Needs check, 42% confidence", then the explanation.
The bar group is a progress bar with the content description "Confidence", the value text as its state description and the progress range; the explanation is a separate text after it.
The band is always in words; the icon is optional and the color is never the only signal.
The percentage is formatted in the configuration locale.
Not interactive. Text grows with the font size setting and the bar header wraps.
The bar fill animates with the theme motion and changes at once when animations are off; it starts at the start edge and mirrors in right-to-left layouts.
edgeCases: A value exactly on the low threshold is medium; exactly on the high threshold is high.
If lowThreshold is above highThreshold there is no medium band.
Not-a-number reads as 0% and low.

name: MonarchAiConnectorPicker
title: AiConnectorPicker
wrapsNative: Content for MonarchBottomSheet: MonarchSwitch on a Modifier.toggleable row, MonarchMenu with MonarchMenuItem, MonarchSearchBar, MonarchFavicon, MonarchBadge, MonarchButton and MonarchEmptyState
summary: A searchable list, for a sheet, where a person chooses which connected apps and data sources an assistant may use in this conversation, and whether each tool runs, asks first or never runs.
whenToUse: From the composer of an AI chat, when the assistant can reach the person's apps (drive, mail, calendar, CRM) and the person should choose which it may use and how its tools run.
whenNotToUse: For the scopes an assistant asks for once, at install, use MonarchAiPermissionScope. For a single on or off setting, use MonarchSwitchRow.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiConnectorPicker(connectors: List<MonarchAiConnector>, onConnectorsChange: (List<MonarchAiConnector>) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, title: String? = null, allowsDestructiveAutoApprove: Boolean = false, searchable: Boolean = true, onConnect: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, onManage: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, onDone: (() -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiConnectorPickerLabels = MonarchAiConnectorPickerLabels())

data class MonarchAiConnector(id: String, name: String, status: MonarchAiConnectorStatus, enabled: Boolean, description: String? = null, account: String? = null, reason: String? = null, tools: List<MonarchAiConnectorTool> = emptyList(), image: Painter? = null)
data class MonarchAiConnectorTool(id: String, name: String, risk: MonarchAiConnectorToolRisk, permission: MonarchAiConnectorToolPermission, description: String? = null)
enum class MonarchAiConnectorStatus { Connected, NeedsSignIn, Error, Unavailable }
enum class MonarchAiConnectorToolRisk { Read, Write, Destructive }
enum class MonarchAiConnectorToolPermission { Allow, Ask, Never }

class MonarchAiConnectorPickerLabels(title: String? = null, searchPrompt: String? = null, done: String? = null, summary: ((on: Int, total: Int, asking: Int) -> String)? = null, results: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, noResults: ((query: String) -> String)? = null, clearSearch: String? = null, empty: String? = null, status: ((MonarchAiConnectorStatus) -> String)? = null, account: ((account: String) -> String)? = null, enable: ((name: String) -> String)? = null, disabledReason: ((MonarchAiConnectorStatus) -> String?)? = null, signIn: String? = null, reconnect: String? = null, manage: String? = null, actionLabel: ((action: String, connector: String) -> String)? = null, tools: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, permissionLabel: ((tool: String) -> String)? = null, permission: ((MonarchAiConnectorToolPermission) -> String)? = null, risk: ((MonarchAiConnectorToolRisk) -> String)? = null, destructiveLocked: String? = null)

options.name: connectors
options.description: The connectors with their state, icon and tools.

options.name: onConnectorsChange
options.description: Called with the whole new list when a switch or a permission changes. Store and enforce the values in the app.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the picker; give it the sheet's padding and, for long lists, a vertical scroll.

options.name: title
options.description: Replaces the heading "Connectors".

options.name: allowsDestructiveAutoApprove
options.description: Lets a tool that can delete data be set to Allow. By default Allow is not offered for such a tool and a line says why.

options.name: searchable
options.description: Shows a MonarchSearchBar that filters connectors by name.

options.name: onConnect
options.description: Signs in to a connector that needs it, or reconnects one with a problem, given its id. Shows Sign in or Reconnect on those rows.

options.name: onManage
options.description: Opens a connector's settings, given its id. Shows Manage on every row.

options.name: onDone
options.description: Shows Done next to the heading. Close the sheet in it.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including the summary, counts, statuses, reasons, permissions and risks.

states.name: connected
states.description: The switch can be used; the status in the strong success color, "Connected as <account>" when the account is known.

states.name: sign-in needed
states.description: The switch is disabled; "Sign-in needed" in the strong warning color, the reason, and Sign in with onConnect.

states.name: connection problem
states.description: The switch is disabled; "Connection problem" in the strong danger color, the reason, and Reconnect with onConnect.

states.name: unavailable
states.description: The switch is disabled; "Unavailable" in the muted text color and the reason.

states.name: tools
states.description: A "4 tools" button opens the tools under the row; each has its name, a risk MonarchBadge (neutral Reads data, warning Changes data, danger Can delete data) and a permission button with a menu of Allow, Ask first and Never. The menus are disabled while the connector is off.

states.name: destructive locked
states.description: Allow is not in the menu and "Tools that can delete data can’t run without asking." is shown under it.

states.name: no results
states.description: A filtered MonarchEmptyState naming the search, with Clear search.

states.name: empty
states.description: A small MonarchEmptyState: "No connectors are available."

appearance: The heading in the heading style with a caption summary in the muted text color; each connector row has its favicon, the name in the strong body style, the status in the strong color of its tone and descriptions in the muted text color, and a Material 3 switch at the end. All colors are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: Same names as iOS. iOS binds the connectors; Android hoists them as connectors with onConnectorsChange, which receives the whole new list (the web reports onEnabledChange and onPermissionChange separately). The picker is the content of a MonarchBottomSheet, with Done next to the heading instead of a navigation bar button. The web's radio group of Allow, Ask first and Never is a MonarchMenu behind a button, which stays readable at large font sizes; a disabled Allow radio is Allow left out of the menu, unless it is already the stored value. Connector icons are a Painter the app loads (Monarch has no image loader), with MonarchFavicon's letter tile otherwise. Monarch bundles no icons, so the status is words in the status color without a symbol. The tools open under a button rather than in a disclosure group. The web's controlled query and expandedIds are internal state.
accessibility: Each connector row is one switch element (Modifier.toggleable with the switch role) named "Use <name> in this conversation" followed by its status and, when it cannot be turned on, the reason; the inner Switch has no callback of its own.
A connector that is not connected has a disabled switch, and the reason is written under it.
Status and risk are always words next to their colors.

Sign in, Reconnect, Manage and the tools button are MonarchButtons named with the action and the connector, such as "Sign in: Mail", with 48dp targets; the tools button has the expand or collapse action.
Each permission button is named "Permission for <tool>" with the current choice as its state description.
The number of connectors found is announced through a polite live region when the search text changes.
The heading has the heading semantics.
edgeCases: The summary counts every connector, whatever the search, and only connected connectors that are turned on count as on.
Search ignores case, accents and spaces around the text.
A connector stored as enabled while not connected shows its switch on but disabled and does not count as on.
Turning on a connector that is not connected is refused by the rules, not only by the disabled switch.
Setting Allow on a locked destructive tool is refused even if the menu was bypassed.

name: MonarchAiContextChips
title: AiContextChips
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow of androidx.compose.material3.AssistChip for removable items; android.icu.text.CompactDecimalFormat for counts
summary: What the AI will see with the next prompt, as chips with a kind, a name, a token count with a weight mark, and a total; removable chips remove on tap.
whenToUse: Above or inside an AI composer, to show the files, selections, pages, records, apps and people attached to the next prompt and let the person remove them.
whenNotToUse: For tags on user data use MonarchTag. For a divider that marks where the context was reset in a thread use MonarchAiContextDivider.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiContextChips(items: List<MonarchAiContextItem>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, budget: Int? = null, showTotal: Boolean? = null, enabled: Boolean = true, emptyText: String? = null, onRemove: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, kindIcon: (@Composable (MonarchAiContextKind) -> Unit)? = null, removeIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiContextChipsLabels = MonarchAiContextChipsLabels())
class MonarchAiContextItem(id: String, kind: MonarchAiContextKind, label: String, tokens: Int? = null, description: String? = null, removable: Boolean = true)
enum class MonarchAiContextKind { File, Selection, Page, Record, App, Person }
enum class MonarchAiContextWeight { Light, Medium, Heavy; companion object { fun of(tokens: Int, reference: Int): MonarchAiContextWeight } }

class MonarchAiContextChipsLabels(label: String? = null, kind: ((MonarchAiContextKind) -> String)? = null, tokens: ((formatted: String, count: Int) -> String)? = null, total: ((formatted: String, count: Int) -> String)? = null, remove: ((label: String) -> String)? = null, removed: ((label: String) -> String)? = null)

options.name: items
options.description: What the AI will see, in the order it was added.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the chips.

options.name: budget
options.description: Tokens the context may use. When set, each weight is the item's share of the budget instead of the total.

options.name: showTotal
options.description: Whether the total is shown after the chips. By default when any item has a token count; never with no items.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether chips can be removed. Disabled chips use the muted fill and disabled text.

options.name: emptyText
options.description: Shown when items is empty, in the subtle text color. Without it nothing is shown.

options.name: onRemove
options.description: Called with the id of the item to remove; take it out of items. No chip is removable without it; items with removable = false never are.

options.name: kindIcon
options.description: An icon for the kind at the start of each chip, tinted with the AI strong color and hidden from TalkBack. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: removeIcon
options.description: A decorative close mark at the end of removable chips. Without it the chip is still removed by a tap.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the group name, kind names, count and total texts, the remove action and the removal announcement.

states.name: weight
states.description: Light, medium or heavy fill one, two or three bars of the mark in the AI strong color; heavy also draws the count in the default text color.

states.name: removable
states.description: An AssistChip: a tap, or Delete and Backspace on a hardware keyboard, removes it.

states.name: not removable
states.description: The same look without an action or a touch target.

states.name: empty
states.description: Shows emptyText in the subtle text color, or nothing.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Muted fill, subtle border, disabled text and bars; the chips do not remove.

appearance: Fully rounded chips in the AI subtle fill with the AI border; the kind icon and the filled bars in the AI strong role, empty bars in the default border role, counts and the total in the muted text role. Disabled chips use the muted background, subtle border and disabled text roles. All are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: Same kinds, weights, compact counts and strings as the web and iOS. The parity map names InputChip; removable chips are AssistChips instead, as in MonarchTag, because InputChip is selectable and TalkBack would read every chip as a checkbox. The whole chip is the remove action, as Material 3 input chips are, instead of a separate remove button: TalkBack reads the chip as a button with the action "Remove … from context". The web shows the description as a tooltip; on Android it is read by TalkBack after the chip. The web and iOS move focus to the next chip after a removal; on Android focus is left to the system. The kind icons are a slot because Monarch bundles no icons; the kind is always read as text. Compact counts use android.icu.text.CompactDecimalFormat in the configuration's locale; iOS takes a locale parameter.
accessibility: The chips are a traversal group named "Context".
Each chip is one element read as kind, name and count, "File: contract.pdf, 1.2K tokens", then the description; the full name is read even when it is cut on screen.
A removable chip is a button whose action is named "Remove contract.pdf from context", with a 48dp touch target reserved in the layout.
After a removal, "contract.pdf removed from context" is announced through a polite live region.
The weight is shown by the number of filled bars and by the count, not by color alone; the kind and remove icons are hidden.
edgeCases: A long name is cut in the middle at 192dp, scaled with the font size.
Chips wrap onto new rows; the total follows the last chip.
Exactly one token reads "1 token"; negative counts are shown as 0; items without a count have no mark and do not add to the total.
Removal announcements happen when the chip is tapped, even if the app keeps the item.

name: MonarchAiContextDivider
title: AiContextDivider
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row with drawBehind hairlines and androidx.compose.material3.Text; MonarchCollapsible and MonarchButton for the controls
summary: A labelled rule between messages in a thread: a calendar day, a context reset, or a point where earlier messages were summarized, with the summary behind a disclosure.
whenToUse: In an AI conversation, to mark a new day, the point from which the assistant no longer sees earlier messages, or where earlier messages were condensed.
whenNotToUse: For a plain rule between content use MonarchDivider. For a section heading use MonarchText with a heading style.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiContextDivider(kind: MonarchAiContextDividerKind, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, dateMillis: Long? = null, nowMillis: Long? = null, summary: String? = null, onExpand: (() -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiContextDividerLabels = MonarchAiContextDividerLabels())
enum class MonarchAiContextDividerKind { Day, ContextReset, Summarized }

class MonarchAiContextDividerLabels(label: String? = null, detail: String? = null, today: String? = null, yesterday: String? = null, showSummary: String? = null, summaryPrefix: String? = null, expand: String? = null)

options.name: kind
options.description: Day, ContextReset or Summarized.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the divider.

options.name: dateMillis
options.description: The day of a Day divider, in epoch milliseconds (UTC). Without it a day divider has an empty label.

options.name: nowMillis
options.description: The reference time for Today and Yesterday. null is the current time.

options.name: summary
options.description: For Summarized: the summary the assistant now works from, shown behind a disclosure.

options.name: onExpand
options.description: For Summarized: shows a "Show earlier messages" button that calls this.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the label, the reset description, Today, Yesterday, "Show summary", the spoken summary prefix and "Show earlier messages".

states.name: day
states.description: The label is Today, Yesterday, a weekday and date in this year, or a full date. Solid subtle lines.

states.name: contextReset
states.description: The label, dashed lines and one line of description under them.

states.name: summarized
states.description: The label in the strong AI color and the lines in the AI border color. With a summary, a disclosure; with onExpand, a button.

states.name: summary expanded
states.description: The summary is shown in a box with the subtle AI fill and the AI border.

appearance: A centered caption between two hairlines. The lines use the subtle border role for a day, the default border role, dashed, for a reset, and the AI border role for a summary; the label is muted text, or the strong AI role for a summary. The summary box is the subtle AI fill with the AI border. All roles come from the theme.
platformNotes: The web takes locale, timeZone and now; on Android the locale comes from the configuration, the time zone is the device's, and only nowMillis is a parameter. Today and Yesterday are Monarch strings here, so they can be replaced, unlike iOS which uses the system relative formatter. Dates are epoch milliseconds and formatted with android.icu.text.DateFormat skeletons. The summary is a String, not arbitrary content. The disclosure is MonarchCollapsible, so its title is a full-width row. The web gives the divider the separator role; Compose has no separator role, so it is read as text, as on iOS. Built-in strings are replaced through one labels value.
accessibility: Without controls the divider is one TalkBack element whose content description is the label, then the description of a reset.
A context reset has dashed lines and its own text, so it does not depend on color.
With controls, the label, the disclosure header and the button are separate elements in reading order.
The summary is read after "AI-generated summary:", which is not shown.
The disclosure header and the button each have a 48dp touch target.
The lines are drawn and never read. Text grows with the font size setting and wraps.
edgeCases: A day divider without a date has an empty label and shows only the lines.
A long label wraps and stays centered; the lines keep a least length of 16dp.
summary and onExpand are ignored for Day and ContextReset.
Tomorrow and later days are shown as a date, not as a relative name.
The day is counted in the device time zone, so the same moment can be Today in one zone and Yesterday in another.

name: MonarchAiContextWindowMeter
title: AiContextWindowMeter
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.LinearProgressIndicator (single bar), MonarchStackedProportionBar (parts and legend), MonarchInlineNotice, MonarchButton and MonarchPopover (compact form)
summary: How full the model's context window is: a bar of what fills it with a legend, a notice as it nears the limit, and an optional Summarize earlier messages button.
whenToUse: In an AI chat where long conversations reach the model's context limit, so the person sees why earlier messages may be left out and can summarize them.
whenNotToUse: For quotas of tokens or credits over a turn, a conversation or a month, use MonarchAiUsageMeter. For a plain progress value, use MonarchProgress.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiContextWindowMeter(used: Long, limit: Long, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, breakdown: List<MonarchAiContextWindowPart> = emptyList(), warningAt: Double = 0.8, approximate: Boolean = false, summarizing: Boolean = false, compact: Boolean = false, onSummarize: (() -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiContextWindowMeterLabels = MonarchAiContextWindowMeterLabels())

@Composable fun MonarchAiContextWindowMeter(usage: MonarchAiUsage, limit: Long, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, breakdown: List<MonarchAiContextWindowPart> = emptyList(), warningAt: Double = 0.8, approximate: Boolean = false, summarizing: Boolean = false, compact: Boolean = false, onSummarize: (() -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiContextWindowMeterLabels = MonarchAiContextWindowMeterLabels())
class MonarchAiContextWindowPart(label: String, tokens: Long, id: String? = null)
enum class MonarchAiContextWindowState { Ok, Warning, Full; companion object { fun of(used: Long, limit: Long, warningAt: Double = 0.8): MonarchAiContextWindowState } }

class MonarchAiContextWindowMeterLabels(label: String? = null, amount: ((used: String, limit: String, percent: String) -> String)? = null, approximate: ((amount: String) -> String)? = null, legend: String? = null, other: String? = null, tokens: ((formatted: String) -> String)? = null, warning: String? = null, full: String? = null, summarize: String? = null, showDetails: String? = null)

options.name: used
options.description: The tokens in the context window now. A negative count counts as zero.

options.name: usage
options.description: The usage the latest reply reported in the conversation model; its input plus output tokens are used.

options.name: limit
options.description: The model's context window, in tokens. Zero or less is always ok and shows 0%.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the meter.

options.name: breakdown
options.description: What the tokens are made of, drawn as coloured segments with a legend of token counts. Tokens no part covers are listed as Other.

options.name: warningAt
options.description: The share of the limit at which the meter warns.

options.name: approximate
options.description: The count is an estimate: the summary reads "About …".

options.name: summarizing
options.description: A summary is being made: the button shows its progress indicator and ignores taps.

options.name: compact
options.description: A small bar and the share as one button, for a toolbar; it opens the full meter in a MonarchPopover.

options.name: onSummarize
options.description: Adds "Summarize earlier messages", which calls this.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces every built-in string: the name, the summary format, About, the legend name, Other, the token amount, the notices, the button and the compact meter's action.

states.name: ok
states.description: Below warningAt: no notice; the single bar is the accent color and the summarize button is a ghost button.

states.name: warning
states.description: At or above warningAt: a warning MonarchInlineNotice; the single bar is the warning color and the button is secondary.

states.name: full
states.description: At or over the limit: a danger MonarchInlineNotice saying earlier messages are being left out; the single bar is the danger color.

states.name: breakdown
states.description: A MonarchStackedProportionBar of the parts, palette colors for the first five and neutral after, with Other for uncovered tokens and a legend of token counts.

states.name: approximate
states.description: The summary starts with "About".

states.name: summarizing
states.description: The button shows its progress indicator and ignores taps.

states.name: compact
states.description: Bar and share as one button with a 48dp target; the share takes the strong warning or danger color when not ok, and the full meter opens in a popover.

appearance: The name in the label style and the summary in the caption style in the muted text color, over a bar on the muted background filled with the accent, warning or danger solid color, or the chart palette for parts. Notices are MonarchInlineNotice in the warning and danger tones. All colors are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: Same names as iOS; counts are Long because MonarchAiUsage counts tokens as Long on Android. The web's useAiContextUsage hook and its token estimator are not offered: pass used and approximate, or the usage the latest message reported. The web hides the header in its compact form; Android, like iOS, keeps the details one tap away in a MonarchPopover. Monarch bundles no icons, so the notice carries the state in words and the compact form shows no tone icon; its share changes color and its spoken state is the full summary. The web cycles the five data colors for a sixth part; Android follows MonarchStackedProportionBar and draws the sixth part and later in neutral, as iOS does.
accessibility: The header and the single bar are one TalkBack element read as "Context window" and the summary, for example "45,000 of 128,000 tokens (35%)", with the range of a progress bar.
With a breakdown the legend is a group named "What fills the context window" and each entry reads its name and token count (from MonarchStackedProportionBar).
The warning and full states are written in a notice, not shown by color alone.
A change of state while the meter is on screen is announced once through a polite live region on an always-present node; the state on first appearance is not announced.
The compact meter is a button named "Context window" with the summary as its state description, the action "Show what fills the context window" and a 48dp touch target.
Summarize earlier messages is a MonarchButton with a 48dp touch target that ignores taps while summarizing.
edgeCases: Negative counts are drawn as zero; a limit of zero or less is always ok and shows 0%.
When the parts add up to more than the window, the bar is scaled to their total so every part stays visible.
Parts that cover all of used produce no Other entry.
The share is capped at 100% in the summary and the bar.
The name and summary share a line when they fit and wrap onto two lines at large font sizes.

name: MonarchAiConversation
title: useAiConversation
wrapsNative: kotlinx.coroutines.flow.StateFlow over an injected transport that returns kotlinx.coroutines.flow.Flow, collected in a caller-supplied CoroutineScope
summary: Headless state for an AI conversation: it sends prompts through an injected transport, streams the reply into the vendor-neutral message model, and handles stop, regenerate, retry, edit and resend as branches, tool approval, client-side tools, an offline queue and feedback.
whenToUse: As the model behind any chat surface. Create it with rememberMonarchAiConversation, or in a ViewModel with viewModelScope, collect messages, status and error in the UI, and implement MonarchAiTransport for your backend.
whenNotToUse: It draws nothing: use the AI components (MonarchAiArtifactCard, MonarchAiErrorMessage and the others) to show the messages. For a single completion in a text field, call your service directly.
api: class MonarchAiConversation(transport: MonarchAiTransport, scope: CoroutineScope, connectionLostMessage: String, toolResultFailedMessage: String, initialMessages: List<MonarchAiConversationMessage> = emptyList(), conversationId: String? = null, body: Map<String, MonarchAiJSON> = emptyMap(), queuesWhileOffline: Boolean = true, slowAfterMillis: Long? = 10_000L, generateId: (() -> String)? = null)

val messages: StateFlow<List<MonarchAiConversationMessage>>; val status: StateFlow<MonarchAiConversationStatus>; val error: StateFlow<MonarchAiConversationError?>; val conversationId: StateFlow<String?>; val agent: StateFlow<MonarchAiAgentRef?>; val slow: StateFlow<Boolean>; val online: StateFlow<Boolean>; val queued: StateFlow<List<MonarchAiQueuedMessage>>; val busy: Boolean; val canSend: Boolean

var body: Map<String, MonarchAiJSON>; var onFinish: ((MonarchAiConversationMessage) -> Unit)?; var onError: ((MonarchAiConversationError) -> Unit)?; var onToolResponse: ((MonarchAiToolResponse) -> Unit)?; var onToolCall: (suspend (MonarchAiToolCallPart) -> MonarchAiJSON)?; var toolPolicy: ((MonarchAiToolCallPart) -> MonarchAiToolDecision)?; var onMemoryEvent: ((MonarchAiMemoryPart, MonarchAiConversationMessage) -> Unit)?
fun send(text: String, files: List<MonarchAiFilePart> = emptyList(), body: Map<String, MonarchAiJSON> = emptyMap()): Boolean

fun cancelQueued(id: String); fun setOnline(online: Boolean); fun stop(); fun regenerate(messageId: String? = null, body: Map<String, MonarchAiJSON> = emptyMap()); fun retry(messageId: String? = null, body: Map<String, MonarchAiJSON> = emptyMap()); fun editAndResend(messageId: String, text: String, files: List<MonarchAiFilePart>? = null, body: Map<String, MonarchAiJSON> = emptyMap())

fun approveTool(toolCallId: String, input: MonarchAiJSON? = null); fun denyTool(toolCallId: String, reason: String? = null); fun submitToolResult(toolCallId: String, result: MonarchAiToolResult); fun resumeRun(messageId: String? = null); fun branchTo(messageId: String, index: Int); fun setFeedback(messageId: String, feedback: MonarchAiMessageFeedback?); fun reset(messages: List<MonarchAiConversationMessage> = emptyList())

interface MonarchAiTransport { fun stream(request: MonarchAiTransportRequest): Flow<MonarchAiStreamEvent>; val respondsToTools: Boolean; fun respondToTool(response: MonarchAiToolResponse): Flow<MonarchAiStreamEvent>; val resumesRuns: Boolean; fun resume(request: MonarchAiResumeRequest): Flow<MonarchAiStreamEvent> }

data class MonarchAiConversationMessage(id, role, parts, createdAt, agent, model, usage, feedback, branch, finishReason, runId, queued) { val text: String; val streaming: Boolean; val toolCalls; val memories; val createdAtMillis: Long?; fun toJson(): MonarchAiJSON; companion object { fun fromJson(json: MonarchAiJSON); fun listFromJson(text: String); fun listToJson(messages): String; fun timestamp(millis: Long): String } }

Value types: MonarchAiPlanStep, MonarchAiUsage, MonarchAiAgentRef, MonarchAiBranchPosition, MonarchAiJSON (Null, Bool, Number, Text, Array, Object; parse, toJsonString)

Enumerations: MonarchAiRole, MonarchAiPartState, MonarchAiToolCallState, MonarchAiToolCallRisk, MonarchAiFinishReason, MonarchAiSourceKind, MonarchAiArtifactKind, MonarchAiEditProposalState, MonarchAiPlanStepState, MonarchAiMemoryAction, MonarchAiMessageFeedback, MonarchAiTrigger, MonarchAiConversationStatus, MonarchAiToolDecision

Requests and results: MonarchAiTransportRequest, MonarchAiToolResponse, MonarchAiResumeRequest, MonarchAiToolCallPatch, MonarchAiQueuedMessage, MonarchAiToolResult (Output, Failure), MonarchAiConversationError (companion fun isRetryable(code: String?): Boolean)

options.name: transport
options.description: Connects the conversation to your backend. Monarch does no networking.

options.name: scope
options.description: Collects replies and runs client-side tools. Use a main-thread scope such as viewModelScope; rememberMonarchAiConversation uses rememberCoroutineScope().

options.name: connectionLostMessage
options.description: The message of the error raised when the transport's flow throws. Built-in: monarch_aiconversation_connection_lost.

options.name: toolResultFailedMessage
options.description: The error of a client-side tool that threw without a message. Built-in: monarch_aiconversation_tool_result_failed.

options.name: initialMessages
options.description: Messages to start with, for example a stored conversation. Shown as one branch.

options.name: conversationId
options.description: The id from an earlier session, sent with every request. A Done event replaces it.

options.name: body
options.description: Request fields sent on every turn, merged under the fields given to send. Also a settable property.

options.name: queuesWhileOffline
options.description: While offline, send keeps the message in queued and sends it, in order, once setOnline(true) is called.

options.name: slowAfterMillis
options.description: The time without any event from a running reply before slow becomes true. null turns it off.

options.name: generateId
options.description: Custom message ids. The default is a random UUID.

states.name: Idle
states.description: Nothing is running.

states.name: Submitted
states.description: Sent, waiting for the first event. busy is true.

states.name: Streaming
states.description: Events are arriving and messages changes with each one. busy is true.

states.name: AwaitingApproval
states.description: A tool call waits for approveTool or denyTool. canSend is false and send returns false.

states.name: AwaitingToolResult
states.description: The model called a tool the client runs: onToolCall runs it, or call submitToolResult.

states.name: Error
states.description: The last turn failed. error holds the code, the message and whether it can be retried or resumed; the reply ends with an error part.

states.name: Stopped
states.description: stop() ended the reply. What arrived stays, streaming parts are closed and running tool calls are cancelled.

states.name: offline
states.description: After setOnline(false), sent messages wait in queued and appear at the end of messages with queued set.

states.name: slow
states.description: slow is true while a running reply has sent nothing for slowAfterMillis.

appearance: None: it is a model and draws nothing.
platformNotes: The web is the useAiConversation hook; Android has a class with StateFlows, created with rememberMonarchAiConversation or in a ViewModel. The message model has the web's fields and reads and writes the web's JSON (camelCase fields, kebab-case values, a type field per part, empty optional fields left out), with a small built-in JSON reader so no serialisation library is added. Kotlin names follow Android: booleans without is (queued, redacted, retryable, resumable, approved, streaming, busy, online, slow), times in milliseconds (durationMs, retryAfterMs, slowAfterMillis), and createdAtMillis next to the ISO 8601 createdAt. Parts are a sealed interface the part classes implement, where iOS wraps them in enum cases. The transport returns a Flow; there is no AbortSignal: stopping cancels the collection. Not offered, because they belong to the browser or to a transport: file uploads (send takes file parts the app has already uploaded), the SSE, provider, AG-UI and Rook transports and their mappers, and the testing kit. The Rook transport stays Rook-scoped. The network state comes from setOnline, fed by the app, for example from a ConnectivityManager callback. The slow timer restarts on every event. With a tool policy, every waiting call is put to the policy before the status is decided, as on iOS.
accessibility: It draws nothing and announces nothing; the components that show the messages do.
slow, queued, the error message and the tool call states are plain values, so a view can show and announce them.
edgeCases: Sending while a reply streams ends that reply, keeping what arrived, and starts the next.
A Done or Error event ends the reply even if the transport keeps the flow open; a flow that ends without Done leaves the status Idle and does not call onFinish.
A flow that throws ends the reply with the retryable code network. With a run id and a transport that resumes runs, the error is resumable.
retry rewrites the same message; regenerate and editAndResend add a branch, and messages then carry branch with the index and count.
A queued message that fails holds the rest of the queue until the connection comes back again.
Sending a new message cancels tool calls that still waited for a client-side result.
Ending the scope cancels the collection of the transport's flow and any client-side tools.
Reading a part with an unknown type throws IllegalArgumentException.
The functions are not thread-safe: call them from the thread of the scope, normally the main thread.

The open row has the subtle background and an accent start bar. Dialogs are Material 3 on the raised background. All colors are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: Same names as iOS, except that the time is nowMillis with an IANA zone id instead of a Date with a Calendar, and isSearchable is searchable. Search is a MonarchSearchBar at the top of the list instead of the system search field of a NavigationStack. iOS swipe actions and the context menu become a long press, an optional menu button (Monarch bundles no icons, so its icon is the app's) and TalkBack custom actions. Rename uses a Material 3 AlertDialog with a text field instead of the web's inline field; the web's arrow keys, F2 and Delete key are not offered. onDelete is synchronous; the web can keep its dialog open on a promise.
accessibility: The list is named "Conversation history"; group headings have the heading semantics.
Each row is one element with the button role, read as its title and preview; the open conversation also has the selected state.
The open row is marked by a start bar, a bold title and a fill as well as the selected state, not by color alone.
Rename, Pin or Unpin and Delete are TalkBack custom actions on the row, and a long press opens them in a menu.
The optional menu button is named "More actions for <title>" and has a 48dp target.
After a local search changes, the number of matching conversations is announced through a polite live region.
Rows are at least 48dp high.
edgeCases: An empty or white-space title shows "New conversation".
Days are counted in the time zone given; anything dated in the future is Today, and seven days before the start of today is still Previous 7 days.
A summary made from messages uses the last message's time and the text of the last message that has text, on one line; without messages it is dated at the epoch (Older).
Long titles wrap to two lines and previews to one, with an ellipsis.
A rename or delete dialog closes on its own if its conversation disappears from the list.

wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.adaptive.layout.SupportingPaneScaffold from the expanded width class (androidx.compose.material3.adaptive.currentWindowAdaptiveInfoV2), with the app content in the main pane and MonarchAiAssistantPanel (Inline) in the supporting pane; below it the content alone with MonarchAiAssistantPanel as a ModalBottomSheet (Sheet), opened by MonarchAiLauncher; androidx.activity.compose.BackHandler closes the docked pane
summary: A recipe, not a component: the app's content with an assistant docked beside it on wide windows and opened as a sheet on phones, where the assistant sees what the person selected on the page.
whenToUse: An app screen where the assistant should act on the rows, text or records the person has selected, and the content should make room for the assistant on a wide window instead of being covered.
whenNotToUse: A full-screen chat with history: use the ai-chat-page recipe. An assistant that never needs page context: MonarchAiAssistantPanel opened from MonarchAiLauncher is enough.
api: val docked = currentWindowAdaptiveInfoV2().windowSizeClass.isWidthAtLeastBreakpoint(WindowSizeClass.WIDTH_DP_EXPANDED_LOWER_BOUND)

SupportingPaneScaffold(directive = calculatePaneScaffoldDirective(adaptiveInfo).copy(maxHorizontalPartitions = if (open) 2 else 1), value = calculateThreePaneScaffoldValue(directive.maxHorizontalPartitions, SupportingPaneScaffoldDefaults.adaptStrategies(), ThreePaneScaffoldDestinationItem<Nothing>(SupportingPaneScaffoldRole.Main)), mainPane = { AnimatedPane { content() } }, supportingPane = { AnimatedPane { MonarchAiAssistantPanel(…, placement = Inline) } }) while docked

content() and MonarchAiAssistantPanel(conversation, title, open, onOpenChange = { open = it }, placement = MonarchAiAssistantPanelPlacement.Sheet, context = page and selection chips, onRemoveContext = …) below the expanded width class
MonarchAiLauncher(open, onOpenChange = { open = it }, icon = …) at the bottom end of the content, hidden while the assistant is docked open
MonarchAiAssistantPanel(…, body = mapOf("selection" to MonarchAiJSON.Array(…))) so the selection is sent with each prompt
BackHandler(enabled = docked && open) { open = false }

options.name: conversation
options.description: The conversation the docked assistant shows and sends to, held above the navigation so it survives moving between screens.

options.name: title
options.description: The assistant's heading, such as "Assistant", passed to MonarchAiAssistantPanel.

options.name: open
options.description: Whether the assistant is shown; app state, set by MonarchAiLauncher, the panel's close button and, when docked, the back gesture.

options.name: content
options.description: The app screen. It writes the selection; it is the main pane while docked and the whole screen otherwise.

options.name: selection
options.description: What the person selected on the page. Shown as a Selection chip after the always-present chips and sent under the selection request field as label and text objects, as the web's body.selection is.

options.name: context
options.description: Chips that always show, such as the current page (removable = false); the selection chip follows them.

options.name: onRemoveContext
options.description: Removing the selection chip clears the selection, so nothing is sent.

options.name: launcher
options.description: Leave it out when the app opens the assistant from its own toolbar button (a Subtle MonarchAiLauncher in the top app bar).

options.name: starters / footer / toolbar
options.description: Passed straight to the panel, as the web's panelProps are.

states.name: closed
states.description: The content uses the full width; the launcher shows at the bottom end.

states.name: docked open
states.description: From the expanded width class (840dp) the content reflows into the main pane and the assistant takes the supporting pane at the directive's preferred width; the launcher hides; the back gesture closes the assistant.

states.name: sheet open
states.description: Below the expanded width class the assistant is a full-height Material 3 modal bottom sheet over the content; back, a swipe down or a tap outside closes it.

states.name: with selection
states.description: A Selection chip with the count of selected rows shows in the assistant, and the selection goes in the request body of the next prompt; removing the chip clears it.

appearance: Every part is an existing component: the Material 3 supporting pane scaffold, MonarchAiAssistantPanel on the surface color (or the Material 3 sheet colors), MonarchAiLauncher in its solid accent form and the app's content in the Monarch theme. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web ships AiCopilotLayout as one component with a React selection context (useAiSelectionContext), a side option, a 24rem rail of at most 45%, a full-screen sheet under 640px and a launcher with Cmd+J or Ctrl+J. On Android it is a recipe, because Compose hoists state: the selection is ordinary app state the screen writes, shown as a MonarchAiContextItem chip and sent by setting MonarchAiConversation.body, so no context object is needed. The docked form is the supporting pane of SupportingPaneScaffold from the expanded width class (840dp), as Material 3 places supporting content; the scaffold decides the edge and the width, so there is no side option, and medium widths (600 to 840dp) use the sheet, where the web docks from 640px. The directive is limited to one partition while the assistant is closed, so the content keeps the full width. The phone form is MonarchAiAssistantPanel's ModalBottomSheet. The keyboard shortcut is not offered: Android has no app-wide Cmd+J convention; a hardware-keyboard app can add one with onKeyEvent. The web moves focus to the input on open and back to the launcher on close; here the input is not focused on open (the panel's choice, so the keyboard does not cover the page) and the sheet returns focus itself. The web's clearSelectionOnSend and panelProps.onSend become app code: clear the selection after send, or use the panel overload that takes onSend. The catalogue page uses BoxWithConstraints and a Row because the sample app does not depend on the adaptive artifacts. iOS has not covered this entry yet.
accessibility: MonarchAiLauncher is a button named by its label that states whether the assistant is open.
MonarchAiAssistantPanel names its pane with its title for TalkBack; its close button is named "Close assistant".
What the assistant will receive is visible before sending: the Selection chip names the number of selected rows, and the chip can be removed.
The selection on the page is made with MonarchCheckboxRow, whose whole row toggles and reads its checked state.
On a phone the sheet closes with the back gesture; while docked, BackHandler closes the assistant with the back gesture.
Replies, errors and the offline notice are announced by the panel's MonarchAiThread through polite live regions.
edgeCases: The panel's thread is a lazy list: give the layout a bounded height (the screen, or a fixed height in a scrolling page) and never put it in a vertically scrolling parent. The content pane may scroll itself.
The panel's body is merged over the conversation's own request fields for each message, so the conversation's body is never overwritten.
A prompt queued while offline keeps the body it was sent with, so it goes with the selection the person saw when sending it.
Crossing the expanded width class while open moves the panel between the pane and the sheet; hoist the prompt TextFieldState to keep a draft across the change.
An empty selection sends no selection field and shows no chip.

summary: A short reminder that AI output can be wrong, worded and styled for a low, medium or high risk.
whenToUse: Under an AI composer or answer, with the risk set by how much harm a wrong answer could do where it appears: high for money, health, legal or deleting data.
whenNotToUse: To mark one piece of content as AI-generated use MonarchAiGeneratedBadge. For errors and other notices use MonarchInlineNotice or MonarchCalloutBanner.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiDisclaimer(modifier: Modifier = Modifier, risk: MonarchAiDisclaimerRisk = MonarchAiDisclaimerRisk.Low, text: String? = null, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null)
enum class MonarchAiDisclaimerRisk { Low, Medium, High }

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the disclaimer.

options.name: risk
options.description: Low, Medium or High. Selects the wording and the look.

options.name: text
options.description: Replaces the built-in wording of the risk. Already localised. Null or blank text keeps the built-in wording.

options.name: icon
options.description: An icon before the text, tinted by the risk and hidden from TalkBack. Monarch bundles no icons.

states.name: low
states.description: A centered caption in the muted text color; the icon in the AI strong color.

states.name: medium
states.description: A caption at the start in the default text color; the icon in the info strong color.

states.name: high
states.description: A warning MonarchInlineNotice: the warning subtle fill with the text and icon in the warning strong color.

appearance: Low uses the muted text role and the AI strong role for the icon; medium the default text role and the info strong role for the icon; high the warning subtle fill and the warning strong role, as MonarchInlineNotice draws it. All roles come from the theme, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: Same three risks and wording as the web and iOS. The web draws a bot, information and warning glyph; Monarch for Android bundles no icons, so the icon is an optional slot and the text carries the meaning. The web marks the element with role note, which has no TalkBack equivalent; on Android it is one merged text element. Wording is replaced per call through text, or for every call through the string resources monarch_aidisclaimer_low, _medium and _high, rather than a messages object. Because every parameter is optional, modifier comes first, before risk and text, following the Compose API guidelines; iOS takes text first.
accessibility: The icon and the text are one TalkBack element, read as the text; the icon is hidden.
The high risk is read with the tone name "Warning" first, so the risk does not depend on color.
The text grows with the font size setting and wraps.
edgeCases: Long custom text wraps; the low risk stays centered.
Null or blank text falls back to the built-in wording of the risk.

name: MonarchAiDraftQueue
title: AiDraftQueue
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of MonarchCard (androidx.compose.material3.Surface) drafts with MonarchBadge, MonarchAiGeneratedBadge, MonarchAiTypingDots, MonarchButton in androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow, MonarchTextField (androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedTextField) for editing, MonarchProgress (androidx.compose.material3.LinearProgressIndicator), androidx.compose.ui.focus.FocusRequester
summary: A review queue for AI-written drafts (replies, messages, notes): each draft with its context and Approve, Edit, Regenerate, Skip and Send, so nothing is sent without a person approving it.
whenToUse: When an assistant prepares several messages or notes that a person must approve, edit or skip before anything is sent.
whenNotToUse: For one proposed change to existing text use an edit proposal in MonarchAiConversation. For a single reply in a chat use the conversation itself with its message actions.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiDraftQueue(drafts: List<MonarchAiDraft>, onApprove: (id: String) -> Unit, onEdit: (id: String, body: String) -> Unit, onRegenerate: (id: String) -> Unit, onSkip: (id: String) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, title: String? = null, onSend: ((id: String) -> Unit)? = null, advancesOnAction: Boolean = true, labels: MonarchAiDraftQueueLabels = MonarchAiDraftQueueLabels())

data class MonarchAiDraft(id: String, title: String, body: String, context: String? = null, status: MonarchAiDraftStatus = MonarchAiDraftStatus.Draft) { constructor(message: MonarchAiConversationMessage, title: String, context: String? = null, status: MonarchAiDraftStatus = MonarchAiDraftStatus.Draft) }
enum class MonarchAiDraftStatus { Draft, Regenerating, Approved, Sent, Skipped }

class MonarchAiDraftQueueLabels(label: String? = null, progress: ((reviewed: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, empty: String? = null, status: ((status: MonarchAiDraftStatus) -> String)? = null, writing: String? = null, aiDraft: String? = null, context: String? = null, approve: String? = null, send: String? = null, edit: String? = null, regenerate: String? = null, skip: String? = null, save: String? = null, cancel: String? = null, editField: ((title: String) -> String)? = null, announce: ((status: MonarchAiDraftStatus, title: String) -> String)? = null)

options.name: drafts
options.description: The drafts in review order, each with a unique id, a title, the body, optional context and a status. A draft can be made from a MonarchAiConversationMessage.

options.name: onApprove
options.description: Called with the id of an approved draft. Set its status to Approved (or send it).

options.name: onEdit
options.description: Called with the id and the trimmed text when the person saves an edit that changed the text.

options.name: onRegenerate
options.description: Asks for a new version; set the status to Regenerating while it is written and back to Draft when it is ready.

options.name: onSkip
options.description: Called with the id of a skipped draft.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the queue.

options.name: title
options.description: A heading above the queue. It also names the queue for TalkBack.

options.name: onSend
options.description: Adds Send to approved drafts; called with the id.

options.name: advancesOnAction
options.description: Whether focus moves to the next draft that needs review (wrapping to the top) after Approve, Send or Skip.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces any built-in string; the ones that depend on a value are functions.

states.name: draft
states.description: "Needs review" in a neutral badge; Approve (primary), Edit, Regenerate and Skip (ghost).

states.name: regenerating
states.description: "Writing" in an info badge; the body is replaced by still-or-moving typing dots and "AI is still writing…"; no actions.

states.name: approved
states.description: "Approved" in a success badge; Send (primary, with onSend) and Edit.

states.name: sent
states.description: "Sent" in a success badge; no actions.

states.name: skipped
states.description: "Skipped" in a neutral badge; the body uses the muted text color; no actions.

states.name: editing
states.description: The body is replaced by a multi-line field labelled "Edit draft: <title>", focused, with Save (disabled while the text is blank) and Cancel.

states.name: empty
states.description: A small success empty state: "No drafts to review".

appearance: Each draft is a MonarchCard with the heading type for the title, a status badge, the small AI generated mark above the body, and the context on the subtle background with the medium radius in the muted text color. The header shows the title in the title type, the progress line in the caption type and a progress bar. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The parity map named a pager or a list; the queue is a plain column like iOS and the web, because every draft shows its own actions and a pager would hide the others. It is not lazy: place it in a screen that scrolls. The web's opt-in J and K keyboard shortcuts are not offered; Android moves between drafts with TalkBack, Switch Access or the keyboard focus order. Status badges have no icons because Monarch for Android bundles none; the badge text names the status. The context is a String, where the web takes any content. Focus after a decision moves with FocusRequester to the next draft's heading; announcements use a polite live region instead of a posted announcement.
accessibility: The queue is a traversal group named by its title, or "Drafts to review".
The queue title and each draft's title are headings.
Each status is a badge with its name, so it does not rest on color.
Each body is read after "AI draft"; the AI generated mark and the typing dots are hidden from TalkBack because text says the same.
After Approve, Send or Skip, focus moves to the next draft that needs review, wrapping to the top.
Every status change is announced through a polite live region that is always present, for example "Approved: Reply to Alex", or "New draft ready: Reply to Alex" when a draft needs review again.
The editor is focused when it opens and is labelled "Edit draft: <title>"; Save is disabled while the text is blank.
Every button has a 48dp touch target and the buttons wrap onto new rows at large font sizes.
The progress bar is hidden from TalkBack; the visible line "n of m reviewed" is read instead.
edgeCases: Saving text that is unchanged after trimming closes the editor without calling onEdit.
Drafts that appear in the list later are not announced; only status changes of known drafts are.
If no other draft needs review, focus stays where it is after a decision.
Draft ids must be unique; with repeated ids the first status wins in announcements.

examples.title: Review queue
examples.template:
MonarchAiDraftQueue(
    drafts = listOf(
        MonarchAiDraft({{drafts.0.id}}, {{drafts.0.title}}, {{drafts.0.body}}, context = {{drafts.0.context}}, status = MonarchAiDraftStatus.{{drafts.0.status|pascal}}),
        MonarchAiDraft({{drafts.1.id}}, {{drafts.1.title}}, {{drafts.1.body}}, context = {{drafts.1.context}}, status = MonarchAiDraftStatus.{{drafts.1.status|pascal}}),
        MonarchAiDraft({{drafts.2.id}}, {{drafts.2.title}}, {{drafts.2.body}}, context = {{drafts.2.context}}, status = MonarchAiDraftStatus.{{drafts.2.status|pascal}}),
    ),
    onApprove = {},
    onEdit = { _, _ -> },
    onRegenerate = {},
    onSkip = {},
    title = {{title}},
)
examples.code:
MonarchAiDraftQueue(
    drafts = listOf(
        MonarchAiDraft("1", "Reply to Alex Morgan", "Hi Alex,\n\nThursday afternoon works. Shall we say 2 pm?\n\nThanks", context = "Could we move Thursday’s review to the afternoon?", status = MonarchAiDraftStatus.Draft),
        MonarchAiDraft("2", "Reply to Sam Lee", "Hi Sam,\n\nYes, the updated report is attached. Let me know if anything needs changing.", context = "Is the updated report ready to share?", status = MonarchAiDraftStatus.Draft),
        MonarchAiDraft("3", "Reply to Kim Park", "You are welcome. Glad they helped.", context = "Thanks for the notes from yesterday.", status = MonarchAiDraftStatus.Regenerating),
    ),
    onApprove = {},
    onEdit = { _, _ -> },
    onRegenerate = {},
    onSkip = {},
    title = "Replies to review",

name: MonarchAiEditProposal
title: AiEditProposal
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of word-diff androidx.compose.material3.Text with MonarchButton, MonarchBadge and MonarchAiGeneratedBadge, on MonarchDiffViewer's word diff
summary: A reviewable diff of edits an AI proposes to a document or record, accepted or rejected per change or all at once, and revertible once applied.
whenToUse: When an assistant proposes changes to something outside the conversation (a document, a record, a form) and a person must decide before anything is applied.
whenNotToUse: For comparing two versions of a file without decisions use MonarchDiffViewer. For a suggestion inside a text field use MonarchAiGhostText or MonarchAiAutofillField.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchAiEditProposal(part: MonarchAiEditProposalPart, hunks: List<MonarchAiEditHunk>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, title: String? = null, onAcceptAll: (() -> Unit)? = null, onRejectAll: (() -> Unit)? = null, onAcceptHunk: ((id: String) -> Unit)? = null, onRejectHunk: ((id: String) -> Unit)? = null, onRevert: (() -> Unit)? = null, statusIcon: (@Composable (MonarchAiEditHunkStatus) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiEditProposalLabels = MonarchAiEditProposalLabels())
class MonarchAiEditHunk(id: String, before: String, after: String, label: String? = null, status: MonarchAiEditHunkStatus? = null)
enum class MonarchAiEditHunkStatus { Proposed, Accepted, Rejected }
enum class MonarchAiEditProposalEvent { Accepted, Rejected, AcceptedAll, RejectedAll }

class MonarchAiEditProposalLabels(badge: String? = null, state: ((MonarchAiEditProposalState) -> String)? = null, hunkState: ((MonarchAiEditHunkStatus) -> String)? = null, count: ((total: Int, pending: Int) -> String)? = null, hunkName: ((index: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, acceptAll: String? = null, rejectAll: String? = null, accept: String? = null, reject: String? = null, revert: String? = null, deleted: String? = null, inserted: String? = null, unchanged: String? = null, announcement: ((event: MonarchAiEditProposalEvent, left: Int) -> String)? = null, readOnly: ((MonarchAiEditProposalState) -> String)? = null)

options.name: part
options.description: The edit-proposal part of the message. Its state decides whether the edits can change; its id scopes remembered decisions.

options.name: hunks
options.description: The changes in document order, each with the text before and after.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the card.

options.name: title
options.description: Replaces "Suggested edits"; the title is a heading.

options.name: onAcceptAll
options.description: Accepts every undecided change; shows Accept all while proposed.

options.name: onRejectAll
options.description: Rejects every undecided change; shows Reject all while proposed.

options.name: onAcceptHunk
options.description: Accepts one change by id; shows Accept on each undecided change.

options.name: onRejectHunk
options.description: Rejects one change by id; shows Reject on each undecided change.

options.name: onRevert
options.description: Undoes applied edits; shows Revert once the part is applied.

options.name: statusIcon
options.description: An icon before a change's decision, tinted like the decision. Monarch bundles no icons; the decision is always written.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

states.name: proposed
states.description: Info state badge, the count of changes left, per-change and all buttons.

states.name: change accepted
states.description: "Accepted" in the strong success color; the removed text turns subtle and the added text plain, still underlined.

states.name: change rejected
states.description: "Rejected" in the muted color; the original text is plain without the strike and the proposed text subtle, still underlined.

states.name: applied
states.description: Success badge, "These edits were applied.", every change accepted unless rejected, and Revert.

states.name: rejected
states.description: Neutral badge and every change rejected; no buttons.

states.name: reverted
states.description: Warning badge; every change shows undecided because none of it is in the document.

states.name: no change
states.description: A change whose text is the same shows it with "(No change)".

appearance: A card on the surface color with the default border and a 3dp start accent in the AI border role; each change on the subtle background with the subtle border. Removed words use the AI diff-remove fill and strong text and are struck through; added words use the AI diff-add fill and strong text and are underlined. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow the roles.
platformNotes: The web takes the title as a node; here it is a String. The web's word tokens keep inner apostrophes in one word and group neighbouring changes; this component reuses MonarchDiffViewer's word diff, which splits at apostrophes, so a changed contraction can show a smaller change, as on iOS. The web moves keyboard focus to the next undecided change; Compose requests input focus on the next Accept button with a FocusRequester; buttons take focus only outside touch mode (keyboard), TalkBack focus is not moved, and the announcement says what changed. The web and iOS show check and cross glyphs; Monarch for Android bundles no icons, so they are the optional statusIcon slot. Decisions are kept with rememberSaveable per part id. The part is the conversation model's MonarchAiEditProposalPart. Marked experimental because it is a domain composite that no Rook app has adopted yet.
accessibility: The card is a traversal group; its title is a heading.
Each change is one TalkBack element read as its name, its decision, then the diff with "Deleted:" and "Inserted:" before removed and added words.
Per-change buttons are named with the change, for example "Accept, Change 2 of 3".

After a decision the result is announced through a polite live region ("Change accepted. 1 left.") and input focus is requested on the next undecided change's Accept button, which takes effect with a keyboard (outside touch mode).
Removed text is struck through and added text underlined, and decisions are written words, so nothing depends on color.
Buttons are MonarchButton with 48dp touch targets; text wraps at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: A change with empty before is a pure addition and reads "Inserted:" only; empty after reads "Deleted:" only.
A new part id (a regenerated proposal that reuses change ids) starts undecided.
A change's status, when given by the app, wins over the remembered decision.
Without any callbacks the card is read-only even while proposed.
