name: MonarchAiErrorMessage
title: AiErrorMessage
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column on the MonarchBanner surface, with MonarchButton actions in a FlowRow and MonarchCollapsible for the details
summary: The failure card for an assistant turn: what went wrong in plain words, the actions that can fix it, an optional retry countdown and a technical details disclosure.
whenToUse: In place of, or at the end of, an assistant reply that failed: a rate limit, a conversation that is too long, a safety block, a lost connection or a failed tool.
whenNotToUse: For a failure outside an AI conversation use MonarchInlineErrorRetry or MonarchBanner. For a whole screen that failed to load use MonarchErrorState.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiErrorMessage(modifier: Modifier = Modifier, kind: MonarchAiErrorKind = MonarchAiErrorKind.Unknown, title: String? = null, message: String? = null, details: String? = null, retryAfterMillis: Long? = null, retrying: Boolean = false, announce: Boolean = true, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiErrorMessageLabels = MonarchAiErrorMessageLabels(), onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null, onEditPrompt: (() -> Unit)? = null, onSwitchModel: (() -> Unit)? = null, onNewConversation: (() -> Unit)? = null, onSummarize: (() -> Unit)? = null, actions: (@Composable FlowRowScope.() -> Unit)? = null)
enum class MonarchAiErrorKind { RateLimit, ContextOverflow, SafetyBlock, Network, ToolFailure, Unknown; companion object { fun fromCode(code: String?): MonarchAiErrorKind } }

class MonarchAiErrorMessageLabels(tone: String? = null, retry: String? = null, retryIn: ((seconds: Int) -> String)? = null, retryReady: String? = null, editPrompt: String? = null, switchModel: String? = null, newConversation: String? = null, summarize: String? = null, details: String? = null)

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the card.

options.name: kind
options.description: Why the turn failed. MonarchAiErrorKind.fromCode maps a raw error code.

options.name: title
options.description: Replaces the built-in title of the kind.

options.name: message
options.description: Replaces the built-in description of the kind.

options.name: details
options.description: Technical information, shown in code type behind a disclosure.

options.name: retryAfterMillis
options.description: Time until a retry is allowed, counted from when the card appears.

options.name: retrying
options.description: Shows a progress indicator on the retry action.

options.name: announce
options.description: Announces the title and message when the card appears.

options.name: icon
options.description: An icon at the start of the card. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the tone name, the action titles, the countdown text, the ready announcement and the details title.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows "Try again".

options.name: onEditPrompt
options.description: Shows "Edit message".

options.name: onSwitchModel
options.description: Shows "Switch model".

options.name: onNewConversation
options.description: Shows "New conversation".

options.name: onSummarize
options.description: Shows "Summarize and continue", for ContextOverflow only.

options.name: actions
options.description: Extra actions after the built-in ones.

states.name: kind
states.description: RateLimit, ContextOverflow and SafetyBlock use the warning tone; Network, ToolFailure and Unknown the danger tone. Each kind has its own title, description and action order.

states.name: counting down
states.description: The retry action is disabled and reads "Try again in 12s". Without onRetry the same text is shown as a caption.

states.name: retrying
states.description: The retry action shows a progress indicator, reads "Loading" and does not run.

states.name: details expanded
states.description: The technical details are shown in code type in a bordered box.

appearance: The surface of MonarchBanner: the subtle fill and the border of the warning or danger tone, the strong role of the tone for the icon, default text for the title and muted text for the description. The first action is a primary button, the others secondary. The details box is the surface role with the default border.
platformNotes: The parity map names MonarchBanner, but the banner takes one action and no extra content, so the card is drawn with the same tone palette and looks the same. The web's code prop is MonarchAiErrorKind.fromCode. title and message are Strings, and details is a String shown in code type. The many built-in strings are replaced through one labels value, as on iOS. The web draws action and kind glyphs; Monarch for Android bundles no icons, so the kind icon is a slot and the actions are text. The actions wrap in a FlowRow. retryAfter is milliseconds, as AiErrorPart's retryAfterMs; the countdown starts when the card appears and is updated every half second. The web announces through role=alert filled after mounting; Android fills an assertive live region after the first frame.
accessibility: The tone name, title and message are one TalkBack element, read as "Warning" or "Error", then the title, then the message.
Each action is a separate button with a 48dp touch target; the details disclosure header is 48dp high.
The title and message are announced once through an assertive live region after the card appears, unless announce is false.
"You can try again now." is announced through a polite live region when a countdown ends.
The tone is a spoken word as well as a color. The raw error code is never shown or spoken.
While retrying, the retry button reads "Loading" as its state and is reported as disabled.
edgeCases: Without handlers and without extra actions there is no action row.
onSummarize is ignored unless the kind is ContextOverflow.
A non-positive retryAfterMillis is no countdown.
A code that matches several rules takes the first: rate limit, then context, safety, tool, network.
Long titles, messages and details wrap; details keep their line breaks.

title: AiEvalReview
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.adaptive.navigation.NavigableListDetailPaneScaffold with a LazyColumn of MonarchListRow for the queue and a verticalScroll Column for the item; MonarchSegmentedControl for the verdict
summary: A recipe, not a component: a review queue for AI outputs, with each output's prompt, output and expected answer, a 1 to 5 rubric per criterion, notes and a pass or fail verdict.
whenToUse: Human evaluation of model or prompt changes, or spot-checking AI outputs before a feature launches or a model is switched.
whenNotToUse: For end-user feedback on one reply use MonarchAiFeedback. For reviewing AI drafts before they are sent use MonarchAiDraftQueue.
api: NavigableListDetailPaneScaffold(navigator, listPane = { AnimatedPane { LazyColumn { MonarchProgress(progress, label); ListItem(headline = title, supporting = verdict, Modifier.selectable(selected = id == current) { … }) } } }, detailPane = { AnimatedPane { Column(Modifier.verticalScroll(…)) { … } } })
MonarchAiMarkdown(text = item.output) after MonarchAiGeneratedBadge(size = MonarchAiGeneratedBadgeSize.Sm)
MonarchRatingPicker(value = scores[criterion.id], onValueChange = …, label = criterion.label, options = MonarchRatingOption.range(1, criterion.scale))
MonarchTextField(value = notes, onValueChange = …, label = "Notes", singleLine = false)
SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow { SegmentedButton(selected = verdict == "pass", onClick = …, shape = SegmentedButtonDefaults.itemShape(0, 2)) { Text("Pass") } … }
MonarchButton(text = "Previous" / "Next", onClick = …, size = MonarchButtonSize.Sm, enabled = …)

options.name: items
options.type: App list of outputs: id, title, prompt, output, reference
options.description: The queue. The output is Markdown text for MonarchAiMarkdown; the reference is optional and its block is left out without it.

options.name: rubric
options.type: App list of criteria: id, label, description, scale
options.description: One MonarchRatingPicker per criterion, scored 1 to scale (at most 5), with its description as a caption above it.

options.name: reviews
options.type: Scores, notes and verdict per item id
options.description: Held by the app and persisted on every change, as the web's onReviewChange.

options.name: current
options.description: The item shown in the detail pane; Previous and Next change it.

options.name: advance on verdict
options.description: Set current to the next item in the verdict's onClick to move on after pass or fail, as the web's advanceOnVerdict.

states.name: pending
states.description: A queue row reads "Not reviewed" under its title.

states.name: pass / fail
states.description: The row reads "Pass" or "Fail", and the segmented button is selected with Material 3's check mark.

states.name: current
states.description: The queue row of the item shown is selected (Modifier.selectable), so TalkBack reads it as selected.

states.name: scored
states.description: "Score 9 / 13" sums the scores given; each picker reads its value.

states.name: first / last
states.description: Previous is disabled on the first item, Next on the last.

states.name: done
states.description: The progress bar is full and Submit reviews is enabled once every item has a verdict.

states.name: empty
states.description: With no items, show a MonarchEmptyState in the list pane instead of the queue.

appearance: Every part is an existing component: Material 3 list items and segmented buttons in the Monarch theme, the linear MonarchProgress, MonarchAiGeneratedBadge on the AI roles, MonarchAiMarkdown, MonarchRatingPicker, MonarchTextField and small MonarchButtons. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web ships AiEvalReview as one component with a sticky queue column beside the item from 768px and the queue stacked above it below. On Android it is a recipe on the list-detail pattern: NavigableListDetailPaneScaffold shows the queue and the item side by side on a wide window and as a list that opens the item, with the system back gesture, on a phone. The web's radio choices per criterion are MonarchRatingPicker; its pass and fail radios are a single-choice segmented button row. The web's J / K and P / F shortcuts and the visible shortcut hint are left out: the web hides the hint on touch screens, and an app that wants them for hardware keyboards adds Modifier.onPreviewKeyEvent on the detail pane. The web moves focus to the new item's heading after Previous and Next; this recipe does not move focus. The web's check, cross and dot glyphs in the queue are left out because Monarch bundles no icons; the verdict is the row's supporting text. iOS has not covered this entry yet.
accessibility: Each queue row is one a MonarchListRow made selectable, so TalkBack reads its title, its verdict as text and whether it is the current item.
The item's title and the Prompt, Output, Expected, Rubric and Verdict labels are MonarchText headings, so TalkBack can move between them.
The output carries MonarchAiGeneratedBadge, read as AI-generated.
Each MonarchRatingPicker is named by its criterion and reads its value, for example "3 of 5".
Pass and Fail are Material 3 segmented buttons in a single-choice row: radio buttons with a selected state and a check mark, not color alone.

states.name: details

states.name: sending

appearance: Material 3 outlined icon toggle buttons or filter chips in Monarch's theme; the sheet uses the raised surface with the checkbox group, text field and buttons in their own appearance. The thank-you is muted caption text and the error danger-strong caption text. All are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web shows the reasons as chips and the form inline under the thumbs; as on iOS, the form is a modal bottom sheet and the reasons are a MonarchCheckboxGroup. Monarch bundles no icons, so the thumb glyphs come from the icon slot; without them each thumb is a FilterChip with its name, so meaning never depends on a glyph. Pressed thumbs use the Material toggle colors where the web uses the AI colors. The rating type is MonarchAiMessageFeedback, shared with MonarchAiConversation. The web moves focus to the thank-you; Android announces it through a polite live region because the sheet closes. onSubmit is a suspend function that throws in place of a promise. The web's uncontrolled mode is not offered: selection is hoisted. iOS uses a Binding and a trailing onSubmit closure; Android hoists selection with onSelectionChange and keeps onSubmit last. Experimental: an AI product composite that waits for a Rook app to adopt it.
accessibility: Each thumb is a Material toggle (icon button, with on or off state) or a selectable chip, named "Good response" or "Bad response"; the thumbs are a traversal group named "Rate this response".
Thumbs and sheet buttons have touch targets of at least 48dp.
In the sheet the title is a heading, the reasons are labelled checkboxes under the question and the comment has a visible label.
The thank-you and the error under the thumbs are one always-present polite live region; the error in the sheet is a polite notice.
The pressed state is a toggle state or a chip's check mark, not color alone.
edgeCases: Pressing the pressed thumb again clears the rating and closes any sheet without sending.
A rating with no reasons shows only the comment in the sheet.
Without onSubmit, ratings still change and the thank-you shows.
A send cancelled by leaving the screen is not shown as an error.
Reason ids that are not offered are left out of the submission.

The web and iOS draw the AI bot glyph; Monarch for Android bundles no icons, so the glyph is the icon slot, and iconOnly without an icon shows the label. A long custom label wraps inside the capsule.

iconOnly without an icon shows the label, because the badge would otherwise be empty.

name: MonarchAiGenerativeUi
title: AiGenerativeUi
wrapsNative: A name-to-composable registry (MonarchAiUiRegistry) with a decoder per component into its own typed model; MonarchInlineNotice for refused parts; MonarchProgress (androidx.compose.material3.CircularProgressIndicator) while props stream
summary: Renders a component the model asked for in a ui part of the conversation, but only when its name is in the app's allow-listed registry, with the props treated as untrusted data.
whenToUse: When an assistant may answer with an interactive card (a booking slot, a chart, a form) that the app has built and allowed in advance.
whenNotToUse: For text, citations, tool calls and other standard parts use MonarchAiConversation's own rendering. Never use it to show markup or code produced by a model.

class MonarchAiUiRegistry { val names: List; operator fun contains(name: String): Boolean; fun

register(name: String, decode: (MonarchAiJSON) -> P?, description: String? = null, streaming: MonarchAiUiStreaming = MonarchAiUiStreaming.Progressive, validate: ((P) -> Boolean)? = null, content: @Composable (props: P, emit: MonarchAiUiEmit) -> Unit); fun manifest(): String }
class MonarchAiUiEmit(handler: ((type: String, payload: MonarchAiJSON?) -> Unit)? = null) { val connected: Boolean; operator fun invoke(type: String, payload: MonarchAiJSON? = null) }
data class MonarchAiUiAction(type: String, payload: MonarchAiJSON? = null, component: String, partId: String? = null, toolCallId: String? = null)
enum class MonarchAiUiRejection { UnknownComponent, InvalidProps }
enum class MonarchAiUiStreaming { Progressive, OnComplete }
data class MonarchAiGenerativeUiLabels(unknown: String? = null, invalid: String? = null, loading: String? = null)

options.name: part
options.description: The ui part of the message: the component name, the props (or, while streaming, JSON text still arriving), the part id and the tool call it answers.

options.name: registry
options.description: The allow-list. Only names registered here render. Build it once, in remember or outside composition.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the result.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces the notices for an unknown component and for invalid props, and the TalkBack name of the progress indicator, "Loading".

options.name: onReject
options.description: Called once per refused part, with the reason, for logging.

options.name: onAction
options.description: Receives actions the component sends through its MonarchAiUiEmit, with the payload sanitised and the component, part id and tool call id filled in. Without it the channel is not connected.

states.name: rendered
states.description: The registered component, drawn from its decoded props.

states.name: pending
states.description: While props stream and do not decode yet, or for a component registered with OnComplete, a circular progress indicator at least 48dp high, named "Loading".

states.name: unknown component
states.description: A neutral notice: "This part of the answer can’t be shown here."

states.name: invalid props
states.description: A neutral notice: "This part of the answer had data that couldn’t be shown."

appearance: The rendered component brings its own appearance. The notice is a neutral MonarchInlineNotice with the muted fill; the progress indicator is the Material 3 circular indicator in the accent color. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Same allow-list model, notices, streaming policies, sanitising limits and action channel as the web and iOS. Kotlin has no reflection-free Decodable, so each component registers a decoder function from MonarchAiJSON to its own typed model; returning null or throwing refuses the props. Compose cannot catch a composable that fails while composing, so there is no render error case: MonarchAiUiRejection has UnknownComponent and InvalidProps, and a decoder or validator that throws counts as invalid props. Blocked prop names of the web (style, className, on… handlers) have no meaning on Android and are not filtered. The manifest lists names and descriptions without a schema summary. Streaming props are read with a partial JSON reader built on the conversation model's MonarchAiJSON, as on iOS.
accessibility: The rendered component brings its own accessibility.
The notice is static text; the neutral tone adds no spoken tone name.
The progress indicator while props stream is named "Loading", replaceable with labels.loading.
Model output is never rendered as markup, so nothing unexpected becomes focusable.
The notice text wraps at large font sizes.
edgeCases: A streaming part is never refused for its props, because they may still become valid; once complete, props given as text instead of data are refused.
Registering a name twice replaces the earlier component and keeps its place in names and the manifest; an empty name is ignored.

Strings longer than 20,000 characters are cut, arrays and objects keep 500 members, nesting stops at 8 levels, numbers that are not finite are dropped, and links that are not http, https, mailto or relative are dropped.
A refusal is reported to onReject once per part, not on every recomposition.
The registry is not observable: register everything before the part is shown.

A name that is not allowed

MonarchAiGenerativeUi(
    part = MonarchAiUiPart("WebView", MonarchAiJSON.Object(emptyMap())),
    registry = MonarchAiUiRegistry(),
    onReject = { reason, _ -> refused = reason.name },
)

title: AiGhostText

summary: A text field with inline completion: the model's suggested continuation is drawn in the muted text color after the typed text and accepted by a tap on it, an Accept suggestion button, a TalkBack action or Tab on a hardware keyboard. MonarchAiCompletion is the state behind it.
whenToUse: Where an assistant can finish what the person is writing: a reply, a description, a commit message.
whenNotToUse: For a list of completions to choose from use a menu or suggestion chips. For rewriting text the person selected use an assistant action, not inline completion.

@Stable class MonarchAiCompletion(scope: CoroutineScope, debounceMillis: Long = 300L, minimumCharacters: Int = 3, enabled: Boolean = true, complete: suspend (text: String, cursor: Int) -> String?)
MonarchAiCompletion: val status: MonarchAiCompletionStatus; val suggestion: String; val text: String; val cursor: Int; var enabled: Boolean; var onError: ((Throwable) -> Unit)?

MonarchAiCompletion: fun update(text: String, cursor: Int); fun dismiss(); fun accept(): MonarchAiCompletionAcceptance?; fun acceptWord(): MonarchAiCompletionAcceptance?; fun setComposing(composing: Boolean); companion fun nextWord(suggestion: String): String

@Composable fun rememberMonarchAiCompletion(debounceMillis: Long = MonarchAiCompletion.DEFAULT_DEBOUNCE_MILLIS, minimumCharacters: Int = MonarchAiCompletion.DEFAULT_MINIMUM_CHARACTERS, enabled: Boolean = true, complete: suspend (text: String, cursor: Int) -> String?): MonarchAiCompletion
enum class MonarchAiCompletionStatus { Idle, Waiting, Loading, Ready, Error }
data class MonarchAiCompletionAcceptance(inserted: String, text: String, cursor: Int)
enum class MonarchAiGhostTextAcceptKind { All, Word }
class MonarchAiGhostTextLabels(announce: ((String) -> String)? = null, accept: String? = null, dismiss: String? = null, accepted: String? = null, dismissed: String? = null)

options.name: state
options.description: The text of the field. The suggestion is never written into it until accepted.

options.name: completion
options.description: Completion state you keep, from rememberMonarchAiCompletion, to read or drive it. Replaces complete, debounceMillis, minimumCharacters and completionEnabled.

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label, also the TalkBack label.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the component.

options.name: placeholder
options.description: An example shown while the field is empty and focused.

options.name: helperText
options.description: Guidance shown below the field.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the field can be edited. A disabled field shows no suggestion.

options.name: completionEnabled
options.description: Turns suggestions off when false (second overload).

options.name: debounceMillis
options.description: How long typing must pause before a request is sent (second overload).

options.name: minimumCharacters
options.description: The fewest characters before the cursor, without surrounding white space, for a request (second overload).

options.name: showAcceptButton
options.description: Shows the Accept suggestion button under the field while a suggestion shows. Its 48dp room is always kept.

options.name: lineLimits
options.description: The lines of the field.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the announcements and action names.

options.name: onAccept
options.description: Called after a suggestion, or one word of it, went into the text.

options.name: onDismiss
options.description: Called when the user dismissed the suggestion.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the focus and press interactions of the field.

options.name: complete
options.description: Asks the model for a continuation of the text at the cursor, a UTF-16 offset. Return the text to insert, or null for none. It is cancelled when its answer is stale.

states.name: idle
states.description: Only the typed text, or the placeholder while the field is empty.

states.name: waiting, loading
states.description: Nothing extra is drawn while the request waits for the pause or is in flight.

states.name: ready
states.description: The suggestion is drawn after the typed text in the muted text color, and the Accept suggestion button appears in the room kept for it.

states.name: error
states.description: Nothing is drawn. onError of the completion is called.

states.name: focused
states.description: The field's border takes the focus ring color. Suggestions are only made while the field has focus.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The disabled text and fill colors, no editing and no suggestion.

appearance: The field uses the Monarch text field colors of MonarchTextField; the suggestion uses the muted text color and the accept button is a small ghost MonarchButton, in every theme.
platformNotes: The web wraps any textarea or input; on Android the component is the field, because the suggestion must be drawn by the field's OutputTransformation. Because of that the field takes a TextFieldState instead of a value and callback, the Compose text API that supports output transformations. On iOS the system's inline predictions are turned off; on Android the suggestion is never shown while the keyboard is composing a word, so it does not compete with the keyboard's suggestion strip, and the keyboard's predictions are left on. Android has no accessibility hint, so iOS's instruction label is not offered: the announcement of a new suggestion says how to accept it, and TalkBack has Accept suggestion and Dismiss suggestion actions. The keys are the web's: Tab or the forward arrow accepts, Ctrl or Alt with the forward arrow accepts a word, Escape dismisses; they need a hardware keyboard. The cursor is a UTF-16 offset, as on the web. Accepting edits the TextFieldState, so it is one step in its undo history. The tap area on the suggestion is computed from the default Material 3 content padding of the field. The web's useAiRewrite and applyAiRewrite are not part of this entry.
accessibility: The field is a Material 3 text field labelled by label; TalkBack reads the typed text only, never the suggestion.
A new suggestion is announced through a polite live region under the field, with how to accept it; the rest of one being typed through or taken word by word is not announced again.
"Suggestion accepted." and "Suggestion dismissed." are announced through the same live region.
While a suggestion shows, the field has the TalkBack actions "Accept suggestion" and "Dismiss suggestion".
The Accept suggestion button has a 48dp touch target; the tap area on the suggestion itself is its text with a 4dp margin, which is smaller, so the button is the full-size alternative.
The suggestion differs from typed text by its position after the caret as well as its color.
edgeCases: A suggestion is only shown with the caret at the end of the text (white space may follow), never in the middle or with a selection.
Losing focus, disabling the field, a selection or the keyboard composing a word dismisses the suggestion.
A change to the text from the app is treated like typing: a new request is made after the pause.
A request whose text has since changed is cancelled and its answer ignored.

The tap on the suggestion, the hardware keys and the alignment of the suggestion with the caret were tested under Robolectric only; a device check with TalkBack and a hardware keyboard is still needed.

states.description: The target is a square agent avatar; the border and the side lines use the AI border color.

states.name: to a person

All colors are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.

The web drops the side lines below 30rem of its container; Android draws them only on windows from 640dp (the sm breakpoint), so phones show the full-width marker. The web marks the root with the note role; Compose has no note role, so the marker is one element whose description starts with "Handoff". The web and iOS draw an arrow glyph; Monarch for Android bundles no icons, so the arrow is the optional arrowIcon slot. The person target is MonarchAiHandoffTarget.Person instead of an object with kind human; pictures are Painters loaded by the app, not URLs. Agent names are read with "(AI agent)" after them and a person's name is not, so the direction is clear without the pictures.
The avatars, the arrow and the lines are not read.
The sentence is built by a function of both names, so a translation can reorder it; the names are made strong wherever they appear.
Nothing is interactive; text wraps at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: Long names and reasons wrap; nothing is cut.
A blank reason is left out of the view and of the spoken text.
Without dateMillis no time is shown.
A name that also appears inside the other name is made strong at each occurrence.

summary: Images generated by AI as a grid of variations: placeholders while they generate, previews with progress while they refine, then each image with a required alt text field and "Use image" and "More like this" actions.
whenToUse: In an assistant reply or a creation flow that generates several image variations for the person to choose from and describe.
whenNotToUse: For images that already exist use an image grid or MonarchFilePreview. For one finished artifact use MonarchAiArtifactCard.

options.name: images
options.description: The images or their slots, in order: each with an id, a Painter the app loaded (null while generating or when it failed to load) and the alt text.

options.name: status
options.description: Pending: placeholders. Progressive: previews, blurred while they refine. Done: final images with fields and actions. Error: the error message.

options.name: onAltChange
options.description: Called with an image's id and its new alt text as the person types. Store it and pass it back in images.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the group.

options.name: progress
options.description: Overall progress from 0 to 1, shown as a percentage and a bar while generating. Values outside 0..1 are clamped; NaN counts as unknown.

options.name: selection
options.description: The id of the chosen image.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Adds "Use image" to each finished image; called with its id.

options.name: onVariations
options.description: Adds "More like this" to each finished image; called with its id.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Adds a "Try again" button in the error state.

options.name: error
options.description: Replaces the built-in error message.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces any built-in string; the ones that depend on a number or a position are functions.

states.name: pending
states.description: Each slot is a MonarchSkeleton placeholder (still when animations are off); the status line reads "Generating images…" with the percentage when known, over a progress bar; alt fields are disabled; there are no actions.

states.name: progressive
states.description: Loaded previews are shown, blurred on Android 12 and later; the status line reads "Refining images…".

states.name: done
states.description: Final images; the status line counts them; each empty alt field shows its error; the actions appear when their callbacks are given.

states.name: error
states.description: The images are replaced by the error message: a MonarchInlineErrorRetry banner with onRetry, otherwise a danger MonarchInlineNotice.

states.name: selected
states.description: The chosen image has a thicker ring in the solid assistant color, a "Selected" mark, and its "Use image" button becomes primary and selected.

states.name: unavailable
states.description: An image without a Painter after generation shows "Preview unavailable".

appearance: Square slots with the medium radius and a subtle border on the muted background, the status line in the caption type and the muted text color, and the selected mark as a pill in the solid assistant color. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The parity map named LazyVerticalGrid; the images are laid out in plain rows of equal cells instead (as many columns of at least 160dp as fit, the web's 10rem, scaled with the font size), because a few variations sit in a conversation that already scrolls and a lazy grid cannot be nested in a vertical scroll. Images are Painters the app loaded: Monarch adds no image loader, so there is no URL parameter (iOS takes a URL or an Image). The web and iOS bind the alt text; Android is controlled and calls onAltChange. Selection is a value with onSelect instead of a binding. The refining blur uses Modifier.blur, which draws only on Android 12 and later. Completion is announced through a polite live region instead of a posted announcement.
accessibility: The group is a traversal group named "AI generated images", replaceable with labels.label.
Each image has the image role and is read by its alt text, or "Generated image n" while that is empty.
The status line is text; the progress bar is hidden from TalkBack because the line carries the percentage.
Completion is announced once, through a polite live region that is always present, when the status changes to done.
Each alt field has its own label ("Alt text for image n") and, while empty, an error that TalkBack reads.
"Use image" and "More like this" are named with the image's position and have 48dp touch targets; "Use image" is selected on the chosen image.
Placeholders and the "Selected" mark are hidden from TalkBack; an unavailable slot is read as "Preview unavailable".
edgeCases: Large font sizes give one column, so fields and buttons keep their width.
Image ids must be unique; the selection and the callbacks use them.
An image whose Painter is null after generation shows "Preview unavailable" and no actions.
With no images and status done the status line reads "0 images generated".

summary: AI-suggested changes marked inline in read-only text, with Previous and Next between changes and Accept and Reject for the active one.
whenToUse: When an assistant suggests rewording for a paragraph, a description or a message draft and the changes are small and best read in context.
whenNotToUse: For edits that span several labelled fields or sections use MonarchAiEditProposal; for code use MonarchDiffViewer; wait until streamed text is complete before showing suggestions.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchAiInlineDiff(segments: List<MonarchAiDiffSegment>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, onAccept: ((id: String) -> Unit)? = null, onReject: ((id: String) -> Unit)? = null, showNavigation: Boolean = true, labels: MonarchAiInlineDiffLabels = MonarchAiInlineDiffLabels())

data class MonarchAiDiffSegment(type: MonarchAiDiffSegmentType, text: String, id: String? = null) { companion object { fun diffWords(before: String, after: String): List<MonarchAiDiffSegment>; fun changes(segments: List<MonarchAiDiffSegment>): List<MonarchAiInlineDiffChange>; fun resolve(segments: List<MonarchAiDiffSegment>, id: String, accept: Boolean): List<MonarchAiDiffSegment> } }
enum class MonarchAiDiffSegmentType { Equal, Insert, Delete }
data class MonarchAiInlineDiffChange(id: String, segmentIndexes: List<Int>, deleted: String, inserted: String)

class MonarchAiInlineDiffLabels(label: String? = null, deleted: String? = null, inserted: String? = null, position: ((index: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, none: String? = null, previous: String? = null, next: String? = null, accept: String? = null, reject: String? = null, acceptChange: ((index: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, rejectChange: ((index: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, announcement: ((accepted: Boolean, left: Int) -> String)? = null)

options.name: segments
options.description: The text as unchanged, added and removed runs in reading order, for example from MonarchAiDiffSegment.diffWords. Controlled: update it after each decision, for example with MonarchAiDiffSegment.resolve.

options.name: onAccept
options.description: Accepts a change by id; shows Accept for the active change and the Accept custom action.

options.name: onReject
options.description: Rejects a change by id; shows Reject for the active change and the Reject custom action.

options.name: showNavigation
options.description: Shows the bar with the position, or "No suggested changes", and Previous and Next. Hide it for one short suggestion.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings: name, Deleted:, Inserted:, position, none, Previous, Next, Accept, Reject, the spoken names of Accept and Reject and the announcement.

states.name: active change
states.description: Outlined in the AI border color; its position is the text's state and the bar's text; Accept and Reject act on it.

states.name: no changes
states.description: The bar reads "No suggested changes", the text is plain and there are no buttons or actions.

states.name: one change
states.description: Previous and Next are disabled.

states.name: read only
states.description: Without onAccept and onReject the changes can be stepped through but not decided.

appearance: Unchanged text in the default text color. Removed runs use the AI diff-remove fill and strong text and are struck through; added runs use the AI diff-add fill and strong text and are underlined. The active change has a hairline outline in the AI border role, and the position line is muted caption text. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web renders each change as a focusable span with inline icon buttons next to it, roving focus and arrow keys. On Android the text is one Text element and the controls sit outside the text: Previous and Next in the bar above, Accept and Reject below, because 48dp buttons inside a line of text break the line height. Tapping a change makes it active, and TalkBack users get custom actions on the text (Next, Previous, Accept change, Reject change) instead. Buttons are text buttons because Monarch bundles no icons. The web's AiDiffSegment, aiInlineDiffChanges and resolveAiInlineDiff are MonarchAiDiffSegment and its companion functions diffWords, changes and resolve. Marks inside an editor (the web's planned editor adapters) are not offered. iOS has no entry yet.
accessibility: The whole diff is a traversal group named "AI suggested changes".
The text is one element read with "Deleted:" and "Inserted:" before removed and added runs; its state is the position, "Change 1 of 2".
Custom actions on the text move to the next or previous change and accept or reject the active one, so a tap on the text is never required.
Accept and Reject are named with the change, "Accept change 2 of 5", and have 48dp targets.
Each decision is announced through a polite live region that is always present: "Change accepted. 1 left."
Removed text is struck through and added text underlined, so the kind never depends on color.
The text wraps at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: Neighbouring removed and added runs with the same id (or none) form one change; a different id starts a new change.
After a decision the app removes the change, and the change that takes its place becomes active; the last change moves back to the one before.
An id that is not a change leaves the segments unchanged in resolve.
Empty segments are dropped by resolve; unchanged neighbours without ids are joined.
A change without an id is named by the index of its first segment, so the ids of later changes shift after a decision; use the id passed to onAccept or onReject at once, or give segments ids.

parityExceptions.reason: The web puts a 20px check and a cross beside the active change inside the sentence. summary: A prompt about selected text: an "Ask AI" action in the text selection menu that opens a bottom sheet with an excerpt of the selection, a prompt field and quick prompts.
whenToUse: In documents, emails or notes where AI rewrites what the person selected, opened from the selection menu or from a visible button such as "Edit paragraph with AI".
whenNotToUse: For an open-ended conversation, use MonarchAiPromptInput in an assistant screen. For suggesting the value of one form field, use MonarchAiAutofillField. For completing text as it is typed, use MonarchAiGhostText.

public class MonarchAiInlinePromptLabels(label: String? = null, placeholder: String? = null, inputLabel: String? = null, submit: String? = null, context: String? = null, suggestions: String? = null, pending: String? = null)

options.name: onDismissRequest
options.description: Called when the sheet should close: after a swipe down, a tap on the scrim, Back, or after sending with closeOnSubmit. Stop showing it.

options.name: onSubmit
options.description: Receives the trimmed prompt or the tapped suggestion. Never called with blank text or while pending.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the sheet.

options.name: context
options.description: What the prompt acts on, usually the selected text. Shown as an excerpt of at most 140 characters under the label "Selection".

options.name: suggestions
options.description: Quick prompts such as "Shorten". Tapping one sends it at once.

options.name: initialValue
options.description: The text the field starts with each time the sheet is shown, with the caret after it.

options.name: closeOnSubmit
options.description: Slides the sheet away and calls onDismissRequest after sending. Off, the sheet stays and the field is cleared.

options.name: pending
options.description: A request is being sent: the field, Send and the suggestions are disabled and "Sending…" is shown and announced.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings: label, placeholder, inputLabel, submit, context, suggestions, pending.

options.name: sendIcon
options.description: The Send button's icon. The button shows the word Send without it and is named Send either way.

options.name: MonarchAiInlinePromptArea onAskAi
options.description: Wrap a SelectionContainer or a text field: "Ask AI" is added to its selection menu, and picking it closes the menu and calls onAskAi.

options.name: MonarchAiInlinePromptArea state, onAskAi
options.description: The text-field overload: the item is added only while text is selected in state, and onAskAi receives the selected text.

options.name: MonarchAiInlinePromptArea enabled
options.description: Off, the menu item is not added.

options.name: MonarchAiInlinePromptArea label
options.description: The menu item's text; the built-in "Ask AI" without it.

options.name: MonarchAiInlinePromptArea content
options.description: The selectable text or the text field, placed in a Box.

states.name: open
states.description: The sheet is fully expanded (no half-open stop), the prompt field has focus and the keyboard opens.

states.name: empty
states.description: Send is disabled until the field holds text other than spaces.

states.name: with context
states.description: An excerpt box with the AI border shows "Selection" and the first 140 characters of the context, cut with an ellipsis.

states.name: pending
states.description: The field, Send and the suggestions are disabled and "Sending…" appears under them.

states.name: closed
states.description: After sending (with closeOnSubmit), a swipe, a scrim tap or Back, onDismissRequest is called and the app stops showing it.

appearance: A Material 3 bottom sheet on the surface fill. The excerpt sits in a box with the subtle fill and the AI border role, its label in the strong AI color and the excerpt in muted text. The prompt box and the primary Send button come from MonarchAiPromptInput; suggestions are ghost buttons. Dark and both high-contrast themes swap the same roles.
platformNotes: The web shows a floating popover anchored to the selection rectangle. Android has no such floating panel for a selection; the platform pattern is an item in the system selection toolbar plus a bottom sheet, so this is two parts: MonarchAiInlinePromptArea for the toolbar item (a wrapper rather than a Modifier, because the built-in label is a string resource and the Foundation API that hands a Context to the menu builder is internal) and MonarchAiInlinePrompt for the sheet. There is no anchor, side or align, and no returnFocusTo: when the sheet's window closes the system gives focus back to the window underneath. The web's open and onOpenChange become the Material 3 idiom of showing the sheet while a state is true with onDismissRequest. The keyboard hint line of the web is left out, because touch is the main input; a hardware keyboard still sends with Enter, adds a line with Shift+Enter and closes with Escape (Back). With closeOnSubmit off the field is cleared after sending, where the web keeps the text. Compose does not expose the selected text of a SelectionContainer, so the app passes context itself; the TextFieldState overload reads the selection of a text field. iOS has no entry for this id yet.
accessibility: The sheet's content has the pane title "Ask AI", and the same text is shown as a heading.
The prompt field takes focus when the sheet opens and is named "Prompt".
The excerpt is one TalkBack element that reads "Selection" followed by the excerpt.
The quick prompts are a traversal group named "Suggestions"; each is a button with a 48dp touch target.
While pending, "Sending…" is announced through a polite live region that is always present, and the field, Send and suggestions report disabled.
The "Ask AI" item is a regular item of the system selection menu, built with the same Foundation API as Cut, Copy and Paste; picking it closes the menu before onAskAi runs.
The Material 3 drag handle keeps its TalkBack collapse and dismiss actions, with a 48dp touch target reserved around it.
edgeCases: A blank prompt or blank suggestion is never sent; the prompt is trimmed before onSubmit.
Context longer than 140 characters is cut at a character boundary with trailing spaces removed and an ellipsis added; blank context shows no excerpt.
The toolbar may move "Ask AI" to its overflow menu when there is no room after Cut, Copy, Paste and Select all.
The TextFieldState overload adds nothing while only a caret is placed, so the caret menu (Paste) is unchanged.
Long prompts grow the field up to eight lines and then scroll inside it.

On a phone the on-screen keyboard covers the area under a paragraph, so the same panel (the selection, the prompt field with Send and the three quick prompts, in the web's order) opens as a bottom sheet above the keyboard, and the keyboard shortcuts line is left out because a phone has no Shift+Enter or Esc.
parityExceptions.convention: Material bottom sheet for input that the keyboard would cover; no hardware-key hints on a touch device

name: MonarchAiInsightCallout
title: AiInsightCallout
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row and FlowRow with background, drawBehind and border, MonarchCollapsible, MonarchButton, androidx.compose.material3.IconButton
summary: A proactive insight about the current record or screen: what was noticed, why, the evidence and one action, with its origin shown honestly as "AI insight" or "Rule-based".
whenToUse: On a record or dashboard, to raise one thing the person should know or act on, such as a renewal at risk, with the reason and where it came from.
whenNotToUse: For several insights side by side use MonarchInsightStrip. For a system message that is not an insight use MonarchInlineNotice or MonarchBanner. For an error in an assistant reply use MonarchAiErrorMessage.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiInsightCallout(title: String, why: String, origin: MonarchAiInsightOrigin, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, tone: MonarchTone = MonarchTone.Info, heading: Boolean = false, actionLabel: String? = null, onAction: (() -> Unit)? = null, onDismiss: (() -> Unit)? = null, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, originIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, dismissIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiInsightCalloutLabels = MonarchAiInsightCalloutLabels(), evidence: (@Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)? = null)
enum class MonarchAiInsightOrigin { Ai, Rule }
data class MonarchAiInsightCalloutLabels(tone: String? = null, ai: String? = null, rule: String? = null, evidence: String? = null, dismiss: String? = null)

options.name: title
options.description: The insight in one line, already localised, such as "Renewal at risk".

options.name: why
options.description: Why it was raised, in plain words. Shown as plain text.

options.name: origin
options.description: Ai: produced by a model, labelled "AI insight" in the assistant colors. Rule: a fixed rule written by people, labelled "Rule-based" in neutral colors. Always shown.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the callout.

options.name: tone
options.description: How much it matters: Info, Warning, Danger (needs action now), Success (good news) or Neutral. Sets the fill, border, bar and icon color and the tone name read before the title.

options.name: heading
options.description: Marks the title as a heading for TalkBack navigation.

options.name: actionLabel
options.description: The label of the one follow-up action, a small MonarchButton. Shown only together with onAction.

options.name: onAction
options.description: The follow-up action.

options.name: onDismiss
options.description: Adds a dismiss button at the end. The app removes the callout and decides where focus goes.

options.name: icon
options.description: The tone icon at the start, tinted with the tone's strong color. Decorative.

options.name: originIcon
options.description: A mark before the origin label, such as a bot icon for the AI origin. Decorative.

options.name: dismissIcon
options.description: The close mark of the dismiss button. Without it the button shows "Dismiss insight" as text.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces the built-in strings: the tone name, "AI insight", "Rule-based", "Show evidence" and "Dismiss insight".

options.name: evidence
options.description: Supporting data, shown in a collapsed "Show evidence" disclosure.

states.name: tone
states.description: Each tone uses its subtle fill, its border and its strong color for the start bar and the icon.

states.name: evidence collapsed
states.description: Only the "Show evidence" row is shown; it reads as collapsed.

states.name: evidence expanded
states.description: The evidence is shown under the disclosure row, animated only when animations are on.

states.name: dismissible
states.description: With onDismiss, a dismiss button sits at the end; the callout stays until the app removes it.

appearance: A container with the large radius, the tone's subtle fill and border and a four-dp bar in the tone's strong color on the start edge. The title uses the strong body type, the reason the body type in the default text color. The origin label is a pill: the subtle assistant fill, assistant border and strong assistant text for AI, the surface fill, default border and muted text for rule-based. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Same parts as the web and iOS. The web's severity names (info, warning, critical, positive) map to MonarchTone Info, Warning, Danger and Success, and the spoken tone names keep the web words (Info, Warning, Critical, Positive). Monarch for Android bundles no icons, so the tone icon, the origin mark and the close mark are optional slots; without a close mark the dismiss button shows its label. The web renders the title as a heading of a chosen level; Android has one heading level, set with heading. The evidence disclosure keeps its open state across configuration changes.
accessibility: TalkBack reads the title with the tone name first, for example "Warning: Renewal at risk", so the tone is never color alone; the neutral tone, or an empty tone label, reads the title alone.
With heading true the title is a heading.
The origin label is visible text, "AI insight" or "Rule-based", and is read as such.
The evidence disclosure is a button with the expand and collapse actions and a collapsed or expanded state.
The action button, the disclosure row and the dismiss button each have a 48dp touch target; the dismiss button is named "Dismiss insight".
The icons are decorative and hidden from TalkBack.
The tone bar and the dismiss button follow the layout direction.
edgeCases: A long title wraps, and the origin label moves to the next line when it does not fit beside it.
actionLabel without onAction, or onAction without actionLabel, shows no action.
Without a dismiss icon the dismiss button is a text button and takes more width.

name: MonarchAiKnowledgeScope

wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.TriStateCheckbox in rows with androidx.compose.foundation.selection.triStateToggleable, in a androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
summary: A tree of spaces, documents and apps with checkboxes, where a person picks what grounds the assistant's answers.
whenToUse: In an assistant's settings or composer, to let people limit the answers to chosen spaces, documents and connected apps.
whenNotToUse: For a flat list of options, use MonarchCheckboxGroup. To browse a hierarchy and open items, use MonarchTreeView. To connect new apps, use MonarchAiConnectorPicker.

class MonarchAiKnowledgeSource(id: String, label: String, kind: MonarchAiKnowledgeSourceKind, description: String? = null, children: List<MonarchAiKnowledgeSource> = emptyList()) { val isGroup: Boolean }
enum class MonarchAiKnowledgeSourceKind { Space, Document, App }

class MonarchAiKnowledgeScopeLabels(label: String? = null, kind: ((MonarchAiKnowledgeSourceKind) -> String)? = null, itemLabel: ((label: String, kind: String) -> String)? = null, summary: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, empty: String? = null, expand: ((label: String) -> String)? = null, collapse: ((label: String) -> String)? = null)

options.name: sources
options.description: The sources as a tree: each has an id, a label, a kind (space, document, app), an optional description and optional children.

options.name: selection
options.description: The ids of the selected sources. A group's id stands for everything in it.

options.name: onSelectionChange
options.description: Called after every toggle with every fully selected source, groups included, in tree order; ids that are not in the tree are kept at the end.

options.name: expandIcon
options.description: A chevron that points to the end, such as a MonarchIcon of size Sm with mirrorInRtl. It turns a quarter turn while a group is open. Required because Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the tree.

options.name: enabled
options.description: false makes every checkbox impossible to change; groups can still be opened.

options.name: initiallyExpanded
options.description: The ids of the groups that start open. Later opening and closing is kept across configuration changes.

options.name: showSummary
options.description: Shows "3 sources selected" under the tree. A fully selected group counts as one.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for "Knowledge sources", the kind names, "Handbook, Space", the summary, "No sources available" and "Show contents of" / "Hide contents of" (strings_aiknowledgescope.xml).

states.name: unchecked
states.description: An empty checkbox. Checking it selects the source and everything in it.

states.name: checked
states.description: A ticked checkbox. Checking it again clears the source and everything in it.

states.name: mixed
states.description: A group with some of its contents selected shows the Material 3 indeterminate box with a dash. Checking it clears the group.

states.name: expanded
states.description: The chevron turns a quarter turn and the group's contents follow, indented one level.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With enabled = false the checkboxes and texts take the disabled roles and cannot change; groups can still be opened.

states.name: empty
states.description: No sources: a small MonarchEmptyState reading "No sources available".

appearance: Material 3 checkboxes in the Monarch theme (accent fill when checked or mixed) beside the source name in default text and the kind and description in muted caption text; the chevron is muted text. Disabled rows use the disabled text role. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web builds an ARIA tree with a roving focus and arrow keys; Android uses checkbox rows in a column, so TalkBack, Switch Access and a hardware keyboard move through them like any controls, and a group's disclosure is a separate button. The row also offers TalkBack's expand and collapse actions. Level, set size and position are not spoken. MonarchTreeView is not reused: it has single and multiple selection but no tri-state checkboxes, and it is a lazy list that cannot sit in a scrolling screen. The web's controlled expanded and onExpandedChange are not offered; initiallyExpanded sets the first state, as iOS's startsExpanded. The web announces the summary politely; Android shows it as text and lets each checkbox speak its new state, as iOS does. The chevron is a required slot because Monarch bundles no icons.
accessibility: The tree is a traversal group named "Knowledge sources".
Each source is one element with the checkbox role, named "Handbook, Space" followed by its description, read as checked, not checked or partially checked.
A partly selected group is a tri-state checkbox in the indeterminate state, so the state is spoken, not only drawn as a dash.
Each group has a disclosure button named "Show contents of Handbook" or "Hide contents of Handbook", and its row offers the expand and collapse actions.
Every row and disclosure button has a 48dp touch target; names and descriptions wrap at font scale 2.0.
The chevron turns the other way in right-to-left layouts so it points down when open, and the disclosure button sits at the start edge.
edgeCases: A group with every child selected counts as selected, and its id is added to the selection.
Ids in the selection that are not in the tree are kept, at the end, so a source that is temporarily missing is not lost.
The tree is not lazy; for hundreds of sources offer a search instead.
An empty children list is a single source, not an empty group.

name: MonarchAiLauncher
title: AiLauncher
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.FloatingActionButton and ExtendedFloatingActionButton (solid), androidx.compose.material3.Button (subtle), androidx.compose.material3.BadgedBox with Badge
summary: The button that opens and closes an AI assistant: a round floating action button or a quieter toolbar button, with an unread dot, a count or a working ring.
whenToUse: As the one entry point to an assistant on a screen: in the floatingActionButton slot of a Scaffold, or in a toolbar or navigation rail.
whenNotToUse: For the main action of a screen that is not the assistant use a FloatingActionButton or MonarchButton. Inside the assistant panel use its own close control.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiLauncher(open: Boolean, onOpenChange: (Boolean) -> Unit, icon: @Composable () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchAiLauncherVariant = MonarchAiLauncherVariant.Solid, badge: MonarchAiLauncherBadge? = null, enabled: Boolean = true, showLabel: Boolean? = null, closeIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, label: String? = null, badgeLabel: String? = null, openLabel: String? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)
enum class MonarchAiLauncherVariant { Solid, Subtle }
sealed interface MonarchAiLauncherBadge { data object Unread; data object Working; data class Count(val count: Int) }

options.name: open
options.description: Whether the assistant the launcher controls is open.

options.name: onOpenChange
options.description: Called with the new state when the user activates the button.

options.name: icon
options.description: The assistant glyph. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the launcher.

options.name: variant
options.description: Solid: a round, filled floating action button with the medium shadow. Subtle: a tinted button with its label for a toolbar.

options.name: badge
options.description: Unread (a dot), Working (a ring) or Count(n).

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the user can activate the launcher.

options.name: showLabel
options.description: Shows the label beside the icon. null shows it for the subtle variant only.

options.name: closeIcon
options.description: Replaces icon on the solid variant while the assistant is open.

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the name "Assistant" (monarch_ailauncher_label).

options.name: badgeLabel
options.description: Replaces the spoken text of the badge.

options.name: openLabel
options.description: Replaces the spoken "Open" (monarch_ailauncher_open).

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the interactions of the button.

states.name: open
states.description: The solid variant shows closeIcon, when given, instead of icon; the subtle variant's border takes the solid assistant color.

states.name: pressed
states.description: The solid variant takes the active assistant fill and the subtle variant the hovered-subtle assistant fill.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The muted fill and the disabled text color; the click is ignored and the button is exposed as disabled.

states.name: unread
states.description: A dot in the solid danger color at the top end corner.

states.name: working
states.description: Half of the outline, in the thinking assistant color, travels around the button. With animations off the whole outline is drawn and still.

states.name: count
states.description: The number at the top end corner, "99+" above 99, nothing for zero or less.

appearance: Solid: the solid assistant fill with the on-solid assistant content color and the medium Monarch shadow. Subtle: the subtle assistant fill, the strong assistant content color and the assistant border. Badges use the solid danger fill. The same roles apply in light, dark and high contrast.
platformNotes: The parity map listed this entry as style (a themed FloatingActionButton with BadgedBox); it is built as a wrapper, as on iOS, because the open state, the spoken badge and the working ring are behavior the theme cannot give a plain FloatingActionButton. The web positions the launcher (bottom-end, bottom-start, inline) and moves it above other floating elements; on Android the app places it, usually in the floatingActionButton slot of a Scaffold, so there are no position or avoid parameters. The web's global Ctrl/Cmd+J shortcut is not offered: Compose has no window-wide key listener a component can own, so an app that wants it handles the key in onPreviewKeyEvent at the root of the screen and calls onOpenChange. Material 3 floating action buttons have no disabled state, so a disabled solid launcher ignores clicks and is marked disabled for TalkBack. The badge has no ring in the surface color as on the web.
accessibility: A button whose content description is "Assistant", or label.
Its state description is "Open" while open, followed by the badge: "New messages", "Working" or "3 unread messages", so nothing rests on the dot alone.
The icon and the badge are hidden from TalkBack as separate elements.
Both variants reserve a 48dp touch target.
The working ring stands still when the user has turned animations off.
The badge sits at the top end corner, which mirrors in right-to-left layouts.
edgeCases: The count text uses a plural resource for one and for more; languages with more forms are covered by the plural resource or badgeLabel.
The badge stands outside the button's corner; leave room around it.
The working ring is drawn 2dp outside the button and is not clipped by the component.

name: MonarchAiMarkdown
title: AiMarkdown
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.Text with AnnotatedString and androidx.compose.ui.text.LinkAnnotation.Url for inline content; androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column, Row and a custom androidx.compose.ui.layout.Layout for blocks and tables; androidx.compose.material3.Checkbox for task items; MonarchCodeBlock for code
summary: Renders GitHub-flavoured Markdown written by a model (headings, emphasis, links, lists, task lists, quotations, code, tables, rules and footnotes) as Compose text and layouts, never as HTML.
whenToUse: For the text of an assistant answer or any other model output that arrives as Markdown, including while it streams.
whenNotToUse: For content the app writes itself, use MonarchProse with its blocks. For a single code sample, use MonarchCodeBlock. For a table of data the app owns, use a data table component.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiMarkdown(text: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, streaming: Boolean = false, showLinkHosts: Boolean = true, onOpenLink: ((url: String) -> Unit)? = null, image: (@Composable (url: String, alt: String) -> Unit)? = null, codeBlock: (@Composable (language: String, code: String, complete: Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiMarkdownLabels = MonarchAiMarkdownLabels())
class MonarchAiMarkdownLabels(table: String? = null, footnotes: String? = null, task: String? = null, linkHost: ((host: String) -> String)? = null)

options.name: text
options.description: The Markdown source, treated as untrusted. While it grows, only the last block is parsed again.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the column.

options.name: streaming
options.description: The text is still arriving: an unclosed code block is incomplete, so MonarchCodeBlock hides its copy button and codeBlock receives complete = false.

options.name: showLinkHosts
options.description: Shows the host after a link whose text does not name it, such as "paypal.com (evil.test)".

options.name: onOpenLink
options.description: Opens links in the app instead of through the platform UriHandler. When given, relative links are links too.

options.name: image
options.description: Renders a paragraph that is only an image with an http or https source and alt text. Monarch loads no images; without it the alt text is shown.

options.name: codeBlock
options.type: (@Composable (language: String, code: String, complete: Boolean) -> Unit)?
options.description: Renders every code block instead of MonarchCodeBlock, for example a diagram for mermaid or typeset maths for math.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces "Table", "Footnotes", "Task" and the "(host)" text after links.

states.name: complete
states.description: Every block is rendered; footnotes are numbered by first reference and listed at the end under "Footnotes".

states.name: streaming
states.description: The last block is parsed again on every update; an unclosed code block renders as code without its copy button.

states.name: empty
states.description: An empty text renders nothing.

appearance: Small body text with relaxed leading in the default text color; headings are semibold at the large, base or small size for #, ## and ### and below. Links use the link color and are always underlined. Inline code uses the code face on the muted fill. Quotations have a bar in the default border color and muted text; list markers and struck-through text are muted. Tables have a subtle border, a subtle header fill and subtle row lines. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The parser is a port of the web parser (same block and inline rules, same incremental re-parse while streaming) and is internal: Android takes the text and keeps the parse state itself instead of exposing parseMarkdownBlocks and a blocks prop. Heading levels do not exist in Android semantics, so headingLevelOffset is not offered and the visual size follows the Markdown level as on the web. Links open through LinkAnnotation.Url (the platform UriHandler) or onOpenLink; there is no new-tab option. Protocol-relative links are never links, and relative links are links only when onOpenLink handles them, because a native app has no base URL. Images are off unless the app passes image, as the web's allowImages; the web's allowImageHosts and resolveImageUrl belong in the app's slot, and only a paragraph that is a single image is handed to it. Inline maths shows as inline code (the web's renderMath has no inline slot here); display maths reaches codeBlock with language math. Footnote references are superscript numbers and footnotes are listed at the end with a heading; there are no in-page anchors or back links on Android. The web's trailing slot (the streaming caret) is not offered. Tables scroll sideways inside their own border, and columns are capped at 240dp and wrap. There is no iOS equivalent yet.
accessibility: Each block is its own TalkBack element; headings have heading semantics.
Links are LinkAnnotation links that TalkBack lists and opens; they are always underlined, so they do not depend on color.
Unsafe links (javascript:, data:, other schemes, //host) keep their text but are not links.
Task items expose a checkbox role named "Task" with their checked state, and cannot be changed.
Ordered list numbers are read; bullets are decoration and hidden.
A table's scroll area is named "Table", and the grid gives TalkBack its row and column counts and each cell's position.
Rules are hidden from TalkBack.
edgeCases: Raw HTML such as <script> or <b> is shown as text.
A link whose text names a different site shows the real host after it, such as "paypal.com (evil.test)".
An unclosed code fence renders the rest of the text as code until the fence closes.
A footnote reference without a definition stays as "[^label]"; a definition that is never referenced is not listed.
A single $ is never maths, so prices stay text.
Long words and URLs wrap; wide tables and code scroll sideways in their own area.

examples.title: A full answer
examples.template: MonarchAiMarkdown(text = {{text}})
examples.code:
MonarchAiMarkdown(text = "# Release checklist

Here is what is left before the **Friday** release, based on the open tasks[^1].

1. Finish the migration review

name: MonarchAiMemoryChip
title: AiMemoryChip
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.AssistChip with androidx.compose.material3.DropdownMenu and androidx.compose.material3.AlertDialog; the row variant and the read-only chip are a Row with the Monarch surface
summary: One thing the assistant remembers, from a MonarchAiMemoryPart, shown as "Remembered: …" with a menu to edit or forget it.
whenToUse: Inside an assistant reply, to show a memory the assistant used, saved or forgot, and in a list of memories (the Row variant) where people review and correct what the assistant keeps.
whenNotToUse: For what the next prompt will see use MonarchAiContextChips. For a plain label on data use MonarchTag.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiMemoryChip(memory: MonarchAiMemoryPart, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchAiMemoryChipVariant = MonarchAiMemoryChipVariant.Chip, showScope: Boolean? = null, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiMemoryChipLabels = MonarchAiMemoryChipLabels(), onEdit: ((id: String, text: String) -> Unit)? = null, onForget: ((id: String) -> Unit)? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)
enum class MonarchAiMemoryChipVariant { Chip, Row }

class MonarchAiMemoryChipLabels(prefix: ((action: MonarchAiMemoryAction) -> String)? = null, options: String? = null, edit: String? = null, forget: String? = null, editTitle: String? = null, editField: String? = null, save: String? = null, cancel: String? = null)

options.name: memory
options.description: The memory from the conversation model: its id, action (Read, Write, Forget), text and scope.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the chip or the row.

options.name: variant
options.description: Chip: an inline pill in the AI colors with the prefix. Row: a full-width row without the prefix.

options.name: showScope
options.description: Whether the scope is shown under the text. By default on the chip and not on the row.

options.name: icon
options.description: An AI glyph at the start, tinted with the AI strong color. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces the prefixes, the tap action name, Edit, Forget and the edit dialog strings.

options.name: onEdit
options.description: Adds Edit. Receives the id and the trimmed new text; never called with empty or unchanged text.

options.name: onForget
options.description: Adds Forget. Runs at once, without confirmation.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the press, focus and hover interactions of the chip or the row.

states.name: read
states.description: Prefix "Used memory:".

states.name: write
states.description: Prefix "Remembered:".

states.name: forget
states.description: Prefix "Forgotten:" (also on the row), muted struck-through text and no commands.

states.name: read only
states.description: No callbacks: text only, not a button.

states.name: editable
states.description: Tapping opens a menu with Edit and Forget, as given; TalkBack offers both as actions.

states.name: editing
states.description: A dialog with a text field, Save and Cancel. Save is disabled while the text is empty or unchanged.

appearance: The chip is a pill with the AI subtle fill, the AI border and default text with a bold prefix; the icon uses the AI strong color. The row uses the surface fill and the subtle border. A forgotten memory uses the muted fill, muted text and the subtle border, with the text struck through. The menu uses the raised background; Forget is in the danger strong color.
platformNotes: Built on the shared MonarchAiMemoryPart, as on iOS: the web's entity becomes the part's scope and the prefix follows the part's action (the web always says "Remembered:"). The parity map names InputChip, but an InputChip is a selectable chip that TalkBack reads as checked or not checked; the chip opens a menu, so it is an AssistChip, which has the button role. The web's separate Edit and Forget buttons and the iOS menu button are a DropdownMenu opened by tapping the chip itself, because Monarch for Android bundles no menu glyph; both are also TalkBack custom actions. Editing happens in an AlertDialog with a multi-line field instead of inline, so there are no Enter and Escape shortcuts. The row shows "Forgotten:" for a forgotten memory so its state never depends on the strike-through. The web's leading and meta slots are not offered. Same names as iOS; iOS's options closure (a spoken name built from the text) is a plain tap action name here, because the chip's own text is its name.
accessibility: The prefix, the text and the scope are one TalkBack element.
An editable chip has the button role and a 48dp touch target; an editable row is a button at least 48dp high whose tap action is read as "show options".
Edit and Forget are TalkBack custom actions of the element as well as menu items.
A forgotten memory is struck through and also says "Forgotten:", so the state does not depend on the line.
The icon slot is decoration; the prefix says that the assistant kept the memory.
The edit field is labelled "Memory" and Save reports itself disabled while it cannot save.
edgeCases: Long text wraps; the chip grows in height.
An empty or white-space scope is never shown.
A forgotten memory offers no commands even when callbacks are given.
Saving text that only differs by spaces at the ends is treated as unchanged.
