summary: Everything the assistant remembers, grouped by the person, organization or project it is about, with search, edit, forget one, and select several to forget after a confirmation.
whenToUse: On a settings or privacy screen where people review and correct what the assistant keeps about them and their work.
whenNotToUse: For the memories a single reply used or saved, use MonarchAiMemoryChip in the message. For what the next prompt will see, use MonarchAiContextChips.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchAiMemoryPanel(memories: List<MonarchAiMemoryItem>, onEdit: (id: String, text: String) -> Unit, onForget: (id: String) -> Unit, onForgetMany: (ids: List<String>) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, locale: Locale? = null, timeZone: String? = null, state: LazyListState = rememberLazyListState(), contentPadding: PaddingValues = PaddingValues(), searchIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, clearIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiMemoryPanelLabels = MonarchAiMemoryPanelLabels())

data class MonarchAiMemoryItem(id: String, text: String, entity: MonarchAiMemoryEntity, updatedAt: Long) { companion object { fun apply(memories: List<MonarchAiMemoryItem>, event: MonarchAiMemoryPart, now: Long, defaultEntityName: String = "General", entity: ((MonarchAiMemoryPart) -> MonarchAiMemoryEntity)? = null): List<MonarchAiMemoryItem> } }
data class MonarchAiMemoryEntity(kind: MonarchAiMemoryEntityKind, name: String)
enum class MonarchAiMemoryEntityKind { Person, Organization, Project, Other }

class MonarchAiMemoryPanelLabels(search: String? = null, selectAll: ((shown: Int) -> String)? = null, selectGroup: ((name: String) -> String)? = null, select: ((text: String) -> String)? = null, kind: ((kind: MonarchAiMemoryEntityKind) -> String)? = null, count: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, updated: ((date: String) -> String)? = null, empty: String? = null, noMatches: ((query: String) -> String)? = null, matches: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, forget: String? = null, confirmTitle: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, confirmMessage: String? = null, cancel: String? = null, forgotten: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, edited: String? = null, chip: MonarchAiMemoryChipLabels = MonarchAiMemoryChipLabels(), bulkBar: MonarchBulkActionBarLabels = MonarchBulkActionBarLabels())

options.name: memories
options.description: Everything remembered: id, text, the entity it is about and when it was last updated (epoch milliseconds). The app's state: change it in the callbacks. MonarchAiMemoryItem.apply keeps it in step with a conversation's memory events.

options.name: onEdit
options.description: Saves an edited memory with the trimmed new text, from the row's Edit dialog.

options.name: onForget
options.description: Forgets one memory straight away, from the row's Forget.

options.name: onForgetMany
options.description: Forgets the selected memories after the person confirms in the dialog.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the panel. Give it a bounded height: the list is lazy.

options.name: locale
options.description: The locale for search, the order of names and dates. null uses the first locale of the configuration.

options.name: timeZone
options.description: The time zone of the updated dates. An IANA id such as Europe/Berlin; null, or an id the device does not know, is the device's zone.

options.name: state
options.description: The scroll state of the list.

options.name: contentPadding
options.description: The padding around the list content.

options.name: searchIcon
options.description: The search glyph at the start of the field. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: clearIcon
options.description: The glyph of the field's clear button; without it there is no clear button.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces every built-in string, the row strings (chip) and the bulk bar strings.

states.name: listing
states.description: The search field, the select-all row and one section per entity: people, then organizations, projects and other, each by name; newest memory first.

states.name: searching
states.description: Only memories whose text or entity name contains the search are shown; the count is announced after 300 ms.

states.name: selecting
states.description: Checked memories show MonarchBulkActionBar with the count and Forget; group and select-all checkboxes are indeterminate for a partial selection.

states.name: confirming
states.description: An AlertDialog asks "Forget 2 memories?" with Forget (danger) and Cancel.

states.name: empty
states.description: "Nothing is remembered yet." without the search or select-all row.

states.name: no matches
states.description: "No memories match “…”."

appearance: Group names in default semibold text with the kind and count in muted caption text; each memory is a MonarchAiMemoryChip row on the surface fill with its date in muted caption text. The bulk bar and the dialog use their own appearance. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: A product pattern, experimental until a Rook app adopts it. On a phone the web's toolbar (search, select-all checkbox and a Forget selected button) becomes the search field and a select-all row at the top of the list, and the bulk action is MonarchBulkActionBar under the list, as Android selection screens do. Each row reuses MonarchAiMemoryChip's Row variant, so Edit and Forget are in the menu opened by tapping the memory (and are TalkBack actions) rather than separate buttons; the date is a line under the row because the chip has no meta slot. The web's AiMemoryItem.entity kind org is Organization here. The web's onForgetMany may return a promise that keeps the dialog pending; here the dialog closes on confirm and the app updates memories. The web moves focus to the next row after a forget; Android leaves focus to the system. The web's headingLevel is not offered (no heading levels in Android semantics). There is no iOS equivalent yet.
accessibility: Group names are headings; each group checkbox is named "Select all memories about {name}" and is tri-state.
The select-all row is one tri-state checkbox element named by its text, "Select all (3)", with a 48dp height.
Each memory's checkbox is named "Select memory: {text}" with the text shortened to 48 characters, with a 48dp touch target.
Each memory row is a button whose menu offers Edit and Forget, also as TalkBack actions.
Search results, "Memory updated" and "2 memories forgotten" are announced from a polite live region that is always present; nothing is announced on first show.
Forgetting several always asks first in a dialog; the confirm button is the danger MonarchButton.
edgeCases: Selected ids of memories that no longer exist are dropped from the count and from onForgetMany.
Memories with the same entity kind and name are one group.
A long memory wraps in its row; its checkbox name is shortened.
Search ignores case and spaces around the query.

summary: The @ context menu of an AI prompt: documents, people, records and apps that can be added to what the AI sees, grouped by kind, with token estimates and loading, empty and error states.
whenToUse: Above an AI prompt field, while the person types @ to add a document, person, record or app to the conversation's context; the chosen result becomes a MonarchAiContextChips chip.
whenNotToUse: To mention people or channels in a message to other people, use MonarchMentionPicker. For slash commands, use MonarchSlashMenu.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiMentionContext(query: MonarchMentionQuery?, items: List<MonarchAiMentionItem>, onSelect: (MonarchAiMentionItem) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, status: MonarchMentionPickerStatus = MonarchMentionPickerStatus.Ready, onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null, kindIcon: (@Composable (MonarchAiMentionKind) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiMentionContextLabels = MonarchAiMentionContextLabels())

data class MonarchAiMentionItem(id: String, kind: MonarchAiMentionKind, label: String, description: String? = null, tokens: Int? = null, image: Painter? = null, enabled: Boolean = true) { val contextItem: MonarchAiContextItem }
enum class MonarchAiMentionKind { Doc, Person, Record, App; val contextKind: MonarchAiContextKind }

class MonarchAiMentionContextLabels(label: String? = null, group: ((MonarchAiMentionKind) -> String)? = null, loading: String? = null, empty: ((query: String) -> String)? = null, error: String? = null, retry: String? = null, tokens: ((formatted: String, count: Int) -> String)? = null, count: ((Int) -> String)? = null)

options.name: query
options.description: The @ query found with MonarchMentionQuery.find. Nothing is drawn while it is null.

options.name: items
options.description: The results of the product's search, without ids already in the context.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Receives the chosen result. Add item.contextItem to the context and remove the query from the prompt.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the strip.

options.name: status
options.description: Loading shows placeholder rows, Failed an error, Ready the results or the empty text.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Repeats a failed search; adds a Retry button.

options.name: kindIcon
options.description: A decorative icon for documents, records and apps; without it a tinted tile with the first letter.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

states.name: results
states.description: Rows with an avatar or tile, the label, the description and the token estimate; headings when more than one kind is present.

states.name: searching
states.description: Three placeholder rows read as Searching….

states.name: empty
states.description: "Type to search" for an empty query, else "Nothing matches “q3”".

states.name: failed
states.description: "Couldn’t load results.", with Retry when onRetry is given.

states.name: disabled result
states.description: Disabled text color; the row cannot be chosen.

states.name: closed
states.description: Nothing is drawn while query is null, or after a query with a space found nothing.

appearance: A strip on the surface color with a subtle top border; labels in default text, descriptions, token estimates and headings in muted text, disabled results in the disabled text color. All are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web is a listbox under the caret driven by aria-activedescendant and a useAiMentionContext hook that wires it into the prompt input. Compose gives no caret rectangle, so this is a strip above the keyboard (the layout of MonarchMentionPicker) and results are buttons; the app finds the query with MonarchMentionQuery and searches in a LaunchedEffect keyed by it. There is no highlighted result or arrow-key navigation, and no hook. The status reuses MonarchMentionPickerStatus (Loading, Ready, Failed) where the web has idle, loading, ready and error. The parity map called it a mention picker preset; MonarchMentionPicker's items are people and channels only, so this component has its own item type and reuses the picker's query and open rule. aiMentionToContextChip is the contextItem property. Monarch bundles no icons, so kind icons are a slot. Same names and parameters as iOS, with the query as a named parameter. Experimental: an AI product composite that waits for a Rook app to adopt it.
accessibility: Each result is a button read as its label, description and token estimate ("Q3 report.pdf, Finance, 12.4K tokens"), built by a tested pure function; a disabled result is reported disabled.
The strip is a traversal group named "Add context" whose state description is Searching…, the number of results, the empty text or the error, in a polite live region, so focus stays in the prompt.
Group names are headings when more than one kind is present.
Rows are at least 48dp high and grow with the font size; avatars and icons are decorative.
edgeCases: A query with a space that finds nothing closes the strip: it is ordinary prose.
A negative token estimate reads as 0 tokens.
The order within a kind is kept; kinds follow Documents, People, Records, Apps.
The list scrolls after about four rows.

summary: One chat message: its text, reasoning, tool calls, sources, citations, files, memories, plans, artifacts, generated UI, edit proposals and errors in the order the model produced them, with the layout of its role, the time, the version switcher and the action row.
whenToUse: For each message of a conversation driven by MonarchAiConversation, in the app's LazyColumn of messages, so every part type gets the matching Monarch component.
whenNotToUse: For a single answer outside a conversation use MonarchAiStreamingText or MonarchAiStructuredAnswer; for a whole thread with its input use the conversation components around a LazyColumn of these messages.

options.name: message
options.description: The message: role, ordered parts, creation time, agent, feedback, branch, finish reason and queued flag.

options.name: agent
options.description: The agent shown when the message has none of its own.

options.name: agentImage
options.description: The agent's picture, loaded by the app; the avatar shows agentIcon or initials meanwhile.

options.name: announces
options.description: Whether streamed text and errors announce themselves; pass false when the thread has one announcer.

options.name: showTimestamp
options.description: Shows the time the message was created: in the header of an assistant message, in the footer otherwise.

options.name: timeZone
options.description: IANA zone of the time; null is the device's zone.

options.name: is24Hour
options.description: 24-hour clock; null follows the device setting.

options.name: showActions
options.description: Shows the action row; it is hidden while the message streams, is edited or is queued.

options.name: copyable
options.description: Shows Copy (the web's onCopy={false} hides it).

options.name: editing
options.description: Shows MonarchAiUserMessageEdit in place of the person's bubble.

options.name: speaking
options.description: Whether the app is reading the message aloud; Read aloud then reads Stop reading.

options.name: onCopy
options.description: Called with the text after Copy has put it on the clipboard.

options.name: onRegenerate / onFeedback / onReadAloud
options.description: Show Regenerate, the thumbs and Read aloud on an assistant message.

options.name: onEdit
options.description: Shows Edit on the person's message.

options.name: onShare
options.description: Shows Share.

options.name: onBranch
options.description: Switches versions; the switcher shows when the message has more than one version and both version icons are given.

options.name: onRetry / onResume
options.description: Try again on a retryable error part, Resume on a resumable one.

options.name: onCancelQueued
options.description: Shows Cancel on a queued message of the person.

options.name: onForgetMemory / onEditMemory
options.description: Forget and Edit on a memory the reply saved.

options.name: onApproveTool / onDenyTool
options.description: With either, a tool call waiting for approval shows as MonarchAiToolApproval.

options.name: onAlwaysAllowTool
options.description: Offers Always allow on the approval card.

options.name: onEditSubmit / onEditCancel
options.description: Save or cancel the edit of the person's message.

options.name: onOpenArtifact
options.description: Shows artifact parts as MonarchAiArtifactCard; without it they show nothing.

options.name: onOpenFile
options.description: Makes file chips open the file.

options.name: onOpenSource
options.description: Opens a source from the list or a citation.

options.name: onOpenLink
options.description: Opens a link in the text; null opens it with the system.

options.name: uiRegistry / onUiAction
options.description: Shows ui parts with MonarchAiGenerativeUi from this allow-list; without it ui parts show nothing.

options.name: editHunks
options.description: Turns an edit proposal into hunks for a read-only MonarchAiEditProposal; null shows nothing.

options.name: renderPart
options.description: Returns content for a part, {} for nothing, or null to keep the default component.

options.name: agentIcon
options.description: The avatar's icon while there is no picture.

options.name: actionIcon / moreIcon
options.description: Glyphs of the action row; without them the actions show as text.

options.name: previousVersionIcon / nextVersionIcon
options.description: Icons of the version switcher, required for it to show.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings and the labels of each part component.

options.name: moreActions
options.description: Items of the menu of further actions.

states.name: assistant
states.description: A header with the avatar, the agent's name, role and time, then the parts at full width and the action row.

states.name: person
states.description: The parts in an end-aligned bubble on the muted background, at most 85% of the width; time and actions under it.

states.name: system or tool
states.description: The parts at full width without a header.

states.name: streaming
states.description: Text shows a caret and announces new sentences; the action row is hidden and the version switcher disabled.

states.name: finished short
states.description: A Length, ContentFilter or Refusal finish reason adds a warning-coloured notice under a finished reply.

states.name: queued
states.description: The note Queued. It will send when you are back online. with Cancel; no action row.

states.name: editing
states.description: MonarchAiUserMessageEdit replaces the bubble.

states.name: tool approval
states.description: A tool call waiting for approval shows Approve and Deny when the app handles them.

states.name: error
states.description: An error part shows MonarchAiErrorMessage with Try again and Resume when allowed.

appearance: The person's bubble uses the muted background with the default text color and the extra-large radius; the agent's role, the time and the queued note use the muted text color; the finish notice uses the warning strong color. Each part takes the colors of its own component, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow the theme roles.
platformNotes: The web's AiMessageView is memoised and hides the action row until hover; on Android the row is always visible under a finished message and Compose skips unchanged messages when the app keys its LazyColumn items by message id. Callbacks do not receive the message, because the caller has it in scope. The web's onCopy={false} is copyable = false; Monarch copies with MonarchCopyButton. The avatar picture is a Painter the app loads (no URL loading). The version switcher needs app-supplied icons because Monarch bundles none. The web announces an error part only the first time it mounts; here announces controls it, so a thread that re-shows old messages should pass false. The web renders a tool call as a compact row; Android uses MonarchAiToolCall, which can expand to show input and output. iOS has no MonarchAiMessage view yet; the name follows the iOS model note that reserves it for the message view.
accessibility: TalkBack reads You said:, Assistant said: or System message: on the message before its parts.
The avatar is decorative; the agent's name is text in the header.
Copy, Edit, the version buttons and Resume have 48dp touch targets.
Citations are named Source n: title.
The finish notice and the queued note are text, not only color.
Streamed text announces new sentences politely and the last text part announces Response complete once the reply, including its tool calls, is done; announces = false turns this off.
edgeCases: Artifact, ui and edit-proposal parts show nothing until the app gives onOpenArtifact, uiRegistry or editHunks.
Several source parts show one source list, at the first source.
A citation whose source is not in the message shows nothing.
Without both version icons and onBranch the switcher is left out.
Long text wraps inside the bubble; the bubble never grows beyond 85% of the width.
The message does not scroll; put it in the app's LazyColumn.

examples.title: Assistant answer with reasoning, tool, sources and file
examples.webExample: Assistant answer with reasoning, tool, sources and file
examples.template:
CompositionLocalProvider(LocalConfiguration provides locale) {
    @OptIn(ExperimentalMonarchApi::class)
    MonarchAiMessage(
        message = MonarchAiConversationMessage(
            id = "a1",
            role = MonarchAiRole.Assistant,
            parts = listOf(
                MonarchAiReasoningPart({{reasoning.text}}, durationMs = {{reasoning.durationMs}}),
                MonarchAiToolCallPart(
                    id = {{tool.id}},
                    name = {{tool.name}},
                    input = MonarchAiJSON.Object(mapOf("query" to MonarchAiJSON.Text({{tool.query}}))),
                    state = MonarchAiToolCallState.Succeeded,
                    startedAt = {{tool.startedAt}},
                    endedAt = {{tool.endedAt}},
                ),
                MonarchAiTextPart({{answer}}),
                MonarchAiSourcePart({{source.id}}, {{source.title}}, url = {{source.url}}, kind = MonarchAiSourceKind.{{source.kind|pascal}}),
                MonarchAiCitationPart({{citation.id}}, {{citation.sourceId}}),
                MonarchAiFilePart({{file.name}}, {{file.mediaType}}, size = {{file.size}}),
            ),
            createdAt = {{createdAt}},
            agent = MonarchAiAgentRef({{agent.name}}, role = {{agent.role}}),
            branch = MonarchAiBranchPosition(index = {{branch.index}}, count = {{branch.count}}),
            feedback = feedback,
        ),
        onRegenerate = {},
        onFeedback = { feedback = it },
        onBranch = {},
    )
}

parityExceptions.reason: The web example is a 614px page with 24px targets: the number of the source, the citation chip, the file chip and the icon buttons sit close under each other. Android asks every control for a 48dp touch target, so the numbered source link, the citation chip and the action buttons keep a 48dp box and the rhythm between them is looser than on the web. The order, the data, the copy and the icons are the web's.
parityExceptions.convention: Material touch target of 48dp for every control

name: MonarchAiMessageActions
title: AiMessageActions
wrapsNative: MonarchIconButton, androidx.compose.material3.IconToggleButton and androidx.compose.material3.TooltipBox with PlainTooltip (with icons), or MonarchButton and MonarchChip (without), MonarchCopyButton and MonarchMenu, in an androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow
summary: The action row under a chat message: copy, regenerate, edit, rate, share, read aloud and a menu of further actions.
whenToUse: Under each assistant answer (copy, regenerate, rate, share, read aloud) and under a person's own message (copy, edit) in a conversation.
whenNotToUse: For rating with reasons and a comment use MonarchAiFeedback; for actions on a whole conversation use a TopAppBar menu; for one copy button use MonarchCopyButton.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiMessageActions(messageText: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, onCopy: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, onRegenerate: (() -> Unit)? = null, onEdit: (() -> Unit)? = null, feedback: MonarchAiMessageFeedback? = null, onFeedback: ((MonarchAiMessageFeedback?) -> Unit)? = null, onShare: (() -> Unit)? = null, speaking: Boolean = false, onReadAloud: ((speaking: Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, enabled: Boolean = true, icon: (@Composable (action: MonarchAiMessageAction, active: Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, moreIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiMessageActionsLabels = MonarchAiMessageActionsLabels(), more: (@Composable ColumnScope.(close: () -> Unit) -> Unit)? = null)
enum class MonarchAiMessageAction { Copy, Regenerate, Edit, Good, Bad, Share, ReadAloud, More }

class MonarchAiMessageActionsLabels(toolbar: String? = null, copy: String? = null, copied: String? = null, regenerate: String? = null, edit: String? = null, good: String? = null, bad: String? = null, share: String? = null, readAloud: String? = null, stopReading: String? = null, more: String? = null)

options.name: messageText
options.description: The message's plain text: what Copy copies and what the app reads aloud.

options.name: onCopy
options.description: Shows Copy (a MonarchCopyButton); called with the text after it is on the clipboard.

options.name: onRegenerate
options.description: Shows Regenerate.

options.name: onEdit
options.description: Shows Edit, for the person's own messages.

options.name: feedback
options.description: The current rating, shown as a pressed thumb.

options.name: onFeedback
options.description: Shows thumbs up and down; called with the new rating, or null when the pressed thumb is pressed again.

options.name: onShare
options.description: Shows Share; start Intent.ACTION_SEND with Intent.createChooser here.

options.name: speaking
options.description: Whether the app is reading the message aloud; the button then reads Stop reading.

options.name: onReadAloud
options.description: Shows Read aloud; called with true to start and false to stop. The app owns TextToSpeech.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the actions can be used, for example false while the answer streams.

options.name: icon
options.description: The glyph of each action, given whether it is active (copied, pressed or speaking). Null shows the actions as text.

options.name: moreIcon
options.description: The glyph of the More actions button; null shows it as text.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

options.name: more
options.description: The items of the menu of further actions, for example DropdownMenuItems; null hides the More actions button.

states.name: rated
states.description: The chosen thumb is on (a checked toggle, or a selected chip) and its glyph uses the AI strong color.

states.name: copied
states.description: Copy shows Copied and the copied glyph where the system shows no clipboard confirmation (below Android 13); the copy is announced.

states.name: speaking
states.description: Read aloud becomes Stop reading and its glyph is given as active.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Every action is disabled and uses the disabled text color.

states.name: menu open
states.description: A MonarchMenu with the app's items.

appearance: Icon buttons without a container in the muted text color; a pressed thumb uses the AI strong color, disabled actions the disabled text color. Without icons, ghost Monarch buttons and Material 3 filter chips in the theme. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web shows the row on hover with pointer devices and as one tab stop with arrow keys; on Android the row is always visible and each action is its own TalkBack element. The web speaks with speechSynthesis itself; Android leaves TextToSpeech to the app (it needs an engine, initialisation and a lifecycle), which passes speaking and starts or stops speech in onReadAloud. Share is a callback so the app chooses what to send through Intent.ACTION_SEND. Web tooltips on hover become Material 3 plain tooltips on long press. Monarch bundles no icons, so icons are a slot and every action can also be shown as text. The thumbs use the same Material 3 controls as MonarchAiFeedback (IconToggleButton or MonarchChip); for reasons and a comment after a rating, show MonarchAiFeedback instead of onFeedback. The web's more slot is a menu here: moreIcon and more open a MonarchMenu. iOS has no entry yet.
accessibility: The row is a traversal group named "Message actions".
Each icon button is named for TalkBack ("Regenerate", "Share") and has a 48dp target; the glyph is hidden.
The thumbs are toggles that report on and off; as chips they report selected.
Long-pressing an icon button shows its name in a plain tooltip, so the meaning never rests on the glyph.
Copy announces the copy through MonarchCopyButton's polite live region.
Read aloud changes its name to "Stop reading" while speaking.
Text actions wrap onto more rows at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: With no callbacks the row is empty.
Pressing the pressed thumb again clears the rating (onFeedback(null)).
Copy copies messageText as given; strip markdown before passing it if the answer is formatted.
Keep enabled false while the answer streams so Copy and Read aloud do not act on partial text.

name: MonarchAiMessageBranch
title: AiMessageBranch
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.IconButton, androidx.compose.material3.Text in a androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row
summary: The previous, position, next switcher between versions of a message, made when a reply is regenerated or a prompt is edited and resent.
whenToUse: Under a message that has more than one version.
whenNotToUse: For pages of a list use a pager or a pagination control. For a choice between named options use a segmented button.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiMessageBranch(selection: Int, count: Int, onSelectionChange: (Int) -> Unit, previousIcon: @Composable () -> Unit, nextIcon: @Composable () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, showSingle: Boolean = false, label: String? = null, previousLabel: String? = null, nextLabel: String? = null, formatPosition: ((Int, Int) -> String)? = null, formatAnnouncement: ((Int, Int) -> String)? = null)

options.name: selection
options.description: The version shown, counted from 0.

options.name: count
options.description: How many versions exist. Below 1 is treated as 1.

options.name: onSelectionChange
options.description: Called with the version to show, counted from 0.

options.name: previousIcon
options.description: The icon of the previous button, a chevron to the start. Monarch bundles no icons; use MonarchIcon with mirrorInRtl = true.

options.name: nextIcon
options.description: The icon of the next button, a chevron to the end.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the switcher.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the buttons can be used, for example false while a reply streams.

options.name: showSingle
options.description: Shows the switcher when there is only one version.

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the TalkBack name "Versions" (monarch_aimessagebranch_label).

options.name: previousLabel
options.description: Replaces "Previous version" (monarch_aimessagebranch_previous).

options.name: nextLabel
options.description: Replaces "Next version" (monarch_aimessagebranch_next).

options.name: formatPosition
options.description: The visible position from the version, counted from 1, and the count. Built in: "2 / 3" (monarch_aimessagebranch_position).

options.name: formatAnnouncement
options.description: The position as TalkBack reads it. Built in: "Version 2 of 3" (monarch_aimessagebranch_announcement).

states.name: first version
states.description: The previous button is disabled.

states.name: last version
states.description: The next button is disabled.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Both buttons are disabled and the position uses the disabled text color.

states.name: hidden
states.description: With fewer than two versions nothing is shown, unless showSingle is true.

appearance: The position uses the caption type in the muted text color and the buttons the muted text color; disabled parts use the disabled text color, in every theme.
platformNotes: The web takes index and onChange and iOS a Binding; Android takes selection and onSelectionChange, the Compose convention. The chevrons are slots because Monarch bundles no icons; the web draws its own. The group label is the content description of the row, a TalkBack stop of its own. As on the web, when the button that had keyboard focus becomes disabled at an end, focus moves to the other button.
accessibility: The row is a traversal group with the content description "Versions".
The buttons are Material 3 icon buttons named "Previous version" and "Next version", each with a 48dp touch target.
The position shows "2 / 3" and TalkBack reads it as "Version 2 of 3".
After a button changes the version, the position is a polite live region, so the new position is announced; a change made by the app is not announced.
Previous comes before next in reading order in both layout directions.
edgeCases: A selection outside the range shows the nearest version; a step then starts from the version shown.
Large counts widen the position; it does not wrap and the buttons keep their size.
The icons must mirror themselves in right-to-left layouts; the component does not flip them.

name: MonarchAiModeSwitcher
title: AiModeSwitcher
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow, androidx.compose.material3.SegmentedButton
summary: Switches how the assistant works (Ask, Edit, Agent by default) with the selected mode's description underneath, so the consequence of the choice is always visible.
whenToUse: In a prompt toolbar or an assistant panel, when the assistant can work in two to five modes that change what it may do.
whenNotToUse: For views or filters of the same content use the Material 3 segmented buttons on their own (SegmentedControl). For more than five modes or long descriptions use MonarchRadioCardGroup. For the writing tone use MonarchAiTonePicker.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiModeSwitcher(selection: String, onSelectionChange: (String) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, modes: List<MonarchAiMode> = MonarchAiMode.defaults(), size: MonarchAiModeSwitcherSize = MonarchAiModeSwitcherSize.Sm, enabled: Boolean = true, showDescription: Boolean = true, label: String? = null)
class MonarchAiMode(id: String, label: String, description: String? = null, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, iconOnly: Boolean = false, enabled: Boolean = true)
@Composable fun MonarchAiMode.Companion.defaults(): List<MonarchAiMode>
enum class MonarchAiModeSwitcherSize { Sm, Md }

options.name: selection
options.description: The id of the selected mode. An id that matches no mode selects nothing.

options.name: onSelectionChange
options.description: Called with the id of the mode the user chose. Never called for a disabled mode or the mode already selected.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the switcher.

options.name: modes
options.description: The modes, two to five: each with an id, a label, an optional description, an optional decorative icon, iconOnly and enabled. The defaults are Ask, Edit and Agent (ids ask, edit, agent) with built-in descriptions.

options.name: size
options.description: Sm: the label type and tighter padding, for a prompt toolbar. Md: the body type and the Material 3 padding.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the user can change the mode, for example false while a response runs.

options.name: showDescription
options.description: Whether the selected mode's description is shown under the control. Turn it off when it is shown elsewhere.

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the TalkBack name of the choice, "Mode" (monarch_aimodeswitcher_label).

states.name: selected
states.description: The selected segment takes the Material 3 selected fill from MonarchTheme and the check mark; its description is shown underneath.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Every segment is disabled and the description uses the disabled text color.

states.name: mode disabled
states.description: That segment is disabled and choosing it does not change the selection.

states.name: no description
states.description: When no mode has a description, or showDescription is false, there is no description line.

appearance: The Material 3 segmented buttons as MonarchTheme colors them, full width, with the description in the caption type and the muted text color underneath. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web builds on Monarch's SegmentedControl and iOS on the system segmented Picker; Android uses the Material 3 single-choice segmented buttons, which show a check mark on the selected segment. A mode's icon is a composable slot (iOS takes an SF Symbol name) and shows before the label on segments that are not selected, because Material 3 puts the check mark in that place on the selected one. The built-in Ask, Edit and Agent modes match iOS; the web has no defaults. Disabling the whole switcher is the enabled parameter. The description is a polite live region, where iOS posts an announcement.
accessibility: The segments are radio buttons in a selectable group with the content description "Mode", replaceable with label; TalkBack reads each one's position and selected state.
Each segment has a 48dp touch target, from Material 3.
The selected segment shows a check mark as well as its fill, so the choice does not rest on color.
The description line is a polite live region, so TalkBack reads the new mode's description after a switch.
An icon-only segment is read as the mode's label; other icons are decorative and hidden from TalkBack.
Segment labels and the description wrap at large font sizes.
edgeCases: A selection that matches no mode leaves no segment selected and shows an empty description line.
A mode with no description shows an empty line while another mode has one, so the layout does not jump.
With more than five modes the segments become too narrow for their labels; use a radio card group instead.

name: MonarchAiModelPicker
title: AiModelPicker
wrapsNative: MonarchButton that opens an androidx.compose.material3.ModalBottomSheet holding an androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn of selectable rows with an androidx.compose.material3.RadioButton mark, provider headings and MonarchBadges
summary: A button showing the current AI model that opens a sheet of models grouped by provider, with capabilities, context size, speed, cost and the state of the provider key.
whenToUse: When people may choose which model answers, for example in a prompt toolbar or a conversation's settings.
whenNotToUse: For a short list of plain choices without details use MonarchSelect. For the assistant's mode (chat, research, agent) use MonarchAiModeSwitcher.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchAiModelPicker(selection: String?, models: List<MonarchAiModelOption>, onSelectionChange: (String) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, size: MonarchButtonSize = MonarchButtonSize.Md, enabled: Boolean = true, trailingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiModelPickerLabels = MonarchAiModelPickerLabels(), interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null, onConfigureKey: ((MonarchAiModelOption) -> Unit)? = null)

public class MonarchAiModelOption(id: String, provider: String, name: String, description: String? = null, capabilities: List<MonarchAiModelCapability> = emptyList(), contextTokens: Long? = null, speed: MonarchAiModelSpeed? = null, costTier: Int? = null, requiresKey: Boolean = false, keyConfigured: Boolean = false, enabled: Boolean = true)
public enum class MonarchAiModelCapability { Vision, Tools, Reasoning, Web }
public enum class MonarchAiModelSpeed { Fast, Balanced, Slow }

public class MonarchAiModelPickerLabels(label: String? = null, placeholder: String? = null, capability: ((MonarchAiModelCapability) -> String?)? = null, context: ((formatted: String) -> String)? = null, speed: ((MonarchAiModelSpeed) -> String?)? = null, cost: ((tier: Int) -> String)? = null, ownKey: String? = null, keyNeeded: String? = null, addKeyHint: String? = null, unavailable: String? = null, done: String? = null)

options.name: selection
options.description: The id of the selected model, null for none.

options.name: models
options.description: The models in display order, grouped by provider in first-seen order.

options.name: onSelectionChange
options.description: Called with the id of the chosen model; the sheet closes.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the button.

options.name: size
options.description: The height and padding of the button.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the button opens the sheet.

options.name: trailingIcon
options.description: An icon at the end of the button, such as a chevron. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the button's interactions.

options.name: onConfigureKey
options.description: Runs when a model whose key is missing is chosen, to add the key. Without it such models cannot be chosen.

states.name: placeholder
states.description: No model selected, or an unknown id: the button reads "Choose a model" in muted text.

states.name: selected
states.description: The button shows the model and its provider; in the sheet the row's radio mark is on and the row is selected.

states.name: your key
states.description: A model on a configured workspace key shows a success "Your key" badge.

states.name: key needed
states.description: A model whose key is missing shows a warning "Key needed" badge; choosing it calls onConfigureKey.

states.name: unavailable
states.description: A disabled model, or one whose key cannot be added, uses the disabled text role and cannot be chosen.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The button uses the disabled colors and does not open.

appearance: The button is the secondary MonarchButton with the name in default text and the provider in muted text. The sheet is on the surface color: names in strong body text, details muted captions, capabilities info badges, key badges success or warning, the radio mark in the strong accent role; unavailable rows use the disabled text role. Every color is a theme role, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: Same parameters as iOS: selection becomes a value with onSelectionChange in place of a Binding, isKeyConfigured is keyConfigured, and isDisabled is enabled (true by default) as in MonarchSelectOption and Material 3. The web opens a popover listbox with arrow-key navigation and typeahead; Android, like iOS, opens a list in a Material 3 ModalBottomSheet, because a DropdownMenu cannot show badges and several lines per model. The selected model has a RadioButton mark where iOS has a check mark. The web's controlled open state is not offered; the button owns the sheet. Monarch bundles no icons, so the web's chevron and lock are a trailingIcon slot or left out; key state is always a word in a badge. The composable is experimental: an AI pattern that waits for a Rook app to adopt it.
accessibility: The button is named "Model" and its state is the selected model and provider, or "Choose a model".
The sheet has the heading "Model" and each provider is a heading.
Each model is one row with the radio button role, read as its name, key badge, description, capabilities, context and speed, with the cost in words ("Cost: high"), never the dollar signs.
The selected model is selected and shows a filled radio mark, so selection is not color alone.
A model whose key is missing reads "Select to add an API key."; one that cannot be chosen is disabled and reads "Unavailable".
Rows and Done have 48dp touch targets; text wraps at large font sizes.
edgeCases: A selection id that matches no model shows the placeholder.
Without onConfigureKey a model needing a key is shown but disabled.
Context sizes are compact in the current locale with at most one decimal: 32 768 tokens is "32.8K".
A cost tier outside 1 to 3 is clamped.
Empty models give a sheet with only the heading and Done.

name: MonarchAiMultiAgentRoster
title: AiMultiAgentRoster
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of MonarchAiAgentAvatar rows, or MonarchAvatarGroup in androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow for the stack
summary: Every agent taking part in a task and what each is doing now, as a list of rows or a compact stack of pictures.
whenToUse: When several AI agents work on one task and people need to see who is working, who waits for them and who failed: in a task screen (list) or a header (stack).
whenNotToUse: For one agent use MonarchAiAgentAvatar with showState. For the people present in a document use MonarchPresenceAvatars. For a shared conversation with people and agents use MonarchAiSharedSession.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchAiMultiAgentRoster(members: List<MonarchAiMultiAgentRosterMember>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchAiMultiAgentRosterVariant = MonarchAiMultiAgentRosterVariant.List, maxVisible: Int = 4, showSummary: Boolean = true, announcesChanges: Boolean = true, labels: MonarchAiMultiAgentRosterLabels = MonarchAiMultiAgentRosterLabels())
class MonarchAiMultiAgentRosterMember(agent: MonarchAiAgentRef, state: MonarchAiAgentState = MonarchAiAgentState.Idle, task: String? = null, image: Painter? = null) { val id: String }
enum class MonarchAiMultiAgentRosterVariant { List, Stack }

class MonarchAiMultiAgentRosterLabels(label: String? = null, agentKind: String? = null, state: ((MonarchAiAgentState) -> String)? = null, summary: ((total: Int, counts: Map<MonarchAiAgentState, Int>) -> String)? = null, changed: ((name: String, state: String) -> String)? = null, empty: String? = null)

options.name: members
options.description: The agents, each with a state, an optional task and an optional picture. Keep agent ids stable between updates.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the roster.

options.name: variant
options.description: List: a row per agent. Stack: overlapping pictures beside the summary.

options.name: maxVisible
options.description: In the stack, the pictures shown before "+N". At least one is shown; with exactly one too many, all are shown.

options.name: showSummary
options.description: Shows the "3 agents · 2 working" line.

options.name: announcesChanges
options.description: Announces state changes to TalkBack. Never the first state.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the list name, "AI agent", the state names, the summary, the change announcement and the empty text.

states.name: idle
states.description: No ring; the state text is muted.

states.name: working
states.description: The avatar's turning ring (still when animations are removed); the state text uses the strong AI color.

states.name: waiting
states.description: The row is tinted with the subtle warning color and the state text is strong warning; second in the stack.

states.name: error
states.description: The row is tinted with the subtle danger color and the state text is strong danger; first in the stack.

states.name: empty
states.description: "No agents are working on this." in muted text, without a summary.

appearance: Rows are transparent, or tinted with the subtle warning or danger role; names use the default text role, roles, tasks and the summary the muted role; the state text uses the muted, strong AI, strong warning or strong danger role. The stack is MonarchAvatarGroup with square agent avatars. All colors are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web's task is any node; here it is a String, and each member may carry a Painter picture. The web uses a polite live region; so does Android, on an always-present node. The stack reuses MonarchAvatarGroup, so a "+1" tile is never shown: with one agent too many all are shown, as on iOS. When the stack and the summary do not fit on one line, the summary wraps under the pictures (FlowRow). The parity map listed presence-avatars and status-badge; as on iOS, the stack is the avatar group that presence-avatars builds on, and the state is plain coloured text as on the web, so neither is used directly. The list is a Column, not a lazy list, so it can sit inside a scrolling screen. Marked experimental because it is a domain composite that no Rook app has adopted yet.
accessibility: The list is a traversal group named "Agents".
A list row is one TalkBack element read as the name with "(AI agent)", the role, the task and the state; the picture is not read because the text says the same.
In the stack each picture is read by MonarchAiAgentAvatar as the name, "AI agent" and its state; "+N" reads every hidden agent with its state.
Every state is written text as well as a ring and a tint, so it never depends on color or motion.

A state change is announced through a polite live region, for example "Research agent: Error"; several changes are joined. The first state is not announced, and announcesChanges false turns announcements off.
Names, roles and tasks wrap at font scale 2.0; the state stays on one line at the end of the row.
edgeCases: Members without an id are matched by name; two agents with the same name and no id are treated as one for announcements.
An agent that joins counts as a change and is announced.
maxVisible below 1 shows one picture.
Blank roles and tasks are left out.

name: MonarchAiOnboardingTour
title: AiOnboardingTour
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.pager.HorizontalPager of steps with MonarchStepper and MonarchButton, presented by the app in MonarchBottomSheet or inline
summary: A short, step-by-step introduction to AI in a product (what it can see, what it can do, how to turn it off) with Back, Next and Turn off AI on every step.
whenToUse: The first time someone meets an AI feature, to explain in a few steps what it sees, what it does and how to turn it off, before they rely on it.
whenNotToUse: For a one-line note about AI use MonarchAiDisclaimer. For a general product walkthrough that is not about AI use a pager of your own or MonarchStepper. To point at one control, use a Material 3 tooltip.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiOnboardingTour(steps: List<MonarchAiOnboardingTourStep>, step: Int, onStepChange: (Int) -> Unit, onDisable: () -> Unit, onFinish: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, skipIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiOnboardingTourLabels = MonarchAiOnboardingTourLabels(), onSkip: (() -> Unit)? = null)

@Composable fun MonarchAiOnboardingTour(steps: List<MonarchAiOnboardingTourStep>, onDisable: () -> Unit, onFinish: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, skipIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiOnboardingTourLabels = MonarchAiOnboardingTourLabels(), onSkip: (() -> Unit)? = null)
data class MonarchAiOnboardingTourStep(title: String, body: String, id: String? = null)

class MonarchAiOnboardingTourLabels(eyebrow: String? = null, stepOf: ((step: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, back: String? = null, next: String? = null, finish: String? = null, skip: String? = null, disable: String? = null)

options.name: steps
options.description: The steps, each with a title and a body.

options.name: step
options.description: The position of the current step, from 0, when the app keeps it. Kept inside the steps. The other overload keeps it itself.

options.name: onStepChange
options.description: Called with the new position by Back, Next and a swipe.

options.name: onDisable
options.description: Called by Turn off AI, which is on every step.

options.name: onFinish
options.description: Called by the last step's Got it button.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the tour.

options.name: icon
options.description: An AI glyph beside the eyebrow, in the AI strong color. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: skipIcon
options.description: The icon of the skip button; without it the button shows the words Skip introduction.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces "AI", "Step … of …", Back, Next, Got it, Skip introduction and Turn off AI.

options.name: onSkip
options.description: Adds a button that skips the tour.

states.name: first step
states.description: Next and Turn off AI; no Back.

states.name: middle step
states.description: Back, Next and Turn off AI.

states.name: last step
states.description: Back, Got it and Turn off AI.

states.name: one step
states.description: Got it and Turn off AI, without the stepper.

states.name: no steps
states.description: The eyebrow and the buttons only.

appearance: The eyebrow in caption type and the AI strong color, then MonarchStepper (compact when the names do not fit), the step title in the heading style and default text, the body in muted text. Next and Got it are primary buttons, Back secondary and Turn off AI ghost; the skip button is ghost or an icon button in the muted text color.
platformNotes: The web's target option, which outlines an element on the page, has no equivalent: point at a control with a Material 3 tooltip. The web's floating placement becomes a sheet the app presents (MonarchBottomSheet), as on iOS. Steps can be swiped as well as moved with Back and Next. iOS has an internal-state and a Binding initialiser; Android has an uncontrolled overload and a controlled one with step and onStepChange. iOS steps take an SF Symbol; Monarch for Android bundles no icons, so there is one icon slot for the tour and none per step. The close button is a skip button whose icon is a slot; without an icon it shows its words. The web's controlled defaultStep is the uncontrolled overload, which starts at the first step. TalkBack focus is not moved when the step changes (Compose has no API to move accessibility focus); the step and its title are announced through a polite live region instead. Pages are composed ahead so the pager measures every step, but its height follows the page in view and may change between steps of different lengths.
accessibility: Each step's title is a heading.
When the step changes, "Step 2 of 4" and the step's title are announced through a polite live region; nothing is announced when the tour appears.
MonarchStepper reads the position and the name of the step.
Turn off AI is on every step, so the opt-out is always reachable.
Every button has a 48dp touch target; the buttons wrap onto more lines when they do not fit.
The skip icon button is named "Skip introduction".
edgeCases: A step outside the range is clamped to the first or the last step.
Step ids default to the position; the stepper always gets unique ids even when titles repeat.
With one step there is no stepper; with no steps only the eyebrow and buttons show, and the primary button is Got it.
Long titles and bodies wrap at large text sizes.

name: MonarchAiPermissionScope
title: AiPermissionScope
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of FlowRow rows; androidx.compose.material3.SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow with SegmentedButton for the editable control; MonarchFavicon, MonarchLink
summary: What an AI agent may read or edit, app by app: each row names the app and the resources it covers and shows No access, Can read or Can read and edit, or a None / Read / Write control when editable.
whenToUse: In assistant settings or before connecting an agent, to show or change what it may see and change in each connected app.
whenNotToUse: For a single yes/no permission use MonarchSwitchRow. For the system permissions of the device (microphone, location) use the Android permission request.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiPermissionScope(scopes: List<MonarchAiPermissionScopeItem>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, onScopesChange: ((List<MonarchAiPermissionScopeItem>) -> Unit)? = null, enabled: Boolean = true, accessIcon: (@Composable (MonarchAiAccessLevel) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiPermissionScopeLabels = MonarchAiPermissionScopeLabels(), onManage: (() -> Unit)? = null)
data class MonarchAiPermissionScopeItem(app: String, access: MonarchAiAccessLevel, resources: String? = null, icon: Painter? = null)
enum class MonarchAiAccessLevel { None, Read, Write; fun includes(needed: MonarchAiAccessLevel): Boolean }

class MonarchAiPermissionScopeLabels(label: String? = null, access: ((MonarchAiAccessLevel) -> String)? = null, option: ((MonarchAiAccessLevel) -> String)? = null, control: ((app: String) -> String)? = null, manage: String? = null, empty: String? = null)

options.name: scopes
options.description: One row per app, each with a unique app name, the access level, optional resources and an optional icon Painter.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the list.

options.name: onScopesChange
options.description: Makes the list editable: called with the whole list, one row changed, when the person picks another level. Pass the new list back in scopes. null shows the access as text.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the editable controls take input.

options.name: accessIcon
options.description: An icon before the access text of a read-only row, given the level (for example a lock, an eye or a pencil). Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces the list name, the level texts, the short option names, the control name, the manage text and the empty text.

options.name: onManage
options.description: Adds a "Manage permissions" link under the list.

states.name: read only
states.description: Each row writes the level: No access in muted text, Can read, Can read and edit, with the optional access icon.

states.name: editable
states.description: Each row has a None / Read / Write segmented control; the chosen segment is filled and has a check mark.

states.name: narrow
states.description: When the access or the control does not fit beside the app name, it moves under it.

states.name: empty
states.description: "The AI has no access to any app." in muted text.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With enabled false the segments use the disabled roles and take no input.

appearance: App names are strong body text with resources in muted caption text; rows are separated by the subtle border color. The segmented control is the Material 3 one in the Monarch theme. The manage link is the standalone MonarchLink in the link color. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web's manageHref link becomes an onManage callback, as on iOS, since a native app opens its own settings screen. The web's onChange(scopes, changed) and iOS's binding become onScopesChange with the whole list. The app icon is a Painter shown with MonarchFavicon (iOS takes a URL; Monarch for Android loads no images). The web draws lock, eye and pencil glyphs; Android bundles no icons, so they are the accessIcon slot and the level is always written. The parity map named a LazyColumn; the list is a Column, because a permission list is short and usually sits in a settings screen that already scrolls, where a nested LazyColumn cannot be measured.
accessibility: The list is a TalkBack traversal group named "What the AI can access".
A read-only row is one element read as the app and its resources, with the access ("Can read") as its state description.
The level is always written, so it never depends on color or on an icon.
An editable row's control is a traversal group named "Access to <app>"; each segment keeps the Material 3 radio button role and selected state.
The favicon is decorative and hidden.
Segments and the manage link have touch targets of at least 48dp by 48dp; rows wrap and stack at large font sizes.
edgeCases: App names must be unique: they are the rows' identity.
An empty or blank resources string is not shown or read.
Picking the level a row already has does not call onScopesChange.
Long app names and resources wrap; the control moves under them.

name: MonarchAiPlan
title: AiPlan
wrapsNative: MonarchCard with MonarchReorderableList (androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn) of compact bordered text field rows with Move up and Move down buttons, androidx.compose.material3.IconButton or MonarchButton to remove, MonarchButton footer, and MonarchAiChainOfSteps once decided
summary: The plan an agent proposes before it acts, which a person edits, reorders, approves or rejects, and which then shows the steps as the agent works through them.
whenToUse: When an agent asks for approval before it takes several steps that change things, so the person can correct the plan first.
whenNotToUse: For steps that run without approval, use MonarchAiChainOfSteps. For a single risky tool call, use MonarchAiPermissionScope or the tool call's own approval.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchAiPlan(part: MonarchAiPlanPart, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, decision: MonarchAiPlanDecision? = null, editable: Boolean = true, removeIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiPlanLabels = MonarchAiPlanLabels(), onChange: ((List<MonarchAiPlanStep>) -> Unit)? = null, onReject: (() -> Unit)? = null, onApprove: ((List<MonarchAiPlanStep>) -> Unit)? = null)
enum class MonarchAiPlanDecision { Pending, Approved, Rejected }

class MonarchAiPlanLabels(title: String? = null, description: String? = null, editHint: String? = null, approvedNotice: String? = null, rejectedNotice: String? = null, stepLabel: ((position: Int) -> String)? = null, stepPlaceholder: String? = null, untitledStep: ((position: Int) -> String)? = null, remove: ((step: String) -> String)? = null, removeText: String? = null, removed: ((step: String) -> String)? = null, addStep: String? = null, approve: String? = null, reject: String? = null, emptyPlan: String? = null, reorder: MonarchReorderableListLabels = MonarchReorderableListLabels())

options.name: part
options.description: The plan part the agent proposed. Its steps seed the draft; a new part from the model (not an echo of the draft) replaces it.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the card.

options.name: decision
options.description: The decision, when the app keeps it. When null the view keeps its own after Approve or Reject.

options.name: editable
options.description: Whether the person can change the steps before deciding. Once decided the plan is always read-only.

options.name: removeIcon
options.description: The icon of each step's remove button, in a 48dp Material 3 IconButton. Without it the button reads "Remove". Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, including the title and the reorderable list's strings.

options.name: onChange
options.description: Called with the draft after every edit, move, addition and removal.

options.name: onReject
options.description: Called when the person rejects the plan.

options.name: onApprove
options.description: Called with the approved steps, labels trimmed and empty steps left out.

states.name: pending, editable
states.description: Each step is a row with the reorder handle, its number, the step text in a bordered field, a remove button and Move up and Move down buttons; Add step, Reject and Approve plan follow.

states.name: pending, read-only
states.description: editable false: the steps as a MonarchAiChainOfSteps with Reject and Approve plan.

states.name: empty
states.description: Every step empty: Approve plan is disabled and a note says to add a step.

states.name: approved
states.description: The description reads the approved notice, which is announced; the cleaned steps show as a MonarchAiChainOfSteps whose states follow the part and are announced.

states.name: rejected
states.description: The description reads the rejected notice, which is announced; the steps show read-only with no buttons.

states.name: dragging
states.description: A step held after a long press follows the finger and the others slide out of its way, as in MonarchReorderableList.

appearance: A MonarchCard with the title in the subheading style, a muted caption, step numbers in the label style in the muted color, bordered step fields, ghost Add step and Remove buttons, a secondary Reject and a primary Approve plan. All are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: Same names as iOS, with Kotlin names: isEditable is editable and the callbacks follow the labels. The parity map names an editable ordered list; Android builds it on MonarchReorderableList, a LazyColumn, so a long press anywhere on a step drags it and the handle offers Move up and Move down to TalkBack, Switch Access and the arrow keys. Because the plan sits inside a scrolling conversation, the list of steps is limited to four rows of the spacing scale (384dp) and scrolls inside the card past that. iOS builds a VStack with drag and drop onto another step. Like the web, each step's text is an always-open compact bordered field, followed by Remove, Move up and Move down; a new step takes focus at once. Monarch bundles no icons, so the remove button is text unless the app gives an icon. The web's title prop is labels.title. Android announces removals and the decision through a polite live region; iOS posts announcements. The composable is experimental: an AI panel that waits for a Rook app to adopt it.
accessibility: The title is a heading; the card is a traversal group.
Each step's text is a text field named "Step 2"; the visible number is hidden from TalkBack because that name carries it.
Each handle is named "Reorder <step>" and offers Move up and Move down; a move is announced by the reorderable list.
Each remove button is named "Remove <step>" and has a 48dp touch target; a removal is announced as "Removed <step>".
An empty step is named "step 2" in these names.
Approving or rejecting announces the notice through a polite live region; once approved the chain of steps announces starts and failures.
Approve plan is disabled while every step is empty and a visible note says why; the footer buttons wrap when they do not fit.
edgeCases: A step whose text is only spaces counts as empty and is left out of the approved steps.
A new step gets the id new-1, new-2… skipping ids in use, and opens its editor at once.
When the app passes a decision and neither onApprove nor onReject, no buttons are shown.
Long steps wrap at every text size; more than about four steps scroll inside the card.

name: MonarchAiPromptInput
title: AiPromptInput
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.text.BasicTextField (TextFieldState) with androidx.compose.foundation.content.contentReceiver and Modifier.imePadding, MonarchAiAttachmentTray, MonarchButton and MonarchAiStopButton
summary: The prompt box of an AI conversation: text that grows with the prompt, Send that becomes Stop while a response runs, attachments, a slot for slash commands and mentions, a toolbar, a character counter and a token estimate.
whenToUse: At the bottom of an assistant conversation or an AI panel, where the person writes the next prompt.
whenNotToUse: For messages between people, use MonarchMessageComposer (mentions, reply and edit modes, drafts). For a one-line question, use MonarchSearchBar or MonarchTextField.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchAiPromptInput(label: String, state: TextFieldState, onSubmit: suspend (String) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, busy: Boolean = false, showLabel: Boolean = false, submitOn: MonarchAiPromptInputSubmitOn = MonarchAiPromptInputSubmitOn.Enter, minLines: Int = 1, maxLines: Int = 8, maxLength: Int? = null, warnAt: Float = 0.9f, countTokens: ((CharSequence) -> Int)? = null, attachments: List<MonarchAiAttachmentTrayFile> = emptyList(), accept: List<String> = listOf("image/*"), keyboardPadding: Boolean = true, placeholder: String? = null, disabledReason: String? = null, focusRequester: FocusRequester? = null, labels: MonarchAiPromptInputLabels = MonarchAiPromptInputLabels(), onStop: (() -> Unit)? = null, onAttach: (() -> Unit)? = null, onReceiveFiles: ((List<Uri>) -> Unit)? = null, onRemoveAttachment: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, onRetryAttachment: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, attachIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, sendIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, triggerMenu: (@Composable (value: TextFieldValue, onValueChange: (TextFieldValue) -> Unit) -> Unit)? = null, toolbar: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, footer: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null)
public enum class MonarchAiPromptInputSubmitOn { Enter, CtrlEnter }

public class MonarchAiPromptInputLabels(placeholder: String? = null, send: String? = null, stop: String? = null, attach: String? = null, dropHint: String? = null, counter: ((count: Int, max: Int) -> String)? = null, counterLabel: ((count: Int, max: Int) -> String)? = null, counterWarning: ((remaining: Int) -> String)? = null, counterOver: ((over: Int) -> String)? = null, tokens: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, attachments: MonarchAiAttachmentTrayLabels = MonarchAiAttachmentTrayLabels())

options.name: label
options.description: The accessible name of the text field, such as "Message the assistant". Shown above the box with showLabel.

options.name: state
options.description: The text. The app owns it, so it can save and restore a draft (rememberTextFieldState survives configuration changes).

options.name: onSubmit
options.description: Receives the text as typed. The field clears at once; if onSubmit throws, the text comes back unless something new was typed.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the prompt input.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Off, nothing can be typed or sent.

options.name: busy
options.description: A response is running: Send becomes MonarchAiStopButton and Escape calls onStop.

options.name: showLabel
options.description: Shows the label above the box.

options.name: submitOn
options.description: Which hardware key sends: Enter (Shift+Enter adds a line) or Ctrl+Enter. Ctrl+Enter sends with either.

options.name: minLines
options.description: The fewest visible lines.

options.name: maxLines
options.description: The lines the text grows to before it scrolls.

options.name: maxLength
options.description: The most characters. Shows the counter; over the limit sending is off and the field has an error. The text is never cut.

options.name: warnAt
options.description: The share of maxLength at which the counter turns to the warning color and the characters left are announced.

options.name: countTokens
options.description: Estimates tokens for the "≈ N tokens" readout. Called on every change.

options.name: attachments
options.description: The attached files, shown by MonarchAiAttachmentTray inside the box. Allow sending without text.

options.name: accept
options.description: The MIME types onReceiveFiles takes from the keyboard, the clipboard and drag and drop.

options.name: keyboardPadding
options.description: Pads the component by the on-screen keyboard with Modifier.imePadding(), so a prompt docked at the bottom stays above it.

options.name: placeholder
options.description: Shown while the text is empty; the built-in "Send a message…" without it.

options.name: disabledReason
options.description: Why the input is disabled, shown under it while enabled is false.

options.name: focusRequester
options.description: Moves focus to the text field itself (not the box, whose first focus stop may be the attach button), for example when the panel that holds the input opens.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, including the attachment tray's.

options.name: onStop
options.description: Stops the running response, from Stop and Escape. Without it Stop is disabled.

options.name: onAttach
options.description: Adds the attach button. Open the app's picker (PickVisualMedia or OpenMultipleDocuments).

options.name: onReceiveFiles
options.description: Receives content URIs of files the keyboard sends (image keyboards), pasted from the clipboard or dropped on the box, filtered by accept. Pasted text is still typed.

options.name: onRemoveAttachment
options.description: Removes an attachment by id. Without it the tray's buttons are disabled.

options.name: onRetryAttachment
options.description: Retries a failed upload by id.

options.name: attachIcon
options.description: The attach button's icon; the button shows "Attach files" without it.

options.name: sendIcon
options.description: The Send button's icon; the button shows "Send" without it and is named Send either way.

options.name: triggerMenu
options.description: A menu above the box, given the text with its caret and a way to change both: MonarchAiSlashCommands, or MonarchAiMentionContext with MonarchMentionQuery.find.

options.name: toolbar
options.description: Controls in the bar under the text, after the attach button, such as MonarchAiPromptToolbar or a model picker.

options.name: footer
options.description: Under the box, such as MonarchAiDisclaimer.

states.name: empty
states.description: The placeholder shows and Send is disabled.

states.name: typing
states.description: The text grows to maxLines and then scrolls; Send is enabled.

states.name: near the limit
states.description: The counter turns to the strong warning color and the characters left are announced once.

states.name: over the limit
states.description: The counter and the box border turn to the danger colors, the field has an error that says by how much, and Send is disabled.

states.name: busy
states.description: Send is replaced by MonarchAiStopButton; Escape on a hardware keyboard stops.

states.name: dragging
states.description: While files are dragged over the box it takes the accent fill and border and shows "Drop files to attach".

states.name: disabled
states.description: Muted box and text, disabled buttons, and the reason under the box.

appearance: A rounded box with the surface fill and the input border; the danger border over the limit, the accent subtle fill and border while files are dragged over it, and the subtle fill when disabled. Send is the primary MonarchButton; the counter is muted, then strong warning, then strong danger. All colors are theme roles, so dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web component keeps its own attachments and opens its own file input; on Android the attachments are hoisted (attachments, onRemoveAttachment) because the app picks and uploads files with its own picker, and onReceiveFiles takes the files that reach the field without a picker through Modifier.contentReceiver: image keyboards, clipboard pastes and drag and drop between apps (the web's paste and drop). The web's triggers and renderTriggerMenu become one triggerMenu slot that gets the text and caret as a TextFieldValue, which is what MonarchAiSlashCommands takes; Escape closing the menu stays with the menu. The web's screen reader hints for Enter and Escape are not added: on a phone the on-screen keyboard's Enter adds a line and Send sends; Enter, Ctrl+Enter and Escape work on a hardware keyboard. Keyboard avoidance has no web equivalent: keyboardPadding applies Modifier.imePadding(). usePromptDraft has no counterpart: the app keeps the TextFieldState (rememberTextFieldState survives configuration changes, and the app may save it). onSubmit gets the text only, because the app already holds the attachments. iOS has no entry for this id yet; the names follow the web and MonarchMessageComposer.
accessibility: The text field is named by label, and over the limit it carries an error that says how many characters too many.
Send and Stop are buttons with 48dp touch targets; with sendIcon or attachIcon the buttons are still named Send and Attach files.
The counter is read as "120 of 4000 characters" instead of "120 / 4000".
Reaching the warning share ("12 characters left") and going over the limit ("3 characters over the limit") are announced once through a polite live region that is always present.
The attachments are the tray's: a traversal group with remove buttons named after each file.
The drop hint is decoration; the state is also shown by the accent border.
edgeCases: Over the limit the text is kept, never cut; sending is off until it is shortened.
Whitespace alone cannot be sent unless there are attachments.
If onSubmit throws after the person started a new prompt, the new text is kept and the old one is not restored.
Pasted text goes into the field; only content whose type matches accept and that carries a URI is passed to onReceiveFiles.
maxLines below minLines is raised to minLines.

Do not put the prompt inside a vertically scrolling parent with keyboardPadding on a screen that already resizes for the keyboard; the padding is consumed, so a parent that pads by the keyboard is not doubled.

name: MonarchAiPromptTemplatePicker
title: AiPromptTemplatePicker

whenToUse: From an AI composer, so people can start from a saved prompt (their own or the team's) and fill in the parts that change, then review it in the prompt field before sending.
whenNotToUse: For a few suggested first questions use MonarchAiStarterPrompts. For follow-ups after an answer use MonarchAiFollowUpSuggestions. For document templates use MonarchTemplatePicker.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiPromptTemplatePicker(templates: List<MonarchAiPromptTemplate>, onUse: (text: String, template: MonarchAiPromptTemplate, values: Map<String, String>) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, categories: List<MonarchAiPromptTemplateCategory> = emptyList(), initialTemplateId: String? = null, labels: MonarchAiPromptTemplatePickerLabels = MonarchAiPromptTemplatePickerLabels(), onCancel: (() -> Unit)? = null)

data class MonarchAiPromptTemplate(id: String, title: String, body: String, description: String? = null, category: String? = null, keywords: List<String> = emptyList(), variables: List<MonarchAiPromptTemplateVariable>? = null) { val resolvedVariables: List<MonarchAiPromptTemplateVariable>; companion object { fun variableNames(body: String): List<String>; fun fill(body: String, values: Map<String, String>): String } }
