data class MonarchAiPromptTemplateCategory(id: String, label: String)

class MonarchAiPromptTemplatePickerLabels(title: String? = null, search: String? = null, allCategories: String? = null, template: String? = null, preview: String? = null, use: String? = null, cancel: String? = null, back: String? = null, optional: String? = null, missing: ((label: String) -> String)? = null, empty: String? = null, noResults: ((query: String) -> String)? = null)

options.name: templates
options.description: The templates, each with a title, a body with {{blanks}}, and optional description, category, keywords and variables.

options.name: onUse
options.type: (text: String, template: MonarchAiPromptTemplate, values: Map<String, String>) -> Unit
options.description: Receives the filled prompt, the template and the trimmed values. Put the text in the prompt field; do not send it without the person seeing it.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the picker. Give it a bounded height: it scrolls itself.

options.name: categories
options.description: Adds category filters above the list.

options.name: initialTemplateId
options.description: Opens this template's page at first.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces every built-in string.

options.name: onCancel
options.description: Adds a Cancel button to the gallery, for example to hide the sheet.

states.name: gallery
states.description: The heading, the search field, the category filters when categories are given, and a card per template.

states.name: empty
states.description: A first-run empty state: "No templates yet".

states.name: no results
states.description: A filtered empty state with the query and a Clear filters button that clears the search and the category.

states.name: template without blanks
states.description: The description, the template text under a Template heading, and Use template.

states.name: template with blanks
states.description: One field per blank (multi-line where asked), a live preview with [Label] for empty blanks, and Use template.

states.name: missing value
states.description: After Use template, each empty required field shows "Enter …" as its error until it is filled.

appearance: The heading in the heading style; templates are MonarchCards with the title in strong body text and the description in muted caption text. Categories are selectable MonarchTags. The template text and the preview sit in blocks with the subtle background, the subtle border and the control corner radius, under muted label headings. Use template is a full-width primary button; Back and Cancel are ghost buttons.
platformNotes: The web shows the gallery and a preview side by side, then a form step; Android, like iOS, shows the gallery and then a page per template, here as two pages of the same content with an "All templates" button instead of a navigation bar back button, so it belongs in a MonarchBottomSheet. Categories are selectable MonarchTags (filter chips), as on the web, instead of the iOS picker. iOS isRequired and isMultiline are required and multiline, and initialTemplateID is initialTemplateId, following Kotlin naming; the back label is Android only. Multi-line blanks use MonarchTextField with singleLine false. The first error is announced through an assertive live region, because it blocks the action; errors are written as text under the field by MonarchTextField, not shown by color alone. The picker scrolls itself, so it needs a bounded height and cannot sit inside another vertically scrolling container.
accessibility: Each template is one button read as its title and description, at least 48dp high.
The gallery heading, the template title and the Template and Prompt preview headings are headings.
Each field is labelled with its label, and ", Optional" when it may be empty; help and errors are read with the field.
When Use template finds an empty required field, the first error is announced through an assertive live region and every error is written under its field.
The template text and the preview can be selected.
edgeCases: A blank used twice is one field and is filled everywhere.
A blank without a value stays as {{name}} in fill; an empty value removes it, so an empty optional blank disappears from the used prompt.
Without variables every blank is required and labelled from its name: customer_name becomes "Customer name".
Search ignores case and accents and looks at the title, description, body and keywords.
An initialTemplateId that matches no template opens the gallery.

parityExceptions.reason: The web example shows the search field and the three category filters on one line, and the templates three across. parityExceptions.convention: a toolbar wraps and a grid takes fewer columns on a compact window (Material adaptive layout)

name: MonarchAiPromptToolbar
title: AiPromptToolbar
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow; MonarchButton (androidx.compose.material3.Button) for MonarchAiPromptToolbarButton; androidx.compose.material3.FilterChip for MonarchAiPromptToolbarToggle
summary: The row of compact controls under a prompt (attach, web search, mode, model, tone), with a compact ghost button and an on/off toggle for consistent sizing.
whenToUse: Under or beside an AI prompt field, for options that change how the next prompt is sent.
whenNotToUse: For the actions of a form use MonarchFormActionsBar. For a choice of one tone use MonarchAiTonePicker inside the toolbar rather than several toggles.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiPromptToolbar(modifier: Modifier = Modifier, label: String? = null, content: @Composable FlowRowScope.() -> Unit)

@Composable fun MonarchAiPromptToolbarButton(text: String, onClick: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, hideLabel: Boolean = false, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)

@Composable fun MonarchAiPromptToolbarToggle(text: String, checked: Boolean, onCheckedChange: (Boolean) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, hideLabel: Boolean = false, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the toolbar, button or toggle.

options.name: label
options.description: MonarchAiPromptToolbar: replaces the TalkBack name of the group, "Prompt options" (monarch_aiprompttoolbar_label).

options.name: content
options.description: MonarchAiPromptToolbar: the controls in order. Controls that do not fit move to a new line.

options.name: text
options.description: Button and toggle: the label, and always the TalkBack name.

options.name: onClick
options.description: Button: called when activated. Not called when not enabled.

options.name: checked
options.description: Toggle: whether the option is on.

options.name: onCheckedChange
options.description: Toggle: called with the new state. Not called when not enabled.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Button and toggle: whether the control takes input.

options.name: hideLabel
options.description: Button and toggle: shows only the icon; the text stays the TalkBack name. Ignored without an icon.

options.name: icon
options.description: Button and toggle: an icon before the label, for example a MonarchIcon with a null content description. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: Button and toggle: the source of the press, focus and hover interactions.

states.name: toggle on
states.description: The assistant subtle fill, the assistant border and strong assistant text.

states.name: toggle off
states.description: A ghost control in muted text with no border.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Button and toggle use the disabled text role; a toggle that is on keeps the muted fill and the subtle border, so its state stays visible.

states.name: wrapped
states.description: Controls that do not fit move to a new line.

appearance: The button is the ghost MonarchButton at the small size. The toggle is transparent with muted text when off, and the assistant subtle fill, assistant border and strong assistant text when on. Both use the control radius. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ships AiPromptToolbarButton and AiPromptToolbarToggle and Android ships the same two, because Compose cannot restyle arbitrary buttons through the environment as iOS does. The toggle is a Material 3 FilterChip, the Material 3 toggle with a text label (as the toggle-button entry documents), so TalkBack reads it as selected or not selected instead of the web's pressed state. The toggle is 36dp high inside a 48dp touch target. The web's uncontrolled defaultPressed is not offered: state is hoisted. The check mark iOS adds for Differentiate Without Color has no Android setting; the on state always has a border.
accessibility: The toolbar is a TalkBack traversal group named "Prompt options" or the label given; each control inside is its own element, read in order.
The button keeps the Material 3 button role; an icon-only button is named by its text.
The toggle keeps the FilterChip role and selected state; its label does not change with its state.
An icon-only toggle is named by its text.
Every control has a touch target of at least 48dp by 48dp.
A toggle that is on also differs by its border, so the state does not depend on color alone.
edgeCases: Controls wider than the row get a line of their own and their text wraps.
An empty toolbar takes no height.
hideLabel without an icon shows the label, because the control would be empty.

name: MonarchAiReasoning
title: AiReasoning
wrapsNative: MonarchCollapsible (androidx.compose.animation.AnimatedVisibility) with androidx.compose.foundation.text.selection.SelectionContainer, MonarchAiThinkingIndicator before text arrives, android.icu.text.MeasureFormat for the duration
summary: The model's reasoning for one answer, as a disclosure that reads "Thinking…" with a live timer while it streams and "Thought for 12s" once it finishes.
whenToUse: In an assistant message, for a reasoning part from the message model, so people can see that the model is working and read how it reached the answer if they want to.
whenNotToUse: For a waiting state before any reasoning or answer exists, use MonarchAiThinkingIndicator. For the steps of a tool-using run, use MonarchAiChainOfSteps.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiReasoning(part: MonarchAiReasoningPart, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, startedAt: Long? = null, initiallyExpanded: Boolean = false, onExpandedChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, expandIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiReasoningLabels = MonarchAiReasoningLabels())

class MonarchAiReasoningLabels(prefix: String? = null, thinking: String? = null, thoughtFor: ((String) -> String)? = null, thought: String? = null, reasoningHidden: String? = null, duration: ((Long) -> String)? = null)

options.name: part
options.description: The reasoning part from the message model: its text, whether it streams, its durationMs and whether it is redacted.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the reasoning.

options.name: startedAt
options.description: When the reasoning started, in epoch milliseconds. Pass it when the view can leave the composition while the part streams, for example in a lazy list, so the timer does not restart. Counts from when streaming was first seen when null.

options.name: initiallyExpanded
options.description: Whether finished reasoning starts open. Streaming reasoning always starts open.

options.name: onExpandedChange
options.description: Called when the disclosure opens or closes, by the person or automatically when the reasoning finishes or starts again.

options.name: icon
options.description: The assistant mark of the thinking indicator and the still row, tinted with the strong assistant color. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: expandIcon
options.description: An icon after the header, such as a chevron; it turns half a turn while open.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, including the duration format.

states.name: streaming, no text yet
states.description: A MonarchAiThinkingIndicator with the assistant mark, "Thinking…" and the elapsed time after 3 seconds.

states.name: streaming
states.description: Open; the header reads "Thinking…", then "Thinking… 5s" after 3 seconds, ticking once a second; the text below grows.

states.name: finished
states.description: Closed; the header reads "Thought for" the part's durationMs, or the time this view measured, or "Thought" when neither is known.

states.name: touched
states.description: If the person opens or closes it while it streams, it stays as they left it when the reasoning finishes.

states.name: restarted
states.description: When a finished part streams again (a regeneration), it opens and measures again.

states.name: redacted
states.description: A still row with the mark and "Reasoning hidden"; no disclosure and no text.

appearance: The MonarchCollapsible header in the label style, the reasoning text in the body style in the muted text color, and the mark in the strong assistant color. All are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: Same names and states as iOS, with Kotlin names: startedAt is epoch milliseconds, startsExpanded is initiallyExpanded and the duration label takes milliseconds as a Long. The web renders the text with AiStreamingText; Android, like iOS, uses selectable plain text because there is no streaming text component yet. The web chevron leads; MonarchCollapsible puts the icon at the end, and Monarch bundles no icons, so the chevron and the assistant mark are slots. The web prefixes the summary with hidden text; Android names the group "Assistant reasoning" for TalkBack. The web's locale prop is the device locale here. The plan's live timer is in the header text, which TalkBack reads when it reaches it and never announces. The composable is experimental: an AI panel that waits for a Rook app to adopt it.
accessibility: The header is MonarchCollapsible's button with the state Expanded or Collapsed and the TalkBack expand and collapse actions, and a 48dp touch target.
The whole is a traversal group named "Assistant reasoning".
Redacted or empty reasoning is one element read as "Assistant reasoning: Reasoning hidden" with no button.
The live timer is not announced; the thinking indicator's announcement is turned off.
With animations off the disclosure opens and closes at once and the mark stops pulsing; the timer still ticks once a second.
The header wraps at the largest font size.
edgeCases: A part that streams with no text yet shows the thinking indicator, then becomes a disclosure when text arrives.
A durationMs on the part wins over the time this view measured.
Durations round to whole seconds and are at least 1 second.
Long reasoning wraps; the disclosure has no height limit.

name: MonarchAiRelatedEntities
title: AiRelatedEntities
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of rows with MonarchAvatar, MonarchBadge and androidx.compose.material3.LinearProgressIndicator; the graph is a androidx.compose.ui.layout.Layout of MonarchAvatar nodes with lines drawn by androidx.compose.ui.draw.drawBehind
summary: People, organizations, projects and records the assistant found related to the current content, ranked by relevance with their relations, as a list or a radial graph.
whenToUse: Beside a document, a record or an answer, to show which people, companies and records the assistant connected to it and how strongly.
whenNotToUse: For the sources an answer is based on, use MonarchAiSourceList. For a large network that people explore, use MonarchForceGraph.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiRelatedEntities(entities: List<MonarchAiRelatedEntity>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchAiRelatedEntitiesVariant = MonarchAiRelatedEntitiesVariant.List, relations: List<MonarchAiEntityRelation> = emptyList(), centerId: String? = null, maxGraphNodes: Int = 12, onSelect: ((MonarchAiRelatedEntity) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiRelatedEntitiesLabels = MonarchAiRelatedEntitiesLabels())
class MonarchAiRelatedEntity(id: String, label: String, kind: MonarchAiRelatedEntityKind, weight: Double? = null, image: Painter? = null)
class MonarchAiRelatedEntityKind(value: String) { companion object { val Person; val Org; val Project; val Document; val Record; val Place; val Other } }
class MonarchAiEntityRelation(from: String, to: String, label: String? = null)
enum class MonarchAiRelatedEntitiesVariant { List, Graph }

class MonarchAiRelatedEntitiesLabels(label: String? = null, kind: ((MonarchAiRelatedEntityKind) -> String)? = null, weight: ((weight: Double) -> String)? = null, relation: ((other: String, label: String?) -> String)? = null, relatedTo: String? = null, empty: String? = null)

options.name: entities
options.description: The entities: id, label, kind, optional weight from 0 to 1 and optional image Painter. The list is sorted by weight, highest first; unweighted entities keep their order after the weighted ones.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the list or graph.

options.name: variant
options.description: A ranked list, or a radial graph.

options.name: relations
options.description: Links between entities by id, with an optional label such as "works at". Shown under each entity and as lines in the graph; unknown ids are skipped.

options.name: centerId
options.description: The graph's middle entity. The one with the highest weight when null or unknown.

options.name: maxGraphNodes
options.description: Above this many entities the graph variant shows the list.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Makes every entity a button that calls this with the entity.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for "Related entities", the kind names, "Relevance 90%", the relation text, "Related to" and "No related entities" (strings_airelatedentities.xml).

states.name: list
states.description: Bordered rows with the avatar, the name, the kind badge, the relations line and a relevance bar.

states.name: graph
states.description: Up to 320dp across: the center entity with a large avatar in the middle and the others on a ring from the top, clockwise, with medium avatars, one-line names and relation lines behind them.

states.name: graph fallback
states.description: More than maxGraphNodes entities, or a font scale above 1.3: the list is shown instead.

states.name: selectable
states.description: With onSelect each row or node is a button with a ripple and a focus ring.

states.name: empty
states.description: A small MonarchEmptyState reading "No related entities".

appearance: List rows have a subtle border on the large container shape; names are strong default text, relations muted caption text, the kind a neutral subtle MonarchBadge, and the relevance bar the accent fill on the muted track. Graph lines use the default border role. Avatars without a picture use MonarchAvatar's fallback colors. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web draws the graph in SVG with circles; Android places MonarchAvatar nodes with a Layout and draws the relation lines behind them, as iOS does. The diagram is drawn the same way in both layout directions, because a radial diagram has no reading direction and the lines must meet the nodes. The graph falls back to the list above font scale 1.3, where the one-line names would be cut, as iOS does at accessibility sizes. Entities can carry an image Painter for the avatar (iOS takes an imageURL; Monarch for Android loads no images); the web shows no pictures. The web's kind is any string; Android uses a class with constants for the common kinds, so custom kinds still work. Node labels are cut with an ellipsis instead of at 18 characters; the full name is always spoken.
accessibility: The list or the graph is a traversal group named "Related entities".
Each entity is one element read as "Jordan Lee. Person. Relevance 90%. Related to: works at Acme"; with onSelect it is a button, otherwise a graph node has the image role.
Avatars are decorative; relevance bars and relation lines are hidden because the spoken name carries them.
The kind is written in a badge, so it does not depend on the avatar.
Rows and nodes are at least 48dp in both directions; the list wraps text at font scale 2.0 and the graph becomes the list above 1.3.
edgeCases: Weights outside 0 to 1 are limited; NaN counts as no weight.
A relation to an unknown id is ignored.
Below about 192dp wide the graph's nodes are narrower than 48dp and overlap; use the list in narrow places.
The graph needs one center: an unknown centerId falls back to the highest weight.

name: MonarchAiResponseSkeleton
title: AiResponseSkeleton
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column and Row of MonarchSkeleton bars (androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Box with a drawBehind gradient), androidx.compose.material3.HorizontalDivider
summary: A placeholder shaped like the answer that is on its way (paragraph lines, a column of cards or a table), shown between sending a prompt and the first streamed token.
whenToUse: In the place of an assistant reply while it is being generated and before any text arrives, when you know roughly what shape the answer takes.
whenNotToUse: Once tokens stream in, show the reply itself. For a small 'assistant is writing' mark use MonarchAiTypingDots or MonarchAiThinkingIndicator; for a non-AI loading placeholder use MonarchSkeleton.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiResponseSkeleton(modifier: Modifier = Modifier, shape: MonarchAiResponseSkeletonShape = MonarchAiResponseSkeletonShape.Text, lines: Int? = null, columns: Int = 3, label: String? = null)
enum class MonarchAiResponseSkeletonShape { Text, Cards, Table }

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the placeholder. It fills the available width.

options.name: shape
options.description: Text: paragraph lines with a shorter last line. Cards: a column of card outlines. Table: a header row and body rows.

options.name: lines
options.description: The number of text lines, cards or table body rows. null gives 3 for text and cards and 4 for a table. Values below 1 draw 1.

options.name: columns
options.description: The number of table columns. Values below 1 draw 1. Only used by the table shape.

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken text, "Generating response…" (monarch_airesponseskeleton_label).

states.name: waiting
states.description: The bars shimmer: a lighter band sweeps from the start edge to the end edge.

states.name: animations off
states.description: When the user has turned animations off, the bars stand still in the resting fill.

appearance: The bars use the MonarchSkeleton roles: the muted background with the subtle background as the moving band. Cards are surface-coloured outlines with the subtle border and the container radius; table rows are separated by the subtle border color. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web lays cards out in a responsive grid; Android draws them in one column, as iOS does, which holds at every font size. The bars are MonarchSkeleton, so they shimmer with its neutral roles rather than the assistant tint iOS pulses with. The web's role="status" with aria-busy maps to one TalkBack element with a content description and an indeterminate progress, so TalkBack reads it as busy. Android uses the same names as iOS.
accessibility: The placeholder is one TalkBack element read as "Generating response…" or the label given.
It reports an indeterminate progress, so TalkBack reads it as in progress.
The bars are not separate elements and are not read.
It posts no announcement; the conversation announces its own progress.
When animations are off the shimmer stops and the bars stay still.
edgeCases: lines and columns below 1 draw one line, card, row or column.
A single text line is full width; with several, the last one is shorter (62%).
Many table columns get narrow bars; widths are fractions of each cell.
Text bars are as high as three quarters of the body font size, so they grow with the font size setting.

name: MonarchAiSafetyNotice
title: AiSafetyNotice
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column on the MonarchBanner surface, with MonarchButton and MonarchLink actions in a FlowRow; androidx.compose.ui.platform.LocalUriHandler opens the link
summary: Says, calmly and specifically, that a safety system blocked a request, changed an answer or removed parts of it, with an optional reason, next steps, an Edit prompt button and a link to the content guidelines.
whenToUse: In an AI conversation, where the answer would have been, when a safety or moderation system blocked the request or changed or shortened the answer.
whenNotToUse: For a failed turn (rate limit, lost connection, a safety block reported as an error code) use MonarchAiErrorMessage. For a general warning outside a conversation use MonarchBanner. For the standing "AI can make mistakes" note use MonarchAiDisclaimer.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiSafetyNotice(kind: MonarchAiSafetyNoticeKind, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, title: String? = null, message: String? = null, reason: String? = null, nextSteps: String? = null, learnMoreUrl: String? = null, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiSafetyNoticeLabels = MonarchAiSafetyNoticeLabels(), onEditPrompt: (() -> Unit)? = null, onOpenLearnMore: ((String) -> Unit)? = null)
enum class MonarchAiSafetyNoticeKind { Blocked, Modified, Filtered }

class MonarchAiSafetyNoticeLabels(title: ((kind: MonarchAiSafetyNoticeKind) -> String)? = null, message: ((kind: MonarchAiSafetyNoticeKind) -> String)? = null, reason: String? = null, editPrompt: String? = null, learnMore: String? = null)

options.name: kind
options.description: What the safety system did. Sets the tone and the built-in title and explanation.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the notice.

options.name: title
options.description: Replaces the title of the kind for this notice.

options.name: message
options.description: Replaces the explanation of the kind for this notice.

options.name: reason
options.description: Why, in plain words, shown after a bold "Reason:" label. Blank text is not shown.

options.name: nextSteps
options.description: What the person can do next, as a sentence. Blank text is not shown.

options.name: learnMoreUrl
options.description: Adds a "Content guidelines" link. Only http, https and mailto links are shown.

options.name: icon
options.description: An icon at the start in the tone color, for example a lock. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces the built-in titles, explanations, "Reason:", "Edit prompt" and "Content guidelines".

options.name: onEditPrompt
options.description: Adds an "Edit prompt" button, usually to put the prompt back in the composer.

options.name: onOpenLearnMore
options.description: Called with the link instead of opening it with LocalUriHandler, for example to open a Custom Tab.

states.name: blocked
states.description: Warning colors: "This request wasn’t answered".

states.name: modified
states.description: Info colors: "This response was adjusted".

states.name: filtered
states.description: Info colors: "Some content was hidden".

states.name: static
states.description: Without onEditPrompt and a safe learnMoreUrl the notice has no action row.

appearance: The surface of MonarchBanner: the subtle fill and the border of the warning tone for a blocked request and of the info tone otherwise, the strong role of the tone for the icon, default text for the title and the bold "Reason:" label, muted text for the explanation, reason and next steps. Edit prompt is a small secondary button and the guidelines a standalone link.
platformNotes: The parity map names MonarchBanner, but the banner takes one string and one action, so the notice draws the same surface and tone palette and adds its own text and actions, as MonarchAiErrorMessage does. The web takes rich content for the reason and next steps; Android takes plain strings, as iOS does. The web's children replace the explanation; here that is message. learnMoreUrl is a String (iOS takes a URL) and opens through LocalUriHandler or onOpenLearnMore instead of a new tab. The web and iOS draw a glyph per kind; Monarch for Android bundles no icons, so the icon is a slot and each kind is told by its title. Same names as iOS.
accessibility: The title, the explanation, the reason with its "Reason:" label and the next steps are one TalkBack element, read in that order.
Edit prompt is a separate button and the guidelines link a separate link read with "opens in the browser"; both have 48dp touch targets.
Each kind has its own title, so the kind does not depend on color or on the icon; the icon slot is decoration.
The notice does not announce itself; place it where the answer would have been.
edgeCases: A reason or next steps that are empty or only white space are not shown.
A javascript:, file: or custom-scheme link is dropped and no link is shown; spaces around a link are trimmed.
The actions sit on one line when they fit and wrap when they do not, at large text sizes.
title and message given to the notice win over the labels.

examples.code: MonarchAiSafetyNotice(kind = MonarchAiSafetyNoticeKind.Modified)

    message = "Two links were removed from this answer.",
)

name: MonarchAiScore
title: AiScore
wrapsNative: MonarchScoreRing (androidx.compose.material3.CircularProgressIndicator), MonarchProgress (androidx.compose.material3.LinearProgressIndicator), MonarchBadge, MonarchAiGeneratedBadge and MonarchCollapsible in a androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
summary: A 0 to 100 score produced by a model, as a ring or a bar, with its band, the rationale and the factors that raised or lowered it.
whenToUse: For a model's score of a lead, an account, a ticket or a document, when people need to see why the model scored it that way.
whenNotToUse: For a score with no model behind it, use MonarchScoreRing. For how sure the model is of an answer, use MonarchAiConfidenceMeter.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiScore(value: Double?, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchAiScoreVariant = MonarchAiScoreVariant.Ring, size: MonarchAiScoreSize = MonarchAiScoreSize.Md, label: String? = null, bands: List<MonarchAiScoreBand> = MonarchAiScoreBand.defaults(), rationale: String? = null, factors: List<MonarchAiScoreFactor> = emptyList(), showBands: Boolean = true, aiIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, bandIcon: (@Composable (MonarchTone) -> Unit)? = null, expandIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiScoreLabels = MonarchAiScoreLabels())
class MonarchAiScoreBand(minimum: Double, label: String, tone: MonarchTone = MonarchTone.Neutral) { companion object { @Composable fun defaults(): List<MonarchAiScoreBand> } }
class MonarchAiScoreFactor(label: String, impact: Double, detail: String? = null)
enum class MonarchAiScoreVariant { Ring, Bar }
enum class MonarchAiScoreSize { Sm, Md }

class MonarchAiScoreLabels(label: String? = null, aiGenerated: String? = null, valueText: ((value: String, max: String) -> String)? = null, unavailable: String? = null, factors: String? = null, impact: ((amount: String, raised: Boolean) -> String)? = null, noImpact: String? = null, bands: String? = null, currentBand: String? = null)

options.name: value
options.description: The score from 0 to 100; values outside are limited. null, or not a number, while there is no score.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the component.

options.name: variant
options.description: A ring with the number in its center, or a bar with the number above it.

options.name: size
options.description: The size of the ring: Sm (48dp) or Md (80dp) at the default font size.

options.name: label
options.description: What is scored, such as "Lead score". A heading, and the name of the ring or bar. "Score" when null.

options.name: bands
options.description: Named ranges with a minimum, a label and a MonarchTone: Low (0, danger), Medium (40, warning) and High (70, success) by default, named from strings_aiscore.xml.

options.name: rationale
options.description: Why the model gave this score, in plain words.

options.name: factors
options.description: The inputs that moved the score, each with a label, a signed impact and an optional detail.

options.name: showBands
options.description: Whether the band legend is offered, folded under "How to read this score".

options.name: aiIcon
options.description: An icon for the AI mark. Monarch bundles no icons; the mark is written in any case.

options.name: bandIcon
options.description: An icon for the band badge, given the band's tone. Decorative: the band name is written.

options.name: expandIcon
options.description: The chevron of the band legend header, passed to MonarchCollapsible.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for "Score", "AI score", "72 out of 100", "No score yet", "What affects this score", the spoken impacts, "How to read this score" and "this score" (strings_aiscore.xml).

states.name: scored
states.description: The ring fills to the score in the band's tone, or the bar fills in the band's tone; the band badge shows the band's name in its tone.

states.name: no score
states.description: An empty neutral ring with a dash, or "No score yet" above an empty bar; no band badge.

states.name: factors
states.description: Each factor shows its label, detail, a signed impact ("+18", "−9") and a bar sized against the largest impact, in the success or danger strong color.

states.name: legend
states.description: A folded MonarchCollapsible listing each band with a swatch and its range; the current band is marked "(this score)" in semibold.

appearance: The label is a subheading next to the AI mark in the AI colors. The ring takes the solid color of the band's tone with the number in the tone's strong color; the bar is MonarchProgress in the band's tone (neutral without a band). The band badge is the subtle MonarchBadge of the tone. Factor impacts use the success or danger strong roles, details and ranges the muted text role. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web lists factors and bands in tables; Android shows rows, each read as one element, as iOS does. A band can take any MonarchTone, including Ai and Accent, as the web's ai and accent tones. On the bar variant the bar takes the band's tone, as on the web; the band is also written in the badge and the spoken value, so it never rests on color alone. The web's locale prop is the app's configuration locale. label, rationale and factor text are plain strings, not arbitrary content. The default band names come from resources through MonarchAiScoreBand.defaults(), a composable, so they can be translated; pass your own bands to rename them. The web draws arrow icons by the impacts; Android writes the sign and takes optional icons from the app because Monarch bundles none.
accessibility: The ring is one element named by the label, with the state "72 out of 100" or "No score yet" and the range as progress information; the band badge is read after it.
The bar is one element named by the label, with the state "72 out of 100, High".
The band is always written, so it never depends on color.
Each factor is one element: its label, then "Raised the score by 18" or "Lowered the score by 9", then its detail.
The legend header is the MonarchCollapsible button with a 48dp target; each band row is one element and the current band is marked in words.
The label and the factors heading are headings; text wraps at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: Values above 100 or below 0 are limited; NaN is no score.
A score below the lowest band's minimum takes the lowest band.
Empty bands give a neutral ring, no badge and no legend.
Impact bars are sized against the largest absolute impact, at least 1 point.

title: AiScrollAnchor
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn with reverseLayout = true, androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyListState.animateScrollToItem
summary: Keeping a growing conversation pinned to its newest message is a property of the platform list: a LazyColumn with reverseLayout. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: For a conversation or a log that grows at the bottom and should follow new entries while the person is at the end.
whenNotToUse: For a list read from the top, such as search results, use a normal LazyColumn. For a short thread inside a screen that already scrolls, use a Column.
api: @Composable fun LazyColumn(modifier: Modifier = Modifier, state: LazyListState = rememberLazyListState(), contentPadding: PaddingValues = PaddingValues(0.dp), reverseLayout: Boolean = false, ..., content: LazyListScope.() -> Unit)
suspend fun LazyListState.animateScrollToItem(index: Int, scrollOffset: Int = 0)
suspend fun LazyListState.scrollToItem(index: Int, scrollOffset: Int = 0)
val LazyListState.firstVisibleItemIndex: Int

states.name: at the bottom
states.description: With reverseLayout, item 0 (the newest) is at the bottom; while it is the first visible item, new items appear at the bottom and the list stays there.

states.name: scrolled up
states.description: The person's position is kept while items are added. animateScrollToItem(0) returns to the newest entry; scrollToItem(0) does so without animation.

appearance: No appearance of its own: messages use Monarch components and follow the theme in light, dark and high contrast.
platformNotes: The web ships a hook and a headless container that measure the scroller, pin it while the person is within 48 pixels of the bottom and report atBottom. In Compose, reverseLayout lays the list out from the bottom, so pinning is the list's own behavior and there is no Monarch type. atBottom is a derivedStateOf on firstVisibleItemIndex == 0, which can show a Jump to latest button. Give the messages in newest-first order, with stable keys. iOS uses defaultScrollAnchor(.bottom) on a ScrollView.
accessibility: System behavior: TalkBack moves through the items and scrolls the list as it goes.
Scrolling to the newest entry does not move TalkBack focus.
Use scrollToItem instead of animateScrollToItem when MonarchTheme.motion.reducedMotion is true; the example does.
edgeCases: With reverseLayout the item order is newest first; pass the messages reversed or index from the end.
Content shorter than the list is laid out from the bottom.
While a message streams and grows, the list keeps the bottom edge of item 0 in place only while the person is at the bottom.
A LazyColumn inside a vertical scroll needs a bounded height.

title: AiSettingsSection
wrapsNative: MonarchSectionCard with androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow in its footer; rows are MonarchSwitchRow, MonarchFormField with MonarchSelect, and MonarchSecretField for the provider key
summary: A recipe, not a component: workspace AI settings in a settings card (AI on or off per app, data sharing, memory, conversation retention and a bring-your-own provider key), kept as a draft until Save changes.
whenToUse: On a workspace settings screen where admins decide where AI is available and how it handles data.
whenNotToUse: For switches that save one by one as they change, use MonarchSwitchSettingsList. For a spending limit, use MonarchAiSpendCap; for the model choice, MonarchAiModelPicker.
api: MonarchSectionCard(title = "AI", description = …, busy = saving, footer = { … Discard and Save changes … }) { rows }
MonarchSwitchRow(checked = id in apps, onCheckedChange = …, label = appLabel)
MonarchFormField(label = "Conversation history", helperText = …) { controlModifier -> MonarchSelect(…, modifier = controlModifier) }
MonarchSecretField(value = apiKey, label = "<Provider> API key", onValueChange = …, helperText = …, saved = keyConfigured)

options.name: apps
options.type: List of app ids and labels
options.description: One MonarchSwitchRow per app under a "Use AI in" heading; leave the group out when there are no apps.

options.name: dirty
options.description: The draft differs from the saved settings, or a new key was typed: the footer says so and enables Discard and Save changes.

options.name: saving
options.description: Passed to Save changes' loading and the card's busy; disable the rows meanwhile.

options.name: read only
options.description: Every row disabled, the reason as the description, and no footer.

states.name: ready
states.description: The saved settings with Discard and Save changes disabled.

states.name: dirty
states.description: "You have unsaved changes." in a polite live region, Discard and Save changes enabled.

states.name: provider chosen
states.description: A secret field for the provider's key; a saved key shows as set and is never sent back to the screen.

states.name: saving
states.description: Save changes shows its loading state and the card reads busy.

states.name: read only
states.description: Rows disabled and the reason shown under the title.

states.name: save failed
states.description: Keep the draft and show the error in a MonarchInlineNotice in the card.

appearance: Every part is an existing Monarch component: the section card's surface, border and header, switch rows, form fields with selects, the secret field, and small buttons in a footer. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web ships AiSettingsSection as one component with a value, a draft and onSave. On Android, as for settings-section, it is a recipe: MonarchSectionCard gives the card, the busy state and the footer slot, and the rows are existing Monarch rows, so the app keeps the draft and the saved value itself. The web shows the apps with SwitchSettingsList; that component saves each switch as it changes, so this recipe uses MonarchSwitchRow for the apps to keep them in the same draft as the other rows. The web's NativeSelect is MonarchSelect, its SecretField with isSet is MonarchSecretField with saved. The web's bot icon in the heading is left out because Monarch bundles no icons. iOS has not covered this entry yet.
accessibility: The card title is a heading, from MonarchSectionCard; "Use AI in" is a heading too.
Each switch row is one TalkBack element with the switch role; form fields name their select by the label.
The unsaved-changes line is a polite live region, so it is announced when it appears.
The provider key is a MonarchSecretField: hidden by default, with a reveal button, and a saved key read as set.
Discard and Save changes are MonarchButtons with 48dp targets; the footer wraps at large font sizes.
edgeCases: Apps missing from the saved settings count as off.
Changing the provider clears a typed key; leaving the key blank keeps the saved one.
Send the key only when one was typed, and never show a saved key.
For a long settings screen, prefer one MonarchFormActionsBar for the whole screen over a footer per section.

examples.title: Workspace AI settings
examples.template:
MonarchSectionCard(
    title = {{messages.title}},
    description = {{messages.description}},
    icon = { MonarchIcon(SampleIcons.Bot, contentDescription = null, tint = MonarchTheme.colors.aiStrong) },
    footer = {
        FlowRow(
            modifier = Modifier.weight(1f),
            horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space2, Alignment.End),
            verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space2),
            itemVerticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically,
        ) {
            MonarchButton(
                text = {{messages.discard}},
                onClick = {
                    apps = savedApps
                    sharing = savedSharing
                    memory = savedMemory
                    retention = savedRetention
                    provider = savedProvider
                },
                enabled = dirty,
            )
            MonarchButton(
                text = {{messages.save}},
                onClick = {
                    // The app saves the draft here.
                    savedApps = apps
                    savedSharing = sharing
                    savedMemory = memory
                    savedRetention = retention
                    savedProvider = provider
                },
                variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Primary,
                enabled = dirty,
            )
        }
    },
) {
    MonarchText(text = {{messages.appsTitle}}, style = MonarchTextStyle.Label, heading = true)
    MonarchText(text = {{messages.appsDescription}}, style = MonarchTextStyle.Caption)
    MonarchSwitchRow(
        checked = apps[{{apps.0.id}}] == true,
        onCheckedChange = { on -> apps = apps + ({{apps.0.id}} to on) },
        label = {{apps.0.label}},
        description = {{apps.0.description}},
    )
    MonarchSwitchRow(
        checked = apps[{{apps.1.id}}] == true,
        onCheckedChange = { on -> apps = apps + ({{apps.1.id}} to on) },
        label = {{apps.1.label}},
        description = {{apps.1.description}},
    )
    MonarchSwitchRow(
        checked = apps[{{apps.2.id}}] == true,
        onCheckedChange = { on -> apps = apps + ({{apps.2.id}} to on) },
        label = {{apps.2.label}},
    )
    MonarchSwitchRow(
        checked = sharing,
        onCheckedChange = { sharing = it },
        label = {{messages.dataSharing}},
        description = {{messages.dataSharingDescription}},
    )
    MonarchSwitchRow(
        checked = memory,
        onCheckedChange = { memory = it },
        label = {{messages.memory}},
        description = {{messages.memoryDescription}},
    )
    MonarchFormField(
        label = {{messages.retention}},
        helperText = {{messages.retentionDescription}},
    ) { controlModifier ->
        MonarchSelect(
            options = listOf(
                MonarchSelectOption({{retentionOptions.0.value}}, {{retentionOptions.0.label}}),
                MonarchSelectOption({{retentionOptions.1.value}}, {{retentionOptions.1.label}}),
                MonarchSelectOption({{retentionOptions.2.value}}, {{retentionOptions.2.label}}),
                MonarchSelectOption({{retentionOptions.3.value}}, {{retentionOptions.3.label}}),
            ),
            selected = retention,
            onSelect = { retention = it },
            modifier = controlModifier,
        )
    }
    MonarchFormField(
        label = {{messages.provider}},
        helperText = {{messages.providerDescription}},
    ) { controlModifier ->
        MonarchSelect(
            options = listOf(
                MonarchSelectOption({{value.provider}}, {{messages.providerDefault}}),
                MonarchSelectOption({{providers.0.id}}, {{providers.0.label}}),
                MonarchSelectOption({{providers.1.id}}, {{providers.1.label}}),
            ),
            selected = provider,
            onSelect = { provider = it },
            modifier = controlModifier,
        )
    }
}
examples.code:
MonarchSectionCard(
    title = "AI",
    description = "Choose where AI is available in this workspace and how it handles your data.",
    icon = { MonarchIcon(SampleIcons.Bot, contentDescription = null, tint = MonarchTheme.colors.aiStrong) },
    footer = {
        FlowRow(
            modifier = Modifier.weight(1f),
            horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space2, Alignment.End),
            verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space2),
            itemVerticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically,
        ) {
            MonarchButton(
                text = "Discard",
                onClick = {
                    apps = savedApps
                    sharing = savedSharing
                    memory = savedMemory
                    retention = savedRetention
                    provider = savedProvider
                },
                enabled = dirty,
            )
            MonarchButton(
                text = "Save changes",
                onClick = {
                    // The app saves the draft here.
                    savedApps = apps
                    savedSharing = sharing
                    savedMemory = memory
                    savedRetention = retention
                    savedProvider = provider
                },
                variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Primary,
                enabled = dirty,
            )
        }
    },
) {
    MonarchText(text = "Use AI in", style = MonarchTextStyle.Label, heading = true)
    MonarchText(text = "Turn AI features on or off for each app.", style = MonarchTextStyle.Caption)
    MonarchSwitchRow(
        checked = apps["docs"] == true,
        onCheckedChange = { on -> apps = apps + ("docs" to on) },
        label = "Documents",
        description = "Summaries, drafts and answers about pages.",
    )
    MonarchSwitchRow(
        checked = apps["mail"] == true,
        onCheckedChange = { on -> apps = apps + ("mail" to on) },
        label = "Mail",
        description = "Reply suggestions and thread summaries.",
    )
    MonarchSwitchRow(
        checked = apps["calendar"] == true,
        onCheckedChange = { on -> apps = apps + ("calendar" to on) },
        label = "Calendar",
    )
    MonarchSwitchRow(
        checked = sharing,
        onCheckedChange = { sharing = it },
        label = "Share data to improve AI",
        description = "Allow prompts and responses to be used to improve AI quality. Off keeps them private to this workspace.",

name: MonarchAiSharedSession
title: AiSharedSession
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow with MonarchAvatarGroup and MonarchButton, androidx.compose.material3.ModalBottomSheet with androidx.compose.material3.ListItem and androidx.compose.material3.FilterChip for the participant list
summary: The presence and turn-taking bar of an AI conversation shared by several people and agents: who is here, who is typing, whose request is being answered, what waits, and whether you may send.
whenToUse: Above or below the thread of an AI conversation that several people use at once, so everyone sees whose turn it is and what waits.
whenNotToUse: For presence in a document without an assistant use MonarchPresenceAvatars. For the agents of a task without people use MonarchAiMultiAgentRoster.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchAiSharedSession(participants: List<MonarchAiSharedSessionParticipant>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, answering: MonarchAiSharedSessionAnswering? = null, queue: List<MonarchAiSharedSessionRequest> = emptyList(), maxVisible: Int = 4, following: Set<String> = emptySet(), onFollowingChange: ((Set<String>) -> Unit)? = null, queueExpanded: Boolean? = null, onQueueExpandedChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, accessRequested: Boolean = false, announcesChanges: Boolean = true, onWithdraw: ((id: String) -> Unit)? = null, onReorder: ((ids: List<String>, move: MonarchAiSharedSessionMove) -> Unit)? = null, onRemove: ((id: String) -> Unit)? = null, onInvite: (() -> Unit)? = null, onRequestAccess: (() -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiSharedSessionLabels = MonarchAiSharedSessionLabels())

class MonarchAiSharedSessionParticipant(id: String, name: String, kind: MonarchAiSharedSessionKind = MonarchAiSharedSessionKind.Person, role: MonarchAiSharedSessionRole = MonarchAiSharedSessionRole.Editor, presence: MonarchAiSharedSessionPresence = MonarchAiSharedSessionPresence.Active, activity: MonarchAiSharedSessionActivity? = null, you: Boolean = false, image: Painter? = null)
enum class MonarchAiSharedSessionKind { Person, Agent }
enum class MonarchAiSharedSessionRole { Owner, Editor, Viewer }
enum class MonarchAiSharedSessionPresence { Active, Idle, Away }
enum class MonarchAiSharedSessionActivity { Typing, Speaking, Reviewing }
class MonarchAiSharedSessionAnswering(participantId: String, forParticipantId: String, label: String? = null)
class MonarchAiSharedSessionRequest(id: String, participantId: String, preview: String)
data class MonarchAiSharedSessionMove(id: String, from: Int, to: Int)

class MonarchAiSharedSessionLabels(label, listTitle, people, agents, agentKind, assistant, someone, quiet, queueTitle, withdraw, remove, moveUp, moveDown, invite, follow, viewerNotice, requestAccess, accessRequested, done: String? = null; here: ((people: Int, agents: Int) -> String)?; showAll, several, queueCount, queueToggle: ((Int) -> String)?; nameWithYou, followLabel: ((String) -> String)?; role, presence, activity: per-enum ((…) -> String)?; activityLine: ((MonarchAiSharedSessionActivity, names: String, count: Int) -> String)?; answering: ((agent: String, requester: String, label: String?) -> String)?; answeringYou: ((agent: String, label: String?) -> String)?; requestAction: ((action: String, requester: String, position: Int) -> String)?; moved: ((requester: String, position: Int, total: Int) -> String)?, all defaulting to null)

options.name: participants
options.description: Everyone in the session, people and agents, in display order. Mark one person you; their role decides what they can do.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the bar.

options.name: answering
options.description: The answer in progress: which agent, whose request and an optional short label.

options.name: queue
options.description: Requests waiting for their turn, first in line first.

options.name: maxVisible
options.description: The avatars shown before "+N". At least one; with exactly one too many, all are shown.

options.name: following
options.description: The ids of the people you follow.

options.name: onFollowingChange
options.description: Shows a Follow toggle beside every other person in the list; receives the new set.

options.name: queueExpanded
options.description: Whether the queue is shown, when the app owns it. null lets the Queue button own it.

options.name: onQueueExpandedChange
options.description: Called when the Queue button is pressed, with the new value.

options.name: accessRequested
options.description: Replaces a viewer's Request access button with "Access requested".

options.name: announcesChanges
options.description: Announces status changes and queue moves to TalkBack.

options.name: onWithdraw
options.description: Shows Withdraw on your own requests.

options.name: onReorder
options.description: Shows Move up and Move down to an owner; receives the request ids in their new order and the move.

options.name: onRemove
options.description: Shows Remove on other people's requests to an owner.

options.name: onInvite
options.description: Shows an Invite button; the app opens its own invite flow.

options.name: onRequestAccess
options.description: Shows Request access in a viewer's notice.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

states.name: quiet
states.description: "No requests in progress" in the subtle text color.

states.name: answering
states.description: The answering agent's avatar ring turns (still when animations are removed) and the status starts with whose request it answers, "your request" when it is yours.

states.name: activity
states.description: Other people typing, speaking or reviewing are named, two at most, else counted; your own activity is left out.

states.name: queue
states.description: "Queue (2)" shows or hides the waiting requests; your own requests are on the subtle AI fill.

states.name: owner
states.description: Move up, Move down and Remove on requests when the callbacks are given; the moves at the ends are disabled.

states.name: viewer
states.description: A notice "You can watch but not send" with Request access, or "Access requested".

states.name: empty
states.description: No avatars; only the status line.

appearance: The status line is caption text in the default role (subtle when quiet). The viewer notice is on the muted fill; your requests on the subtle AI fill with the AI border, others on the subtle fill with the subtle border. Avatars carry presence dots (online, away, offline colors). All colors are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web opens the participant list in a popover; Android presents it in a Material 3 ModalBottomSheet, as iOS uses a sheet, and the whole stack is one button because overlapping avatars are too small to tap. Follow toggles are Material 3 FilterChips with a selected state. The web throttles announcements with announceInterval; as on iOS, each change of the announced clauses is announced, and typing and speaking never are. Follows are a hoisted Set with onFollowingChange instead of following, defaultFollowing and onFollowChange; the queue's open state is optionally hoisted with queueExpanded and onQueueExpandedChange; the list's open state is internal. The Queue button has expand and collapse actions, so TalkBack reads its expanded state. Presence is the avatar's presence dot (active online, idle away, away offline) and always written in the list. The web restores keyboard focus after a queue action; Compose does not move focus, the move is announced instead. The web passes a locale for numbers and lists of names; Android uses string resources. The parity map listed presence-avatars; as on iOS this bar uses MonarchAvatarGroup directly because it mixes people and agents. Marked experimental because it is a domain composite that no Rook app has adopted yet.
accessibility: The bar is a traversal group named "Shared session".
The avatar stack is one button read as "2 people and 1 agent here" with every visible participant's name, role or "AI agent", presence and activity; its click label is "Show all 3 participants".

In the list each participant row is merged into one element with name, "(you)", role, presence and what they are doing; Follow toggles are separate, named "Follow Sam Lee" and selected while following.
Changes of who is being answered, of who is reviewing and of the queue length are announced through a polite live region; typing and speaking are not, and neither is the first status.
Queue buttons are named with the request, for example "Move up: request 2, from Sam Lee"; a move made here is announced with the new position.
Every button has a 48dp touch target; text wraps at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: An answering agent or requester missing from participants is named "Assistant" or "Someone".
More than two people with the same activity are counted ("3 people are typing…").
Without a participant marked you nobody can manage the queue and no viewer notice is shown.
Queue buttons appear only when their callback is given.

name: MonarchAiSlashCommands
title: AiSlashCommands
wrapsNative: MonarchSlashMenu (MonarchListRow rows in a androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn placed above the prompt field), found with MonarchSlashMenuQuery over androidx.compose.ui.text.input.TextFieldValue
summary: The / command menu of an AI prompt: commands such as /summarize filtered by what is typed after the slash, replaced with the app's text when picked.
whenToUse: Above an AI prompt field, to offer commands that change the request or run an action (/summarize, /translate, /clear).
whenNotToUse: For inserting blocks in a document editor use MonarchSlashMenu; for @mentions use MonarchMentionPicker; for saved prompts use MonarchAiPromptTemplatePicker.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiSlashCommands(value: TextFieldValue, onValueChange: (TextFieldValue) -> Unit, commands: List<MonarchAiSlashCommand>, onSelect: (MonarchAiSlashCommand) -> String?, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, trigger: Char = '/', labels: MonarchAiSlashCommandsLabels = MonarchAiSlashCommandsLabels())
class MonarchAiSlashCommand(val id: String, val name: String, val description: String? = null, val icon: Painter? = null, val keywords: List<String> = emptyList(), val enabled: Boolean = true)
class MonarchAiSlashCommandsLabels(label: String? = null, empty: ((typed: String) -> String)? = null, count: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null)

options.name: value
options.description: The prompt field's text and caret; the command is the word before the caret that starts with the trigger.

options.name: onValueChange
options.description: Called with the text and caret after a command is picked.

options.name: commands
options.description: Every command, in the app's order.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Called with the picked command; returns the text that replaces the typed command ("/summarize " keeps it), or null to remove it.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the strip.

options.name: trigger
options.description: The character that starts a command; also written before each name.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for "Commands", the empty message and the count.

states.name: closed
states.description: Nothing is drawn while no command is being typed.

states.name: open
states.description: The matching commands as rows with "/name" and the description.

states.name: no match
states.description: "No commands match “/text”" in the muted color, announced.

states.name: disabled command
states.description: The row is in the disabled colors and cannot be picked.

appearance: MonarchSlashMenu's strip: the raised surface with a subtle line above it, names in the default text color, descriptions muted, disabled rows in the disabled text color. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web AiSlashCommands is a listbox under AiPromptInput's trigger with arrow keys, Enter and Tab to pick, wired by the useAiSlashCommands hook, and combineAiPromptMenus merges it with mentions. On Android it works over any text field's TextFieldValue: the strip sits directly above the field because Compose gives no caret rectangle to anchor a popup to, focus stays in the field, and commands are picked by tapping a row (the web's highlighted option and keyboard picking are not offered). MonarchSlashMenu's own filter also matches the command id. The web's onSelect may return nothing; here it returns String?. Experimental until a Rook app adopts it. No iOS entry exists yet.
accessibility: The strip is a traversal group named "Commands", and a polite live region whose state is the number of matches ("4 commands") or the no-match message.
Each command is a button row with a 48dp touch target, read as "/name" and its description.
A disabled command is read as disabled and cannot be picked.
Focus stays in the text field while the menu is open.
edgeCases: A slash inside a word ("and/or") does not open the menu.
A leading slash in a command's name is ignored.
Long descriptions wrap; the list scrolls past its maximum height.

name: MonarchAiSourceList
title: AiSourceList
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of clickable source rows with MonarchFavicon, and a MonarchButton toggle; androidx.compose.ui.platform.LocalUriHandler opens links
summary: The block of sources under an AI answer: each with its favicon, [n] number, title, host, product, kind and snippet, grouped into Used and Considered, and collapsed to the first few.
whenToUse: Under an assistant reply that cites sources, so people can see and open what the answer is based on, in the same numbering as the citation markers in the text.
whenNotToUse: For one citation inside the text use MonarchAiCitation. For a preview of one source with the quoted passage use MonarchAiSourcePreview. For a list of links that are not AI sources use MonarchLinkCard or a plain list.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiSourceList(items: List<MonarchAiSourceListItem>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, collapseAfter: Int? = 3, initiallyExpanded: Boolean = false, numbered: Boolean = true, favicon: (@Composable (MonarchAiSourcePart) -> Painter?)? = null, labels: MonarchAiSourceListLabels = MonarchAiSourceListLabels(), onOpen: ((MonarchAiSourceListItem) -> Unit)? = null)

data class MonarchAiSourceListItem(source: MonarchAiSourcePart, used: Boolean = true, snippet: String? = null) { val id: String; companion object { fun sources(message: MonarchAiConversationMessage): List<MonarchAiSourceListItem> } }

class MonarchAiSourceListLabels(heading: String? = null, used: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, considered: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, showAll: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, showFewer: String? = null, source: ((number: Int, title: String) -> String)? = null, openSource: String? = null, kind: ((kind: MonarchAiSourceKind) -> String)? = null)

options.name: items
options.description: The sources in citation order; the first is [1]. Each wraps the conversation model's MonarchAiSourcePart with used and a snippet.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the list.

options.name: collapseAfter
options.description: How many sources show while collapsed. null never collapses.

options.name: initiallyExpanded
options.description: Whether a collapsible list starts expanded.

options.name: numbered
options.description: Shows the [n] number that matches each source's citation marker.

options.name: favicon
options.description: The favicon the app loaded for a source; null shows MonarchFavicon's letter tile. Monarch loads no images.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the heading, group headings, toggle titles, spoken source name, tap action name and kind names.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Makes each source a button that calls this, for example to show MonarchAiSourcePreview. Without it, safe addresses open through LocalUriHandler.

states.name: ungrouped
states.description: All sources are used: one list under the heading.

states.name: grouped
states.description: Some sources were considered but not used: Used (n) and Considered (n) groups, used first.

states.name: collapsed
states.description: More sources than collapseAfter: the first few of used then considered show, with Show all n sources.

states.name: expanded
states.description: Every source shows, with Show fewer.

states.name: actionable
states.description: With onOpen each row is a button; otherwise a row with a safe address opens it and its title uses the link color.

states.name: plain
states.description: A source without onOpen and without a safe address is text in the default color.

appearance: The heading and group headings are muted text; titles use the link color when the row opens and default text otherwise; the [n] number, the meta line and the two-line snippet are muted. The favicon is MonarchFavicon at its small size, with its letter tile when there is no painter. A pressed row shows the Material ripple.
platformNotes: As on iOS, the whole row is the touch target, a button with onOpen or a link opened through LocalUriHandler otherwise (the web opens a new tab from the title). The web's messages object is one labels value with lambdas for the counted strings. Sources come from the conversation model; MonarchAiSourceListItem adds the web's used and snippet fields, and sources(message) gives a message's sources in first-appearance order. iOS uses isUsed, isNumbered and isInitiallyExpanded; Android drops the is prefix, as Material 3 does. The favicon field of a source is an address; Monarch loads no images, so the app passes painters through favicon, and a source without one shows a letter tile instead of the web's kind glyph. The parity map names collapsible, but only the sources after the first few are hidden, so the toggle is a ghost MonarchButton under the list rather than a MonarchCollapsible header. iOS's opensSource hint is the tap action name openSource here, because TalkBack reads it as "double tap to open the source".
accessibility: The list heading and the Used and Considered headings are headings.
Each source is one element read as "Source 1: title", then host, product and kind, then the snippet; with numbered false the number is left out.
A row that opens is a button at least 48dp high whose tap action is read as "open the source".
The favicon is decorative and hidden.
The toggle is a separate button whose text says Show all 5 sources or Show fewer.
edgeCases: Unsafe addresses such as javascript: are never opened; the row becomes plain text unless onOpen is given.
The group headings count every source, also the ones hidden while collapsed; a group with no source shown while collapsed has no heading.
collapseAfter 0 hides every source until the list is expanded.
Long titles and meta lines wrap; snippets stop at two lines with an ellipsis.
An empty list shows only the heading; leave the list out when a reply has no sources.

whenNotToUse: For the list of all sources use MonarchAiSourceList. To open a source in full, open its address directly. For a link preview in a chat message use MonarchLinkCard.

options.description: Adds a Close button that calls this, for example to hide the sheet.

options.description: Called with the address instead of opening it with LocalUriHandler, for example to open a Custom Tab.

states.name: quote found
states.description: The passage is highlighted in its paragraph and scrolled to the middle of the viewport.

states.name: quote not found
states.description: The quote is shown on its own under a Quoted passage caption, above the content.

states.name: quote only

states.name: no original

appearance: The title in the subheading style and default text, the meta line in muted caption text, the favicon at the medium size. The highlighted passage has the AI subtle fill and an underline; the quote block has a bar in the AI border color at its start. Open original is a full-width secondary button and Close a small ghost button.
platformNotes: The web component is a side sheet with open and onOpenChange; on Android, as on iOS, it is the content of a sheet: the app presents it in a MonarchBottomSheet, which owns the drag handle, the scrim, the back gesture and returning TalkBack focus. The web accepts arbitrary nodes as content and scrolls to the first mark; here content is plain text. Open original opens through LocalUriHandler or onOpenOriginal instead of a new tab. The underline of the passage is in the text color, because a Compose SpanStyle cannot color an underline (iOS uses the AI citation color). The favicon is a Painter the app loads; the kind names are shared with MonarchAiSourceList. iOS takes originalURL as a URL; Android takes a String.
accessibility: The source title is a heading.
The highlighted passage has an underline as well as a fill, and its paragraph reads "Quoted passage" as its state.
The passage is scrolled into view when the preview appears, with the theme's motion, which is an immediate jump when animations are off.
Close and Open original are buttons with 48dp touch targets; Open original appears only for safe addresses.
The text can be selected.
edgeCases: Only the first match of the quote is highlighted.
A quote that crosses a blank line is highlighted in each paragraph it covers.
Characters such as . or ( in the quote are matched literally.
A javascript: or relative address shows no Open original.
Very long content scrolls inside the preview; Open original stays under it.
The text scrolls itself, so the preview needs a bounded height (a sheet gives one) and cannot sit inside another vertically scrolling container.

name: MonarchAiSpendCap
title: AiSpendCap
wrapsNative: Card with androidx.compose.material3.LinearProgressIndicator in the tone of the state, MonarchStatusBadge, MonarchInlineNotice, and an inline form of MonarchCurrencyInput, MonarchSelect, MonarchRadioCardGroup and MonarchButtons; removal is confirmed in androidx.compose.material3.AlertDialog
summary: A spending limit for AI usage: what has been spent against the limit this period, whether that is fine, close or reached, and a form to change the limit, when to warn and what happens at the limit.
whenToUse: In workspace or account settings where an admin sets how much AI may spend per day, week or month, and where people check how much is left.
whenNotToUse: Not for token or credit usage without money, which is MonarchAiUsageMeter. Not for plan quotas of a subscription, which is MonarchUsageMeter.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable public fun MonarchAiSpendCap(spent: Long, limit: Long?, currencyCode: String, period: MonarchAiSpendCapPeriod, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, unit: MonarchAiSpendCapUnit = MonarchAiSpendCapUnit.Minor, warnAt: Double = MonarchAiSpendCapTokens.DEFAULT_WARN_AT, behavior: MonarchAiSpendCapBehavior = MonarchAiSpendCapBehavior.Pause, resetsAtMillis: Long? = null, breakdown: List<MonarchAiSpendCapBreakdownItem> = emptyList(), maxLimit: Long? = null, warnAtOptions: List<Double> = MonarchAiSpendCapTokens.DefaultWarnAtOptions, editing: Boolean? = null, onEditingChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, canEdit: Boolean = true, saving: Boolean = false, timeZone: String? = null, labels: MonarchAiSpendCapLabels = MonarchAiSpendCapLabels(), onSave: ((MonarchAiSpendCapSettings) -> Unit)? = null, onRequestIncrease: (() -> Unit)? = null)
