public class MonarchAiSpendCapBreakdownItem(id: String, label: String, spent: Long)
public enum class MonarchAiSpendCapPeriod { Day, Week, Month }
public enum class MonarchAiSpendCapBehavior { Pause, Notify }
public enum class MonarchAiSpendCapState { Ok, Warning, Reached, NoLimit }
public enum class MonarchAiSpendCapUnit { Minor, Micros }

public class MonarchAiSpendCapLabels(title, period, state, spentOfLimit, spentNoLimit, meterLabel, remaining, over, warnsAt, behaviorSummary, resets, breakdownLabel, edit, setLimit, pausedTitle, pausedBody, raiseLimit, requestIncrease, readOnly, amountLabel, amountHint, errorRequired, errorPositive, errorMax, belowSpent, warnAtLabel, warnAtOption, behaviorLabel, behaviorOption, behaviorDescription, save, saveAnyway, cancel, removeLimit, removeConfirmTitle, removeConfirmBody, removeCancel, announce), every parameter nullable with a null default

options.name: spent
options.description: Spent so far this period, as an integer in unit. Negative values count as zero.

options.name: limit
options.description: The limit as an integer in unit, or null when none is set.

options.name: currencyCode
options.description: The ISO 4217 code of every amount.

options.name: period
options.description: The window the limit applies to: day, week or month.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the card.

options.name: unit
options.description: What the integers count: the currency's minor unit, or micros (millionths of the major unit).

options.name: warnAt
options.description: The share of the limit at which the state becomes warning.

options.name: behavior
options.description: What happens at the limit: pause and ask, or keep going and tell.

options.name: resetsAtMillis
options.description: When the period starts again, in epoch milliseconds (UTC); shown with the day and month, and the time for a daily limit.

options.name: breakdown
options.description: Spending per agent or feature, listed under the bar.

options.name: maxLimit
options.description: The highest limit this person may set.

options.name: warnAtOptions
options.description: The warn-at choices; the current value is always offered, values outside 0 to 1 are left out.

options.name: editing
options.description: Whether the form is open, when the app controls it. Kept inside, closed at first, when null.

options.name: onEditingChange
options.description: Called when the form opens or closes.

options.name: canEdit
options.description: Whether this person may change the limit. false shows a read-only note and no form.

options.name: saving
options.description: Shows Save as busy and disables the form while the app saves.

options.name: timeZone
options.description: The time zone of the reset date. An IANA id such as Europe/Berlin; null, or an id the device does not know, is the device's zone.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: onSave
options.description: Runs with the new settings on Save, or with a null limit once removal is confirmed; the form then closes. Nothing is applied by the component.

options.name: onRequestIncrease
options.description: For people who cannot edit: adds "Request a higher limit".

states.name: ok
states.description: "Within limit" in a neutral badge and a muted bar.

states.name: warning
states.description: "Close to the limit" in a warning badge and a warning bar.

states.name: reached
states.description: "Limit reached" in a danger badge and a full danger bar; with Pause, a danger notice says AI is paused and offers Raise limit, or Request a higher limit for people who cannot edit.

states.name: no limit
states.description: "No limit set", no bar, and Set a limit instead of Edit limit.

states.name: editing
states.description: The amount field, the warn-at choice, the behavior cards, Remove limit, Cancel and Save.

states.name: below spent
states.description: A limit below what is spent shows a warning notice and Save becomes Save anyway; saving the same amount again confirms.

states.name: invalid
states.description: An empty, zero, negative or too-high amount shows an error on the field.

states.name: saving
states.description: Save shows its loading state and the form is disabled.

states.name: read only
states.description: "Only a workspace admin can change this limit.", with Request a higher limit when given.

appearance: A card on the surface color with the subtle border and the large radius; the state is a small status badge in its tone, the amount line is strong default text, the bar's track is the emphasis background and its fill the accent, warning or danger solid role, facts and the breakdown caption are muted captions. Every color is a theme role, so it follows light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Same parameters as iOS where Compose allows: isEditing as a Binding becomes editing with onEditingChange, isSaving is saving, resetsAt is resetsAtMillis (epoch milliseconds, as Monarch for Android takes every date), and the integers are Long. The web builds the form with a native select and a radio group and confirms removal inline; Android uses MonarchSelect for the warn-at choice, MonarchRadioCardGroup for the behavior, and a Material 3 AlertDialog for removal, as iOS uses a confirmationDialog. The amount field is MonarchCurrencyInput in minor units, which accepts only numbers, so the web's "not an amount" error does not arise; amounts in micros are rounded to the currency's digits in the field. The web's children slot is left out; place content beside the card. The bar is a Material 3 LinearProgressIndicator coloured by the state, without Material's track gap and stop dot. The state badge shows the web's state glyph and the Edit limit button the web's pencil, both bundled by Monarch. Times use the configuration locale and an optional timeZone in place of the web's locale and timeZone props. The composable is experimental: an AI settings pattern that waits for a Rook app to adopt it.
accessibility: The title is a heading and the card is one traversal group.
The state is a word in a status badge, never color alone.
The bar is named "Spent against the limit" with the amount line as its state description.

A change of state after the card appears is announced once through a polite live region, such as "AI spending limit: Close to the limit. $45.00 of $50.00 this month"; later changes of the amount are not announced.
Errors are the amount field's own error; the below-spent warning is a MonarchInlineNotice announced politely.
Removing the limit asks in an AlertDialog with a danger Remove limit and Keep limit.
Every button is a MonarchButton with a 48dp target; facts and rows wrap at large font sizes.
edgeCases: A limit of zero is always reached and draws no bar.
Spending over the limit reads "$2.10 over the limit"; the bar stays full.
Amounts in micros are rounded to the currency's digits when shown and when typed.
Currencies without minor units, such as JPY, show whole amounts.
A saved warn-at share the list cannot offer starts the form on the nearest choice.
Long breakdown labels wrap.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Called with the starter the user chose.

options.name: modifier

platformNotes: The parity map named LazyVerticalGrid; the starters are laid out in plain rows instead, because four to six of them sit inside a screen that already scrolls and a lazy grid cannot be nested in a vertical scroll. Cells in one row share their height, as in the web grid. The web tints a card on hover; touch has no hover, so the tint is the pressed state (a mouse hover also tints). onSelect receives the starter (the web passes the prompt and the starter). The icon is a composable slot, not an SF Symbol name as on iOS.
accessibility: The group is a traversal group with the content description "Suggested prompts".
Each starter is one button that TalkBack reads as its title and prompt; with hidePrompt only the title.
Each starter is at least 48dp high.
The icon is decorative and hidden from TalkBack.
The title wraps at large font sizes and the grid becomes one column from font scale 1.5.
edgeCases: The prompt is cut after two lines; TalkBack still reads all of it.
Starters need unique ids.
A last row with fewer starters keeps their width the same as the others.

name: MonarchAiStopButton
title: AiStopButton

summary: The Stop control of a streaming assistant response: a secondary button with a filled square, replaced by "Stopped." and an optional Continue button once the response has stopped.
whenToUse: Next to a response that is streaming, so the person can stop it.
whenNotToUse: For cancelling a form or a dialog use MonarchButton with "Cancel". For a task with progress use the cancel action of that task's component.

options.name: stopped
options.description: Whether the response has stopped. Replaces Stop with the stopped text.

options.name: showLabel
options.description: Shows the title beside the square. When false the title is still the TalkBack name.

platformNotes: The web offers sm and md; Android takes any MonarchButtonSize, so Lg also works, as on iOS. The web's buttonProps pass-through has no equivalent: pass a modifier. The stopped text is a live region that stays in the layout from the start, so the change is announced; the web uses a role="status" element in the same way and iOS posts an announcement. The stopped text is a polite live region that is in the layout before it has text, so "Stopped." is announced when the response stops.
Stop and Continue keep a 48dp touch target at every size.
When the stopped text and Continue do not fit on one line, Continue moves under it.
If Stop had keyboard focus when it was replaced, focus moves to Continue.
edgeCases: The component does not track the request; it shows Stop until stopped is set.
stopped with no onContinue shows only the text; there is nothing to activate.
The empty stopped text keeps the height of one line in the row while Stop shows.

options.description: The modifier of the column.

options.name: showCaret
options.description: Shows the still caret after the text while streaming.

options.name: showLinkHosts
options.description: Passed to MonarchAiMarkdown.

options.name: onOpenLink
options.description: Passed to MonarchAiMarkdown.

options.name: image
options.description: Passed to MonarchAiMarkdown.

options.description: Passed to MonarchAiMarkdown; complete is false for a code block still arriving.

states.name: streaming
states.description: The last block is drawn with open emphasis and code spans closed, link targets hidden and unconfirmed table rows held back; a caret follows the text.

platformNotes: iOS has no entry for this id yet. The web passes completed blocks to AiMarkdown; Compose draws each block with its own keyed MonarchAiMarkdown so recomposition skips finished blocks, with the gaps MonarchAiMarkdown uses between blocks. The web's caret sits inline after the last character and blinks; here it is a still bar on its own line under the text, because MonarchAiMarkdown has no trailing slot and an endless blink adds nothing on touch. Compose has no aria-busy, so nothing marks the text as busy for TalkBack; the announcements carry the progress. The announcement interval is fixed at the web's minimum of one second instead of an announceInterval option. headingLevelOffset, allowImageHosts, resolveImageUrl, renderMath and codeBlockProps have no counterpart: MonarchAiMarkdown takes image and codeBlock slots instead.
accessibility: A polite live region on an always-present node announces new complete sentences and paragraphs, never single tokens, at most once a second.
Code blocks and tables are announced as "Code block" and "Table" instead of being read out.
When streaming stops, the rest of the text and "Response complete" are announced; with announceComplete false the end is held until it is true.
Text that was never streamed here is not announced, and announces false turns announcements off.
The caret is hidden from TalkBack.
Each block keeps MonarchAiMarkdown's semantics: headings, task states and table positions; text wraps at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: A table header that has no delimiter row yet is not shown, so it never flashes as a paragraph of pipes.
An unfinished link shows its text until the closing bracket of its target arrives.
A regenerated answer that does not start with the previous text starts the announcements over.
Text that changes in the middle rather than growing is parsed again from the start; finished blocks then get new identities.
Empty text while streaming shows only the caret.

name: MonarchAiStructuredAnswer
title: AiStructuredAnswer
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column card over MonarchDescriptionList, with MonarchBadge, MonarchAiMarkdown and androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow
summary: A model's structured output shown as labelled fields (text, lists, numbers, badges or Markdown) in a card marked AI answer, with placeholders for fields still streaming.
whenToUse: When the model returns structured data that people scan and compare: an interview brief, a lead summary, fields extracted from a document.
whenNotToUse: For a free-form answer, use MonarchAiMarkdown in the conversation. For many rows of the same shape, use MonarchAiTableAnswer. For facts the product already knows, use MonarchDescriptionList.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiStructuredAnswer(schema: List<MonarchAiStructuredField>, data: Map<String, MonarchAiJSON>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, layout: MonarchAiStructuredAnswerLayout = MonarchAiStructuredAnswerLayout.List, streaming: Boolean = false, title: String? = null, locale: Locale? = null, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, onOpenLink: ((url: String) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiStructuredAnswerLabels = MonarchAiStructuredAnswerLabels(), actions: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null)

class MonarchAiStructuredField(key: String, label: String, type: MonarchAiStructuredFieldType = MonarchAiStructuredFieldType.Text, format: ((Double) -> String)? = null, tone: ((value: String) -> MonarchTone)? = null, wide: Boolean? = null)
enum class MonarchAiStructuredFieldType { Text, List, Number, Badge, Markdown }
enum class MonarchAiStructuredAnswerLayout { List, Grid }
class MonarchAiStructuredAnswerLabels(aiAnswer: String? = null, pending: String? = null, empty: String? = null, complete: String? = null)

options.name: schema
options.description: The fields to show, in order: key, label, type, an optional number format, badge tone and wide flag. Values without a field are ignored.

options.name: data
options.description: The values by key, usually parsed with MonarchAiJSON.parse from the model's structured output. Treated as untrusted data.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the card.

options.name: layout
options.description: List: one field per row, label beside the value where there is room. Grid: label above value, two fields per row from 640dp wide.

options.name: streaming
options.description: The answer is still arriving: missing fields show a placeholder read as Still generating, and Response complete. is announced when it turns false.

options.name: title
options.description: A title under the AI answer label, such as Interview brief.

options.name: locale
options.description: The locale of Number fields. Null uses the configuration's locale.

options.name: icon
options.description: An AI glyph before the AI answer label, tinted in the AI color. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: onOpenLink
options.description: Opens links in Markdown fields instead of the system browser.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for AI answer, Still generating, Not provided and Response complete.

options.name: actions
options.description: Controls under the fields, such as a copy button; they wrap onto more lines when narrow.

states.name: complete
states.description: Every field shows its value; a missing value shows a dash read as Not provided.

states.name: streaming
states.description: Fields still to come show a static bar in the AI subtle color, read as Still generating; the heading's state is Still generating.

states.name: grid
states.description: Labels sit above values, two fields per row from 640dp wide; List and Markdown fields take a whole row unless wide says otherwise.

appearance: A card on the surface color with the default border and large radius. The AI answer label (and the optional icon) is in the AI strong color, the title in the subheading style, labels in muted caption text and values in the body style. Badges use MonarchBadge tones; the placeholder bar uses the AI subtle color. The same roles adapt to dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web takes data as an object of unknown values and a schema with Intl.NumberFormatOptions; Android takes MonarchAiJSON values (the conversation model's JSON type) and an optional (Double) -> String format, with the locale as a java.util.Locale. The web's heading level is not offered: the AI answer label and title are one heading. The web's placeholder shimmers; on Android it is a still bar, so it needs no reduced-motion form. The grid's columns come from MonarchDescriptionList (two from 640dp) instead of responsive auto columns. The parity map lists ai-citation as a dependency, but the web component shows no citations; put MonarchAiCitation in the actions slot or after the card. iOS has no entry for this id yet. Experimental: a domain pattern until a Rook app adopts it.
accessibility: The AI answer label and the title are one TalkBack heading, so provenance is always read in words.
Each field is one element read as its label and value, from MonarchDescriptionList.
A field still to come is read as Still generating; an empty field after streaming as Not provided.
While streaming the heading's state description is Still generating.
Response complete. is announced once through a polite live region when streaming ends, never per field.
List bullets are hidden from TalkBack; links in Markdown fields and the actions stay separate elements.
Values wrap at the largest font scale and labels stack above values there.
edgeCases: Null, empty strings and empty arrays count as missing.
A Number field whose value is not a number shows the value as text; text such as 1,200 is read as a number.
A List field with a single value shows a list of one; null items in an array are skipped.
Objects and arrays in a Text field are shown as compact JSON.
Keep the schema stable while streaming so the layout does not jump.

name: MonarchAiSubagentTree
title: AiSubagentTree
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of rows with androidx.compose.foundation.selection.selectable agents and androidx.compose.foundation.clickable toggles; MonarchStatusBadge and MonarchButton
summary: A lead AI agent and the sub-agents it handed work to, as a tree with each agent's status, activity, progress and result, and actions for the selected agent.
whenToUse: For a multi-agent run, so the person can follow which agent does what, select one, and answer, open or stop it.
whenNotToUse: For one agent's steps, use MonarchAiPlan or MonarchAiChainOfSteps. For the timing of one run, use MonarchAiAgentRunTimeline or MonarchAiTraceView. For a hierarchy that is not agents, use MonarchTreeView.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchAiSubagentTree(agents: List<MonarchAiSubagent>, expandIcon: @Composable () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, selection: String? = null, expanded: Set<String>? = null, onExpandedChange: ((Set<String>) -> Unit)? = null, locale: Locale? = null, timeZone: String? = null, labels: MonarchAiSubagentTreeLabels = MonarchAiSubagentTreeLabels(), onSelect: ((MonarchAiSubagent) -> Unit)? = null, onRespond: ((MonarchAiSubagent) -> Unit)? = null, onOpen: ((MonarchAiSubagent) -> Unit)? = null, onOpenPart: ((MonarchAiSubagent) -> Unit)? = null, onStop: ((MonarchAiSubagent) -> Unit)? = null)

data class MonarchAiSubagent(id: String, name: String, status: MonarchAiSubagentStatus, role: String? = null, activity: String? = null, stepsDone: Int? = null, stepsTotal: Int? = null, toolCalls: Int? = null, startedAt: Long? = null, endedAt: Long? = null, summary: String? = null, children: List<MonarchAiSubagent> = emptyList(), partId: String? = null, messageId: String? = null)
enum class MonarchAiSubagentStatus { Working, NeedsInput, Waiting, Done, Failed, Stopped }

class MonarchAiSubagentTreeLabels(label: String? = null, status: ((MonarchAiSubagentStatus) -> String)? = null, agentCount: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, statusCount: ((status: MonarchAiSubagentStatus, count: Int) -> String)? = null, empty: String? = null, steps: ((done: Int, total: Int?) -> String)? = null, toolCalls: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, started: ((time: String) -> String)? = null, ran: ((start: String, end: String) -> String)? = null, actionsFor: ((name: String) -> String)? = null, stop: String? = null, open: String? = null, respond: String? = null, openPart: String? = null, announce: ((name: String, status: String) -> String)? = null, expand: ((name: String) -> String)? = null, collapse: ((name: String) -> String)? = null)

options.name: agents
options.description: The top-level agents (usually one lead), each with the agents it handed work to in children.

options.name: expandIcon
options.description: A chevron that points to the end; it turns a quarter when the agent is open. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the tree.

options.name: selection
options.description: The id of the selected agent. The tree keeps the person's choice and starts again from this value when it changes.

options.name: expanded
options.description: The ids of the open agents. Null keeps them inside the tree: active branches start open and a branch that becomes active opens once.

options.name: onExpandedChange
options.description: Called with the new set of open ids.

options.name: locale
options.description: The locale of counts and times. Null uses the configuration's locale.

options.name: timeZone
options.description: The time zone of start and end times. An IANA id such as Europe/Berlin; null, or an id the device does not know, is the device's zone.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Called with the agent the person selects.

options.name: onRespond
options.description: Shows Respond for a selected agent that needs input.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Shows Open for the selected agent, for example its transcript.

options.name: onOpenPart
options.description: Shows Show in conversation for a selected agent that has a partId or messageId.

options.name: onStop
options.description: Shows Stop for a selected agent that is waiting or working. Nothing stops until it is pressed.

states.name: open and closed
states.description: An agent with children has a toggle; its children are listed under it, indented 24dp per level, while it is open.

states.name: selected
states.description: The row takes the accent subtle fill and an accent mark at its start, and the actions for that agent appear under the tree.

states.name: working
states.description: The agent's activity is shown under its role.

states.name: ended
states.description: Done, failed or stopped agents show their summary.

states.name: empty
states.description: The summary reads No agents yet and no tree is drawn.

appearance: Names in the strong body style, roles in body text, activity, facts and times in muted caption text. Statuses are small subtle MonarchStatusBadges: info for working, warning for needs input, success for done, danger for failed, neutral for waiting and stopped. The selected row uses the accent subtle fill with an accent solid mark. The same roles adapt to dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web builds on TreeView with a tree role, arrow keys and typeahead; Android has no tree role, so, as on iOS, each agent is a selectable button and the chevron is a separate button, which TalkBack users move through in order. The rows are a Column, not a lazy list, so the tree can sit in a scrolling screen. expandIcon is required because Monarch bundles no icons (iOS draws a system chevron). Selection is a hoisted id plus onSelect instead of a binding; the expanded set is a hoisted Set with onExpandedChange. Times are epoch milliseconds formatted with java.text.DateFormat in the given locale and time zone; the web takes ISO strings. Status icons of the web are replaced by the status badge; the status is always in words. Callbacks receive the agent; the web passes the id and the agent, and onOpenPart passes the part link. The web's Stop moves focus back to the row; on Android the button simply disappears. Experimental: a domain pattern until a Rook app adopts it.
accessibility: A summary such as 3 agents: 1 working, 1 needs you, 1 done is read first.
Each agent is one selectable element read as its name, status, role, activity, steps, tool calls, times and summary, with a 48dp touch target.
The open and close button is a separate element named Expand or Collapse and the agent's name, with a 48dp target.
The selected state is exposed to TalkBack and drawn with a mark as well as a fill, so it does not rest on color alone.
The actions of the selected agent are a group named Actions for and the agent's name.
Status changes after the first look, and new agents that already need input or failed, are announced through a polite live region.
The chevron turn follows the reduced-motion setting.
edgeCases: Ids must be unique across the whole tree; a repeated id selects the first agent with it.
Deep trees indent 24dp per level; keep them to three levels on a phone.
Steps without a total read 3 steps; with a total, 3 of 7 steps.
An agent that starts working inside a closed branch opens its ancestors once, unless the app keeps expanded.

summary: A short list of next best actions suggested for the current record, each with Run, text tags for risk and approval, an approval dialog for risky ones and an optional dismiss.
whenToUse: On a record screen, to offer a few next steps that a model or a rule set suggests and let people run them in place.
whenNotToUse: For a tool call an agent makes during a conversation, use MonarchAiToolApproval in the thread. For one insight with one action, use MonarchAiInsightCallout. For commands that are always available, use a menu or a toolbar.

public data class MonarchAiSuggestedAction(id: String, label: String, description: String? = null, requiresApproval: Boolean = false, risk: MonarchAiToolCallRisk = MonarchAiToolCallRisk.Low, consequences: List<String> = emptyList(), confirmLabel: String? = null, status: MonarchAiSuggestedActionStatus? = null) { val needsApproval: Boolean }
public enum class MonarchAiSuggestedActionStatus { Ready, Running, Done, Failed }
public enum class MonarchAiSuggestedActionsOrigin { Ai, Rule }

public class MonarchAiSuggestedActionsLabels(title: String? = null, originAi: String? = null, originRule: String? = null, run: String? = null, runAction: ((label: String) -> String)? = null, running: String? = null, done: String? = null, failed: String? = null, dismiss: ((label: String) -> String)? = null, dismissText: String? = null, needsApproval: String? = null, risk: ((MonarchAiToolCallRisk) -> String?)? = null, approvalTitle: ((label: String) -> String)? = null, approvalDescription: String? = null, approve: String? = null, cancel: String? = null, doneAnnouncement: ((label: String) -> String)? = null, empty: String? = null)

options.name: actions
options.description: The suggestions, most useful first: id, label, description, requiresApproval, risk, consequences, confirmLabel and an optional status.

options.name: onRun
options.description: Runs an action, after approval when it needs it. Running… while it suspends, Done when it returns, Failed when it throws.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the list.

options.name: origin
options.description: Where the suggestions came from, always shown: "Suggested by AI" in the assistant colors or "Rule-based" in neutral colors.

options.name: title
options.description: The heading; "Suggested actions" without it.

options.name: onDismiss
options.description: Adds a dismiss button to each action. Remove the action from actions; keyboard focus moves to the next action.

options.name: originIcon
options.description: A decorative mark before the origin label, such as a bot icon.

options.name: dismissIcon
options.description: The dismiss button's icon; the button shows "Dismiss" without it.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

states.name: ready
states.description: Run is available.

states.name: running
states.description: Run shows a progress indicator, reads "Running…" as its state and ignores taps.

states.name: done
states.description: Run is replaced by "Done" in the strong success color, the label turns muted and "“…” done." is announced.

states.name: failed
states.description: A line in the strong danger color says "That didn’t work. Try again." and Run is available again.

states.name: needs approval
states.description: A "Needs approval" tag; Run opens an AlertDialog with the description and consequences. A failure keeps the dialog open with the failed line.

states.name: risk
states.description: Medium and high show a warning tag, destructive a danger tag and a danger confirm button; low shows no tag.

states.name: empty
states.description: "No suggestions right now." under the heading.

appearance: A subheading with the origin label beside it (assistant subtle fill, strong text and border for AI; surface, muted text and default border for rules), then actions separated by subtle dividers. Tags are MonarchBadge in the warning, danger and neutral tones. All colors are theme roles, so dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web lays each action out as a row with Run and dismiss at the end; on a phone the buttons go under the text so long labels wrap at font scale 2.0. The web's approval is its ConfirmDialog; Android uses the Material 3 AlertDialog of the confirm-dialog recipe. The parity map names MonarchAiToolApproval as a dependency, but that component reviews an agent's tool call and its arguments, which a suggested action does not have, so it is not used. The parity map names a LazyColumn; the list is a Column because it is short and sits on a scrolling record screen, where a lazy list cannot be nested. The risk vocabulary is MonarchAiToolCallRisk (Low, Medium, High, Destructive), shared with the conversation model. onRun is a suspending function instead of a returned promise. Description and consequences are strings, not React nodes. The web moves focus to the Done text after a run; on Android TalkBack hears the announcement and focus is not moved. Keyboard focus moves to the next action after a dismiss made with the keyboard. The heading level is not offered: Android has one heading level. iOS has no entry for this id yet. Experimental: a product composite that waits for a Rook app to adopt it.
accessibility: The heading is a heading; the origin is text, never color alone.
Each action's label, description and tags are one TalkBack element; risk and approval are words in tags.
Run is a button named "Run" followed by the action's label, with "Running…" as its state while the action runs.
Dismiss is a button named "Dismiss “…”" with the action's label; Run and dismiss have 48dp touch targets.
A finished action is announced through a polite live region that is always present; a failure line is a polite live region.
After a dismiss made with the keyboard, focus moves to the next action's Run button (or the previous one).
edgeCases: An action with a status from the app shows that status whatever onRun did.
A destructive action always asks for approval, even without requiresApproval.
The dialog cannot be dismissed while the action runs from it.
Long labels wrap; nothing is cut.

name: MonarchAiSummaryCard
title: AiSummaryCard
wrapsNative: MonarchCard (androidx.compose.material3.Surface) composing MonarchAiGeneratedBadge, MonarchAiMarkdown, MonarchAiSourceList, MonarchBanner, MonarchButton and MonarchSkeleton; android.text.format.DateUtils for the age
summary: A model-written summary of a record or a page on a card: the summary as Markdown, when it was written, its sources and a Refresh action, with generating, stale and error states, always marked as an AI summary.
whenToUse: At the top of a record or a page (an account, a deal, a long thread) where a model summarises what the person would otherwise read in full, and where the summary can go stale.
whenNotToUse: For a reply in a conversation, use the conversation message components. For a single highlighted insight, use MonarchAiInsightCallout or a banner.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchAiSummaryCard(title: String, summary: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, status: MonarchAiSummaryCardStatus = MonarchAiSummaryCardStatus.Ready, refreshing: Boolean = false, generatedAt: Long? = null, now: Long? = null, sources: List<MonarchAiSourcePart> = emptyList(), error: String? = null, onRefresh: (() -> Unit)? = null, onOpenSource: ((MonarchAiSourcePart) -> Unit)? = null, onOpenLink: ((url: String) -> Unit)? = null, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, refreshIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, actions: (@Composable FlowRowScope.() -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiSummaryCardLabels = MonarchAiSummaryCardLabels())
enum class MonarchAiSummaryCardStatus { Ready, Generating, Stale, Error }

class MonarchAiSummaryCardLabels(aiSummary: String? = null, refresh: String? = null, generated: ((relativeTime: String) -> String)? = null, generating: String? = null, updated: String? = null, stale: String? = null, error: String? = null, empty: String? = null, sources: String? = null)

options.name: title
options.description: What is summarised, for example "Account summary". A heading.

options.name: summary
options.description: The summary as Markdown, rendered by MonarchAiMarkdown as untrusted model output. Blank while there is none.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the card.

options.name: status
options.description: Ready, Generating (placeholder or busy Refresh), Stale (a warning banner) or Error (an error banner).

options.name: refreshing
options.description: A refresh is running: Refresh shows a spinner and the start and end are announced.

options.name: generatedAt
options.description: When the summary was written, in epoch milliseconds (UTC). Shown as "Generated 3 hours ago"; TalkBack reads the date and time.

options.name: now
options.description: The reference time for generatedAt, in epoch milliseconds. null uses the current time when composed.

options.name: sources
options.description: The documents or records the summary was written from, listed by MonarchAiSourceList under "Sources".

options.name: error
options.description: A detail shown under the error title when status is Error.

options.name: onRefresh
options.description: Adds Refresh, which asks for a new summary.

options.name: onOpenSource
options.description: Opens a source, for example in a preview sheet; without it MonarchAiSourceList opens a safe URL through the system.

options.name: onOpenLink
options.description: Opens a link in the summary; passed to MonarchAiMarkdown.

options.name: icon
options.description: The AI mark before "AI summary". Monarch bundles no icons; the words carry the meaning.

options.name: refreshIcon
options.description: An icon before "Refresh".

options.name: actions
options.description: More actions after the age line, for example Copy or Open in assistant.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces every built-in string.

states.name: ready
states.description: The summary, its sources and its age.

states.name: generating
states.description: Without a summary: "Generating summary…" and three placeholder lines. With one: the summary stays and Refresh shows a spinner.

states.name: stale
states.description: A warning banner above the summary asks for a refresh.

states.name: error
states.description: A danger banner with "The summary couldn’t be generated." and the detail, announced assertively; the body is empty.

states.name: empty
states.description: "No summary yet." in muted text.

appearance: MonarchCard's surface fill, default border and 12dp corners. The AI badge in the AI colors above the title in default text, the age in muted caption text, the warning and error banners in their tone colors. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: A product pattern, experimental until a Rook app adopts it, built only from Monarch parts. The web marks the summary with a bot glyph and an eyebrow; Android uses MonarchAiGeneratedBadge with the label "AI summary" and the glyph as an optional slot, since Monarch bundles no icons. The web's heading levels do not exist in Android semantics, so headingLevel is not offered; the title is a heading. The web dims the previous summary while refreshing; Android does not dim with alpha and shows the spinner on Refresh and an announcement instead. The web's sources list is a plain ordered list of links; Android reuses MonarchAiSourceList (numbered, collapsible). Dates are epoch milliseconds and the relative time comes from DateUtils, so it is not updated live: recompose with a new now to refresh it. There is no iOS equivalent yet.
accessibility: The title is a heading; "AI summary" is visible text read before it, so the provenance does not depend on an icon.
Refresh is a MonarchButton with a 48dp touch target; while busy it shows the loading state.
"Generating summary…" is announced politely when work starts and "Summary updated." when it ends, from a live region that is always present, so nothing is announced when the card first appears.
The error banner is announced assertively; the stale warning is not announced.
The age line reads the date and time instead of the relative phrase.
Sources are buttons in MonarchAiSourceList; links in the summary are LinkAnnotation links.
edgeCases: A blank summary while generating shows the placeholder; after an error it shows nothing but the banner.
Untrusted Markdown in the summary is rendered safely by MonarchAiMarkdown: raw HTML stays text and unsafe links are not links.
Without generatedAt and actions there is no footer.
A long title wraps; Refresh stays at the end.

name: MonarchAiTableAnswer
title: AiTableAnswer
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.horizontalScroll Row of cells sized with androidx.compose.ui.text.TextMeasurer, with MonarchCopyButton, MonarchButton and MonarchSkeleton
summary: A table the model produced, shown as a real table: column types inferred, sortable headers, Copy as CSV, an optional Open as artifact, and rows that can stream in.
whenToUse: In an assistant reply whose answer is tabular, for example a tool's rows or a comparison the model built, so people can sort it, copy it and open it at full size.
whenNotToUse: For the app's own records with selection, filtering and paging use the data table components. For a few numbers in a sentence use text with MonarchTabularNumber.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiTableAnswer(rows: List<Map<String, MonarchAiJSON>>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, title: String? = null, columns: List<MonarchAiTableColumn>? = null, streaming: Boolean = false, sortable: Boolean = true, copyable: Boolean = true, visibleRows: Int = 200, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiTableAnswerLabels = MonarchAiTableAnswerLabels(), onOpenAsArtifact: (() -> Unit)? = null)
data class MonarchAiTableColumn(key: String, label: String? = null, type: MonarchAiTableColumnType? = null, alignment: MonarchAiTableColumnAlignment? = null)
enum class MonarchAiTableColumnType { Text, Number, Date }
enum class MonarchAiTableColumnAlignment { Start, End }

class MonarchAiTableAnswerLabels(aiTable: String? = null, rowCount: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, copyCsv: String? = null, copied: String? = null, openAsArtifact: String? = null, sorted: ((column: String, ascending: Boolean) -> String)? = null, sortState: ((ascending: Boolean) -> String)? = null, empty: String? = null, noRows: String? = null, loadingRows: String? = null, complete: String? = null, showAllRows: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null)

options.name: rows
options.description: The rows, as the conversation model's JSON values, for example a tool's output.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the table answer.

options.name: title
options.description: The title under the AI table label.

options.name: columns
options.description: Order, headers, types and alignment. null makes a column of every key, in the order the keys first appear, with inferred types.

options.name: streaming
options.description: Rows are still arriving: a placeholder row, Open as artifact disabled, and "Table complete." announced when it turns false.

options.name: sortable
options.description: Whether the headers sort the table.

options.name: copyable
options.description: Shows Copy as CSV.

options.name: visibleRows
options.description: Rows drawn before Show all rows. Sorting and the CSV use every row.

options.name: icon
options.description: An AI glyph before the label, in the AI strong color. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: onOpenAsArtifact
options.description: Shows Open as artifact.

states.name: unsorted
states.description: Rows in the order the model gave; every header shows two subtle chevrons.

states.name: sorted
states.description: The active header draws its direction's chevron strong and reads Sorted ascending or Sorted descending. Blanks stay last.

states.name: streaming
states.description: A placeholder row of skeleton bars under the rows; Open as artifact is disabled.

states.name: empty
states.description: No rows and not streaming: No rows. Copy as CSV is disabled.

states.name: long
states.description: More rows than visibleRows: a Show all n rows button under the table.

appearance: The AI table label in the AI strong color, the title in the subheading style and the row count in muted caption text. The grid has a subtle border and row separators, a header row on the subtle background with muted label text, and default body text in cells; numbers use tabular digits and an empty cell shows a dash in the subtle text color.
platformNotes: Compose has no data table, so the grid is drawn by Monarch, as on iOS: headers are buttons with the heading role and the sort as their state, and each row is one TalkBack element of header and value pairs (the web uses an HTML table with aria-sort). Android's MonarchAiJSON.Object keeps its key order, so inferred columns follow the order keys first appear; iOS sorts them alphabetically because Swift dictionaries have no order. Column widths are measured with a TextMeasurer so rows line up; long cells stay on one line and the table scrolls sideways. The web's per-column render function is not offered; cells are text. Dates are ISO strings shown as given and sorted as UTC when they have no zone. iOS's leading and trailing alignment are Start and End, isStreaming, isSortable and isCopyable drop the is prefix, copyCSV is copyCsv and sortValue is sortState, following Kotlin and Material 3 naming. Monarch bundles no icons, so the sort chevrons are drawn on a Canvas and the AI glyph is a slot. Copy as CSV uses MonarchCopyButton, which writes the system clipboard; Android 13 and later show their own confirmation.
accessibility: The AI table label, title and row count are one heading element.
Each sortable header is a button with the heading role, read as its name with Sorted ascending or Sorted descending as its state, with a 48dp touch target.
A sort is announced through a polite live region, for example "Sorted by Revenue, ascending.".
Each row is one element read as "Region: North, Revenue: 1,200"; an empty cell is read as Empty.
The streaming placeholder is read as "More rows are being generated", and the end of streaming is announced as "Table complete.".
The sort chevrons are decorative; the direction is the spoken state.
edgeCases: Text a spreadsheet would run as a formula (=, +, -, @) is prefixed with ' in the CSV; numbers such as -3 are kept.
Numeric text such as "1,200", "12%" and "−3" sorts by value; mixed columns are text, compared ignoring case and accents with numbers in numeric order.
A date or time without a zone is read as UTC for sorting; an impossible date makes the column text.
JSON numbers in a number column are formatted for the locale; numeric text is shown as given.
Arrays and objects in a cell are shown as compact JSON.
The CSV is rebuilt when the rows or the order change while copyable; very large tables should set copyable false and offer an export.

name: MonarchAiTaskProgress
title: AiTaskProgress
wrapsNative: MonarchCard with MonarchBadge, MonarchProgress (androidx.compose.material3.LinearProgressIndicator), MonarchAiChainOfSteps, MonarchButton, androidx.compose.material3.FilterChip and androidx.compose.material3.IconButton; android.text.format.DateUtils.getRelativeTimeSpanString for the start time
summary: A long-running assistant task in a card, with its status, a progress bar, when it started and how long is left, its steps, and controls to cancel, minimize or be notified.
whenToUse: For an assistant task that takes minutes, such as summarising many documents or an export, so people can follow it, leave it running and come back.
whenNotToUse: For a short wait inside a reply, use MonarchAiThinkingIndicator. For the steps alone, use MonarchAiChainOfSteps. For a file upload, use MonarchUploadQueue.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiTaskProgress(title: String, status: MonarchAiTaskStatus, startedAt: Long, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, steps: List<MonarchAiPlanStep> = emptyList(), progress: Float? = null, etaMillis: Long? = null, notifying: Boolean = false, now: Long? = null, onNotifyingChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, onMinimize: (() -> Unit)? = null, onCancel: (() -> Unit)? = null, statusIcon: (@Composable (MonarchAiTaskStatus) -> Unit)? = null, minimizeIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiTaskProgressLabels = MonarchAiTaskProgressLabels())
enum class MonarchAiTaskStatus { Running, Paused, Done, Failed, Cancelled }

class MonarchAiTaskProgressLabels(status: ((MonarchAiTaskStatus) -> String)? = null, progressLabel: ((title: String) -> String)? = null, progressValue: ((percent: Int) -> String)? = null, started: ((relative: String) -> String)? = null, eta: ((millis: Long) -> String)? = null, cancel: String? = null, minimize: String? = null, notify: String? = null, announce: ((title: String, status: String) -> String)? = null)

options.name: title
options.description: What the task is, such as "Summarising 40 documents". A heading, and part of the bar's name.

options.name: status
options.description: Running, Paused, Done, Failed or Cancelled. Changes are announced.

options.name: startedAt
options.description: When the task started, in epoch milliseconds (UTC), shown as "Started 5 minutes ago".

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the card.

options.name: steps
options.description: The steps, shown as a MonarchAiChainOfSteps. A task may have only a bar.

options.name: progress
options.description: Completion from 0 to 1. By default the share of finished (done, failed or skipped) steps; with no steps the bar is indeterminate while running.

options.name: etaMillis
options.description: Estimated time left in milliseconds, shown while running: "Less than a minute left", "About 3 minutes left", "About 2 hours left".

options.name: notifying
options.description: Whether "Notify me when done" is on.

options.name: now
options.description: The reference time of the start text, for previews, tests and identical renders. The clock, refreshed every minute, when null.

options.name: onNotifyingChange
options.description: Shows the "Notify me when done" toggle while running or paused, and receives the new value.

options.name: onMinimize
options.description: Shows a Minimize button, for example to dock the task in a tray.

options.name: onCancel
options.description: Shows a Cancel button while the task runs or is paused.

options.name: statusIcon
options.description: An icon in the status badge. Decorative: the status is written.

options.name: minimizeIcon
options.description: Makes Minimize an icon button named "Minimize". Without it the button is written, because Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the status names, "<title> progress", "40% complete", "Started …", the time left, Cancel, Minimize, "Notify me when done" and the announcement (strings_aitaskprogress.xml).

states.name: running
states.description: Info badge; the bar fills, or is indeterminate without progress (still when animations are off); the time left is shown; Notify and Cancel are offered.

states.name: paused
states.description: Warning badge; no time left; Notify and Cancel are still offered.

states.name: done
states.description: Success badge; the bar is full; no controls but Minimize.

states.name: failed
states.description: Danger badge; the failure is announced assertively; no controls but Minimize.

states.name: cancelled
states.description: Neutral badge; the bar stays where it was or empty; no controls but Minimize.

appearance: A MonarchCard on the surface role with a subheading title, the status as a subtle MonarchBadge in its tone, a MonarchProgress bar in the tone of the status (accent while running) and muted caption text for the start, percentage and time left. Notify is a Material 3 filter chip in the theme; Cancel a secondary small MonarchButton. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: As on the web, the bar takes the tone of the status (accent while running). The running badge uses the AI tone, as the web's status pill does. The web's etaMs is etaMillis; startedAt and now are epoch milliseconds, as everywhere on Android. Hours left are whole hours, where the web writes one decimal. The web's children slot and stepsProps are not offered: put extra content after the card and pass ready steps. The web announces through live regions, and so does Android: a polite one, assertive for a failure. iOS's isNotifying binding is notifying with onNotifyingChange. The minimize icon is an optional slot because Monarch bundles no icons.
accessibility: The card is a traversal group; the title is a heading.
The status is a badge with its name in words, never color alone.
The bar is one element named "<title> progress" with "40% complete" as its state and the range as progress information, or the status name and indeterminate progress when there is no value.
A status change is announced as "<title>: <status>" through a live region that is always present: polite, assertive for a failure; the first status is not announced.
The steps announce their own starts and failures (MonarchAiChainOfSteps).

Notify is a filter chip whose selected state is read; Minimize is a written button or an icon button named "Minimize"; every control has a 48dp touch target and the controls wrap when they do not fit.
edgeCases: progress outside 0 to 1 is limited; NaN counts as unknown.
With no steps, no progress and a running status the bar is indeterminate; when paused or cancelled it is empty.
A negative etaMillis is not shown.
Without now the start text refreshes every minute.

name: MonarchAiThinkingIndicator
title: AiThinkingIndicator
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow of androidx.compose.material3.Text, androidx.compose.ui.draw.drawWithContent with a Brush.linearGradient for the shimmer, androidx.compose.animation.core.rememberInfiniteTransition; MonarchAiTypingDots as the default mark
summary: Shows that the assistant is working before its first token arrives: a "Thinking…" label with a soft shimmer or a pulsing mark and, after a few seconds, how long it has been thinking.
whenToUse: In the place of the assistant reply between sending a prompt and the first streamed token, especially when the wait can be long (reasoning, tool use, searching files).
whenNotToUse: Where there is no room for a sentence use MonarchAiTypingDots. To reserve the shape of the coming answer use MonarchAiResponseSkeleton. Once text streams, show the text.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiThinkingIndicator(modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchAiThinkingIndicatorVariant = MonarchAiThinkingIndicatorVariant.Shimmer, label: String? = null, startedAt: Long? = null, showElapsedAfterMillis: Long = 3_000L, announce: Boolean = true, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, elapsedLabel: ((seconds: Int) -> String)? = null)
enum class MonarchAiThinkingIndicatorVariant { Shimmer, Mark }

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the indicator.

options.name: variant
options.description: Shimmer: a band of the strong assistant color sweeps through the label. Mark: a pulsing mark before a still label.

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Thinking…" (monarch_aithinkingindicator_label), for example "Searching your files…".

options.name: startedAt
options.description: When the assistant started working, in epoch milliseconds (UTC). null counts from when the indicator first appeared; pass it when the indicator can leave the composition during one turn, for example in a lazy list.

options.name: showElapsedAfterMillis
options.description: How long before the elapsed time appears after the label. Long.MAX_VALUE never shows it.

options.name: announce
options.description: Announces the label when the indicator appears and when the label changes.

options.name: icon
options.description: The mark of the Mark variant, given the strong assistant color as its content color; it pulses. null uses MonarchAiTypingDots. Monarch bundles no icons. Ignored by the Shimmer variant.

options.name: elapsedLabel
options.description: Formats whole elapsed seconds. By default the narrow unit format of the current locale: "5s", "1m 5s".

states.name: thinking
states.description: The label in muted text, with the shimmer or the mark.

states.name: long wait
states.description: After showElapsedAfterMillis the elapsed time follows the label in subtle text and updates every second.

states.name: animations off
states.description: The shimmer and the pulse stop; the label stays muted text and the mark is still. The clock still ticks once a second.

appearance: The label is muted text; the shimmer is a band of the strong assistant role drawn only over the label's own pixels, so contrast holds in light, dark and both high-contrast themes. The elapsed time is subtle caption text. The mark takes the strong assistant role; the default mark is MonarchAiTypingDots in its assistant roles.
platformNotes: The web shimmers a band behind the label; Android, like iOS, sweeps the assistant color through the label's own text. The web uses an assistant bot glyph as the mark; Monarch for Android bundles no icons, so the mark is an icon slot and falls back to MonarchAiTypingDots, which the plan named. iOS posts an announcement; Android uses an always-present polite live region holding only the label, as the web does. startedAt is epoch milliseconds (iOS takes a Date) and the delay is showElapsedAfterMillis (iOS showsElapsedAfter in seconds); announce matches MonarchAiTypingDots (iOS isAnnounced).
accessibility: The label is one TalkBack element, with the elapsed time as its state description once it shows.

The label is announced through a polite live region filled one frame after the indicator appears, and again when the label changes; the live region never holds the elapsed time, so the ticking clock is not announced.
With announce set to false there is no live region.
The mark is decorative and hidden from TalkBack.
When animations are off the shimmer and the pulse stop.
The label and the elapsed time wrap at large font sizes; nothing has a fixed height.
edgeCases: A startedAt in the future counts as 0 seconds.
Without startedAt the clock restarts if the indicator leaves the composition and comes back.
The elapsed time moves to a new line when it does not fit after a long label.
Exactly a whole minute is written without seconds: "1m".

examples.title: Shimmer (default)
examples.template: MonarchAiThinkingIndicator(variant = MonarchAiThinkingIndicatorVariant.{{variant|pascal}})
examples.code: MonarchAiThinkingIndicator(variant = MonarchAiThinkingIndicatorVariant.Shimmer)

examples.title: A long search, with a pulsing mark
examples.setup: val startedAt = remember { System.currentTimeMillis() }
examples.code:
MonarchAiThinkingIndicator(
    variant = MonarchAiThinkingIndicatorVariant.Mark,
    label = "Searching your files…",
    startedAt = startedAt,
)

name: MonarchAiThread
title: AiThread
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn (reverseLayout = true) composing MonarchAiMessage, MonarchAiContextDivider, MonarchAiThinkingIndicator, MonarchLoadMore, MonarchInlineNotice and MonarchButton
summary: The scrolling list of an AI conversation: messages oldest first with day labels, pinned to the newest, with Jump to latest, Load earlier, a thinking indicator, connection notices and one announcer for the whole conversation.
whenToUse: The message area of an assistant screen, above a MonarchAiPromptInput, fed from a MonarchAiConversation.
whenNotToUse: For person-to-person chat use MonarchVirtualMessageList with MonarchMessageRow. For one answer without a conversation use MonarchAiMessage or MonarchAiStructuredAnswer on their own.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchAiThread(messages: List<MonarchAiConversationMessage>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, state: LazyListState = rememberLazyListState(), contentPadding: PaddingValues = PaddingValues(), status: MonarchAiConversationStatus = MonarchAiConversationStatus.Idle, error: MonarchAiConversationError? = null, offline: Boolean = false, queuedCount: Int = 0, slow: Boolean = false, hasEarlier: Boolean = false, loadingEarlier: Boolean = false, daySeparators: Boolean = true, timeZone: String? = null, nowMillis: Long? = null, announces: Boolean = true, announceIntervalMillis: Long = 1_000L, labels: MonarchAiThreadLabels = MonarchAiThreadLabels(), onStop: (() -> Unit)? = null, onLoadEarlier: (() -> Unit)? = null, jumpIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, empty: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, message: @Composable LazyItemScope.(message: MonarchAiConversationMessage, context: MonarchAiThreadMessageContext) -> Unit = { item, context -> MonarchAiMessage(message = item, announces = context.announces, timeZone = timeZone) })
class MonarchAiThreadMessageContext(index: Int, isLast: Boolean, announces: Boolean)

class MonarchAiThreadLabels(label: String? = null, jumpToLatest: String? = null, newMessages: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, loadEarlier: String? = null, loadingEarlier: String? = null, thinking: String? = null, responseComplete: String? = null, responseStopped: String? = null, error: ((message: String) -> String)? = null, codeBlock: String? = null, today: String? = null, yesterday: String? = null, offline: String? = null, offlineQueued: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, sendingQueued: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, slow: String? = null)

options.name: messages
options.description: The visible conversation, oldest first: MonarchAiConversation.messages.

options.name: state
options.description: The scroll state. Index 0 is the bottom row, so firstVisibleItemIndex == 0 means the newest message is in view.

options.name: contentPadding
options.description: Padding around the messages inside the scrolling area.

options.name: status
options.description: Submitted shows the thinking indicator; Submitted and Streaming make Escape call onStop; Stopped ends the announcement with "Response stopped".

options.name: error
options.description: Announced assertively as "Error: <message>" when the newest message has no error part of its own.

options.name: offline
options.description: Shows the offline notice under the messages.

options.name: queuedCount
options.description: How many messages wait for the connection; named in the offline notice, and once online shows "Back online. Sending N queued messages…".

options.name: slow
options.description: Shows "This is taking longer than usual. Still working…" while a reply is submitted or streaming.

options.name: hasEarlier
options.description: Older messages exist. With onLoadEarlier, "Load earlier messages" is the top row.

options.name: loadingEarlier
options.description: The load button shows progress and "Loading earlier messages…" as its state.

options.name: daySeparators
options.description: A MonarchAiContextDivider day label above the first message of each calendar day.

options.name: timeZone
options.description: IANA zone of the day labels and of the default messages' times. null is the device zone.

options.name: nowMillis
options.description: Reference time for Today and Yesterday, epoch milliseconds UTC. null reads the clock.

options.name: announces
options.description: The thread announces for the whole conversation and tells each message not to; false lets each message announce itself.

options.name: announceIntervalMillis
options.description: Least time between two polite announcements while a reply streams.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: onStop
options.description: Called by the Escape key inside the thread while a reply is running.

options.name: onLoadEarlier
options.description: Loads older messages; prepend them to messages. The view does not move.

options.name: jumpIcon
options.description: Icon before "Jump to latest". Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: empty
options.description: Shown instead of the list when there are no messages, no older ones and no submitted reply, for example a MonarchAiWelcome.

options.name: message
options.description: Draws one message, given its index, whether it is the newest and whether it should announce itself.

states.name: pinned
states.description: While the newest row is within 48dp of the bottom, a new message or the thinking indicator scrolls into view and a growing reply stays anchored at the bottom.

states.name: scrolled up
states.description: New messages do not move the view; a "Jump to latest" button over the bottom of the list counts them ("2 new messages") and scrolls back, animated unless animations are off.

states.name: submitted
states.description: A MonarchAiThinkingIndicator is the bottom row, and "Thinking…" is announced once.

states.name: streaming
states.description: The reply is read out in whole sentences, then "Response complete" or "Response stopped" when it ends.

states.name: earlier
states.description: "Load earlier messages" (MonarchLoadMore) is the top row; while loading it shows progress.

states.name: offline / sending / slow
states.description: One MonarchInlineNotice under the list, offline first: warning tone for the connection, neutral for a slow reply.

states.name: error
states.description: An error no message shows is announced assertively; nothing is drawn for it.

states.name: empty
states.description: The empty content replaces the list.

appearance: The thread has no surface of its own: it shows on the screen's background. Messages, day labels, the thinking indicator and the load button keep their own roles; the notice uses the warning or neutral tone of MonarchInlineNotice, and the jump button is a small secondary MonarchButton. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web renders a scrolling div with role=log, measures rows and windows them itself after 200 messages (virtualizeAfter, keepLast, estimatedMessageHeight). On Android the LazyColumn composes only the rows on screen, so those parameters do not exist; reverseLayout keeps the newest at the bottom and LazyListState.requestScrollToItem follows new rows while the person is at the bottom. The web's renderMessage and messageProps are one trailing message lambda; pass MonarchAiMessage's parameters there. The web's locale prop is the configuration locale. The web reads Markdown tables as "Table"; this announcer names code blocks, drops heading and bold marks and reads the rest as text, so there is no table label. The web draws warning and clock glyphs in the notice; Monarch bundles no icons, so the notice's tone and text carry the meaning. The composer is not part of the thread on either platform: put a MonarchAiPromptInput under it. iOS has not covered this entry yet. Experimental until a Rook app adopts it.
accessibility: The list's TalkBack name is "Conversation" (labels.label).
Day labels are MonarchAiContextDividers, read as one element: "Today", "Yesterday" or the date.

With announces, one always-present polite live region says "Thinking…" when a reply is submitted, reads a reply that arrives while the thread is shown in whole sentences at most once per announceIntervalMillis, then "Response complete" or "Response stopped"; replies that were already finished are not read.
The messages get announces = false from the context, so streamed text is not read token by token.
A conversation error that no message shows is announced from an always-present assertive live region.
The offline, sending and slow notices sit outside the list in an always-present polite live region.
"Jump to latest" and "Load earlier messages" are MonarchButtons with 48dp targets; the jump button reads its count of new messages with its label.
Escape inside the thread calls onStop while a reply is submitted or streaming.
Jumping uses scrollToItem instead of an animation when animations are off.
edgeCases: Give the thread a bounded height; it cannot sit in a vertically scrolling parent.
Message ids must be unique and stable: they are the lazy list keys.
Older messages prepended to messages keep the view where it is.
A message whose createdAt is not an ISO 8601 time gets no day label, and the next message starts a new day, as on the web.
Without onLoadEarlier, hasEarlier shows nothing.
The empty content shows only when there are no messages, nothing to load and no submitted reply.
Offline wins over the sending and slow notices; slow shows only while a reply is running.

examples.title: A finished turn
Older history, a custom message and the offline notice
examples.code:
@OptIn(ExperimentalMonarchApi::class)
MonarchAiThread(
    messages = messages,
    modifier = Modifier.height(MonarchTheme.spacing.space24 * 3),
    offline = true,
    queuedCount = 1,
    hasEarlier = true,
    loadingEarlier = loading,
    timeZone = "Europe/Madrid",
    onLoadEarlier = { loading = true },
) { message, context ->
    MonarchAiMessage(
        message = message,
        announces = context.announces,
        timeZone = "Europe/Madrid",
        showActions = context.isLast,
    )
}

parityExceptions.reason: The web shows the copy, edit and regenerate buttons of a message only on hover and focus. A phone has no hover, so the buttons are always shown under each message (copy under the person's message; copy and regenerate under the assistant's). The web composer is drawn as a Send a message button and a Stop button; on Android the composer is the prompt field with its Stop button inside it, the field the person types in.
parityExceptions.convention: no hover on a touch device: message actions are always visible (Material)

name: MonarchAiTonePicker
title: AiTonePicker
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.RadioButton rows with androidx.compose.foundation.selection.selectable in a selectableGroup (cards); androidx.compose.material3.ExposedDropdownMenuBox (compact); MonarchTextField for the custom tone
summary: Chooses the tone the assistant writes in: Professional, Technical, Casual and Executive by default, each with a one-line description, and an optional custom tone in the person's own words.
whenToUse: In assistant settings or next to a prompt, where the person picks how the reply should read.
whenNotToUse: For other single choices use MonarchRadioRow in a selectableGroup. For a length or format setting use a segmented button.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiTonePicker(selection: String, onSelectionChange: (String) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, tones: List<MonarchAiTone> = MonarchAiTone.defaults(), variant: MonarchAiTonePickerVariant = MonarchAiTonePickerVariant.Cards, enabled: Boolean = true, customText: String = "", onCustomTextChange: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, label: String? = null, customLabel: String? = null, customDetail: String? = null, customFieldLabel: String? = null, customPrompt: String? = null)
data class MonarchAiTone(id: String, label: String, detail: String)
companion object MonarchAiTone.Companion { const val CUSTOM_ID: String = "custom"; @Composable fun defaults(): List<MonarchAiTone> }
enum class MonarchAiTonePickerVariant { Cards, Compact }

options.name: selection
options.description: The id of the selected tone, or MonarchAiTone.CUSTOM_ID for the Custom option.

options.name: onSelectionChange
options.description: Called with the id of the tone the user chose.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the picker.

options.name: tones
options.description: The tones to offer, each with an id, a label and a one-line detail.

options.name: variant
options.description: Cards: one row per tone with its description. Compact: a field that opens a menu.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the user can change the tone.

options.name: customText
options.description: The person's own description of the tone.

options.name: onCustomTextChange
options.description: Called as the custom description changes. Passing it adds the Custom option and, while it is selected, a text field.

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the name of the choice, "Tone".

options.name: customLabel
options.description: Replaces the name of the Custom option.

options.name: customDetail
options.description: Replaces the description of the Custom option.

options.name: customFieldLabel
options.description: Replaces the label of the custom text field.

options.name: customPrompt
options.description: Replaces the placeholder of the custom text field.

states.name: selected
states.description: The row has the subtle assistant fill, a 2dp assistant border and a filled radio mark in the solid assistant color.

states.name: not selected
states.description: A surface row with a 1dp default border and an empty radio mark.

states.name: custom selected
states.description: A MonarchTextField for the custom tone appears under the options.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Rows use the disabled text color and do not respond; the selected row keeps its thicker border and filled mark.

states.name: compact
states.description: A read-only outlined field labelled with the name of the choice; activating it opens a menu of the tone names.

appearance: Rows use the medium radius, the surface fill and the default border; the selected row uses the subtle assistant fill and the assistant border. Labels use the body type and descriptions the caption type in the muted text color, in every theme.
platformNotes: The web lays the cards in a grid of columns at least 176px wide; Android shows one column, as iOS does, which holds at every font size. The web's compact variant is a native select; Android uses the Material 3 exposed dropdown menu, whose arrow icon comes from Material 3. The web's uncontrolled custom text (defaultCustomText) is not offered: pass customText and onCustomTextChange. MonarchAiTone.defaults() is a composable function because the built-in names and descriptions are string resources.
accessibility: In cards each tone is one row with the radio button role, read as its label and description, and the rows are a selectableGroup, so TalkBack reads the position in the list and the selected state.
The selected row is also marked by a filled radio mark and a thicker border, not by color alone.
The name of the choice is a visible text above the rows.
Every row is at least 48dp high and its text wraps at large font sizes.
The compact variant is the Material 3 exposed dropdown menu, labelled with the name of the choice.
The custom field is a MonarchTextField with its own label.
edgeCases: A selection that matches no tone shows no row as selected.
A tone whose id is "custom" is dropped while the Custom option is shown, so ids stay unique.
A tone with an empty detail shows only its label.
The custom text is kept when another tone is selected; the app decides whether to use it.

examples.title: Cards with a custom tone
examples.template:
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space2)) {
    MonarchAiTonePicker(
        selection = tone,
        onSelectionChange = { tone = it },
        tones = listOf(
            MonarchAiTone({{tones.0.id}}, {{tones.0.label}}, {{tones.0.description}}),
            MonarchAiTone({{tones.1.id}}, {{tones.1.label}}, {{tones.1.description}}),
            MonarchAiTone({{tones.2.id}}, {{tones.2.label}}, {{tones.2.description}}),
            MonarchAiTone({{tones.3.id}}, {{tones.3.label}}, {{tones.3.description}}),
        ),
        customText = customText,
        onCustomTextChange = { customText = it },
        label = {{messages.label}},
        customLabel = {{messages.custom}},
        customDetail = {{messages.customDescription}},
    )
    MonarchText(text = "Selected: " + tone)
}
examples.setupTemplate:
var tone by remember { mutableStateOf({{value}}) }
var customText by remember { mutableStateOf("") }
examples.setup:
var tone by remember { mutableStateOf("professional") }
var customText by remember { mutableStateOf("") }
examples.code:
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space2)) {
    MonarchAiTonePicker(
        selection = tone,
        onSelectionChange = { tone = it },
        tones = listOf(
