summary: The approval gate for a tool call the assistant wants to run: what it will do, its arguments, the risk, and Approve and Deny, with editable arguments, a reason and Always allow.
whenToUse: In an AI conversation, for a tool call in the PendingApproval state that a person must approve before it runs (MonarchAiConversation's approveTool and denyTool).
whenNotToUse: To show a tool call that runs or ran without approval use MonarchAiToolCall; for a destructive action the person started themselves use a confirmation dialog.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchAiToolApproval(part: MonarchAiToolCallPart, onApprove: (input: MonarchAiJSON?) -> Unit, onDeny: (reason: String?) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, risk: MonarchAiToolCallRisk = part.risk ?: MonarchAiToolCallRisk.Medium, consequence: String? = null, toolLabels: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(), argumentLabels: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(), editable: Boolean = true, onAlwaysAllow: ((toolName: String) -> Unit)? = null, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiToolApprovalLabels = MonarchAiToolApprovalLabels(), describeTool: ((MonarchAiToolCallPart) -> String?)? = null)

class MonarchAiToolApprovalLabels(eyebrow: String? = null, risk: ((MonarchAiToolCallRisk) -> String)? = null, consequence: ((MonarchAiToolCallRisk) -> String?)? = null, details: String? = null, noArguments: String? = null, approve: String? = null, deny: String? = null, editArguments: String? = null, discardEdits: String? = null, argumentsJson: String? = null, invalidJson: String? = null, addReason: String? = null, reason: String? = null, alwaysAllow: String? = null, approved: String? = null, denied: String? = null, cancelled: String? = null, announce: ((title: String) -> String)? = null)

options.name: part
options.description: The tool call waiting for a decision. A call in another state shows its outcome instead of the buttons.

options.name: onApprove
options.description: Called on Approve with the edited arguments, or null when they were not edited.

options.name: onDeny
options.description: Called on Deny with the trimmed reason, or null.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the card.

options.name: risk
options.description: Low (neutral), Medium and High (warning), Destructive (danger, consequence line, danger Approve, no Always allow).

options.name: consequence
options.description: What happens if this is approved; null uses the risk's default line (only destructive has one).

options.name: toolLabels
options.description: Display names per tool name; others are humanized (send_email gives "Send email").

options.name: argumentLabels
options.description: Labels per argument key; others are humanized (sendAt gives "Send at").

options.name: editable
options.description: Offers Edit arguments, a JSON editor that must parse before Approve.

options.name: onAlwaysAllow
options.description: Shows the Always allow this tool checkbox; called with the tool name just before onApprove when ticked.

options.name: icon
options.description: A decorative icon before the eyebrow. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: describeTool
options.description: The title in plain words, such as "Send email to 3 people"; null uses the tool's display name.

states.name: pending
states.description: Approve and Deny with Add a reason and, when editable, Edit arguments.

states.name: editing
states.description: A multi-line field with the arguments as JSON; invalid JSON shows "Fix the JSON before approving." and Approve does nothing.

states.name: reason
states.description: A reason field above the buttons; its trimmed text is sent with Deny.

states.name: approved, denied, cancelled
states.description: The buttons are replaced by the outcome in the success, danger or muted color.

states.name: destructive
states.description: The danger badge "Can’t be undone", the consequence line and a danger Approve button; Always allow is not offered.

appearance: MonarchCard's surface with the subtle border. The eyebrow and argument keys are muted captions, the title is strong body text, the risk is a subtle MonarchBadge in its tone, the consequence uses the strong color of the risk's tone, and the outcome uses the success strong, danger strong or muted text color. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web AiToolApproval is announced with an assertive alert and can move focus to Deny or Approve (focusOnMount). On Android the card is announced through a polite live region on an always-present node, because an assertive announcement is reserved for blocking errors and no announce API exists in Compose; focus is never moved. Arguments are stacked label-over-value rows instead of a two-column list, for narrow screens. onApprove receives MonarchAiJSON? and onDeny String?, instead of optional arguments. The web's describe returns a node; here describeTool returns a String, as in MonarchAiToolCall. Experimental until a Rook app adopts it. No iOS entry exists yet.
accessibility: The card is a traversal group; the title and the Details label are headings.
When the card appears, "Approval needed: title" is announced through a polite live region.
The risk is written in words in a badge, and a destructive call also states its consequence in words.
Each argument is read as its label and value together.
The outcome (Approved, Denied, Cancelled) is a polite live region, so the decision is announced.
Every button and the Always allow row have a 48dp touch target.
edgeCases: Arguments that are not an object are shown as text; no arguments show "No arguments.".
Edited arguments equal to the original (ignoring surrounding spaces) are sent as null.
A new part id resets the decision, the editor, the reason and Always allow.
A list of plain values is joined with commas; nested values are shown as indented JSON.

name: MonarchAiToolCall
title: AiToolCall
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.clickable header with expand and collapse semantics, androidx.compose.animation.AnimatedVisibility, MonarchStatusBadge for the state and MonarchAiCodeBlock for the input and output
summary: One tool call of an assistant turn as a card that opens: what was done in plain words, the state as a word in a status badge, how long it took and, on demand, the exact input and output.
whenToUse: For each tool-call part of an assistant message, when people should see what the assistant did; and in audit or debugging views where the raw arguments and results must be inspectable.
whenNotToUse: Not while the call waits for a decision: show an approval with MonarchAiPermissionScope instead. Not to show the result as a thing, such as a created record, which is MonarchAiToolResultCard.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchAiToolCall(part: MonarchAiToolCallPart, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, summary: String? = null, toolLabels: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(), expanded: Boolean? = null, onExpandedChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, announcesChanges: Boolean = true, maxValueLength: Int = MonarchAiToolCallTokens.DEFAULT_MAX_VALUE_LENGTH, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, stateIcon: (@Composable (MonarchAiToolCallState) -> Unit)? = null, toggleIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiToolCallLabels = MonarchAiToolCallLabels(), describeTool: ((MonarchAiToolCallPart) -> String?)? = null)

public class MonarchAiToolCallLabels(state: ((MonarchAiToolCallState) -> String?)? = null, formatDuration: ((millis: Long) -> String)? = null, input: String? = null, output: String? = null, error: String? = null, tool: String? = null, empty: String? = null, stateChanged: ((label: String, state: String) -> String)? = null, showMore: String? = null, truncated: ((shown: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, expanded: String? = null, collapsed: String? = null)

options.name: part
options.description: The call from the conversation model: name, input, state, output, error, start and end times, streamed input text.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the card.

options.name: summary
options.description: The one-line summary in words. Wins over describeTool.

options.name: toolLabels
options.description: Display names by tool name. Unlisted tools get a humanized name: search_documents is "Search documents".

options.name: expanded
options.description: Whether the details are open, when the app controls it. Kept inside, closed at first, when null.

options.name: onExpandedChange
options.description: Called with the new state when the header is activated.

options.name: announcesChanges
options.description: Whether a change of state is announced. Turn it off when the thread already announces it.

options.name: maxValueLength
options.description: The longest input or output shown before Show all, in characters. 0 shows everything.

options.name: icon
options.description: A decorative icon before the title in the AI tool color, such as a wrench. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: stateIcon
options.description: A decorative icon inside the state badge for each state. The state is always a word too.

options.name: toggleIcon
options.description: An icon at the start of the header, such as a chevron pointing to the end; it turns a quarter turn while open.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the state names, the duration format, the headings, the empty and truncation notes, the announcement, Show all and the expanded and collapsed states.

options.name: describeTool
options.description: Builds the summary from the call. Return null to fall back to the tool's label.

states.name: pending approval
states.description: Warning tone and "Waiting for approval".

states.name: awaiting result
states.description: Neutral tone and "Waiting for result".

states.name: running
states.description: Info tone and "Running". No duration until it ends.

states.name: succeeded
states.description: Success tone, "Done" and the duration, such as 0.4s, 12s or 2m 05s.

states.name: failed
states.description: Danger tone, "Failed", and the error under the card without opening it.

states.name: denied
states.description: Neutral tone and "Denied".

states.name: cancelled
states.description: Neutral tone and "Cancelled".

states.name: expanded
states.description: "Tool: <name>", then the input and the output in MonarchAiCodeBlocks named Input and Output, or "No details yet.".

states.name: truncated
states.description: A value longer than maxValueLength is cut at a line end when one is near, with "Showing 4,000 of 52,113 characters" and a Show all button.

appearance: A card on the subtle background with the subtle border and the medium radius; the icon uses the AI tool role, the state is a small MonarchStatusBadge in its tone, the duration and notes are muted caption text and the error is the strong danger role. Every color is a theme role, so it follows light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Same parameters as iOS where Compose allows: isExpanded as a Binding becomes expanded with onExpandedChange, and the SF Symbol name systemImage becomes the icon slot, because Monarch for Android bundles no icons; stateIcon and toggleIcon are slots for the same reason, so without them the state is only a word in a tinted badge. The web uses <details>/<summary> and iOS a DisclosureGroup; Material 3 has no disclosure, and MonarchCollapsible takes only a text label, so the header is built with the same expand and collapse semantics as MonarchCollapsible. The web shows a spinner while running; Android shows the word, as iOS does. Values are pretty-printed with two-space indentation in the order of the object's members, as on the web (iOS sorts the keys). Times are ISO 8601 strings from the conversation model. The composable is experimental: an AI pattern that waits for a Rook app to adopt it.
accessibility: The header is one button read as the title, the state and the duration, with the state Expanded or Collapsed and the TalkBack expand and collapse actions.
The header is at least 48dp high; Show all is a MonarchButton with a 48dp target.
The state is always a word as well as a tone; the icon slots are decorative.
A change of state after the card appears is announced through a polite live region as "<tool>: <state>"; the first state is not announced, and announcesChanges turns announcements off.
The error line under a failed call is read as "Error: message".
The input and output are MonarchAiCodeBlocks named Input and Output, with a Copy button.
The title wraps and the state line moves under it at large font sizes.
edgeCases: A call without input and output shows "No details yet." when open.
While arguments stream, inputText stands in for a null or empty input.
A string that holds JSON is re-indented; text that only starts with a brace is shown as it is.
Times that cannot be read, or an end before the start, show no duration.
Show all is kept per block while the card is on screen; a new maxValueLength cuts again.

name: MonarchAiToolResultCard
title: AiToolResultCard
wrapsNative: MonarchCard (androidx.compose.material3.Surface) with androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row and Column, androidx.compose.material3.Text, MonarchKeyValue, MonarchLink and MonarchButton
summary: A preview of what an AI tool did (a record created, an email sent, an event booked, a ticket filed): the kind, the title, a line of detail, key facts, a link to open the result and an optional Undo.
whenToUse: In an AI conversation, under a tool call that succeeded and changed something the person may want to see or reverse, such as a record the assistant created.
whenNotToUse: For a tool call still waiting for approval or running, show the call's state instead. For a change to fields the person is looking at, use MonarchAiUndoBanner, which lists before and after.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiToolResultCard(title: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, kind: MonarchAiToolResultKind = MonarchAiToolResultKind.Generic, description: String? = null, meta: List<MonarchKeyValueItem> = emptyList(), icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, onOpen: (() -> Unit)? = null, onUndo: (suspend () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiToolResultCardLabels = MonarchAiToolResultCardLabels())
enum class MonarchAiToolResultKind { RecordCreated, EmailSent, EventBooked, TicketFiled, Generic }

class MonarchAiToolResultCardLabels(kind: ((MonarchAiToolResultKind) -> String?)? = null, open: String? = null, openLabel: ((title: String) -> String)? = null, undo: String? = null, undone: String? = null, undoFailed: String? = null)

options.name: title
options.description: What the tool made or changed: the record's name, the email's subject.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the card.

options.name: kind
options.description: What the tool did; picks the label above the title.

options.name: description
options.description: One line of detail, such as "To 3 people".

options.name: meta
options.description: Short facts, shown with MonarchKeyValue in the stacked layout.

options.name: icon
options.description: A glyph for the kind, in a tile at the start in the success colors, muted once undone. Hidden from TalkBack. Monarch bundles no icons, so without it there is no tile.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Shows an Open link that calls it, for example to open the record. Hidden once undone.

options.name: onUndo
options.description: Shows Undo. Runs in a coroutine of the card; throw to report a failure.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the kind labels, Open and its TalkBack name, Undo, Undone and the failure text.

states.name: result
states.description: The tile, the text, the facts, Open and Undo.

states.name: undoing
states.description: Undo shows its progress indicator, reads "Loading" and ignores taps.

states.name: undone
states.description: Open and Undo go away, the tile turns muted, and "Undone" is shown in the muted text color and announced.

states.name: undo failed
states.description: "Couldn’t undo. Try again." is shown in the danger strong color and announced; Undo stays and can run again.

appearance: A MonarchCard on the surface color with the default border. The kind is a caption in the muted text color, the title is in the strong body style, and the icon tile uses the success subtle fill with the success strong glyph, or the muted fill and muted text once undone. Open is a standalone link and Undo a small ghost button. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web's title and description accept nodes; here they are Strings and the facts are MonarchKeyValueItem values, as on iOS. The web's href and external flag become onOpen: the app opens the record or the URL (for example with LocalUriHandler), so there is no URL filter. The web's onUndo may return a promise; here it is a suspend function run in the card's coroutine scope, and a thrown exception shows the built-in failure text. The web draws a glyph for each kind and iOS uses SF Symbols; Monarch for Android bundles no icons, so the glyph is an optional slot and the kind is always said in text. The web moves focus back to the card when Undo disappears; Compose keeps TalkBack focus on the nearest element and the result is announced through the live region. The card does not read a MonarchAiToolCallPart itself, because a tool's output has no standard title; the app maps the output to the title and facts, as the example shows.
accessibility: The kind, the title and the description are one TalkBack element, read as "Record created, Acme Ltd, Added to Accounts".
Each fact is read as its label and value by MonarchKeyValue.
Open is a link named "Open" and the title, such as "Open Acme Ltd"; Undo is a button. Each is a separate element with a 48dp touch target.
Undo reads "Loading" while it runs and ignores taps.
"Undone" and the failure text are shown and announced through a polite live region that is always present.
The icon tile is hidden from TalkBack; the kind is spoken as text.
edgeCases: Long titles and descriptions wrap; Open and Undo wrap onto a second line at large font sizes.
Without onOpen and onUndo the card is a plain summary with no actions.
An undo cancelled because the card left the composition is not shown as a failure.

The undone state lives in the card; if the card is recreated (for example scrolled out of a lazy list and back), it shows the result again. Keep the undone state in the app's model and stop passing onUndo when it must survive.

summary: The technical trace of one agent run: model calls, tool calls, retrievals, sub-agents and guardrails as a tree of rows with duration, tokens, cost and a bar on a shared time axis, run totals, a filter and the details of a span in a sheet.
whenToUse: For developers and operators who debug or audit an agent run: which step was slow, which failed, what went in and came out, what it cost.
whenNotToUse: For a short, flat list of a run's events for end users, use MonarchAiAgentRunTimeline. For several agents and their status, use MonarchAiSubagentTree.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchAiTraceView(spans: List<MonarchAiTraceSpan>, expandIcon: @Composable () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, currency: String = "USD", now: Long? = null, selection: String? = null, onSelectionChange: ((String?) -> Unit)? = null, filter: MonarchAiTraceFilter? = null, onFilterChange: ((MonarchAiTraceFilter) -> Unit)? = null, expanded: Set<String>? = null, onExpandedChange: ((Set<String>) -> Unit)? = null, locale: Locale? = null, labels: MonarchAiTraceViewLabels = MonarchAiTraceViewLabels(), onOpenPart: ((MonarchAiTraceSpan) -> Unit)? = null)

data class MonarchAiTraceSpan(id: String, kind: MonarchAiTraceSpanKind, name: String, status: MonarchAiTraceSpanStatus, start: Long, end: Long? = null, parentId: String? = null, inputTokens: Long? = null, outputTokens: Long? = null, costMicros: Long? = null, currency: String? = null, model: String? = null, error: String? = null, attributes: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(), input: String? = null, output: String? = null, partId: String? = null, messageId: String? = null)
enum class MonarchAiTraceSpanKind { Model, Tool, Retrieval, Agent, Guardrail, Other }
enum class MonarchAiTraceSpanStatus { Ok, Error, Cancelled, Running }
enum class MonarchAiTraceFilter { All, Errors, Slowest }

class MonarchAiTraceViewLabels(label: String? = null, filterLabel: String? = null, filter: ((MonarchAiTraceFilter) -> String)? = null, kind: ((MonarchAiTraceSpanKind) -> String)? = null, status: ((MonarchAiTraceSpanStatus) -> String)? = null, totalDuration: String? = null, totalTokens: String? = null, totalCost: String? = null, errors: String? = null, notAvailable: String? = null, empty: String? = null, noErrors: String? = null, tokens: ((count: Long) -> String)? = null, formatDuration: ((millis: Long) -> String)? = null, timing: ((start: String, duration: String?) -> String)? = null, closeDetails: String? = null, openPart: String? = null, start: String? = null, end: String? = null, duration: String? = null, inputTokens: String? = null, outputTokens: String? = null, model: String? = null, statusName: String? = null, kindName: String? = null, error: String? = null, attributes: String? = null, input: String? = null, output: String? = null, expand: ((name: String) -> String)? = null, collapse: ((name: String) -> String)? = null)

options.name: spans
options.description: The spans of one run, in any order; times in milliseconds from the run start. Children come from parentId, in start order.

options.name: expandIcon
options.description: A chevron that points to the end; it turns a quarter when the span is open. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the trace.

options.name: currency
options.description: The ISO 4217 currency of spans that name none.

options.name: now
options.description: The end of running spans, in milliseconds from the run start. Null ends them at the latest known time; the view never reads the clock.

options.name: selection
options.description: The id of the span whose details are open. The view keeps the person's choice and starts again from this value when it changes.

options.name: onSelectionChange
options.description: Called with the id of the span the person opens, and with null when the details close.

options.name: filter
options.description: All, Errors (failed spans and their ancestors) or Slowest (siblings slowest first). Null lets the view keep it, starting from All.

options.name: onFilterChange
options.description: Called when the person changes the filter.

options.name: expanded
options.description: The ids of the open spans. Null keeps them inside the view, starting with top-level spans, failed spans and their ancestors open.

options.name: onExpandedChange
options.description: Called with the new set of open ids.

options.name: locale
options.description: The locale of numbers, durations and money. Null uses the configuration's locale.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string and the duration format.

options.name: onOpenPart
options.description: Adds Show in conversation to the details of a span with a partId or messageId.

states.name: open and closed
states.description: A span with children has a toggle; its children are listed under it, indented 16dp per level, while it is open.

states.name: selected
states.description: The span's row takes the accent subtle fill and its details open in a bottom sheet.

states.name: error
states.description: The row shows an Error badge in the danger tone and a danger bar; the details show the error message.

states.name: running
states.description: The row shows a Running badge; the bar ends at now and uses the AI thinking color.

states.name: errors only
states.description: Only failed spans and their ancestors; No errors in this run when there are none.

states.name: empty
states.description: No spans recorded.

appearance: A subheading, totals with the value in strong tabular digits over a muted caption, Material 3 segmented buttons in the Monarch theme, then rows with the name in the label style, a muted facts line and a thin bar on a muted track. Bars are coloured by kind (AI solid for models, AI tool for tools, info for retrievals, default text for agents, warning strong for guardrails, strong border for others), danger solid for errors, disabled text for cancelled spans and AI thinking for running ones. The details sheet uses the raised background. The same roles adapt to dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web shows a six-column tree grid with arrow keys, windowing and an inline details panel. A phone cannot fit six columns, so, as on iOS, each row shows the name with a facts line and the bar under it, and the details open in a Material 3 ModalBottomSheet. The rows are a Column rather than a lazy list so the trace can sit in a scrolling screen; with the default open set only top-level spans, failed spans and their ancestors are listed, and very large traces belong in their own screen. Times are Long milliseconds from the run start (iOS uses seconds); attributes are strings. expandIcon is required because Monarch bundles no icons. Durations follow the web's format (850 ms, 1.42 s, 12.5 s, 2 min 5 s) with the locale given explicitly; costs show two decimals, four below one unit. The web's OpenTelemetry converters are not offered; map spans in the app. Selection, filter and the open set are hoisted values with callbacks instead of bindings. The web's copy announcements come from MonarchCopyButton. Experimental: a domain pattern until a Rook app adopts it.
accessibility: The title Run trace is a heading; each total is one element read as its name and value, such as Total time, 4.2 s.

Each span is one button read as its name, status (when not OK), kind, tokens, cost and timing, such as Starts at +1.4 s, takes 600 ms; it has a 48dp touch target and exposes the selected state while its details are open.
The open and close button is a separate element named Expand or Collapse and the span name, with a 48dp target.
Bars and the facts line are hidden inside the span's element, so nothing depends on bar color or length; status is a word in a badge.
The details sheet has the span name as a heading, facts read as label and value, headings for attributes, input and output, and copy buttons named after what they copy.
The filter is a Material 3 segmented button row named Show, with the selected state of each option.
The chevron turn follows the reduced-motion setting.
edgeCases: A repeated id keeps the first span; an unknown parent makes a top-level span; spans in a parent loop are each shown at the top level.
A span that ends before it starts counts as zero long; the shortest bar is 2dp so instant spans stay visible.
Costs in several currencies are listed side by side in the total.
Token and cost totals add every span; parents must carry only their own usage.
Without now, a running span ends at the latest time any span knows.

parityExceptions.reason: The web draws one table of six columns (Span, Kind, Duration, Tokens, Cost and Timeline) in about 620px. A phone window leaves 344dp, and the six columns at a readable width need 736dp, so a table that fits would break words in the span names. The phone therefore draws each span as two lines in the same order of data: the name, the kind and the duration on the first, the timeline bar with the tokens and the cost under it on the second, under one header row.
parityExceptions.convention: a wide table is a two-line row on a compact window rather than a sideways scroll or a squeezed column (Material list items)

name: MonarchAiTypingDots
title: AiTypingDots
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.animation.core.rememberInfiniteTransition, androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row, androidx.compose.ui.draw.drawBehind
summary: Three dots that rise and brighten in turn to show the assistant is writing, for places with no room for a sentence.
whenToUse: In a chat dock, a list row or an empty assistant message bubble while the reply has not started to stream.
whenNotToUse: For other people typing in a conversation use MonarchTypingIndicator, which names them. For the progress of a task use MonarchProgress.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiTypingDots(modifier: Modifier = Modifier, size: MonarchAiTypingDotsSize = MonarchAiTypingDotsSize.Md, announce: Boolean = true, label: String? = null)
enum class MonarchAiTypingDotsSize { Sm, Md }

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the dots.

options.name: size
options.description: Sm: 4dp dots for docks and dense rows. Md: 6dp dots for a message bubble.

options.name: announce
options.description: Makes the dots a polite live region whose text is set one frame after they appear, so TalkBack announces them. Pass false when something else already announces the state.

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the built-in text "Assistant is typing" (monarch_aitypingdots_label).

states.name: animating
states.description: Each dot rises by 0.6 of its size and turns from the assistant border color to the strong assistant color, one after another, in a 1.2-second cycle.

states.name: animations off
states.description: The dots stand still in the strong assistant color.

appearance: Dots in the strong assistant color at the top of their rise and the assistant border color at rest, in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The timing follows the web: a cycle of three quarters of the shimmer duration and an eighth of it between dots. The web fades the dots from 40% opacity; Android moves between two assistant color roles instead, because Monarch does not dim colors with alpha. The web keeps the label in visually hidden text; Android sets it as the content description of the one element. iOS names the flag isAnnounced; Android uses announce, as the web does.
accessibility: The dots are one TalkBack element whose content description is the label, "Assistant is typing" by default.
With announce the element is a polite live region and its text is set one frame after it appears, so the label is announced without moving focus.
With announce false the element has the label but no live region.
The dots do not move when the user has turned animations off.
The dots grow with the font size setting.
edgeCases: The label is announced each time the dots enter the composition; insert them once per reply, not per token.
A rising dot is drawn above the element's bounds by up to 0.6 of its size, inside the vertical padding the component keeps.

examples.title: Sizes
Small, in a dock that announces the state itself
examples.code: MonarchAiTypingDots(size = MonarchAiTypingDotsSize.Sm, announce = false)

name: MonarchAiUndoBanner
title: AiUndoBanner
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row on the AI subtle surface with androidx.compose.material3.Text, MonarchCollapsible, MonarchButton and MonarchLink; androidx.compose.ui.platform.AccessibilityManager.calculateRecommendedTimeoutMillis and kotlinx.coroutines.delay for the time limit
summary: An inline banner after the AI changed something on the person's behalf: what changed, before and after, an Undo and a link to the audit log, optionally for a limited time.
whenToUse: Right where the AI changed fields or records the person is looking at, such as a deal the assistant updated, so they can check and reverse the change.
whenNotToUse: For a change made somewhere else, or one that does not need its details, a snackbar with Undo is enough (see undo-toast). For the result of a tool that created something new, use MonarchAiToolResultCard.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiUndoBanner(title: String, onUndo: suspend () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, description: String? = null, changes: List<MonarchAiChange> = emptyList(), durationMillis: Long? = null, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, onAudit: (() -> Unit)? = null, onExpire: (() -> Unit)? = null, onDismiss: (() -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiUndoBannerLabels = MonarchAiUndoBannerLabels())
class MonarchAiChange(label: String, before: String, after: String)

class MonarchAiUndoBannerLabels(aiPrefix: String? = null, undo: String? = null, audit: String? = null, dismiss: String? = null, showChanges: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, change: ((label: String, before: String, after: String) -> String)? = null, undone: String? = null, undoFailed: String? = null, expired: String? = null)

options.name: title
options.description: What the AI did, in the past tense: "AI changed 3 fields".

options.name: onUndo
options.description: Reverts the change. Runs in a coroutine of the banner; throw to report a failure.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the banner.

options.name: description
options.description: One line of detail.

options.name: changes
options.description: The fields that changed, before and after. More than three are put in a disclosure.

options.name: durationMillis
options.description: How long Undo stays available. null keeps it. Extended to the accessibility setting "Time to take action" when that is longer.

options.name: icon
options.description: A glyph at the start in the AI strong color, hidden from TalkBack. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: onAudit
options.description: Shows a "View in audit log" link that calls it.

options.name: onExpire
options.description: Called once when durationMillis runs out without an undo.

options.name: onDismiss
options.description: Shows a Dismiss button that calls it. The app removes the banner.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including the spoken form of a change.

states.name: active
states.description: AI subtle fill and AI border, with Undo.

states.name: undoing
states.description: Undo shows its progress indicator, reads "Loading" and ignores taps; the time limit is paused.

states.name: undone
states.description: Subtle neutral fill and the default border; "Changes undone" is shown and announced; Undo goes away.

states.name: failed
states.description: "Couldn’t undo. Try again." in the danger strong color, announced; Undo stays.

states.name: expired
states.description: Subtle neutral fill; "Undo is no longer available." is shown and announced; onExpire runs once.

appearance: A rounded panel with a 1dp border. While Undo is offered it uses the AI subtle fill, the AI border and the AI strong glyph; once undone or expired, the subtle background and the default border. The old value is struck through in the muted text color, the new value is in the default text color, and the failure uses the danger strong role. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The parity map names MonarchBanner, but that banner has one action; this banner uses the same layout in the colors of MonarchTone.Ai, and adds Undo, the audit link and Dismiss, as on iOS. On the web the time limit pauses while the pointer is over the banner or focus is inside it; on Android it pauses while the undo runs and while the changes disclosure is open, and it is extended by AccessibilityManager.calculateRecommendedTimeoutMillis, as Material snackbars are, so a person who asked for more time gets it. iOS instead turns the limit off with VoiceOver on. The web's auditHref becomes onAudit: the app opens the entry. The web's onUndo may return a promise; here it is a suspend function, and a thrown exception shows the built-in failure text. Monarch bundles no icons: the web's bot glyph and close icon become an optional icon slot and a Dismiss text button. The web's useAiUndoToast hook is a snackbar with an Undo action on Android (see undo-toast).
accessibility: The title is read as "AI change:" followed by the title and the description, as one TalkBack element.
Each change is one element read as "Status changed from Open to Closed"; the old value is struck through as well as muted, and the arrow is not read.
More than three changes sit in a MonarchCollapsible, which reads its expanded state.
Undo, the audit link and Dismiss are separate elements with 48dp touch targets; Undo reads "Loading" while it runs.
"Changes undone", the failure and the end of the time limit are shown and announced through a polite live region that is always present.
The time limit follows the accessibility setting "Time to take action" when that is longer.
edgeCases: Long titles, labels and values wrap; the parts of a change wrap onto the next line at large font sizes.
The arrow between the values points the reading direction: it is reversed right to left.
Changing durationMillis restarts the time limit.
An undo cancelled because the banner left the composition is not shown as a failure, and onExpire is not called after the banner has left.
The state lives in the banner: if it is recreated, it starts again as active. Remove the banner, or stop showing it, once the app has recorded the outcome.

name: MonarchAiUsageMeter
title: AiUsageMeter
wrapsNative: MonarchUsageMeter (androidx.compose.material3.LinearProgressIndicator per scope), androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Box with a polite live region
summary: How much AI the person has used against their quotas: one meter per scope (this turn, the conversation, this month) in tokens or credits.
whenToUse: In an assistant panel, a settings screen or a billing screen, to show AI usage against quotas and warn before a limit is reached.
whenNotToUse: For usage that is not about AI (seats, storage, requests) use MonarchUsageMeter. For how full the model's context window is use a context window meter.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiUsageMeter(scopes: List<MonarchAiUsageScope>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, title: String? = null, period: String? = null, resetsAtMillis: Long? = null, warningAt: Double = 0.8, loading: Boolean = false, error: String? = null, onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiUsageMeterLabels = MonarchAiUsageMeterLabels())
class MonarchAiUsageScope(label: String, used: Double, limit: Double? = null, unit: MonarchAiUsageUnit = MonarchAiUsageUnit.Tokens, id: String? = null)
enum class MonarchAiUsageUnit { Tokens, Credits }

class MonarchAiUsageMeterLabels(label: String? = null, unit: ((unit: MonarchAiUsageUnit, count: Double) -> String)? = null, nearLimit: ((label: String, percent: String) -> String)? = null, overLimit: ((label: String) -> String)? = null, meter: MonarchUsageMeterLabels = MonarchUsageMeterLabels())

options.name: scopes
options.description: The quotas in order, each with a label, the amount used, an optional limit, a unit (tokens or credits) and an optional id.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the meter.

options.name: title
options.description: A visible heading. Without it the group is named "AI usage" for TalkBack.

options.name: period
options.description: The period measured, shown under the title.

options.name: resetsAtMillis
options.description: When the quotas reset, in epoch milliseconds (UTC), shown under the title.

options.name: warningAt

options.name: loading

options.name: error

options.name: onRetry

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces the group name, the unit names, the two announcements and the strings of the underlying MonarchUsageMeter.

states.name: normal
states.description: Below the warning share: the meter uses the accent fill and the share in muted text.

states.name: near the limit
states.description: At or above warningAt, and exactly at the limit: warning fill and "Near the limit" written with the share.

states.name: over the limit
states.description: Above the limit: danger fill and "Over the limit" written with the share.

states.name: no limit
states.description: The amount and unit alone, with no meter.

states.name: loading
states.description: A progress indicator and "Loading usage".

states.name: error
states.description: The message in the danger text role, and a retry button with onRetry.

appearance: The look of MonarchUsageMeter: label text, the figures in strong body text, a Material 3 linear indicator on the emphasis track in the accent, warning or danger solid role, and the level in muted, warning strong or danger strong caption text. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: A preset of MonarchUsageMeter, so like iOS it also offers a title, a period, a reset date, loading and error, which the web does not. The web calls a scope exceeded when it reaches its limit; the shared meter, on iOS and Android, calls a scope over the limit only above it and near the limit at exactly 100%. Units come from Android plural resources. The web announces the most serious warning through a status region; Android does the same with an always-present polite live region, filled only after the most serious state changes while the meter is on screen. MonarchUsageMeter shows no warning icon on Android (Monarch bundles no icons); the level is written instead.
accessibility: The meter is a TalkBack traversal group named by the title, or by "AI usage".
Each scope is one element read as its label, its figures with the unit and its level and share (from MonarchUsageMeter).
Near and over the limit are written, so they do not depend on color.

When the most serious scope reaches near or over the limit while the meter is on screen, it is announced once through a polite live region, for example "This month: 85% of the limit used"; the state on first appearance is not announced.
The retry button has a touch target of at least 48dp by 48dp.
edgeCases: A negative amount counts as zero; a limit of zero or less, or one that is not finite, is no limit.
Scopes are identified by position unless they have an id, so labels may repeat.
The unit is singular only for exactly one (the limit, or the amount when there is no limit); fractional counts use the other form.
No announcement is made while loading or showing an error.

parityExceptions.convention: a meter is read from its visible lines (Android accessibility)

name: MonarchAiUserMessageEdit
title: AiUserMessageEdit
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedTextField with minLines and maxLines, MonarchButton, androidx.compose.ui.input.key.onPreviewKeyEvent
summary: An inline editor for a prompt the person already sent: a multi-line field, a note that resending starts a new branch, and Cancel and Send buttons.
whenToUse: In place of a sent user message when the person chooses to edit it.
whenNotToUse: For writing a new message use the prompt input of the conversation. For editing other text use MonarchTextField.

options.name: original
options.description: The prompt as it was sent. The field starts with it.

options.name: onSubmit
options.description: Called with the trimmed text when the user sends it.

options.name: onCancel
options.description: Called when the user cancels. Leave edit mode here.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the editor.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the field and buttons can be used.

options.name: maxLines
options.description: The lines the field grows to before it scrolls. At least 2.

options.name: focusOnAppear
options.description: Moves focus into the field, caret at the end, when the editor appears.

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the TalkBack label "Edit message".

options.name: branchHint
options.description: Replaces the note that resending keeps the original.

options.name: sendLabel
options.description: Replaces "Send".

options.name: cancelLabel
options.description: Replaces "Cancel".

states.name: unchanged or empty
states.description: Send is disabled: the trimmed text is empty or equal to the trimmed original.

states.name: changed
states.description: Send is the primary button and calls onSubmit with the trimmed text.

states.name: focused
states.description: The field's border takes the focus ring color.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The field uses the subtle fill and disabled text, and both buttons are disabled.

appearance: The field is a Material 3 outlined field in the Monarch text field colors: surface fill, input border, focus ring color while focused. The note uses the muted text color. Cancel is a ghost button and Send a primary button, in every theme.
platformNotes: On the web Enter sends and Shift+Enter adds a line. On Android Return adds a line, as in every multi-line field, so Send is a button; with a hardware keyboard Ctrl+Enter (or Meta+Enter) sends and Escape cancels. The web's hidden keyboard hint is therefore not offered. The field starts two lines high. The text is held by the component and starts again from original when original changes; it survives configuration changes.
accessibility: The field's content description is "Edit message" (or label).
The branch note is the field's supporting text, shown under it and read with it.
Send is disabled, and exposed as disabled, until the text can be resent.
Both buttons keep a 48dp touch target; they wrap onto a second line when they do not fit.
Cancel comes before Send in reading order in both layout directions.
edgeCases: Leading and trailing white space and line breaks are trimmed before comparing and before onSubmit.
A maxLines below 2 is treated as 2.
Text longer than maxLines scrolls inside the field.
focusOnAppear raises the keyboard as soon as the editor is shown; a disabled editor does not take focus.

name: MonarchAiVoiceInput
title: AiVoiceInput
wrapsNative: android.speech.SpeechRecognizer (through MonarchAiSystemSpeechRecognizer, behind the MonarchAiSpeechRecognizer interface), androidx.activity.compose.rememberLauncherForActivityResult with ActivityResultContracts.RequestMultiplePermissions; MonarchButton, MonarchAudioLevelMeter and MonarchInlineNotice
summary: A microphone button that dictates into a prompt (press to start and again to stop, or hold to talk), with a level meter, the words as they are recognised and guidance when microphone access is refused.
whenToUse: Beside an AI prompt field, so people can speak a prompt instead of typing it. The text goes into the field; the person still sends it.
whenNotToUse: For a live spoken conversation with the assistant use MonarchAiVoiceMode. For a recording that is kept as audio use the app's own recorder.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchAiVoiceInput(onTranscript: (text: String, final: Boolean) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, recognizer: MonarchAiSpeechRecognizer? = null, locale: Locale? = null, mode: MonarchAiVoiceInputMode = MonarchAiVoiceInputMode.Toggle, size: MonarchButtonSize = MonarchButtonSize.Md, enabled: Boolean = true, showLevel: Boolean = true, showTranscript: Boolean = true, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiVoiceInputLabels = MonarchAiVoiceInputLabels(), onStateChange: ((MonarchAiVoiceInputState) -> Unit)? = null)
enum class MonarchAiVoiceInputMode { Toggle, PushToTalk }
enum class MonarchAiVoiceInputState { Idle, Starting, Listening, Denied, Error }

interface MonarchAiSpeechRecognizer { val requiredPermissions: List<String> get() = emptyList(); fun isAvailable(locale: Locale?): Boolean; fun start(locale: Locale?, continuous: Boolean): Flow<MonarchAiSpeechEvent>; fun stop() }
sealed interface MonarchAiSpeechEvent { data object Started; data class Level(value: Float); data class Partial(text: String); data class Final(text: String) }
enum class MonarchAiSpeechError { Denied, NoSpeech, NoMicrophone, Unavailable, Failed }
class MonarchAiSpeechException(error: MonarchAiSpeechError) : Exception
@ExperimentalMonarchApi class MonarchAiSystemSpeechRecognizer(context: Context, preferOffline: Boolean = false) : MonarchAiSpeechRecognizer

class MonarchAiVoiceInputLabels(dictate: String? = null, holdToTalk: String? = null, holdHint: String? = null, starting: String? = null, listening: String? = null, stopped: String? = null, denied: String? = null, noSpeech: String? = null, noMicrophone: String? = null, unavailable: String? = null, error: String? = null, transcript: String? = null, openSettings: String? = null)

options.name: onTranscript
options.description: Recognised text. Guesses come with final false and may change; each settled phrase comes once with final true. Put final text into the prompt; never send it automatically.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the voice input.

options.name: recognizer
options.description: The speech engine. null uses MonarchAiSystemSpeechRecognizer (the device's android.speech.SpeechRecognizer). Implement the interface for a server recogniser, an on-device model or a scripted one.

options.name: locale
options.description: The language of the speech. The device language by default.

options.name: mode
options.description: Toggle: press to start and again to stop. PushToTalk: listen while held.

options.name: size
options.description: The size of the button: Sm, Md or Lg.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the button can start a session. Turning it off stops a running session.

options.name: showLevel
options.description: Shows a five-segment level meter while listening.

options.name: showTranscript
options.description: Shows the words under the button as they are recognised.

options.name: icon
options.description: A microphone icon before the label. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: onStateChange
options.description: Called with every change of state.

states.name: idle
states.description: The button in the secondary variant, off.

states.name: starting
states.description: The button is on (primary variant) and the status reads Starting microphone… while the permission and the microphone are requested.

states.name: listening
states.description: The button is on, the level meter moves, the status reads Listening… and the transcript grows.

states.name: denied
states.description: A warning notice explains that microphone access is off, with an Open settings action that opens the app's page in the system settings.

states.name: error
states.description: A notice with the reason: nothing heard (info), no microphone or recognition unavailable (warning), or an unexpected failure (danger).

states.name: disabled
states.description: With enabled false the button uses the disabled roles and does not start; a running session is stopped.

appearance: The button is MonarchButton: the secondary variant when idle and the primary accent variant while listening. The level meter is the small MonarchAudioLevelMeter, the status is muted caption text, the transcript body text, and failures use MonarchInlineNotice in the info, warning or danger tone. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web uses the browser's Web Speech API and getUserMedia; iOS uses the Speech framework; Android uses android.speech.SpeechRecognizer through MonarchAiSystemSpeechRecognizer, behind the same recogniser abstraction (a Kotlin Flow of events instead of an AsyncThrowingStream). The app must declare android.permission.RECORD_AUDIO and, on Android 11 and later, list android.speech.RecognitionService in <queries>; the component asks for the permission at run time with the Activity Result API. Languages, session length and on-device support depend on the installed recognition service (usually the Google app); preferOffline asks for on-device recognition where the language allows. The system recogniser stops after a pause, so in toggle mode it is restarted after each phrase until stopped. TalkBack has no escape gesture, so Escape on a hardware keyboard stops listening; there is no Android equivalent of iOS's escape gesture. The web's createRecognition hook is the recognizer parameter. Experimental: MonarchAiSystemSpeechRecognizer compiles and its error mapping is unit tested, but it has not been run against a device's recognition service; the component itself is tested with scripted recognisers.
accessibility: In toggle mode the button is a MonarchButton that also reports an on or off toggle state, so TalkBack reads it as on while listening.
In push-to-talk mode, which cannot be held with TalkBack or Switch Access, the button's click action starts and a second one stops; the action is labelled "start or stop listening".
"Listening…" is announced on start and "Stopped listening." when it ends, through an always-present polite live region; failures are announced by the notice.
The level meter is decorative; when animations are off it follows MonarchAudioLevelMeter's still form.
The transcript is read as "Transcript:" followed by the words; the visible status is not read twice.
The notice has the tone's spoken name and the message, so the failure is not conveyed by color alone.
The button keeps a touch target of at least 48dp by 48dp; text wraps at large font sizes.
edgeCases: When the recogniser is not available the component draws nothing.
Releasing push-to-talk, or pressing again, while the permission request is open ends the session at once.
Leaving the composition cancels the session and discards pending words without an announcement.
A second start while a session runs is ignored.
Without an ActivityResultRegistryOwner (for example in a bare preview) a missing permission counts as refused.
Empty guesses and phrases are ignored.

name: MonarchAiVoiceMode
title: AiVoiceMode
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column with an androidx.compose.foundation.Canvas visual, a verticalScroll captions log and MonarchButton controls (androidx.compose.material3.Button); polite live regions for announcements
summary: The surface for a live, two-way spoken conversation with an AI assistant: a calm central visual, always-visible state text, live captions, and explicit Mute, Interrupt, Captions and End controls.
whenToUse: While the person talks with the assistant by voice, in a full-screen dialog (Md) or inside an assistant panel (Compact).
whenNotToUse: To dictate text into a prompt use MonarchAiVoiceInput. For a call between people use the call components.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiVoiceMode(state: MonarchAiVoiceModeState, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, level: Float = 0f, agent: MonarchAiAgentRef? = null, agentAvatar: Painter? = null, captions: List<MonarchAiConversationMessage> = emptyList(), captionsVisible: Boolean? = null, muted: Boolean? = null, elapsedSeconds: Int? = null, error: String? = null, size: MonarchAiVoiceModeSize = MonarchAiVoiceModeSize.Md, labels: MonarchAiVoiceModeLabels = MonarchAiVoiceModeLabels(), onCaptionsVisibleChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, onMuteChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, onInterrupt: (() -> Unit)? = null, onEnd: (() -> Unit)? = null, onRestart: (() -> Unit)? = null, onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null)
enum class MonarchAiVoiceModeState { Connecting, Listening, Thinking, Speaking, Muted, Reconnecting, Ended, Error }
enum class MonarchAiVoiceModeSize { Md, Compact }

class MonarchAiVoiceModeLabels(label: ((agentName: String) -> String)? = null, assistant: String? = null, you: String? = null, states: Map<MonarchAiVoiceModeState, String> = emptyMap(), microphoneMuted: String? = null, mute: String? = null, interrupt: String? = null, captions: String? = null, captionsLabel: String? = null, end: String? = null, restart: String? = null, retry: String? = null, captionsEmpty: String? = null, elapsed: String? = null, lasted: ((duration: String) -> String)? = null, errorFallback: String? = null)

options.name: state
options.description: Where the call is, reported by the app.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the surface. It fills the available width.

options.name: level
options.description: The live audio level, 0 to 1, of whoever is talking. Drives the halo and the bars while listening or speaking, not when animations are off.

options.name: agent
options.description: The assistant; its name labels the surface and its captions.

options.name: agentAvatar
options.description: The assistant's picture, loaded by the app, shown beside its name and hidden from TalkBack.

options.name: captions
options.description: The conversation's messages, oldest first. User and assistant text is shown; a message with streaming text is an interim caption.

options.name: captionsVisible
options.description: Whether captions show. null lets the surface keep its own value, on at first.

options.name: muted
options.description: Whether the microphone is muted. By default only in the Muted state.

options.name: elapsedSeconds
options.description: How long the call has run, shown as a clock while live and as the duration once ended.

options.name: error
options.description: What went wrong, shown on the Error state. A general sentence by default.

options.name: size
options.description: Md stands on its own on the canvas background; Compact is a bordered card with small buttons.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including the state texts.

options.name: onCaptionsVisibleChange
options.description: Called with the wanted value when the person turns captions on or off.

options.name: onMuteChange
options.description: Called with the wanted value from Mute or the Space key. Shows Mute while the call is live.

options.name: onInterrupt
options.description: Shows Interrupt while the assistant thinks or speaks.

options.name: onEnd
options.description: Shows End while the call is live. Only this button ends the call.

options.name: onRestart
options.description: Shows Start again on the Ended state.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Retry on the Error state.

states.name: connecting, thinking, reconnecting
states.description: The orb shows three dots that rise in turn; the state text says which.

states.name: listening, speaking
states.description: The orb shows five bars and the halo grows with the level.

states.name: muted
states.description: A neutral orb with a resting line; Mute is on. Muted in another state adds the note Your microphone is muted.

states.name: ended
states.description: A neutral orb, Conversation ended, the duration, and Start again when onRestart is given.

states.name: error
states.description: A danger orb with an exclamation mark, the error text, and Retry when onRetry is given.

appearance: Md fills the width on the canvas background; Compact is a surface card with the subtle border and the container radius. The halo uses the assistant subtle role and the orb the assistant solid role with assistant on-solid marks; an error uses the danger roles, muted and ended the subtle and emphasis backgrounds with muted text marks. The state is heading text (body strong when compact), the name and clock label text, captions body text with the speaker in semibold (strong assistant for the assistant, muted for the person). The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Android, like iOS, ships only the surface; the web also ships browser and realtime session helpers. The app owns audio focus, the audio mode, routes and interruptions as the KDoc describes (requestAudioFocus with USAGE_VOICE_COMMUNICATION, ACTION_AUDIO_BECOMING_NOISY), where iOS describes AVAudioSession. Show the Md size in a full-screen Dialog. Captions use the shared MonarchAiConversationMessage model, as on iOS. Space toggles mute as on the web; Android has no Magic Tap. The agent picture is a Painter (agentAvatar), because Monarch for Android loads no images; the web shows an AiAgentAvatar. Monarch bundles no icons, so the controls are text buttons without the web's glyphs, and the muted orb shows a resting line instead of a crossed-out microphone; the state text always says Muted. captionsVisible is hoisted with onCaptionsVisibleChange, or kept by the surface when null (iOS takes an optional Binding). The captions log keeps the newest caption in view unless the person scrolled up, as on the web.
accessibility: The surface is a TalkBack traversal group named "Voice conversation with" and the assistant's name.
The state is always written; each change is announced through a polite live region, except the first state and changes into listening or speaking. An error is announced with its text.

Final captions are announced once each, through a second polite live region, as "You:" or the assistant's name followed by the words; interim captions are hidden from TalkBack until they are final. Captions that are final on appearance or while captions are hidden are not announced.
Mute and Captions are buttons that also report an on or off toggle state.
When Interrupt goes away while it has focus, focus moves to Mute.
The visual is decorative and hidden; it holds still when animations are off. The state text carries the meaning, not color.
Buttons keep 48dp touch targets; text wraps at large font sizes and the captions log scrolls, growing with the font size.
edgeCases: System and tool messages, and messages with no text, are not captions.
Captions show while the call is live even when there are none yet (with a hint), and after it only when there are some.
A level outside 0 to 1 is limited; not a number is 0.
Times of an hour or more show hours: 1:02:09; a negative time is 0:00.
muted is ignored once the call has ended or failed.

name: MonarchBanner
title: Alert
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row, androidx.compose.material3.Text
summary: An inline message about the state of a screen or a section, with a tone, an optional title, icon and action.
whenToUse: For a status that stays visible until it is resolved: an error, a warning, a confirmation.
whenNotToUse: For a brief confirmation that disappears on its own use the Material 3 Snackbar. For a decision that blocks the flow use AlertDialog. For the status of one item use MonarchBadge.
api: @Composable fun MonarchBanner(message: String?, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, tone: MonarchTone = MonarchTone.Info, title: String? = null, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = { MonarchBannerToneIcon(tone) }, action: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, announcement: MonarchBannerAnnouncement = MonarchBannerAnnouncement.None)
enum class MonarchBannerAnnouncement { None, Polite, Assertive }

options.name: message
options.description: The message, one or two sentences; null for a banner that is only a title.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the component.

options.name: tone
options.description: Neutral, Info, Success, Warning or Danger.

options.name: title
options.description: A short summary above the message.

options.name: icon
options.description: The icon at the start, in the tone colour. By default the tone's icon, as on the web and iOS (info circle for neutral and info, check circle for success, warning triangle for warning and danger); null for none.

options.name: action
options.description: An action at the end, for example a small ghost MonarchButton.

options.name: announcement
options.description: None, Polite or Assertive.

states.name: default
states.description: Stays in the layout until the app removes it.

states.name: announced
states.description: A live region: TalkBack reads it when it appears or changes.

appearance: The tinted background and border of the tone with default text; the icon takes the strong color of the tone. The neutral banner sits on the subtle background.
platformNotes: Named MonarchBanner on Android and iOS, because Alert means a modal dialog on both platforms; the web calls it Alert. The tone icon is shown by default as on the web and iOS, from the glyphs Monarch bundles. One action slot instead of the web's list of actions.
accessibility: Title and message are one TalkBack element.
Polite or Assertive makes that element a live region.
The action stays a separate element with its own 48dp touch target.
The icon is at the start and the action at the end, following the layout direction.
Text wraps and the banner grows with the font size setting.
edgeCases: A banner that is on screen from the start should not be a live region.
With a wide action and a large font size the text column gets narrow; keep the action label short.
With icon = null the tone is carried by colour and text only; say the status in the text.

summary: A recipe, not a component: one timely announcement across the top of a screen (a launch, a maintenance window, a policy change), with a link and a dismiss button, built from MonarchCalloutBanner in the page placement under the top app bar.
whenToUse: For a short message that concerns everyone using the app for a while: a new feature, planned maintenance, a change of terms.
whenNotToUse: For a message about one record or one form, use MonarchCalloutBanner in the section placement or MonarchInlineNotice. For the result of something the person just did, use a snackbar. For a session state such as impersonation, use MonarchImpersonationBanner.

states.name: shown
states.description: The banner sits under the top app bar, above the scrolling content, with the link and the dismiss button.

states.name: dismissed
states.description: The banner is removed and the content moves up; store the dismissal so it stays dismissed.

states.name: not dismissible
states.description: Without onDismiss there is no dismiss button, for a maintenance window that must stay visible.

appearance: MonarchCalloutBanner in the page placement: a full-width band without rounded corners in the tone's subtle colors, with the message in the default text color and the link in the link color. Use the info tone for news, warning for maintenance. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web AnnouncementBar is its own component with accent and inverse tones and a sticky option. On Android it is a recipe: the topBar slot of Scaffold keeps it above the scrolling content, which is what sticky does on the web. MonarchTone has no accent or inverse tone, so the recipe uses info, warning or neutral. The web leaves storing the dismissal to the product; on Android keep it in the app's settings (for example DataStore) keyed by the announcement, and use rememberSaveable only for the screen's lifetime. iOS uses the same recipe with safeAreaInset.
accessibility: MonarchCalloutBanner reads the tone and the message as one TalkBack element, so the announcement is not conveyed by color alone.
The link and the dismiss button are separate elements with 48dp touch targets; the dismiss button is named "Dismiss".
The banner is not a live region by default: it is present when the screen opens. Pass announcement = MonarchBannerAnnouncement.Polite when it appears while the person is on the screen.
edgeCases: Long messages wrap; keep them to one sentence so the banner does not take half a phone screen.
Show one announcement at a time; queue the others.
If the link opens a web page, use LocalUriHandler.current.openUri in its onClick.

parityExceptions.reason: The web strip is 614px wide: the message, the link with its arrow and the close button fit on one centred line (about 400px). The phone window is 344dp wide, which leaves about 250dp after the close button's 48dp target and the padding, so the link goes under the message on its own centred line. The strip is the same: red tint, no icon, the message, the link with the arrow, then the close button.
parityExceptions.convention: a banner wraps its action under the message on a compact window (Material banner)

name: MonarchApiKeyRow
title: ApiKeyRow
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.ListItem with androidx.compose.material3.DropdownMenu for the actions and androidx.compose.material3.AlertDialog (ConfirmDialog) for the confirmations; MonarchStatusBadge, MonarchBadge, MonarchTypeToConfirmInput, MonarchInlineErrorRetry; android.text.format.DateUtils for the times
summary: One API key in a list: name and status, the visible prefix with the rest masked, created, last used and expiry times, scopes, and Rotate and Revoke actions that ask for confirmation before calling the app.
whenToUse: In a developer settings screen that lists a workspace's API keys or tokens.
whenNotToUse: To show a new secret once use MonarchKeyCreatedDialog. For a secret the person pastes or edits use MonarchSecretField.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchApiKeyRow(name: String, prefix: String, createdAt: Long, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, lastUsedAt: Long? = null, expiresAt: Long? = null, scopes: List<String> = emptyList(), maxScopes: Int = 3, status: MonarchApiKeyStatus = MonarchApiKeyStatus.Active, now: Long? = null, revokeConfirmPhrase: String? = null, onRotate: (suspend () -> Unit)? = null, onRevoke: (suspend () -> Unit)? = null, menuIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchApiKeyRowLabels = MonarchApiKeyRowLabels(), actions: (@Composable ColumnScope.(close: () -> Unit) -> Unit)? = null)
public enum class MonarchApiKeyStatus { Active, Expiring, Expired, Revoked }

public class MonarchApiKeyRowLabels(prefix: ((prefix: String) -> String)? = null, created: String? = null, lastUsed: String? = null, neverUsed: String? = null, expires: String? = null, scopes: String? = null, noScopes: String? = null, moreScopes: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, status: ((status: MonarchApiKeyStatus) -> String)? = null, menu: String? = null, actions: ((name: String) -> String)? = null, rotate: String? = null, revoke: String? = null, rotateTitle: ((name: String) -> String)? = null, rotateMessage: String? = null, rotateConfirm: String? = null, revokeTitle: ((name: String) -> String)? = null, revokeMessage: String? = null, revokeConfirm: String? = null, revokePhrasePrompt: ((phrase: String) -> String)? = null, cancel: String? = null, rotating: String? = null, revoking: String? = null, rotateFailed: String? = null, revokeFailed: String? = null)

options.name: name
options.description: The key's name, also used in the confirmations and the menu's spoken name.

options.name: prefix
options.description: The visible, non-secret start of the key; the rest is drawn as a mask.

options.name: createdAt
options.description: When the key was created, in epoch milliseconds, shown as a relative time.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the row.

options.name: lastUsedAt
options.description: When the key was last used; without it the row says Never used.

options.name: expiresAt
options.description: When the key expires, if it does.

options.name: scopes
options.description: Scope names, shown as outline badges; without any the row says No scopes.

options.name: maxScopes
options.description: Scopes shown before a +N badge; a negative number shows only the +N badge.

options.name: status
options.description: Active, expiring, expired or revoked; expired and revoked keys have no actions.

options.name: now
options.description: The reference time for relative times; without it they follow the clock, updated every minute.

options.name: revokeConfirmPhrase
options.description: A phrase, usually the name, that must be typed in the revoke dialog before Revoke key works.

options.name: onRotate
options.description: Rotates the key after confirmation. A thrown exception is shown in the row with Try again.

options.name: onRevoke
options.description: Revokes the key after confirmation, like onRotate.

options.name: menuIcon
options.description: Makes the actions button an icon button, such as three dots. Without it the button shows Actions.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string; strings that name something are functions.

options.name: actions
options.description: More menu items after Rotate and Revoke, such as Edit; call close to close the menu.

states.name: active, expiring
states.description: A success or warning status badge and the actions menu.

states.name: expired, revoked
states.description: A neutral or danger status badge and no actions.

states.name: confirming
states.description: Rotate shows an AlertDialog with a primary Rotate key button; Revoke shows one with a danger Revoke key button and, with a phrase, a MonarchTypeToConfirmInput that keeps the button disabled until it matches.

states.name: running
states.description: A small spinner with Rotating… or Revoking…, announced; the menu is disabled.

states.name: failed
states.description: MonarchInlineErrorRetry with the exception's message or the built-in sentence; Try again runs the action again.

appearance: A transparent Material 3 list item: the name in the strong body type with a small status badge, the prefix and mask in the code type and muted text, the times in muted caption text, and outline scope badges. The menu's Revoke item is in the strong danger color. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow the theme roles.
platformNotes: The web row shows Rotate and Revoke as buttons and keeps its ConfirmDialog open while the promise runs, showing a rejection inside it. On Android, as on iOS, the actions sit in a trailing menu, as list rows do; the Material 3 AlertDialog closes when a button is tapped, so progress and failures are shown in the row. The web's rotateConfirmOptions and revokeConfirmOptions are replaced by labels, and its separate list of consequences is one revoke message. iOS takes async throwing closures; Android takes suspend functions. Times are epoch milliseconds written with DateUtils.getRelativeTimeSpanString in the language of the app's resources (no java.time below API 26). The web's `as` and link-name options have no meaning on Android. Monarch bundles no icons, so the menu button shows Actions unless menuIcon is given. Android has no destructive menu role: Revoke is drawn in the danger color and its confirmation uses the danger button.
accessibility: The name and the status badge are merged into one element; the status is a word, not only a color.
The prefix is read as "Key starting with sk_live_4f2a"; the mask is not read.
Scopes are one element read as "Scopes" and every scope, including those behind +N.
The menu button is named "Actions for Reporting job" with a 48dp touch target, at the end of the row in both directions.
The confirmation title has heading semantics.
Rotating… or Revoking… is announced through a polite live region when an action starts; the failure is announced by MonarchInlineErrorRetry.
Text wraps at font scale 2.0; the name and status wrap onto two lines when they do not fit.
edgeCases: A long prefix is shortened in the middle, so its start and the mask stay visible.
Only one action runs at a time; the menu is disabled while it runs.
The Revoke key button is disabled until the phrase matches (case-sensitive, ignoring surrounding spaces), and the click checks it again.
A negative maxScopes shows only the +N badge.
The action runs in the row's coroutine scope: if the row leaves the composition, the action is cancelled.

summary: A checklist of apps to grant a member, with each app's logo, name, tag and description, Select all or Clear all with a count, and MonarchAppAccessSummary, the compact read-only line of granted apps for a member row.
whenToUse: When inviting someone to a workspace or editing a member's access, to choose which apps they can open; use MonarchAppAccessSummary in the member list to show what they have.
whenNotToUse: For roles with permissions, use MonarchRolePicker or MonarchPermissionMatrix. For a generic list of options, use MonarchCheckboxGroup.

states.description: An empty checkbox; the row reads as an unchecked checkbox.

states.name: selected
states.description: A ticked checkbox; the count goes up and the bulk button reads Clear all once every changeable app is selected.

states.name: fixed app
states.description: An app with enabled false is shown in the disabled text color with its checkbox disabled, ticked or not; Select all and Clear all leave it as it is.

states.name: disabled

states.name: loading

states.name: empty

states.name: summary

appearance: Rows of a Material 3 checkbox, a square MonarchAvatar logo (the initial on a tinted tile without a logo), the name in default body text with an optional neutral MonarchBadge and the description in muted caption text; disabled rows use the disabled text color. The count is muted caption text and the bulk action a small ghost button. All are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web's fieldset with a legend becomes a heading and a traversal group; with hideLabel the group carries the label as its content description. The web takes a logo URL; Android takes a Painter loaded by the app, as every Monarch picture does. The web's badge and description are React nodes; here they are strings. The web's small xs button is the Sm ghost MonarchButton, which keeps a 48dp touch target. The rows are a plain Column, not a LazyColumn, because the picker sits in the app's scrolling invite or member form. The summary sorts the names with java.text.Collator for the device locale where the web uses localeCompare. There is no iOS AppAccessPicker yet. Experimental: a product composite that waits for a Rook app to adopt it.
accessibility: Each row is one TalkBack element with the checkbox role and its on or off state, read as the name, the tag and the description, and is at least 48dp high.
Apps that cannot be changed and a disabled picker are reported as disabled and ignore taps.
The selection count is a polite live region, so a change is announced.
The label is a heading; with hideLabel it names the group instead.
Placeholder rows are hidden and read once as "Loading apps".
Logos are decorative; the summary is read as one element that includes the names behind +N.
Selection is shown by the checkbox mark, not by color alone.
edgeCases: Ids in value that are not in apps are kept by Select all and Clear all, and the summary shows them as the id.
A duplicate id in value is counted once in the summary.
Long names and descriptions wrap; the tag moves to the next line.
max below one still shows one name.
With no changeable apps the bulk button is disabled.
