title: AppShell
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.adaptive.navigationsuite.NavigationSuiteScaffold, which puts androidx.compose.material3.NavigationBar, NavigationRail or a navigation drawer around the content for the window size
summary: The app shell is the Material 3 adaptive navigation container: NavigationSuiteScaffold shows a bottom navigation bar on a phone and a navigation rail on larger windows around the current destination. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: As the top level of an app with three to five main destinations, so the navigation adapts to phones, foldables, tablets and desktop windows by itself.
whenNotToUse: For an app with one main screen, use a Scaffold with a TopAppBar only. For more than five destinations, use a navigation drawer (see sidebar-nav). Inside a destination, use tabs for sections.
api: @Composable fun NavigationSuiteScaffold(navigationSuiteItems: NavigationSuiteScope.() -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, layoutType: NavigationSuiteType = NavigationSuiteScaffoldDefaults.calculateFromAdaptiveInfo(currentWindowAdaptiveInfoV2()), navigationSuiteColors: NavigationSuiteColors = …, containerColor: Color = …, contentColor: Color = …, content: @Composable () -> Unit)

fun NavigationSuiteScope.item(selected: Boolean, onClick: () -> Unit, icon: @Composable () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, label: @Composable (() -> Unit)? = null, alwaysShowLabel: Boolean = true, badge: @Composable (() -> Unit)? = null, …)
NavigationSuiteType.NavigationBar, NavigationSuiteType.NavigationRail, NavigationSuiteType.NavigationDrawer, NavigationSuiteType.None

states.name: compact width
states.description: A NavigationBar at the bottom, below the content.

states.name: medium and expanded width
states.description: A NavigationRail at the start, beside the content.

states.name: no navigation
states.description: layoutType = NavigationSuiteType.None hides it, for example on a full-screen detail or editor.

appearance: The bar and the rail use the colors Monarch maps to the Material scheme: the raised surface, the accent subtle color for the selected indicator and the muted text color for the other destinations. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web AppShell lays out a rail, an identity bar and the main region, and adds a skip link, landmarks and contained scrolling. On Android the navigation suite does the layout and adapts to the window; there are no landmarks or skip links to add: TalkBack moves between the navigation and the content, and each destination scrolls on its own. The web's identity bar becomes the actions of each destination's TopAppBar, such as an account menu. iOS uses TabView. The catalogue page shows the bar and the rail with plain layout because the sample app does not depend on the navigation suite library; the example uses the real NavigationSuiteScaffold.
accessibility: System behavior: each destination is a selectable item; TalkBack reads its label, its selected state and its badge.
Each item has a touch target of at least 48dp.
Keep a label on every item (alwaysShowLabel = true), so a destination is never named by its icon alone.
Icons are decorative (contentDescription = null) because the label names the destination.
edgeCases: Keep each destination's state with rememberSaveable or a view model: the suite recomposes the content when the window changes size.
A badge with a count should also be said in the label or the item's semantics when it matters, such as "Inbox, 3 unread".

name: MonarchAppearancePanel
title: AppearancePanel
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of rows: MonarchThemeToggle, androidx.compose.material3.SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow for contrast, motion and density, MonarchSelect for the accent, separated by androidx.compose.material3.HorizontalDivider
summary: A settings panel for appearance with labelled, described rows for theme, contrast, accent, motion and density, bound to one MonarchAppearancePreferences value.
whenToUse: On an app's appearance or accessibility settings screen, to let people override the device's dark theme, contrast and motion settings and pick an accent.
whenNotToUse: For only the light, dark or system choice, use MonarchThemeToggle on its own.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAppearancePanel(preferences: MonarchAppearancePreferences, onPreferencesChange: (MonarchAppearancePreferences) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, title: String? = null, rows: List<MonarchAppearancePanelRow> = MonarchAppearancePanelRow.Standard, accents: List<MonarchAccent> = emptyList(), enabled: Boolean = true, labels: MonarchAppearancePanelLabels = MonarchAppearancePanelLabels())

data class MonarchAppearancePreferences(accent: MonarchAccent, scheme: MonarchScheme = MonarchScheme.System, contrast: MonarchContrast = MonarchContrast.System, motion: MonarchAppearanceMotion = MonarchAppearanceMotion.System, density: MonarchAppearanceDensity = MonarchAppearanceDensity.Comfortable) { fun reducesMotion(systemReducesMotion: Boolean): Boolean }
enum class MonarchAppearanceMotion { System, Reduce }
enum class MonarchAppearanceDensity { Comfortable, Compact }
enum class MonarchAppearancePanelRow { Theme, Contrast, Accent, Motion, Density; companion object { val Standard: List<MonarchAppearancePanelRow> } }

class MonarchAppearancePanelLabels(theme: String? = null, themeDescription: String? = null, light: String? = null, dark: String? = null, system: String? = null, contrast: String? = null, contrastDescription: String? = null, contrastStandard: String? = null, contrastMore: String? = null, contrastSystem: String? = null, accent: String? = null, accentDescription: String? = null, motion: String? = null, motionDescription: String? = null, motionSystem: String? = null, motionReduce: String? = null, density: String? = null, densityDescription: String? = null, densityComfortable: String? = null, densityCompact: String? = null)

options.name: preferences
options.description: All choices, built with the starting accent, for example MonarchAppearancePreferences(accent = MonarchTokens.Accents.rook). Pass scheme, contrast and accent to MonarchTheme; apply motion and density in the app.

options.name: onPreferencesChange
options.description: Called with all the choices after any one changes. Store them here, for example in DataStore.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the panel.

options.name: title
options.description: A heading above the rows.

options.name: rows
options.description: The rows to show, in order, each once. The standard rows are theme, contrast, motion and density, as on the web; add Accent for the accent menu.

options.name: accents
options.description: The accents the accent row offers, usually MonarchTokens.Accents.all. The current accent is always offered, even when it is not in the list.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the choices can be changed.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in row label, description and choice name. Unset theme names keep MonarchThemeToggle's.

states.name: device settings
states.description: The default: System scheme, System contrast and System motion are selected, so the app follows the device's dark theme, contrast and animation settings.

states.name: overridden
states.description: Any row set to a fixed choice; its segment is selected with Material's check mark, or the accent field shows the chosen accent's name.

states.name: disabled
states.description: enabled false: every segment, the theme toggle and the accent field are disabled.

appearance: Rows separated by subtle dividers; each row's label in the label style and its description in the caption style in the muted color, then Material 3 segmented buttons or the outlined MonarchSelect field in the Monarch colors. All are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: Same rows and names as iOS. The web panel writes the rook_theme and mn_contrast cookies and applies its choices to the html element; on Android the panel only reports the new value: the app passes scheme, contrast and accent to MonarchTheme and stores the choices. MonarchTheme reads the device's animation setting and has no motion input, so the motion choice is applied by the app's own animations through reducesMotion(systemReducesMotion); Monarch components keep following the device setting (a motion input on MonarchTheme is requested at merge). Density has no Monarch-wide meaning on Android yet; the app reads preferences.density. The accent row is native-only, because the plan asks for the accent as a theme input; the web panel has no accent row. The default theme is System, where the web default is Light, because Android apps follow the device. The parity map lists switch among the dependencies; the motion row is segmented System or Reduce, as on the web and iOS, instead of a switch. Unlike iOS, the accent has no default in MonarchAppearancePreferences and accents defaults to an empty list: Monarch components may not read MonarchTokens.Accents (a source rule keeps token primitives out of components), so the app passes the starting accent and the list.
accessibility: Each row's label and description are merged into one element, read before the row's control.
Contrast, motion and density are Material 3 single-choice segmented buttons named by the row label; TalkBack reads each choice with its selected state, and the chosen one also shows a check mark.
The theme row is MonarchThemeToggle, named by the row label.
The accent row is a MonarchSelect labelled by the row label; accents are chosen by name, not by color.
The title has the heading semantics.
Every segment and the accent field have a touch target of at least 48dp; descriptions wrap at the largest font size.
edgeCases: Long translated choice names wrap inside the segments; keep them short.
An accent that is not in accents is added to the end of the menu, so the current choice is always visible; with the default empty accents the menu offers only the current accent.
A row listed twice is shown once; an empty rows list shows only the title.
Accent names come from the tokens' MonarchAccent.label (English); an app that translates them passes its own MonarchAccent values or leaves the accent row out.

name: MonarchApprovalChainEditor
title: ApprovalChainEditor
wrapsNative: MonarchReorderableList (androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn with a long-press drag and TalkBack move actions) of steps built from MonarchSelect (androidx.compose.material3.ExposedDropdownMenuBox), MonarchEntityPicker (androidx.compose.material3.ModalBottomSheet) and MonarchTextField (androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedTextField)
summary: Edits the ordered steps of an approval chain: who approves each step (a kind of approver, plus a role or person where the kind needs one), an optional label, and the order, with add, remove and accessible reordering.
whenToUse: An admin sets up multi-step approval for requests such as leave, expenses, purchases or access, where each step names a kind of approver and sometimes a role or person.
whenNotToUse: To show how one request moved through its chain, use MonarchApprovalTimeline. When conditions decide what happens, use MonarchConditionEditor with MonarchActionEditor.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchApprovalChainEditor(value: List<MonarchApprovalChainStep>, onValueChange: (List<MonarchApprovalChainStep>) -> Unit, approverTypes: List<MonarchApprovalApproverType>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, description: String? = null, minSteps: Int = 1, maxSteps: Int = 10, showLabels: Boolean = true, showErrors: Boolean = false, enabled: Boolean = true, createStep: (() -> MonarchApprovalChainStep)? = null, removeIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, addIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, state: LazyListState = rememberLazyListState(), labels: MonarchApprovalChainEditorLabels = MonarchApprovalChainEditorLabels())

public data class MonarchApprovalChainStep(id: String, approver: String, target: String? = null, label: String? = null) { companion object { fun validate(steps: List<MonarchApprovalChainStep>, approverTypes: List<MonarchApprovalApproverType>): Set<String>; fun summarize(steps: List<MonarchApprovalChainStep>, approverTypes: List<MonarchApprovalApproverType>, separator: String = " → "): String } }
public class MonarchApprovalApproverType(value: String, label: String, targets: List<MonarchEntityPickerEntity>? = null, targetLabel: String? = null)

public class MonarchApprovalChainEditorLabels(title: String? = null, step: ((position: Int) -> String)? = null, approver: String? = null, target: String? = null, targetPlaceholder: String? = null, label: String? = null, labelPlaceholder: String? = null, addStep: String? = null, remove: String? = null, removeStep: ((position: Int) -> String)? = null, targetRequired: String? = null, maxReached: ((max: Int) -> String)? = null, reorder: MonarchReorderableListLabels = MonarchReorderableListLabels())

options.name: value
options.description: The steps, in order. Ids must be unique.

options.name: onValueChange
options.description: Called with the whole new list after every edit, move, add or remove.

options.name: approverTypes
options.description: The kinds of approver; the first is used for new steps. A kind with targets adds a MonarchEntityPicker to its steps.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the editor. Give it a bounded height.

options.name: description
options.description: Help under the heading, such as how skipped steps work.

options.name: minSteps
options.description: The fewest steps; the remove buttons are disabled at this count.

options.name: maxSteps
options.description: The most steps; the add button is replaced by a note at this count.

options.name: showLabels
options.description: Shows the optional label field (up to 60 characters) on each step.

options.name: showErrors
options.description: Shows Choose who decides this step on steps without a target, for example after a save attempt.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the chain can be changed.

options.name: createStep
options.description: Makes a new step; by default the first kind with the first free step-<n> id.

options.name: removeIcon
options.description: The icon of each remove button; without it the button reads Remove.

options.name: addIcon
options.description: An icon before the text of the add button.

options.name: state
options.description: The scroll state of the list of steps.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, including those of the reorderable list.

states.name: editing
states.description: Each step shows its heading, remove button, approver menu, target picker when the kind has targets, and label field.

states.name: dragging
states.description: A long press lifts a step; the other steps move out of its way and the new order is reported on drop.

states.name: incomplete
states.description: With showErrors, a step without a target shows Choose who decides this step as the picker's error.

states.name: at the minimum
states.description: The remove buttons are disabled.

states.name: at the limit
states.description: The add button is replaced by A chain can have up to 10 steps.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Every field and button is disabled and nothing can be moved.

appearance: A Subheading heading, then the reorderable rows with their drag handles and Up and Down buttons from MonarchReorderableList; each step has a strong heading, outlined menus and fields with the input border, and the add button is a small secondary MonarchButton. The description and notes use the muted text color. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from the color roles.
platformNotes: Same data shape, defaults and checks as the web (validateApprovalChain and summarizeApprovalChain are MonarchApprovalChainStep.validate and summarize; validate returns the ids of incomplete steps). Targets are MonarchEntityPickerEntity values shown in MonarchEntityPicker, a searchable sheet with avatars, where the web uses a native select of options. The web's messages prop is labels, as in other Android components. The list is a LazyColumn (MonarchReorderableList), so the editor needs a bounded height and cannot sit in a vertically scrolling parent; the web's fieldset grows with the page. Focus after a remove is left to Compose. There is no iOS entry yet.
accessibility: The list heading and each step's heading (Step 1) are headings; each step is read as a traversal group.
Each step's drag handle offers Move up and Move down as TalkBack custom actions, and Up and Down buttons are shown on every row, so no step needs a drag.
Every move, pick up, drop and cancel is announced through a polite live region, from MonarchReorderableList.
Remove buttons are named with the position (Remove step 1) and are 48dp targets; the add button is a 48dp MonarchButton.
A missing target is an error on the MonarchEntityPicker, read with the field and announced when it appears; it is text, not only color.
edgeCases: A step whose kind is no longer in approverTypes keeps its stored value; its menu shows no choice until one is picked.
Changing the kind drops a target the new kind does not offer, and clearing the label stores null.
Labels longer than 60 characters are cut at 60, as the web's maxLength.
Put the editor in a screen or sheet with a bounded height: a vertically scrolling parent gives the lazy list an unbounded height and fails.

name: MonarchApprovalQueue
title: ApprovalQueue
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn of rows, each an androidx.compose.material3.SwipeToDismissBox (springs back after the action); androidx.compose.material3.Checkbox and TriStateCheckbox for selection, androidx.compose.material3.AlertDialog for Send back and bulk confirmation; MonarchAvatar, MonarchBadge, MonarchButton, MonarchSearchBar, MonarchTextField, MonarchEmptyState and MonarchBulkActionBar
summary: Requests waiting on the viewer, with Approve, Send back with a reason and Review on each, swipe actions, search and bulk approval.
whenToUse: When a manager or admin has requests (expenses, leave, timesheets, access) that need their decision, on an approvals screen or, with limit and a footer, in a dashboard card.
whenNotToUse: For the steps of one request, use MonarchApprovalTimeline. For a list of conversations or notifications, use MonarchInboxRow rows.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchApprovalQueue(items: List<MonarchApprovalQueueItem>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, rejectReason: MonarchApprovalQueueRejectReason = MonarchApprovalQueueRejectReason.Required, searchable: Boolean = false, limit: Int? = null, now: Long? = null, onApprove: (suspend (MonarchApprovalQueueItem) -> Unit)? = null, onReject: (suspend (MonarchApprovalQueueItem, String?) -> Unit)? = null, onReview: ((MonarchApprovalQueueItem) -> Unit)? = null, onApproveMany: (suspend (List<MonarchApprovalQueueItem>) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchApprovalQueueLabels = MonarchApprovalQueueLabels(), footer: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null)

class MonarchApprovalQueueItem(id: String, requesterName: String, title: String, requesterImage: Painter? = null, requesterSeed: String? = null, requesterDetail: String? = null, summary: String? = null, submittedMillis: Long? = null, overdue: Boolean = false, badges: List<MonarchStatusDefinition> = emptyList(), searchText: String? = null, canDecide: Boolean = true)
enum class MonarchApprovalQueueRejectReason { Required, Optional, None }

class MonarchApprovalQueueLabels(label: String? = null, approve: String? = null, reject: String? = null, review: String? = null, approveItem: ((requester: String) -> String)? = null, rejectItem: ((requester: String) -> String)? = null, reviewItem: ((requester: String) -> String)? = null, selectItem: ((requester: String) -> String)? = null, selectAll: String? = null, approveSelected: String? = null, overdue: String? = null, search: String? = null, emptyTitle: String? = null, emptyDescription: String? = null, noMatchesTitle: String? = null, rejectTitle: ((requester: String) -> String)? = null, rejectDescription: String? = null, rejectReason: String? = null, rejectReasonPrompt: String? = null, bulkTitle: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, bulkDescription: String? = null, bulkConfirm: String? = null, cancel: String? = null, approved: ((requester: String) -> String)? = null, rejected: ((requester: String) -> String)? = null, bulkApproved: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, failed: String? = null)

options.name: items
options.description: The requests, in the order to show them. Ids must be unique. The app removes a request once it is decided.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the queue. Give it a bounded height: the list is lazy.

options.name: rejectReason
options.description: Required and Optional add a reason field to the Send back dialog (Send back is disabled while a required reason is blank); None asks for confirmation only.

options.name: searchable
options.description: Adds a MonarchSearchBar above the list that filters by requester and title, or by each item's searchText, ignoring case.

options.name: limit
options.description: Shows at most this many requests, after the search, for a dashboard card.

options.name: now
options.description: The reference time for relative times, in epoch milliseconds. Without it they follow the clock, refreshed every minute.

options.name: onApprove
options.description: Adds Approve (button and swipe toward the start). The button shows progress until it returns; throwing marks the row as failed.

options.name: onReject
options.description: Adds Send back. Receives the trimmed reason or null. The dialog stays open with a progress button until it returns and shows the failure if it throws.

options.name: onReview
options.description: Adds Review (button and swipe toward the end), which opens the full request.

options.name: onApproveMany
options.description: Adds row checkboxes, Select all and a MonarchBulkActionBar with Approve selected, confirmed by an AlertDialog. Throwing shows the failure under Select all.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including the announcements and the per-request button names.

options.name: footer
options.description: Content after the requests, inside the list, such as a See all requests button.

states.name: pending
states.description: While onApprove runs, the row's Approve shows a progress indicator and is read as Loading; Send back and the approve swipe are unavailable.

states.name: failed
states.description: The row shows "That did not work. Try again." in the strong danger color, the text is part of the row's TalkBack reading, and it is announced.

states.name: sending back
states.description: The Send back dialog shows a progress button and a disabled reason field and Cancel until onReject returns; a failure stays in the dialog as the field's error.

states.name: selected
states.description: With onApproveMany, checked rows are counted in the bulk action bar under the list; Select all is on, off or partly checked.

states.name: read-only request
states.description: canDecide false: no Approve, no Send back, a disabled checkbox; Review stays.

states.name: overdue
states.description: A danger Past due badge after the title.

states.name: empty
states.description: A success MonarchEmptyState, Nothing to review, with no search field and no Select all.

states.name: no matches
states.description: A filtered MonarchEmptyState with Clear filters, which empties the search.

appearance: A plain list on the surface color with subtle dividers. Names use the strong body style in the default text color; details, times and summaries the caption style in the muted text color. Approve is a primary button, Send back secondary and Review ghost. The swipe backgrounds use the solid success role for Approve and the solid accent role for Review, with their on-solid text. The same roles adapt to dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: A domain composite, marked experimental until a Rook app adopts it. Android follows the iOS API with Kotlin conventions: suspend handlers instead of async throws, submittedMillis (epoch milliseconds, UTC) instead of Date, requesterName, requesterImage (a Painter loaded by the app) and requesterSeed instead of a MonarchApprovalPerson, and footer as an optional trailing slot. A Material 3 SwipeToDismissBox has one action per direction, so swipe toward the start approves and toward the end reviews; iOS also offers Send back in the trailing swipe, here it is the row's button. The web uses a success button for Approve; MonarchButton has no success variant, so Approve is primary. As on iOS, the Send back dialog stays open while onReject runs and the bulk confirmation closes while the bulk bar shows progress. TalkBack reads the relative submission time ("2 days ago"), where iOS reads the absolute date. The web moves focus back into the queue when a decided row disappears; Compose has no equivalent here, so focus follows the system default. Titles, summaries and badges are strings and MonarchStatusDefinition values rather than rich content.
accessibility: The list is named "Requests waiting for you".
Each request is one element read as requester, detail, title, relative submission time, Past due, badges, summary and, after a failure, the error.
Approve, Send back, Review and each checkbox name the request they act on, such as "Approve request from Sam Lee".
Approving, sending back, bulk approval and failures are announced through a polite live region that is always present.
Swipe actions repeat the row's buttons, so every action is reachable without swiping; the swipe backgrounds are hidden from TalkBack.
Select all is a tri-state checkbox row read as checked, unchecked or partly checked.
While Approve runs its state is read as Loading.
Overdue is a badge with a word and failures are text, so nothing relies on color.
Buttons and checkboxes have 48dp touch targets.
edgeCases: Decided requests stay until the app removes them from items; the queue does not hide them itself.
Selections of requests that are no longer in items, or that cannot be decided, are ignored.
limit applies after the search; a negative limit shows nothing.
The list is lazy: give the queue a bounded height. Inside a vertically scrolling parent it would get an infinite height and fail; in a loose height it takes the height of its rows.
The same announcement twice in a row (two failures) is not repeated by the live region.
Long names, titles and summaries wrap; the buttons wrap onto more lines at large font sizes.

name: MonarchApprovalTimeline
title: ApprovalTimeline
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column, Row and FlowRow with androidx.compose.foundation.Canvas markers; MonarchAvatar for deciders; android.text.format.DateUtils and android.icu.text.DateFormat for times
summary: The history and outlook of one approval: who submitted it, each step with its decision, who is deciding now and what comes next.
whenToUse: On a request, expense, purchase order or document under review, to show where the approval stands and who decides next.
whenNotToUse: For the queue of requests waiting for the current user's decision, use an approval queue; for a flow the user moves through, use MonarchStepper; for any record's history, MonarchActivityTimeline.
api: @Composable fun MonarchApprovalTimeline(steps: List<MonarchApprovalTimelineStep>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, now: Long? = null, absoluteAfterMillis: Long = 7 * DateUtils.DAY_IN_MILLIS, showAvatars: Boolean = true, timeZone: String? = null, labels: MonarchApprovalTimelineLabels = MonarchApprovalTimelineLabels())

class MonarchApprovalTimelineStep(id: String, label: String, status: MonarchApprovalStepStatus, actor: MonarchApprovalPerson? = null, approvers: List<MonarchApprovalPerson> = emptyList(), delegatedFrom: MonarchApprovalPerson? = null, date: Long? = null, comment: String? = null, note: String? = null)
class MonarchApprovalPerson(name: String, image: Painter? = null, seed: String? = null)
enum class MonarchApprovalStepStatus { Submitted, Approved, Rejected, Pending, Waiting, Skipped, Cancelled }

class MonarchApprovalTimelineLabels(label: String? = null, status: ((status: MonarchApprovalStepStatus) -> String)? = null, approvers: ((names: String) -> String)? = null, delegatedFrom: ((name: String) -> String)? = null, current: String? = null, empty: String? = null)

options.name: steps
options.description: The steps in order, from submission to the outcome. Each has an id, a label, a status, and optionally who decided, who can decide, who is stood in for, when (epoch milliseconds, UTC), a comment and a note.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the timeline.

options.name: now
options.description: The reference time for relative times, as epoch milliseconds. null is the current time, refreshed every minute; pass a fixed time in tests and screenshots.

options.name: absoluteAfterMillis
options.description: How far from now a time is shown as a date and time instead of "2 hours ago".

options.name: showAvatars
options.description: Shows a small decorative avatar before the name of whoever decided or submitted.

options.name: timeZone
options.description: The zone of absolute dates. An IANA id such as Europe/Berlin; null, or an id the device does not know, is the device's zone.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the status names, the approvers and delegation phrases, the group name, Current step and the empty text.

states.name: submitted / approved
states.description: A filled success marker with a check; the rail below it is the success border.

states.name: rejected
states.description: A filled danger marker with a cross; the status text is semibold in the strong danger color.

states.name: pending
states.description: A subtle warning marker with a warning outline and a dot; the status is semibold in the strong warning color, the approvers are listed and TalkBack adds "Current step".

states.name: waiting
states.description: An empty outlined marker and a muted label; the approvers are listed.

states.name: skipped / cancelled
states.description: A dashed outlined marker with a dash or a cross, and the note.

states.name: empty
states.description: No steps: the text "Not submitted yet".

appearance: Markers are 20dp circles (larger at large font scales) with a 1.5dp outline: success, danger or subtle warning fills with their glyph colors, or the surface color with the strong border, dashed for skipped and cancelled steps. The 2dp rail is the success border after a completed step and the subtle border otherwise. Labels are strong body text, muted for steps that have not happened; meta lines are muted caption text; comments are caption text on the muted background with 8dp corners. Every color is a theme role, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes are covered.
platformNotes: Matches the web ApprovalTimeline. Labels, comments and notes are plain strings rather than rich content. Times are epoch milliseconds; relative times use DateUtils in the device locale, absolute ones the ICU skeleton yMMMdjmm in the given zone. Avatars take a Painter the app loads, following the Monarch image convention, where iOS takes a URL. The web's status-badge dependency is not used: the status is coloured caption text next to the label, as on the web and iOS. Monarch bundles no icons, so the marker glyphs are drawn as strokes. MonarchApprovalPerson is declared here and is meant to be shared with an approval queue later. iOS uses the same names, except showAvatars (iOS showsAvatars), absoluteAfterMillis (iOS absoluteAfter in seconds), image (iOS avatarURL), timeZone (iOS reads the environment) and the PascalCase enum constants.
accessibility: The timeline is one group named "Approval timeline".
Each step is one element read as its label, status, actor, absolute date and time, approvers, delegation, comment and note, such as "Manager, Approved, Ana Ruiz, Mar 4, 2026, 2:00 PM, Fine by me."
The step waiting for a decision adds "Current step".
Markers differ by shape (check, cross, dot, dash, empty, dashed outline) and the status is written, so nothing relies on color.
Markers, rails and avatars are hidden from TalkBack; markers and text grow with the font scale.
edgeCases: Long labels and comments wrap; the rail stretches with the step.
A decided step without an actor or a date has no meta line.
Approvers are only shown on pending and waiting steps; a delegation on a decided step gets its own line.
Times in the future are relative too ("In 2 hours").
Relative times refresh every minute when now is null.

name: MonarchAreaChart
title: AreaChart
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.Canvas through the MonarchLineChart core (its plot area, drawing, axis, inspection row and TalkBack elements) with pointerInput tap and horizontal drag gestures; the stack computed by Monarch; inside MonarchChartFrame with MonarchChartLegend (square markers) and MonarchChartTable
summary: An area chart for volumes over ordered categories or dates: several series overlapping, stacked so the top edge is the total, or stacked to 100% to show shares, with touch inspection, legend toggles and a data table.
whenToUse: To show a total over time made of parts (traffic by platform, revenue by plan) with Stacked, how the mix changes when the total does not matter with Expand, or one or two volumes where the filled area helps read magnitude with Overlap.
whenNotToUse: To compare trends of independent measures, use MonarchLineChart: overlapping fills hide each other beyond two series. For values that go negative, use MonarchBarChart. For parts of one whole at a single moment, use MonarchDonutChart or MonarchStackedProportionBar.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAreaChart(title: String, categories: List<String>, series: List<MonarchLineChartSeries>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, description: String? = null, xTitle: String? = null, summary: String? = null, stacking: MonarchAreaChartStacking = MonarchAreaChartStacking.Overlap, curve: MonarchLineChartCurve = MonarchLineChartCurve.Linear, status: MonarchChartFrameStatus = MonarchChartFrameStatus.Ready, hiddenSeries: Set<String>? = null, onHiddenSeriesChange: ((Set<String>) -> Unit)? = null, activeIndex: Int? = null, onActiveIndexChange: ((Int?) -> Unit)? = null, referenceLines: List<MonarchLineChartReferenceLine> = emptyList(), valueRange: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Double>? = null, includeZero: Boolean = true, legendToggle: Boolean = true, tableToggle: Boolean = true, emptyMessage: String? = null, footer: String? = null, height: Dp? = null, labels: MonarchAreaChartLabels = MonarchAreaChartLabels(), formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = null, onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null, onSelect: ((Int) -> Unit)? = null)

@Composable fun MonarchAreaChart(title: String, dates: List<Long>, series: List<MonarchLineChartSeries>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, description: String? = null, xTitle: String? = null, summary: String? = null, stacking: MonarchAreaChartStacking = MonarchAreaChartStacking.Overlap, curve: MonarchLineChartCurve = MonarchLineChartCurve.Linear, status: MonarchChartFrameStatus = MonarchChartFrameStatus.Ready, hiddenSeries: Set<String>? = null, onHiddenSeriesChange: ((Set<String>) -> Unit)? = null, activeIndex: Int? = null, onActiveIndexChange: ((Int?) -> Unit)? = null, referenceLines: List<MonarchLineChartReferenceLine> = emptyList(), valueRange: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Double>? = null, includeZero: Boolean = true, legendToggle: Boolean = true, tableToggle: Boolean = true, emptyMessage: String? = null, footer: String? = null, height: Dp? = null, labels: MonarchAreaChartLabels = MonarchAreaChartLabels(), formatDate: ((Long) -> String)? = null, formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = null, onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null, onSelect: ((Int) -> Unit)? = null)
enum class MonarchAreaChartStacking { Overlap, Stacked, Expand }

class MonarchAreaChartLabels(frame: MonarchChartFrameLabels = MonarchChartFrameLabels(), category: String? = null, date: String? = null, noData: String? = null, details: String? = null, clearSelection: String? = null, total: String? = null, share: ((value: String, share: String) -> String)? = null)

options.name: title
options.description: The chart's name: the frame heading and the plot's spoken name.

options.name: categories
options.description: The x values in order, already localised. Spaced evenly.

options.name: dates
options.description: The x values in order as epoch milliseconds (UTC). Spaced by time.

options.name: series
options.description: The measures, bottom of the stack first: key, label, one value per x value (null or not finite is a gap), optional color slot and dashed. The MonarchLineChart type.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the frame.

options.name: description
options.description: One line under the title.

options.name: xTitle
options.description: The heading of the x column of the data table. Built in: "Category" or "Date".

options.name: summary
options.description: Replaces the generated spoken summary of the plot.

options.name: stacking
options.description: Overlap: each area from the baseline; Stacked: piled so the top edge is the total; Expand: piled as shares of 100%.

options.name: curve
options.description: Linear, or Monotone: smooth edges that never overshoot.

options.name: status
options.description: Ready, loading, empty or error, drawn by the frame. Ready with no x values or no series is empty.

options.name: hiddenSeries
options.description: The keys of the hidden series. null lets the chart keep its own set, changed by the legend.

options.name: onHiddenSeriesChange
options.description: Called with the new hidden set when the legend changes it.

options.name: activeIndex
options.description: The inspected x value, used when onActiveIndexChange is set, to share a crosshair between charts.

options.name: onActiveIndexChange
options.description: Makes the inspection controlled: called with the inspected index, or null when cleared.

options.name: referenceLines
options.description: Dashed lines with a label and value. Not drawn or read in Expand, whose axis is shares.

options.name: valueRange
options.description: Fixes the value axis. Ignored in Expand, which is always 0 to 100%.

options.name: includeZero
options.description: Whether the value axis keeps zero when the areas overlap. Stacks always start at zero.

options.name: legendToggle
options.description: Whether legend entries show and hide their series. The legend shows for two or more series and keeps one visible.

options.name: tableToggle
options.description: Whether "View as table" is offered.

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: The empty-state message.

options.name: footer
options.description: Notes under the chart.

options.name: height
options.description: The plot height, kept in every status; 240dp by default.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, including the frame's, "Total" and the "820 (45%)" share text.

options.name: formatDate
options.description: Dates overload: writes a date everywhere. Default: abbreviated month and day in the current locale, in UTC.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes values in the inspection row, TalkBack, the table, the summary and on the axis. Default: numbers in the current locale, compact on the axis. Shares and the Expand axis are percentages in the locale.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Try again in the error status.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Drill-in: called with the x index from Details in the inspection row or from the TalkBack action of that x value.

states.name: overlap
states.description: Each shown series is a fill from the baseline (zero, or the bottom of the axis without includeZero) with its top line drawn over every fill.

states.name: stacked
states.description: Series pile up in order, the first at the bottom; the top edge of the last is the total. Bands are a stronger shade because they touch. A negative value counts as zero in the stack.

states.name: expand
states.description: Series pile up as shares of each x value's total; the axis reads 0% to 100% and reference lines are not drawn or read. An x value whose total is zero has every share at zero.

states.name: inspecting
states.description: After a tap or drag, or with activeIndex: a crosshair, dots on the top edges and a row under the plot with each real value (with its share in Expand) and the total of a stack of two or more, with Details and Clear.

states.name: series hidden
states.description: The series leaves the plot and the stack; its legend entry shows Hidden; it stays in the data table and the table's total.

states.name: gap
states.description: A missing value breaks that series' band; in a stack the series above keep their place. A lone value between gaps is a dot.

states.name: loading, empty, error
states.description: Drawn by MonarchChartFrame at the chart's height.

appearance: Top lines are 2dp in the theme's data colors 1 to 5 in series order (Neutral in the subtle text color), dashed series dashed. Fills are opaque mixes of the series color towards the surface color: 80% when the areas overlap (90% for a dashed series), 60% for stacked bands. Gridlines, axis labels, reference lines and the crosshair are the line chart's roles. Every color is a theme role or a mix of two roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes are covered.
platformNotes: Drawn with a Compose Canvas through the MonarchLineChart core (iOS uses Swift Charts, the web SVG); Android has no first-party chart library and Monarch adds none. The stack is computed by Monarch, as on the web and iOS, so gaps break a band and negatives count as zero. Fills are opaque, never translucent as on the web: overlapping fills cover each other, so every top line is drawn over the fills; a stack is painted from the top band down, each fill reaching the baseline. Series, reference lines and the curve reuse the MonarchLineChart types. Names follow the Android MonarchLineChart (valueRange, includeZero, legendToggle, hiddenSeries with onHiddenSeriesChange) where iOS has valueDomain, includesZero, isLegendInteractive and Bindings; totalLabel and shareLabel are the total and share fields of MonarchAreaChartLabels. Unlike iOS, Android keeps the inspected x value after the finger lifts, shows it in a row under the plot with a polite live region, gives one TalkBack element per x value and a spoken summary, and offers onSelect drill-in, as MonarchLineChart does. The web's valueFormat, formatTick and numeric x values are not offered.
accessibility: The frame's title is a heading; the plot is one TalkBack element named by the title (role Image) whose state is the summary: the number and range of x values, each shown series' low, high and latest real value, the total of a stack of two or more, and the reference lines.

After the plot come one element per x value, in order and mirrored in right to left, read as the x value, each shown series' real value ("No value" for a gap, the share in Expand) and the total: "Mon: Web 420, iOS 210, Total 630".
With onSelect each x value has a "Details, Mon" TalkBack action; the inspection row's Details and Clear buttons have 48dp targets.
The inspection row is a polite live region, so the values are announced when the inspected x value changes.
"View as table" shows every series with real values and, in a stack of two or more, the total.
Series differ by name in the legend and every text alternative and, where dashed, by a dashed line and an outlined marker, never by color alone.
edgeCases: Missing, null and non-finite values are gaps, never zero; values beyond the x values are ignored.
In Stacked and Expand a negative value counts as zero in the stack; TalkBack, the inspection row and the table still give the real value.
Hiding series changes the stack and the shares but not the table's total, which sums every series.
A single series has no legend and no total.
A ready chart with no x values or no series shows the empty state.
Overlapping opaque fills cover each other; with more than two overlapping series prefer Stacked or MonarchLineChart.

In the multiple-choice picker Assign to me adds the current user to the end of the selection.
A current user who is not in people is not added to the list.
Long names wrap in the rows; the field shows one line.

name: MonarchAttachmentChip
title: AttachmentChip
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row, androidx.compose.material3.IconButton, MonarchFileTypeIcon, MonarchProgress, MonarchButton, android.text.format.Formatter.formatShortFileSize
summary: A compact chip for one attached file: the type icon, the name, the size, upload progress or failure, and remove and retry buttons.
whenToUse: For files attached to a message, a form or a ticket reply, alone or in a list, while they upload and after.
whenNotToUse: For a file in a file browser with a preview, use a file card or MonarchFilePreview. For a tag that is not a file, use MonarchTag.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAttachmentChip(name: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, status: MonarchUploadStatus = MonarchUploadStatus.Done, enabled: Boolean = true, sizeBytes: Long? = null, contentType: String? = null, progress: Float? = null, errorMessage: String? = null, onOpen: (() -> Unit)? = null, onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null, onRemove: (() -> Unit)? = null, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, retryIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, removeIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAttachmentChipLabels = MonarchAttachmentChipLabels())
enum class MonarchUploadStatus { Queued, Uploading, Done, Failed, Cancelled; val active: Boolean }

class MonarchAttachmentChipLabels(remove: ((name: String) -> String)? = null, retry: ((name: String) -> String)? = null, uploading: ((name: String) -> String)? = null, queued: String? = null, failed: String? = null, cancelled: String? = null, removeText: String? = null, retryText: String? = null)

options.name: name
options.description: The file name; long names are shortened in the middle.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the chip.

options.name: status
options.description: Queued, Uploading, Done, Failed or Cancelled.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Disables the retry and remove buttons, for example while the message is sending.

options.name: sizeBytes
options.description: The size in bytes, shown once uploaded in the user's units.

options.name: contentType
options.description: The MIME type; with the name it picks the type icon.

options.name: progress
options.description: The uploaded fraction from 0 to 1 while uploading. null shows a moving bar and no percentage.

options.name: errorMessage
options.description: Why the upload failed, shown instead of "Upload failed".

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Opens the file once uploaded; the name becomes a button. The app opens the file.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Adds a retry button to a failed upload.

options.name: onRemove
options.description: Adds a remove button.

options.name: icon
options.description: Replaces the type icon, for example with a thumbnail. Decorative.

options.name: retryIcon
options.description: The icon of the retry button; without it the button shows the word "Retry".

options.name: removeIcon
options.description: The icon of the remove button; without it the button shows the word "Remove".

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings monarch_attachmentchip_*.

states.name: done
states.description: The size under the name; with onOpen the name is an underlined link-coloured button.

states.name: queued
states.description: "Waiting" under the name.

states.name: uploading
states.description: The percentage under the name and a progress bar named "Uploading report.pdf"; a moving bar without progress.

states.name: failed
states.description: The subtle danger fill and border, the error in danger text (announced) and the retry button.

states.name: cancelled
states.description: "Cancelled" under the name.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The retry and remove buttons are disabled.

appearance: A bordered row with medium rounded corners on the surface color and the default border; a failed upload takes the subtle danger fill and the danger border. The name is label text, the line under it muted caption text (strong danger for a failure). The progress bar is MonarchProgress in the accent color. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The parity map names InputChip; an input chip is one touch target, and this chip has up to three (open, retry, remove) and a second line, so it is a bordered Row with Material 3 IconButtons and MonarchButtons. The web accepts any thumbnail as the icon, as the icon slot does here. The web retry and close glyphs are not bundled: with retryIcon and removeIcon the buttons are icon buttons, without them they show a word. The web href and download become onOpen, because components do not open files. Progress is a fraction from 0 to 1, as in MonarchProgress, where the web takes 0 to 100. The web marks the failure as an alert; here it is a polite live region. The parity map lists tag as a dependency; MonarchTag is not used, as on iOS. iOS shares the name and the statuses.
accessibility: The name and the line under it are one TalkBack element; TalkBack reads the whole name even when it is shortened.
With onOpen that element is a button with a touch target of at least 48dp; the link state is shown by an underline as well as the color.
The retry and remove buttons are separate elements named after the file, "Retry budget.xlsx" and "Remove budget.xlsx", each with a 48dp touch target.
The progress bar is named "Uploading photo.jpg" and exposes its range.
The failure line is a polite live region, so a failure is announced.
The type icon and the button icons are hidden from TalkBack.
edgeCases: A long name stays on one line, shortened in the middle, so the extension stays visible.
onOpen is ignored until the upload is done.
progress outside 0 to 1 is limited; NaN shows a moving bar.

name: MonarchAudioLevelMeter
title: AudioLevelMeter
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.Canvas
summary: Shows how loud a microphone is, as rising segments or a thin bar, from a level the app measures.
whenToUse: In a call tile, a pre-call check or a recorder, to show that the microphone picks up sound.
whenNotToUse: For the progress of a recording or an upload use MonarchProgress. For a waveform over time, draw one from the samples.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAudioLevelMeter(level: Float, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchAudioLevelMeterVariant = MonarchAudioLevelMeterVariant.Segments, size: MonarchAudioLevelMeterSize = MonarchAudioLevelMeterSize.Md, segments: Int = 5, muted: Boolean = false, decorative: Boolean = false, label: String? = null, mutedLabel: String? = null)
enum class MonarchAudioLevelMeterVariant { Segments, Bar }
enum class MonarchAudioLevelMeterSize { Sm, Md }

options.name: level
options.description: The loudness, 0 to 1. Values outside are limited to that range; a value that is not finite is silence.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the meter.

options.name: variant
options.description: Segments are rising bars the size of a word; Bar is one thin bar that fills the width.

options.name: size
options.description: Sm (12dp high) or Md (16dp). Segments only.

options.name: segments
options.description: The number of segments. At least one.

options.name: muted
options.description: The microphone is off: the meter is empty and reads "Muted".

options.name: decorative
options.description: Hides the meter from TalkBack.

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the built-in name "Microphone level" (monarch_audiolevelmeter_label).

options.name: mutedLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in value "Muted" (monarch_audiolevelmeter_muted).

states.name: silent
states.description: Every segment is a dot in the strong border color; the bar is an empty track.

states.name: sound
states.description: Segments up to the level are tall and in the success color; the bar is filled to the level.

states.name: muted
states.description: Empty, in the disabled color, and read as "Muted".

states.name: animations removed
states.description: The meter does not follow the level: it is full at or above a level of 0.08 and empty below.

appearance: Segments that are on use the success solid color and those that are off the strong border color; the bar's track is the muted background. A muted meter uses the disabled text color and the muted background. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web component can measure a MediaStream itself with the Web Audio API; on Android capturing audio needs the RECORD_AUDIO permission and an AudioRecord or a call SDK, which belong to the app, so the meter only takes a level, as on iOS. The level is a Float, as Compose progress values are. On the web a segment that is off keeps its height and changes color; here it is a dot, as on iOS. The web variants bars and bar are named Segments and Bar.
accessibility: The meter is one element named "Microphone level" (or label), with a progress range from 0 to 1 and a state description that is the level as a whole percentage in the user's locale, or "Muted".
It is not a live region, so TalkBack does not read every change of the level.
When animations are removed the meter shows only whether there is sound; the spoken value is still the real level.
Segments that are on are tall and segments that are off are dots, so the level does not depend on color.
decorative hides it when the same information is given elsewhere.
It is not interactive and has no touch target.
edgeCases: A level that is not finite is treated as silence.
A segment count below one draws one segment.
The level changes without animation; pass a smoothed level for a calmer meter.
Segments rise towards the end and the bar fills from the start in both layout directions; the mirroring is done when drawing and is not covered by a pixel test.

title: AuditLogViewer

summary: A recipe, not a component: a searchable, filterable audit log of who did what, when and from where, as list rows that open one event's details (including field changes) in a bottom sheet.
whenToUse: For workspace security and admin screens where people review sign-ins, permission changes, exports and API activity.
whenNotToUse: For one request's raw details use the log-drawer recipe; for streaming output use MonarchLogViewer; for a person's own activity feed use a timeline.
api: MonarchSearchBar(query = query, onQueryChange = …, onSearch = …, placeholder = "Search the audit log")
MonarchTag(text = "Automations and API", selected = …, onSelectedChange = …); MonarchDownloadReportButton(onDownload = …, labels = MonarchDownloadReportButtonLabels(label = "Export CSV"))

MonarchCursorList(items = events, label = "Audit log", hasMore = …, onLoadMore = …, key = { it.id }) { event -> ListItem(headlineContent = …, overlineContent = { MonarchBadge(kind) }, supportingContent = …, leadingContent = { MonarchAvatar(…, decorative = true) }, trailingContent = { Text(relative time) }, modifier = Modifier.clickable(onClickLabel = "Details") { … }) }
DateUtils.getRelativeTimeSpanString(time, now, DateUtils.MINUTE_IN_MILLIS)
ModalBottomSheet(onDismissRequest = …) { Column(Modifier.verticalScroll(…)) { MonarchText("Event details", heading = true); MonarchDescriptionList(items = …); MonarchButton("Close", …) } }

options.description: Each event: id, time in epoch milliseconds, actor (name, kind), action, target, IP, device, location, source, reason, field changes.

options.name: query and filters
options.description: The search text and filter tags; the app filters, or queries the server and pages with the cursor.

options.name: hasMore / onLoadMore
options.description: Cursor paging of MonarchCursorList.

options.name: export
options.description: Export CSV of the filtered events.

options.name: now
options.description: The instant relative times are measured from.

states.name: events
states.description: One row per event: overline tag for automations and API keys, actor and action, target, relative time.

states.name: loading / more
states.description: MonarchCursorList shows placeholders on the first load and a load-more footer after.

states.name: empty
states.description: MonarchCursorList's empty state; for a search, say no events match.

states.name: error
states.description: MonarchCursorList's failed state with Try again.

states.name: details
states.description: A bottom sheet titled Event details with time, actor, action, target, IP address with copy, device and the field changes as before → after.

appearance: Material 3 list items on the surface with Monarch avatars and badges, the search bar and tags above, and a bottom sheet of description lists for one event. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web ships AuditLogViewer as a pattern with a table (time, actor, action, target, IP and device columns), a details drawer from the side with a before-and-after table, an export button and messages. On a phone, as on iOS, it is a recipe: the table becomes list rows that open a bottom sheet, the before-and-after table becomes description items reading Before → After, and the relative time with a tooltip becomes DateUtils' relative text with the full time in the sheet. Paging uses MonarchCursorList.
accessibility: Each row is one element whose click is labelled Details; the avatar is decorative and the actor is text.
Automation and API actors carry a word badge, not only a color or an icon.
The sheet is modal, its title has heading semantics, and Back closes it.
The IP address has a copy button named for it.
The search bar and tags keep their own roles and selected states.
edgeCases: An unknown actor: show "Unknown" instead of an empty name.
A field set for the first time or cleared: write None for the missing side.
Long targets wrap in the row; the full text is in the sheet.
Keep the event's id in rememberSaveable so the open sheet survives rotation.

name: MonarchAutosaveIndicator
title: AutosaveIndicator
wrapsNative: kotlinx.coroutines (delay, Job, sync.Mutex), MonarchSaveStatusIndicator
summary: Saves a value automatically after the person stops changing it (debounced, one save at a time, retried, flushable) and shows where saving stands.
whenToUse: For drafts and settings that save without a Save button: notes, descriptions, document content, preferences edited in place.
whenNotToUse: When people must confirm before anything is stored, use a Save button with MonarchFormActionsBar. To show a status your own code computes, use MonarchSaveStatusIndicator directly.

options.name: MonarchAutosaveState.retryDelayMillis
options.description: Milliseconds before the first automatic retry; doubled for each further one.

options.name: MonarchAutosaveState.initialSavedAt
options.description: When the first value was last saved, in epoch milliseconds (UTC). Starts the status at Saved with the time.

options.name: MonarchAutosaveState.isEqual
options.description: Decides whether two values are the same, so an equal value is not saved again.

options.name: MonarchAutosaveState.clock
options.description: The current time for savedAt. Replace it in tests.

options.name: MonarchAutosaveState.enabled
options.description: While false, changes only mark the value unsaved; flush and retry still save.

states.name: idle
states.description: Nothing changed since the start and no save time is known: nothing is drawn.

states.name: unsaved
states.description: A change waits for the delay, or saving is disabled: "Unsaved changes".

states.name: saving
states.description: A save runs, or an automatic retry waits: a small progress ring and "Saving…".

states.name: saved
states.description: "Saved · 2 minutes ago"; announced.

states.name: error
states.description: The retries are used up: "Couldn't save" (or errorMessage) and a Retry button; announced.

appearance: Exactly MonarchSaveStatusIndicator: a dot or progress ring in the status color, caption text in muted or danger colors by role, and a ghost Retry button. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web splits this into a useAutosave hook and an AutosaveIndicator; on Android the hook is MonarchAutosaveState (a state holder on coroutines that can live in a ViewModel) with rememberMonarchAutosaveState for screens, and the indicator takes the state. The web compares values with Object.is then JSON; Android uses == (data classes compare by content) or isEqual. The web flush returns a promise; on Android it is a suspend function. Dates are epoch milliseconds. iOS has no entry yet; the names follow the web.
accessibility: The status is read as one element, "Saved, 2 minutes ago", from MonarchSaveStatusIndicator.
Saved and the error are announced through a polite live region; Saving only with announceSaving, so frequent autosaves stay quiet.
Retry is a MonarchButton with a 48dp touch target.
The status is always written in words; color is never the only signal.
edgeCases: An edit during a save is saved after it, once the delay has passed again; two saves never overlap.
Changing the value back to the saved one cancels the pending save.
During automatic retries the status stays Saving; only after the last retry it becomes Error.
rememberMonarchAutosaveState stops when it leaves the composition: call flush before navigating away, or keep the state in a ViewModel.
delayMillis, retries, retryDelayMillis and isEqual are read once when the state is created.

name: MonarchAvailabilityToggle
title: AvailabilityToggle
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.Switch, androidx.compose.foundation.selection.toggleable, androidx.compose.material3.CircularProgressIndicator
summary: An on and off switch for whether automatic assignment may give someone new work: a status word with a mark, an optional hint and a Material 3 Switch, as one row.
whenToUse: Where work is assigned automatically (round robin, load balancing) and people must be able to step out of it: an account menu, a navigation drawer or a home screen.
whenNotToUse: For a chat-style presence with custom statuses use a status picker. For a setting saved with a form use MonarchSwitchRow inside the form.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchAvailabilityToggle(available: Boolean, onAvailableChange: (Boolean) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, pending: Boolean = false, showHint: Boolean = false, labels: MonarchAvailabilityToggleLabels = MonarchAvailabilityToggleLabels(), interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)

@Immutable public class MonarchAvailabilityToggleLabels(public val label: String? = null, public val available: String? = null, public val away: String? = null, public val availableHint: String? = null, public val awayHint: String? = null, public val pending: String? = null)

options.name: available
options.description: Whether the person is available for new work.

options.name: onAvailableChange
options.description: Called with the new value when the person toggles the row. Update optimistically and roll back if saving fails.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the component.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the person may change it; false when they have no permission to.

options.name: pending
options.description: A change is being saved: the switch cannot be toggled, a small progress ring is shown and TalkBack adds "Saving" to the state.

options.name: showHint
options.description: Shows one line under the status word that says what being available or away changes.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings: label ("Available for new work"), available ("Available"), away ("Away"), availableHint, awayHint and pending ("Saving").

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The interaction source of the row.

states.name: available
states.description: Switch on; a filled dot in the solid success color and the word "Available".

states.name: away
states.description: Switch off; a ring in the solid warning color and the word "Away".

states.name: pending
states.description: The switch is disabled, a progress ring precedes it and the state reads "Available, Saving" or "Away, Saving". The ring is still when animations are off.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The switch is disabled and the text uses the disabled color; announced as disabled.

states.name: focused
states.description: The focus ring around the row.

appearance: The mark uses the solid success color (available) or the solid warning color (away) in every theme, and differs in shape as well: a filled dot or a ring. The status word uses the default text color and the hint the muted text color; the switch is the Material 3 Switch in Monarch's accent colors. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes change only the roles.
platformNotes: The web renders nothing while the value is null; on Android the value is a Boolean and the app shows the toggle once it is known. The web's inMenu flag stops key events reaching a surrounding menu and has no meaning in Compose. The mark's filled and ring shapes, used on the web only in forced-colors mode, are always used here, as on iOS. A progress ring is shown while pending, as on iOS; the web only disables the switch. The built-in strings are one MonarchAvailabilityToggleLabels value instead of iOS's separate parameters, as Monarch for Android does for every component with several strings; the names match iOS (label, available, away, availableHint, awayHint, pending).
accessibility: The row is one TalkBack element with the switch role and the on or off toggle state; the whole row is the touch target and is at least 48dp high.
Its name is "Available for new work" (or labels.label); its state description is the visible status word, "Available" or "Away", so the state is read in the words that are shown.
The status word and the mark are not read a second time; the mark is decorative and differs in shape as well as color.
With showHint the hint is merged into the row and read after the name.
While pending the row is disabled and the state reads "Available, Saving"; the progress ring is hidden from TalkBack.
The text wraps at font scale 2.0 and the switch stays at the end; in a right-to-left layout the text is on the right and the switch on the left.
edgeCases: Long status words and hints wrap; the switch keeps its size.
A tap while pending is ignored, so a second change cannot start before the first is saved.
The app must show its own error (a snackbar) and roll back the value when saving fails; the toggle only reports the new value.

name: MonarchAvatar
title: Avatar
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.Image (through the internal MonarchImage) clipped to a shape, androidx.compose.foundation.text.BasicText with TextAutoSize for the initials, androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row with negative spacing for MonarchAvatarGroup
summary: A picture of a person or an entity, with initials or an icon as the fallback, an optional presence dot, and an overlapping group with a "+N" tile.
whenToUse: Next to a person's or an organization's name in lists, comments, assignees and headers; the group for the people on one item.
whenNotToUse: For the people in a live session with a list of everyone use MonarchPresenceAvatars. For an AI agent use MonarchAiAgentAvatar. For a file use MonarchFileTypeIcon.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchAvatar(image: Painter?, name: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, shape: MonarchAvatarShape = MonarchAvatarShape.Circle, size: MonarchAvatarSize = MonarchAvatarSize.Md, status: MonarchPresenceStatus? = null, seed: String? = null, decorative: Boolean = false, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, statusLabel: String? = null)

@Composable public fun MonarchAvatar(image: @Composable () -> Unit, name: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, shape: MonarchAvatarShape = MonarchAvatarShape.Circle, size: MonarchAvatarSize = MonarchAvatarSize.Md, status: MonarchPresenceStatus? = null, decorative: Boolean = false, statusLabel: String? = null)

@Composable public fun <T> MonarchAvatarGroup(items: List<T>, label: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, maxVisible: Int? = null, size: MonarchAvatarSize = MonarchAvatarSize.Md, shape: MonarchAvatarShape = MonarchAvatarShape.Circle, overflowLabel: ((Int) -> String)? = null, avatar: @Composable (T) -> Unit)
public enum class MonarchAvatarSize { Xs, Sm, Md, Lg, Xl }
public enum class MonarchAvatarShape { Circle, Square }

options.name: image
options.description: The picture, loaded by the app (a resource, a BitmapPainter, Coil's rememberAsyncImagePainter). null shows the fallback, which also stands for loading and failure. The slot overload lets the app compose the picture itself; it is clipped to the shape.

options.name: name
options.description: The person or entity. Read by TalkBack and used for the initials.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the avatar.

options.name: shape
options.description: Circle for people, Square (rounded) for workspaces, organizations and brands.

options.name: size
options.description: 20, 24, 32, 40 or 56dp at the default font size, multiplied by the font scale.

options.name: status
options.description: A MonarchPresenceDot with a surface-coloured ring at the bottom end corner; its name is added to what TalkBack reads.

options.name: seed
options.description: Painter overload: picks the fallback color; the name by default. Pass a stable id so a renamed person keeps their color.

options.name: decorative
options.description: Hides the avatar from TalkBack when the name is written next to it.

options.name: icon
options.description: Painter overload: shown instead of the initials when there is no picture, for an entity without a logo. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: statusLabel
options.description: Replaces the spoken name of the presence; the built-in strings are those of MonarchPresenceDot.

options.name: items (group)
options.description: The people or entities of the group, in order.

options.name: label (group)
options.description: Names the group for TalkBack, for example "Assignees".

options.name: maxVisible (group)
options.description: Show at most this many avatars, then a "+N" tile. With exactly one too many, all are shown.

options.name: overflowLabel (group)
options.description: Replaces the spoken "N more" of the tile.

options.name: avatar (group)
options.description: The avatar of one item; give it the size and shape of the group.

states.name: picture
states.description: The picture fills the shape, cropped.

states.name: initials
states.description: No picture: one or two initials on a subtle fill picked from the seed, in the strong color of the same family.

states.name: icon
states.description: With icon, the icon on the same colors instead of the initials.

states.name: no readable initials
states.description: An empty name or one without letters or digits, and no icon: the color alone. TalkBack still reads the name as given.

states.name: presence
states.description: A presence dot ringed in the surface color at the bottom end corner.

states.name: group overflow
states.description: A "+N" tile in the muted colors after the shown avatars, each ringed in the surface color.

appearance: Fallbacks use five pairs of theme roles, each a subtle fill with the strong text of one family (accent, info, success, warning, AI), so they follow light, dark and both high-contrast themes; danger is left out. The tile uses the muted background with muted text, and the ring the surface color.
platformNotes: The web derives a soft color from a hue per name, or one of five data colors with palette="tokens"; Android, as iOS, always uses five theme role pairs, picked with the web's hash so a seed lands on the same index. The web's xs and xl sizes and pixel sizes are not offered: the touch vocabulary is Sm, Md and Lg. Monarch ships no image loader on Android, so the picture is a Painter or a slot rather than a URL, and a failed load is the app passing null. Monarch bundles no icons, so the person glyph of the web is not drawn: without an icon a name without letters shows the color alone. The presence uses MonarchPresenceStatus, which adds do not disturb to the web's four. AvatarGroup on the web counts its children; Compose cannot count slot children, so the group takes the items and a composable per item, as on iOS.
accessibility: The avatar is one TalkBack element with the image role, named by the name, and by the presence when there is one ("Ana Silva, Online"); the initials and the dot are not read on their own.
decorative = true hides the avatar from TalkBack when the name is written beside it.
The presence dot keeps its forms (bar, ring, and in high contrast half and square), so presence does not depend on color.
The group is a traversal group named by its label; each avatar is read by its own name, then the tile as "2 more".
The avatar grows with the font size setting, and the initials shrink to fit rather than being cut.
Avatars are not interactive, so they have no touch target; wrap one in a button when it must act.
edgeCases: Initials keep whole characters, so an emoji or a letter with a combining accent is never cut in half.
An empty name gives no initials; give decorative = true or a name, since TalkBack reads the name as given.
In a group, give each avatar the same size and shape as the group; the group uses them for the overlap, the ring and the tile.
The same seed gives the same color on Android, iOS and the web.
