name: MonarchAvatarUpload
title: AvatarUpload
wrapsNative: androidx.activity.result.contract.ActivityResultContracts.PickVisualMedia, androidx.compose.foundation.Canvas, androidx.compose.foundation.gestures.transformable, androidx.compose.material3.Slider, android.graphics.ImageDecoder, MonarchAvatar, MonarchButton
summary: Picks a profile or workspace picture with the system photo picker and crops it to a circle or a square before handing it over.
whenToUse: On a profile or workspace settings screen, wherever people set the picture that MonarchAvatar shows.
whenNotToUse: For attachments, documents or several files, use MonarchFileUpload. To show a picture without changing it, use MonarchAvatar.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAvatarUpload(name: String, image: Painter?, onChange: suspend (MonarchAvatarUploadResult) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, shape: MonarchAvatarShape = MonarchAvatarShape.Circle, enabled: Boolean = true, accept: List<String> = listOf("image/png", "image/jpeg", "image/webp", "image/gif"), maxSize: Long? = null, outputSize: Int = 512, onRemove: (() -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAvatarUploadLabels = MonarchAvatarUploadLabels())
class MonarchAvatarUploadResult(image: ImageBitmap, file: MonarchPickedFile, crop: MonarchAvatarCrop)
data class MonarchAvatarCrop(x: Float, y: Float, size: Float)

class MonarchAvatarUploadLabels(upload: String? = null, change: String? = null, remove: String? = null, cropArea: String? = null, cropHint: String? = null, zoom: String? = null, zoomValue: ((percent: Int) -> String)? = null, moveLeft: String? = null, moveRight: String? = null, moveUp: String? = null, moveDown: String? = null, zoomIn: String? = null, zoomOut: String? = null, save: String? = null, cancel: String? = null, saveFailed: String? = null, openFailed: String? = null, validation: MonarchFileUploadLabels = MonarchFileUploadLabels())

options.name: name
options.description: The person's or workspace's name, for the initials and the TalkBack name of the picture.

options.name: image
options.description: The current picture, loaded by the app, or null for the initials. Decides between Upload photo and Change photo.

options.name: onChange
options.description: Stores the cropped picture. Save stays busy until it returns; throwing shows the save failure and keeps the editor open.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the component.

options.name: shape
options.description: Circle for people, Square for workspaces and organizations. Also the crop mask.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the user can change the picture.

options.name: accept
options.description: Allowed image types. Also chooses what the photo picker shows.

options.name: maxSize
options.description: The largest file accepted, in bytes.

options.name: outputSize
options.description: The width and height of the cropped picture, in pixels.

options.name: onRemove
options.description: Removes the picture. The Remove photo button shows only with a picture and this callback.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the strings monarch_avatarupload_*, and validation for the type and size messages shared with MonarchFileUpload.

states.name: no picture
states.description: The initials avatar and Upload photo.

states.name: picture
states.description: The picture, Change photo and, with onRemove, Remove photo.

states.name: cropping
states.description: The picture in a square area masked to the shape, the hint, the zoom slider, Save photo and Cancel.

states.name: saving
states.description: Save photo shows progress; the crop, the slider and Cancel are locked.

states.name: error
states.description: A refused file, an unreadable image or a failed save is written in danger text and announced.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The buttons are disabled.

appearance: A large MonarchAvatar with small secondary and ghost buttons. While cropping, the picture fills a square of at most 288dp; outside the kept circle or square the canvas color hides it (no dimming), and a ring in the strong border color marks the edge. The hint is a muted caption and errors use the strong danger color. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web picks with a file input and produces a Blob from a canvas; on Android the picker is the system photo picker (PickVisualMedia, no storage permission) and the result is an ImageBitmap the app encodes, with the picked file and the crop. The web src is an image URL; on Android the picture is a Painter the app loads. The crop editor is inline, as on the web, rather than in a sheet, so the drag of a sheet never competes with moving the photo; an app can place the component in a ModalBottomSheet itself. Pinch zooms on Android, in addition to the slider and the plus and minus keys; TalkBack users move and zoom with custom actions. Images are decoded off the main thread and scaled down to 2048 pixels; from API 28 ImageDecoder applies the EXIF rotation, on API 24 to 27 BitmapFactory does not. The web outputType and outputQuality are left to the app's encoding. iOS has no entry yet; the names follow the web.
accessibility: Upload photo, Change photo, Remove photo, Save photo and Cancel are MonarchButtons with 48dp touch targets.
The crop area is named "Photo position", reads the zoom as its state ("150%") and offers the TalkBack actions Move left, Move right, Move up, Move down, Zoom in and Zoom out.
With a keyboard, the arrow keys move, plus and minus zoom, Home resets, Enter saves and Escape cancels; the crop area draws the focus ring.
Focus moves to the crop area when it opens and back to the picker button when it closes.
The zoom slider is labelled "Zoom" and reads the zoom as a percentage.
Errors are written as text and announced through a polite live region.
edgeCases: The crop is clamped so the picture always covers the area; zoom is between 100% and 400%.
The picked image is kept in memory only; after a configuration change the editor closes and the person picks again.
Large photos are scaled down before cropping, so the crop is in the pixels of the scaled image.
A file the decoder cannot read shows "The photo could not be opened.".

title: BackLink
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.TopAppBar navigationIcon with MonarchIconButton, androidx.activity.compose.BackHandler
summary: Going back is the system back gesture and the navigation icon of the top app bar. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: Put a MonarchIconButton with a back arrow in the navigationIcon slot of the TopAppBar of every screen below the top level; its onClick navigates up. Use BackHandler only to intercept system back, for example to confirm discarding unsaved changes.
whenNotToUse: Do not put a "Back to …" link in the content of a screen; the top app bar and the system gesture already go back. Do not use BackHandler to block back without telling the person why.
api: @Composable fun TopAppBar(title: @Composable () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, navigationIcon: @Composable () -> Unit = {}, actions: @Composable RowScope.() -> Unit = {}, ...)

@Composable fun MonarchIconButton(label: String, onClick: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchButtonVariant = MonarchButtonVariant.Ghost, size: MonarchButtonSize = MonarchButtonSize.Md, enabled: Boolean = true, loading: Boolean = false, loadingLabel: String? = null, shape: Shape? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null, icon: @Composable () -> Unit)

@Composable fun MonarchIcon(painter: Painter, contentDescription: String?, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, size: MonarchIconSize = MonarchIconSize.Md, tint: Color = LocalContentColor.current, mirrorInRtl: Boolean = false)
appearance: The top app bar and its icon button use the Material 3 colors mapped from the Monarch theme. The arrow is the app's icon, mirrored in a right-to-left layout.
platformNotes: The web BackLink is a link in the page content with a leading arrow, a variant and its own text ("Back to domains"). On Android back is owned by the system: the back gesture and button, with predictive back, and the navigation icon of the top app bar. The arrow has no visible text; its content description is "Back" or "Navigate up" in the app's strings, and the screen's title in the bar tells people where they are. The web's variant has no equivalent. Monarch bundles no icons, so the app passes the arrow and mirrors it with mirrorInRtl = true or an auto-mirrored vector. iOS uses the NavigationStack back button.
accessibility: The navigation icon is a MonarchIconButton: one TalkBack button named by the icon's content description, with a 48dp touch target.
System back works with TalkBack's back gesture as well.
The arrow must point to the start: mirror it in a right-to-left layout.
edgeCases: On the top-level screen there is no navigation icon; back leaves the app.
An enabled BackHandler takes system back from the screens below it until it is disabled.

name: MonarchBacklogPlanner
title: BacklogPlanner
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn with detectDragGesturesAfterLongPress and Modifier.animateItem; androidx.compose.material3.DropdownMenu with DropdownMenuItem for Move to; MonarchDragHandle, MonarchProgress, MonarchButton and MonarchText
summary: Backlog and iteration planning on one screen: buckets stacked top to bottom with items moved within and between them by dragging, TalkBack actions or a Move to menu, and points against capacity.
whenToUse: For planning which work goes into which sprint, release or iteration, with the backlog at the bottom.
whenNotToUse: For work moving through stages (To do, Doing, Done), use MonarchKanbanBoard. For ordering one flat list, use MonarchReorderableList.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun <T> MonarchBacklogPlanner(buckets: List<MonarchBacklogBucket<T>>, key: (T) -> String, itemLabel: (T) -> String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, itemPoints: ((T) -> Int?)? = null, onMove: (suspend (move: MonarchBacklogMove<T>, buckets: List<MonarchBacklogBucket<T>>) -> Unit)? = null, canMove: ((item: T, toBucketId: String, fromBucketId: String) -> Boolean)? = null, moveMenu: Boolean = true, collapsed: Set<String>? = null, onCollapsedChange: ((Set<String>) -> Unit)? = null, state: LazyListState = rememberLazyListState(), labels: MonarchBacklogPlannerLabels = MonarchBacklogPlannerLabels(), collapseIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, menuIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, itemContent: @Composable RowScope.(item: T, state: MonarchBacklogPlannerItemState) -> Unit)

class MonarchBacklogBucket<T>(id: String, title: String, items: List<T>, subtitle: String? = null, capacity: Int? = null, emptyText: String? = null, badge: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, actions: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null, footer: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null) { fun withItems(items: List<T>): MonarchBacklogBucket<T> }
data class MonarchBacklogMove<T>(item: T, itemKey: String, fromBucketId: String, fromIndex: Int, toBucketId: String, toIndex: Int)
class MonarchBacklogPlannerItemState(bucketId: String, index: Int, dragged: Boolean, pending: Boolean)

class MonarchBacklogPlannerLabels(summary: ((count: Int, points: Int?, unestimated: Int) -> String)? = null, capacity: ((points: Int, capacity: Int) -> String)? = null, overCapacity: ((by: Int) -> String)? = null, points: ((points: Int) -> String)? = null, unestimated: String? = null, notEstimated: String? = null, handle: ((label: String) -> String)? = null, moveMenu: ((label: String) -> String)? = null, move: String? = null, moveTo: ((bucket: String) -> String)? = null, empty: String? = null, expanded: String? = null, collapsed: String? = null, pickedUp: ((label: String, bucket: String, position: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, moved: ((label: String, bucket: String, position: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, dropped: ((label: String, bucket: String, position: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, cancelled: ((label: String) -> String)? = null, failed: ((label: String) -> String)? = null, actions: Map<MonarchDragHandleDirection, String> = emptyMap())

options.name: buckets
options.description: The buckets, top to bottom: usually the active and planned iterations, then the backlog.

options.name: key
options.description: A stable, unique key for an item, across every bucket.

options.name: itemLabel
options.description: The short plain-text name of an item, used in the handle's name, the menu and announcements.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the planner. Give it a bounded height: the list is lazy.

options.name: itemPoints
options.description: The points of an item, null when it has no estimate. Adds totals, points on rows and the capacity meters.

options.name: onMove
options.description: Saves a finished move with the buckets after it. Without it items cannot be moved. Throwing puts the item back and announces it.

options.name: canMove
options.type: ((item: T, toBucketId: String, fromBucketId: String) -> Boolean)?
options.description: Whether an item may go to a bucket. Refused buckets are skipped by the drag and the actions and disabled in the menu.

options.name: moveMenu
options.description: Adds the Move to button to each row.

options.name: collapsed
options.description: The ids of closed buckets. null keeps them inside the planner, all open at first.

options.name: onCollapsedChange
options.description: Called with the new set when the person opens or closes a bucket.

options.name: state
options.description: The scroll state of the list.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

options.name: collapseIcon
options.description: An icon at the start of each bucket title that turns a quarter turn while the bucket is open. None by default: Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: menuIcon
options.description: An icon for the Move to button. null shows the word Move.

options.name: itemContent
options.description: The content of a row after the handle: the item's key, title and pickers.

states.name: dragging
states.description: After a long press the row follows the finger above the others with a shadow and the accent border; its handle is read as Picked up. Other rows slide aside; the list scrolls at its edges.

states.name: pending
states.description: While onMove runs the item stays in its new place and its row's state has pending true.

states.name: failed
states.description: When onMove throws, the item goes back and "ABC-12 could not be moved. It is back where it was." is announced.

states.name: collapsed
states.description: A closed bucket shows only its header, read as Collapsed; drags and Move up and Move down skip it.

states.name: empty
states.description: An open bucket with no items shows its emptyText, or "Nothing here yet."

states.name: over capacity
states.description: The capacity meter is full and "Planned work is over capacity by 3 points." is written in the strong danger color.

states.name: refused
states.description: Buckets canMove refuses are disabled in the Move to menu and skipped by the drag and the actions.

states.name: read only
states.description: Without onMove there is no handle, no Move to button and no drag.

appearance: Bucket headers use the subheading style in the default text color with captions in the muted text color. Rows are surface-coloured cards with a subtle border and the medium radius; a dragged row gets the accent border and a medium shadow. The capacity meter is MonarchProgress; the over-capacity note uses the strong danger color and is written out. The same roles adapt to dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: A domain composite, marked experimental until a Rook app adopts it. The web picks items up with the keyboard (Space, arrows, Space) or a pointer; on Android a long press anywhere on the row starts the drag, and the handle offers Move up and Move down as TalkBack actions and arrow keys, each saving one step, so there is no separate keyboard pick-up mode. Bucket titles, subtitles and empty text are strings; badge, actions and footer are slots. Points are whole numbers. Collapse is hoisted as collapsed and onCollapsedChange. The web's chevron and menu glyphs are app-supplied slots because Monarch bundles no icons; without them the header has no glyph and the menu button reads Move. Announcements use a polite live region where the web uses an assertive one. There is no iOS entry yet.
accessibility: Each bucket title is a heading and a button read with the state Expanded or Collapsed, with the TalkBack expand and collapse actions.
Each row's handle is named "Move ABC-12" and offers Move up and Move down actions that cross into the next open bucket.
The Move to button is named "Move ABC-12 to another bucket" and opens a menu of the other buckets; refused buckets are disabled.
Pick up, each move, drop, cancel and a failed save are announced through a polite live region that is always present.
A row with no estimate shows a dash that TalkBack reads as "Not estimated".
Capacity is a progress indicator named "18 of 20 points", and over capacity is written as text, not shown by color alone.
Headers, handles and Move to buttons have 48dp touch targets.
edgeCases: The planner shows a saved move until onMove returns and the app passes the new buckets list; passing a new list instance replaces it.
Moving to the same place does not call onMove.
The list is lazy: give the planner a bounded height. Inside a vertically scrolling parent it would get an infinite height and fail.
Move up at the top of the first open bucket, or Move down at the end of the last, does nothing.
Long titles and subtitles wrap; rows grow at font scale 2.0.

name: MonarchBadge
title: Badge
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row, androidx.compose.material3.Text
summary: A short status or metadata label in five tones and three variants.
whenToUse: For the status of an item in a list, a table or a card.
whenNotToUse: For a message about a screen or a section use MonarchBanner. For the notification dot on a navigation item use the Material 3 Badge.

states.name: default
states.description: Not interactive; one look per tone and variant.

appearance: Subtle is a tinted fill with strong text, solid a strong fill with the text color made for it, outline a border with strong text. Each pair comes from one tone family, in every theme.
platformNotes: The web also has an accent tone, an accent tone; it is not offered. A sm size and a dot are offered. The badge is at least 24dp high, against 22px on the web, and grows with the font size setting.
accessibility: Read as text; the tone is never the only carrier of meaning.
Not interactive, so it has no touch target.
Grows with the font size setting.
edgeCases: Long text wraps inside the pill; keep it short.
An icon passed as leadingIcon takes the content color of the badge.

name: MonarchBarChart
title: BarChart
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.Canvas (DrawScope.drawPath, drawLine, drawRoundRect) with androidx.compose.ui.text.TextMeasurer and drawText; inside MonarchChartFrame with MonarchChartLegend and MonarchChartTable
summary: A bar or column chart of one or more series per category, grouped or stacked, vertical or horizontal, with value labels, a highlighted category, reference lines, touch inspection, legend toggles, drill-in and the data as a table.
whenToUse: To compare amounts across a handful of categories or periods, or to show how a few series make up each category's total.
whenNotToUse: For a ranked list of labelled values with no axis, use MonarchBarList. For a word-sized trend use MonarchSparkline. For parts of one whole, use MonarchDonutChart.
api: @Composable fun MonarchBarChart(title: String, categories: List<String>, series: List<MonarchBarChartSeries>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, description: String? = null, categoryTitle: String? = null, summary: String? = null, orientation: MonarchBarChartOrientation = MonarchBarChartOrientation.Vertical, layout: MonarchBarChartLayout = MonarchBarChartLayout.Grouped, status: MonarchChartFrameStatus = MonarchChartFrameStatus.Ready, hiddenSeries: Set<String>? = null, onHiddenSeriesChange: ((Set<String>) -> Unit)? = null, highlightedIndex: Int? = null, referenceLines: List<MonarchBarChartReferenceLine> = emptyList(), valueRange: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Double>? = null, showValueLabels: Boolean = false, legendToggle: Boolean = true, tableToggle: Boolean = true, emptyMessage: String? = null, footer: String? = null, height: Dp? = null, labels: MonarchBarChartLabels = MonarchBarChartLabels(), formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = null, onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null, onSelect: ((Int) -> Unit)? = null)
class MonarchBarChartSeries(key: String, label: String, values: List<Double?>, color: MonarchChartColor? = null)
class MonarchBarChartReferenceLine(value: Double, label: String? = null)

class MonarchBarChartLabels(frame: MonarchChartFrameLabels = MonarchChartFrameLabels(), category: String? = null, total: String? = null, noData: String? = null, details: String? = null, clearSelection: String? = null, highlighted: String? = null)
enum class MonarchBarChartOrientation { Vertical, Horizontal }
enum class MonarchBarChartLayout { Grouped, Stacked }

options.name: title
options.description: The chart's name: the frame heading and the plot's spoken name.

options.name: categories
options.description: The categories in display order, already formatted by the app (dates, months, names).

options.name: series
options.description: The measures: a key, a label, one value per category and an optional color slot.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the frame.

options.name: description
options.description: One line under the title.

options.name: categoryTitle
options.description: The heading of the category column of the table.

options.name: summary
options.description: Replaces the generated spoken summary.

options.name: orientation
options.description: Vertical columns or Horizontal bars.

options.name: layout
options.description: With several series, Grouped side by side or Stacked.

options.name: status
options.description: Ready, Loading, Empty or Error. Ready with no categories or no series shows Empty.

options.name: hiddenSeries
options.description: The keys of hidden series. null lets the chart keep its own set (rememberSaveable), changed by the legend.

options.name: onHiddenSeriesChange
options.description: Called with the new hidden set when the legend changes it, in both modes.

options.name: highlightedIndex
options.description: A category to emphasise: the bars of the others take the disabled text color and TalkBack reads "Highlighted" on it.

options.name: referenceLines
options.description: Dashed lines across the bars at a value, with an optional label.

options.name: valueRange
options.description: Fixes the value axis. null fits the values, zero and the reference lines to round ticks.

options.name: showValueLabels
options.description: Writes each bar's value at its end; a stack shows its net total once.

options.name: legendToggle
options.description: Whether legend entries show and hide their series. The legend appears with two or more series; without toggles it lists only the series that are drawn.

options.name: tableToggle
options.description: Whether "View as table" is offered.

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: The message of the empty state.

options.name: footer
options.description: Notes under the chart.

options.name: height
options.description: The plot height: 240dp for columns; 32dp per category plus one, at least 120dp, for horizontal bars.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, including the frame's.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes values on the axis, in value labels, the inspection row, TalkBack, the table and the summary. By default a number in the current locale, compact ("1.2K") on the axis and the bars.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Try again in the error status.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Drill-in: called with the category index from Details in the inspection row or from the TalkBack action "Details, <category>".

states.name: ready
states.description: The plot with value gridlines, the legend (two or more series) and "View as table".

states.name: inspecting
states.description: After a tap on the plot, or a drag along columns: the category's band is shaded with the muted background and a row under the plot shows its values (and the stack total), announced politely, with Details (when onSelect is set) and Clear. It stays until Clear or another category is touched.

states.name: highlighted
states.description: With highlightedIndex, the bars of the other categories take the disabled text color; TalkBack reads "Highlighted" on the highlighted category.

states.name: series hidden
states.description: A hidden series is not drawn, read or summarised; its legend chip reads "Hidden" and is struck through. The table still lists it.

states.name: table
states.description: "View as table" replaces the plot with every category and series as text, plus a Total column when two or more series are stacked.

states.name: loading
states.description: The frame's skeleton of the plot's height, read as "Loading chart".

states.name: empty
states.description: MonarchEmptyState with "No data yet" and the empty message; also shown when there are no categories or no series.

states.name: error
states.description: The frame's error, with Try again when onRetry is set.

appearance: Bars take the theme's data colors 1 to 5 in series order, then the subtle text color, with the far end rounded. Gridlines use the subtle border color, the zero line the strong border color, tick, category and value labels the muted text color in the caption style. Reference lines are dashed in the subtle text color. The inspected band uses the muted background; dimmed bars use the disabled text color. Every color is a theme role, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes are covered.
platformNotes: Android has no first-party chart library and Monarch adds none, so the chart is drawn with a Compose Canvas (iOS uses Swift Charts, the web hand-drawn SVG). Positions are computed from the start edge and mirrored when drawn, so the chart reads right to left in RTL locales; text is drawn unmirrored. Android has no chart descriptor like iOS's AXChartDescriptor (Audio Graphs): TalkBack gets a summary on the plot, one element per category it can swipe through, and the table. The highlight is drawn with the disabled color rather than iOS's reduced opacity, because Monarch never dims with transparency. hiddenSeries is either controlled (with onHiddenSeriesChange) or kept by the chart; iOS uses a Binding. Not offered: the web's keyboard arrow navigation and controlled activeIndex, date categories formatted by the chart (the app formats categories), dashed series, and iOS's valueTitle (there is no value axis for TalkBack to name). Horizontal bars inspect on tap only, so a vertical drag still scrolls the screen.
accessibility: The plot is one element with the image role, named by the title, whose state description is the generated summary (number and range of categories, each shown series' total and highest category, each reference line) or the summary parameter.
After it, one element per category in category order (traversal index), read as the category and each shown series' value, with "No value" for a gap and the total of a stack of two or more series.
With onSelect, each category element has a TalkBack custom action named "Details, <category>"; without it the elements have no action.
The highlighted category's element has the state description "Highlighted", so the highlight is not shown by color alone.
The inspection row is a polite live region followed by MonarchButton controls (Details, Clear) with touch targets of at least 48dp.
The legend is MonarchChartLegend: each entry is a filter chip with the state "Shown" or "Hidden"; the last shown series cannot be hidden.
"View as table" shows every value as text; each table row is read as the category, then each series and its value.
Category elements and taps are mirrored in right to left, so the first category is at the start edge.
edgeCases: Gaps (null) and values that are not finite draw no bar, are read "No value" and shown "—" in the table, and are left out of the summary.
Negative values draw below (or before) the zero line; in a stack they stack down from zero apart from the positive values, and a stack's value label shows the net total at the end of the larger side.
More than five series: the sixth and later take the neutral color, as in the legend.
Category labels that do not fit are cut with an ellipsis, and with many columns only every n-th label is drawn; the full names are in the category elements, the inspection row and the table.
A highlightedIndex outside the categories dims every bar.
The inspection row takes room from the plot inside the frame's fixed height; at the largest font size the plot gets shorter.
With a valueRange that excludes some values, bars are drawn beyond the plot edge; the values are still read and listed.
TalkBack navigation, the custom actions and the drag gesture were checked only with Robolectric semantics tests, not on a device with TalkBack.

name: MonarchBarList
title: BarList
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column, androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Box, androidx.compose.material3.Text
summary: A ranked list with a bar behind each row's label: top pages, top referrers, rivals by score.
whenToUse: To compare a handful of values by size where the labels matter more than exact axes: top pages, top referrers, conversion by channel.
whenNotToUse: For a value against a limit use MonarchProgress or MonarchUsageMeter. For a trend over time use MonarchSparkline. For a long, scrolling list of records use a LazyColumn of list items.
api: @Composable fun MonarchBarList(items: List<MonarchBarListItem>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, sort: MonarchBarListSort = MonarchBarListSort.Descending, maximum: Double? = null, limit: Int? = null, ranked: Boolean = false, loading: Boolean = false, label: String? = null, formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = null, onSelect: ((MonarchBarListItem) -> Unit)? = null, missingLabel: String? = null, emptyLabel: String? = null, loadingLabel: String? = null, overflowLabel: String? = null)

class MonarchBarListItem(label: String, value: Double?, id: String = label, description: String? = null, displayValue: String? = null, highlighted: Boolean = false, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null)
enum class MonarchBarListSort { Descending, Ascending, None }

options.name: items
options.description: The rows.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the list.

options.name: sort
options.description: Descending, Ascending or None. Rows without a value go last; equal values keep their order.

options.name: maximum
options.description: The value of a full bar. The largest value when null. Pass 1.0 for ratios of a whole.

options.name: limit
options.description: Shows only the first rows, with a "Top 5 of 12" footer.

options.name: ranked
options.description: Numbers the rows. The numbers are not read; the order carries the rank.

options.name: loading
options.description: Shows a progress indicator and "Loading" instead of the rows.

options.name: label
options.description: Names the list for TalkBack, such as "Top pages".

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes a value. The default is a number in the current locale.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Makes every row a button.

options.name: missingLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in text "No value" (monarch_barlist_missing).

options.name: emptyLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in text "No data yet" (monarch_barlist_empty).

options.name: loadingLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in text "Loading" (monarch_barlist_loading).

options.name: overflowLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in footer "Top 5 of 12" (monarch_barlist_overflow).

states.name: default
states.description: Rows sorted by value, each with a bar as long as its share of the largest value.

states.name: highlighted row
states.description: A semibold label and value.

states.name: missing value
states.description: A dash instead of the value, read as "No value", and no bar.

states.name: selectable
states.description: With onSelect every row is at least 48dp high, shows the ripple and draws the focus ring.

states.name: empty
states.description: The text "No data yet".

states.name: loading
states.description: A circular progress indicator and the loading text.

appearance: Each row has an 8dp muted track under its label, filled in the first data color for its share; a highlighted row has a semibold label and value; descriptions, rank numbers, the footer and the dash use muted text. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web draws the bar on a track under the label or inline; here the bar is behind the label, the usual form on a narrow screen, as on iOS, so there is no layout option. The web formats numbers, percentages and currencies from options; here formatValue takes a function. Row links (href) become onSelect, because navigation in an app is not a URL. The web loading state draws skeleton rows; here it is a progress indicator. The parity map named a LazyColumn; the rows are a plain Column instead, because a bar list is short (use limit) and a LazyColumn cannot sit inside a scrolling screen.
accessibility: Each row is one TalkBack element: its label and description, then its value.
A row without a value reads "No value" in place of the dash.
Bars and rank numbers are not read; the order of the rows carries the rank.
The list exposes collection info (a list of n rows) and, with a label, the label as its content description.
With onSelect each row has the Button role, a click action and a touch target at least 48dp high, and draws the focus ring.
A highlighted row has a heavier label and value; the emphasis is not spoken, so say why in the label.
Labels wrap and are not cut off at font scale 2.0; row content starts at the start edge in both layout directions.
edgeCases: Equal values keep the order they were given in.
Values that are not finite are treated as missing.
Negative values and an all-zero list draw no bars.
A value above maximum draws a full bar.
limit hides rows but the scale still uses the largest value of all items.
Item ids default to the label.

name: MonarchBlockEditor
title: BlockEditor
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn of androidx.compose.foundation.text.BasicTextField blocks (one MonarchRichTextEditorState each), with MonarchEditorToolbar, MonarchSlashMenu, MonarchDragHandle with androidx.compose.material3.DropdownMenu, androidx.compose.material3.Checkbox, MonarchCalloutBlock, MonarchToggleBlock, MonarchTableBlock, MonarchEmbedBlock and androidx.compose.foundation.text.contextmenu.modifier.appendTextContextMenuComponents
summary: A block document editor: paragraphs, headings, lists, checklists, quotes, code, callouts, toggles, tables and embeds, with a / menu, a handle per block to move or change it, a formatting toolbar and formats in the text selection menu.
whenToUse: For documents people build out of blocks, such as notes, specs, wiki pages and briefs, stored as a list of blocks.
whenNotToUse: For one formatted text such as a description or a comment use MonarchRichTextEditor; for plain text use MonarchTextField; to show a finished document without editing it, readOnly = true is enough.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable public fun MonarchBlockEditor(label: String, state: MonarchBlockEditorState, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, blocks: Set<MonarchBlockEditorBlockType> = MonarchBlockEditorBlockType.entries.toSet(), tools: List<List<MonarchEditorTool>> = MonarchBlockEditorDefaults.Tools, enabled: Boolean = true, readOnly: Boolean = false, bubbleMenu: Boolean = true, dragHandles: Boolean = true, slashMenu: Boolean = true, slashItems: List<MonarchSlashMenuItem> = emptyList(), slashGroupOrder: List<String> = emptyList(), embedProviders: List<MonarchEmbedProvider> = MonarchEmbedProvider.Defaults, icons: Map<MonarchEditorTool, Painter> = emptyMap(), labels: MonarchBlockEditorLabels = MonarchBlockEditorLabels(), listState: LazyListState = rememberLazyListState(), onSlashItem: ((MonarchSlashMenuItem) -> Unit)? = null, onTool: ((MonarchEditorTool) -> Unit)? = null, onOpenLink: ((String) -> Unit)? = null)

@Stable public class MonarchBlockEditorState(blocks: List<MonarchBlockEditorBlock> = emptyList()) { val blocks: List<MonarchBlockEditorBlock>; val focusedBlockId: String?; val canUndo: Boolean; val canRedo: Boolean; fun setBlocks(blocks: List<MonarchBlockEditorBlock>); fun undo(); fun redo(); fun insertBlock(block: MonarchBlockEditorBlock, afterId: String? = focusedBlockId); fun updateBlock(block: MonarchBlockEditorBlock); fun moveBlock(id: String, offset: Int); fun duplicateBlock(id: String); fun deleteBlock(id: String); companion object { fun newId(): String; val Saver: Saver<MonarchBlockEditorState, Any> } }
@Composable public fun rememberMonarchBlockEditorState(blocks: List<MonarchBlockEditorBlock> = emptyList()): MonarchBlockEditorState

public sealed interface MonarchBlockEditorBlock { val id: String; val type: MonarchBlockEditorBlockType; data class Text(id: String, style: MonarchBlockEditorTextStyle = Paragraph, text: String = "", spans: List<MonarchRichTextSpan> = emptyList(), checked: Boolean = false); data class Callout(id: String, text: String = "", spans: List<MonarchRichTextSpan> = emptyList(), tone: MonarchTone = MonarchTone.Info); data class Toggle(id: String, text: String = "", spans: List<MonarchRichTextSpan> = emptyList(), body: String = "", expanded: Boolean = true); data class Table(id: String, data: MonarchTableBlockData = MonarchTableBlockData.empty()); data class Embed(id: String, url: String = "", caption: String? = null) }
public enum class MonarchBlockEditorBlockType { Paragraph, Heading1, Heading2, Heading3, BulletedList, NumberedList, Checklist, Quote, Code, Callout, Toggle, Table, Embed }

public enum class MonarchBlockEditorTextStyle(val type: MonarchBlockEditorBlockType) { Paragraph, Heading1, Heading2, Heading3, BulletedList, NumberedList, Checklist, Quote, Code; val isList: Boolean; val isHeading: Boolean; companion object { fun of(type: MonarchBlockEditorBlockType): MonarchBlockEditorTextStyle? } }
public object MonarchBlockEditorDefaults { val Tools: List<List<MonarchEditorTool>> }

public class MonarchBlockEditorLabels(placeholder: String? = null, names: Map<MonarchBlockEditorBlockType, String> = emptyMap(), descriptions: Map<MonarchBlockEditorBlockType, String> = emptyMap(), groupText: String? = null, groupLists: String? = null, groupBlocks: String? = null, handle: ((block: String) -> String)? = null, moveUp: String? = null, moveDown: String? = null, duplicate: String? = null, delete: String? = null, turnInto: String? = null, tone: String? = null, neutralTone: String? = null, moved: ((block: String, position: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, toggleShow: String? = null, toggleHide: String? = null, toggleContent: String? = null, embedLink: String? = null, embedAdd: String? = null, toolbar: MonarchEditorToolbarLabels = MonarchEditorToolbarLabels(), slashMenu: MonarchSlashMenuLabels = MonarchSlashMenuLabels(), table: MonarchTableBlockLabels = MonarchTableBlockLabels(), embed: MonarchEmbedBlockLabels = MonarchEmbedBlockLabels())

options.name: label
options.description: The spoken name of the document, already localized. Show a visible title nearby.

options.name: state
options.description: The document, the block with the caret and the undo history. Create it with rememberMonarchBlockEditorState.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the editor. Give it a bounded height: the editor scrolls itself.

options.name: blocks
options.description: The kinds of block offered in the / menu, the toolbar, the shortcuts and the Turn into menu. Paragraphs are always offered; blocks of other kinds already in the document are still shown.

options.name: tools
options.description: The toolbar's tools in groups; an empty list for no toolbar. Custom tools go to onTool.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the document can be edited. Disabled shows the blocks in the disabled colors without the toolbar and the handles.

options.name: readOnly
options.description: Shows the document as read: text with links that open, callouts, toggles that open and close, tables and embeds; no fields, toolbar or handles.

options.name: bubbleMenu
options.description: Adds Bold, Italic, Strikethrough and Code to the system menu of selected text.

options.name: dragHandles
options.description: Shows the handle beside each block, which is dragged to move the block and tapped for its menu.

options.name: slashMenu
options.description: Opens the / menu when / is typed at the start of a text block.

options.name: slashItems
options.description: The app's entries of the / menu, after the built-in ones; their ids must not be the built-in ids.

options.name: slashGroupOrder
options.description: Group headings of the / menu in display order.

options.name: embedProviders
options.description: The sites an embed may frame; other links are shown as links.

options.name: icons
options.description: The icons of the toolbar's tools. A tool without one shows its name.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including those of the toolbar, the / menu, tables and embeds.

options.name: listState
options.description: The scroll state of the document.

options.name: onSlashItem
options.description: Receives the app's / menu entries after the typed command is removed; change the document with state.

options.name: onTool
options.description: Receives the custom tools of the toolbar.

options.name: onOpenLink
options.description: Opens a link of an embed outside the app; null uses the system browser.

states.name: editing
states.description: Each block is a text field at least 48dp high with its handle at the start; the toolbar acts on the block with the caret and shows its style and formats as on.

states.name: empty
states.description: A new document is one empty paragraph that shows "Write, or type / for blocks"; an empty block with the caret shows the placeholder (or the name of its kind).

states.name: slash menu
states.description: While / and a word are typed at the start of a text block, the / menu under the document lists the matching kinds; choosing one turns the block into it, or inserts a table or an embed.

states.name: block menu
states.description: A tap on a handle opens Move up, Move down, Duplicate, Turn into (the kinds that keep the text), Tone for a callout and Delete block.

states.name: dragging
states.description: While a handle is dragged, its block follows the finger with an accent outline and a shadow, the other blocks slide aside and the list scrolls at its edges; the move is made on release.

states.name: read only
states.description: Blocks are shown as text, callouts, toggles that open and close, tables and embeds, without fields, toolbar or handles; links open on a tap.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Blocks are shown in their fields with the disabled text color, without the toolbar and the handles.

appearance: Text uses the default text role (headings in the title, heading and subheading styles, quotes in the muted text role beside a strong border bar, code on the subtle background with a subtle border), placeholders the subtle text role, list markers the muted text role, checklist boxes the accent solid role; a dragged block has the surface fill, the accent border and a medium shadow, and Delete block is in the danger strong role. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web BlockEditor is one Tiptap (ProseMirror) document. Compose has no rich-text engine, so on Android each block is its own BasicTextField over a MonarchRichTextEditorState in a LazyColumn, and the document is a list of MonarchBlockEditorBlock values instead of HTML or Tiptap JSON; no conversion is shipped, so it is experimental until the interchange format is agreed across platforms, like MonarchRichTextEditor. Consequences: a selection stays inside one block (no selection or copy across blocks); undo is the editor's own history of the whole document, grouped by word while typing. On a phone the handle is a 48dp gutter beside every block instead of appearing on hover, a tap opens the block menu and a drag moves the block; the / menu is a strip under the document, above the keyboard, because Compose gives no caret rectangle; the web's selection bubble is items added to the system text selection menu. Not offered: columns (blocks side by side do not fit a phone; the document is already one column), images (Monarch takes pictures as Painters, and an editor that stores them needs the app's upload and loading; insert them through slashItems and the app's own UI), heading levels 4 to 6, nested lists, Tab to indent, the onEditorReady and editorRef handles, maxLength, mentions, HTML or JSON output and a hidden form field. A toggle's content is plain text. iOS has no BlockEditor entry yet; the names follow the web.
accessibility: Every block is a text field named by its kind ("Heading 1", "Bulleted list", "Numbered list 2"); headings are headings in editing and reading.

Each handle is one TalkBack element, a button named "Block actions" and the kind, that opens the block menu, with Move up and Move down as custom actions; Alt+Shift+Up and Down move the block from the keyboard.
Every move is announced through a polite live region: "Heading 1 moved to position 2 of 4."
A checklist item's checkbox is named by the item's text and is checked or not, and a ticked item is also struck through, so the state is not color alone.
Blocks, handles, checkboxes and buttons are at least 48dp high, also at the largest font size, and the document scrolls instead of cutting text.
The document list is named by label; the / menu announces the number of matches itself.
edgeCases: Return in a list or checklist item starts a new item; Return on an empty item turns it into a paragraph. Return in code adds a line.
Pasting several lines into a text block makes one block per line.

Backspace at the start of a heading, list item, quote, code, callout or empty toggle turns it into a paragraph; at the start of a paragraph it joins the paragraph to the block above, or deletes it when empty after a table or embed. Soft keyboards send Backspace on an empty field as a key event only on some devices.
Deleting the last block leaves one empty paragraph.
Blocks with repeated ids are given new ids when loaded.
The editor needs a bounded height; inside a vertically scrolling parent it throws, as every LazyColumn does.

title: BookingFlow
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column with verticalScroll, androidx.activity.compose.BackHandler; MonarchStepper (compact), MonarchRadioRow, MonarchSlotPicker (with its MonarchTimezoneSelect), MonarchTextField, MonarchDescriptionList, MonarchButton and MonarchEmptyState for the confirmation
summary: A recipe, not a component: booking an appointment one step per screen (service, date and time, details, review), with a compact stepper, Back and Continue, and a confirmation.
whenToUse: For a customer booking a service, a call or a visit in the app, when it takes more than one choice.
whenNotToUse: To move an existing booking use the reschedule-dialog recipe; for one choice of time on its own use MonarchSlotPicker directly.
api: MonarchStepper(steps = …, current = step, compact = MonarchStepperCompactMode.Always, onSelect = { _, index -> if (index < step) step = index })
MonarchText(text = title, modifier = Modifier.semantics { liveRegion = LiveRegionMode.Polite }, style = MonarchTextStyle.Heading, heading = true)
MonarchSlotPicker(slots = …, selection = slot, onSelectionChange = …, day = …, onDayChange = …, timeZone = zone, previousMonthIcon = …, nextMonthIcon = …, onTimeZoneChange = { zone = it })
MonarchButton(text = "Back", …, variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Ghost); MonarchButton(text = if (last) "Confirm booking" else "Continue", …, variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Primary, enabled = complete)
BackHandler(enabled = step > 0) { step-- }
MonarchEmptyState(title = "Booking complete", kind = MonarchEmptyStateKind.Success, message = …)

appearance: Existing Monarch components on the screen background: the compact stepper, a heading, radio rows, the slot picker, text fields, a description list and a ghost Back with a primary Continue. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web ships BookingFlow as a pattern component with steps, step, onStepChange, onSubmit, submitLabel, confirmation, completed, pending, error and messages, plus a useBookingFlow hook, a progress list and a summary panel beside the steps on wide screens. On a phone it is a recipe: one step per screen with the compact MonarchStepper, the system back gesture going to the previous step through BackHandler, and the summary as the last step. Completed steps can be reopened from the stepper (onSelect) instead of Change buttons. A wide window can show the summary in a supporting pane.
accessibility: Each step's heading has heading semantics and sits in a polite live region, so moving between steps is announced.
The stepper reads its position (Step 2 of 4) and completed steps; reached steps are buttons.
Back is a button and also the system back gesture.
Continue is disabled, not hidden, until the step is complete.
Radio rows and the slot picker carry their own selected states.
edgeCases: A service that has no choices: leave its step out.
Changing the day clears the chosen time.
At the largest text sizes each step scrolls while the buttons stay at the bottom.
Keep the state in rememberSaveable so rotation keeps the person's place.

name: MonarchBreadcrumb
title: Breadcrumb
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyRow of MonarchLink in the subtle style, with a ghost MonarchButton that opens androidx.compose.material3.DropdownMenu and DropdownMenuItem for the collapsed levels
summary: A trail of the levels above the current screen, the current level last, with the middle levels of a long trail collapsed into a menu.
whenToUse: For deep hierarchies the person moves up and down, such as folders, document trees or nested settings, where knowing and jumping to an ancestor helps.
whenNotToUse: On ordinary screens: the top app bar's title and back button already say where the person is. For moving between sections of one screen, use tabs.
api: @Composable fun MonarchBreadcrumb(items: List<MonarchBreadcrumbItem>, onItemClick: (MonarchBreadcrumbItem) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, maxVisible: Int = 4, enabled: Boolean = true, separator: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchBreadcrumbLabels = MonarchBreadcrumbLabels())
class MonarchBreadcrumbItem(title: String, id: String = title, linked: Boolean = true)
class MonarchBreadcrumbLabels(label: String? = null, more: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, current: String? = null)

options.name: items
options.description: The levels from the root to the current screen. Each has a title, an id (the title by default) and linked.

options.name: onItemClick
options.description: Goes to the chosen level, for example by popping the back stack. Not called for the last level or for a level that is not linked.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the trail.

options.name: maxVisible
options.description: The most levels shown. Above it the first level stays, the middle levels collapse into a menu and the last maxVisible - 2 stay. Values below 3 count as 3.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the links and the menu can be used. When not, they use the disabled text color.

options.name: separator
options.description: Replaces the separator, a single angle quotation mark that mirrors right to left. Hidden from TalkBack.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the TalkBack name of the trail ("Breadcrumb"), of the menu button ("Show 3 more levels") and of the current level's state ("Current page").

states.name: linked ancestor
states.description: A MonarchLink in the subtle style: muted text, underlined while pressed or focused.

states.name: not linked
states.description: An ancestor with linked = false is muted text, and a disabled item in the collapsed menu.

states.name: current
states.description: The last level is text in the default color and a medium weight, never a link.

states.name: collapsed
states.description: An ellipsis button in the ghost style stands for the middle levels and opens a DropdownMenu of them.

states.name: overflowing
states.description: When the trail is wider than the space it scrolls sideways; it starts scrolled to the current level.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With enabled = false every link and the menu button are disabled and use the disabled text color.

appearance: Links in the muted text color, the current level in the default text color and medium weight, and separators in the subtle text color, on whatever surface holds the trail. The menu uses the Material 3 menu colors Monarch maps to the raised surface. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web Breadcrumb is a nav of links with href and a linkAs component. On Android each level calls onItemClick, so the app pops its back stack or loads the folder, as on iOS. The web's locale prop is not needed: the hidden count is formatted by the plurals resource in the app's locale. A web item without href is linked = false. Monarch bundles no icons, so the web's chevron separator is a mirrored text character, and a separator slot takes the app's own glyph. The plan's LazyRow is used, which also keeps a long trail on one line instead of wrapping it.
accessibility: The trail is one traversal group named "Breadcrumb" (replaceable with labels.label); TalkBack moves through its levels in order.
Ancestors are links with their title as the name and a 48dp touch target. The last level is text with the state "Current page".
The separators are hidden from TalkBack.
The collapsed-levels button is named "Show 3 more levels" from a plurals resource and has a 48dp touch target; levels without a screen are disabled in its menu.
Text scales with the font size and stays on one line; the trail scrolls instead of cutting a title.
The default separator is a mirrored character, so it points the reading direction in right-to-left layouts.
edgeCases: One level shows only the current level, with no separator and no link.
An empty list shows nothing.
maxVisible below 3 counts as 3: the first level, the menu and the last level.
Levels with the same title need distinct ids when the app tells them apart.

title: BubbleMenu
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.text.contextmenu.modifier.appendTextContextMenuComponents with androidx.compose.foundation.text.contextmenu.builder.item
summary: Actions over selected text are items added to the system text selection menu (the floating toolbar with Cut, Copy and Paste) with Modifier.appendTextContextMenuComponents. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: For a few actions that apply to the selected text of a field, such as Comment, Bold or Ask AI, without a permanent toolbar.
whenNotToUse: For formatting that people use all the time, use MonarchEditorToolbar above the text (MonarchRichTextEditor and MonarchBlockEditor have one). Not for actions on a whole item: use a MonarchMenu or MonarchContextMenu.
api: fun Modifier.appendTextContextMenuComponents(builder: TextContextMenuBuilderScope.() -> Unit): Modifier
fun TextContextMenuBuilderScope.item(key: Any, label: String, leadingIcon: Int = Resources.ID_NULL, onClick: TextContextMenuSession.() -> Unit)
fun TextContextMenuBuilderScope.separator()
interface TextContextMenuSession { fun close() }
fun Modifier.filterTextContextMenuComponents(filter: (TextContextMenuComponent) -> Boolean): Modifier

states.name: hidden
states.description: Nothing is shown while there is no selection; the builder is asked again each time the menu opens.

states.name: open
states.description: After a selection is made, the system floating toolbar shows Cut, Copy, Paste and Select all, then the added items; extra items go into its overflow.

states.name: after an action
states.description: Call close() in the item's onClick to dismiss the menu; the selection stays as the app leaves it.

appearance: The system draws the floating toolbar in the device theme (with a hardware mouse, a dropdown menu), not in the Monarch theme; added items look like the system's own Cut and Copy.
platformNotes: The web BubbleMenu is a Monarch toolbar that floats over a Tiptap selection, with Alt+F10 to reach it and placement and offset props. On Android a second floating toolbar would cover or fight the system selection toolbar, so actions are added to that toolbar instead, as Google Docs and Keep do. The parity map named LocalTextToolbar custom actions: the TextToolbar interface only shows the system's own items, so the API is the text context menu builder of Compose foundation 1.8 and later (on by default in 1.12). The items are text, not toggles, so a format's on or off state is not shown in the menu; show it in a MonarchEditorToolbar. Placement, offset, Alt+F10 and Escape are the system's. iOS covers the same idea with the system edit menu.
accessibility: System behavior: the floating toolbar and its items are read by TalkBack like the system's Cut and Copy, and are reached by its actions on the selected text.
Give each item a short verb as its label ("Comment", "Bold"); the label is all TalkBack reads.
The menu never takes focus from the text; the selection is kept when the menu closes.
edgeCases: The builder runs each time the menu opens: read the field's current selection there and add nothing when it is collapsed.
On a small screen the toolbar shows a few items and puts the rest in its overflow; put the most used action first.
The same modifier works on BasicTextField, MonarchTextField, MonarchTextField and SelectionContainer.

name: MonarchBulkActionBar
title: BulkActionBar
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.Surface, androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow, androidx.compose.material3.DropdownMenu, MonarchButton
summary: The bar shown while items are selected: the count, the actions for the selection with a More menu for the rest, and Clear selection, with the count announced.
whenToUse: Under or over a list or table with multiple selection, while at least one item is selected: archive, export, tag or delete the selection.
whenNotToUse: For actions on one item, use a row actions menu. For actions that do not depend on a selection, use the screen's top app bar.
api: @Composable fun MonarchBulkActionBar(count: Int, onClear: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, totalCount: Int? = null, actions: List<MonarchBulkAction> = emptyList(), maxVisibleActions: Int = 3, busy: Boolean = false, busyActionId: String? = null, labels: MonarchBulkActionBarLabels = MonarchBulkActionBarLabels(), accessories: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null)
class MonarchBulkAction(id: String, title: String, destructive: Boolean = false, enabled: Boolean = true, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, onClick: () -> Unit)
class MonarchBulkActionBarLabels(selected: ((count: Int, total: Int?) -> String)? = null, cleared: String? = null, clear: String? = null, more: String? = null, bar: String? = null)

options.name: count
options.description: The number of selected items. The bar is shown while it is above 0 and takes no room at 0.

options.name: onClear
options.description: Empties the selection.

options.name: totalCount
options.description: The number of items that could be selected, for "3 of 120 selected".

options.name: actions
options.description: The actions. A destructive one uses the danger button variant and the strong danger color in the menu.

options.name: maxVisibleActions
options.description: How many actions are buttons; the rest go into a More menu. A negative value counts as 0.

options.name: busy
options.description: Blocks every action, More and Clear selection while the app runs one.

options.name: busyActionId
options.description: The running action shows a progress indicator and is announced as Loading; the other actions, More and Clear selection are disabled.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the count, the Clear selection and More labels, the cleared announcement and the bar's TalkBack name.

options.name: accessories
options.description: Extra controls after the actions, such as a picker for a property.

states.name: closed
states.description: Nothing is selected: nothing is drawn and the bar takes no room; only an empty live region stays.

states.name: open
states.description: The count, the action buttons, More and Clear selection on a raised surface.

states.name: busy
states.description: With busyActionId the action shows progress and the others are disabled; with busy every control is disabled.

states.name: narrow
states.description: When one line does not fit, the controls wrap onto further lines in reading order.

appearance: A raised surface (the raised background role) with the large radius, a subtle border and a small shadow. The count is label text in the default text role; actions are small secondary MonarchButtons, destructive ones the danger variant, and Clear selection a ghost button. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The parity map named a contextual TopAppBar or BottomAppBar. Both have a fixed height that cuts the count and the actions at large font sizes and hold only icons well, so the bar is a raised Surface with a FlowRow of MonarchButtons that the app places as the bottomBar of a Scaffold or inline above a list. The web toolbar has one tab stop with arrow keys; on Android each control is its own TalkBack element and keyboard stop. The web can wait on a promise returned by an action; here the app sets busyActionId or busy. The web placement option (sticky) is the app's placement. Confirmation of destructive actions stays in the app (AlertDialog). iOS uses the same name; isDestructive and isDisabled are destructive and enabled on Android, following Compose naming, and the icon is a slot because Monarch bundles no icons.
accessibility: The controls are a traversal group named "Bulk actions"; the count is read first, then each action, More and Clear selection.
Every change of the count is announced through a polite live region ("2 of 4 selected"), including when the bar first appears, and "Selection cleared" when the count returns to 0.
Icons are decorative; every action has a visible title.
Every button has a 48dp touch target; the running action is announced as Loading through MonarchButton, and blocked controls are announced as disabled.
edgeCases: maxVisibleActions of 0 puts every action in the More menu; a negative value counts as 0.
An action that empties the selection closes the bar and announces "Selection cleared".
The count uses plurals in strings_bulkactionbar.xml; pass labels.selected to write it differently.

whenToUse: When a bulk action deletes or changes many records at once and cannot be undone: delete selected leads, remove members, purge files.
whenNotToUse: For one item, use a confirm dialog. For an action that can be undone, run it at once and offer Undo in a snackbar. For a reversible archive, use MonarchBulkActionBar alone.

states.description: The title with the count, a sample of three names and "+34 more", the consequences, a field asking for the count, and a danger button disabled until the count matches.

states.name: running
states.description: A linear MonarchProgress with "12 of 37 deleted"; the sheet cannot be swiped or dismissed.

states.name: done
states.description: A success banner when every item was deleted, announced politely.

states.name: partial

appearance: A Material 3 bottom sheet in the colors Monarch maps to the scheme, holding Monarch parts: a heading, body text, MonarchConsequenceList, MonarchTypeToConfirmInput, a danger MonarchButton, a linear MonarchProgress and a success or warning MonarchBanner. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web BulkDestructiveFlow is a component built on WizardDialog with plural rules, a typeCountAbove threshold, an optional step-up authentication and a retry step. On Android it composes existing parts in a MonarchBottomSheet, so the app decides the threshold for typing the count, writes plural forms with plurals resources, and runs re-authentication (for example BiometricPrompt, which needs androidx.biometric in the app) before the deletion. The web's progress callback is the app's own loop updating a counter. The sheet is locked with dismissible = false while it runs. iOS uses the same recipe with a sheet.
accessibility: The title is a heading; MonarchConsequenceList reads each consequence with its kind.
MonarchTypeToConfirmInput announces when the typed count matches, and the delete button stays disabled until it does.
MonarchProgress exposes its range and value, so TalkBack can follow "12 of 37 deleted".
The result banner is a polite live region, so the result is announced when the run ends without moving focus.
edgeCases: Lock the sheet with dismissible = false while the deletion runs, so it cannot be dismissed half way.
Keep the failed items selected after Done so the person can retry or inspect them.
If nothing could be deleted (the request failed), show the error in the confirm phase and keep the typed count.

name: MonarchBurndownChart
title: BurndownChart
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.Canvas with the MonarchLineChart core (drawMonarchLineChart for the grid, axis, remaining and dashed ideal lines and the crosshair) plus a step Path for the scope, change dots and labels and a dashed today marker; pointerInput tap and horizontal drag gestures; inside MonarchChartFrame with MonarchChartLegend and MonarchChartTable
summary: A sprint burndown: work remaining each day against the ideal line, with the scope as a step line and its changes, a today marker and a sentence saying whether the sprint is ahead or behind.
whenToUse: For a time-boxed iteration with an estimate of the work left per day, to show whether it will finish on time, with scope changes next to progress so a flat stretch is explained.
whenNotToUse: For open-ended work without a fixed end, use MonarchLineChart of throughput or a stacked MonarchAreaChart for cumulative flow. To compare several sprints, use MonarchBarChart of the work completed per sprint.
api: @Composable fun MonarchBurndownChart(title: String, points: List<MonarchBurndownChartPoint>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, description: String? = null, summary: String? = null, idealStart: Double? = null, todayIndex: Int? = null, showToday: Boolean = true, showScope: Boolean = true, status: MonarchChartFrameStatus = MonarchChartFrameStatus.Ready, hiddenLines: Set<MonarchBurndownChartLine>? = null, onHiddenLinesChange: ((Set<MonarchBurndownChartLine>) -> Unit)? = null, activeIndex: Int? = null, onActiveIndexChange: ((Int?) -> Unit)? = null, tableToggle: Boolean = true, emptyMessage: String? = null, footer: String? = null, height: Dp? = null, labels: MonarchBurndownChartLabels = MonarchBurndownChartLabels(), formatDate: ((Long) -> String)? = null, formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = null, onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null, onSelect: ((Int) -> Unit)? = null)

class MonarchBurndownChartPoint { constructor(label: String, remaining: Double? = null, scope: Double? = null); constructor(date: Long, remaining: Double? = null, scope: Double? = null); val label: String?; val date: Long?; val remaining: Double?; val scope: Double? }
enum class MonarchBurndownChartLine { Remaining, Ideal, Scope }

class MonarchBurndownChartLabels(remaining: String? = null, ideal: String? = null, scope: String? = null, day: String? = null, today: String? = null, scopeChange: String? = null, change: ((amount: String, added: Boolean) -> String)? = null, status: ((day: String, remaining: String, ideal: String) -> String)? = null, ahead: ((amount: String) -> String)? = null, behind: ((amount: String) -> String)? = null, onTrack: String? = null, scopeSummary: ((scope: String, added: String, removed: String) -> String)? = null, notStarted: String? = null, details: String? = null, clearSelection: String? = null, frame: MonarchChartFrameLabels = MonarchChartFrameLabels())

options.name: title
options.description: The chart's name: the frame heading and the plot's spoken name.

options.name: points
options.description: One point per sprint day, in order, including days not reached yet (no remaining), each with a label or a date (epoch milliseconds, UTC), the work left and the scope.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the frame.

options.name: description
options.description: One line under the title. Default: the generated summary, such as "Thu: 31 remaining, ideal 16, 15 behind ideal. Scope 43, 5 added and 2 removed since the start".

options.name: summary
options.description: Replaces the generated spoken summary of the plot.

options.name: idealStart
options.description: The work at the start of the ideal line. Default: the first day's scope, else its work left. The ideal reaches zero on the last day.

options.name: todayIndex
options.description: The day of the today marker. Default: the latest day with work left, when later days exist. An index outside the days draws no marker.

options.name: showToday
options.description: Whether the today marker is drawn at all.

options.name: showScope
options.description: Whether the scope line, its changes and the scope columns are shown, when any day has a scope.

options.name: status
options.description: Ready, loading, empty or error, drawn by the frame. Ready with no points is empty.

options.name: hiddenLines
options.description: The hidden lines. null lets the chart keep its own set, changed by the legend, which keeps one line visible.

options.name: onHiddenLinesChange
options.description: Called with the new hidden set when the legend changes it.

options.name: activeIndex
options.description: The inspected day, used when onActiveIndexChange is set, to share a crosshair between charts.

options.name: onActiveIndexChange
options.description: Makes the inspection controlled: called with the inspected day, or null when cleared.

options.name: tableToggle
options.description: Whether "View as table" is offered.

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: The empty-state message.

options.name: footer
options.description: Notes under the chart.

options.name: height
options.description: The plot height, kept in every status; 240dp by default.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including the frame's.

options.name: formatDate
options.description: Writes a dated day. Default: the abbreviated month and day in the current locale, in UTC.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes a value, such as "24 pts", everywhere the chart writes one, the axis included. Default: a number in the current locale, compact on the axis.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Try again in the error status.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Drill-in, such as the issues closed that day: called with the day's index from Details or from its TalkBack action.

states.name: in progress
states.description: The remaining line stops at the latest day with data; the dashed today marker stands on that day; the summary says how far ahead or behind the ideal it is.

states.name: ahead, behind, on track
states.description: The summary compares the latest work left with the ideal that day, rounded half up to two decimals.

states.name: not started
states.description: No day has work left: the summary says "Not started" and only the ideal and the scope are drawn.

states.name: scope changes
states.description: The scope is a step line; each day it changes has a dot and a "+5" or "−2" label, and the day is read with its scope change.

states.name: inspecting
states.description: After a tap or drag, or with activeIndex: a crosshair, larger dots on the remaining and ideal lines and a row under the plot with the day's values, with Details and Clear.

states.name: line hidden
states.description: Remaining, Ideal or Scope can be hidden from the legend; the last visible line stays. Hidden lines stay in the data table.

states.name: loading, empty, error
states.description: Drawn by MonarchChartFrame at the chart's height.

appearance: The work left is the first data color, 2dp; the ideal is the neutral series color (subtle text), dashed; the scope is the second data color as a 1dp step line with 3dp change dots. Change labels are the default text color, the today marker a dashed strong border line with a muted label, the crosshair the strong border color; gridlines and axis labels are the line chart's roles. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow the same roles.
platformNotes: Drawn with a Compose Canvas on the MonarchLineChart core (iOS uses Swift Charts, the web SVG); Android has no first-party chart library and Monarch adds none. Days are spaced by position, so left-out days (weekends) make no flat stretch, as on the web and iOS. As on iOS the generated summary is the visible description unless the app gives one; Android also makes it the plot's spoken state and lets summary replace it. A point has a label or a date (epoch milliseconds, UTC) instead of the web's mixed date, number or label. hiddenLines with onHiddenLinesChange and activeIndex with onActiveIndexChange replace the iOS Bindings; showToday and showScope are the iOS showsToday and showsScope. Unlike iOS, Android keeps the inspected day after the finger lifts, shows it in a row under the plot with a polite live region, gives one TalkBack element per day and offers onSelect drill-in (the web's onDaySelect), as MonarchLineChart does. The inspected day gets dots on the remaining and the ideal lines (the web marks only the remaining). The web's valueFormat and formatTick are formatValue; formatX is formatDate for dated days.
accessibility: The frame's title is a heading; the plot is one TalkBack element named by the title (role Image) whose state is the summary: where the sprint stands and how the scope changed.

After the plot come one element per day, in order and mirrored in right to left, read as the day, each shown line's value ("No value" for days not reached) and the scope change: "Wed: Remaining 37, Ideal 24, Scope 45, Scope change +5".
With onSelect each day has a "Details, Wed" TalkBack action; the inspection row's Details and Clear buttons have 48dp targets.
The inspection row is a polite live region, so the values are announced when the inspected day changes.
"View as table" shows each day with remaining, ideal, scope and scope change.
Values are read with formatValue, so TalkBack says "24 pts".
The ideal differs from the other lines by its dash and its name; remaining and scope by their names and line weights, never by color alone.
Legend entries are toggles with 48dp targets; the last visible line cannot be hidden.
edgeCases: Days not reached yet have no work left; the remaining line ends at the latest day with a value and a lone value is a dot.
A gap in the middle of the work left breaks the line.
Without idealStart, a scope or a first work-left value there is no ideal line.
A single day has an ideal equal to its start, drawn in the middle.
Float noise never reads as behind: the difference to the ideal is rounded half up to two decimals.
No day with a scope means no scope line, legend entry or table columns, whatever showScope says.
A ready chart with no points shows the empty state.

whenToUse: For support, SLA or office-hours settings, where a calendar needs a zone, a weekly pattern and dates that replace it.

appearance: A form of sections on the screen's background: Monarch text fields, buttons and menus, a subheading for the holidays, help and notes in the muted text color, errors in the danger strong color and subtle dividers between rows. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow the theme roles.
platformNotes: The web lays the name and dates out in a grid and each exception as one row of inline controls; on a phone each exception is a stacked group (date button, name field, menu, times, remove), the phone's form layout. Dates are epoch milliseconds of UTC midnight from the Material 3 DatePickerDialog, not ISO strings; weekdays are ISO 1 to 7 as in MonarchWeeklyHoursEditor. The web reports errors with each change (onValueChange(value, errors)); here onValueChange takes the value and MonarchBusinessHoursValue.validate gives the errors, so the app calls it when saving. The web's isDefault is default, weekStartsOn is firstDayOfWeek, hourCycle is is24Hour and the validation object is requireName and requireOpen. After a row is removed the web moves focus to the next remove button; Android leaves focus to the system. The time zone picker is MonarchTimezoneSelect, which has no read-only mode, so read-only shows the zone id as text. iOS has no BusinessHoursEditor yet. The parity map lists time-off-panel as a dependency; the editor does not embed MonarchTimeOffPanel, because a calendar's holidays are dates of the calendar, not people's time off; its date dialog follows the same Material 3 pattern.
accessibility: Each date is a labelled field (Date 1, Effective from) whose button reads the chosen date or Choose a date and opens the Material 3 date dialog.
Each row's name, menu and times are labelled with the row's position (Name of date 1, Hours on date 1, Opening time of date 1).
The remove button is named by the date's name (Remove Christmas Day) or position, with a 48dp target.
Errors are text in the danger color, announced through a polite live region.
The holidays heading has heading semantics; Default is a checkbox row read as one control.
edgeCases: A new row has no date and no name; its errors wait until the row is changed or showErrors is set.
A saved time off the step grid stays selectable.
The editor is several screens tall and does not scroll: put it in a scrolling screen.
An exception may hold several intervals in the data; the editor edits the first and keeps the rest.

In the high-contrast themes the same roles resolve to stronger colors.

The web xs size and the brand variant are not offered on touch platforms. Disabled is the variant at half opacity, like the web. A loading button keeps its size: the spinner replaces the leading icon, or is drawn over the label when there is none.
