The touch target is at least 48dp by 48dp at every size and reserves that space in the layout.
While loading it keeps its place in the focus order, ignores taps and announces Loading, or loadingLabel, as its state.
A disabled button is announced as disabled.
The label wraps and the button grows instead of being cut off at large font sizes.
Draws the focus ring around the visible button for keyboard and switch navigation.
Icons are at the start and end and follow the layout direction.
edgeCases: A long label wraps and the button grows in height.
loading does not change the size of the button.

name: MonarchButtonGroup
title: ButtonGroup

summary: Related buttons shown as one control: joined into one shape with square inner corners, or kept apart with a small gap, with one variant and size for all of them.
whenToUse: For two to five closely related actions that belong together, such as Previous and Next, Day, Week and Month, or zoom in and out.
whenNotToUse: For one choice out of several that stays selected use segmented buttons (SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow) or MonarchRadioRow. For options that stay on or off use the toggles in ToggleButton. For a single action use MonarchButton.

options.description: The modifier of the group.

options.name: orientation
options.description: A row or a column (androidx.compose.foundation.gestures.Orientation).

options.name: variant
options.description: Primary, Secondary, Ghost or Danger, for every button.

options.name: size
options.description: Sm, Md or Lg: the visible height of every button in a row. In a column every button is at least 48dp high.

options.name: attached

options.name: fullWidth

options.name: label
options.description: What the buttons have in common, read by TalkBack. Already localised.

options.name: content
options.description: Declares the buttons in order with button(text, onClick, enabled, leadingIcon) and iconButton(contentDescription, onClick, enabled, icon).

states.name: resting
states.description: One shape with rounded outer corners. Secondary buttons share one 1dp border between neighbours; the other variants are separated by a 1dp gap.

states.name: pressed
states.description: Only the pressed button shows the Material ripple.

states.name: disabled
states.description: A button declared with enabled = false takes the disabled fill and text color of its variant and ignores taps; the others are unchanged.

states.name: focused
states.description: The focused button draws the Monarch focus ring around its own shape.

states.name: not attached
states.description: Each button is drawn alone with full corners and an 8dp gap.

appearance: Every button uses the colors of its MonarchButton variant: accent solid for Primary, the surface with the default border for Secondary, no fill for Ghost and danger solid for Danger, with the disabled roles when disabled. The outer corners are 8dp. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web group joins any child and lets each child keep its own variant; here, as on iOS, the group sets one variant and size for all its buttons. A Compose container cannot restyle a MonarchButton passed to it, so the buttons are declared through MonarchButtonGroupScope (as items are declared in a LazyColumn) and drawn by the group with Material 3 Buttons and the MonarchButton tokens. Material 3 1.4 has a ButtonGroup and connected button shapes only as experimental expressive APIs, so they are not used. In a row each button is drawn at its size inside a 48dp touch target, and all buttons take the height of the tallest one, found from their intrinsic heights. In a column every button is at least 48dp high because the buttons touch.
accessibility: The group is a traversal group, and with a label its content description is the label, so TalkBack reads it before the buttons.
Every button stays its own element with the Button role, its own click action and its own enabled state.
An icon button is named by its contentDescription; its icon is given a null description.
Every button reserves a touch target of at least 48dp by 48dp, in a row and in a column.
Labels wrap instead of being cut off at font scale 2.0, and the other buttons in the row grow to the same height.
The first button is at the start in both layout directions, and the rounded corners follow it.
A focused button draws the Monarch focus ring.
edgeCases: One button gives a single shape with all corners rounded. A group with no buttons draws nothing.
With fullWidth in a row, a long label wraps inside its equal share of the width.
Attached secondary buttons overlap by 1dp so that neighbours share one border line.
The label is optional; without one the buttons are read without a group name.

name: MonarchCalendarHeatmap
title: CalendarHeatmap
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout (Row, Column, BoxWithConstraints) with Modifier.drawBehind and Modifier.horizontalScroll, inside MonarchChartFrame with MonarchHeatmap's scale and legend
summary: Values by day on a calendar grid, a contribution-style year or a month calendar with day numbers, binned into four color steps with a Less to More legend, today, notes, non-working days, markers, tap inspection, drill-in and the days as a table.
whenToUse: To show a daily measure over weeks or months where the weekday and the season matter, such as commits, hours worked or check-ins.
whenNotToUse: For a matrix whose rows and columns are not days use MonarchHeatmap. For a trend over time use MonarchLineChart or MonarchSparkline. To pick a date use the Material 3 DatePicker.

enum class MonarchCalendarHeatmapLayout { Year, Month }

options.name: days
options.description: One entry per day with something to show: a date (epoch milliseconds, UTC), a value (null for no data), and optional value text, note, non-working flag and marker. Days in the range without an entry are no data; a later entry for the same day wins.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the frame.

options.name: firstDayOfWeek
options.description: The first day of the week as a java.util.Calendar constant (Calendar.MONDAY). null uses the current locale's.

options.name: status
options.description: Ready, Loading, Empty or Error. Ready without an entry in the range shows Empty.

options.name: color
options.description: The data color of the four steps.

options.name: thresholds

options.name: showLegend

options.name: emptyMessage

options.name: labels

states.name: level
states.description: Each day with a value takes one of five fills: the muted background for zero, then the data color mixed in at 25%, 50% and 75%, then the data color itself.

states.name: no data
states.description: A day in the range without a value is empty with a hairline in the subtle border color.

states.name: non-working
states.description: A day marked inactive without a value above zero has the subtle background and a dashed outline, and is read "Non-working day".

states.name: today
states.description: The day of today has a thick outline in the accent color and is read "Today".

states.name: inspected
states.description: After a tap the day has a thick outline in the default text color, is selected for TalkBack, and its date, value and notes are written under the grid in a polite live region.

states.name: marker
states.description: A day with marker has a small dot in the warning color in its top end corner and is read "Marked".

states.name: month values
states.description: In the month layout a day at least 44dp wide writes its value text, its value or its note under its number; on the two strongest steps the text sits on a surface chip.

states.name: table
states.description: "View as table" lists every day with an entry: date, value and, when any day has one, note.

states.name: loading, empty, error
states.description: The frame's skeleton, empty state and error with Try again, at the chart's height.

appearance: Steps mix the chosen data color into the muted background, as MonarchHeatmap does; non-working days use the subtle background, outlines the subtle and default border colors, today the accent color, the inspected day the default text color and markers the warning color. Weekday and month names are in the muted text color. Every color is a theme role, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes are covered.
platformNotes: The web draws an SVG that shrinks a year to fit the width; on Android, as on iOS, the year keeps 14dp days and scrolls sideways on a phone, opening at the latest week. Days are epoch milliseconds in UTC compared as whole days (minSdk 24 has no java.time without desugaring), and date, weekday and month names come from android.icu in the current locale; the web takes ISO date strings and weekStartsOn, which is firstDayOfWeek here (iOS uses the environment's Calendar). The inspected day is internal state, not a controlled activeDate. There is no keyboard navigation (arrows, Page Up/Down) and no floating tooltip: the inspected day is written under the grid. Android has no chart descriptor like iOS's AXChartDescriptor (Audio Graphs) and no adjustable element: in both layouts every day is its own TalkBack element, in date order. Non-working days and markers are also read as words ("Non-working day", "Marked"), which the web leaves to the note.
accessibility: The grid is a traversal group whose content description is the generated summary ("8 days from Thu, Jan 1, 2026 to Thu, Jan 8, 2026. Total 28. Highest: Tue, Jan 6, 2026: 12 commits") or summary.

Every day in the range is one TalkBack element in date order, read as its date and its value or No data, followed by its note, Non-working day, Marked and Today as they apply; weekday and month names are hidden.
The inspected day carries the selected state.
With onSelect each day has a TalkBack custom action "Select"; days have no click action, because year days are 14dp, far below the 48dp target, and a tap on them is a convenience.
The inspection line under the grid is a polite live region, so a newly inspected day is announced.
The legend is one element read as its name and the range of every step.
Zero, no data, non-working days, today and markers differ by fill, outline and dot, and are also in the spoken text and the table, not color alone.
Weeks are laid out from the start edge, so they mirror right to left.
edgeCases: A range that ends before it starts, no entries and no range, or no entry inside the range shows the empty state.
Entries outside from..to are ignored.
Any time of a UTC day counts as that day; the device's time zone does not shift days.
In the year layout days are 14dp; the tap is a convenience and TalkBack uses the Select action.
At the largest font size weekday names may overlap the empty rows between them, month names are skipped when they would overlap, and month days grow taller.
Tap inspection, the horizontal scroll and TalkBack were checked with Robolectric tests, not on a device with TalkBack; the dates, model, styles, text and summary are unit-tested.

name: MonarchCalendarMonthView
title: CalendarMonthView
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.pager.HorizontalPager with a grid of androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row and Column, androidx.compose.foundation.selection.selectable, CollectionInfo and CollectionItemInfo semantics, androidx.compose.foundation.gestures.detectDragGesturesAfterLongPress, MonarchEventChip, android.icu.text.DateFormat
summary: A month of days with their events: weekday headers, today, the selected day and the neighbouring months' days marked, a swipe between months, dots or titles per day, and the selected day's events listed under the grid, where they can be opened and dragged to another day.
whenToUse: The month view of a calendar (bookings, interviews, releases, shifts), above or beside the day's events. Put a MonarchCalendarToolbar above it for Today, previous, next and the month title.
whenNotToUse: When times and overlaps matter, use a time grid. To pick one date in a form, use the Material 3 DatePicker or MonarchMiniMonth. For a long list of upcoming events, use MonarchAgendaList.

options.name: month
options.description: Any day of the month shown, as epoch milliseconds (UTC). Swiping calls onMonthChange; changing it moves the pager, animated unless animations are off.

options.name: events
options.description: The events in any order, the same type MonarchAgendaList takes. A longer event is shown on every day it touches.

options.name: onMonthChange
options.description: Called with the first day (UTC midnight) of the month the person swipes to. Store it in month.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the view.

options.name: selectedDay
options.description: The day whose events are listed under the grid, or null for no list. Also marked selected in the grid.

options.name: onDayClick
options.description: Called with the UTC midnight of the day the person taps. Without it the days are not buttons.

options.name: onEventClick
options.description: Opens an event of the selected day's list, for example in a MonarchEventPopover inside a ModalBottomSheet. Without it the events are labels.

options.name: onEventMove
options.description: Called with the event and the number of days to move it (negative is earlier) when the person drags an event of the selected day's list onto a day of the grid, or uses a TalkBack move action. Without it events cannot be moved.

options.name: today
options.description: Today's date. null is today in timeZone.

options.name: timeZone
options.description: The zone events are placed on days and their times shown in. An IANA id such as Europe/Berlin; null, or an id the device does not know, is the device's zone.

options.name: firstDayOfWeek
options.description: The first column, Calendar.SUNDAY to Calendar.SATURDAY. null follows the locale's calendar.

options.name: fixedWeeks
options.description: Always six week rows, so the height does not jump between months.

options.name: maxEvents
options.description: The events a wide day lists before "+N more"; with more, one fewer is listed so the overflow line takes the last place. At least 1.

options.name: dayState
options.description: Hatching and a short badge for a day, such as time off or a holiday.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

states.name: narrow days
states.description: Under 80dp per day (phones), a day shows its number and up to three dots in the event colors (hollow for tentative, cancelled and declined, grey for cancelled and declined) and "+N" for the rest.

states.name: wide days
states.description: From 80dp per day (tablets), a day lists up to maxEvents events as dot chips with their start time and title, and "+N more" when there are more.

states.name: today
states.description: The number sits in an accent ring with strong accent text and semibold weight, and TalkBack adds "Today".

states.name: selected
states.description: The number sits on a solid accent circle; the day is selected for TalkBack, and its events are listed under the grid with a heading.

states.name: outside days
states.description: Days of the neighbouring months are on the subtle fill with subtle text; the first of each month shows the month's short name ("Dec 1").

states.name: hatched and badge
states.description: dayState draws diagonal lines over the day and writes its badge under the number; the badge is read with the day.

states.name: empty day
states.description: The selected day's list says "No events".

states.name: dragging
states.description: After a long press an event of the list follows the finger with a shadow and a haptic tick; the day under it gets an accent outline; letting go on another day calls onEventMove.

states.name: narrow screen
states.description: Under 336dp the month scrolls sideways so every day keeps its 48dp target.

appearance: Days sit in a grid of subtle border lines; neighbouring months' days are on the subtle fill. Today's number has an accent ring and strong accent text, the selected day's number a solid accent circle with on-solid text, dots and chips use each event's color (the accent when unspecified) and the strong border color for cancelled and declined events, hatching uses the default border color, and badges and "+N" the muted text color, in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web CalendarMonthView is a role="grid" with arrow-key movement, clickable chips in every cell and a "+N more" popover; below 36rem it shows dots that open the day's list. On Android a phone gets the pattern people know from calendar apps: a swipeable month (HorizontalPager) whose days are single 48dp buttons with dots, and the selected day's events listed under the grid, which replaces both the per-cell chips and the overflow popover; wide windows list titles in each day but still open events from the list. TalkBack reads the month as a grid through CollectionInfo, so arrow keys and the keyboard focus stop of the web are not reimplemented. Moving events by dragging is Android only (the web has no drag): a long press on an event of the list lifts it, with a system haptic, and dropping it on a day calls onEventMove with the number of days; TalkBack and switch users get the same through custom actions. Month navigation stays with the app, as on the web: month plus onMonthChange. Days are UTC-midnight epoch milliseconds, as in the Material 3 DatePickerState, and the event type is MonarchAgendaEvent, so one list feeds both the agenda and the month; the web's renderEvent and per-chip href have no equivalent. The first day of the week follows the locale's calendar and times the person's 12- or 24-hour setting. iOS has not built this entry yet.
accessibility: The month is a TalkBack grid (CollectionInfo of the week rows plus the header row, seven columns); each weekday header is read by its full name.
Each day is one element read as "Wednesday, November 4, 2026, 5 events", then "Today" and its badge when they apply; the visible number, dots and titles are not read separately.
With onDayClick each day is a button with a 48dp target reserved in the layout, and the selected day is selected; without it the days are not actionable.
Under 336dp the month scrolls sideways instead of shrinking days below 48dp.
The selected day's heading is a heading and a polite live region, so changing the selected day announces its date.
Each event of the list is a MonarchEventChip read as "title, time, status, detail" with the time spoken as "9:00 AM to 9:15 AM" or "until 2:00 AM".
With onEventMove each event of the list has four TalkBack actions: move one day earlier or later, one week earlier or later.
Statuses are never color alone: dots are hollow for tentative, cancelled and declined events, and the list writes the status.
Right to left, the first day of the week is at the right and the grid lines mirror.
edgeCases: Events are placed on days in timeZone: an all-day event's start must be midnight in that zone (with UTC, the UTC midnight the Material 3 date picker returns).
A timed event that ends exactly at midnight does not appear on the next day; an end before the start counts as no end.
A long title in a wide day is cut with an ellipsis at the default font size and wraps from font scale 1.3; the full title is in the day's list.
A drag can only end on a day of the month on screen; drop it outside the grid or on its own day and nothing moves.
Swiping is limited to the years 1900 to 2299.
onEventMove reports days, not a new instant: add them in the event's zone so a move across a daylight-saving change keeps the wall-clock time.

appearance: Today is a secondary MonarchButton, the arrows are icon buttons in the default text color (the disabled text color when off), the title uses the subheading style in the default text color and the switcher is a small secondary button. The menu takes the theme's raised surface. High contrast themes use their stronger borders and text.
platformNotes: The web shows a segmented control for the views; on a phone width four segments next to the navigation do not fit, so Android uses a menu button, as iOS does, and the segmented control stays available as SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow for apps with room. The web's titleAs (heading level) is heading semantics. The web's datePicker slot is part of actions. The web accepts product-defined view ids; this enum has the four built-in views. The web's chevron glyphs are required icon slots because Monarch bundles no icons. iOS builds the same component with the same name.
accessibility: The title has heading semantics and is a polite live region, so TalkBack announces the new range after an arrow is pressed.
The arrows are named for the view's unit ("Previous week", "Next month") and have 48dp touch targets.
The switcher is named "Calendar view" with the current view as its state description; in the menu the current view has the selected state and a radio button.
The busy indicator is named "Loading".
Every control has a touch target of at least 48 by 48dp; at the largest font size the parts wrap instead of being cut.
edgeCases: A long title wraps on its own line instead of pushing the controls off screen.
With views set to one view the switcher is hidden, but that view still names the arrows.
Choosing the view that is already current closes the menu without calling onViewChange.
The title is announced on every change, including the app's own; set it once per move.

appearance: 48dp round controls on the muted background role with the default text role; a device that is off takes the danger solid role, sharing the success solid role and a raised hand the warning solid role, each with its on-solid content. Leave is a danger MonarchButton. Menus are Material 3 menus on the raised background role. High-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colors.
platformNotes: The web toolbar labels toggles by the action ("Mute", "Unmute") with aria-pressed; on Android each toggle keeps one name ("Microphone") and reports "On" or "Off", as on iOS. The web keyboard shortcuts (M, V, S, H, F) and roving arrow-key focus are not offered; a hardware keyboard moves between the controls with Tab. Full screen is left out because a call screen on a phone is already full screen. The extra slot for product controls is left out; place them beside the controls. The web CallIcon glyphs are replaced by the required icon slot, because Monarch bundles no icons. States are hoisted value and callback pairs where iOS takes Bindings.
accessibility: The row is a traversal group named "Call controls".
Microphone, camera, sharing and hand are toggles with their name as content description and "On" or "Off" as state description.
A state change changes the icon slot's glyph as well as the color.
Reactions and More are named by content description; each reaction in the menu is read as "React" and the emoji.
The layout choices are radio items with a selected state; low data is a checkable item.
Every control has a 48dp touch target and the row wraps onto a second line at large font sizes.
edgeCases: With no callbacks the row is empty.
An empty reactions list hides the reactions menu.
More appears only when it has an item; in the minimal form it never appears.
Choosing a layout closes More; toggling low data keeps it open so the change can be seen.
How TalkBack reads the toggles and menus on a device was not checked; the semantics were checked in Robolectric tests.

parityExceptions.reason: The web toolbar is 44px round controls with the Leave button on the same row (about 370px). Android asks every control for a 48dp touch target, and the phone window is 344dp wide, so the six round controls fill the first line and Leave goes on a centred second line. The controls, their order, the states and the Layout and Last action line are the web's.
parityExceptions.convention: Material touch target of 48dp for every control

states.name: reconnecting

states.name: docked and pip

appearance: The tiles are MonarchCallTile on the inverse surface; the header uses the default text color for the title and the muted text color for the timer and head count, with a warning MonarchBadge; notices are MonarchCalloutBanner in the warning and danger tones. Every color is a theme role, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes are covered.
platformNotes: The web's region becomes a traversal group named "Call" when there is no title (with a title the heading names it, so it is not read twice). Video is a composable slot per participant, such as the call SDK's SurfaceView in an AndroidView, instead of a MediaStream and onVideoElement; the app enters picture in picture itself (Activity.enterPictureInPictureMode), so onPictureInPicture only reports the button. The web's 'mini' surface change is onMinimize, as on iOS. The timer is a Text that ticks every second outside any live region, so TalkBack reads it when focused and never announces each second; now pins the time for tests, as in MonarchCallTile. iOS's pinnedID Binding becomes pinnedId with onPinnedIdChange. The web's muted hint mentions keyboard shortcuts; Android says to turn the microphone on. The grid's narrow-screen cap is a width of 480dp (the web's 30rem). It is experimental because it is a product screen built from Monarch primitives that no Rook app has adopted yet.
accessibility: The stage is a traversal group; without a title it is named "Call" (or labels.region).
The title is a heading.
The timer is one element read as "Call duration, 04:12"; it is not a live region.
The head count ("3 in call" or "Waiting for others…") is a polite live region, so a change is announced once.
The reconnecting notice and the muted hint are polite live regions; the error is assertive.
Header buttons are MonarchButton or Material 3 IconButton with a label and a 48dp touch target.
Each tile is MonarchCallTile: one element per person named by their name with speaking, muted, hand raised, screen, status and quality as its state, and Pin and full screen as separate buttons.
edgeCases: A pinned or spotlighted id that is not among the participants is ignored and the grid is shown.
Your own shared screen never takes the spotlight; the speaker is never yourself.
Ids in a given layout without a participant draw nothing.
Many participants make the stage tall; it does not scroll itself, so put it in a scrolling container or give it a height.
Long titles and names wrap; at the largest font sizes tiles grow taller than 16 by 9.
Announcements and the timer were checked with Robolectric semantics tests, not with TalkBack on a device; the layout choice, columns, buttons, head count and duration are unit-tested.

name: MonarchCallStatsPanel
title: CallStatsPanel
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column with MonarchDescriptionList (Inline) and MonarchStatusBadge per person; presented by the app in MonarchBottomSheet
summary: The data a call has used and each person's round trip, packet loss and connection grade.
whenToUse: In a call's "Connection" sheet or pane, opened from the call controls, when people need to see why audio or video is poor.
whenNotToUse: For a single indicator of call quality in the call view, use a MonarchStatusBadge or MonarchAudioLevelMeter; for analytics over many calls, a chart or a table.
api: @Composable fun MonarchCallStatsPanel(usage: MonarchCallStatsPanelUsage, peers: List<MonarchCallStatsPanelPeer>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, lowData: Boolean = false, footnote: String? = null, labels: MonarchCallStatsPanelLabels = MonarchCallStatsPanelLabels())
class MonarchCallStatsPanelUsage(sentBytes: Long, receivedBytes: Long, upBitsPerSecond: Double? = null, downBitsPerSecond: Double? = null)

class MonarchCallStatsPanelPeer(id: String, name: String, roundTripMilliseconds: Double? = null, inboundLossPercent: Double? = null, outboundLossPercent: Double? = null, quality: MonarchCallStatsPanelQuality = MonarchCallStatsPanelQuality.Unknown)
enum class MonarchCallStatsPanelQuality { Good, Fair, Poor, Unknown }

class MonarchCallStatsPanelLabels(dataUsed: String? = null, usageSummary: ((total: String, up: String, down: String) -> String)? = null, lowData: String? = null, connections: String? = null, roundTrip: String? = null, loss: String? = null, noPeers: String? = null, notMeasured: String? = null, qualityNames: Map<MonarchCallStatsPanelQuality, String> = emptyMap())

options.name: usage
options.description: Bytes sent and received, and the current upload and download rates in bits per second.

options.name: peers
options.description: One entry per remote person: name, round trip in milliseconds, inbound and outbound loss in percent, and a grade.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the panel.

options.name: lowData
options.description: Adds the note "Low data mode is on: audio only.".

options.name: footnote
options.description: A closing note, such as how media is routed or protected. App copy: Monarch does not know how the app connects calls.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the heading, the usage line, the low data note, the list name, Round trip, Loss, the no-peers text, "Not measured yet" and the grade names.

states.name: default
states.description: The heading and the usage line, then one block per person: the name with a grade badge, then Round trip and Loss rows.

states.name: low data
states.description: A muted note under the usage line.

states.name: not measured
states.description: A missing number shows a dash; an unknown grade is a neutral badge "Not measured yet".

states.name: no peers
states.description: "No one else is connected yet." instead of the people.

appearance: The heading is subheading text; the usage line, notes and footnote muted caption text; names body strong text. Grades are small subtle status badges: Good in the success tone, Fair in the warning tone, Poor in the danger tone, Unknown neutral. Rows are an inline description list. Every color is a theme role, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes are covered.
platformNotes: The web shows a table with a column per number and signal bars for the grade; on a phone a four-column table does not fit at large text sizes, so, as on iOS, each person is a block with description list rows and the grade is a MonarchStatusBadge. The parity map named LazyColumn rows in a MonarchBottomSheet: the panel is the sheet's content, not the sheet, because the sheet's state, detents and dismissal belong to the app (see the example and the catalogue page); it is a Column so it also fits a pane or a scrolling sheet. Bytes use powers of 1,024 and rates powers of 1,000, written in the current locale with halves rounded up, as the web's formatCallBytes and formatCallRate do; those helpers are not public API. Loss uses the locale's percent format. iOS uses the same names; isLowData is lowData in Kotlin style.
accessibility: "Data used this call" is a heading; the usage line is plain text.
The people are a traversal group named "Connection to each person".
Each person is one element read as the name, the round trip, the loss and the grade, such as "Alex Chen, Round trip 186 ms, Loss 3.4%, Unstable connection".
A number that was not measured is read as "Not measured yet", not as the dash shown.
The grade is a badge with its name, so it is not told by color alone.
Text wraps and scales with the font size; long names wrap.
edgeCases: Loss shows the worse of the two directions; a direction that is missing or not finite is ignored.
Negative or non-finite rates count as 0 bps; negative byte counts as 0.
The round trip is rounded to whole milliseconds; loss has one decimal.
Rates of 10 Mbps and more have no decimal.
The panel holds no timer: pass new numbers as statistics arrive, every second or two.

name: MonarchCallTile
title: CallTile
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Box with overlays, androidx.compose.animation.AnimatedVisibility for reactions, androidx.compose.material3.IconButton or MonarchButton for actions, MonarchAvatar
summary: One participant in a call: their video or avatar, name, muted microphone, raised hand, status, connection quality and floating reactions, with Pin and full-screen buttons.
whenToUse: In the grid, the filmstrip or the main spot of a video call, one tile per participant, fed by the app's call SDK.
whenNotToUse: Not for a shared screen with zoom and pan; use MonarchScreenShareView. Not for the call's own controls; use buttons in the call screen's bar.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchCallTile(name: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, statusTone: MonarchTone = MonarchTone.Neutral, size: MonarchCallTileSize = MonarchCallTileSize.Md, self: Boolean = false, micOff: Boolean = false, speaking: Boolean = false, handRaised: Boolean = false, screen: Boolean = false, pinned: Boolean = false, showVideo: Boolean = true, status: String? = null, quality: MonarchCallQuality? = null, reaction: MonarchCallReaction? = null, now: Long? = null, image: Painter? = null, onPinnedChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, onFullScreen: (() -> Unit)? = null, icons: MonarchCallTileIcons = MonarchCallTileIcons(), labels: MonarchCallTileLabels = MonarchCallTileLabels(), video: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null)
public enum class MonarchCallTileSize { Sm, Md, Lg }
public enum class MonarchCallQuality { Good, Fair, Poor }
public class MonarchCallReaction(emoji: String, sentAt: Long)

public class MonarchCallTileIcons(micOff: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, screen: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, handRaised: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, pin: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, unpin: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, fullScreen: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null)

public class MonarchCallTileLabels(you: ((String) -> String)? = null, muted: String? = null, sharingScreen: String? = null, handRaised: String? = null, speaking: String? = null, pin: ((String) -> String)? = null, unpin: ((String) -> String)? = null, fullScreen: ((String) -> String)? = null, pinButton: String? = null, unpinButton: String? = null, fullScreenButton: String? = null, reacted: ((name: String, emoji: String) -> String)? = null, quality: ((MonarchCallQuality) -> String)? = null)

options.name: name
options.description: The participant's display name. Names the tile and its buttons.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the tile. Give it a width; the height is at least 9/16 of it.

options.name: statusTone
options.description: The color of the status text.

options.name: size
options.description: Sm for the filmstrip (32dp avatar, no buttons), Md for the grid, Lg for the main spot.

options.name: self
options.description: This is the person using the app: "(you)" is added to the name.

options.name: micOff
options.description: The microphone is off: the muted mark in the name bar.

options.name: speaking
options.description: The participant is speaking: a 2dp accent border, and "Speaking" is read.

options.name: handRaised
options.description: A raised-hand badge at the top start corner.

options.name: screen
options.description: The video is a shared screen: the screen mark in the name bar.

options.name: pinned
options.description: Pinned to the main spot: the Pin button becomes Unpin and is marked selected.

options.name: showVideo
options.description: Shows the video slot. Pass false while connecting or when the camera is off.

options.name: status
options.description: A short status in the name bar, "Reconnecting…" or "Presenting".

options.name: quality
options.description: Three connection bars; null when unknown.

options.name: reaction
options.description: A reaction that rises over the tile for three seconds from sentAt.

options.name: now
options.description: The current time in epoch milliseconds, for tests. null reads the clock when a reaction arrives and when it ends.

options.name: image
options.description: The participant's picture for the avatar, loaded by the app. null shows initials.

options.name: onPinnedChange
options.description: Shows the Pin button, called with the next pinned state.

options.name: onFullScreen
options.description: Shows the full-screen button. The app presents the participant full screen.

options.name: icons
options.description: Icons for the muted, screen, hand, Pin and full-screen marks. Without an icon the word is written instead.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

options.name: video
options.description: The participant's video from the app's call SDK, filling the tile. Without it the avatar is shown.

states.name: avatar
states.description: Without video the avatar is centered on the emphasis background.

states.name: video
states.description: The slot fills the tile behind the overlays.

states.name: speaking
states.description: A 2dp border in the accent solid color.

states.name: muted
states.description: A crossed-out microphone icon or the word "Muted" in the name bar, in the danger color for the inverse surface.

states.name: hand raised
states.description: A solid warning badge with "Hand raised" (and the hand icon when given) at the top start corner.

states.name: pinned
states.description: The Pin button reads "Unpin Ana", shows the unpin icon or "Unpin", and is marked selected.

states.name: reaction
states.description: The emoji fades in and rises over the name bar, stays for three seconds from when it was sent, then fades. With animations removed it appears and disappears at once.

states.name: poor connection
states.description: One lit bar of three, in the danger solid color, and the spoken "Poor connection".

appearance: The tile on the emphasis background with 16dp corners; the name bar on the inverse surface with inverse text; status text in the tone's strong inverse color; icon buttons on the inverse surface, text buttons as small secondary MonarchButtons; the hand badge in the warning solid color; the speaking border in the accent solid color; lit connection bars in the success, warning or danger solid color. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web tile takes a MediaStream, mirrors your own camera and calls the Fullscreen API. On Android, as on iOS, the video is a slot for the call SDK's renderer (a SurfaceView or TextureView in an AndroidView, or the SDK's composable); mirroring is the renderer's job (for example setMirror on WebRTC's SurfaceViewRenderer) because a SurfaceView ignores Compose transforms, and full screen is the app's presentation through onFullScreen. Pinned is a value with onPinnedChange, as on the web. Reactions carry an epoch-millisecond sentAt; the tile reads the clock only when a reaction arrives and when it ends, and tests pass now. Monarch bundles no icons, so every mark has a written fallback and the icons are optional in MonarchCallTileIcons. The avatar is 40dp at most, the largest MonarchAvatar size, where the web uses its extra-large avatar. Hover-only buttons are always visible on touch screens. The web's "unknown" quality is null. The speaking border uses the accent color like iOS, where the web uses the success color.
accessibility: The tile is a traversal group; its name bar is one element read first, named "Ana (you)", with what is true now as its state: "Speaking, Muted, Hand raised, Sharing screen, Presenting, Poor connection".
Speaking is also a thicker border, muted and the hand are words or icons, and quality is the number of lit bars, so nothing depends on color alone.
Pin and full screen are buttons named "Pin Ana", "Unpin Ana" and "Show Ana full screen", with 48dp touch targets; Pin is marked selected while pinned.
A new reaction is announced through a polite live region as "Ana reacted 👏".
The video, the avatar and the hand badge are hidden from TalkBack; their meaning is in the name bar.
The tile grows taller at large font sizes so the name and status wrap instead of being cut.
edgeCases: A reaction with a sentAt in the future or three seconds or more ago is not shown.
Sending the same emoji again with a new sentAt plays it again.
A long name or status wraps in the name bar and makes the tile taller.
With showVideo false the slot is not composed, so a frozen frame never shows.
In a Row without a width the tile has no 16 by 9 minimum and is as tall as its content.

name: MonarchCalloutBanner
title: CalloutBanner
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row, androidx.compose.material3.Text, androidx.compose.material3.IconButton
summary: A banner for a screen or a section, with a tone, an optional title, one action and a dismiss button; also a compact notice that the view is narrowed.
whenToUse: For account and product messages that concern a whole screen or section: a trial, a maintenance window, a billing problem, a failed sync, or a narrowed scope such as "Showing tickets in Support".
whenNotToUse: For the status of one form or card, use MonarchInlineNotice. For a brief confirmation, use a snackbar through MonarchSnackbarHost. For a decision that blocks the flow, use AlertDialog.
api: @Composable fun MonarchCalloutBanner(message: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, tone: MonarchTone = MonarchTone.Info, variant: MonarchCalloutBannerVariant = MonarchCalloutBannerVariant.Callout, placement: MonarchCalloutBannerPlacement = MonarchCalloutBannerPlacement.Section, title: String? = null, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, action: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, onDismiss: (() -> Unit)? = null, dismissIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, announcement: MonarchBannerAnnouncement = MonarchBannerAnnouncement.None, toneLabel: String? = null, dismissLabel: String? = null)
enum class MonarchCalloutBannerVariant { Callout, Scope }
enum class MonarchCalloutBannerPlacement { Section, Page }

options.name: message
options.description: The message; one or two sentences.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the banner. The banner fills the width it is given.

options.name: tone
options.description: Neutral, Info, Success, Warning or Danger: the colors and the spoken tone name.

options.name: variant
options.description: Callout, or Scope: a compact notice in caption text with the action at the end.

options.name: placement
options.description: Section: rounded, bordered. Page: a full-width strip with square corners and a bottom border.

options.name: title
options.description: A bold first line.

options.name: icon
options.description: An icon at the start in the tone color. Hidden from TalkBack; Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: action
options.description: An action, for example a small MonarchButton. Under the text in the callout, at the end in the scope notice.

options.name: onDismiss
options.description: Adds a dismiss button. The app removes the banner.

options.name: dismissIcon
options.description: The close mark of the dismiss button; without it the button shows its label as text.

options.name: announcement
options.description: None, Polite or Assertive: makes the text a live region.

options.name: toneLabel
options.description: The tone name read first. null uses monarch_calloutbanner_tone_info, _success, _warning or _danger.

options.name: dismissLabel
options.description: Label or TalkBack name of the dismiss button. null uses monarch_calloutbanner_dismiss, "Dismiss".

states.name: callout
states.description: Icon, title, message and an action under the text, with 12dp corners in a section.

states.name: scope
states.description: One compact line in caption text, 8dp corners, the action at the end.

states.name: page
states.description: Square corners and a border only at the bottom.

states.name: dismissible
states.description: A dismiss button at the end, when onDismiss is given. The app removes the banner.

states.name: announced
states.description: With Polite or Assertive the text is a live region.

appearance: The subtle background and border of the tone, with default text and muted message text under a title; the icon takes the strong color of the tone. The neutral banner sits on the subtle background with the default border. The same roles are used in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The banner does not hide itself: the web keeps its own open state when uncontrolled; here the app removes it in onDismiss. One action slot instead of the web's actions slot and actionPlacement option. No accent tone, because MonarchTone has none. The web landmark option has no equivalent; the web live option is the announcement parameter, which reuses MonarchBannerAnnouncement. Monarch bundles no icons: the web and iOS show a default icon per tone, here the app passes the icon, and the dismiss button shows the word Dismiss unless a dismissIcon is given. Insets are the app's: put a page banner under the top app bar or in the content of a Scaffold. The spoken tone name comes from the shared Monarch tone names (Information, Success, Warning, Error, AI), the same words as iOS. Deprecated (D7): the component's own string keys monarch_calloutbanner_tone_info, _success, _warning and _danger are now aliases of the shared names. An app that redefines one still gets its text, but they are removed no earlier than 2027-02-13 (90-day window, two patch releases); override the shared monarch_internal_tone_* names or pass toneLabel instead.
accessibility: The tone name, title and message are one TalkBack element, read in that order, so the tone does not depend on color; toneLabel replaces the tone name.
The neutral tone and the scope variant have no spoken tone name.
The icon is hidden from TalkBack.
The action and the dismiss button are separate buttons with 48dp touch targets; the dismiss button is named "Dismiss" unless dismissLabel says otherwise.
With announcement Polite or Assertive the text is a live region; by default the banner does not announce itself.
The dismiss button is at the end in both layout directions, and the text wraps at the largest font size.
edgeCases: Long titles and messages wrap; the banner grows taller.
A banner that is on the screen from the start should keep announcement None.
In the scope variant a long action label narrows the message; keep it short.

name: MonarchCelebration
title: Celebration
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.Canvas, androidx.compose.animation.core.Animatable, androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
summary: A success moment for a real milestone: an icon in a tinted tile with confetti that falls once, a title, a message and the next actions.
whenToUse: After a milestone the person worked towards: a workspace set up, a domain verified, a first payment received. Inline at the end of a flow, or inside a MonarchDialog or MonarchBottomSheet.
whenNotToUse: For routine confirmations (saved, sent), use a snackbar or MonarchBanner. Not for every step of a flow: one celebration per milestone.
api: @Composable fun MonarchCelebration(title: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, message: String? = null, tone: MonarchTone = MonarchTone.Success, decoration: MonarchCelebrationDecoration = MonarchCelebrationDecoration.Confetti, announces: Boolean = true, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, actions: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null)
enum class MonarchCelebrationDecoration { Confetti, None }

options.name: title
options.description: What was achieved. A heading.

options.name: message
options.description: What it means or what to do next, in muted text.

options.name: tone
options.description: The tile's colors: the tone's subtle fill and strong foreground.

options.name: decoration
options.description: Confetti that falls once behind the icon, or none.

options.name: announces
options.description: Announces the title and message through a polite live region when it appears. Turn it off when it is part of the screen from the start.

options.name: icon
options.description: The icon in the tile, such as a MonarchIcon with a null content description; it takes the tone's strong color. Without it no tile is drawn.

options.name: actions
options.description: The next steps, side by side when they fit and wrapped onto more lines when they do not.

states.name: appearing
states.description: The tile grows from 85% to full size and twelve pieces fall once over about 1.9 seconds, fading in and out.

states.name: settled
states.description: The confetti has faded and the Canvas stops drawing it; only the tile and text remain.

states.name: reduced motion
states.description: With animations removed the tile appears at full size and the pieces rest as a still scatter at 70% opacity.

appearance: Centered text on the surrounding background: the title in the subheading style and the default text role, the message in the muted text role. The tile is a circle in the tone's subtle role with the icon in its strong role; the confetti uses the five data roles. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ships two components: CelebrationPanel (inline) and Celebration (a dialog with a Continue button). On Android one composable covers both: place it inline, or inside a MonarchDialog or MonarchBottomSheet with the Continue button in actions. The web tone accent is not offered because MonarchTone has no accent tone; any MonarchTone works, success by default. The web media slot is the icon slot; the web defaults to a check mark, but Monarch for Android bundles no icons, so without an icon no tile is drawn and the confetti falls on its own. The web heading level becomes the heading semantics on the title. iOS uses the same name and options, with an SF Symbol instead of the icon slot.
accessibility: The title is a heading; the message is read after it.
With announces on, the title and message are announced through a polite live region one frame after it appears.
The tile and the confetti are hidden from TalkBack; everything is said in the text.
The confetti only moves and fades, never flashes, falls once, and is still when animations are removed; the tile's growth is skipped too.
Buttons in actions keep their own 48dp touch targets.
edgeCases: Long titles and messages wrap and stay centered; the panel is at most 448dp wide.
The confetti is drawn with Canvas, which is not mirrored in right-to-left layouts; the scatter has no direction, so it looks the same.
Composing it again under a new key plays the confetti again.

summary: Release notes as a What's new screen: a LazyColumn of entries, newest first, each with its date and version, a heading, tag badges, the notes as MonarchProse and an optional Read more link.
whenToUse: For a What's new screen or sheet in the app, from release notes the app fetches or ships.
whenNotToUse: For a one-off announcement, use a banner or a dialog. For an activity history of a record, use MonarchActivityTimeline.
api: LazyColumn { items(entries, key = { it.id }) { entry -> Column { MonarchText(text = "$date · $version", style = MonarchTextStyle.Caption); MonarchText(text = entry.title, style = MonarchTextStyle.Heading); FlowRow { entry.tags.forEach { MonarchBadge(text = it, tone = …) } }; MonarchProse { paragraph(entry.body) }; entry.href?.let { MonarchLink(text = "Read more", onClick = { uriHandler.openUri(it) }, variant = MonarchLinkVariant.Standalone, external = true) } } } }

options.description: Release notes, newest first: id (the LazyColumn key), date, version, title, tags, body and an optional link.

options.name: date
options.description: The release day in epoch milliseconds, written with java.text.DateFormat in UTC (DateFormat.getDateInstance(DateFormat.LONG, locale) with timeZone = UTC), so a date-only release shows the same day everywhere.

options.name: MonarchBadge.tone
options.description: Neutral for most tags; a status tone only when the tag means that status.

options.name: MonarchProse
options.description: The notes as paragraphs and list items; MonarchAiMarkdown when the notes arrive as Markdown.

options.name: MonarchLink
options.description: Read more, opening the full note through LocalUriHandler; only for a safe http or https link.

states.name: entries
states.description: One entry per release, newest first.

states.name: empty
states.description: A line of muted text, such as "No updates yet.", in place of the list.

appearance: Muted caption text for the date and version, the heading style for titles, badges in their tones, prose in default text and the link color for Read more, in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ChangelogFeed is a public changelog page with a timeline marker, permalinks and an RSS link in the header. In an app it is a What's new screen: a LazyColumn of entries with no timeline line, no permalinks and no RSS link, as the plan says; Read more opens the full note in the browser. Dates are epoch milliseconds formatted in UTC, matching the web's default time zone. The heading and description above the list are the screen's top app bar. iOS shares the recipe approach.
accessibility: Each entry title is a heading (MonarchTextStyle.Heading), so TalkBack users can jump between releases.
Tags are words on badges, not colors.
Read more is a MonarchLink with a 48dp touch target and is read with "opens in the browser".
The list scrolls with the system scroll and keeps its position by entry id.
edgeCases: Long notes wrap; keep each entry's body short and link to the full note.
Use the entry id as the key so the list keeps its position when entries are added at the top.

options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings: View as table, View as chart, Loading chart, No data yet, This chart didn't load., Legend, No value, Show all.

options.name: actions
options.description: Controls at the end of the header, such as a period picker.

options.name: content
options.description: The chart, in a box of the frame's width and height.

states.name: ready
states.description: The chart, the legend and, when there is a table, the "View as table" button; after it, the data table in the chart's place and "View as chart".

states.name: loading
states.description: A MonarchSkeleton of the chart's height, read as "Loading chart" with an indeterminate progress value.

states.name: empty
states.description: MonarchEmptyState with "No data yet" and the empty message.

states.name: error
states.description: MonarchInlineErrorRetry with "This chart didn't load." and Try again when onRetry is set; otherwise the message in the strong danger color as a polite live region.

appearance: A MonarchCard: the surface color with the default border and 12dp corners. The title in the strong body style, the description and footer in the muted caption color, the table header in the label style over a default-border line and rows over subtle-border lines. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ChartFrame is a figure that always renders the data table for screen readers; Android has no hidden-but-readable content and no chart descriptor equivalent of iOS's AXChartDescriptor, so the data reaches TalkBack through "View as table", whose rows are each read as the category and every series with its value. The table view state is kept inside the frame (rememberSaveable), as on iOS; the web's controlled showTable and onShowTableChange are not offered. The web's headingLevel is not offered (Compose has one heading property) and emptyActions is not offered, as on iOS. onLegendToggle becomes hiddenSeries and onHiddenSeriesChange, as on iOS. The table columns share the width equally and text wraps; the web table scrolls sideways instead. Same names as iOS: MonarchChartTable, MonarchChartTableSeries, MonarchChartFrameLabels, MonarchChartFrameStatus; iOS's isTableToggleShown is tableToggle here. The web retry that keeps the button busy until a promise settles is not offered: retrying is the app's status change.
accessibility: The title is a heading.

With a table, "View as table" is a button with a touch target of at least 48dp; the table's header row is one heading element and each row is one element read as the category, then each series and its value, with "No value" for a gap.
The loading skeleton is one element named "Loading chart" with an indeterminate progress value.
The error without retry is a polite live region, so a change to the error status is announced; with onRetry it is MonarchInlineErrorRetry.
Without a table, the chart content keeps its own semantics; give it a description, as MonarchSparkline does.
The title wraps at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: Gaps (null values) show a dash and are read as "No value".
Values without formattedValues are formatted with the locale's number format (android.icu.text.NumberFormat).
Many series make table columns narrow; their text wraps.
Loading and the chart keep exactly the given height; the empty and error states use it as a minimum.
While the status is not Ready the body shows that status; a table view chosen before comes back when the status is Ready again.

name: MonarchChartLegend
title: ChartLegend
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow, androidx.compose.material3.FilterChip, androidx.compose.foundation.Canvas
summary: The names and colors of a chart's series in the theme's data slots, as a plain list or as toggle chips that show and hide each series, with a Show all reset.
whenToUse: Under or beside a chart with two or more series, so each line, bar or area has a visible name. Use the toggle form when people compare series and need to hide some.
whenNotToUse: For a chart with one series, name it in the title instead. For filters that change the data rather than its display, use MonarchTag or segmented buttons.
api: @Composable fun MonarchChartLegend(items: List<MonarchChartLegendItem>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, marker: MonarchChartLegendMarker = MonarchChartLegendMarker.Line, orientation: Orientation = Orientation.Horizontal, enabled: Boolean = true, legendLabel: String? = null)

@Composable fun MonarchChartLegend(items: List<MonarchChartLegendItem>, hiddenSeries: Set<String>, onHiddenSeriesChange: (Set<String>) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, marker: MonarchChartLegendMarker = MonarchChartLegendMarker.Line, orientation: Orientation = Orientation.Horizontal, enabled: Boolean = true, keepOneVisible: Boolean = true, showAllButton: Boolean = true, legendLabel: String? = null, showAllLabel: String? = null, shownLabel: String? = null, hiddenLabel: String? = null)
class MonarchChartLegendItem(key: String, label: String, color: MonarchChartColor? = null, dashed: Boolean = false, value: String? = null)
enum class MonarchChartColor { Data1, Data2, Data3, Data4, Data5, Neutral }
enum class MonarchChartLegendMarker { Line, Square, Dot }

options.name: items
options.description: The entries in series order: key, label, optional palette slot, dashed flag and formatted value.

options.name: hiddenSeries
options.description: The keys of the hidden series. Passing it selects the toggle overload. Keys the legend does not list are kept.

options.name: onHiddenSeriesChange
options.description: Called with the new hidden set after a toggle or Show all.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the legend.

options.name: marker
options.description: Line, Square or Dot; use the shape the chart draws.

options.name: orientation
options.description: Horizontal wraps entries onto new rows; Vertical stacks them with values at the end.

options.name: enabled
options.description: False draws markers and text in the disabled color; toggles ignore taps.

options.name: keepOneVisible
options.description: Toggle overload: the last shown series ignores the tap, so the chart is never blank.

options.name: showAllButton
options.description: Toggle overload: shows Show all while one of the legend's series is hidden.

options.name: legendLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken name "Legend" (monarch_chartlegend_legend).

options.name: showAllLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in button text "Show all" (monarch_chartlegend_show_all).

options.name: shownLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in state "Shown" (monarch_chartlegend_shown).

options.name: hiddenLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in state "Hidden" (monarch_chartlegend_hidden).

states.name: shown
states.description: The marker in the series color and the label in the default text color; a toggle is selected with the state "Shown".

states.name: hidden
states.description: Toggles only: the marker in the disabled text color, the label muted and struck through, the state "Hidden".

states.name: locked
states.description: Toggles only: with keepOneVisible the last shown series ignores the tap.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Markers and text in the disabled text color; toggles do not respond.

appearance: Markers use the theme's data colors data1 to data5 in entry order, then the subtle text color for neutral entries; hidden or disabled markers use the disabled text color. Labels use the default text color, muted when hidden; values the default text color in medium weight. Toggle chips have no fill or border of their own, only the Material pressed ripple. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Material 3 has no legend, so Monarch builds one; toggle entries are Material 3 FilterChips, as the plan asked. The web legend becomes a toolbar with one Tab stop and arrow keys and reports the hovered entry through onActiveChange; on Android each toggle is its own TalkBack element and there is no hover, so neither is offered, as on iOS. The web is controlled or uncontrolled (defaultHiddenSeries); here state is hoisted, a Set<String> where iOS uses a Binding. The web's toggleable flag is the choice of overload. The web messages.entry spoken-name builder is not offered: a toggle is read as its label and value with its state. The web marks the locked entry aria-disabled; here, as on iOS, the tap is ignored. Same names as iOS: MonarchChartLegendItem, MonarchChartColor, MonarchChartLegendMarker; axis is orientation (the Compose Orientation).
accessibility: The legend is a traversal group named "Legend" (or legendLabel).
A plain entry is one element read as its label and its value; the marker is drawn on a Canvas without semantics.
A toggle entry is a Material 3 FilterChip: selected while its series is shown, with the state description "Shown" or "Hidden".
A hidden series is shown by a struck-through, muted label and a grey marker, not by color alone.
Toggle entries and the Show all button have touch targets of at least 48dp and follow the layout direction.
Labels wrap at font scale 2.0 instead of being cut.
edgeCases: From the sixth entry on, entries without a color are neutral; fold extra series into "Other" or split the chart.
Keys in hiddenSeries that the legend does not list stay hidden after Show all, so several legends can share one set.
A locked entry gives no spoken feedback when tapped; this was not checked with TalkBack on a device.
Long labels wrap and the row wraps onto new rows.

summary: Chat that stays one tap away on any screen: a floating action button with the unread count that opens the chat in a bottom sheet. The app supplies the chat.
whenToUse: In an app that offers its team chat (Rook Chat or its own screens) from every screen.
whenNotToUse: For a chat that is the main screen of the app, use the collaboration components in a full screen. For a single conversation thread, use MonarchThreadPanel.

options.name: open
options.description: Whether the chat sheet is shown.

options.name: onOpenChange
options.description: Called with true when the launcher is tapped and false when the sheet is dismissed.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the launcher.

options.name: unread
options.description: Unread messages; 0 shows no badge, more than 99 shows "99+".

options.name: loading
options.description: Shows a spinner and "Loading chat…" in the sheet instead of the content.

options.name: label
options.description: The spoken name of the launcher and the sheet. null uses "Rook Chat".

options.name: loadingLabel
options.description: The text while loading. null uses "Loading chat…".

options.name: icon
options.description: The launcher icon.

options.name: content
options.description: The chat, in the sheet.

states.name: closed
states.description: The launcher with its count badge.

states.name: open
states.description: A bottom sheet with the chat.

states.name: loading
states.description: The sheet shows a spinner and "Loading chat…".

appearance: The launcher is the inverse surface with inverse content, as the web's dark launcher; the badge is the danger solid with its on-solid text. The sheet uses MonarchBottomSheet's roles. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ChatDock embeds the Rook Chat web app in an iframe that stays alive behind the launcher, with a postMessage protocol for unread counts, calls and sessions. On Android the app supplies the chat in the content slot and reports unread and loading itself; the sheet content is composed while the sheet is open and is not kept alive when it closes. Incoming call prompts are not part of this component.
accessibility: The launcher is read as the label and the unread count, such as "Rook Chat, 3 unread"; the badge itself is not read again.
The sheet is a pane named by the label.
While loading, the spinner is read as "Loading chat…".
edgeCases: A negative unread count shows no badge.
Keeping the chat state across opening and closing is the app's job.

name: MonarchCheckboxRow
title: Checkbox
wrapsNative: Modifier.triStateToggleable
summary: The Monarch checkbox: a 16dp box with a 4dp corner, a 1dp input border, the accent fill with a check mark or a dash, inside a 48dp touch target, with an optional label. MonarchCheckboxRow is the labelled row.
whenToUse: An option in a form that is submitted later, or a selection column of a list (without a label).
whenNotToUse: For a setting that takes effect immediately use a switch.
api: @Composable fun MonarchCheckbox(checked: Boolean, onCheckedChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)?, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, invalid: Boolean = false, label: String? = null, description: String? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)

@Composable fun MonarchCheckbox(state: ToggleableState, onClick: (() -> Unit)?, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, invalid: Boolean = false, label: String? = null, description: String? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)
@Composable fun MonarchCheckboxRow(checked: Boolean, onCheckedChange: (Boolean) -> Unit, label: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, description: String? = null)

options.name: checked
options.description: Whether the box is ticked.

options.name: onCheckedChange
options.description: Called with the new value; null draws the box only, for a row that handles the tap itself.

options.name: state
options.description: Off, On or Indeterminate (a dash, read as partially checked).

options.name: invalid
options.description: Draws the danger border.

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label; the whole row toggles and TalkBack reads it with the state.

options.name: description
options.description: Secondary text under the label.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the control.

options.name: enabled
options.description: A disabled control is drawn at half opacity and ignores input.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the press and focus interactions.

states.name: checked
states.description: The control is filled with the strong accent.

states.name: unchecked
states.description: The control is empty.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Disabled control and the disabled text color; announced as disabled.

states.name: focused
states.description: The focus ring around the row.

appearance: A 16dp box, 4dp corners, a 1dp input border and the surface fill. On and partly on: the strong accent fill and border with the on-accent check or dash. Invalid: the danger border. Pressed: the muted fill. Disabled: half opacity. The focus ring (2dp, 2dp away) shows for keyboard and D-pad focus.
platformNotes: Replaces the Material 3 Checkbox (18dp box, 40dp state layer). Same behaviour: toggleable with Role.Checkbox, tri-state support, a 48dp touch target around the 16dp box. Migrating: Checkbox(checked, onCheckedChange) becomes MonarchCheckbox(checked, onCheckedChange); TriStateCheckbox(state, onClick) becomes MonarchCheckbox(state, onClick); drop colors.
accessibility: The row is one TalkBack element with the checkbox role, the label, the description and the checked state.
The whole row is the touch target and is at least 48dp high.
A disabled row is announced as disabled.
The box is at the start and follows the layout direction.
The bare Checkbox needs a name: Modifier.semantics { contentDescription = ... }.
edgeCases: A long label wraps beside the box and the row grows.
Inside the row the Checkbox has no click handler of its own, so there is one target, not two.

name: MonarchCheckboxGroup
title: CheckboxGroup
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.Checkbox, androidx.compose.material3.TriStateCheckbox, Modifier.toggleable, Modifier.triStateToggleable, androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow, MonarchFormField
summary: A labelled set of checkboxes for picking any number of choices, with an optional tri-state Select all.
whenToUse: When people may pick any number of related choices from a short list: notification channels, working days, export columns.
whenNotToUse: For exactly one choice use MonarchRadioCardGroup or radio rows. For a single yes or no use MonarchCheckboxRow. For a long, searchable list use a multi-select picker.
api: @Composable fun <T> MonarchCheckboxGroup(options: List<MonarchCheckboxGroupOption<T>>, value: List<T>, onValueChange: (List<T>) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, orientation: MonarchCheckboxGroupOrientation = MonarchCheckboxGroupOrientation.Vertical, enabled: Boolean = true, required: Boolean = false, invalid: Boolean = false, selectAll: Boolean = false, label: String? = null, helperText: String? = null, errorText: String? = null, selectAllLabel: String? = null)
class MonarchCheckboxGroupOption<out T>(value: T, label: String, description: String? = null, enabled: Boolean = true)
enum class MonarchCheckboxGroupOrientation { Vertical, Horizontal }

options.name: options
options.description: The choices, in order. Each has a value, a label, an optional description and enabled.

options.name: value
options.description: The checked values.

options.name: onValueChange
options.description: Called with every checked value, always in the order of options.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the group. Inside your own MonarchFormField, pass the field's control modifier.

options.name: orientation
options.description: One choice per line, or side by side and wrapping onto further lines.

options.name: enabled
options.description: false disables every choice and Select all.

options.name: required
options.description: Marks the label as required and adds "Required" to the group's name. The group does not enforce a minimum.

options.name: invalid
options.description: Draws the boxes in the danger color. Also on whenever errorText is given.

options.name: selectAll
options.description: Adds a tri-state Select all row above the choices, which are indented under it.

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label and TalkBack name of the group. With a label the group is drawn inside a MonarchFormField.

options.name: helperText
options.description: Help text under the choices. Drawn only with a label.

options.name: errorText
options.description: The error message, shown under the choices and set as the group's error. Drawn only with a label.

options.name: selectAllLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in string monarch_checkboxgroup_select_all, "Select all".

states.name: default
states.description: Each choice is a checkbox row with its label and optional description.

states.name: select all
states.description: Select all is checked when every enabled choice is checked, partly checked when some are, unchecked when none are.

states.name: disabled choice
states.description: The row is drawn in the disabled colors, ignores taps, and keeps its state when Select all is pressed.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Every row and Select all are disabled.

states.name: invalid
states.description: The boxes use the strong danger color and, with a label, the error text is shown under the group.

appearance: Material 3 checkboxes beside body text, with descriptions in muted caption text. An invalid group draws its boxes in the strong danger color with the danger on-strong tick; otherwise the boxes use the accent as in every Material checkbox. The label and the error are those of MonarchFormField. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web group can be controlled or uncontrolled and submits each value under a form name; on Android the value is hoisted and there is no form submission. The web takes the label, description, error and disabled state from a surrounding Field; on Android pass label, helperText and errorText to the group, which draws a MonarchFormField itself, or leave label null and put the group in your own MonarchFormField. The web disabled option is enabled = false on the option, following Compose. The web aria-controls link between Select all and the choices has no TalkBack equivalent. iOS has no entry yet; the names follow the web.
accessibility: Each choice is one row with the Checkbox role, its label as name and its on or off state; the whole row is the target and is at least 48dp high.
Select all is a TriStateCheckbox row whose state is on, off or indeterminate (partly checked).
A disabled choice and a disabled group are reported as disabled and ignore taps.
With a label, the group is named by it (with "Required" when required) and carries the error; a new error is announced by MonarchFormField's polite live region.
An invalid group is shown by the error text, not by color alone.
Labels wrap at the largest font size, also in the horizontal layout.
edgeCases: Values not in options are dropped from the next onValueChange.
With every choice disabled, Select all is disabled.
Values must be unique within the group; two options with the same value are toggled together.

title: ChoiceDialog
wrapsNative: MonarchDialog with MonarchRadioRow rows in a Modifier.selectableGroup() column
summary: Picking one of a few options is a MonarchDialog with a radio list as its content and a confirm action. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: When the person must choose one of two to six options before going on, and each option may need a line of description: the export format, which copy to keep.
whenNotToUse: For more options, or options that are long, use a screen or MonarchBottomSheet with a list. For a choice of actions without a confirm step use MonarchMenu. For a setting that changes at once use radio rows on the screen itself.

The selection is a filled radio, not color alone.
The dialog's title names the choice and is read first.

Keep the current value selected when the dialog edits an existing setting, so Confirm is enabled at once.
