name: MonarchCodeBlock
title: CodeBlock
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.Text with an androidx.compose.ui.text.AnnotatedString per line in androidx.compose.foundation.horizontalScroll, androidx.compose.material3.FilterChip (wrap toggle), MonarchCopyButton
summary: A code sample with a header (title or language), copy, a wrap toggle, optional line numbers, light syntax colouring and a diff mode.
whenToUse: To show code people read or copy: an API request in settings, a configuration snippet in onboarding, a change in a message.
whenNotToUse: For a short token inside a sentence use MonarchInlineCodeStyle. For a single value to copy, such as a URL or key, use MonarchCopyField.
api: @Composable fun MonarchCodeBlock(code: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, language: String? = null, title: String? = null, diff: Boolean? = null, highlighted: Boolean = true, showLineNumbers: Boolean = false, showWrapToggle: Boolean = true, copyable: Boolean = true, wrapped: Boolean? = null, onWrappedChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, onCopy: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchCodeBlockLabels = MonarchCodeBlockLabels())

class MonarchCodeBlockLabels(copy: String? = null, copied: String? = null, copiedAnnouncement: String? = null, wrap: String? = null, added: String? = null, removed: String? = null, codeName: ((title: String?, language: String?) -> String)? = null)

options.name: code
options.description: The code, exactly as it is copied. Tabs are drawn as four spaces and copied as tabs.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the block.

options.name: language
options.description: A language id ("ts", "python", "bash", "diff"). Picks the highlighter and the header text. Highlighted: JavaScript and TypeScript, JSON, Python, shell, CSS and SCSS, HTML, XML and SVG, SQL, Go, Rust. Others are plain text, and an unknown id is shown as given.

options.name: title
options.description: Header text, such as a file name or what the snippet does. Also names the code. null shows the language name.

options.name: diff
options.description: Draws + and - lines as a diff. null means true when language is "diff" or "patch".

options.name: highlighted
options.description: Turns syntax colouring on or off.

options.name: showLineNumbers
options.description: Shows line numbers before the lines. TalkBack does not read them and they are not copied.

options.name: showWrapToggle
options.description: Shows the "Wrap lines" toggle in the header.

options.name: copyable
options.description: Shows the copy button in the header.

options.name: wrapped
options.description: Whether long lines wrap instead of scrolling sideways. null lets the block keep the state itself (saved across configuration changes), starting unwrapped.

options.name: onWrappedChange
options.description: Called with the new state when the user uses the wrap toggle.

options.name: onCopy
options.description: Called with the copied code after each copy.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings: copy, copied, copiedAnnouncement, wrap, added, removed and codeName.

options.name: headerActions
options.description: Extra controls in the header, before the wrap toggle and copy button.

states.name: unwrapped
states.description: Default. Each line stays on one line and the code scrolls sideways inside the block.

states.name: wrapped
states.description: Long lines wrap inside the block; the wrap chip is selected.

states.name: diff
states.description: Added and removed lines get the diff fills and a visible + or − marker; hunk headers use the info strong color; file headers before the first hunk are muted and semibold.

states.name: copied
states.description: The copy button follows MonarchCopyButton: the system confirms on Android 13 and later, earlier versions show "Copied" for two seconds; TalkBack is told "Copied to clipboard" in both.

states.name: no header
states.description: With no title, no language, no wrap toggle and no copy button, the header is not drawn.

appearance: A subtle fill with a subtle border and medium corners; the header has the muted fill and its text in the muted text color. Code uses the code type role of the theme. Keywords use the info strong role, strings success strong, numbers warning strong, tags danger strong, attributes and properties AI strong, and comments the muted text color in italics; diff lines use the AI diff add and remove roles. All are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow the theme.
platformNotes: The tokenizer is ported from the web and gives the same tokens, without the web's incremental mode for streaming code. Kotlin names drop the iOS is/shows prefixes, as Material 3 does: diff, highlighted, showLineNumbers, showWrapToggle, copyable and wrapped (a nullable value with onWrappedChange in place of an optional Binding). labels.codeName receives the title and the language id, as the web label function does. The wrap toggle is a Material 3 FilterChip, the Android form of a text toggle (see toggle-button); the web uses a ghost button with aria-pressed. The web code region is focusable so a keyboard can scroll it; on Android it scrolls by touch and TalkBack reads it line by line. The web has a CodeTabs companion for one sample in several languages; on Android put several MonarchCodeBlock in Material 3 tabs. AiCodeBlock's Apply and Insert are not part of this component.
accessibility: The code region carries the name of the code as its content description: the title, else "<Language> code", else "Code"; it is a traversal group, so its lines are read in order after it.
Each line is one element read as its text; added and removed lines of a diff start with "Added:" or "Removed:"; lines with only white space are skipped.
Line numbers and diff markers are not read, and diff lines carry a visible + or − marker, so a change does not depend on color alone.
The wrap toggle is a Material 3 FilterChip named "Wrap lines", read as selected or not selected.
The copy button is MonarchCopyButton named "Copy" followed by the code's name; after a copy its state is "Copied to clipboard" in a polite live region.
The code reads left to right in right-to-left layouts; the header follows the layout direction.
The header wraps at large font sizes, so the title is never cut, and the toggle and copy button keep a 48dp touch target.
edgeCases: A final line break does not add an empty line; Windows line breaks are treated as line breaks.
Tabs are drawn as four spaces; the copied code keeps its tabs.
Empty code draws one empty line.
An unknown language is plain text, and its id is shown as given in the header and in the name ("toml code").
Every line is composed (not lazily); keep samples to a screenful or two.
The highlighter is not a grammar: unusual code can be coloured imperfectly, never changed.

name: MonarchCodeSnippetTabs
title: CodeSnippetTabs

summary: The same code example in several languages or tools, one tab each, with a copy button, optionally kept on the reader's language across every set that shares a sync key.
whenToUse: In developer documentation or an API settings screen, to show one request in cURL, Kotlin, Swift and other languages.
whenNotToUse: For one snippet use MonarchCodeBlock. For tabs that switch between different content use the Material 3 tab rows (Tabs).

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the tabs and the code.

options.name: label
options.description: The spoken name of the tab row. Built in: Language.

options.name: selection
options.description: The id of the snippet to show, when the app controls it. An id with no snippet falls back to the synced or own choice, then the first snippet.

options.name: onSelectionChange
options.description: Called with the id of the snippet the reader chose.

options.name: syncKey
options.description: Keeps every set with this key on the same language and remembers it in SharedPreferences (file monarch_code_snippet_tabs, key monarch.codeSnippetTabs.<key>).

options.name: showLineNumbers
options.description: Whether the code shows line numbers.

options.name: onCopy
options.description: Called with the copied code after each copy.

options.name: codeBlockLabels

states.name: several snippets

states.name: one snippet
states.description: Only the code block, without tabs.

states.name: no snippets
states.description: Nothing is drawn.

states.name: synced
states.description: Choosing a tab in one set switches every set on screen with the same syncKey that has that snippet, and the choice is restored on the next launch.

appearance: The Material 3 secondary tab row in the theme's Material colors (the selected tab and its line in the accent), over the MonarchCodeBlock surface with its code type. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow the theme.
platformNotes: The web keeps the synced choice in localStorage and notifies the other sets on the page; on Android the choice is snapshot state shared in the process, so every set on screen follows it, and it is written to SharedPreferences, so it survives a restart (iOS uses UserDefaults; DataStore is not a Monarch dependency). The iOS variant parameter (a line or a pill) is not offered: Material 3 has one tab row for this, and SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow does not scroll with many languages. iOS takes a selection binding; Android takes selection with onSelectionChange.
accessibility: The tab row is named Language (or label); each tab has the tab role and the selected state.
The code block is MonarchCodeBlock: named after its title or language, with a copy button that announces the copy.
Tabs have 48dp touch targets, scroll sideways when they do not fit and keep their text whole at font scale 2.0; they mirror in right-to-left layouts.
Code reads left to right in right-to-left layouts, as in MonarchCodeBlock.
edgeCases: A stored choice that a set has no snippet for is ignored by that set, which keeps its own choice.
Two snippets with the same label need distinct ids.
Changing tabs replaces the code block, so its wrap toggle resets.
Nothing is stored without syncKey.

whenToUse: For one block of secondary content that most people do not need: advanced settings, details, the evidence behind a figure.
whenNotToUse: For several sections of a page where one opens at a time use an accordion. For a choice that changes a setting use MonarchSwitchRow.

options.name: onExpandedChange
options.description: Called with the new state when the header is activated.

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label of the header; name the content.

accessibility: The header is one TalkBack element with the button role, the label and the state "Expanded" or "Collapsed".
TalkBack offers the expand action while collapsed and the collapse action while expanded.
A disabled header is announced as disabled and offers neither action.
Hidden content is not in the composition, so TalkBack does not reach it.
The header is at least 48dp high and the whole row responds to touch.
The content appears without animation when the user has turned animations off.
The trailing icon is decoration; give it a null content description.
edgeCases: A long label wraps; the icon stays centered on it.
Content that starts expanded is not animated in.
State inside the content, such as a text field's value, is lost when it closes unless the app holds it.

The selected one has a ring in the default text color and an 8dp surface-coloured mark in the middle. The hex field is a MonarchTextField. Ring and mark take their roles from the theme in every theme; the swatch colors do not change with the theme.
platformNotes: Android has no system color picker, so the custom part is the hex field (the web also has the browser's color input; iOS uses the system ColorPicker and has no hex field). The value is the same lower-case #rrggbb text as on the web and iOS, so a stored color moves between platforms; opacity is not supported. The selection mark is a ring and a dot rather than the web's check glyph, because Monarch for Android bundles no icons. The web's roving arrow-key focus is not reproduced: each swatch is its own focusable radio button. The web's hidden form input (name) has no meaning in a Compose app.
accessibility: Each swatch is a radio button named by its name and value, for example "Blue, #2563eb", with the selected state on the chosen one.
The swatches are a selectable group named "Preset colors".
The selection is also a ring and a mark, so it does not depend on seeing the color.
Every swatch has a 48dp touch target reserved in the layout and draws the Monarch focus ring.
The label is a heading; the hex field has a label and announces its error through the error semantics.
Text grows with the font size setting and the swatches wrap.
edgeCases: Hex text is checked when the user presses Done or leaves the field; empty text restores the current value.
#rgb, rgb and upper-case text are accepted and normalised to lower-case #rrggbb.
MonarchColorSwatch.of returns null for a value that is not a hex color, so listOfNotNull skips it.
Choosing the color that is already selected does not call onValueChange.

appearance: The title in the subheading style with the count in muted caption text under it; rows are MonarchSwitchRow in Monarch colors, and reorderable rows have the surface fill and subtle border of MonarchReorderableList. platformNotes: The web panel uses checkboxes and Move up and Move down icon buttons; Android uses the platform switch, as iOS does, and reorders with MonarchReorderableList: a long press drags a row, and the row's handle offers Move up and Move down to TalkBack, Switch Access and the arrow keys. Each column is one switch row read with its name, its note and its state.
Columns that cannot be hidden and the last shown columns are disabled switches.

edgeCases: A column id in hiddenColumns that cannot be hidden is still shown.
Ids in order that are not columns are ignored.
While the search filters, rows cannot move; clear the search to reorder.
minimumVisible larger than the number of columns disables every shown switch.

name: MonarchColumnMapping
title: ColumnMapping
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn of rows, each with a MonarchSelect (androidx.compose.material3.ExposedDropdownMenuBox) per column; MonarchBadge for suggestions, MonarchButton for the bulk actions
summary: The mapping step of an import: one picker per imported column with example values, suggested fields from names and aliases, and the required fields still unmapped and the fields chosen twice.
whenToUse: After someone picks a CSV or spreadsheet to import, on its own screen, to choose which product field each column fills.
whenNotToUse: To choose which columns a table shows, use MonarchColumnChooser. To preview the rows that will be imported, use MonarchPreviewRows.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchColumnMapping(sources: List<MonarchColumnMappingSource>, mapping: Map<String, String>, fields: List<MonarchColumnMappingField>, onMappingChange: (Map<String, String>) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, suggestions: Map<String, MonarchColumnMappingSuggestion>? = null, showIssues: Boolean = true, showBulkActions: Boolean = true, enabled: Boolean = true, state: LazyListState = rememberLazyListState(), contentPadding: PaddingValues = PaddingValues(), labels: MonarchColumnMappingLabels = MonarchColumnMappingLabels())
public data class MonarchColumnMappingSource(name: String, samples: List<String> = emptyList())
public data class MonarchColumnMappingField(id: String, label: String, required: Boolean = false, description: String? = null, aliases: List<String> = emptyList())
public data class MonarchColumnMappingSuggestion(fieldId: String, confidence: MonarchColumnMappingConfidence, score: Double)
public enum class MonarchColumnMappingConfidence { Exact, Similar }
public data class MonarchColumnMappingIssues(missing: List<MonarchColumnMappingField>, duplicates: Map<String, List<String>>) { val isEmpty: Boolean }

public object MonarchColumnMappingDefaults { const val DEFAULT_THRESHOLD: Double = 0.75; fun suggest(sources: List<MonarchColumnMappingSource>, fields: List<MonarchColumnMappingField>, threshold: Double = DEFAULT_THRESHOLD): Map<String, MonarchColumnMappingSuggestion>; fun mapping(suggestions: Map<String, MonarchColumnMappingSuggestion>): Map<String, String>; fun issues(mapping: Map<String, String>, fields: List<MonarchColumnMappingField>): MonarchColumnMappingIssues }

public class MonarchColumnMappingLabels(label: String? = null, fieldFor: ((String) -> String)? = null, skip: String? = null, required: String? = null, exactMatch: String? = null, suggested: String? = null, noSamples: String? = null, summary: ((Int, Int) -> String)? = null, missing: ((String) -> String)? = null, duplicate: ((String, String) -> String)? = null, useSuggestions: String? = null, skipAll: String? = null, position: ((Int) -> String)? = null)

options.name: sources
options.description: The columns of the imported data in file order: the header and a few example values.

options.name: mapping
options.description: Column name to field id. A column missing from it is not imported. Start from MonarchColumnMappingDefaults.mapping(MonarchColumnMappingDefaults.suggest(sources, fields)).

options.name: fields
options.description: The fields the columns can be mapped to, with required flags, help and aliases.

options.name: onMappingChange
options.description: Called with the whole new mapping when a picker or a bulk action changes it.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the list. Give it a bounded height inside scrolling content.

options.name: suggestions
options.description: The suggestions behind the badges and Use suggestions. By default, MonarchColumnMappingDefaults.suggest(sources, fields).

options.name: showIssues
options.description: Shows the missing required fields and the duplicate errors. Pass false until the person first tries to go on.

options.name: showBulkActions
options.description: Shows Use suggestions (when the mapping differs from them) and Don’t import any (when something is mapped).

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the pickers and the bulk buttons can be used.

options.name: state
options.description: The scroll state of the list.

options.name: contentPadding
options.description: The padding around the rows, inside the scrolling area, for example for a bottom bar.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string: picker labels, the skip option, badges, the summary, the errors, the buttons and the name of a blank header.

states.name: suggested
states.description: A column set to its suggested field shows a success "Matched" badge for an exact match or an info "Suggested" badge for a close one.

states.name: not imported
states.description: The picker shows "Don’t import"; the column is missing from the mapping.

states.name: missing required
states.description: Under the count, "Map a column to: …" in the strong danger color on the danger subtle fill with the danger border.

states.name: duplicate
states.description: Each column that chose the same field shows its picker in the error state with "<Field> is also chosen for <other columns>." under it.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With enabled = false, the pickers and the bulk buttons cannot be used and take their disabled colors.

appearance: A list of rows separated by subtle dividers. Column headers in the default text color and strong weight, example values, the count and help in the muted text color; the pickers are MonarchSelect outlined fields with the input border. Errors use the danger roles and are always words. The roles follow light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ColumnMapping is a three-column grid (column, example values, field) with a native select per row and column headings on wide screens. On a phone a three-column grid does not fit, so, as on iOS, each column is a list row with its header and example values above the picker, and the headings are left out. The picker is MonarchSelect, a Material 3 exposed dropdown menu whose visible label is "Field for <column>"; a field's help also shows as the option's description in the menu. The list is a LazyColumn that scrolls itself, like the iOS List, so give it its own screen or a bounded height; state and contentPadding are offered for that. The web size prop (sm, md) has no counterpart: rows size themselves with the font size setting. The web value and onValueChange become mapping and onMappingChange; the web's uncontrolled defaultValue is the app's initial state. The suggestion algorithm (normalising names, word overlap, containment and edit distance, threshold 0.75, each field once) is the same as the web's suggestColumnMapping; the web's toFieldMapping is not offered (mapping.entries.associate { it.value to it.key } gives it). iOS names showsIssues and showsBulkActions and has static functions on the view; Android uses the Compose style showIssues and showBulkActions, and the functions live on MonarchColumnMappingDefaults. MonarchColumnMappingLabels adds position, the name of a blank header, so every built-in string can be replaced.
accessibility: The list is a group named "Column mapping".
Each column's header and example values are one element, read before its picker.
Each picker is labelled "Field for <column>" and reads its value, the chosen field or "Don’t import"; a duplicate is the field's error, read with it.
The missing-fields message is an error and a polite live region; errors are words in the danger colors, never color alone; suggestions are a word in a badge, not only a tone.
The count ("3 of 5 columns mapped") is a polite live region, so changes are announced.
The pickers are at least 56dp high and the bulk buttons have 48dp touch targets.
edgeCases: A blank header is shown as its position, "#3".
Two columns with the same header share one entry in the mapping, because the mapping is keyed by name, as on the web.
A field id in the mapping that is not in fields does not count as mapped, and its picker shows "Don’t import".
Long headers and values wrap; nothing is truncated.
Only the first three example values that are not blank are shown.

title: ColumnMenu
wrapsNative: MonarchMenu, MonarchMenuItem, MonarchCheckbox, MonarchDivider
summary: A Columns menu with one checkable item per column, to show and hide the columns of a table: a MonarchButton that opens a MonarchMenu with a checkbox in each item.
whenToUse: Above a table or data grid whose columns people may hide, such as a list of contacts with optional email, plan and created columns.
whenNotToUse: To filter which rows are shown, use filter chips. To reorder columns, use a reorderable list in a settings sheet. To switch between whole layouts, use a view switcher.
api: @Composable fun MonarchMenu(expanded: Boolean, onDismissRequest: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, offset: DpOffset = DpOffset(MonarchTokens.Space.space0.dp, MonarchTokens.Space.space1.dp), content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)

@Composable fun MonarchMenuItem(text: String, onClick: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, destructive: Boolean = false, selected: Boolean? = null, shortcut: String? = null, leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)

@Composable fun MonarchCheckbox(checked: Boolean, onCheckedChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)?, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, invalid: Boolean = false, label: String? = null, description: String? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)

@Composable fun MonarchButton(text: String, onClick: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchButtonVariant = MonarchButtonVariant.Secondary, size: MonarchButtonSize = MonarchButtonSize.Md, …)

states.name: shown
states.description: The item's Checkbox is checked and the item's toggleable state is on.

states.name: last column
states.description: The last visible column's item is disabled, so the table is never empty (the web's minVisible of 1).

states.name: all shown
states.description: Show all columns is disabled when every column is visible.

appearance: The Material 3 menu in the raised background role with Monarch's medium radius; the trigger is a small secondary MonarchButton and each item ends with a MonarchCheckbox in the accent colors Monarch maps to the scheme. The same mapping in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ColumnMenu is a component that takes DataTable's column state and offers minVisible, showAll, onReset and a trigger size. On Android the same result is a few lines of a MonarchMenu with a MonarchCheckbox in each item, so Monarch adds no type: minVisible is enabled = false on the last visible item, Show all and Reset are items after a MonarchDivider, and the trigger size is the MonarchButton size. The web keeps the menu open while items are checked; on Android the item's onClick changes the set and leaves expanded as it is. iOS documents the same menu as a native SwiftUI Menu with Toggles.
accessibility: The trigger is a button; its state description says how many columns are shown ("3 of 4 shown"), like the web's hidden count.
Each column item carries a toggleable state with the checkbox role, so TalkBack says checked or not checked; the MonarchCheckbox inside has a null callback so the item is the one target.
A disabled last column is announced as disabled, so TalkBack users know it cannot be hidden.
Material 3 gives each item a row at least 48dp high.
edgeCases: Keep at least one column visible by disabling the last visible item.
The menu stays open while columns are toggled; close it from Show all or by tapping outside.
Keep the visible set in the view model or rememberSaveable (as a list of ids) so it survives a configuration change.

name: MonarchColumnsBlock
title: ColumnsBlock
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.ui.layout.Layout, androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column, androidx.compose.ui.semantics.isTraversalGroup
summary: Two or more side-by-side columns inside a document, which stack into one column where the width is narrow.
whenToUse: To set two short passages next to each other in a document or an article, such as a before and an after, or three steps of a plan.
whenNotToUse: For a split the user resizes use MonarchResizablePanels. For a screen layout that adapts to the window use the Material 3 adaptive panes. For tabular data use MonarchTableBlock.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchColumnsBlock(modifier: Modifier = Modifier, ratio: Float = MonarchColumnsBlockTokens.DEFAULT_RATIO, content: MonarchColumnsBlockScope.() -> Unit)
public sealed interface MonarchColumnsBlockScope { public fun column(content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit) }

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the block.

options.name: ratio
options.description: The share of the width for the first of two columns, kept between 0.2 and 0.8 (0.5 when not a number). Three or more columns are equal.

options.name: content
options.description: Declares the columns with column { }, in order. Each column lays its content out top to bottom.

states.name: side by side
states.description: From 480dp of available width at the default font size, the columns sit next to each other with a 24dp gap, top-aligned.

states.name: stacked
states.description: Below that width, or with one column, the columns stack in order with a 12dp gap. The 480dp threshold is multiplied by the font scale, so at font scale 2.0 a block narrower than 960dp stacks.

appearance: No surface of its own: the columns sit on whatever is behind the block, in every theme.
platformNotes: The web ColumnsBlock is also a Tiptap editor node with a resize handle that writes the ratio into the document; Android has no Monarch rich-text editor, so only the static block is offered, as on iOS. For a split the user resizes, MonarchResizablePanels exists. The web stacks with a container query at 30rem; Android uses the width offered to the block, 30 times the base type size (480dp), scaled by the font scale as rem is scaled by the browser text size. iOS takes each child view as a column; on Android columns are declared with column { } in a builder scope, as items are in a LazyColumn, so each column can be made a TalkBack traversal group. The parity plan lists resizable-panels as a dependency; it is not used, because the block has no handle.
accessibility: Each column is a TalkBack traversal group, so TalkBack reads one column completely before the next instead of reading across the columns line by line.
Columns are placed from the start edge, so the first column is on the right in right-to-left layouts.
At large font sizes the columns stack sooner, so text keeps a readable width; text is never cut.
edgeCases: One column fills the width; an empty block takes no height.
A column taller than the others sets the height of the block; the others stay at the top.
Inside a horizontally scrolling container, which offers no width limit, the block assumes 480dp.
Content added outside column { } is not shown: the builder only collects columns.

name: MonarchCombobox
title: Combobox
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.ExposedDropdownMenuBox with an editable androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedTextField and ExposedDropdownMenu (menu), or a read-only anchor that opens androidx.compose.material3.ModalBottomSheet with MonarchSearchBar and androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn (sheet)
summary: A labelled field that chooses one option from a searchable list: a filtered menu under an editable field for short lists, or a bottom sheet with a search field for long ones.
whenToUse: For one choice among many options the person finds by typing: an assignee, a country, a project, a label that may need creating.
whenNotToUse: For a short, fixed list without search use MonarchSelect. For several values use MonarchTagInput or MonarchCheckboxGroup. For a free search that shows results rather than choosing a value use MonarchSearchBar.
api: @Composable fun MonarchCombobox(label: String, options: List<MonarchComboboxOption>, selected: String?, onSelectedChange: (String?) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, presentation: MonarchComboboxPresentation = MonarchComboboxPresentation.Automatic, enabled: Boolean = true, loading: Boolean = false, sortByMatch: Boolean = false, placeholder: String? = null, helperText: String? = null, errorText: String? = null, clearOptionLabel: String? = null, limit: Int? = null, query: String? = null, onQueryChange: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, filter: ((MonarchComboboxOption, String) -> Boolean)? = null, onCreate: ((String) -> MonarchComboboxOption?)? = null, clearIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchComboboxLabels = MonarchComboboxLabels())
class MonarchComboboxOption(id: String, label: String, description: String? = null, hint: String? = null, group: String? = null, keywords: String? = null, enabled: Boolean = true)
enum class MonarchComboboxPresentation { Automatic, Menu, Sheet }

class MonarchComboboxLabels(search: String? = null, loading: String? = null, empty: String? = null, create: ((text: String) -> String)? = null, more: ((shown: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, cancel: String? = null, clear: String? = null)

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label, already localised. It names the field and is the title of the sheet.

options.name: options
options.description: The options in order: id, label, description, hint, group, keywords and enabled.

options.name: selected
options.description: The id of the chosen option, or null.

options.name: onSelectedChange
options.description: Called with the id of the chosen option, or null when the selection is cleared.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the field.

options.name: presentation
options.description: Menu, Sheet, or Automatic: a menu for up to eight options the app does not search, a sheet otherwise.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the list can be opened.

options.name: loading
options.description: Options are being fetched: "Loading…" while nothing matches, and the sheet's search field shows its pending state.

options.name: sortByMatch
options.description: While searching, lists labels that start with the text first, then labels with a word that does, then the rest, keeping the order within each.

options.name: placeholder
options.description: Shown in the empty field while nothing is chosen.

options.name: helperText
options.description: Guidance below the field.

options.name: errorText
options.description: An error message; replaces the helper text and is set as the field's error.

options.name: clearOptionLabel
options.description: Adds a first row that clears the selection, such as "Unassigned". Hidden while searching.

options.name: limit
options.description: Shows at most this many matches, with "Showing 50 of 120. Type to narrow the list.".

options.name: query
options.description: The search text, for apps that search a server: pass it with onQueryChange and a filter that keeps every option, and update options and loading from it.

options.name: onQueryChange
options.description: Called with the search text on every keystroke and with "" when the list closes. Setting it makes the automatic presentation a sheet.

options.name: filter
options.description: Decides whether an option matches the trimmed search text. By default the label, hint and keywords are searched, ignoring case and accents.

options.name: onCreate
options.description: Offers "Create “text”" when no label equals the typed text. Return the new option to choose it, or null to only close the list.

options.name: clearIcon
options.description: The icon of a clear button at the end of the field, shown while something is chosen. Monarch bundles no icons; without it there is no clear button.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

options.name: loadError
options.description: The options could not be loaded: the list shows the message (empty uses the built-in one).

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Adds Try again after loadError; the list stays open.

options.name: MonarchComboboxOption.leading
options.description: Decorative content before the label, such as a flag.

options.name: MonarchComboboxOption.labelLocale
options.description: The language of the label, so TalkBack reads an endonym correctly.

states.name: closed
states.description: The field shows the chosen label, or the placeholder (or the floating label) while nothing is chosen.

states.name: menu open
states.description: The field holds the search text, with the chosen label as its placeholder, and the Material 3 menu lists the matches under their group headings.

states.name: sheet open
states.description: A modal bottom sheet titled with the label holds a search field, the list of selectable rows and Cancel.

states.name: chosen
states.description: The chosen row has a filled radio mark in the accent strong color and is selected for TalkBack.

states.name: no matches
states.description: "No matches" in the list, or the Create row when onCreate is given.

states.name: loading
states.description: "Loading…" in the list while nothing matches; the sheet's search field shows the pending indicator.

states.name: cut short
states.description: A note under the list with the number shown and the number of matches.

states.name: error
states.description: The danger outline and label, and the message under the field.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The disabled colors; the list does not open. Disabled options are listed in the disabled color and cannot be chosen.

appearance: The field uses MonarchTextField's colors: a surface fill with the input border, the focus ring when focused, the danger strong color in error. The menu and the sheet are on the surface color; descriptions, hints, headings and messages are muted text; the chosen row's radio mark is the accent strong color and others the input border. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The parity map named two Material 3 forms and both are offered: the exposed dropdown with an editable field for short lists, and a searchable list in a ModalBottomSheet for long ones, chosen automatically or with presentation. iOS always uses a sheet with .searchable. The web shows a popover under a typing field with keyboard navigation; on Android the menu keeps Material's focus handling and hardware-keyboard navigation of the menu. Only single selection is offered (the web's multiple mode is MonarchTagInput). The web's onSearch with built-in debounce and abort, minSearchLength and the error and retry row are replaced by query and onQueryChange: the app runs the search, for example in a LaunchedEffect keyed on the text, which Compose cancels when the text changes. The web's media and renderOption have no equivalent; the label names each option. The iOS isRequired and isClearable options are not offered: a clear button needs an icon, so it is shown only when clearIcon is given, and clearOptionLabel adds a clear row instead. The sheet's title is the label, as on iOS.
accessibility: The field is the Material 3 exposed dropdown anchor: TalkBack reads the label, the chosen value and the expand state, and double tap opens the list; in the menu presentation the field is editable and typing filters the list.

Every option row is read with its label, description and hint, and the chosen row is selected and has a filled radio mark, so the choice does not rely on color. In the sheet each row is a radio button with a 48dp height.
Disabled options are disabled; group headings are headings.
Messages in the list (Loading, No matches, the cut-short note) are polite live regions.
The clear button is a separate button named "Clear" with a 48dp touch target.
The error is the field's error semantics and is shown as text with a danger outline.
edgeCases: A selected id that is not among the options shows an empty field.
Typing in the menu replaces the field's text; closing the menu restores the chosen label and clears the search text.
With query and onQueryChange the combobox does not filter by itself only if filter keeps every option; otherwise the default filter still applies to the options the app passes.
Create is not offered when a label equals the typed text, ignoring case and accents.
Options with the same group that are not next to each other get two headings.
A limit of 0 shows no options, only the note.

title: ComingSoonState
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column with MonarchBadge, MonarchEmptyState and MonarchText
summary: A placeholder for a feature that is planned but not available yet: a "Coming soon" badge, MonarchEmptyState with the feature and an optional action, and a short list of what is planned.
whenToUse: In a tab, a card or a screen of a feature that is announced but not built yet, so people know it is planned rather than broken or empty.
whenNotToUse: For a feature that exists but has no data yet, use MonarchEmptyState. For a feature the plan does not include, use an upgrade prompt.
api: Column { MonarchBadge(text = "Coming soon", tone = MonarchTone.Info); MonarchEmptyState(title = feature, message = description, actions = { MonarchButton(text = "Notify me", onClick = …) }); highlights.forEach { MonarchText(text = "• $it") } }

options.name: MonarchBadge.text
options.description: "Coming soon", in the app's strings. Leave the badge out when the screen title already says it.

options.name: MonarchEmptyState.title
options.description: The name of the feature, "Status pages", or "Coming soon" when there is no name.

options.name: MonarchEmptyState.message
options.description: What the feature will do, in one sentence.

options.name: MonarchEmptyState.actions
options.description: An optional action, such as "Notify me".

options.name: highlights
options.description: A short list of what is planned, one MonarchText per line, under a heading such as "What is planned".

states.name: planned
states.description: The badge, the feature, its description and the action.

states.name: notified
states.description: After "Notify me" the app disables the button and changes its label.

appearance: The info badge above MonarchEmptyState in its own appearance; the list in default text. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ComingSoonState is a component with fixed "Coming soon" wording, the badge read as part of the heading, and a highlights list. On Android it composes existing parts: MonarchEmptyState has no slot for a badge or a list, so they sit above and below it, and the badge is read just before the title. The app supplies all the words, so Monarch ships no strings for it. iOS shares the recipe approach.
accessibility: TalkBack reads the badge, then the title and message of MonarchEmptyState, then the list, in that order.
The action is a MonarchButton with a 48dp touch target.
Nothing is conveyed by color alone: "Coming soon" is written.
edgeCases: Do not put a Notify me action without a way to keep the promise.
Keep the list short; it scrolls with the screen.

title: CommandPalette
wrapsNative: MonarchBottomSheet (fully expanded) holding MonarchSearchBar (androidx.compose.material3.DockedSearchBar) and MonarchSearchResults (a androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn), opened by a button and by androidx.compose.ui.input.key.onPreviewKeyEvent for Ctrl+K
summary: A recipe, not a component: a full-height search sheet whose results are commands and places, grouped, run by tapping one; Ctrl+K opens it on a hardware keyboard.
whenToUse: For apps with many commands or places, so people can type what they want instead of hunting through menus.
whenNotToUse: For searching records only, use MonarchSearchBar with MonarchSearchResults on the screen. For a few actions, use a MonarchMenu (menu-button recipe).
api: Modifier.onPreviewKeyEvent { event -> event.type == KeyEventType.KeyDown && event.isCtrlPressed && event.key == Key.K }
ModalBottomSheet(onDismissRequest = …, sheetState = rememberModalBottomSheetState(skipPartiallyExpanded = true)) { … }
MonarchSearchBar(query = query, onQueryChange = { query = it }, onSearch = {}, placeholder = "Type a command or search")
MonarchSearchResults(groups = commands grouped by heading, onSelect = { result, _ -> run it and close }, modifier = Modifier.weight(1f), query = query)

options.name: commands
options.type: List of id, label and group
options.description: The commands and places, each under a group heading such as Actions or Go to; filter them by the query.

options.name: open
options.description: Whether the sheet is shown, kept with rememberSaveable.

options.name: query
options.description: The search text; cleared when the sheet closes.

options.name: sources
options.description: Results fetched as the person types: run them in a LaunchedEffect keyed on the query, pass loading to MonarchSearchResults and cancel with the effect.

states.name: closed
states.description: Only the trigger button (or a search MonarchIconButton in the top app bar) is shown.

states.name: open
states.description: The sheet fills the screen with the search field at the top and grouped results under it.

states.name: no results
states.description: MonarchSearchResults shows its empty state for the query.

states.name: loading
states.description: Pass loading to MonarchSearchResults while server results arrive.

appearance: A Material 3 bottom sheet in the Monarch theme holding the docked search bar and grouped result rows. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web ships CommandPalette as a centered dialog with keyboard navigation, nested pages, recent items, shortcut hints and async sources. On a phone the native pattern is a full-height sheet with a search field, so the recipe uses MonarchBottomSheet with MonarchSearchBar and MonarchSearchResults; touch replaces arrow keys and TalkBack moves through the results in order. The Ctrl+K shortcut applies to hardware keyboards only; put onPreviewKeyEvent on the screen's root so it works wherever focus is. Shortcut hints are left out because touch users have no keys; nested pages become a second query state or a second sheet; recent items are a Recent group while the query is empty. The system back gesture closes the sheet.
accessibility: The trigger is a button with a 48dp target.
The sheet is a modal pane; back and the scrim close it.
The search field has the search role from Material 3.
Group headings are headings and each result is one button, from MonarchSearchResults, which also announces the result count.
Closing after a command returns focus to the screen.
edgeCases: Never put MonarchSearchResults inside verticalScroll; give it the remaining height with weight(1f).
Clear the query when the sheet closes so the next opening starts fresh.
A command that needs confirmation should close the sheet and open a dialog.

name: MonarchCommentThread
title: CommentThread
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column with MonarchMessageRow for each comment, MonarchMessageComposer (Foundation BasicTextField with TextFieldState) for the reply field, MonarchButton, MonarchBadge and androidx.compose.material3.AlertDialog for the delete confirmation
summary: One threaded discussion shown in place: an optional quote, the starting comment, replies with older ones folded, Resolve and Reopen, and a reply field that stays busy while saving.
whenToUse: For a discussion anchored to one thing, shown next to it: a comment on a document passage, a field or a ticket, in a sheet or under the item. Use resolved for review flows where threads are settled.
whenNotToUse: For a chat-style conversation, use MonarchVirtualMessageList with MonarchMessageRow and MonarchMessageComposer. For one message alone, use MonarchMessageRow. For a feed of events, use MonarchActivityTimeline.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchCommentThread(comments: List<MonarchCommentThreadComment>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, quote: String? = null, resolved: Boolean = false, visibleReplies: Int = 3, now: Long? = null, replyState: TextFieldState = rememberTextFieldState(), labels: MonarchCommentThreadLabels = MonarchCommentThreadLabels(), onResolvedChange: (suspend (Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, onReply: (suspend (String) -> Unit)? = null, onDeleteComment: (suspend (String) -> Unit)? = null, resolveIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null)
class MonarchCommentThreadComment(id: String, author: String, body: String, createdAt: Long, authorImage: Painter? = null, authorSeed: String? = null, canDelete: Boolean = false)

class MonarchCommentThreadLabels(label: ((author: String) -> String)? = null, quote: ((quote: String) -> String)? = null, showEarlier: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, reply: String? = null, replyPlaceholder: String? = null, send: String? = null, resolve: String? = null, reopen: String? = null, resolved: String? = null, resolvedHint: String? = null, resolvedNotice: String? = null, reopenedNotice: String? = null, sentNotice: String? = null, actionFailed: String? = null, deleteComment: String? = null, deleteTitle: String? = null, deleteDescription: String? = null, deleteConfirm: String? = null, cancel: String? = null, messageRow: MonarchMessageRowLabels = MonarchMessageRowLabels())

options.name: comments
options.description: The comments, oldest first. The first starts the thread; the rest are replies. Each has an id, author, body, creation time in epoch milliseconds, an optional avatar Painter and canDelete.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the thread.

options.name: quote
options.description: The passage the thread is about, shown above it in the muted color with a bar along the start edge.

options.name: resolved
options.description: A Resolved badge, the subtle fill, Reopen instead of Resolve, and a hint instead of the reply field.

options.name: visibleReplies
options.description: The latest replies shown before older ones fold behind Show N earlier replies. Folding never hides a single reply.

options.name: now
options.description: Fixes now for the relative times. Without it the times follow the clock.

options.name: replyState
options.description: The reply text. Hoist it to keep a draft.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including the comments' MonarchMessageRowLabels.

options.name: onResolvedChange
options.description: Resolves (true) or reopens (false); shows the Resolve or Reopen button, which shows progress while it runs. Throw to report a failure.

options.name: onReply
options.description: Posts the trimmed reply; shows the reply field. The field clears when it returns and keeps the text when it throws.

options.name: onDeleteComment
options.description: Deletes the comment with this id after a confirmation dialog; offered on comments with canDelete, by long press and as a TalkBack action.

options.name: resolveIcon
options.description: The icon before Resolve, a MonarchIcon with a null description. Text only without it.

states.name: open
states.description: The comments, Resolve when onResolvedChange is given, and the reply field when onReply is given.

states.name: folded
states.description: With more replies than visibleReplies plus one, the starting comment, a Show N earlier replies button and the latest replies. The button reveals all and moves focus to the first revealed reply.

states.name: resolving
states.description: The Resolve or Reopen button shows a progress indicator until onResolvedChange returns.

states.name: sending
states.description: The composer's send button shows Sending… until onReply returns; the text clears on success.

states.name: resolved
states.description: The subtle fill, a success Resolved badge, Reopen, and This thread is resolved. Reopen it to reply. instead of the reply field.

states.name: failed
states.description: That didn't work. Try again. in the strong danger color under the thread; a failed reply keeps its text.

states.name: confirming delete
states.description: A Material 3 AlertDialog: Delete this comment?, a danger Delete comment button and Cancel.

states.name: empty
states.description: With no comments, only the reply field (when onReply is given); the thread has no TalkBack name.

appearance: No fill while open and the subtle background role when resolved. The quote is muted text beside a strong border bar; the Resolved badge uses the success subtle roles; a failure uses the strong danger text role; comments and the reply field keep the MonarchMessageRow and MonarchMessageComposer roles. The same roles adapt to dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web's CommentThread shows a delete icon button on each deletable comment and a hint about Enter and Shift+Enter; on Android, Delete is in the comment's long-press menu and a TalkBack action (MonarchMessageRow's actions), and the on-screen keyboard's Enter adds a line while the send button sends (MonarchMessageComposer's behavior), so there is no keyboard hint. The web returns promises from its callbacks; Android takes suspending functions and treats a thrown exception as the failure. A resolved thread on the web is muted with opacity; Monarch never dims with alpha, so Android uses the subtle background and a Resolved badge, which also says the state in text. The web's success notices are visually hidden; on Android the same live region shows them as a muted caption. The thread is a Column, not a LazyColumn, so it can sit in a scrolling screen or sheet; folding keeps it short. Comment bodies are plain strings, where the web accepts any React node. iOS has no entry for this id yet.
accessibility: The thread is a traversal group named Thread started by <first author>.
The quote is one element read as Quoted text: <quote>.
Each comment is a MonarchMessageRow: author, full date and body are one element.
Delete comment is a TalkBack custom action and a long-press menu item on comments with canDelete, and asks for confirmation in a dialog.
Resolve, Reopen, Show N earlier replies and Send reply are buttons with a 48dp touch target.
Resolved is written as a badge, not shown by color alone.
Success (Reply sent, Thread resolved, Thread reopened) and failure are written in a polite live region that is always present, so changes are announced.
Show N earlier replies moves focus to the first revealed reply.
The reply field is named Reply for TalkBack.
edgeCases: Folding never hides a single reply: with visibleReplies 3, four replies are all shown and five fold two.
A negative visibleReplies counts as 0.
With no comments the thread has no TalkBack name and shows only the reply field.
onReply receives the trimmed text; an empty or blank field cannot be sent.
Without now, the relative times refresh every minute while on screen.
A second tap on Resolve while it is saving is ignored.

examples.title: Open thread with a quote
examples.template:
@OptIn(ExperimentalMonarchApi::class)
MonarchCommentThread(
    comments = comments,
    quote = {{quote}},
    resolved = resolved,
    now = {{now|millis}},
    onResolvedChange = { resolved = it /* Save on the server; throw on failure. */ },
    onReply = { body ->
        comments += MonarchCommentThreadComment("c${comments.size + 1}", "Lee Park", body, System.currentTimeMillis(), canDelete = true)
    },
    onDeleteComment = { id -> comments.removeAll { it.id == id } },
)
examples.code:
@OptIn(ExperimentalMonarchApi::class)
MonarchCommentThread(
    comments = comments,
    quote = "Billed monthly, cancel any time.",
    resolved = resolved,
    now = 1_773_144_000_000L,
    onResolvedChange = { resolved = it /* Save on the server; throw on failure. */ },
    onReply = { body ->
        comments += MonarchCommentThreadComment("c${comments.size + 1}", "Lee Park", body, System.currentTimeMillis(), canDelete = true)
    },
    onDeleteComment = { id -> comments.removeAll { it.id == id } },
)

examples.title: A read-only thread with older replies folded
examples.code:
@OptIn(ExperimentalMonarchApi::class)
MonarchCommentThread(comments = comments, visibleReplies = 2)

name: MonarchCommentsPanel
title: CommentsPanel
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn of MonarchListRow rows under a MonarchSegmentedControl, with MonarchCommentThread for the open thread and androidx.activity.compose.BackHandler; placed by the app in a MonarchBottomSheet or a supporting pane
summary: Every comment thread of a document or record in one panel: Open and Resolved threads in a list, and one thread at a time with its quote, replies, Resolve or Reopen and confirmed delete.
whenToUse: Beside a document or record that people discuss in threads anchored to passages: the comments sheet of a document editor, or the comments pane beside it on a tablet. Selecting a thread lets the app highlight its passage.
whenNotToUse: For one thread shown in place next to its passage, use MonarchCommentThread. For a chat conversation, use MonarchVirtualMessageList with MonarchMessageRow. For replies to one chat message, use MonarchThreadPanel.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchCommentsPanel(threads: List<MonarchCommentsPanelThread>?, filter: MonarchCommentsPanelFilter, onFilterChange: (MonarchCommentsPanelFilter) -> Unit, selectedThreadId: String?, onSelectedThreadChange: (String?) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, errorMessage: String? = null, now: Long? = null, locale: Locale? = null, labels: MonarchCommentsPanelLabels = MonarchCommentsPanelLabels(), onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null, onClose: (() -> Unit)? = null, onReply: (suspend (threadId: String, body: String) -> Unit)? = null, onResolvedChange: (suspend (threadId: String, resolved: Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, onDeleteComment: (suspend (threadId: String, commentId: String) -> Unit)? = null, emptyIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, backIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null)

class MonarchCommentsPanelThread(id: String, comments: List<MonarchCommentThreadComment>, quote: String? = null, updatedAt: Long? = null, resolved: Boolean = false, canResolve: Boolean = true, canReply: Boolean = true)
enum class MonarchCommentsPanelFilter { Open, Resolved }

class MonarchCommentsPanelLabels(title: String? = null, close: String? = null, open: String? = null, resolved: String? = null, back: String? = null, loading: String? = null, emptyOpen: String? = null, emptyResolved: String? = null, emptyHint: String? = null, commentCount: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, quote: ((quote: String) -> String)? = null, resolvedNotice: String? = null, reopenedNotice: String? = null, thread: MonarchCommentThreadLabels = MonarchCommentThreadLabels())

options.name: threads
options.description: The threads, or null while they load. Each has an id, its comments (MonarchCommentThreadComment, oldest first), an optional quote and updatedAt, resolved, canResolve and canReply.

options.name: filter
options.description: Open or Resolved: which threads are listed.

options.name: onFilterChange
options.description: Called when the person switches the segmented control. The open thread is closed at the same time.

options.name: selectedThreadId
options.description: The thread shown in full, or null for the list. A thread that is not listed under the current filter shows the list.

options.name: onSelectedThreadChange
options.description: Called with a thread opened from the list, or null when All comments, the system back gesture, a filter change or a successful resolve closes it.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the panel. Give it a bounded height.

options.name: errorMessage
options.description: Loading failed: shown instead of the list.

options.name: now
options.description: The current time in epoch milliseconds for the relative times; null follows the clock, refreshed every minute.

options.name: locale
options.description: The locale of the relative times in the list; null uses the configuration's first locale.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, including the open thread's (MonarchCommentThreadLabels).

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Try again with errorMessage.

options.name: onClose
options.description: Shows a Close button in the header.

options.name: onReply
options.description: Posts a reply; shows the reply field on open threads with canReply. Throw to keep the text and show a failure.

options.name: onResolvedChange
options.description: Resolves or reopens a thread; shows Resolve or Reopen on threads with canResolve. On success the panel returns to the list and announces it; throw to show a failure.

options.name: onDeleteComment
options.description: Deletes a comment after a confirmation dialog; offered on comments with canDelete.

options.name: emptyIcon
options.description: The icon of the empty state.

options.name: backIcon
options.description: The icon before All comments; it should mirror in right to left.

states.name: list
states.description: The heading, the Open and Resolved segments and one row per thread: the starter's avatar and name, the quote cut after two lines, and the number of comments with the last activity.

states.name: thread
states.description: All comments above a MonarchCommentThread with the thread's quote, comments, Resolve or Reopen and reply field. The system back gesture returns to the list.

states.name: loading
states.description: threads is null: a MonarchLoadingState with three rows, read once as Loading comments.

states.name: error
states.description: errorMessage is set: a MonarchInlineErrorRetry with Try again, or the message in the strong danger text role without onRetry.

states.name: empty
states.description: No thread under the filter: a small MonarchEmptyState, No open comments with a hint, or No resolved comments.

states.name: resolved
states.description: After a thread is resolved or reopened, the panel returns to the list and announces Thread resolved or Thread reopened.

appearance: No fill of its own, so it takes the sheet's or pane's surface. The heading uses the default text role, the quote and the line under each thread the muted text role, the dividers the subtle border role, and the segmented control the Material 3 roles Monarch maps from the theme. The same roles adapt to dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web's CommentsPanel is a side panel that keeps its filter and selection itself when uncontrolled; on Android both are hoisted (filter with onFilterChange, selectedThreadId with onSelectedThreadChange), as Compose state is. The web's close button is an icon button; here Close is a text button, because Monarch bundles no icons and a sheet is also closed by swiping or the back gesture. The web delete icon button on each comment is the comment's long-press menu and TalkBack action here (MonarchCommentThread). The web names the filter group Show; on Android the Material 3 segmented buttons are read with their own label and selected state, so there is no group name. The web's Enter to send hint is left out because the on-screen keyboard's Enter adds a line. The panel is a content composable: the app puts it in a MonarchBottomSheet on a phone or a supporting pane at expanded width. iOS has no entry for this id yet.
accessibility: The title is a heading.
Open and Resolved are Material 3 segmented buttons with their selected state.
Each thread row is one button read as the starter, the quote and the number of comments with the last activity; the avatar is decorative.

With a keyboard or switch access, opening a thread moves focus to All comments, and going back moves focus to the row of that thread, or to the first row when it left the list. In touch mode Compose buttons do not take input focus, so TalkBack users start from the top of the new view.
The system back gesture closes the open thread before it closes the sheet.
Thread resolved and Thread reopened are announced through a polite live region that is always present.
Loading is read once as Loading comments; rows, All comments, Close and Try again have 48dp touch targets.
edgeCases: A selectedThreadId that is not listed under the current filter shows the list, so a thread that was just resolved by someone else does not stay open.
Switching the filter closes the open thread.
A thread without comments has an empty name and no avatar in the list.
A long quote is cut after two lines in the list and shown in full in the thread.
Each thread starts with an empty reply field; the draft is not kept across threads.
Without now, the relative times refresh every minute while on screen.
The list is a LazyColumn: give the panel a bounded height and do not put it in a vertically scrolling parent.

    onFilterChange = {},
    selectedThreadId = null,
    onSelectedThreadChange = {},
    modifier = Modifier.height(320.dp),

name: MonarchComparisonSection
title: ComparisonSection
wrapsNative: MonarchPricingTable, androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
summary: A band that compares the product with alternatives: a header, a table of capabilities by option, cards that say whom each option suits, a note on sources and the actions.
whenToUse: On a welcome or product tour screen that explains how the product differs from the tools people use today, with neutral, sourced rows.
whenNotToUse: To compare the product's own plans, use MonarchPricingSection or MonarchPricingTable.

appearance: The table uses MonarchPricingTable's roles: subtle-border row lines, group headings on the subtle background, an accent border around the highlighted header. Best-for cards use the surface with the default border, or the subtle accent with the accent border; the note the subtle background with muted text. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web table scrolls sideways on narrow screens with the first column pinned. On Android the table is MonarchPricingTable in its grid layout, with every column at least 152dp wide (scaled with the font size); when that is wider than the screen the table scrolls sideways, so no word is broken. The capability column scrolls with the rest rather than staying pinned. Values are MonarchPricingFeatureValue, so a check, a dash or text.
accessibility: The table is a traversal group named by caption or the title; each cell is read as the option, the capability and the value, such as "Spreadsheets, Change history: Per file".
Checks and dashes are not read; the words carry the value.
The title, group headings and best-for titles are headings; each best-for card is read as one element.
edgeCases: On a phone the table usually scrolls sideways; the capability column is not pinned.
An option missing from a row's values does not have the capability.

name: MonarchConditionEditor
title: ConditionEditor
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of outlined condition cards; MonarchSelect (androidx.compose.material3.ExposedDropdownMenuBox) for field, operator and one option; MonarchTextField (androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedTextField) for text and numbers; MonarchMultiSelect (androidx.compose.material3.ModalBottomSheet) for several options and free values; androidx.compose.material3.DatePickerDialog for days; androidx.compose.material3.SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow for all / any
summary: Edits a list of conditions, each a field, an operator and a value input that fits the field, with an all / any switch.
whenToUse: When people define when something applies: ticket routing rules, form logic such as "show this question when", eligibility rules. Fields are data, so one editor serves every product.
whenNotToUse: For nested AND / OR groups use MonarchQueryBuilder, which is built on this editor. For filtering a list on screen use filter chips or a filter sheet; for the actions a rule runs use MonarchActionEditor.
api: @Composable fun MonarchConditionEditor(value: List<MonarchCondition>, onValueChange: (List<MonarchCondition>) -> Unit, fields: List<MonarchConditionField>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, match: MonarchConditionMatch? = null, onMatchChange: ((MonarchConditionMatch) -> Unit)? = null, maxConditions: Int = 20, showErrors: Boolean = false, defaultField: String? = null, enabled: Boolean = true, createId: (() -> String)? = null, removeIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, addIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, emptyContent: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchConditionEditorLabels = MonarchConditionEditorLabels())

data class MonarchCondition(id: String, field: String, operator: MonarchConditionOperator, value: MonarchConditionValue? = null) { fun problem(fields: List<MonarchConditionField>): MonarchConditionProblem?; fun matches(actual: Any?): Boolean; companion object { fun create(id: String, field: MonarchConditionField?): MonarchCondition; fun problems(conditions: List<MonarchCondition>, fields: List<MonarchConditionField>): Map<String, MonarchConditionProblem>; fun evaluate(conditions: List<MonarchCondition>, values: Map<String, Any?>, match: MonarchConditionMatch = MonarchConditionMatch.All): Boolean } }

class MonarchConditionField(key: String, label: String, type: MonarchConditionFieldType, options: List<MonarchSelectOption<String>> = emptyList(), group: String? = null, operators: List<MonarchConditionOperator>? = null, placeholder: String? = null, enabled: Boolean = true, disabledReason: String? = null)
enum class MonarchConditionFieldType { Text, Number, Date, Select, MultiSelect, Tags, Boolean }

enum class MonarchConditionOperator { Eq, Neq, In, Nin, Contains, NotContains, Gt, Gte, Lt, Lte, Before, After, IsTrue, IsFalse, IsEmpty, IsNotEmpty; val takesValue: Boolean; val takesList: Boolean; companion object { fun forField(field: MonarchConditionField?): List<MonarchConditionOperator>; fun defaultsFor(type: MonarchConditionFieldType): List<MonarchConditionOperator> } }

sealed interface MonarchConditionValue { val isEmpty: Boolean; val asList: List<String>; data class Text(text: String); data class Number(text: String) { constructor(number: Double); val number: Double? }; data class Date(millis: Long?); data class Values(values: List<String>) }
enum class MonarchConditionMatch { All, Any }
enum class MonarchConditionProblem { Field, Value, Number, Option }

class MonarchConditionEditorLabels(label: String? = null, condition: ((position: Int) -> String)? = null, field: String? = null, operator: String? = null, value: String? = null, remove: String? = null, removeItem: ((position: Int) -> String)? = null, add: String? = null, matchBefore: String? = null, matchAfter: String? = null, matchAll: String? = null, matchAny: String? = null, empty: String? = null, choose: String? = null, operators: Map<MonarchConditionOperator, String> = emptyMap(), unknownField: ((key: String) -> String)? = null, removedOption: ((value: String) -> String)? = null, problems: Map<MonarchConditionProblem, String> = emptyMap(), maxReached: ((max: Int) -> String)? = null, chooseDate: String? = null, confirmDate: String? = null, cancel: String? = null)

options.name: value
options.description: The conditions, in order. Ids must be unique.

options.name: onValueChange
options.description: Called with the whole new list after every change: add, remove, field, operator or value.

options.name: fields
options.description: The fields a condition can test. The type decides the operators and the value input; operators narrows them; options are the choices of Select and MultiSelect and the suggestions of Tags. A disabled field stays listed with its reason as a second line.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the editor.

options.name: match
options.description: All or any. With onMatchChange, shown as a segmented switch once there are two conditions.

options.name: onMatchChange
options.description: Called with the new choice of the all / any switch.

options.name: maxConditions
options.description: The most conditions. At this count the add button is replaced by "You can add up to 20 conditions."

options.name: showErrors
options.description: Shows the problem of each incomplete condition on the control that needs attention and outlines the condition in the danger border, for example after a save attempt.

options.name: defaultField
options.description: The key of the field new conditions start on. The first enabled field when null or unknown.

options.name: enabled
options.description: When false every menu, input and button is disabled.

options.name: createId
options.description: Makes the id of a new condition. By default the first free condition-<n>.

options.name: removeIcon
options.description: The icon of each remove button, shown in a Material 3 IconButton. Monarch bundles no icons; without it the button is a small ghost button that reads "Remove".

options.name: addIcon
options.description: An icon before the text of the add button, such as a plus.

options.name: emptyContent
options.description: Replaces the note shown when there are no conditions.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, including the operator names and problem messages.

states.name: empty
states.description: "No conditions. This applies every time." (or emptyContent) above the add button.

states.name: conditions
states.description: One outlined card per condition: heading "Condition 1" with the remove button, then the field menu, the operator menu and the value input, one per line.

states.name: no value
states.description: Operators such as "is empty" and "is yes" show no value input.

states.name: match switch
states.description: From two conditions, with match and onMatchChange: "Match [all | any] of these conditions", wrapping at large text.

states.name: errors
states.description: With showErrors, an incomplete condition takes the danger border and its problem shows as the error of the field menu (no field) or of the value input (no value, not a number, removed option).

states.name: limit reached
states.description: The add button is replaced by a muted note.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Every control and button takes its disabled colors and does nothing.

states.name: removed field or option
states.description: A stored field the list no longer has shows as "key (removed)"; a stored option as "value (removed option)".

appearance: Each condition is a card on the surface fill with the subtle border (the danger border while it shows a problem), with the subheading style for its title. Menus, text fields, the sheet and the date picker take their Monarch and Material 3 theme colors; notes use the muted text color. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those roles.
platformNotes: The web lays field, operator and value side by side in a row; on Android each condition is a card with one control per line, which fits a phone and large text. The web's native selects are MonarchSelect menus, its multiple Combobox and TagInput are one MonarchMultiSelect sheet (free values are created from the search text), and its date input is a button that opens the Material 3 DatePickerDialog. A day is MonarchConditionValue.Date in epoch milliseconds at UTC midnight, not YYYY-MM-DD text, and Eq, Before and After compare the UTC day. A number keeps the typed text (MonarchConditionValue.Number) so half-typed input survives; its number is read with a dot as the decimal separator. The web field's value is called key here, and its disabled flag is enabled. The web's per-control accessible names ("Condition 1 field") are a visible label per control under a heading per condition. The web moves focus after add and remove; Compose leaves focus to the system. The web's messages object is MonarchConditionEditorLabels. Same name as iOS's plan; iOS has not built it yet.
accessibility: Each condition title ("Condition 1") is a heading, so TalkBack can move between conditions by heading.
The remove button is named with the position ("Remove condition 1") and has a 48dp touch target, also when it shows an icon.
The field, operator and value controls keep their Material 3 roles and visible labels; a problem is set as the error of the control that needs attention, in text, not only as the danger border.
The all / any switch is a Material 3 segmented button row; the selected segment is read as selected and sits between the words "Match" and "of these conditions".
When disabled, the add and remove buttons are announced as disabled.
edgeCases: A field removed from fields keeps its conditions: they show "key (removed)" and report the Field problem.
An operator the field no longer offers stays listed first, so a stored condition is shown as stored.
Changing the field starts the condition again on the new field's first operator; changing the operator keeps the value when its shape allows, and converts between one value and a list.
Evaluation is a convenience for previews: text comparisons ignore case, numbers are read from numbers or text, days from epoch milliseconds. The server stays the authority.
Ids are matched to keep each condition's state; give saved conditions their stored ids.

title: ConfirmDialog
wrapsNative: MonarchDialog with a MonarchButton in the Danger variant as its confirm action
summary: Confirming a consequential action is a MonarchDialog whose confirm button is a danger MonarchButton and whose dismiss button is Cancel. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: Before an action that deletes or cannot be undone. Say in the title what will happen and in the text what changes; name the button after the action.
whenNotToUse: Do not confirm actions that are easy to undo: do them and offer undo in a snackbar. For a choice between several options see choice-dialog; for a value see prompt-dialog.
api: @Composable fun MonarchDialog(onDismissRequest: () -> Unit, title: String?, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, description: String? = null, dismissible: Boolean = true, dismissOnClickOutside: Boolean = dismissible, paneTitle: String? = null, actions: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null, content: (@Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)? = null)

@Composable fun MonarchButton(text: String, onClick: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchButtonVariant = MonarchButtonVariant.Secondary, size: MonarchButtonSize = MonarchButtonSize.Md, enabled: Boolean = true, loading: Boolean = false, …)

states.name: asking
states.description: The title, the consequences and two buttons: Cancel (ghost) and the action (danger).

states.name: type to confirm
states.description: A MonarchTextField as the dialog's content; the danger button is disabled until the phrase matches.

states.name: pending
states.description: The danger button is loading and back and outside taps are turned off, so the dialog stays while the action runs.

states.name: failed
states.description: The content shows the error, for example in a MonarchInlineNotice, and the button can be pressed again.

appearance: MonarchDialog in the raised background role with the default and muted text roles. The confirm button is the danger solid role with its on-solid text; Cancel is a ghost button in the default text role. The high-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colors.
platformNotes: The web ConfirmDialog has consequences, a confirm phrase, an acknowledgement checkbox, a reason field, and pending and error states. An Android MonarchDialog stays until the app stops composing it, so all of these fit in its slots: the consequences and fields in text, a loading MonarchButton for pending, and an error message. Material's own buttons have no danger look, so the confirm button is a MonarchButton. iOS uses the system alert, which closes when a button is tapped.
accessibility: System behavior: TalkBack reads the title and text when the dialog opens and stays inside it.
The danger button says the action ("Delete") so the meaning does not depend on its color.
A loading MonarchButton is announced as busy and ignores taps while the action runs.
Back calls onDismissRequest, which is Cancel, unless it is turned off while pending.
edgeCases: Do not put the danger button where a quick double tap on the opening control would hit it; MonarchDialog places it at the end, after Cancel.
The type-to-confirm phrase compares the exact text; trim or ignore case if the product allows it.

summary: The apps a person signed in to with their account: logo, name, domain, Verified and Suspended badges, when it was connected and last used, the workspace and what it can access, with Remove access behind a confirmation.
whenToUse: On an account's security or privacy screen, so people can see which apps use their account and take access back.
whenNotToUse: For the devices signed in to the account, use MonarchDeviceList. For API keys or tokens the person created, use a list of their own with MonarchSecretField.

options.name: modifier

options.name: state

options.name: title

options.name: description

options.name: retrying
