options.description: Asks before removing access. Turn it off when onRevoke shows the app's own confirmation.

options.name: now
options.description: The reference time for "3 days ago", in epoch milliseconds. Without it the times follow the clock, refreshed every minute.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Retries loading. Adds Try again to the error state.

options.name: onRevoke
options.description: Removes an app's access; remove the app from apps when it returns. Adds Remove access to every row; the row's button is busy while it runs. A thrown exception's message, or a built-in sentence, is shown under the row and announced.

options.name: labels

states.name: ready

states.name: loading

states.name: error

states.name: confirming

states.name: removing

states.name: removal failed

states.name: suspended app
states.description: The name is muted and a warning Suspended badge follows it.

appearance: A MonarchCard with the section header, rows separated by subtle dividers, names in the strong body style, domain, times and workspace in the caption style in the muted color, a success Verified badge and a warning Suspended badge, and a small danger button. All are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The parity map names a LazyColumn; the rows are a plain Column in a MonarchCard instead, because the list is short and sits inside the app's scrolling settings screen, where a LazyColumn without a fixed height cannot be measured (iOS makes the same choice). The confirmation is the Material 3 AlertDialog with MonarchButtons (the confirm dialog on Android). It closes when confirmed, so, as on iOS, the progress moves to the row's button and a failure appears under the row, where the web keeps both inside the dialog. The logo is a Painter the app loads (Monarch adds no image loader), where the web and iOS take a URL. onRevoke is a suspend function that receives the whole app, where the web passes the id. The web's SectionCard is MonarchSectionHeader inside MonarchCard; its headingLevel has no Android equivalent: the title is a heading. The web's danger-subtle button variant does not exist on Android; the danger variant is used. Times are epoch milliseconds formatted by DateUtils in the device's locale; the web's locale prop is not offered.
accessibility: The title is a heading, from MonarchSectionHeader; the list is a traversal group named "Connected apps".
Each app's name, badges, domain, times and workspace are one element: the name as its content description and the rest as its state, built by a tested pure function.
Each scope list is a group named "What Notes can access".
The logo is decorative.
Remove access is a MonarchButton named "Remove access for Notes" with a 48dp touch target and a busy state; the confirmation is a Material 3 alert dialog.
Removal and failures are announced through a polite live region; a failure is also shown as text.
Badges are words, so the verified and suspended states do not depend on color.
edgeCases: A missing logo shows the first letter of the name.
An app with no times, domain or scopes shows only its name and badges.
Two removals can run at once; each row tracks its own progress and failure.
Long names wrap and the badges move to the next line.
A removal that is still running when the list leaves the screen is cancelled with it.

name: MonarchConsentHistory
title: ConsentHistory
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of bordered records with androidx.compose.material3.Text, android.icu.text.DateFormat and android.text.format.DateUtils.getRelativeTimeSpanString, MonarchEmptyState and MonarchButton
summary: A person's recorded consent decisions, newest first: when, how, which policy version and rules applied, and each category allowed or not.
whenToUse: On a privacy screen where people see what they agreed to, or in an admin view of one person's consent.
whenNotToUse: To ask for consent or change it, use a consent preferences sheet or MonarchMarketingConsentCheckbox. For permissions the system grants, such as notifications or location, use the system permission request.
api: @Composable fun MonarchConsentHistory(records: List<MonarchConsentRecord>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, categories: List<MonarchConsentCategory> = emptyList(), title: String? = null, description: String? = null, showRelativeTime: Boolean = false, formatDate: ((Long) -> String)? = null, exportTitle: String? = null, onExport: (suspend () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchConsentHistoryLabels = MonarchConsentHistoryLabels())

class MonarchConsentRecord(id: String, dateMillis: Long, method: MonarchConsentMethod, policyVersion: String, regime: MonarchConsentRegime, categories: Map<String, Boolean>, globalPrivacyControl: Boolean = false)
enum class MonarchConsentMethod { AcceptAll, RejectAll, Custom, GlobalPrivacyControl, Acknowledged, Withdrawn }
enum class MonarchConsentRegime { OptIn, OptOut, Notice }
class MonarchConsentCategory(id: String, label: String)

class MonarchConsentHistoryLabels(method: ((MonarchConsentMethod) -> String)? = null, regime: ((MonarchConsentRegime) -> String)? = null, methodTitle: String? = null, policyVersionTitle: String? = null, regimeTitle: String? = null, categoriesTitle: String? = null, allowed: String? = null, denied: String? = null, signalPresent: String? = null, emptyTitle: String? = null, emptyMessage: String? = null, exportFailed: String? = null)

options.name: records
options.description: The decisions, in any order; shown newest first.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the history.

options.name: categories
options.description: The product's categories, for their names and order. Ids in a record that are not listed are shown as the raw id, after the listed ones, sorted.

options.name: title
options.description: The heading; "Consent history" when null.

options.name: description
options.description: A sentence under the heading.

options.name: showRelativeTime
options.description: Also shows how long ago each decision was ("3 days ago"), updated every minute.

options.name: formatDate
options.description: Formats each decision's date. By default a medium date and short time in the configuration's locale and the device's time zone.

options.name: exportTitle
options.description: The title of the download button; name the format. "Download history" when null.

options.name: onExport
options.description: Builds and shares the file, for example with a CreateDocument launcher or a share sheet. The button shows while there are records and is busy while this runs; throwing shows the export failure.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the methods, regimes, line names, Allowed and Not allowed, the signal note, the empty state and the export failure.

states.name: records
states.description: One bordered record per decision on the surface color.

states.name: empty
states.description: A small MonarchEmptyState and no download button.

states.name: exporting
states.description: The download button shows its progress indicator, reads "Loading" and ignores taps.

states.name: export failed
states.description: "The download did not start. Try again." in the danger strong color under the header, announced; the button can be used again.

appearance: Records use the surface color, a subtle border and 12dp corners. Dates use the strong body style; line names the caption style in the muted color; values the body style. Allowed categories have "Allowed" in the success strong color, refused ones "Not allowed" in the muted color. All are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The parity map names a LazyColumn; the records are a plain Column instead, because a consent history is short and sits inside a scrolling screen, where a LazyColumn without a fixed height cannot be measured. The web shows a table on wide containers and stacked cards below 640 points; Android always shows the stacked records, as iOS does. Dates are epoch milliseconds; the web's locale and timeZone props and iOS's dateFormat are replaced by formatDate, and relative times follow the system clock. The web's headingLevel has no Android equivalent: the title and dates have the heading semantics. The categories show their state in words without the iOS check and cross symbols, because Monarch bundles no icons. onExport is a suspend function; a failure always shows the exportFailed text. The record types are defined here because the consent manager is not built on Android; a later consent preferences component should use them. The parity map lists badge as a dependency; the method is plain text, as on the web and iOS.
accessibility: The title and each decision's date are headings, so TalkBack's heading navigation moves between decisions.
Each line is one element read as its name, value and any note ("Choice, Custom choice, Browser privacy signal present").
Each category is one element read as its name and "Allowed" or "Not allowed", so the state does not depend on color.
The download button is a MonarchButton with a 48dp touch target and a busy state while exporting.
The export failure is announced through a polite live region.
edgeCases: Records with the same date keep the order they were given in.
A record with no categories shows no categories list.
The relative time is static text refreshed every minute, not a ticking clock.
Long policy versions and category names wrap.

title: ConsentProvider
wrapsNative: The app's own state holder (a view model or rememberSaveable) of MonarchConsentRecord, with MonarchBanner and MonarchButtons for the first ask and MonarchBottomSheet holding MonarchConsentPreferences
summary: A recipe, not a component: the app keeps the person's consent as a MonarchConsentRecord, asks once with equal Reject all and Accept all buttons, shows the choices in a sheet with MonarchConsentPreferences, and gates its SDKs on the stored record.
whenToUse: In an app that runs analytics, advertising or other optional processing that needs consent, on first launch and from a "Privacy choices" entry in its settings.
whenNotToUse: For data the app needs to work (sign-in, security), ask for nothing: list it as a required category. For Android runtime permissions (location, camera), use the system permission request.
api: var record by remember { mutableStateOf<MonarchConsentRecord?>(null) } // or the app's settings store
MonarchConsentRecord(id = …, dateMillis = …, method = method, policyVersion = "2026-01", regime = MonarchConsentRegime.OptIn, categories = decided)
MonarchBanner(message = …, title = "Your privacy choices") with MonarchButton("Reject all", …) and MonarchButton("Accept all", …)
ModalBottomSheet(onDismissRequest = …) { MonarchConsentPreferences(categories = categories, onDecide = decide, choices = record?.categories.orEmpty(), record = record) }

options.name: regime
options.description: Decided by the app (usually its server, from the person's region): OptIn asks before anything optional runs, OptOut runs until the person says no (MonarchConsentPreferencesMode.Choice for "Do not sell or share"), Notice only informs.

options.name: policyVersion
options.description: The version of the privacy policy the person decided on. Ask again when it changes.

options.name: record
options.description: The last decision. null means the person has not been asked.

states.name: not asked
states.description: No record: a banner with Reject all, Accept all (equal buttons) and Choose; nothing optional runs.

states.name: choosing
states.description: A sheet with MonarchConsentPreferences: a switch per optional category, required ones always on, and Save, Reject all and Accept all.

states.name: decided
states.description: A record with the method, the date, the policy version, the regime and the categories; the banner is gone and the app starts only the allowed SDKs.

states.name: changed
states.description: Privacy choices reopens the sheet with the stored choices and the date of the last decision; a new record replaces it.

appearance: The banner is MonarchBanner in the info tone; Reject all and Accept all are secondary MonarchButtons of equal weight so neither is pushed; the sheet is the Material 3 sheet surface with MonarchConsentPreferences. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web's ConsentManager is a provider that decides the regime from the visitor's jurisdiction, honours Global Privacy Control, records each decision and feeds the cookie banner, preferences dialog and ConsentGate. Android has no system consent prompt and no Global Privacy Control signal, so the provider is the app's own state: a view model or settings store holding MonarchConsentRecord, the regime from the app's server, and if-checks before starting an SDK in place of ConsentGate. Monarch ships no type for it because the storage and the gating are the app's. iOS documents App Tracking Transparency as a native entry instead; an Android app that also shows ads follows Google Play's own consent requirements (for example the User Messaging Platform), which Monarch does not wrap.
accessibility: The banner is read with its title and message by MonarchBanner; the buttons follow it in reading order.
Reject all and Accept all are buttons with the same size and variant, so neither is easier to reach.
MonarchConsentPreferences gives each category a switch with its name, description and state, and announces when choices are saved.
The sheet's content scrolls, so every category is reachable at the largest font scale.
edgeCases: Store the record before starting any optional SDK; until then treat every optional category as off.
When policyVersion changes, ask again: clear the record or compare its version.
Withdrawal (MonarchConsentPreferences' Withdraw) writes a record that turns every optional category off; stop the SDKs at once.
Keep the history of records on the server; show it with MonarchConsentHistory.

name: MonarchConsentPreferences
title: ConsentPreferences
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column for the content of a MonarchBottomSheet: MonarchSwitchRow (MonarchSwitch) per category, MonarchLink to the policy, MonarchButtons
summary: Privacy choices for a sheet: one switch per category of optional storage or processing, with Reject all, Accept all and Save choices, the saved policy version and time, and Withdraw consent.
whenToUse: Where people choose or change which optional uses of their data the app may turn on, such as analytics or advertising, usually from a Privacy choices item in settings.
whenNotToUse: For marketing messages, use MonarchMarketingConsentCheckbox. For agreeing to the terms on sign-up, use MonarchTermsAcceptance. For what people decided before, use MonarchConsentHistory. For system permissions such as location or notifications, use the system permission request.
api: @Composable fun MonarchConsentPreferences(categories: List<MonarchConsentPreferencesCategory>, onDecide: (MonarchConsentMethod, Map<String, Boolean>) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, choices: Map<String, Boolean> = emptyMap(), mode: MonarchConsentPreferencesMode = MonarchConsentPreferencesMode.Categories, globalPrivacyControl: Boolean = false, record: MonarchConsentRecord? = null, allowWithdraw: Boolean = true, now: Long? = null, onPolicyClick: (() -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchConsentPreferencesLabels = MonarchConsentPreferencesLabels())
class MonarchConsentPreferencesCategory(id: String, label: String, description: String, required: Boolean = false, saleOrSharing: Boolean = false)
enum class MonarchConsentPreferencesMode { Categories, Choice }

class MonarchConsentPreferencesLabels(title: String? = null, description: String? = null, policy: String? = null, alwaysOn: String? = null, globalPrivacyControl: String? = null, on: String? = null, off: String? = null, rejectAll: String? = null, acceptAll: String? = null, save: String? = null, withdraw: String? = null, policyVersion: String? = null, saved: String? = null)

options.name: categories
options.description: The categories in order, each with a name, a description, and whether it is strictly necessary or sells or shares data.

options.name: onDecide
options.description: Called when a button is pressed, with AcceptAll, RejectAll, Custom or Withdrawn and every category's state with the locks applied. Store the record and close the sheet here.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the content. Add verticalScroll and padding inside a sheet.

options.name: choices
options.description: The saved choice by category id. Leave it empty until the person has chosen, so nothing optional is on.

options.name: mode
options.description: Categories: a switch per category and Save choices. Choice: the status of each category and only Reject all and Accept all.

options.name: globalPrivacyControl
options.description: Whether a Global Privacy Control signal is on. Sale-or-sharing categories stay off with a note.

options.name: record
options.description: The saved decision: shows "Policy version 3 · Saved 2 days ago" and allows Withdraw consent.

options.name: allowWithdraw
options.description: Whether Withdraw consent is offered in categories mode when a decision is saved and not already withdrawn.

options.name: now
options.description: The reference time for the saved time, in epoch milliseconds. The clock by default, refreshed every minute.

options.name: onPolicyClick
options.description: Opens the privacy policy and adds the "Privacy policy" link under the description.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, to translate or to use the legal team's wording.

states.name: first time
states.description: Every optional switch is off; required ones are on, disabled and say "Always on".

states.name: saved
states.description: Switches show the saved choice; the record line and Withdraw consent appear.

states.name: Global Privacy Control
states.description: Sale-or-sharing switches are off and disabled, with a note saying why.

states.name: choice mode
states.description: Each category shows On (success strong), Off or Always on as a word; only Reject all and Accept all are offered.

appearance: No container of its own (the sheet is the surface): the title in the heading style, the description in the body style in the muted color, Material 3 switches in the Monarch accent with names in the body style and descriptions in the caption style, and secondary Reject all and Accept all with a primary Save choices. All are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web dialog reads and writes a ConsentProvider; on Android the app passes the categories, saved choices and record and stores the decision from onDecide, because consent storage is the app's. The parity map names a MonarchBottomSheet: the component is the content of a sheet the app shows and closes, as on iOS, so the app keeps the sheet's state and can close it after storing the decision; the example shows the MonarchBottomSheet. The switches the person moves are kept by the component until a button is pressed and start again from choices when it changes. The record type is the shared MonarchConsentRecord and the method is MonarchConsentMethod, as in MonarchConsentHistory. The web's policyHref and policyLink are onPolicyClick. A Global Privacy Control signal is a browser feature; on Android the app passes it if it honours an equivalent setting. The web's default wording speaks of cookies; on Android the built-in wording speaks of optional uses of data. A saved decision older than seven days shows its date.
accessibility: The title is a heading.
Each category is a MonarchSwitchRow: one element with the switch role, its name, and its description with any note, so TalkBack says why a locked switch cannot change.
Locked switches are disabled switches.
In choice mode each category is one element with its name and description as the content description and its status word as the state.
Buttons are MonarchButtons with 48dp touch targets; Reject all and Accept all wrap onto separate lines when they do not fit side by side.
The policy link is a MonarchLink with a 48dp touch target.
edgeCases: Required categories are reported on and signal-locked ones off whatever the person chose.
Every decision reports every category, including ones missing from choices.
A saved decision older than seven days shows its date instead of a relative time.
Withdraw consent is not offered when the saved decision is already a withdrawal.

parityExceptions.reason: The web shows the preferences as a centred dialog with a close button, opened from a link. Android shows the same content in a bottom sheet (drag handle, swipe down to close) opened from a button, because a modal bottom sheet is the platform's surface for a choice sheet. The title, copy, policy link, the four categories with Always on beside the first switch, and Reject all, Accept all and Save choices in that order are the web's.
parityExceptions.convention: Material 3 modal bottom sheet for a sheet of choices

name: MonarchConsequenceList
title: ConsequenceList
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column, androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row, androidx.compose.material3.Text, MonarchSkeleton
summary: A list of what an action deletes, changes and keeps, and what to know first, to read before confirming.
whenToUse: Inside a confirmation dialog or a destructive flow, such as deleting a project or removing a member, to state plainly what will happen.
whenNotToUse: For a single sentence of warning, use the text of the dialog or MonarchInlineNotice. For a list of errors, use the error states of the form.
api: @Composable fun MonarchConsequenceList(items: List<MonarchConsequence>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, grouped: Boolean = false, loading: Boolean = false, heading: String? = null, icon: (@Composable (MonarchConsequenceKind) -> Unit)? = null, loadingRowCount: Int = MonarchConsequenceListTokens.DEFAULT_LOADING_ROWS, kindLabel: ((MonarchConsequenceKind) -> String)? = null, groupTitle: ((MonarchConsequenceKind) -> String)? = null, loadingLabel: String? = null)
class MonarchConsequence(val kind: MonarchConsequenceKind, val label: String, val detail: String? = null, val count: Int? = null, val id: String? = null)
enum class MonarchConsequenceKind { Removed, Changed, Warning, Kept }

options.name: items
options.description: The consequences, in reading order.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the list.

options.name: grouped
options.description: Splits the items under a heading per kind: removed, changed, warning, kept.

options.name: loading
options.description: Shows placeholder rows instead of the items.

options.name: heading
options.description: A heading above the list, such as "What happens".

options.name: icon
options.description: The icon of a kind, tinted by kind and hidden from TalkBack. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: loadingRowCount
options.description: Placeholder rows while loading. Values below 1 count as 1.

options.name: kindLabel
options.description: The word read before an ungrouped row. null uses monarch_consequencelist_kind_*.

options.name: groupTitle
options.description: The heading of a group. null uses monarch_consequencelist_group_*.

options.name: loadingLabel
options.description: What TalkBack reads for the placeholder rows. null uses monarch_consequencelist_loading.

states.name: ungrouped
states.description: Rows in the given order; TalkBack reads the kind before each row.

states.name: grouped
states.description: One block per kind that has items, under its heading, in the order removed, changed, warning, kept.

states.name: loading
states.description: Placeholder rows that shimmer unless animations are off, read as one element.

appearance: Rows of body text in the default text color with muted caption details. The count is semibold with tabular figures, in the danger strong color for removed items. Icons are danger strong for removed, muted for changed, warning strong for warnings and success strong for kept. Group headings are muted label text. The same roles in every theme.
platformNotes: The web error slot is not offered: when the consequences cannot be worked out, show MonarchInlineErrorRetry in place of the list. Monarch bundles no icons, so the per-kind icons the web draws are a slot that receives the kind; without it, the label must say what happens. The count is formatted with java.text.NumberFormat in the locale of the configuration; there is no locale parameter. label and detail are Strings where the web takes any content. The heading level option has no equivalent: headings are marked as headings. The loading rows are MonarchSkeleton, as on the web; iOS uses the system redaction.
accessibility: Each row is one TalkBack element. Ungrouped, it is read as the kind word, the count and label, then the detail.
Grouped, the kind word is left out of the row, because the group heading says it; group headings and the list heading are marked as headings.
With icons, each kind has its own shape, so the kind does not depend on color. Icons are hidden from TalkBack.
While loading, the placeholder rows are one element read as "Checking what will change". Nothing is announced when loading starts or ends.
Text wraps and is not cut off at the largest font size.
edgeCases: Without icons, ungrouped rows have no visual kind marker other than the color of a removed count; write the label so it says what happens.
Kinds with no items have no group and no heading.
Large counts are grouped by the locale, for example 12,000.

title: Container
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.widthIn, androidx.compose.foundation.layout.windowInsetsPadding with WindowInsets.safeDrawing, androidx.compose.material3.adaptive.currentWindowAdaptiveInfoV2
summary: Centring screen content at a maximum width with side gutters is widthIn(max =) inside a centered Box, horizontal padding chosen by the window size class and the window insets. Monarch ships nothing and documents the widths and gutters.
whenToUse: On windows that can be wide (tablets, foldables, landscape, desktop windows) to stop text and forms from stretching: cap the width at 704dp for reading and forms, 1152dp for app screens or 1280dp for dashboards, and pad by 16dp on a compact window and 24dp from a medium window (600dp) up.
whenNotToUse: Not for full-bleed content (maps, media, a canvas) or for a list-detail layout, which uses ListDetailPaneScaffold. Inside a Scaffold, apply the Scaffold's content padding as well; it already includes the system bar insets.
api: fun Modifier.widthIn(min: Dp = Dp.Unspecified, max: Dp = Dp.Unspecified): Modifier
fun Modifier.windowInsetsPadding(insets: WindowInsets): Modifier
fun WindowInsets.only(sides: WindowInsetsSides): WindowInsets
@Composable fun currentWindowAdaptiveInfoV2(): WindowAdaptiveInfo
fun WindowSizeClass.isWidthAtLeastBreakpoint(widthDpBreakpoint: Int): Boolean

states.name: compact window
states.description: Narrower than 600dp: 16dp gutters (space4).

states.name: medium window and wider
states.description: 600dp and wider: 24dp gutters (space6); the maximum width starts to apply.

appearance: No appearance of its own. The gutters are steps of the Monarch space scale.
platformNotes: The web's Container has sizes narrow (44rem, 704px), content (72rem, 1152px), wide (80rem, 1280px) and full, and gutters of 16px that become 24px from 768px. The native tokens carry no width tokens, so the widths are written in the app in dp; the gutters are space4 and space6. Android's window size classes replace the 768px breakpoint with the medium class at 600dp. Display cutouts and the navigation bar in landscape are handled by the safe-drawing insets, which the web does not need. iOS uses frame(maxWidth:) and the horizontal size class in the same way.
accessibility: No behavior of its own: TalkBack reads the content in order.
A maximum width keeps lines short at font scale 2.0 on large windows; text inside still wraps.
edgeCases: widthIn(max =) must come before fillMaxWidth(), or the content takes the full width.
Without the inset padding, content in landscape can sit under a display cutout or the navigation bar.

examples.title: Sizes

parityExceptions.reason: The web example shows the three blocks at 574px, the width of its page, so narrow, content and wide look alike there; the Android window is 344dp, narrower than the narrowest container width (704dp), so the three blocks are alike too. A thin border is drawn on each block so it can be told from the canvas in the light theme.
parityExceptions.convention: Material adaptive layout: a compact window is narrower than every container width

title: ContextMenu
wrapsNative: MonarchMenu opened from androidx.compose.foundation.combinedClickable(onLongClick = …)
summary: A context menu is a MonarchMenu that opens when the person touches and holds an element, through Modifier.combinedClickable(onLongClick = …). Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: For shortcuts to actions on an item in a list or a grid: copy, share, delete. Every action must also be reachable another way, such as a visible More button or the item's own screen.
whenNotToUse: Not as the only way to an action: a long press cannot be seen. Not for actions of a whole screen: use the top app bar's overflow menu.
api: fun Modifier.combinedClickable(interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null, indication: Indication? = null, enabled: Boolean = true, onClickLabel: String? = null, role: Role? = null, onLongClickLabel: String? = null, onLongClick: (() -> Unit)? = null, onDoubleClick: (() -> Unit)? = null, hapticFeedbackEnabled: Boolean = true, onClick: () -> Unit): Modifier

@Composable fun MonarchMenu(expanded: Boolean, onDismissRequest: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, offset: DpOffset = DpOffset(MonarchTokens.Space.space0.dp, MonarchTokens.Space.space1.dp), content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)
var SemanticsPropertyReceiver.customActions: List<CustomAccessibilityAction>

states.name: closed
states.description: A tap opens the item; a long press opens the menu, with haptic feedback.

states.name: open
states.description: The menu is anchored to the item and takes focus; back or a tap outside closes it.

states.name: through TalkBack
states.description: The long-click label and custom actions appear in TalkBack's actions menu.

appearance: The menu is a MonarchMenu in the raised background role with Monarch's medium radius; items use the default text role, and a destructive item the strong danger role. The high-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colors.
platformNotes: The web ContextMenu opens on right-click, Shift F10 or a long press and is composed of Monarch-styled items, checkboxes, radio groups and submenus. On Android a long press opens a MonarchMenu with the same parts as dropdown-menu, anchored to the item rather than at the touch point. A secondary click with a mouse is not a separate event in combinedClickable; a pointer user gets the visible More button. The web's label and modal props have no equivalent. iOS uses contextMenu.
accessibility: onLongClickLabel names the long press, so TalkBack says "double tap and hold to show actions".
Custom accessibility actions expose each menu action directly in TalkBack's actions menu, without opening the menu.
A visible More button opens the same menu, for people who cannot long press and for pointer users.
Items have 48dp touch targets and the menu closes on back.
edgeCases: A long press also starts text selection or drag and drop where those are enabled on the same element; do not combine them.
Place the MonarchMenu in the same Box as the item so it opens next to it.

name: MonarchCookieConsentBanner
title: CookieConsentBanner
wrapsNative: MonarchButton, androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
summary: The first-run consent card of an app that uses cookies or similar tracking: a title, the explanation with a link to the policy, and the choices of the regime (opt-in, opt-out or notice).
whenToUse: On first run of an app, or of web content inside it, that sets optional cookies or tracking and must ask or inform before it does.
whenNotToUse: For the detailed per-category choices, use consent-preferences behind "Customize". For the system tracking prompt on iOS, use the platform API.
api: @Composable fun MonarchCookieConsentBanner(regime: MonarchCookieConsentRegime, onDecide: (MonarchCookieConsentChoice) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, onCustomize: (() -> Unit)? = null, onPolicyClick: (() -> Unit)? = null, announce: Boolean = false, labels: MonarchCookieConsentBannerLabels = MonarchCookieConsentBannerLabels())
enum class MonarchCookieConsentRegime { OptIn, OptOut, Notice }
enum class MonarchCookieConsentChoice { AcceptAll, RejectAll, Acknowledge, DoNotSell }

class MonarchCookieConsentBannerLabels(title: String? = null, description: String? = null, acceptAll: String? = null, rejectAll: String? = null, customize: String? = null, acknowledge: String? = null, doNotSell: String? = null, policy: String? = null)

options.name: regime
options.description: OptIn (Customize, Reject all, Accept all), OptOut (Do not sell or share my personal information, OK) or Notice (OK); it also picks the explanation.

options.name: onDecide
options.description: Called with the choice; the app stores it and stops showing the card.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the card.

options.name: onCustomize
options.description: Opens the app's detailed preferences; null hides "Customize". Opt-in only.

options.name: onPolicyClick
options.description: Opens the cookie policy; null shows no "Cookie policy" link.

options.name: announce
options.description: Whether TalkBack reads the card when it appears (a polite live region).

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the title, the explanation and each button and link.

states.name: opt-in
states.description: "Customize" as a ghost button, then "Reject all" and "Accept all" with the same look.

states.name: opt-out
states.description: "Do not sell or share my personal information" and "OK".

states.name: notice
states.description: "OK" only.

appearance: A raised card: the raised surface with a subtle border and the large shadow, the title in the default text, the explanation muted and the policy link in the link colour, underlined. Reject and accept are both secondary buttons. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web banner is fixed to the bottom of the viewport (or a corner card), reads and stores the decision through ConsentProvider, and honours the browser's Global Privacy Control signal. On Android the card is placed by the app (a Scaffold's bottomBar or above the content), and the app stores the decision from onDecide; there is no Global Privacy Control signal in an app. Positions bottom-start, bottom-end and bottom-center are not offered.
accessibility: The card is a pane named by its title, and a traversal group read before its buttons.
The title is a heading; the policy link is a link inside the explanation.
Every button has a touch target of at least 48dp; reject and accept look the same, so neither is suggested by colour.
With announce, the card is a polite live region.
edgeCases: Long translations wrap the buttons onto more lines.
Without onPolicyClick the explanation ends without a link.

examples.title: Opt-in (ask first)
examples.code:
MonarchCookieConsentBanner(
    regime = MonarchCookieConsentRegime.OptIn,
    onDecide = { decision = it },
    onCustomize = { preferencesOpen = true },
    onPolicyClick = { policyOpen = true },
)

    regime = MonarchCookieConsentRegime.OptOut,
    onDecide = { decision = it },
    labels = MonarchCookieConsentBannerLabels(title = "Your privacy choices"),
)

examples.setup: var decision by remember { mutableStateOf<MonarchCookieConsentChoice?>(null) }

    onDecide = { decision = it },
    labels = MonarchCookieConsentBannerLabels(title = "About cookies"),
)

name: MonarchCopyButton
title: CopyButton
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.ui.platform.LocalClipboard (Clipboard.setClipEntry), androidx.compose.material3.Button, androidx.compose.material3.IconButton
summary: A button that copies a string to the clipboard, plays the confirm haptic, announces "Copied to clipboard" and, below Android 13, shows a short "Copied" state.
whenToUse: Next to a value people paste elsewhere: a link, an ID, an API key, a command.
whenNotToUse: To send a link to another app use the Sharesheet (ShareButton), which already offers Copy. Do not put a copy button on text the user can select and copy in place unless the value is long or hidden.
api: @Composable fun MonarchCopyButton(value: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchButtonVariant = MonarchButtonVariant.Secondary, size: MonarchButtonSize = MonarchButtonSize.Md, enabled: Boolean = true, sensitive: Boolean = false, showConfirmation: Boolean = Build.VERSION.SDK_INT < Build.VERSION_CODES.TIRAMISU, resetAfterMillis: Long = 2000L, target: String? = null, leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, copiedIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, onCopy: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, label: String? = null, copiedLabel: String? = null, copiedAnnouncement: String? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)

@Composable fun MonarchCopyButton(value: String, icon: @Composable () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, sensitive: Boolean = false, showConfirmation: Boolean = Build.VERSION.SDK_INT < Build.VERSION_CODES.TIRAMISU, resetAfterMillis: Long = 2000L, target: String? = null, copiedIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, onCopy: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, label: String? = null, copiedLabel: String? = null, copiedAnnouncement: String? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)

options.name: value
options.description: The text to copy, written as a plain-text clip.

options.name: icon
options.description: Icon-only overload: the copy icon. Passing it selects that overload. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: leadingIcon
options.description: Text overload: an icon before the label.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the button.

options.name: variant
options.description: Primary, Secondary, Ghost or Danger. Text overload only; the icon-only button has no fill.

options.name: size
options.description: Sm, Md or Lg. Text overload only.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the user can copy.

options.name: sensitive
options.description: Marks the clip with ClipDescription.EXTRA_IS_SENSITIVE, so Android 13 and later hide its content in the clipboard preview.

options.name: showConfirmation
options.description: Shows the copied label and copiedIcon after a copy. Android 13 and later show their own clipboard confirmation, so it is off there by default.

options.name: resetAfterMillis
options.description: How long the copied state lasts. Zero keeps it until the button leaves the composition.

options.name: target
options.description: What is copied, added to the spoken name: "Copy webhook URL". Also the label of the clip.

options.name: copiedIcon
options.description: The icon of the copied state, such as a check mark. Without it the idle icon stays.

options.name: onCopy
options.description: Called with the copied text after each copy.

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the built-in label "Copy" (monarch_copybutton_copy).

options.name: copiedLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in label "Copied" (monarch_copybutton_copied).

options.name: copiedAnnouncement
options.description: Replaces the built-in state "Copied to clipboard" (monarch_copybutton_copied_announcement).

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the press, focus and hover interactions.

states.name: idle
states.description: The icon and the label "Copy".

states.name: copied
states.description: For resetAfterMillis: TalkBack reads "Copied to clipboard" as the state. With showConfirmation the label reads "Copied" and copiedIcon replaces the icon. A second copy restarts the time.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The disabled colors of the variant; taps do nothing.

appearance: The text button has the colors of its MonarchButton variant. The icon-only button has no fill and uses the default text color, or the disabled text color when disabled. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web component has an error state because a browser can refuse a clipboard write; writing with the Android Clipboard does not report a failure, so there is no error state, as on iOS. The web value can be a function or a promise; here it is a string. Monarch bundles no icons, so the copy and check icons are slots. Android 13 and later show a system confirmation of every copy, and Android asks apps not to duplicate it, so the visual copied state is off there by default (showConfirmation); the spoken "Copied to clipboard" is kept on every version, because whether TalkBack reads the system confirmation was not verified. Android adds sensitive, which hides passwords and keys in the system preview. The icon-only form is a separate overload over the Material 3 IconButton; the web default variant for it is ghost, which matches.
accessibility: The text form is a MonarchButton and the icon-only form an IconButton, so each has the Button role, its disabled state and a touch target of at least 48dp.
The spoken name is the label followed by target ("Copy webhook URL"), so several copy buttons on a screen have different names. With the icon-only form the label is still the name.
The button is a polite live region; after a copy its state description is "Copied to clipboard" until the copied state ends, so TalkBack announces it.
With showConfirmation the copied state is a changed label and, when given, a changed icon, not a color.
Both labels share one cell, so the button keeps the width of the longer one; at font scale 2.0 the label wraps and the button grows.
The icon is at the start in both layout directions.
The confirm haptic follows the system haptics setting.
edgeCases: resetAfterMillis of zero keeps the copied state until the button leaves the composition.
The icon (or leadingIcon) is the idle icon; the copied icon is a separate slot.
The value is written as a plain-text clip and replaces what was on the clipboard.
Below Android 13 the sensitive flag is written but ignored by the system.

}

name: MonarchCopyField
title: CopyField
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedTextField (readOnly), MonarchCopyButton (androidx.compose.ui.platform.LocalClipboard)
summary: A read-only value in an outlined field with a copy button, for links, records, keys and snippets.
whenToUse: For a value people copy into another tool: a webhook URL, a DNS record, an API key, an embed snippet, a calendar feed link.
whenNotToUse: For a short value inside running text, use MonarchCopyButton beside it. For a value people edit, use MonarchTextField. To send a link to another app, use the Sharesheet.
api: @Composable fun MonarchCopyField(value: String, label: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, multiline: Boolean = false, monospace: Boolean = true, sensitive: Boolean = false, showConfirmation: Boolean = Build.VERSION.SDK_INT < Build.VERSION_CODES.TIRAMISU, resetAfterMillis: Long = 2000L, helperText: String? = null, copyIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, copiedIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, onCopy: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, copyLabel: String? = null, copiedLabel: String? = null, copiedAnnouncement: String? = null)

options.name: value
options.description: The read-only value shown and copied.

options.name: label
options.description: What the value is: the field's floating label and the end of the copy button's spoken name ("Copy Webhook URL").

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the field and its button.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the value can be copied; a disabled field uses the disabled colors.

options.name: multiline
options.description: Shows the whole value on several lines.

options.name: monospace
options.description: Shows the value in the code style.

options.name: sensitive
options.description: Marks the clip as sensitive, so Android 13 and later hide it in the clipboard preview.

options.name: showConfirmation
options.description: Shows the copied state on the button; by default only below Android 13, where the system shows no confirmation.

options.name: resetAfterMillis
options.description: How long the copied state lasts. Zero keeps it.

options.name: helperText
options.description: A line under the field.

options.name: copyIcon
options.description: A copy icon. Given, the button is an icon button inside the field at the end; otherwise a text button beside the field.

options.name: copiedIcon
options.description: The icon of the copied state, such as a check mark.

options.name: onCopy
options.description: Called with the copied text after each copy.

options.name: copyLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in button text "Copy" (monarch_copybutton_copy).

options.name: copiedLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in button text "Copied" (monarch_copybutton_copied).

options.name: copiedAnnouncement
options.description: Replaces the built-in state "Copied to clipboard" (monarch_copybutton_copied_announcement).

options.name: labelVisible
options.description: Whether the label shows above the field. False keeps it as the spoken name only.

states.name: idle
states.description: The value in the field and the button "Copy".

states.name: copied
states.description: For resetAfterMillis the button's state is "Copied to clipboard"; with showConfirmation its label reads "Copied" and copiedIcon replaces the icon.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The field and the button use the disabled colors; the button does not copy.

appearance: The field has the MonarchTextField colors: the surface fill, the input border, the muted floating label and default text, or the subtle fill and disabled text when disabled. The text button is a secondary MonarchButton; the icon button uses the default text color. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Built on OutlinedTextField directly, with MonarchTextField's colors, because MonarchTextField has no text style option and the value is shown in the code style by default. The web selects the value on focus and selects it again when the clipboard write fails; writing with the Android Clipboard does not report a failure, so there is no onCopyError, and the value can be selected by touch and hold in the read-only field. The web's rows option is not offered: a multi-line field shows the whole value, as on iOS. The web's size option is not offered: the field has the Material height of 56dp and the text button is the Lg MonarchButton next to it. The web's copyButtonProps pass-through is not offered. The web's iconOnly is copyIcon here, because Monarch bundles no icons; as on the web the icon button is still named "Copy" and the label. Android adds sensitive and showConfirmation from MonarchCopyButton.
accessibility: The field is a read-only text field: TalkBack reads the label and the whole value, and the value can be selected and copied by touch and hold.
The copy button is a separate element with a touch target of at least 48dp, named with the label: "Copy Webhook URL".
After a copy the button's state description is "Copied to clipboard" in a polite live region.
The text button follows the field in both layout directions and takes at most a third of the row, so a long label or a large font wraps it instead of squeezing the field.
edgeCases: A long single-line value scrolls inside the field; use multiline for certificates and snippets.
With helperText the button is centered on the field and its helper line together.
Below Android 13 the sensitive flag is written but ignored by the system.

name: MonarchCountrySelect
title: CountrySelect
wrapsNative: MonarchCombobox (androidx.compose.material3.ExposedDropdownMenuBox with androidx.compose.material3.ModalBottomSheet) over a bundled ISO 3166-1 list named with java.util.Locale.getDisplayCountry and sorted with java.text.Collator
summary: A searchable picker of a country or territory whose value is its ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, with names in the person's language.
whenToUse: For a country in an address, a billing profile, a shipping rule or a market setting, when the value to store is the ISO code.
whenNotToUse: For a calling code use MonarchPhoneCountrySelect; for a state or province use MonarchRegionSelect; for a whole address with suggestions use MonarchAddressAutocomplete.
api: @Composable fun MonarchCountrySelect(selected: String?, onSelectedChange: (String?) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, locale: Locale? = null, countries: List<String>? = null, exclude: List<String> = emptyList(), priority: List<String> = emptyList(), presentation: MonarchComboboxPresentation = MonarchComboboxPresentation.Automatic, enabled: Boolean = true, showCode: Boolean = true, showFlag: Boolean = false, countryName: ((String) -> String?)? = null, placeholder: String? = null, helperText: String? = null, errorText: String? = null, clearOptionLabel: String? = null, clearIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchCountrySelectLabels = MonarchCountrySelectLabels())
class MonarchCountrySelectLabels(label: String? = null, suggested: String? = null, all: String? = null, empty: String? = null, combobox: MonarchComboboxLabels = MonarchComboboxLabels())

options.name: selected
options.description: The chosen ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code in any case, or null.

options.name: onSelectedChange
options.description: Called with the chosen upper-case code, or null when the selection is cleared.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the field.

options.name: locale
options.description: The language of the names and of the sort order. null uses the first locale of the configuration.

options.name: countries
options.description: Limits the list to these codes, such as the countries the product ships to. null lists all 249.

options.name: exclude
options.description: Codes to leave out.

options.name: priority
options.description: Codes listed first under "Suggested" while nothing is typed; each country is listed once.

options.name: presentation
options.description: Menu, Sheet, or Automatic: a menu for up to eight countries, a sheet otherwise.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the list can be opened.

options.name: showCode
options.description: Shows the ISO code at the end of each row.

options.name: showFlag
options.description: Shows the flag emoji at the end of each row. Off by default because TalkBack reads a flag emoji as "Flag:" and the name, repeating it.

options.name: countryName
options.description: The app's own name for a code, such as a legal wording; null from it keeps the locale's name.

options.name: placeholder
options.description: Shown in the empty field while nothing is chosen.

options.name: helperText
options.description: Guidance below the field.

options.name: errorText
options.description: An error message; replaces the helper text and is set as the field's error.

options.name: clearOptionLabel
options.description: Adds a first row that clears the selection. Hidden while searching.

options.name: clearIcon
options.description: The icon of a clear button at the end of the field while something is chosen. Monarch bundles no icons; without it there is no clear button.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings: the label "Country", the headings "Suggested" and "All countries", "No countries match", and the combobox's own strings.

states.name: closed
states.description: The field shows the chosen country's label, or the placeholder (or the floating label) while nothing is chosen.

states.name: open
states.description: The bottom sheet (or, for eight options or fewer, the menu) lists the options; while nothing is typed the suggested ones come first under their heading.

states.name: searching
states.description: Typing filters the list, best matches first, without headings; when nothing matches the list says so.

states.name: error
states.description: The field has the danger outline and the message below it, and the message is the field's error for TalkBack.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The field takes the disabled colors and does not open.

appearance: The field is MonarchCombobox's: MonarchTextField's colors, a surface fill with the input border, the danger strong color in error; the sheet is on the surface color, second lines, hints and headings are muted text and the chosen row's radio mark is the accent strong color. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Built on MonarchCombobox, so long lists open a Material 3 bottom sheet with a search field instead of the web's popover. The 249 officially assigned codes are bundled (the web component's list) rather than read from Locale.getISOCountries, so every Android version lists the same countries; names come from the platform's locale data and may differ slightly from the browser's Intl.DisplayNames. MonarchComboboxOption has no leading media slot, so the web's flag before the name is an optional flag emoji at the end of the row, off by default. The value is controlled only (selected with onSelectedChange); the web's uncontrolled defaultValue is not offered. iOS has no CountrySelect yet; the name is the planned shared one.
accessibility: The field is MonarchCombobox's Material 3 exposed dropdown anchor: TalkBack reads the label, the chosen value and the expand state; double tap opens the list.

Every row is read with its label, second line and hint, and the chosen row is selected with a filled radio mark, so the choice does not rely on color; in the sheet each row is a radio button at least 48dp high.
The headings over suggested and other entries are headings; the no-match message is a polite live region.
The error is the field's error semantics and is shown as text.
edgeCases: A selected code that is not in the list (excluded or limited away) is still listed, so the field shows its name.
Lower-case codes are accepted; onSelectedChange always reports upper case.
Outside English, the English name is a hidden keyword, so "germany" finds "Allemagne".
Accents and case are ignored when searching: "aland" finds "Åland Islands".
Priority codes that are not in the list are ignored.

title: CreateWorkspaceDialog
wrapsNative: MonarchBottomSheet with dismissible = false while it creates, a scrolling androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column with a heading Row and a Cancel MonarchButton, around the workspace onboarding form (MonarchTextField, MonarchUsernameAvailabilityInput, MonarchRadioCardGroup, MonarchButton)
summary: A recipe, not a component: a sheet titled "Create new workspace" around the workspace onboarding form, which cannot be dismissed while the workspace is being created and closes when it is created.
whenToUse: To create another workspace from inside the app, for example from the workspace switcher or an empty state.
whenNotToUse: For the very first workspace in the first-run flow, show the workspace onboarding form as a full screen instead. For renaming or editing a workspace, use a settings screen.
api: ModalBottomSheet(onDismissRequest = { if (!creating) open = false }, sheetState = rememberModalBottomSheetState(skipPartiallyExpanded = true, confirmValueChange = { !creating }), sheetGesturesEnabled = !creating) { … }
MonarchText(text = "Create new workspace", style = MonarchTextStyle.Heading, heading = true)
MonarchButton(text = "Cancel", onClick = …, variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Ghost, enabled = !creating)
The workspace onboarding form: MonarchTextField, MonarchUsernameAvailabilityInput, MonarchRadioCardGroup and a primary MonarchButton with loading = creating

options.name: open
options.description: Whether the sheet is shown; the app sets it from its New workspace button and clears it when the workspace is created.

options.name: creating
options.description: True while the product creates the workspace: the submit button shows progress, Cancel is disabled and the sheet cannot be swiped or dismissed.

states.name: closed
states.description: Only the button that opens the sheet.

states.name: open
states.description: The sheet with the heading and Cancel in the first row, then the name, username and type fields and the submit button.

states.name: invalid
states.description: Each field shows its own error after a submit, as in the workspace onboarding form.

states.name: creating
states.description: The submit button shows its progress indicator; Cancel is disabled and swiping, tapping outside and Back do not close the sheet.

states.name: created
states.description: The app sets open to false and the sheet closes.

appearance: The Material 3 sheet in the theme's raised surface with its drag handle; the heading in the heading style, Cancel as a ghost button, and the fields and primary button with their Monarch look.
platformNotes: The web ships CreateWorkspaceDialog as one component around WorkspaceOnboardingForm with onSubmit, checkUsername, rules, closeOnSuccess and messages props. On Android it is a recipe, as on iOS: a modal bottom sheet is the phone's surface for a short task, Cancel sits in the sheet's first row because Compose sheets have no navigation bar, and dismissible = false replaces the web's "cannot be dismissed while pending". The rules and the lookup stay in the app.
accessibility: The heading has the heading role, so TalkBack can jump to it.
Cancel is a button with a 48dp touch target and is disabled while creating.
Each field keeps its own label and error, and the username status is announced by MonarchUsernameAvailabilityInput.
The submit button reads "Loading" while creating.
The sheet's content scrolls, so every field is reachable at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: While creating, onDismissRequest ignores Back and taps outside, and confirmValueChange refuses to hide the sheet.
If creation fails, set creating to false and show the error in the sheet, for example with MonarchInlineNotice above the button.

The title, the two fields with their asterisks, the Type cards and the copy are the web's.

parityExceptions.reason: The web puts the helper line (Letters and numbers only, 5 to 30 characters.) between the label and the username field. The Android field shows its helper text under the field, where the status message also appears, so the text is the same and its place is the field's own.

title: CSATSurvey
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of MonarchText, MonarchChip toggles or MonarchRatingPicker, MonarchTextField (singleLine = false), MonarchButton and MonarchSaveStatusIndicator; MonarchLoadingState, MonarchErrorState and MonarchInlineNotice for the other states
summary: A recipe, not a component: a customer-satisfaction survey that saves the rating as soon as it is chosen, then an optional comment, with every saving state, a locked answer, a thank-you, loading and a failed load.
whenToUse: After a support conversation, a delivery or a booking, on a screen opened from a notification or a link, to ask one satisfaction question.
whenNotToUse: For a full feedback form with several questions, compose MonarchFormField rows. For rating an item in a list, use MonarchRatingPicker alone.

@Composable fun MonarchInlineNotice(message: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, tone: MonarchTone = MonarchTone.Info, …)

states.name: unanswered
states.description: The question, Good and Bad (or a 1 to 5 scale) and a hint to choose first.

states.name: saving
states.description: MonarchSaveStatusIndicator shows Saving after a choice or Save comment.

states.name: saved
states.description: Saved with the relative time; the comment field appears.

states.name: save failed
states.description: The indicator shows the error with Retry; the choice stays selected.

states.name: locked
states.description: The choices are read-only or disabled and a MonarchInlineNotice says the answer can no longer change.

states.name: submitted
states.description: A success MonarchInlineNotice thanks the person.

states.name: loading
states.description: MonarchLoadingState with the Spinner variant.

states.name: load failed
states.description: MonarchErrorState with the NotFound kind for an expired or invalid link.

appearance: The question is a heading in default text; Good and Bad are Material 3 filter chips in the theme, selected with the accent container; the comment is a multi-line MonarchTextField; status, notices and errors take their own Monarch appearance in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web CSATSurvey is one component with scale, mode (instant or form), messages and promise handling. On Android, as on iOS, it composes existing parts: the app holds the rating, comment and save status and calls its server; the form mode is the same recipe with one Send feedback button instead of saving on choice. Good and Bad are filter chips (the Android toggle button), so the chosen answer is the chip's selected state; the web's thumbs are app icons passed to the chips' leadingIcon because Monarch bundles none. MonarchTextField takes singleLine = false for the comment, so no separate form field is needed. The app supplies all the words.
accessibility: The question is a heading (MonarchText with the Heading style).
Good and Bad are filter chips whose selected state is read; the five-point scale is MonarchRatingPicker, one adjustable element read as "4 of 5, Good".
MonarchSaveStatusIndicator announces Saved and save failures; its Retry is a separate button.
The comment field is labelled and its helper text reads the characters left.
Every control has a 48dp touch target and wraps at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: Save the rating on choice so a person who leaves after one tap is still counted.
Limit the comment in onValueChange; the helper text counts down.
An expired link replaces the whole survey with MonarchErrorState.

name: MonarchCurrencyInput
title: CurrencyInput
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedTextField (through MonarchNumberInput and MonarchTextField) with KeyboardType.Decimal, formatted with android.icu.text.NumberFormat currency styles (through MonarchMoneyFormat)
summary: A labelled field for an amount of money in one currency, typed and shown in the person's locale with the currency's own decimals, in major units or whole minor units.
whenToUse: For a price, a budget, a refund or any amount of money the person types, in a currency the app already knows.
whenNotToUse: To show an amount that cannot be edited use MonarchMoney. For a plain number without a currency use MonarchNumberInput. For choosing the currency itself use MonarchSelect or MonarchCombobox next to this field.
api: @Composable fun MonarchCurrencyInput(value: Double?, currencyCode: String, onValueChange: (Double?) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, label: String? = null, placeholder: String? = null, helperText: String? = null, errorText: String? = null, currencyDisplay: MonarchMoneyCurrencyDisplay = MonarchMoneyCurrencyDisplay.Symbol, minimum: Double? = null, maximum: Double? = null, step: Double = 1.0, allowNegative: Boolean = false, enabled: Boolean = true, readOnly: Boolean = false, showSteppers: Boolean = false, labels: MonarchNumberInputLabels = MonarchNumberInputLabels(), interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)

@Composable fun MonarchCurrencyInput(minorUnits: Long?, currencyCode: String, onMinorUnitsChange: (Long?) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, label: String? = null, placeholder: String? = null, helperText: String? = null, errorText: String? = null, currencyDisplay: MonarchMoneyCurrencyDisplay = MonarchMoneyCurrencyDisplay.Symbol, minimum: Long? = null, maximum: Long? = null, step: Long? = null, allowNegative: Boolean = false, enabled: Boolean = true, readOnly: Boolean = false, showSteppers: Boolean = false, labels: MonarchNumberInputLabels = MonarchNumberInputLabels(), interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)

options.name: value / minorUnits
options.description: The amount in major units (19.99), or in whole minor units (1999) for APIs that store integers. null while the field is empty.

options.name: currencyCode
options.description: The ISO 4217 code, such as USD, EUR, JPY or KWD. Sets the symbol and the decimals (JPY 0, USD 2, KWD 3).

options.name: onValueChange / onMinorUnitsChange
options.description: Called with the new amount, rounded half up to the currency's decimals, or null when cleared, on every edit that reads as an amount, in range or not, and on a step; an amount out of range is flagged when the field is left, so validate the bounds before saving.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the field.

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label.

options.name: placeholder
options.description: Shown while the field is empty and focused.

options.name: helperText
options.description: Guidance below the field.

options.name: errorText
options.description: An error from the app; replaces the field's own messages while present.

options.name: currencyDisplay
options.description: How the currency is written: Symbol ($ or US$), NarrowSymbol ($), Code (USD) or Name (US dollars).

options.name: minimum
options.description: The smallest amount. Without it the smallest is 0, unless allowNegative. Below it the range message is shown.

options.name: maximum
options.description: The largest amount.

options.name: step
options.description: The amount one press of − or + adds or removes.

options.name: allowNegative
options.description: Allows amounts below zero, for refunds and adjustments.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the field can be used.

options.name: readOnly
options.description: Selectable but not editable.

options.name: showSteppers
options.description: Shows the − and + buttons. Amounts are usually typed, so they are off, as on the web and iOS.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the number field's strings: Increase, Decrease, "Enter a number." and the range message.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the focus and press interactions of the field.

states.name: empty
states.description: The value is null; the placeholder shows while focused.

states.name: amount
states.description: The amount in the locale's currency format, such as "$1,234.57" or "1.234,57 €".

states.name: not a number
states.description: A danger outline and "Enter a number."; the text is kept and the value is not changed.

states.name: out of range
states.description: A danger outline and the range message with formatted bounds, such as "Enter $0.00 or more."; the text is kept.

states.name: error
states.description: The app's message in place of the field's own.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The subtle background and the disabled text color.

states.name: read only
states.description: The amount can be selected but not changed.

appearance: The field is MonarchNumberInput, and through it MonarchTextField: a surface fill with the input border, the focus ring color when focused and the danger strong color in error; the optional − and + signs use the default or disabled text color. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Formatting is MonarchMoneyFormat (android.icu.text.NumberFormat currency styles) in the current locale, so separators and symbol position follow the person's region as the web's Intl formatting does; reading is MonarchNumberInput's locale-aware parser, which ignores currency signs and codes around the number and reads (12.00) as negative. A typed amount is rounded to the currency's decimals when it is committed (Done or leaving the field), as on the web and iOS. iOS takes a single rangeMessage string; Android reuses MonarchNumberInputLabels, which also replaces "Enter a number." and the button names. The web's Page Up and Page Down large step is not offered. The keyboard is KeyboardType.Decimal; Compose has no signed number keyboard, so with allowNegative whether a minus key is shown depends on the keyboard app (a minus can be pasted, and steppers go below zero). The minor-units overload converts through BigDecimal, so 19.99 dollars is exactly 1999 cents.
accessibility: The field is the Material 3 text field: TalkBack reads the label, the formatted amount with its currency, and the error.
A message for unreadable or out-of-range text is the field's error, shown with text and a danger outline, not color alone.
With showSteppers, the − and + buttons are icon buttons named "Decrease" and "Increase" with 48dp touch targets, mirrored in right-to-left layouts, and the field has matching custom actions.
The text scales with the font size and wraps nothing away; the field grows.
edgeCases: An unknown currency code formats the number followed by the code, with two decimals.
The number field keeps three decimals while checking the bounds, so 10.004 against a maximum of 10.00 is flagged although it would round to 10.00.
Changing the amount from outside replaces the text on screen.
An amount too large for a Long in minor units is passed as null by the minor-units overload.

name: MonarchCurrencySelect
title: CurrencySelect
wrapsNative: MonarchCombobox (androidx.compose.material3.ExposedDropdownMenuBox with androidx.compose.material3.ModalBottomSheet) over a bundled list of active ISO 4217 codes named with java.util.Currency.getDisplayName and getSymbol
summary: A searchable picker of a currency whose value is its ISO 4217 code, with names and symbols in the person's language.
whenToUse: For the currency of an invoice, a price list, a payout or a billing profile, when the value to store is the ISO code.
whenNotToUse: For an amount use MonarchCurrencyInput; for a short fixed list of two or three currencies without search a MonarchSelect or a segmented control is enough.
api: @Composable fun MonarchCurrencySelect(selected: String?, onSelectedChange: (String?) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, locale: Locale? = null, currencies: List<String>? = null, priority: List<String> = emptyList(), display: MonarchCurrencySelectDisplay = MonarchCurrencySelectDisplay.Name, presentation: MonarchComboboxPresentation = MonarchComboboxPresentation.Automatic, enabled: Boolean = true, showSymbol: Boolean = true, placeholder: String? = null, helperText: String? = null, errorText: String? = null, clearOptionLabel: String? = null, clearIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchCurrencySelectLabels = MonarchCurrencySelectLabels())

class MonarchCurrencySelectLabels(label: String? = null, suggested: String? = null, all: String? = null, empty: String? = null, combobox: MonarchComboboxLabels = MonarchComboboxLabels())

options.name: selected
options.description: The chosen ISO 4217 code in any case, or null.

options.name: onSelectedChange
options.description: Called with the chosen upper-case code, or null when the selection is cleared.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the field.

options.name: locale
options.description: The language of the names and symbols and of the sort order. null uses the first locale of the configuration.

options.name: currencies
options.description: Limits the list to these codes, such as the currencies the payment provider supports. null lists every active currency.

options.name: priority

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the list can be opened.

options.name: showSymbol
options.description: Shows the symbol next to the code at the end of each row.

options.name: placeholder
options.description: Shown in the empty field while nothing is chosen.

options.name: helperText
options.description: Guidance below the field.

options.name: errorText
options.description: An error message; replaces the helper text and is set as the field's error.

options.name: clearOptionLabel
options.description: Adds a first row that clears the selection. Hidden while searching.

options.name: clearIcon
options.description: The icon of a clear button at the end of the field while something is chosen. Monarch bundles no icons; without it there is no clear button.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings: the label "Currency", "Suggested", "All currencies", "No currencies match" and the combobox's own strings.

states.name: closed
states.description: The field shows the chosen currency's label, or the placeholder (or the floating label) while nothing is chosen.

states.name: open
states.description: The bottom sheet (or, for eight options or fewer, the menu) lists the options; while nothing is typed the suggested ones come first under their heading.

states.name: searching
states.description: Typing filters the list, best matches first, without headings; when nothing matches the list says so.

states.name: error
states.description: The field has the danger outline and the message below it, and the message is the field's error for TalkBack.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The field takes the disabled colors and does not open.

appearance: The field is MonarchCombobox's: MonarchTextField's colors, a surface fill with the input border, the danger strong color in error; the sheet is on the surface color, second lines, hints and headings are muted text and the chosen row's radio mark is the accent strong color. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Built on MonarchCombobox, so long lists open a Material 3 bottom sheet with a search field instead of the web's popover. The parity map named Currency.getAvailableCurrencies, but that list includes funds, precious metals, test codes and retired currencies, so the web component's list of active codes is bundled and java.util.Currency only names them; a code the runtime does not know (a new currency on an old Android version) shows its code as its name. Symbols are java.util.Currency.getSymbol in the locale ("$" in the US, "US$" elsewhere), not the web's narrow symbol. The value is controlled only. iOS has no CurrencySelect yet; the name is the planned shared one.
accessibility: The field is MonarchCombobox's Material 3 exposed dropdown anchor: TalkBack reads the label, the chosen value and the expand state; double tap opens the list.

Every row is read with its label, second line and hint, and the chosen row is selected with a filled radio mark, so the choice does not rely on color; in the sheet each row is a radio button at least 48dp high.
The headings over suggested and other entries are headings; the no-match message is a polite live region.
The error is the field's error semantics and is shown as text.
edgeCases: A selected code that is not in the list is still listed, so the field shows its name.
Searching matches every typed word in the name, the code, the symbol and, outside English, the English name: "$" finds the dollars.
A code unknown to the runtime is listed under its code.
Lower-case codes are accepted; onSelectedChange always reports upper case.
