name: MonarchCursorList
title: CursorList
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn, MonarchLoadMore, MonarchLoadingState, MonarchErrorState, MonarchEmptyState
summary: A list loaded page by page from a cursor: the items, a Load more footer with a count, and the first-load, empty and error states.
whenToUse: For a feed of records that arrive in pages from an API cursor: tickets, activity, audit events, search results.
whenNotToUse: For a list that arrives whole, use a LazyColumn. For rows people sort and compare by column, use a table. For numbered pages people jump between, use a pager.
api: @Composable fun <T> MonarchCursorList(items: List<T>, label: String, hasMore: Boolean, onLoadMore: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, key: ((item: T) -> Any)? = null, loading: Boolean = false, failed: Boolean = false, totalCount: Int? = null, autoLoad: Boolean = false, showEnd: Boolean = true, divided: Boolean = true, focusNewItems: Boolean = true, loadingVariant: MonarchLoadingStateVariant = MonarchLoadingStateVariant.List, state: LazyListState = rememberLazyListState(), contentPadding: PaddingValues = PaddingValues(), onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null, empty: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchCursorListLabels = MonarchCursorListLabels(), row: @Composable LazyItemScope.(item: T) -> Unit)

class MonarchCursorListLabels(loading: String? = null, emptyTitle: String? = null, emptyMessage: String? = null, errorTitle: String? = null, retry: String? = null, footer: MonarchLoadMoreLabels = MonarchLoadMoreLabels())

options.name: items
options.description: Every item loaded so far, in order.

options.name: label
options.description: The TalkBack name of the list.

options.name: hasMore
options.description: Whether there is another page. With no items and no more, the empty state is shown.

options.name: onLoadMore
options.description: Loads the next page.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the list. Give it a bounded height.

options.name: key
options.description: A stable key per item, as for LazyColumn. null uses the position.

options.name: loading
options.description: A page is being fetched. With no items the placeholder is shown; otherwise the footer button shows progress.

options.name: failed
options.description: The last fetch failed. With no items the error state is shown; otherwise the footer shows the failure with Retry.

options.name: totalCount
options.description: The total, when the server knows it, for "Showing 20 of 140 items".

options.name: autoLoad
options.description: Loads the next page when the footer scrolls into view; the button stays. Pauses after a failure.

options.name: showEnd
options.description: Shows "That's everything" after the last page.

options.name: divided
options.description: Draws a MonarchDivider between rows.

options.name: focusNewItems
options.description: Moves focus to the first item of a page asked for from the footer button.

options.name: loadingVariant
options.description: The shape of the first-page placeholder.

options.name: state
options.description: The scroll state of the list.

options.name: contentPadding
options.description: Padding around the rows and the footer.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Repeats the failed request. null calls onLoadMore.

options.name: empty
options.description: Replaces the empty state, for example with a MonarchEmptyState that has a first-run action.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the strings monarch_cursorlist_*, and footer for the MonarchLoadMore strings.

options.name: row
options.description: Draws one item. Put a clickable row inside when the item opens something.

states.name: ready
states.description: The rows and the footer: a Load more button with the count, or the end line.

states.name: loading more
states.description: The footer button shows progress and ignores taps.

states.name: failed later
states.description: The footer shows "Couldn't load more." with Retry; the rows stay.

states.name: first page loading
states.description: A MonarchLoadingState placeholder named "Loading".

states.name: first page failed
states.description: A small MonarchErrorState, "This list could not be loaded", with Retry; while the retry runs the button is busy.

states.name: empty
states.description: A small MonarchEmptyState, "Nothing here yet" with a message, or the empty slot.

appearance: The app's rows separated by subtle dividers, then the MonarchLoadMore footer: the count in muted caption text and a small secondary button. The first-load, error and empty states are the shared Monarch states in their small size. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web CursorList chooses ul or ol and takes an item class; on Android it is a LazyColumn and the row lambda draws each item, so it must have a bounded height and must not sit in a vertically scrolling parent. The web moves keyboard focus to the first new item after a page asked for by keyboard; on Android focus moves to it after a page asked for from the footer button (by touch, keyboard or TalkBack), and auto-loaded pages do not move focus. The web noun is built into its messages; on Android pass labels.footer.count and labels.footer.loaded. The same name and options as iOS, with Android's state names (loading, failed, autoLoad, showEnd, divided, focusNewItems) and the added key, state and contentPadding of LazyColumn.
accessibility: The list is named by label.
The footer is a MonarchLoadMore: its button has a 48dp touch target, and new items, a failure and the end are announced through a polite live region.
After a page asked for from the footer arrives, focus moves to its first new item; that item takes focus only until focus leaves it.
The first-load placeholder, the error state and the empty state are the shared Monarch states with their own names; Retry has a 48dp touch target.
The empty message wraps at the largest font size.
edgeCases: With no items, hasMore true and nothing loading, the list shows only the footer so people can load the first page.
A failure with items keeps the items and shows the failure in the footer; a failure without items replaces the list with the error state.
Whether TalkBack's own focus follows the moved input focus depends on the device; a device check is needed.
The empty slot ignores modifier: apply it to the slot's content.

title: CustomDomainConnect
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of MonarchTextField, MonarchButton, MonarchDomainProgress and MonarchDnsRecordTable; MonarchDialog to confirm removal
summary: A recipe, not a component: enter a custom domain, add the DNS records it needs with copy buttons, verify them, follow the progress to live, and remove the domain.
whenToUse: In settings where a customer connects their own domain to a help center, a booking page or a website.
whenNotToUse: To only show DNS records, use MonarchDnsRecordTable. To only show the progress of a domain, use MonarchDomainProgress.
api: MonarchTextField(value = typed, onValueChange = { … }, label = "Domain", errorText = error, keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(keyboardType = KeyboardType.Uri))
MonarchDomainProgress(host = domain, stage = MonarchDomainStage.Dns)
MonarchDnsRecordTable(records = listOf(MonarchDnsRecord("CNAME", domain, "domains.example.net", MonarchDnsRecordPurpose.Routing, found = false)))
MonarchButton(text = "Verify DNS", onClick = { … }, loading = verifying)
AlertDialog(onDismissRequest = { … }, title = { Text("Remove $domain?") }, confirmButton = { … }, dismissButton = { … })

options.name: domain
options.description: The connected domain, from the app's state; null shows the entry step.

options.name: stage
options.description: Where the domain is: DNS, ownership, certificate, page or live, from the app's server.

options.name: records
options.description: The records to add, from the server, each with found once it is seen.

options.name: verifying
options.description: While a check runs, the verify button shows progress.

states.name: enter
states.description: The domain field with its error and Connect domain.

states.name: records
states.description: The domain as a heading with Remove domain, MonarchDomainProgress, the records to add and Verify DNS.

states.name: verifying
states.description: Verify DNS shows progress; MonarchDomainProgress shows the stage.

states.name: live
states.description: MonarchDomainProgress shows the domain as live; the app may hide the records.

states.name: remove
states.description: A MonarchDialog confirms; the entry step comes back.

appearance: Every part is an existing Monarch component: the text field, the domain progress steps, the record cards or table with copy buttons, and buttons, on the canvas. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web's CustomDomainConnect is one component with a Stepper, a form, a status line, a records table, a provider hint select and a confirm dialog. On Android it is a recipe from MonarchDomainProgress (the steps and the status), MonarchDnsRecordTable (cards on a phone, a table on wide screens) and MonarchTextField and MonarchButton, with a MonarchDialog to confirm removal. The web's provider hints are text the app shows under the records, for example in a MonarchCollapsible. The web's domain syntax checks are the app's validation before it calls its server. iOS has the same plan: a recipe.
accessibility: The domain field has a visible label and its error is set as the field's error.
MonarchDomainProgress reads each step with its state; MonarchDnsRecordTable names each copy button with the record.
Remove is confirmed in a MonarchDialog, which TalkBack reads as a dialog.
edgeCases: Normalise the typed domain (trim, lower case, no trailing dot) before sending it.
DNS can take hours: let people leave and come back; keep the records visible until the domain is live.
The server stays the authority on whether a record is found.

title: DangerZone
wrapsNative: MonarchSectionCard with the danger tone holding androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column rows separated by MonarchDivider; each action is a danger MonarchButton that opens a MonarchDialog
summary: A recipe, not a component: the settings section that holds irreversible actions (delete a workspace, transfer ownership, leave), as a danger-toned section card with one row per action and a confirmation before each.
whenToUse: At the end of a settings screen, for actions that cannot be undone or that hand the workspace or account to someone else.
whenNotToUse: For a single destructive action next to the thing it affects, use a danger MonarchButton with a confirmation (confirm-dialog). For ordinary settings, use the settings-section recipe.
api: MonarchSectionCard(title = "Danger zone", description = …, tone = MonarchTone.Danger) { rows }

Column(Modifier.semantics { isTraversalGroup = true }) { MonarchText(title, style = MonarchTextStyle.BodyStrong, heading = true); MonarchText(consequence, style = MonarchTextStyle.Caption); MonarchText(disabledReason); MonarchButton(…, variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Danger, size = MonarchButtonSize.Sm, enabled = …) }
HorizontalDivider(color = MonarchTheme.colors.borderSubtle)

AlertDialog(onDismissRequest = …, title = …, text = …, confirmButton = { MonarchButton(…, variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Danger) }, dismissButton = { MonarchButton(…, variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Ghost) })

options.name: heading
options.description: The title of the MonarchSectionCard; the danger tone is spoken with it.

options.name: description
options.description: One or two sentences under the heading, such as who can use these actions.

options.name: disabled reason
options.description: Why an action is unavailable: a caption under the consequence, with the action's MonarchButton disabled.

states.name: ready
states.description: Each action is a titled row with its consequence and a danger button under the text.

states.name: unavailable
states.description: The row shows why in a caption and its button is disabled.

states.name: confirming
states.description: The button opens a MonarchDialog with a danger confirm button and Cancel.

states.name: done
states.description: The app reflects the result, for example by disabling the row's button or leaving the screen.

appearance: A MonarchSectionCard with the danger border; item titles are strong body text, consequences and reasons muted captions, actions small danger buttons, rows split by a subtle divider. Every part is an existing component, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web ships DangerZone and DangerZoneItem with heading levels and a layout that places the action beside the text, or under it in a narrow container. On a phone the action always sits under the text, so long titles and font scale 2.0 never squeeze it; MonarchSectionCard already gives the titled card and the danger tone, so Android, like the settings-section recipe, keeps it a recipe. TalkBack has no heading levels, so item titles are headings without a level. The web adds the disabled reason to the row's description; on Android it is a visible caption read in the row's traversal group. Confirmation is a MonarchDialog of the confirm-dialog entry.
accessibility: The card title is a heading and the danger tone is spoken with it, from MonarchSectionCard.
Each item title is a heading, and each row is a traversal group, so the title, consequence, reason and action are read together.
The reason an action is unavailable is visible text, not only a disabled button.
Actions are MonarchButtons with 48dp targets; destructive ones are confirmed in a MonarchDialog that TalkBack focuses.
edgeCases: Keep each consequence to one or two sentences; long text wraps above the button.
After a destructive action succeeds, the app usually leaves the screen; keep the dialog open with a loading confirm button while it runs.
Put the danger zone last on the settings screen.

name: MonarchDashboardGrid
title: DashboardGrid
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.grid.LazyVerticalGrid with GridCells.Fixed and GridItemSpan, sized from androidx.compose.foundation.layout.BoxWithConstraints; MonarchSortableGrid in edit mode
summary: The responsive grid a dashboard's widgets sit in: one column on phones, more on wide screens, widgets spanning columns, and an edit mode in which people rearrange widgets by dragging or with buttons.
whenToUse: For a dashboard screen of MonarchWidget cards whose order each person may arrange and save.
whenNotToUse: For tiles of equal weight that are always reorderable use MonarchSortableGrid. For a fixed layout of a few cards use a Column or a Material 3 adaptive layout. For a list use LazyColumn.
api: @Composable public fun <T> MonarchDashboardGrid(items: List<T>, key: (T) -> String, itemLabel: (T) -> String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, layout: List<String> = emptyList(), onLayoutChange: ((layout: List<String>) -> Unit)? = null, span: (T) -> MonarchDashboardGridSpan = { MonarchDashboardGridSpan.One }, columns: Int = DefaultColumns, editing: Boolean = false, state: LazyGridState = rememberLazyGridState(), labels: MonarchDashboardGridLabels = MonarchDashboardGridLabels(), itemContent: @Composable (item: T) -> Unit)

public class MonarchDashboardGridSpan { companion object { val One: MonarchDashboardGridSpan; val Two: MonarchDashboardGridSpan; val Full: MonarchDashboardGridSpan; fun columns(count: Int): MonarchDashboardGridSpan } }

public class MonarchDashboardGridLabels(label: String? = null, handle: ((label: String) -> String)? = null, earlier: String? = null, later: String? = null, moveEarlier: ((label: String) -> String)? = null, moveLater: ((label: String) -> String)? = null, pickedUp: ((label: String, position: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, moved: ((label: String, position: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, dropped: ((label: String, position: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, cancelled: ((label: String, position: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null)

options.name: items
options.description: The widgets in their default order.

options.name: key
options.description: A widget's stable, unique key, stored in layout.

options.name: itemLabel
options.description: A widget's plain-text name, for the arrange bar, the button names and the announcements.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the grid. The grid scrolls itself; bound its height inside a scrolling parent.

options.name: layout
options.description: The order of keys saved for this person; empty for the default order. Unknown keys are skipped and new widgets appended.

options.name: onLayoutChange
options.description: Called with the whole new order after each finished move, for example to save it. Without it the grid cannot be rearranged.

options.name: span
options.description: The columns a widget spans, clamped to the columns available. Not applied in edit mode.

options.name: columns
options.description: The columns from 1024dp of grid width, 1 to 4. From 640dp the grid has at most two, below it one.

options.name: editing
options.description: Shows an arrange bar on each widget with Move earlier and Move later, and makes the widgets draggable. Needs onLayoutChange.

options.name: state
options.description: The scroll state of the grid.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

options.name: itemContent
options.description: Draws a widget, usually a MonarchWidget.

states.name: viewing
states.description: The widgets in rows with their spans; one column on phones and at font scale 1.5 and above.

states.name: editing
states.description: Each widget is a tile of MonarchSortableGrid with a drag handle and an arrange bar in the subtle background: the widget's name and Move earlier and Move later buttons, disabled at the ends.

states.name: dragged
states.description: The held widget follows the finger with the medium shadow and the accent border; the others slide out of its way.

appearance: Widgets are separated by 16dp. In edit mode each tile has the surface fill and subtle border of MonarchSortableGrid, and the arrange bar uses the subtle background role with small corners. Colors are theme roles, so dark and both high-contrast themes follow the theme.
platformNotes: The web grid is a CSS grid with column spans in rem of grid width; Android uses a LazyVerticalGrid with fixed columns chosen from the grid's own width at the 640dp and 1024dp breakpoints, and one column from font scale 1.5. In edit mode the grid is a MonarchSortableGrid, which has no spans, so every widget takes one cell while editing. A long press drags a widget, as in Android launchers; the handle's actions and the Move earlier and Move later buttons replace the web's Space-and-arrow-keys pick-up. The web takes an uncontrolled defaultLayout and reports the move with its ids; Android hoists the layout as a list of keys and reports the whole new order, as iOS binds it. The web calls the handle "Move Team load"; Android keeps that name.
accessibility: The grid is a traversal group named "Dashboard".
In edit mode each widget has a drag handle named "Move Team load" with the move actions, a 48dp touch target, before the widget in both reading directions.
Move earlier and Move later are named with the widget ("Move Team load earlier"), have 48dp touch targets and are disabled at the ends.
Every move by a button or an action, and every pick up, drop and cancel of a drag, is announced through a polite live region: "Revenue moved to position 2 of 3."
At font scale 1.5 and above the grid has one column; widget names wrap at font scale 2.0.
Moves animate with the motion tokens and are immediate when animations are off.
edgeCases: A key in layout that is not an item is skipped; a repeated key counts once.
A span larger than the row takes the whole row; MonarchDashboardGridSpan.columns(0) is one column.
editing without onLayoutChange shows the viewing grid.
Keys must be unique; the same key twice breaks the lazy grid.

title: DashboardOperational
wrapsNative: MonarchDashboardGrid (androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.grid.LazyVerticalGrid) of a MonarchStatCard row (androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow), MonarchWidget sections with MonarchBadge, MonarchLineChart, MonarchLeaderboard and MonarchActivityTimeline
summary: The home screen of an operational product (incidents, tickets, alerts): key figures, what needs attention, the trend, team load and recent activity, as sections of a MonarchDashboardGrid.
whenToUse: As the home screen of a product whose work arrives continuously, and for a team lead's overview of live work and load.
whenNotToUse: For a sales, hiring or campaign home use the DashboardPipeline recipe; for a set of assets use DashboardPortfolio; for a person's own work use DashboardPersonalWork.

options.name: key figures

options.name: needs attention / my queue / coming up
options.description: Short lists of items with their status as a badge in words, linking to the full list with View all.

options.name: trend
options.description: How the workload moves over time, with its table view.

options.name: team load
options.description: Open work per person.

options.name: activity
options.description: Recent changes (the ActivityWidget recipe).

options.name: insights
options.description: Rule or AI findings as a full-span item under the key figures.

states.name: ready
states.description: Each section shows its data.

states.name: loading or failed section
states.description: MonarchWidget with state = Loading or Failed and onRetry, MonarchStatCard with loading, or the chart's status, per section.

states.name: editing
states.description: MonarchDashboardGrid with editing = true shows arrange bars to move sections, with TalkBack actions.

appearance: A MonarchCard with the title as a subheading beside a status MonarchBadge in the neutral, info, success or danger tone, the description and preparation note in muted text, the status line in default text and primary buttons. All are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web renders the download as a link with an href; Android has no download link, so the app downloads in onDownload (for example with DownloadManager). onRequest is a suspend function that throws instead of a promise that rejects, and the web's errorMessage is replaced by the exception's message. Dates are epoch milliseconds formatted with android.icu.text.DateFormat (medium date, short time) in the device locale and time zone, or by labels.date; the web's locale, timeZone and dateFormat props are not offered. The web's headingLevel has no Android equivalent: the title is a heading. The request runs in the card's coroutine scope, so the app may move the status on while it runs. There is no iOS DataExportRequest yet. Experimental: a product composite that waits for a Rook app to adopt it.
accessibility: The title is a heading and the card is a traversal group.
The status is a word in the badge, never color alone.
The status line and failure reason are one always-present polite live region, so each status change is announced.
The progress indicator while preparing is named Preparing your export.
The scope is a MonarchCheckboxGroup with its label; the missing-scope error is its error text.
A failed request is an assertive MonarchInlineNotice, because it blocks the person.
Buttons keep 48dp touch targets; text wraps at the largest font size.
edgeCases: Without onRequest no form is shown, for products that request exports elsewhere.
The scope and format choices are kept by the card (saved across configuration changes); scope ids no longer offered are dropped from the request.
A missing date leaves its clause out of the status line.
A request that throws CancellationException is not shown as a failure.
Ready without onDownload shows the status line only.

states.name: grid
states.description: A header row on the subtle fill, then a row per record: a checkbox column, start-pinned columns with a line at their inner edge, a band of columns that scrolls sideways together with the header, end-pinned columns and an actions column.

states.name: list
states.description: For phones and large text: a toolbar with select-all and Sort, then one record per row with its name and a "Field value" line per column. Tapping a record with editable cells opens the record editor sheet.

states.name: sorted
states.description: The sorted header shows an arrow mark and its state is "Sorted ascending" or "Sorted descending"; the column menu offers the other direction and Clear sort.

states.name: pinned
states.description: A pinned column stays at its edge while the band scrolls; its header state includes "Pinned to start" or "Pinned to end". Pins that would take more than half the width scroll with the rest.

states.name: editing
states.description: An editable cell opens its MonarchEditableCell editor in place: a text field with Save and Cancel, a menu or the date picker. It shows progress while saving and keeps the editor open with the message when saving fails.

states.name: selected
states.description: The row fills with the accent's subtle fill and its checkbox is checked; the select-all checkbox is on, off or indeterminate.

states.name: loading
states.description: Without rows: placeholder rows named "Loading rows". With rows: an indeterminate progress bar above them.

states.name: empty
states.description: No rows: MonarchEmptyState with "Nothing here yet", or the app's emptyState.

appearance: Rows on the surface fill with a 1dp subtle divider, the header row on the subtle background with muted labels, a default-border line at the inner edge of pinned columns, selected rows on the accent's subtle fill. Numeric cells align to the end with tabular figures; an empty cell shows a muted dash; the first cell is link-coloured when rows open. Every color is a theme role, so dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: Compose and Material 3 have no data grid, so Monarch draws one on a LazyColumn with one shared horizontal ScrollState for the columns that are not pinned. It keeps DataTable's types (MonarchDataTableSort, MonarchDataTableRowAction, MonarchDataTableLayout) as the web DataGrid keeps DataTable's column model. On touch, tapping a header opens the column menu (sort, pin, unpin, hide, widen, narrow) instead of sorting at once; the web's drag-to-resize header edge becomes Widen column and Narrow column in 16dp steps, as the web's Alt+Arrow keys do. Phones get the mobile pattern instead of a squeezed grid: a list of records and an editor in a ModalBottomSheet. Each editable column carries a typed MonarchDataGridEdit with its own onCommit instead of the web's one onCellEdit with untyped values; dates are epoch milliseconds in UTC. Not offered: multi-sort, Shift-click range selection, type-to-edit, the WAI-ARIA grid's single tab stop with arrow-key cell movement (Compose's focus system moves between cells instead) and aria-rowcount for rows not yet loaded. There is no iOS entry yet.
accessibility: The grid is a traversal group named by label.
Headers are headings; a header with menu items is a button whose tap action is read as "Column options" and whose state is its sort and its pin, such as "Sorted descending" or "Pinned to end".
A read-only cell is one focusable element read as "Column: value", with "No value" for an empty cell; with onRowOpen it is a button whose action is "Open details".
An editable cell is a MonarchEditableCell named "Column for row", such as "Customer for INV-1".
Row actions are an actions button named "Actions for row" and TalkBack actions on each read-only cell of the row.
Row checkboxes are named "Select row"; the header's select-all checkbox is on, off or indeterminate.
With a hardware keyboard, Space on a cell that does not use it toggles the row's selection and Ctrl+A or Meta+A selects or clears all rows.
In the list layout each record is one element; a record with editable cells has the tap action "Edit" and, with onRowOpen, a TalkBack action "Open details".
Headers, cells, checkboxes and the actions button are at least 48dp tall; checkboxes and the actions button at least 48dp wide.
edgeCases: Pinned columns that would take more than half of the grid's width scroll with the others, so a narrow screen is never filled by pinned columns.
Each column has a fixed width; long text wraps in its cell and the row grows.
Rows sort by the column's comparator or its text; empty cells sort last in both directions; a sort on an unknown column leaves the app's order.
rowKey values must be unique and savable in a Bundle; the same key twice breaks the lazy list.
onEndReached fires once each time the last row comes into view and again after the number of rows changes, so a short page that leaves the end in view loads the next page.
A column whose edit says a row is not editable shows that row's cell as read-only text, not a disabled control.
The record editor finds its row by key on each change, so values saved in the sheet show at once; when the row disappears the sheet closes.

examples.title: 10,000 editable invoices
examples.template:
MonarchDataGrid(
    label = {{label}},
    rows = rows,
    columns = columns,
    rowKey = { it.id },
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth().height(420.dp),
    layout = MonarchDataTableLayout.Table,
    sort = sort,
    onSortChange = { sort = it },
    selection = selected,
    onSelectionChange = { selected = it },
    rowActions = { row ->
        listOf(
            MonarchDataTableRowAction({{rowActions.0}}) {},
            MonarchDataTableRowAction({{rowActions.1}}, danger = true) { rows = rows.filterNot { it.id == row.id } },
        )
    },
)
examples.setupTemplate:
data class Invoice(val id: String, val number: String, val customer: String, val status: String, val amount: Double, val due: String)
val customers = listOf({{customers.0}}, {{customers.1}}, {{customers.2}}, {{customers.3}})
val statuses = listOf({{statuses.0}}, {{statuses.1}}, {{statuses.2}}, {{statuses.3}})
var rows by remember {
    mutableStateOf(
        (0 until {{rowCount}}).map { i ->
            Invoice(
                id = "inv-$i",
                number = "INV-" + "%05d".format(i + 1),
                customer = customers[i % customers.size],
                status = statuses[i % statuses.size],
                amount = ((i * 7919) % 50_000) / 100.0,
                due = "2026-" + "%02d".format(i % 12 + 1) + "-" + "%02d".format(i % 27 + 1),
            )
        },
    )
}
var sort by remember { mutableStateOf<MonarchDataTableSort?>(null) }
var selected by remember { mutableStateOf(emptySet<String>()) }
val columns = listOf<MonarchDataGridColumn<Invoice>>(
    MonarchDataGridColumn({{columns.0.header}}, id = {{columns.0.id}}, width = {{columns.0.width}}.dp, hideable = false, pinned = MonarchDataGridPin.Start) { it.number },
    MonarchDataGridColumn(
        {{columns.1.header}},
        id = {{columns.1.id}},
        width = {{columns.1.width}}.dp,
        edit = MonarchDataGridEdit(
            editor = MonarchEditableCellEditor.Text,
            value = { it.customer },
            onCommit = { row, value -> rows = rows.map { if (it.id == row.id) it.copy(customer = value.orEmpty()) else it } },
            required = true,
        ),
    ) { it.customer },
    MonarchDataGridColumn(
        {{columns.2.header}},
        id = {{columns.2.id}},
        width = {{columns.2.width}}.dp,
        edit = MonarchDataGridEdit(
            editor = MonarchEditableCellEditor.Select(statuses.map { MonarchSelectOption(it, it) }),
            value = { it.status },
            onCommit = { row, value -> rows = rows.map { if (it.id == row.id) it.copy(status = value.orEmpty()) else it } },
        ),
    ) { it.status },
    MonarchDataGridColumn(
        {{columns.3.header}},
        id = {{columns.3.id}},
        width = {{columns.3.width}}.dp,
        numeric = true,
        edit = MonarchDataGridEdit(
            editor = MonarchEditableCellEditor.Number(min = 0.0),
            value = { it.amount },
            onCommit = { row, value -> rows = rows.map { if (it.id == row.id) it.copy(amount = value ?: it.amount) else it } },
        ),
    ) { "%.2f".format(it.amount) },
    MonarchDataGridColumn({{columns.4.header}}, id = {{columns.4.id}}, width = {{columns.4.width}}.dp) { it.due },
)

parityExceptions.reason: The web grid is 614px wide, so Invoice, Customer and part of Status show beside the pinned actions column. The phone window is 344dp wide: the pinned Invoice column and the selection column leave room for part of Customer, and Status, Amount and Due are reached by scrolling sideways, as on the web. The row actions button scrolls with the row on Android and is pinned at the end on the web. The columns, rows, order and copy are the web's.
parityExceptions.convention: Material adaptive layout: a compact window shows fewer columns

title: DataSubjectRequestForm
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column with androidx.compose.foundation.verticalScroll, holding MonarchRadioCardGroup, MonarchTextField, MonarchCountrySelect, MonarchCheckboxRow, MonarchButton and MonarchBanner
summary: A privacy request form (access, deletion, correction) composed from Monarch fields: the request type as radio cards, who it is for, contact details, the country or region, details, an accuracy acknowledgement, an error summary on submit and the reference once sent.
whenToUse: On a privacy or account screen where people ask for a copy of their data, its deletion or correction, in line with GDPR, CCPA and similar laws.
whenNotToUse: For deleting the signed-in account directly use a danger-zone action with a confirmation; for consent toggles use MonarchConsentManager.
api: Column(Modifier.verticalScroll(rememberScrollState()), verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space4)) { if (submitted && problems.isNotEmpty()) MonarchBanner(title = …, message = …, tone = MonarchTone.Danger, announcement = MonarchBannerAnnouncement.Assertive); MonarchRadioCardGroup(options = types, selected = type, onSelect = …, label = "What would you like to do?"); MonarchRadioCardGroup(options = listOf(MonarchRadioCardOption(true, "Myself"), MonarchRadioCardOption(false, "Someone I am authorized to act for")), …); MonarchTextField(name, …); MonarchTextField(email, …, errorText = …, keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(keyboardType = KeyboardType.Email)); if (!forSelf) MonarchTextField(agentName, …); MonarchCountrySelect(selected = country, onSelectedChange = …, errorText = …); MonarchTextField(details, …, singleLine = false); MonarchCheckboxRow(checked = accurate, onCheckedChange = …, label = "The information I gave is accurate"); MonarchButton(text = "Send request", onClick = …, variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Primary) }
MonarchBanner(title = "Request received", message = "Your reference is …", tone = MonarchTone.Success, announcement = MonarchBannerAnnouncement.Polite)

options.name: request types
options.description: The kinds of request the product offers (access, delete, correct, object, opt out, withdraw consent); which apply where is for the product's legal team.

options.name: relationship
options.description: Whether the request is for the person or made by an authorized agent; an agent also gives their own name (and email).

options.name: email
options.description: Identifies the account; validated on submit with KeyboardType.Email.

options.name: country
options.description: The jurisdiction, as an ISO code from the locale's country list; limit it with countries.

options.name: details
options.description: Required for a correction request.

options.name: acknowledgement
options.description: The form is not sent until it is ticked.

options.name: error summary
options.description: Lists every problem in words; each field also shows its own error.

options.name: success
options.description: Shows the reference the app's API returns.

states.name: filling in
states.description: No errors are shown until Send request is tapped.

states.name: invalid
states.description: A danger banner with the number of problems and each message, and each field's own error.

states.name: agent
states.description: Labels change to "Their full name" and "Their email" and the agent's own name field appears.

states.name: sent
states.description: The form is replaced by a success banner with the reference.

appearance: Each part keeps its own appearance: radio cards with the accent border when chosen, text fields with the input border and the danger color in error, the danger and success banners in their tones. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web DataSubjectRequestForm is one component with default request types, built-in strings, a promise-based onSubmit with a busy state, and focus moved to the first problem. On Android it is a recipe the app owns: the request types, the strings and the API call are the app's, the country comes from MonarchCountrySelect (the web takes the product's own list or a text input), and the error summary is an assertive MonarchBanner instead of moving focus. Wrap the Column in a screen with verticalScroll; the catalogue page leaves the scroll out because the catalogue scrolls. iOS has no entry yet.
accessibility: Both radio card groups are named by their questions and read each card's title and description.
Every field has a visible label; errors are shown under the field and read with it.
After an invalid submit the danger banner is announced assertively with the number of problems and each message.
The acknowledgement is one MonarchCheckboxRow: one TalkBack element with the checkbox role and a 48dp row.
The success banner is announced politely with the reference.
edgeCases: Errors appear only after the first submit and update as the person fixes them.
A correction request needs details; other types do not.
Switching to an agent request asks for the agent's name; switching back keeps what was typed but does not require it.

examples.title: Public privacy request form

parityExceptions.reason: The web marks the optional answers inline after the label (Full name Optional, Details Optional), puts the asterisk after the questions What would you like to do? and Country or region, and draws the radio on the left of each card. The Android fields show Optional as supporting text under the field, the group and country labels carry no asterisk (required is spoken by the field's name only), and the radio sits at the end of the card as in Material list items. The cards are one per line, full width, as the phone pattern for a list of choices (the web has two columns at 614px); the question order, copy and the notice, checkbox and button are the web's.
parityExceptions.convention: Material 3 text field: supporting text under the field; trailing radio in selectable rows

name: MonarchDataTable
title: DataTable
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn with a header row, sized by androidx.compose.foundation.layout.BoxWithConstraints; androidx.compose.material3.Checkbox and TriStateCheckbox for selection; androidx.compose.material3.DropdownMenu for row actions and the sort menu; MonarchSkeleton, MonarchEmptyState and MonarchErrorState for the states
summary: Records in columns: a table on wide screens and a list of records with a labelled line per field on phones, with sorting, selection, row actions, column visibility and order, and the loading, empty, filtered and error states. Read-only.
whenToUse: For a set of records the person scans, sorts, selects and acts on: tickets, invoices, contacts, users.
whenNotToUse: For editable cells there is no Monarch component yet; open a form instead. For a short list of things use a LazyColumn of rows such as MonarchInboxRow. For key and value pairs of one record use MonarchDescriptionList.
api: @Composable public fun <T, K : Any> MonarchDataTable(caption: String, rows: List<T>, columns: List<MonarchDataTableColumn<T>>, rowKey: (T) -> K, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, sort: MonarchDataTableSort? = null, onSortChange: ((MonarchDataTableSort) -> Unit)? = null, selection: Set<K>? = null, onSelectionChange: ((Set<K>) -> Unit)? = null, hiddenColumns: Set<String> = emptySet(), columnOrder: List<String> = emptyList(), layout: MonarchDataTableLayout = MonarchDataTableLayout.Automatic, sortsRows: Boolean = true, loading: Boolean = false, errorMessage: String? = null, filtered: Boolean = false, rowLabel: ((T) -> String)? = null, rowSelectable: (T) -> Boolean = { true }, rowActions: ((T) -> List<MonarchDataTableRowAction>)? = null, onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null, onClearFilters: (() -> Unit)? = null, onOpen: ((T) -> Unit)? = null, actionsIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, state: LazyListState = rememberLazyListState(), labels: MonarchDataTableLabels = MonarchDataTableLabels(), footer: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null)

public class MonarchDataTableColumn<T>(title: String, id: String = title, numeric: Boolean = false, sortable: Boolean = true, hideable: Boolean = true, weight: Float = 1f, comparator: Comparator<T>? = null, value: (T) -> String) { val chooserColumn: MonarchColumnChooserColumn }
public class MonarchDataTableSort(columnId: String, direction: MonarchDataTableSortDirection = MonarchDataTableSortDirection.Ascending) { fun toggled(): MonarchDataTableSort }
public enum class MonarchDataTableSortDirection { Ascending, Descending }
public class MonarchDataTableRowAction(title: String, id: String = title, danger: Boolean = false, enabled: Boolean = true, onClick: () -> Unit)
public enum class MonarchDataTableLayout { Automatic, Table, List }

public class MonarchDataTableLabels(selectAll: String? = null, selectRow: ((row: String) -> String)? = null, selectedCount: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, rowActions: ((row: String) -> String)? = null, actionsText: String? = null, open: String? = null, sort: String? = null, sortedAscending: String? = null, sortedDescending: String? = null, notSorted: String? = null, noValue: String? = null, loading: String? = null, emptyTitle: String? = null, emptyMessage: String? = null, filteredTitle: String? = null, filteredMessage: String? = null, errorTitle: String? = null)

options.name: caption
options.description: Names the table for TalkBack, such as "Open tickets".

options.name: rows
options.description: The rows, in the app's order.

options.name: columns
options.description: Every column in its default order: header, cell text, numeric alignment, sort rule, whether it sorts and hides, width share.

options.name: rowKey
options.description: A row's stable, unique key, also the key in selection and the lazy key; use a String, Int or Long.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the table. The table scrolls itself; bound its height inside a scrolling parent.

options.name: sort
options.description: The sort, one column and a direction, or null for the app's order.

options.name: onSortChange
options.description: Receives the new sort from a header or the Sort menu. Without it nothing sorts.

options.name: selection
options.description: The selected keys. With onSelectionChange, rows get checkboxes and a select-all checkbox appears above them.

options.name: onSelectionChange
options.description: Receives the whole new selection.

options.name: hiddenColumns
options.description: Ids of hidden columns, as MonarchColumnChooser writes them. Columns that are not hideable stay shown.

options.name: columnOrder
options.description: Column ids in display order; missing ids follow in their default order.

options.name: layout
options.description: A table from 640dp of width below font scale 1.5 and a list of records otherwise, or always one of them.

options.name: sortsRows
options.description: Whether the table sorts rows itself; false when the server sorts and the app reloads on sort changes.

options.name: loading
options.description: With no rows, shows placeholder rows; with rows, adds them after the last row.

options.name: errorMessage
options.description: With no rows, shows the error state with this message.

options.name: filtered
options.description: No rows means the filters matched nothing: the filtered empty state.

options.name: rowLabel
options.description: A row's name in the list layout and in spoken labels. By default the first shown cell.

options.name: rowSelectable
options.description: Whether a row has a checkbox.

options.name: rowActions
options.description: A row's actions: an actions menu and the same actions as TalkBack actions.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Adds a retry button to the error state.

options.name: onClearFilters
options.description: Adds Clear filters to the filtered empty state.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Makes each row a button that opens the record; its name is in the link color.

options.name: actionsIcon
options.description: The actions button's icon. Without it the button shows "Actions".

options.name: state
options.description: The scroll state of the rows.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

options.name: footer
options.description: Content after the last row, such as a MonarchLoadMore for paged data.

states.name: table
states.description: A header row with sortable headers (a mark after the sorted one), then a row per record with a cell per shown column, a checkbox column and an actions column when used.

states.name: list
states.description: One record per row: checkbox, the name in bold (link-coloured when it opens), a field name and value per other column, and an actions button; a Sort button sits above the rows.

states.name: selected
states.description: Checked checkboxes on the accent's subtle fill, and "3 selected" beside Select all rows.

states.name: loading
states.description: With no rows, skeleton rows named "Loading rows"; with rows, skeleton rows after the last one.

states.name: failed
states.description: With no rows, a MonarchErrorState, "These rows could not be loaded", with the message and a retry button.

states.name: filtered
states.description: A filtered MonarchEmptyState, "No rows match these filters", with Clear filters.

states.name: empty
states.description: A MonarchEmptyState, "Nothing here yet".

appearance: Rows on the surface fill with a 1dp subtle divider; selected rows on the accent's subtle fill. Headers and field names are muted; numeric cells are aligned to the end with tabular figures; an empty cell shows a muted dash. Danger actions use the danger text color. Every color is a theme role, so dark and both high-contrast themes follow the theme.
platformNotes: Compose has no data table, so Monarch draws one on a LazyColumn; the table layout gives each column at least 128dp and scrolls sideways when the columns need more than the screen, so a phone shows the first columns and the rest are a swipe away; a MonarchColumnChooser can hide columns to fit. Cells are text from each column's value; the web's custom cell renderers, expandable rows, column resizing, multi-column sort, keyboard grid navigation, pagination, density and select-all-matching are not offered (use footer with a MonarchLoadMore for paging). Sorting, selection, hidden columns and the order are hoisted, as on iOS; iOS can also keep the sort internally. Row actions are a menu and TalkBack actions; iOS adds swipe actions, which Android leaves to the app (see the row-actions-menu recipe). The automatic layout switches at 640dp, the breakpoint the web uses, rather than iOS's size classes. The sort marks and the empty-cell dash are built-in resources that are not read by TalkBack and have no override.
accessibility: The table is a traversal group named by caption.
In the list layout each record is one element read as its name and "Field, value" for each column, with "No value" for an empty cell; with onOpen it is a button with the action "Open details".
Row actions are TalkBack actions on the row, and also a separate button named "Actions for" and the row's name with a 48dp touch target.
Each checkbox is named "Select" and the row's name; Select all rows is a tri-state checkbox read with the selected count.
Sortable headers are headings and buttons with the state "Sorted ascending", "Sorted descending" or "Not sorted"; the list layout's Sort button reads the sorted column and direction as its state.
Loading rows are one element named "Loading rows" with an indeterminate progress.
At font scale 1.5 and above the automatic layout is the list, and record text wraps.
edgeCases: Empty cells sort last in both directions; numeric columns sort by the number in the text, ignoring grouping marks and currency.
A sort on an unknown or unsortable column leaves the rows in the app's order.
rowKey values must be unique and savable in a Bundle; the same key twice breaks the lazy list.
The select-all checkbox selects only rows that rowSelectable allows and keeps other selected keys.
With rowLabel the list layout shows every shown column under the name; without it the first column is the name.

whenNotToUse: For one date, use the Material 3 DatePicker (see date-picker). For two unrelated dates, use two DatePickers. For a few fixed periods with no custom range, use a MonarchSegmentedControl (see segmented-control) or MonarchSelect.

states.description: The field's button reads "Choose dates"; the dialog opens with no day selected.

states.name: chosen
states.description: The button shows the first and last day in the locale's medium format; the dialog opens with the range highlighted from start to end.

states.name: half chosen
states.description: In the dialog the first tap sets the start and the second the end; until both are set the app keeps Save disabled, so a filter never runs on half a range.

states.name: limited
states.description: Days SelectableDates rejects (before the earliest or after the latest day) are dimmed and cannot be chosen; yearRange limits the years.

states.name: too long
states.description: The app disables Save while the range is longer than its longest length, and says the limit in the field's helper text.

states.name: input mode
states.description: The mode toggle switches to two typed date fields in the locale's pattern, validated by Material 3, which also reports an end before the start.

states.name: disabled

appearance: The dialog uses the raised surface with extra-large corners; the start and end days sit on the accent solid circle with on-solid text, the days between on the accent subtle band, today is outlined in the accent role and disabled days use the disabled text role, all from MonarchTheme in the light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Planned and kept as native: Material 3 has a range picker, and an Android user expects it (Google Calendar, Settings). The web DateRangePicker is a single field with two typed inputs and a one- or two-month calendar that previews the range as the pointer moves, with presets, minimum and maximum lengths, week numbers and day dots. On Android the Material 3 DateRangePicker is a full-height scrolling calendar (in a DatePickerDialog, or full screen) with its own typed input mode; presets are a MonarchMenu beside the field and call DateRangePickerState.setSelection; the earliest and latest days are SelectableDates; a shortest or longest length is checked by the app before Save, because SelectableDates cannot depend on the chosen start. Values are epoch milliseconds at UTC midnight (selectedStartDateMillis, selectedEndDateMillis), both ends inclusive, not ISO strings. Week numbers and day dots are not offered by Material 3; for those use MonarchMiniMonth. iOS builds MonarchDateRangePicker, Start and End rows of system date pickers, because iOS has no range calendar.
accessibility: System behavior: the dialog is a window with its own title, so TalkBack moves into it and returns to the field's button when it closes.
System behavior: each day is a button read with its full date and whether it is the start, the end, in the range, today or disabled.
System behavior: the input mode has two labelled text fields whose errors are read by TalkBack.
The field's button is a MonarchButton with a 48dp target, labelled by MonarchFormField, and its text says the range or "Choose dates".
Preset items are MonarchMenuItem buttons; Save is a ghost MonarchButton read as disabled while the range is incomplete or too long.
Font scale and right-to-left calendars are handled by Material 3.
edgeCases: selectedStartDateMillis and selectedEndDateMillis are UTC midnights: formatting them in the device zone can show the previous day west of UTC.
A range of one day has the same start and end; the user taps the same day twice.
The state is remembered once: after a preset, call setSelection so the dialog opens on the preset range.
The dialog is tall; give DateRangePicker Modifier.weight(1f) inside DatePickerDialog so its months scroll.

whenToUse: For one moment in a form that needs both a day and a time: an interview, a booking start, a reminder. Show the two buttons side by side, as Android calendar apps do, so the person can change one without the other.
whenNotToUse: For a day alone use the Material 3 DatePicker (see date-picker); for a time alone the Material 3 TimePicker or TimeInput. To pick from offered times (booking slots), use slot-picker. For a start and an end, use two of these rows or a date range picker.

The zone label uses the muted text role.
platformNotes: The web DateTimePicker is one field: a DatePicker plus a typed time with arrow-key steps, min and max to the minute, presets and a time zone slot, with the value as a zone-less YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm string. On Android the expected control is two buttons that open the Material 3 date and time pickers, as in Android calendar apps; the time follows the person's 12- or 24-hour system setting (rememberTimePickerState reads it) instead of the locale alone. Keep the value as the day's UTC midnight (DatePickerState.selectedDateMillis) plus hour * 60 + minute, a wall-clock value that never shifts with the device's zone; format it with a UTC formatter. The time zone is a separate slot: a label or a time zone select beside the buttons; neither picker converts between zones. The time picker has no step, minimum or maximum: round and check in the app. Presets are a MonarchMenu as in date-picker. iOS uses the SwiftUI DatePicker with .date and .hourAndMinute components in the same MonarchFormField row.
accessibility: System behavior: each dialog is a window with its own title, so TalkBack moves into it and returns to the button that opened it when it closes.

The time zone is plain text read after the buttons; nothing depends on color.
Font scale, right to left and the 12- or 24-hour clock are handled by Material 3.
edgeCases: selectedDateMillis is a UTC midnight: format the date and the combined value with a UTC formatter, or west of UTC it shows the previous day.
A wall-clock time that does not exist or exists twice on a daylight-saving change is not checked by either picker; resolve it when converting to an instant in the event's zone.
TimePickerState keeps the time while the dialog is closed; copy hour and minute into the app's value only on OK, so Cancel discards the change.
Both dialogs are tall; at the largest font scale on a small phone the date dialog scrolls and TimeInput fits better than the clock face.

title: DeactivateFlow
wrapsNative: MonarchBottomSheet with rememberModalBottomSheetState(confirmValueChange) to stop dismissal while working, holding a verticalScroll Column of MonarchText, MonarchConsequenceList, MonarchTextField, MonarchInlineNotice and MonarchButtons
summary: A recipe, not a component: confirm a reversible pause (a partnership, a tracker, a person) in a sheet that says where to turn it back on, lists what changes meanwhile and can record a reason; the same sheet confirms reactivation.
whenToUse: Before pausing something that can be turned back on and keeps its data, when the person should see what stops working meanwhile and may give a reason.
whenNotToUse: For something that cannot be undone, such as deleting, use the confirm dialog (an MonarchDialog with a danger MonarchButton) or MonarchTypeToConfirmInput. For a pause with no consequences and no reason, a MonarchDialog with a primary button is enough.

appearance: Every part is an existing Monarch component in the theme on the Material 3 sheet surface: the title in the title style, the consequence list with its kind marks, the text field with its helper text, and a full-width primary button over a ghost Cancel. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.

On Android a MonarchDialog has room for neither a consequence list nor a text field, so, as on iOS, the recipe uses a MonarchBottomSheet with a primary (not danger) confirm button, since nothing is deleted; Monarch has no warning button variant. The web's mode, subject and reactivateFrom props become the app's own state and strings in the recipe. rememberModalBottomSheetState's confirmValueChange keeps the sheet open while the request runs, where iOS uses interactiveDismissDisabled. The parity map lists confirm-dialog: the dialog is replaced by the sheet for the reason above.

The reversibility line is plain text, read in order after the description.
MonarchConsequenceList reads each consequence with its kind, not by its mark's color alone.
The reason field is a MonarchTextField with its label and helper text.
Buttons are MonarchButtons with 48dp touch targets and a busy state while working; the sheet cannot be dismissed while the request runs.
edgeCases: If the request fails, keep the sheet open with the error so the person can retry or cancel.
Send the reason with the request only when it is not blank.
Offer reactivation from the place the reversibility line names, so the promise in the line is true.

options.description: Why the last save failed, shown in a danger banner.

options.name: reasonLimit
options.description: The longest reason accepted, in characters.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

options.name: onDecide
options.description: Receives the decision to save. Without it the card is read-only.

options.name: context
options.description: Evidence for the decision, shown above the choices.

states.name: unchanged
states.description: The Save button is disabled while the form equals the saved decision.

states.name: selected choice
states.description: The radio button of the choice is selected; its note is shown under the choices.

states.name: reason missing
states.description: After Save is activated without a required reason, the field is in the error state with a message.

states.name: near the limit
states.description: From 50 characters left, the number left is shown under the reason.

states.name: saving
states.description: The choices and the reason are disabled and the button shows progress.

states.name: saved
states.description: "Decision saved." is shown under the time until the next edit.

states.name: failed
states.description: The choice and the reason are kept and the error is shown in a danger banner.

states.name: read-only
states.description: A badge in the option's tone, or "No decision yet", then the reason and who decided when.

appearance: A MonarchCard with the group name, notes, time and saved message in the muted text color. The choices are Material 3 radio buttons, the reason an outlined text field and Save a primary button; the read-only decision is a subtle badge in the option's tone. Colors come from these components' roles in every theme.
platformNotes: The web card uses radio inputs and a Textarea and calls onDecide, which may return a promise. Android draws the choices as a row of selectable tiles with MonarchRadioCardGroup in its Tile layout, as the web does, where iOS draws button rows with a checkmark. Saving is hoisted, as Compose state is: onDecide receives the decision and the app sets saving and then the new value, or errorText, instead of an async function that throws. The web headingLevel, now and locale properties have no counterpart: the title is a heading, and the time uses the user's locale and is redrawn every minute. The built-in "characters left" text is a plurals resource.
accessibility: The title is a heading.
Each choice is one TalkBack element with the radio button role, read as its label and description, inside a selectable group with the visible name "Decision".
Selection is the radio mark as well as a color.
The note of the selected choice is a polite live region, so a newly selected choice's note is announced.
A missing reason puts the field in the error state, which TalkBack reads with the message.
The saved message and the error banner are polite live regions.
The time of the decision is shown as a relative time and read as an absolute date and time.
Every choice and the Save button have 48dp touch targets.
edgeCases: A new value or reason from the app resets the form.
A reason of white space only counts as empty, and the reason is trimmed before it is passed to onDecide.
Text beyond reasonLimit is cut as it is typed or pasted.
With allowNone false and no saved value, no choice is selected and Save stays disabled until one is chosen.
The empty saved-message line keeps its height so the live region is always present.

Read-only, for people who cannot change it
examples.code:
MonarchDecisionCard(
    options = listOf(MonarchDecisionOption(label = "Keep", value = "keep", tone = MonarchTone.Success)),
    value = "keep",
    reason = "Still in use by the support team.",
    decidedBy = "Ana",
    readOnly = true,
)

parityExceptions.reason: The web shows the four decisions in one row of 120px tiles and Reason optional with a muted word after the label. The phone window is 344dp wide, so the four tiles do not fit on one line: three share the first line and No decision wraps onto a second; the Reason label reads Reason (optional) in one style, as the field's label, and the textarea text starts at its top as on the web. The title, usage line, tiles, reason, Decided line and Save decision are the web's.

title: DeleteAccountFlow
wrapsNative: MonarchBottomSheet (confirmValueChange keeps it open while deleting) with a scrolling androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of MonarchConsequenceList, MonarchInlineNotice, MonarchDataExportRequest, MonarchSelect, MonarchTextField, MonarchTypeToConfirmInput, MonarchStepUpAuthDialog and MonarchButtons
summary: A recipe, not a component: a person deletes their own account after resolving the workspaces they own alone, with an optional data export and reason, typing their email and confirming who they are.
whenToUse: In account settings, for a person who wants their account gone. Google Play and the App Store require apps that let people create an account to let them delete it from the app.
whenNotToUse: To delete a workspace, use the delete-workspace recipe. To leave one workspace, use the leave-workspace recipe. To pause an account, use the deactivate recipe.
api: ModalBottomSheet(onDismissRequest = { if (!deleting) open = false }, sheetState = rememberModalBottomSheetState(skipPartiallyExpanded = true, confirmValueChange = { !deleting })) { … }
MonarchConsequenceList(items = listOf(MonarchConsequence(MonarchConsequenceKind.Removed, "Your profile and settings"), …), heading = "What happens")
MonarchDataExportRequest(status = export, onRequest = { … }) // @ExperimentalMonarchApi, opted in at the call
MonarchSelect(options = …, selected = reason, onSelect = { reason = it }, label = "Reason", placeholder = "Choose a reason")
MonarchTypeToConfirmInput(phrase = email, value = typed, onValueChange = { typed = it }, label = "Type $email to confirm")
MonarchStepUpAuthDialog(onVerify = …, description = "Deleting your account needs you to confirm your identity.", onCancel = …, onVerified = …, onVerifyingChange = { deleting = it })

options.name: confirmPhrase
options.description: What the person types to confirm, usually their account email. Matching is case-sensitive and ignores spaces around it (MonarchTypeToConfirmInputDefaults.matches).

options.name: ownedWorkspaces
options.description: Workspaces the person owns alone. While the list is not empty the review step lists them, each with Transfer or delete, and Continue is disabled. Update it as they are resolved.

options.name: consequences
options.description: What deleting the account does, shown on the review step.

options.name: export
options.description: Offer the optional export step with MonarchDataExportRequest; leave the step out when the product has no export.

options.name: reasons
options.description: Choices for "Why are you leaving?"; leave the step out to skip it.

options.name: stepUp
options.description: Re-authentication before the delete; biometric through onRequestBiometric, which the app backs with BiometricPrompt.

options.name: deleting, failure
options.description: While the request runs the sheet cannot be dismissed; a failure goes back to the confirm step with a danger notice.

states.name: review
states.description: The title, what happens (consequence list) and, when the person owns workspaces alone, a warning notice with each workspace and Transfer or delete; Continue is disabled until none is left.

states.name: export
states.description: MonarchDataExportRequest offers a copy of the data; Continue goes on with or without it.

states.name: reason
states.description: An optional reason in a MonarchSelect and a multi-line comment field.

states.name: confirm
states.description: The email field and a danger Delete account button, disabled until the email matches; a failure shows here.

states.name: verify
states.description: MonarchStepUpAuthDialog asks for the password, a code or the device's lock; Cancel returns to confirm.

states.name: deleting
states.description: After verification the request runs; the sheet cannot be swiped or backed away.

states.name: done
states.description: "Account deleted" and Done; the app then signs the person out.

appearance: Every part is an existing Monarch component on the Material 3 sheet surface: title styles, the consequence list with its kind marks, a warning notice, the export card, the select and text fields, the type-to-confirm field, and full-width primary, danger and ghost buttons. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web's DeleteAccountFlow is one component on WizardDialog with review, export, reason and confirm steps, step-up and a farewell screen. On Android it is a recipe, as on iOS: a MonarchBottomSheet holds the steps as a when over the app's step state, because a dialog has no room for the lists and fields. The web's renderWorkspaceAction and onResolveWorkspace are the app's Transfer or delete button, which opens the workspace's settings. The web's step progress ("Step 2 of 4") and Back are the app's to add when it wants them. Biometric step-up uses onRequestBiometric on MonarchStepUpAuthDialog; the app owns BiometricPrompt. The web's member counts are formatted by the app.
accessibility: Each step starts with a title in the title style, which MonarchText marks as a heading.
MonarchConsequenceList reads each line with its kind, so removed and kept do not depend on the mark.
Each Transfer or delete button is named with its workspace, "Transfer or delete Acme"; Continue is announced as disabled while workspaces remain, and the warning notice says why in words.
MonarchTypeToConfirmInput announces when the email matches; Delete account is disabled until then.
MonarchStepUpAuthDialog labels its fields and announces errors; the sheet cannot be dismissed while deleting.
Every button has a 48dp target; the steps scroll at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: Check ownership, the email and the step-up on the server as well; the recipe only gates the buttons.
When the person owns no workspace alone, the review step shows only the consequences and Continue.
A grace period (deleted in 30 days) changes the done text; offer a way to cancel by signing in again.
After deletion sign the person out and leave every account screen: the account no longer exists.

parityExceptions.reason: The web shows the steps in a centred dialog with a close button, and Cancel and Continue side by side at the bottom. Android shows them in a modal bottom sheet with the dialog's title, one full-width Continue button and Cancel under it, because a sheet is the phone's surface for a task of several steps. The Danger zone card, the four-part step progress, the review list and the copy are the web's.

title: DeleteWorkspaceFlow
wrapsNative: MonarchBottomSheet (confirmValueChange keeps it open while deleting) with a scrolling androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of MonarchConsequenceList, MonarchTypeToConfirmInput, MonarchStepUpAuthDialog, MonarchInlineNotice and MonarchButtons
summary: A recipe, not a component: an owner deletes a whole workspace after seeing what is lost, being offered an export, typing the workspace's name and confirming who they are.
whenToUse: On a workspace's settings screen, in its danger zone, for an owner who wants the workspace and everything in it gone.
whenNotToUse: For a member leaving, use the leave-workspace recipe. For pausing, use the deactivate recipe. For deleting one item, a confirm dialog is enough.
api: ModalBottomSheet(onDismissRequest = { if (!deleting) open = false }, sheetState = rememberModalBottomSheetState(skipPartiallyExpanded = true, confirmValueChange = { !deleting })) { … }
MonarchConsequenceList(items = listOf(MonarchConsequence(MonarchConsequenceKind.Removed, "Apps", count = 4), …), heading = "What will be deleted")
MonarchTypeToConfirmInput(phrase = workspace, value = typed, onValueChange = { typed = it }, label = "Type $workspace to confirm")
MonarchButton("Delete workspace", …, variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Danger, enabled = MonarchTypeToConfirmInputDefaults.matches(typed, workspace))
MonarchStepUpAuthDialog(onVerify = …, description = "Deleting a workspace needs you to confirm it’s you.", onCancel = …, onVerified = …, onVerifyingChange = { deleting = it })

options.name: impact
options.description: What is lost, with counts from the server: apps, records, members, subscriptions and domains. Leave out a line whose count is 0; pass loading = true to MonarchConsequenceList while the counts load.

options.name: gracePeriodDays
options.description: When the server keeps the workspace for a while, say "Schedule deletion" and the date (DateUtils) instead of "deleted at once".

options.name: deleting
options.description: While the request runs the sheet cannot be dismissed and the step-up dialog shows its progress.

options.name: failure
options.description: A failed request, shown in a danger MonarchInlineNotice; the person can try again.

states.name: review
states.description: The title naming the workspace, a sentence that it cannot be undone, the consequence list, Export data, the name field and a disabled danger button until the name matches.

states.name: verify
states.description: MonarchStepUpAuthDialog in the sheet asks for the password, a code or the device's lock; Cancel goes back to the review.

states.name: deleting
states.description: After verification the request runs; the sheet cannot be swiped or backed away.

states.name: failed
states.description: A danger MonarchInlineNotice above the step-up content; the person can verify and try again.

states.name: done
states.description: A title that the workspace was deleted and a Done button; the app then leaves the workspace's screens.

appearance: Every part is an existing Monarch component on the Material 3 sheet surface: the title style, the consequence list with its kind marks and counts, a secondary Export button, the type-to-confirm field, and full-width danger and ghost buttons. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web's DeleteWorkspaceFlow is one component on WizardDialog with impact, export, transfer, confirm and done steps and a step-up requirement. On Android it is a recipe, as on iOS: a MonarchBottomSheet holds the steps, because a MonarchDialog has no room for the consequence list, the name field and the step-up content, and the steps are a when over the app's step state. The web's transfer step is a MonarchButton the app adds that opens its transfer ownership screen. The web's default messages and counts formatting are written by the app; MonarchConsequence's count is formatted by MonarchConsequenceList. Biometric step-up uses onRequestBiometric on MonarchStepUpAuthDialog; the app owns BiometricPrompt.
accessibility: The sheet's title uses the title style, which MonarchText marks as a heading.
MonarchConsequenceList reads each line with its kind and count, so removed and warning do not depend on the mark.
MonarchTypeToConfirmInput announces when the typed name matches; the danger button is announced as disabled until then.
MonarchStepUpAuthDialog labels its fields and announces errors; its buttons have 48dp targets.
The sheet cannot be dismissed while deleting, so the result is not lost.
edgeCases: Check the name and the step-up on the server as well; the recipe only gates the button.
The typed name must match exactly, case included; white space around it is ignored (MonarchTypeToConfirmInputDefaults.matches).
After deletion, navigate away: the workspace's screens no longer exist.
With a grace period, offer to cancel the deletion from the workspace's settings until the date.
