name: MonarchDeltaIndicator
title: DeltaIndicator
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row, androidx.compose.material3.Text
summary: A change between two periods: a signed value, an optional arrow and an optional comparison, such as "+12% vs last month". The color follows which direction is better.
whenToUse: Next to a figure in a stat card, a table cell or a chart summary, to say how it moved since the previous period.
whenNotToUse: For a status that is not a change use MonarchBadge. For a trend over many periods use MonarchSparkline next to the figure.
api: @Composable fun MonarchDeltaIndicator(value: Double?, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, comparison: String? = null, goodDirection: MonarchDeltaIndicatorGoodDirection = MonarchDeltaIndicatorGoodDirection.Up, variant: MonarchDeltaIndicatorVariant = MonarchDeltaIndicatorVariant.Plain, size: MonarchDeltaIndicatorSize = MonarchDeltaIndicatorSize.Sm, flatThreshold: Double = 0.0, icon: (@Composable (direction: MonarchDeltaIndicatorDirection) -> Unit)? = null, formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = null, flatLabel: String? = null, noDataLabel: String? = null, spokenLabel: String? = null)

@Composable fun MonarchDeltaIndicator(current: Double?, previous: Double?, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, comparison: String? = null, goodDirection: MonarchDeltaIndicatorGoodDirection = MonarchDeltaIndicatorGoodDirection.Up, variant: MonarchDeltaIndicatorVariant = MonarchDeltaIndicatorVariant.Plain, size: MonarchDeltaIndicatorSize = MonarchDeltaIndicatorSize.Sm, flatThreshold: Double = 0.0, icon: (@Composable (direction: MonarchDeltaIndicatorDirection) -> Unit)? = null, formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = null, flatLabel: String? = null, noDataLabel: String? = null, spokenLabel: String? = null)
enum class MonarchDeltaIndicatorGoodDirection { Up, Down, Neither }
enum class MonarchDeltaIndicatorVariant { Plain, Subtle }
enum class MonarchDeltaIndicatorSize { Sm, Md }
enum class MonarchDeltaIndicatorDirection { Up, Down, Flat }

options.name: value
options.description: The change. With the default writer a ratio: 0.12 is 12%. null, NaN or infinity means there is nothing to compare with.

options.name: current, previous
options.description: In the second overload: the two periods. The change is (current − previous) / |previous|; a previous value of 0 has no baseline.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the indicator.

options.name: comparison
options.description: The comparison period after the change, such as "vs last month". Shown muted and spoken.

options.name: goodDirection
options.description: Up, Down or Neither: which direction is an improvement.

options.name: variant
options.description: Plain is inline text; Subtle puts the change in a tinted pill.

options.name: size
options.description: Sm is the caption style, Md the label style.

options.name: flatThreshold
options.description: Changes whose size is at or below this count as no change.

options.name: icon
options.description: Draws the arrow for the direction, tinted with the tone color and hidden from TalkBack. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes the size of the change without a sign. The default is a percentage with at most one fraction digit in the current locale.

options.name: flatLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in text "No change" (monarch_deltaindicator_flat).

options.name: noDataLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in text "No earlier data" (monarch_deltaindicator_no_data).

options.name: spokenLabel
options.description: Replaces the whole sentence TalkBack reads.

states.name: better
states.description: A change in the good direction: the success color, a sign and "better" in the spoken sentence.

states.name: worse
states.description: A change in the other direction: the danger color, a sign and "worse" in the spoken sentence.

states.name: neutral
states.description: goodDirection is Neither: muted text and a sign.

states.name: no change
states.description: Zero, inside flatThreshold, or written the same as zero: "No change" in the muted color.

states.name: no data
states.description: null or not finite: "No earlier data", with no arrow and no comparison.

appearance: Plain draws the change in the strong color of its tone (success strong, danger strong, or muted text for neutral) and the comparison in muted text. Subtle puts the change in a fully rounded pill with the tone's subtle background and strong text. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web formats percentages, numbers with a unit and currencies from options; here the default is a percentage in the current locale and formatValue takes a function for anything else, as on iOS. The web appearance values plain and pill are the variants Plain and Subtle. The web draws its own arrow; Monarch for Android bundles no icons, so the arrow is an optional slot that receives the direction, and without it the sign and the spoken words carry the direction. The web lets each spoken word be replaced; here the words are string resources (monarch_deltaindicator_*) that an app can translate, and spokenLabel replaces the whole sentence. The current and previous overload always gives a ratio.
accessibility: The indicator is one element whose content description is a sentence: "up 12% vs last month, better".
Better and worse are spoken, and the visible change has a sign, so nothing depends on color.
A decrease is written with a real minus sign (U+2212).
The icon slot is decoration and is not read.
The indicator has no click action and no touch target.
Digits use tabular figures, and a long comparison wraps inside the available width at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: A change that the writer writes the same as zero, such as 0.00001 as a percentage, is "No change", never "+0%".
With current and previous, a previous value of zero has no baseline and shows "No earlier data".
A negative baseline uses its absolute value, so −100 to −50 is an increase of 50%.
The comparison is not shown when there is no data.

examples.title: Better, worse and lower-is-better
Lower is better, written in milliseconds
examples.code:
MonarchDeltaIndicator(
    value = -42.0,
    goodDirection = MonarchDeltaIndicatorGoodDirection.Down,
    variant = MonarchDeltaIndicatorVariant.Subtle,
    formatValue = { "${it.toInt()} ms" },
)

examples.title: From two periods, with an arrow
examples.code:
MonarchDeltaIndicator(
    current = 120.0,
    previous = 100.0,
    comparison = "vs last week",
    size = MonarchDeltaIndicatorSize.Md,
    icon = { MonarchIcon(SampleIcons.ArrowUp, contentDescription = null) },
)

name: MonarchDependencyPicker
title: DependencyPicker
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of relation headings and link rows (MonarchStatusGlyph, MonarchText, androidx.compose.foundation.clickable); MonarchSelect (androidx.compose.material3.ExposedDropdownMenuBox) for the relation and MonarchCombobox in its sheet presentation (androidx.compose.material3.ModalBottomSheet with a search field) to find the item
summary: Lists an item's links (blocked by, blocks, related to, duplicates, duplicated by) and adds new ones by choosing a relation and searching for the item in a sheet.
whenToUse: On an issue, task or ticket detail screen, to show and edit what blocks it, what it blocks, and related or duplicate items.
whenNotToUse: To pick one related record without a relation, use MonarchCombobox or MonarchEntityPicker. For a dependency graph across many items, use a timeline such as MonarchGanttTimeline.
api: @Composable fun MonarchDependencyPicker(value: List<MonarchDependencyLink>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, onAdd: ((MonarchDependencyRelation, MonarchDependencyItem) -> Unit)? = null, onRemove: ((MonarchDependencyLink) -> Unit)? = null, onOpen: ((MonarchDependencyItem) -> Unit)? = null, items: List<MonarchDependencyItem> = emptyList(), excludeIds: Set<String> = emptySet(), relations: List<MonarchDependencyRelation> = MonarchDependencyRelation.entries, defaultRelation: MonarchDependencyRelation? = null, readOnly: Boolean = false, enabled: Boolean = true, loading: Boolean = false, query: String? = null, onQueryChange: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, removeIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchDependencyPickerLabels = MonarchDependencyPickerLabels())
enum class MonarchDependencyRelation { BlockedBy, Blocks, Relates, Duplicates, DuplicatedBy }
class MonarchDependencyItem(id: String, title: String, key: String? = null, status: MonarchStatusOption? = null)
class MonarchDependencyLink(id: String, relation: MonarchDependencyRelation, item: MonarchDependencyItem)

class MonarchDependencyPickerLabels(relations: Map<MonarchDependencyRelation, String> = emptyMap(), relationLabel: String? = null, searchLabel: String? = null, searchPlaceholder: String? = null, noResults: String? = null, empty: String? = null, remove: String? = null, removeItem: ((relation: String, item: String) -> String)? = null, added: ((relation: String, item: String) -> String)? = null, removed: ((relation: String, item: String) -> String)? = null, status: ((name: String) -> String)? = null)

options.name: value
options.description: The current links, shown grouped by relation in the order of relations.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the picker.

options.name: onAdd
options.description: Asks the app to save a new link and update value. Without it there are no add controls.

options.name: onRemove
options.description: Asks the app to remove a link. Without it rows have no remove button.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Opens a linked item, for example its detail screen. Makes the row's text a button.

options.name: items
options.description: The items the search offers. Items already linked and excludeIds are left out.

options.name: excludeIds
options.description: Ids that cannot be linked, such as the item itself.

options.name: relations
options.description: The relations offered, in display order.

options.name: defaultRelation
options.description: The relation chosen at first; the first of relations when null.

options.name: readOnly
options.description: Hides the add controls and the remove buttons.

options.name: enabled
options.description: When false the relation menu, the search and the remove buttons are disabled.

options.name: loading
options.description: Items are being fetched: the search sheet shows its loading state.

options.name: query
options.description: The search text, for a server search, with onQueryChange.

options.name: onQueryChange
options.description: Called with the search text on every keystroke. With it, every item in items is offered: the app filters on its server.

options.name: removeIcon
options.description: The icon of each remove button. Monarch bundles no icons; without it the buttons read "Remove".

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, including the relation names.

states.name: empty
states.description: "No linked items." above the add controls.

states.name: links
states.description: A subheading per relation with links, then one row per link: the status glyph, the key in code style, the title and a remove button.

states.name: adding
states.description: The relation menu, then a search field that opens a bottom sheet with a search box and the matching items; picking one calls onAdd.

states.name: read only
states.description: Only the grouped links.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The menu, the search and the remove buttons are disabled.

appearance: Relation names use the subheading style, keys the code style in the muted text color, and titles the body style. The status glyph takes its category colors from MonarchStatusGlyph. Menus, the search sheet and buttons take their Monarch colors. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those roles.
platformNotes: The web searches in an inline combobox popover; on Android the search opens in a bottom sheet (MonarchCombobox's sheet presentation), the phone pattern for picking from a long list. The web links a title to an href; on Android onOpen makes the row a button and the app navigates, because components do not navigate. The web's onSearch with an AbortSignal is query and onQueryChange with app-side loading, as in MonarchCombobox. The web's headingLevel has no Android equivalent: headings are headings. Same name as iOS's plan; iOS has not built it yet.
accessibility: Each relation name is a heading, so a relation is never conveyed by position or color.
A row's glyph, key and title are read as one element, with the status by name ("Status: In progress"); with onOpen the element is a button with a 48dp touch target.
Remove buttons are named with the relation and the item ("Remove “Blocked by” link to STR-12 Fix the login redirect") and have 48dp touch targets.
Additions and removals are announced through a polite live region on an always-present node.
edgeCases: An item cannot be linked twice: linked items are left out of the search, whatever the relation.
Links whose relation is not in relations are not shown.
The app decides whether a reverse link (blocks / blocked by) is created on the other item.
Long titles wrap; keys stay on one line.

name: MonarchDescriptionList
title: DescriptionList
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column, androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row, androidx.compose.foundation.layout.BoxWithConstraints
summary: Key and value facts of a record (owner, stage, created), stacked or inline, in one or more columns, with optional copy buttons, line limits and a "Not set" dash for empty values.
whenToUse: On detail screens, for the facts of a record people read rather than edit.
whenNotToUse: For editable values use form fields. For data people compare across many records use a table or list. For one fact in running text, write it out.
api: @Composable fun MonarchDescriptionList(items: List<MonarchDescriptionItem>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, layout: MonarchDescriptionListLayout = MonarchDescriptionListLayout.Stacked, columns: Int = 1, copyIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, emptyLabel: String? = null, showMoreLabel: String? = null, showLessLabel: String? = null)

class MonarchDescriptionItem(term: String, value: String?, copyable: Boolean = false, copyValue: String? = null, maxLines: Int? = null, wide: Boolean = false, content: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null)
enum class MonarchDescriptionListLayout { Stacked, Inline }

options.name: items
options.description: The facts: term, value text, copy options, line limit, wide flag and an optional content slot such as a badge.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the list.

options.name: layout
options.description: Stacked puts the term above the value; Inline puts them side by side and stacks when the list is narrower than 288dp or the font scale is 1.5 or more.

options.name: columns
options.description: How many items share a row from 640dp wide; below that every item takes its own row. Wide items always take a whole row.

options.name: copyIcon
options.description: A copy icon; given, copy buttons are icon buttons, otherwise small ghost text buttons.

options.name: emptyLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken text of an empty value, "Not set" (monarch_descriptionlist_empty).

options.name: showMoreLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Show more" of values with a line limit (MonarchTruncatedText).

options.name: showLessLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Show less" of values with a line limit.

states.name: stacked
states.description: The term in the muted caption style above the value in the body style.

states.name: inline
states.description: The term at the start in two fifths of the row and the value beside it.

states.name: empty
states.description: A dash in the subtle text color, read as "Not set"; no copy button.

states.name: truncated
states.description: The value cut at maxLines with a Show more button that expands it.

appearance: Terms in the caption style and the muted text color, values in the body style and the default text color, an empty value's dash in the subtle text color. Copy buttons are ghost MonarchCopyButtons. No borders or fills. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: iOS styles the system LabeledContent (MonarchLabeledContentStyle) and composes copy, truncation and columns; Compose has no labelled-content component, so Android ships MonarchDescriptionList with those options built in, as the web does. The web DescriptionList and DescriptionItem are a list and children; here the items are data (MonarchDescriptionItem) with a content slot for anything that is not plain text. The web's copyable true or string is copyable and copyValue. The web's truncate number is maxLines, using MonarchTruncatedText. The web's placeholder node is not offered: an empty value is always the dash with emptyLabel. The web's auto column count is not offered; columns is a number. The web uses an extra-small icon copy button; Android has no extra-small size on touch, so the copy button is the Sm ghost text button or, with copyIcon, an icon button with a 48dp target. The web's 420px inline breakpoint is 288dp here, and inline also stacks from font scale 1.5.
accessibility: Each item is one TalkBack element read as the term and then the value.
An empty value is shown as a dash and read as "Not set".
A copy button is a separate element named "Copy" and the term, with a touch target of at least 48dp; it copies the value or copyValue.
A Show more button of a truncated value is a separate element with a 48dp target.
In the inline layout the term is before the value in both layout directions; at font scale 2.0 the list is stacked and nothing is cut.
edgeCases: An item with content but no value has no copy button unless it has copyValue.
An empty string counts as empty.
A row that is not full keeps its columns aligned with empty space at the end.
Columns are decided from the width the list is given, not the window.

examples.title: Record facts
examples.template:
MonarchDescriptionList(
    items = listOf(
        MonarchDescriptionItem({{items.0.term}}, {{items.0.value}}),
        MonarchDescriptionItem({{items.1.term}}, {{items.1.value}}),
        MonarchDescriptionItem({{items.2.term}}, {{items.2.value}}),
        MonarchDescriptionItem({{items.3.term}}, {{items.3.value}}),
        MonarchDescriptionItem({{items.4.term}}, {{items.4.value}}, wide = {{items.4.wide}}),
    ),
    columns = {{columns}},
)
examples.code:
MonarchDescriptionList(
    items = listOf(
        MonarchDescriptionItem("Owner", "Ada Lovelace"),
        MonarchDescriptionItem("Stage", "Proposal"),
        MonarchDescriptionItem("Created", "3 March"),
        MonarchDescriptionItem("Source", "Inbound"),
        MonarchDescriptionItem("Notes", "Follow up after the product review.", wide = true),
    ),
    columns = 2,
)

examples.title: Inline, two columns on wide screens
examples.code:
MonarchDescriptionList(
    items = listOf(
        MonarchDescriptionItem("Plan", "Team"),
        MonarchDescriptionItem("Seats", "12 of 50"),
        MonarchDescriptionItem("Notes", "Renews in March after the finance review.", maxLines = 1, wide = true),
    ),
    layout = MonarchDescriptionListLayout.Inline,
    columns = 2,
)

name: MonarchDeviceFrame
title: DeviceFrame
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Box with Modifier.aspectRatio, Modifier.clip and Modifier.drawBehind
summary: A phone or tablet outline around a preview: a link page, an email, a mobile layout.
whenToUse: In builders and editors that show how something will look on a phone or a tablet: a link page, an email template, a mobile layout. Mostly on a tablet; on a phone the frame is smaller than the device.
whenNotToUse: To show a screenshot as a plain picture use an Image. To preview a live web page use the app's WebView screen without a frame.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchDeviceFrame(label: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, device: MonarchDeviceFrameDevice = MonarchDeviceFrameDevice.Phone, screenSize: DpSize? = null, statusBarTime: String? = null, interactive: Boolean = false, flat: Boolean = false, content: @Composable BoxScope.() -> Unit)
public enum class MonarchDeviceFrameDevice { Phone, Tablet }

options.name: label
options.description: What the frame shows, for example "Preview of your link page on a phone". It names the preview for TalkBack.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the component.

options.name: device
options.description: Phone: 44dp corners, a 10dp bezel and a camera island. Tablet: 28dp corners, a 14dp bezel and no island.

options.name: screenSize
options.description: The width the frame never exceeds and, with the height, its aspect ratio. 390 by 844dp for a phone and 820 by 1180dp for a tablet by default.

options.name: statusBarTime
options.description: Shows a decorative status bar with this time text, for example "9:41".

options.name: interactive
options.description: Lets people scroll and use the content. Put a scrolling container in the content when it is taller than the screen.

options.name: flat
options.description: Leaves out the side buttons and the shadow, for dense layouts.

options.name: content
options.description: The screen content, laid out in the screen area and clipped to it.

states.name: preview
states.description: The default: the frame is one image for TalkBack and its content takes no touches and no keyboard focus.

states.name: interactive
states.description: The content keeps its own elements, touches and focus.

states.name: flat
states.description: No side buttons and no shadow.

appearance: The frame, the island and the side buttons use the inverse background, so the device stands out from the canvas in light, dark and both high-contrast themes; the screen uses the surface color with default text. The frame casts the xl shadow unless flat.
platformNotes: Dimensions follow the web and iOS: a 10dp bezel and 44dp corners for the phone, 14 and 28 for the tablet, screen sizes of 390 by 844 and 820 by 1180. The web takes separate width and height numbers; Android takes one DpSize, like iOS's CGSize. The frame scales to the width it is given and keeps its aspect ratio, but its content is not scaled, as on the web. The web's interactive frame scrolls its own content; here the app places a scrolling container in the content. Low priority on a phone.
accessibility: A frame that is not interactive is one TalkBack element with the image role, named by label; its content is removed from the accessibility tree, takes no touches and takes no keyboard focus.
An interactive frame is a traversal group named by label, and the elements of its content stay reachable and usable.
The island, the status bar and the side buttons are hidden from TalkBack.
The side buttons follow the layout direction: the volume buttons are on the start edge.
The status bar time grows with the font size setting; the bezel and the island do not.
edgeCases: In a container narrower than the screen size the frame shrinks and keeps the aspect ratio; content laid out for the full width may be clipped.
Content taller than the screen is clipped unless the frame is interactive and the content scrolls.

name: MonarchDeviceList
title: DeviceList
wrapsNative: MonarchCard with a androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of rows (androidx.compose.material3.Text, MonarchBadge, android.text.format.DateUtils.getRelativeTimeSpanString, MonarchButton), androidx.compose.material3.AlertDialog to confirm, MonarchInlineNotice, MonarchLoadingState, MonarchEmptyState and MonarchErrorState
summary: The devices that have accessed an account: name, system, browser and location, when each was last used and first seen, This device and Blocked badges, and an optional Remove action behind a confirmation.
whenToUse: On an account's security screen, so people can see where they are signed in and sign out a device they do not recognise.
whenNotToUse: For apps that use the account, use MonarchConnectedAppsList. For security events such as a new sign-in, use MonarchSecurityAlertCard.
api: @Composable fun MonarchDeviceList(devices: List<MonarchDevice>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, title: String? = null, description: String? = null, state: MonarchDeviceListState = MonarchDeviceListState.Ready, retrying: Boolean = false, confirmRemoval: Boolean = true, now: Long? = null, onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null, onRemove: (suspend (String) -> Unit)? = null, deviceIcon: (@Composable (MonarchDeviceKind) -> Unit)? = null, rowActions: (@Composable RowScope.(MonarchDevice) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchDeviceListLabels = MonarchDeviceListLabels())

class MonarchDevice(id: String, name: String, kind: MonarchDeviceKind = MonarchDeviceKind.Desktop, os: String? = null, browser: String? = null, location: String? = null, lastUsedMillis: Long? = null, firstSeenMillis: Long? = null, blocked: Boolean = false, current: Boolean = false)
enum class MonarchDeviceKind { Desktop, Mobile, Tablet, Unknown }
enum class MonarchDeviceListState { Ready, Loading, Failed }

class MonarchDeviceListLabels(listLabel: String? = null, unnamed: String? = null, current: String? = null, blocked: String? = null, lastUsed: String? = null, firstSeen: String? = null, remove: String? = null, removeLabel: ((String) -> String)? = null, confirmTitle: ((String) -> String)? = null, confirmMessage: String? = null, cancel: String? = null, removed: ((String) -> String)? = null, removeFailed: ((String) -> String)? = null, loading: String? = null, emptyTitle: String? = null, emptyMessage: String? = null, errorTitle: String? = null)

options.name: devices
options.description: The devices, shown in the order given.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the card.

options.name: title
options.description: Replaces the built-in title "Devices".

options.name: description
options.description: Replaces the line under the title.

options.name: state
options.description: Ready, Loading or Failed. A ready, empty list shows the empty state.

options.name: retrying
options.description: Shows the retry button busy in the failed state.

options.name: confirmRemoval
options.description: Asks with an alert dialog before removing. Set false when onRemove opens the app's own confirmation.

options.name: now
options.description: The reference time for relative times, in epoch milliseconds. Without it they follow the clock, refreshed every minute.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Retries loading. Shows Try again in the failed state.

options.name: onRemove
options.description: Signs the device out and forgets it, given its id; remove it from devices when it returns. Shows Remove on every device except the current one; throwing shows the failure.

options.name: deviceIcon
options.description: An icon for each device's kind, hidden from TalkBack and tinted with the danger strong color when blocked. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: rowActions
options.description: Extra controls after Remove in a row, such as a block or rename menu.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every other built-in string.

states.name: list
states.description: One row per device inside the card, separated by subtle dividers.

states.name: current
states.description: A success This device badge and no Remove button.

states.name: blocked
states.description: A danger Blocked badge and the device icon in the danger strong color.

states.name: removing
states.description: The row's Remove button shows its progress indicator; other Remove buttons are disabled.

states.name: remove failed
states.description: A danger MonarchInlineNotice under the header, "Couldn’t remove MacBook. Try again.", announced.

states.name: loading
states.description: Two skeleton rows from MonarchLoadingState, announced as "Loading devices".

states.name: empty
states.description: A small MonarchEmptyState.

states.name: failed
states.description: A small MonarchErrorState with Try again when onRetry is given.

appearance: A MonarchCard with the section header and rows separated by subtle dividers; names in the strong body style, the system line and the times in the caption style in the muted color, a success This device badge, a danger Blocked badge and small secondary Remove buttons. All are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The parity map names LazyColumn rows; the rows are a plain Column inside a MonarchCard instead, because the list sits inside the app's own scrolling settings screen, where a LazyColumn without a fixed height cannot be measured (iOS makes the same choice). The web's renderActions is rowActions, a composable slot. The confirmation is the Material 3 AlertDialog with MonarchButtons, which closes when confirmed, so the pending state moves to the row's button and a failure appears as a notice in the card instead of inside the dialog, as on iOS. Monarch bundles no icons, so the device icon is a slot given the kind; the web draws its own. The web's headingLevel has no Android equivalent (the title is a heading) and its locale prop is the device's locale used by DateUtils. Times are epoch milliseconds.
accessibility: The title is a heading, from MonarchSectionHeader; the list is a traversal group named "Devices".

Each device is one element whose content description is its name and whose state is the badges, the system, browser and location and the times, built by a tested pure function; Blocked and This device are words, not only color or an icon.
The device icon is decorative and hidden.
The Remove button is a separate MonarchButton with a 48dp touch target, named "Remove MacBook".
The confirmation is a Material 3 alert dialog with a danger Remove and a ghost Cancel.
Removal and a failed removal are announced through a polite live region.
Badges and actions wrap onto further lines, so nothing is cut off at the largest font size.
edgeCases: A device with a blank name reads "Unknown device".
Missing system, browser or location parts are left out of the detail line; with none, there is no detail line.
The app removes the device from devices after onRemove returns; the list does not remove it itself.
Only one removal runs at a time.

name: MonarchDevicePicker
title: DevicePicker
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.ExposedDropdownMenuBox through MonarchSelect, with MonarchInlineNotice; device data from android.media.AudioManager and android.hardware.camera2.CameraManager supplied by the app
summary: Microphone, camera and audio output menus for a call's lobby or settings, with a notice that explains camera and microphone access and a way to fix it.
whenToUse: In a pre-join lobby or a call's settings sheet, so people can choose which microphone, camera and audio output the call uses.
whenNotToUse: To show the camera preview use the app's CameraX or call SDK view beside it. For a generic choice from a list use MonarchSelect.
api: @Composable fun MonarchDevicePicker(modifier: Modifier = Modifier, microphone: String? = null, onMicrophoneChange: ((String?) -> Unit)? = null, camera: String? = null, onCameraChange: ((String?) -> Unit)? = null, speaker: String? = null, onSpeakerChange: ((String?) -> Unit)? = null, microphones: List<MonarchDevicePickerDevice> = emptyList(), cameras: List<MonarchDevicePickerDevice> = emptyList(), speakers: List<MonarchDevicePickerDevice> = emptyList(), access: MonarchDevicePickerAccess = MonarchDevicePickerAccess.Granted, size: MonarchDevicePickerSize = MonarchDevicePickerSize.Md, enabled: Boolean = true, labels: MonarchDevicePickerLabels = MonarchDevicePickerLabels(), onRequestAccess: (() -> Unit)? = null, onOpenSettings: (() -> Unit)? = null)
class MonarchDevicePickerDevice(id: String, name: String)
enum class MonarchDevicePickerAccess { Granted, NotDetermined, Denied, Unavailable }
enum class MonarchDevicePickerSize { Sm, Md }

class MonarchDevicePickerLabels(microphone: String? = null, camera: String? = null, speaker: String? = null, systemDefault: String? = null, unnamedMicrophone: ((position: Int) -> String)? = null, unnamedCamera: ((position: Int) -> String)? = null, unnamedSpeaker: ((position: Int) -> String)? = null, notDetermined: String? = null, allowAccess: String? = null, denied: String? = null, openSettings: String? = null, unavailable: String? = null)

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the column.

options.name: microphone
options.description: The chosen microphone's id; null is "System default".

options.name: onMicrophoneChange
options.description: Shows the microphone field; called with the new id, null for System default.

options.name: camera
options.description: The chosen camera's id; null is "System default".

options.name: onCameraChange
options.description: Shows the camera field; called with the new id, null for System default.

options.name: speaker
options.description: The chosen audio output's id; null is "System default".

options.name: onSpeakerChange
options.description: Shows the audio output field; called with the new id, null for System default.

options.name: microphones
options.description: The microphones offered, usually AudioManager.getDevices(GET_DEVICES_INPUTS) mapped by the app.

options.name: cameras
options.description: The cameras offered, usually CameraManager.cameraIdList named by lens facing.

options.name: speakers
options.description: The audio outputs offered, usually AudioManager.availableCommunicationDevices (API 31) mapped by the app.

options.name: access
options.description: The camera and microphone permission state to explain, as the app knows it.

options.name: size
options.description: Md for a lobby or settings screen; Sm has tighter spacing and a small notice button, for a sheet during a call.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the fields and the notice's button can be used.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: onRequestAccess
options.description: Shows Allow access while access is not asked; the app requests the permissions, usually with rememberLauncherForActivityResult(RequestMultiplePermissions()).

options.name: onOpenSettings
options.description: Replaces what Open Settings does when access is refused. null opens the app's page in the system Settings (Settings.ACTION_APPLICATION_DETAILS_SETTINGS).

states.name: granted
states.description: No notice; the fields only.

states.name: not asked
states.description: An info notice "Allow camera and microphone access to choose devices." with Allow access when onRequestAccess is set; the microphone and camera fields are disabled.

states.name: denied
states.description: A warning notice that access is off, with Open Settings; the microphone and camera fields are disabled.

states.name: unavailable
states.description: A neutral notice "No camera or microphone was found.", also shown when access is granted but no shown microphone or camera field has a device.

states.name: removed device
states.description: A selected id that is no longer listed stays selected, numbered after the listed devices: "Microphone 3".

states.name: disabled
states.description: With enabled false every field and the notice's button are disabled.

appearance: MonarchSelect fields with the outline, label and text colors of MonarchTextField, and MonarchInlineNotice in the info, warning or neutral tone. Every color is a theme role, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes are covered.
platformNotes: The web lists devices with navigator.mediaDevices and selects outputs with setSinkId; on Android the app lists inputs and outputs with AudioManager and cameras with CameraManager, applies the choice itself (AudioManager.setCommunicationDevice from API 31, the camera id it opens) and passes new lists when devices change (AudioDeviceCallback). Unlike iOS, which must use the system route picker, Android has its own audio output menu. Monarch declares no permissions and does not read or request them: access is a parameter and the request is onRequestAccess, because only the app's activity can launch the permission request and know whether Android still shows it (Denied is the state after the request is no longer shown). Device names are always known on Android, so the web's "names hidden" state becomes the not-asked state. The picker does not show a camera preview (no CameraX dependency); put the app's preview beside it.
accessibility: Each field is MonarchSelect: a read-only Material 3 field named by its label (Microphone, Camera, Speaker) with the current choice as its text, which opens a menu whose chosen option is read as selected.
The notice is MonarchInlineNotice, a polite live region read as its tone and message; its action is a separate MonarchButton with a 48dp touch target.
Fields that cannot be used without access are disabled, so TalkBack reads them as disabled.
States are text, never color alone.
edgeCases: Devices with an empty id are left out, and a repeated id is listed once; an empty selection is System default.
Devices with a blank name are numbered by their position: "Camera 2".
With access granted and no microphone or camera to list, the unavailable notice explains the empty menus.
Open Settings without onOpenSettings starts the app's details page in Settings; on a device without it nothing happens.
The menus, notices and buttons were checked with Robolectric tests, not on a device with TalkBack; the permission request and the Settings page are the app's and were not run.

examples.title: Before access is allowed
examples.template:
MonarchDevicePicker(
    microphone = microphone,
    onMicrophoneChange = { microphone = it },
    camera = camera,
    onCameraChange = { camera = it },
    speaker = speaker,
    onSpeakerChange = { speaker = it },
    microphones = listOf(
        MonarchDevicePickerDevice({{microphones.0.id}}, {{microphones.0.label}}),
        MonarchDevicePickerDevice({{microphones.1.id}}, {{microphones.1.label}}),
    ),
    cameras = listOf(MonarchDevicePickerDevice({{cameras.0.id}}, {{cameras.0.label}})),
    speakers = listOf(MonarchDevicePickerDevice({{speakers.0.id}}, {{speakers.0.label}})),
    access = MonarchDevicePickerAccess.NotDetermined,
    onRequestAccess = {},
)
examples.code:

    microphone = microphone,
    onMicrophoneChange = { microphone = it },
    camera = camera,
    onCameraChange = { camera = it },
    speaker = speaker,
    onSpeakerChange = { speaker = it },
    microphones = listOf(
        MonarchDevicePickerDevice("a", ""),
        MonarchDevicePickerDevice("b", ""),
    ),
    cameras = listOf(MonarchDevicePickerDevice("c", "")),
    speakers = listOf(MonarchDevicePickerDevice("d", "")),
    access = MonarchDevicePickerAccess.NotDetermined,
    onRequestAccess = {},
)

examples.title: Before access is asked, small
examples.setup: var asked by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
examples.code:
MonarchDevicePicker(
    onMicrophoneChange = {},
    onCameraChange = {},
    access = if (asked) MonarchDevicePickerAccess.Granted else MonarchDevicePickerAccess.NotDetermined,
    size = MonarchDevicePickerSize.Sm,
    onRequestAccess = { asked = true },
)

name: MonarchDialog
title: Dialog
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.BasicAlertDialog (window, scrim, focus, back and Escape, motion) with a Monarch panel; androidx.compose.ui.window.Dialog for a full-screen form
summary: A modal dialog: MonarchDialog is the Material 3 BasicAlertDialog with a Monarch panel (title, description, content and actions on the raised surface). The platform keeps the window, scrim, focus and back.
whenToUse: When the person must read or decide something before going on: an AlertDialog with a title, a message and up to two buttons, or a Dialog with Monarch components for a short form. For a form that fills a phone, a full-screen Dialog with a top app bar.
whenNotToUse: Not for information that can wait: use a MonarchBanner or a snackbar. Not for a long task with several steps on a phone: use ModalBottomSheet (see sheet) or a screen of its own. Not for a choice of actions: use DropdownMenu.
api: @Composable fun MonarchDialog(onDismissRequest: () -> Unit, title: String?, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, description: String? = null, dismissible: Boolean = true, dismissOnClickOutside: Boolean = dismissible, paneTitle: String? = null, actions: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null, content: (@Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)? = null)

options.name: onDismissRequest
options.description: Called on back, Escape or a tap on the scrim, unless not dismissible. Stop showing the dialog here.

options.name: title
options.description: The heading at 18/600, also the pane title TalkBack reads when the dialog opens.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the panel.

options.name: description
options.description: A short line under the title, 14 in the muted text colour.

options.name: dismissible
options.description: Whether back, Escape and a tap on the scrim dismiss it. False while work runs or when a choice is required.

options.name: actions
options.description: The buttons at the end, right aligned, for example a ghost Cancel and a primary MonarchButton. They wrap when there is no room.

options.name: content
options.description: The body under the description; it scrolls when the dialog is taller than the window.

states.name: shown
states.description: The dialog is centered over the scrim and takes focus; the screen behind does not respond.

states.name: dismissed
states.description: Back, a tap on the scrim or a button calls onDismissRequest; the app stops composing the dialog.

states.name: busy
states.description: With dismissOnBackPress and dismissOnClickOutside set to false while an action runs, and a loading MonarchButton, the dialog stays until the action ends.

states.name: full screen
states.description: With usePlatformDefaultWidth = false the Dialog fills the window, for a form on a phone.

appearance: A panel up to 512dp wide and 16dp from the window edges, 16dp corners, the raised background with a subtle border (strong in the high-contrast themes), one soft shadow in the light themes and none in the dark ones, 20dp padding, the title at 18/600 and the description at 14 in the muted text role. Actions are MonarchButtons, right aligned with 8dp between them. The scrim dims by the alpha of the overlay scrim role.
platformNotes: The web Dialog is one component with sizes, a header, a footer, a close button with closeLabel, busy, closeOnOutsideClick, escapeGuard and fullScreenOnPhone. On Android: the header is title and description, the footer is actions, closeOnOutsideClick is dismissOnClickOutside, busy and escapeGuard are dismissible = false, and fullScreenOnPhone is a Dialog with usePlatformDefaultWidth = false, a Scaffold and a TopAppBar. A dialog stays until the app stops composing it, so unlike the iOS alert it can show progress and errors itself. There is no close button by default; a Cancel action or the back gesture closes it. Content with its own heading (a celebration) passes title = null and a paneTitle for TalkBack.
accessibility: The dialog is a separate window: focus and TalkBack move into it, stay there, and return to the screen when it closes.
TalkBack reads the title as the pane title and as a heading.
Back and Escape call onDismissRequest unless dismissible is false.
The action buttons keep 48dp targets; name them after the action ("Delete project"), not "OK".
The title and description wrap at font scale 2.0; the content scrolls.
edgeCases: A long message scrolls inside AlertDialog's text slot at the largest font size.
With dismissOnClickOutside = false a tap on the scrim does nothing; keep a visible way to close.
On a phone in landscape a tall Dialog is cut by the window; make its content scroll.

name: MonarchDiffViewer
title: DiffViewer
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn, androidx.compose.ui.text.AnnotatedString, androidx.compose.material3.SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow, MonarchButton
summary: Shows what changed between two texts or two versions of a document, unified or side by side: added and removed lines, changed words inside them, folded unchanged runs, totals and previous and next change buttons.
whenToUse: To compare two versions of a text the person reads: a document's version history, an edited configuration, a proposed change to a template.
whenNotToUse: To show one version of code, use MonarchCodeBlock (its diff option marks + and − lines of a patch the app already has). To compare structured records field by field, use a merge dialog or a description list.
api: @Composable fun MonarchDiffViewer(before: List<String>, after: List<String>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, mode: MonarchDiffViewerMode? = null, onModeChange: ((MonarchDiffViewerMode) -> Unit)? = null, granularity: MonarchDiffViewerGranularity = MonarchDiffViewerGranularity.Word, context: Int? = 3, beforeLabel: String? = null, afterLabel: String? = null, showModeSwitch: Boolean = true, showLineNumbers: Boolean = true, state: LazyListState = rememberLazyListState(), labels: MonarchDiffViewerLabels = MonarchDiffViewerLabels(), actions: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null)

@Composable fun MonarchDiffViewer(before: String, after: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, mode: MonarchDiffViewerMode? = null, onModeChange: ((MonarchDiffViewerMode) -> Unit)? = null, granularity: MonarchDiffViewerGranularity = MonarchDiffViewerGranularity.Word, context: Int? = 3, beforeLabel: String? = null, afterLabel: String? = null, showModeSwitch: Boolean = true, showLineNumbers: Boolean = true, state: LazyListState = rememberLazyListState(), labels: MonarchDiffViewerLabels = MonarchDiffViewerLabels(), actions: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null)
class MonarchDiffViewerLine(kind: MonarchDiffViewerLineKind, text: String, oldNumber: Int? = null, newNumber: Int? = null)
fun MonarchDiffViewerLine.Companion.diff(before: List<String>, after: List<String>): List<MonarchDiffViewerLine>
fun MonarchDiffViewerLine.Companion.lines(text: String): List<String>
enum class MonarchDiffViewerLineKind { Same, Added, Removed }
enum class MonarchDiffViewerMode { Unified, Split }
enum class MonarchDiffViewerGranularity { Line, Word }

class MonarchDiffViewerLabels(caption: ((before: String, after: String) -> String)? = null, before: String? = null, after: String? = null, mode: String? = null, unified: String? = null, split: String? = null, stats: ((added: Int, removed: Int) -> String)? = null, added: String? = null, removed: String? = null, blankLine: String? = null, expand: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, previous: String? = null, next: String? = null, position: ((index: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, noChanges: String? = null)

options.name: before
options.description: The earlier text: its lines or blocks (one entry per paragraph for a document), or a string split on line breaks.

options.name: after
options.description: The later text, in the same shape.

options.name: mode
options.description: The layout when the app owns it. null is side by side from 768dp of width and unified below; the reader's choice in the switch is then kept by the viewer (rememberSaveable).

options.name: onModeChange
options.description: Called when the reader picks a layout in the switch.

options.name: granularity
options.description: Word also marks the changed words inside a changed line; Line marks whole lines only.

options.name: context
options.description: Unchanged lines kept around each change; longer runs fold behind a Show N unchanged lines button. null never folds; a negative value counts as 0.

options.name: beforeLabel
options.description: The name of the earlier side, such as a version name; read in the TalkBack name of the lines and for side by side rows.

options.name: afterLabel
options.description: The name of the later side.

options.name: showModeSwitch
options.description: Whether the segmented layout switch is shown. It is only shown when two columns fit (768dp).

options.name: showLineNumbers
options.description: Whether line numbers are shown: both numbers in unified, one per side in side by side. Hide them for document blocks.

options.name: state
options.description: The scroll state of the lines, for example to restore the position.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: actions
options.description: Controls at the end of the header, such as Restore.

states.name: unified
states.description: One column: the removed lines, then the added lines of each change, each with both line numbers and a + or − marker.

states.name: side by side
states.description: Two columns: the k-th removed line beside the k-th added line; an empty side has the subtle background fill.

states.name: folded
states.description: Unchanged runs longer than the context fold into a full-width ghost button that shows them.

states.name: current change
states.description: After previous or next, the first row of that change has an accent bar at its start edge and is scrolled into view (at once when animations are off).

states.name: no changes
states.description: "No changes." in the muted text color instead of the lines.

appearance: A surface in the surface background role with a subtle border and the medium radius. Added lines use the subtle success fill and removed lines the subtle danger fill; changed words have the success or danger border color as a fill, removed words are struck through and added words underlined. Markers and totals use the strong success and danger colors, line numbers the subtle text color, the current change bar the solid accent. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The diff algorithm is ported from the web (longest common subsequence over lines, then over words, with the same limits), not shared. The web is a table that scrolls sideways; on Android long lines wrap so the text grows with the font scale, and the layout switch appears only from 768dp because two columns do not fit a phone. The viewer is a LazyColumn, so it needs a bounded height and cannot sit inside a verticalScroll; iOS lays it out in the app's ScrollView instead. Previous and next scroll the list and announce "Change 2 of 5" through a polite live region; Compose has no API to move TalkBack focus to the change, so focus stays on the button (the web and iOS move focus). The web's controlled mode, defaultMode and onModeChange are mode and onModeChange here; the default follows the width instead of being unified. The web's hidden column headers (Line before, Line after, Change, Text) have no TalkBack counterpart because each row is read as one element; their strings are not offered. iOS uses the same names; showsModeSwitch and showsLineNumbers are showModeSwitch and showLineNumbers, following Compose naming.
accessibility: The lines are a traversal group named "Changes from <before> to <after>".
Each unified line is one TalkBack element read as its text after "Added" or "Removed"; an empty line reads "Blank line". Line numbers and markers are not read.
A side by side row reads each side after its name, or once when the line is unchanged.
The totals read "2 added, 2 removed" instead of the + and − figures.
Previous and next announce "Change 2 of 5" through a polite live region.
Changes are marked by + and − signs, strikethrough and underline as well as color.
Text wraps and grows with the font scale; the buttons have 48dp touch targets.
edgeCases: Inputs with more than a million line pairs show every line removed and added; lines with more than 250,000 word pairs are not split into words.
A change of the texts resets the expanded runs and the current change; new lists with the same lines keep them.
A run of unchanged lines only one longer than the context is shown instead of folded.
An empty before shows every line as added.
Previous and next appear only when there are at least two changes.

name: MonarchDnsRecordTable
title: DnsRecordTable
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column, Row, FlowRow and BoxWithConstraints (cards, or a table at 640dp and wider); MonarchCopyButton, MonarchStatusBadge and MonarchText
summary: The DNS records a user must add at their DNS provider to connect a custom domain or verify a sender: type, name and value with copy buttons, what each record is for, and whether public DNS already shows it.
whenToUse: On a custom domain or sender verification screen, to list the records the user has to create and show which ones public DNS already returns.
whenNotToUse: For progress through DNS, certificate and live, use MonarchDomainProgress next to it; for one value to copy, use MonarchCopyField; for general tabular data, a data table.
api: @Composable fun MonarchDnsRecordTable(records: List<MonarchDnsRecord>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, zone: String? = null, layout: MonarchDnsRecordTableLayout = MonarchDnsRecordTableLayout.Automatic, copyIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, onCopy: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchDnsRecordTableLabels = MonarchDnsRecordTableLabels())

class MonarchDnsRecord(type: String, name: String, value: String, purpose: MonarchDnsRecordPurpose? = null, ttl: String? = null, priority: Int? = null, found: Boolean? = null, id: String = "$type:$name:$value")
sealed interface MonarchDnsRecordPurpose { data object Routing; data object Verification; data object Certificate; data class Custom(heading: String) }
enum class MonarchDnsRecordTableLayout { Automatic, Cards, Table }

class MonarchDnsRecordTableLabels(type: String? = null, name: String? = null, value: String? = null, ttl: String? = null, priority: String? = null, status: String? = null, found: String? = null, waiting: String? = null, purpose: ((purpose: MonarchDnsRecordPurpose?) -> String)? = null, copyName: ((record: MonarchDnsRecord, shownName: String) -> String)? = null, copyValue: ((record: MonarchDnsRecord, shownName: String) -> String)? = null, fullName: ((name: String) -> String)? = null, label: ((zone: String?) -> String)? = null, summary: ((found: Int, checked: Int) -> String)? = null)

options.name: records
options.description: The records, in the order the user should create them. Each has a type, a full name, a value, and optionally a purpose, TTL, priority and found state (found true is Found, false is Waiting, null when not checked).

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the records.

options.name: zone
options.description: The DNS zone the user manages, such as example.com. Names inside it are shown relative to it (book, @ for the apex), with "Full name: …" under the card.

options.name: layout
options.description: Cards: one card per record. Table: one row per record under column headings. Automatic: a table when the width is at least 640dp and the font scale at most 1.3, cards otherwise.

options.name: copyIcon
options.description: A copy icon. Given, each copy button is an icon button; otherwise a small ghost text button "Copy".

options.name: onCopy
options.description: Called with the copied text after a name or a value is copied.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string: the column and term headings, Found and Waiting, the purpose headings, the spoken names of names and values, the full name line, the group name and the found announcement.

states.name: not checked
states.description: A record with found null has no status badge; the table has no Status column when no record was checked.

states.name: waiting
states.description: found false shows a neutral "Waiting" status badge.

states.name: found
states.description: found true shows a success "Found" status badge. When the number of found records changes, "1 of 2 records found." is announced.

states.name: cards
states.description: Each record is a card with its purpose as a heading, the status, the type with the priority and TTL when given, the name and value with copy buttons, and the full name when the name is shown relative to the zone.

states.name: table
states.description: A heading row (Type, Name, Value, and Priority, TTL and Status only when a record uses them) and one row per record, with single-line names and values shortened in the middle.

states.name: empty
states.description: No records draws nothing but the named group.

appearance: Cards and the table are on the surface color with a default border and 12dp corners. Card headings are strong body text in the default text color, terms and table headings muted caption text, types, names and values code text in the default color. Found is a success status badge, Waiting a neutral one. Every color is a theme role, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes are covered.
platformNotes: The web table scrolls sideways when narrow; on Android, as on iOS, the automatic layout switches to cards when the window is narrower than 640dp or the font scale is above 1.3, and the table's names and values are single lines shortened in the middle. The copy buttons are MonarchCopyButton rather than MonarchCopyField: a copy field shows its label as a floating label, while here the visible term is short (Name, Value) and the spoken name is long ("name of the CNAME record"). Monarch bundles no icons, so copyIcon is optional and the buttons are text buttons without it. The web's headingLevel has no Android equivalent: card headings are headings. TTL is a string the app formats. The web's DnsProviderGuide is not part of this component. iOS uses the same names, except found (iOS isFound), copyIcon (Android only) and MonarchDnsRecordPurpose.Custom (iOS custom(String)). The plan's dependency description-list is not used: its copy affordance has no spoken name per record.
accessibility: The records are one group named "DNS records for <zone>", or "DNS records" without a zone.
Each card heading is a heading.
A name is read as "name of the CNAME record, book" and a value as "value of the CNAME record book, domains.example.net"; the visible terms Name and Value are not read again.
Each copy button is its own element named "Copy name of the CNAME record" with a touch target of at least 48dp, and says "Copied to clipboard" after a copy.
The type, priority and TTL are read with their term, such as "Type, CNAME".
The found state is a word in a status badge, not only a color.
When the number of found records changes, the summary "1 of 2 records found." is announced through a polite live region that is always present.
In the table, the column headings are headings.
Card text wraps at font scale 2.0, and the automatic layout uses cards above font scale 1.3.
edgeCases: A name outside the zone, or any name without a zone, is shown in full with no full name line.
The zone and names are compared ignoring case and a trailing dot.
Long values (DKIM keys) wrap in full in the cards and are shortened in the middle in the table; the copied value is always complete.
Copying a name copies it as shown (relative to the zone), which is what most providers expect.
Priority and TTL appear in a card only when the record has them, and as columns only when a record has them.
The found announcement fires on a change only, not when the records first appear.
A record without a purpose uses the verification heading, as on iOS.

summary: A recipe, not a component: the record-page block for linked docs and links, as MonarchLinkedDocsPanel in its card, optionally behind a "Docs" toggle that composes the panel only when opened.
whenToUse: On a record's detail screen, to show and manage the docs and links attached to the record; behind a toggle in long lists of records so docs load only for the record that is opened.
whenNotToUse: For files uploaded to the record, use the file list components. To pick one doc, use a select or a combobox.
api: MonarchLinkedDocsPanel(items = items, onOpen = …, onLinkDoc = …, onAddLink = …, onUnlink = …)
MonarchCollapsible(expanded = expanded, onExpandedChange = …, label = "Docs, 3 linked") { LaunchedEffect(Unit) { /* load */ }; MonarchLinkedDocsPanel(…) }

options.name: frame
options.description: MonarchLinkedDocsPanel already draws the section card; for a stacked side panel put a HorizontalDivider under it.

options.name: collapsible
options.description: Wrap the panel in MonarchCollapsible; its content is composed only while expanded, so load the items there.

options.name: count
options.description: When the app already knows the linked count, put it in the toggle's label: "Docs, 3 linked".

states.name: open
states.description: The panel with its items, actions and space filter, from MonarchLinkedDocsPanel.

states.name: closed
states.description: Only the "Docs" toggle, read as collapsed; nothing is composed or loaded.

states.name: loading
states.description: items = null: the panel's loading state while the app fetches.

states.name: read only
states.description: readOnly = true: the items without link, add or unlink actions.

appearance: MonarchLinkedDocsPanel's section card, and MonarchCollapsible's header row when collapsible. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web ships DocsPanel with a frame prop (card, divider, none) and a collapsible mode with its own disclosure button and toggle strings. On Android MonarchLinkedDocsPanel is already a MonarchSectionCard, and MonarchCollapsible is the disclosure, so DocsPanel is a recipe: the toggle text and count are the collapsible's label, and loading on open is a LaunchedEffect inside the collapsible's content, which leaves the composition while closed. The web's doc icon and chevron are left out (Monarch bundles no icons; MonarchCollapsible takes a trailingIcon slot). iOS has not covered this entry yet.
accessibility: The toggle is one button with the state Expanded or Collapsed and the TalkBack expand and collapse actions, from MonarchCollapsible.
The count is part of the toggle's label, so it is read with it.
Inside, the panel's title is a heading and its actions are MonarchButtons with 48dp targets, from MonarchLinkedDocsPanel.
edgeCases: Closing the toggle removes the panel from the composition: hoist any state, such as the items, above it.
Without a known count, label the toggle "Docs" only.
Items that fail to load: pass errorMessage and onRetry to the panel.

class MonarchDocumentRelationsLabels(label: String? = null, add: String? = null, sheetTitle: String? = null, sheetDescription: String? = null, type: String? = null, search: String? = null, results: String? = null, noResults: String? = null, cancel: String? = null, removeText: String? = null, remove: ((title: String) -> String)? = null, added: ((title: String) -> String)? = null, removed: ((title: String) -> String)? = null, failed: String? = null, none: String? = null, working: String? = null)

options.name: relations
options.description: This document's relations: type, direction and the document at the other end.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the component.

options.name: types
options.description: The relation types, their labels and inverses. The defaults are the web's seven types with built-in labels from strings_documentrelations.xml.

options.name: candidates
options.description: Documents that can be linked, listed in the sheet without those already related, at most twelve.

options.name: defaultType
options.description: The type chosen when the sheet opens; related-to, or the first type, by default.

options.name: showEmpty
options.description: Shows "No relations yet." when there are none.

options.name: onSearch
options.description: Searches on the server as the person types, with the trimmed text; update candidates with the results. Without it, candidates are filtered by title.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Opens a related document, usually by navigating to it. Without it, rows are not interactive.

options.name: onAdd
options.description: Adds a relation with the target's id and the type's value, and shows Add relation. Throw to keep the sheet open with the error.

options.name: onRemove
options.description: Removes a relation by its id, and shows a remove button on each row. A thrown error is shown under the list.

options.name: removeIcon
options.description: The icon of each remove button. Monarch bundles no icons; without it the button is the text "Remove".

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings. Type labels are replaced by passing types.

states.name: read only
states.description: Rows without remove buttons and without Add relation; not interactive without onOpen.

states.name: empty
states.description: Nothing is drawn, or "No relations yet." with showEmpty, then Add relation.

states.name: adding
states.description: The chosen document shows a progress indicator and the other results, the type and the search are disabled until onAdd returns; the sheet then closes.

states.name: removing
states.description: The row's remove button becomes a progress indicator and the other remove buttons and Add relation are disabled.

states.name: failed
states.description: The error's message, or "That didn't work. Try again.", in a danger notice in the sheet or under the list.

appearance: The relation's type is a caption in the muted text role above the title, which takes the link role when the row opens its document and the default text role otherwise; descriptions use the muted role and file icons the file type colors. The sheet uses the surface role. All come from MonarchTheme in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web DocumentRelations shows chips with an arrow glyph and links, and a modal dialog with a native select and a search field. On Android the relations are the web's pill chips in a wrapping row, each with its direction arrow, the type, the title and a remove button (the target's description is for the picker only), the dialog is a Material 3 bottom sheet with MonarchSelect for the type and MonarchSearchBar, and choosing a result adds the relation directly, as on iOS. The relation is also said in words, not by the arrow alone. The web's href and renderLink become onOpen, so the app navigates. The chips are a plain FlowRow, so the component can sit in a scrolling detail screen. The web's promise callbacks become suspend functions; an exception's message is shown like the web's error message. Each target can carry a file name for MonarchFileTypeIcon, which the web does not show. The web moves focus to the next remove button after a removal; on Android TalkBack keeps its place and the removal is announced. iOS also offers a context menu on each row; Android does not. Experimental until a Rook app adopts it.
accessibility: The list is a traversal group named "Relations".
Each row is one element read as "Parent of, Q3 plan, Finance", a button when onOpen is set, at least 48dp high.
The remove button is a separate element named "Remove relation to Q3 plan" with a 48dp target.
Adding and removing are announced through a polite live region ("Relation to Q3 plan removed").
The file icon is decorative; the relation is said in words.
In the sheet, the title is a heading, the type is a MonarchSelect, the results have a heading and each result is a button read as its title and description.
edgeCases: An unknown type value is shown as the value itself.
An incoming relation whose type has no inverse is read as the type itself, like related-to.
Documents already related are not offered again; the list shows at most twelve candidates.
While an add runs, dismissing the sheet is ignored until onAdd returns or throws.
Long titles wrap; the remove button stays at the end of the row.

name: MonarchDomainProgress
title: DomainProgress
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column and Row drawn as a vertical stepper; androidx.compose.material3.CircularProgressIndicator for the step in progress; MonarchInlineNotice for problems; android.text.format.DateUtils.getRelativeTimeSpanString for the last check
summary: Stage-by-stage progress for connecting a custom domain (DNS record found, HTTPS certificate issued, live), with the problems the product found, what public DNS shows right now and that checking continues on its own.
whenToUse: On a custom domain screen after the user added DNS records, to show where the connection stands and what to fix, while the app polls the product.
whenNotToUse: For the records themselves, use MonarchDnsRecordTable; for a general multi-step flow the user moves through, use MonarchStepper.
api: @Composable fun MonarchDomainProgress(host: String, stage: MonarchDomainStage, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, problems: List<MonarchDomainProblem> = emptyList(), dnsFound: MonarchDomainDnsSnapshot? = null, checkedAt: Long? = null, now: Long? = null, rechecking: Boolean = true, notify: MonarchDomainNotify? = null, labels: MonarchDomainProgressLabels = MonarchDomainProgressLabels())
object MonarchDomainProgressDefaults { fun recheckIntervalMillis(stage: MonarchDomainStage?, suggestedMillis: Long? = null, stopped: Boolean = false): Long? }
enum class MonarchDomainStage { Dns, Ownership, Certificate, Page, Live }
enum class MonarchDomainStep { Dns, Certificate, Live }
enum class MonarchDomainStepState { Done, Current, Todo, Error }
class MonarchDomainProblem(message: String, code: String? = null, severity: MonarchDomainProblemSeverity = MonarchDomainProblemSeverity.Blocking, step: MonarchDomainStep? = null)
enum class MonarchDomainProblemSeverity { Blocking, Info }
class MonarchDomainDnsSnapshot(cnames: List<String> = emptyList(), a: List<String> = emptyList(), aaaa: List<String> = emptyList())
enum class MonarchDomainNotify { Email, InApp }

class MonarchDomainProgressLabels(title: ((step: MonarchDomainStep, state: MonarchDomainStepState, stage: MonarchDomainStage) -> String)? = null, detail: ((step: MonarchDomainStep, state: MonarchDomainStepState, host: String) -> String)? = null, state: ((state: MonarchDomainStepState) -> String)? = null, listLabel: ((host: String) -> String)? = null, announcement: ((position: Int, count: Int, title: String, state: String) -> String)? = null, dnsSeen: ((host: String, seen: String) -> String)? = null, noRecord: String? = null, rechecking: ((notify: MonarchDomainNotify?) -> String)? = null, checked: ((time: String) -> String)? = null)

options.name: host
options.description: The custom host name, such as book.example.com. Used in the live step text, the DNS line and the group name.

options.name: stage
options.description: Dns or Ownership: the DNS step is in progress. Certificate: DNS done, certificate in progress. Page: certificate done, the site load check in progress. Live: every step done.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the progress.

options.name: problems
options.description: What the last check found. A blocking problem marks its step (the current one by default) as needing attention and is shown as a warning notice; when there is none, the first informational problem is shown as a neutral notice.

options.name: dnsFound
options.description: What public DNS shows for the host right now, shown as "Public DNS for <host> shows CNAME → …" or "no record yet". null hides the line.

options.name: checkedAt
options.description: When the product last checked, as epoch milliseconds (UTC). Shown as "Checked 2 minutes ago."

options.name: now
options.description: The reference time for checkedAt, as epoch milliseconds. null is the current time, refreshed every minute; pass a fixed time in tests and screenshots.

options.name: rechecking
options.description: Whether the product keeps checking on its own; adds "We keep checking automatically…".

options.name: notify
options.description: How the product tells the user it went live: Email or InApp changes the end of the rechecking sentence.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string: step titles and details, spoken states, the group name, the announcement, the DNS line, the rechecking sentence and the last check line.

states.name: done
states.description: The step marker is the success fill with a check mark, and the line after it is the success color.

states.name: current
states.description: The step marker is the accent fill with a spinner; when animations are off the spinner is a still dot.

states.name: todo
states.description: The step marker is an empty surface circle with the default border, and the title is muted.

states.name: error
states.description: A blocking problem: the step marker is the warning fill with an exclamation mark, and the problem is shown as a warning notice.

states.name: live
states.description: Every step is done and the DNS, rechecking and last check lines are hidden.

appearance: Markers are 24dp circles (larger at large font scales) with a 2dp border: success, accent or warning solid fills with their on-solid glyph color, or the surface color with the default border. The line between markers is 2dp, the success color after a finished step and the default border otherwise. Titles are strong body text, muted before the step starts; details and status lines are muted caption text. Every color is a theme role, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes are covered.
platformNotes: Built as its own vertical stepper rather than on MonarchStepper, as on iOS, because MonarchStepper always draws a current step (it cannot show every step done once live) and has no in-progress spinner; the plan's dependency on stepper is therefore not used. The spinner is the Material 3 CircularProgressIndicator. Monarch bundles no icons, so the check and exclamation marks are drawn as the web's SVG strokes, as MonarchStepper does. The web's rich-content messages (dnsSeen, checked) take and return strings, and the host is not set in code font inside the sentence. The web's polling helper domainPollMs is MonarchDomainProgressDefaults.recheckIntervalMillis, returning milliseconds (iOS returns a Duration from a static function on the view). Times are epoch milliseconds. iOS uses the same names, except rechecking (iOS isRechecking), stopped (iOS isStopped) and the PascalCase enum constants.
accessibility: The steps are one group named "Progress for <host>".
Each step is one element: its title as the name and "<state>, <detail>" as the state description, such as "in progress, Being issued now, usually 1 to 5 minutes."
The state is a spoken word and a glyph in the marker, not only a color; markers are hidden from TalkBack.

When the active step or its state changes, "Step 2 of 3: HTTPS certificate, in progress." is announced through a polite live region that is always present; nothing is announced when the view first appears.
Problems are MonarchInlineNotice, which speaks the tone name with the message.
When animations are off, the in-progress marker is a still dot.
Text wraps and the marker grows with the font scale.
edgeCases: A blocking problem on a step that is already done does not change it.
A blocking problem without a step marks the current step; with several problems all blocking ones are shown and informational ones are hidden.
Long host names wrap in the step details and the DNS line.
The view never checks DNS itself; the app polls and passes the new stage.
The relative time uses DateUtils, in the device locale.
