name: MonarchDonutChart
title: DonutChart
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.Canvas (DrawScope.drawArc and drawCircle) and androidx.compose.foundation.text.BasicText with TextAutoSize for the center; inside MonarchChartFrame with MonarchChartLegend and MonarchChartTable
summary: Parts of one whole as a donut inside a chart frame: the total in the middle, a legend of values and shares, folding of small segments into Other, and every segment in the data table.
whenToUse: For two to six parts of one whole where the share matters more than an exact comparison, such as assets by type on a dashboard card.
whenNotToUse: To compare or rank parts precisely, or for many categories, use MonarchBarList or MonarchBarChart. For values that change over time or do not add up to a whole, use MonarchBarChart.
api: @Composable fun MonarchDonutChart(title: String, segments: List<MonarchDonutChartSegment>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, description: String? = null, centerValue: String? = null, centerLabel: String? = null, summary: String? = null, sort: MonarchDonutChartSort = MonarchDonutChartSort.Descending, maxSegments: Int = 6, legendContent: MonarchDonutChartLegendContent = MonarchDonutChartLegendContent.Both, status: MonarchChartFrameStatus = MonarchChartFrameStatus.Ready, size: Dp? = null, thickness: Dp? = null, percentDigits: Int = 0, showCenterValue: Boolean = true, showLegend: Boolean = true, tableToggle: Boolean = true, emptyMessage: String? = null, footer: String? = null, labels: MonarchDonutChartLabels = MonarchDonutChartLabels(), formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = null, onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null)
class MonarchDonutChartSegment(key: String, label: String, value: Double, color: MonarchChartColor? = null)

class MonarchDonutChartLabels(frame: MonarchChartFrameLabels = MonarchChartFrameLabels(), other: String? = null, segment: String? = null, value: String? = null, share: String? = null, total: String? = null)
enum class MonarchDonutChartLegendContent { Both, Value, Percent, None }
enum class MonarchDonutChartSort { Descending, None }

options.name: title
options.description: The chart's name: the frame heading and the donut's spoken name.

options.name: segments
options.description: The parts: key, label, value (negative and non-finite count as 0) and an optional color slot.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the frame.

options.name: description
options.description: One line under the title.

options.name: centerValue
options.description: The large text in the middle.

options.name: centerLabel
options.description: Small text under the center value, such as "assets".

options.name: summary
options.description: Replaces the generated spoken summary.

options.name: sort
options.description: The largest slice first, or the given order.

options.name: maxSegments
options.description: The most slices drawn (at least 2); the smallest beyond it fold into a neutral Other slice.

options.name: legendContent
options.description: What each legend entry shows after its label: Both ("412 · 48%"), Value, Percent or None.

options.name: status
options.description: Ready, Loading, Empty or Error. Ready with a total of 0 shows Empty.

options.name: size
options.description: The outer diameter, and the height kept in every status.

options.name: thickness
options.description: The ring's thickness, kept between 4dp and half the size.

options.name: percentDigits
options.description: Decimal places in shares.

options.name: showCenterValue
options.description: Whether the middle shows the center value and label.

options.name: showLegend
options.description: Whether the frame shows the legend.

options.name: tableToggle
options.description: Whether "View as table" is offered.

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: The message of the empty state.

options.name: footer
options.description: Notes under the chart.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for Other, Segment, Value, Share, Total and the frame's strings.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes values in the center, the legend, the table, TalkBack and the summary. A number in the current locale by default.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Try again in the error status.

states.name: ready
states.description: The donut with its center text, and the legend in the frame's legend row.

states.name: folded
states.description: With more segments than maxSegments, the smallest are drawn as one Other slice in the neutral color; the legend and the slice elements show Other, the table lists every segment.

states.name: table
states.description: "View as table" replaces the donut with every segment, then the total, with Value and Share columns.

states.name: loading
states.description: The frame's skeleton of the donut's height, read as "Loading chart".

states.name: empty
states.description: MonarchEmptyState with "No data yet"; also shown when the total is 0.

states.name: error
states.description: The frame's error, with Try again when onRetry is set.

appearance: Slices take the theme's data colors 1 to 5 in order and Other the subtle text color, over a ring in the muted background color that shows in the gaps between slices. The center value is heading text in the default text color, the center label caption text in the muted color. Legend markers are squares. Every color is a theme role, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes are covered.
platformNotes: Drawn with a Compose Canvas and drawArc (iOS uses Swift Charts SectorMark, the web SVG circles); Android has no first-party chart library and Monarch adds none. The legend is the frame's legend row above the donut, wrapping onto new rows, instead of a column beside it as on iOS and the web: the frame keeps the body at a fixed height, and a column beside a 160dp donut would be cut at large font sizes. As on iOS, slices are not interactive (the web dims the other slices on hover); every value and share is in the legend, in one TalkBack element per slice and in the table. The center value is a String rather than any node. There is no chart descriptor like iOS's Audio Graphs on Android. In right to left the slices run anticlockwise from the top.
accessibility: The donut is one element with the image role, named by the title, whose state description is the generated summary ("Total 865. Laptops 412 (48%), …") or the summary parameter.
After it, one element per drawn slice, in slice order (traversal index), placed on the ring and read as its name, value and share; Other is read with its folded total.
The center text is hidden from TalkBack, because the summary already reads the total.
Each legend entry is one element read as its label then its value and share; the color marker is decoration.
"View as table" shows every segment, the total and the shares as text; each row is read as the segment, then its value and share.
Every built-in word (Other, Segment, Value, Share, Total and the frame's strings) can be replaced through labels.
edgeCases: Negative and non-finite values count as 0; a total of 0 shows the empty state.
A share that rounds to 0 reads "<1%" and one that rounds to the whole without being it ">99%", so rounding never hides a segment; a tiny slice keeps a sliver of 2dp along the ring.
maxSegments below 2 is treated as 2, so Other never stands alone.
A long center value or label shrinks to half its size, then is cut with an ellipsis, to stay inside the hole at large text sizes.
Long legend labels wrap; many entries wrap onto new rows above the donut.
The slice elements and the summary were checked with Robolectric semantics tests, not with TalkBack on a device.

name: MonarchDownloadReportButton
title: DownloadReportButton
wrapsNative: MonarchButton (androidx.compose.material3.Button) for one format, or with androidx.compose.material3.DropdownMenu for several; androidx.activity.result.contract.ActivityResultContracts.CreateDocument through androidx.activity.compose.rememberLauncherForActivityResult for the system save dialog; MonarchProgress and MonarchInlineErrorRetry
summary: Downloads a report in one or several formats, with progress while the file is prepared, a note when it is prepared in the background, the system save dialog for a ready file, and Try again on failure.
whenToUse: Next to a table, a chart or a list whose data people take elsewhere: an export of invoices, a usage report.
whenNotToUse: Not for sharing a link or a small text: use the Android Sharesheet (see share-button). Not for opening a file in another app: start an ACTION_VIEW intent.
api: @Composable fun MonarchDownloadReportButton(onDownload: suspend (MonarchDownloadReportFormat) -> MonarchDownloadReportResult, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, formats: List<MonarchDownloadReportFormat> = listOf(MonarchDownloadReportFormat.Csv), progress: Float? = null, variant: MonarchButtonVariant = MonarchButtonVariant.Secondary, size: MonarchButtonSize = MonarchButtonSize.Sm, enabled: Boolean = true, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, menuIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchDownloadReportButtonLabels = MonarchDownloadReportButtonLabels(), errorMessage: ((Throwable, MonarchDownloadReportFormat) -> String)? = null)

data class MonarchDownloadReportFormat(val label: String, val id: String, val description: String? = null, val mimeType: String = "application/octet-stream") { companion object { val Csv: MonarchDownloadReportFormat } }
sealed class MonarchDownloadReportResult { data object Downloaded; data class Queued(val message: String? = null); class File(val fileName: String, val write: suspend (OutputStream) -> Unit) }

class MonarchDownloadReportButtonLabels(label: String? = null, single: ((format: String) -> String)? = null, preparing: ((format: String) -> String)? = null, downloaded: ((format: String) -> String)? = null, queued: String? = null, error: ((format: String) -> String)? = null, progress: String? = null)

options.name: onDownload
options.description: Prepares the file. Return File(fileName) { stream -> … } to open the system save dialog, Downloaded when the app saved or shared it, Queued(message) when it is prepared in the background; throw on failure.

options.name: formats
options.description: The formats offered. One shows a plain button "Download CSV"; several open a menu from "Download" with each format's label and description.

options.name: progress
options.description: How far the preparation is, 0 to 1, drawn as a MonarchProgress bar under the button while it runs. Clamped; a value that is not finite is not drawn.

options.name: variant
options.description: The button's visual weight.

options.name: size
options.description: The button's height; the touch target is 48dp at every size.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the button can be used.

options.name: icon
options.description: A download icon before the text; Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: menuIcon
options.description: A chevron after the text when there are several formats.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string (monarch_downloadreportbutton_*).

options.name: errorMessage
options.description: Turns a thrown exception into the text shown. Default: "The CSV download failed."

states.name: idle
states.description: A button; with several formats it opens a menu.

states.name: preparing
states.description: The button shows progress, reports "Preparing CSV…" as its state and does not start a second download; the bar shows when progress is given.

states.name: saving
states.description: The system save dialog is open for the prepared file; then the file is written on a background thread.

states.name: saved
states.description: Back to idle; "CSV downloaded" is announced.

states.name: queued
states.description: A muted note under the button says the file is prepared in the background; it is announced.

states.name: failed
states.description: A MonarchInlineErrorRetry with Try again, which repeats the same format; the message is announced.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The button's disabled colors; nothing starts.

appearance: The MonarchButton colors of the variant, the MonarchProgress bar in the accent role, the queued note in the muted text role, and the danger tone of MonarchInlineErrorRetry. The save dialog is the system's. High-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colors.
platformNotes: On the web onDownload saves the file through the browser. On Android a file needs a place to go, so returning File opens the system save dialog (ACTION_CREATE_DOCUMENT through ActivityResultContracts.CreateDocument with the format's MIME type), and Monarch writes the bytes the app gives to the chosen document; an app that shares instead returns Downloaded. A cancelled save dialog returns to idle without a message. The web passes the format id to onDownload; Android passes the whole format, as iOS does. Android's File carries a writer instead of iOS's file URL, so the app does not need a temporary file. The menu shows each format's description under its label.
accessibility: The button is a MonarchButton with a 48dp touch target; icons are decorative.
While the file is prepared the button's state description is "Preparing CSV…".
Preparing, saved and queued are announced through a polite live region that is always present.
The progress bar is named "Download progress" and reports its value.
A failure is MonarchInlineErrorRetry: text and a Try again button in a polite live region, not color alone.
edgeCases: Only one download runs at a time; activating the button again while it is busy does nothing, and the menu does not open.
A progress value outside 0 to 1 is clamped; a value that is not finite is not drawn.
The save dialog needs an ActivityResultRegistryOwner (any ComponentActivity provides one).
If the app's process is recreated while the save dialog is open, the prepared file is lost and the button returns to idle.
The real save dialog was not run on a device; the save path was tested with a test activity result registry and a registered output stream.

name: MonarchDragHandle
title: DragHandle
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.Canvas (grip dots), androidx.compose.foundation.focusable, androidx.compose.ui.semantics.CustomAccessibilityAction, androidx.compose.ui.input.key.onKeyEvent; the caller attaches Modifier.draggable, pointerInput or dragAndDropSource
summary: The grip an item is dragged by: a dotted glyph in a 48dp touch target with a spoken name, idle, grabbed and dropped states, and move actions for TalkBack, Switch Access and hardware keyboards.
whenToUse: At the start of each row of a list, or on each card of a board, that the person can reorder.
whenNotToUse: For a list that is not reordered, use no handle. For the handle at the top of a bottom sheet use BottomSheetDefaults.DragHandle.
api: @Composable fun MonarchDragHandle(label: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, state: MonarchDragHandleState = MonarchDragHandleState.Idle, axis: MonarchDragHandleAxis = MonarchDragHandleAxis.Vertical, size: MonarchDragHandleSize = MonarchDragHandleSize.Md, enabled: Boolean = true, onMove: ((MonarchDragHandleDirection) -> Unit)? = null, actionLabels: Map<MonarchDragHandleDirection, String> = emptyMap(), stateLabels: Map<MonarchDragHandleState, String> = emptyMap(), interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)
enum class MonarchDragHandleState { Idle, Grabbed, Dropped }
enum class MonarchDragHandleAxis { Vertical, Horizontal, Both }
enum class MonarchDragHandleSize { Sm, Md }
enum class MonarchDragHandleDirection { Up, Down, Backward, Forward }

options.name: label
options.description: The TalkBack name, naming the item: "Reorder Design review".

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the handle. Attach the drag gesture here.

options.name: state
options.description: Idle, Grabbed or Dropped. The component that moves items owns it.

options.name: axis
options.description: Vertical, Horizontal or Both. Selects the grip pattern and the move actions.

options.name: size
options.description: Sm: 24dp. Md: 32dp. The touch target is 48dp at both.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the handle offers its actions.

options.name: onMove
options.description: Moves the item one step. Without it the handle offers no actions and is not focusable.

options.name: actionLabels
options.description: Replaces the built-in action names "Move up", "Move down", "Move backward", "Move forward".

options.name: stateLabels
options.description: Replaces the built-in states "Picked up" and "Dropped".

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the focus interactions of the handle.

states.name: idle
states.description: Muted grip dots, no fill.

states.name: grabbed
states.description: Subtle accent fill, strong accent dots and a 1dp accent outline. TalkBack state "Picked up".

states.name: dropped
states.description: Subtle success fill and strong success dots, as a brief confirmation. TalkBack state "Dropped".

states.name: disabled
states.description: Dots in the disabled text color, no actions, exposed as disabled.

appearance: Idle dots use the muted text color; grabbed uses the subtle accent fill, strong accent dots and the accent border; dropped the subtle and strong success colors, in every theme.
platformNotes: On the web the handle is a button with keyboard instructions and aria-pressed. On Android, as on iOS, it is not a button: activating it does nothing, the drag is a gesture the caller attaches, and assistive technology uses named custom actions instead of keyboard instructions. With a hardware keyboard the arrow keys move the item while the handle has focus; left and right follow the reading order. The web's custom icon slot and hover style are not offered. iOS has a hint parameter; Android has no accessibility hint, so it is not offered. The grabbed state uses the colors of the accent tone.
accessibility: The handle is one TalkBack element whose content description is label; the grip is decorative.
With onMove, TalkBack and Switch Access get one custom action per direction of the axis: Move up and Move down, Move backward and Move forward, or all four.
The grabbed and dropped states are the element's state description; an idle handle has none.
The grabbed handle has an outline as well as a color change.
The touch target is 48dp at both sizes, reserved in the layout.
With onMove the handle is focusable and draws the focus ring; the arrow keys move the item, mirrored in right-to-left layouts.
The color change is animated only when animations are on.
edgeCases: The handle does not move anything itself and does not announce the new position; announce it from onMove or from the list.
It installs no gesture. A drag works only when the caller attaches one.
An empty string in actionLabels or stateLabels keeps the built-in text.
The glyph keeps its 16dp size at every font size.

title: Drawer
wrapsNative: MonarchBottomSheet with androidx.compose.material3.BottomSheetDefaults.DragHandle
summary: A bottom drawer with a grab handle is a MonarchBottomSheet with its default drag handle, which opens partially expanded when its content is tall. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: On a phone, for content the person may want to see partly or fully: a list of options, details of a map pin, a short form that should leave the screen visible above it.
whenNotToUse: For a task that must be finished before going on use MonarchDialog (see dialog). For navigation between the app's destinations use a navigation drawer (see sidebar-nav).
api: @Composable fun MonarchBottomSheet(onDismissRequest: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, title: String? = null, description: String? = null, dismissible: Boolean = true, showHandle: Boolean = true, fullyExpanded: Boolean = true, fullWidthContent: Boolean = false, content: @Composable MonarchBottomSheetScope.() -> Unit)

@Composable fun BottomSheetDefaults.DragHandle(modifier: Modifier = Modifier, width: Dp = SheetDefaults.DragHandleWidth, height: Dp = SheetDefaults.DragHandleHeight, shape: Shape = MaterialTheme.shapes.extraLarge, color: Color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant)

states.name: partially expanded
states.description: A tall drawer opens at half the screen; dragging the handle up expands it.

states.name: expanded
states.description: The drawer covers most of the screen and its content scrolls.

states.name: drag to close off
states.description: With dismissible = false the drawer does not follow drags; close it with a button or back.

appearance: The drawer uses the raised background role with Monarch's extra-large top corners, the drag handle the muted text role (Material onSurfaceVariant), and the overlay scrim role behind it, in every theme.
platformNotes: The web Drawer is a bottom panel with a grab handle and dragToClose, built on the web Sheet. On Android it is MonarchBottomSheet: the handle is its built-in Monarch handle, dragToClose={false} is dismissible = false, and partial expansion is fullyExpanded = false. iOS uses the system sheet with detents.
accessibility: System behavior: the drag handle is a button that TalkBack reads with actions to expand, collapse and close, so the drawer can be moved without a drag gesture.
System behavior: the drawer is announced when it opens and back closes it.
Rows inside keep their own 48dp touch targets.
edgeCases: A drawer with short content opens fully expanded: there is no half state for content shorter than half the screen.
Lazy lists inside scroll with the drawer's nested scrolling; do not put a verticalScroll column around a LazyColumn.

title: DropZone
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.draganddrop.dragAndDropTarget with androidx.compose.ui.draganddrop.DragAndDropTarget, beside MonarchFileUpload (androidx.activity.result.contract.ActivityResultContracts.OpenMultipleDocuments) as the main path
summary: Compose's drop target on an existing region, such as a file list or a conversation, so files dragged from another app can be dropped where they belong, with MonarchFileUpload's picker button as the path that works everywhere. Monarch ships no type.
whenToUse: On tablets, foldables and desktop windows, where people drag files between apps in split screen, add Modifier.dragAndDropTarget to the region the files belong to, and keep MonarchFileUpload in it for everyone else.
whenNotToUse: Never as the only way to add files: on a phone, with TalkBack, Switch Access or a keyboard, the picker button is the way in. For one image or video use MonarchMediaUpload.
api: fun Modifier.dragAndDropTarget(shouldStartDragAndDrop: (startEvent: DragAndDropEvent) -> Boolean, target: DragAndDropTarget): Modifier

interface DragAndDropTarget { fun onDrop(event: DragAndDropEvent): Boolean; fun onStarted(event: DragAndDropEvent) {}; fun onEntered(event: DragAndDropEvent) {}; fun onMoved(event: DragAndDropEvent) {}; fun onExited(event: DragAndDropEvent) {}; fun onChanged(event: DragAndDropEvent) {}; fun onEnded(event: DragAndDropEvent) {} }
fun DragAndDropEvent.mimeTypes(): Set<String>
fun DragAndDropEvent.toAndroidDragEvent(): android.view.DragEvent
fun Activity.requestDragAndDropPermissions(event: DragEvent): DragAndDropPermissions?
@Composable fun MonarchFileUpload(onFiles: (accepted: List<MonarchPickedFile>, rejected: List<MonarchFileRejection>) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, …)
fun MonarchPickedFile.Companion.of(resolver: ContentResolver, uri: Uri): MonarchPickedFile

states.name: idle
states.description: The region looks as it always does; the MonarchFileUpload button in it is the visible way in.

states.name: targeted
states.description: Between onEntered and onExited or onEnded, draw the region in the accent subtle fill with the accent border, and say so in text ("Release to add the images").

states.name: refused
states.description: shouldStartDragAndDrop returns false for types the region does not take, so the system shows that the drop is not accepted; checks of size and count after the drop are the app's, shown in a danger MonarchInlineNotice.

states.name: full or disabled
states.description: Return false from shouldStartDragAndDrop and disable MonarchFileUpload with enabled = false.

appearance: The system draws the dragged shadow. The region's targeted state uses the accent subtle and accent border roles from MonarchTheme, and the idle state the region's own colors, in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web DropZone listens to a region or the whole window, shows an overlay while files are dragged and refuses a wrong type before the drop. On Android the Compose drop target does this for the region it is on, and a whole-screen zone is the modifier on the screen's root. The dragged MIME types are known when the drag starts, so a wrong type is refused then; sizes are known only after the drop, through MonarchPickedFile.of. Dropped content URIs from another app need Activity.requestDragAndDropPermissions before they are read. MonarchFileUpload's checks are internal, so after a drop the app checks size and count itself; a public validate function, like iOS's MonarchFileUpload.validate, is requested. Dragging files between apps is a tablet, foldable and desktop interaction; the picker is the main path on phones. iOS uses dropDestination with the same rules.
accessibility: Dragging is an extra: MonarchFileUpload's button is a standard button with a 48dp target, and is how TalkBack, Switch Access and keyboard users add files.
The targeted state is a fill and a border plus a line of text, so nothing relies on color alone.
After a drop, update a polite live region with the number of files added and refused, because focus does not move.
edgeCases: Drops from the same app carry no permission request; drops from other apps need requestDragAndDropPermissions, and the permission ends with the activity.
ClipData items can be text or intents instead of URIs; count only items with a uri.
onEnded runs after every drag, also one that was dropped elsewhere; reset the targeted state there.
A phone in single-window mode never receives a drag from another app.

title: DropdownMenu
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.DropdownMenu (popup, position, focus, back, motion) with Monarch rows: MonarchMenuItem, MonarchMenuLabel, MonarchMenuDivider
summary: A list of actions that opens from a control: MonarchMenu is the Material 3 DropdownMenu with a Monarch panel and rows (icon, text, shortcut, accent check, destructive tone).
whenToUse: For a short list of actions or options that belong to one control: More on a row, Sort, the actions of a split button.
whenNotToUse: Not for choosing a value in a form: use ExposedDropdownMenuBox. Not for content that is not a list of actions: use MonarchPopover. Not for a destructive action without confirmation: open a confirm dialog from the item.
api: @Composable fun MonarchMenu(expanded: Boolean, onDismissRequest: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, offset: DpOffset = DpOffset(0.dp, 4.dp), content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)

@Composable fun MonarchMenuItem(text: String, onClick: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, destructive: Boolean = false, selected: Boolean? = null, shortcut: String? = null, leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)
@Composable fun MonarchMenuLabel(text: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier)
@Composable fun MonarchMenuDivider(modifier: Modifier = Modifier)

options.name: expanded
options.description: Whether the menu is open.

options.name: onDismissRequest
options.description: Called on a tap outside, back or Escape.

options.name: offset
options.description: Moves the menu from its place next to the anchor.

options.name: MonarchMenuItem.destructive
options.description: Shows the row in the strong danger colour with the danger tint when highlighted.

options.name: MonarchMenuItem.selected
options.description: true or false for an option, with an accent check when true; null for an action.

options.name: MonarchMenuItem.shortcut
options.description: A keyboard shortcut at the end, 12 in the subtle text colour.

options.name: MonarchMenuItem.leadingIcon
options.description: An outlined 20dp icon in the muted text colour.

states.name: open
states.description: The menu appears below the trigger (or above when there is no room) and takes focus.

states.name: disabled item
states.description: DropdownMenuItem with enabled = false is drawn in the disabled colors and announced as disabled.

states.name: danger item
states.description: MenuDefaults.itemColors(textColor = MonarchTheme.colors.dangerStrong) for an item that deletes.

states.name: checkable item
states.description: A Checkbox with onCheckedChange = null as the trailingIcon, and the item toggles the value.

states.name: groups
states.description: HorizontalDivider between groups; a section title is a disabled item or a MonarchText.

appearance: A panel 192 to 352dp wide with 12dp corners, the raised background, a 1dp border (subtle in light, default in dark, strong in high contrast), a soft shadow in the light themes and 4dp around the rows. Rows are 48dp touch targets with a 40dp highlight (6dp corners) one surface step darker on press, hover and focus; text 14, icons 20 in the muted text role, an accent check for a chosen option, the strong danger role for a destructive row, the disabled text role for a disabled one.
platformNotes: The web builds DropdownMenu from Radix parts (content, item, checkbox item, radio item, label, separator, submenu). On Android: MonarchMenu holds MonarchMenuItem rows (selected = true or false for a radio-like option, with the accent check; the content overload with trailingContent for a checkbox item or a count), MonarchMenuLabel, MonarchMenuDivider, and a second MonarchMenu opened from an item for a submenu. The web item's tone danger is destructive = true; its shortcut is the shortcut parameter. iOS uses Menu.
accessibility: The menu is a focusable popup: focus moves into it and back to the anchor when it closes; back and Escape close it.
Every row has a 48dp target and the click action; a disabled row is announced as disabled.
An option row says whether it is selected; a group label is a heading.
Long text wraps at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: The menu scrolls when it is taller than the window.
Close the menu (expanded = false) in each item's onClick; it does not close by itself.

name: MonarchDuplicatePanel
title: DuplicatePanel
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column, androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow, MonarchCard, MonarchBadge, MonarchButton
summary: Saved records that look like the one being created or viewed, why each one matched, and buttons to open, merge or dismiss each one.
whenToUse: Under a create form when the entered data matches existing records, or on a record screen to list likely duplicates.
whenNotToUse: To block saving, use form validation with an error. To merge two records field by field, use a merge screen; start it from onMerge.
api: @Composable fun MonarchDuplicatePanel(matches: List<MonarchDuplicateMatch>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchDuplicatePanelVariant = MonarchDuplicatePanelVariant.Hint, footer: String? = null, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, onOpen: ((MonarchDuplicateMatch) -> Unit)? = null, onMerge: ((MonarchDuplicateMatch) -> Unit)? = null, onDismiss: ((MonarchDuplicateMatch) -> Unit)? = null, title: String? = null, openLabel: String? = null, mergeLabel: String? = null, dismissLabel: String? = null)
class MonarchDuplicateMatch(val id: String, val title: String, val kind: String? = null, val reasons: List<String> = emptyList(), val detail: String? = null, val score: Float? = null)
enum class MonarchDuplicatePanelVariant { Hint, Panel }

options.name: matches
options.description: The likely duplicates, in order. Nothing is drawn when empty.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the panel.

options.name: variant
options.description: Hint: a warning box under a form. Panel: a plain section.

options.name: footer
options.description: A closing line, for example "You can still create it."

options.name: icon
options.description: An icon before the heading of the hint. Decorative; Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Adds an Open button to each match. The app navigates.

options.name: onMerge
options.description: Adds a Merge button to each match.

options.name: onDismiss
options.description: Adds a "Not a duplicate" button to each match. The app removes the match.

options.name: title
options.description: The heading. null uses monarch_duplicatepanel_title_one or _other by the number of matches.

options.name: openLabel
options.description: Label of the Open buttons. null uses monarch_duplicatepanel_open.

options.name: mergeLabel
options.description: Label of the Merge buttons. null uses monarch_duplicatepanel_merge.

options.name: dismissLabel
options.description: Label of the dismiss buttons. null uses monarch_duplicatepanel_dismiss.

states.name: one match
states.description: The heading is singular.

states.name: several matches
states.description: The heading is plural, with one card per match.

states.name: no matches
states.description: Nothing is drawn and no space is taken.

appearance: The hint is a box in the warning subtle background with the warning border and a heading in the strong warning color; the panel has no box and a heading in the default text color. Each match is a MonarchCard on the surface color with the name in strong body text, kind and score as neutral badges, and reasons and detail in muted caption text.
platformNotes: The web takes an href per match and opens it in a new tab; here onOpen hands the match to the app, which navigates. The web meta slot takes any content; detail is a String. The heading level option has no equivalent: the heading is marked as a heading. The heading chooses between a singular and a plural string by count, as on iOS. The parity map named a LazyColumn of cards; it is a Column, because the matches are few and the panel sits inside a scrolling form, where a nested lazy list cannot be measured. The web shows kind, reasons and score on one muted line; here kind and score are badges. The warning icon of the hint is a slot, because Monarch bundles no icons.
accessibility: The heading is marked as a heading. In the hint variant it is a polite live region, so TalkBack announces it when it changes.
The name, badges, reasons and detail of a match are one element and not actionable.
Each button is read as its label and the name of the record, for example "Merge: Example Ltd".
Buttons reserve a 48dp touch target and wrap onto a new line when they do not fit.
The icon is hidden from TalkBack. The score is text, so it does not depend on color.
edgeCases: A score outside 0 to 1 is clamped before it is shown as a percentage.
Long names and reasons wrap; nothing is cut off at the largest font size.
The live region announces changes of the heading, so a change from one to two matches is announced, but a change between two sets of the same size is not.

name: MonarchDurationInput
title: DurationInput
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedTextField (through MonarchTextField) with autocorrection off, androidx.compose.material3.IconButton for the stepper, and android.icu.text.MeasureFormat for the spoken duration
summary: A labelled field for a length of time typed as free text ("1h 30m", "90", "1.5h", "1:30"), saved as whole minutes, with − and + buttons that step on a grid.
whenToUse: For an estimate, a time limit, a break or a buffer that people think of as hours and minutes and like to type quickly.
whenNotToUse: For a time of day use the Material 3 TimePicker. For a plain count of units use MonarchNumberInput. For a date range use the Material 3 DateRangePicker.
api: @Composable fun MonarchDurationInput(minutes: Int?, onMinutesChange: (Int?) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, label: String? = null, placeholder: String? = null, helperText: String? = null, errorText: String? = null, minimum: Int = 0, maximum: Int? = null, step: Int = 15, largestUnit: MonarchDurationInputUnit = MonarchDurationInputUnit.Hours, minutesPerDay: Int = 1440, enabled: Boolean = true, readOnly: Boolean = false, showSteppers: Boolean = true, format: ((Int) -> String)? = null, parse: ((String) -> Int?)? = null, labels: MonarchDurationInputLabels = MonarchDurationInputLabels(), interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)
enum class MonarchDurationInputUnit { Hours, Days }

class MonarchDurationInputLabels(invalid: String? = null, range: ((minimum: Int, maximum: Int?) -> String)? = null, valueText: ((minutes: Int) -> String)? = null, increment: String? = null, decrement: String? = null)

options.name: minutes
options.description: The duration in whole minutes, or null while the field is empty.

options.name: onMinutesChange
options.description: Called with the new duration, or null when cleared, when the text is read (Done, leaving the field, before a step) or a step is taken; never on every keystroke.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the field.

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label.

options.name: placeholder
options.description: Replaces the built-in placeholder "e.g. 1h 30m", shown while the field is empty and focused.

options.name: helperText
options.description: Guidance below the field.

options.name: errorText
options.description: An error from the app; replaces the field's own messages while present.

options.name: minimum
options.description: The shortest allowed duration in minutes. Shorter text is flagged; steps stop at it.

options.name: maximum
options.description: The longest allowed duration in minutes. Longer text is flagged; steps stop at it.

options.name: step
options.description: Minutes one press of − or +, an arrow key or a TalkBack action adds or removes, on a grid from zero.

options.name: largestUnit
options.description: Writes 26 hours as "26h" (Hours) or "1d 2h" (Days).

options.name: minutesPerDay
options.description: The minutes in a "d" when reading and writing; 480 for eight-hour work days.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the field and the buttons can be used.

options.name: readOnly
options.description: Selectable but not editable; the buttons are disabled.

options.name: showSteppers
options.description: Shows the − and + buttons and the Increase and Decrease actions.

options.name: format
options.description: Writes minutes as text. The default writes "0m", "45m", "1h 30m".

options.name: parse
options.description: Reads trimmed, non-empty text as minutes, or returns null when it cannot. Empty text always clears the value.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the invalid and range messages, the spoken duration and the button names.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the focus and press interactions of the field.

states.name: empty
states.description: The value is null; the placeholder shows while focused. The first step starts from the minimum.

states.name: value
states.description: The text is the duration written as "1h 30m"; TalkBack reads it in words as the field's state.

states.name: unreadable
states.description: A danger outline and "Use a duration like 1h 30m, 90m or 1.5h." under the field. The text is kept and the value is not changed.

states.name: out of range
states.description: A danger outline and "Enter between 15m and 2h.", "Enter at least 15m." or "Enter at most 2h.". The text is kept and the value is not changed.

states.name: error
states.description: The app's message in place of the field's own, drawn the same way.

states.name: at a bound
states.description: The button that would pass the bound is disabled and its action is removed.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The subtle background and the disabled text color; both buttons are disabled.

states.name: read only
states.description: The text can be selected but not changed; both buttons are disabled.

appearance: The field is MonarchTextField: a surface fill with the input border, the focus ring color when focused and the danger strong color in error. The − and + signs use the default text color, or the disabled text color when their button is disabled. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Matches the web's DurationInput and iOS: the same forms are read (90, 90m, 1h 30m, 1h30, 1.5h, 1,5h, 1:30, 2 hours 15 minutes, 1d 4h), the same "1h 30m" format is written, the value is whole minutes and unreadable text is kept and flagged, never saved. The web's sm, md and lg sizes are not offered; the field is the size of MonarchTextField. The web steps with ArrowUp and ArrowDown and moves an hour with PageUp and PageDown; Android does the same with a hardware keyboard, and adds − and + icon buttons (on by default, as on iOS) and Increase and Decrease TalkBack actions. Home, End and Escape are not handled. With a minimum of 0 and a maximum, the range message is "Enter at most 2h." where the web says "Enter between 0m and 2h.", as on iOS. Unit words are read in English, as on the web; the spoken duration uses android.icu.text.MeasureFormat in the person's language. iOS has an errorHint label for its "Error: …" hint; Android has no such string because TalkBack announces the field's error semantics itself. The keyboard is the text keyboard with autocorrection off, since unit letters must be typed.
accessibility: The field is the Material 3 text field: TalkBack reads the label, the text, the error and, as the state, the duration in words ("1 hour, 30 minutes").
A new message for unreadable or out-of-range text is the field's error, shown with text and a danger outline, not color alone.
The − and + buttons are Material 3 icon buttons named "Decrease" and "Increase", each with a 48dp touch target; the sign itself is hidden from TalkBack.
The field has Increase and Decrease custom actions while a step is possible.
The decrease button is at the start and the increase button at the end, mirrored in right-to-left layouts.
With a hardware keyboard the up and down arrows step and Page Up and Page Down move an hour.
Autocorrection is off so unit letters are not replaced.
edgeCases: Changing minutes from outside replaces the text on screen and clears the field's own message.
Fractions of a minute are rounded to the nearest minute: "0.5" is 1 minute.
"1:75" is not a clock and is flagged; "30m 5" is flagged, while "1h30" is 90 minutes.
A step from text that cannot be read starts from the saved value, else from the minimum.
A maximum below the minimum counts as the minimum.
A step of zero or less steps by one minute.

name: MonarchEditableCell
title: EditableCell
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedTextField (through MonarchTextField) for text and numbers, androidx.compose.material3.DropdownMenu for choices, androidx.compose.material3.DatePickerDialog with DatePicker for dates, switched in place from a clickable androidx.compose.material3.Text
summary: A table cell that edits its value in place: text, a number, a choice from a menu or a date from the Material 3 date picker, with checks, an asynchronous save and an error that keeps the editor open.
whenToUse: For changing one value of a row where it is shown: an amount, a stage, an owner's name or a close date in a list of deals or a record's detail rows.
whenNotToUse: For a title or a note outside a table use MonarchInlineEditText. For several values saved together use a form with MonarchTextField, MonarchSelect and a save button.
api: @Composable fun <T : Any> MonarchEditableCell(value: T?, label: String, editor: MonarchEditableCellEditor<T>, onCommit: suspend (T?) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, required: Boolean = false, placeholder: String? = null, startEditing: Boolean = false, saveOnFocusLoss: Boolean = true, format: ((T) -> String)? = null, validate: ((T?) -> String?)? = null, onCancel: (() -> Unit)? = null, onEditingChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchEditableCellLabels = MonarchEditableCellLabels())

sealed class MonarchEditableCellEditor<T : Any> { data object Text : MonarchEditableCellEditor<String>; class Number(min: Double? = null, max: Double? = null) : MonarchEditableCellEditor<Double>; class Select<T : Any>(options: List<MonarchSelectOption<T>>) : MonarchEditableCellEditor<T>; class Date(min: Long? = null, max: Long? = null) : MonarchEditableCellEditor<Long> }

class MonarchEditableCellLabels(edit: ((label: String) -> String)? = null, save: String? = null, cancel: String? = null, saving: String? = null, invalidNumber: String? = null, required: String? = null, belowMin: ((min: String) -> String)? = null, aboveMax: ((max: String) -> String)? = null, noValue: String? = null, saveFailed: String? = null)

options.name: value
options.description: The saved value, or null for an empty cell.

options.name: label
options.description: What the cell holds, for example "Status for Acme": the spoken name of the cell and the label of its field.

options.name: editor
options.description: Text, Number(min, max), Select(options) or Date(min, max); it also fixes the type of the value: String, Double, the option value, or epoch milliseconds in UTC.

options.name: onCommit
options.description: Saves the new value. Not called when the value did not change. Throw to keep the cell editing with the error; the exception's message is shown.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the cell.

options.name: enabled
options.description: When false the value is plain text in the disabled color and cannot be edited.

options.name: required
options.description: Refuses an empty value with "Enter a value." and leaves out the select cell's None item.

options.name: placeholder
options.description: Shown in view mode while the cell is empty, and as the field's placeholder.

options.name: startEditing
options.description: Opens the editor when the cell first appears, for a new row.

options.name: saveOnFocusLoss
options.description: Saves a text or number when focus leaves the field, like the web's save on blur.

options.name: format
options.description: Writes the value for view mode. By default the text, the number in the locale's format, the option's label or the medium date in UTC.

options.name: validate
options.description: Returns a message to refuse a value before it is saved, or null to allow it. Runs after the required and range checks.

options.name: onCancel
options.description: Called when editing is cancelled with Cancel, back, Escape or by dismissing the menu or dialog.

options.name: onEditingChange
options.description: Called when the editor opens or closes.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

states.name: viewing
states.description: The formatted value, or the placeholder in the subtle text color, as one button at least 48dp high. Numbers are aligned to the end with tabular figures.

states.name: editing text or number
states.description: A focused MonarchTextField with the cell's label and the current value as the draft, and Save and Cancel buttons under it.

states.name: choosing
states.description: A select cell shows a menu from the cell with None (unless required) and the options; the current one is selected and disabled options are dimmed.

states.name: picking a date
states.description: A date cell shows the Material 3 date picker in a dialog limited to min and max, with Save, Cancel and None (unless required).

states.name: saving
states.description: A progress indicator; the text field is disabled and Save shows its loading state. A menu or dialog has closed and the cell shows the progress at its end.

states.name: refused or failed
states.description: A text or number editor stays open with the message as the field's error. A select or date cell shows the message under the value in the danger color and keeps the saved value.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Plain text in the disabled color, without a button.

appearance: In view mode the value uses the default text role and the placeholder the subtle text role, with no border so the cell sits in a table row. The field, menu and dialog take their Monarch colors from MonarchTheme in light, dark and both high-contrast themes; errors use the danger strong role and also have text.
platformNotes: The web EditableCell opens with a click, Enter or F2, saves with Enter and on blur and cancels with Escape, using a text input, a native select or an ISO date input. On Android the select cell opens a Material 3 menu from the cell and the date cell opens the Material 3 date picker dialog, so dates are epoch milliseconds in UTC instead of YYYY-MM-DD strings and a typed invalid date cannot happen. Text and number cells keep the web's keys (Done saves, a hardware Escape cancels) and add visible Save and Cancel buttons and the system back gesture, because a phone keyboard has no Escape key. The web's controlled editing prop, initialDraft (type to edit) and trigger="none" for a DataGrid that owns focus are not offered: startEditing and onEditingChange cover a new row. The value type is fixed by the editor, so a number cell takes and returns a Double. There is no iOS entry yet.
accessibility: In view mode the cell is one button whose name is the label and whose state description is the shown value or the placeholder; the double-tap action is read as "Edit" with the label.
The view button and Save are at least 48dp by 48dp.
The text editor is a Material 3 text field labelled with the cell's label; a refusal or failure is set as its error, so TalkBack reads it with the field.
Menu items carry the selected state for the current value, and disabled options are read as disabled.
The error under a select or date cell is in a polite live region, so it is announced when it appears.
The progress while saving has the spoken name "Saving".
edgeCases: A blank text or number draft is an empty value (null); a required cell refuses it.
Number drafts ignore spaces and read the locale's decimal comma when there is no dot, so "2,5" is 2.5 in German; group separators other than spaces are not read.
Range errors format the limit in the locale: "Enter 10,000 or less." in US English.
An unchanged value closes the editor without calling onCommit; for text the comparison is after trimming.
With saveOnFocusLoss, moving focus out of the field commits the draft, so a refused draft shows its message again each time focus leaves.
Date values are UTC midnights from the Material 3 picker; formatting them in the device zone instead of UTC can show the previous day west of UTC.

name: MonarchEditorToolbar
title: EditorToolbar
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.FilledTonalIconToggleButton, androidx.compose.material3.FilterChip, androidx.compose.material3.IconButton, androidx.compose.material3.DropdownMenu, androidx.compose.material3.AlertDialog in a horizontally scrolling androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row
summary: A formatting toolbar for a text editor: undo and redo, a text style menu, inline formats, lists, quotes, code and links, plus product tools.
whenToUse: Above a rich text field or above the keyboard while one is focused: notes, comments, documents, email bodies.
whenNotToUse: For a plain text field with no formatting, show no toolbar. For actions on the whole document (share, export), use the top app bar.
api: @Composable fun MonarchEditorToolbar(onAction: (MonarchEditorTool) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, groups: List<List<MonarchEditorTool>> = MonarchEditorTool.DefaultGroups, active: Set<MonarchEditorTool> = emptySet(), disabled: Set<MonarchEditorTool> = emptySet(), enabled: Boolean = true, icons: Map<MonarchEditorTool, Painter> = emptyMap(), labels: MonarchEditorToolbarLabels = MonarchEditorToolbarLabels(), onLink: ((String?) -> Unit)? = null)

class MonarchEditorTool { val id: String; val level: Int?; val title: String?; companion object { val Undo; val Redo; val Paragraph; val Bold; val Italic; val Strikethrough; val Code; val Link; val BulletList; val OrderedList; val TaskList; val Blockquote; val CodeBlock; fun heading(level: Int): MonarchEditorTool; fun custom(id: String, title: String): MonarchEditorTool; val DefaultGroups: List<List<MonarchEditorTool>>; val InlineGroups: List<List<MonarchEditorTool>> } }

class MonarchEditorToolbarLabels(toolbar: String? = null, tools: Map<MonarchEditorTool, String> = emptyMap(), textStyle: String? = null, linkTitle: String? = null, linkAddress: String? = null, linkApply: String? = null, linkRemove: String? = null, linkCancel: String? = null, linkHelp: String? = null)

options.name: onAction
options.description: Runs when a tool is pressed or a text style is chosen. The app applies it to its editor.

options.name: groups
options.description: The tools in groups separated by dividers. Neighbouring paragraph and heading tools become one text style menu; empty groups are dropped. MonarchEditorTool.InlineGroups gives inline formats only.

options.name: active
options.description: The formats that are on at the caret or selection, and the current text style. The app's editor works these out.

options.name: disabled
options.description: Tools that cannot be used now, such as undo with nothing to undo.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether any tool can be used, for example false while the editor loads.

options.name: icons
options.description: The icon of each tool, drawn in the control's content color. A format with an icon is an icon toggle button; without one it is a filter chip with its name.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the toolbar name, every tool name (by tool), the text style menu and the link form.

options.name: onLink
options.description: Makes the link tool open a form for the address. Receives a safe address to apply, or null when Remove link is pressed. Without it, the link tool goes to onAction.

states.name: on
states.description: A format in active is a checked icon toggle (the tonal fill) or a selected filter chip with its check mark.

states.name: disabled tool
states.description: Drawn in the disabled colors, announced as disabled, and cannot be pressed.

states.name: link form
states.description: An AlertDialog with an address field, Apply (enabled only for a safe address), Remove link when a link is active, and Cancel.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With enabled = false every control is disabled.

states.name: narrow
states.description: The row scrolls sideways when the tools do not fit.

appearance: A row on the surface background role with thin dividers in the subtle border role between groups. The controls take the colors Monarch maps to the Material scheme: tonal fill for a checked icon toggle, the selected chip colors for a chip, the ghost MonarchButton for named actions and the text style menu. The same mapping in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web toolbar drives a Tiptap editor directly. Android has no Monarch rich text editor yet, so this toolbar is editor-agnostic: the app passes which formats are on and applies what is pressed. The parity map named a row of icon toggle buttons above the keyboard: Monarch bundles no icons, so the app passes them in icons (a Painter per tool, sized and tinted by the control) and a tool without one shows its name as a FilterChip or ghost button; the placement above the keyboard is the app's, with Modifier.imePadding(). Headings are one text style menu instead of a button per level, to fit a phone. The link popover is an AlertDialog. The web's arrow-key roving focus and shortcut hints are not offered; TalkBack and a hardware keyboard move through each control, and shortcuts belong to the app's text field. iOS uses the same name; its action closure is onAction, and its custom tool's SF Symbol is an entry in icons.
accessibility: The toolbar is a traversal group named "Formatting".
Formats are Material 3 toggles: an icon toggle is read with its name and on or off; a chip is read with its name and selected state. The on state is also a fill or a check mark, not color alone.
Undo, redo and product tools are buttons named by their title.
The text style menu is a button named "Text style" whose state is the current style; its entries show a radio mark and carry the selected state.
Group dividers are hidden from TalkBack.
Every control has a 48dp touch target; icon-only tools are named through their content description.
edgeCases: Empty groups are dropped, so two dividers never meet.
Heading levels outside 1 to 6 become the nearest level.
A link typed as a bare domain becomes https and an email address becomes mailto; javascript, data and other schemes, and text with spaces, are refused and Apply stays disabled.

name: MonarchEmailVerificationBanner
title: EmailVerificationBanner
wrapsNative: MonarchCalloutBanner with MonarchButton actions in a androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow, a LaunchedEffect countdown and a polite live region
summary: A notice that the email address is not verified yet, with the address, a Resend button that waits out a cooldown, and an optional Change email button.
whenToUse: While a signed-in person has not verified their email address, or after they changed it and the new one is not verified.
whenNotToUse: On the verification screen itself, where entering a code is the task, use MonarchOtpPinInput. For general notices use MonarchCalloutBanner.
api: @Composable fun MonarchEmailVerificationBanner(email: String, onResend: suspend () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, tone: MonarchTone = MonarchTone.Warning, placement: MonarchCalloutBannerPlacement = MonarchCalloutBannerPlacement.Section, cooldownSeconds: Int = 60, initialCooldownSeconds: Int = 0, onChangeEmail: (() -> Unit)? = null, onDismiss: (() -> Unit)? = null, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, dismissIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchEmailVerificationBannerLabels = MonarchEmailVerificationBannerLabels())

class MonarchEmailVerificationBannerLabels(title: String? = null, message: ((email: String) -> String)? = null, resend: String? = null, resendIn: ((seconds: Int) -> String)? = null, sent: String? = null, changeEmail: String? = null, dismiss: String? = null, error: String? = null)

options.name: email
options.description: The address waiting for verification, shown in the message.

options.name: onResend
options.description: Sends the email again. Throwing shows the error from labels and starts no cooldown.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the banner.

options.name: tone
options.description: Warning when features are locked until verified; Info when nothing is blocked yet. Other tones draw as Warning.

options.name: placement
options.description: A rounded callout in the content, or a full-width strip at the top of a screen.

options.name: cooldownSeconds
options.description: Seconds before another send after a successful one.

options.name: initialCooldownSeconds
options.description: Seconds already remaining when the banner appears, for example right after sign-up sent the first email.

options.name: onChangeEmail
options.description: Shows a Change email button.

options.name: onDismiss
options.description: Shows a dismiss button. The banner does not hide itself; remove it here.

options.name: icon
options.description: An icon at the start in the tone color. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: dismissIcon
options.description: The close mark of the dismiss button. Without it the button shows "Dismiss" as text.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the title, the message, the button titles, the sent line, the dismiss name and the error.

states.name: ready
states.description: Resend email can be used.

states.name: sending
states.description: The resend button shows its progress indicator, reads "Loading" and ignores taps.

states.name: sent
states.description: "Verification email sent" in the success strong color, announced; the cooldown starts.

states.name: cooldown
states.description: The button reads "Resend in 42s", counts down every second and is disabled until 0.

states.name: error
states.description: "Couldn’t send the email. Try again." in the danger strong color, announced; Resend is available at once.

appearance: The surface of MonarchCalloutBanner: the subtle fill and border of the warning or info tone, rounded in a section, a strip with a line below on a page. Resend is a small secondary button, Change email a small ghost button; the status line uses the success strong or danger strong role. All roles come from the theme.
platformNotes: The parity map names MonarchBanner; the component is built on MonarchCalloutBanner instead, because it needs two actions and a page placement, as on iOS. The web exports useResendCooldown for other resend controls; on Android the cooldown is the internal MonarchResendCooldown, to be promoted if another component needs it. onResend is a suspend function run in the banner's coroutine scope. A failed send always shows the error from labels: Android exception messages are not written for people, so the thrown message is not shown (iOS shows a LocalizedError description). On the web the cooldown button keeps focus with aria-disabled; on Android it is disabled, which TalkBack still reads with the seconds left in its title. The web's landmark and actionPlacement props have no Android equivalent.
accessibility: The tone name, title and message with the address are one TalkBack element, as MonarchCalloutBanner reads them.
Resend, Change email and Dismiss are separate buttons with 48dp touch targets.
During the cooldown the resend button is disabled and its title says the seconds left.
"Verification email sent" and failures are announced through a polite live region and shown as text, not color alone.
edgeCases: Long addresses wrap inside the message.
The countdown runs while the banner is on screen; a banner removed and shown again starts from initialCooldownSeconds.
A send started while the banner leaves the screen is cancelled with it.

examples.title: Info tone as a page strip
examples.code:

name: MonarchEmbedBlock
title: EmbedBlock
wrapsNative: android.webkit.WebView, androidx.compose.ui.viewinterop.AndroidView, MonarchLinkCard
summary: Shows a video, design or demo from an allow-listed site in a locked-down web view, and any other web link as a link card.
whenToUse: In documents, posts and notes where people paste a share link to a YouTube, Vimeo or Loom video, a Figma file or a CodePen.
whenNotToUse: For a link the app has unfurled with a picture and description, use MonarchLinkCard directly. For a web page that is part of the app, use the app's own web view or a Custom Tab.
api: @Composable fun MonarchEmbedBlock(url: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, caption: String? = null, title: String? = null, providers: List<MonarchEmbedProvider> = MonarchEmbedProvider.Defaults, onOpenLink: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchEmbedBlockLabels = MonarchEmbedBlockLabels())

class MonarchEmbedProvider(id: String, name: String, hosts: List<String>, aspectRatio: Float = 16f / 9f, toEmbedUrl: (Uri) -> String?) { companion object { val YouTube: MonarchEmbedProvider; val Vimeo: MonarchEmbedProvider; val Loom: MonarchEmbedProvider; val Figma: MonarchEmbedProvider; val CodePen: MonarchEmbedProvider; val Defaults: List<MonarchEmbedProvider> } }

sealed interface MonarchEmbedResolution { val url: String; class Frame(url: String, src: String, provider: MonarchEmbedProvider); class Link(url: String, host: String); class Invalid(url: String); companion object { fun resolve(raw: String, providers: List<MonarchEmbedProvider> = MonarchEmbedProvider.Defaults): MonarchEmbedResolution } }
class MonarchEmbedBlockLabels(frameTitle: ((provider: String) -> String)? = null, invalid: String? = null)

options.name: url
options.description: The URL someone pasted: a share link, not an embed code. Only the provider's embed address is ever loaded.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the block.

options.name: caption
options.description: Text under the frame or the card. Also the TalkBack name of the frame.

options.name: title
options.description: The TalkBack name of the frame when there is no caption. null uses "YouTube content".

options.name: providers
options.description: The sites that may be framed: YouTube, Vimeo, Loom, Figma and CodePen by default. Pass your own list to add or remove sites.

options.name: onOpenLink
options.description: Opens a link outside the app: the link card, or a tapped link that leaves the provider. null uses LocalUriHandler.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the strings monarch_embedblock_*.

states.name: frame
states.description: An https share link on an allow-listed host: a web view of the provider's embed address in the provider's aspect ratio, on a subtle fill while it loads.

states.name: link
states.description: Any other http or https link: a MonarchLinkCard with the host and the URL that opens outside the app.

states.name: invalid
states.description: Any other text (javascript:, data:, relative or malformed URLs, a user name in the URL): "This link can't be shown." in muted text.

appearance: The frame has the large container radius and the subtle background while the provider's page loads; the page itself is the provider's. The caption is a muted caption under the frame or the card. The link card is MonarchLinkCard. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web frames with a sandboxed iframe and a sandbox token list per provider; on Android the WebView runs the provider's scripts but has no file or content access, no geolocation, no new windows, no mixed content and no JavaScript bridge, and media play only after a tap. Main-frame navigation is allowed only to https pages on the embed address's host; a tapped link elsewhere opens outside the app, other navigations are blocked. Fullscreen video is not supported (no custom view). A provider's toEmbedUrl takes an android.net.Uri, and aspectRatio is a Float instead of a CSS ratio. The web also ships a Tiptap editor extension with a URL form; Android has no rich-text editor in Monarch, so the block shows URLs only. iOS has no entry yet; the names follow the web.
accessibility: The frame is named by the caption, the title or "YouTube content"; the provider's page inside is read by TalkBack as web content.
The link card is a MonarchLinkCard: one element with a 48dp touch target that opens the link.
A URL that cannot be shown is written as text.
The caption wraps at the largest font size.
edgeCases: An http link to an allow-listed site, or one with a port, is shown as a card, never framed.
A share link without an embeddable form (a YouTube channel page) is shown as a card.
Previews in Android Studio show the tinted frame without the page.
Whether a provider's player plays inside a WebView depends on the provider and the device; check the providers you enable on a device.

examples.title: A pasted video link
Only your own allow-list

MonarchEmbedBlock(
    url = "https://vimeo.com/76979871",
    providers = listOf(MonarchEmbedProvider.Vimeo, MonarchEmbedProvider.Loom),
)

parityExceptions.reason: The web embed block is an editor block that loads a third-party frame by URL; the web example shows the frame chrome only, and the native EmbedBlock cannot show the same web content.
parityExceptions.convention: Native shows a link card or a system web view, per HIG and Material 3.

name: MonarchEmbeddedAppFrame
title: EmbeddedAppFrame
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Box, MonarchSpinner, MonarchButton
summary: A framed area that shows a screen owned by another app or module, such as another Rook app's settings page, with its loading and error states.
whenToUse: When a screen hosts content it does not own: another module's settings, a partner's page in a WebView, or a screen that may fail to load.
whenNotToUse: For content the screen owns, compose it directly. For a full-screen web page, open Custom Tabs.
api: @Composable fun MonarchEmbeddedAppFrame(title: String, state: MonarchEmbeddedAppFrameState, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, height: Dp? = null, onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null, onOpen: (() -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchEmbeddedAppFrameLabels = MonarchEmbeddedAppFrameLabels(), content: @Composable BoxScope.() -> Unit)
enum class MonarchEmbeddedAppFrameState { Loading, Ready, Error }
class MonarchEmbeddedAppFrameLabels(loading: String? = null, errorTitle: String? = null, errorDescription: String? = null, retry: String? = null, open: String? = null)

options.name: title
options.description: The name of what the frame shows, such as "Example Desk: Email notifications"; the frame's pane name.

options.name: state
options.description: Loading, Ready or Error, reported by the app.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the frame.

options.name: height
options.description: A fixed height; null wraps the content, and loading and error keep at least 160dp.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Called by "Try again"; null hides it.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Called by "Open the page" to open the screen outside the frame; null hides it.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for "Loading…", the error title and explanation, "Try again" and "Open the page".

options.name: content
options.description: The embedded screen, shown when ready: native content, or a WebView through AndroidView.

states.name: loading
states.description: A spinner and "Loading…" in the middle.

states.name: ready
states.description: The content.

states.name: error
states.description: "This page didn’t open", the explanation, "Try again" and "Open the page".

appearance: The frame is the surface with the default border and the large radius; loading and error text is muted, the error title the default text. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web EmbeddedAppFrame is an iframe with a postMessage handshake (the App Settings embed contract): it detects readiness and resizes to the page height. Android has no iframe contract, so the app composes the content (natively, or a WebView it manages) and reports the state; there is no automatic timeout or resize. The web's "Open in a new tab" is "Open the page", and onOpen decides where it goes.
accessibility: The frame is a traversal group and a pane named by title.
While loading, the spinner is read as "Loading…".
The error title and explanation are read together as a polite live region; the buttons are separate with 48dp touch targets.
edgeCases: A fixed height smaller than the content clips it; the app scrolls inside.
Without onRetry and onOpen the error shows only its message.

examples.title: An embedded settings page (ready, auto-height)
A page that never answers

    state = MonarchEmbeddedAppFrameState.Error,
    height = 220.dp,
    onRetry = { attempts++ },
    onOpen = { opened = true },
    labels = MonarchEmbeddedAppFrameLabels(open = "Open in Example Desk"),
) {}

name: MonarchEmojiPicker
title: EmojiPicker
wrapsNative: androidx.emoji2.emojipicker.EmojiPickerView (androidx.emoji2:emoji2-emojipicker) inside androidx.compose.ui.viewinterop.AndroidView
summary: An emoji picker with category tabs, recently used emoji first and skin-tone variants: the AndroidX system EmojiPickerView, hosted in Compose.
whenToUse: To let people choose any emoji for a reaction or a message, usually in a MonarchBottomSheet opened from a reaction or emoji button, or as the picker of MonarchReactionBar.
whenNotToUse: For a few fixed reactions use a row of buttons or MonarchReactionBar quickReactions. For typing emoji in text, the keyboard already has a picker with search.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchEmojiPicker(onEmojiPicked: (String) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, columns: Int? = null, rows: Float? = null, label: String? = null)

options.name: onEmojiPicked
options.description: Called with the emoji the person picks, including the skin-tone variant chosen with a long press.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the picker. It fills the width and is 320dp high unless the modifier sets a size first.

options.name: columns
options.description: Emoji per row. null keeps the view's 9.

options.name: rows
options.description: Rows visible at once; a fraction shows that the grid scrolls. null keeps the view's 7.5.

options.name: label
options.description: The pane name TalkBack reads; the built-in "Emoji" (monarch_emojipicker_label) without it.

states.name: default
states.description: Category tabs over a scrolling grid; the first tab holds the recently used emoji once the person has picked one.

states.name: variant menu
states.description: A long press on an emoji with skin-tone or gender variants opens the view's own popup of variants.

appearance: EmojiPickerView draws its own tabs and grid and takes its colors from the Activity's View theme, not from MonarchTheme; place it on a raised surface such as a MonarchBottomSheet. Light, dark and high-contrast themes are not checked on a device yet.
platformNotes: The web EmojiPicker and the iOS MonarchEmojiPicker are custom pickers with a bundled index of 517 emoji, search, categories, recents and skin tones, because neither platform has a picker outside the keyboard. Android has one in AndroidX, so Monarch hosts EmojiPickerView instead of drawing one: it covers recents, skin-tone and gender variants and the emoji font of the device. It has no search field and no categories or recents parameters; the keyboard's emoji search covers search. Recently used emoji are kept by the view in the app's shared preferences.
accessibility: The picker is a pane named "Emoji" (or label) and a traversal group, so TalkBack announces it when it appears in a sheet.
Each emoji in the grid and each category tab is read by the AndroidX view itself; this is not covered by Robolectric tests and is listed for a device check.
edgeCases: EmojiPickerView is created once in AndroidView's factory and keeps its own state across recompositions; columns and rows are applied on update.
The latest onEmojiPicked is called, also after the lambda changes between recompositions.
Give the picker a bounded height when it sits in a scrolling column; the default 320dp does this.

name: MonarchEmptyState
title: EmptyState
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column, androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow, androidx.compose.material3.Text
summary: What will appear in an empty view and the action that creates it: an icon tile, a heading, a message, actions and a tip.
whenToUse: When a list, a table, a card or a screen has nothing to show yet, when a search or filter matched nothing, or when there is nothing left to do.
whenNotToUse: When content failed to load, use MonarchErrorState. While content loads, use MonarchSkeleton or MonarchProgress.
api: @Composable fun MonarchEmptyState(title: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, kind: MonarchEmptyStateKind = MonarchEmptyStateKind.FirstRun, size: MonarchEmptyStateSize = MonarchEmptyStateSize.Md, message: String? = null, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, tip: String? = null, onClearFilters: (() -> Unit)? = null, actions: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, clearFiltersLabel: String? = null)
enum class MonarchEmptyStateKind { FirstRun, Filtered, Success }
enum class MonarchEmptyStateSize { Sm, Md, Lg }

options.name: title
options.description: What is missing. Marked as a heading.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the empty state.

options.name: kind
options.description: FirstRun, Filtered or Success: the tile color and the clear-filters button.

options.name: size
options.description: Sm, Md or Lg: spacing, tile size and type sizes. The web calls them compact, inline and page.

options.name: message
options.description: What will appear here and how to create it.

options.name: icon
options.description: An icon in a tinted tile. Hidden from TalkBack; no tile without it.

options.name: tip
options.description: A short hint under the actions, in small muted text.

options.name: onClearFilters
options.description: With kind Filtered, adds a "Clear filters" button before the actions.

options.name: actions
options.description: Buttons, laid out in a centered row that wraps.

options.name: clearFiltersLabel
options.description: Label of the clear-filters button. null uses monarch_emptystate_clear_filters.

states.name: first run
states.description: The icon tile in the accent tint.

states.name: filtered
states.description: The accent tint, and a "Clear filters" button when onClearFilters is given.

states.name: success
states.description: The icon tile in the success tint.

appearance: A centered column: an optional 40dp tile (32dp when small) in the accent subtle background with the icon in the accent strong color, or the success pair for Success; a heading in default text; a muted message; centered actions; a muted caption tip. The same roles in every theme.
platformNotes: Material 3 has no empty state, so it is built; iOS wraps ContentUnavailableView. Actions are a slot, where iOS takes up to two titles and closures. The web line layout (one row with icon, text and actions) and the children slot are not offered. Web sizes compact, inline and page are Sm, Md and Lg. The web shows a check icon for success by default; Monarch bundles no icons, so the tile appears only when the app passes an icon. The title is a heading for TalkBack; the web headingLevel has no equivalent.
accessibility: The title is marked as a heading.
The icon tile is hidden from TalkBack; the title and message carry the meaning.
Buttons keep their own roles and 48dp touch targets; the row of actions wraps at large font sizes.
Title, message and tip wrap and are not cut off at the largest font size.
edgeCases: onClearFilters is ignored unless kind is Filtered.
The empty state has no maximum width; inside a wide screen give it one with the modifier.

A filter that matched nothing

MonarchEmptyState(
    title = "No matching tickets",
    kind = MonarchEmptyStateKind.Filtered,
    size = MonarchEmptyStateSize.Sm,
    message = "Try another search.",
    onClearFilters = { cleared++ },
)
