name: MonarchEntityPicker
title: EntityPicker
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.ModalBottomSheet with MonarchSearchBar and an androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn of MonarchAvatar rows with androidx.compose.material3.RadioButton or Checkbox marks; MonarchFormField around a clickable field
summary: A field for picking one or several people or records from a list that the app can search on its server, shown with avatars, in a bottom sheet.
whenToUse: For an owner, an assignee, reviewers, a company or a project: entities with a name, a picture and often too many to list without search.
whenNotToUse: For plain options without pictures use MonarchCombobox or MonarchMultiSelect. For a short fixed list use MonarchSelect. For mentions inside text use MonarchMentionPicker.
api: @Composable fun MonarchEntityPicker(label: String, entities: List<MonarchEntityPickerEntity>, selected: String?, onSelectedChange: (String?) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, selectedEntities: List<MonarchEntityPickerEntity> = emptyList(), enabled: Boolean = true, required: Boolean = false, loading: Boolean = false, placeholder: String? = null, helperText: String? = null, errorText: String? = null, clearOptionLabel: String? = null, minSearchLength: Int = 0, debounceMillis: Long = 250L, search: (suspend (String) -> List<MonarchEntityPickerEntity>)? = null, onCreate: (suspend (String) -> MonarchEntityPickerEntity?)? = null, clearIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchEntityPickerLabels = MonarchEntityPickerLabels())

@Composable fun MonarchEntityPicker(label: String, entities: List<MonarchEntityPickerEntity>, selected: List<String>, onSelectedChange: (List<String>) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, selectedEntities: List<MonarchEntityPickerEntity> = emptyList(), enabled: Boolean = true, required: Boolean = false, loading: Boolean = false, placeholder: String? = null, helperText: String? = null, errorText: String? = null, minSearchLength: Int = 0, debounceMillis: Long = 250L, search: (suspend (String) -> List<MonarchEntityPickerEntity>)? = null, onCreate: (suspend (String) -> MonarchEntityPickerEntity?)? = null, clearIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchEntityPickerLabels = MonarchEntityPickerLabels())

class MonarchEntityPickerEntity(id: String, name: String, description: String? = null, hint: String? = null, image: Painter? = null, shape: MonarchAvatarShape = MonarchAvatarShape.Circle, keywords: String? = null, enabled: Boolean = true)

class MonarchEntityPickerLabels(select: String? = null, search: String? = null, cancel: String? = null, done: String? = null, loading: String? = null, empty: String? = null, tooShort: ((minLength: Int) -> String)? = null, failed: String? = null, retry: String? = null, create: ((text: String) -> String)? = null, summary: ((first: String, others: Int) -> String)? = null, clear: String? = null, none: String? = null)

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label, already localised. It names the field and is the title of the sheet.

options.name: entities
options.description: The entities to pick from: id, name, description, hint, image (a Painter the app loads), shape, keywords and enabled. With search, shown until the first search runs.

options.name: selected
options.description: The chosen id, or the chosen ids in pick order. The list form lets several be picked and keeps the sheet open until Done.

options.name: onSelectedChange
options.description: Called with the new choice.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the field.

options.name: selectedEntities
options.description: Entities for chosen ids that may not be in entities, so the field can show their names and pictures. Entities chosen from search results or created are also remembered while the field is shown.

options.name: enabled
options.description: When false the field does nothing and takes the disabled colors.

options.name: required
options.description: Shows a mark after the label and adds "Required" to the field's name.

options.name: loading
options.description: Shows "Loading…" in the list while entities is empty.

options.name: placeholder
options.description: Shown in the field while nothing is chosen. "Select…" when null.

options.name: helperText
options.description: Guidance under the field.

options.name: errorText
options.description: An error message, shown under the field with the form field's error style, set on the field and announced.

options.name: clearOptionLabel
options.description: Single choice only. Adds a first row that clears the selection, such as "Unassigned". Hidden while searching.

options.name: minSearchLength
options.description: The shortest trimmed text search runs for. Shorter text shows "Type at least N characters to search."

options.name: debounceMillis
options.description: How long to wait after typing before search runs. A newer text cancels the wait and the older search.

options.name: search
options.description: Loads the entities matching the trimmed text. Throw to show "The results could not be loaded." with Try again. Without it, entities are filtered by name, hint and keywords.

options.name: onCreate
options.description: Offers "Create “text”" when no shown name equals the typed text. The returned entity is chosen; null chooses nothing.

options.name: clearIcon
options.description: The icon of a clear button at the end of the field, shown while something is chosen. Monarch bundles no icons; without it there is no clear button.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

states.name: empty
states.description: The field shows the prompt in the subtle text color.

states.name: chosen
states.description: The field shows the first chosen entity's avatar and name, or "First +N" for several, and the clear button when there is a clearIcon.

states.name: searching
states.description: The list shows "Loading…" and the search field its pending state while the debounce waits or the search runs.

states.name: too short
states.description: The list asks for more characters and does not search.

states.name: failed
states.description: The list shows MonarchInlineErrorRetry with the message and Try again, which runs the same text again.

states.name: no match
states.description: The list shows "No matches", or the Create row when there is onCreate.

states.name: error
states.description: The field's border takes the danger color and the message shows under it.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The field takes the muted fill and the disabled text color and does not open. A disabled entity's row is dimmed and cannot be chosen.

appearance: The field is a surface with the input border role (danger border with an error, subtle border and muted fill when disabled); rows show a small MonarchAvatar, the name in the default text role and the description and hint in the muted text role, with radio or check marks in the accent solid role. The sheet uses the surface role. All come from MonarchTheme in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web opens a popover under a trigger; on Android the list opens in a Material 3 bottom sheet with a search field, as in the system contact pickers, and the same on iOS. The web's custom trigger, renderOption, renderValue, footer and sm/md/lg sizes are not offered: rows are fixed avatar rows with 48dp targets, and a footer action belongs in the screen. Search is a suspend function cancelled through coroutine cancellation instead of an AbortSignal. Pictures are Painters the app loads, as everywhere in Monarch, instead of iOS's Image or URL; iOS's systemImage has no Android counterpart because Monarch bundles no icons, so an entity without a picture shows initials. Duration becomes debounceMillis. Same name as iOS.
accessibility: The field is one button named by the field's label (with "Required" when required); its state description is every chosen name joined with commas, or "None".
The error is set on the field and announced through the form field's polite live region.
Avatars are decorative because the name is written beside them.
The clear button is a separate button named "Clear" with a 48dp target.

Each row is one element read with its name, description and hint: a radio button with the selected state for one choice, a checkbox with its checked state for several. Disabled entities are read as disabled.
Loading, too short and no match messages are polite live regions; a failed search offers a Try again button.
The field and every row are at least 48dp high.
edgeCases: A chosen id that is in neither entities nor selectedEntities, and was not picked while the field was shown, is not displayed; pass it in selectedEntities.
With search, the entities are shown while the text is empty and until the first search answers.
An exact name match hides the Create row, ignoring case and accents.
Creating an entity that is already chosen in the multiple form does not remove it.
Long names wrap in the rows; the field shows the first name with "+N".

title: ErrorPage
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Box (fillMaxSize, background) with MonarchErrorState
summary: A whole screen that failed (not found, forbidden, server error, offline or maintenance): MonarchErrorState at the large size, centered on the canvas color.
whenToUse: As the content of a screen the app navigated to that cannot be shown at all: a record that does not exist, no access, the service down, no connection.
whenNotToUse: When only part of a screen failed, use MonarchErrorState in that region or MonarchInlineErrorRetry. For a failure the user can fix in a form, use field errors.
api: Box(Modifier.fillMaxSize().background(MonarchTheme.colors.bgCanvas), contentAlignment = Alignment.Center) { MonarchErrorState(title, kind = MonarchErrorStateKind.NotFound, size = MonarchEmptyStateSize.Lg, message = …, requestId = …, onRetry = …, actions = { … }) }

options.name: kind
options.description: NotFound, Forbidden, Server, Offline or Maintenance; sets the default wording of the state.

options.name: size
options.description: Lg for a whole screen.

options.name: title
options.description: What happened, in plain words, supplied by the app.

options.name: message
options.description: What the person can do next. Never a raw error.

options.name: requestId
options.description: The id of the failed request, for support.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: A retry button, for Server, Offline and Maintenance.

options.name: actions
options.description: The app's way out, such as "Go to projects".

states.name: not found, forbidden
states.description: The title, message and a way out; no retry.

states.name: server, offline, maintenance
states.description: The same with a retry button; retrying shows the button as busy.

appearance: MonarchErrorState at its large size, centered on the canvas background color that fills the screen. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ErrorPage is a component with a large faint numeral (404, 403, 500), an optional brand, a support slot and a retry when the browser comes back online, and it can render without the app shell. On Android a destination that fails is a screen inside the app's navigation, so the recipe fills it with MonarchErrorState; the numeral is left out because it means little in an app, and the title says what happened. To retry when the network returns, register a ConnectivityManager.NetworkCallback in the app and call the same retry. focusOnMount has no equivalent: TalkBack reads the new screen from the top. iOS shares the recipe approach.
accessibility: MonarchErrorState marks its title as a heading and reads the message after it.
Retry and the actions are buttons with 48dp touch targets.
The screen keeps the app's top app bar, so back and navigation still work.
edgeCases: Use fillMaxSize inside a scrolling container only with a bounded height; the catalogue uses fillMaxWidth.
Offline: do not retry in a loop; retry once when the connection returns.

name: MonarchErrorState
title: ErrorState
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column, androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow, androidx.compose.foundation.text.selection.SelectionContainer, MonarchButton
summary: A region failed to load: what failed, why in plain words, and a retry button, in the layout of MonarchEmptyState.
whenToUse: When a screen, a panel or a large card could not load its content and there is nothing else to show in its place.
whenNotToUse: For a small part of a screen, use MonarchInlineErrorRetry. For an empty result that is not a failure, use MonarchEmptyState. For a form error, use field errors.
api: @Composable fun MonarchErrorState(title: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, kind: MonarchErrorStateKind = MonarchErrorStateKind.Error, size: MonarchEmptyStateSize = MonarchEmptyStateSize.Md, retrying: Boolean = false, message: String? = null, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, requestId: String? = null, onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null, actions: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, retryLabel: String? = null, retryingLabel: String? = null, requestIdLabel: String? = null)
enum class MonarchErrorStateKind { Error, Forbidden, NotFound, Offline, Server, Maintenance }

options.name: title
options.description: What failed. Marked as a heading.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the error state.

options.name: kind
options.description: What went wrong: the tile color and whether retry is offered.

options.name: size
options.description: Sm, Md or Lg, shared with MonarchEmptyState.

options.name: retrying
options.description: Shows the retry button as busy; it ignores taps.

options.name: message
options.description: Why, in plain words, and what the user can do.

options.name: icon
options.description: An icon in a tinted tile. Hidden from TalkBack; Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: requestId
options.description: The request id of the failed response, selectable so it can be copied.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Adds a primary retry button, except for Forbidden and NotFound.

options.name: actions
options.description: Further buttons after the retry button.

options.name: retryLabel
options.description: Label of the retry button. null uses monarch_errorstate_retry, "Try again".

options.name: retryingLabel
options.description: State of the retry button while retrying. null uses monarch_errorstate_retrying, "Retrying".

options.name: requestIdLabel
options.description: Label before the request id. null uses monarch_errorstate_request_id, "Request ID".

states.name: error, server
states.description: The tile in the danger tint; retry is offered.

states.name: offline
states.description: The tile in the warning tint; retry is offered.

states.name: maintenance
states.description: A muted tile; retry is offered.

states.name: forbidden, not found
states.description: A muted tile and no retry button, even when onRetry is given.

states.name: retrying
states.description: A progress indicator in the retry button, which ignores taps and reports "Retrying" as its state.

appearance: The layout and type of MonarchEmptyState. The icon tile is the danger subtle background with the danger strong icon for Error and Server, the warning pair for Offline, and the muted background with muted icon for Forbidden, NotFound and Maintenance. The request id is a muted caption with the id in the code typeface and default text color.
platformNotes: The web has a copy button beside the request id; here the id is in a SelectionContainer, so it is copied with the system text selection, and Monarch does not write to the clipboard. Further actions are a slot where iOS takes one title and closure. The web errorKindFromStatus helper is not offered. The busy state is always controlled with retrying. The web sets role=alert; here the state does not announce itself, as on iOS. Monarch bundles no icons, so the app passes the icon the web chooses by kind.
accessibility: The title is marked as a heading; the icon tile is hidden from TalkBack. Title and message say what failed, so nothing depends on the icon or its color.
While retrying the retry button stays in the focus order, ignores taps and has the state "Retrying".
The request id is one element, read as its label, a colon and the id, and can be selected and copied.
Buttons reserve 48dp touch targets and wrap at large font sizes.
The state does not announce itself when it replaces content.
edgeCases: onRetry is ignored for Forbidden and NotFound, because a retry cannot change the outcome.
A long request id wraps inside the text.

name: MonarchEscalationPolicyEditor
title: EscalationPolicyEditor

summary: Edits an escalation ladder: at each level, after how long and whom to notify, so an alert or request nobody acts on reaches someone else.
whenToUse: Unacknowledged incidents or overdue approvals must move to other people over time, and each level notifies one or more channels, rotas or people.
whenNotToUse: For approvals that happen in order, use MonarchApprovalChainEditor. For messages sent to customers on a schedule, use a sequence of steps built from MonarchActionEditor.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchEscalationPolicyEditor(value: List<MonarchEscalationLevel>, onValueChange: (List<MonarchEscalationLevel>) -> Unit, targets: List<MonarchEntityPickerEntity>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, timing: MonarchEscalationTiming = MonarchEscalationTiming.Cumulative, description: String? = null, defaultStepMinutes: Int = 15, minLevels: Int = 1, maxLevels: Int = 10, showErrors: Boolean = false, enabled: Boolean = true, createId: (() -> String)? = null, removeIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, addIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchEscalationPolicyEditorLabels = MonarchEscalationPolicyEditorLabels())

public data class MonarchEscalationLevel(id: String, afterMinutes: Int, targets: List<String> = emptyList()) { companion object { fun validate(levels: List<MonarchEscalationLevel>, timing: MonarchEscalationTiming = MonarchEscalationTiming.Cumulative): Map<String, MonarchEscalationLevelProblem> } }
public enum class MonarchEscalationTiming { Cumulative, Interval }
public enum class MonarchEscalationLevelProblem { Targets, Order }

public class MonarchEscalationPolicyEditorLabels(label: String? = null, level: ((position: Int) -> String)? = null, after: String? = null, notify: String? = null, summary: ((duration: String, names: String) -> String)? = null, nobody: String? = null, remove: String? = null, removeLevel: ((position: Int) -> String)? = null, add: String? = null, noTargets: String? = null, targetsProblem: String? = null, orderProblem: String? = null, maxReached: ((max: Int) -> String)? = null)

options.name: value
options.description: The levels, in order. Ids must be unique.

options.name: onValueChange
options.description: Called with the whole new list after every change.

options.name: targets
options.description: What a level can notify: channels, rotas or people, with an optional description such as the kind.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the editor.

options.name: timing
options.description: Cumulative measures every time from the start, so levels must get later; Interval measures each from the previous level.

options.name: description
options.description: Help under the levels.

options.name: defaultStepMinutes
options.description: The minutes a new level adds to the last one (cumulative), or its time (interval).

options.name: minLevels
options.description: The fewest levels; the remove buttons are disabled at this count.

options.name: maxLevels
options.description: The most levels; the add button is replaced by a note at this count.

options.name: showErrors
options.description: Shows the problems of each level, for example after a save attempt.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the policy can be changed.

options.name: createId
options.description: Makes the id of a new level; by default the first free level-<n>.

options.name: removeIcon
options.description: The icon of each remove button; without it the button reads Remove.

options.name: addIcon
options.description: An icon before the text of the add button.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

states.name: editing
states.description: Each level shows its heading, a summary such as After 15m, notify On-call rota, a remove button, the time field and the target picker.

states.name: no targets
states.description: A warning notice says there is nothing to notify yet.

states.name: invalid
states.description: With showErrors, a level that notifies nobody shows the problem on the picker, and a level not later than the one before shows it on the time field; the level takes the danger outline.

states.name: at the minimum
states.description: The remove buttons are disabled.

states.name: at the limit
states.description: The add button is replaced by A policy can have up to 10 levels.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Every field and button is disabled.

appearance: Each level is an outlined card on the surface color with a subtle border, or the danger border while it shows a problem. Headings are strong body text, summaries muted captions; the fields have the input border and the add button is a small secondary MonarchButton. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from the color roles.
platformNotes: Same data shape, defaults and checks as the web (validateEscalationPolicy is MonarchEscalationLevel.validate). Targets are MonarchEntityPickerEntity values chosen in a multiple-choice MonarchEntityPicker sheet, where the web lists a checkbox per target; the sheet searches and scales to long lists of people. Problems are shown as the error of the field concerned instead of a paragraph under the level, so TalkBack reads them with that field. The web's numbered marker beside each level is left out: the Level 1 heading carries the number. The web's messages prop is labels. There is no iOS entry yet.
accessibility: Each level heading (Level 1) is a heading, and each level is a traversal group with its summary, fields and remove button.
The list of levels is named Escalation levels.
Remove buttons are named with the position (Remove level 1) and are 48dp targets.
A problem is the error of the field concerned, read with it and announced when it appears; the danger outline is never the only signal.
The no-targets warning is a MonarchInlineNotice that says its tone.
edgeCases: Clearing the time field stores 1 minute, the minimum, as on the web.
Target ids that are not in targets keep their place at the end of the level and show the id in the summary.
Durations of a day or more show days in the summary, such as 1d 2h.
The editor does not scroll on its own: put it in a scrolling screen.

    description = {{description}},

)

)

name: MonarchEventChip
title: EventChip
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Box, androidx.compose.foundation.clickable, androidx.compose.material3.Text
summary: One event in a calendar view: a color dot or bar, the title, the time and the status, as a button that opens the event or as a label.
whenToUse: For an event in a month cell, an agenda row, an all-day row or a time grid, where tapping it opens the event.
whenNotToUse: For a list of events with more detail per row use a Material 3 ListItem. For a status alone use MonarchBadge.
api: @Composable fun MonarchEventChip(title: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchEventChipVariant = MonarchEventChipVariant.Dot, status: MonarchEventChipStatus = MonarchEventChipStatus.Confirmed, color: Color = Color.Unspecified, past: Boolean = false, compact: Boolean = false, enabled: Boolean = true, time: String? = null, timeLabel: String? = null, detail: String? = null, statusLabel: String? = null, onClick: (() -> Unit)? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)
enum class MonarchEventChipVariant { Dot, Bar, Block }
enum class MonarchEventChipStatus { Confirmed, Tentative, Cancelled, Declined }

options.name: title
options.description: The event title, already localised.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the component. Give a Block chip its size here.

options.name: variant
options.description: Dot, Bar or Block.

options.name: status
options.description: Confirmed, Tentative, Cancelled or Declined.

options.name: color
options.description: The event's color, for the marker, the border and the tint only. Unspecified is the theme's accent.

options.name: past
options.description: The event has ended: muted title and a faded marker.

options.name: compact
options.description: A Block chip on one line, time then title, without the status word and the detail.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether onClick can be triggered. The look does not change.

options.name: time
options.description: The visible time, already formatted. Leave it out for an all-day event in an all-day row.

options.name: timeLabel
options.description: The time as TalkBack reads it when time is abbreviated, such as "9:30 to 10:15" or "All day".

options.name: detail
options.description: A second, muted line in Bar and Block chips.

options.name: statusLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in name of the status (monarch_eventchip_tentative, _cancelled, _declined), in the visible word and in what TalkBack reads.

options.name: onClick
options.description: Opens the event. With it the chip is a button; without it a label.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the press and focus interactions.

states.name: confirmed
states.description: A filled dot or a solid bar; Bar and Block chips have a light tint of the event color (14% over the surface).

states.name: tentative
states.description: A hollow dot or a dashed bar, a lighter tint (6%) and a border in the event color. The status word is drawn in Bar and Block chips and read in all.

states.name: cancelled, declined
states.description: Muted text, the title struck through, the marker in the strong border color (a ring in a Dot chip) and the muted fill instead of the tint. The status word is drawn in Bar and Block chips and read in all.

states.name: past
states.description: Muted title and the marker mixed 45% towards the surface color.

states.name: pressed
states.description: With an action: a Dot chip gets the muted fill, a tinted chip a stronger tint (22%), a cancelled chip the emphasis fill. A ripple is drawn too.

states.name: disabled
states.description: enabled = false stops the action and TalkBack says it is disabled. The look does not change.

appearance: Text uses the default and muted text roles in every theme; the event color (or the accent) is only the marker, the border of a tentative chip and a tint mixed into the surface color. Cancelled and declined chips use the muted background and the strong border color. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes change the roles; the event color is the app's.
platformNotes: The same statuses, variants and compact density as the web and iOS. The web chip is always a button or a link; here, as on iOS, the action is optional, and a link is an onClick that opens the URL. The web's asChild is not needed. The web tints with color-mix; here the event color is mixed into the surface color with lerp at the same ratios, and the faded past marker is mixed towards the surface rather than drawn with opacity, because Monarch does not dim with alpha. With an action the chip reserves a 48dp touch target in the layout (the web uses 24px on touch screens, iOS 44pt), so chips stacked in a small month cell need that room.
accessibility: One TalkBack element whose content description is "title, time, status, detail". The status is left out when confirmed and the detail in a Dot chip; the texts inside are not read separately.
timeLabel replaces the visible time in what TalkBack reads.
With an action the element has the Button role and a touch target of at least 48dp reserved in the layout; the visible chip stays compact inside it.
The status is never color alone: a hollow or dashed marker, a struck-through title, and the status word.
The text grows with the font size setting. From font scale 1.3 the title of a Dot chip wraps instead of ending with an ellipsis.
The color bar is at the start edge and moves to the right edge in right-to-left layouts.
edgeCases: A Block chip fills the size it is given and clips what does not fit. A Block chip under 48dp high with an action cannot reserve its touch target; give it at least 48dp.
A long title in a Dot chip ends with an ellipsis at standard font sizes; TalkBack still reads all of it.
In a Bar chip the time and the status move under the title when they do not fit on one line.
past is not read; the time already says when the event was.
An empty title leaves the spoken name to the time and the status.

An agenda row that opens the event

examples.code:
MonarchEventChip(
    title = "Design review",
    variant = MonarchEventChipVariant.Bar,
    color = MonarchTheme.colors.successSolid,
    time = "14:00 – 15:00",
    timeLabel = "2 to 3 in the afternoon",
    detail = "Room 4",
    onClick = { open = true },
)

examples.title: A block in a time grid
examples.code:
MonarchEventChip(
    title = "Workshop",
    modifier = Modifier.height(96.dp),
    variant = MonarchEventChipVariant.Block,
    time = "10:00 – 12:00",
    detail = "Lab",
)

name: MonarchEventPopover
title: EventPopover
wrapsNative: Content for MonarchPopover (androidx.compose.ui.window.Popup) or androidx.compose.material3.ModalBottomSheet; android.icu.text.DateFormat for the times; MonarchDescriptionList for the details; MonarchBadge for the status; androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow for the actions
summary: The content of a quick view of a calendar event: color swatch, title, subtitle, status badge, date and time in a stated zone, labelled details, a note and actions.
whenToUse: When a person taps an event in a calendar, agenda or booking list and needs its time, place and people without leaving the screen.
whenNotToUse: For the event in a grid or list, use MonarchEventChip. For editing an event, open a full screen or a sheet with a form.
api: @Composable fun MonarchEventPopover(title: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, subtitle: String? = null, start: Long? = null, end: Long? = null, allDay: Boolean = false, color: Color = Color.Unspecified, status: MonarchEventChipStatus? = null, details: List<MonarchEventPopoverDetail> = emptyList(), note: String? = null, timeZone: String? = null, labels: MonarchEventPopoverLabels = MonarchEventPopoverLabels(), actions: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null)
class MonarchEventPopoverDetail(label: String, value: String, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null)
class MonarchEventPopoverLabels(time: String? = null, allDay: String? = null, status: ((MonarchEventChipStatus) -> String)? = null)

options.name: title
options.description: The event title, a heading.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the content.

options.name: subtitle
options.description: A second line under the title, such as the calendar or the service.

options.name: start
options.description: When the event starts, in epoch milliseconds (UTC); for an all-day event its first day as a UTC midnight. Without it there is no time row.

options.name: end
options.description: When the event ends; for an all-day event its last day, inclusive. An end before the start is ignored.

options.name: allDay
options.description: Shows the day or day range and "All day" instead of times.

options.name: color
options.description: The event's color for the swatch. Unspecified uses the accent role.

options.name: status
options.description: Confirmed, tentative, cancelled or declined, shown as a badge in the success, warning, neutral or danger tone.

options.name: details
options.description: Labelled rows under the time, shown as an inline MonarchDescriptionList. A row's icon is shown before its value.

options.name: note
options.description: A sentence on a subtle fill under the details, such as a cancellation reason.

options.name: timeZone
options.description: The zone the times are shown in, named after the times. An IANA id such as Europe/Berlin; null, or an id the device does not know, is the device's zone.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for "Time", "All day" and the status names (strings_eventpopover.xml).

options.name: actions
options.description: Buttons at the bottom, laid out in a wrapping row. The app dismisses the popover or sheet from them.

states.name: timed
states.description: "Sat, Nov 14, 2026" then "9:30 AM – 10:15 AM EST".

states.name: spans days
states.description: The start day and time on the first line, the end day, time and zone on the second.

states.name: all day
states.description: The day or "first – last" day range, then "All day".

states.name: confirmed, tentative, cancelled, declined
states.description: A badge with the status name in its tone; cancelled and declined titles are struck through.

states.name: no time
states.description: Without start the time row is left out.

appearance: A small round swatch in the event color or the accent role, the title as a subheading in default text, the subtitle and the times in muted text, the status as a subtle MonarchBadge, details as an inline description list with muted terms, and the note on the subtle background with the control corner radius. Inside MonarchPopover it sits on the raised surface with a shadow. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web EventPopover includes its own Popover and trigger. On Android, as on iOS, this is the content: put it in a MonarchPopover next to the MonarchEventChip that opens it, or in a ModalBottomSheet on a phone; they handle dismissal and focus return. The web's hourCycle option has no counterpart: Android follows the person's 12 or 24 hour setting through the locale's skeleton. Product-specific statuses (the web's custom status node) are not supported; pass labels.status to rename the built-in ones. Dates are epoch milliseconds, not ISO strings; the zone is an IANA id, as on the web. Detail rows always show their label; an icon is shown before the value rather than replacing the label as on the web and iOS, because the rows are a MonarchDescriptionList.
accessibility: The title is a heading; the swatch is decorative.
The status is a badge with its name in words, so it does not rely on color; cancelled and declined titles are also struck through.
The time row is one element read as "Time, Sat, Nov 14, 2026, 9:30 AM – 10:15 AM EST".
Each detail row is one element read as its label and value; detail icons are hidden.
Actions are separate buttons with 48dp targets that wrap onto more lines when they do not fit.
Text wraps at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: An end before the start is ignored and only the start is shown.
All-day dates are formatted in UTC so a UTC-midnight day does not move with the device zone.
ICU writes a narrow no-break space before AM and PM in recent locale data.
Without start there is no time row, for example for a task without a due time.

An all-day event with a note

MonarchEventPopover(
    title = "Team offsite",
    start = 1_794_614_400_000L,
    end = 1_794_700_800_000L,
    allDay = true,
    status = MonarchEventChipStatus.Cancelled,
    note = "Cancelled because of the rail strike.",
)

name: MonarchFacetedFilterPanel
title: FacetedFilterPanel
wrapsNative: MonarchCheckbox rows with androidx.compose.foundation.selection.toggleable, androidx.compose.material3.RangeSlider, MonarchButton, androidx.compose.animation.AnimatedVisibility; shown by the app in MonarchBottomSheet on a phone
summary: A panel of filter groups: checkboxes with match counts and minimum to maximum range sliders, each group collapsible and clearable, with a Clear all button.
whenToUse: To narrow a list of results by several properties at once: status, owner, size, date. On a phone open it in a MonarchBottomSheet from a Filters button.
whenNotToUse: For one or two quick filters, use a MonarchChip in a row above the results. For saved combinations of filters, use MonarchSavedViews. For a single choice, use MonarchSelect.
api: @Composable fun MonarchFacetedFilterPanel(facets: List<MonarchFacet>, value: Map<String, MonarchFacetSelection>, onValueChange: (Map<String, MonarchFacetSelection>) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, showTitle: Boolean = true, expandIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchFacetedFilterPanelLabels = MonarchFacetedFilterPanelLabels(), footer: (@Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)? = null)
class MonarchFacet(id: String, label: String, kind: MonarchFacetKind, initiallyExpanded: Boolean = true)
fun MonarchFacet.Companion.options(id: String, label: String, options: List<MonarchFacetOption>, maxVisible: Int = 6, initiallyExpanded: Boolean = true): MonarchFacet
fun MonarchFacet.Companion.range(id: String, label: String, bounds: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Float>, step: Float = 1f, unit: String? = null, initiallyExpanded: Boolean = true): MonarchFacet

sealed interface MonarchFacetKind { class Options(options: List<MonarchFacetOption>, maxVisible: Int = 6); class Range(bounds: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Float>, step: Float = 1f, unit: String? = null) }
class MonarchFacetOption(id: String, label: String, count: Int? = null, enabled: Boolean = true)
sealed interface MonarchFacetSelection { class Options(ids: Set<String>); class Range(range: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Float>) }

class MonarchFacetedFilterPanelLabels(title: String? = null, clearAll: String? = null, clearGroup: String? = null, clearGroupLabel: ((String) -> String)? = null, activeCount: ((Int) -> String)? = null, showMore: ((Int) -> String)? = null, showFewer: String? = null, noOptions: String? = null, range: ((String, String) -> String)? = null, expanded: String? = null, collapsed: String? = null)

options.name: facets
options.description: The groups in order: MonarchFacet.options with choices, their counts and how many show before Show more, or MonarchFacet.range with bounds, step and unit.

options.name: value
options.description: The active filters by facet id. A facet without a filter has no entry: no checked options, or a range equal to the bounds.

options.name: onValueChange
options.description: Called with the whole new value after every change.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the panel.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether filters can be changed and groups opened.

options.name: showTitle
options.description: Shows the Filters heading. Hide it inside a sheet whose title already says it; Clear all stays.

options.name: expandIcon
options.description: An icon at the start of each group header, such as a chevron pointing down; it turns half a turn while open. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the title, Clear all, Clear, the spoken group clear name, the active count, Show more, Show fewer, No options, the range text and the Expanded and Collapsed states.

options.name: footer
options.description: Content after the groups, such as a Show results button in a sheet.

states.name: no filters
states.description: Clear all is disabled; group headers show only their names.

states.name: active
states.description: A group with filters shows "2 selected" under its name in the strong accent color, and a Clear button beside its header.

states.name: collapsed
states.description: The group shows only its header; initiallyExpanded sets the first state, and opening and closing animates unless animations are off.

states.name: more options
states.description: Past maxVisible, a Show 1 more button reveals the rest and becomes Show fewer. Checked options stay visible.

states.name: empty facet
states.description: An options facet with no options shows "No options".

states.name: disabled
states.description: enabled = false gives every control its disabled colors and stops changes.

appearance: Headings and labels use the default text color, counts and the range text the muted text color, the active count the strong accent color, and groups are separated by subtle dividers. Checkboxes and the range slider are Material 3 controls in the theme's accent roles. Disabled text uses the disabled text role. All colors come from the theme, in every theme.
platformNotes: The web FacetedFilterPanel is a sidebar with typed minimum and maximum number inputs and an invalid state when the minimum is above the maximum. On Android a range is a Material 3 RangeSlider between known bounds, so it cannot be inverted and has no invalid state; a range facet needs bounds, and values are Float, as RangeSlider takes. On a phone the panel goes in a MonarchBottomSheet rather than a sidebar, and the web's heading levels are a single heading semantics. The web value is an object of arrays and min/max pairs; here it is a map of MonarchFacetSelection, as on iOS, which builds the same component with the same name (value with onValueChange instead of a selection binding, showTitle instead of showsTitle, enabled instead of isDisabled). Group headers are drawn here rather than with MonarchAccordion because they carry the active count and a Clear button. Option rows are Material 3 Checkboxes in toggleable rows instead of MonarchCheckboxGroup, so the count can sit at the end of the row. The chevron is a slot because Monarch bundles no icons. The web's accent color for the active count is the strong accent role directly, because MonarchTone has no accent tone.
accessibility: The title is a heading; without the title the panel is a traversal group named "Filters".
Each group header is one button with heading semantics that reads the group name and the active count ("Status, 2 selected"), with the state Expanded or Collapsed.
Each option is one checkbox element read with its label and its count in the locale's digits ("Done, 1,204"); a disabled option is read as disabled.
A group's clear button is named after the group ("Clear Status filter").
A range slider is named with the facet's label and its state is the range with its unit ("10 MB – 50 MB"); each thumb is a Material 3 slider thumb that TalkBack adjusts.
Checked options are never hidden behind Show more.
Headers, options and buttons have 48dp touch targets, and text wraps at the largest font size; right to left the rows mirror.
edgeCases: A value for a facet id that is not in facets is kept and passed back unchanged.
A step that gives more than 1,000 positions, or a step of 0, makes the slider continuous.
Clearing a group or reaching the bounds removes the facet's entry, so an empty value means no filters.
The panel does not scroll: put it in a verticalScroll inside the sheet.

name: MonarchFavicon
title: Favicon
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.Image (through Monarch's internal MonarchImage), androidx.compose.material3.Text
summary: A site's icon at a fixed size, with a tile showing the first letter of the site name while there is no image.
whenToUse: Beside a link, a domain or a connected service, so people recognise the site at a glance.
whenNotToUse: For a person or an organization use an avatar. For an icon that stands for an action use MonarchIcon.
api: @Composable fun MonarchFavicon(image: Painter?, name: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, label: String? = null, size: MonarchFaviconSize = MonarchFaviconSize.Sm, shape: MonarchFaviconShape = MonarchFaviconShape.Rounded)
enum class MonarchFaviconSize { Sm, Md, Lg }
enum class MonarchFaviconShape { Rounded, Circle, Square }

options.name: image
options.description: The icon loaded by the app, or null to show the letter tile.

options.name: name
options.description: The site's name or domain; its first letter or digit is shown on the tile.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the component.

options.name: label
options.description: What TalkBack reads. Without it the favicon is decoration and hidden.

options.name: size
options.description: Sm 16dp, Md 24dp, Lg 32dp.

options.name: shape
options.description: Rounded (4dp corners), Circle or Square.

states.name: image
states.description: The picture is fitted inside the tile and clipped to the shape.

states.name: fallback
states.description: A tile in the muted background color with a subtle border and one upper-case letter in the muted text color. Shown while loading, after a failure and when there is no icon.

appearance: The letter tile uses the muted background, the subtle border and the muted text color in every theme. The image is shown as it is.
platformNotes: The web Favicon takes a domain or URL, an optional resolveSrc function and a size in pixels, and checks that the URL is safe to load. Android follows the Monarch picture convention instead: the app loads the icon with its own pipeline and passes a Painter, so there is no URL to check and Monarch never calls a favicon service. iOS also offers a URL initialiser; Android does not, because Monarch ships no image loader. Sizes are the named Sm, Md and Lg, as on iOS. The tile keeps its size at every font size, as Android icons do; on iOS it scales with Dynamic Type.
accessibility: Without a label the favicon is hidden from TalkBack, because the site name is normally written next to it.
With a label it is one TalkBack element with the image role, read as the label.
Not interactive, so it has no touch target.
edgeCases: A name without a letter or digit shows "?".
The letter is upper-cased in the default locale, so "istanbul" gives a dotted capital I in Turkish.
A letter outside the Basic Multilingual Plane is kept whole.
The image is fitted, not cropped: an icon with another aspect ratio leaves space at the sides.

name: MonarchFavoritesList
title: FavoritesList
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.NavigationDrawerItem for the rows, with MonarchReorderableList (androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn) in edit mode and androidx.compose.ui.semantics.CustomAccessibilityAction for removal outside edit mode
summary: A navigation section of pinned destinations with a heading, the current destination marked, and an Edit button that turns on reorder and remove.
whenToUse: For the person's pinned projects, views or documents at the top of a navigation drawer or rail, where the app stores the favourites.
whenNotToUse: For the app's fixed destinations use NavigationDrawerItem or NavigationSuiteScaffold directly. To pin or unpin the current screen use a FilledTonalIconToggleButton with a star (ToggleButton), not this list.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchFavoritesList(items: List<MonarchFavoriteItem>, onSelect: (MonarchFavoriteItem) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, editing: Boolean? = null, onEditingChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, emptyMessage: String? = null, onRemove: ((MonarchFavoriteItem) -> Unit)? = null, onReorder: ((List<MonarchFavoriteItem>) -> Unit)? = null, headingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, removeIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchFavoritesListLabels = MonarchFavoritesListLabels())
public class MonarchFavoriteItem(title: String, id: String, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, current: Boolean = false)

public class MonarchFavoritesListLabels(title: String? = null, edit: String? = null, editLabel: String? = null, done: String? = null, remove: String? = null, removeLabel: ((title: String) -> String)? = null, removed: ((title: String) -> String)? = null, reorder: MonarchReorderableListLabels = MonarchReorderableListLabels())

options.name: items
options.description: The pinned destinations, in order. current marks the screen the person is on; items are equal when their ids are.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Opens a destination when its row is tapped outside edit mode.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the section.

options.name: editing
options.description: Edit mode controlled by the app. null lets the section keep it, starting off.

options.name: onEditingChange
options.description: Called when Edit or Done is tapped, and with false when the last item is removed.

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: Shown under the heading when there are no items. Without it the section draws nothing when empty.

options.name: onRemove
options.description: Removes an item. With it edit mode shows a remove button on each row, and each row offers a remove action to TalkBack.

options.name: onReorder
options.description: Receives the new order after a move. With it edit mode shows the rows as a MonarchReorderableList.

options.name: headingIcon
options.description: An icon before the heading, such as a star. Decorative.

options.name: removeIcon
options.description: Makes the remove buttons icon buttons. Without it they show Remove.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for Favorites, Edit, Edit favorites, Done, Remove, the remove name, the removal announcement and the reorderable list's strings.

states.name: browsing
states.description: Rows are NavigationDrawerItems with an optional icon and the name; the Edit button shows when onRemove or onReorder is given and there are items.

states.name: current
states.description: The current destination is selected, in semibold, in the strong accent text on the subtle accent fill.

states.name: editing
states.description: With onReorder the rows become a reorderable list with drag handles; with onRemove each row has a remove button; rows stop opening their destination; the button reads Done.

states.name: empty
states.description: With emptyMessage, the heading and the message in muted text; without it nothing is drawn.

appearance: The heading is in the label type and muted text. Rows are Material 3 navigation drawer items: transparent at rest in the default text color, the current one on the subtle accent fill in the strong accent text and semibold. The Edit, Done and Remove buttons are small ghost Monarch buttons. Every color is a theme role, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow the theme.
platformNotes: The web FavoritesList is a nav of links with an Edit button, a ReorderableList and remove buttons; iOS uses its List edit mode with the system delete control. Android has no list edit mode, so edit mode swaps the rows for MonarchReorderableList (long press and drag, or the handle's Move up and Move down actions) and adds remove buttons; outside edit mode removal is a TalkBack custom action rather than swipe to delete, which Material 3 navigation drawers do not use. Rows report onSelect instead of following an href. The iOS showsIcon flag is the headingIcon slot, because Monarch for Android bundles no star glyph. The web's FavoriteToggle is not a separate type: use FilledTonalIconToggleButton with a star icon (see ToggleButton). In edit mode the reorderable list is at most 384dp tall and scrolls inside itself, so the section can sit in a scrolling drawer sheet.
accessibility: The heading (icon and title) is one element with heading semantics; the icon is decorative.
Rows are Material 3 navigation drawer items named by the destination; the current one is selected and also semibold, so it is not shown by color alone.
The Edit button is named Edit favorites and is named Done while editing.
With onRemove each row has a TalkBack custom action, Remove Roadmap from favorites; in edit mode the remove buttons have the same name.
In edit mode with onReorder each row's handle is named Reorder and the title, with Move up and Move down actions, from MonarchReorderableList.
After a removal "Roadmap removed from favorites." is announced through a polite live region that stays in the tree.
Rows, the Edit button and the remove buttons have 48dp touch targets; names wrap at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: With neither onRemove nor onReorder there is no Edit button and no remove action.
Removing the last item ends edit mode (onEditingChange(false)); without emptyMessage the section then draws nothing.
Long names wrap; the Edit button stays at the end of the heading.
The section is a Column, not a lazy list: it is meant for a handful of favourites in a drawer. In edit mode with many items the reorderable list scrolls inside its 384dp.

name: MonarchFieldRenderer
title: FieldRenderer
wrapsNative: A when over MonarchFormFieldType to MonarchFormField with MonarchTextField, MonarchNumberInput, MonarchSelect, MonarchRadioRow, MonarchRatingPicker and MonarchFileUpload; MonarchMultiSelect, MonarchCheckboxGroup and MonarchCheckboxRow; androidx.compose.material3.DatePickerDialog and androidx.compose.material3.TimePickerDialog for dates and times
summary: Renders one form question from data: the right Monarch input for its type, with the label, help, required mark, error and an optional “filled in automatically” note.
whenToUse: Questions are authored by admins and stored as data, or a form shows answers that were filled in automatically and people must check them.
whenNotToUse: When the form is fixed in code, compose MonarchFormField, MonarchTextField and the other inputs directly.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchFieldRenderer(field: MonarchFormFieldDefinition, value: MonarchFormFieldValue?, onValueChange: (MonarchFormFieldValue?) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, problem: MonarchFormFieldProblem? = null, errorText: String? = null, confidence: Float? = null, confidenceThreshold: Float = 0.6f, labels: MonarchFieldRendererLabels = MonarchFieldRendererLabels())

public class MonarchFormFieldDefinition(id: String, type: MonarchFormFieldType, label: String, description: String? = null, placeholder: String? = null, required: Boolean = false, options: List<MonarchFormFieldOption> = emptyList(), minLength: Int? = null, maxLength: Int? = null, min: Double? = null, max: Double? = null, minDate: Long? = null, maxDate: Long? = null, minSelections: Int? = null, maxSelections: Int? = null, accept: List<String> = emptyList(), maxFileSize: Long? = null, maxFiles: Int = 1, consentText: String? = null, conditions: List<MonarchCondition> = emptyList(), conditionMatch: MonarchConditionMatch = MonarchConditionMatch.All, readOnly: Boolean = false) { fun problem(value: MonarchFormFieldValue?): MonarchFormFieldProblem?; fun isVisible(values: Map<String, MonarchFormFieldValue?>): Boolean }
public enum class MonarchFormFieldType { ShortText, LongText, Email, Phone, Url, Number, Date, Time, Select, MultiSelect, Radio, Checkboxes, YesNo, Consent, Rating, File, Section }

public sealed interface MonarchFormFieldValue { val isEmpty: Boolean; val raw: Any; data class Text(text: String); data class Number(number: Double); data class Date(millis: Long); data class Flag(checked: Boolean); data class Values(values: List<String>); data class Files(files: List<MonarchFormFieldFile>) }

public sealed interface MonarchFormFieldProblem { data object Required; data object MustAgree; data object Email; data object Url; data object NotANumber; data class Min(min: Double); data class Max(max: Double); data class MinLength(min: Int); data class MaxLength(max: Int); data class MinSelections(min: Int); data class MaxSelections(max: Int) }
public data class MonarchFormFieldOption(value: String, label: String)
public data class MonarchFormFieldFile(name: String, size: Long? = null, file: MonarchPickedFile? = null)

public class MonarchFieldRendererLabels(required: String? = null, mustAgree: String? = null, email: String? = null, url: String? = null, number: String? = null, min: ((min: String) -> String)? = null, max: ((max: String) -> String)? = null, minLength: ((min: Int) -> String)? = null, maxLength: ((max: Int) -> String)? = null, minSelections: ((min: Int) -> String)? = null, maxSelections: ((max: Int) -> String)? = null, yes: String? = null, no: String? = null, choose: String? = null, chooseDate: String? = null, chooseTime: String? = null, confirm: String? = null, cancel: String? = null, aiFilled: String? = null, aiCheck: String? = null, remove: String? = null, removeFile: ((name: String) -> String)? = null)

options.name: field
options.description: The question: its type, label, help, required flag, options, limits, conditions and read-only flag.

options.name: value
options.description: The current answer, or null for none.

options.name: onValueChange
options.description: Called with the new answer; null when it is cleared.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the question.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the answer can be changed.

options.name: problem
options.description: A problem from MonarchFormFieldDefinition.problem, shown as the error with its built-in message.

options.name: errorText
options.description: An error message, such as a server error; replaces the message of problem.

options.name: confidence
options.description: The confidence, from 0 to 1, of an answer filled in automatically; shows a note under the question.

options.name: confidenceThreshold
options.description: The confidence under which the note asks people to check the answer.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings and messages.

states.name: empty
states.description: The input shows its placeholder, Choose…, Choose a date or Choose a time.

states.name: answered
states.description: The input shows the answer: text, the chosen option, a date such as Nov 14, 2026, a time, a rating or the chosen files.

states.name: error
states.description: The message shows under the question in the danger color and is the error of the input for TalkBack.

states.name: filled in automatically
states.description: With confidence, a note says the answer was filled in; below the threshold it asks for a check in the warning color.

states.name: read-only
states.description: Text questions keep a readable, read-only input; other questions are disabled.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Every input is disabled.

states.name: section
states.description: A heading with an optional description and no input.

appearance: Every question uses the look of the Monarch input it renders: outlined fields with the input border, radio and checkbox rows, buttons for date and time. Errors use the danger text color, the automatic-fill note the AI text color or, when unsure, the warning text color; section descriptions use the muted text color. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from the color roles.
platformNotes: Same question types, checks, order of checks and default messages as the web (validateFormField is MonarchFormFieldDefinition.problem, which returns a typed problem; the renderer turns it into the message, and errorText replaces it). Differences: a date answer is UTC epoch milliseconds, as the Material 3 DatePickerState gives it, where the web stores YYYY-MM-DD; a time stays HH:MM. Dates and times are buttons that open the Material 3 DatePickerDialog and TimePickerDialog instead of typed inputs. File limits are MIME types and bytes (accept, maxFileSize) as in MonarchFileUpload, where the web takes an accept string and megabytes. A rating uses the numbered scale of MonarchRatingPicker because Monarch bundles no star glyph. The rows of a long-text question are not applied: MonarchTextField grows with its text. A consent shows no visible required mark; its error explains it. headingLevel and locale are not parameters: TalkBack has no heading levels, and the locale comes from the configuration. The AI note is text without the web's assistant glyph. There is no iOS entry yet.
accessibility: Inputs without a label of their own sit in a MonarchFormField, so TalkBack reads the label, Required and the error on the input, and a new error is announced through a polite live region.
Multi-select and checkboxes questions use the labels, required marks and errors of MonarchMultiSelect and MonarchCheckboxGroup.
Radio and yes-or-no options are selectable 48dp rows in a selectable group; a consent is one checkbox row with its statement as the name.
A consent error is text under the row, announced through a polite live region, and is set as the error of the row.
A section is a heading.
Each chosen file has a 48dp remove button named Remove followed by the file name.
The automatic-fill note is text, not only color.
edgeCases: Text is cut at maxLength while typing; problem also reports a stored answer that is too long.
Spaces alone are no answer, and length checks ignore spaces at either end, as on the web.
A yes-or-no question with an answer that is not a Flag counts as unanswered.
Use isVisible to leave out questions whose conditions do not hold; the renderer does not hide itself.
A time answer that is not HH:MM shows Choose a time.

name: MonarchFileCard
title: FileCard
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.Surface, MonarchCheckbox, MonarchFileTypeIcon, MonarchBadge
summary: One file as a card or a row: a picture or the type icon, the name, the type and size, optional badges, an optional selection checkbox and an optional place for actions.
whenToUse: In a grid or list of files where people open, select and act on files: documents, attachments, uploads that have finished.
whenNotToUse: For a file attached to a message or form, use MonarchAttachmentChip. For uploads in progress, use MonarchUploadQueue. To show the file's contents, use MonarchFilePreview.
api: @Composable fun MonarchFileCard(name: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, sizeBytes: Long? = null, contentType: String? = null, meta: String? = null, image: Painter? = null, badges: List<String> = emptyList(), layout: MonarchFileCardLayout = MonarchFileCardLayout.Card, selected: Boolean = false, onSelectedChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, enabled: Boolean = true, onOpen: (() -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchFileCardLabels = MonarchFileCardLabels(), interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null, actions: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null)
enum class MonarchFileCardLayout { Card, Row }
class MonarchFileCardLabels(select: ((name: String) -> String)? = null, type: String? = null)

options.name: name
options.description: The file name with its extension. Two lines in a card, cut at the end; one line in a row, cut in the middle so the extension stays visible.

options.name: sizeBytes
options.description: The size in bytes, shown in the locale's file units with Formatter.formatShortFileSize, such as "2.4 MB".

options.name: contentType
options.description: The MIME type. With the name it decides the type icon and the type in the meta line.

options.name: meta
options.description: More text after the size, already localised, such as "Edited yesterday" or an owner.

options.name: image
options.description: A preview the app has loaded. While it is null (none, loading or failed) the type icon is shown on a tinted tile.

options.name: badges
options.description: Short states shown as neutral MonarchBadges under the name, such as "Shared".

options.name: layout
options.description: Card: a 4:3 preview above the name, for grids. Row: a 40dp preview beside the name, for lists.

options.name: selected
options.description: Whether the file is selected. Shown only with onSelectedChange.

options.name: onSelectedChange
options.description: Shows a selection checkbox: at the top start corner of a card, at the start of a row.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the file can be opened and selected. The app disables its own actions.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Opens the file. Makes the picture, name and meta one button with a pressed state.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the checkbox's TalkBack name and the type in the meta line.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the press and focus interactions of the open area.

options.name: actions
options.description: The file's actions, such as a MonarchIconButton that opens a MonarchMenu, at the top end corner of a card or the end of a row.

states.name: rest
states.description: The surface background with a subtle border.

states.name: pressed
states.description: With onOpen: the subtle background and the default border, with a ripple.

states.name: selected
states.description: The checkbox is ticked; the card has the accent subtle background and a 2dp accent border.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The subtle background, disabled text colors, and the open area and checkbox cannot be used.

states.name: no picture or failed picture
states.description: The file type icon on a subtle tile.

appearance: A Surface in the surface background role with a subtle border and the large radius (medium in a row). The name is strong body text, the meta line muted caption text, the placeholder the subtle background with the file type icon's muted tile. Selected uses the accent subtle and accent border roles. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web's href becomes onOpen: the app opens the file itself, for example with an ACTION_VIEW intent. The web's actions slot stays a slot, because Monarch bundles no icons for a menu trigger; iOS draws an ellipsis Menu from its menu items instead. The web reports Shift for range selection; Android has no Shift-click on touch, so range selection belongs to the app. Badges are strings shown as neutral MonarchBadges instead of free content. The size parameter is sizeBytes, as in MonarchAttachmentChip, because size names the size option of other components. The picture is a Painter the app loads (Monarch adds no image loader), where iOS takes an Image or a URL; iOS isSelected as a binding is selected with onSelectedChange.
accessibility: The picture, name, meta line and badges are one merged element that reads the name, then the type, size, meta and badges; with onOpen it is a button.
The checkbox is a MonarchCheckbox named "Select" and the file name, read with its checked state, with a 48dp touch target.
The actions are separate elements; name an icon-only trigger after the file ("Actions for Q3 report.pdf").
Selection is shown by the check mark and a thicker border as well as color.
The picture and the type icon are hidden from TalkBack, because the meta line already says the type.
edgeCases: Long names take two lines in a card and are cut at the end; in a row they take one line and are cut in the middle.
A picture that fails to load is passed as null and shows the type icon; it is not an error state.
Without onOpen the card is not a button but is still one element for TalkBack.
A blank meta is left out of the meta line.

name: MonarchFileList
title: FileList
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.grid.LazyVerticalGrid, androidx.compose.material3.TriStateCheckbox, MonarchFileCard, MonarchBulkActionBar, MonarchEmptyState
summary: A list or grid of files with optional selection, a place for each file's actions, a bar of actions for the selected files and an empty state.
whenToUse: To show the files of a project, a folder or a record, where people open, select and act on several files at once.
whenNotToUse: For one file, use MonarchFileCard. For files being uploaded, use the upload queue. For a folder hierarchy, use MonarchTreeView.
api: @Composable fun MonarchFileList(items: List<MonarchFileListItem>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, layout: MonarchFileListLayout = MonarchFileListLayout.List, selected: Set<String> = emptySet(), onSelectedChange: ((Set<String>) -> Unit)? = null, onOpen: ((MonarchFileListItem) -> Unit)? = null, label: String? = null, bulkActions: List<MonarchBulkAction> = emptyList(), state: LazyGridState = rememberLazyGridState(), labels: MonarchFileListLabels = MonarchFileListLabels(), empty: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, actions: (@Composable (MonarchFileListItem) -> Unit)? = null)

class MonarchFileListItem(id: String, name: String, sizeBytes: Long? = null, contentType: String? = null, meta: String? = null, image: Painter? = null, badges: List<String> = emptyList(), enabled: Boolean = true)
enum class MonarchFileListLayout { List, Grid }

class MonarchFileListLabels(selectAll: String? = null, empty: String? = null, card: MonarchFileCardLabels = MonarchFileCardLabels(), bulkActionBar: MonarchBulkActionBarLabels = MonarchBulkActionBarLabels())

options.name: items
options.description: The files in display order: id, name, size, MIME type, meta, image, badges and enabled.

options.name: layout
options.description: List: one row per file. Grid: cards with previews in adaptive columns at least 160dp wide, wider at larger font scales.

options.name: selected
options.description: The ids of the selected files. Shown only with onSelectedChange.

options.name: onSelectedChange
options.description: Makes the files selectable: a checkbox on each file, "Select all files" and the bulk action bar. Receives the new set of ids.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Opens a file, for example in a preview. Makes each enabled file a button.

options.name: label
options.description: The TalkBack name of the files, such as "Project files".

options.name: bulkActions
options.description: Actions for the selection (Download, Move, Delete), shown in MonarchBulkActionBar while any file is selected.

options.name: state
options.description: The scroll state of the files.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for "Select all files", the empty title, and the strings of the cards and the bar.

options.name: empty
options.description: Replaces the built-in empty state when there are no files, for example with an upload action.

options.name: actions
options.description: Each file's actions, such as a button that opens a DropdownMenu, at the end of a row or the top end of a card.

states.name: read only
states.description: Without onSelectedChange: the files only, as rows or cards.

states.name: selectable
states.description: Each file has a checkbox and "Select all files" heads the list.

states.name: some selected
states.description: Select all is mixed and the bulk action bar shows the count, the actions and Clear selection.

states.name: all selected
states.description: Select all is checked; pressing it clears the selection.

states.name: file disabled
states.description: The file cannot be opened or selected and is left out of select all.

states.name: empty
states.description: MonarchEmptyState with "No files yet", or the app's empty content.

appearance: Rows and cards are MonarchFileCards on the surface role with a subtle border; a selected file has the subtle accent fill and a thicker accent border. The select all row uses the Material 3 checkbox in Monarch's accent colors and the bulk bar MonarchBulkActionBar's raised surface. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The parity map named LazyColumn or LazyVerticalGrid: both layouts are one LazyVerticalGrid (one fixed column for rows, adaptive columns for cards), so the list scrolls itself and needs a bounded height; it cannot sit inside a verticalScroll. iOS stacks the cards in the app's scroll view instead. The web shows "3 files selected" beside select all; on Android, as on iOS, the count, the actions and Clear selection are MonarchBulkActionBar, which also announces each change. The web's renderActions and bulkActions slots are an actions slot per file and MonarchBulkAction values. Shift-click ranges have no touch equivalent and are not offered. Escape clears the selection with a hardware keyboard. Selection is hoisted as selected and onSelectedChange, as in Compose, where iOS takes a Binding. The web's uncontrolled defaultSelectedIds and its links (href) are not offered: the app owns the selection and opens files in onOpen.
accessibility: Select all is one TalkBack element with the checkbox role and a checked, mixed or unchecked state; it is disabled when no file can be selected.
Each file's checkbox is named "Select <file name>" and announced as checked or not checked; a disabled file's checkbox is disabled.
The picture, name and meta of a file are one element, a button when onOpen is set (MonarchFileCard).
The bulk action bar announces the count when it changes and "Selection cleared" when it empties.
The files carry the label as their TalkBack name and the lazy grid's collection information.
Every control has a 48dp touch target; names wrap at the largest font scale and grid columns widen with it.
edgeCases: Ids in selected that are no longer in items are not counted; clear them in the app when files are deleted.
With only disabled files, select all is disabled.
Pressing select all while it is mixed selects every enabled file.
Long file names wrap in rows and cards.

name: MonarchFilePreview
title: FilePreview
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.Image; android.graphics.pdf.PdfRenderer in a androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn; androidx.compose.foundation.text.selection.SelectionContainer with verticalScroll; a player slot for androidx.media3.ui.PlayerView
summary: Shows a file's content in place (a picture, the pages of a PDF, text, or the app's video or audio player) and falls back to the type icon, the name and a download action.
whenToUse: In an attachment detail, a document library or a chat, to show a file without leaving the screen.
whenNotToUse: To open a file in the app the user chooses, start an ACTION_VIEW intent. For a small icon of the file type use MonarchFileTypeIcon; for a video poster use MonarchVideoThumbnail.
api: @Composable fun MonarchFilePreview(name: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, contentType: String? = null, kind: MonarchFilePreviewKind? = null, image: Painter? = null, text: String? = null, pdf: Uri? = null, onDownload: (() -> Unit)? = null, failed: Boolean = false, alwaysShowDownload: Boolean = false, imageDescription: String? = null, labels: MonarchFilePreviewLabels = MonarchFilePreviewLabels(), player: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, fallback: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null)
enum class MonarchFilePreviewKind { Image, Pdf, Text, Video, Audio, None }
fun MonarchFilePreviewKind.Companion.of(fileName: String?, contentType: String? = null): MonarchFilePreviewKind

class MonarchFilePreviewLabels(previewOf: ((name: String) -> String)? = null, unavailable: String? = null, failed: String? = null, download: String? = null, downloadName: ((name: String) -> String)? = null, page: ((number: Int, count: Int) -> String)? = null)

options.name: name
options.description: The file name, for the kind, the labels and the fallback.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the preview. It fills the width it is given.

options.name: contentType
options.description: The MIME type. Decides the kind with the name.

options.name: kind
options.description: Forces a kind instead of detecting it. None shows the fallback.

options.name: image
options.description: The picture of an image file, loaded by the app.

options.name: text
options.description: The content of a text or code file.

options.name: pdf
options.description: A file: or content: URI of a PDF the app can read.

options.name: onDownload
options.description: Shows a Download button; the app saves or opens the file.

options.name: failed
options.description: Loading the content failed; the fallback says so.

options.name: alwaysShowDownload
options.description: Shows Download under every preview, not only in the fallback.

options.name: imageDescription
options.description: What the picture shows. null uses the file name; an empty string hides the picture from TalkBack.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings (strings_filepreview.xml).

options.name: player
options.description: The app's video or audio player, for example a Media3 PlayerView in an AndroidView.

options.name: fallback
options.description: Replaces the default fallback.

states.name: image
states.description: The picture, fitted to the width, at most 70% of the window height.

states.name: pdf
states.description: The pages, rendered at the width of the preview as they scroll into view, in a column at most 70% of the window height; a surface-coloured placeholder while a page renders.

states.name: text
states.description: The text in the code style on the surface color, selectable, scrolling inside at most 70% of the window height.

states.name: video or audio
states.description: The app's player; video sits on the inverse background.

states.name: no preview
states.description: The type icon, the name, "There is no preview for this file type." and the Download button.

states.name: waiting
states.description: For a kind that has a preview but whose content was not given yet: the icon and the name without a message.

states.name: failed
states.description: With failed, or a PDF that cannot be opened: "The preview could not be loaded.".

appearance: A bordered block with 12dp corners on the subtle background, with a 1dp default border. Text, PDF pages and the download footer sit on the surface color; the footer has a subtle line above it. The fallback is centered, with the name in the strong body style and the message in muted text. PDF pages are drawn on white in every theme, because a page is paper.
platformNotes: Android has no single preview view, so each kind has its own renderer, as the plan says; iOS presents Quick Look instead and ships nothing. The web loads every kind from a URL; Monarch for Android adds no networking or image loading, so a picture is a Painter the app loaded, text is a String, a PDF is a local file: or content: URI read with PdfRenderer, and video and audio are a slot for the app's player because Monarch does not depend on Media3 (androidx.media3 is not in the version catalog). The web's captions track belongs to that player. The download link is a callback: the app saves the file with CreateDocument or opens it with an intent. PDF pages are rendered only for the PDF kind; there is no search or zoom.
accessibility: The preview is a traversal group. A picture is named by imageDescription or the file name; an empty imageDescription hides it.
Text, PDF and player content are named "Preview of <name>"; each PDF page is an image named "Page 1 of 3".
The text is selectable and scrolls inside the preview.
The fallback reads the type ("Archive"), the name and the message; the Download button is named "Download <name>" and has a 48dp target.
Text wraps and grows with the font size setting.
edgeCases: An image file without a painter shows the fallback without a message until the painter arrives.
A PDF URI that cannot be opened or is not a PDF shows the failed message.
A PDF is rendered at the current width; rotating the device renders the pages again.
A video or audio file without a player shows the fallback.
kind = MonarchFilePreviewKind.None always shows the fallback.
