name: MonarchFileTypeIcon
title: FileTypeIcon
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.Canvas, androidx.compose.ui.graphics.vector.PathParser, android.webkit.MimeTypeMap
summary: A glyph for the family of a file (image, PDF, spreadsheet, archive and so on), worked out from its name and MIME type, with a spoken name.
whenToUse: Next to a file name in an attachment row, an upload list or a file card, so the type can be seen at a glance.
whenNotToUse: For a picture of the file itself use the image or MonarchFilePreview. For an icon that is not a file type use MonarchIcon with the app's own vector.
api: @Composable fun MonarchFileTypeIcon(fileName: String?, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, contentType: String? = null, size: MonarchFileTypeIconSize = MonarchFileTypeIconSize.Md, decorative: Boolean = false, label: String? = null)

@Composable fun MonarchFileTypeIcon(family: MonarchFileTypeFamily, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, size: MonarchFileTypeIconSize = MonarchFileTypeIconSize.Md, decorative: Boolean = false, label: String? = null)
enum class MonarchFileTypeFamily { Image, Video, Audio, Pdf, Document, Spreadsheet, Presentation, Archive, Code, Text, Other }
fun MonarchFileTypeFamily.Companion.of(fileName: String?, contentType: String? = null): MonarchFileTypeFamily
enum class MonarchFileTypeIconSize { Sm, Md, Lg }

options.name: fileName
options.description: The file name or path; its extension decides the family when the MIME type does not. First overload.

options.name: family
options.description: The family to draw, when it is already known. Second overload.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the icon.

options.name: contentType
options.description: The MIME type. A specific type takes precedence over the extension; application/octet-stream does not.

options.name: size
options.description: Sm is a 16dp glyph, Md 20dp, Lg a 24dp glyph on a 40dp tile.

options.name: decorative
options.description: Hides the icon from TalkBack when nearby text already says the type.

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken name of the family (strings_filetypeicon.xml).

states.name: default
states.description: One image element named after the family.

states.name: decorative
states.description: Hidden from TalkBack; nothing changes visually.

appearance: A stroked page outline with a folded corner and a mark for the family. Images and video use the first data color, documents and text the second, spreadsheets and code the third, audio and slides the fourth, PDF the fifth, archives and other files the muted text color. The large size sits on a muted tile with 8dp corners. The data colors have their own values in the dark and high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Android draws the web's glyph (one page outline with a mark inside); iOS uses a separate SF Symbol per family. The extension and MIME tables are the web's, so a file gets the same family on every platform; an extension the tables do not list is looked up with android.webkit.MimeTypeMap, as iOS does with UTType. The large size is a 24dp glyph on a 40dp tile, as on iOS (the web draws 28 on 40). The glyph has a fixed size and does not grow with the font size setting, like other Android icons. The web's FileTypeGlyph is not a separate type: pass decorative = true.
accessibility: The icon is one element with the image role and the family name as its content description, for example "PDF document".
label replaces the built-in name; decorative = true removes the icon from TalkBack.
Every family has a different mark, so the type does not depend on the tint.
It is not interactive and has no touch target.
edgeCases: A MIME type with parameters ("application/json; charset=utf-8") is read without them, and case does not matter.
A file name that starts with a dot and has no other dot (".gitignore") has no extension and is Other.
Only the last extension counts: "backup.tar.gz" is an archive because of gz.
A path with / or \ is accepted; only the last part is read.

appearance: Zone: a subtle background with the default border and the large container radius, the muted fill when disabled and the danger border when invalid or after a refusal; the label in strong body text, the hint in muted caption text, a small secondary button. Compact: the button and the hint on one line. Refusals are a plain danger MonarchInlineNotice. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web drop zone also accepts dragged and pasted files; on Android files come from the system pickers only (drag and drop from other apps on tablets and ChromeOS is not supported yet). The web takes File objects; Android hands over MonarchPickedFile with the content URI, display name, MIME type and size read from the provider, and never reads the content. accept is a list instead of a comma-separated string. The web capture attribute has no equivalent: for a camera capture use ActivityResultContracts.TakePicture. The web reads the label and error from a surrounding Field; on Android pass invalid and errorText. iOS has no entry yet; the names follow the web.
accessibility: Browse files is a MonarchButton with a 48dp touch target; it is disabled while the component is disabled or full.
"2 files added." is announced through a polite live region after files are accepted.
Refusals are shown as text in a MonarchInlineNotice announced politely, and the first refusal (or errorText while invalid) is the button's error.
The icon is hidden from TalkBack; the label and the hint are read as text.
Texts wrap at the largest font size; the button follows the text in the layout direction.
edgeCases: Files over maxFiles are refused in order after the other checks, so the first valid files are kept.
With multiple false, only the first file a picker returns is checked; any others are refused as too many.
An extension in accept that the system cannot map to a MIME type opens the document picker unfiltered; the check still refuses other files.
The read permission of a picked URI lasts while the app's task lives; take a persistable permission to keep it.
The name and size are read on the main thread when the picker returns; this is a provider query, not a read of the content.

whenToUse: Above a list or table with filters applied, so people can see, change and remove them, and for one-tap quick filters such as Assigned to me.
whenNotToUse: For switching between exclusive views use tabs or a segmented button; for tags on a record use MonarchBadge or MonarchTag; for a few sort options use a MonarchMenu.

appearance: Material 3 chips in Monarch colors: outlined when off, filled when a quick filter is on; removable chips with the app's close glyph; the result count as body text. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web FilterBar is a wrapping toolbar with MonarchChip (removable, editable in a popover, or a toggle with a count), a FilterMenu (Add filter), Clear all, a result count, trailing controls, URL helpers and an optional collapse into a sheet below a width. On a phone the native pattern is a single sideways-scrolling chip row under the search field, with the full filter set in a bottom sheet, so this recipe uses Material 3 chips and MonarchFacetedFilterPanel in a MonarchBottomSheet instead of popovers per chip; Add filter becomes the Filters chip. Search parameters in the URL have no counterpart: keep the filters in the screen's state or ViewModel. iOS has no entry yet; its plan is also a recipe.
accessibility: The Filters chip is a button whose name carries the count, "Filters (2)".
Quick filters are filter chips that report selected.
Each removable chip's remove target is named, "Remove Status: Open", and has a 48dp target from MonarchTag.
The result count is a polite live region, so a change is announced.
The sheet is a modal pane; back and the scrim close it.
edgeCases: Keep the chip row on one line with horizontalScroll; at font scale 2.0 people scroll it.
Clear the applied chips when Clear all is pressed, and close the sheet with Show results.
MonarchFacetedFilterPanel is not lazy: in the sheet put it in a verticalScroll Column.

title: FocusTrap

summary: Keeping focus inside a modal surface is done by the platform's modal windows: Dialog, MonarchDialog, MonarchBottomSheet and a focusable Popup each open a window that holds TalkBack and keyboard focus. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: For any surface that must be finished or dismissed before the rest of the screen can be used: a confirmation, a form in a dialog, a sheet of options.
whenNotToUse: For content that may be used alongside the screen, such as a side panel or a non-modal tooltip, use a non-modal container and let focus move freely.

states.name: dismissed
states.description: Back, a tap on the scrim or a button calls onDismissRequest; the app removes the window and focus returns to the screen.

appearance: No appearance of its own: dialogs and sheets take the Monarch colors through MonarchTheme's Material 3 mapping, in light, dark and high contrast.
platformNotes: The web needs a FocusTrap component and hook because a browser lets Tab leave a dialog. On Android a Dialog, MonarchBottomSheet or focusable Popup is a separate window, so TalkBack and the keyboard stay inside it. The web's initialFocus is a FocusRequester with requestFocus() in a LaunchedEffect inside the window; returnFocus is the system's; onEscape is onDismissRequest, which Back and Escape trigger. iOS uses sheet and fullScreenCover in the same way.
accessibility: System behavior: a dialog or modal sheet is a separate window; TalkBack and keyboard focus stay inside it until it is dismissed.
System behavior: Back, and Escape on a hardware keyboard, call onDismissRequest unless the properties turn that off.
A Popup only takes focus with PopupProperties(focusable = true); a non-focusable popup does not confine focus.
Give a dialog a title so TalkBack announces it when it opens.
edgeCases: MonarchDialog(dismissible = false), or DialogProperties(dismissOnBackPress = false) on a Dialog, keeps a dialog with unsaved changes open; keep a visible button that dismisses it.
A custom overlay drawn inside the screen (a Box over the content) does not confine focus; use Dialog or Popup instead.
The catalogue page opens the dialog and the sheet only on a tap; the compiled example shows the dialog closed until a button is pressed.

name: MonarchForceGraph
title: ForceGraph
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.Canvas with androidx.compose.ui.text.drawText, androidx.compose.foundation.gestures.detectTapGestures, awaitEachGesture with calculateZoom and calculatePan, inside MonarchChartFrame; a built-in force layout
summary: A network of linked nodes placed by a small built-in force layout, with groups in data colors, link kinds, drag, pan and zoom.
whenToUse: To show how a few dozen items connect, such as linked notes, service dependencies or people and teams, where the shape of the network matters.
whenNotToUse: For a hierarchy, use MonarchTreeView or an outline. For exact links of many items, use a list; the table of this graph is the same data as text.
api: @Composable fun MonarchForceGraph(title: String, nodes: List<MonarchForceGraphNode>, edges: List<MonarchForceGraphEdge>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, groups: List<MonarchForceGraphGroup>? = null, edgeKinds: List<MonarchForceGraphEdgeKind> = emptyList(), description: String? = null, status: MonarchChartFrameStatus = MonarchChartFrameStatus.Ready, height: Dp = 420.dp, showLabels: Boolean = true, selectedId: String? = null, summary: String? = null, emptyMessage: String? = null, footer: String? = null, layoutOptions: MonarchForceGraphLayoutOptions = MonarchForceGraphLayoutOptions(), onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null, onSelect: ((MonarchForceGraphNode) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchForceGraphLabels = MonarchForceGraphLabels())

options.description: Ready, Loading, Empty or Error. A ready chart without nodes shows the empty state.

options.description: The height of the canvas. The zoom buttons, the details and the link legend are added around it.

options.name: showLabels
options.description: Draws each node's label under it.

options.description: The id of a node drawn with an accent ring and marked selected for TalkBack, such as the open document.

options.description: Replaces the generated summary that TalkBack reads for the graph.

options.description: The message of the empty state.

options.description: Link distance, repulsion, collision, gravity and steps of the layout.

options.name: onRetry

options.description: Runs with a node when it is tapped or activated with TalkBack, for example to open it.

states.name: ready
states.description: Nodes as dots in their group's color with labels, links as lines in their kind's color and dash, on the subtle background, with Zoom in, Zoom out and Reset view above.

states.name: inspected node
states.description: After a tap, the node has a default-text ring, its links are thicker, other nodes, labels and links turn to the disabled and subtle colors, and its group, links and description are written under the canvas and announced politely.

states.name: selected node
states.description: selectedId draws an accent ring and marks the node selected for TalkBack.

states.name: orphan node
states.description: A node without links is a dashed outline on the surface color.

states.name: moved, panned, zoomed
states.description: Dragging moves a node or pans; pinching or the buttons zoom between 0.35 and 3 times; Reset view undoes all three. Zoom buttons are disabled at the limits.

states.name: table
states.description: View as table lists every node by label with its group and its links.

states.name: empty
states.description: The frame's empty state, also when the chart is ready but has no nodes.

states.name: loading
states.description: The frame's skeleton at the canvas height.

states.name: error
states.description: The frame's error message, with Try again when onRetry is given.

appearance: Nodes use the data colors by group (the sixth group and later, ungrouped and unlinked nodes are neutral) with a surface-coloured outline; links use the kind's color or neutral; the canvas is the subtle background, labels are default text with a halo of the canvas color. While a node is inspected the others use the disabled text color and other links the subtle border, instead of transparency. The same roles hold in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ForceGraph shows a tooltip on hover and moves between nodes with the arrow keys; on Android a tap inspects a node and writes its details under the canvas, and TalkBack moves through the nodes in label order, each node its own 48dp element over the canvas. Pinch zooms as well as the buttons. Zoom in, Zoom out and Reset view are text buttons, as Monarch bundles no icons. The layout is a port of the web's algorithm, including Barnes-Hut above 300 nodes, so it gives the same shape. The whole graph is mirrored right to left. Faded nodes and links use disabled and subtle colors instead of opacity. The controlled activeId is not offered and the layout is not public. The group legend uses dots, the shape of the nodes, as on iOS. Dragging on the canvas does not scroll an enclosing scroll view, like a map. iOS showsLabels and isDashed are showLabels and dashed, following Compose naming; Android adds describeLinked and linkWithKind labels for text iOS builds in.
accessibility: The canvas is a traversal group whose content description is the generated summary (nodes, links, groups and the most connected node) or the summary given.
Every node is a TalkBack element, in label order, read as its label, group, number of links and the linked nodes with their kinds; the node of selectedId is marked selected.
With onSelect each node element is a button with a 48dp touch target; activating it inspects the node and calls onSelect.
The details of the inspected node are a polite live region that is always present, so each new inspection is announced.
Zoom in, Zoom out and Reset view are Monarch buttons with 48dp targets, disabled at the zoom limits.
View as table is the list alternative: every node with its group and links as text.
Color is not the only key: groups are named in the legend and in each node's text, and link kinds are dashed as well as coloured.
Node labels scale with the font size and are cut with an ellipsis at 144dp; the controls wrap.
edgeCases: A link to an unknown node or to itself is ignored, and does not count as a connection.
Nodes with a repeated id: the first wins.
A single node, or nodes at one place, are centered at the largest fit scale.
Graphs over 300 nodes use approximate repulsion and collision and fewer steps; the layout runs during composition when the nodes, links or options change, so very large graphs cost a frame.
Moved nodes, zoom and pan are kept until Reset view or until the graph changes.
Node elements that are panned or zoomed out of the canvas are clipped with it.
A link whose kind is not in edgeKinds is drawn as a neutral solid line and its kind is not named.

name: MonarchFormActionsBar
title: FormActionsBar
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.Surface, androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row, androidx.compose.material3.AlertDialog, androidx.compose.material3.Button (through MonarchButton)
summary: The Save and Discard bar of a form, for the bottomBar of a Scaffold, with unsaved, pending and error states and a confirmation before discarding.
whenToUse: At the bottom of an edit screen with a long form, so Save and Discard stay in reach while the form scrolls.
whenNotToUse: For a dialog or a short form put the buttons at the end of the form or in the dialog's actions. For a top app bar with a Save action use the TopAppBar actions slot.
api: @Composable fun MonarchFormActionsBar(dirty: Boolean, onSave: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, onDiscard: (() -> Unit)? = null, pending: Boolean = false, confirmDiscard: Boolean = true, hideWhenClean: Boolean = false, error: String? = null, status: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchFormActionsBarLabels = MonarchFormActionsBarLabels(), windowInsets: WindowInsets = BottomAppBarDefaults.windowInsets, actions: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null)

class MonarchFormActionsBarLabels(unsaved: String? = null, save: String? = null, saving: String? = null, discard: String? = null, discardTitle: String? = null, discardDescription: String? = null, discardConfirm: String? = null, keepEditing: String? = null)

options.name: dirty
options.description: Whether the form has unsaved changes. Save and Discard respond only while it is true.

options.name: onSave
options.description: Saves the form. The app sets pending while it runs and error if it fails.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the bar. It fills the width.

options.name: onDiscard
options.description: Reverts the form. When given, a Discard button is shown.

options.name: pending
options.description: A save is running: Save shows progress and announces "Saving", Discard is off.

options.name: confirmDiscard
options.description: Asks before discarding, in an AlertDialog with a danger button.

options.name: hideWhenClean
options.description: Shows nothing while there are no changes, no error and nothing pending.

options.name: error
options.description: The message of a failed save, shown in the danger color in place of the status.

options.name: status
options.description: Replaces the "You have unsaved changes" text.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings (strings_formactionsbar.xml).

options.name: windowInsets
options.description: The insets kept clear, the navigation bar by default. Pass WindowInsets(0) when the bar is not at the bottom edge.

options.name: actions
options.description: More actions placed before Discard, for example a ghost MonarchButton.

states.name: clean
states.description: Save and Discard are disabled and no message is shown.

states.name: dirty
states.description: Both respond and "You have unsaved changes" is shown and announced.

states.name: pending
states.description: Save shows a progress indicator and the state "Saving"; Discard is disabled.

states.name: error
states.description: The error replaces the status in the danger color, with the error semantics, and is announced.

states.name: confirming discard
states.description: An AlertDialog asks "Discard unsaved changes?" with "Discard changes" (danger) and "Keep editing".

states.name: hidden
states.description: With hideWhenClean, nothing is composed while there is nothing to save or report.

appearance: A full-width surface-coloured bar with a 1dp subtle line along its top edge, the message in muted text above the buttons, and the buttons aligned to the end: Discard as a ghost button, Save as the primary button. The dialog uses the raised background. Each role has its own value in the dark and high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: iOS ships nothing for this entry and puts Save and Discard in the navigation bar; Android builds the bar because a bottom bar is where Android forms keep these actions on long screens. The web's onSave returns a promise that drives the pending and error states; in Compose state is hoisted, so the app sets pending and error itself. Without onSave the web button submits the surrounding form; Compose has no form element, so onSave is required. The web's sticky positioning is the Scaffold bottomBar's job here, and the web's named region (aria-label "Form actions") has no Android equivalent, so the bar is a traversal group without a name. The web's warning glyph before an error is not drawn, because Monarch for Android bundles no icons; the danger color is not the only cue, the text says it.
accessibility: The message line is always present and is a polite live region, so "You have unsaved changes" and an error are announced when they appear.
An error also carries the error semantics.
Save and Discard are MonarchButtons with 48dp touch targets; disabled ones are announced as disabled.
While pending, Save keeps its place and announces "Saving" as its state.
The confirmation is a Material 3 AlertDialog, which TalkBack announces and which Back dismisses.
The message wraps, and at large font sizes Save takes the width that is left and its label wraps instead of being cut.
edgeCases: Save with dirty false and pending false does nothing even if the button is reached.
If the app changes dirty to false while the confirmation is open, the dialog stays until it is answered; Discard then calls onDiscard.
The confirmation state survives a configuration change.
With confirmDiscard false, Discard calls onDiscard at once.

title: FormBuilder
wrapsNative: MonarchTabs for Build and Preview, MonarchMenu for the field palette and MonarchBottomSheet for field settings, around MonarchReorderableList and MonarchFieldRenderer
summary: A recipe, not a component: a form builder on a phone, with Build and Preview tabs, an Add a field menu, a reorderable list of fields, a settings sheet per field and a live preview rendered by MonarchFieldRenderer.
whenToUse: When people design their own forms in an app (intake, surveys, request forms) and the questions are stored as MonarchFormFieldDefinition data.
whenNotToUse: To fill in a form, render it with MonarchFieldRenderer alone. For a fixed form the app defines, use MonarchFormField and the form controls directly.
api: PrimaryTabRow(selectedTabIndex = tab) { Tab(selected = tab == 0, onClick = { tab = 0 }, text = { Text("Build") }); Tab(…) }
DropdownMenu(expanded = paletteOpen, onDismissRequest = …) { DropdownMenuItem(text = { Text(type) }, onClick = { fields += MonarchFormFieldDefinition(…) }) }
MonarchReorderableList(items = fields, key = { it.id }, itemLabel = { it.label }, onReorder = { from, to -> fields.add(to, fields.removeAt(from)) }) { field, _ -> … }
ModalBottomSheet(onDismissRequest = …) { MonarchTextField(…); MonarchSelect(…); MonarchSwitchRow(…) }
MonarchFieldRenderer(field = field, value = answers[field.id], onValueChange = { answers[field.id] = it })

options.name: fields
options.description: The form, owned by the app as a snapshot list; the same data MonarchFieldRenderer renders and the app stores.

options.name: palette
options.description: The field types the builder offers, with their names; the Add a field menu and the Type select use it.

options.name: settings
options.description: The settings sheet of one field: question, type, required, and any type-specific settings (options, limits) the app supports.

options.name: preview
options.description: MonarchFieldRenderer for every visible field, with answers kept in a state map so conditions can be tried.

states.name: build
states.description: The Add a field button, then the fields in a reorderable list, each with its type, a required mark and an Edit button.

states.name: empty
states.description: MonarchEmptyState says there are no fields yet.

states.name: editing
states.description: A bottom sheet with the question, the type, Required, Remove field and Done. A blank question shows an error.

states.name: preview
states.description: The form as people will fill it in, rendered by MonarchFieldRenderer.

appearance: Material 3 tabs, menu and bottom sheet in the Monarch theme around Monarch rows, fields and buttons. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web FormBuilder is one component with three columns on wide screens (palette, field list, settings) and two or one on smaller ones; a phone has no room for side-by-side panes, so Build and Preview are tabs, the palette is a MonarchMenu behind Add a field and each field's settings open in a MonarchBottomSheet. The parts already exist as Monarch components, so Android keeps it a recipe. The web's condition editor, duplicate, undo after remove, maximum field count and the full per-type settings (options, limits, accepted files) are not in the recipe: the app adds the settings it supports to the sheet, and MonarchConditionEditor for logic. Reordering is MonarchReorderableList: drag the handle, or use its TalkBack actions Move up and Move down. MonarchFormFieldDefinition is a class, not a data class, so the recipe rebuilds a definition to change it. iOS has the same recipe coverage.
accessibility: Build and Preview are Material 3 tabs with the selected state.
Each field row has MonarchReorderableList's drag handle, named Reorder and the field's question, with the TalkBack actions Move up and Move down as the drag equivalent; moves are announced.
Each Edit button is named Edit and the question, so the buttons can be told apart.
The type and required mark are text under the question, not color.
Settings controls are labelled Monarch fields; a blank question is an error on the field.
The preview is the real form, with MonarchFieldRenderer's labels, required marks and errors.
edgeCases: The reorderable list is lazy, so give it a bounded height (heightIn max) when the screen scrolls, or make it the screen's scrolling list.
Removing the field that is being edited closes the sheet.
Changing the type keeps the question; settings that belong to the old type are dropped by the app.

name: MonarchFormField
title: Field
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column and Row around any control, with androidx.compose.ui.semantics contentDescription and error applied to the control through a Modifier, and a polite liveRegion
summary: A visible label, one control, help text and an error message, with the label and the error given to the control for TalkBack.
whenToUse: Around a control that has no label of its own: a MonarchSwitch, a Slider, a picker, a group of buttons, or a MonarchTextField when the label should sit above the field instead of inside it.
whenNotToUse: For a plain text input MonarchTextField already has a label, helper and error. For a switch that is a whole settings row use MonarchSwitchRow.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchFormField(label: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, layout: MonarchFormFieldLayout = MonarchFormFieldLayout.Stack, enabled: Boolean = true, required: Boolean = false, helperText: String? = null, errorText: String? = null, optionalText: String? = null, errorIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, requiredLabel: String? = null, control: @Composable (controlModifier: Modifier) -> Unit)
public enum class MonarchFormFieldLayout { Stack, Row }

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label, and the TalkBack name of the control.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the field.

options.name: layout
options.description: Stack puts the label above the control; Row puts the label and help text at the start, the control at the end and the error under both.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Draws the label, mark and help text in the disabled color. Pass the same state to the control.

options.name: required
options.description: Shows a mark after the label and adds "Required" to the TalkBack name of the control.

options.name: helperText
options.description: Help text. Under the control in the stack layout, under the label in the row layout.

options.name: errorText
options.description: An error message under the field in the danger color, set as the error of the control and announced when it appears or changes. In the stack layout it replaces the help text. A blank string is no error.

options.name: optionalText
options.description: Text after the label of an optional field, such as "Optional". Ignored when required is true.

options.name: errorIcon
options.description: An icon before the error message, in the danger color. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: requiredLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken "Required".

options.name: control
options.description: One control without a visible label of its own. It must apply the Modifier it is given, which carries the name and the error.

states.name: default
states.description: Label in the default text color with the label type, help text in the muted color with the caption type.

states.name: required
states.description: A "*" in the strong danger color after the label; "Required" is added to the name of the control.

states.name: optional
states.description: The optional text in the muted color after the label.

states.name: error
states.description: The error, with the optional icon, under the field in the strong danger color; the control is in the error state for TalkBack; announced when it appears or changes.

states.name: disabled
states.description: enabled = false draws the label, mark and help text in the disabled color; the control is disabled by the app.

appearance: Texts use the default, muted and disabled text roles and the strong danger role for the mark and the error, in every theme. The field draws no surface; the control draws its own.
platformNotes: On the web, Field gives the control its id, aria-describedby, aria-invalid and aria-required through context, and NativeSelect lives in the same file. Compose has no label-for wiring, so the control slot receives a Modifier that sets the control's contentDescription to the label (with "Required") and its error semantics; the control must apply it. Compose has no described-by either, so the help text stays a readable element after the control instead of being part of the control's name; iOS puts it in the hint. The control is not told it is invalid or disabled: MonarchTextField has its own errorText parameter for its border, and enabled must be passed to the control as well. The error is announced through an always-present polite live region. The parity map lists inline-notice as a dependency; it is not used, because the error is one line of caption text under the control as on the web.
accessibility: The control is named by the label, or by the label and "Required"; the visible label and required mark are hidden from TalkBack so they are not read twice.
The error is set as the error of the control, so TalkBack reads it with the control; the visible error text is hidden from TalkBack.
A new error is announced through an always-present polite live region.
The help text is its own readable element; the error has text and an optional icon, and the required mark is backed by the spoken "Required", so neither depends on color.
In the row layout the label column comes first from the start edge, also in right-to-left layouts.
Texts wrap at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: If the control does not apply the Modifier it is given, TalkBack reads the help text and the announcement but not the label on the control.
Put one control in the slot: a control made of several elements, such as a group of chips, is better given its own description.
A MonarchSwitch or MonarchCheckbox in the row layout keeps its own 48dp touch target; the label is not part of it. For a row that toggles as a whole use MonarchSwitchRow.
In the row layout the control keeps its size and the label column takes the rest, so long labels wrap.

name: MonarchFreshnessIndicator
title: FreshnessIndicator
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow, androidx.compose.material3.Text, MonarchButton, android.text.format.DateUtils.getRelativeTimeSpanString
summary: How fresh a data set or a sync is, such as "Updated 3 minutes ago", turning to warning and danger as it ages, with an optional Refresh button.
whenToUse: Above or below data that is synced or cached: a directory, a report, a registry import, where people need to know how old the data is and refresh it.
whenNotToUse: For the source and age of one value, use MonarchProvenance. For the outcome of the user's own edits, use MonarchSaveStatusIndicator.

enum class MonarchFreshnessIndicatorVariant { Inline, Banner }

options.name: updatedAt
options.description: When the data was last updated or synced, in epoch milliseconds (UTC). null means never.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the indicator.

options.name: variant
options.description: Inline is a line of muted text; Banner is a bordered bar.

options.name: status
options.description: Replaces the status worked out from the age, for example Checking or Error.

options.name: refreshing
options.description: A refresh the app runs is in progress; the button is busy and ignores taps. When it turns false the outcome is announced.

options.name: staleAfterMillis
options.description: The age after which the data is stale (warning). null never turns stale.

options.name: expiredAfterMillis
options.description: The age after which the data is expired (danger). null never expires.

options.name: source
options.description: Names the data or its source, shown first.

options.name: details
options.description: Further facts appended with middle dots. Empty strings are left out.

options.name: error
options.description: The error text for the error status. Without it "Status unavailable" is shown.

options.name: onRefresh
options.description: Adds a Refresh button. Not called while refreshing.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings monarch_freshnessindicator_*.

states.name: fresh
states.description: A dot in the success color and "Updated 3 minutes ago".

states.name: stale
states.description: A warning dot and "Out of date" in semibold warning text after the time.

states.name: expired
states.description: A danger dot and "Very out of date" in semibold danger text after the time.

states.name: never
states.description: A neutral dot and "Never updated".

states.name: checking
states.description: An info dot and "Checking…".

states.name: error
states.description: A danger dot and the error text, after the time when there is one.

states.name: refreshing
states.description: The Refresh button shows progress, ignores taps and has the state "Refreshing".

appearance: Caption text in the muted text color after a small dot in the solid color of the status tone (subtle text for never). Flags and errors use the strong color of the tone at semibold weight. The banner adds the subtle background and the subtle border with large rounded corners. The Refresh button is a small ghost MonarchButton. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web onRefresh can return a promise that keeps the button busy; here the app controls refreshing, and when it turns false "Refreshed." is announced, or "Refresh failed." when the status is then Error. The web wakes up exactly when a limit is passed; here the status and the relative time are worked out again every minute, so a change can show up to a minute late. The web actions slot and the live and now options are not offered: place other controls beside the indicator. The web retry glyph on the button is not drawn, because Monarch bundles no icons. Times are epoch milliseconds, formatted with DateUtils. iOS shares the name and the statuses and takes an async onRefresh.
accessibility: The dot and the line are one TalkBack element, read with commas between the parts: "Directory, Updated 3 minutes ago, Out of date".
The status is written in words ("Out of date", "Very out of date", the error), so the color of the dot is never the only signal.
A change to stale, expired or error after the first composition is announced through a polite live region; the first status is not announced.
When refreshing turns false, "Refreshed." or "Refresh failed." is announced through the same live region.
The Refresh button is a separate element with a 48dp touch target; while refreshing it ignores taps and has the state "Refreshing".
The button moves under the line when both do not fit, so nothing is cut off at the largest font size.
edgeCases: Without either limit the data never turns stale.
status = Error with no updatedAt shows only the error text.
Two refreshes in a row announce "Refreshed." each time: the live region is emptied for a frame before the words are set again.

name: MonarchFunnelChart
title: FunnelChart
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column and Row with androidx.compose.foundation.background bars, inside MonarchChartFrame; androidx.compose.foundation.clickable for selectable stages
summary: A conversion funnel: how many reach each step, the share that continues to the next step and how many drop off.
whenToUse: To show a fixed sequence of steps that people pass through, such as sign-up or hiring, where the drop between steps matters.
whenNotToUse: For values that are not steps of one flow, use MonarchBarList. For change over time, use a line or bar chart in MonarchChartFrame.

enum class MonarchFunnelChartAlignment { Center, Start }

class MonarchFunnelChartLabels(frame: MonarchChartFrameLabels = MonarchChartFrameLabels(), stage: String? = null, value: String? = null, fromPrevious: String? = null, ofFirst: String? = null, step: String? = null, stages: ((count: Int, first: String, last: String) -> String)? = null, overall: String? = null, largestDrop: String? = null, describeFirst: String? = null, describe: String? = null)

options.name: title
options.description: The name of the chart, shown as the frame's heading.

options.name: stages
options.description: The steps, first (widest) to last.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the frame.

options.name: description
options.description: One line under the title, such as the period.

options.name: status
options.description: Ready, Loading, Empty or Error. A ready chart without stages shows the empty state.

options.name: alignment
options.description: Centered bars read as a funnel; Start bars begin at the start edge and are easier to compare.

options.name: showSteps
options.description: Shows the line between stages with the share that continued and the number dropped.

options.name: summary
options.description: Replaces the generated summary that TalkBack reads for the stages.

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: The message of the empty state.

options.name: footer
options.description: Notes under the chart, such as the source.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes a count. The default is a number in the current locale.

options.name: formatRate
options.description: Writes a share from 0 to 1. The default is a percentage in the current locale with at most one decimal.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Try again in the error status.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Makes every stage a button, for example to list the people who dropped.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, including the frame's. Sentences with values are format strings with %1$s placeholders; the stage count sentence is a function so it can follow the language's plural rules.

states.name: ready
states.description: One row per stage: the step line, the label with its value and share of the first stage, and the bar.

states.name: pressed
states.description: A selectable stage shows the Material ripple while pressed and the Monarch focus ring when focused from a keyboard.

states.name: table
states.description: View as table replaces the bars with the counts, the share of the previous stage and the share of the first.

states.name: empty
states.description: The frame's empty state, also when the chart is ready but has no stages.

states.name: loading
states.description: The frame's skeleton at the chart's height.

states.name: error
states.description: The frame's error message, with Try again when onRetry is given.

appearance: Bars use the first data color (or the stage's palette slot) on the card surface. Labels and values are default text, the share and the step line muted text, in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web FunnelChart highlights a stage on hover and keyboard focus and announces it in a live region; on Android there is no hover, so every stage is its own TalkBack element instead, and a selectable stage is a button with a ripple. The web controlled activeIndex is not offered. Web align start is MonarchFunnelChartAlignment.Start and mirrors right to left. Number formats are functions instead of Intl options. The step line has no arrow glyph, as Monarch bundles no icons. The stage count sentence is a plural resource, replaced with a function, where iOS takes two strings. The rest of the names match iOS (showsSteps is showSteps, following Compose naming).
accessibility: The stages are a traversal group whose content description is the generated summary: the number of stages, the overall conversion and the largest drop, or the summary given.
Each stage is one TalkBack element read as its label and value, then the share of the previous and of the first stage; it carries its position as a collection item.
With onSelect each stage is a button with a touch target of at least 48dp and the Monarch focus ring.
Bars are decoration; every number they show is also text.
The frame title is a heading, and View as table lists every count and share.
The chart measures its stages, so at font scale 2.0 labels wrap and the chart grows instead of overlapping the footer.
edgeCases: Negative and non-finite values count as zero.
A stage after a stage of zero continues at 0%, without dividing by zero.
A stage larger than the one before shows a share above 100% and is not counted as a drop.
A value above zero but tiny next to the widest stage still draws a sliver of bar.
Stage keys default to the label, so give a key when two stages share a label.
The first frame uses an estimated height (76dp per stage with step lines, 56dp without, never under 120dp); the measured height replaces it on the next frame.

examples.title: Sign-up funnel
Aligned to the start edge, selectable, without step lines
examples.setup: var selected by remember { mutableStateOf("") }
examples.code:
MonarchFunnelChart(
    title = "Hiring pipeline",
    stages = listOf(
        MonarchFunnelChartStage("Applied", 120.0),
        MonarchFunnelChartStage("Interviewed", 30.0),
        MonarchFunnelChartStage("Hired", 4.0),
    ),
    alignment = MonarchFunnelChartAlignment.Start,
    showSteps = false,
    onSelect = { selected = it.label },
)

name: MonarchGanttTimeline
title: GanttTimeline
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.ui.layout.SubcomposeLayout (row labels measured first, so rows grow with their text) and androidx.compose.ui.layout.Layout with Modifier.drawWithContent (the grid, gridlines and dependency arrows) in androidx.compose.foundation.horizontalScroll; androidx.compose.foundation.gestures.detectDragGesturesAfterLongPress with HapticFeedbackType for moving and resizing; androidx.compose.material3.TooltipBox with PlainTooltip (milestones); androidx.compose.material3.ListItem, DatePickerDialog and DateRangePicker (the list view); androidx.compose.material3.SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow and DropdownMenu (toolbar); MonarchCalendarToolbar, MonarchCollapsible, MonarchButton, MonarchDivider, MonarchText; android.icu.text.DateFormat
summary: Items as bars on a calendar from their first to their last day, with dependency arrows, milestones, a today line, zoom from weeks to years and a list view that writes every date in words and changes dates with the Material 3 date range picker.
whenToUse: To plan and reschedule dated work where overlaps and dependencies matter: tasks, phases or issues with start and due dates, in a project or roadmap screen. Save each onChange as it arrives and pass the new items back.
whenNotToUse: For work that moves through statuses without dates use a board or MonarchStepper. For events at times of day use MonarchAgendaList or a calendar. For one date use the Material 3 DatePicker (see date-picker).

options.name: items
options.description: The rows: id, label, start and end day keys (one of them makes a one-day marker, neither makes it unscheduled), parentId for sub-tasks, groupId, progress from 0 to 1, tone (null is the accent), editable, conflict text and a short meta text.

options.name: previousIcon
options.description: The backward chevron of the toolbar's Earlier button, passed to MonarchCalendarToolbar. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: nextIcon
options.description: The forward chevron of the toolbar's Later button.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the timeline.

options.name: state
options.description: The first visible day, the zoom, chart or list, and the collapsed parents. Kept across configuration changes; the app can read and set every value.

options.name: groups
options.description: Heading rows; items with a matching groupId are listed under them. A group with dates shows a thin span on its row.

options.name: dependencies
options.description: Links between items, drawn as arrows (finish to start, start to start or finish to finish) and written as "Depends on" in the list. conflict = true draws the arrow dashed in the danger color.

options.name: milestones
options.description: Dated checkpoints drawn as diamonds: on their item's row with itemId, otherwise in a lane under the header with their name.

options.name: zoomLevels
options.description: The zoom levels offered in the toolbar's zoom menu. With one level or none there is no menu.

options.name: undated
options.description: Top-level items without dates go in an Unscheduled MonarchCollapsible under the chart (List) or stay as chart rows that say "No dates" (Row).

options.name: today
options.description: Any time on the day of the today line, read in timeZone. null hides the line and disables Today. Pass a fixed value in tests and previews.

options.name: timeZone
options.description: The zone today is read in; null is the device's zone. Item dates are always read in UTC. An IANA id such as Europe/Berlin; null, or an id the device does not know, is the device's zone.

options.name: toolbar
options.description: Shows the toolbar: Today, Earlier, Later, the visible range, the zoom menu, the chart and list switch and toolbarActions.

options.name: onChange
options.description: Called once per finished drag, arrow key, TalkBack action or date range picker save, with the item and its new dates as day keys. Without it the timeline is read-only. The timeline never changes items itself.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Makes each bar and list row a button that opens the item.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including the bar description, the TalkBack action names and the announcement after a change.

options.name: toolbarActions
options.description: Extra controls at the end of the toolbar, such as a filter or a New item button.

states.name: read only
states.description: Without onChange bars have no drag, no key handling and no TalkBack actions; with onOpen they are still buttons.

states.name: editable
states.description: A visible hint above the chart; each bar can be moved by touch and hold then drag, its ends by holding within 12dp of an end, by the arrow keys and by six TalkBack actions. The list shows Change dates.

states.name: dragging
states.description: The bar follows the finger by whole days with a large shadow, the dependency arrows follow it, and a haptic tick marks each day. Release reports the change once.

states.name: conflict
states.description: The bar uses the danger tone with a dashed 2dp outline; the conflict text is read with the bar and written in the list in the strong danger color.

states.name: one-day marker
states.description: An item with only a start or an end is a small diamond centered on its day; it can only be moved.

states.name: parent
states.description: The row label reads "Hide 2 sub-items" or "Show 2 sub-items" and toggles the children; a parent without dates shows a bracket over its children's span.

states.name: outside the window
states.description: The row says "Ended Jan 9, 2026" or "Starts Mar 2, 2026" instead of a bar.

states.name: unscheduled
states.description: Items without dates are listed in an Unscheduled collapsible under the chart, or as rows saying "No dates".

states.name: list
states.description: One Material 3 ListItem per row with the dates, length, progress, dependencies and conflict in words, then the unscheduled items and the milestones.

appearance: The chart sits on the surface color with a subtle outline; the header, weekends (week and month zoom) and group rows use the subtle background, gridlines and row lines the subtle border. A bar is a light tint of its tone with an outline and a bottom progress strip in the tone's strong fill (accent by default, neutral uses the muted background and the strong border) and its label in the default text color. The today line and its label use the accent fill with accent-on-solid text. Arrows use the subtle text color, or the strong danger color dashed when broken. Done milestones are filled with the accent; open ones are the surface with a muted outline. High contrast themes use their own roles.
platformNotes: There is no iOS GanttTimeline inventory entry yet, so the names follow the web and the plan (MonarchGanttTimeline). The web table view becomes a list (MonarchGanttTimelineView.List) of Material 3 ListItems, the phone and TalkBack pattern; its date inputs become one Change dates button that opens the Material 3 DateRangePicker in a DatePickerDialog. Web pointer drag becomes touch and hold then drag (detectDragGesturesAfterLongPress), so a plain swipe still scrolls the calendar; web keyboard moves stay for hardware keyboards (arrow keys, Shift for the end, Alt for the start, without the web's Up and Down jumps between bars) and are also TalkBack custom actions. The chart scrolls sideways only, not in two axes as the plan said: it does not scroll vertically, so put it in a scrolling screen, and a drag does not scroll the calendar when the finger reaches its edge. The time axis runs left to right in every layout direction, as on the web; the row labels stay at the start. Dates are day keys in epoch milliseconds (UTC midnight) instead of ISO strings, progress is 0 to 1 instead of 0 to 100, and dates are formatted in the configuration's locale. onChange returns nothing: the web's promise with a saving state and rollback is replaced by the app passing new items (or the old ones) back. Zoom, the first visible day, chart or list and the collapsed parents live in a MonarchGanttTimelineState instead of uncontrolled defaults. Tones are MonarchTone with null for the web's accent tone, because MonarchTone has no accent. Title and meta are plain strings, not composable slots, and the conflict has no warning glyph (Monarch bundles no icons): the dashed outline and the words carry it. Experimental because it is a product pattern not yet adopted by a Rook Android app.
accessibility: Each bar is one element read as "<label>, <first day> to <last day>, <n>% complete", with ". Conflict: <message>" when there is a conflict; a one-day marker reads one date.
With onOpen a bar is a button with a 48dp touch target reserved in the layout (the node is at least 48dp wide and as tall as the row, around a narrower visible bar).

Editable bars offer TalkBack custom actions: Move a day earlier, Move a day later, Start a day earlier, Start a day later, End a day earlier, End a day later (markers only the first two). Locked items and read-only timelines offer none.
After a change the new dates are announced through a polite live region on an always-present node: "Design: Jan 12, 2026 to Jan 24, 2026".
A parent's row label is a button with the state Expanded or Collapsed and a visible Hide or Show caption.
The chart and the list are named "Timeline"; group labels are headings; header ticks, the today label and the grid lines are decorative and hidden from TalkBack.
Milestones are images read as "Milestone <name>, <date>" with ", done" when reached; lane milestones also show a plain tooltip on touch and hold.
The list writes every date, length, progress, dependency and conflict, so nothing in the chart depends on dragging, color or position alone.
Rows grow with their label at font scale 2.0, so labels wrap instead of being cut.
edgeCases: Start after end is swapped; dates at any time of day are read as their UTC date.
A drag or key move never lets the first day pass the last when changing one end.
Unknown parent ids, self-parents and parent cycles are ignored; groups that are not listed leave their items at the end.
Bars narrower than five edge zones (60dp) hide their label; every bar is at least 6dp wide on screen.
Items outside the visible window show "Ended …" or "Starts …" in their row.
A dependency to an item that is not shown (collapsed or unscheduled) is not drawn.
Long labels wrap and make their row taller; the bar label inside a bar is cut with an ellipsis but read in full.
The year zoom spans 730 days at 1.6dp a day; the week zoom 28 days at 40dp a day.

parityExceptions.reason: The web's Unscheduled list is a disclosure that starts collapsed: its item names are in the page source but not shown until it is opened. Android starts it collapsed too, as the web does, so "Pricing research" is not on screen in the example.
parityExceptions.convention: a disclosure starts closed on every platform; its items are read once it is opened

name: MonarchGauge
title: Gauge
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.Canvas (DrawScope.drawArc)
summary: A half-circle meter for one reading against a scale: bands give the scale a meaning, a target is marked, and the value is written as text.
whenToUse: For one reading against a known scale where the bands matter: utilisation, a health score, a quota used.
whenNotToUse: For progress of a task use MonarchProgress. For several quotas use MonarchUsageMeter. For a value over time use MonarchSparkline.
api: @Composable fun MonarchGauge(value: Double?, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, range: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Double> = 0.0..100.0, bands: List<MonarchGaugeBand> = emptyList(), target: Double? = null, tone: MonarchTone? = null, indicator: MonarchGaugeIndicator = MonarchGaugeIndicator.Arc, size: MonarchGaugeSize = MonarchGaugeSize.Md, showRange: Boolean = true, label: String? = null, description: String? = null, formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = null, valueLabel: String? = null, noValueLabel: String? = null)
class MonarchGaugeBand(range: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Double>, tone: MonarchTone, label: String? = null)
enum class MonarchGaugeIndicator { Arc, Needle }
enum class MonarchGaugeSize { Sm, Md, Lg }

options.name: value
options.description: The reading. null, or a value that is not finite, shows an empty track and a dash.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the gauge.

options.name: range
options.description: The scale.

options.name: bands
options.description: Stretches of the scale with a tone and a name.

options.name: target
options.description: A target on the scale, marked with a tick and added to the spoken value.

options.name: tone
options.description: The color of the value. null takes the tone of the value's band, Neutral outside every band, or the accent without bands.

options.name: indicator
options.description: Arc fills the track to the value; Needle draws the bands on the track and points at the value.

options.name: size
options.description: Sm (120dp), Md (160dp) or Lg (200dp) wide.

options.name: showRange
options.description: Writes the ends of the scale under the dial.

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label under the gauge and its spoken name. "Gauge" (monarch_gauge_name) is spoken without one.

options.name: description
options.description: A second line under the label.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes every number. The default is a number in the current locale.

options.name: valueLabel
options.description: Replaces the value TalkBack reads.

options.name: noValueLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in text "No data" (monarch_gauge_no_value).

states.name: with a value
states.description: The track is filled to the value (Arc) or a needle points at it (Needle); the value is written in or under the dial.

states.name: in a band
states.description: The arc takes the band's color and the band's name is written under the value.

states.name: no value
states.description: An empty track, a dash, and "No data" as the spoken value.

states.name: out of range
states.description: Drawn at the nearest end of the scale; the text shows the real value.

appearance: The track is the muted background. The value arc uses the solid color of its tone, the accent solid without bands, and the strong border color for neutral; bands use the solid color of their tone. The target tick and the needle use the default text color; the range, band name and description use muted text. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web draws its own SVG and exposes a meter role; here the dial is drawn on a Compose Canvas and the gauge is one element with a progress range and a state description, because Android has no meter role. The web size is a number of pixels and the thickness can be set; here there are three sizes and the thickness is 12% of the width, as on iOS. The web tone accent is a null tone here. With the Arc indicator the bands are drawn as a thin arc inside the track, not outside it as on the web, so the dial needs no extra room. The scale starts at the start edge, so the dial is mirrored in right-to-left layouts; the web one is not. Above font scale 1.3, and with a needle, the value is written under the dial instead of inside it.
accessibility: The gauge is one element. Its content description is the label, or "Gauge".
It exposes a progress range from the start to the end of the scale, with the value limited to the scale.
Its state description is the reading and the name of its band ("72, At risk"), or the reading and the range ("72 (from 0 to 100)"), followed by the target ("Target 80").
Without a value it reads "No data" and has no progress range.
The value and the band name are written as text, so the reading does not depend on the arc or its color.
Text scales with the font size; the dial keeps its size, and above font scale 1.3 the value moves under it so it is never clipped.
The change of the arc and the needle is animated with the Monarch motion spec, and immediate when animations are removed.
It is not interactive and has no touch target.
edgeCases: A range whose ends are equal is widened by one.
A value that is not finite is treated as no value.
A value exactly on the boundary of two bands belongs to the upper one; the end of the scale belongs to the band that reaches it.
A band without a label falls back to the range in the spoken value; give every band a label.
Bands that reach beyond the range are drawn up to its end.

A ratio, small
examples.code:
MonarchGauge(
    value = 0.55,
    range = 0.0..1.0,
    size = MonarchGaugeSize.Sm,
    label = "Quota used",
    formatValue = { "${(it * 100).toInt()}%" },
)

examples.title: A needle
examples.code:
MonarchGauge(
    value = 40.0,
    bands = listOf(
        MonarchGaugeBand(0.0..50.0, MonarchTone.Danger, "Low"),
        MonarchGaugeBand(50.0..100.0, MonarchTone.Success, "Good"),
    ),
    indicator = MonarchGaugeIndicator.Needle,
    label = "Score",
)

parityExceptions.reason: The web formats the value with an Intl.NumberFormat option bag (unit percent, no decimals); the native gauge takes a formatValue closure, so the template writes the same text (76%) with a closure.
parityExceptions.convention: Locale-driven formatting is native: Swift and Kotlin format numbers in code, not with Intl options.

title: GdprEraseFlow
wrapsNative: MonarchBottomSheet (confirmValueChange keeps it open while erasing) with a scrolling androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of MonarchConsequenceList, MonarchInlineNotice, MonarchCheckboxRow, MonarchTypeToConfirmInput, MonarchStepUpAuthDialog and MonarchButtons
summary: A recipe, not a component: an administrator erases one person's personal data after seeing what is erased and what is kept and why, acknowledging that it cannot be undone, typing the person's email and confirming who they are; the done step shows the audit reference.
whenToUse: In an admin or support tool, to act on a person's right to erasure (GDPR article 17) for one data subject.
whenNotToUse: For a person deleting their own account, use an account deletion flow with a grace period. For removing a member from a workspace without erasing their data, use the members screen's remove action.
api: ModalBottomSheet(onDismissRequest = { if (!erasing) open = false }, sheetState = rememberModalBottomSheetState(skipPartiallyExpanded = true, confirmValueChange = { !erasing })) { … }

MonarchConsequenceList(items = …, heading = "Will be erased") and MonarchConsequenceList(items = listOf(MonarchConsequence(MonarchConsequenceKind.Kept, "Invoices", detail = "Kept for 7 years to meet tax law")), heading = "Will be kept")
MonarchCheckboxRow(checked = understood, onCheckedChange = { understood = it }, label = "I understand the data is erased for good")
MonarchTypeToConfirmInput(phrase = subject, value = typed, onValueChange = { typed = it }, label = "Type $subject to confirm")
MonarchStepUpAuthDialog(onVerify = …, description = "Erasing someone’s data needs you to confirm it’s you.", onCancel = …, onVerified = …, onVerifyingChange = { erasing = it })

options.name: erased
options.description: The kinds of personal data that are erased, with counts from the server. Pass loading = true to MonarchConsequenceList and keep the button disabled while they load.

options.name: retained
options.description: Data that is kept, each with its reason as the detail, such as a legal retention period.

options.name: confirmPhrase
options.description: What the administrator types, usually the subject's email.

options.name: erasing
options.description: While the request runs the sheet cannot be dismissed.

options.name: auditId
options.description: The audit log entry the server returns, shown on the done step.

states.name: review
states.description: The title naming the person, the erased and kept lists, a warning notice, the acknowledgement checkbox, the email field and a disabled danger button until both are done.

states.name: verify
states.description: MonarchStepUpAuthDialog asks the administrator to confirm who they are; Cancel goes back.

states.name: erasing
states.description: The request runs; the sheet cannot be swiped or backed away.

states.name: done
states.description: "Personal data erased" with the audit reference and Done.

appearance: Every part is an existing Monarch component on the Material 3 sheet surface: two consequence lists with their removed and kept marks, a warning inline notice in the subtle warning fill, a checkbox row, the type-to-confirm field, full-width danger and ghost buttons, and the audit reference as body text. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web's GdprEraseFlow is one component on WizardDialog with review, confirm, step-up and done steps. On Android it is a recipe: a MonarchBottomSheet holds the steps as a when over the app's step state, because the two lists, the acknowledgement and the step-up content do not fit a MonarchDialog. The review and confirm steps of the web are one scrolling sheet here, with the button enabled only after the checkbox and the typed phrase. The web's loading and error props are MonarchConsequenceList's loading and an inline error with retry that the app shows. The web's messages and count formatting are written by the app. iOS has no plan entry for this flow yet.
accessibility: The sheet's title uses the title style, which MonarchText marks as a heading.
Each list has a heading, and MonarchConsequenceList reads each line with its kind, so erased and kept do not depend on the mark.
The warning is a MonarchInlineNotice read with its tone; the acknowledgement is one checkbox element with its label.
MonarchTypeToConfirmInput announces when the typed email matches; the danger button is announced as disabled until both conditions are met.
The sheet cannot be dismissed while erasing.
edgeCases: Check the acknowledgement, the phrase and the step-up on the server as well.
When the retained list is empty, leave out its heading.
Erasure in backups often happens later: say so in the warning when it does.
Keep the audit id with the request so support can find it.

name: MonarchGoalTree
title: GoalTree
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of goal rows with androidx.compose.foundation.clickable toggles and FlowRow headings; MonarchProgress (androidx.compose.material3.LinearProgressIndicator), MonarchStatusBadge, MonarchAvatar, MonarchButton, MonarchEmptyState
summary: Nested goals (objectives and key results) with progress, status, owner and alignment; branches open and close, open goals can offer an add button, and each goal can carry its own actions.
whenToUse: For OKRs and other goal hierarchies, where readers scan progress and status and drill into the key results of an objective.
whenNotToUse: For a hierarchy without progress (folders, departments), use MonarchTreeView. For reporting lines between people, use MonarchOrgChart. For a single figure, use MonarchProgress.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchGoalTree(goals: List<MonarchGoal>, expandIcon: @Composable () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, expanded: Set<String>? = null, onExpandedChange: ((Set<String>) -> Unit)? = null, quietChildren: Boolean = true, canAddChild: ((goal: MonarchGoal, depth: Int) -> Boolean)? = null, onAddChild: ((MonarchGoal) -> Unit)? = null, addIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchGoalTreeLabels = MonarchGoalTreeLabels(), actions: (@Composable (MonarchGoal) -> Unit)? = null)

class MonarchGoal(id: String, parentId: String? = null, title: String, progress: Float, status: MonarchGoalStatus, ownerName: String? = null, ownerImage: Painter? = null, meta: String? = null, alignedTo: String? = null)
enum class MonarchGoalStatus { NotStarted, OnTrack, AtRisk, OffTrack, Done }

class MonarchGoalTreeLabels(status: ((MonarchGoalStatus) -> String)? = null, expand: ((String) -> String)? = null, collapse: ((String) -> String)? = null, alignedTo: ((String) -> String)? = null, addChild: String? = null, addChildTo: ((String) -> String)? = null, childCount: ((Int) -> String)? = null, empty: String? = null)

options.name: goals
options.description: Every goal, flat. Nesting comes from parentId; a missing or self-referencing parent makes a top-level goal, a repeated id keeps its first goal, and goals only reachable through a cycle are not shown.

options.name: expandIcon
options.description: A chevron that points to the end. It turns a quarter to point down when the goal is open. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the tree.

options.name: expanded
options.description: The ids of open goals. Kept inside the tree when null, with every goal that has children open at first.

options.name: onExpandedChange
options.description: Called with the new set of open ids.

options.name: quietChildren
options.description: Children that are on track or not started hide their badge; their status is still read.

options.name: canAddChild
options.description: Which goals get the add button, from the goal and its depth (0 at the top). Top-level goals when null.

options.name: onAddChild
options.description: Adds an "Add key result" button inside the open goals canAddChild allows. Receives the parent; the app adds the goal.

options.name: addIcon
options.description: A decorative icon before the add button's text.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the status names, the button names, Aligned to, Add key result, the child count and the empty text.

options.name: actions
options.description: Controls at the end of each goal's row, such as a button that opens a MonarchMenu with Check in and History.

states.name: open
states.description: The chevron points down and the children (and the add button) are listed under the goal, indented by 24dp per level.

states.name: closed
states.description: The chevron points to the end and the heading shows the number of children, such as "3 key results".

states.name: quiet children
states.description: Children on track or not started have no badge.

states.name: empty
states.description: A small MonarchEmptyState, No goals yet.

appearance: Top-level titles use the strong body style and children the body style, in the default text color. Status badges are subtle MonarchStatusBadges in the neutral, info, warning, danger or success tone. The bar is MonarchProgress (accent fill on the emphasis track) with the percentage, meta, child count and alignment in muted caption text. The same roles adapt to dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The parity map names tree rows over MonarchTreeView; MonarchTreeView rows hold a label and a description only, so the goal tree draws its own rows with the same toggle, indent and chevron behavior. The rows are a Column, not a lazy list, so the tree can sit in a scrolling screen with other content; very large trees belong in a list with a detail screen. The progress bar is always in the accent color because MonarchProgress has no tone; the web colors the bar by status, and the status is in words in the badge and the description. Progress is a fraction from 0 to 1 (the web takes 0 to 100), as on iOS. Titles, meta and alignment are plain strings (the web takes React nodes). expandIcon is required because Monarch bundles no icons, as in MonarchTreeView. The web's renderActions is the trailing actions lambda. Experimental: a domain pattern until a Rook app adopts it.
accessibility: Each goal is one TalkBack element described as its title, status, owner, meta, alignment and, when closed, its number of children; it carries its progress as a progress value with the percentage in the device locale as its state.
Quiet children have no badge but their status is still in the description, so status never depends on color or on the badge.
The open and close button is a separate element with the button role, named "Expand …" or "Collapse …", with a 48dp touch target.
The add button is named "Add key result to …" and has a 48dp touch target.
The chevron turn follows the reduced motion setting; avatars, badges and the bar are hidden inside the goal's element.
Titles wrap at the largest font scale without being cut.
edgeCases: Progress outside 0 to 1 is clamped; not-a-number reads as 0%.
Long titles wrap; badges and facts flow onto the next line.
A goal whose only child is the add button still has a toggle.
Deep trees indent by half a touch target per level; keep them to three levels on a phone.
Changing goals keeps the inside expanded set; new parents start closed unless expanded is controlled.

title: Grid
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.grid.LazyVerticalGrid with GridCells.Adaptive, androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow
summary: A responsive grid is the standard LazyVerticalGrid with GridCells.Adaptive, and a short grid inside a scrolling screen is a FlowRow, with gaps from the Monarch space scale. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: LazyVerticalGrid with GridCells.Adaptive(minSize) for card grids and tiles that can be long: as many columns as fit items of that width. GridCells.Fixed(n) for a set number of columns. FlowRow with maxItemsInEachRow and weight(1f) for a few tiles inside a screen that already scrolls.
whenNotToUse: For a single wrapping row of chips or tags use FlowRow without a column count (see inline). For a table with aligned columns, headers and sorting use a data grid.
api: @Composable fun LazyVerticalGrid(columns: GridCells, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, state: LazyGridState = rememberLazyGridState(), contentPadding: PaddingValues = PaddingValues(0.dp), reverseLayout: Boolean = false, verticalArrangement: Arrangement.Vertical = ..., horizontalArrangement: Arrangement.Horizontal = Arrangement.Start, ..., content: LazyGridScope.() -> Unit)
class GridCells.Adaptive(minSize: Dp)
class GridCells.Fixed(count: Int)

@Composable inline fun FlowRow(modifier: Modifier = Modifier, horizontalArrangement: Arrangement.Horizontal = Arrangement.Start, verticalArrangement: Arrangement.Vertical = Arrangement.Top, itemVerticalAlignment: Alignment.Vertical = Alignment.Top, maxItemsInEachRow: Int = Int.MAX_VALUE, maxLines: Int = Int.MAX_VALUE, content: @Composable FlowRowScope.() -> Unit)

states.name: empty
states.description: Show MonarchEmptyState in place of the grid.

appearance: No appearance of its own: the items are Monarch components; the gaps are steps of the space scale.
platformNotes: The web's Grid takes minItemWidth (default 16rem), column counts per breakpoint, a gap from the space scale (default 16px) and fit or fill. On Android minItemWidth is GridCells.Adaptive(minSize), which behaves like the web's fit: columns stretch to share the width. Columns per breakpoint become GridCells.Fixed with a count chosen from the window size class. The gap is horizontalArrangement and verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space4). A lazy grid cannot sit inside a vertical scroll of the same direction; FlowRow can. iOS uses LazyVGrid with adaptive GridItems.
accessibility: System behavior: TalkBack moves through the cells in reading order, row by row, and reports the collection size of a lazy grid.
Items that have not been composed are reached by scrolling, which TalkBack does as it moves.
edgeCases: A LazyVerticalGrid inside verticalScroll throws because it would be measured with infinite height; give it a bounded height or make it the screen's scrolling container.
At font scale 2.0 items grow taller; Adaptive keeps the columns, so keep minSize wide enough for the text.

name: MonarchText
title: Heading
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.Text with androidx.compose.ui.semantics.heading
summary: A heading is MonarchText in one of the heading roles (Display, Title, Heading, Subheading), which TalkBack announces as a heading. Monarch ships no separate heading type.
whenToUse: For the title of a screen, a section or a card. Choose the role by how large the heading should look; for a small heading in BodyStrong or Label pass heading = true.
whenNotToUse: For the title of a top app bar use the Material 3 TopAppBar title slot, which is already a heading for TalkBack. For running text use MonarchText in the Body role.
api: @Composable fun MonarchText(text: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, style: MonarchTextStyle = MonarchTextStyle.Body, color: Color = Color.Unspecified, textAlign: TextAlign? = null, overflow: TextOverflow = TextOverflow.Clip, softWrap: Boolean = true, maxLines: Int = Int.MAX_VALUE, minLines: Int = 1, heading: Boolean = style.isHeading)

options.name: style
options.description: The look. Display is the web size 4xl, Title 2xl, Heading xl, Subheading lg, BodyStrong base and Label sm.

options.name: heading
options.default: true for Display, Title, Heading, Subheading
options.description: Whether TalkBack announces the text as a heading. Pass true for a heading in BodyStrong or Label, false for a large text that is not a heading.

options.name: color
options.description: MonarchTheme.colors.textMuted for a secondary heading, such as the title of an empty section.

options.name: maxLines
options.description: 1 with overflow = TextOverflow.Ellipsis keeps the heading to one line.

options.name: overflow
options.description: Ellipsis ends a cut heading with an ellipsis.

states.name: muted
states.description: color = MonarchTheme.colors.textMuted.

states.name: one line
states.description: maxLines = 1 and overflow = TextOverflow.Ellipsis keep the heading to one line and end it with an ellipsis.

appearance: The heading roles use the default text color in semibold (Display in bold) with tight or snug line height and letter spacing, in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web Heading sets the outline level (h1 to h6) and the visual size separately. Compose has no heading levels: Modifier.semantics { heading() } marks a heading, and TalkBack moves between headings without a level, so the web's level is not offered (iOS adds a level with accessibilityHeading). The web sizes 3xl and 5xl have no role; Display (4xl) is the nearest. The web weight option is not offered: the role decides the weight. Tone and truncation are the color, maxLines and overflow parameters of MonarchText.
accessibility: Display, Title, Heading and Subheading set the heading semantics property, so TalkBack users can move between headings.
heading = true makes a BodyStrong or Label text a heading; heading = false removes it from a large text.
Every role is in sp and grows with the font size setting.
A heading wraps by default, so no text is lost at large sizes; a one-line heading still gives TalkBack its whole text.
edgeCases: A heading role used for a large number or a price is still announced as a heading; pass heading = false.
With maxLines = 1 and an ellipsis the cut-off part is still read by TalkBack, because the text is the whole string.
Text balancing (the web text-wrap: balance) is not available in Compose.

    heading = true,
)

parityExceptions.reason: Android semantics have one heading flag and no outline levels (h1 to h4); the type style carries the visual size.
parityExceptions.convention: Android accessibility: SemanticsPropertyReceiver.heading() marks a heading; TalkBack has no heading levels.

title: Heatmap
