summary: A matrix of values as shaded cells, such as activity by weekday and hour, with a Less to More legend.
whenToUse: To show where values cluster across two categories, such as weekday by hour or team by week.
whenNotToUse: To compare exact values, use a table or MonarchBarList. For one value per calendar day over months, use a calendar heatmap.

options.name: title
options.description: The name of the chart, shown as the frame's heading.

options.name: rows
options.description: The rows, top to bottom.

options.name: columns
options.description: The columns, start to end.

options.name: cells
options.description: The values in any order. A row and column pair without a cell is no data.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the frame.

options.name: description
options.description: One line under the title, such as the period.

options.name: status
options.description: Ready, Loading, Empty or Error. A ready chart without any value shows the empty state.

options.name: color
options.description: The data color of the levels.

options.name: thresholds
options.description: Three ascending values where levels 2, 3 and 4 start. Quarters of the largest value when null; a list of fewer than three is ignored.

options.name: showValues
options.description: Writes each value in its cell when the text fits in the cell at the current font size.

options.name: showLegend
options.description: Shows the Less to More legend under the matrix.

options.name: summary
options.description: Replaces the generated summary that TalkBack reads for the matrix.

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: The message of the empty state.

options.name: footer
options.description: Notes under the chart, such as the source.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes a value. The default is a number in the current locale.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Try again in the error status.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Runs with the tapped cell, or the cell chosen with the TalkBack Select action; its value is null when it has no data.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, including the frame's. Sentences with values are format strings with %1$s placeholders; the row and column counts are functions so they can follow the language's plural rules.

states.name: ready
states.description: Square cells in five levels: the muted background for zero, three mixes of the data color and the color itself, and an outlined cell for no data.

states.name: cell selected
states.description: A tapped cell gets a default-text outline, is marked selected for TalkBack, and its row, column and value are written under the matrix and announced politely.

states.name: values shown
states.description: Values are written in cells where the text fits; on the two strongest levels they sit on a surface chip.

states.name: table
states.description: View as table lists one row per heatmap row and one column per heatmap column, with notes.

states.name: empty
states.description: The frame's empty state, also when the chart is ready but has no value.

states.name: loading
states.description: The frame's skeleton.

states.name: error
states.description: The frame's error message, with Try again when onRetry is given.

appearance: Levels mix the chosen data color into the muted background at a quarter, half and three quarters, in Oklab, and use the color itself for the darkest step; zero is the muted background and no data is a subtle-border outline. Axis labels and the legend words are muted text; a selected cell is outlined in default text; values on strong levels sit on the surface color. The mix is computed from the theme's roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes keep five distinct steps.
platformNotes: The web Heatmap shows a tooltip on hover and moves an active cell with the arrow keys; on Android a tap selects a cell and its details are written under the matrix, and TalkBack moves through the cells row by row, each cell its own element. Cells are smaller than 48dp, so a cell is not a TalkBack button: with onSelect each cell has a Select custom action instead, while a finger taps anywhere on the matrix. iOS makes the matrix one adjustable element; Android has no equivalent that is not a slider. The web maxCellSize (36dp) and gap (2dp) are fixed here, the controlled activeCell is not offered, and the legend is not a separate public component. Column labels that would overlap are thinned to every second, third or later label. The iOS showsValues and showsLegend are showValues and showLegend, following Compose naming; the extra labels above and withNote cover text iOS builds in.
accessibility: The matrix is a traversal group whose content description is the generated summary (its size and its highest cell) or the summary given, with collection info of its rows and columns.
Every cell is a TalkBack element read as row, column and value with its note, in row order, with its row and column as collection item info, and the selected cell is marked selected.
With onSelect each cell has a Select custom action that selects it and calls onSelect.
The details of the selected cell are a polite live region that is always present, so each new selection is announced.
The legend is one element read as Legend followed by the range of each step, so the shades are not the only key.
The axis labels are hidden from TalkBack, as each cell names its row and column.
The frame title is a heading, and View as table lists every value as text.
Axis labels, values and the legend scale with the font size; the chart measures its content and grows instead of cutting it.
edgeCases: Cells for keys that are not in rows or columns are ignored.
Two cells for the same position: the later one wins.
Negative values are level 0; values that are not finite are no data.
When every value is zero or less, every threshold is zero and any positive value is level 1.
Many columns make cells narrow, down to 4dp steps; column labels are thinned so they never overlap.
Row labels take at most 35% of the width and wrap beyond it.
A value is written in its cell only when its text fits inside the cell.

title: HelpCenterHome
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column with MonarchSectionHeader, MonarchSearchBar (androidx.compose.material3.DockedSearchBar), MonarchSearchResults (a androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn of grouped results) and MonarchLink
summary: A recipe, not a component: the help home of an app on a phone, with a title, a search that filters the articles as you type, the articles grouped by category and a way to contact support.
whenToUse: For the in-app help or support home where people look for an answer before they ask.
whenNotToUse: For searching thousands of articles on a server, keep the layout but pass the server's groups to MonarchSearchResults. For a short list of questions, use the faq recipe or MonarchAccordion.
api: MonarchSectionHeader(title = "Help center", description = …, size = MonarchSectionHeaderSize.Md)
MonarchSearchBar(query = query, onQueryChange = { query = it }, onSearch = {}, placeholder = "Search articles")
MonarchSearchResults(groups = articles grouped by category, onSelect = { result, _ -> open the article }, modifier = Modifier.weight(1f), query = query)
MonarchLink(text = "Still need help? Contact support", onClick = …, variant = MonarchLinkVariant.Standalone)

options.name: articles
options.type: List of id, title and category
options.description: The published articles; group them by category, with General for those without one.

options.name: query
options.description: The search text, kept with rememberSaveable. An empty query shows every article by category.

options.name: contact
options.description: Opens the contact form or chat when nothing fits.

states.name: browse
states.description: An empty query lists every article under its category heading.

states.name: search
states.description: Articles whose title or category contain every word of the query; MonarchSearchResults says how many matched.

states.name: no results
states.description: MonarchSearchResults shows its empty state for the query; the contact link stays under it.

states.name: loading and error
states.description: Pass loading or failed with onRetry to MonarchSearchResults while the articles load from the server.

appearance: Every part is an existing Monarch component in the theme: the section header, the docked Material 3 search bar, grouped result rows and a standalone link. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from them.
platformNotes: The web ships HelpCenterHome as one pattern with columns, rows, cards and dense layouts, a page heading level, router links and an unavailable state. On a phone Android uses one list: the categories become group headings of MonarchSearchResults, which is a lazy list, so it takes the remaining height with weight(1f) rather than sitting in a scrolling column. Article links become onSelect; the app opens the article in its own screen. The web's accent-insensitive match is replaced by a plain lowercase match in the recipe; use java.text.Normalizer in the app if accents matter. For a site without a help center, show MonarchEmptyState with the contact link instead. iOS has no entry for this id yet.
accessibility: The title is a heading from MonarchSectionHeader.
The search field has the search role and the keyboard's search action from Material 3.
Category headings are headings and each article is one button with a 48dp target, from MonarchSearchResults.
The result count is announced by MonarchSearchResults as the query changes.
The contact link is a link with a 48dp target.
edgeCases: Never put MonarchSearchResults inside verticalScroll; give it the remaining height.
Articles without a category go under a General heading.
Long titles wrap in the result rows.

title: HoverCard
wrapsNative: MonarchPopover (androidx.compose.ui.window.Popup) anchored to a MonarchLink in a androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Box, holding MonarchAvatar, MonarchText and MonarchButton
summary: A recipe, not a component: a preview card for a link, such as a person or a document, opened by a tap on the link in MonarchPopover, with the details and an action.
whenToUse: When a name or a reference in a list or a sentence has details worth a glance without leaving the screen: a person's role, a document's owner and date.
whenNotToUse: When the details are the destination, open the screen instead. For a one-line explanation, use a tooltip. For actions on the item, use a dropdown or context menu.
api: @Composable fun MonarchPopover(expanded: Boolean, onDismissRequest: () -> Unit, label: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, side: MonarchPopoverSide = MonarchPopoverSide.Bottom, content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)
@Composable fun MonarchLink(text: String, onClick: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchLinkVariant = MonarchLinkVariant.Inline, …)
@Composable fun MonarchAvatar(image: Painter?, name: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, …, size: MonarchAvatarSize = MonarchAvatarSize.Md, …, decorative: Boolean = false, …)

states.name: closed
states.description: The link alone.

states.name: open
states.description: A tap opens the card under the link (or above it with MonarchPopoverSide.Top), on the raised surface.

states.name: dismissed
states.description: A tap outside or back closes it.

appearance: MonarchPopover's raised surface with the default border and shadow, holding a large avatar, the name in the strong body style, a detail line in the muted text color and a small button. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web HoverCard opens after a delay on pointer hover or keyboard focus and closes when both leave. Touch has no hover, so on Android a tap on the link opens the same content in MonarchPopover, and the link's own destination moves into the card as a button ("View profile"). If the link must keep its tap for navigation, open the card from a long press with Modifier.combinedClickable instead and say so in the link's onLongClickLabel. There is no open or close delay. iOS uses the touch-and-hold context menu with a preview.
accessibility: The link has a 48dp touch target; TalkBack reads it as a link to activate.
MonarchPopover is named by its label and closes with back; TalkBack moves into it when it opens.
The avatar is decorative because the name is in the card as text.
The action in the card is a MonarchButton with a 48dp touch target.
edgeCases: Near the bottom of the screen, use MonarchPopoverSide.Top so the card has room.
Do not put a hover card inside another popover.

name: MonarchIcon
title: Icon
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.Icon
summary: An icon at a Monarch size, in the content color. Monarch bundles no icon set.
whenToUse: For Material Symbols exported as vector drawables, or the app's own vectors.
whenNotToUse: For photos and illustrations use Image. An icon is not a button; put it in one to make it tappable.
api: @Composable fun MonarchIcon(imageVector: ImageVector, contentDescription: String?, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, size: MonarchIconSize = MonarchIconSize.Md, tint: Color = LocalContentColor.current)

@Composable fun MonarchIcon(painter: Painter, contentDescription: String?, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, size: MonarchIconSize = MonarchIconSize.Md, tint: Color = LocalContentColor.current, mirrorInRtl: Boolean = false)
enum class MonarchIconSize { Sm, Md, Lg }

name: MonarchIconButton
title: Icon button
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.clickable, androidx.compose.material3.ripple
summary: A square button that shows only an icon; the label is its TalkBack name.
whenToUse: For a toolbar or row action that an icon says well: close, more actions, refresh.
whenNotToUse: When the action needs a word to be understood use MonarchButton with an icon.

options.name: onClick

options.name: modifier

options.name: variant

options.description: To observe or drive press and focus.

options.name: icon
options.description: The icon, for example a MonarchIcon with a null content description.

states.name: resting
states.description: The fill, border and label color of the variant; primary, secondary, danger, success and warning have the xs shadow.

states.name: hovered
states.description: The hover fill of the variant (accent, danger, success or warning solid hover; muted for neutral buttons).

states.name: pressed
states.description: The pressed fill of the variant and the ripple in the label color.

states.name: focused
states.description: The Monarch focus ring, 2dp, with a 2dp gap, around the visible button.

states.name: disabled

states.name: loading
states.description: A spinner takes the place of the leading icon, or is drawn over the label when there is no icon; the button keeps its size; taps are ignored; the state is announced.

appearance: Primary is filled with the accent, danger with the danger color, success and warning with their solid roles, in every theme. Secondary is a bordered surface, ghost has no fill, danger-subtle is the tinted danger fill with a danger border, link is the link color with an underline. In the high-contrast themes the same roles resolve to stronger colors.
platformNotes: The square of the web's icon button: 32, 36 or 40dp visible with a 48dp touch target reserved around it. It replaces the Material 3 IconButton, which has no variants and a 40dp state layer.
accessibility: Has the button role and the label as its name; the icon is decoration.
The touch target is at least 48dp by 48dp and reserves that space.
While loading it keeps its name and focus place, ignores taps and announces Loading.
A disabled button is announced as disabled.
edgeCases: Pass a null content description to the icon; the label already names the button.

title: IdentityBar
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.TopAppBar with MonarchNotificationsBell, MonarchIconButton and MonarchMenu (the account-menu recipe) in its actions, and MonarchSearchBar (androidx.compose.material3.DockedSearchBar) under it
summary: A recipe, not a component: the top bar of a Rook app on a phone, with the product name as the title, notifications and the account menu as actions, and search under the bar.
whenToUse: At the top of the main screens of a Rook app, as the content of the screen's top app bar.
whenNotToUse: For a detail screen, use a TopAppBar with a back button and the record's actions (the record-header recipe). For the whole app frame with navigation, use the app-shell recipe.
api: TopAppBar(title = { Text(product, Modifier.semantics { heading() }, maxLines = 1, overflow = TextOverflow.Ellipsis) }, actions = { … })
MonarchNotificationsBell(onClick = …, unreadCount = …) { MonarchIcon(…) }
MonarchIconButton(label = "Account: …", onClick = { accountOpen = true }) { MonarchAvatar(image = …, name = …, size = MonarchAvatarSize.Sm, decorative = true) }
MonarchMenu(expanded = accountOpen, onDismissRequest = …) { MonarchMenuItem(text = …, onClick = …) }
MonarchSearchBar(query = query, onQueryChange = …, onSearch = …, placeholder = "Search …")

options.name: product
options.description: The product name, always visible, as the title; a logo goes before it in the title Row and is decorative.

options.name: notifications
options.description: MonarchNotificationsBell with the unread count; the app opens its notifications screen or sheet.

options.name: account
options.description: An avatar MonarchIconButton with a MonarchMenu (or a MonarchBottomSheet on small screens), as in the account-menu recipe.

options.name: search
options.description: MonarchSearchBar under the bar, or a search MonarchIconButton that opens the command-palette recipe.

states.name: scrolled
states.description: Pass TopAppBarDefaults.enterAlwaysScrollBehavior() to keep the bar in reach while the list scrolls, as the web's sticky option.

states.name: account menu open
states.description: The MonarchMenu lists the signed-in address, Profile and preferences, Rook account and Sign out in the danger color.

states.name: unread notifications
states.description: The bell shows the count and says it in words.

appearance: The Material 3 top app bar in the Monarch theme, with the bell, the small avatar and the docked search bar. Sign out uses the danger strong text color. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web ships IdentityBar as a sticky header with product, start, search, notifications, actions and account slots. On Android the top app bar is the banner, so the recipe fills the bar's slots instead of drawing a bar: the product is the title, notifications and the account menu are actions, and search sits under the bar because a phone's bar has no room for a field. The web's start slot (breadcrumb or space switcher) becomes the title or a title MonarchMenu; extra actions beyond two go into an overflow menu. Rook account opens in the browser from the app. iOS fills the navigation bar the same way with searchable.
accessibility: The product name is the title and a heading.
The bell is a button that says the unread count in words.
The avatar button is named Account: and the person's name; the avatar itself is decorative.
Menu items are MonarchMenuItems with 48dp targets; Sign out is in words, not color alone.
The search field has the search role from Material 3.
edgeCases: A long product name is cut with an ellipsis in the bar.
Keep at most two icon actions in the bar; move the rest to an overflow MonarchMenu.
Without a signed-in person, replace the avatar with a Sign in button.

name: MonarchImpersonationBanner
title: ImpersonationBanner
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row on the inverse surface with androidx.compose.material3.Text, android.text.format.DateUtils.getRelativeTimeSpanString and MonarchButton; placed in the topBar slot of androidx.compose.material3.Scaffold
summary: A persistent bar in inverse colors shown while acting as another person, with who, since when, why, and one way out: Stop.
whenToUse: While a support or admin person is signed in as, or viewing as, another person, and anything they do happens in that person's account.
whenNotToUse: For a read-only preview with no real actions, a MonarchCalloutBanner is enough. For ordinary notices such as a trial ending, use MonarchCalloutBanner with the page placement.
api: @Composable fun MonarchImpersonationBanner(name: String, onStop: suspend () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, detail: String? = null, reason: String? = null, startedAtMillis: Long? = null, stopping: Boolean? = null, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchImpersonationBannerLabels = MonarchImpersonationBannerLabels())

class MonarchImpersonationBannerLabels(viewingAs: ((name: String) -> String)? = null, started: String? = null, reason: String? = null, stop: String? = null, stopLabel: ((name: String) -> String)? = null, stopError: String? = null)

options.name: name
options.description: The person being viewed as, in bold in the main line.

options.name: onStop
options.description: Ends the session. Stop is busy while it runs and ignores taps; throwing shows the stop error in the banner.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the banner.

options.name: detail
options.description: A second identifier, such as their email, in brackets after the name in the muted inverse color.

options.name: reason
options.description: Why the session started, such as a ticket number, after "Reason:".

options.name: startedAtMillis
options.description: When the session started, in epoch milliseconds (UTC), shown as "Started 5 minutes ago" and refreshed every minute.

options.name: stopping
options.description: The busy state of Stop when the app tracks the stop itself; tracked from onStop when null.

options.name: icon
options.description: An icon at the start in the solid warning color, hidden from TalkBack. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the main line, "Started", "Reason:", "Stop", its TalkBack name and the stop error.

states.name: active
states.description: The main line, the start and reason line, and Stop.

states.name: stopping
states.description: Stop shows its progress indicator, reads "Loading" and ignores taps.

states.name: error
states.description: "Couldn’t stop. Try again." under the text in the danger strong inverse color, announced; the banner stays.

states.name: large text
states.description: From font scale 1.5 Stop moves under the text and fills the width.

appearance: The inverse background with inverse text, the muted inverse text for the detail and the meta line, and a 4dp edge and icon in the solid warning color, so it looks unlike every other banner in light, dark and both high-contrast themes. Stop is a small secondary MonarchButton. Errors use the danger strong inverse role.
platformNotes: The web's sticky prop and iOS's safeAreaInset placement become the topBar slot of a Scaffold on Android, after the TopAppBar. The web's now and locale props are not needed: the relative time uses the system clock and DateUtils. onStop is a suspend function run in the banner's coroutine scope, as iOS runs an async closure. A failed stop always shows the stop error from labels: Android exception messages are not written for people, so the thrown message is not shown. A replacement main line from labels is shown without bold, as on iOS. The parity map names MonarchBanner and lists callout-banner; the banner is drawn on its own instead, because its inverse colors, warning edge and missing dismiss button are what set it apart, as on the web and iOS. Monarch bundles no icons, so the eye icon is a slot.
accessibility: The icon is decorative; the main line and the start and reason line are one TalkBack element.
The main line is announced once through a polite live region when the banner appears.
Stop is named "Stop viewing as" and the name, has a 48dp touch target and reads "Loading" while stopping.
A failed stop is shown as text and announced through the same polite live region.
There is no dismiss button: the only way out is to stop.
edgeCases: Long names, details and reasons wrap.
The app removes the banner when the session ends; a successful onStop does not hide it by itself.
With stopping set, taps while it is true are ignored even if onStop has returned.
A stop cancelled because the banner left the screen is not shown as a failure.

examples.title: Viewing as a person

MonarchImpersonationBanner(
    name = {{name}},
    onStop = { delay(800) },
    detail = {{detail}},
    reason = {{reason}},
    startedAtMillis = System.currentTimeMillis() - {{startedMinutesAgo}} * 60_000L,
)
examples.code:
MonarchImpersonationBanner(

    onStop = { delay(800) },
    detail = "sam@example.com",
    reason = "Case 4821",
    startedAtMillis = System.currentTimeMillis() - 12 * 60_000L,
)

title: ImportWizard
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column holding MonarchStepper, MonarchFileUpload (androidx.activity.result.contract.ActivityResultContracts.OpenDocument underneath), MonarchColumnMapping, MonarchPreviewRows, MonarchProgress and MonarchBanner; android.content.ContentResolver.openInputStream to read the file
summary: A recipe, not a component: import records from a CSV file in four steps (upload, map columns to fields, preview every row with its problems, import and report) composed from MonarchStepper, MonarchFileUpload, MonarchColumnMapping, MonarchPreviewRows, MonarchProgress and MonarchBanner.
whenToUse: When people bring their own records from a spreadsheet or another product: contacts, products, leads, transactions.
whenNotToUse: For adding one record, use a form. For files that are kept as attachments rather than read, use MonarchFileUpload alone.
api: @Composable fun MonarchStepper(steps: List<MonarchStepperStep>, current: Int, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, …)

@Composable fun MonarchFileUpload(onFiles: (accepted: List<MonarchPickedFile>, rejected: List<MonarchFileRejection>) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, …, accept: List<String> = emptyList(), maxSize: Long? = null, maxFiles: Int? = null, …, hint: String? = null, errorText: String? = null, …)

@Composable public fun MonarchColumnMapping(sources: List<MonarchColumnMappingSource>, mapping: Map<String, String>, fields: List<MonarchColumnMappingField>, onMappingChange: (Map<String, String>) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, …, showIssues: Boolean = true, …)

fun MonarchColumnMappingDefaults.suggest(sources: List<MonarchColumnMappingSource>, fields: List<MonarchColumnMappingField>, threshold: Double = DEFAULT_THRESHOLD): Map<String, MonarchColumnMappingSuggestion>
fun MonarchColumnMappingDefaults.issues(mapping: Map<String, String>, fields: List<MonarchColumnMappingField>): MonarchColumnMappingIssues

@Composable fun MonarchPreviewRows(rows: List<MonarchPreviewRow>, columns: List<MonarchPreviewRowsColumn>, label: String, filter: MonarchPreviewRowStatus?, onFilterChange: (MonarchPreviewRowStatus?) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, …)
@Composable fun MonarchProgress(modifier: Modifier = Modifier, progress: Float? = null, variant: MonarchProgressVariant = MonarchProgressVariant.Linear, label: String? = null)

@Composable fun MonarchBanner(message: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, tone: MonarchTone = MonarchTone.Info, title: String? = null, …, announcement: MonarchBannerAnnouncement = MonarchBannerAnnouncement.None)

states.name: upload
states.description: The stepper on Upload and MonarchFileUpload for one CSV file; a file without data rows shows the error on the Browse files button.

states.name: map
states.description: MonarchColumnMapping with the suggested mapping; Check rows shows the missing required fields and duplicates, and moves on only when there are none.

states.name: preview
states.description: MonarchPreviewRows with every row's status and problems, filterable by status; the import button names how many rows will be imported and is disabled when none can be.

states.name: importing
states.description: An indeterminate MonarchProgress with "Importing 12 rows"; Back and Import are disabled.

states.name: results
states.description: A success MonarchBanner with the counts, announced politely, and Import another file.

appearance: Monarch parts on the screen's surface: the stepper with the current step in the accent, the dashed upload zone, the mapping list, the preview list with status badges in their tones, a linear progress bar and a success banner. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ImportWizard is one component with built-in CSV parsing, a duplicate-rule choice, a template download, paging in the preview, a downloadable problems CSV and a report of created, updated, skipped and failed rows. On Android it is a recipe the app owns: MonarchFileUpload opens the system document picker, the app reads the file through the ContentResolver off the main thread with its own CSV or spreadsheet reader, runs its own validation and import, and writes counts with plurals resources. A duplicate rule, when needed, is a radio group or segmented buttons on the preview step; the problems file is written with ActivityResultContracts.CreateDocument. The web's mapping is field to column; MonarchColumnMapping keeps column to field. Steps that hold MonarchColumnMapping and MonarchPreviewRows give them the remaining height, because both are lazy lists. There is no iOS entry yet.
accessibility: Each MonarchStepper step is one element read with its position, such as "Step 2 of 4, Map columns", and its state.
MonarchFileUpload's Browse files button opens the system picker; errorText is the button's error and is shown under the zone.
MonarchColumnMapping labels each picker "Field for <column>"; the missing-fields message is an error and a polite live region.
MonarchPreviewRows reads each row with its outcome, values and problems; the filter tabs read their name with the count.
MonarchProgress is named "Importing 12 rows"; the result banner is a polite live region, so the result is announced without moving focus.
edgeCases: Read the file on Dispatchers.IO; a large file read on the main thread freezes the screen.
A file with only a header row is refused on the upload step with a message, not on the preview step.
Splitting lines on commas breaks quoted fields that contain commas; a real import uses a CSV reader.
Rows with errors are skipped and counted, so the import button names only the rows that will be saved.
Going back from the preview keeps the mapping, so a fix to one column does not lose the others.

name: MonarchInboxRow
title: InboxRow
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.ListItem, androidx.compose.material3.SwipeToDismissBox and androidx.compose.foundation.combinedClickable, with MonarchAvatar
summary: One conversation in an inbox list: avatar, name, compact age, a one-line preview, badges, an unread dot or count, selection for bulk actions and swipe actions.
whenToUse: As the row of a LazyColumn of conversations, tickets or threads.
whenNotToUse: Not for a notification feed item; use the notifications components. Not for a plain settings row; use a Material 3 ListItem.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchInboxRow(title: String, onClick: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, unread: Boolean = false, unreadCount: Int? = null, selected: Boolean = false, selecting: Boolean = false, preview: String? = null, timestamp: Long? = null, now: Long? = null, avatarName: String? = null, avatarImage: Painter? = null, showAvatar: Boolean = true, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, iconLabel: String? = null, onSelectedChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, swipeActions: List<MonarchInboxRowSwipeAction> = emptyList(), labels: MonarchInboxRowLabels = MonarchInboxRowLabels(), interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null, badges: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null, trailing: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null)
public sealed class MonarchInboxRowSwipeAction { abstract val onAction: () -> Unit; class ToggleRead(onAction: () -> Unit); class Archive(onAction: () -> Unit); class Delete(onAction: () -> Unit) }
public enum class MonarchInboxRowAgeUnit { Now, Minutes, Hours, Days, Weeks }

public class MonarchInboxRowLabels(unread: ((Int?) -> String)? = null, age: ((MonarchInboxRowAgeUnit, Int) -> String)? = null, select: String? = null, markRead: String? = null, markUnread: String? = null, archive: String? = null, delete: String? = null)

options.name: title
options.description: Who or what the conversation is with. Cut to one line.

options.name: onClick
options.description: Opens the conversation.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the row.

options.name: unread
options.description: An accent dot before a semibold title, and the age in the default text color.

options.name: unreadCount
options.description: A count capsule at the end of the first line instead of the dot, 99+ above 99. A count above zero makes the row unread.

options.name: selected
options.description: Selected for bulk actions: the accent subtle background and a checked checkbox.

options.name: selecting
options.description: The list is in selection mode: a tap selects instead of opening, and the checkbox replaces the avatar.

options.name: preview
options.description: The latest message or a summary, cut to one line.

options.name: timestamp
options.description: When the conversation last changed, in epoch milliseconds (UTC).

options.name: now
options.description: The current time for the age, for tests. null uses the clock, refreshed every minute.

options.name: avatarName
options.description: The name for the avatar's initials and color; the title by default.

options.name: avatarImage
options.description: The avatar picture, loaded by the app. null shows initials.

options.name: showAvatar
options.description: Shows the 32dp avatar.

options.name: icon
options.description: A small decorative icon after the title, such as the channel.

options.name: iconLabel
options.description: The spoken description of the icon, "via email".

options.name: onSelectedChange
options.description: Makes the row selectable by a long press, and by a tap while selecting.

options.name: swipeActions
options.description: ToggleRead runs when swiping toward the end; Archive, or Delete without Archive, when swiping toward the start. All are TalkBack actions.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, including the age units.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The interaction source of the row.

options.name: badges
options.description: Markers on the last line, such as MonarchBadge.

options.name: trailing
options.description: The end of the last line: a reference number or the assignee's avatar.

states.name: read
states.description: Regular title, muted age, no mark.

states.name: unread
states.description: An accent dot before a semibold title, and the age semibold in the default text color.

states.name: unread count
states.description: An accent capsule with the count, or 99+, at the end of the first line instead of the dot.

states.name: selected
states.description: The accent subtle background; with selecting or selected, a checkbox replaces the avatar.

states.name: swiping
states.description: The row slides over a coloured band naming the action: info for read, accent for archive, danger for delete. Past the threshold the action runs and the row springs back.

appearance: The row on the surface color; title in the default text color, preview and age in the muted text color, the unread dot and count in the accent solid color with its on-solid text. Swipe bands use the info, accent and danger solid colors with their on-solid text. The same roles in every theme.
platformNotes: The web row is a link with an href, an open-conversation state (aria-current) and a keyboard cursor. On Android the row calls onClick and the app navigates; the highlight of the conversation open in a list-detail layout is the app's, as on iOS. Bulk selection follows Android: a long press selects (the web uses a checkbox on the avatar and long-press on touch), and selecting turns taps into selection. Swipe actions follow Material's SwipeToDismissBox, which offers one action per direction: ToggleRead toward the end, Archive (or Delete without Archive) toward the start; iOS offers all three in the swipe, so on Android Delete next to Archive is reached through TalkBack actions or the app's own menu. The age units are overridable together through labels.age; the short date uses android.icu skeletons in the device's locale and time zone.
accessibility: The row is one TalkBack element read as the title with the unread state and channel ("Ana, 3 unread, via email"), the full date and time, the preview, then the badges and trailing content.
The compact age is replaced by the full date and time for TalkBack.
The unread dot and count are hidden; the state is spoken after the title, and shown by a semibold title, so it does not depend on color.
Swipe actions are also TalkBack actions named "Read" or "Unread", "Archive" and "Delete".
With onSelectedChange the row has the selected state and a long-click action named "Select".
The avatar and the icon are decorative; the icon is read only through iconLabel.
The row is at least 56dp high and grows with the font size setting.
edgeCases: A time in the future reads as now.
Counts above 99 show 99+, while TalkBack reads the exact number.
A count of zero with unread false is a read row.
Older than 30 days shows a short date, with the year when it is not the current year.
The title and preview are cut to one line each; badges and trailing content share the last line.

examples.title: Inbox with selection
Swipe to mark read or archive, long-press to select
examples.setup:
var unread by remember { mutableStateOf(true) }
var selected by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
examples.code:
MonarchInboxRow(
    title = "Ben Okafor",
    onClick = {},
    unread = unread,
    selected = selected,
    onSelectedChange = { selected = it },
    swipeActions = listOf(
        MonarchInboxRowSwipeAction.ToggleRead { unread = !unread },
        MonarchInboxRowSwipeAction.Archive { /* Archive the conversation. */ },
    ),
)

name: MonarchIncidentTimeline
title: IncidentTimeline
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column, Row and FlowRow drawn as a timeline; MonarchStatusBadge for stages, MonarchTag for Automated; android.icu.text.DateFormat for times
summary: The story of one incident: each update with its stage (investigating, identified, monitoring, resolved), time and text, joined by a line, with system-posted updates tagged Automated.
whenToUse: On a status page or an incident detail screen, to show the updates posted during one incident in order.
whenNotToUse: For the history of any record, use MonarchActivityTimeline; for the uptime of a service over days, use MonarchUptimeBar; for the current status alone, a MonarchStatusBadge.
api: @Composable fun MonarchIncidentTimeline(updates: List<MonarchIncidentUpdate>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, stages: Map<String, MonarchStatusDefinition> = emptyMap(), density: MonarchIncidentTimelineDensity = MonarchIncidentTimelineDensity.Regular, live: Boolean = false, timeZone: String? = "UTC", labels: MonarchIncidentTimelineLabels = MonarchIncidentTimelineLabels())

class MonarchIncidentUpdate(id: String, stage: String, body: String, time: Long, automated: Boolean = false, author: String? = null) { constructor(id: String, stage: MonarchIncidentStage, body: String, time: Long, automated: Boolean = false, author: String? = null) }
enum class MonarchIncidentStage(val key: String) { Investigating, Identified, Monitoring, Resolved }
enum class MonarchIncidentTimelineDensity { Regular, Compact }

class MonarchIncidentTimelineLabels(list: String? = null, automated: String? = null, empty: String? = null, investigating: String? = null, identified: String? = null, monitoring: String? = null, resolved: String? = null)

options.name: updates
options.description: The updates in the order to show them, usually oldest first. Each has an id, a stage key, the text (line breaks kept), the time (epoch milliseconds, UTC), whether the system posted it and an optional author.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the timeline.

options.name: stages
options.description: Product stages by key, or overrides of the label and tone of the standard ones. Looked up before the standard stages.

options.name: density
options.description: Compact tightens the space between updates for cards and side panels.

options.name: live
options.description: Announces an update added while the timeline is shown, for a page that refreshes while someone reads it.

options.name: timeZone
options.description: The zone of the times. UTC by default, so every reader quotes the same time; the zone name is shown. An IANA id such as Europe/Berlin; null, or an id the device does not know, is the device's zone.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the group name, the Automated tag, the empty text and the four standard stage labels.

states.name: investigating
states.description: Danger tone badge and dot, "Investigating".

states.name: identified
states.description: Warning tone badge and dot, "Identified".

states.name: monitoring
states.description: Info tone badge and dot, "Monitoring".

states.name: resolved
states.description: Success tone badge and dot, "Resolved".

states.name: product stage
states.description: A key from stages uses its label and tone; an unknown key is made readable ("partial_outage" is "Partial outage") with the neutral tone and a strong border dot.

states.name: automated
states.description: An update the system posted carries an "Automated" tag after the time.

states.name: empty
states.description: No updates shows "No updates posted yet" in the muted text color.

appearance: Each update has a 12dp dot in its stage tone's solid color (the strong border for neutral) on a 2dp line in the default border color, a small status badge, the time and author as muted caption text, a small tag for automated updates and the text as body text. Every color is a theme role, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes are covered.
platformNotes: The parity map names a LazyColumn; the timeline is a Column instead, as on iOS, because an incident has a few dozen updates at most and a Column can sit inside the app's scrolling status page without a fixed height (a LazyColumn cannot be nested in a vertical scroll). An app with very long incidents can show them page by page. The web accepts rich content for the body and author and a footer slot; here they are strings, and the app places its own form under the timeline. The web formats times with Intl in UTC; Android uses the ICU skeleton MMMdHHmmz (month, day, 24-hour time and the zone name) in the device locale and the given zone, so the characters can differ slightly from the web. Stage tones are given as MonarchStatusDefinition, the same type the status badge uses. iOS uses the same names, except live (iOS isLive), automated (iOS isAutomated) and the PascalCase enum constants; MonarchIncidentStage has a key property for the web's string keys.
accessibility: The updates are one group named "Incident updates".
Each update is one element read as the stage, the time, the author and "Automated", then the text, such as "Identified, Mar 4, 15:15 UTC, Ada. A migration locked a table."
The stage is a word in a badge as well as a color; dots and the line are hidden from TalkBack.
With live, an update added while the timeline is shown is announced with the same text through a polite live region that is always present.
Text wraps at font scale 2.0 and the dot column grows with the font scale.
edgeCases: Updates are shown in the order given; the timeline does not sort them.
Stage keys are matched to the standard stages ignoring case; product keys in stages are matched exactly and win.
An empty body shows only the header line.
Removing updates or replacing the list with a shorter one announces nothing.
Times use the device locale's month and day names with a 24-hour clock.

title: IncomingCall
wrapsNative: androidx.core.app.NotificationCompat.CallStyle.forIncomingCall(androidx.core.app.Person, android.app.PendingIntent, android.app.PendingIntent), posted with androidx.core.app.NotificationManagerCompat
summary: An incoming call is a call-style notification that the system shows as a heads-up or full-screen ringing screen, on the lock screen too. Monarch ships no ringing banner; while the app is in the foreground it may show MonarchBanner instead.
whenToUse: Whenever the app receives a call: post a NotificationCompat.CallStyle.forIncomingCall notification in the call channel, with a full-screen intent for the lock screen. While the app is open, a MonarchBanner with Decline and Answer can be shown in addition.
whenNotToUse: Do not draw a custom ringing screen or rely on an in-app banner alone: it cannot ring on the lock screen or while the app is in the background. For a message that is not a call, use an ordinary notification.
api: NotificationCompat.CallStyle.forIncomingCall(person: Person, declineIntent: PendingIntent, answerIntent: PendingIntent): NotificationCompat.CallStyle
NotificationCompat.Builder(context: Context, channelId: String).setStyle(style).setCategory(NotificationCompat.CATEGORY_CALL).setFullScreenIntent(intent: PendingIntent, highPriority: Boolean)
NotificationManagerCompat.from(context: Context).notify(id: Int, notification: Notification)

options.name: person
options.description: The caller, with a name and optionally an icon.

options.name: declineIntent
options.description: What Decline does: end the call in the app's call service.

options.name: answerIntent
options.description: What Answer does: open the call screen and connect.

states.name: heads-up
states.description: While the phone is in use, the system shows the call at the top of the screen with Decline and Answer.

states.name: full screen
states.description: On the lock screen, the full-screen intent opens the app's ringing activity.

states.name: in-app banner
states.description: While the app is in the foreground, a MonarchBanner with Decline and Answer may also be shown.

appearance: The notification is drawn by the system in its own colors. The in-app banner is a MonarchBanner in the info tone with a primary Answer and a danger Decline button, in every Monarch theme.
platformNotes: The web IncomingCall is a banner with Decline and Answer that the product places and rings itself. On Android the system owns the ringing: a call-style notification, as iOS uses CallKit. androidx.core.telecom (CallsManager, for Bluetooth and car audio routing) is not a Monarch dependency; the app adds it if it needs it. "Answer with audio only" for a video call has no counterpart in CallStyle; the app can add an action.
accessibility: System behavior: the call notification and the ringing screen are accessible, announce the caller and work with TalkBack.
The in-app banner is a polite live region, so TalkBack announces the call; its buttons have 48dp touch targets.
edgeCases: From Android 13 posting needs the POST_NOTIFICATIONS permission, and from Android 14 a full-screen intent needs USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT; check both before posting.
Create the call notification channel with high importance before posting; on Android 8 and later the channel sets the sound and the heads-up.
A call-style notification must be shown from a foreground service of type phoneCall, or use a full-screen intent, or the system shows it as an ordinary notification.
The example and the catalogue page were compiled and composed; the notification was not posted on a device.

examples.title: Audio call
Post the incoming call notification
examples.setup: val context = LocalContext.current
examples.code:
MonarchButton(
    text = "Simulate an incoming call",
    onClick = {
        val manager = NotificationManagerCompat.from(context)
        manager.createNotificationChannel(
            NotificationChannelCompat.Builder("calls", NotificationManagerCompat.IMPORTANCE_HIGH)
                .setName("Calls")
                .build(),
        )
        // The app's call activity; here the app's launch screen stands in for it.
        val open = PendingIntent.getActivity(
            context,
            0,
            Intent(Intent.ACTION_MAIN).setPackage(context.packageName),
            PendingIntent.FLAG_IMMUTABLE,
        )
        val caller = Person.Builder().setName("Ana Flores").setImportant(true).build()
        val notification = NotificationCompat.Builder(context, "calls")
            // Here the app icon; a real app passes its monochrome notification icon, R.drawable.….
            .setSmallIcon(context.applicationInfo.icon)
            .setStyle(NotificationCompat.CallStyle.forIncomingCall(caller, open, open))
            .setCategory(NotificationCompat.CATEGORY_CALL)
            .setFullScreenIntent(open, true)
            .build()
        val allowed = Build.VERSION.SDK_INT < Build.VERSION_CODES.TIRAMISU ||
            ContextCompat.checkSelfPermission(context, Manifest.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS) ==
            PackageManager.PERMISSION_GRANTED
        if (allowed) manager.notify(1, notification)
    },
    variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Primary,
)

title: InfoTooltip
wrapsNative: MonarchPopover (a Compose Popup) anchored to a MonarchIconButton, opened by its onClick
summary: The small info button next to a label that opens a short explanation is a MonarchPopover anchored to a MonarchIconButton, shown when the button is tapped and kept until the person taps elsewhere. Monarch ships no separate type.
whenToUse: Next to a field label or a metric whose meaning needs a sentence or two, such as how a score is calculated.
whenNotToUse: For text the person needs to fill in a field, use the field's helper text, which is always visible. For a name of an icon button, use a PlainTooltip (see tooltip). For interactive content such as a form, use MonarchPopover.
api: @Composable fun MonarchPopover(expanded: Boolean, onDismissRequest: () -> Unit, label: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, side: MonarchPopoverSide = MonarchPopoverSide.Bottom, content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)

@Composable fun MonarchIconButton(label: String, onClick: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchButtonVariant = MonarchButtonVariant.Ghost, size: MonarchButtonSize = MonarchButtonSize.Md, enabled: Boolean = true, loading: Boolean = false, loadingLabel: String? = null, shape: Shape? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null, icon: @Composable () -> Unit)

states.name: closed
states.description: Only the info button is shown, in the default icon color.

states.name: open
states.description: A tap shows the rich tooltip above the button, with a title and the explanation; with isPersistent it stays until a tap outside or back.

states.name: long press
states.description: Only a tap opens it; there is no hover on touch screens, and a long press is left to the system.

appearance: The popover on the raised surface with a hairline border and the presented shadow, the title in the default text color and the explanation in the muted text color. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web InfoTooltip is a toggletip on Popover that keeps focus on the button and copies its text into a live region. On Android the toggletip is a MonarchPopover opened from the button's onClick: it takes focus, so TalkBack moves into it, announces its label and returns to the button when it closes. The web's side becomes MonarchPopoverSide; the popover moves to the other side when there is no room. Monarch bundles no icons, so the info glyph comes from the app (the example uses SampleIcons.Info). The parity map named the native tooltip, and iOS builds a MonarchInfoTooltip on its popover; Android needs no wrapper because MonarchPopover already has the anchored, dismissible, rich form.
accessibility: The button is a MonarchIconButton with a 48dp touch target and a content description that names what it explains, such as "About visibility score".
With focusable = true the tooltip takes focus when it opens, so TalkBack reads the title and the explanation; back or a tap outside closes it.
The popover takes focus when it opens, so TalkBack reads its label and content and returns to the button when it closes.
The explanation wraps within the tooltip's maximum width at large font sizes.
edgeCases: Use one rememberTooltipState per button; tooltips share a MutatorMutex, so opening one closes another.
Keep the explanation short; a tooltip that needs scrolling should be a sheet or a help screen.

title: Inline
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow with Arrangement.spacedBy
summary: A horizontal row that wraps onto new rows when its children do not fit is the standard FlowRow, with spacing from the Monarch space scale. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: For rows of buttons, tags, badges or metadata that must not overflow a narrow screen or a large font size.
whenNotToUse: For a row that must stay on one line use a Row (with weights, or horizontalScroll for overflow). For a grid of equal tiles use LazyVerticalGrid (see grid).
api: @Composable inline fun FlowRow(modifier: Modifier = Modifier, horizontalArrangement: Arrangement.Horizontal = Arrangement.Start, verticalArrangement: Arrangement.Vertical = Arrangement.Top, itemVerticalAlignment: Alignment.Vertical = Alignment.Top, maxItemsInEachRow: Int = Int.MAX_VALUE, maxLines: Int = Int.MAX_VALUE, content: @Composable FlowRowScope.() -> Unit)
fun Arrangement.spacedBy(space: Dp, alignment: Alignment.Horizontal): Arrangement.Horizontal
appearance: No appearance of its own: the children are Monarch components; the gaps are steps of the space scale.
platformNotes: The web's Inline is a flex row with wrap, a gap, align and justify. On Android the gap is horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(space) for the gap between items and verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(space) for the gap between rows; align is itemVerticalAlignment; justify is the alignment argument of spacedBy (Alignment.CenterHorizontally, Alignment.End). The web's wrap={false} is a Row. FlowRow mirrors in a right-to-left layout. iOS has no wrapping stack and builds MonarchFlowLayout; Android uses the platform FlowRow and ships nothing.
accessibility: System behavior: TalkBack reads the children in order, row by row, starting at the start edge.
At font scale 2.0 children wrap onto more rows instead of being cut.
edgeCases: A child wider than the row takes a row of its own and is measured at the full width.
FlowRow is experimental in some Compose versions; Monarch's examples opt in to ExperimentalLayoutApi.

name: MonarchInlineCodeStyle
title: InlineCode
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.ui.text.SpanStyle in an androidx.compose.ui.text.AnnotatedString, drawn by androidx.compose.material3.Text
summary: The look of a code fragment inside running text, as a SpanStyle of an AnnotatedString: the code typeface at 0.9 of the surrounding size, on the muted background (Subtle) or without one (Plain).
whenToUse: For a function name, a path, a command or a value to type inside a sentence. Use markdown for text with backticks, annotatedString for a single fragment, spanStyle with buildAnnotatedString for anything else.
whenNotToUse: For a block of code on its own lines use MonarchText in the Code role. For a keyboard shortcut use MonarchKbd.
api: object MonarchInlineCodeStyle
fun spanStyle(colors: MonarchColors, typography: MonarchTypography, variant: MonarchInlineCodeVariant = MonarchInlineCodeVariant.Subtle): SpanStyle
@Composable @ReadOnlyComposable fun spanStyle(variant: MonarchInlineCodeVariant = MonarchInlineCodeVariant.Subtle): SpanStyle
@Composable @ReadOnlyComposable fun annotatedString(code: String, variant: MonarchInlineCodeVariant = MonarchInlineCodeVariant.Subtle): AnnotatedString
@Composable @ReadOnlyComposable fun markdown(text: String, variant: MonarchInlineCodeVariant = MonarchInlineCodeVariant.Subtle): AnnotatedString
enum class MonarchInlineCodeVariant { Subtle, Plain }

options.name: variant
options.description: Subtle draws the muted background behind the code and uses the default text color; Plain only switches to the code typeface and keeps the surrounding color.

options.name: code
options.description: In annotatedString, the code fragment.

options.name: text
options.description: In markdown, the text with backticks around the code.

options.name: colors, typography
options.description: In the non-composable spanStyle, the theme to take the roles from, for code outside composition.

appearance: Subtle: the code typeface in the default text color on the muted background. Plain: the code typeface in the color of the surrounding text. Both follow light, dark and both high-contrast themes when built inside composition.
platformNotes: The web InlineCode is an element; in Compose running text is one Text, so Monarch provides a span style and helpers that build AnnotatedString runs, as iOS builds AttributedString runs. Text draws the background flush with the characters: the padding and rounded corners of the web chip are not available. The code is 0.9em of the surrounding text, as on the web (iOS uses the full size). The web nowrap option is not offered; a long token breaks where it does not fit. The parity map named MonarchTypography; it has a Code role for whole texts but nothing for a run inside a sentence, so the style is shipped under the iOS name MonarchInlineCodeStyle.
accessibility: The code run is part of the text and TalkBack reads it in place, as its characters.
Code differs from the text around it by the monospaced face, so it is recognisable without the background color, also in the Plain variant.
The size is relative (0.9em), so the code grows with the surrounding text and the font size setting.
edgeCases: A SpanStyle holds resolved colors. Build it in composition from the theme so that it follows light, dark and high contrast; the non-composable spanStyle takes the theme's colors explicitly.
markdown reads backticks only. An unmatched backtick and the text after it are shown unchanged; an empty pair of backticks is removed.
Ligatures are turned off in the code run, so -> and != are shown as typed.
A long token such as a hash wraps where it does not fit a line.

name: MonarchInlineEditText
title: InlineEditText
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedTextField (through MonarchTextField) and androidx.compose.material3.Button (through MonarchButton), switched in place from androidx.compose.material3.Text
summary: Text that turns into a field in place, with an asynchronous save, a saving state and an error that keeps the editor open.
whenToUse: For renaming or correcting one value where it is shown: a document title, a name in a header, a note on a detail screen.
whenNotToUse: For a form of several fields that are saved together use MonarchTextField with a save button. For text that is edited all the time use a field that is always shown.
api: @Composable fun MonarchInlineEditText(value: String, onSave: suspend (String) -> Unit, label: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, placeholder: String? = null, errorText: String? = null, enabled: Boolean = true, multiline: Boolean = false, startEditing: Boolean = false, trim: Boolean = true, saveOnFocusLoss: Boolean = true, validate: ((String) -> String?)? = null, errorMessage: ((Throwable) -> String?)? = null, onCancel: (() -> Unit)? = null, onEditingChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, editIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchInlineEditTextLabels = MonarchInlineEditTextLabels())
class MonarchInlineEditTextLabels(editHint: String? = null, save: String? = null, cancel: String? = null, saving: String? = null, saveFailed: String? = null)

options.name: value
options.description: The saved text.

options.name: onSave
options.description: Saves the new text and updates value. Throw to keep the editor open with the error and the draft. Not called when the trimmed text is unchanged.

options.name: label
options.description: What the text is, for example "Title": the field's label, and the spoken name in view mode.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the component.

options.name: placeholder
options.description: Shown in view mode while the value is empty, and as the field's placeholder.

options.name: errorText
options.description: An error from the app, such as an edit conflict, shown while editing.

options.name: enabled
options.description: When false the value is plain text in the disabled color and cannot be edited.

options.name: multiline
options.description: A field of several lines: Enter adds a line, Save or Ctrl or Cmd with Enter saves.

options.name: startEditing
options.description: Opens the editor when the component first appears.

options.name: trim
options.description: Trims the text before comparing and saving.

options.name: saveOnFocusLoss
options.description: Saves when focus leaves the field.

options.name: validate
options.description: Returns a message to refuse the text before saving.

options.name: errorMessage
options.description: Turns a failed save into a message. By default the exception's message, or "Couldn't save. Try again."

options.name: onCancel
options.description: Called when the user cancels with the button or Escape.

options.name: onEditingChange
options.description: Called when the editor opens or closes.

options.name: editIcon
options.description: An icon after the text in view mode, such as a pencil. Decoration; Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for "Edit", "Save", "Cancel", "Saving" and "Couldn't save. Try again."

states.name: viewing
states.description: The value in the default text color, or the placeholder in the subtle color, with the optional icon.

states.name: editing
states.description: A MonarchTextField with the focus ring color, and Save (primary) and Cancel (ghost) buttons under it.

states.name: saving
states.description: The field is disabled, Save shows progress with the state "Saving" and Cancel is disabled.

states.name: error
states.description: The field's danger outline and the message under it. The draft is kept.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Plain text in the disabled color that cannot be edited.

appearance: In view mode the text uses the body style in the default text color, the subtle color for the placeholder and the disabled color when disabled; the icon is muted. In edit mode it is MonarchTextField with small MonarchButtons. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: On the web, Enter saves and Escape cancels and the buttons are optional for one line. A touch keyboard has no Escape key, so, as on iOS, Save and Cancel are always shown; Done saves one line and a hardware Escape still cancels. The web shows a spinner inside the field; here the Save button shows the progress. The saved value is hoisted: onSave stores it and the app passes the new value, in place of the web's controlled and uncontrolled value. The web's controlled editing state is reduced to startEditing with an onEditingChange callback, and onSaveError is the exception thrown by onSave, which the app can catch in its own code. The web's rows and maxLength are not offered; a multi-line field grows with its text. The system back gesture does not cancel; it is left to the screen.
accessibility: In view mode it is one button: the label as its name, the value (or the placeholder) as its state, and "Edit" as the action TalkBack announces.
In edit mode the field has the same label and takes focus; an error is the field's error, shown as text and a danger outline, not color alone.
While saving, the Save button's state is "Saving" and the field and Cancel are disabled.
The text in view mode and the buttons are at least 48dp high; text scales with the font size setting.
The icon is hidden from TalkBack.
edgeCases: Leaving the field to tap Save or Cancel does not save twice: a save that is running ignores further requests.
A save that fails gives focus back to the field.
With trim, a value that only gained spaces is unchanged and closes without saving.
Disabling the component while it is editing shows the value as plain text; the draft is kept for when it is enabled again.

options.name: retryLabel
options.description: The button label. null uses monarch_inlineerrorretry_retry, "Try again".

options.name: retryingLabel
options.description: The button state while retrying. null uses monarch_inlineerrorretry_retrying, "Retrying".

states.name: failed
states.description: The message and the retry button.

states.name: retrying
states.description: A progress indicator in the button, which ignores taps and reports "Retrying" as its state.

states.name: banner
states.description: The subtle background and border of the tone around the row.

appearance: The message is default text; the icon takes the strong color of the tone. The banner variant adds the subtle background and border of the tone with 12dp corners. The button is a small secondary MonarchButton. The same roles in every theme.
platformNotes: The busy state is always controlled with retrying; the web can also track a promise returned by onRetry. The web actions slot and returnFocusTo are not offered: when the row is replaced by content, TalkBack focus follows the system's rules. Any MonarchTone is accepted, where the web allows danger and warning. The message is a polite live region, where the web uses role=alert. The web retry glyph in the button is not drawn, because Monarch bundles no icons. iOS posts "Retrying" as an announcement when the retry starts; here it is the state of the button, read when the button has TalkBack focus. The spoken tone name comes from the shared Monarch tone names (Information, Success, Warning, Error, AI), the same words as iOS. Deprecated (D7): the component's own string keys monarch_inlineerrorretry_tone_info, _success, _warning and _danger are now aliases of the shared names. An app that redefines one still gets its text, but they are removed no earlier than 2027-02-13 (90-day window, two patch releases); override the shared monarch_internal_tone_* names or pass toneLabel instead.
accessibility: The tone name and the message are one TalkBack element, read in that order; toneLabel replaces the tone name. The neutral tone has no spoken name.
That element is a polite live region, so TalkBack announces a changed message.
The icon is hidden from TalkBack.
The retry button is a separate element with a 48dp touch target.
While retrying the button stays in the focus order, ignores taps and has the state "Retrying".
The button moves under the message when both do not fit on one line, so nothing is cut off at the largest font size.
edgeCases: When a retry fails with the same message, the text does not change and the live region does not announce it again; change the message, for example with the number of attempts.
A very long message takes the whole width and the button always sits under it.

name: MonarchInlineNotice
title: InlineNotice
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row, androidx.compose.material3.Text, androidx.compose.material3.IconButton
summary: A one-line message with a tone, attached to a field, a row, a card or a panel.
whenToUse: For a short status next to the thing it is about: a conflict on a form, a note under a field, a warning in a table row or a card.
whenNotToUse: For a message about a whole screen or section, use MonarchCalloutBanner or MonarchBanner. For a field error, use the error text of MonarchTextField. For a transient confirmation, use a snackbar through MonarchSnackbarHost.
api: @Composable fun MonarchInlineNotice(message: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, tone: MonarchTone = MonarchTone.Info, variant: MonarchInlineNoticeVariant = MonarchInlineNoticeVariant.Subtle, title: String? = null, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, action: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, onDismiss: (() -> Unit)? = null, dismissIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, announcement: MonarchBannerAnnouncement = MonarchBannerAnnouncement.None, toneLabel: String? = null, dismissLabel: String? = null)
enum class MonarchInlineNoticeVariant { Subtle, Plain }

options.name: message
options.description: The message; one sentence.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the notice.

options.name: tone
options.description: Neutral, Info, Success, Warning or Danger: the colors and the spoken tone name.

options.name: variant
options.description: Subtle: a tinted strip. Plain: coloured icon and text, no fill.

options.name: title
options.description: A short bold lead-in on the same line.

options.name: icon
options.description: An icon at the start in the tone color. Hidden from TalkBack; Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: action
options.description: One small action at the end.

options.name: onDismiss
options.description: Adds a dismiss button. The app removes the notice.

options.name: dismissIcon
options.description: The close mark of the dismiss button; without it the button shows its label as text.

options.name: announcement
options.description: None, Polite or Assertive: makes the text a live region.

options.name: toneLabel
options.description: The tone name read first. null uses monarch_inlinenotice_tone_info, _success, _warning or _danger.

options.name: dismissLabel
options.description: Label or TalkBack name of the dismiss button. null uses monarch_inlinenotice_dismiss, "Dismiss".

states.name: subtle
states.description: The tinted background of the tone with default text and an icon in the strong tone color.

states.name: plain
states.description: No fill; icon and text in the strong tone color, muted text for neutral.

states.name: dismissible
states.description: A dismiss button at the end, when onDismiss is given. The app removes the notice.

states.name: announced
states.description: With Polite or Assertive the text is a live region.

appearance: Subtle: the subtle background of the tone (the muted background for neutral), 8dp corners, default text and an icon in the strong tone color. Plain: no background, text and icon in the strong tone color. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The notice does not hide itself: the app removes it in onDismiss, where the web can keep its own open state. The web live option (true picks assertive for danger) is the announcement parameter, which reuses MonarchBannerAnnouncement and is never chosen by tone. The action is a slot, as on the web; iOS takes a title and a closure. Monarch bundles no icons: the web and iOS show a default icon per tone, here the app passes one, and the dismiss button shows the word Dismiss unless a dismissIcon is given. The action stays at the end at every font size, where iOS moves it under the text. The spoken tone name comes from the shared Monarch tone names (Information, Success, Warning, Error, AI), the same words as iOS. Deprecated (D7): the component's own string keys monarch_inlinenotice_tone_info, _success, _warning and _danger are now aliases of the shared names. An app that redefines one still gets its text, but they are removed no earlier than 2027-02-13 (90-day window, two patch releases); override the shared monarch_internal_tone_* names or pass toneLabel instead.
accessibility: The tone name, title and message are one TalkBack element, read in that order; toneLabel replaces the tone name. The neutral tone has no spoken name.
The icon is hidden from TalkBack.
The action and the dismiss button are separate buttons with 48dp touch targets.
With announcement Polite or Assertive the text is a live region; by default the notice does not announce itself.
The action and the dismiss button are at the end in both layout directions; the text wraps.
edgeCases: Long text wraps; with an action and a dismiss button at the largest font size the text column gets narrow, so keep the action label short.
A plain notice has no padding, so it lines up with the field above it.

title: InputGroup
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedTextField leadingIcon and trailingIcon slots, through MonarchTextField
summary: A recipe, not a component: text, a unit or a button attached to a MonarchTextField through its leading and trailing slots.
whenToUse: For a field with a fixed prefix or unit (https://, a currency sign, kg) or an action that belongs to the field (copy, show, search).
whenNotToUse: For a password use MonarchPasswordInput, for a number with steps MonarchNumberInput. For actions about the whole form put MonarchButtons under the fields.
api: MonarchTextField(value, onValueChange, label = …, leadingIcon = { MonarchText(prefix) }, trailingIcon = { MonarchButton(…, variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Ghost, size = MonarchButtonSize.Sm) })

options.name: leadingIcon
options.description: Text or an icon attached at the start of the field, such as https:// or a currency sign.

options.name: trailingIcon
options.description: Text, a unit or a ghost MonarchButton attached at the end of the field.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Set enabled = false on MonarchTextField and on the attached button.

states.name: error
states.description: Set errorText on MonarchTextField: the outline, the attached text and the message take the danger color.

appearance: One outlined field: the attached text uses the muted color of the field's icons and the attached button the ghost variant, all inside the field's input border and focus ring. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web's InputGroup, InputGroupAddon and InputGroupButton are three components around an Input; on Android they are the leading and trailing slots of MonarchTextField, which mirror in right-to-left layouts without an align option. The parity plan names prefix and suffix slots: the Material 3 OutlinedTextField has prefix and suffix, but MonarchTextField does not expose them yet, so the recipe uses the icon slots; text in the leading slot is always shown, while a Material prefix only shows once the field has focus or text. The web's sizes are not offered. iOS composes the same recipe from TextField and MonarchButton in an HStack.
accessibility: The field keeps its label; attached text is read by TalkBack as part of the field, before or after the value.
An attached MonarchButton is its own element with its own name and a 48dp touch target.
The field is at least 48dp high.
edgeCases: A long prefix takes width from the text; keep attached text short.
At font scale 2.0 the attached text grows with the field's text.
