name: MonarchInsightStrip
title: InsightStrip
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyRow, androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column, androidx.compose.foundation.layout.BoxWithConstraints, with MonarchCard, MonarchBadge, MonarchCollapsible, MonarchButton and MonarchBanner
summary: A row of insight cards for the top of a dashboard, each showing whether a fixed rule or a model raised it, sorted most severe first.
whenToUse: At the top of a dashboard or a record, for a few findings that need attention: expiring domains, failed backups, a renewal at risk.
whenNotToUse: For one message about the whole screen use MonarchBanner. For a list of records use a list or a table.
api: @Composable fun MonarchInsightStrip(insights: List<MonarchInsight>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, title: String? = null, layout: MonarchInsightStripLayout = MonarchInsightStripLayout.Scroll, loading: Boolean = false, errorText: String? = null, limit: Int? = null, sortBySeverity: Boolean = true, onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null, onDismiss: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchInsightStripLabels = MonarchInsightStripLabels())

class MonarchInsight(id: String, title: String, why: String, origin: MonarchInsightOrigin, tone: MonarchTone = MonarchTone.Info, evidence: String? = null, actionLabel: String? = null, onAction: (() -> Unit)? = null)
enum class MonarchInsightOrigin { Rule, Ai }
enum class MonarchInsightStripLayout { Scroll, Stack, Grid }

class MonarchInsightStripLabels(showMore: ((Int) -> String)? = null, showLess: String? = null, empty: String? = null, loading: String? = null, retry: String? = null, dismiss: String? = null, evidence: String? = null, ruleOrigin: String? = null, aiOrigin: String? = null, toneLabel: ((MonarchTone) -> String)? = null)

options.name: insights
options.description: The insights: id, title, reason, origin, tone, and optionally evidence and one action.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the component.

options.name: title
options.description: A heading above the strip.

options.name: layout
options.description: Scroll: one sideways row. Stack: one column. Grid: one to three columns by width.

options.name: loading
options.description: Shows three placeholder cards.

options.name: errorText
options.description: Replaces the insights with this failure in a danger banner.

options.name: limit
options.description: Shows at most this many, with "Show N more" for the rest. Zero or less is ignored.

options.name: sortBySeverity
options.description: Orders critical, warning, info, a note, positive; the given order is kept within a tone.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Adds "Try again" to the error banner.

options.name: onDismiss
options.description: Adds a dismiss button to every insight; called with its id. The app removes it.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, including the tone words.

states.name: loading
states.description: Three placeholder cards in the muted background color, one TalkBack element named "Loading insights".

states.name: error
states.description: A danger banner with the message and "Try again" when onRetry is given.

states.name: empty
states.description: "Nothing needs attention right now." in the muted text color.

states.name: limited
states.description: Only the first insights, with "Show N more"; then "Show fewer".

appearance: Each insight is a MonarchCard with a subtle badge in its tone, an outline badge for its origin, the title in the strong body style and the reason in the muted text color. Placeholders use the muted background. Colors come from the roles of the components used, in every theme.
platformNotes: The web strip is built from AiInsightCallout and an EmptyState, InlineErrorRetry and Skeleton, which Android does not have yet; it draws its cards from MonarchCard and MonarchBadge, as iOS does. Severity is MonarchTone (Danger for critical, Success for positive), with Neutral offered as a note. Evidence is a String in a MonarchCollapsible, not arbitrary content. The dismiss button is a text button, "Dismiss", because Monarch bundles no close icon. The default layout is the scrolling row, as on iOS. Moving TalkBack focus to the next insight after a dismissal, which the web does, is not implemented. The web empty={null} has no counterpart: leave the strip out instead. The web heading level has no counterpart: the title is a heading. The badge words (Note, Info, Positive, Warning, Critical) differ from the shared tone names on purpose: they are the visible severity vocabulary of the web AiInsightCallout (info, warning, critical, positive), shown as text on the badge, not only spoken, so they follow the web copy. The monarch_insightstrip_tone_* keys are not deprecated.
accessibility: The title is a heading.
Each insight is one TalkBack element read as its tone word, its origin, its title and its reason, so neither the tone nor the origin depends on color.
The evidence section, the action and the dismiss button are separate elements with 48dp touch targets.
The loading placeholder is one element named "Loading insights".
The error banner is a polite live region.
Text wraps inside the cards at every font size.
edgeCases: In the scrolling row every card is 85% of the width, at most 320dp, so cards in one row can differ in height.
A limit of zero or less is ignored.
An insight with an actionLabel but no onAction shows no button.
After a dismissal TalkBack focus is left to the system.
In the grid, cards in one row can differ in height.

name: MonarchInstallVerify
title: InstallVerify
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column with MonarchCodeSnippetTabs (androidx.compose.material3.SecondaryScrollableTabRow over MonarchCodeBlock), MonarchCopyButton, MonarchButton, MonarchProgress and the system share sheet (android.content.Intent.ACTION_SEND through Intent.createChooser)
summary: Install a snippet on a website and wait for it to report: code per platform with copy, a handoff for a developer through the share sheet, then a status that turns from waiting to connected, with the expected sites and when each was last seen.
whenToUse: In onboarding or settings where a person must add a tag, script or plugin to their site and the product can tell when it loads.
whenNotToUse: For code examples with no verification, use MonarchCodeSnippetTabs. For DNS records, use MonarchDnsRecordTable with MonarchDomainProgress.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchInstallVerify(snippets: List<MonarchInstallSnippet>, status: MonarchInstallVerifyStatus, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, part: MonarchInstallVerifyPart = MonarchInstallVerifyPart.All, selection: String? = null, onSelectionChange: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, connectedOn: List<String>? = null, targets: List<MonarchInstallTarget> = emptyList(), now: Long? = null, developerInstructions: String? = null, testDisabled: Boolean = false, testHint: String? = null, labels: MonarchInstallVerifyLabels = MonarchInstallVerifyLabels(), onShareInstructions: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, onOpenTest: (() -> Unit)? = null, onConnected: (() -> Unit)? = null, credential: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null)
data class MonarchInstallSnippet(id: String, label: String, code: String, language: String? = null, description: String? = null)
data class MonarchInstallTarget(label: String, lastSeenAt: Long? = null, id: String? = null)
enum class MonarchInstallVerifyStatus { Waiting, Connected, Unavailable }
enum class MonarchInstallVerifyPart { All, Install, Verify }

class MonarchInstallVerifyLabels(installHeading: String? = null, verifyHeading: String? = null, platforms: String? = null, copyInstructions: String? = null, instructionsCopied: String? = null, shareInstructions: String? = null, waitingTitle: String? = null, waitingBody: ((targets: List<String>) -> String)? = null, connectedTitle: ((hosts: List<String>) -> String)? = null, connectedBody: String? = null, unavailableTitle: String? = null, unavailableBody: String? = null, targetsLabel: String? = null, seen: ((time: String) -> String)? = null, notSeen: String? = null, openTest: String? = null)

options.name: snippets
options.description: The install options, one tab each; a single snippet shows without tabs. The shown snippet's description is above its code.

options.name: status
options.description: Waiting for the first report, Connected once seen, or Unavailable when the product cannot check.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the component.

options.name: part
options.description: Both halves under Install and Verify headings, or one half without heading for a wizard step.

options.name: selection
options.description: The id of the snippet shown. The component keeps the person's choice and starts again from this value when it changes.

options.name: onSelectionChange
options.description: Called with the id of the snippet the person picks.

options.name: connectedOn
options.description: The hosts for the connected title. Null uses the targets that have a lastSeenAt.

options.name: targets
options.description: The sites the install is expected on, listed with when each was last seen.

options.name: now
options.description: The time last seen is measured from, in epoch milliseconds. Null reads the clock once.

options.name: developerInstructions
options.description: A plain-text handoff for a developer. Shows Copy instructions for your developer and Share with your developer.

options.name: testDisabled
options.description: Disables Open a test page; say why in testHint.

options.name: testHint
options.description: One line under the test page button.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: onShareInstructions
options.description: Shares the handoff instead of the system share sheet.

options.name: onOpenTest
options.description: Shows Open a test page; the app opens the page, for example with a browser intent.

options.name: onConnected
options.description: Called once, the first time status is Connected while the component is shown.

options.name: credential
options.description: Content above the snippets: the key the snippet needs and its state (creating, ready, failed with a retry).

states.name: waiting
states.description: A small spinning indicator with Waiting for your site… and the sites to open; the box uses the subtle background.

states.name: connected
states.description: A success dot with Connected on and the hosts; the box uses the success subtle fill and border.

states.name: unavailable
states.description: An info dot with Live verification isn't available and what to check by hand; the box uses the info subtle fill and border.

states.name: site seen and not seen
states.description: Each site has a success dot and seen 5 minutes ago, or a strong-border dot and not seen yet.

states.name: test page disabled
states.description: The button is disabled and the hint says why.

appearance: Headings in the subheading style. Snippets use MonarchCodeSnippetTabs. The status box has the large radius with subtle, success subtle or info subtle fills and matching borders, a strong body title and muted body text. Sites are body text with muted caption times. The same roles adapt to dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web shows the code in a multi-line CopyField and links for the email handoff and the test page. On Android the code is MonarchCodeSnippetTabs (with its own copy button), the developer handoff opens the system share sheet, as the plan asks, beside a copy button, and the test page is a callback, because components do not navigate. The web's mailto link is covered by the share sheet. Times are epoch milliseconds and last seen uses DateUtils.getRelativeTimeSpanString in the device language. The web's heading level is not offered. The waiting indicator is MonarchProgress, which stands still when animations are off. iOS has no entry for this id yet. Experimental: a product pattern until a Rook app adopts it.
accessibility: Install and Verify are headings when both halves are shown.
The snippet tabs are Material 3 tabs named Platform, with the selected state.
The status is one element in a polite live region, so a change from waiting to connected is announced; its indicator is hidden.
The sites are a group named Websites, one element per site read as its name and when it was last seen; the dots are hidden and the state is in words.
Copy, Share and Open a test page are buttons with 48dp touch targets; the disabled test button is not enabled for TalkBack.
Status and site text wrap at the largest font scale.
edgeCases: No snippets: the install half shows only the credential and the handoff.
A selection no snippet has shows the first snippet.
Connected without connectedOn or seen sites reads Connected.
onConnected fires once per time the component is in the composition, even if the status flips back and forth.
When no app can share text the share button does nothing; the copy button still works.

Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space4)) {

            MonarchInstallSnippet(id = {{snippets.1.id}}, label = {{snippets.1.label}}, code = {{snippets.1.code}}, description = {{snippets.1.description}}),
            MonarchInstallSnippet(id = {{snippets.2.id}}, label = {{snippets.2.label}}, code = {{snippets.2.code}}, description = {{snippets.2.description}}),
        ),
        status = if (connected) MonarchInstallVerifyStatus.Connected else MonarchInstallVerifyStatus.Waiting,
        targets = listOf(

title: InviteMembersDialog
wrapsNative: MonarchBottomSheet (dismissible = false keeps it open while sending) with a scrolling androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of MonarchTagInput, MonarchRolePicker, MonarchAppAccessPicker, MonarchTextField, MonarchInlineNotice and MonarchButtons
summary: A recipe, not a component: invite people to a workspace by email address, with a role, the apps they get and an optional note, keeping any address the server refused with its reason.
whenToUse: From a workspace's members screen, when an admin invites one or more people by email.
whenNotToUse: To change the role of someone already in the workspace, use MonarchRolePicker on their member screen. To share one record with a person, use the share recipe.
api: MonarchBottomSheet(onDismissRequest = { open = false }, title = "Invite people", description = …, dismissible = !sending) { … }
MonarchTagInput(tags = emails, onTagsChange = { … }, label = "Email addresses", removeIcon = { … }, separators = setOf(',', ' ', ';'), maxCount = 50, normalize = { … }, validate = { tag, _ -> … })
MonarchRolePicker(roles = …, selected = role, onSelect = { role = it }, layout = MonarchRolePickerLayout.Compact, label = "Role")
MonarchAppAccessPicker(apps = …, value = apps, onValueChange = { apps = it }) // @ExperimentalMonarchApi, opted in at the call
MonarchTextField(value = note, onValueChange = { note = it }, label = "Personal note", helperText = "Optional", singleLine = false)
MonarchButton(text = if (emails.size > 1) "Send ${emails.size} invites" else "Send invite", onClick = …, variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Primary, loading = sending)

options.name: roles
options.description: The roles to choose from, least access first; the first enabled one is chosen when the sheet opens.

options.name: apps
options.description: The apps that can be granted; leave the picker out when the product has one app.

options.name: maxEmails
options.description: The most addresses per invitation, passed to MonarchTagInput's maxCount, as on the web.

options.name: validate
options.description: Checks each address before it becomes a chip; return a message to refuse it. Replace it to accept usernames.

options.name: allowMessage
options.description: Whether to show the personal note field.

options.name: failures
options.description: Addresses the server refused with the reason; they stay as chips and are listed in a danger notice.

states.name: editing
states.description: The addresses as chips, the role, the apps, the note and Send invite, which counts the addresses: "Send 3 invites".

states.name: invalid
states.description: MonarchTagInput refuses an address that is not one and says why; an empty list on Send shows "Add at least one email address."

states.name: sending
states.description: Send shows the loading state, every field is disabled, and the sheet cannot be swiped or backed away.

states.name: partly failed
states.description: The invited addresses are removed; the refused ones stay as chips and a danger MonarchInlineNotice lists each with its reason.

states.name: done
states.description: The sheet closes; the app shows a snackbar such as "Invited 3 people".

appearance: Every part is an existing Monarch component on the Material 3 sheet surface: the title style, the tag input with its chips, the compact role picker, the app access picker, the multi-line text field and full-width primary and ghost buttons. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web's InviteMembersDialog is one component on Dialog. On Android it is a recipe, as on iOS: a MonarchBottomSheet, because a phone dialog has no room for the chips, the role cards and the app list, and the sending state is a few lines of the app's state. The web's onInvite result ({ failed }) is the app's server response mapped to failures; the web's trigger prop is the app's own button; closeOnSuccess and the success announcement are the app's snackbar. The web adds a typed address on submit; MonarchTagInput adds an address when a separator is typed or on the keyboard's done action.
accessibility: MonarchTagInput reads each chip with its remove action and announces added, refused and removed addresses.
MonarchRolePicker reads each role as a radio button with its description; MonarchAppAccessPicker reads each app as a checkbox.
Send is read as loading while sending, and the sheet cannot be dismissed so the result is not lost.
The refused addresses are listed in words in a danger notice, not only by color.
Every button has a 48dp target; the fields grow at font scale 2.0 inside the scrolling sheet.
edgeCases: Check the addresses on the server as well; the email pattern only catches typos.
Duplicates are refused by MonarchTagInput; addresses are compared as typed, so lower-case them in normalize if the server does.
Pasting a list adds every address split by the separators, up to maxCount.
When every address fails, keep the sheet open with the reasons; when some fail, report the invited ones too.

name: MonarchInvoiceView
title: InvoiceView
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of MonarchText, MonarchStatusBadge, MonarchDescriptionList, MonarchMoney and androidx.compose.material3.HorizontalDivider; printing through android.print.PrintManager with android.print.pdf.PrintedPdfDocument and a androidx.compose.ui.graphics.layer.GraphicsLayer capture
summary: A read-only invoice: issuer and billed party, number and dates, a status, line items, totals and notes, with an optional Print button.
whenToUse: To show an invoice that has been issued (sent, paid, overdue or cancelled), in a client portal or an invoice detail screen, and to print it or save it as a PDF.
whenNotToUse: To create or edit invoice lines, use a form the app builds. For a list of many invoices, use rows with MonarchMoney and MonarchStatusBadge. For a payment receipt, use MonarchReceiptPreview.
api: @Composable fun MonarchInvoiceView(items: List<MonarchInvoiceLineItem>, currencyCode: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, title: String? = null, number: String? = null, status: MonarchStatusDefinition? = null, issueDateMillis: Long? = null, dueDateMillis: Long? = null, details: List<MonarchInvoiceDetail> = emptyList(), from: MonarchInvoiceParty? = null, to: MonarchInvoiceParty? = null, locale: Locale? = null, taxRate: BigDecimal? = null, discount: MonarchInvoiceDiscount? = null, totals: MonarchInvoiceTotals = MonarchInvoiceTotals(), notes: String? = null, footer: String? = null, showPrintButton: Boolean = false, onPrint: (() -> Unit)? = null, brand: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, actions: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchInvoiceViewLabels = MonarchInvoiceViewLabels())
class MonarchInvoiceLineItem(id: String, description: String, quantity: BigDecimal, unitPrice: BigDecimal, detail: String? = null, amount: BigDecimal? = null)
class MonarchInvoiceParty(name: String, details: List<String> = emptyList())
class MonarchInvoiceDetail(label: String, value: String)

class MonarchInvoiceTotals(subtotal: BigDecimal? = null, discount: BigDecimal? = null, tax: BigDecimal? = null, total: BigDecimal? = null, amountPaid: BigDecimal? = null, amountDue: BigDecimal? = null)
sealed interface MonarchInvoiceDiscount { class Percent(percent: BigDecimal); class Amount(amount: BigDecimal) }

class MonarchInvoiceViewLabels(title: String? = null, from: String? = null, to: String? = null, issueDate: String? = null, dueDate: String? = null, lineItems: String? = null, description: String? = null, quantity: String? = null, unitPrice: String? = null, amount: String? = null, subtotal: String? = null, discount: String? = null, tax: String? = null, taxWithRate: ((String) -> String)? = null, total: String? = null, amountPaid: String? = null, amountDue: String? = null, noItems: String? = null, notes: String? = null, print: String? = null)

options.name: items
options.description: The billed lines, read-only. Empty shows "No line items.".

options.name: currencyCode
options.description: The ISO 4217 code of every amount.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the invoice.

options.name: title
options.description: The main heading. null uses "Invoice".

options.name: number
options.description: The invoice number, written after the title and so part of the heading TalkBack reads.

options.name: status
options.description: A status beside the title, drawn as a small MonarchStatusBadge.

options.name: issueDateMillis
options.description: The issue date in epoch milliseconds (UTC), written as a medium date in the locale.

options.name: dueDateMillis
options.description: The due date in epoch milliseconds (UTC).

options.name: details
options.description: More facts after the dates: payment terms, purchase order, project.

options.name: from
options.description: Who issues the invoice, under the heading "From".

options.name: to
options.description: Who is billed, under the heading "Bill to".

options.name: locale
options.description: The locale of amounts, quantities and dates. null uses the first locale of the configuration.

options.name: taxRate
options.description: The tax rate in percent, used to work out tax when totals has none; the tax label then shows the rate.

options.name: discount
options.description: A percent or amount discount used to work out the totals when totals has none.

options.name: totals
options.description: The totals from the billing system; a given value wins over the worked-out one.

options.name: notes
options.description: Payment instructions or terms under the totals, with the heading "Notes".

options.name: footer
options.description: Small print at the bottom, in the caption style.

options.name: showPrintButton
options.description: Shows a small secondary Print button in the header.

options.name: onPrint
options.description: Replaces the built-in printing, for example to print the app's own PDF.

options.name: brand
options.description: A logo or wordmark at the top. The app gives it a content description, or null when decorative.

options.name: actions
options.description: More header actions after Print, such as Download PDF or Send. Left out of the printed copy.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, for example in the invoice's own language.

states.name: compact
states.description: Below 640dp each line is a block: the description and amount on the first row, "Qty 2 · Unit price $400.00" under it. Parties and facts are stacked.

states.name: wide
states.description: From 640dp the lines are a table with Description, Qty, Unit price and Amount columns, and the parties and facts sit side by side.

states.name: empty
states.description: No lines: "No line items." in the muted color replaces the lines; the totals show zero.

states.name: discount
states.description: The discount row, with a decorative minus sign, shows only when the discount is not zero.

states.name: tax
states.description: The tax row shows when a tax amount or a tax rate is given; with a worked-out tax its label carries the rate, "Tax (10%)".

states.name: paid and due
states.description: Amount paid and Amount due rows show only when given in totals.

states.name: printing
states.description: The Print button is disabled while the off-screen copy is captured; the system print dialog then opens.

appearance: Text in the default and muted text colors on the surrounding surface, with subtle dividers between lines and a default border rule over the total, which is in the heading style. The status badge carries its tone colors. It works the same in light, dark and both high-contrast themes; the printed copy is always in the light theme.
platformNotes: The web InvoiceView is an article with a real table, print styles and ReactNode slots, and takes decimal or minor-unit amounts. On Android amounts are BigDecimal in major units, dates are epoch milliseconds (UTC) formatted with android.icu.text.DateFormat, the status is a MonarchStatusDefinition, and the brand and actions are slots. The parity map named LazyColumn sections; the invoice is a Column instead, so it can sit inside the screen's verticalScroll with other content and be captured whole for printing, as on iOS. A Compose layout cannot be printed directly, so the built-in Print composes a copy off screen in the light theme without the header actions, captures it with a GraphicsLayer and writes it as PDF pages through PrintManager and PrintedPdfDocument; the system dialog also saves a PDF. Pages are cut at the page height, so a line can be split across two pages, which the web print styles avoid. The headingLevel option has no Android equivalent; the title and section names are TalkBack headings. iOS ships the same MonarchInvoiceView.
accessibility: The title, with the number, is a heading; "From", "Bill to", "Line items" and "Notes" are headings.
Each line is one TalkBack element read as its description, detail and labelled figures: "Discovery workshop, Two sessions, Qty 2, Unit price $400.00, Amount $800.00".
The list of lines carries collection info, so TalkBack reads the number of lines; each line carries its row index.
The column headings of the wide table are hidden from TalkBack because every line reads its own labels.
Each total row is read as its label and amount; the discount minus sign is hidden and the "Discount" label carries the meaning.
The Print button keeps a 48dp touch target.
Text wraps and grows at font scale 2.0; no row has a fixed height.
Right to left, labels and amounts mirror.
edgeCases: A total given in totals wins over the worked-out one even when they disagree; the view never corrects the billing system.
Line amounts are rounded half away from zero to the currency's digits (JPY 0, USD 2, KWD 3).
A discount larger than the subtotal is capped at the subtotal; a percent above 100 counts as 100.
Built-in printing needs an Activity context; elsewhere the button does nothing, so pass onPrint.
A very long invoice makes a tall bitmap while printing; the app can pass onPrint and print its own PDF instead.

name: MonarchIssueCard
title: IssueCard
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.Surface drawn as MonarchCard, androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow; MonarchStatusPicker and MonarchPriorityPicker (androidx.compose.material3.DropdownMenu), MonarchTag, MonarchAvatar
summary: An issue on a board or in a list: key, title, status, priority, tags, due date and assignee, with status and priority changeable in place.
whenToUse: For issues, tasks or tickets in a board column or a list, where readers scan status, urgency, ownership and dates and open the issue from the title.
whenNotToUse: For a dense list with many columns, use a list of rows with a detail screen. For a calendar entry, use MonarchEventChip. For a plain card without issue fields, use MonarchCard.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchIssueCard(title: String, key: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, status: MonarchStatusOption? = null, statuses: List<MonarchStatusOption> = emptyList(), priority: MonarchPriorityLevel? = null, assignee: MonarchIssueCardAssignee? = null, tags: List<String> = emptyList(), dueDate: Long? = null, today: Long? = null, selected: Boolean = false, dragging: Boolean = false, labels: MonarchIssueCardLabels = MonarchIssueCardLabels(), onStatusChange: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, onPriorityChange: ((MonarchPriorityLevel) -> Unit)? = null, onOpen: (() -> Unit)? = null)
sealed interface MonarchIssueCardAssignee { class Person(name: String, image: Painter? = null); data object Unassigned }

class MonarchIssueCardLabels(due: ((String) -> String)? = null, overdue: String? = null, tags: ((String) -> String)? = null, unassigned: String? = null, assignee: ((String) -> String)? = null, status: ((String) -> String)? = null, priority: ((String) -> String)? = null, priorityLevel: ((MonarchPriorityLevel) -> String)? = null)

options.name: title
options.description: The issue's title, already localised.

options.name: key
options.description: The issue key, such as STR-142. Shown above the title and read before it.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the card.

options.name: status
options.description: The current status, shown with the glyph of its category. Completed and cancelled issues are never overdue.

options.name: statuses
options.description: Every status. With onStatusChange, the status becomes a MonarchStatusPicker.

options.name: priority
options.description: The priority, shown as its glyph at the end of the header. None when null.

options.name: assignee
options.description: Person shows an avatar at the end of the last row; Unassigned an empty dashed slot. No slot when null.

options.name: tags
options.description: Labels on the issue, shown as small MonarchTags.

options.name: dueDate
options.description: The due day in epoch milliseconds, read in UTC as a Material 3 DatePickerState stores it, shown as "Due Mar 12" in the device locale.

options.name: today
options.description: The reference day for overdue, in the same form. The device's current day in its time zone when null.

options.name: selected
options.description: Tints the card with the subtle accent fill and a thicker accent border; the title gets the selected state.

options.name: dragging
options.description: Lifts the card with the large shadow instead of the extra-small one.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the due and overdue text, the priority names and every spoken phrase.

options.name: onStatusChange
options.description: Changes the status from the card. Receives the chosen status id. Needs statuses.

options.name: onPriorityChange
options.description: Changes the priority from the card; the glyph becomes a glyph-only MonarchPriorityPicker.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Opens the issue. Makes the title a button with a 48dp target.

states.name: default
states.description: Surface fill, default border, extra-small shadow.

states.name: selected
states.description: Subtle accent fill and a 2dp accent border instead of the 1dp default one; the title has the selected state.

states.name: dragging
states.description: The large shadow lifts the card.

states.name: overdue
states.description: The due text turns the strong danger color and the word Overdue is added. Completed and cancelled issues are never overdue.

states.name: editable
states.description: Status and priority open Material 3 menus with every option, when their change handlers are given.

appearance: The card uses the MonarchCard surface, large radius and default border. The key is muted caption text and the title strong body text. Priority glyphs use the strong danger, strong warning, default or muted text colors, and status glyphs the subtle, muted, strong warning or strong success colors. The due text is muted, or strong danger when overdue. The same roles adapt to dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Built from MonarchStatusPicker and MonarchPriorityPicker, as the web card uses its StatusPicker and PriorityPicker. MonarchCard has no selected state, so the card draws the same surface with a Material 3 Surface and its own fill and border for selection; the thicker border, not the color alone, marks it. The web's href is not offered: components do not navigate, so the app opens the issue in onOpen. The due date is epoch milliseconds read in UTC (the web also takes YYYY-MM-DD strings and date-times), and today is epoch milliseconds rather than a string. The web's labels are tags here because labels names the strings parameter, as on iOS. The web's calendar glyph is not drawn: Monarch bundles no icons and the word Due carries the meaning. iOS adds a check mark to a selected card; Android marks selection with the thicker border and the selected state. Experimental: a domain pattern until a Rook app adopts it.
accessibility: The title is read with the key first ("STR-142, Sign-in fails…"); with onOpen it is a button with a 48dp touch target, and on a selected card it has the selected state.

A read-only priority is an image read as "Priority: High"; a read-only status is read as "Status: In progress"; the due date as "Due Mar 12, Overdue"; tags as "Labels: Bug, Auth"; the assignee as "Assigned to Ana Ruiz" or "Unassigned".
Editable status and priority are the Monarch pickers: drop-down list role, named with the current value, 48dp touch targets.
Every priority level and status category has its own glyph, overdue is written and selection thickens the border, so nothing relies on color alone.
The title wraps at the largest font scale without being cut.
edgeCases: Long titles wrap; status, tags and the due date flow onto new lines while the assignee stays at the end.
A due date later today is not overdue: days are compared, not times.
With onStatusChange but no statuses, the status stays read-only.
today defaults to the device's current day, so a card shown across midnight changes only when it recomposes; pass today to fix it.

title: JSONViewer
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn over a flattened model of the open part of the tree; MonarchTextField for search, MonarchButton for Collapse all, MonarchCopyButton for Copy path and Copy value
summary: A collapsible, searchable tree for a JSON document, with copy path and copy value for the selected node, that stays fast on large payloads.
whenToUse: In developer and support tools, to inspect webhook payloads, API responses, event data or settings stored as JSON.
whenNotToUse: For a short JSON snippet the user reads or copies whole, use MonarchCodeBlock; for a hierarchy of records that are not JSON, use MonarchTreeView; for a few labelled values, MonarchDescriptionList.
api: @Composable fun MonarchJsonViewer(value: MonarchJsonValue, expandIcon: @Composable () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, expandDepth: Int = 1, maxChildren: Int = 100, maxStringLength: Int = 500, searchable: Boolean = true, maxMatches: Int = 500, copyable: Boolean = true, rootPath: String = "$", searchIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, clearIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, state: LazyListState = rememberLazyListState(), labels: MonarchJsonViewerLabels = MonarchJsonViewerLabels(), onSelect: ((path: String, value: MonarchJsonValue) -> Unit)? = null, onCopy: ((String) -> Unit)? = null)

sealed interface MonarchJsonValue { data class Object(members: List<Pair<String, MonarchJsonValue>>); data class Array(items: List<MonarchJsonValue>); data class String(value: String); data class Number(text: String); data class Bool(value: Boolean); data object Null; companion object { fun parse(text: String): MonarchJsonValue; fun from(value: Any?): MonarchJsonValue } }
class MonarchJsonParseException(offset: Int) : IllegalArgumentException

class MonarchJsonViewerLabels(label: String? = null, search: String? = null, searchPrompt: String? = null, clearSearch: String? = null, matches: ((count: Int, capped: Boolean) -> String)? = null, collapseAll: String? = null, copyPath: String? = null, copyValue: String? = null, selectedPath: String? = null, keys: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, items: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, showMore: ((next: Int, remaining: Int) -> String)? = null, truncated: ((length: Int) -> String)? = null, expanded: String? = null, collapsed: String? = null)

options.name: value
options.description: The document. Build it with MonarchJsonValue.parse, which keeps the order of object keys and the exact text of numbers, with MonarchJsonValue.from for Kotlin maps and lists, or with the cases.

options.name: expandIcon
options.description: A chevron that points to the end, such as a MonarchIcon of size Sm with mirrorInRtl = true. It turns a quarter turn while its container is open. Required, as in MonarchTreeView, because Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the viewer. The rows scroll inside it: give it a bounded height, or let it fill a screen or pane.

options.name: expandDepth
options.description: Levels open at first: 1 shows the root's children, 0 only the root.

options.name: maxChildren
options.description: Children shown per object or array before a "Show more" row; each Show more adds this many. At least 1.

options.name: maxStringLength
options.description: Strings longer than this are cut in the tree with "… (n characters)". Copy value always copies the whole string.

options.name: searchable
options.description: Shows the search field and the match count.

options.name: maxMatches
options.description: The search stops after this many matches and the count shows "500+ matches".

options.name: copyable
options.description: Shows the footer with the selected path, Copy path and Copy value.

options.name: rootPath
options.description: The first part of shown and copied paths: $ gives $.users[0].name, an empty string gives users[0].name.

options.name: searchIcon
options.description: An icon at the start of the search field.

options.name: clearIcon
options.description: The icon of a button that clears the search, shown while there is a query. Without it the search is cleared by deleting the text or with Collapse all.

options.name: state
options.description: The scroll state of the rows.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string: the tree name, the search field, the match count, Collapse all, the copy buttons, the selected path, the summaries, Show more, the cut string suffix and the spoken open state.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Called with the formatted path and the value when the user selects another node (a tap, Show more or Collapse all).

options.name: onCopy
options.description: Called with the copied text after the path or the value is copied.

states.name: collapsed
states.description: A closed object or array shows the chevron pointing to the end and its summary: { } 3 keys or [ ] 2 items.

states.name: expanded
states.description: An open container shows the chevron turned a quarter and its children, indented one level.

states.name: selected
states.description: The selected row has the muted fill and the selected state; the footer shows its path. The root is selected at first.

states.name: searching
states.description: Containers that hold a match open, matched text is highlighted and bold, and the toolbar shows the match count.

states.name: show more
states.description: A container with more children than maxChildren ends with a link-coloured "Show 100 more (250 hidden)" row. Search reveals hidden children that match.

states.name: collapsed all
states.description: Collapse all clears the search, closes every container below the root and selects the root.

appearance: The viewer is a surface-coloured box with a subtle border and 12dp corners, with subtle lines between the toolbar, the rows and the footer. Rows are code text: object keys in the strong info color, array indexes and punctuation muted, strings in the strong success color, numbers in the strong accent color, booleans and null in the strong warning color. The selected row has the muted background; matches have the subtle warning background and are bold. Every color is a theme role, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes are covered.
platformNotes: The web takes any JavaScript value and shows circular references, undefined and Dates; on Android, as on iOS, the input is MonarchJsonValue, which cannot be circular, parsed by a small parser that keeps key order and number text (org.json does not promise either). The web's tree keyboard pattern (arrows, Home, End, *) is replaced by touch: tapping a row selects it and opens or closes it, and TalkBack moves row by row. The plan's dependency tree-view is not used directly: MonarchTreeView takes labels as plain strings and keeps the expanded set in the app, while the viewer needs coloured, highlighted key and value text and its own flattened, batched model; the chevron convention (expandIcon pointing to the end, a quarter turn when open) is the same. Search is a MonarchTextField rather than MonarchSearchBar, which expands into a search view of its own. Monarch bundles no icons, so expandIcon is required and searchIcon and clearIcon are optional. onCopy receives the text only; the web also passes whether it was the path or the value. The toolbar has no slot for extra actions. iOS uses the same name; Android adds expandIcon, searchIcon, clearIcon and state, and uses Kotlin-style booleans (searchable, copyable) and PascalCase value cases.
accessibility: The rows are named "JSON".
Each row is a button read as "key: value", such as "amount: 4200" or "lines: [ ] 2 items".
Containers have Expanded or Collapsed as their state description; the chevron is decorative.
The selected row has the selected state, and the footer path is read as "Selected, <path>".
Matches are bold as well as highlighted, so they are not shown by color alone.
The match count is a polite live region, so a new count is announced while searching.
Rows, Show more and the copy buttons are at least 48dp tall.
Copy path and Copy value are MonarchCopyButton, which says "Copied to clipboard" after a copy.
edgeCases: Only open containers are walked, so a closed 10 MB document costs one row; search walks the whole document once per query and stops at maxMatches.
Long keys and values wrap; very long strings are cut at maxStringLength in the tree only.
A repeated key in parsed text keeps its first position and its last value, as JSON.parse does. Repeated keys built by hand are not merged; avoid them, because rows are identified by path.
Numbers keep the text they were written with (1.50, 12345678901234567890).
A primitive root is one row; an empty object or array cannot open.
MonarchJsonValue.parse rejects nesting deeper than 100 levels with MonarchJsonParseException, which also bounds the recursion of search, flattening and copying.
The open state, limits and selection reset when the value changes; the query is kept across configuration changes.

name: MonarchKanbanBoard
title: KanbanBoard
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.pager.HorizontalPager of columns with androidx.compose.material3.PrimaryScrollableTabRow and Tab; androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn per column; detectDragGesturesAfterLongPress on the board; androidx.compose.material3.DropdownMenu with DropdownMenuItem for Move to; MonarchDragHandle, MonarchButton and MonarchText
summary: A board of columns of cards where people move cards within and between columns by dragging, TalkBack actions or a Move to menu, with counts against work-in-progress limits.
whenToUse: For work that moves through stages, such as To do, Doing and Done, or a sales pipeline.
whenNotToUse: For planning work into sprints or releases with points and capacity, use MonarchBacklogPlanner. For ordering one list, use MonarchReorderableList; for a grid of tiles, MonarchSortableGrid.
api: @Composable fun <T> MonarchKanbanBoard(columns: List<MonarchKanbanColumn<T>>, key: (T) -> String, itemLabel: (T) -> String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, onMove: (suspend (move: MonarchKanbanMove<T>, columns: List<MonarchKanbanColumn<T>>) -> Unit)? = null, canMove: ((item: T, toColumnId: String, fromColumnId: String) -> Boolean)? = null, enforceWipLimits: Boolean = false, enabled: Boolean = true, itemEnabled: (T) -> Boolean = { true }, moveMenu: Boolean = true, minColumnWidth: Dp = MonarchKanbanBoardTokens.MinColumnWidth, pagerState: PagerState = rememberPagerState { columns.size }, labels: MonarchKanbanBoardLabels = MonarchKanbanBoardLabels(), menuIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, cardContent: @Composable ColumnScope.(item: T, state: MonarchKanbanCardState) -> Unit)

class MonarchKanbanColumn<T>(id: String, title: String, items: List<T>, wipLimit: Int? = null, emptyText: String? = null, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, actions: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null, footer: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null) { fun withItems(items: List<T>): MonarchKanbanColumn<T> }
data class MonarchKanbanMove<T>(item: T, itemKey: String, fromColumnId: String, fromIndex: Int, toColumnId: String, toIndex: Int)
class MonarchKanbanCardState(columnId: String, index: Int, dragging: Boolean, overlay: Boolean, pending: Boolean, enabled: Boolean)

class MonarchKanbanBoardLabels(handle: ((card: String) -> String)? = null, moveMenu: ((card: String) -> String)? = null, move: String? = null, moveTo: ((column: String) -> String)? = null, countText: ((count: Int, limit: Int?) -> String)? = null, count: ((count: Int, limit: Int?) -> String)? = null, empty: String? = null, blocked: String? = null, pickedUp: ((card: String, column: String, position: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, moved: ((card: String, column: String, position: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, dropped: ((card: String, column: String, position: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, cancelled: ((card: String, column: String) -> String)? = null, notAllowed: ((card: String, column: String) -> String)? = null, failed: ((card: String, column: String) -> String)? = null, actions: Map<MonarchDragHandleDirection, String> = emptyMap())

options.name: columns
options.description: The columns and their cards.

options.name: key
options.description: A stable, unique key for a card, across every column.

options.name: itemLabel
options.description: The plain-text name of a card, used in the handle's name, the menu and announcements.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the board. Give it a bounded height, such as a screen: its columns are lazy.

options.name: onMove
options.description: Saves a finished move with the columns after it. Without it cards cannot be moved. Throwing puts the card back and announces it.

options.name: canMove
options.type: ((item: T, toColumnId: String, fromColumnId: String) -> Boolean)?
options.description: Whether a card may go to another column. Its own column always takes it.

options.name: enforceWipLimits
options.description: A column at or over its wipLimit refuses cards from other columns.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether any card can be moved.

options.name: itemEnabled
options.description: Whether a card can be moved, such as one the person may not edit.

options.name: moveMenu
options.description: Adds the Move to button to each card.

options.name: minColumnWidth
options.description: The narrowest a column gets. A phone shows one column per page; wider screens as many as fit.

options.name: pagerState
options.description: The state of the pager, to choose the first column shown or follow the column in view.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

options.name: menuIcon
options.description: An icon for the Move to button. null shows the word Move.

options.name: cardContent
options.description: The content of a card after the handle, such as a MonarchIssueCard.

states.name: dragging
states.description: After a long press a copy of the card follows the finger with a large shadow and the accent border; its place shows a muted placeholder, and an accent line shows where it will land.

states.name: turning the page
states.description: Holding the finger at the start or end of the board for 600 milliseconds shows the previous or next column; near the top or bottom of a column the column scrolls.

states.name: refused
states.description: A column canMove refuses, or a full one with enforceWipLimits, gets the danger border and "Not allowed here" while the card is over it; a drop there is refused and announced. In the Move to menu it is disabled.

states.name: at and over the limit
states.description: The count reads "2 / 2" in the strong warning color at the limit and in the strong danger color over it; TalkBack reads "2 cards, limit 2, at the limit".

states.name: pending
states.description: While onMove runs the card stays in its new place and its state has pending true.

states.name: failed
states.description: When onMove throws, the card goes back and "Could not move Fix login. It is back in To do." is announced.

states.name: locked and read only
states.description: A card itemEnabled refuses, every card when enabled is false, and every card without onMove has no handle, no menu and cannot be dragged.

states.name: empty
states.description: A column with no cards shows its emptyText, or "No cards".

appearance: Columns are panels in the subtle background color with a subtle border and the large radius; cards are surface-coloured with a subtle border and the medium radius. Column titles use the subheading style; counts the caption style in the muted text color, warning at the limit and danger over it. The tabs use the surface color, with the accent color for the selected tab. The same roles adapt to dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web lays all columns side by side and scrolls the board sideways; on a phone the board is a pager with one column per page and a tab row of the columns, the pattern Android apps use for boards, and wider screens show as many columns as fit at minColumnWidth. A long press anywhere on a card starts the drag (the web's dragFrom option is not needed on touch). The board does not reorder cards during the drag; it shows a line where the card will land and moves it on drop. The keyboard pick-up mode of the web is replaced by the handle's four TalkBack actions and arrow keys, each saving one step. The Move to menu is on by default here (off on the web) so a single-tap path always exists. Columns cannot collapse: with one column per page there is nothing to save room for. defaultColumns, onMoveError, dragFrom, collapsible and headingLevel are not offered; onMove is a suspend function whose exception reports the failure. Announcements use a polite live region where the web uses an assertive one. Icons are app-supplied slots because Monarch bundles no icons. There is no iOS entry yet.
accessibility: Each column title is a heading; its count is read in words, such as "1 card, limit 2".
The column tabs are Material 3 tabs with the selected state.
Each card's handle is named "Move Fix login" and offers Move up, Move down, Move backward and Move forward actions; moving to another column shows that column.
The Move to button is named "Move Fix login to another column" and opens a menu of the other columns; refused columns are disabled.
Pick up, drop, each move, cancel, a refused drop and a failed save are announced through a polite live region that is always present.
The copy that follows the finger is hidden from TalkBack.
Tabs, handles and Move to buttons have 48dp touch targets.
edgeCases: The board shows a saved move until onMove returns and the app passes the new columns list; passing a new list instance replaces it.
Dropping a card where it was does not call onMove.
Give the board a bounded height: each column is a lazy list.
Move backward and Move forward skip refused columns and keep the card's position, clamped to the end of the column.
With enforceWipLimits a column that is already over its limit keeps its cards and still lets them move within it.
Long titles and card text wrap; cards grow at font scale 2.0.

examples.title: Board with a WIP limit
A column that takes no cards and a locked card
examples.code:
MonarchKanbanBoard(
    columns = columns,
    key = { it.key },
    itemLabel = { it.key },
    modifier = Modifier.height(400.dp),
    onMove = { _, _ -> },
    canMove = { _, to, _ -> to != "released" },
    itemEnabled = { it.key != "ABC-2" },
) { issue, _ ->
    MonarchText(text = issue.key, style = MonarchTextStyle.Code)
    MonarchText(text = issue.title)
}

name: MonarchKbd
title: Kbd
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Box, androidx.compose.material3.Text, androidx.compose.ui.platform.LocalConfiguration
summary: A keyboard key or shortcut drawn as a key cap, such as Ctrl+K or ⌘K. By default it is drawn only while a hardware keyboard is attached.
whenToUse: Beside a menu item, a button or a search field to show its keyboard shortcut to people who use a hardware keyboard, on tablets, Chromebooks and desktop windows.
whenNotToUse: For code in running text use MonarchInlineCodeStyle. For a shortcut that only exists on the web, show nothing.
api: @Composable fun MonarchKbd(keys: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, alwaysVisible: Boolean = false, labels: MonarchKbdLabels = MonarchKbdLabels())

class MonarchKbdLabels(command: String? = null, shift: String? = null, option: String? = null, control: String? = null, returnKey: String? = null, escape: String? = null, delete: String? = null, tab: String? = null, space: String? = null, capsLock: String? = null, upArrow: String? = null, downArrow: String? = null, leftArrow: String? = null, rightArrow: String? = null)

options.name: keys
options.description: The key or shortcut as it is shown, such as "Esc", "Ctrl+K" or "⇧⌘P".

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the component. Not applied while the cap is hidden.

options.name: alwaysVisible
options.description: Draw the cap without a hardware keyboard too.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the names TalkBack reads for the key glyphs ⌘ ⇧ ⌥ ⌃ ↩ ⎋ ⌫ ⇥ ␣ ⇪ ↑ ↓ ← → (monarch_kbd_command and the others).

states.name: keyboard attached
states.description: Configuration.keyboard is KEYBOARD_QWERTY and the keyboard is not hidden: the cap is drawn.

states.name: no keyboard
states.description: Nothing is drawn and the component takes no room, unless alwaysVisible is true. The configuration changes when a keyboard is attached or detached, so the cap appears and disappears.

appearance: A key cap with 4dp corners on the subtle background, a default border with a thicker bottom edge, and the keys in muted text in the code typeface, in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web Kbd is always visible, because a browser cannot tell whether a keyboard is present; on Android, as on iOS, the hint is hidden on a device without one. The web text is 11px; Android uses the code role (14sp) because smaller text is not legible on a phone. The spoken key names are an addition shared with iOS: a browser leaves the glyphs to the screen reader. iOS calls the flag isAlwaysVisible and the label return; Kotlin uses alwaysVisible and returnKey because return is a keyword.
accessibility: The cap is one TalkBack element whose content description names the keys: "⇧⌘P" is read as "Shift Command P".
Characters that are not key glyphs are read as written, so "Esc" and "Ctrl+K" are unchanged.
The text grows with the font size setting and the smallest size of the cap grows with it.
The cap is not interactive and has no click action.
The key is shown by a border and a shape, not by color alone.
edgeCases: Whether a keyboard is attached comes from LocalConfiguration: keyboard is KEYBOARD_QWERTY and hardKeyboardHidden is not HARDKEYBOARDHIDDEN_YES. A 12-key keypad does not count.
Emulators often report a QWERTY keyboard, so the cap shows there.
Long text wraps inside the cap.
An empty string draws an empty cap of the smallest size.

examples.title: Shortcut
Always visible, in a list of shortcuts
examples.code: MonarchKbd(keys = "⇧⌘P", alwaysVisible = true)

name: MonarchKeyCreatedDialog
title: KeyCreatedDialog
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.AlertDialog with androidx.compose.ui.window.DialogProperties, MonarchCopyField or MonarchSecretField, MonarchBanner and MonarchCheckboxRow
summary: A dialog that shows a newly created secret exactly once: the value with a copy button, a "store it now" warning, and an acknowledgement the person must tick before the dialog can close.
whenToUse: Right after the server creates an API key, token, signing secret or client secret that it will not show again, or after a rotation.
whenNotToUse: For a secret that can be viewed again in settings use MonarchSecretField. For a confirmation before creating or revoking a key use the Material 3 AlertDialog (ConfirmDialog).
api: @Composable public fun MonarchKeyCreatedDialog(secret: String, onDone: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, kind: MonarchKeyCreatedDialogKind = MonarchKeyCreatedDialogKind.Secret, label: String? = null, name: String? = null, title: String? = null, description: String? = null, requiresAcknowledgement: Boolean? = null, masked: Boolean = false, multiline: Boolean = false, note: String? = null, onCopy: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchKeyCreatedDialogLabels = MonarchKeyCreatedDialogLabels())
public enum class MonarchKeyCreatedDialogKind { Secret, Public }

public class MonarchKeyCreatedDialogLabels(title: String? = null, label: String? = null, secretNoticeTitle: String? = null, secretNotice: String? = null, publicNoticeTitle: String? = null, publicNotice: String? = null, acknowledge: ((label: String) -> String)? = null, acknowledgeRequired: String? = null, done: String? = null, copy: String? = null, copied: String? = null)

options.name: secret
options.description: The value to show once.

options.name: onDone
options.description: Called when Done or Back closes the dialog after the value was acknowledged, or at once for a public value. Stop showing the dialog here.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the dialog.

options.name: kind
options.description: Secret: a warning notice and an acknowledgement before closing. Public: an information notice and nothing to confirm.

options.name: label
options.description: What the value is, such as "Signing secret". The field's label (unless name is given), part of the copy button's name and of the acknowledgement. "API key" when null.

options.name: name
options.description: The name the person gave it, shown as the field's label; the label then shows under the value.

options.name: title
options.description: Replaces the title "Copy your new key".

options.name: description
options.description: Text under the title.

options.name: requiresAcknowledgement
options.description: Overrides whether the checkbox must be ticked before closing (by default only for a secret).

options.name: masked
options.description: Shows the value in a read-only MonarchSecretField with a reveal toggle; copy works without revealing.

options.name: multiline
options.description: Wraps the whole value over several lines, for certificates and private keys. Ignored when masked.

options.name: note
options.description: Extra text under the value, such as when an old key stops working.

options.name: onCopy
options.description: Called with the copied text after each copy.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string: title, default label, both notices, the acknowledgement, the "confirm first" message, Done, Copy and Copied.

states.name: unacknowledged
states.description: For a secret: Back and taps outside do nothing; Done stays enabled.

states.name: nudged
states.description: Done tapped before ticking: "Confirm that you have saved it before you close this dialog." appears under the checkbox in the strong danger color, is announced through an assertive live region, and is set as the checkbox's error.

states.name: acknowledged
states.description: The checkbox is ticked: Done and Back call onDone.

states.name: public
states.description: An information notice and no checkbox; Done, Back and taps outside are not blocked (taps outside never close it).

states.name: masked
states.description: The value is dots until revealed with the Show toggle.

states.name: new secret
states.description: When the secret changes, the acknowledgement and the message reset.

appearance: The Material 3 alert dialog surface and shape from the theme, a heading title, a warning (secret) or information (public) MonarchBanner, the read-only outlined field in the code type with a copy button, and a checkbox row. The early-Done message is in the strong danger color. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow the theme roles.
platformNotes: The web dialog blocks Escape, outside clicks and its close button until acknowledged; on Android Back is blocked through DialogProperties.dismissOnBackPress until then, and taps outside never close it, so the secret cannot be lost by accident. iOS presents the content in a sheet with swipe to dismiss disabled; Android uses the Material 3 AlertDialog, which the app shows by composing it, as with AlertDialog. The web passes any content as children under the value; here it is the note string. Copy failures cannot happen with the Android clipboard, so there is no onCopyError. TalkBack focus is not moved to the checkbox when Done is tapped early (Compose 1.12 has no API to move accessibility focus); the message is announced and set as the checkbox's error instead. The copied clip of a secret is marked sensitive, so Android 13 and later hide it in the clipboard preview. Monarch does not set FLAG_SECURE: set it on the window of a screen that shows secrets.
accessibility: The title has heading semantics.
The notice is MonarchBanner, which reads its tone with the title and message.
The value is a read-only field named by its label; its copy button is named "Copy API key" (the label) and announces the copy.
The acknowledgement is a MonarchCheckboxRow: one checkbox element with the visible label as its name.
Tapping Done too early announces why through an assertive live region and sets it as the checkbox's error.
Done, the copy button, the reveal toggle and the checkbox have 48dp touch targets; the content scrolls inside the dialog at font scale 2.0 and the title wraps whole.
edgeCases: Back and outside taps are blocked while unacknowledged, but the app can still stop composing the dialog itself; onDone is not called then.
Long and multi-line values wrap in full with multiline; otherwise the field scrolls sideways and copies the whole value.
At the largest text sizes the content scrolls inside the dialog while Done stays visible.
With name given, the label is shown under the field so the person still sees what kind of value it is.

name: MonarchKeyValue
title: KeyValue
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow, androidx.compose.material3.Text, MonarchCopyButton
summary: Compact metadata as inline label and value pairs, such as "Region eu-west · Plan Team · ID 4f2a…".
whenToUse: For a few facts about a record under its title or in a card: region, plan, owner, an id that can be copied.
whenNotToUse: For a full set of facts on a detail screen, use a list of rows or a description list with one fact per row. For a single status, use MonarchStatusBadge.
api: @Composable fun MonarchKeyValue(items: List<MonarchKeyValueItem>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, separator: MonarchKeyValueSeparator = MonarchKeyValueSeparator.Dot, size: MonarchKeyValueSize = MonarchKeyValueSize.Sm, layout: MonarchKeyValueLayout = MonarchKeyValueLayout.Wrap, copyIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, onCopy: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, emptyLabel: String? = null)
class MonarchKeyValueItem(label: String, value: String?, copyable: Boolean = false, copyValue: String? = null, monospace: Boolean = false)
enum class MonarchKeyValueSeparator { Dot, Divider, None }
enum class MonarchKeyValueSize { Sm, Md }
enum class MonarchKeyValueLayout { Wrap, Stack }

options.name: items
options.description: The pairs, in reading order.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the list.

options.name: separator
options.description: Dot, Divider or None, between pairs in the wrap layout.

options.name: size
options.description: Sm uses caption text, Md body text.

options.name: layout
options.description: Wrap flows pairs onto more lines; Stack puts each pair on its own line.

options.name: copyIcon
options.description: The icon of the copy buttons. With it the buttons show only the icon; without it they show the word "Copy".

options.name: onCopy
options.description: Called with the copied text after a copy button is used.

options.name: emptyLabel
options.description: What TalkBack reads for an empty value. null uses monarch_keyvalue_empty, "Not set".

options.name: MonarchKeyValueItem.label
options.description: The key, shown muted.

options.name: MonarchKeyValueItem.value
options.description: The value; null or empty shows a dash.

options.name: MonarchKeyValueItem.copyable
options.description: Adds a copy button that copies the value.

options.name: MonarchKeyValueItem.copyValue
options.description: Adds a copy button that copies this text instead, such as the full id behind a shortened one.

options.name: MonarchKeyValueItem.monospace
options.description: Draws the value in the code face.

states.name: value
states.description: The label in muted text, then the value in default text.

states.name: empty value
states.description: A dash in muted text, read as "Not set". No copy button.

states.name: copyable
states.description: A ghost MonarchCopyButton after the value, with the word "Copy" or the copy icon.

appearance: Labels are muted text and values default text, in caption or body size; monospaced values use the code face. The dot separator is subtle text; the divider is a one-pixel line in the default border color. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web has KeyValue and KeyValueItem as a container and children with any content as the value; here the pairs are values with text, so separators and copy buttons are placed by the component, as on iOS. The web copy button is icon only; Monarch for Android bundles no icons, so without copyIcon the button shows the word "Copy". The web semantics is a description list; Compose has no such role, so each label and value are one TalkBack element read together. iOS shares the name and the options.
accessibility: Each label and its value are one TalkBack element, read label first.
An empty value is shown as a dash and read as "Not set" (or emptyLabel).
Separators are hidden from TalkBack.
A copy button is a separate element named "Copy" followed by the label, for example "Copy ID", with a 48dp touch target; it announces the copy as MonarchCopyButton does.
Pairs and values wrap onto more lines at the largest font size instead of being cut off.
edgeCases: An empty list draws nothing.
copyable on an empty value shows no copy button.
In the wrap layout a separator belongs to the pair after it, so a line can start with a separator when pairs wrap.

title: KeyboardShortcutsSheet
wrapsNative: android.app.Activity.onProvideKeyboardShortcuts and Activity.requestShowKeyboardShortcuts (the system Keyboard Shortcuts Helper), with androidx.compose.ui.input.key.onKeyEvent
summary: An app declares its keyboard shortcuts to the system in Activity.onProvideKeyboardShortcuts, and the system's Keyboard Shortcuts Helper lists them (Meta+/ or requestShowKeyboardShortcuts()). Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: Declare a KeyboardShortcutGroup per area with a KeyboardShortcutInfo per shortcut, handle the keys in Compose with onKeyEvent or onPreviewKeyEvent, and offer a "Keyboard shortcuts" menu item that calls requestShowKeyboardShortcuts().
whenNotToUse: Do not build an in-app sheet that copies the system list; it would drift from the shortcuts the system shows. Do not take shortcuts the system reserves (Meta combinations, Alt+Tab).
api: override fun onProvideKeyboardShortcuts(data: MutableList<KeyboardShortcutGroup>, menu: Menu?, deviceId: Int)
fun Activity.requestShowKeyboardShortcuts()
KeyboardShortcutGroup(label: CharSequence?, items: List<KeyboardShortcutInfo>)
KeyboardShortcutInfo(label: CharSequence?, keycode: Int, modifiers: Int)
fun Modifier.onPreviewKeyEvent(onPreviewKeyEvent: (KeyEvent) -> Boolean): Modifier
val LocalActivity: ProvidableCompositionLocal<Activity?>
appearance: The list is drawn by the system in its own style; Monarch does not theme it.
platformNotes: The web KeyboardShortcutsSheet is a side sheet opened with "?" that lists groups of shortcuts, can be filtered and shows the Command or Control symbol for the platform. On Android the list is the system's Keyboard Shortcuts Helper: the activity returns its groups from onProvideKeyboardShortcuts, and the system shows them, with its own system shortcuts, when the person presses Meta+/ or the app calls requestShowKeyboardShortcuts(). Filtering and the modifier symbols are the system's. The labels are the app's localised strings. Only matters with a hardware keyboard. iPadOS shows its own list in the same way.
accessibility: System behavior: the system shortcuts list is accessible to TalkBack and to keyboard navigation.
Every shortcut must also be reachable without a keyboard, through a visible control.
edgeCases: Without a hardware keyboard requestShowKeyboardShortcuts() may show nothing.
Shortcuts handled in onPreviewKeyEvent run before a focused text field gets the key; check the modifiers so typing is not taken.

title: KPIRow
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow (two columns) or androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyRow with androidx.compose.foundation.gestures.snapping.rememberSnapFlingBehavior (one row that scrolls sideways), holding MonarchStatCard; MonarchInlineErrorRetry for a row that failed
summary: A recipe, not a component: the row of key figures at the top of a dashboard, made of MonarchStatCard in two columns, or in one row that scrolls sideways, with one loading and one error state for the whole row.
whenToUse: At the top of a dashboard or a report screen, for three to six headline figures that are read together, such as revenue, new customers and churn for this month.
whenNotToUse: For one figure, use MonarchStatCard on its own. For figures that each need a title, a menu and a body, use MonarchWidget in a grid. For a long table of figures, use a list with a detail screen.
api: FlowRow(modifier = Modifier.semantics { isTraversalGroup = true; contentDescription = label }, maxItemsInEachRow = 2, horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space3), verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space3)) { items.forEach { MonarchStatCard(label = …, value = …, modifier = Modifier.weight(1f), change = …, loading = loading) } }

LazyRow(state = state, flingBehavior = rememberSnapFlingBehavior(state), horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space3)) { items(items, key = { it.id }) { MonarchStatCard(…, modifier = Modifier.fillParentMaxWidth(0.7f)) } }
MonarchInlineErrorRetry(message = …, onRetry = …, variant = MonarchInlineErrorRetryVariant.Banner)

states.name: two columns
states.description: FlowRow with maxItemsInEachRow = 2 and Modifier.weight(1f) on each card: equal columns that wrap onto new rows. An odd last card takes the full width.

states.name: scroll
states.description: A LazyRow of cards at 70% of the width, so the next card peeks in, with snapping to each card. Use it for a hero row with many figures.

states.name: loading
states.description: Pass loading = true to every card; each shows its value placeholder and reads as loading. With no figures yet, show four placeholder cards labelled "Loading" in the app's language.

states.name: error
states.description: Replace the row with MonarchInlineErrorRetry in its Banner variant: the message, and Try again when the app can retry.

states.name: sizes and variants
states.description: Pass the same size (Sm for a dense row, Lg for a hero row) and variant (Card, or Plain inside a MonarchWidget) to every card.

appearance: Each figure is a MonarchStatCard: the card surface with its subtle border, the label in muted text, the value in the strong text style and the change in its success or danger color with a sign. The gaps are the theme's space3. The same roles change in dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web KPIRow is a component over StatCardGroup with an automatic CSS grid (columns, minItemWidth) and overflow = wrap or scroll. On a phone there is no room for an automatic grid of many columns, so on Android, as planned, it is a recipe: two equal columns (FlowRow) or one row that scrolls sideways with snapping (LazyRow, the pattern of a home screen's tiles). For three or more columns on a tablet, read currentWindowAdaptiveInfo() and raise maxItemsInEachRow. The web's whole-row loading and error props become loading = true on each card and MonarchInlineErrorRetry in place of the row; Monarch ships no strings for the recipe, so the app supplies "Loading" and the group label in its language. The web makes the scrolling row a tab stop; on Android a LazyRow scrolls with swipes and TalkBack's scroll actions. There is no iOS entry for this id.
accessibility: Each figure is one MonarchStatCard, read as one TalkBack element with its label, value and change; the change is also a sign and words, never color alone.
The row is a traversal group with the app's label ("This month"), so the figures are read together.
A scrolling LazyRow exposes TalkBack's scroll forward and backward actions.
A loading card reads its loading state instead of a value; the error banner's Try again is a button with a 48dp touch target.
edgeCases: An odd number of figures in two columns leaves the last card alone on its row at the full width; pass an even number or accept the wide card.
At font scale 2.0 the cards grow taller and the values wrap; the two-column layout keeps working down to a 320dp screen.
A LazyRow cannot sit inside another LazyRow; inside a vertically scrolling screen a LazyRow is fine because it scrolls the other way.
Keys: give each figure a stable id so a scrolling row keeps its position when values update.
