name: MonarchLanguageSelect
title: LanguageSelect
wrapsNative: MonarchCombobox (androidx.compose.material3.ExposedDropdownMenuBox with androidx.compose.material3.ModalBottomSheet) over BCP 47 tags named with java.util.Locale.forLanguageTag and getDisplayName
summary: A searchable picker of a language whose value is its BCP 47 tag, each language shown under its own name with its name in the interface language below.
whenToUse: For the language of the interface, of emails, of a document or of a translation, when the value to store is a language tag.
whenNotToUse: To follow the device language, use the system per-app language setting (AppCompatDelegate.setApplicationLocales or the Android 13 app language screen) instead of a picker of your own.
api: @Composable fun MonarchLanguageSelect(selected: String?, onSelectedChange: (String?) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, locale: Locale? = null, languages: List<String>? = null, priority: List<String> = emptyList(), labelStyle: MonarchLanguageSelectLabelStyle = MonarchLanguageSelectLabelStyle.Endonym, presentation: MonarchComboboxPresentation = MonarchComboboxPresentation.Automatic, enabled: Boolean = true, showTag: Boolean = false, placeholder: String? = null, helperText: String? = null, errorText: String? = null, clearOptionLabel: String? = null, clearIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchLanguageSelectLabels = MonarchLanguageSelectLabels())
enum class MonarchLanguageSelectLabelStyle { Endonym, Localized }
class MonarchLanguageSelectLabels(label: String? = null, suggested: String? = null, all: String? = null, empty: String? = null, combobox: MonarchComboboxLabels = MonarchComboboxLabels())

options.name: selected
options.description: The chosen BCP 47 tag, such as "pt-BR", or null. It is compared in its canonical form.

options.name: onSelectedChange
options.description: Called with the chosen canonical tag, or null when the selection is cleared.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the field.

options.name: locale
options.description: The interface language: the second name of each row and the sort order use it. null uses the first locale of the configuration.

options.name: languages
options.description: Limits the list to these tags, such as the languages the product is translated into. null lists about 80 widely used languages.

options.name: priority
options.description: Tags listed first under "Suggested" while nothing is typed, such as the device's languages.

options.name: labelStyle
options.description: Which name each row shows first: the language's own ("Deutsch") or the interface language's ("German").

options.name: presentation
options.description: Menu, Sheet, or Automatic: a menu for up to eight languages, a sheet otherwise.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the list can be opened.

options.name: showTag
options.description: Shows the tag at the end of each row.

options.name: placeholder
options.description: Shown in the empty field while nothing is chosen.

options.name: helperText
options.description: Guidance below the field.

options.name: errorText
options.description: An error message; replaces the helper text and is set as the field's error.

options.name: clearOptionLabel
options.description: Adds a first row that clears the selection. Hidden while searching.

options.name: clearIcon
options.description: The icon of a clear button at the end of the field while something is chosen. Monarch bundles no icons; without it there is no clear button.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings: the label "Language", "Suggested", "All languages", "No languages match" and the combobox's own strings.

states.name: closed
states.description: The field shows the chosen language's label, or the placeholder (or the floating label) while nothing is chosen.

states.name: open
states.description: The bottom sheet (or, for eight options or fewer, the menu) lists the options; while nothing is typed the suggested ones come first under their heading.

states.name: searching
states.description: Typing filters the list, best matches first, without headings; when nothing matches the list says so.

states.name: error
states.description: The field has the danger outline and the message below it, and the message is the field's error for TalkBack.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The field takes the disabled colors and does not open.

appearance: The field is MonarchCombobox's: MonarchTextField's colors, a surface fill with the input border, the danger strong color in error; the sheet is on the surface color, second lines, hints and headings are muted text and the chosen row's radio mark is the accent strong color. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Built on MonarchCombobox, so long lists open a Material 3 bottom sheet with a search field instead of the web's popover. Names come from java.util.Locale.getDisplayName, which names regional variants with the region in brackets ("English (United Kingdom)") where the web's Intl.DisplayNames says "British English". The web marks each endonym with its lang attribute so screen readers pronounce it in its language; MonarchComboboxOption takes plain strings, so TalkBack reads every name with the interface voice. The value is controlled only. iOS has no LanguageSelect yet; the name is the planned shared one.
accessibility: The field is MonarchCombobox's Material 3 exposed dropdown anchor: TalkBack reads the label, the chosen value and the expand state; double tap opens the list.

Every row is read with its label, second line and hint, and the chosen row is selected with a filled radio mark, so the choice does not rely on color; in the sheet each row is a radio button at least 48dp high.
The headings over suggested and other entries are headings; the no-match message is a polite live region.
The error is the field's error semantics and is shown as text.
Endonyms are read in the interface language's voice; the second line gives the name in the interface language, so the row is understandable either way.
edgeCases: Tags are canonicalised ("EN-us" becomes "en-US"); invalid tags and repeats are dropped from the list.
A selected tag that is not in the list is still listed.
When both names are the same (English in an English interface) the row has no second line.
Searching matches either name, the tag and the English name.

name: MonarchLeaderboard
title: Leaderboard
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of rows with androidx.compose.foundation.clickable, MonarchAvatar, MonarchProgress (androidx.compose.material3.LinearProgressIndicator), MonarchDeltaIndicator, MonarchBadge, MonarchSkeleton, MonarchEmptyState and MonarchInlineErrorRetry
summary: A ranked list for dashboards: rank, avatar, name, value, an optional change and a bar relative to the leader, with ties sharing a rank and the viewer's own row tagged.
whenToUse: On a dashboard that compares a few people, teams or things by one figure (tickets solved per agent, reply time per team), especially when viewers want to see where they stand.
whenNotToUse: For many columns per entry, use a data table. For plain ranked bars without people or ranks, use MonarchBarList. For a single figure, use a metric.

public class MonarchLeaderboardEntry(name: String, value: Double, id: String? = null, display: String? = null, secondary: String? = null, image: Painter? = null, seed: String? = null, avatarShape: MonarchAvatarShape = MonarchAvatarShape.Circle, change: Double? = null, badge: String? = null, badgeTone: MonarchTone = MonarchTone.Neutral, current: Boolean = false)
public class MonarchLeaderboardLabels(you: String? = null, empty: String? = null, loading: String? = null, retry: String? = null, more: ((Int) -> String)? = null, rank: ((Int) -> String)? = null)

options.name: entries
options.description: The entries, best first, or set sort.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the board.

options.name: sort
options.description: Descending ranks the largest value first, Ascending the smallest (response times), None keeps the order given. Equal values share a rank.

options.name: label
options.description: Names the board for TalkBack, "Top agents by tickets solved".

options.name: valueLabel
options.description: What the value counts, read after it: "42 tickets solved".

options.name: changeComparison
options.description: The period every change compares with, "vs last week".

options.name: changeGoodDirection
options.description: Which direction of change is good, for every row.

options.name: showAvatars
options.description: Shows the 24dp avatars.

options.name: showBars
options.description: Shows a bar under each name, its length relative to the largest value shown.

options.name: highlightTop
options.description: Puts ranks 1 to 3 on a filled accent marker.

options.name: limit
options.description: Shows at most this many rows. null, 0 or less shows all.

options.name: total
options.description: How many entries exist when entries is already a top N; adds "N more".

options.name: loading
options.description: Shows placeholder rows instead of the list.

options.name: loadingRows
options.description: The number of placeholder rows; at least one.

options.name: errorMessage
options.description: Replaces the list with this failure.

options.name: retrying
options.description: The retry is running: the Retry button shows its busy state.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes a value without display. null writes a number in the current locale.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Repeats a failed load: adds a Retry button to the error.

options.name: onShowMore
options.description: Makes "N more" a button, for example to open the full report.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Makes each row a button.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

states.name: ready
states.description: Ranked rows; equal values share a rank.

states.name: current
states.description: The viewer's row on the accent subtle background with the accent border, tagged "(you)".

states.name: top three
states.description: With highlightTop, ranks 1 to 3 sit on a filled accent circle.

states.name: loading
states.description: Placeholder rows, one element read as "Loading ranking".

states.name: empty
states.description: A small MonarchEmptyState, "Nothing to rank yet".

states.name: failed
states.description: The message with a Retry button when onRetry is given, or the message in the danger text color as a polite live region.

appearance: Names and values in the default text color; ranks, secondary lines and the "(you)" tag in the muted text color. Bars are MonarchProgress: the accent solid fill on the emphasis track. The current row uses the accent subtle background and the accent border. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes come from these roles.
platformNotes: The parity map names a LazyColumn; a board shows a handful of rows inside a dashboard that already scrolls, and a LazyColumn cannot be nested in a vertically scrolling parent, so the rows are a Column; for hundreds of entries use limit and onShowMore. The web names become links with href and "N more" links to moreHref; on Android, as on iOS, rows and "N more" call onSelect and onShowMore and the app navigates. The web secondary line and badge take any content; here they are strings, the badge drawn as a MonarchBadge. Each entry's change is a ratio, with the comparison and good direction set once for the board. The web's format and notation become formatValue, the same writer MonarchBarList takes, so no metric format type is added; the sort reuses MonarchBarListSort. Compose has no ordered-list role, so each row speaks its rank. iOS moves the value under the name at the largest text sizes; on Android the name wraps beside the value.
accessibility: Each row is one TalkBack element read in order: "Rank 1:", the name, "(you)", the badge, the secondary line, the value with its valueLabel ("42 tickets solved") and the change.
Avatars and bars are hidden; the name and the number with its unit carry the data.
The viewer's row is marked in words, not only by its tint.
With onSelect each row is a button at least 48dp high.
The placeholder rows are one element named "Loading ranking".
The board is a traversal group named by label.
An error without retry is a polite live region.
edgeCases: Equal values share a rank and the next rank skips: 1, 1, 3.
Bars are relative to the largest magnitude shown, so a negative value draws a bar of its size; all zero draws empty bars.
A limit of 0 or less shows every row.
A total smaller than the rows shown adds no "N more".
Long names wrap; the value column keeps its width.

title: LeaveWorkspaceFlow
wrapsNative: MonarchDialog for the blocked case, or a warning MonarchBanner on the screen; MonarchBottomSheet with dismissible = false while leaving for the confirmation, holding MonarchConsequenceList, MonarchInlineNotice and MonarchButtons
summary: A recipe, not a component: a member leaves a workspace after a confirmation that lists what they lose and what stays, or learns why they cannot leave yet and how to fix it.
whenToUse: On a workspace's settings screen, for a member who wants to leave a shared workspace.
whenNotToUse: To remove someone else, use the members screen's own remove action. To delete the workspace, use a confirm dialog with MonarchTypeToConfirmInput. For a pause that keeps the membership, use the deactivate recipe.
api: MonarchButton(text = "Leave workspace", onClick = { if (isLastOwner) blocked = true else confirming = true }, variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Danger)

MonarchDialog(onDismissRequest = …, title = "You can’t leave yet", description = reason, actions = { MonarchButton("Close", …, variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Ghost); MonarchButton("Transfer ownership", …) })

MonarchBottomSheet(onDismissRequest = { confirming = false }, title = "Leave Acme?", dismissible = !leaving) { MonarchConsequenceList(…); MonarchButton("Leave workspace", …, variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Danger, loading = leaving) }
MonarchBanner(message = reason, tone = MonarchTone.Warning, title = "You can’t leave yet", action = { … })

options.name: isLastOwner
options.description: The app's check, or any other reason leaving is blocked: the button opens the explanation instead of the confirmation.

options.name: leaving
options.description: Passed to the danger button's loading while the request runs; it also disables Cancel and stops the sheet from being dismissed.

options.name: failure
options.description: A failed request, shown in a danger MonarchInlineNotice in the sheet.

states.name: confirm
states.description: A sheet with the title naming the workspace, a line saying it happens at once, the consequence list and a danger Leave workspace button with Cancel.

states.name: leaving
states.description: Leave workspace shows its progress indicator; Cancel is disabled and the sheet cannot be swiped or backed away.

states.name: failed
states.description: A danger MonarchInlineNotice in the sheet; the person can try again.

states.name: blocked
states.description: When the person is the last owner, or the app has another reason, the button opens an alert dialog that says why and offers the fix (Transfer ownership) instead of leaving. A warning MonarchBanner can say the same on the screen before the button is pressed.

appearance: Every part is an existing Monarch component in the theme on the Material 3 sheet and dialog surfaces: the title in the title style, the consequence list with its kind marks, a full-width danger button over a ghost Cancel, and the warning banner's subtle warning fill. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web's LeaveWorkspaceFlow is one component built on ConfirmDialog and Dialog. On Android it is a recipe, as on iOS: the confirmation, with a consequence list and the pending and error states, is a MonarchBottomSheet, and the blocked case, which only needs a sentence and two buttons, is a MonarchDialog. The parity map lists alert (MonarchBanner on Android): the second example shows the blocked reason as a warning MonarchBanner with the fix as its action, for screens that know beforehand that leaving is blocked; iOS uses only the system alert. The web's default consequences and messages are written in the app here. dismissible = !leaving keeps the sheet open while leaving, where iOS uses interactiveDismissDisabled.
accessibility: The sheet's title uses the title style, which MonarchText marks as a heading.
MonarchConsequenceList reads each consequence with its kind, so removed, kept and warning do not depend on the mark.
The blocked explanation is a Material 3 alert dialog, read in full by TalkBack with its buttons, or a MonarchBanner read with its tone.
Buttons are MonarchButtons with 48dp touch targets and a busy state while leaving.
The sheet cannot be dismissed while leaving, so the result is not lost.
edgeCases: Check whether the person is the last owner on the server as well; the recipe's check only decides which dialog opens.
After leaving, navigate away from the workspace: its screens are no longer available.
List the apps the person loses by name when the workspace has several.

name: MonarchLifecycleBadge
title: LifecycleBadge
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row, androidx.compose.material3.Text
summary: The release stage of an API, SDK or feature (planned, preview, stable, deprecated) or a custom stage, as a quiet capsule with a coloured dot and a text label.
whenToUse: Beside the name of an API, an SDK, an endpoint or a feature to say how far it is in its lifecycle, or for a custom stage such as a customer's lifecycle stage.
whenNotToUse: For a status such as Draft or Overdue use MonarchBadge. For an HTTP method use MonarchMethodBadge.
api: @Composable fun MonarchLifecycleBadge(lifecycle: MonarchLifecycle, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, tone: MonarchTone? = null, showDot: Boolean = true, label: String? = null)
@Composable fun MonarchLifecycleBadge(stage: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, tone: MonarchTone? = null, showDot: Boolean = true, label: String? = null)
enum class MonarchLifecycle(val key: String) { Planned, Preview, Stable, Deprecated }

options.name: lifecycle
options.description: The built-in stage: Planned, Preview, Stable or Deprecated.

options.name: stage
options.description: In the second overload, the key of a stage. One of the four built-in keys, matched exactly, is drawn as that stage; any other key is neutral and shown as readable text unless label and tone are given.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the component.

options.name: tone
options.description: Replaces the tone of the stage: planned neutral, preview info, stable success, deprecated warning, anything else neutral.

options.name: showDot
options.description: Whether the dot before the label is drawn.

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the built-in label (monarch_lifecyclebadge_planned, _preview, _stable, _deprecated). Already localised.

states.name: default
states.description: Not interactive; one look per tone.

states.name: without dot
states.description: showDot = false leaves the bordered capsule and the label.

appearance: A capsule on the surface color with default text and a 1dp border; the tone is only in the border (the tone's border role) and the dot (its strong role). Neutral uses the default border and the subtle text color for the dot, in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The parity map named MonarchBadge as the base. MonarchBadge colors its text with the tone and has no dot, so this component draws the web's quieter look from the same tone palette, as iOS does. The web's accent tone is not offered because MonarchTone has no accent case; the web's sm size is not offered: the label is the caption role and follows the font size setting. The web's messages map is the label parameter and the string resources. The web's dot prop is showDot; iOS calls it showsDot.
accessibility: Read by TalkBack as its label; the dot has no semantics, so the label carries the meaning without the color.
The label and the dot grow with the font size setting.
Not interactive: it has no click action and no touch target.
edgeCases: A stage key the app does not know is shown as the key with underscores and hyphens turned into spaces and a capital first letter; that text is not localised.
Keys are matched exactly: "Stable" is not the built-in stage stable.
An empty key with no label draws a capsule with only the dot.
Long labels wrap inside the capsule.

name: MonarchLightbox
title: Lightbox
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.ui.window.Dialog (full screen), androidx.compose.foundation.pager.HorizontalPager, androidx.compose.foundation.gestures.transformable and detectTapGestures
summary: A full-screen viewer for images and videos: swipe or step between items, pinch, double-tap or use buttons to zoom, with a caption and a position count.
whenToUse: To look at one or more pictures or videos at full size from a thumbnail, with a caption that belongs to the design: attachments in a conversation, a gallery on a record.
whenNotToUse: Not for documents, PDFs or files of unknown type: hand them to the system with an Intent.ACTION_VIEW, or use file-preview. Not for a single decorative image.
api: @Composable fun MonarchLightbox(items: List<MonarchLightboxItem>, selectedIndex: Int, onSelectedIndexChange: (Int) -> Unit, onDismissRequest: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, looping: Boolean = false, maximumZoom: Float = 4f, onShare: ((index: Int) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchLightboxLabels = MonarchLightboxLabels())
class MonarchLightboxItem(image: Painter?, alt: String, caption: String? = null, video: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null)

class MonarchLightboxLabels(title: String? = null, previous: String? = null, next: String? = null, zoomIn: String? = null, zoomOut: String? = null, resetZoom: String? = null, close: String? = null, share: String? = null, position: ((number: Int, count: Int) -> String)? = null, unavailable: String? = null)

options.name: items
options.description: The images and videos, in order. Each has an image Painter (or null), alt text, an optional caption and optionally the app's video player.

options.name: selectedIndex
options.description: The item on screen, from 0. An index outside the items shows the nearest item; it is not reported back until the person moves.

options.name: onSelectedIndexChange
options.description: Called with the new index after a swipe, Previous, Next or an arrow key.

options.name: onDismissRequest
options.description: Called by Close, the back gesture and Escape. Stop showing the viewer in it.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the viewer's surface.

options.name: looping
options.description: Whether Next on the last item goes to the first, and Previous on the first to the last. Swiping does not wrap.

options.name: maximumZoom
options.description: The largest zoom factor of an image. Values below 1 count as 1, which turns zoom off and hides the zoom buttons.

options.name: onShare
options.description: When set, a Share button calls it with the index of the item on screen; the app starts its share sheet.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings: the viewer's name, the button names, the position text and the unavailable text.

states.name: fitted
states.description: The image fits the stage. A sideways swipe moves to the next or previous item. Zoom out and the level button are disabled.

states.name: zoomed
states.description: The image is larger than the stage and a drag pans it, without leaving its edges. The level shows as a percentage on the reset button. Zoom in is disabled at the largest zoom.

states.name: first or last item
states.description: Without looping, Previous or Next is disabled.

states.name: single item
states.description: No position count and no Previous and Next.

states.name: unavailable
states.description: An item without a picture or video, and an empty list, show "This file can’t be shown." in place of the media. Zoom is hidden.

states.name: video
states.description: The app's player, named by the alt text. Zoom is hidden.

appearance: The viewer fills the screen with the canvas background role and the default text role. Toolbar buttons are ghost MonarchButtons, Previous and Next secondary ones, with their disabled roles; the unavailable text uses the muted text role. The same roles are used in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web Lightbox is a dialog over a translucent scrim with arrow buttons beside the image; here it is a full-screen Dialog on the opaque canvas, and swiping is the main gesture, with Previous and Next under the media for TalkBack, Switch Access and keyboard users. Pinch and double tap are added to the web's zoom buttons. Monarch bundles no icons, so the tools are text: a minus sign, the level, a plus sign, Share and Close, each with a spoken name. Monarch loads nothing: an image is a Painter the app has loaded (the web takes a URL and checks its scheme), and a video is the app's own player in the item's video slot, because Media3 is not a Monarch dependency; the web's caption tracks belong to that player. The web's Download link becomes onShare, which the app answers with its share sheet. The web's trigger is not needed: any button sets the state that shows the viewer. iOS uses the same names, with selection and onClose where Android uses selectedIndex with onSelectedIndexChange and onDismissRequest, as Compose does.
accessibility: The viewer is a pane named "Media viewer", shown in its own dialog window, so TalkBack stays inside it; back, Escape and Close call onDismissRequest.
An image is one element with its alt text as the name, the image role and the zoom level as its state; its custom actions Zoom in and Zoom out step the zoom.
The position text is a polite live region read as "2 of 5: Team photo", so moving to another item is announced.
Zoom in, zoom out, reset zoom, share, close, previous and next are buttons with spoken names and 48dp touch targets; unavailable steps and zoom limits are disabled, not hidden.
A video's alt text names the area that holds the app's player.
Zoom changes from buttons, keys and double tap animate unless animations are removed. The toolbar wraps at large font sizes and a long caption scrolls in its box.

With a keyboard, the left and right arrows step (mirrored right to left), +, - and 0 zoom and Escape closes, once focus is in the viewer. The key mapping is unit-tested; delivery of key events to the dialog window was not exercised end to end.
edgeCases: Zoom belongs to one item: moving to another item returns to fitted.
While zoomed, a sideways drag pans the image and does not change the item; zoom out first, or use the buttons.
An empty alt is allowed by the type but leaves the image without a spoken name; always give one.
A caption taller than 96dp scrolls inside its box.
Looping from the last item to the first jumps without the paging animation.
Pinch and pan were exercised only through the zoom arithmetic in unit tests; real multi-touch was not run on a device.
Pinch zooms around the center of the image, not around the fingers.

name: MonarchLineChart
title: LineChart
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.Canvas (DrawScope.drawPath, drawLine, drawCircle and drawText) with pointerInput tap and horizontal drag gestures; inside MonarchChartFrame with MonarchChartLegend and MonarchChartTable; axis ticks and scale from the MonarchBarChart core
summary: A line or area chart for trends over ordered categories or dates, with several series, gaps, reference lines, touch inspection, legend toggles and a data table.
whenToUse: For a trend over time or another ordered axis, such as sessions per day or latency per hour, with one to five series.
whenNotToUse: To compare separate categories, use MonarchBarChart; for parts of a whole, MonarchDonutChart or MonarchStackedProportionBar; for a word-sized trend inside text or a table cell, MonarchSparkline.
api: @Composable fun MonarchLineChart(title: String, categories: List<String>, series: List<MonarchLineChartSeries>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, description: String? = null, xTitle: String? = null, summary: String? = null, variant: MonarchLineChartVariant = MonarchLineChartVariant.Line, curve: MonarchLineChartCurve = MonarchLineChartCurve.Linear, status: MonarchChartFrameStatus = MonarchChartFrameStatus.Ready, hiddenSeries: Set<String>? = null, onHiddenSeriesChange: ((Set<String>) -> Unit)? = null, activeIndex: Int? = null, onActiveIndexChange: ((Int?) -> Unit)? = null, referenceLines: List<MonarchLineChartReferenceLine> = emptyList(), valueRange: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Double>? = null, includeZero: Boolean = true, showPoints: Boolean = false, legendToggle: Boolean = true, tableToggle: Boolean = true, emptyMessage: String? = null, footer: String? = null, height: Dp? = null, labels: MonarchLineChartLabels = MonarchLineChartLabels(), formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = null, onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null, onSelect: ((Int) -> Unit)? = null)

@JvmName("MonarchLineChartOfDates") @Composable fun MonarchLineChart(title: String, dates: List<Long>, series: List<MonarchLineChartSeries>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, description: String? = null, xTitle: String? = null, summary: String? = null, variant: MonarchLineChartVariant = MonarchLineChartVariant.Line, curve: MonarchLineChartCurve = MonarchLineChartCurve.Linear, status: MonarchChartFrameStatus = MonarchChartFrameStatus.Ready, hiddenSeries: Set<String>? = null, onHiddenSeriesChange: ((Set<String>) -> Unit)? = null, activeIndex: Int? = null, onActiveIndexChange: ((Int?) -> Unit)? = null, referenceLines: List<MonarchLineChartReferenceLine> = emptyList(), valueRange: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Double>? = null, includeZero: Boolean = true, showPoints: Boolean = false, legendToggle: Boolean = true, tableToggle: Boolean = true, emptyMessage: String? = null, footer: String? = null, height: Dp? = null, labels: MonarchLineChartLabels = MonarchLineChartLabels(), formatDate: ((Long) -> String)? = null, formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = null, onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null, onSelect: ((Int) -> Unit)? = null)
class MonarchLineChartSeries(key: String, label: String, values: List<Double?>, color: MonarchChartColor? = null, dashed: Boolean = false)
class MonarchLineChartReferenceLine(value: Double, label: String? = null)

class MonarchLineChartLabels(frame: MonarchChartFrameLabels = MonarchChartFrameLabels(), category: String? = null, date: String? = null, noData: String? = null, details: String? = null, clearSelection: String? = null)
enum class MonarchLineChartVariant { Line, Area }
enum class MonarchLineChartCurve { Linear, Monotone }

options.name: title
options.description: The chart's name: the frame heading and the plot's spoken name.

options.name: categories
options.description: The x values in order, already localised. Spaced evenly.

options.name: dates
options.description: The x values in order, as epoch milliseconds in UTC. Spaced by time, so uneven dates show.

options.name: series
options.description: The measures: key, label, one value per x value (null or not finite is a gap), an optional color slot and dashed.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the frame.

options.name: description
options.description: One line under the title: the period, the unit or the question it answers.

options.name: xTitle
options.description: The heading of the x column of the data table.

options.name: summary
options.description: Replaces the generated spoken summary.

options.name: variant
options.description: Line, or Area: the line with a soft fill down to the baseline.

options.name: curve
options.description: Linear, or Monotone: smooth without overshooting the values.

options.name: status
options.description: Ready, Loading, Empty or Error, passed to the frame. Ready without x values or series shows Empty.

options.name: hiddenSeries
options.description: The keys of hidden series. null lets the chart keep its own set, changed by the legend.

options.name: onHiddenSeriesChange
options.description: Called with the new hidden set when the legend changes it.

options.name: activeIndex
options.description: The inspected x value, used when onActiveIndexChange is set. Give several charts on the same x values one state to share the crosshair. An index outside the x values is ignored.

options.name: onActiveIndexChange
options.description: Makes the inspection controlled: called with the index the user inspects, or null when it is cleared. null keeps the inspection inside the chart.

options.name: referenceLines
options.description: Dashed horizontal lines with a value and a label: targets, baselines, service levels.

options.name: valueRange
options.description: Fixes the value axis, such as 0.0..100.0 for percentages.

options.name: includeZero
options.description: Whether the value axis keeps zero. Turn it off for values far from zero.

options.name: showPoints
options.description: A dot on every value. Lone values between gaps always get one.

options.name: legendToggle
options.description: Whether legend entries show and hide their series. The legend appears with two or more series.

options.name: tableToggle
options.description: Whether "View as table" is offered.

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: The message of the frame's empty state.

options.name: footer
options.description: Notes under the chart: the source, the last update.

options.name: height
options.description: The plot height, kept in every status.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for Category, Date, No data, Details, Clear and the frame's strings; frame.noValue is also the text of a gap.

options.name: formatDate
options.description: Writes a date on the axis, in the inspection row, TalkBack, the table and the summary. The abbreviated month and day in the current locale, in UTC, by default.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes values in the inspection row, TalkBack, the table, the summary and on the axis. A number in the current locale (compact on the axis) by default.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Try again in the error status.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Drill-in: called with the x index from Details in the inspection row or from the TalkBack action of that x value.

states.name: default
states.description: One line per shown series in its color slot, over subtle gridlines with value labels at the start edge and x labels under the plot; dashed series have a dashed line.

states.name: inspecting
states.description: After a tap or during a drag, or while activeIndex is set: a vertical crosshair in the strong border color, a larger ringed dot on each shown series and a row under the plot with the x value and every shown series' value, plus Details (with onSelect) and Clear.

states.name: series hidden
states.description: The series leaves the plot and the value range; its legend entry reads Hidden; it stays in the data table.

states.name: gap
states.description: A missing value breaks the line; a lone value between gaps is a dot.

states.name: area
states.description: Each line has a fill of its own hue mixed towards the surface color, down to zero, or to the nearest end of the axis when zero is left out.

states.name: loading, empty, error
states.description: The frame's skeleton, empty state or error with Try again, at the chart's height.

states.name: table
states.description: "View as table" swaps the plot for the data table, one row per x value.

appearance: Lines are 2dp in the theme's data colors 1 to 5 in series order, Neutral in the subtle text color; the area fill is the series color mixed 80% towards the surface color, opaque. Gridlines use the subtle border color, the zero line and crosshair the strong border color, axis labels the muted text color and reference lines the subtle text color. Every color is a theme role or a mix of two roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes are covered.
platformNotes: Drawn with a Compose Canvas (iOS uses Swift Charts, the web SVG); Android has no first-party chart library and Monarch adds none. The value axis, ticks and scale are the MonarchBarChart core, so the two charts read alike. The web xScale option is the choice of overload: categories are spaced evenly, dates (epoch milliseconds, UTC) by time; the web's numeric x values are not offered. Inspection follows MonarchBarChart rather than iOS: the tap or drag keeps the inspected point after the finger lifts, and its values are shown in a row under the plot with Details and Clear instead of a floating tooltip, so they are announced as a polite live region and can be read at large font sizes. As on the web, the activeIndex is controlled only through onActiveIndexChange, because Kotlin cannot tell an unset value from null. onSelect is the web onPointSelect and is offered here (iOS does not). The area fill is an opaque mix of the series color and the surface color instead of the web's transparent fill, because Monarch never dims with alpha. There is no keyboard arrow navigation of points: TalkBack users swipe through one element per x value. The web formatTick option is formatValue. The frame's header actions slot is not offered.
accessibility: The plot is one element with the image role, named by the title, whose state description is the generated summary ("5 points, Mon to Fri. This week: low 820, high 1,330, latest 1,330. Target 1,200") or the summary parameter.

After it, one element per x value in order (traversal index), placed over that point's strip of the plot and read as the x value and each shown series' value ("Mon: This week 820, Last week 700"); a gap is read as "No value".
With onSelect each x value element has a custom action "Details, Mon"; without it, the elements have no action.
The values of an inspected point are shown under the plot in a polite live region, with Details and Clear buttons that keep a 48dp touch target.
Series differ by their names in the legend and, where dashed is set, by a dashed line and marker, not by color alone.
Legend entries are toggles named by the series, with Hidden as their state while hidden; the last shown series cannot be hidden.
"View as table" shows every value as text; each row is read as the x value then every series and its value.
edgeCases: null and non-finite values are gaps, never zero; a series shorter than the x values ends in gaps and extra values are ignored.
A ready chart without x values or without series shows the empty state.
A single series has no legend; the title names it.
With includeZero off and no valueRange, the axis fits the values and a flat series is padded by a tenth of its value; the area fills down to the bottom of the axis.
Reference lines are part of the value range, so a target far above the data stays visible.
X labels thin out to keep their width apart, always keeping the first and the last; long labels are cut with an ellipsis.
Duplicate categories are separate points; equal dates share one position.
Touch inspection and the point elements were checked with Robolectric semantics and touch tests, not with TalkBack on a device.

name: MonarchLineItemsEditor
title: LineItemsEditor
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of rows, each in an androidx.compose.material3.SwipeToDismissBox (swipe toward the start removes); MonarchTextField, MonarchNumberInput and MonarchCurrencyInput fields, MonarchMoney amounts, MonarchButton; androidx.compose.material3.SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow for the discount kind and MonarchSelect (ExposedDropdownMenuBox) for preset tax rates; a polite live region for announcements
summary: Editable invoice, quote or proposal rows (description, quantity, unit price) with each row's amount and an optional discount, tax and total computed exactly in BigDecimal and kept in minor units.
whenToUse: To create or edit the billable rows of an invoice, quote, proposal or purchase order inside the app's scrolling form, or to show the rows of a sent document read-only with the same totals.
whenNotToUse: For a finished invoice laid out as a document, use MonarchInvoiceView. For payroll lines that are calculated, not typed, use MonarchPayslipView. For editable tables of non-monetary data, use MonarchDataTable.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchLineItemsEditor(items: List<MonarchLineItem>, onItemsChange: (List<MonarchLineItem>) -> Unit, currencyCode: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, taxRate: BigDecimal? = null, onTaxRateChange: ((BigDecimal) -> Unit)? = null, taxRateOptions: List<MonarchLineItemsTaxRateOption> = emptyList(), discount: MonarchLineItemsDiscount? = null, onDiscountChange: ((MonarchLineItemsDiscount) -> Unit)? = null, error: String? = null, minimumItems: Int = 0, required: Boolean = false, readOnly: Boolean = false, enabled: Boolean = true, showTotals: Boolean = true, labels: MonarchLineItemsEditorLabels = MonarchLineItemsEditorLabels(), makeItem: (() -> MonarchLineItem)? = null)
class MonarchLineItem(id: String = UUID.randomUUID().toString(), description: String = "", quantity: BigDecimal? = BigDecimal.ONE, unitPrice: BigDecimal? = null)
class MonarchLineItemsDiscount(kind: MonarchLineItemsDiscountKind, value: BigDecimal)
enum class MonarchLineItemsDiscountKind { Percent, Amount }
class MonarchLineItemsTaxRateOption(value: BigDecimal, label: String)

class MonarchLineItemsTotals(items: List<MonarchLineItem>, currencyCode: String, taxRate: BigDecimal? = null, discount: MonarchLineItemsDiscount? = null) { val lines: List<Long>; val subtotal: Long; val discount: Long; val tax: Long; val total: Long }

class MonarchLineItemsEditorLabels(label: String? = null, item: ((number: Int) -> String)? = null, description: String? = null, quantity: String? = null, unitPrice: ((currencyCode: String) -> String)? = null, amount: String? = null, descriptionPlaceholder: String? = null, addItem: String? = null, remove: String? = null, removeItem: ((number: Int, description: String) -> String)? = null, empty: String? = null, added: ((number: Int) -> String)? = null, removed: ((number: Int) -> String)? = null, subtotal: String? = null, discount: String? = null, discountType: String? = null, percentOption: String? = null, tax: ((rate: String) -> String)? = null, taxRate: String? = null, total: String? = null, required: String? = null, quantityTimesPrice: ((quantity: String, unitPrice: String) -> String)? = null)

options.name: items
options.description: The rows: an id, a description and a BigDecimal quantity and unit price (null while a field is empty, counted as zero).

options.name: onItemsChange
options.description: Called with the whole new list after an edit, an addition or a removal. The editor keeps no rows of its own.

options.name: currencyCode
options.description: The ISO 4217 code of the document: the symbol, the unit price heading and the minor unit (USD 2, JPY 0, KWD 3). The editor never converts.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the editor.

options.name: taxRate
options.description: The tax as a percentage of the discounted subtotal (18 for 18%). null for no tax row.

options.name: onTaxRateChange
options.description: Makes the tax rate editable in the totals (iOS isTaxRateEditable with a Binding): a menu of taxRateOptions or a number field.

options.name: taxRateOptions
options.description: Preset rates offered in a menu when the rate is editable. Empty for a typed percentage.

options.name: discount
options.description: A percentage or an amount off the subtotal, capped at it. null for no discount row.

options.name: onDiscountChange
options.description: Makes the discount's value (number or currency field) and kind (segmented buttons) editable (iOS isDiscountEditable with a Binding).

options.name: error
options.description: An error for the whole list, such as "Add at least one item", shown under the rows in the danger text color and announced politely.

options.name: minimumItems
options.description: Rows cannot be removed below this count.

options.name: required
options.description: An asterisk after the heading, read as "Required".

options.name: readOnly
options.description: Rows as text (description and "12 × $95.00") without fields, buttons or swipe, for a sent document.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether anything can be changed. When off the fields and buttons are disabled, rows cannot be swiped and the rate editors are not shown.

options.name: showTotals
options.description: Whether the subtotal, discount, tax and total are shown.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: makeItem
options.description: Builds the row added by Add item. Default: an empty row of one unit with a random UUID.

states.name: editing
states.description: Each row has a header ("Item n" and its amount) with a Remove button, the description field, and the quantity and unit price fields side by side (stacked from font scale 1.3). Add item follows the rows.

states.name: empty
states.description: "No items yet. Add one to start." in place of the rows; totals are zero.

states.name: error
states.description: The error under the rows in the danger text color, in a polite live region.

states.name: read-only
states.description: Rows are text; no fields, add, remove or swipe; the discount and tax rates are written in their titles ("Tax (18%)").

states.name: disabled
states.description: With enabled = false every field and button is disabled, rows cannot be swiped and the rate editors are hidden.

states.name: at the minimum
states.description: Remove buttons are disabled and rows cannot be swiped.

appearance: Rows sit on the surface color divided by subtle borders. Row headers are the muted label style with the amount in the default text color; fields are the Monarch field surface and border; the required marker and the error are the danger text color; the swipe background is the danger subtle surface with danger text; the total row is the strong body style below a divider. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow the same roles.
platformNotes: A Column, not the planned LazyColumn: the editor sits inside the app's own scrolling form (as iOS uses Sections inside a Form), and a LazyColumn nested in a vertically scrolling parent cannot be measured; invoices have tens of rows, not thousands. The web table becomes the phone pattern of one block per row. Rows are removed with the Remove button or the Material 3 swipe toward the start. Numbers are typed in MonarchNumberInput and MonarchCurrencyInput, which read the text when the field loses focus or on Done and flag text that is not a number, so there is no web parseDecimal; values are BigDecimal and the unit price is kept to the currency's decimals by MonarchCurrencyInput (minor units). Enter does not add a row and focus does not move to a new row; additions and removals are announced instead, as on iOS. Hoisted callbacks (onItemsChange, onTaxRateChange, onDiscountChange) replace the iOS Bindings and is-editable flags; required, readOnly and enabled replace isRequired, isReadOnly and .disabled. Monarch bundles no icons, so Add item and Remove are text buttons and the error has no icon. Marked experimental, as a billing pattern, until a Rook app adopts it. computeLineItemTotals is MonarchLineItemsTotals.
accessibility: The heading is a heading, read as "Line items, Required" when required.
Each row starts with a heading read as "Item 2, Amount $1,140.00".
The description, quantity and unit price fields are named by their visible labels and keep the behavior of MonarchTextField, MonarchNumberInput and MonarchCurrencyInput.
The Remove button is read as "Remove item 2: Design hours" and has a 48dp target; the swipe background is hidden from TalkBack because the button does the same.
Adding and removing a row is announced through a polite live region ("Added item 3", "Removed item 2"), and so is the error.
Each totals row is one element read as its title and amount, such as "Total, $2,174.74".
edgeCases: Each row is rounded to the minor unit half away from zero (1 × 1.005 USD is $1.01) and totals are sums of whole minor units, so the total equals the rows shown; ten rows of 0.10 make exactly 1.00.
A discount larger than the subtotal, or over 100%, is capped at the subtotal; zero or a negative discount takes nothing off; a negative subtotal gets no discount.
Empty quantity or price fields count as zero.
A long description wraps; the description field is multi-line.
Rows are matched by id: give every row a unique, stable id.
A unit price with more decimals than the currency is shown rounded in its field but counted exactly in the totals until it is edited.

name: MonarchLink
title: Link
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.Text with androidx.compose.foundation.clickable; androidx.compose.ui.text.LinkAnnotation with androidx.compose.ui.text.TextLinkStyles for links inside text
summary: A text link in the variants inline, standalone and subtle: MonarchLink for a link that is an element of its own, and MonarchLinkDefaults.styles() for a link inside a sentence.
whenToUse: MonarchLink for a link under a field, at the end of a row, in a footer or after a paragraph. A LinkAnnotation with MonarchLinkDefaults.styles() for words inside a sentence that open a page.
whenNotToUse: For an action that changes something (save, delete, send) use MonarchButton, in the Ghost variant when it must look light. For the top-level destinations of an app use a NavigationBar or NavigationRail (see top-nav).
api: @Composable fun MonarchLink(text: String, onClick: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchLinkVariant = MonarchLinkVariant.Inline, enabled: Boolean = true, external: Boolean = false, trailingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, externalLabel: String? = null, actionLabel: String? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)
enum class MonarchLinkVariant { Inline, Standalone, Subtle }
object MonarchLinkDefaults { @Composable fun styles(variant: MonarchLinkVariant = MonarchLinkVariant.Inline): TextLinkStyles }

options.name: text
options.description: The link text. Say where it goes.

options.name: onClick
options.description: Opens the destination: a screen of the app, or a URL with LocalUriHandler.current.openUri(url). Not called when disabled.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the link.

options.name: variant
options.description: Inline: link color, underlined. Standalone: link color, medium weight, underlined while pressed or focused. Subtle: muted text color, which turns to the default text color and underlined while pressed or focused.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the link can be activated.

options.name: external
options.description: Whether the link leaves the app. TalkBack reads externalLabel after the text.

options.name: trailingIcon
options.description: An icon after the text, such as an arrow for an external link. It takes the link color. Monarch bundles no icon.

options.name: externalLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "opens in the browser" (monarch_link_external).

options.name: actionLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "open link" (monarch_link_action), read by TalkBack as "double tap to open link".

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the press, focus and hover interactions.

options.name: MonarchLinkDefaults.styles(variant)
options.description: The same look for a LinkAnnotation.Url or LinkAnnotation.Clickable inside an annotated string, with pressed, hovered and focused styles.

states.name: resting
states.description: Inline is underlined in the link color; standalone is the link color in medium weight; subtle is the muted text color.

states.name: pressed, hovered or focused
states.description: Every variant is underlined; subtle takes the default text color. A focused link also shows the focus ring.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The disabled text color; announced as disabled and does not respond.

states.name: high contrast
states.description: In the two high-contrast themes every variant is underlined at rest, so a link is not told from text by color alone.

states.name: external
states.description: TalkBack reads "opens in the browser" after the text; an optional trailing icon shows it.

appearance: Text in the link role (inline, standalone) or the muted text role (subtle, turning to the default text role when pressed), the disabled text role when disabled; the underline is the text color. No background. The high-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colors and underline every variant.
platformNotes: The parity map lists Link as build on Android and as a ButtonStyle (MonarchLinkStyle) on iOS. Compose has no link control, so Android builds MonarchLink, with the same variant names and the same external label. Like the web link, an Inline or Subtle link takes the type size of the surrounding text (LocalTextStyle); wrap it in ProvideTextStyle(MonarchTheme.typography.caption) for a smaller one. A Standalone link is an element of its own and is label size (14sp, medium weight) like the text of a button, whatever surrounds it. The web underlines inline links at 40% of the text color; Monarch does not dim with opacity, so the underline is full strength. The web's hover underline for standalone and subtle is applied on press, focus and pointer hover. iOS underlines every variant when Button Shapes is on; Android has no such setting, so the high-contrast themes do it. Where an external URL opens is the app's decision: the plan mentions Custom Tabs, which needs androidx.browser, not a Monarch dependency; LocalUriHandler opens the default browser, and an app that wants Custom Tabs provides its own UriHandler through LocalUriHandler. The web's asChild has no equivalent; target="_blank" is the explicit external flag. Compose has no link role, so a MonarchLink is announced as an actionable element whose action is "open link"; a LinkAnnotation inside text is announced as a link by TalkBack.
accessibility: The link is one TalkBack element with its text; its click action is named "open link", so TalkBack says "double tap to open link".
An external link is read with "opens in the browser" after its text.
The touch target is at least 48dp high and wide, reserved in the layout; the visible text is centered vertically in it.
Pressed and focused states are shown by an underline, not by color alone, and the high-contrast themes underline every variant at rest.
A disabled link is announced as disabled and does not call onClick.
The text wraps at large font sizes, and the trailing icon follows the text in both layout directions.
edgeCases: The 48dp target makes a MonarchLink taller than a line of text: it is not meant to sit inside a paragraph. Use a LinkAnnotation there.
Links inside text (LinkAnnotation) are only as tall as the line; Compose does not enlarge them. Keep them to words that are not crowded by other links.
Without ProvideTextStyle an Inline or Subtle link uses the body style that MonarchTheme provides through Material 3; a Standalone link is always label size (14sp).
A trailing icon is decoration; give it a null content description and use external for the spoken note.

name: MonarchLinkCard
title: LinkCard
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.Surface (through MonarchCard), androidx.compose.ui.platform.LocalUriHandler, androidx.compose.foundation.Image (through Monarch's internal MonarchImage), MonarchFavicon
summary: A preview of a shared link from data the app unfurled: picture, site, title and description in one tappable card, with an optional remove button.
whenToUse: Under a message, comment or post that contains a link the app has unfurled.
whenNotToUse: For a link inside running text use a text link. For a file use a file card. Do not fetch the page from the device just to show a card; unfurl on the server.
api: @Composable fun MonarchLinkCard(title: String, url: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, description: String? = null, siteName: String? = null, image: Painter? = null, hasImage: Boolean = image != null, imageAspectRatio: Float? = null, favicon: Painter? = null, video: Boolean = false, size: MonarchLinkCardSize = MonarchLinkCardSize.Md, onOpen: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, onDismiss: (() -> Unit)? = null, dismissIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, dismissLabel: String? = null, removeLabel: String? = null, videoLabel: String? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)
enum class MonarchLinkCardSize { Sm, Md }

options.name: title
options.description: The page title, up to two lines.

options.name: url
options.description: The link. Only http, https and mailto open; anything else shows the card as plain text.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the card.

options.name: description
options.description: The page description, up to two lines.

options.name: siteName
options.description: The site above the title; the host without "www." by default.

options.name: image
options.description: The page's picture, loaded by the app.

options.name: hasImage
options.description: Whether the page has a picture; pass true while it loads so a muted tile keeps its place.

options.name: imageAspectRatio
options.description: The picture's width over height; kept between 1.2 and 2.2, and 2.2 when unknown.

options.name: favicon
options.description: The site's icon; without it MonarchFavicon draws a letter tile.

options.name: video
options.description: Shows a "Video" badge on the picture (or by the site without a picture), also read by TalkBack.

options.name: size
options.description: Md: the picture above the text. Sm: a 64dp thumbnail beside it.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Called with the url instead of opening it with LocalUriHandler.

options.name: onDismiss
options.description: Shows a remove button.

options.name: dismissIcon
options.description: The remove button's icon; the button then sits in the top end corner. Without it the button is a small "Remove" button under the card.

options.name: dismissLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken name "Remove the preview of" and the title (monarch_linkcard_dismiss).

options.name: removeLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in text "Remove" of the button without an icon (monarch_linkcard_remove).

options.name: videoLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in badge "Video" (monarch_linkcard_video).

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the press, focus and hover interactions of the card.

states.name: picture loading
states.description: With hasImage and no painter, a muted tile keeps the picture's place; it stays if loading fails.

states.name: not a safe link
states.description: The card is shown as plain text, read as one element, and does not open.

states.name: dismissible
states.description: A remove button, an icon button with a surface-coloured circle in the top end corner or a small text button under the card.

appearance: A MonarchCard (surface color, default border, 12dp corners) without padding; the picture fills its top or a thumbnail at the end. Site in the muted caption style, title in the strong body style, description in the muted caption style. The picture's placeholder uses the muted background. The video badge is a solid neutral MonarchBadge. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web LinkCard renders an anchor that opens a new tab with rel attributes, has a footer slot and comes with LinkCardList and LinkCardSkeleton. On Android the card opens the link through LocalUriHandler, which the app can replace (for example with Custom Tabs), or through onOpen; there is no footer (place product actions under the card), a list is a Column of cards, and there is no skeleton type (use MonarchSkeleton). Following the Monarch picture convention, the picture and favicon are Painters the app loads; there is no URL loading, unlike the iOS imageURL initialiser. The web draws a play mark on a video's picture; Monarch draws no glyphs, so a "Video" badge says it in text. The remove button needs an icon the app supplies; without one it is a text button under the card, so it never sits over the text. The picture ratio rule (1.2 to 2.2, 2.2 when unknown) matches iOS. Compose has no link role, so the card is read as a button.
accessibility: A safe link is one element with the Button role, read as the site, the title, the description and "Video" for a video; the picture and favicon are hidden.
A link that does not open is one plain element with the same text.
The remove button is a separate element named "Remove the preview of" and the title, with a touch target of at least 48dp, at the end in both layout directions.
The title is not cut at font scale 2.0 when it fits in two lines; longer titles and descriptions end with an ellipsis.
edgeCases: Long titles and descriptions are limited to two lines.
Very tall or very wide pictures are cropped to the 1.2 to 2.2 ratio range.
Without a site name and with a URL that has no host (mailto), the site line is left out.
With an icon remove button and no banner, the text keeps 48dp free at the end so the button never covers it.
Opening the link on a device was not tried; tests check the call to LocalUriHandler.

appearance: A MonarchSectionCard with the row count beside the title. Titles are strong body text, meta lines muted captions, statuses neutral subtle badges, and the Space chips MonarchTag in their selectable colors. Every color is a theme role, so dark and both high-contrast themes follow the theme.
platformNotes: The web panel is built around Rook Dossier and an EntityPicker popover with async search; on Android the doc menu is a DropdownMenu with a MonarchSearchBar that filters docOptions, and server search goes through onDocQueryChange. The web handles promises from onLinkDoc, onAddLink and onUnlink to show progress and errors; Android hoists that state: unlinkingId shows progress and errorMessage the error. Rows are buttons that call onOpen instead of anchors; there is no "opens in a new tab". The web moves focus to the next row after an unlink; Android leaves focus to the framework. The Space filter is kept by the panel across configuration changes and is not reported to the app. The rows are a Column, not a LazyColumn, because a record has few links and the panel sits in a scrolling screen. There is no iOS type to match yet.
accessibility: The title is a heading, read with the row count.
Each row is one button read as its title, its meta or host name, and its status, with the action "Open"; its file type icon is hidden because the text says what it is.
The unlink button is a separate element named "Unlink" and the row's title, with a 48dp touch target.
The Space chips are a group named "Filter by Space"; each chip is selected or not, so the filter does not depend on color.
The add-link form's fields have labels, and an invalid address shows its error as text under the field.
Rows wrap at font scale 2.0 and follow the reading direction; the unlink button follows the row.
edgeCases: A Space filter for a Space that no longer has rows shows every row.
A link without meta shows its host name without "www.".
An address such as "example.com" or "javascript:…" is refused by the form.
With neither docOptions nor onDocQueryChange there is no Link doc button.
Docs already linked are left out of the menu by docId.

title: LiveRegion
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.ui.semantics.liveRegion with androidx.compose.ui.semantics.LiveRegionMode (Polite, Assertive)
summary: Telling TalkBack about a change without moving focus is a live-region property on the element that changes. Monarch ships nothing and uses the same property inside its components.
whenToUse: Set liveRegion = LiveRegionMode.Polite on an element that is always on screen and whose text or content description changes when something happens the person did not cause directly or cannot see: a save finished, a result count changed, an item moved. Use Assertive only for an error that blocks the person.
whenNotToUse: Do not put a live region on a value that changes continuously (a timer, a progress percentage), or TalkBack talks without pause; give it a state description that is read when focused. Do not use View.announceForAccessibility, which Android 16 (API 36) deprecates.
api: var SemanticsPropertyReceiver.liveRegion: LiveRegionMode
LiveRegionMode.Polite, LiveRegionMode.Assertive
fun Modifier.semantics(mergeDescendants: Boolean = false, properties: SemanticsPropertyReceiver.() -> Unit): Modifier
var SemanticsPropertyReceiver.paneTitle: String

states.name: polite
states.description: TalkBack reads the new content when it finishes what it is saying.

states.name: assertive
states.description: TalkBack interrupts what it is saying. For blocking errors only.

appearance: No appearance of its own: the live region is a property of an element that is drawn with Monarch components.
platformNotes: The web renders an aria-live region and changes its text, and offers a useAnnouncer() hook to read a message from any event handler. Android has no hidden announcer: TalkBack reads an element marked as a live region when its content changes, so the element must already be on screen (composed) before the change, and an empty node that only carries the message works as the announcer. View.announceForAccessibility, named in the plan, is deprecated in Android 16 and is not used. iOS posts an AccessibilityNotification.Announcement instead. Monarch components that announce (MonarchRecordingIndicator, MonarchBanner, MonarchSnackbarHost) use the same property.
accessibility: System behavior: TalkBack reads a polite live region after it finishes speaking and an assertive one at once.
Only changes are read: the first composition of a live region is not announced, so keep the node on screen and change its content.
A live region whose content changes many times a second is read repeatedly; keep it for discrete events.
edgeCases: A live region added together with its message is not announced on some TalkBack versions; compose the node empty first.
Two live regions changing at once are both queued; prefer one per screen.

summary: The footer of a paginated list: a Load more button with loading, failure and retry, the end of the list, a count and polite announcements.
whenToUse: As the last item of a LazyColumn whose data comes in pages from a cursor or an offset: tickets, activity, search results.
whenNotToUse: For a list that fits in one response, show it whole. For numbered pages people jump between, use a pager with page numbers.

options.name: onLoadMore

options.name: showEnd
options.description: Shows and announces "That's everything" at the end.

options.name: loadedCount

states.name: loading

states.name: failed

appearance: A centered column with vertical padding: the count and the end line in muted caption text, the failure in the strong danger color, and a small secondary MonarchButton. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web also ships a useLoadMore hook that keeps the cursor and the pages; on Android the app's view model keeps them (or Paging's LazyPagingItems) and the footer only shows where loading stands. Auto-loading starts when the footer is composed instead of an IntersectionObserver, so there is no root margin: put the footer in the lazy list, where it is composed when it nears the screen. The web noun option is replaced by plurals in strings_loadmore.xml and the count and loaded labels. The web moves focus to the end line when the button disappears; Android leaves TalkBack focus to the system, and the end is announced. The failure is a line of text above the button instead of a MonarchInlineErrorRetry, so the one button keeps its place for Load more and Retry. iOS shares the name and the options.
accessibility: The button is a MonarchButton with a 48dp touch target; while loading it ignores taps and has the state "Loading".
A growing loadedCount is announced through a polite live region: "20 more items loaded."
A new failure and the end of the list are announced through the same live region; nothing is announced on the first composition.
The failure and the end are written as text, not only coloured.
Long messages wrap at the largest font size.
edgeCases: With autoLoad outside a lazy list every page loads at once, because the footer is always composed.
Auto-loading stays paused while failed is true; Retry or clearing failed resumes it.
A count that goes down, for example after a reset, is not announced.

summary: A placeholder for a region that is loading: skeleton rows, cards or a detail layout, or a progress ring with a label, announced once.
whenToUse: While the first page of a list, a set of cards or a detail screen loads and its layout is known.
whenNotToUse: For a short wait inside a button, use the loading state of MonarchButton. For a known amount of work, use MonarchProgress with a value. For one placeholder shape, use MonarchSkeleton.
api: @Composable fun MonarchLoadingState(label: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchLoadingStateVariant = MonarchLoadingStateVariant.List, rows: Int = 4)
enum class MonarchLoadingStateVariant { List, Rows, Cards, Detail, Spinner }

options.name: label
options.description: What is loading, such as "Loading tickets". Announced; shown by the spinner variant.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the region.

options.name: variant
options.description: List (avatar and two lines), Rows (a line and a short value), Cards (blocks), Detail (a title and paragraphs) or Spinner.

options.name: rows
options.description: The rows or cards drawn by List, Rows and Cards. Negative counts draw none.

states.name: skeleton
states.description: MonarchSkeleton placeholders in the chosen layout; the shimmer stands still when animations are off.

states.name: spinner
states.description: An indeterminate progress ring with the label under it.

appearance: Skeletons use the muted background with a subtle shimmer. The ring takes the accent solid color on the emphasis track; the label is muted label text. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web marks the region aria-busy; Compose has no busy state, so the label is announced once through a polite live region filled after the first frame, as iOS posts an announcement. The web Cards layout is a grid; here cards are stacked, because the placeholder takes the width it is given. iOS shares the name and the variants.
accessibility: The skeletons and the ring are hidden from TalkBack.
The label is set on a polite live region after the first frame, so TalkBack announces it once; it can also be reached by swiping.
In the spinner variant the visible label is that live region, so it is read once, not twice.
The spinner label wraps at the largest font size.
edgeCases: rows = 0 or below draws no rows, but the label is still announced.
Replacing the loading state with the content does not announce the content; say what loaded, for example with the count, when it matters.

options.description: The address: country and region codes, region and city as read, the city id when chosen from the list, and the postal code. The app keeps it.

options.name: onValueChange

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the column.

options.name: adapter
options.description: Where the lists come from: countries to offer, a region loader and the country's word for its regions, and the city search. Without a city search the city is a text field.

options.name: fields
options.description: The parts to show, in order.

options.name: errors
options.description: An error message per part; that field is in the error state.

options.description: Whether the fields can be used.

options.name: cityMinQuery
options.description: The letters needed before cities are searched while no region is chosen.

options.name: cityDebounceMillis
options.description: The wait after the last keystroke before cities are searched.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the field labels and the city list messages.

states.name: no country
states.description: The region field is disabled and says "Choose a country first"; so does the city search. A city text field stays usable.

states.name: region list
states.description: For a country with a list (built in, or from adapter.regions) the region is a combobox under the country's own word; otherwise a text field.

states.name: loading
states.description: The region combobox and the city list show their loading state while the adapter answers.

states.name: too short
states.description: Without a region, the city list says "Type at least 2 letters to search." and nothing is searched.

states.name: search failed
states.description: The city list says "Couldn’t load cities. Type again to retry."; the next keystroke searches again. A failed region load shows MonarchRegionSelect's Try again.

states.name: error
states.description: A field with a message in errors shows it under the field in the danger color.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Every field is disabled.

appearance: Each field keeps its own appearance: MonarchTextField's surface fill and input border, the danger strong color in error, and the combobox list on the surface color with muted second lines. The legend is a subheading in the default text color. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web LocationFields lays the four fields in a responsive grid inside a fieldset and takes an adapter whose countries, regions and cities calls are promises with an AbortSignal. On Android the fields stack in one column, as address forms do on a phone; the adapter's functions are suspending and a newer request cancels the older coroutine. The country list is synchronous here: MonarchCountrySelect names every ISO country in the locale, and adapter.countries only limits it. adapter.regions is optional because MonarchRegionSelect has built-in lists, and the country's word for its regions is adapter.regionLabel instead of a field of the regions answer. The city search opens a bottom sheet (MonarchCombobox's sheet), not an inline list. The web's required marks and the uncontrolled defaultValue are not offered: the value is always hoisted, and the app shows required errors through errors. The web's Try again button after a failed city search is replaced by searching again on the next keystroke. No iOS entry exists yet.
accessibility: The fields form one traversal group; the legend is a heading.
Each field has a visible label that TalkBack reads as its name; the region field is named by the country's word for its regions.
Errors are shown under their field and read with it.
Each field carries its autofill type (country through MonarchCountrySelect, region, city as AddressLocality, postal code as PostalCode).
Every field is at least 48dp tall.
edgeCases: Changing the country clears the region, city and postal code; choosing the same country again changes nothing.
A city chosen before a region fills the region from the city; a region already chosen is kept.
A typed city is stored with cityId = null; a chosen city keeps its id and stays shown even when it is not in the latest results.
Without adapter.cities the city is a plain text field.
With adapter.regions, a country whose loader returns no regions gets a text field.
