title: LogDrawer
wrapsNative: MonarchBottomSheet with androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column and androidx.compose.foundation.verticalScroll, MonarchMethodBadge, MonarchDescriptionList (with its MonarchCopyButton), MonarchBadge, MonarchCodeBlock and MonarchButton; android.text.format.DateUtils for the time
summary: A recipe, not a component: the full record of one log entry (an API request, a webhook delivery, a job run) in a bottom sheet, with method and path, status, request ID with copy, time, duration and the payload.
whenToUse: When a row of a request log, webhook log or job list is tapped and the person needs every detail of that one entry.
whenNotToUse: For the streaming output of a run use MonarchLogViewer. For a short summary that fits in the row, leave it in the list.
api: MonarchBottomSheet(onDismissRequest = { open = false }, title = "Request details") { Column(Modifier.verticalScroll(rememberScrollState())) { … } }
MonarchText(text = "Request details", style = MonarchTextStyle.Heading, heading = true)
MonarchMethodBadge(method = "POST")
MonarchDescriptionList(items = listOf(MonarchDescriptionItem("Status", "502") { MonarchBadge(text = "502", tone = statusTone(502)) }, MonarchDescriptionItem("Request ID", id, copyable = true), …))
MonarchCodeBlock(code = body, language = "json", title = "Response")
DateUtils.formatDateTime(context, millis, DateUtils.FORMAT_SHOW_DATE or DateUtils.FORMAT_SHOW_TIME)

options.name: entry
options.description: The log entry: method, path, status, request ID, time in epoch milliseconds, duration and payload.

options.name: open
options.description: Whether the sheet is shown; set it from the row's tap and clear it in onDismissRequest and Close.

options.name: statusTone
options.description: Success for 2xx, info for 3xx, warning for 4xx and danger for 5xx, as the web's httpStatusTone.

states.name: closed
states.description: Only the list or button that opens the sheet.

states.name: open
states.description: A modal bottom sheet, half height and pulled to full height, titled "Request details", with Close at the end.

states.name: loading
states.description: While the entry loads, show MonarchLoadingState with the Detail variant and the label "Loading details" in the sheet.

states.name: load error
states.description: MonarchInlineErrorRetry with "The details did not load." and Try again in the sheet.

states.name: status tones
states.description: The status badge uses success for 2xx, info for 3xx, warning for 4xx and danger for 5xx, with the code as its text.

appearance: Every part is an existing Monarch component on the sheet's surface: a heading, the method badge and the path in the code type, a stacked description list, a toned status badge, the code block and a full-width button. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web ships LogDrawer as one component: a side sheet from the right that fills the screen on phones, with request, fields, loading, error, onRetry, locale, now and messages props. On Android, as on iOS, it is a recipe: a modal bottom sheet is the phone's surface for one record's details, and each fact is a MonarchDescriptionItem the app lists itself, leaving out the facts the entry does not have. The web's httpStatusTone helper is a small function in the recipe. There is no relative time with a tooltip; write the time with DateUtils (minSdk 24, no java.time). On a large screen the same content can go in MonarchResponsiveDialog or a supporting pane.
accessibility: The sheet is modal for TalkBack and Back closes it; the title has heading semantics.
Each fact of MonarchDescriptionList is read as the term and the value.
The request ID's copy button is named "Copy Request ID" and announces the copy.
The status is a word in a badge, not only a color.
Close is a 48dp MonarchButton at the end of the content.
edgeCases: Long paths wrap in the code type; the payload code block scrolls sideways inside itself or wraps with its toggle.
Leave out a fact the entry does not have instead of showing an empty value.
At the largest text sizes the content scrolls inside the sheet; pull the sheet to full height.

name: MonarchLogViewer
title: LogViewer
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn of monospaced lines with androidx.compose.ui.input.nestedscroll.NestedScrollConnection for pausing; MonarchSearchBar, androidx.compose.material3.FilterChip for the levels, Follow and Wrap lines, MonarchEmptyState and MonarchLoadingState
summary: A streaming log with level filters and counts, search that filters or highlights, follow mode that keeps the newest line in view, and a wrap toggle.
whenToUse: To watch the output of a deployment, a job run or a service as it streams, or to read back a finished run's log.
whenNotToUse: For one log entry's full record use the LogDrawer recipe (a sheet with a description list and code block). For static code use MonarchCodeBlock.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchLogViewer(lines: List<MonarchLogLine>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, levels: Set<MonarchLogLevel>? = null, onLevelsChange: ((Set<MonarchLogLevel>) -> Unit)? = null, query: String? = null, onQueryChange: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, following: Boolean? = null, onFollowingChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, wrapped: Boolean? = null, onWrappedChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, searchMode: MonarchLogViewerSearchMode = MonarchLogViewerSearchMode.Filter, showTimestamps: Boolean = true, showLineNumbers: Boolean = false, loading: Boolean = false, state: LazyListState = rememberLazyListState(), clearSearchIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchLogViewerLabels = MonarchLogViewerLabels(), actions: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null)
public data class MonarchLogLine(id: String, message: String, level: MonarchLogLevel = MonarchLogLevel.Info, time: Long? = null, source: String? = null)
public enum class MonarchLogLevel { Debug, Info, Warn, Error }
public enum class MonarchLogViewerSearchMode { Filter, Highlight }

public class MonarchLogViewerLabels(log: String? = null, levels: String? = null, levelName: ((level: MonarchLogLevel) -> String)? = null, search: String? = null, clearSearch: String? = null, follow: String? = null, wrap: String? = null, count: ((shown: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, jumpToLatest: String? = null, newLines: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, followPaused: String? = null, followResumed: String? = null, empty: String? = null, noMatches: String? = null, clearFilters: String? = null, loading: String? = null)

options.name: lines
options.description: The lines, oldest first. Append to the list to stream.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the viewer. Give it a bounded height.

options.name: levels
options.description: The levels shown. Kept inside, with all four on at first, when null.

options.name: onLevelsChange
options.description: Called when a level filter is toggled or the filters are cleared.

options.name: query
options.description: The search text. Kept inside when null. Trimmed and matched against the message and the source, ignoring case.

options.name: onQueryChange
options.description: Called on every edit and when the filters are cleared.

options.name: following
options.description: Whether the newest line is kept in view. Kept inside, on at first, when null.

options.name: onFollowingChange
options.description: Called with false when the reader drags toward older lines or turns Follow off, and with true when they return to the end, tap the jump button or turn Follow on.

options.name: wrapped
options.description: Whether long lines wrap. Kept inside, off at first, when null. Unwrapped lines scroll sideways.

options.name: onWrappedChange
options.description: Called when Wrap lines is toggled.

options.name: searchMode
options.description: Filter hides lines without a match; Highlight keeps every line. Both mark the matches.

options.name: showTimestamps
options.description: Shows each line's time as 24-hour HH:mm:ss.SSS in the device's time zone.

options.name: showLineNumbers
options.description: Shows each line's 1-based position in lines, which stays the same when filters hide lines.

options.name: loading
options.description: Shows Loading log while lines is empty.

options.name: state
options.description: The scroll state of the log.

options.name: clearSearchIcon
options.description: An icon for the search field's clear button, named Clear search; without it the field has no clear button.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including the level names, the count and the jump button.

options.name: actions
options.description: Extra controls after Follow and Wrap lines, such as Share or Clear.

states.name: following
states.description: Every change of the lines scrolls the log to the newest one. Follow is selected.

states.name: paused
states.description: The log stays where the reader is. A Jump to latest button floats over the bottom of the log and reads "3 new lines" when lines arrive.

states.name: wrapped
states.description: Long lines wrap inside the width; otherwise each line is one row and the log scrolls sideways.

states.name: filtered
states.description: The footer reads "2 of 5 lines". When nothing is left, a filtered MonarchEmptyState offers Clear filters, which empties the search and turns every level back on.

states.name: loading
states.description: MonarchLoadingState's spinner with Loading log while there are no lines yet.

states.name: empty
states.description: A small MonarchEmptyState, No log lines yet.

appearance: The log sits on the subtle background in the code type, one row per line. The level is a word in semibold, coloured by level (muted for debug, the strong info, warning and danger roles); warning and error rows have the subtle warning or danger fill. Times, line numbers and sources are muted. Matches are underlined on the subtle accent fill. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow the theme roles.
platformNotes: The web LogViewer measures and virtualises rows itself; on Android a LazyColumn composes only the rows in view. The web pauses following from the scroll position; here a drag toward older lines (a nested scroll from user input) pauses it and coming to rest at the end of the log resumes it, as on iOS. Home and End keys are not offered; Follow and the jump button do the same. The time is fixed to HH:mm:ss.SSS in the device's time zone and cannot be replaced (the web's formatTime). The web's estimatedRowHeight, overscan and atBottomThreshold have no meaning with a LazyColumn. The level filters, Follow and Wrap lines are Material 3 FilterChips rather than a segmented toggle group, so they wrap onto new rows on a narrow phone and at large text sizes. Monarch bundles no icons, so the search field's clear button appears only with clearSearchIcon. Android uses the same name and API shape as iOS, with a value and an on…Change callback for each binding.
accessibility: The log is named "Log".
Each line is one element read as its level, time, source and message.
The level filters are a group named "Levels"; each filter is a FilterChip with the selected state, read with its count.
Follow and Wrap lines are FilterChips with the selected state.
Pausing and resuming following are announced through a polite live region: "Following paused" and "Following new lines".
Search matches are underlined as well as tinted, and the level is written as a word, so neither relies on color.
The chips and the jump button have 48dp touch targets; the toolbar mirrors in right-to-left layouts while the lines read left to right.
edgeCases: Lines without a time leave out the time column; lines without a source leave out the source.
Long lines without wrap make the whole log scroll sideways.
Ids must be unique and stable: they are the keys of the rows.
The viewer takes the height it is given and scrolls inside it: do not put it in another vertical scroll.
Line numbers keep their positions in the full list, so a filtered log shows gaps.
TalkBack scrolling is not a drag: it does not pause following; turn Follow off to read back.

edgeCases: Long names wrap inside their cell.
An empty list shows only the title.
A logo with a link but no onLogoClick is not interactive.

states.description: The question as a heading, the notes, then one checkbox row per channel.

appearance: The checkboxes are MonarchCheckboxRow. The question heading uses the default text color, the notes the muted text color and the policy link the link color with an underline; all switch to the disabled text color when disabled. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ignores defaultChecked so the boxes cannot start ticked; here the selection is hoisted, as for every Compose control, so the component cannot enforce it: the documentation tells the app to start it empty. The web posts hidden form inputs (name, textName); a native app has no form post, so the app stores the MonarchMarketingConsent it receives. The wording is built from the strings the component draws. The web takes React nodes and a policy href; here the texts are plain strings and the policy is a title with an onPolicyClick callback, because Monarch components do not navigate. iOS takes a URL for the policy. The time is epoch milliseconds (UTC) instead of an ISO string or a Date.
accessibility: Each checkbox is a MonarchCheckboxRow: one TalkBack element with the Checkbox role, the label (and, with one channel, the notes), read as checked or not checked; the whole row is the touch target, at least 48dp high.
With several channels the question has the heading property, so it can be reached with heading navigation.
The policy link reserves a touch target of at least 48dp by 48dp, draws the focus ring and is underlined, so it does not depend on color.
When disabled every checkbox and the link are read as disabled and ignore taps.
Text wraps at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: The same channel listed twice is shown once.
An empty channels list is treated as email.
The wording collapses runs of whitespace, so line breaks in a description do not change the proof text.
The policy title without onPolicyClick is not shown, because it could not be opened.

name: MonarchMediaUpload
title: MediaUpload
wrapsNative: MonarchFileUpload with androidx.activity.result.contract.ActivityResultContracts.PickVisualMedia, android.media.MediaMetadataRetriever for video length, MonarchProgress (androidx.compose.material3.LinearProgressIndicator), androidx.compose.foundation.Image for the preview, MonarchButton and MonarchInlineNotice
summary: A field that holds one image or video: pick it with the system photo picker, see it checked and uploaded with progress, then preview it with Replace and Remove.
whenToUse: For one picture or clip that belongs to a record: a cover image, a product photo, an intro video.
whenNotToUse: For a profile picture with cropping use MonarchAvatarUpload. For several files or documents use MonarchFileUpload with MonarchUploadQueue.
api: @Composable fun MonarchMediaUpload(label: String, value: String?, onValueChange: (String?) -> Unit, onUpload: suspend (MonarchPickedFile, MonarchMediaUploadContext) -> MonarchMediaUploadResult, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, kind: MonarchMediaUploadKind? = null, preview: Painter? = null, helperText: String? = null, kinds: Set<MonarchMediaUploadKind> = setOf(MonarchMediaUploadKind.Image), maxImageSize: Long? = null, maxVideoSize: Long? = null, maxVideoDurationMillis: Long? = null, enabled: Boolean = true, videoUnavailable: String? = null, previewLabel: String? = null, onPlay: (() -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchMediaUploadLabels = MonarchMediaUploadLabels())
enum class MonarchMediaUploadKind { Image, Video }
class MonarchMediaUploadResult(url: String, warnings: List<String> = emptyList())
class MonarchMediaUploadContext(kind: MonarchMediaUploadKind, progress: (Float) -> Unit) { fun reportProgress(fraction: Float) }

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label, already localised. It is a heading.

options.name: value
options.description: The address of the stored file, or null when empty.

options.name: onValueChange
options.description: Called with the new address after an upload, and with null after Remove.

options.name: onUpload
options.description: Stores the file, reports progress through the context and returns the stored address and any warnings. Cancel upload cancels its coroutine. Throw to show the error.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the field.

options.name: kind
options.description: The kind of the current file. When null, the kind of the latest upload, or a guess from the address's extension.

options.name: preview
options.description: The stored image or the video's poster, loaded by the app. A tinted tile while null.

options.name: helperText
options.description: Guidance under the label.

options.name: kinds
options.description: The kinds that are taken; the photo picker offers only these.

options.name: maxImageSize
options.description: The largest image, in bytes. Larger images are refused with the file name and the limit.

options.name: maxVideoSize
options.description: The largest video, in bytes.

options.name: maxVideoDurationMillis
options.description: The longest video, in milliseconds, read from the file's metadata before upload. A video whose length cannot be read is refused.

options.name: enabled
options.description: When false the picker, Replace and Remove do nothing and take the disabled colors.

options.name: videoUnavailable
options.description: Why videos cannot be added, in the product's words. Shown in the hint when kinds has no video, and videos can then be picked so the refusal explains itself.

options.name: previewLabel
options.description: The spoken name of the image preview. "Uploaded image" when null.

options.name: onPlay
options.description: Plays the video, for example in the system player. Makes the video preview a "Play video" button.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, and the file picker area's strings including formatSize.

states.name: empty
states.description: The MonarchFileUpload zone with "Add an image" (or "Add an image or video"), the hint lines and the Choose button.

states.name: checking
states.description: An indeterminate progress bar with "Checking clip.mp4…" and Cancel upload while a video's length is read.

states.name: uploading
states.description: A progress bar, indeterminate until the first report, with "Uploading photo.png · 40%" and Cancel upload.

states.name: filled
states.description: The preview at 16:9, then Replace (a compact picker) and Remove.

states.name: refused
states.description: The picker's danger notice names the file and the reason: a video where only images are taken, or too large. Too long and unreadable videos are shown as a danger notice under the field.

states.name: failed
states.description: A danger notice with the error's message, or "The upload failed. Try again."; the value is unchanged.

states.name: warnings
states.description: A warning notice titled "Uploaded with warnings." with one line per warning.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The picker and buttons do nothing and take the disabled colors.

appearance: The empty zone and the Replace button are MonarchFileUpload's; the label uses the default text role, help and status text the muted role, the preview placeholder the muted background role, the progress bar the accent solid role, and notices the danger and warning tone roles. All come from MonarchTheme in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web has a drop zone and a hidden file input. On Android the path is the system photo picker (PickVisualMedia), which needs no storage permission and also reaches cloud photos on recent versions; iOS offers Photos and Files buttons, Android offers the one photo picker. Dragging files onto the field is not offered (see drop-zone). The web's transform callback is not offered: an app shrinks or converts the file inside onUpload. Cancellation is coroutine cancellation instead of an AbortSignal, progress is a fraction from 0 to 1 instead of a percentage, and the length limit is in milliseconds. The value is the stored file's address; Monarch loads no images, so the app passes the stored image or poster as preview, and plays a video through onPlay instead of iOS's built-in player. Same name as iOS.
accessibility: The label is a heading and the help text follows it.
Choose, Cancel upload, Replace and Remove are buttons with 48dp touch targets.
The progress bar's spoken name is the status text, with the percentage when known.
Refusals and failures are shown with text in a danger notice, not by color alone, and announced through a polite live region.
"Image uploaded", "Video uploaded", "Upload cancelled" and "Image removed" are announced through a polite live region.
The image preview is one image named "Uploaded image" or previewLabel; a video preview with onPlay is a "Play video" button.
edgeCases: A file whose provider reports no size passes the size limit; the app can check the bytes in onUpload.
The kind is read from the MIME type, then from the extension; a stored address without an extension is taken as an image unless kind is passed.
Cancelling during the length check stops before onUpload is called.
Remove only clears the value; deleting the stored file is the app's job in onValueChange.
Reported fractions outside 0 to 1 are clamped.

Group headings are headings, read in the case they were given.
Icons and chevrons are not read.
Expanding animates with the theme motion, and is immediate when animations are off.
edgeCases: Only one entry is expanded at a time.
An entry with neither a link nor sections does nothing when tapped.
Long descriptions wrap.

summary: One member of a workspace, space or channel: avatar, name, email, role, status (active, invited, suspended) and actions that are confirmed and may run for a while.
whenToUse: In a list of people with a role that some viewers may change, including pending invitations with resend and revoke.
whenNotToUse: For choosing people to add, use a searchable picker. For a dense table with many columns per person, use a data table with MonarchAvatar cells. For choosing a role with descriptions on its own, use MonarchRolePicker.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchMemberRow(name: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, image: Painter? = null, email: String? = null, meta: String? = null, presence: MonarchPresenceStatus? = null, status: MonarchMemberRowStatus = MonarchMemberRowStatus.Active, role: String? = null, roles: List<MonarchRoleOption<String>> = emptyList(), badges: List<String> = emptyList(), self: Boolean = false, enabled: Boolean = true, canChangeRole: Boolean? = null, canRemove: Boolean? = null, removeConsequences: List<String> = emptyList(), onRoleChange: (suspend (String) -> Unit)? = null, onResend: (suspend () -> Unit)? = null, onRemove: (suspend () -> Unit)? = null, removeIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchMemberRowLabels = MonarchMemberRowLabels(), actions: (@Composable FlowRowScope.() -> Unit)? = null)

public class MonarchMemberRowLabels(you: String? = null, invited: String? = null, suspended: String? = null, presence: ((MonarchPresenceStatus) -> String)? = null, roleLabel: ((String) -> String)? = null, chooseRole: String? = null, resend: String? = null, resendLabel: ((String) -> String)? = null, resent: String? = null, remove: ((String) -> String)? = null, revoke: ((String) -> String)? = null, removeTitle: ((String) -> String)? = null, revokeTitle: ((String) -> String)? = null, removeDescription: String? = null, revokeDescription: String? = null, removeConfirm: String? = null, revokeConfirm: String? = null, cancel: String? = null, failed: String? = null)

options.name: name
options.description: The display name; also seeds the avatar's initials and color. For an invitation, the email.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the row.

options.name: image
options.description: The avatar picture, loaded by the app. Initials show without it.

options.name: email
options.description: Email or handle under the name, shortened in the middle.

options.name: meta
options.description: Extra detail: joined date, invite expiry, availability.

options.name: presence
options.description: Presence dot on the avatar, also read in words.

options.name: status
options.description: Invited adds an info badge, Resend invite and Revoke invite; suspended a warning badge and a muted name.

options.name: role
options.description: The value of the member's role, one of roles.

options.name: roles
options.description: The roles allowed here (the role picker's type). Titles also show for a read-only role; disabled options cannot be picked.

options.name: badges
options.description: Extra neutral badges after the name, such as "Guest".

options.name: self
options.description: The signed-in person: a "You" badge after the name; role picker and Remove hidden by default.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Disables every control in the row.

options.name: canChangeRole
options.description: Shows the role picker. By default when onRoleChange is given and it is not your own row.

options.name: canRemove
options.description: Shows Remove. By default when onRemove is given and it is not your own row.

options.name: removeConsequences
options.description: Lines added under the text of the remove confirmation.

options.name: onRoleChange
options.description: Makes the role a picker. The new role shows while it runs and until role changes; a thrown error restores the previous role and shows the error in the row.

options.name: onResend
options.description: Sends an invitation again; shown for invited rows. "Invite sent again." is shown and announced when it returns.

options.name: onRemove
options.description: Removes the member or revokes the invitation after a confirmation. The app removes the row; a thrown error is shown in the row.

options.name: removeIcon
options.description: An icon before the word of the remove button. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string; functions receive the member's name.

options.name: actions
options.description: More trailing controls after Remove, such as a menu button. Name them after the member.

states.name: active
states.description: No status badge.

states.name: invited
states.description: Info badge "Invited", a Resend invite button, and Remove becomes Revoke invite.

states.name: suspended
states.description: Warning badge "Suspended" and the name in the muted text color.

states.name: self
states.description: A "You" badge after the name; the role is text and Remove is hidden unless canChangeRole or canRemove say otherwise.

states.name: read-only role
states.description: Without the role picker the role title is a muted line under the name.

states.name: busy
states.description: A circular progress indicator beside the role picker, which is disabled, while onRoleChange runs; Resend and Remove show their loading state while their action runs.

states.name: error
states.description: The failure under the identity in the danger strong color, announced.

states.name: done
states.description: "Invite sent again." under the identity in the success strong color, announced.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Every control is disabled.

appearance: A transparent Material 3 list item with the avatar at the start, the name in the strong body style (muted when suspended), email and meta in the muted caption style, status badges in the info and warning tones; the controls sit under it. Notices use the danger strong and success strong roles. All colors are theme roles, so dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: Same parameters as iOS, with Android conventions: the picture is a Painter, isSelf is self, actions are suspending functions, and the extra controls are a FlowRowScope slot. The role picker is MonarchRolePicker's compact exposed dropdown, labelled "Role for <name>", instead of the web's native select and iOS's menu Picker; it always sits under the identity, because a phone row has no room beside it. The web keeps the remove dialog open while onRemove runs and shows its error there; the Material 3 AlertDialog closes when confirmed, so the Remove button shows progress and the error appears in the row, as on iOS. Consequences are lines of the dialog's text. iOS offers swipe actions in a List; Android has no standard swipe actions for list rows, so Remove and Resend are buttons only. The web's MemberList is not needed: a Column or LazyColumn holds the rows. Monarch bundles no icons, so the notice has no icon; its text carries the meaning.
accessibility: The identity is one TalkBack element: the name ("Priya Raman, You") as its name, and status, presence, badges, a read-only role, email and meta as its state description.
The avatar is decorative next to the visible name; presence is read in words.
The role picker is labelled "Role for <name>"; Resend is read "Resend invite, <name>" and Remove "Remove <name>" or "Revoke invite for <name>".
Resend success and every failure are shown as text and announced through a polite live region, not color alone.
Resend and Remove keep 48dp touch targets.
edgeCases: A role value that is not in roles is shown as its raw value when read-only; the picker shows "Choose a role" for it.
With no role yet, the picker shows "Choose a role" until one is picked.
A second change while a role change runs is ignored; the picker is disabled until it finishes.
Errors with a message are shown in its words; other errors show "That did not work. Try again.".
Long names wrap to two lines and emails are shortened in the middle.

name: MonarchMentionPicker
title: MentionPicker
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn of MonarchListRow rows, with MonarchAvatar, MonarchSkeleton and MonarchInlineErrorRetry; androidx.compose.ui.text.input.TextFieldValue for the caret
summary: Suggestions for an @mention or #channel: a strip of people and channels above the message field and the keyboard, with loading, empty and error states, and helpers that find the mention being typed and replace it.
whenToUse: In a message or comment composer where people mention others with @ or channels with #.
whenNotToUse: Not for general search suggestions; use a Material 3 SearchBar with its suggestion list. Not for choosing people in a form; use a list with checkboxes or a dropdown menu.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchMentionPicker(query: MonarchMentionQuery?, items: List<MonarchMentionItem>, onSelect: (MonarchMentionItem) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, status: MonarchMentionPickerStatus = MonarchMentionPickerStatus.Ready, onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchMentionPickerLabels = MonarchMentionPickerLabels())

public class MonarchMentionQuery(trigger: Char, text: String, start: Int, end: Int) { fun replacing(text: String, replacement: String): String; fun replacing(value: TextFieldValue, replacement: String): TextFieldValue; companion object { fun find(text: String, caret: Int = text.length, triggers: Set<Char> = setOf('@')): MonarchMentionQuery?; fun find(value: TextFieldValue, triggers: Set<Char> = setOf('@')): MonarchMentionQuery? } }

public class MonarchMentionItem(id: String, label: String, kind: MonarchMentionKind = MonarchMentionKind.Person, detail: String? = null, image: Painter? = null, enabled: Boolean = true) { fun token(trigger: Char = '@'): String }
public enum class MonarchMentionKind { Person, Channel }
public enum class MonarchMentionPickerStatus { Loading, Ready, Failed }

public class MonarchMentionPickerLabels(label: String? = null, people: String? = null, channels: String? = null, loading: String? = null, empty: String? = null, error: String? = null, retry: String? = null, count: ((Int) -> String)? = null)

options.name: query
options.description: The mention being typed, from MonarchMentionQuery.find; null closes the picker.

options.name: items
options.description: The suggestions from the app's search. People and channels are grouped under headings when both are present; more than about four scroll.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Called with the chosen suggestion. Complete the mention with query.replacing(value, item.token(query.trigger) + " ").

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the strip. Place it directly above the message field.

options.name: status
options.description: Loading shows placeholder rows, Failed the error.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Repeats a failed search: adds a Retry button.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

states.name: closed
states.description: No query: nothing is drawn.

states.name: loading
states.description: Three placeholder rows, one element read as "Searching…".

states.name: results
states.description: A row per suggestion with an avatar, or a square number-sign tile for a channel; people and channels under headings when both are present.

states.name: disabled suggestion
states.description: Text in the disabled color; the row cannot be chosen.

states.name: no matches
states.description: "No matches". When a query with a space finds nothing, the picker closes.

states.name: failed
states.description: "Couldn’t load suggestions." with a Retry button when onRetry is given.

appearance: A strip on the surface color with a subtle top border; labels in the default text color, details, headings and notes in the muted text color, disabled rows in the disabled text color; avatars with their fallback colors and a square number-sign tile for channels. The same roles in every theme.
platformNotes: The web anchors a listbox to the caret with aria-activedescendant and arrow keys, and ships hooks that debounce and abort the search. Compose gives no caret rectangle, so on Android, as on iOS, the picker is a full-width strip that the app places directly above the message field, so it sits above the keyboard with the field's imePadding; suggestions are buttons. The app runs its search in a LaunchedEffect keyed by the query, which cancels the previous one; Monarch adds no debounce timer. MonarchMentionQuery.find reads the caret from TextFieldValue.selection, so a mention in the middle of the text is found. The token format matches the web's formatMentionToken; the web's parseMentionTokens and getCaretRect have no Android counterpart in this release.
accessibility: The strip is a group named "Suggestions" and a polite live region whose state is the result count, "Searching…", "No matches" or the error, so the change is announced while focus stays in the text field.
Each suggestion is a button whose name is its label and detail; a disabled suggestion is marked disabled and cannot be activated.
Group headings are headings.
Avatars and the channel tile are decorative.
Rows are at least 56dp high and grow with the font size setting; long details wrap.
edgeCases: A trigger inside a word, such as in an email address, finds no query.
A query ends after two words, a line break or a word longer than 40 characters.
Replacing a query removes one space after it when the replacement ends with a space, so a mention typed mid-sentence does not leave two spaces.
A query's range belongs to the text it was found in; replacing in a shorter text leaves it unchanged.
While a range of text is selected, find on a TextFieldValue returns null.

    onRetry = { /* Search again. */ },
)

title: MenuButton

summary: A button that opens a menu of actions: a MonarchButton with a trailing chevron and a MonarchMenu, placed together in a Box. Monarch ships no type for it.
whenToUse: For a short list of actions that belong to one object or screen, such as Rename, Duplicate and Delete, when there is no single main action.
whenNotToUse: When one action is the usual choice, use MonarchSplitButton. For choosing a value in a form use ExposedDropdownMenuBox. For a row's overflow menu with an icon only, use a MonarchIconButton with a content description as the trigger.
api: Box { MonarchButton(text: String, onClick = { expanded = true }, trailingIcon = { MonarchIcon(…, contentDescription = null) }); MonarchMenu(expanded: Boolean, onDismissRequest: () -> Unit) { MonarchMenuItem(text: String, onClick: () -> Unit, …) } }
Modifier.semantics { stateDescription = …; expand { … }; collapse { … } }

options.name: expanded
options.description: Whether the menu is open; kept by the app with rememberSaveable.

options.name: variant
options.description: The trigger's weight: Primary, Secondary, Ghost or Danger.

options.name: size
options.description: The trigger's height: Sm, Md or Lg; the touch target is 48dp at every size.

options.name: trailingIcon
options.description: The chevron, a MonarchIcon with a null content description. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: enabled
options.description: On the MonarchButton: a disabled trigger does not open the menu.

states.name: closed
states.description: The trigger looks like any MonarchButton of its variant, with the chevron after the label.

states.name: open
states.description: The menu appears under the trigger (above when there is no room) and takes focus; the trigger's state is "Expanded".

states.name: disabled
states.description: The trigger uses the disabled colors and cannot open the menu.

appearance: The trigger follows the MonarchButton variant colors; the menu is the MonarchMenu on the raised background role with the default text role, and a danger item uses the strong danger role through destructive = true. High-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colors.
platformNotes: The web MenuButton is a Radix MonarchMenu trigger with an items shorthand, controlled open state, alignment, side and a chevron that turns while open. On Android the MonarchMenu places the menu and handles back and outside taps, so the recipe is a MonarchButton and a MonarchMenu in one Box; the chevron does not turn. The items shorthand is a list of MonarchMenuItems; links open from the item's onClick. iOS covers it with the system Menu and the Monarch button style.
accessibility: The trigger is a Button with its label; the recipe adds the stateDescription "Expanded" or "Collapsed" and the expand and collapse actions so TalkBack says what the button does.
The chevron has a null content description; an icon-only trigger needs a content description such as "More actions".
Menu items are 48dp tall and the menu takes focus when it opens (system behavior).
A danger item says what it does ("Delete"); its color is not the only signal.
edgeCases: Close the menu (expanded = false) in each item's onClick; it does not close by itself.
A long label wraps inside the trigger rather than widening it past the screen.
There is no loading state on the trigger; disable it while the actions are unavailable.

options.description: What else happens, shown with MonarchConsequenceList under "What happens".

options.name: blockers
options.description: Problems that stop the merge, shown in a warning MonarchBanner; the merge button is disabled.

options.name: merging
options.description: The merge runs: the merge button shows progress and the choices and Cancel are disabled.

options.name: failed
options.description: The last merge failed: a danger MonarchBanner shows labels.error (or the built-in message) and is announced; every choice stays.

options.name: onCancel
options.description: Shows a Cancel button that calls it. The app closes the dialog.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, including the failure message.

states.name: choosing
states.description: The record choice with a Kept badge on the selected record, a choice per differing field (defaulting to the kept record's value, or the first other value when it is empty), and matching fields listed once.

states.name: blocked
states.description: With blockers, or fewer than two records, the merge button is disabled; blockers are shown in a warning banner.

states.name: merging
states.description: The merge button shows a progress indicator and is announced as Loading; the choices and Cancel are disabled.

states.name: failed
states.description: A danger banner with the message under the choices, announced politely; the choices stay as they were.

appearance: A heading and a muted description at the top, the choices in a scrolling column of MonarchRadioRows with subheadings, matching fields as muted names with default-text values, and the buttons at the bottom: Cancel as a ghost button and Merge as a primary button. Colors come from the parts' roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web MergeDialog is a modal with radio groups and a full-screen layout on phones that opens itself. On Android Monarch ships the content: the app presents it in a Material 3 Dialog with DialogProperties(usePlatformDefaultWidth = false) (the plan's full-screen dialog) or in a ModalBottomSheet, and closes it. The web onMerge returns a promise and the dialog waits on it; on Android the app sets merging while it runs and failed when it fails, and closes the dialog on success; iOS uses an async throwing closure instead. Values and consequences are strings and MonarchConsequence items instead of any node. The web size option has no meaning on a phone, and the web children slot is not offered. iOS uses the same name.
accessibility: Each choice is a MonarchRadioRow in a selectable group, so TalkBack reads its label, its source and its selected state.
A value option is one element that reads its value and its source, such as "hello@acme.com, from Acme Ltd"; an empty value reads "Empty".
The title, the section headings and the field names are headings; the Kept badge is hidden because the selected state already says it.
A failure is announced through a polite live region on the danger banner; while merging the merge button is announced as Loading.
Every button and row has a 48dp touch target.
edgeCases: A value that is blank after trimming counts as empty, and values equal after trimming count as matching.
Changing the kept record moves every field the person has not picked to the new record's value, or fills it from another record when it is empty.
With one record the dialog shows it and the merge button is disabled.
The merge button's count uses plurals in strings_mergedialog.xml; pass labels.confirm to write it differently.
The choices survive a configuration change; recompose with a new key to start again from the defaults.

whenToUse: At the bottom of a chat, a comment thread or a support conversation, under the messages.
whenNotToUse: For a prompt to an AI assistant, use the intelligence components such as MonarchAiConversation. For a single-line field in a form, use MonarchTextField. For formatted text, wait for the rich text editor; this composer writes plain text.

options.name: label
options.description: The accessible name of the text field, such as Message #design.

options.name: state
options.description: The text. The app owns it, so it saves and restores drafts.

options.name: onSend
options.description: Receives the trimmed text, the mentions still in it and the mode. The send button shows Sending… while it runs; the text clears when it returns and stays when it throws.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the composer.

options.name: sending
options.description: Shows the sending state, for apps that track sending themselves.

options.description: Allows sending without text.

options.name: placeholder

options.name: replyTo

options.name: modes

options.name: onModeChange

options.name: draftStatus
options.description: The app's draft save state, shown with MonarchSaveStatusIndicator as Saving draft…, Draft saved or Draft not saved.

options.name: sendShortcut

options.name: typingIntervalMillis

options.name: disabledReason

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including the mention picker's.

options.name: onAttach

options.name: onDismissReply
options.description: Adds a button named Stop replying that removes the reply context.

options.name: onCancelEdit
options.description: Adds Cancel while editing; Escape on a hardware keyboard calls it.

options.name: onEditLast
options.description: Up on a hardware keyboard in an empty box, to edit the last message.

options.name: onTyping
options.description: Called at most once per typingIntervalMillis while the focused text changes.

options.name: onTypingStop
options.description: Called after onTyping when the text is emptied or sent, focus leaves, or the composer leaves the screen.

options.name: attachIcon
options.description: The attach button's icon, a MonarchIcon with a null description. The button shows its name as text without it.

options.name: emojiIcon
options.description: The emoji button's icon. Text without it.

options.name: dismissIcon
options.description: The icon of the button that removes the reply context. Text without it.

options.name: emojiPicker
options.description: The app's emoji picker, shown while the emoji button is open; the emoji is inserted at the caret. Adds the emoji button.

options.name: attachments
options.description: The attachment row above the text, such as MonarchAttachmentChips. Wraps onto new rows.

options.name: actions
options.description: Extra buttons before the send button.

states.name: empty
states.description: The placeholder in the subtle text color; the send button is disabled.

states.name: ready
states.description: Text or attachments present: the send button is enabled.

states.name: sending
states.description: The send button shows a spinner and reads Sending…; another send is blocked.

states.name: replying
states.description: A context row with Replying to the author, the excerpt and a Stop replying button.

states.name: editing
states.description: A context row with Editing message, a Cancel button and Save instead of Send.

states.name: note mode
states.description: The box uses the subtle warning fill and the warning border; the send label can change, such as Add note.

states.name: over the limit
states.description: The count is negative in the strong danger color and the send button is disabled.

states.name: focused
states.description: The Monarch focus ring around the box.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Subtle fill and border, disabled text color, no emoji button, and the reason under the box.

states.name: draft status
states.description: Saving draft…, Draft saved or Draft not saved under the box.

appearance: The box is the surface color with the input border and the container radius; a note mode uses the subtle warning fill and the warning border, and a disabled composer the subtle fill and border with disabled text. The placeholder is subtle text, the caret the solid accent, the count muted or strong danger over the limit. The same roles adapt to dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web composer is a rich text editor with a formatting toolbar; Android writes plain text until the rich text editor exists, so mentions are written as @Label, as on iOS, and reported as items. On the web Enter sends; on Android the on-screen keyboard's Enter adds a line and the send button sends, while a hardware keyboard's Enter (or Ctrl+Enter) sends, detected by the absence of the soft-keyboard flag on the key event. The web shows a send-key hint under the box; Android does not, because most people type on the on-screen keyboard. Files arrive by paste, drop and picker on the web; on Android onAttach lets the app open the system photo picker or document picker. Monarch has no emoji picker on Android yet (androidx.emoji2:emoji2-emojipicker is not a dependency), so the emoji button appears only with the app's emojiPicker; the emoji is inserted at the caret, which iOS cannot do. Monarch bundles no icons: the attach, emoji and dismiss buttons show their names as text until the app gives icons. onSend is a suspending function, the Kotlin form of iOS's async throws. Draft debouncing is the app's: it owns the TextFieldState. sendShortcut is Enter or CtrlEnter (iOS returnKey or commandReturn) and booleans have no is prefix. Experimental: a domain pattern until a Rook app adopts it.
accessibility: The text field is named by label; the placeholder is drawn inside it.
The reply or edit context is one TalkBack element read as its title and excerpt; the dismiss button is separate and named Stop replying.
The attach, emoji and dismiss buttons are named, with touch targets of at least 48dp, as icon buttons or text buttons.
The send button is a MonarchButton; while sending it reads Sending….
The character count is read as characters left, or characters over the limit, not as a bare number.
The draft status uses MonarchSaveStatusIndicator.
Mention suggestions use MonarchMentionPicker, which announces the result count while focus stays in the text field.
The note mode is named by its segment as well as shown by the warning tint; the segments are named Message type.
The text field reserves 48dp and grows from one to eight lines with the font size, then scrolls.
edgeCases: Text of only spaces cannot be sent; sent text is trimmed.
A mention picked mid-sentence reuses the space after it, so there are never two.
A mention whose @Label was edited away is not sent in mentions.
Typing over the limit is allowed; sending is not, as on the web and iOS.
Text typed while onSend runs is cleared with the sent text when onSend returns.
Hardware key handling can only be confirmed on a device with a keyboard; in tests key events without the soft-keyboard flag stand in for one.

parityExceptions.reason: The web composer is 560px wide: its reply banner sits above the box and the whole toolbar (ten tools, the emoji button and Send) fits one row. A phone is 344dp wide and each tool keeps a 48dp touch target, so the tools share one row that scrolls sideways beside Send and the later tools are reached by scrolling. The reply context is the first row inside the box, so it stays attached to the field it answers.
parityExceptions.convention: Material touch target of 48dp; a toolbar that does not fit scrolls sideways on a compact window

whenToUse: For each message of a chat, a comment thread or a support conversation, with grouped set on follow-ups from the same author.
whenNotToUse: For a list of conversations, use MonarchInboxRow. For an AI assistant's turn, use the intelligence components such as MonarchAiConversation. For an activity feed of events, use MonarchActivityTimeline.

options.name: author
options.description: The name, and the avatar picture as a Painter the app loaded; initials otherwise.

options.name: time
options.description: When the message was sent, in epoch milliseconds (UTC).

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the row.

options.name: timeStyle

options.name: reactionPicker
options.description: The app's emoji picker for the reaction bar's add button.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including the reaction bar's.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Adds Retry to a failed message.

options.name: onDiscard
options.description: Adds Discard to a failed message.

options.name: onShowEdits

states.name: first of a group
states.description: Avatar, author in the strong body style, tags and the muted time above the body.

states.name: grouped
states.description: No avatar or header; the body lines up under the first message and the vertical padding is smaller.

states.name: pending
states.description: The body's content color is muted and Sending… is shown under it. No actions.

states.name: failed
states.description: The error, or Not sent, in the strong danger color under the body, with Retry and Discard when given. No actions.

states.name: edited
states.description: An (edited) caption after the body, a link-coloured button when onShowEdits is given.

states.name: deleted
states.description: The body is replaced by This message was deleted. in muted italics; reactions, replies and actions are hidden.

states.name: internal
states.description: The subtle warning fill with a bar in the warning border color along the start edge.

states.name: highlighted
states.description: The subtle accent fill, animated in and out unless animations are off.

states.name: system
states.description: A centered muted caption with the time below it, without avatar, author, reactions or actions.

appearance: The row has no fill of its own; internal notes use the subtle warning fill with a warning border bar, and a highlighted row the subtle accent fill. The author is default text in the strong body style, the time and markers muted captions, a failure the strong danger color and the edited link the link color. The same roles adapt to dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: On the web the per-message actions are a hover toolbar that also appears on focus, and on iOS a contextMenu; on Android they are a Material 3 DropdownMenu opened by long press with a long-press haptic, the touch convention, and each action is also a TalkBack action. Actions are MonarchMessageRowAction values rather than a slot, because TalkBack actions need a label and a callback. The web shows a grouped message's clock time in the gutter on hover; there is no hover on touch, so the gutter stays empty and TalkBack reads the author and full date on every message. The web and iOS draw a danger icon on failures; Monarch bundles no icons, so the error text carries the meaning. The reaction bar's add button opens the app's picker or a menu of quickReactions, because Monarch has no emoji picker on Android yet (androidx.emoji2:emoji2-emojipicker is not a dependency). The web's avatar slot and footer slot are not offered: the avatar is MonarchAvatar from author, and a footer goes in content. Times are epoch milliseconds; the web also takes Date and ISO strings, and its locale and timeZone parameters are the device's here. Booleans have no is prefix (grouped, edited, deleted, highlighted), unlike iOS. Experimental: a domain pattern until a Rook app adopts it.
accessibility: The author, tags, full date and time, body, edited marker and Sending… are merged into one TalkBack element.
A grouped message still begins with the author and the full date and time for TalkBack, through a node that is not drawn.
The visible relative or clock time is replaced by the full date and time for TalkBack.
Actions are TalkBack custom actions, and the long press is announced as Message actions.
A failure is written in a polite live region that is always present, so it is announced when the status changes; Retry and Discard are separate buttons.
Reactions use MonarchReactionBar: chips named by emoji name and count. The thread button is a separate button.
The avatar is decorative; the author is read from the header.
Retry, Discard, the edit-history marker, the thread button and reaction chips have touch targets of at least 48dp; text wraps at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: A time in the future reads as now; from seven days the relative time shows a short date, with the year when it is not this year.
A deleted message with edited set shows no edited marker.
Actions are not offered while pending or failed, so a long press does nothing then.
A reply count of zero shows nothing.
Without now, a LaunchedEffect refreshes the relative time every minute while the row is on screen.

wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn (reverse layout) inside MonarchVirtualMessageList, with MonarchMessageRow rows, MonarchTypingIndicator in its status slot and MonarchReadReceipt in its footer
summary: A recipe, not a component: a conversation's messages grouped by day, with a New messages divider, older history loaded at the top, who is typing under the list and who has seen the last message.
whenToUse: For the message area of a chat, a channel or a support conversation: MonarchVirtualMessageList draws the day separators, the unread divider, grouping and the jump to latest; the rows are MonarchMessageRows.
whenNotToUse: For the replies to one message, use MonarchThreadPanel. For comments anchored to a document, use MonarchCommentThread. For a feed of events rather than messages, use MonarchActivityTimeline.
api: @Composable fun <T> MonarchVirtualMessageList(items: List<T>, key: (item: T) -> Any, time: (item: T) -> Long, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, state: LazyListState = rememberLazyListState(), authorId: (item: T) -> String? = { null }, firstUnreadKey: Any? = null, hasOlder: Boolean = false, loadingOlder: Boolean = false, …, onLoadOlder: (() -> Unit)? = null, …, footer: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, status: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, …, row: @Composable LazyItemScope.(item: T, context: MonarchVirtualMessageListContext<T>) -> Unit)
@ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchMessageRow(author: MonarchMessageRowAuthor, time: Long, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, …, grouped: Boolean = false, …, content: @Composable () -> Unit)
@Composable fun MonarchTypingIndicator(names: List<String>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, text: String? = null, reserveSpace: Boolean = true, announceChanges: Boolean = true)
@Composable fun MonarchReadReceipt(readers: List<MonarchReadReceiptReader>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, display: MonarchReadReceiptDisplay = MonarchReadReceiptDisplay.Text, …)

states.name: grouped by day
states.description: A Today, Yesterday or date separator before the first message of each day, in the given locale and time zone.

states.name: unread
states.description: With firstUnreadKey, a New messages divider above the first unread message.

states.name: grouped
states.description: Consecutive messages by one author within five minutes are drawn with grouped = true, without a repeated name and avatar.

states.name: older history
states.description: With hasOlder, older messages load when the reader nears the top; loadingOlder and olderFailed show progress or a retry.

states.name: typing and seen
states.description: MonarchTypingIndicator in the status slot under the list; MonarchReadReceipt in the footer after the last message.

appearance: The separators and divider use MonarchVirtualMessageList's roles: muted text with subtle borders, and the accent role for New messages. The rows, typing indicator and read receipt keep their own roles. The same roles adapt to dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web's MessageTimeline is one component with exported helpers (shouldGroupMessages, formatMessageDay, the separators) for products that virtualise rows themselves. On Android, MonarchVirtualMessageList already virtualises with a lazy list and draws the day separators, the unread divider, grouping and the jump button, so the timeline is the recipe below and there is no separate type; iOS uses the same recipe. The web's imperative handle (scrollToBottom, scrollToItem) is the LazyListState passed as state and scrollToKey. Dates are epoch milliseconds in UTC, grouped in the given time zone.
accessibility: MonarchVirtualMessageList announces messages that arrive in a polite live region; the rows themselves are not live, so scrolling stays quiet.
Day separators and the New messages divider are read as headings.
Each MonarchMessageRow reads its author, full date and body as one element.
MonarchTypingIndicator announces who starts typing; MonarchReadReceipt reads who has seen the message.
edgeCases: Keep firstUnreadKey fixed while the conversation is open, so the divider does not move as the reader catches up.
Pass now, locale and timeZone for output that does not depend on the device, for example in screenshots.
The list scrolls itself: give it a bounded height and do not put it in a vertically scrolling parent.

examples.title: Conversation with older history
examples.template:
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space2)) {
    MonarchVirtualMessageList(
        items = messages,
        key = { it.id },
        time = { it.time },
        modifier = Modifier.height(860.dp),
        authorId = { it.authorId },
        firstUnreadKey = {{firstUnreadId}},
        hasOlder = {{hasOlder}},
        now = now,
        timeZone = {{timeZone}},
        status = { MonarchTypingIndicator(names = listOf({{typing}})) },
    ) { message, context ->
        MonarchMessageRow(
            author = MonarchMessageRowAuthor(message.author, seed = message.authorId),
            time = message.time,
            now = now,
            timeStyle = MonarchMessageRowTimeStyle.Clock,
            locale = Locale.UK,
            timeZone = {{timeZone}},
            grouped = context.grouped,
        ) { MonarchText(message.text) }
    }
    MonarchButton(
        text = {{addLabel}},
        onClick = {},
        variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Secondary,
        size = MonarchButtonSize.Sm,
    )
}
examples.setup:
class Message(val id: String, val authorId: String, val author: String, val text: String, val time: Long)
val now = 1_772_452_800_000L
val messages = remember {
    listOf(
        Message(id = "m1", authorId = "ana", author = "Ana Lopez", text = "Morning! Is the launch checklist up to date?", time = 1_772_393_400_000L),
        Message(id = "m2", authorId = "ana", author = "Ana Lopez", text = "Mostly. Legal sign-off is still open.", time = 1_772_393_580_000L),
        Message(id = "m3", authorId = "ben", author = "Ben Okafor", text = "I’ll chase it after standup.", time = 1_772_433_000_000L),
        Message(id = "m4", authorId = "chloe", author = "Chloé Martin", text = "Thanks. The press kit is in the shared folder.", time = 1_772_436_600_000L),
        Message(id = "m5", authorId = "chloe", author = "Chloé Martin", text = "Looks good. One typo on page two.", time = 1_772_436_720_000L),
        Message(id = "m6", authorId = "ana", author = "Ana Lopez", text = "Fixed, and the screenshots are refreshed.", time = 1_772_443_800_000L),
        Message(id = "m7", authorId = "ben", author = "Ben Okafor", text = "Great. Shall we freeze copy at 15:00?", time = 1_772_449_200_000L),
        Message(id = "m8", authorId = "ben", author = "Ben Okafor", text = "Works for me.", time = 1_772_449_320_000L),
    )
}
examples.code:
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space2)) {
    MonarchVirtualMessageList(
        items = messages,
        key = { it.id },
        time = { it.time },
        modifier = Modifier.height(860.dp),
        authorId = { it.authorId },
        firstUnreadKey = "m7",
        hasOlder = true,
        now = now,
        timeZone = "UTC",

            locale = Locale.UK,
            timeZone = "UTC",

name: MonarchMethodBadge
title: MethodBadge
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Box, androidx.compose.material3.Text
summary: An HTTP method label (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) in the code typeface, with a tone per method.
whenToUse: In endpoint lists, API references and request logs, before the path of a request.
whenNotToUse: For a status or other metadata use MonarchBadge. For the release stage of an API use MonarchLifecycleBadge.
api: @Composable fun MonarchMethodBadge(method: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, tone: MonarchTone? = null)
object MonarchMethodBadgeDefaults { fun toneFor(method: String): MonarchTone }

options.name: method
options.description: The HTTP method in any case. It is trimmed and shown in upper case.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the component.

options.name: tone
options.description: Replaces the tone chosen from the method. null keeps GET success, POST info, PUT and PATCH warning, DELETE danger and everything else neutral.

states.name: default
states.description: Not interactive; one look per tone.

appearance: A tinted fill of the tone with strong text and a border of the tone, in 6dp corners; the neutral tone is the muted background with muted text and no border. Every pair comes from one tone family, in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The parity map named MonarchBadge as the base. MonarchBadge is a capsule in the caption role and cannot take the code typeface or a minimum width, so this component draws its own surface from the same tone palette, as iOS does. The web's sm and md sizes are not offered: the text is the code role (14sp) and follows the font size setting. The web's tone type has no accent; MonarchTone is used. The tone map is MonarchMethodBadgeDefaults.toneFor, the web's methodTone and iOS's tone(for:).
accessibility: Read by TalkBack as the method name, which is always the visible text, so color is never the only signal.
The text grows with the font size setting and the 56dp minimum width grows with it.
Not interactive: it has no click action and no touch target.
edgeCases: A method outside GET, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE is neutral, including HEAD and OPTIONS.
An empty method draws an empty badge at the minimum width.
A long method wraps inside the badge; real methods are one word.
With a custom code font family in monarchTypography, that family is used.

examples.title: Every method
examples.template:
FlowRow(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space2)) {
    MonarchMethodBadge(method = {{methods.0}})
    MonarchMethodBadge(method = {{methods.1}})
    MonarchMethodBadge(method = {{methods.2}})
    MonarchMethodBadge(method = {{methods.3}})
    MonarchMethodBadge(method = {{methods.4}})
    MonarchMethodBadge(method = {{methods.5}})
    MonarchMethodBadge(method = {{methods.6}})
}

    MonarchMethodBadge(method = "PATCH")
    MonarchMethodBadge(method = "DELETE")
    MonarchMethodBadge(method = "HEAD")
    MonarchMethodBadge(method = "OPTIONS")
}

examples.title: A custom method with its own tone
examples.code: MonarchMethodBadge(method = "purge", tone = MonarchTone.Danger)

name: MonarchMetric
title: Metric
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column or FlowRow of androidx.compose.material3.Text, numbers written by android.icu.text.NumberFormat and CompactDecimalFormat (money by MonarchMoneyFormat); the change is a MonarchDeltaIndicator
summary: One number with its label, an optional unit and an optional change, formatted for the locale in tabular figures, with no surface around it.
whenToUse: For a key figure in a dashboard, a card, a toolbar or a table footer: "Open tickets 128 up 12%".
whenNotToUse: Not for an amount of money on its own: use MonarchMoney. Not for a tile with a chart and actions: put the metric in a MonarchWidget or a MonarchCard. Not for a number inside running text: use MonarchTabularNumber.
api: @Composable fun MonarchMetric(label: String, value: Double?, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, unit: String? = null, change: MonarchMetricChange? = null, format: MonarchMetricFormat = MonarchMetricFormat.Number, size: MonarchMetricSize = MonarchMetricSize.Md, layout: MonarchMetricLayout = MonarchMetricLayout.Stacked, alignment: Alignment.Horizontal = Alignment.Start, compact: Boolean = false, locale: Locale? = null, emptyLabel: String? = null)

@Composable fun MonarchMetric(label: String, text: String?, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, spokenText: String? = null, unit: String? = null, change: MonarchMetricChange? = null, size: MonarchMetricSize = MonarchMetricSize.Md, layout: MonarchMetricLayout = MonarchMetricLayout.Stacked, alignment: Alignment.Horizontal = Alignment.Start, emptyLabel: String? = null)

class MonarchMetricChange(value: Double?, comparison: String? = null, goodDirection: MonarchDeltaIndicatorGoodDirection = MonarchDeltaIndicatorGoodDirection.Up, variant: MonarchDeltaIndicatorVariant = MonarchDeltaIndicatorVariant.Plain, flatThreshold: Double = 0.0, formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = null, icon: (@Composable (direction: MonarchDeltaIndicatorDirection) -> Unit)? = null) { companion object { fun between(current: Double?, previous: Double?, comparison: String? = null, goodDirection: …, variant: …, flatThreshold: Double = 0.0, formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = null, icon: … = null): MonarchMetricChange } }
sealed class MonarchMetricFormat { abstract fun format(value: Double, compact: Boolean, locale: Locale): String; data object Number; data object Percent; data class Currency(val code: String) }
enum class MonarchMetricSize { Sm, Md, Lg }
enum class MonarchMetricLayout { Stacked, Inline }

options.name: label
options.description: What the number measures, such as "Open tickets". Always visible.

options.name: value
options.description: The number. null, NaN or infinity shows a dash that TalkBack reads as "No data".

options.name: text
options.description: In the second overload: the value already written by the app. null or empty shows the dash.

options.name: spokenText
options.description: In the second overload: what TalkBack reads instead of text.

options.name: unit
options.description: Written smaller and muted after the value. Hidden for an empty value.

options.name: change
options.description: The change against an earlier period, drawn by MonarchDeltaIndicator under the value (after it when inline). MonarchMetricChange(value) takes a ratio; MonarchMetricChange.between(current, previous) works it out.

options.name: format
options.description: Number, Percent (a ratio: 0.12 is 12%) or Currency(code).

options.name: size
options.description: Sm for dense rows, Md, Lg for a headline figure. Lg also draws the change one size larger.

options.name: layout
options.description: Stacked puts the label above the value; Inline puts label, value and change on one line that wraps.

options.name: alignment
options.description: The alignment of the stacked layout; Alignment.End for numeric columns.

options.name: compact
options.description: Writes 12K or €3.4M with the locale's compact notation; TalkBack reads the full value.

options.name: locale
options.description: The locale to write in. Default: the first locale of the configuration.

options.name: emptyLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "No data" read for a missing value (monarch_metric_empty).

states.name: default
states.description: The label in the muted text role, the value in the default text role with tabular figures, the unit muted, the change under it.

states.name: empty
states.description: A dash in the subtle text role instead of the value, read as "No data"; the unit is hidden.

states.name: compact
states.description: The value is written short (12K); its content description is the full number.

appearance: No surface. The label uses the muted text role, the value the default text role in the heading role (bodyStrong for Sm, display for Lg), the unit the muted text role, and the change the tones of MonarchDeltaIndicator. High-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colors.
platformNotes: The web value accepts any React node and Intl.NumberFormat options; on Android a number is written by android.icu.text.NumberFormat (number, percent, compact) or MonarchMoneyFormat (currency) in the locale, and any other value is passed as text with an optional spoken form, as on iOS. The web align start/end is an Alignment.Horizontal. The web shows the full compact value as a hover title; Android has no hover on touch, so only TalkBack gets it. The change takes the main MonarchDeltaIndicator options; its flat and no-data labels keep their built-in text. iOS uses the same name and options.
accessibility: The metric is one TalkBack element (merged semantics): the label, the value with its unit and the change sentence of MonarchDeltaIndicator, for example "Latency, 840, ms, down 8% vs last week, better".
A compact value is read in full ("12,345"), and the dash for a missing value is read as "No data" or emptyLabel.
The change's meaning is carried by its sign, its arrow slot and the spoken sentence, not by color.
Text uses Monarch type roles, so it scales with the font size setting and wraps instead of being cut off.
edgeCases: A value that is not finite (infinity, NaN) is shown as empty.
Very long values and units wrap; the unit moves under the value when both do not fit.
Percent takes a ratio: pass 0.12 for 12%. The percent format has no compact form.
Currency digits follow the currency: JPY has none.
A metric is not tappable; put it in a MonarchCard with onClick for a tile that opens a detail screen.

examples.title: Number, unit and change
examples.template:
MonarchMetric(
    label = {{label}},
    value = {{value|double}},
    unit = {{unit}},
    change = MonarchMetricChange(
        value = {{change.value}},
        comparison = {{change.comparison}},
        goodDirection = MonarchDeltaIndicatorGoodDirection.{{change.goodDirection|pascal}},
    ),
)
examples.code:
MonarchMetric(
    label = "Median response",
    value = 182.0,
    unit = "ms",
    change = MonarchMetricChange(
        value = -0.08,
        comparison = "vs last week",
        goodDirection = MonarchDeltaIndicatorGoodDirection.Down,
    ),
)

examples.title: Currency, percent and a missing value
examples.code:
Column {
    MonarchMetric(label = "Revenue", value = 3_400_000.0, format = MonarchMetricFormat.Currency("EUR"), compact = true)
    MonarchMetric(
        label = "Conversion",
        value = 0.12,
        format = MonarchMetricFormat.Percent,
        layout = MonarchMetricLayout.Inline,
        change = MonarchMetricChange.between(current = 0.12, previous = 0.1),
    )
    MonarchMetric(label = "Errors", value = null, unit = "per hour")
}

title: MiniCall
wrapsNative: android.app.Activity.enterPictureInPictureMode(android.app.PictureInPictureParams), with androidx.core.app.PictureInPictureModeChangedInfo from androidx.activity.ComponentActivity
summary: A call that continues while people do something else is shown in the system's picture-in-picture window. Monarch ships no floating call window.
whenToUse: To keep a video call visible when the person leaves the call screen or the app: enter picture in picture from the call activity, and hide the controls while the activity is in picture in picture.
whenNotToUse: Do not build a draggable in-app window; it cannot leave the app and duplicates the system one. For an audio-only call the ongoing call notification is enough.
api: Activity.enterPictureInPictureMode(params: PictureInPictureParams): Boolean
PictureInPictureParams.Builder().setAspectRatio(aspectRatio: Rational).build()
ComponentActivity.addOnPictureInPictureModeChangedListener(listener: Consumer<PictureInPictureModeChangedInfo>)

options.name: aspectRatio
options.description: The shape of the window, for example 16:9 for a shared screen or 9:16 for a phone camera.

options.name: autoEnterEnabled
options.description: Android 12 and later: enters picture in picture when the person goes home, without a button.

states.name: full screen
states.description: The call activity with all its controls.

states.name: picture in picture
states.description: The same activity in a small system window; the app hides its controls and the system draws its own.

appearance: The system draws the window, its frame and its controls. The content inside is the app's call screen in the Monarch theme, without its controls.
platformNotes: The web MiniCall is a draggable in-page window with a timer, mute, expand and leave. Android uses its own picture-in-picture mode, as iOS uses AVPictureInPictureController. Mute and leave stay on the call screen, in the ongoing call notification, or as RemoteAction items set with PictureInPictureParams.Builder.setActions. The activity must declare android:supportsPictureInPicture="true" in the manifest.
accessibility: System behavior: the picture-in-picture window is accessible and can be moved, expanded and closed with TalkBack.
Give the button that starts it a visible label, such as "Continue in picture in picture".
edgeCases: Picture in picture needs Android 8 (API 26); check Build.VERSION.SDK_INT and PackageManager.FEATURE_PICTURE_IN_PICTURE.
Without android:supportsPictureInPicture in the manifest, enterPictureInPictureMode throws IllegalStateException.
The whole activity goes into the window, so a call screen is usually its own activity.

The example and the catalogue page were compiled and composed; the window was not opened on a device. The catalogue activity declares picture in picture with the configuration changes it handles; its page sets setAutoEnterEnabled and setSourceRectHint on Android 12 and later while it is open.

examples.title: Continue the call in picture in picture
examples.setup: var micOn by remember { mutableStateOf(true) }

examples.title: Hide the call controls while in picture in picture
