parityExceptions.convention: iOS AVPictureInPictureController and Android picture-in-picture.

name: MonarchMiniMonth
title: MiniMonth
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row and Column, androidx.compose.foundation.selection.selectable, androidx.compose.material3.IconButton, android.icu.text.DateFormat
summary: A month calendar for choosing a day, with an earliest and latest day, days the app marks unavailable, ISO week numbers and up to three dots under days that have events.
whenToUse: For a calendar that shows which days have events or are available: a sidebar calendar beside an agenda, a booking day picker with unavailable days.
whenNotToUse: For entering a date in a form use the Material 3 DatePicker or DatePickerDialog, which also offer text input and a year picker. For a range of dates use the Material 3 DateRangePicker.
api: @Composable fun MonarchMiniMonth(selection: Long?, onSelectionChange: (Long) -> Unit, previousMonthIcon: @Composable () -> Unit, nextMonthIcon: @Composable () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, visibleMonth: Long? = null, onVisibleMonthChange: ((Long) -> Unit)? = null, minimumDate: Long? = null, maximumDate: Long? = null, today: Long? = null, firstDayOfWeek: Int? = null, showWeekNumbers: Boolean = false, showOutsideDays: Boolean = true, fixedWeeks: Boolean = true, enabled: Boolean = true, isDateDisabled: ((Long) -> Boolean)? = null, dayInfo: ((Long) -> MonarchMiniMonthDayInfo?)? = null, labels: MonarchMiniMonthLabels = MonarchMiniMonthLabels())
class MonarchMiniMonthDayInfo(dots: List<MonarchTone?>, description: String? = null) { constructor(dotCount: Int, description: String? = null); companion object { const val MAX_DOTS: Int = 3 } }
class MonarchMiniMonthLabels(previousMonth: String? = null, nextMonth: String? = null, today: String? = null, week: String? = null, weekNumber: ((Int) -> String)? = null)

options.name: selection
options.description: The selected day in epoch milliseconds (any time of that UTC day), or null for none.

options.name: onSelectionChange
options.description: Called with the day the user chooses, as the UTC midnight of that date.

options.name: previousMonthIcon
options.description: The icon of the previous-month button. Monarch bundles no icons; pass one that mirrors in right-to-left layouts, with a null content description.

options.name: nextMonthIcon
options.description: The icon of the next-month button.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the component.

options.name: visibleMonth
options.description: Any day of the month on screen. null lets the calendar keep it (saved across configuration changes), starting on the month of the selection or of today.

options.name: onVisibleMonthChange
options.description: Called with the first day of the month the user moves to.

options.name: minimumDate
options.description: The earliest day that can be chosen. Earlier months cannot be reached.

options.name: maximumDate
options.description: The latest day that can be chosen. Later months cannot be reached.

options.name: today
options.description: Today's date, for example in the workspace's time zone. null is today on the device's calendar.

options.name: firstDayOfWeek
options.description: The first column, Calendar.SUNDAY to Calendar.SATURDAY. null follows the locale of the configuration.

options.name: showWeekNumbers
options.description: Shows ISO 8601 week numbers in a column at the start.

options.name: showOutsideDays
options.description: Shows the neighbouring months' days, dimmed, not selectable and not read by TalkBack.

options.name: fixedWeeks
options.description: Always six week rows, so the height does not change between months.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether days and the month buttons can be used.

options.name: isDateDisabled
options.description: Returns true for a day that cannot be chosen. Called for every day of the month shown.

options.name: dayInfo
options.description: The dots and their description for a day: accent dots (dotCount, or null entries) or toned dots; at most three are drawn.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings (monarch_minimonth_previous_month, _next_month, _today, _week, _week_number).

states.name: selected
states.description: The day's number in the accent's on-solid color on a solid accent circle; TalkBack says selected.

states.name: today
states.description: An accent ring and semibold strong accent text; TalkBack reads "Today" before the date.

states.name: unavailable
states.description: Days outside the bounds and days the app disables are in the disabled text color and cannot be chosen; days the app disables are also struck through. TalkBack says disabled.

states.name: with dots
states.description: Up to three 6dp dots under the number: the accent, or the solid color of a tone; the neutral tone is the subtle text color.

states.name: disabled
states.description: enabled = false: no day and no month button can be used.

appearance: Default text on the surface; weekday initials and week numbers in the subtle text color; the selected day a solid accent circle, today an accent ring. All roles follow light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The parity map asked for a custom grid because the Material 3 DatePicker cannot show event dots or week numbers; iOS wraps UICalendarView under the same name and cannot show week numbers. The web's month and year pickers behind the title are not offered: the title is a heading, and an app that needs to jump far sets visibleMonth (or uses the Material 3 DatePicker). Also not offered: the web's highlighted range and range preview (use the Material 3 DateRangePicker), several months side by side, a footer (put a button under the calendar), and the web's keyboard grid model with arrow keys and Page Up/Down; days are reached with Tab and the platform's focus search. The web's accent dot tone is a null entry or dotCount, because MonarchTone has no accent case. Days are epoch milliseconds of their UTC midnight, as in DatePickerState, not ISO strings. Each day reserves a 48dp target, so the seven days need 336dp; narrower, the grid scrolls sideways (the web shrinks its days). Decision (C-091, closed 2026-11-15): compact day cells below 336dp are not built. The touch target wins: every day keeps a 48dp target (WCAG 2.5.8 and the Material 3 minimum), and the grid scrolls sideways on a window narrower than 336dp, 368dp with week numbers. iOS can differ because UICalendarView sizes its own days.
accessibility: Each day is one TalkBack element read as its full date in the locale ("Saturday, November 14, 2026"), with "Today" before today and the dot description after.
The selected day has the selected state; unavailable days are disabled and do not react to taps.
The month title is a heading and a polite live region, so moving to another month is announced.
The month buttons are Material 3 icon buttons named "Previous month" and "Next month", disabled at the bounds.
Every day reserves a 48dp by 48dp touch target in the layout; the grid scrolls sideways rather than shrinking it.
Days of the neighbouring months are not read and cannot be chosen.
Right to left, the first day of the week and the previous button are at the right edge.
The numbers grow with the font size setting; the day circles grow with them.
The meaning of a dot is never color alone only if the app gives a description.
edgeCases: A selection outside the bounds or on a disabled day is not shown as selected; the selection value is left as it is.
A latest day before the earliest day leaves only the earliest day available.
A visibleMonth outside the bounds shows the nearest month inside them.
isDateDisabled and dayInfo are called for every day of the month on every composition, so they must be cheap.
Days are UTC dates. today defaults to the device's local date written as a UTC midnight; pass today to use a workspace's time zone.
On a screen narrower than 336dp (368dp with week numbers) the grid scrolls sideways.
With visibleMonth set and no onVisibleMonthChange that updates it, the month buttons do not move the calendar.

examples.title: Sidebar calendar with events
A booking calendar: the next 30 days, no weekends

name: MonarchMoney
title: Money
wrapsNative: android.icu.text.NumberFormat (CURRENCYSTYLE, ACCOUNTINGCURRENCYSTYLE, ISOCURRENCYSTYLE, PLURALCURRENCYSTYLE) and android.icu.text.CompactDecimalFormat, drawn by MonarchTabularNumber (androidx.compose.material3.Text with tabular figures)
summary: An amount of money in one currency, written by the platform's currency format in tabular figures, with an empty state and a spoken full amount for the compact form.
whenToUse: Wherever an app shows a price, a balance, a refund or a total. Use MonarchMoneyFormat.format when the text itself is needed, for example in a content description or an export.
whenNotToUse: Not for plain numbers or percentages: use MonarchTabularNumber or MonarchMetric. Not for entering an amount: use MonarchNumberInput.
api: @Composable fun MonarchMoney(amount: BigDecimal?, currencyCode: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, notation: MonarchMoneyNotation = MonarchMoneyNotation.Standard, signDisplay: MonarchMoneySignDisplay = MonarchMoneySignDisplay.Automatic, currencyDisplay: MonarchMoneyCurrencyDisplay = MonarchMoneyCurrencyDisplay.Symbol, accountingSign: Boolean = false, fractionDigits: IntRange? = null, locale: Locale? = null, style: MonarchTextStyle = MonarchTextStyle.Body, toneNegative: Boolean = false, color: Color = Color.Unspecified, textAlign: TextAlign? = null, emptyText: String? = null, emptyLabel: String? = null)

@Composable fun MonarchMoney(minorUnits: Long?, currencyCode: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, notation: MonarchMoneyNotation = MonarchMoneyNotation.Standard, signDisplay: MonarchMoneySignDisplay = MonarchMoneySignDisplay.Automatic, currencyDisplay: MonarchMoneyCurrencyDisplay = MonarchMoneyCurrencyDisplay.Symbol, accountingSign: Boolean = false, fractionDigits: IntRange? = null, locale: Locale? = null, style: MonarchTextStyle = MonarchTextStyle.Body, toneNegative: Boolean = false, color: Color = Color.Unspecified, textAlign: TextAlign? = null, emptyText: String? = null, emptyLabel: String? = null)

object MonarchMoneyFormat { fun format(amount: BigDecimal, currencyCode: String, locale: Locale, notation: MonarchMoneyNotation = MonarchMoneyNotation.Standard, signDisplay: MonarchMoneySignDisplay = MonarchMoneySignDisplay.Automatic, currencyDisplay: MonarchMoneyCurrencyDisplay = MonarchMoneyCurrencyDisplay.Symbol, accountingSign: Boolean = false, fractionDigits: IntRange? = null): String; fun amountOfMinorUnits(minorUnits: Long, currencyCode: String): BigDecimal; fun currencyDigits(currencyCode: String): Int }
enum class MonarchMoneyNotation { Standard, Compact }
enum class MonarchMoneySignDisplay { Automatic, Always, ExceptZero, Never }
enum class MonarchMoneyCurrencyDisplay { Symbol, NarrowSymbol, Code, Name }

options.name: amount
options.description: The amount in major units (19.99 for $19.99), or null when there is none.

options.name: minorUnits
options.description: In the second overload: the amount in minor units. 1999 with USD is $19.99; the conversion is exact.

options.name: currencyCode
options.description: The ISO 4217 code, such as USD, EUR or INR. It selects the symbol and the digits; the amount is never converted.

options.name: notation
options.description: Standard writes every digit; Compact writes $1.3M and TalkBack reads the full amount.

options.name: signDisplay
options.description: Automatic, Always (also +$0.00), ExceptZero (+$42.00 for gains) or Never.

options.name: currencyDisplay
options.description: Symbol, NarrowSymbol ($, Android 11 and later), Code (USD) or Name (US dollars).

options.name: accountingSign
options.description: Writes negatives in parentheses where the locale does: ($42.00). Symbol forms only.

options.name: fractionDigits
options.description: The least and most digits after the decimal separator. Default: the currency's own (USD 2, JPY 0, KWD 3). Rounds half up.

options.name: locale
options.description: The locale to write in. Default: the first locale of the configuration.

options.name: style
options.description: The type role.

options.name: toneNegative
options.description: Colors a negative amount with the strong danger role. The sign or parentheses always carry the meaning.

options.name: color
options.description: The text color; unspecified keeps the surrounding content color.

options.name: textAlign
options.description: The alignment inside the available width, for example End in a numeric column.

options.name: emptyText
options.description: Replaces the built-in dash shown for a missing amount (monarch_money_empty).

options.name: emptyLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "No amount" that TalkBack reads for a missing amount (monarch_money_empty_label).

states.name: standard
states.description: The amount in the surrounding content color with tabular digits.

states.name: negative
states.description: A minus sign, or parentheses with accountingSign; with toneNegative the text uses the strong danger role.

states.name: compact
states.description: The short form is shown; its content description is the full amount.

states.name: empty
states.description: A null amount shows an em dash in the muted text role, read as "No amount".

appearance: Text in the chosen type role with tabular figures, in the surrounding content color. A toned negative amount uses the strong danger text role and a missing amount the muted text role; both resolve to stronger colors in the high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Formatting is android.icu.text.NumberFormat with the currency styles available from API 24, so the output can differ in small ways from the web's Intl.NumberFormat and iOS's FormatStyle. ICU before Android 11 has no sign-display or compact currency option, so Monarch adds them: the plus sign replaces the locale's minus sign, and the compact form puts CompactDecimalFormat's short number where the digit stands in the currency format of one unit. The narrow symbol needs API 30 and falls back to the symbol before that. The web takes numbers, bigints or decimal strings; Android takes BigDecimal or Long minor units, as iOS takes Decimal or Int. The web hover title of compact amounts has no touch equivalent; TalkBack reads the full amount.
accessibility: A compact amount has the full amount as its content description, so TalkBack reads "$1,300,000.00" for "$1.3M".
A missing amount shows "—" and is read as "No amount"; both strings can be replaced.
Negative amounts keep their sign or parentheses, so color is never the only cue.
The text scales with the font size setting through its type role and wraps instead of being cut off.
edgeCases: Minor units are converted with the currency's own digits (USD 2, JPY 0, KWD 3); an unknown code uses 2. Long.MAX_VALUE minor units convert exactly.
An unknown or malformed currency code writes the number in the locale's format followed by the code.
fractionDigits 0..0 rounds the amount for display only, half up.
The compact form uses the locale's significant digits, so small amounts lose their cents (19.99 is $20); use it for large figures only.
With Name and Compact the plural name is used ($1.3M is "1.3M US dollars").
accountingSign has no effect with Code or Name, which ICU writes with a minus sign.

A refund, a gain and a compact total

name: MonarchMultiSelect
title: MultiSelect
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.ModalBottomSheet with MonarchSearchBar and an androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn of toggleable rows with androidx.compose.material3.Checkbox marks; MonarchTag (androidx.compose.material3.AssistChip) for the chosen values, MonarchButton and MonarchFormField
summary: A field for choosing several values from a long list, searched in a bottom sheet, with the chosen values shown as removable tags.
whenToUse: For several values from a list too long to show at once: teams, labels, countries, skills.
whenNotToUse: For one value use MonarchCombobox or MonarchSelect. For a few fixed options use MonarchCheckboxGroup. For free text values use MonarchTagInput. For people and records with pictures use MonarchEntityPicker.
api: @Composable fun MonarchMultiSelect(label: String, options: List<MonarchComboboxOption>, selected: List<String>, onSelectedChange: (List<String>) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, required: Boolean = false, loading: Boolean = false, sortByMatch: Boolean = false, placeholder: String? = null, helperText: String? = null, errorText: String? = null, maxSelections: Int? = null, limit: Int? = null, query: String? = null, onQueryChange: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, filter: ((MonarchComboboxOption, String) -> Boolean)? = null, onCreate: ((String) -> MonarchComboboxOption?)? = null, removeIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchMultiSelectLabels = MonarchMultiSelectLabels())

class MonarchMultiSelectLabels(select: String? = null, change: String? = null, done: String? = null, none: String? = null, count: ((count: Int, max: Int) -> String)? = null, remove: ((label: String) -> String)? = null, list: MonarchComboboxLabels = MonarchComboboxLabels())

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label, already localised. It names the button and is the title of the sheet.

options.name: options
options.description: The options in order, with the same fields as a combobox option: label, description, hint, group, keywords and enabled.

options.name: selected
options.description: The ids of the chosen options, in the order they were picked.

options.name: onSelectedChange
options.description: Called with every chosen id after each pick or removal.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the field.

options.name: enabled
options.description: When false the button and the tags' remove buttons do nothing and take the disabled colors.

options.name: required
options.description: Shows a mark after the label and adds "Required" to the button's name.

options.name: loading
options.description: Shows "Loading…" in the list while nothing matches.

options.name: sortByMatch
options.description: While searching, lists labels that start with the text first, then labels with a word that does.

options.name: placeholder
options.description: The button's text while nothing is chosen. "Select…" when null.

options.name: helperText
options.description: Guidance under the field.

options.name: errorText
options.description: An error message, shown under the field and set as the button's error.

options.name: maxSelections
options.description: The most values that can be chosen. Other rows are disabled at the limit and "2 of 3 selected" shows under the field and in the sheet.

options.name: limit
options.description: Shows at most this many matches, with a note to keep typing.

options.name: query
options.description: The search text, for a server search, with onQueryChange and a filter that keeps every option. Kept inside when null; cleared when the sheet closes.

options.name: onQueryChange
options.description: Called with the search text on every keystroke, and with "" when the sheet closes.

options.name: filter
options.description: Decides whether an option matches. By default the label, hint and keywords are searched, ignoring case and accents.

options.name: onCreate
options.description: Offers "Create “text”" when no label equals the typed text and the limit is not reached. The returned option is chosen.

options.name: removeIcon
options.description: The icon of each tag's remove button. Monarch bundles no icons; without it tags are plain and values are removed in the sheet.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings; list takes the combobox list strings (search, loading, empty, create, more).

states.name: empty
states.description: No tags; the secondary button shows the prompt.

states.name: chosen
states.description: The picks are tags in pick order above a ghost button that reads "Edit selection".

states.name: open
states.description: A bottom sheet with the label as its title, the count when there is a limit, a search field, the checklist under group headings and Done; it stays open between picks.

states.name: limit reached
states.description: Rows that are not chosen are disabled and Create is not offered; chosen rows can still be removed.

states.name: loading
states.description: The list shows "Loading…" while nothing matches.

states.name: error
states.description: The message shows under the field with the form field's error style and is set on the button.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Text takes the disabled colors and the button and tag remove buttons do nothing.

appearance: Tags use the neutral tag colors, the button the secondary or ghost button colors, the sheet the surface role with check marks in the accent solid role and unchecked boxes in the input border role; descriptions, hints, headings and the count use the muted text role. All come from MonarchTheme in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web opens a popover listbox under an input with chips; on Android the list opens in a Material 3 bottom sheet with a search field, the pattern of system pickers, and the chips sit above a button, as on iOS. The web submits values as hidden form inputs (name); a Compose app reads the hoisted list instead. Matching, ordering, grouping, the limit note and Create are shared with MonarchCombobox. Tags are removable only when the app gives a removeIcon, because Monarch bundles no icons. The web's server search with onSearch and an AbortSignal becomes query and onQueryChange with app-side loading, as in MonarchCombobox. Same name as iOS.
accessibility: The button is one element named by the field's label (with "Required" when required); its state description is the chosen labels joined with commas, or "None".
The error is set on the button and announced through the form field's polite live region.
Each tag's remove button is named "Remove" with the value's label and has a 48dp target.
In the sheet each option row is one checkbox element with its label, description and hint; disabled and over-limit rows are read as disabled.
Group headings are headings; Loading, No matches and the count are polite live regions.
The button and every row are at least 48dp high.
edgeCases: A chosen id with no option is shown as the id itself, so a value from an older list stays visible and removable.
Creating an option that is already chosen does not remove it.
At the limit, Create is hidden; a new pick needs a removal first.
Long labels wrap in the tags and in the rows; the button keeps its own short text.

examples.title: In a Field, controlled
examples.template:
MonarchMultiSelect(
    label = {{label}},
    options = options,
    selected = labels,
    onSelectedChange = { labels = it },
    placeholder = {{placeholder}},
    helperText = {{description}},
    removeIcon = { Icon(SampleIcons.Close, contentDescription = null) },
)

    placeholder = "Add labels",
    helperText = "Type to filter. Picked labels show as chips.",
    removeIcon = { Icon(SampleIcons.Close, contentDescription = null) },
)

name: MonarchMyStatus
title: MyStatus
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row with Modifier.clickable (Role.Button, Material 3 ripple) around MonarchAvatar with its presence dot and two androidx.compose.material3.Text lines; a LaunchedEffect with kotlinx.coroutines.delay that redraws when the status ends
summary: The signed-in person's avatar, presence and custom status, as one row that opens their status settings.
whenToUse: At the top of a navigation drawer, an account screen or a workspace switcher, where people check and change their own status.
whenNotToUse: Not for other people (use MonarchAvatar with a status, or MonarchMemberRow). Not for the account menu itself.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchMyStatus(name: String, presence: MonarchPresenceStatus, onClick: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, image: Painter? = null, customStatus: MonarchMyStatusCustomStatus? = null, now: Long? = null, enabled: Boolean = true, labels: MonarchMyStatusLabels = MonarchMyStatusLabels(), interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)
public data class MonarchMyStatusCustomStatus(text: String? = null, emoji: String? = null, until: Long? = null)
public class MonarchMyStatusLabels(hint: String? = null, setStatus: String? = null, presence: ((MonarchPresenceStatus) -> String)? = null)

options.name: name
options.description: The person's display name, already localised. Also the avatar's initials.

options.name: presence
options.description: Online, away, busy, do not disturb or offline. Drawn as the avatar's presence dot and read in words.

options.name: onClick
options.description: Opens the status settings, usually a MonarchBottomSheet the app shows.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the row.

options.name: image
options.description: The avatar picture, loaded by the app; null shows the initials.

options.name: customStatus
options.description: The person's own message and emoji, with an optional until time in epoch milliseconds after which it is hidden.

options.name: now
options.description: The time until is compared with, in epoch milliseconds. Without it the row reads the clock and redraws itself when the status ends; pass it for a fixed rendering.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the row can be pressed.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the click action, the "Set a status" invitation and the presence names.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The interaction source of the row.

states.name: custom status
states.description: The emoji and message under the name, in the muted text color.

states.name: presence only
states.description: Without a status, away, busy and do not disturb are written under the name.

states.name: no status
states.description: Online or offline without a status shows "Set a status" in the subtle text color.

states.name: expired
states.description: A status whose until has passed is hidden, at that moment, without the app doing anything.

states.name: pressed
states.description: The Material 3 ripple.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The row cannot be pressed and TalkBack reads it as disabled.

appearance: A small avatar with its presence dot, the name in the strong body style and a caption line under it in the muted text color (subtle for the invitation), on no background; pressing shows the ripple. All colors are theme roles, so dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: Same parameters as iOS, with the Android conventions: the picture is a Painter the app loads, until and now are epoch milliseconds, and the action is onClick. The web renders a link with href or a button; on Android the row is always a button and the app navigates or opens a sheet in onClick. The web reads "Your status and settings" before the name; on Android that is the click action label, read by TalkBack as "Double tap to open your status and settings". iOS redraws with a TimelineView; Android waits with a LaunchedEffect until the status ends.
accessibility: The row is one TalkBack button named by the person's name.
Its state description is the presence and the status line, such as "Online, 🌴 On holiday", or just the presence when the line is the presence.
Its click action label is "open your status and settings".
The presence is always in words, so it never depends on the dot's color; the avatar is decorative.
The row is at least 48dp high and its text wraps at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: A status made of spaces is treated as no status.
An emoji without a message shows the emoji alone.
An until in the past hides the status at once.

title: NoAppAccess
wrapsNative: MonarchErrorState (kind Forbidden) with MonarchButton and MonarchWorkspaceSwitcher in its actions, a MonarchText polite live region (androidx.compose.ui.semantics.liveRegion) and MonarchInlineNotice
summary: A recipe, not a component: the screen a workspace member sees when they have no access to the app they opened, with who can fix it, Request access, Back to workspace and Switch workspace.
whenToUse: In place of an app's content when the signed-in person belongs to the workspace but has no grant for this app.
whenNotToUse: When the person is not signed in, show the sign-in screen. When the content does not exist, use the error-page recipe with NotFound. When a single record is off limits inside an app the person can use, use MonarchErrorState with Forbidden and no request.
api: MonarchErrorState(title = "You don’t have access to $app", kind = MonarchErrorStateKind.Forbidden, size = MonarchEmptyStateSize.Lg, message = "Ask an admin of $workspace to give you access to $app.", actions = { … })
MonarchButton(text = if (sent) "Access requested" else "Request access", onClick = …, variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Primary, enabled = !sent, loading = pending)
MonarchWorkspaceSwitcher(workspaces = …, selection = workspace, onSelectionChange = { … }) // @ExperimentalMonarchApi, opted in at the call
MonarchText(text = sentMessage, modifier = Modifier.semantics { liveRegion = LiveRegionMode.Polite })
MonarchInlineNotice(message = "The request didn’t go through. Try again.", tone = MonarchTone.Danger)

options.name: appName
options.description: The app the person cannot open, named in the title and the message.

options.name: workspaceName
options.description: The current workspace, named in the message: "Ask an admin of Acme…"; without it, "Ask a workspace admin…".

options.name: request
options.description: The access request: the button shows progress while pending and "Access requested", disabled, once sent; an open request from the server starts as sent.

options.name: onRequestAccess
options.description: Sends the request; without it there is no Request access button.

options.name: contactAdmin
options.description: A ghost MonarchButton "Contact an admin" that opens a mail intent or the list of admins.

options.name: switchWorkspace
options.description: MonarchWorkspaceSwitcher in the actions, or a ghost button that opens the app's workspace list.

states.name: idle
states.description: The title, the message, Request access (primary), Back to workspace and the workspace switcher.

states.name: pending
states.description: Request access shows the MonarchButton loading state.

states.name: sent
states.description: The button reads "Access requested" and is disabled; "Request sent. You can open Rook Tickets once an admin approves it." is announced.

states.name: error
states.description: A danger MonarchInlineNotice under the actions; Request access can be tapped again.

appearance: MonarchErrorState at the large size: the title, the muted message and the actions centered, on the screen's canvas; the app may pass a lock icon in its icon slot. The status line uses the muted text role and the error the danger notice. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web's NoAppAccess is a component built on ErrorPage (forbidden). On Android it is a recipe, as on iOS: MonarchErrorState with the Forbidden kind and the actions as MonarchButtons, because the state machine is a few lines and the app owns navigation. The web's links (homeHref, contactHref, switchWorkspaceHref, linkAs) are callbacks: components do not navigate. The web's focusOnMount and heading level are TalkBack's job on Android: MonarchErrorState's title is a heading. Monarch bundles no lock glyph; pass one in MonarchErrorState's icon slot.
accessibility: MonarchErrorState's title is a TalkBack heading and the message is read after it.
Request access is read as loading while pending and as disabled once sent.
The status line is an always-present polite live region, so "Request sent…" is announced without moving focus.
The failure is a danger MonarchInlineNotice with its tone in words.
Every action has a 48dp target and the actions wrap at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: The access check stays on the server; the screen only explains it.
If a request is already open, start in the sent state so the person does not request twice.
When the person has access in no app of the workspace, offer only Switch workspace.
After a workspace switch, check access again: the screen may no longer apply.

    },
)

        MonarchButton(text = "Request access", onClick = {}, variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Primary)
        MonarchButton(text = "Back to workspace", onClick = {})
        MonarchButton(text = "Switch workspace", onClick = {}, variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Ghost)
        MonarchLink(text = "Contact an admin", onClick = {}, variant = MonarchLinkVariant.Standalone)
    },
)

name: MonarchNotificationCenter
title: NotificationCenter
wrapsNative: MonarchTabs with androidx.compose.material3.Tab, androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn; MonarchInboxRow (MonarchListRow, SwipeToDismissBox), MonarchLoadMore, MonarchLoadingState, MonarchErrorState, MonarchEmptyState
summary: The in-app list of notifications: a heading with Mark all as read, All and Unread tabs, rows grouped under Today, Yesterday and dates, paging, and loading, error and empty states.
whenToUse: As the content of a MonarchBottomSheet or a screen opened from MonarchNotificationsBell, for the notifications the app keeps for each person.
whenNotToUse: For system notifications in the status bar, post them with NotificationManagerCompat; Monarch does not cover them. For a conversation list, use MonarchInboxRow in a LazyColumn. For a one-off message, use MonarchSnackbarHost or MonarchBanner.

class MonarchNotificationCenterItem(id: String, title: String, time: Long, message: String? = null, read: Boolean = false, actorName: String? = null, actorImage: Painter? = null, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, iconLabel: String? = null)
enum class MonarchNotificationCenterFilter { All, Unread }

class MonarchNotificationCenterLabels(title: String? = null, all: String? = null, unread: String? = null, unreadTab: ((Int) -> String)? = null, markAllRead: String? = null, markRead: String? = null, unreadItem: String? = null, today: String? = null, yesterday: String? = null, emptyTitle: String? = null, emptyMessage: String? = null, emptyUnreadTitle: String? = null, loading: String? = null, loadMore: MonarchLoadMoreLabels = MonarchLoadMoreLabels())

options.name: items
options.description: The loaded notifications, newest first.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the column. Give it a bounded height; the list scrolls.

options.name: unreadCount
options.description: The unread total from the server, which may exceed the loaded items. The unread loaded items by default.

options.name: initialFilter
options.description: The tab shown first. The component keeps the selection across configuration changes.

options.name: now
options.description: Fixes now for the compact ages and the day headings. Without it they read the clock.

options.name: loading

options.name: loadingMore

options.name: groupByDay

options.name: markReadOnSelect

options.description: Receives the tab, for apps that fetch each tab from the server.

states.name: unread item
states.description: An accent dot before a semibold title and a stronger age, from MonarchInboxRow; TalkBack reads Unread.

states.name: read item
states.description: Regular title and muted age.

states.name: unread tab
states.description: Only unread items; the tab shows the unread count in an info badge, 99+ above 99.

states.name: loading
states.description: Three placeholder rows, read as Loading notifications.

states.name: error
states.description: MonarchErrorState with the message and Try again.

states.name: empty
states.description: MonarchEmptyState: You're all caught up, or No unread notifications in the Unread tab.

states.name: loading more
states.description: MonarchLoadMore at the end of the list in its loading or failed state.

states.name: nothing unread
states.description: Mark all as read is disabled.

appearance: The heading is default text in the heading style; day headings are muted captions. The tabs are the Material 3 primary tab row in the Monarch theme, and the unread count is an info badge. Rows are MonarchInboxRow on the surface color, with the accent unread dot. The same roles adapt to dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web component is a bell that opens a popover. On Android the bell is MonarchNotificationsBell and the list is this component, placed by the app in a MonarchBottomSheet or a screen, because a popover from a bell is a sheet on a phone; iOS presents it in a sheet with its own navigation bar and a Done button, which Android does not need since sheets and screens close with the system back gesture. Marking one item read is a swipe toward the end, also a TalkBack action, instead of a per-row button. Rows reuse MonarchInboxRow, so titles and messages are cut to one line each and ages are compact (5m, 3h). Items have no href: onSelect navigates. A custom empty state and a custom trigger are not offered. The unread count uses the accent tone, as on the web. The tab parameter is initialFilter, because the component keeps the selection (iOS names it filter); groupByDay and markReadOnSelect follow the Android naming of MonarchActivityTimeline. Without now, day headings are computed when the list composes and do not change at midnight while it stays open. Experimental: a domain pattern until a Rook app adopts it.
accessibility: The tabs are Material 3 Tabs; the Unread tab is read as Unread, with the unread total.
The heading has the heading role, and so do the day headings.
Each item is one MonarchInboxRow element read as the title, Unread when unread, the full date and time, and the message.
The unread dot is not read; the state is spoken, and shown by a semibold title as well as the color.
Mark as read is a TalkBack custom action on unread items as well as a swipe.
The loading placeholder is one element named Loading notifications.
Rows, tabs, Mark all as read and Load more have touch targets of at least 48dp and grow at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: A server unread count of 120 shows 99+ but TalkBack reads 120.
A negative unreadCount is treated as zero.
An item marked read while the Unread tab is shown leaves the tab, because the tab filters the items the app passes.
Items that are not newest first start a new day heading each time the day changes.
With hasMore but no onLoadMore, no load-more row is shown.

name: MonarchNotificationsBell
title: NotificationsBell
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.IconButton, androidx.compose.material3.BadgedBox, androidx.compose.material3.Badge
summary: The entry to the notifications: a bell with the unread count, as a Material 3 IconButton with a BadgedBox, or as a labelled row.
whenToUse: In a top app bar (Icon) or a navigation drawer or menu (Row), to open the app's notifications and show how many are unread.
whenNotToUse: For a count on a bottom navigation destination use the badge parameter of NavigationBarItem. For the list of notifications itself use the app's own screen or ModalBottomSheet.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchNotificationsBell(onClick: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, unreadCount: Int = 0, variant: MonarchNotificationsBellVariant = MonarchNotificationsBellVariant.Icon, enabled: Boolean = true, title: String? = null, unreadLabel: String? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null, icon: @Composable () -> Unit)
public enum class MonarchNotificationsBellVariant { Icon, Row }

options.name: onClick
options.description: Opens the notifications: show a ModalBottomSheet or navigate to a screen.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the component.

options.name: unreadCount
options.description: The number of unread notifications. Zero or less shows no badge. Above 99 the badge reads "99+".

options.name: variant
options.description: Icon: a 48dp icon button with the count on the bell. Row: a row with the bell, the title and the count at the end.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the person can open the notifications.

options.name: title
options.description: Replaces the built-in name "Notifications", which is also the visible title of a row.

options.name: unreadLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in state "3 unread". Pass the whole phrase for the current count.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The interaction source of the button or the row.

options.name: icon
options.description: The bell. Monarch bundles no icons; pass a MonarchIcon with a null content description. It is hidden from TalkBack.

states.name: unread
states.description: A badge with the count in the solid danger color, on the bell (Icon) or at the end of the row (Row).

states.name: none unread
states.description: No badge and no state description.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The bell and the title use the disabled text color; announced as disabled.

appearance: The bell and the row title use the default text color; the badge is the Material 3 Badge filled with the solid danger color and its on-solid text, in every theme. High-contrast themes change only the roles.
platformNotes: On the web the bell owns the NotificationCenter panel and passes its props through (items, filters, mark as read, load more, a See all link). On Android, as on iOS, this component is only the trigger with the count: the app presents its notifications from onClick, so there is no open state, panel side, closeOnSelect or seeAllHref. The web derives the count from unread items when unreadCount is missing; here the app always passes it. The web's collapsed row (icon only with a tooltip, for a collapsed rail) is the Icon variant. Monarch bundles no icons, so the bell is a required slot here; iOS uses the system bell symbol. The "99+" text is the same on every platform and is not translated.
accessibility: One TalkBack element with the button role, named "Notifications" (or title).
The unread count is the state description ("3 unread", a plural resource), not part of the name. It is the exact count even when the badge shows "99+", and it is absent when nothing is unread.
The bell and the badge are hidden from TalkBack, so the count is read once; an icon description passed by the app is not read.
The touch target is at least 48dp by 48dp in both variants and reserved in the layout.
The row title wraps at font scale 2.0.
The unread state is a badge with a number, not a color change.
edgeCases: A negative count is treated as zero.
Counts above 99 show "99+" in the badge.
A long row title wraps; the badge stays at the end.

name: MonarchNumberInput
title: NumberInput
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedTextField (through MonarchTextField) with KeyboardType.Decimal, and androidx.compose.material3.IconButton for the stepper
summary: A labelled number field that reads and writes numbers in the user's locale, with − and + buttons that step without drift, bounds, helper text and an error state.
whenToUse: For a number the user types or nudges: a quantity, a price, a count of seats.
whenNotToUse: For a value on a continuous range where precision does not matter use the Material 3 Slider. For a code or PIN use MonarchOtpPinInput. For text that only looks numeric, such as a phone number, use MonarchTextField with KeyboardType.Phone.
api: @Composable fun MonarchNumberInput(value: Double?, onValueChange: (Double?) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, label: String? = null, placeholder: String? = null, helperText: String? = null, errorText: String? = null, minimum: Double? = null, maximum: Double? = null, step: Double = 1.0, enabled: Boolean = true, readOnly: Boolean = false, showSteppers: Boolean = true, format: ((Double) -> String)? = null, parse: ((String) -> Double?)? = null, labels: MonarchNumberInputLabels = MonarchNumberInputLabels(), interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)
class MonarchNumberInputLabels(increment: String? = null, decrement: String? = null, invalid: String? = null, range: ((minimum: String?, maximum: String?) -> String)? = null)

options.name: value
options.description: The number, or null while the field is empty.

options.name: onValueChange
options.description: Called with the new number, or null when cleared, on every edit that reads as a number, in range or not, and on a step, so a button tapped right after typing reads it; a number out of range is flagged when the field is left, so validate the bounds before saving. The number is rounded to the digits shown.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the field.

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label.

options.name: placeholder
options.description: Shown while the field is empty and focused.

options.name: helperText
options.description: Guidance below the field.

options.name: errorText
options.description: An error from the app; replaces the field's own messages while present.

options.name: minimum
options.description: The smallest allowed value. Typed values below it are flagged; steps stop at it.

options.name: maximum
options.description: The largest allowed value. Typed values above it are flagged; steps stop at it.

options.name: step
options.description: The amount one press of − or + changes the value, on a grid counted from minimum or 0.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the field and the buttons can be used.

options.name: readOnly
options.description: Selectable but not editable; the buttons are disabled.

options.name: showSteppers
options.description: Shows the − and + buttons and the increase and decrease actions.

options.name: format
options.description: Replaces the locale's number format for display. By default up to three fraction digits, or as many as step has.

options.name: parse
options.description: Replaces the reading of the text. Receives non-blank text; returns null when it is not a number.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for "Increase", "Decrease", "Enter a number." and the range message.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the focus and press interactions of the field.

states.name: empty
states.description: The value is null and the placeholder shows while focused. The first step starts from the minimum, or from 0.

states.name: focused
states.description: The outline takes the focus ring color.

states.name: not a number
states.description: A danger outline and "Enter a number." under the field. The text is kept and the value is not changed.

states.name: out of range
states.description: A danger outline and "Enter a number from 0 to 99." under the field. The text is kept and the value is not changed.

states.name: error
states.description: The app's message in place of the field's own, drawn the same way.

states.name: at a bound
states.description: The button that would pass the bound is disabled, and its action is removed.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The subtle background and the disabled text color; both buttons are disabled.

states.name: read only
states.description: The text can be selected but not changed; both buttons are disabled.

appearance: The field is MonarchTextField: a surface fill with the input border, the focus ring color when focused and the danger strong color in error. The − and + signs use the default text color, or the disabled text color when their button is disabled. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The same behavior as the web: the text is read in the locale's conventions (grouping and decimal separators, the locale's own digits, currency signs and a percent sign around the number, accounting negatives), unreadable or out-of-range text is kept, flagged and never saved, and steps move to the next point on the step grid in decimal arithmetic. iOS uses the system TextField(value:format:), which puts unreadable text back, and the system Stepper. The web's arrow keys, Page Up and Page Down and largeStep have no touch equivalent and are not offered; TalkBack users get Increase and Decrease custom actions on the field instead of a spinbutton role, which Android does not have. The web's formatOptions (Intl.NumberFormat) are replaced by the format and parse lambdas, so percent and currency styles are the app's java.text.NumberFormat; there is no percent mode that divides by 100. The web's sm, md and lg sizes are not offered; the field is the size of MonarchTextField. The buttons do not repeat while held. The keyboard is KeyboardType.Decimal; Compose has no signed number keyboard, so whether a minus key is shown depends on the keyboard app.
accessibility: The field is the Material 3 text field: TalkBack reads the label, the text and the error.
A new message for unreadable or out-of-range text is the field's error, shown with text and a danger outline, not color alone.
The − and + buttons are Material 3 icon buttons named "Decrease" and "Increase", each with a 48dp touch target; the sign itself is hidden from TalkBack.
The field has Increase and Decrease custom actions while a step is possible, so TalkBack users can step without leaving the field.
The decrease button is at the start and the increase button at the end, mirrored in right-to-left layouts.
A disabled or read-only field disables both buttons.
edgeCases: Changing value from outside replaces the text on screen and clears the field's own message.
A typed value with more digits than shown is rounded half up to the digits shown when it is saved.
A step from text that cannot be read starts from the last saved value.
A step of zero or less does not move the value.

title: OAuthConsentScreen
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column with MonarchAvatar (square, for the app), MonarchBadge or MonarchInlineNotice, MonarchCard with the account, MonarchConsequenceList for the permissions, MonarchLink in an androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow, and two MonarchButtons of equal width in a Row
summary: A recipe, not a component: the screen where a person allows or cancels a third-party app's access to their account, showing which app asks, which account would grant access, and what the app could do.
whenToUse: In an identity provider's app, when another app asks for access to the signed-in account (an OAuth or OpenID Connect authorization request).
whenNotToUse: Not for Android's own runtime permissions (camera, location), which the system asks for. To remove access an app already has, use the revoke access flow recipe.
api: MonarchAvatar(image = appLogo, name = appName, shape = MonarchAvatarShape.Square, size = MonarchAvatarSize.Lg, decorative = true)
MonarchBadge(text = "Verified", tone = MonarchTone.Success)
MonarchInlineNotice(message = "Only continue if you know and trust Notes.", title = "This app hasn’t been verified.", tone = MonarchTone.Warning)
MonarchConsequenceList(items = scopes, heading = "Notes will be able to:", kindLabel = { … })
MonarchLink(text = "privacy policy", onClick = …, external = true)
MonarchButton(text = "Cancel", onClick = …, modifier = Modifier.weight(1f), loading = denying)
MonarchButton(text = "Allow", onClick = …, modifier = Modifier.weight(1f), variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Primary, loading = allowing)

options.name: verified
options.description: Whether the identity provider has verified the app: a success badge, else a warning notice.

options.name: scopes
options.description: What the app could do, one line each; sensitive scopes are warnings with a detail line.

options.name: allowing / denying
options.description: Which answer is being sent; that button shows progress and the other is disabled.

states.name: verified
states.description: The app's logo or initial, its name and domain, a success Verified badge, the account card, the permissions, then Cancel and Allow of equal width.

states.name: unverified
states.description: No badge, and a warning notice "This app hasn’t been verified" above the account.

states.name: sensitive permission
states.description: A warning row in the permission list, read as "Sensitive", with a detail line.

states.name: pending
states.description: The pressed button shows its progress indicator and the other is disabled.

appearance: Existing Monarch parts in the theme: a square avatar for the app, the success badge or warning notice, a card on the surface color for the account, the consequence list's kind colors, inline links, and a secondary and a primary button side by side.
platformNotes: The web ships OAuthConsentScreen as one pattern with app, account, scopes and callback props. On Android it is a recipe, as on iOS, because the authorization request, the redirect and the session are the identity provider's own code. The links open the app's policies with the app's own browser handling (for example a Custom Tab), so MonarchLink only calls back. Cancel and Allow share the width so neither looks preferred.
accessibility: The request "Notes wants to access your account" has the heading role.
The app's square avatar is decorative because its name is written next to it.
Each permission is read with its kind, "Allowed" or "Sensitive", so it does not depend on color.
The links say they open in the browser; Cancel and Allow are buttons with 48dp touch targets and read "Loading" while pending.
edgeCases: A long app name or domain wraps under the logo.
With many scopes, put the column in a verticalScroll so the buttons stay reachable.

examples.title: Verified app with a sensitive permission
examples.webExample: Verified app with a sensitive permission

parityExceptions.reason: The web draws the same check for every scope, the sensitive one too, with its note under it, so the third scope is written as the kept kind instead of the warning triangle.
parityExceptions.convention: icon parity: the web check glyph for every scope

parityExceptions.reason: The web puts Use another account at the end of the account row, beside the name and email. At a phone width of 344dp that left the name and the address about 90dp and both broke in the middle of a word, so on Android the button sits under the name, at the end, in the same card.
parityExceptions.convention: no text broken inside a word on a compact window; a row that does not fit wraps its action below (Material adaptive layout)

name: MonarchOnboardingChecklist
title: OnboardingChecklist
wrapsNative: MonarchCard (androidx.compose.material3.Surface) containing MonarchProgress (androidx.compose.material3.LinearProgressIndicator) and MonarchCollapsible (androidx.compose.animation.AnimatedVisibility)
summary: A first-run checklist: steps with a done state and an optional call to action, a progress summary, and collapse and dismiss controls.
whenToUse: To guide people through setting up a product with a short list of steps (three to seven) that the app can mark done from its own data.
whenNotToUse: For a linear form split into pages use MonarchStepper. For a to-do list people tick themselves use MonarchCheckboxRow.
api: @Composable fun MonarchOnboardingChecklist(title: String, steps: List<MonarchOnboardingStep>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, description: String? = null, completeMessage: String? = null, collapsible: Boolean = true, expanded: Boolean? = null, onExpandedChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, onDismiss: (() -> Unit)? = null, expandIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, dismissIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, doneIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchOnboardingChecklistLabels = MonarchOnboardingChecklistLabels(), action: (@Composable (MonarchOnboardingStep) -> Unit)? = null)
class MonarchOnboardingStep(id: String, title: String, description: String? = null, done: Boolean = false)

class MonarchOnboardingChecklistLabels(progress: ((done: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, progressLabel: String? = null, dismiss: String? = null, done: String? = null, notDone: String? = null, current: String? = null, complete: String? = null, expanded: String? = null, collapsed: String? = null)

options.name: title
options.description: The heading, such as "Get started". Read as a heading.

options.name: steps
options.description: The steps in order: id, title, optional description and done. The app decides when each is done.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the card.

options.name: description
options.description: Text under the heading.

options.name: completeMessage
options.description: Replaces "All done. You are set up.", shown when every step is done.

options.name: collapsible
options.description: Makes the progress row a MonarchCollapsible header that shows and hides the steps.

options.name: expanded
options.description: Whether the steps are shown. null lets the checklist keep the state itself (saved across configuration changes), starting expanded. Hoist it to keep the state across launches.

options.name: onExpandedChange
options.description: Called with the new state when the user uses the progress row.

options.name: onDismiss
options.description: Shows a dismiss button that calls this. The app hides the checklist and remembers it.

options.name: expandIcon
options.description: An icon after the progress text, such as a chevron pointing down; it turns half a turn while expanded.

options.name: dismissIcon
options.description: An icon for the dismiss button, such as a close mark. Without it the button shows its label.

options.name: doneIcon
options.description: A check mark drawn in the marker of a done step and before the complete message.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings: progress, progressLabel, dismiss, done, notDone, current, complete, expanded and collapsed.

options.name: action
options.description: The call to action of a step, such as a small MonarchButton. Shown under the step text only while the step is not done.

states.name: in progress
states.description: The bar and "n of m done" show progress; the first open step has the subtle fill and an accent ring around its number.

states.name: step done
states.description: The marker is a filled success circle (with doneIcon when given); the title is muted; the description and action are hidden.

states.name: complete
states.description: Every step is done: a success message (with doneIcon when given) appears above the steps.

states.name: collapsed
states.description: Only the heading, the bar and the progress row are shown; the expand icon turns back.

states.name: empty
states.description: With no steps the progress reads "0 of 0 done" and the checklist is not complete.

appearance: A MonarchCard (surface fill, subtle border). The progress uses MonarchProgress (accent fill on the emphasis track). Open steps have a number in a strong-border ring, the current step an accent-strong ring on the subtle row fill, done steps a success-solid circle with content in the on-solid color. The complete message uses the success subtle fill and success strong text. All are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow the theme.
platformNotes: Kotlin names follow Material 3: done instead of isDone, collapsible instead of isCollapsible, and expanded as a nullable value with onExpandedChange in place of an optional Binding. The action is a nullable trailing lambda instead of a second initialiser. Monarch for Android bundles no icons, so the chevron, close mark and check are slots (expandIcon, dismissIcon, doneIcon); without dismissIcon the dismiss button shows its label as a ghost button, and without doneIcon a done step is a filled circle, which differs from the numbered ring by shape and by its spoken state. The web turns the progress bar to the success tone when complete; MonarchProgress has no tone, so the bar stays accent and the success message shows completion. The web sets a heading level; Android marks the title as a heading without a level. The web places the action beside the step on wide screens; Android places it under the step text. The progress row is MonarchCollapsible, so its spoken name is the progress text rather than "Setup progress"; the bar itself carries "Setup progress" with the progress text as its state.
accessibility: The title is a heading.
The progress bar is named "Setup progress" and its state is "n of m done" instead of a percentage.

With collapsing, the progress row is one button read as "n of m done" with the state "Expanded" or "Collapsed" and the TalkBack expand and collapse actions; hidden steps leave the screen and are not reached.
Without collapsing, the visible progress text is not read again; the progress bar carries it.
Each step is one element read as its title and description, with the state "Done" or "Not done" ("Not done, Current step" for the first open step); the step number and marker are not read.
Each step's action is a separate element after the step.
Done is shown by a filled marker in place of the numbered ring and by the spoken state, not by color alone.
The dismiss button is named "Dismiss checklist" (its visible label, or the spoken name of the icon form) and, like the progress row, has a 48dp touch target.
Markers grow with the font size and text wraps at font scale 2.0; the expand animation follows MonarchCollapsible and is removed when animations are off.
edgeCases: The checklist does not hide itself on dismiss; the app removes it.
Step ids must be unique; they key the rows.
An empty step list is never complete.
Long titles and descriptions wrap; the marker stays at the top of the step.
The complete message is not announced when it appears; it is read in order with the steps.

name: MonarchOrgChart
title: OrgChart
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row and Column tree in horizontalScroll and verticalScroll with a scaling layout modifier, androidx.compose.foundation.gestures.transformable for pinch, Canvas drawing (drawBehind) for connector and dotted lines, detectDragGesturesAfterLongPress for moving, CustomAccessibilityAction; the list layout is androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn; MonarchAvatar, MonarchText, MonarchButton
summary: People as cards under their managers, with teams that open and close, teams loaded on demand, zoom and pan, dotted reporting lines and drag to move; an indented list on a phone or at large font sizes.
whenToUse: To show who reports to whom across an organization, let people explore teams, open a person's details, and let admins move people to a new manager. Large organizations pass childCount and load teams with onLoadChildren.
whenNotToUse: For a hierarchy of things rather than people (folders, departments), use MonarchTreeView. For goals with progress, use MonarchGoalTree. For a flat directory with filters, use a list of rows with a detail screen.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchOrgChart(nodes: List<MonarchOrgChartNode>, expandIcon: @Composable () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, expanded: Set<String>? = null, onExpandedChange: ((Set<String>) -> Unit)? = null, focusId: String? = null, dottedLines: List<MonarchOrgChartDottedLine> = emptyList(), layout: MonarchOrgChartLayout = MonarchOrgChartLayout.Auto, zoomable: Boolean = true, enabled: Boolean = true, labels: MonarchOrgChartLabels = MonarchOrgChartLabels(), onSelect: ((MonarchOrgChartNode) -> Unit)? = null, onLoadChildren: (suspend (MonarchOrgChartNode) -> Unit)? = null, onMoveRequest: ((MonarchOrgChartNode, MonarchOrgChartMoveTarget) -> Unit)? = null)

class MonarchOrgChartNode(id: String, parentId: String? = null, name: String, title: String? = null, meta: String? = null, image: Painter? = null, kind: MonarchOrgChartNodeKind = MonarchOrgChartNodeKind.Person, dashed: Boolean = false, childCount: Int? = null)
enum class MonarchOrgChartNodeKind { Person, Vacancy }
class MonarchOrgChartDottedLine(from: String, to: String)
enum class MonarchOrgChartLayout { Auto, Chart, List }
sealed interface MonarchOrgChartMoveTarget { data class Manager(id: String); data object TopLevel; data object Unspecified }

class MonarchOrgChartLabels(label: String? = null, vacant: String? = null, dashed: String? = null, alsoReportsTo: ((String) -> String)? = null, reports: ((Int) -> String)? = null, expanded: String? = null, collapsed: String? = null, loading: String? = null, expand: ((String) -> String)? = null, collapse: ((String) -> String)? = null, move: String? = null, moveHint: String? = null, loadFailed: ((String) -> String)? = null, zoomIn: String? = null, zoomOut: String? = null, zoomReset: ((String) -> String)? = null)

options.name: nodes
options.description: Every person and open position, flat. Reporting lines come from parentId; a node whose manager is missing or itself is top level; a repeated id keeps its first node; nodes reachable only through a cycle are not drawn.

options.name: expandIcon
options.description: A chevron that points to the end, shown in the team chips; it turns to point down when the team is shown. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the chart. Both layouts scroll themselves, so it needs a bounded height.

options.name: expanded
options.description: The ids of people whose team is shown. null keeps the state inside the chart, starting with the top level, the level under it when there are three or fewer top-level people, and the path to focusId; teams that still need loading start hidden.

options.name: onExpandedChange
options.description: Called with the new set of ids when a team is shown or hidden, or when focusId opens a path.

options.name: focusId
options.description: The person to highlight: the path to them opens, the chart scrolls to them, and their card has a thicker accent border and the selected state.

options.name: dottedLines
options.description: Secondary reporting lines: dashed curves in the chart layout, and "Also reports to …" on the card in both layouts.

options.name: layout
options.description: Chart, List, or Auto: the chart when the component is at least 640dp wide at a font scale of 1.3 or less, the list otherwise.

options.name: zoomable
options.description: Shows the zoom buttons (40% to 160% in steps of 10%) and allows pinching, in the chart layout.

options.name: enabled
options.description: false gives text the disabled role and borders the subtle role; cards, chips and drag do not respond.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Called when a card is tapped, for example to open a detail screen. Without it, cards are not buttons.

options.name: onLoadChildren
options.description: Loads a team whose childCount is larger than the reports in nodes; the app adds the reports to nodes. The team opens when it returns; an exception is announced.

options.name: onMoveRequest
options.description: Turns on moving and shows the move hint. Receives the person and Manager(id) for a drop on a card, TopLevel for a drop on the background, or Unspecified when Move was chosen from the TalkBack actions.

states.name: team shown and hidden
states.description: The chip under a manager shows the number of reports and a chevron that points to the end when the team is hidden and down when it is shown; the team is drawn beneath, joined by lines (chart) or indented (list).

states.name: loading
states.description: While onLoadChildren runs, the chip shows a spinner (none when animations are off) and is disabled, and the state reads "Loading team".

states.name: focused
states.description: The focusId card has a 2dp accent border and the selected state.

states.name: vacancy
states.description: A muted card with a dashed strong border, a plain tile instead of an avatar and the line "Open position". It cannot be moved or take people.

states.name: temporary line
states.description: dashed draws a dashed strong border; read with "Temporary reporting line".

states.name: dragging
states.description: After touch and hold, with a haptic tick, the card follows the finger; the card under it takes the subtle accent fill and strong accent border when the move is allowed.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Text takes the disabled role, borders the subtle role, and nothing responds.

states.name: empty
states.description: With no nodes nothing is drawn inside the scrolling area.

appearance: Cards use the surface fill with a subtle border, the muted fill for open positions, the strong border role for dashed borders, the accent solid role for the focused card and the subtle accent fill with the strong accent border for a drop target. Names are in the body strong style and default text role; titles, meta and notes in the caption style and muted role. Connector lines and chip borders use the default border role; dotted lines the subtle text role. Every color is a theme role, so dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web OrgChart is an ARIA tree with roving focus and arrow keys; on Android each card is one TalkBack element with Show team or Hide team and Move custom actions, and the chip under a manager is also a button, which is the platform's equivalent. The web switches to the list below 40rem of its own width; Android does the same at 640dp and also above a font scale of 1.3, as iOS does at accessibility sizes. The list is a LazyColumn of cards with the chip at the start and an indent that stops after four levels, the phone pattern. The web's renderNode and ReactNode meta are not offered: meta is a line of text, because a card is one element and must not hold controls. The web's toolbar slot is not offered: put export or other buttons beside the chart. Ctrl/Cmd + wheel zoom becomes pinch, and the keyboard M shortcut becomes the Move custom action. Moving uses touch and hold, then drag, inside the chart (not the system drag and drop, so it works in both layouts and is hit-tested against the cards); a refused drop (own team, current manager, an open position) does nothing. The parity map named a custom tree Layout: the tree is laid out with Row and Column and a layout modifier reports the zoomed size to the scroll views; lines are drawn from the measured card positions, so they follow right to left. While a card is dragged it is drawn above its own siblings but can pass under cards of other branches. The zoom buttons show + and − as text with spoken names, because Monarch bundles no icons. expandIcon is required for the same reason, as in MonarchTreeView. Images are a Painter loaded by the app, not a URL. Experimental: a domain pattern until a Rook app adopts it.
accessibility: The chart is a traversal group named "Organization chart" (labels.label).
Each card is one element read as name, title, meta, then "Open position", "Temporary reporting line" and "Also reports to …" when they apply.
A manager's state says "Team shown", "Team hidden" or "Loading team" and the number of direct reports; a person without reports has no state.
Custom actions "Show team of …" or "Hide team of …" and, with onMoveRequest, "Move"; with onSelect the card is a button.
The focused person has the selected state.
Avatars, the vacancy tile, connector lines, dotted lines and the chip's count and chevron are hidden; the chip is a button named "Show team of …" or "Hide team of …" with the team state.

A team that fails to load is announced through a polite live region ("Could not load the team of Jo Park."); the zoom level button is a polite live region named "Reset zoom, 80%", and the zoom buttons have spoken names.
Chips, cards and zoom buttons have 48dp touch targets; card width grows with the font scale in the chart, and names wrap without being cut.
edgeCases: Nodes with a missing manager, or that are their own manager, are top level; nodes in a cycle are not drawn; a repeated id keeps its first node.
Long names and titles wrap inside the card.
The list stops indenting after four levels, so deep teams keep room on a phone.
Both layouts scroll themselves, so the chart needs a height from its parent; in a scrolling screen give it a fixed height.
Scrolling to focusId uses the zoomed position as the scroll views report it; away from 100% zoom the person may not be centered exactly.
Teams opened or closed while another team loads are kept when it finishes.
At zoom levels below 100% the chips are drawn smaller than 48dp; zoom is the user's choice and the list layout keeps full targets.

name: MonarchOtpPinInput
title: OTPPinInput
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.text.BasicTextField (decorationBox draws the cells) with androidx.compose.ui.autofill.ContentType.SmsOtpCode
summary: A one-time code or PIN drawn as one cell per character, over a single text field with the one-time code autofill type.
whenToUse: For a verification code sent by text message or email, a PIN, or a short room or invite code of fixed length.
whenNotToUse: For a password use MonarchPasswordInput. For a number with steps use MonarchNumberInput. For a code of unknown length use MonarchTextField.
api: @Composable fun MonarchOtpPinInput(value: String, onValueChange: (String) -> Unit, label: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, length: Int = 6, helperText: String? = null, errorText: String? = null, mode: MonarchOtpPinInputMode = MonarchOtpPinInputMode.Numeric, size: MonarchOtpPinInputSize = MonarchOtpPinInputSize.Md, enabled: Boolean = true, masked: Boolean = false, groupSize: Int? = null, lengthHint: String? = null, onComplete: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)
enum class MonarchOtpPinInputMode { Numeric, Alphanumeric }
enum class MonarchOtpPinInputSize { Md, Lg }

options.name: value
options.description: The code. Only cleaned text reaches onValueChange: digits, or digits and A to Z in upper case, never longer than length.

options.name: onValueChange
options.description: Called with the cleaned code on every change.

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label, already localised.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the field.

options.name: length
options.description: The number of characters. Values under 1 count as 1.

options.name: helperText
options.description: Guidance under the cells.

options.name: errorText
options.description: The error message; replaces the helper text and gives every cell the danger border.

options.name: mode
options.description: Numeric accepts digits with the number keyboard; Alphanumeric accepts A to Z, upper-cased, and digits.

options.name: size
options.description: Md cells are up to 48dp wide and 48dp high; Lg cells up to 64dp with larger characters.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the field can be focused and edited.

options.name: masked
options.description: Shows dots instead of the characters, uses the password transformation and a password keyboard.

options.name: groupSize
options.description: Draws a wider gap after every this many cells. Visual only.

options.name: lengthHint
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken state "Code length: 6".

options.name: onComplete
options.description: Called each time the code reaches length characters, typed, pasted or filled.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the focus interactions of the field.

states.name: empty
states.description: Empty cells with the input border.

states.name: focused
states.description: The cell that takes the next character has a 2dp border in the focus ring color and, while empty, a caret.

states.name: filled
states.description: Each character is drawn in its cell, or as a dot when masked; a filled cell has the subtle text color as its border.

states.name: error
states.description: Every cell has the danger strong border and the message under the cells is in the danger strong color.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Cells use the subtle background, the default border and the disabled text color.

appearance: Cells are the surface color with the input border and medium corners; the active cell's border is the focus ring color, filled cells use the subtle text color for the border, errors the danger strong color. Characters use the default text color with the subheading style (heading at Lg). The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The same single-field design as the web and iOS: one input under drawn cells, so paste, the keyboard and TalkBack treat it as one field. Android uses the Compose SmsOtpCode autofill content type in place of autocomplete="one-time-code". The caret does not blink. Cell sizes are 48dp (Md) and 64dp (Lg) high, taller than the web's 40 and 48 pixels, so the field is a 48dp touch target. The web's hover state and readOnly are not offered. The length is spoken as the field's state description, because Compose has no hint property; iOS speaks it as a hint. Characters typed in other scripts' digits are read as 0 to 9.
accessibility: One TalkBack element, the real text field: the label, the code, the state "Code length: 6", and the error when there is one.
With masked the field is a password field, so the code is not read out.
The error is text under the cells as well as a danger border, not color alone.
The field is at least 48dp high; tapping any cell focuses it.
The cells keep left-to-right order in right-to-left layouts, because a code is read left to right.
Characters and the label scale with the font size setting; cells shrink in width to fit the available width.
edgeCases: Pasting a longer text keeps the first length accepted characters.
A value with characters that are not accepted is shown cleaned.
The cursor always stays at the end of the code; editing in the middle is not possible.
The masked state should not change while the field is shown: Compose keeps the password flag of a text field from its first composition.
