title: OverflowTabs
wrapsNative: MonarchTabs with androidx.compose.material3.Tab
summary: A tab strip with more tabs than fit is the MonarchTabs: the tabs that do not fit scroll sideways, and the selected tab is brought into view. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: For five or more sections of one screen, or tabs whose labels are long or translated, where a fixed MonarchTabs would squeeze them.
whenNotToUse: For two to four short sections, use MonarchTabs, which fills the width (see tabs). For top-level destinations, use the navigation bar or rail (see app-shell). For a long list of views, use a dropdown menu.
api: @Composable fun MonarchTabs(selectedIndex: Int, onSelectedIndexChange: (Int) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, panel: (@Composable (selectedIndex: Int) -> Unit)? = null, tabs: MonarchTabsScope.() -> Unit)

interface MonarchTabsScope { fun tab(text: String, enabled: Boolean = true, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, count: String? = null, countTone: MonarchTone = MonarchTone.Neutral, contentDescription: String? = null) }

states.name: fits
states.description: All tabs are visible, packed from the start with the edge padding.

states.name: overflowing
states.description: The row scrolls sideways; the tabs at the end are reached by swiping.

states.name: selected out of view
states.description: Selecting a tab, or setting selectedTabIndex from code, scrolls it into view.

appearance: The tab row uses the colors Monarch maps to the Material scheme: the canvas surface, the accent color for the selected tab's text and indicator, the muted text color for the others and a subtle divider. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web OverflowTabs measures the strip and moves the last tabs into a More menu as the width shrinks. On Android the scrolling tab row is the platform pattern: every tab stays one swipe away and nothing is measured. When the extra tabs should sit in a menu instead, compose a MonarchTabs of the first tabs with a last Tab that opens a MonarchMenu. The web's TabsContent panels are the app's own content switched on the selected index. iOS documents a recipe on MonarchTabs, which also scrolls.
accessibility: System behavior: each Tab has the tab role and its selected state; TalkBack reads "Tab, 3 of 8" with the row as a collection.
Each tab has a touch target of at least 48dp.
Tabs scrolled out of view are still reached by TalkBack, which scrolls the row as it moves.
The selected tab is marked by the indicator and its color, and by the selected state for TalkBack.
edgeCases: Labels do not wrap: a very long label makes a wide tab; keep them to one or two words.
At large font sizes fewer tabs fit and more scroll.

whenToUse: At the top of every screen. Use LargeTopAppBar for the top screen of a section, collapsing into the small bar as the person scrolls, and TopAppBar for detail screens.
whenNotToUse: Do not put status badges, key facts or a banner in the bar itself; put them in the content under it. For a record's header with navigation between records, see the record-header recipe.

states.description: LargeTopAppBar shows the title large under the actions.

states.name: collapsed
states.description: As the content scrolls, the bar collapses to the small title, connected through the scroll behavior's nestedScroll.

states.name: overflow open
states.description: The More button opens a MonarchMenu with the secondary actions.

appearance: The bar uses the canvas colors Monarch maps to the Material scheme: the surface behind the title, the default text color for the title and icons, and the scrolled container color when content passes under it. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web PageHeader draws the title, eyebrow, breadcrumbs, back link, status, details, tabs, a banner and an action row that overflows into a More menu below 640 pixels. On Android the top app bar owns the title, the back button and two or three actions, and the rest go in an overflow MonarchMenu chosen by the app. Breadcrumbs and the eyebrow are not used on phones: the back button and the navigation hierarchy replace them (use MonarchBreadcrumb only for deep hierarchies). Status, details, a banner and tabs are the first rows of the content. The web's sticky option is the default: the bar stays and collapses. iOS uses the navigation bar the same way.
accessibility: System behavior: the title is a heading for TalkBack, and the bar's icon buttons have 48dp touch targets.
Every icon-only action needs a contentDescription, such as "Add contact" and "More actions".
The back button is named "Back" and its arrow mirrors in right-to-left layouts (an autoMirror vector).
The status under the bar is said in text ("Active"), not by its color alone.
edgeCases: A long title is cut with an ellipsis in the small bar; LargeTopAppBar wraps it to two lines when expanded.
Keep at most three action icons; the rest belong in the overflow menu.
Connect the scroll behavior with Modifier.nestedScroll(scrollBehavior.nestedScrollConnection) on the Scaffold, or the bar does not collapse.

title: PageOutline
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn of clickable rows with androidx.compose.material3.Text; scrolls itself with LazyListState.animateScrollToItem
summary: A document's headings as a nested list, with the section being read marked as current; picking a heading lets the app scroll to it.
whenToUse: Beside or over a long document, note or help article, usually in a MonarchBottomSheet on phones and in a side pane on tablets, so people can see its structure and jump to a section.
whenNotToUse: For moving between screens, use the app's navigation. For a hierarchy people expand and select, use MonarchTreeView.

class MonarchPageOutlineStats(words: Int, minutes: Int) { companion object { const val WORDS_PER_MINUTE: Int = 220; fun fromText(text: String): MonarchPageOutlineStats } }
class MonarchPageOutlineLabels(title: String? = null, empty: String? = null, stats: ((MonarchPageOutlineStats) -> String)? = null, current: String? = null)

options.name: headings
options.description: The headings in document order, each with its text, level 1 through 6 and the id used to scroll to it.

options.name: onNavigate
options.description: Called when a heading is picked. Scroll the document here, for example with LazyListState.animateScrollToItem, and close the sheet.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the outline. Give it a bounded height: it scrolls on its own.

options.name: currentId
options.description: The id of the heading of the section being read. The app works it out from the document's scroll position.

options.name: maxLevel
options.description: The deepest heading level listed.

options.name: stats
options.description: The word count and reading time shown under the list, such as "1,234 words · 6 min read". MonarchPageOutlineStats.fromText counts them.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether headings can be picked.

options.name: showTitle
options.description: Shows the "On this page" title. Hide it when the sheet's title already says it; the outline keeps it as its spoken name.

options.name: state
options.description: The scroll state of the outline's own list.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the title, the empty message, the stats line and the spoken "Current section".

states.name: current
states.description: The current heading is in the accent strong color and the strong body style, with an accent bar at its start.

states.name: other headings
states.description: Muted text with a subtle bar, indented one step per nesting level.

states.name: empty
states.description: "Headings you add appear here." in muted text.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Headings use the disabled text color and cannot be picked.

appearance: No container of its own: the title in the label style, headings in the body style with a 2dp bar at their start, the current one in the accent strong color with an accent strong bar, the others muted with a subtle border-coloured bar. All are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web outline reads headings from a Tiptap editor or the page and follows the scroll position with an IntersectionObserver. On Android the app passes the headings and the current id, because only the app knows its document and its LazyListState, and scrolls to a heading in onNavigate; this is the same split as iOS. There is no rich text editor on Android yet, so the editor mode and its caret tracking are not offered; MonarchPageOutlineStats.fromText replaces the editor's word count. The outline is a LazyColumn, as the plan says, so it needs a bounded height (a sheet or a pane) and cannot sit inside another vertical scroll; it scrolls itself to keep the current heading in view, which the web does not need. Headings are rows, not links: Android has no link role. The iOS isTitleHidden is showTitle here, following the Android naming of booleans.
accessibility: The outline is a traversal group named by its title ("On this page"); the visible title is a heading.
Each heading is one clickable element with a 48dp minimum height.
The current heading is selected and has the state "Current section", and is shown with a stronger weight and a bar as well as color.
Indentation uses start padding, so nesting mirrors right to left.
Long headings wrap at the largest font size; nothing is truncated.
Scrolling to the current heading is immediate when animations are turned off.
edgeCases: Skipped levels (a level 3 under a level 1) add one step of indent, not two.
Blank headings and headings deeper than maxLevel are left out.
Levels outside 1 through 6 are clamped.
Heading ids are list keys, so they must be unique.
fromText counts at least one minute, even for an empty text.

    onNavigate = { heading -> current = heading.id },
    currentId = current,
    labels = MonarchPageOutlineLabels(title = {{title}}),
)

    MonarchPageOutlineHeading({{headings.4.text}}, {{headings.4.level}}, {{headings.4.id}}),
)

    MonarchPageOutlineHeading("Accounts", 3, "accounts"),
    MonarchPageOutlineHeading("Permissions", 3, "permissions"),
    MonarchPageOutlineHeading("Billing", 2, "billing"),

name: MonarchPageTree
title: PageTree

summary: The pages of a multi-page document in named groups, with running page numbers; read only it is navigation, with editing handlers it organises pages and groups.
whenToUse: In the side pane or a sheet of a multi-page document, handbook or course, to move between its pages and, for editors, to reorder, add, rename and delete pages and groups.
whenNotToUse: For a folder hierarchy of any depth, use MonarchTreeView. For the headings inside one page, use the page outline. For app navigation, use the navigation bar or rail.

enum class MonarchPageTreeMoveKind { Page, Group }

class MonarchPageTreeLabels(label, untitled, number, noPages, addPage, addPageText, addFirstPage, addGroup, groupActions, pageActions, more, renameGroup, moveGroupUp, moveGroupDown, deleteGroup, moveTo, deletePage, addGroupTitle, groupName, newGroupName, renameSubmit, cancel, deleteGroupTitle, deleteGroupConsequence, typeToConfirm, deletePageTitle, cannotUndo, groupMoved, pageMovedTo, reorderableList), every parameter optional

options.name: groups
options.description: The groups and their pages, in order.

options.name: selected
options.description: The id of the open page: the selected row, with the accent fill and bar.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Called with a page's id when it is chosen. The app navigates.

options.name: numbered
options.description: Shows page numbers (01, 02, …) running across groups, in the locale's digits.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether pages can be chosen and edited. Disabled uses the disabled text role.

options.name: scrollState
options.description: The scroll state of the tree, which scrolls itself.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including the drag reorder strings.

options.name: onReorder
options.description: Makes the order editable: drag and the handle's actions within a group, "Move to" another group from a page's menu, Move group up and down from a group's menu. Receives the new groups and what moved.

options.name: onAddPage
options.description: Shows an add button on each group heading and "Add first page" under an empty group. Receives the group id; the app adds the page.

options.name: onAddGroup
options.description: Shows "Add group" at the end, which asks for a name in an alert dialog. Receives the trimmed name.

options.name: onRenameGroup
options.description: Shows "Rename group" in the group menu, which asks for the new name. Called only when the name changed.

options.name: onDeleteGroup
options.description: Shows "Delete group" while there is more than one group, behind a confirmation that asks for the group's name when it has pages.

options.name: onDeletePage
options.description: Shows "Delete page" in the page menu while there is more than one page, behind a confirmation.

options.name: addIcon
options.description: The icon of the heading add buttons, such as a plus MonarchIcon; without it they show "Add page". Their TalkBack name is "Add page to <group>" either way.

options.name: menuIcon
options.description: The icon of the menu buttons, such as a more MonarchIcon; without it they show "More". Their TalkBack name is "Actions for <name>" either way.

states.name: navigation
states.description: Without handlers: the groups as headings and the pages as rows; the open page is the selected row.

states.name: editing
states.description: With onReorder, each group's pages are a MonarchReorderableList with a drag handle per row, and the headings show the page count and a menu.

states.name: empty group
states.description: "No pages yet." in the subtle role under the heading, or "Add first page" with onAddPage.

states.name: dialog
states.description: An alert dialog asks for a name (rename, add) or confirms a delete; the confirm button stays disabled until the input is valid.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With enabled = false: the disabled text roles, and nothing can be chosen or edited.

appearance: Headings are label text in the muted role, numbers code text in the subtle role. The open page has the subtle accent fill with the small radius, a solid accent bar at its start and its title in the strong accent role. In editing, pages are MonarchReorderableList rows on the surface role with a subtle border. Danger menu items use the strong danger role. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web PageTree is a nav with links, a collapse toggle and a footer slot; on Android the selection callback replaces the links (the app navigates), the collapse toggle is left to the app's pane (a list-detail scaffold hides it), and content after the tree replaces the footer. Page and group menus are buttons with Material 3 DropdownMenus, as on the web; iOS uses context menus and swipe actions instead. Monarch bundles no icons, so the add and menu buttons show text unless the app passes addIcon and menuIcon. The web's prompt and confirm dialogs are Material 3 AlertDialogs with MonarchTextField and MonarchTypeToConfirmInput. Pages reorder within a group by drag or the handle's TalkBack actions through MonarchReorderableList, and move between groups only through "Move to", as on the web and iOS. The tree scrolls itself (a verticalScroll column), so it needs a bounded height and cannot sit inside another vertical scroll; each group's reorderable list is bounded so it can sit inside the tree. The parity map named a tree with drag reorder; a two-level grouping reads better as headings and rows, as on iOS. Selection is selected and onSelect, where iOS takes a Binding.
accessibility: The tree is a traversal group named "Pages"; group labels are headings.
Each page is one selectable element read by its title, with the selected state for the open page; page numbers and group counts are not read.
Add and menu buttons are named "Add page to <group>" and "Actions for <name>", whether they show an icon or text.
In editing, each page has a drag handle with Move up and Move down actions for TalkBack and Switch Access, from MonarchReorderableList, which also announces each move.
Moving a page to another group or moving a group is announced through a polite live region ("Welcome moved to Guides.").
Rows and buttons have 48dp touch targets; titles wrap at the largest font scale.
The open page is marked by the accent bar and the selected state as well as by color.
edgeCases: A blank title shows "Untitled page".
The last page of the document and the only group cannot be deleted: their delete items are not offered.
Deleting a group with pages needs its name typed; an empty group is deleted after a plain confirmation.
Renaming to the same name or to blank text keeps the confirm button disabled.
"Move to" adds the page at the end of the other group.

title: Pagination
wrapsNative: MonarchButton and MonarchText in a Row; no Material component exists for numbered pages
summary: Numbered pages with previous and next, and a compact range such as 81-100 of 143, composed from MonarchButton and MonarchText. For feeds that scroll, MonarchLoadMore is the alternative.
whenToUse: For any list that comes from a paged API where people jump between pages: invoices, members, search results. Show the numbered pages with the current one marked; use the compact range for a narrow toolbar.
whenNotToUse: For a feed that people scroll through, load the next page at the end of the list with MonarchLoadMore instead. For a short list that fits in one response, show it all.

options.name: MonarchLoadMore.loading

options.name: MonarchLoadMore.loadedCount / totalCount

states.name: more to load
states.description: "Showing 20 of 60" and a Load more button, or automatic loading with autoLoad.

states.name: loading
states.description: The button shows its progress; the list stays where it is.

states.name: failed
states.description: "Couldn't load more" with Retry; loaded items stay.

states.name: end
states.description: "That's everything" once every page is loaded.

appearance: The rows are the app's own (MonarchListRow or Monarch recipe rows); the footer is MonarchLoadMore with its secondary button and muted count, in every theme including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Matches the web Pagination: previous and next chevrons, page buttons with the current page selected, ellipses between ranges, and the compact range with previous and next. The recipe is built from MonarchButton (ghost, small) and MonarchText; the app asks the server for the chosen page. iOS uses the same recipe. MonarchLoadMore remains available for endless lists.
accessibility: MonarchLoadMore's button is a standard button with a 48dp target; the count is read before it.
New rows, failures and the end of the list are announced by MonarchLoadMore through a polite live region.
Focus stays on the list; keyed rows keep their position when a page is added.
edgeCases: Give the LazyColumn a bounded height when it sits inside another vertical scroll.
With autoLoad, a short first page that does not fill the screen loads the next page at once.
Keep loaded rows on failure; Retry repeats the same page.

states.name: busy row
states.description: While a rename or removal runs, the row's Remove shows its progress indicator and the other row actions are disabled.

states.name: unsupported
states.description: Add is disabled and a warning notice says the device cannot create passkeys.

appearance: A MonarchCard with the section header and a small primary Add a passkey button, rows separated by subtle dividers, names in the strong body style, the detail and times in the caption style in the muted color, an info Synced badge, and small ghost Rename and secondary Remove buttons. All are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: Monarch does not create passkeys: the app runs androidx.credentials CredentialManager.createCredential inside onAdd, because the relying party and the server challenge are the app's, and androidx.credentials is not a Monarch dependency. Because a cancelled system sheet is an exception of that library (CreateCredentialCancellationException), onAdd returns false for a cancellation instead of throwing, where iOS recognises the system's cancellation error. The web detects support from window.PublicKeyCredential; on Android the app passes supported. The web renames in place; Android asks for the name in a Material 3 AlertDialog with a MonarchTextField (the prompt dialog) whose Save is disabled while the name is blank or unchanged, as on iOS. The removal confirmation is an AlertDialog that closes when confirmed, so the pending state moves to the row and a failure appears as a notice in the card. The parity map names a LazyColumn; the rows are a plain Column inside the card because the list sits inside a scrolling settings screen. The web's headingLevel and locale props have no equivalent (the title is a heading; DateUtils uses the device's locale).
accessibility: The title is a heading, from MonarchSectionHeader; the list is a traversal group named "Your passkeys".
Each passkey is one element whose content description is its name and whose state is Synced, the detail and the times, built by a tested pure function.
The passkey icon is decorative and hidden.
Rename and Remove are separate MonarchButtons with 48dp touch targets, named "Rename Pixel" and "Remove Pixel".
Rename and the removal confirmation are Material 3 alert dialogs; the removal confirm button is the danger variant.
Adding, renaming, removing, cancelling and every failure are announced through a polite live region.
The unsupported state is said in words in a warning notice, not only by the disabled button.
edgeCases: The app updates passkeys after onAdd, onRename and onRemove return; the list does not change itself.
A name made only of spaces cannot be saved; the saved name is trimmed.
The last-method warning appears only when lastSignInMethod is true and exactly one passkey is left.
Only one rename or removal runs at a time.

name: MonarchPasswordInput
title: PasswordInput
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedTextField (through MonarchTextField) with androidx.compose.ui.text.input.PasswordVisualTransformation and androidx.compose.ui.autofill.ContentType
summary: A labelled password field with a toggle that shows the password as text, and the autofill content type for a current or a new password.
whenToUse: For a password or another secret the user types: sign-in, sign-up, password reset, confirming an action.
whenNotToUse: For a one-time code use MonarchOtpPinInput. For text that is not secret use MonarchTextField.
api: @Composable fun MonarchPasswordInput(value: String, onValueChange: (String) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, label: String? = null, placeholder: String? = null, helperText: String? = null, errorText: String? = null, purpose: MonarchPasswordInputPurpose = MonarchPasswordInputPurpose.Current, enabled: Boolean = true, revealed: Boolean? = null, onRevealedChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, revealIcon: (@Composable (revealed: Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, keyboardActions: KeyboardActions = KeyboardActions.Default, labels: MonarchPasswordInputLabels = MonarchPasswordInputLabels(), interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)
enum class MonarchPasswordInputPurpose { Current, New }
class MonarchPasswordInputLabels(reveal: String? = null, show: String? = null, hide: String? = null)

options.name: value
options.description: The password.

options.name: onValueChange
options.description: Called with the new text.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the field.

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label; it floats into the outline.

options.name: placeholder
options.description: Shown while the field is empty and focused.

options.name: helperText
options.description: Guidance below the field.

options.name: errorText
options.description: When not null the field is in the error state and this replaces the helper text.

options.name: purpose
options.description: Current sets the Password autofill content type; New sets NewPassword, so the password manager offers to generate and save one.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the field and the toggle can be used.

options.name: revealed
options.description: Whether the password is shown as text. Null lets the field keep the state itself, starting hidden and surviving configuration changes.

options.name: onRevealedChange
options.description: Called with the new state when the toggle is used.

options.name: revealIcon
options.description: Replaces the text of the toggle, for example with an eye icon. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: keyboardActions
options.description: What the IME action does, for example submit the form.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings: reveal ("Show password"), show ("Show"), hide ("Hide").

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the focus and press interactions of the field.

states.name: hidden
states.description: The text is drawn as dots and the toggle reads "Show".

states.name: revealed
states.description: The text is drawn as typed and the toggle reads "Hide".

states.name: focused
states.description: The outline takes the focus ring color, as in MonarchTextField.

states.name: error
states.description: A danger outline and the error message under the field in place of the helper text.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The subtle background and the disabled text color; the toggle is disabled too.

appearance: The field is MonarchTextField: a surface fill with the input border, the focus ring color when focused and the danger strong color in error. The toggle text uses the accent strong color, or the disabled text color when disabled, with the label type style. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web warns while Caps Lock is on; a touch keyboard has no Caps Lock state to read, so the warning is dropped, as on iOS. The web has sm, md and lg sizes; Android has the one size of MonarchTextField. iOS draws an eye symbol on the toggle; Monarch for Android bundles no icons, so the toggle shows the words Show and Hide unless the app passes revealIcon. The web's autocomplete current-password and new-password are the Compose autofill content types Password and NewPassword. iOS swaps a SecureField for a TextField, so VoiceOver reads a revealed password; Compose 1.12 does not update the password flag of an existing text field (CoreTextFieldSemanticsModifierNode.updateNodeSemantics never stores it), so TalkBack keeps treating the field as a password, and recreating the field would move TalkBack focus off the toggle. The reveal state is either hoisted (revealed with onRevealedChange) or kept by the field, as the web's controlled and uncontrolled forms.
accessibility: The field is the Material 3 text field with the password keyboard: TalkBack reads the label and the error and treats the text as a password. Compose 1.12 keeps the password flag of a text field from its first composition, so a field that starts hidden stays a password field for TalkBack after the toggle is used; the drawn text does change.
The toggle has the Checkbox role, the spoken name "Show password" in both states, and is read as on or off; its visible Show or Hide text is hidden from TalkBack so the name does not change.
The toggle reserves a touch target of at least 48dp by 48dp and draws the Monarch focus ring.
A disabled field also disables the toggle, which then ignores taps.
The autofill content type is Password or NewPassword, so password managers fill or generate the password.
The error is a message as well as a danger outline, not color alone.
edgeCases: A long toggle text at font scale 2.0 takes width from the text area of the field; keep the replacement short or use revealIcon.
Passing revealed without onRevealedChange makes the toggle report changes nobody stores, so it does not change.
The keyboard is the password keyboard without suggestions in both states.

title: PasswordResetForm
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column with a when over the steps, MonarchTextField with KeyboardType.Email, MonarchPasswordInput with the New purpose, MonarchPasswordStrengthMeter, MonarchButton and MonarchInlineNotice; an Android App Link (an intent filter with android:autoVerify) returns the link to the app
summary: A recipe, not a component: request a reset link by email, then, when the emailed link opens the app, choose a new password with a live strength meter.
whenToUse: For a 'Forgot password' flow in an app that signs people in with its own email and password.
whenNotToUse: When people sign in with Rook ID (MonarchSignInWithRookButton), Google or passkeys, the provider owns password reset; link to it instead. For changing a password while signed in, ask for the current password with MonarchPasswordInput instead of a link.
api: MonarchTextField(value = email, onValueChange = …, label = "Email", errorText = emailError, keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(keyboardType = KeyboardType.Email))
MonarchPasswordInput(value = password, onValueChange = …, label = "New password", purpose = MonarchPasswordInputPurpose.New)
MonarchPasswordStrengthMeter(password = password)
MonarchButton(text = "Send reset link", onClick = …, modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(), variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Primary, loading = working)
<intent-filter android:autoVerify="true"> with ACTION_VIEW, BROWSABLE and the https host and path of the link; read intent.data in the activity

options.name: step
options.description: The app's state: request, sent, reset or done. Start on reset when the activity was opened by the reset link.

options.name: resetToken
options.description: The token from the App Link, read from intent.data in onCreate and onNewIntent. Sent with the new password.

options.name: working
options.description: Passed to the primary button's loading while the request or the save runs.

options.name: formError
options.description: A failed request or save, or an expired link, shown in a danger MonarchInlineNotice above the step.

states.name: request
states.description: The email field and Send reset link. An invalid address shows its error on the field.

states.name: sent
states.description: Check your email, naming the address, with a way back to use a different email.

states.name: reset
states.description: Opened by the emailed link: the new password with the strength meter and the confirmation. Change password stays disabled until every rule is met and the two match.

states.name: done
states.description: Password changed, with Back to sign in.

states.name: working
states.description: The primary button shows its progress indicator and reads "Loading" while the request or the save runs.

states.name: failed
states.description: A failed request or save, or an expired link, goes in a danger MonarchInlineNotice above the step.

appearance: Every part is an existing Monarch component in the theme: titles in the title style, MonarchTextField and MonarchPasswordInput with their own borders and errors, the strength meter's segments, and full-width primary buttons. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web's PasswordResetForm is one component with a step prop and messages; on Android it is a recipe, as on iOS, because the steps, the network calls and the link handling belong to the app. The link returns through an Android App Link: an intent filter with android:autoVerify="true" for the https host and path, verified by a Digital Asset Links file on the site; the activity reads the token from intent.data in onCreate and onNewIntent. The web gets it from the page URL and iOS from a Universal Link. The web's resend cooldown on the sent step is not part of the recipe; MonarchEmailVerificationBanner keeps its cooldown internal today. The web moves focus to each step's heading; on Android each title has the heading semantics so TalkBack's heading navigation finds it. MonarchPasswordInput with the New purpose lets autofill services offer and save a strong password.
accessibility: Each step's title has the heading semantics.
The email and password fields are MonarchTextField and MonarchPasswordInput, so labels, errors and error semantics come from those components.
The password inputs use the New purpose, so autofill services can offer a strong password and save it.
The strength meter reads each rule as met or not met, not by color alone.
Buttons are MonarchButtons with 48dp touch targets and a Loading state while working.
edgeCases: Say that a link was sent whether or not an account exists, so the form does not reveal which addresses have accounts.
The reset step needs the token from the link; keep it in the app and send it with the new password.
A link opened after it expired should show the error on the reset step and offer to request a new one.
The link can arrive while the app is running: handle it in onNewIntent as well as onCreate.

name: MonarchPasswordStrengthMeter
title: PasswordStrengthMeter
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row and Column with androidx.compose.ui.semantics.liveRegion
summary: Shows how strong a password is while it is typed: a four-part bar, the strength in words, and each requirement as met or not met.
whenToUse: Under a MonarchPasswordInput with purpose New, on sign-up and password reset screens.
whenNotToUse: On a sign-in screen, where the password already exists. For a general measure use MonarchProgress.
api: @Composable fun MonarchPasswordStrengthMeter(password: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, rules: List<MonarchPasswordRule> = MonarchPasswordRule.defaults(), showRules: Boolean = true, score: ((String) -> MonarchPasswordStrength)? = null, labels: MonarchPasswordStrengthMeterLabels = MonarchPasswordStrengthMeterLabels())

class MonarchPasswordRule(id: String, label: String, test: (String) -> Boolean) { companion object { const val DEFAULT_MIN_LENGTH: Int = 8; fun defaults(length: String, case: String, number: String, symbol: String): List<MonarchPasswordRule>; @Composable fun defaults(): List<MonarchPasswordRule> } }

enum class MonarchPasswordStrength { VeryWeak, Weak, Fair, Good, Strong; companion object { const val STRONG_LENGTH: Int = 14; fun score(password: String, rules: List<MonarchPasswordRule>): MonarchPasswordStrength } }
class MonarchPasswordStrengthMeterLabels(strengthText: ((MonarchPasswordStrength?) -> String)? = null, rulesLabel: String? = null, ruleText: ((label: String, met: Boolean) -> String)? = null)

options.name: password
options.description: The password to rate. It is only read; nothing is stored.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the meter.

options.name: rules
options.description: The requirements listed and counted by the default score: at least 8 characters, upper and lower case, a number, a symbol or space. An empty list hides the list.

options.name: showRules
options.description: Whether to list the requirements.

options.name: score
options.description: A custom estimator. By default MonarchPasswordStrength.score(password, rules). Not called for an empty password.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the strength line, the spoken name of the list ("Password requirements") and the spoken text of a rule ("Met: …", "Not met: …").

states.name: empty
states.description: No segment is filled, the line reads "Password strength: Not entered" and no rule is met.

states.name: very weak, weak
states.description: One segment in the danger solid color.

states.name: fair
states.description: Two segments in the warning solid color.

states.name: good, strong
states.description: Three or four segments in the success solid color.

states.name: rule met
states.description: A filled disc and the success strong text color; a rule not met has an empty ring and the muted text color.

appearance: Empty segments use the emphasis background; filled ones the danger, warning or success solid color. The strength line is muted caption text. A met rule is in the success strong color with a filled disc, an unmet one in the muted text color with a ring. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The same rules, score, levels and texts as the web and iOS. Rule tests are Kotlin lambdas; lengths count Unicode code points, as the web counts code points, so the platforms agree on the same password. The default rule labels are Android string resources, so MonarchPasswordRule.defaults() is a composable; MonarchPasswordRule.defaults(length, case, number, symbol) builds the same rules with the app's own labels outside composition. The web draws a check and a dot as the rule marks and iOS uses SF Symbols; Monarch for Android bundles no icons, so the marks are a filled disc and an empty ring drawn as shapes. Strength texts are replaced through one labels object, as on iOS, instead of the web's messages object.
accessibility: The bar is hidden from TalkBack; the strength is always a line of text.
The strength line is a polite live region, so TalkBack announces it when it changes.
Each rule is one element read as "Met: …" or "Not met: …".
Met and not met differ by the shape of the mark (filled disc or empty ring) as well as color.
The list has the spoken name "Password requirements" and collection information with one row per rule.
Text wraps at font scale 2.0; the bar keeps its height.
edgeCases: An empty password is never scored: the custom score is not called and no rule is met.
An empty rules list hides the list and makes every non-empty password at least Good with the default score.
Each change of the password announces the strength line again only when its text changes.

examples.setupTemplate: var password by remember { mutableStateOf({{password}}) }
examples.setup: var password by remember { mutableStateOf("Lighthouse7") }

examples.title: Your own rules and estimator
examples.code:
MonarchPasswordStrengthMeter(

    rules = listOf(

    ),
    score = { if (it.length >= 20) MonarchPasswordStrength.Strong else MonarchPasswordStrength.Fair },
)

name: MonarchPaymentMethodCard
title: PaymentMethodCard

summary: A saved payment card: network, last four digits, expiry and holder, a Default badge, and actions to make it the default or remove it after a confirmation.
whenToUse: On a billing or wallet screen that lists the cards a payment provider has saved for the account.
whenNotToUse: Not for entering a card: card entry stays with the payment provider's SDK. Not for a plan or an invoice: use MonarchPlanCard or MonarchReceiptPreview.
api: @Composable fun MonarchPaymentMethodCard(brand: String, last4: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, expiryMonth: Int? = null, expiryYear: Int? = null, holderName: String? = null, expiry: MonarchPaymentMethodCardExpiry? = null, now: Long = System.currentTimeMillis(), default: Boolean = false, removeEnabled: Boolean = true, brandImage: Painter? = null, labels: MonarchPaymentMethodCardLabels = MonarchPaymentMethodCardLabels(), onMakeDefault: (suspend () -> Unit)? = null, onRemove: (suspend () -> Unit)? = null, actions: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null)

enum class MonarchPaymentMethodCardExpiry { Valid, Expiring, Expired; companion object { fun status(month: Int, year: Int, now: Long = System.currentTimeMillis(), soonMonths: Int = 1): MonarchPaymentMethodCardExpiry } }

class MonarchPaymentMethodCardLabels(name: ((brand: String, last4: String) -> String)? = null, expires: ((date: String) -> String)? = null, expiredOn: ((date: String) -> String)? = null, defaultBadge: String? = null, expiringBadge: String? = null, expiredBadge: String? = null, makeDefault: String? = null, remove: String? = null, actionLabel: ((action: String, name: String) -> String)? = null, removeTitle: ((name: String) -> String)? = null, removeMessage: String? = null, removeConfirm: String? = null, cancel: String? = null, failed: String? = null)

options.name: brand
options.description: A network id (visa, mastercard, amex, rupay, discover, diners, jcb, unionpay, maestro) shown by its display name, or any display name, shown as given.

options.name: last4
options.description: The last four digits, exactly as the payment provider returns them.

options.name: expiryMonth
options.description: The expiry month, 1 to 12.

options.name: expiryYear
options.description: The expiry year, two digits (read as 20YY) or four.

options.name: holderName
options.description: The cardholder's name, shown before the expiry.

options.name: expiry
options.description: Replaces the status worked out from the date, when the payment provider already reports it.

options.name: now
options.description: The current time in epoch milliseconds, for working out the status; pass a fixed value in tests.

options.name: default
options.description: Shows the Default badge and hides Make default.

options.name: removeEnabled
options.description: Disables Remove, for example on the only method of an active subscription.

options.name: brandImage
options.description: The network's logo, always decorative. While null a muted tile stands in.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string (monarch_paymentmethodcard_*).

options.name: onMakeDefault
options.description: Shows Make default on a card that is not the default. Progress shows while it runs; a thrown exception shows the failure with Try again.

options.name: onRemove
options.description: Shows Remove, which asks for confirmation in an AlertDialog first. Progress shows while it runs; a thrown exception shows the failure with Try again.

options.name: actions
options.description: Further buttons after Make default and Remove, for example a small MonarchButton.

states.name: valid
states.description: No expiry badge; the line reads "Expires MM/YY".

states.name: expiring
states.description: A warning MonarchBadge "Expires soon", this month or next.

states.name: expired
states.description: A danger MonarchBadge "Expired", the line reads "Expired MM/YY", and Make default is disabled.

states.name: default
states.description: A Default badge in the accent roles; Make default is hidden.

states.name: working
states.description: The button of the running action shows progress and reports "Loading"; the other action is disabled until it ends.

states.name: failed
states.description: A MonarchInlineErrorRetry under the card with Try again; the message is a polite live region.

states.name: remove disabled
states.description: Remove uses the disabled colors and cannot be activated.

appearance: A MonarchCard on the surface role with the default border. The name uses the default text role, the expiry line the muted text role, and the Default badge the accent subtle fill with the accent strong text. Expiring and expired badges use the warning and danger tones. A missing network image is a tile in the muted background role. High-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colors.
platformNotes: The web card shows a ConfirmDialog that stays open while removal runs and shows a rejection inside the dialog. Android, like iOS, closes the Material 3 AlertDialog on confirm, shows progress on the Remove button and a failure under the card with Try again. The web onMakeDefaultError callback is replaced by the same inline error. The web heading level has no Android equivalent; the header is a heading for TalkBack. The web uses an accent badge tone; MonarchTone has no accent tone, so the Default badge draws the accent roles itself. The actions are suspend functions where iOS uses async throws. The expiry status is worked out in UTC from epoch milliseconds.
accessibility: The network image is hidden; the name, badges, holder and expiry are merged into one element marked as a heading.
Expiry states are badges with text, never color alone.
Make default and Remove are read with their label and the card, for example "Remove, Visa ending in 4242".
Removal is confirmed in a Material 3 AlertDialog with a danger confirm button and a Cancel button.
A failed action is shown in MonarchInlineErrorRetry, a polite live region, so it is announced.
Action buttons keep 48dp touch targets; badges and actions wrap onto new rows at large font sizes.
edgeCases: Two-digit years are read as 20YY; months outside 1 to 12 are clamped.
A card is valid to the end of its expiry month, in UTC.
Without a month and a year the status is valid unless expiry is given.
Retrying a failed removal does not ask for confirmation again.
An unknown network id is shown as given, so pass a localised display name.
When onRemove removes the card from the app's list, the card leaves composition and its running action is cancelled with it.

appearance: Text in the default and muted text colors on the surrounding surface, subtle dividers between lines, a default border rule over net pay in the heading style, and year-to-date tiles filled with the subtle background. The status badge carries its tone. It reads the same in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web PayslipView is an article with lists and description lists, accepts ReactNode slots and decimal or minor-unit amounts. On Android amounts are BigDecimal in major units and the status is a MonarchStatusDefinition. The parity map named LazyColumn sections; the payslip is a Column instead, so it can sit inside the screen's verticalScroll with other content, as on iOS. The web Download button is primary; here it is a small secondary button, as on iOS, so it does not compete with the screen's main action, and Monarch bundles no download icon. The headingLevel option has no Android equivalent; the title and group names are TalkBack headings. iOS ships the same MonarchPayslipView.
accessibility: The title, the group names and the year-to-date heading are TalkBack headings.
Each line is one element read as its name, note and amount; each summary row as its label and amount; each year-to-date tile as its label and amount.
The lines of a group are a traversal group named after the group.
While downloading, the Download button is disabled and its state reads "Preparing PDF".
The Download button keeps a 48dp touch target.
Names wrap and grow at font scale 2.0; right to left, names and amounts mirror.
edgeCases: Totals are never recalculated, so lines that do not add up to the totals are shown as given.
Deductions are positive numbers; no minus sign is added.
Employer lines that are hidden leave the summary unchanged.
Very long names wrap; amounts keep their own width at the end.

On Android the placement is the adaptive scaffold's: beside the main pane when the window is wide enough, in its place otherwise; the header is ordinary content (MonarchText, MonarchButton for previous, next and close); its J and K shortcuts are onPreviewKeyEvent handlers in the app. The catalogue app does not depend on the adaptive libraries, so its page shows the phone form, a MonarchBottomSheet; the scaffold example is compiled and composed in the unit tests. iOS uses the inspector.

Give the panel a visible Close button; at expanded width there is no back gesture to close it.
Buttons in the panel keep their 48dp targets.
edgeCases: The panes' widths come from the scaffold directive; at medium width only one pane is shown.
Keep the selected row highlighted in the main pane so the panel's subject is clear at expanded width.

states.name: ready

states.name: expired
states.description: The status badge reads Expired, the expiry is left out of the detail line and Copy link is hidden; Resend and Revoke stay.

states.name: error

appearance: MonarchSectionCard's surface and border with the title in the heading style, rows without padding of their own separated by subtle dividers, each member row with its initials avatar, the email in the strong body style, the info Invited (or Expired) badge, the role and detail in muted caption text, and secondary and danger buttons. The same roles in dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: A product pattern, experimental until a Rook app adopts it, built only from Monarch parts. Names and parameters follow iOS; isRetrying is retrying, isExpired is expired, and onResend and onRevoke are suspending functions, Compose's equivalent of async throws. Each invitation is a MonarchMemberRow in its invited status, which brings Resend invite, Revoke and its Material 3 confirmation dialog, progress and errors; the rows are a Column inside a MonarchSectionCard, not a lazy list, so the card can sit under the member list on a screen that scrolls. The web's async getInviteLink is the link field on each invitation, copied with MonarchCopyButton, which leaves the copy confirmation to the system on Android 13 and later. Because the member row runs the revoke after the dialog closes, the pending state and a failure show in the row instead of inside the dialog, as on iOS. The web's Resend "Sent" label for three seconds is the member row's "Invite sent again." note. The Expired badge reuses the member row's invited badge, so it keeps the info tone; the word, not the color, says it has expired. The web's detail slot (for example an app access summary) and headingLevel are not offered. Relative times use android.icu.text.RelativeDateTimeFormatter in the given or configured locale.
accessibility: The title is a heading (MonarchSectionCard).
The rows are a traversal group named "Pending invitations".
Each invitation is one TalkBack element read as the email, with Invited or Expired, the role and the detail line as its state, so expiry never depends on color.
The detail line is built by a tested pure function: "Invited by Sam Rivera · Sent 2 days ago · Expires in 5 days".

Resend invite, Copy link and Revoke are separate buttons named after the email: "Resend invite, ana@example.com", "Copy link for ana@example.com", "Revoke invite for ana@example.com", each with a 48dp touch target.
"Invite sent again." and a failure are announced by the row; a revoke is announced as "Invitation to ana@example.com revoked" from a polite live region that stays when the row goes away.
edgeCases: expired = null works the expiry out from expiresAt and now; an explicit false wins over a past expiresAt.
An invitation without a sender, times or role shows only its email and status.
A long email is shown in full on several lines at font scale 2.0.
A ready list with no invitations shows the empty state; loading and error ignore invites.
Times in the future read "in 5 days"; past ones "2 days ago"; less than a minute away reads "now".

options.description: The latest day custom dates may end, UTC midnight. null is today.

options.name: maxDays
options.description: The longest custom range in days. A longer range shows "Choose 30 days or fewer" and Save stays off.

options.name: locale
options.description: The locale of the written dates and of the week. null uses the configuration's.

options.name: timeZone
options.description: The zone whose calendar day is today when today is null. An IANA id such as Europe/Berlin; null, or an id the device does not know, is the device's zone.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string: the name, each preset, the custom button, Save, Cancel and the too-long message.

states.name: preset
states.description: The chosen segment is selected (filled with a check mark); with showRange its days are written under the row.

states.name: custom, no dates
states.description: A button "Choose dates" under the presets opens the date range picker.

states.name: custom with dates
states.description: The button shows the dates, such as "Oct 3 – Nov 15, 2026", and opens the picker on them.

states.name: picking
states.description: The Material 3 DateRangePicker in a dialog. Days before minDate and after maxDate cannot be picked. Save is off until a first day is picked and while the range is longer than maxDays; one picked day saves a one-day range.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Every segment, the select field and the custom button are disabled; the dates use the disabled text color.

appearance: The Material 3 segmented buttons in the Monarch theme: the outline border, the selected segment filled with the secondary container color and a check mark. The dates under the row use the caption style in the muted text role, the disabled role when disabled. The too-long message uses the danger strong role. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from MonarchTheme.
platformNotes: The web has the presets as a segmented control or a Select and the DateRangePicker field inline under them. On Android the custom dates are picked in the Material 3 DateRangePicker dialog, opened as soon as Custom is chosen and again from a button that shows the dates. The web's size prop (sm, md) is not offered: Material 3 segmented buttons have one height with a 48dp target. Dates are UTC midnight epoch milliseconds as in the Material 3 pickers, not ISO strings. The web calls onValueChange with the value and the resolved range; on Android onValueChange takes the value and MonarchPeriodSelectorDefaults.resolve gives the range. The web's dateRangeMessages are the Material 3 picker's own strings, translated by the system; Save, Cancel and the too-long message are in labels. iOS has not built this component yet.
accessibility: Each preset is a Material 3 segmented button, read as a radio button with its selected state; the row is named "Period" for TalkBack.
Every segment, the custom dates button and the select field have a 48dp touch target.
The custom dates button is read as "Custom period" and its dates, or "Choose dates".
A range longer than maxDays is said in words above the calendar, in a polite live region, and Save is disabled.
The segment row scrolls sideways instead of cutting labels at font scale 2.0, and the dates under it wrap.
In right to left the first preset is at the right.
edgeCases: Rolling periods count today: Last 7 days on 15 November is 9 to 15 November.
This week starts on the locale's first day; pass firstDayOfWeek for a workspace setting.
Last month and last quarter are whole months, so Last month on 31 March is 1 to 28 February.
Choosing Custom keeps the dates shown until then, so the picker opens on them; Cancel keeps them.
A custom value without a range resolves to null; the app shows nothing until dates are saved.
today is the device's date at composition; pass today when the period must follow a workspace time zone.

name: MonarchPermissionMatrix
title: PermissionMatrix
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.Checkbox (grid cells), androidx.compose.material3.PrimaryScrollableTabRow with Tab (role picker), MonarchCheckboxRow (one role at a time), androidx.compose.foundation.layout.BoxWithConstraints
summary: Which permissions each role has: roles by permissions, edited with checkboxes or shown read only, grouped, with cells that cannot change and say why.
whenToUse: On a roles settings screen, to show and edit which permissions each role of a workspace grants.
whenNotToUse: To give one person a role, use MonarchRolePicker. To show the permissions an AI assistant asks for, use MonarchAiPermissionScope.
api: @Composable fun MonarchPermissionMatrix(roles: List<MonarchPermissionMatrixRole>, permissions: List<MonarchPermissionMatrixPermission>, value: Map<String, Set<String>>, onValueChange: (Map<String, Set<String>>) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, title: String? = null, layout: MonarchPermissionMatrixLayout = MonarchPermissionMatrixLayout.Automatic, enabled: Boolean = true, readOnly: Boolean = false, lockReason: ((roleId: String, permissionId: String) -> String?)? = null, labels: MonarchPermissionMatrixLabels = MonarchPermissionMatrixLabels())
class MonarchPermissionMatrixRole(id: String, label: String, description: String? = null)
class MonarchPermissionMatrixPermission(id: String, label: String, description: String? = null, group: String? = null)
enum class MonarchPermissionMatrixLayout { Automatic, Grid, ByRole }

class MonarchPermissionMatrixLabels(permissionHeader: String? = null, rolePicker: String? = null, cellLabel: ((permission: String, role: String) -> String)? = null, allowed: String? = null, notAllowed: String? = null, locked: String? = null)

options.name: roles
options.description: The roles, in order: columns of the grid, tabs of the one-role layout.

options.name: permissions
options.description: The permissions, in order. Those with the same group are listed together under its heading, groups in the order they first appear.

options.name: value
options.description: The granted permission ids by role id. A missing role has none; a role id that is not in roles is kept and ignored.

options.name: onValueChange
options.description: Called with the whole new value when a cell is toggled.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the matrix.

options.name: title
options.description: A heading above the matrix, with the heading semantics.

options.name: layout
options.description: Automatic shows the grid when every column fits the width and the font scale is at most 1.3, and one role at a time otherwise; Grid always shows the grid, scrolling sideways; ByRole always shows one role at a time.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the cells and role tabs can be used, for example false while saving.

options.name: readOnly
options.description: Shows a check or a dash, read as Allowed or Not allowed, instead of checkboxes.

options.name: lockReason
options.description: Why a cell cannot change, or null when it can. An empty string uses "This can’t be changed".

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces the column heading, the role tabs' name, the cell name, Allowed, Not allowed and the default lock reason.

states.name: grid
states.description: A header row of roles, a divider, group headings and one row per permission with a checkbox per role in 80dp columns.

states.name: one role at a time
states.description: A scrollable tab row of roles, the role's description, then group headings and a MonarchCheckboxRow per permission.

states.name: locked
states.description: The checkbox is disabled; its reason is written under the permission in the grid ("Owner: …") or under the row, and added to the cell's spoken name.

states.name: read only
states.description: A check in the strong success color or a dash in the subtle text color, read as Allowed or Not allowed; in the one-role layout the words are written.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With enabled = false every checkbox and tab uses the disabled colors and cannot be changed.

states.name: no roles
states.description: Only the title is shown.

appearance: Role and permission names use the label and body styles in the default text color, descriptions, group headings and lock reasons the caption and label styles in the muted text color. Checkboxes and tabs are Material 3 in the Monarch theme. All colors are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: Same names as iOS. The web's controlled and uncontrolled value with onValueChange is hoisted state here: value with onValueChange, which receives the whole new value (the web also passes the changed cell). The web's table has arrow-key grid navigation (WAI-ARIA grid); a phone has no arrow keys, so TalkBack moves cell by cell. A two-axis grid does not fit a phone, so the automatic layout shows one role at a time with a Material 3 tab row, as iOS does with MonarchTabs. Monarch bundles no icons, so a locked cell shows no lock symbol; its reason is written instead. The web's isLocked may return a rich reason; here it is a String. disabled is the enabled parameter.
accessibility: Each grid cell is a Material 3 Checkbox with the checkbox role and on or off state, named "<permission> for <role>" by a replaceable string.
A locked cell is disabled and its reason is part of its spoken name and written on screen.
In the one-role layout each permission is a MonarchCheckboxRow: one element with the label, the description and the reason, and a 48dp target.
Read only, each grid cell is one element named by the cell with Allowed or Not allowed as its state description, so the mark's shape and color are not the only signal.
The title, the permission column heading, role headings and group headings have the heading semantics.
The role tabs are Material 3 tabs with the selected state and 48dp targets.
At font scales above 1.3 the automatic layout shows one role at a time, so no text is cut off.
edgeCases: With no roles, only the title is shown.
A role id in the value that is not in roles is kept in the new value and ignored on screen.
The forced grid scrolls sideways when it is wider than its space.
Locked cells keep whatever the value says; the app decides their value.
The selected tab is remembered across configuration changes and clamped when roles are removed.

parityExceptions.reason: The phone shows each row as a card: the first column is the card title and every other cell carries its column name as a label, so the column header row is not drawn. TalkBack reads each cell with its column name.

name: MonarchPhoneCountrySelect
title: PhoneCountrySelect
wrapsNative: MonarchCombobox (androidx.compose.material3.ExposedDropdownMenuBox with androidx.compose.material3.ModalBottomSheet) over a bundled ITU-T E.164 calling-code table, country names from java.util.Locale.getDisplayCountry
summary: A searchable picker of the country calling code of a phone number: each country by name with its code, such as "Portugal (+351)".
whenToUse: Before or beside a phone number field, when the number is stored with its country and calling code.
whenNotToUse: For a country of residence or an address use MonarchCountrySelect; for a whole phone number field with formatting use MonarchPhoneInput when it is available.
api: @Composable fun MonarchPhoneCountrySelect(selected: String?, onSelectedChange: (code: String?, dialCode: String?) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, locale: Locale? = null, countries: List<String>? = null, preferred: List<String> = emptyList(), presentation: MonarchComboboxPresentation = MonarchComboboxPresentation.Automatic, enabled: Boolean = true, showFlag: Boolean = false, placeholder: String? = null, helperText: String? = null, errorText: String? = null, clearOptionLabel: String? = null, labels: MonarchPhoneCountrySelectLabels = MonarchPhoneCountrySelectLabels())

class MonarchPhoneCountrySelectLabels(label: String? = null, suggested: String? = null, all: String? = null, empty: String? = null, option: ((name: String, dialCode: String) -> String)? = null, combobox: MonarchComboboxLabels = MonarchComboboxLabels())

options.name: selected
options.description: The chosen ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code in any case, or null.

options.name: onSelectedChange
options.description: Called with the chosen upper-case code and its calling code ("+44"), or two nulls when the selection is cleared.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the field.

options.name: locale
options.description: The language of the country names and of the sort order. null uses the first locale of the configuration.

options.name: countries
options.description: Limits the list to these codes; unknown codes are dropped. null lists every country with a calling code.

options.name: preferred
options.description: Codes listed first under "Suggested" while nothing is typed, such as the person's own country.

options.name: presentation
options.description: Menu, Sheet, or Automatic: a menu for up to eight countries, a sheet otherwise.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the list can be opened.

options.name: showFlag
options.description: Shows the flag emoji at the end of each row. Off by default because TalkBack reads a flag emoji as "Flag:" and the name, repeating it.

options.name: placeholder
options.description: Shown in the empty field while nothing is chosen.

options.name: helperText
options.description: Guidance below the field.

options.name: errorText
options.description: An error message; replaces the helper text and is set as the field's error.

options.name: clearOptionLabel
options.description: Adds a first row that clears the selection. Hidden while searching.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings: the label "Country code", "Suggested", "All countries", "No matching country", the row text "%1$s (%2$s)" and the combobox's own strings.

states.name: closed
states.description: The field shows the chosen country's label, or the placeholder (or the floating label) while nothing is chosen.

states.name: open
states.description: The bottom sheet (or, for eight options or fewer, the menu) lists the options; while nothing is typed the suggested ones come first under their heading.

states.name: searching
states.description: Typing filters the list, best matches first, without headings; when nothing matches the list says so.

states.name: error
states.description: The field has the danger outline and the message below it, and the message is the field's error for TalkBack.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The field takes the disabled colors and does not open.

appearance: The field is MonarchCombobox's: MonarchTextField's colors, a surface fill with the input border, the danger strong color in error; the sheet is on the surface color, second lines, hints and headings are muted text and the chosen row's radio mark is the accent strong color. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Built on MonarchCombobox, so long lists open a Material 3 bottom sheet with a search field instead of the web's popover. Neither Android nor the JDK exposes calling codes, so the ITU-T E.164 table is bundled: the same table as the web component (Monarch, MIT), whose calling codes are public assignments of the ITU. The web's matchPhoneCountry and getPhoneCountry helpers are internal here; MonarchPhoneInput, when built, is expected to share the table. There is no clear button: a phone number always needs a country, and clearOptionLabel adds a clear row when an app needs one. iOS has no PhoneCountrySelect yet; the name is the planned shared one.
accessibility: The field is MonarchCombobox's Material 3 exposed dropdown anchor: TalkBack reads the label, the chosen value and the expand state; double tap opens the list.

Every row is read with its label, second line and hint, and the chosen row is selected with a filled radio mark, so the choice does not rely on color; in the sheet each row is a radio button at least 48dp high.
The headings over suggested and other entries are headings; the no-match message is a polite live region.
The error is the field's error semantics and is shown as text.
edgeCases: Several countries share a calling code (+1, +44, +7); each is listed under its own name, and typing "+1242" finds the Bahamas through its leading digits.
Typing "44" or "+44" finds the countries with that code.
Unknown codes in countries and preferred are ignored; a selected code without a calling code shows an empty field.
Kosovo is listed as XK, a user-assigned code that the platform names.

name: MonarchPhoneInput
title: PhoneInput
wrapsNative: MonarchPhoneCountrySelect (androidx.compose.material3.ExposedDropdownMenuBox with androidx.compose.material3.ModalBottomSheet) above MonarchTextField (androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedTextField) with KeyboardType.Phone and androidx.compose.ui.autofill.ContentType.PhoneNumberNational
summary: A phone number entered as a country calling code and the national number, with one E.164 value out, such as "+442079460958".
whenToUse: Contact, profile, booking and application forms that store a callable number from any country in one format.
whenNotToUse: For codes sent by SMS use MonarchOtpPinInput; for picking only a calling code use MonarchPhoneCountrySelect; for carrier validation or formatting by country use a phone library on the server.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchPhoneInput(value: String?, onValueChange: (String?) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, defaultCountry: String = "US", onCountryChange: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, label: String? = null, placeholder: String? = null, helperText: String? = null, errorText: String? = null, countries: List<String>? = null, preferred: List<String> = emptyList(), locale: Locale? = null, enabled: Boolean = true, readOnly: Boolean = false, labels: MonarchPhoneInputLabels = MonarchPhoneInputLabels(), interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)
public class MonarchPhoneInputLabels(invalid: String? = null, country: MonarchPhoneCountrySelectLabels = MonarchPhoneCountrySelectLabels())

public object MonarchPhoneInputDefaults { fun toE164(dialCode: String, national: String, country: String? = null): String?; fun isValidE164(value: String): Boolean; fun parse(phone: String, preferred: String? = null): MonarchPhoneInputParts? }
public data class MonarchPhoneInputParts(country: String, dialCode: String, national: String)

options.name: value
options.description: The number in E.164 ("+442079460958"), or null while there is none. Other international forms ("+44 20 7946 0958", "0044…") are read too.

options.name: onValueChange
options.description: Called with the new E.164 number when the field loses focus, on Done or when the country changes; null when the number is cleared. Never called with an incomplete number.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the whole input.

options.name: defaultCountry
options.description: The ISO code of the country shown while value does not say. Set it from the person's profile or locale.

options.name: onCountryChange
options.description: Called with the ISO code when the country changes, by the picker, a pasted number, a shared calling code or a new value.

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label of the number field.

options.name: placeholder
options.description: An example shown while the number is empty and focused.

options.name: helperText
options.description: Guidance under the number.

options.name: errorText
options.description: An error from the app. It replaces the input's own "Enter a complete phone number." while present.

options.name: countries
options.description: Limits the picker to these ISO codes; null lists every country with a calling code.

options.name: preferred
options.description: ISO codes listed first in the picker under "Suggested".

options.name: locale
options.description: The language of the country names. null uses the first locale of the configuration.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the country and the number can be changed.

options.name: readOnly
options.description: Whether the number can be selected and copied but not changed. The picker has no read-only state, so it is disabled.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings: the message "Enter a complete phone number." and the picker's strings, including its label "Country code".

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the focus interactions of the number field.

states.name: empty
states.description: The picker shows the default country, the number field its label (and the placeholder when focused); the calling code is shown at the start of the number.

states.name: typing
states.description: The text is kept as typed and nothing is sent; a typed or pasted full international number switches the country at once and keeps the national digits.

states.name: saved
states.description: On focus loss, Done or a country change, the number is joined with the calling code (one leading 0 dropped, except Italy, San Marino and Vatican City) and sent; the field then shows the national digits of the saved value.

states.name: incomplete
states.description: A number of fewer than 8 or more than 15 digits is kept, the field takes the error state with "Enter a complete phone number." and nothing is sent; the next edit clears the message.

states.name: error
states.description: errorText from the app replaces the input's own message and puts the number field in the error state.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Both the picker and the number take the disabled colors and cannot be used.

states.name: read only
states.description: The number can be selected and copied but not changed; the picker is disabled.

appearance: Both parts are Monarch fields: a surface fill with the input border, the focus ring color when focused, muted labels and the calling code in the muted icon color, and the danger strong color for the error outline and message. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web places the picker and the number side by side and wraps them below about 22rem; on a phone the picker is a full-width field above the number, so neither is cut at 320dp or at the largest font size, and the calling code is repeated at the start of the number. The web's controlled country prop is replaced by defaultCountry plus onCountryChange, and its onValueChange details are available from MonarchPhoneInputDefaults.parse; the web's toE164, isValidE164 and parsePhoneNumber are MonarchPhoneInputDefaults.toE164, isValidE164 and parse. The web's sm, md and lg sizes are not offered: Material text fields have one height. Escape to restore the saved number and the hidden form input have no meaning on Android. The calling-code table is MonarchPhoneCountrySelect's, so both stay in step. iOS has no PhoneInput entry yet; the names follow the web and MonarchCurrencyInput.
accessibility: The picker is MonarchPhoneCountrySelect's exposed dropdown, named "Country code"; the number is a Material 3 text field named by its label, so TalkBack reads them as two elements.
The number field asks for the phone keyboard and is marked as a national phone number for autofill.
An incomplete number sets the field's error semantics to "Enter a complete phone number." and shows it as text, so it is not shown by color alone.
The number is shown left to right on a right-to-left screen, with a left-to-right mark that is not part of the value.
Both parts are at least 48dp high, also at the largest font size.
edgeCases: Several countries share a calling code (+1, +7, +44): a number is moved to the country of its leading digits (+1 242 is the Bahamas), otherwise it stays with the chosen country, otherwise the code's main country.
Arabic-Indic, Persian and full-width digits are read as 0 to 9; spaces, brackets, dots and hyphens are ignored.
A pasted number that starts with + or 00 but matches no calling code is flagged as incomplete on Done.
Only the length is checked (8 to 15 digits after the plus), so a number of the right length that is not in service is accepted.
Clearing the number sends null; changing the country while the number is empty sends nothing.

name: MonarchPlanCard
title: PlanCard
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.Surface (through MonarchCard), androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow
summary: One plan in a plan picker: its name, price, who it is for, what it includes and a call to action, on a Monarch card.
whenToUse: In a plan picker or an upgrade screen, one card per plan, with the current plan marked.
whenNotToUse: For usage against the limits of the current plan use MonarchUsageMeter. The card never starts a purchase by itself: the action must use Google Play Billing for digital goods.
