options.name: name
options.description: The plan name, already localised. A heading.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the card. The card fills the available width.

options.name: price
options.description: The price as the product writes it, such as "$12" or "Contact us". Never formatted by the card.

options.name: period
options.description: Text after the price, such as "per seat / month".

options.name: priceNote
options.description: A line under the price, such as "Billed yearly".

options.name: description
options.description: One or two sentences on who the plan is for.

options.name: featuresLabel
options.description: A heading above the features.

options.name: features
options.description: What the plan includes; included = false lists one it does not have.

options.name: badge
options.description: A short label beside the name, such as "Recommended".

options.name: footer
options.description: Small print under the features.

options.name: highlighted
options.description: Emphasises the card as the recommended plan.

options.name: current
options.description: Adds the "Current plan" badge.

options.name: includedIcon
options.description: A mark before every included feature, such as a check icon. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: currentPlanLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in badge text "Current plan" (monarch_plancard_current).

options.name: notIncludedLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken prefix "Not included:" (monarch_plancard_not_included).

options.name: action
options.description: The call to action, normally one MonarchButton.

states.name: default
states.description: A MonarchCard with the default border and a subtle badge.

states.name: highlighted
states.description: A 2dp accent border, the raised surface with a shadow, and a solid badge.

states.name: current
states.description: An outline badge with "Current plan" beside the name.

appearance: The card is a MonarchCard: the surface color with the default border, or the raised surface with a shadow and a 2dp accent solid border when highlighted. Included features are default text, features that are not included are muted with a dash, and the price period, price note, hints and footer are muted. The included mark is tinted success strong. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web card takes any node for the name, price, features and footer and a heading level; here they are strings, the action is a slot, and the name is always a heading, as on iOS. The web badge on a highlighted card uses the accent tone; MonarchBadge has no accent tone, so it is a solid neutral badge, as on iOS. The web draws a check before included features; Monarch bundles no icons, so the check is the includedIcon slot, and a feature that is not included always shows a dash and is read with "Not included:". As on the web the action follows the description. An app that sells digital goods must use Google Play Billing for the purchase itself.
accessibility: The name is a heading, and the features label is a heading too.
The price and its period are read as one element.
Each feature is one element. A feature that is not included is read with "Not included:" before it and shows a dash, so the difference does not depend on color.
A feature's hint is read after its label.
The action stays a separate element with its own touch target.
Highlighting is a wider border and a badge with text, not color alone.
All text wraps and is not cut off at font scale 2.0; the name and badges flow onto more lines when they do not fit, and the badges follow the name in both layout directions.
edgeCases: Only the name is required; every other part is left out when it is null or empty.
A price without a period, and a period without a price, are both drawn.
The card fills the available width, like a full-width MonarchCard.

title: Popconfirm
wrapsNative: MonarchPopover (androidx.compose.ui.window.Popup) anchored to a MonarchButton in a androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Box, with MonarchText and a Cancel and a Danger MonarchButton in a androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row
summary: A recipe, not a component: a small confirmation anchored to the button that asked, with a question, a line of consequence, Cancel and a danger action that shows its progress.
whenToUse: For a light, reversible-in-practice action next to its button, such as removing a filter or a tag, where a full dialog would interrupt too much.
whenNotToUse: For destructive actions that cannot be undone, use AlertDialog (see confirm-dialog). For an action that can be undone, run it at once and offer Undo in a snackbar.
api: @Composable fun MonarchPopover(expanded: Boolean, onDismissRequest: () -> Unit, label: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, side: MonarchPopoverSide = MonarchPopoverSide.Bottom, content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)

@Composable fun MonarchButton(text: String, onClick: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchButtonVariant = MonarchButtonVariant.Secondary, size: MonarchButtonSize = MonarchButtonSize.Md, enabled: Boolean = true, loading: Boolean = false, …)

states.name: asking
states.description: The popover under the button with the question, the consequence, Cancel and the danger action.

states.name: pending
states.description: The danger action shows its progress indicator and reads "Loading"; Cancel is disabled and a tap outside does not close it.

states.name: failed
states.description: Show the failure as a MonarchInlineNotice in the popover and keep it open.

appearance: MonarchPopover's raised surface with the default border and shadow; the question in the subheading style, the consequence in the muted text color, a small ghost Cancel and a small danger action. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web Popconfirm is a component with a title, a description, confirm and cancel labels, a danger tone, a pending state while onConfirm runs, an error line and initial focus. On Android it is a recipe on MonarchPopover: the app holds the pending state and passes loading to the button. The plan's anchored popover keeps the question next to its button on every screen size; iOS uses the system confirmation dialog, which becomes a bottom sheet on a phone. initialFocus has no equivalent: TalkBack starts at the popover's label.
accessibility: MonarchPopover is named by its label (the question) and TalkBack moves into it when it opens; back closes it.
The question is a heading inside the popover.
The danger action is named by its text ("Remove"), so it does not depend on its color.
Both buttons have 48dp touch targets; the danger action reads "Loading" while pending.
edgeCases: Ignore onDismissRequest while the action runs, so a tap outside does not hide the progress.
Near the bottom of the screen, use MonarchPopoverSide.Top.

name: MonarchPopover
title: Popover
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.ui.window.Popup with a androidx.compose.ui.window.PopupPositionProvider
summary: A floating panel anchored to a control, for a small amount of interactive content that belongs to it. Material 3 has no popover, so Monarch builds one on the Compose Popup.
whenToUse: For a filter panel, a quick edit or a short explanation with a link that belongs to one control and should not take the person to another screen.
whenNotToUse: For a list of actions use DropdownMenu (see dropdown-menu). For text that only names a control use a PlainTooltip (see tooltip). For a decision the person must take before going on use AlertDialog (see dialog). For a task with several steps or a long form on a phone use ModalBottomSheet (see sheet).
api: @Composable fun MonarchPopover(expanded: Boolean, onDismissRequest: () -> Unit, label: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, side: MonarchPopoverSide = MonarchPopoverSide.Bottom, content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)
enum class MonarchPopoverSide { Bottom, Top }

options.name: expanded
options.description: Whether the panel is shown.

options.name: onDismissRequest
options.description: Called on a tap outside, the back gesture or Escape. Set expanded to false in it.

options.name: label
options.description: The spoken name of the panel, announced when it opens. Start the content with a visible heading too.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the panel.

options.name: side
options.description: The preferred side of the anchor. The panel moves to the other side when it does not fit.

options.name: content
options.description: The content, in a column with a 12dp gap and 16dp padding. Text takes the default text color.

states.name: closed
states.description: Nothing is drawn; the popup window does not exist.

states.name: open
states.description: The panel fades and grows in over the fast duration below or above the anchor, aligned with its start edge. With animations removed it appears at once.

states.name: no room on the preferred side
states.description: The panel opens on the other side, and is moved inward to keep 16dp from the window edges.

appearance: The panel uses the raised background role with the default text role, a 1dp border in the subtle border role (the strong border role in the high-contrast themes), 12dp corners and the large elevation. Up to 384dp wide, and never wider than the window minus 16dp on each side.
platformNotes: The parity map lists Popover as build on Android and native on iOS, where SwiftUI has popover(isPresented:). It is placed like the Material 3 DropdownMenu: in a Box next to its anchor, whose bounds it uses. The web Popover is non-modal and leaves the page interactive; on Android the popup takes focus, so a tap outside first closes it (the same as iOS). The web's align (start, center, end) and the left and right sides are not offered: phones have little room beside a control, so the panel is start-aligned and opens below or above. The web's PopoverClose is a button that sets expanded to false. The panel has no arrow, as on the web.
accessibility: The panel is a pane with the label as its title, so TalkBack announces it when it opens.
The popup takes focus: TalkBack and keyboard focus move into it, and back, Escape and a tap outside call onDismissRequest.
Controls inside keep their own 48dp touch targets.
Text inside wraps; the panel's width is limited and its height follows the content.
The opening animation is replaced by an immediate change when animations are removed.
edgeCases: At the largest font size a long content can be taller than the screen; put it in a verticalScroll column of limited height, or use a sheet.
If the anchor scrolls away, the panel follows the anchor's position as long as it is composed.
The panel does not close by itself after an action; call onDismissRequest's code from a Done button.
Two popovers open at once each take focus in turn; open one at a time.

name: MonarchPostCard
title: PostCard
wrapsNative: MonarchCard (androidx.compose.material3.Surface) with androidx.compose.foundation.clickable, androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow, MonarchAvatar and MonarchBadge; android.text.format.DateUtils for the relative time
summary: A post in a community feed or search result: author, relative time, pinned and answered markers, tags, title, a short excerpt, and reaction and comment counts.
whenToUse: In a community feed, a forum list or search results, where each post opens its own screen.
whenNotToUse: Not for a chat message; use the conversation's message bubble. Not for a link preview; use MonarchLinkCard.

public class MonarchPostCardLabels(pinned: String? = null, answered: String? = null, reactions: ((Int) -> String)? = null, comments: ((Int) -> String)? = null)

options.description: The post's title. Wraps.

options.name: author
options.description: Who wrote it.

options.name: onClick
options.description: Opens the post; the app navigates.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the card.

options.name: pinned
options.description: "Pinned" in the author line.

options.name: answered
options.description: A success "Answered" badge.

options.name: authorImage
options.description: The author's picture, loaded by the app. null shows initials.

options.name: excerpt
options.description: The plain-text body, shortened at a word boundary. Empty after trimming is not shown.

options.name: excerptLength
options.description: The longest excerpt shown, in characters, before the ellipsis.

options.name: publishedAt
options.description: When it was published, in epoch milliseconds (UTC), shown as "3 hours ago".

options.name: now
options.description: The current time for the relative time, for tests. null uses the clock, refreshed every minute.

options.name: tags
options.description: Badges after the author line: category, topic or status.

options.name: reactionCount
options.description: "12 reactions" in the footer; null hides it, zero is shown.

options.name: commentCount
options.description: "4 comments" in the footer; null hides it, zero is shown.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The interaction source of the card's button.

options.name: actions
options.description: Controls at the end of the footer, such as a bookmark button. They are separate buttons.

states.name: default
states.description: Author line, title, and the excerpt and counts when given.

states.name: pinned
states.description: "Pinned" in the author line.

states.name: answered
states.description: A success badge "Answered" in the author line.

states.name: pressed
states.description: A ripple over the author line, title and excerpt, and the focus ring when focused from a keyboard.

states.name: title only
states.description: No excerpt and no footer.

appearance: A MonarchCard on the surface color with its default border and 12dp corners; the title in the default text color, the author line, excerpt and counts in the muted text color, and badges in their tones' subtle colors. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web card is an article whose title is a link with an href and an optional renderLink; on Android, as on iOS, the author line, title and excerpt are one button that calls onClick, and the app navigates. The heading level option has no meaning on Android. The time uses DateUtils.getRelativeTimeSpanString in the device's locale instead of the web's RelativeTime. The web draws thumbs-up, comment and pin glyphs before the counts; Monarch bundles no icons, so the counts are written in full ("12 reactions · 4 comments") and pinned is the word. Footer actions are separate buttons, never nested in the card's button.
accessibility: The author line, title and excerpt are one button that TalkBack reads in order: author, time, pinned, answered, tags, title, excerpt.
The counts are one element read as "12 reactions, 4 comments"; the dot between them is hidden.
The avatar is decorative.
The answered state is a badge with text and pinned is a word, so neither depends on color.
Footer actions keep their own names and roles and are reached after the card's button.
All text wraps and grows with the font size setting; the button area is far above 48dp.
edgeCases: An excerpt that is empty after trimming is not shown.
A single word longer than the cut is cut at the limit.
Counts of zero are shown; pass null to hide a count.
Large counts use the locale's grouping, such as 1,204.
Many tags wrap onto new lines.

name: MonarchPreJoinLobby
title: PreJoinLobby
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column with BoxWithConstraints for the preview area; MonarchCallControls (Material 3 FilledIconToggleButton), MonarchAudioLevelMeter, MonarchAvatarGroup, MonarchBanner and MonarchButton. The camera preview is the app's (CameraX PreviewView through AndroidView) in a slot
summary: The screen before joining a call: the camera preview, the microphone level, device choice, the people already in the call, and joining with the microphone or camera off.
whenToUse: Before starting or joining an audio or video call, so people can check how they look and sound and choose their devices before anyone sees or hears them.
whenNotToUse: During the call, use MonarchCallControls and MonarchCallStage. To change devices in the middle of a call, use MonarchDevicePicker in a sheet. For an incoming call, the app posts a call notification (incoming-call).
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchPreJoinLobby(micOn: Boolean, onMicOnChange: (Boolean) -> Unit, onJoin: (micOn: Boolean, cameraOn: Boolean) -> Unit, icon: @Composable (control: MonarchCallControl, on: Boolean) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, cameraOn: Boolean = false, onCameraOnChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, audioLevel: Float = 0f, participants: List<MonarchPreJoinLobbyParticipant> = emptyList(), joining: Boolean = false, showTitle: Boolean = true, error: String? = null, joinLabel: String? = null, labels: MonarchPreJoinLobbyLabels = MonarchPreJoinLobbyLabels(), onCancel: (() -> Unit)? = null, devices: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, preview: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null)
class MonarchPreJoinLobbyParticipant(name: String, image: Painter? = null)

class MonarchPreJoinLobbyLabels(title: String? = null, preview: String? = null, cameraOff: String? = null, startingCamera: String? = null, noPreview: String? = null, micLevel: String? = null, muted: String? = null, participants: String? = null, alreadyIn: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, cancel: String? = null, join: String? = null, joining: String? = null, callControls: MonarchCallControlsLabels = MonarchCallControlsLabels())

options.name: micOn
options.description: Whether the person joins with the microphone on.

options.name: onMicOnChange
options.description: Receives the new microphone choice from the Microphone toggle.

options.name: onJoin
options.description: Joins with the chosen settings.

options.name: icon
options.description: Draws the glyph of the microphone and camera toggles for each state, as for MonarchCallControls. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the lobby.

options.name: cameraOn
options.description: Whether the person joins with the camera on; the preview shows the app's video only then.

options.name: onCameraOnChange
options.description: Shows the Camera toggle. Leave it out for audio-only calls.

options.name: audioLevel
options.description: The microphone loudness from 0 to 1, measured by the app, shown in a bar meter.

options.name: participants
options.description: The people already in the call: up to five small avatars, a +N tile and N already in the call.

options.name: joining
options.description: The join button shows progress and Joining… as its state; the toggles and Cancel are disabled.

options.name: showTitle
options.description: Shows the Join the call heading. Turn it off when the screen or dialog already has a title.

options.name: error
options.description: A problem getting the preview, shown in a danger MonarchBanner; the preview then says No preview.

options.name: joinLabel
options.description: The join button's text, such as Start call. Join now by default.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including the toggles' MonarchCallControlsLabels.

options.name: onCancel
options.description: Shows a Cancel button before the join button.

options.name: devices
options.description: The device choice, usually MonarchDevicePicker with the small size.

options.name: preview
options.description: The app's camera preview, shown while cameraOn is on; it fills the preview area.

states.name: camera off
states.description: The preview area, in the muted background, says Camera is off.

states.name: camera starting
states.description: The camera is on but the app gives no preview yet: Starting camera….

states.name: camera on
states.description: The app's preview fills the area, which is at least a 16:9 picture of the lobby's width.

states.name: microphone off
states.description: The meter is empty in the disabled color and reads Muted; the Microphone toggle reads Off.

states.name: error
states.description: A danger banner with the message, announced politely, and No preview in the preview area.

states.name: joining
states.description: The join button shows a progress indicator and Joining… for TalkBack; the toggles and Cancel are disabled.

states.name: audio only
states.description: Without onCameraOnChange there is no Camera toggle.

appearance: The preview area uses the muted background role with Monarch's container radius and muted text; the toggles, meter, avatars, banner and buttons keep their own roles (the join button is primary, Cancel is ghost). The same roles adapt to dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web lobby takes a MediaStream, draws the video itself and measures the microphone with the Web Audio API. On Android capturing needs the camera and microphone permissions and CameraX or a call SDK, which belong to the app, so the lobby takes the preview as a slot (a CameraX PreviewView through AndroidView) and the level as audioLevel. The web overlays the meter and toggles on the video; Android places them under the preview, so they never sit on uncontrolled video colors. The web passes device picker props; Android takes a devices slot for a MonarchDevicePicker, which keeps the device lists and permission states in one place. The web hides the meter while muted; Android keeps it and reads Muted. Joining calls back with two booleans instead of a settings object. The title is shown or hidden with showTitle instead of a null title. iOS has no entry for this id yet.
accessibility: The title is a heading.
The preview area is one element named Your camera preview, followed by its placeholder text.
The Microphone and Camera toggles are MonarchCallControls toggles: one name each, On or Off as their state, 48dp targets.
The meter is named Microphone level and reads its percentage, or Muted, as its state.
The people in the call are a MonarchAvatarGroup named People in the call, with the count written next to it.
The error is a MonarchBanner announced through a polite live region.
While joining, the join button announces Joining… as its state and ignores taps.
edgeCases: At the largest font scale the preview grows taller than 16:9 when its placeholder text needs it.
An error wins over the camera state: the preview says No preview even with the camera on.
A level outside 0 to 1 is limited to that range by the meter.
More than five people show five avatars and a +N tile.

examples.title: In a dialog
An audio-only call with access blocked
examples.code:
@OptIn(ExperimentalMonarchApi::class)
MonarchPreJoinLobby(
    micOn = false,
    onMicOnChange = {},
    onJoin = { _, _ -> },
    icon = { control, on ->
        val glyph = when (control) {
            MonarchCallControl.Microphone -> if (on) SampleIcons.Mic else SampleIcons.MicOff
            MonarchCallControl.Camera -> if (on) SampleIcons.Video else SampleIcons.VideoOff
            MonarchCallControl.ShareScreen -> SampleIcons.ScreenShare
            MonarchCallControl.RaiseHand -> SampleIcons.RaiseHand
            MonarchCallControl.React -> SampleIcons.React
            MonarchCallControl.More -> SampleIcons.More
            MonarchCallControl.Leave -> SampleIcons.CallEnd
        }
        MonarchIcon(glyph, contentDescription = null)
    },
    showTitle = false,
    error = "Microphone access is blocked. Allow it in Settings.",
    joinLabel = "Start call",
)

name: MonarchPresenceAvatars
title: PresenceAvatars
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.ModalBottomSheet and androidx.compose.material3.ListItem, with MonarchAvatarGroup and MonarchAvatar
summary: Who is here now: an overlapping stack of avatars with presence dots and a "+N" tile, opening a bottom sheet that lists everyone with their presence and activity.
whenToUse: In the header of a shared document, board or call, to show who else is here now and what they are doing.
whenNotToUse: Not for a static list of assignees or members; use MonarchAvatarGroup. Not for one person's presence; use MonarchAvatar with a status.

states.name: empty

appearance: Avatars with a ring in the surface color and presence dots in their presence colors; the "+N" tile on the muted background with muted text. In the list, names in the default text color and the second line in the muted text color, on the sheet's surface, in every theme.
platformNotes: The web opens a popover from the "+N" button and makes each avatar a button. On Android, as on iOS, overlapping 24dp avatars cannot each be a 48dp touch target, so the whole stack is one button that opens a Material 3 ModalBottomSheet, and people are chosen in that list. The callback keeps the web name onPersonClick, where iOS says onPersonTap. The web adds the initials shown on an avatar to the button's name for voice control; Android voice access reads the content description, which names each person in full. The presence words are the built-in strings of MonarchPresenceDot.
accessibility: A stack that does not open the list is a group named "5 people here"; its avatars are images named "Ana Silva, Online, Editing".

A stack that opens the list is one button named "6 people here: Ana Silva, Online, Editing; Ben Okafor, Away · In a meeting; …; 3 more", with the click action "Show everyone here" and a 48dp touch target.
Presence is always spoken with the custom status, so it never depends on the dot color.
In the list the title is a heading, each row is one element with the same text, and with onPersonClick each row is a button at least 48dp high.
Avatars and text grow with the font size setting; long names and activities wrap in the list.
edgeCases: An empty list of people draws nothing.
With one person more than maxVisible, every avatar is shown instead of a "+1" tile.
A maxVisible below zero shows the "+N" tile alone.
An activity that is empty or white space is left out.
Long names and activities wrap in the list; the list scrolls in the sheet.

name: MonarchPresenceDot
title: PresenceDot
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.Canvas with clearAndSetSemantics
summary: A small dot for a person's presence: online, away, busy, do not disturb or offline, read by TalkBack as text.
whenToUse: Beside a name or on an avatar, to show whether a person can be reached.
whenNotToUse: For the status of a thing rather than a person, such as a service or a job, use MonarchStatusDot or MonarchBadge.
api: @Composable fun MonarchPresenceDot(status: MonarchPresenceStatus, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, size: MonarchPresenceDotSize = MonarchPresenceDotSize.Md, customStatus: String? = null, overlay: Boolean = false, decorative: Boolean = false, statusLabel: String? = null)
enum class MonarchPresenceStatus { Online, Away, Busy, DoNotDisturb, Offline }
enum class MonarchPresenceDotSize { Sm, Md, Lg }

options.name: status
options.description: The presence to show.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the dot.

options.name: size
options.description: Sm 8dp, Md 10dp or Lg 12dp at the default font size.

options.name: customStatus
options.description: The person's own status message, added to the text TalkBack reads. Blank text is ignored.

options.name: overlay
options.description: Draws a 2dp ring in the surface color around the dot, for a dot on an avatar.

options.name: decorative
options.description: Hides the dot from TalkBack when nearby text says the same.

options.name: statusLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in name of the presence (monarch_presencedot_online and the others).

states.name: online
states.description: A dot in the success color.

states.name: away
states.description: A dot in the warning color; in the high-contrast themes a ring with its leading half filled.

states.name: busy
states.description: A dot in the danger color; in the high-contrast themes a square.

states.name: do not disturb
states.description: A dot in the danger color with a bar across it in every theme.

states.name: offline
states.description: A ring in the subtle text color on the surface color in every theme.

states.name: overlay
states.description: A 2dp ring in the surface color around the dot.

appearance: The solid status roles of the theme: success for online, warning for away, danger for busy and do not disturb, with the danger on-solid role for the bar. Offline is a ring in the subtle text role on the surface role. The same roles are used in light, dark and both high-contrast themes; the high-contrast themes add the half-filled and square forms.
platformNotes: The web gives each status its own shape only in forced-colors mode; Android does the same in the two Monarch high-contrast themes, the closest equivalent. The web positions an overlay dot itself; on Android place it in a Box with Modifier.align(Alignment.BottomEnd). The web's hover title has no counterpart on touch. The custom status is one string, as on iOS, where the web takes an emoji and a text. The parameter names follow Android (overlay, decorative) for the iOS isOverlay and isDecorative.
accessibility: The dot is one TalkBack element whose content description is its text, such as "Away · In a meeting".
Do not disturb has a bar and offline is a ring in every theme; in the high-contrast themes away is half-filled and busy is a square, so all five differ by form.
decorative removes the dot from the semantics tree when the presence is already in text beside it.
The dot grows with the font size setting.
The dot is not interactive and has no touch target.
edgeCases: A custom status of only white space is ignored; surrounding white space is trimmed.
In the standard themes online, away and busy differ by color only for sighted users; show the presence in text where it matters.
The half-filled away dot fills its leading half, so it mirrors in right-to-left layouts.
The overlay ring makes the dot 4dp wider than its size.

summary: The rows of an import file as the import will treat them: each row's number, outcome (ready, warning, error, duplicate), values and problems, with filter tabs and counts.
whenToUse: In an import flow, after the file is read and before anything is written, so people can see which rows will be imported, which will be skipped and why.
whenNotToUse: For records already stored, use a list or a table. For a summary of an import that has finished, use a result screen with counts.
api: @Composable fun MonarchPreviewRows(rows: List<MonarchPreviewRow>, columns: List<MonarchPreviewRowsColumn>, label: String, filter: MonarchPreviewRowStatus?, onFilterChange: (MonarchPreviewRowStatus?) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, filterable: Boolean = true, state: LazyListState = rememberLazyListState(), statusIcon: (@Composable (MonarchPreviewRowStatus) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchPreviewRowsLabels = MonarchPreviewRowsLabels())

class MonarchPreviewRow(row: Int, values: Map<String, String?>, status: MonarchPreviewRowStatus? = null, errors: List<MonarchPreviewRowIssue> = emptyList(), warnings: List<MonarchPreviewRowIssue> = emptyList(), note: String? = null) { val outcome: MonarchPreviewRowStatus }
class MonarchPreviewRowIssue(message: String, field: String? = null)
class MonarchPreviewRowsColumn(id: String, label: String, numeric: Boolean = false)
enum class MonarchPreviewRowStatus { Ready, Warning, Error, Duplicate }

class MonarchPreviewRowsLabels(filter: String? = null, all: String? = null, ready: String? = null, warning: String? = null, error: String? = null, duplicate: String? = null, row: ((row: Int) -> String)? = null, emptyTitle: String? = null, emptyMessage: String? = null, filteredTitle: String? = null, noValue: String? = null)

options.name: rows
options.description: The rows of the file: number, values by column id, errors, warnings, an optional status override and a note.

options.name: columns
options.description: The columns to show for each row, in order. numeric draws tabular figures.

options.name: label
options.description: The TalkBack name of the preview, for example "Preview of contacts.csv".

options.name: filter
options.description: The outcome shown, or null for every row.

options.name: onFilterChange
options.description: Called with the outcome chosen in the tabs, or null for All and for Clear filters.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the list. Give it a bounded height.

options.name: filterable
options.description: Shows the filter tabs when some row is not ready, or a filter is chosen.

options.name: state
options.description: The scroll state of the list.

options.name: statusIcon
options.description: An icon for each outcome, drawn in its badge. Monarch bundles no icons; the outcome is written either way.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the strings monarch_previewrows_*, including the status names and the row heading.

states.name: every row
states.description: The All tab is selected; each row shows its heading, outcome badge, values and problems.

states.name: filtered
states.description: Only rows with the chosen outcome; the tab of that outcome is selected.

states.name: filter matches nothing
states.description: A filtered MonarchEmptyState, "No rows with this result", with Clear filters.

states.name: no rows
states.description: A MonarchEmptyState, "No rows to preview", and no tabs.

states.name: all ready
states.description: No tabs: every row has the Ready badge.

appearance: Rows separated by subtle dividers. Each starts with "Row 4" in the label style and an outcome badge: success for Ready, warning for Warning, danger for Error, info for Duplicate. Field names and missing-value dashes are muted, errors use the strong danger color and warnings the strong warning color, notes are muted captions. The tabs are Material 3 secondary tabs with a count badge, danger for errors and warning for warnings. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web shows a DataTable on wide screens and cards on phones, with 50 rows per page; on Android every row is a card in a LazyColumn, which needs no pages. The web filter can be uncontrolled; on Android it is hoisted (filter and onFilterChange). Cell values are strings, not arbitrary nodes, and the note is text. The web draws a glyph for each outcome; Monarch for Android bundles no icons, so statusIcon is a slot and the outcome is written. The web exports previewRowStatus and countPreviewRows; on Android the outcome is MonarchPreviewRow.outcome. iOS has no entry yet; the names follow the web.
accessibility: The list is named by label; the tabs are named "Show rows".
Each row is one TalkBack element that reads its heading (marked as a heading), outcome, values and problems; a missing value is read as "No value".
Each problem is read with its kind first: "Error: Seats: Required".
The filter tabs have the Tab role, their selected state and a 48dp touch target, and read their name with the count.
The outcome is always written in the badge; color is never the only signal.
Values and problems wrap at the largest font size and the heading and badge follow the layout direction.
edgeCases: A chosen filter whose outcome has no rows keeps its tab, so it can still be seen as selected.
Row numbers are the keys of the lazy list, so they must be unique.
Values for columns that are not listed in columns are not shown.

name: MonarchPricingSection
title: PricingSection
wrapsNative: MonarchSegmentedControl, MonarchPlanCard, MonarchPricingTable
summary: A pricing band: a header, a billing period picker, one card per plan with its price, features and action, a note, and an optional feature comparison. Prices are shown exactly as given.
whenToUse: On a plans or upgrade screen that presents two to four plans with their features, and optionally compares them feature by feature.
whenNotToUse: For one plan, use MonarchPlanCard. For a comparison only, use MonarchPricingTable. An app that sells digital goods in an app store must follow that store's billing rules; this component only shows plans.

options.name: modifier

options.name: title

options.name: eyebrow

options.name: description
options.description: The muted line under the title.

options.name: periods
options.description: Billing periods; with two or more the period picker is shown. priceSuffix and priceNote are shown with the price.

options.name: period
options.description: The chosen period id. null lets the section keep its own choice, starting with the first.

options.name: onPeriodChange
options.description: Called with the period id the user chooses.

options.name: comparison
options.description: Features compared by plan id, shown under the cards as a MonarchPricingTable grid.

options.name: note
options.description: A muted line under the cards.

options.name: align
options.description: The header centred or at the start edge.

options.name: tone
options.description: No fill, or the subtle background.

options.name: comparisonTitle
options.description: The heading of the comparison. null uses "Compare plans".

options.name: billingPeriodLabel
options.description: The spoken name of the period picker. null uses "Billing period".

options.name: action
options.description: The call to action of each plan, normally a full-width MonarchButton.

states.name: period chosen
states.description: Each card shows the plan's price for the period with the period's suffix and note.

states.name: fallback price
states.description: A plan without a price for the period shows its price, such as "Contact us", without suffix or note.

states.name: highlighted plan
states.description: The card has the accent border and an accent badge.

states.name: with comparison
states.description: "Compare plans" and a grid of features by plan follow the note.

appearance: The header uses the strong accent for the eyebrow, the default text for the title and the muted colour for the description. The picker is MonarchSegmentedControl, the cards MonarchPlanCard and the comparison MonarchPricingTable, each in its own roles. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web PricingSection lays the cards side by side on wide screens and shows the comparison table with prices and actions in its header. On Android the cards are stacked so each plan stays readable on a phone and at large font sizes, and the comparison is the MonarchPricingTable grid without prices, since the cards above carry them; its columns are at least 152dp wide (scaled with the font size) and the grid scrolls sideways when it does not fit, as the web table does. Feature items are MonarchPlanCardFeature (label, hint, included).
accessibility: The title and plan names are headings; the band is a traversal group.
The period picker is named "Billing period"; its segments are radio buttons with 48dp touch targets.
A feature that is not included is read with "Not included:" through MonarchPlanCard.
Comparison cells are read as the plan, the feature and the value.
edgeCases: A period id that is not in periods falls back to the first period.
Prices are text; nothing is calculated or formatted.
On a phone the comparison usually scrolls sideways; the feature column is not pinned.

name: MonarchPricingTable
title: PricingTable
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.pager.HorizontalPager, androidx.compose.material3.SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow, MonarchPlanCard, androidx.compose.foundation.layout.BoxWithConstraints
summary: Plans compared feature by feature with a billing period picker: one plan per page with its features below on a phone, plans as columns and features as rows from 640dp wide. Prices are shown exactly as given.
whenToUse: On an upgrade or plans screen that compares two to five plans across the same features.
whenNotToUse: For one plan, or plans without a shared feature list, use MonarchPlanCard. An app that sells digital goods in an app store must follow that store's billing rules; this component only shows plans.
api: @Composable fun MonarchPricingTable(plans: List<MonarchPricingPlan>, features: List<MonarchPricingFeature>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, periods: List<MonarchPricingPeriod> = emptyList(), period: String? = null, onPeriodChange: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, layout: MonarchPricingTableLayout = MonarchPricingTableLayout.Automatic, showPrices: Boolean = true, showPeriodPicker: Boolean = true, includedIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchPricingTableLabels = MonarchPricingTableLabels(), action: (@Composable (plan: MonarchPricingPlan) -> Unit)? = null)

class MonarchPricingPlan(id: String, name: String, description: String? = null, prices: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(), price: String? = null, priceSuffix: String? = null, badge: String? = null, highlighted: Boolean = false, current: Boolean = false)
class MonarchPricingFeature(id: String, label: String, description: String? = null, group: String? = null, values: Map<String, MonarchPricingFeatureValue> = emptyMap())
sealed interface MonarchPricingFeatureValue { data object Included; data object NotIncluded; data class Text(val text: String) }
class MonarchPricingPeriod(id: String, label: String, suffix: String? = null, priceSuffix: String? = null, priceNote: String? = null)
enum class MonarchPricingTableLayout { Automatic, Paged, Grid }
class MonarchPricingTableLabels(caption: String? = null, included: String? = null, notIncluded: String? = null, currentPlan: String? = null, billingPeriod: String? = null, plan: String? = null)

options.name: plans
options.description: The plans in display order: id, name, description, prices per period, fallback price, price suffix, badge, highlighted and current flags.

options.name: features
options.description: The features: id, label, description, group and a value per plan id (Included, NotIncluded or Text). A plan missing from values does not have the feature.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the table.

options.name: periods
options.description: Billing periods; with two or more the period picker is shown.

options.name: period
options.description: The chosen period id. null lets the table keep its own choice, starting with the first period.

options.name: onPeriodChange
options.description: Called with the id of the period the user chooses.

options.name: layout
options.description: Automatic (the grid from 640dp wide below font scale 1.3, pages otherwise), Paged or Grid.

options.name: showPrices
options.description: Whether prices are shown.

options.name: showPeriodPicker
options.description: Whether the period picker is shown; false when the screen shows its own.

options.name: includedIcon
options.description: A mark for an included feature, such as a check. Without it the word "Included" is shown. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for "Plan comparison", "Included", "Not included", "Current plan", "Billing period" and "Plan".

options.name: action
options.description: The call to action of each plan, normally one MonarchButton.

states.name: paged
states.description: A plan picker (segmented buttons), then one page per plan: a MonarchPlanCard with price, badges and action, and the plan's features grouped below with the included mark or word, a dash or the text.

states.name: grid
states.description: A header per plan with badges, name, price, description and action, then group headings and one row per feature with a cell per plan.

states.name: highlighted plan
states.description: A solid badge and the highlighted MonarchPlanCard on a page; a 2dp accent border around the grid header.

states.name: current plan
states.description: An outlined "Current plan" badge.

states.name: fallback price
states.description: A plan without a price for the period shows its price, such as "Contact us", without the period's suffix and note.

appearance: Plan pages use MonarchPlanCard. Grid headers have the default border, or a 2dp accent border when highlighted, with the plan name in the subheading style, the price in the heading style and the suffix, note and description in the muted caption color. Feature labels use the body style, descriptions the muted caption color, a dash the subtle text color, and rows are separated by subtle-border lines. The pickers are Material 3 segmented buttons in the MonarchTheme colors. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web PricingTable is one table that scrolls sideways on narrow screens with the feature column pinned, and exports BillingPeriodToggle and helpers. On Android, as on iOS, a phone shows one plan per page (a HorizontalPager) with a plan picker, so the comparison stays readable at large font sizes, and the grid is used from 640dp wide (the width the table is given, not the window) below font scale 1.3. The period picker is a Material 3 single-choice segmented button row; the period's suffix is a line under it rather than inside the segment, as on iOS. The web's caption and hideCaption are the table's spoken name only. Names and parameters follow iOS: MonarchPricingPlan, MonarchPricingFeature, MonarchPricingFeatureValue, MonarchPricingPeriod, MonarchPricingTableLayout, MonarchPricingTableLabels; iOS's isPriceShown and isPeriodPickerShown are showPrices and showPeriodPicker, and the binding is period with onPeriodChange. Feature cells take Included, NotIncluded or Text rather than any node. The included check is a slot because Monarch bundles no icons; without it the word "Included" is shown.
accessibility: The table is a traversal group named "Plan comparison" (or labels.caption); the pickers are named "Billing period" and "Plan".
Picker segments have the RadioButton role, show a check mark when chosen and have touch targets of at least 48dp; they follow the layout direction.
On a page each feature is one element read as its name, its value and its description, such as "Single sign-on, Included, SAML and OIDC".
In the grid each cell is one element read as the plan, the feature and the value, such as "Team, Single sign-on: Included".
Group titles are headings, and plan names are headings through MonarchPlanCard on pages.
Checks and dashes are not read; the words carry the value, so nothing depends on color or shape alone.
Feature text wraps at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: More than five plans make grid columns narrow; use pages or fewer plans.
Pages can differ in height; content under the pager moves when a taller page is shown.
Segmented pickers share the width, so long period or plan names wrap; keep them short.
A period id that is not in periods falls back to the first period.
Swiping between pages with TalkBack was not tried on a device; the plan picker is the way to change page without swiping.

title: PriorityPicker
wrapsNative: MonarchButton (androidx.compose.material3.Button) or androidx.compose.material3.IconButton with androidx.compose.material3.DropdownMenu and DropdownMenuItem; androidx.compose.foundation.Canvas for the level shapes
summary: A menu button that shows and changes how urgent an issue is, on the urgent, high, medium, low and no-priority scale, where every level has its own shape and name.
whenToUse: For the priority of an issue, a ticket or a task in a form, a detail panel or a list row; use MonarchPriorityGlyph alone where the priority is shown but not changed.
whenNotToUse: For a scale the product defines itself use MonarchRolePicker or a Material 3 ExposedDropdownMenuBox. For a status use MonarchStatusBadge.
api: @Composable fun MonarchPriorityPicker(value: MonarchPriorityLevel?, onValueChange: (MonarchPriorityLevel) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, size: MonarchPriorityPickerSize = MonarchPriorityPickerSize.Md, levels: List<MonarchPriorityLevel> = MonarchPriorityLevel.entries, showLabel: Boolean = true, enabled: Boolean = true, trailingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchPriorityPickerLabels = MonarchPriorityPickerLabels(), interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null, initiallyOpen: Boolean = false)
@Composable fun MonarchPriorityGlyph(level: MonarchPriorityLevel, modifier: Modifier = Modifier)
enum class MonarchPriorityLevel(val number: Int) { Urgent, High, Medium, Low, None; companion object { fun fromNumber(number: Int?): MonarchPriorityLevel } }
enum class MonarchPriorityPickerSize { Sm, Md }
class MonarchPriorityPickerLabels(trigger: ((String) -> String)? = null, urgent: String? = null, high: String? = null, medium: String? = null, low: String? = null, none: String? = null)

options.name: value
options.description: The current level; null shows No priority.

options.name: onValueChange
options.description: Called with the level the person chooses. Choosing the current level only closes the menu.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the trigger.

options.name: size
options.description: Sm for a dense row, Md for a form. The touch target is 48dp at both sizes.

options.name: levels
options.description: The levels offered, in menu order.

options.name: showLabel
options.description: Shows the level's name next to its shape. false gives a shape-only icon button, still named.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the menu can be opened.

options.name: trailingIcon
options.description: A decorative icon after the name, such as a down chevron. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for "Priority: %s" and the five level names.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the trigger's press and focus interactions.

options.name: level
options.description: MonarchPriorityGlyph: the level whose shape is drawn, 14dp by default.

states.name: levels
states.description: Urgent: a filled tile with an exclamation mark in the strong danger color. High, medium, low: three, two or one filled bars of three (high in the strong warning color). No priority: three dashes in the muted color.

states.name: menu open
states.description: A Material 3 dropdown menu with each level's shape and name; the current level is selected and has a radio button.

states.name: shape only
states.description: An icon button with the shape; the name stays in what TalkBack reads.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The button's disabled colors; the menu does not open.

appearance: The trigger is a secondary MonarchButton with the level's shape and name. Shapes use the strong danger color for urgent, the strong warning color for high, the default text color for medium and low and the muted text color for no priority; bars that are not filled are outlined in the strong border color. High contrast themes use their stronger roles.
platformNotes: The web draws the empty bars as the mark color at 45% opacity; Monarch never dims with alpha, so they are outlined in the strong border color. The web's priorityFromNumber and priorityToNumber are MonarchPriorityLevel.fromNumber and number. The web's PriorityGlyph is MonarchPriorityGlyph. The shapes are drawn on a Canvas from the web's 14-unit grid; they are part of the component, not an icon set. iOS documents this entry as the system menu Picker with SF Symbols and ships no type; Android builds it, because a Material 3 menu takes any composable as an item's icon, so the web's shapes can be kept.
accessibility: The trigger has the drop-down list role and is read as "Priority: High".
In the menu each level is read by name; the current one has the selected state and a radio button.
The shapes are hidden from TalkBack; each level has its own shape and name, so the priority never depends on color alone.
The trigger has a touch target of at least 48dp at both sizes, with or without the name.
The name scales with the font size setting without being cut.
edgeCases: value null and MonarchPriorityLevel.None look and read the same.
Offer a subset of levels with levels; the current level is still shown on the trigger even when it is not offered.
fromNumber maps any number other than 0 to 4 to None.
The bars do not mirror right to left, as on the web: they rise from start to end in every direction.

title: PrivacyChoicesLink
wrapsNative: MonarchBottomSheet with androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column, MonarchLink, MonarchSwitchRow and MonarchButton
summary: A recipe, not a component: a "Your privacy choices" link in settings that opens a sheet with one switch to allow or stop the sale or sharing of personal information.
whenToUse: In settings, for people in regions where they may opt out of the sale or sharing of their personal information (opt-out regimes such as the California rules).
whenNotToUse: Where consent is asked before any optional use (opt-in regimes), ask with full consent preferences (MonarchMarketingConsentCheckbox, MonarchSwitchSettingsList) instead. For the Android advertising ID, the system setting applies; this switch does not replace it.
api: MonarchLink(text = "Your privacy choices", onClick = { draft = allowed; open = true }, variant = MonarchLinkVariant.Standalone)
MonarchBottomSheet(onDismissRequest = { open = false }, title = "Your privacy choices", description = …) { … }
MonarchSwitchRow(checked = draft && !locked, onCheckedChange = { draft = it }, label = "Allow sale or sharing", enabled = !locked, description = …)
MonarchLink(text = "Privacy policy", onClick = { uriHandler.openUri(policyUrl) }, external = true)
MonarchButton(text = "Save", onClick = { allowed = draft; open = false }, variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Primary)

options.name: allowed
options.description: The stored choice, kept by the app with the account.

options.name: draft
options.description: The switch while the sheet is open; reset from the stored choice each time it opens.

options.name: locked
options.description: The account carries an opt-out signal the app knows of, such as Global Privacy Control from its website: the switch is off and disabled and says why.

options.name: policyUrl
options.description: The privacy policy, opened with LocalUriHandler.

states.name: hidden
states.description: Outside opt-out regions the link is not shown; the region check is the app's.

states.name: open
states.description: A sheet with a heading, what sale or sharing means, the switch with its help line, the policy link, and Cancel and Save.

states.name: locked by signal
states.description: With a known opt-out signal the switch is off and disabled and its description says why.

states.name: saved
states.description: Save stores the switch; Cancel and dismissing the sheet leave the stored choice unchanged.

appearance: Every part is an existing Monarch component: a standalone link, a Material 3 sheet on the surface background, a heading, a MonarchSwitchRow and ghost and primary buttons. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web's PrivacyChoicesLink is a footer link component with a dialog and its own strings. On Android, as on iOS, it is a recipe: a settings link opening a MonarchBottomSheet, the usual place for a setting on a phone. A native app receives no browser Global Privacy Control header, so the lock applies only when the app knows of a signal for the account (for example from its website); otherwise leave it out. The web's showIn regimes are the app's own region check. The official California privacy choices icon is the app's to add as an image in the link's trailingIcon; Monarch bundles no icons.
accessibility: The link is a MonarchLink with the link role and a 48dp target.
The switch is a MonarchSwitchRow: one element read as "Allow sale or sharing" with its state and description, so a locked switch also reads why.
The sheet's heading has the heading semantics.
The policy link is an external MonarchLink, read with "opens in the browser".
Cancel and Save are MonarchButtons with 48dp targets.
edgeCases: Show the link only where the opt-out applies, decided by the app's region logic.
Opening the sheet starts from the stored choice, so a cancelled change does not linger.
A signal lock keeps sale and sharing off whatever was stored before.

title: Progress
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.LinearProgressIndicator, CircularProgressIndicator
summary: A progress indicator as a bar or a ring, determinate or indeterminate.
whenToUse: While the app works on something for more than about a second, and for quotas and completion.
whenNotToUse: For the loading state of a button use the loading parameter of MonarchButton.
api: @Composable fun MonarchProgress(modifier: Modifier = Modifier, progress: Float? = null, variant: MonarchProgressVariant = MonarchProgressVariant.Linear, label: String? = null, tone: MonarchTone = MonarchTone.Accent, size: MonarchProgressSize = MonarchProgressSize.Md, showValue: Boolean = false)
enum class MonarchProgressVariant { Linear, Circular }
enum class MonarchProgressSize { Sm, Md, Lg }

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the component.

options.name: progress
options.description: The completed fraction from 0 to 1; null when the duration is unknown. Clamped.

options.name: variant
options.description: Linear or Circular.

options.name: label
options.description: What is in progress, for TalkBack. Indeterminate without a label is named "Loading" (monarch_progress_loading).

options.name: tone
options.description: The color of the indicator: the accent, or a status tone for quotas and checks. Keep the meaning in text too.

options.name: size
options.description: The bar thickness (4, 8, 12dp) or ring diameter (24, 40, 64dp).

options.name: showValue
options.description: Writes the percentage after the bar or small ring, inside a large ring. Determinate only; read once, from the indicator.

states.name: determinate
states.description: The indicator shows the fraction.

states.name: indeterminate
states.description: The indicator animates without a value.

appearance: The indicator is the tone's solid color (the accent by default; neutral uses the strong border) and the track the emphasis background, in every theme.
platformNotes: One component covers the web's Progress and Spinner and iOS's MonarchProgressViewStyle. The Material 3 gap and stop indicator of the linear bar are kept. Stacked segments are not offered yet.

name: MonarchProgress
title: ProgressCircle
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.CircularProgressIndicator
summary: A progress ring, determinate or indeterminate: MonarchProgress with variant = Circular.
whenToUse: For progress in a small area, such as a list row, a card or an upload tile; with a progress value when the fraction is known.
whenNotToUse: For progress across the width of a page or a step in a flow, use MonarchProgress with the Linear variant. Inside a button, use MonarchButton(loading = true).
api: @Composable fun MonarchProgress(modifier: Modifier = Modifier, progress: Float? = null, variant: MonarchProgressVariant = MonarchProgressVariant.Linear, label: String? = null, tone: MonarchTone = MonarchTone.Accent, size: MonarchProgressSize = MonarchProgressSize.Md, showValue: Boolean = false)
enum class MonarchProgressVariant { Linear, Circular }
enum class MonarchProgressSize { Sm, Md, Lg }

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the ring. A size here sets the diameter.

options.name: progress
options.description: The completed fraction from 0 to 1; null spins indeterminately. Clamped.

options.name: variant
options.description: Circular for the ring.

options.name: label
options.description: What is in progress, for TalkBack. Indeterminate without a label is named "Loading" (monarch_progress_loading); determinate without a label has no name.

options.name: tone
options.description: The color of the indicator: the accent, or a status tone for quotas and checks. Keep the meaning in text too.

options.name: size
options.description: The bar thickness (4, 8, 12dp) or ring diameter (24, 40, 64dp).

options.name: showValue
options.description: Writes the percentage after the bar or small ring, inside a large ring. Determinate only; read once, from the indicator.

states.name: determinate
states.description: The arc covers the completed fraction, clamped to 0 through 1.

states.name: complete
states.description: A full ring at 1.

states.name: indeterminate
states.description: An arc that turns; with animations removed in the system settings it does not move.

appearance: The arc is the solid accent color on a track in the emphasis background, in every theme. The Material 3 ring is 40dp across with a 4dp stroke.
platformNotes: No separate type: the web ProgressCircle is MonarchProgress with variant = Circular, as the plan expected. The web size (xs to xl), tone and showValue options are not offered by MonarchProgress today: the ring is the Material 3 size unless the modifier sets one, always in the accent color, and the value is not drawn in the middle; show it as text beside the ring. Adding those to MonarchProgress is a change to an existing component and is left for its owner. iOS ships a separate ring style, MonarchCircularProgressViewStyle. The web formatValue and locale options have no equivalent: TalkBack reads the fraction as a percentage in the device locale.
accessibility: A determinate ring is a progress bar with its fraction, which TalkBack reads as a percentage.
The label is the content description; an indeterminate ring without a label is named "Loading".
A determinate ring without a label has no name: give it one that says what is in progress.
Not a live region; announce the start and end of long work in text if it matters.
edgeCases: Values below 0 or above 1 are clamped.
The color is always the accent; a quota near its limit is not shown in the danger color, so say it in the label or beside the ring.

title: PromptDialog
wrapsNative: MonarchDialog (androidx.compose.material3.BasicAlertDialog with a Monarch panel) with a MonarchTextField in its content
summary: Asking for one value is a MonarchDialog with a MonarchTextField in its content, which shows helper and error text. Monarch ships no prompt type.
whenToUse: To ask for one short value in the middle of a task: a name for a new folder, a new title, an email to invite.
whenNotToUse: For more than one or two fields use a Dialog or a screen with a form. For a value the person picks from a list use choice-dialog.
api: @Composable fun MonarchDialog(onDismissRequest: () -> Unit, title: String?, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, description: String? = null, dismissible: Boolean = true, dismissOnClickOutside: Boolean = dismissible, paneTitle: String? = null, actions: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null, content: (@Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)? = null)

@Composable fun MonarchTextField(value: String, onValueChange: (String) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, label: String? = null, placeholder: String? = null, helperText: String? = null, errorText: String? = null, enabled: Boolean = true, readOnly: Boolean = false, singleLine: Boolean = true, …, keyboardOptions: KeyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions.Default, keyboardActions: KeyboardActions = KeyboardActions.Default, …)

states.name: empty
states.description: The confirm button is disabled until the value is valid.

states.name: invalid
states.description: The field shows errorText, which TalkBack reads with the field.

states.name: keyboard
states.description: The field takes focus when the dialog opens and the keyboard's Done key confirms.

states.name: pending
states.description: The confirm button is loading and dismissal is turned off while the value is saved.

appearance: MonarchDialog in the raised background role; the field is a MonarchTextField with the input border role, the strong accent role when focused and the danger roles for an error. The high-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colors.
platformNotes: The web PromptDialog validates (required, maxLength, url and email types, a validate function), shows an error, stays open while an async save is pending, has a multiline mode and offers usePrompt, which returns a promise. On Android all of this is app code around MonarchDialog: errorText on MonarchTextField, KeyboardOptions(keyboardType = KeyboardType.Email) for the input type, singleLine = false for multiline, and a loading MonarchButton for pending. A promise-style call is a suspendCancellableCoroutine in the app. iOS uses the system alert with a TextField, which closes when a button is tapped.
accessibility: The field has a visible label, which TalkBack reads with its value, helper text and error.
Focus moves to the field when the dialog opens, so the keyboard is ready.
The error is text, not only the red border.
Done on the keyboard confirms, so the value can be entered without reaching for the button.
edgeCases: Request focus after the dialog is shown (LaunchedEffect), not during composition.
Validate on confirm as well as while typing; a pasted value can bypass a length limit set only in onValueChange.

name: MonarchProseStyle
title: Prose
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.ui.text.TextStyle and androidx.compose.ui.text.TextLinkStyles for androidx.compose.material3.Text with AnnotatedString content, laid out by MonarchProse in an androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
summary: Type styles for long-form content (help articles, release notes, rendered Markdown, comments and documents): a base size, a reading measure, the look of each kind of block and the styling of links inside text, with MonarchProse to lay the blocks out.
whenToUse: For text the app does not lay out element by element: release notes, help articles, Markdown from a comment or a CMS, after the app's renderer has split it into blocks.
whenNotToUse: For interface text use MonarchText with a type role. For a single code fragment in a sentence use MonarchInlineCodeStyle; for a code block with copy and line numbers use MonarchCodeBlock. For HTML use a WebView: Monarch renders no HTML.
api: class MonarchProseStyle(size: MonarchProseSize = MonarchProseSize.Md, limitLineLength: Boolean = true) { @Composable fun bodyStyle(): TextStyle; @Composable fun headingStyle(level: Int): TextStyle; @Composable fun linkStyles(): TextLinkStyles }
enum class MonarchProseSize { Sm, Md, Lg }
@Composable fun MonarchProse(modifier: Modifier = Modifier, style: MonarchProseStyle = MonarchProseStyle(), content: MonarchProseScope.() -> Unit)

interface MonarchProseScope { fun heading(text: AnnotatedString, level: Int = 2); fun heading(text: String, level: Int = 2); fun paragraph(text: AnnotatedString); fun paragraph(text: String); fun listItem(text: AnnotatedString, marker: String? = null, depth: Int = 0); fun listItem(text: String, marker: String? = null, depth: Int = 0); fun quote(text: AnnotatedString); fun code(text: String); fun caption(text: String); fun rule() }

options.name: size
options.description: The base size: Sm (14sp) for comments, chat and side panels, Md (16sp) for documents, Lg (18sp) for long reads. Headings, code and spacing are multiples of it.

options.name: limitLineLength
options.description: Limits the column to the reading measure, 42 base sizes (672dp at Md and the default font size), at the start edge. Turn it off when the container already sets the width.

options.name: modifier
options.description: MonarchProse: the modifier of the column.

options.name: style
options.description: MonarchProse: the base size and the measure.

options.name: content
options.description: MonarchProse: adds the blocks in reading order with heading, paragraph, listItem, quote, code, caption and rule.

options.name: level
options.description: heading and headingStyle: 1 to 6, clamped. Level 1 is 1.875 times the base size; level 6 is the base size in the muted color.

options.name: marker
options.description: listItem: a number or letter such as "2.", read by TalkBack; null draws a bullet, which TalkBack skips.

options.name: depth
options.description: listItem: the nesting level; each level indents by 1.5 base sizes and nested bullets are rings.

states.name: default
states.description: Prose has no states of its own. Links keep the behavior of their LinkAnnotation; code blocks scroll sideways.

appearance: Running text in the default text color with relaxed leading; semibold headings with tight or snug leading; list markers and quotations in the muted color with a strong border bar at the start of a quotation; code blocks in the code face on the subtle background with a subtle border; rules in the subtle border color. Links use the link color and are underlined. High contrast themes use their stronger roles.
platformNotes: The parity map named MonarchTypography as the type; MonarchTypography holds the nine interface type roles and has no long-form styles, so this entry adds MonarchProseStyle, the name iOS uses, with MonarchProse to space the blocks. The web Prose styles HTML elements by tag; on Android the app's renderer (or the app) says which kind each block is through MonarchProseScope, and the inline parts (links, bold, inline code) are runs of an AnnotatedString, styled with linkStyles() and MonarchInlineCodeStyle. Rendering HTML and parsing Markdown are out of scope. Compose has no heading levels in its semantics, so every heading is a heading to TalkBack without its level. Not offered: tables, images, figures, definition lists, details and keyboard keys inside prose (use Material 3 and MonarchKbd directly), ProseExclude (other composables placed next to MonarchProse keep their own styles) and the as parameter. The web's base size is called Md, following the shared size vocabulary.
accessibility: A heading has heading semantics, so TalkBack's heading navigation moves through the document.
Each block is its own element, so TalkBack reads the content block by block.
A bullet is hidden from TalkBack; a numbered or lettered marker is read with its item as one element.
The quotation bar and rules are hidden from TalkBack.
Every size is in sp and spacing follows the font size, so prose scales with the font size setting and text wraps; code blocks scroll sideways instead.
Code blocks read left to right in a right-to-left layout; everything else follows the layout direction.
edgeCases: Heading levels outside 1 to 6 are clamped.
Long words wrap inside the column; long code lines scroll inside their block.
MonarchProse does not scroll; place it in a scrolling container or a LazyColumn item.
A negative list depth counts as 0.
Links need a LinkAnnotation with linkStyles() in the AnnotatedString; plain text in paragraph(String) has no links.

name: MonarchProvenance
title: Provenance
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row, androidx.compose.material3.Text, android.text.format.DateUtils.getRelativeTimeSpanString
summary: Where a value came from and how fresh it is, such as "Registry · 2 hours ago".
whenToUse: Next to any value the product did not get from the user: data from a registry, an import or a calculation, so people can judge how far to trust it.
whenNotToUse: For the freshness of a whole data set with a refresh button, use MonarchFreshnessIndicator. For an AI-generated value, use MonarchAiGeneratedBadge.
api: @Composable fun MonarchProvenance(source: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchProvenanceVariant = MonarchProvenanceVariant.Chip, checkedAt: Long? = null, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, onClick: (() -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchProvenanceLabels = MonarchProvenanceLabels())
enum class MonarchProvenanceVariant { Chip, Inline }
class MonarchProvenanceLabels(source: ((source: String) -> String)? = null, checked: ((time: String) -> String)? = null)

options.name: source
options.description: Where the value came from, already localised. Nothing is drawn when it is empty.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the note.

options.name: variant
options.description: Chip is a small bordered tag; Inline is plain muted text.

options.name: checkedAt
options.description: When the value was fetched, checked or computed, in epoch milliseconds (UTC); shown as relative time and redrawn every minute.

options.name: icon
options.description: A decorative icon before the text. Hidden from TalkBack.

options.name: onClick
options.description: Makes the note a button that opens the source record. The app navigates.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the spoken "Source: …" (monarch_provenance_source) and "checked …" (monarch_provenance_checked).

states.name: with time
states.description: The source, a middle dot and the relative time.

states.name: without time
states.description: The source only.

states.name: opens the source
states.description: The source in the link color and underlined; the note is a button with a 48dp touch target.

appearance: Caption text in the muted text color. The chip adds the subtle background and the subtle border with small rounded corners; the inline form has neither. When it opens the source, the source takes the link color and an underline. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web shows the absolute time in a tooltip on hover and focus; touch has no hover, so TalkBack reads the relative time that is shown, as on iOS. The web source can be any content; here it is text. The web href turns the source into a link; components do not navigate on Android, so onClick makes the whole note a button and the app opens the record. Dates are epoch milliseconds, formatted with DateUtils because java.time needs API 26. iOS shares the name and the variants.
accessibility: The note is one TalkBack element read as "Source: Registry, checked 2 hours ago"; the icon and the middle dot are hidden.
With onClick the note has the button role and a touch target of at least 48dp, reserved in the layout.
The link state is shown by an underline as well as the color.
The text wraps at the largest font size instead of being cut off.
edgeCases: An empty source draws nothing.
A time in the future reads as "in 5 minutes".
The relative time is redrawn once a minute while the note is on screen.
