parityExceptions.reason: The web underlines the age ("2 hours ago") with a dotted line because hovering it shows the absolute time in a tooltip. Touch has no hover, so the dotted line would suggest a tap target that does not exist.
parityExceptions.convention: Material guidance: no hover tooltips on touch; do not mark non-interactive text as interactive

name: MonarchQueryBuilder
title: QueryBuilder
wrapsNative: Nested androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column groups, each with an androidx.compose.material3.SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow for AND / OR and a MonarchConditionEditor for its rules; MonarchButton for Add group
summary: Builds a filter query from AND / OR groups of field, operator and value rules, nested to a set depth.
whenToUse: For an advanced filter or a saved segment where people combine rules with AND and OR, such as "open and (amount at least 500 or flagged)".
whenNotToUse: For one flat list of conditions with all / any, use MonarchConditionEditor. For everyday list filtering, use filter chips or a filter sheet, which people expect on a phone.
api: @Composable fun MonarchQueryBuilder(value: MonarchQueryGroup, onValueChange: (MonarchQueryGroup) -> Unit, fields: List<MonarchConditionField>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, maxDepth: Int = 3, maxRulesPerGroup: Int = 20, showErrors: Boolean = false, enabled: Boolean = true, createId: (() -> String)? = null, removeIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, addIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchQueryBuilderLabels = MonarchQueryBuilderLabels(), ruleLabels: MonarchConditionEditorLabels = MonarchConditionEditorLabels())

data class MonarchQueryGroup(id: String, combinator: MonarchQueryCombinator = MonarchQueryCombinator.And, rules: List<MonarchCondition> = emptyList(), groups: List<MonarchQueryGroup> = emptyList()) { fun allRules(): List<MonarchCondition>; fun problems(fields: List<MonarchConditionField>): Map<String, MonarchConditionProblem>; fun matches(values: Map<String, Any?>): Boolean }
enum class MonarchQueryCombinator { And, Or }

class MonarchQueryBuilderLabels(label: String? = null, group: ((path: List<Int>) -> String)? = null, combinatorBefore: String? = null, and: String? = null, or: String? = null, combinatorLabel: ((group: String) -> String)? = null, rule: ((position: Int) -> String)? = null, removeRule: ((group: String, position: Int) -> String)? = null, addRule: String? = null, addGroup: String? = null, removeGroup: ((group: String) -> String)? = null, remove: String? = null, emptyGroup: String? = null, maxDepthReached: String? = null)

options.name: value
options.description: The query: the top group. Group and rule ids must be unique across the query.

options.name: onValueChange
options.description: Called with the whole new query after every change.

options.name: fields
options.description: The fields a rule can test, as in MonarchConditionEditor. Without fields, Add rule and Add group are disabled.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the builder.

options.name: maxDepth
options.description: How many levels of groups are allowed, counting the top group. At the deepest level a note replaces Add group; 1 turns sub-groups off.

options.name: maxRulesPerGroup
options.description: The most rules in one group; at the limit the group's Add rule becomes a note.

options.name: showErrors
options.description: Shows what is missing on each incomplete rule, for example after a submit attempt.

options.name: enabled
options.description: When false nothing can change: switches, menus, inputs and buttons are disabled.

options.name: createId
options.description: Makes the id of a new rule or group. By default the first q-<n> no group or rule in the query has.

options.name: removeIcon
options.description: The icon of each remove button. Monarch bundles no icons; without it the buttons read "Remove".

options.name: addIcon
options.description: An icon before Add rule and Add group.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the builder's strings: group names, the switch, rule headings, remove names, add buttons and notes.

options.name: ruleLabels
options.description: Replacements for the rule editors' strings, such as operator names, problems and the Field, Operator and Value labels.

states.name: empty group
states.description: "No rules in this group." above Add rule.

states.name: rules
states.description: Each rule is a MonarchConditionEditor card headed "Rule 1", with field, operator and value one per line.

states.name: nested
states.description: Sub-groups follow the rules inside their parent, indented and on the alternate fill, each with its own switch, rules and remove button.

states.name: deepest level
states.description: "Groups cannot be nested any deeper." replaces Add group.

states.name: errors
states.description: With showErrors, incomplete rules show their problem as in MonarchConditionEditor.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Everything takes its disabled colors and does nothing.

appearance: Groups are cards with the default border; levels alternate between the subtle and the muted fill so nesting reads without indentation lines. Group names use the subheading style, the join text and notes the muted text color, and rules are MonarchConditionEditor cards. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those roles.
platformNotes: The web shows rules as rows of field, operator and value side by side; on Android each rule is a card with one control per line, and nesting is shown by cards inside cards with alternating fills. Rule headings are "Rule 1" under the group's heading instead of the web's "Top group, rule 1" accessible names; remove buttons keep the group in their names. Rules share the types of MonarchConditionEditor (MonarchCondition, MonarchConditionField), as on the web. The web moves focus after a removal; Compose leaves focus to the system. The web's messages and conditionMessages are labels and ruleLabels. Same name as iOS's plan; iOS has not built it yet.
accessibility: The builder is named "Query"; group names and rule titles are headings, so TalkBack can move through the structure by heading.
Each group's AND / OR switch is a Material 3 segmented button row named after the group ("Top group combinator"), with the chosen segment read as selected.
Remove buttons name what they remove ("Remove Group 1", "Remove rule 1 of Top group") and have 48dp touch targets.
Problems are set on the rule controls as text, as in MonarchConditionEditor.
edgeCases: Deep nesting narrows the controls: keep maxDepth at 3 or less on phones.
A query loaded from storage keeps its ids; generated ids skip every id already in the query.
An empty group matches every record in matches, as on the web.
Evaluation is for previews only; the server stays the authority.

parityExceptions.reason: The web draws a condition as one row: field, operator, value and remove, about 520px wide in the docs window. A phone window of 392dp leaves 344dp for the row (24dp margins). One row needs the field picker at 120dp, the operator picker at 120dp, the value at 96dp, the remove button at 48dp and three 8dp gaps, 408dp, which does not fit. summary: One choice shown as selectable cards, each with a title and an optional description, icon and meta text.
whenToUse: For one choice between a few options that need more than a label to compare, such as plans, shipping speeds or workspace types.
whenNotToUse: For a plain list of short options use MonarchRadioRow in a selectableGroup. For several choices at once use MonarchCheckboxRow. For two to five short options in one line use Material 3 segmented buttons.
api: @Composable fun <T> MonarchRadioCardGroup(options: List<MonarchRadioCardOption<T>>, selected: T?, onSelect: (T) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, label: String? = null, columns: Int = 1, enabled: Boolean = true)

options.name: options
options.description: The cards, in order: value, title, and optional description, meta text, icon and enabled.

options.name: selected
options.description: The value of the chosen card, or null for no choice yet.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Called with the value of the card the user chooses.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the group.

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label of the group.

options.name: columns
options.description: Cards per row, from 1 to 3, on windows at least 640dp wide. Narrower windows and font scales of 1.5 or more use one column.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether any card can be chosen. MonarchRadioCardOption.enabled disables one card.

states.name: unselected
states.description: A surface-coloured card with the default border and an empty radio mark.

states.name: selected
states.description: The accent subtle fill, a 2dp accent strong border, the icon in the accent strong color and a filled radio mark.

states.name: pressed
states.description: The Material ripple over the card.

states.name: focused
states.description: The Monarch focus ring around the card.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The subtle background, the subtle border and the disabled text color, for one card or the whole group.

appearance: Cards have large corners. Unselected cards use the surface color and the default border; the selected card uses the accent subtle fill and a 2dp accent strong border; disabled cards use the subtle background, the subtle border and disabled text. Titles are in the default text color, descriptions and meta text in the muted color. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web builds on its RadioGroup and shows a radio in each card, as Android does with the Material 3 RadioButton; iOS has no radio button and draws its own mark. The value is a generic T instead of the web's string. The web stacks to one column under 40rem of container width; Android uses the width given to the group (one column under 640dp) and also stacks at font scales of 1.5 and above, like iOS at the accessibility text sizes. The web's invalid state and form name are not offered. Icons are a slot because Monarch bundles no icons.
accessibility: The cards are in one selectableGroup, so TalkBack announces their position in the group.
Each card is one element with the RadioButton role: the title, the meta text and the description are read together, and the chosen card is read as selected.
The selection is also a filled radio mark and a heavier border, not color alone.
The whole card is the touch target and is at least 48dp high; it draws the Monarch focus ring.
The icon is hidden from TalkBack.
Text wraps at font scale 2.0, and the cards stack in one column from font scale 1.5.
edgeCases: Two options with the same value are both shown as selected; keep values unique.
Cards in one row take the height of the tallest card.
A selected value that is not in options leaves every card unselected.

appearance: Tiles use the surface color, muted text and the default border; the chosen tile the accent subtle fill, default text and the accent border at 2dp. platformNotes: The web is a radio group with arrow keys, and Android keeps that model: each value is a radio button in a selectableGroup, which TalkBack reads with its position. iOS exposes the picker as one adjustable element instead. Clearing is a second tap or a custom action, in place of Delete and Backspace. Monarch bundles no icons, so the stars are drawn as a five-pointed shape; the star slot takes the app's own icon. The web's invalid and required states and form name are not offered.
accessibility: The values are radio buttons in one selectableGroup; the chosen one is read as selected.
A tile is named by its number and label; a star by "3 of 5" with the label, if any.
A clearable rating with a value has a "Clear rating" custom action.
A read-only picker is one element named by the label, with the value as its state, for example "4 of 5".
Every tile and star reserves a touch target of at least 48dp by 48dp and draws the focus ring.
The rating is not color alone: the chosen tile has a heavier border, stars are filled or outlined, and the stars variant shows the chosen label as text.
Tiles wrap onto more lines at font scale 2.0 instead of cutting text.
edgeCases: A value that is not on the scale shows no rating.
The spoken maximum is the last option's value, so a scale from 0 to 10 is read "7 of 10".
Long tile labels make wider tiles; keep them to a word or two.

summary: The emoji reactions under a message, comment or post: a chip per emoji with its count, selected when the current person reacted, and an add button that opens the app's emoji picker or a menu of quick reactions.
whenToUse: Under messages, comments and posts where people react with emoji and see how many others did.
whenNotToUse: For a single like or upvote use a MonarchButton or a Material 3 IconToggleButton. For filters use MonarchTag with selected. For a rating use MonarchRatingPicker.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchReactionBar(reactions: List<MonarchReactionBarItem>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, onToggle: ((emoji: String, reacted: Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, size: MonarchReactionBarSize = MonarchReactionBarSize.Sm, enabled: Boolean = true, addable: Boolean = true, maxReactions: Int? = null, quickReactions: List<String> = emptyList(), addIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, picker: (@Composable (onPick: (String) -> Unit, onDismiss: () -> Unit) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchReactionBarLabels = MonarchReactionBarLabels())
public class MonarchReactionBarItem(emoji: String, count: Int, reacted: Boolean = false, label: String? = null, reactedBy: String? = null)
public enum class MonarchReactionBarSize { Sm, Md }

public class MonarchReactionBarLabels(label: String? = null, reaction: ((label: String, count: Int) -> String)? = null, reactedBy: ((names: String) -> String)? = null, add: String? = null, addText: String? = null)

options.name: reactions
options.description: The reactions in display order. A count of 0 hides the chip; a repeated emoji is shown once.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the bar.

options.name: onToggle
options.description: Receives the emoji and the new state when a chip is tapped, or true when an emoji is picked. Without it the bar is read-only.

options.name: size
options.description: Sm under messages and comments, Md under posts.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether chips and the add button respond.

options.name: addable
options.description: Whether an interactive bar shows the add button.

options.name: maxReactions
options.description: At most this many distinct reactions; the add button hides when the limit is reached.

options.name: quickReactions
options.description: Emoji offered in the add button's menu when no picker is given.

options.name: addIcon
options.description: The add button's icon. Without it the button shows "+".

options.name: picker
options.description: The emoji picker, composed while the add button is open: usually MonarchEmojiPicker (the system emoji picker) in a ModalBottomSheet.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the bar's name, a chip's name, the "Reacted by" text and the add button's name and text.

states.name: not reacted
states.description: A chip on the subtle background with a 1dp subtle border and the count in regular weight.

states.name: reacted
states.description: A chip in the accent's subtle fill with strong text, a 2dp accent border and a bold count; the chip is selected.

states.name: read-only
states.description: Without onToggle: chips are images, not controls, and there is no add button; nothing is drawn without reactions.

states.name: picker open
states.description: The app's picker, or a menu of the quick reactions; picking closes it.

states.name: limit reached
states.description: The add button is hidden.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Chips and the add button use the disabled text color and do not respond.

appearance: Chips are fully rounded. Not reacted: the subtle background, default text and the subtle border. Reacted: the accent subtle fill, accent strong text and a 2dp accent border. Disabled: the muted fill and disabled text. All colors are theme roles, so dark and both high-contrast themes follow the theme.
platformNotes: The web bar is a toolbar with one tab stop and arrow keys between chips; on Android each chip is a FilterChip that TalkBack reaches by swiping and a keyboard by Tab. The web opens its own emoji picker in a popover and iOS in a sheet; on Android the add button composes the picker slot, usually MonarchEmojiPicker (the AndroidX system picker) in a sheet, or, without one, a DropdownMenu of quickReactions. The web title attribute (who reacted) is read after the chip's name. Without a label a chip reads the emoji character, as on the web; iOS uses its emoji index instead. Reacted chips use the accent tone, as on the web.
accessibility: The bar is a traversal group named "Reactions".
Each interactive chip is a FilterChip named by the emoji's name and count, "thumbs up, 3 reactions"; the emoji character and the digits are not read separately.
A reacted chip is selected, and has a thicker border and a bold count, so the state does not depend on color.
Who reacted is read after the name: "Reacted by Ana and Ben".
Read-only chips are images with the same names and no selected state.
Chips and the add button have 48dp touch targets; the add button is named "Add reaction".
Chips wrap onto new rows at font scale 2.0 and follow the reading direction.
edgeCases: A chip whose count drops to 0 disappears; the app decides when that happens.
The same emoji twice in reactions is shown once, with the first item's values.
Picking an emoji the person already reacted with does nothing.
With neither a picker nor quickReactions there is no add button.
A read-only bar with no reactions draws nothing.

name: MonarchReadReceipt
title: ReadReceipt
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row with androidx.compose.foundation.clickable, MonarchAvatarGroup and MonarchAvatar
summary: "Seen", "Seen by 3" or the readers' avatars under the newest message the other people have read, with the full list of names for TalkBack.
whenToUse: Under the newest message of a conversation that the other people have read, fed by the app with who has read it.
whenNotToUse: Not for the sending or delivery state of a message; show that in the message itself. Not for who is in a document now; use MonarchPresenceAvatars.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchReadReceipt(readers: List<MonarchReadReceiptReader>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, display: MonarchReadReceiptDisplay = MonarchReadReceiptDisplay.Text, maxAvatars: Int = 3, onShowReaders: (() -> Unit)? = null, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchReadReceiptLabels = MonarchReadReceiptLabels(), interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)
public class MonarchReadReceiptReader(name: String, id: String? = null, image: Painter? = null)
public enum class MonarchReadReceiptDisplay { Text, Count, Avatars }
public class MonarchReadReceiptLabels(seen: String? = null, seenByCount: ((Int) -> String)? = null, seenBy: ((String) -> String)? = null, list: ((List<String>) -> String)? = null)

options.name: readers
options.description: Who has read the message, in order. Leave the sender out. Nothing is drawn while it is empty.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the receipt. The conversation's own layout aligns it under the message.

options.name: display
options.description: Text shows "Seen", Count shows "Seen by 3", Avatars shows the readers' faces and "Seen".

options.name: maxAvatars
options.description: With the avatars display, at most this many faces, then a "+N" tile. At least one face is shown.

options.name: onShowReaders
options.description: Makes the receipt a button, for example to open the list of readers with times.

options.name: icon
options.description: A decorative mark before the text of the text and count displays, such as a double check. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings: seen, seenByCount, seenBy and list.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The interaction source of the button, when onShowReaders is given.

states.name: empty
states.description: Nothing is drawn and nothing is read.

states.name: text
states.description: The optional mark and "Seen".

states.name: count
states.description: The optional mark and "Seen by 3".

states.name: avatars
states.description: Overlapping 24dp avatars of the readers, a "+N" tile for the rest, and "Seen".

states.name: button
states.description: With onShowReaders the receipt is a button with a 48dp touch target and a ripple.

appearance: Caption text and the mark in the muted text color; avatars with their fallback colors and a ring in the surface color; the "+N" tile on the muted background. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Same displays, wording and +N rule as the web and iOS. The web's align property is not offered: the conversation's layout aligns the receipt with the modifier. Avatars are 24dp, the smallest MonarchAvatar size, where the web uses 16 pixels. The web draws a double check glyph; Monarch bundles no icons, so the mark is the optional icon slot and the text carries the meaning. Names are joined with built-in strings ("Ana, Ben and Chloé") because android.icu.text.ListFormatter needs API 26 and minSdk is 24; replace the join with labels.list. The web shows the full sentence as a hover title; Android has no hover on touch screens, so it is only read by TalkBack.
accessibility: The receipt is one TalkBack element whose name is the full sentence, "Seen by Ana, Ben and Chloé", in every display.
The mark and the avatars are not read on their own.
With onShowReaders the element has the button role, a click action and a touch target of at least 48dp; without it, it has no role and no action.
The text and the avatars grow with the font size setting, and long text wraps.
edgeCases: An empty list draws nothing.
A maxAvatars of 0 or less still shows one face.
With one reader more than maxAvatars, every face is shown instead of a "+1" tile.
Long custom text wraps.

name: MonarchReceiptPreview
title: ReceiptPreview
wrapsNative: MonarchButton (androidx.compose.material3.Button), androidx.compose.ui.window.Dialog (full screen), MonarchFilePreview, MonarchInlineErrorRetry
summary: A "View receipt" button that shows an expense's receipt full screen, fetching a private file only when pressed, with a loading state, Try again and a "No receipt" fallback.
whenToUse: In an expense, a transaction or an invoice row, to look at the attached receipt without leaving the screen.
whenNotToUse: For any file attachment in a conversation use a file card and MonarchFilePreview. To let people attach a receipt use a file picker.
api: @Composable fun MonarchReceiptPreview(receipt: MonarchReceipt?, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchButtonVariant = MonarchButtonVariant.Ghost, size: MonarchButtonSize = MonarchButtonSize.Sm, enabled: Boolean = true, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, onDownload: ((MonarchReceipt) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchReceiptPreviewLabels = MonarchReceiptPreviewLabels())

@Composable fun MonarchReceiptPreview(load: suspend () -> MonarchReceipt, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchButtonVariant = MonarchButtonVariant.Ghost, size: MonarchButtonSize = MonarchButtonSize.Sm, enabled: Boolean = true, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, onDownload: ((MonarchReceipt) -> Unit)? = null, onLoadError: ((Throwable) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchReceiptPreviewLabels = MonarchReceiptPreviewLabels())
class MonarchReceipt(name: String, contentType: String? = null, image: Painter? = null, pdf: Uri? = null)
class MonarchReceiptPreviewLabels(view: String? = null, none: String? = null, loading: String? = null, loadError: String? = null, retry: String? = null, title: String? = null, close: String? = null)

options.name: receipt
options.description: A receipt the app has: its name, MIME type and a Painter or a local PDF Uri. null shows "No receipt".

options.name: load
options.description: The app's code that fetches the private receipt; run on each press and on Try again. Throw to report a failure.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the button (and the error under it), or of the "No receipt" text.

options.name: variant
options.description: Primary, Secondary, Ghost or Danger.

options.name: size
options.description: Sm, Md or Lg; the touch target is at least 48dp at every size.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the receipt can be opened.

options.name: icon
options.description: An icon before the label, such as a paperclip. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: onDownload
options.description: Shows MonarchFilePreview's Download button; the app saves the file.

options.name: onLoadError
options.description: Second overload: called with the loader's failure, for logging.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for "View receipt", "No receipt", "Loading receipt", "The receipt could not be loaded.", the retry text, "Receipt" and "Close".

states.name: idle
states.description: The button "View receipt".

states.name: loading
states.description: Second overload: the button shows its progress indicator, ignores taps and has the state "Loading receipt".

states.name: previewing
states.description: A full-screen dialog with the heading "Receipt", a Close button and MonarchFilePreview of the picture or the PDF pages. Back closes it.

states.name: failed
states.description: Second overload: MonarchInlineErrorRetry under the button with "The receipt could not be loaded." and Try again.

states.name: none
states.description: Muted caption text "No receipt" instead of the button.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The button uses the disabled colors and does not open or load.

appearance: The button has the colors of its MonarchButton variant; "No receipt" is the muted caption color; the full-screen preview uses the canvas color with the default text color, and MonarchFilePreview's own colors. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ReceiptPreview opens images in a dialog with Download, opens PDFs in a new tab or an embedded viewer, takes a src or a load function returning a Blob or URL, and explains formats the browser cannot draw; iOS presents Quick Look from a local file URL. Android has no system previewer that Compose can embed, so the receipt is shown in a full-screen Dialog with MonarchFilePreview, as the plan says. Monarch does no networking: the loader returns a MonarchReceipt with a Painter the app decoded or a local PDF Uri, rather than a URL. Unsupported types show MonarchFilePreview's "There is no preview for this file type.". The web's controlled open and onOpenChange are not offered; the preview's open state is kept by the component. The web's mimeType is contentType inside MonarchReceipt. Like iOS, the default variant is Ghost and the default size Sm.
accessibility: The button is a MonarchButton with the Button role and a touch target of at least 48dp at every size.
While loading, the button's state description is "Loading receipt" and taps are ignored.
A failure shows MonarchInlineErrorRetry, whose message is a polite live region, with a separate Try again button.
"No receipt" is plain text, not a disabled button.
The full-screen preview has a heading and a Close button; Back also closes it. MonarchFilePreview names the picture or the PDF pages.
The label is not cut at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: Leaving the screen while loading cancels the load; the loader should respect coroutine cancellation.
Pressing Try again while a previous load is still running cancels it first.
Closing the preview returns to the idle state; the next press loads again, so the app can cache in its loader.
The dialog was checked in Robolectric tests; its full-screen look with system bars was not tried on a device.

title: RecordHeader
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.TopAppBar with MonarchIconButton and MonarchMenu, androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column and FlowRow, MonarchTabs, with MonarchAvatar, MonarchInlineEditText, MonarchStatusBadge, MonarchBadge, MonarchKeyValue and MonarchCalloutBanner
summary: The header of a record screen, such as a contact, ticket or deal: the title, back, previous and next and the More menu in the top app bar, and under it the avatar, editable title, status and badges, key facts, a state banner and section tabs.
whenToUse: At the top of a record's detail screen in a CRM, help desk or admin app, under the screen's TopAppBar.
whenNotToUse: Not for the header of a list or a settings page; use a TopAppBar with MonarchSectionHeader. Not for a summary of a record in a list; use MonarchCard.
api: TopAppBar(title = { Text(name, maxLines = 1, overflow = TextOverflow.Ellipsis) }, navigationIcon = { MonarchIconButton(label = "Back to contacts", onClick = back) { … } }, actions = { MonarchIconButton(label = "Previous contact", onClick = previous, enabled = index > 0) { … }; MonarchIconButton(label = "Next contact", onClick = next, enabled = index < lastIndex) { … }; Box { MonarchIconButton(label = "More actions for $name", onClick = { menuOpen = true }) { … }; MonarchMenu(expanded = menuOpen, onDismissRequest = { menuOpen = false }) { MonarchMenuItem(…) } } })

Row { MonarchAvatar(image, name, size = MonarchAvatarSize.Lg, decorative = true); MonarchInlineEditText(value = name, onSave = …, label = "Contact name", modifier = Modifier.weight(1f).semantics { heading() }) }
FlowRow { MonarchStatusBadge(definition = MonarchStatusDefinition(label, tone)); MonarchBadge(text = …) }
MonarchKeyValue(items = listOf(MonarchKeyValueItem(label, value), …))
MonarchCalloutBanner(message = …, tone = MonarchTone.Warning)
MonarchTabs(selectedIndex = currentTab, onSelectedIndexChange = { currentTab = it }) { tab(…) }

options.name: TopAppBar.actions

options.name: MonarchInlineEditText.onSave

options.name: status and badges
options.description: The record's status and markers in a FlowRow, so many badges wrap.

options.name: position
options.description: The web's "3 of 40" is a caption Text under the badges.

options.name: MonarchKeyValue.items
options.description: Key facts. Leave MonarchKeyValue out when there are none rather than passing an empty list.

options.name: MonarchCalloutBanner
options.description: A warning banner for an archived, merged or deleted record.

options.name: MonarchTabs
options.description: The record's sections.

states.name: default
states.description: Avatar, title, status and badges, position, key facts and tabs; the title also in the top app bar, and actions in the More menu.

states.name: editing the title
states.description: MonarchInlineEditText swaps to a text field with Save and Cancel; saving updates the top app bar title.

states.name: previous and next
states.description: The arrows move between records of the list the person came from, disabled at either end.

states.name: state banner
states.description: A warning MonarchCalloutBanner for an archived, merged or deleted record.

states.name: empty fact
states.description: MonarchKeyValue shows its placeholder for a fact without a value.

appearance: Each part keeps its own component's color roles: the avatar's fallback colors, badges in their tones, facts in the muted and default text colors, the banner in its tone, and the tab row's accent indicator. The top app bar takes the Monarch Material color scheme in every theme.
platformNotes: The web RecordHeader is one component with slots for back link, previous and next, avatar, title, badges, facts, actions, banner and tabs. On Android, as on iOS, the back button, the title and the actions belong to the top app bar, so Monarch ships a recipe instead of a type: back, previous, next and More are MonarchIconButtons in TopAppBar, record actions are a MonarchMenu, and the rest is composed under it in the screen's scrolling Column. The web's position text "3 of 40" is plain caption text. The heading level option has no Android meaning; the editable title carries heading semantics. Monarch bundles no icons; the example uses framework drawables.
accessibility: The back, previous, next and More buttons are MonarchIconButtons with 48dp targets, named after the record type and the record: "Previous contact", "More actions for Ada Lovelace".
The editable title has heading semantics, so TalkBack's heading navigation reaches it.

Each composed component keeps its own accessibility: status and badges read their text, facts are read as label and value pairs, the banner is read with its tone, and the tabs are tabs with their selected state.
Everything wraps and grows with the font size setting; the top app bar title is cut to one line by the system and stays in full in the header.
edgeCases: A long title wraps in the header and is truncated in the top app bar.
Many badges wrap onto new lines in the FlowRow.
On the first and last record the previous and next buttons are disabled.
With no facts, leave MonarchKeyValue out rather than passing an empty list.

summary: A recipe, not a component: a record's detail screen on a phone, with the name and actions in the top app bar, a status, section tabs, and the side column and the activity moved into their own tabs.
whenToUse: For the detail screen of a record (a deal, a contact, a ticket) reached from a list.
whenNotToUse: For the list and the record side by side on a tablet or a foldable, put this screen in the detail pane of NavigableListDetailPaneScaffold (split-layout). For the header alone, use the record-header recipe.

MonarchActivityTimeline(events = …, modifier = Modifier.weight(1f), contentPadding = …)

options.name: tabs
options.description: The sections of the record; add a Details tab for the web's side column and an Activity tab for the activity.

options.name: tab
options.description: The selected section, kept with rememberSaveable so it survives rotation.

options.name: actions
options.description: The record's actions in the top app bar; put the rest in an overflow MonarchMenu.

states.name: section
states.description: The selected tab's content fills the space under the tabs and scrolls on its own.

states.name: details
states.description: The web's side column: MonarchDescriptionList with the record's facts, in its own tab.

states.name: activity
states.description: MonarchActivityTimeline, a lazy list, fills the rest of the screen and scrolls on its own.

states.name: wide
states.description: On an expanded window, show the details beside the main column with split-layout instead of a tab.

appearance: Every part is an existing Material 3 or Monarch component: the top app bar and tabs in the Monarch theme, a status badge, a description list and the activity timeline. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web ships RecordPage as one component: a RecordHeader with tabs, the main column, an aside that moves under the main column below a breakpoint, and an activity section. On a phone Android follows the native pattern instead of copying the web layout: the name and actions go to the TopAppBar (as in the record-header recipe), the side column becomes a Details tab, and the activity is its own tab, because MonarchActivityTimeline is a lazy list that must not sit inside a vertically scrolling parent. iOS keeps the side column under the main column with ViewThatFits and the activity as a tab; it also mentions a Details tab as the other phone choice. On wide windows use NavigableSupportingPaneScaffold or the split-layout entry rather than a breakpoint. The web's asideWidth and activityPlacement props are choices in the recipe's own code.
accessibility: The record's name is the top app bar title; actions are buttons with 48dp targets.
Tabs have the tab role and the selected state, from Material 3.
The status is a word in a MonarchStatusBadge, not color alone.
Each section scrolls on its own, so TalkBack scrolls the content under the fixed header and tabs.
edgeCases: A long record name is cut with an ellipsis in the app bar; show it in full in the Overview section.
Many sections: MonarchTabs scrolls the tabs.
Never put MonarchActivityTimeline inside verticalScroll; give it the remaining height with weight(1f).

appearance: Codes sit on a panel with the subtle background and subtle border roles, in the code type style. Buttons are Monarch buttons: ghost for show and hide, secondary for copy and save, danger for generate new codes, primary for Continue. The confirmation is a Material 3 AlertDialog on the raised background with its confirm text in the danger strong role. All colors are theme roles, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web's Download becomes Save or share: by default the system share sheet (Intent.ACTION_SEND with the codes as text), from which the person can save to a file, a password manager or another app; onSave lets the app write a file with a CreateDocument launcher instead. iOS shares a named text file; Android shares text, so there is no fileName. The web's confirm dialog is a Material 3 AlertDialog. The parity map names a grid; the codes are rows of a Column with as many columns as fit, because a LazyVerticalGrid cannot sit in a scrolling screen. Copy marks the clip as sensitive, so Android 13 and later hide it in the clipboard preview. The revealed state is internal (initiallyRevealed), as on iOS. The codes are not selectable as text; Copy covers that.
accessibility: The codes are a traversal group named "Recovery codes".
Each code carries a verbatim text-to-speech annotation, so TalkBack spells it character by character.
A used code has the state "Used", so its state does not depend on the strike-through.
All actions are Monarch buttons with 48dp touch targets; the acknowledgement is a MonarchCheckboxRow, one checkbox element.
New codes are announced through a polite live region after regenerating.
A missing acknowledgement is shown as text and announced through the same live region.
edgeCases: The codes take as many columns as fit at 112dp each, scaled with the font size, so the largest font sizes show one column.
A new set of codes clears the acknowledgement; marking a code used does not.
When onRegenerate throws, the button stops its progress and nothing is announced; the app reports the failure.

Region names in the built-in lists are English in every locale; pass regions for localised names.

title: RelativeTime
wrapsNative: android.text.format.DateUtils.getRelativeTimeSpanString(long, long, long), android.icu.text.RelativeDateTimeFormatter
summary: Relative times such as "3 hours ago" come from the platform's formatters. Monarch ships nothing; the text takes a Monarch type role and color, and TalkBack reads the absolute time.
whenToUse: For timestamps in lists, comments and activity. Use DateUtils.getRelativeTimeSpanString for "3 hours ago" and "in 2 days", and RelativeDateTimeFormatter for words such as "yesterday" or "next week".
whenNotToUse: When the exact time matters more than the age, such as a due date or a log entry, show the absolute date with DateUtils.formatDateTime or android.icu.text.DateFormat.
api: DateUtils.getRelativeTimeSpanString(time: Long, now: Long, minResolution: Long): CharSequence
DateUtils.formatDateTime(context: Context, millis: Long, flags: Int): String
RelativeDateTimeFormatter.getInstance(): RelativeDateTimeFormatter

options.name: time
options.description: The moment, in epoch milliseconds (UTC).

options.name: now
options.description: The reference time, usually System.currentTimeMillis(); redraw it every minute to keep the text true.

options.name: minResolution
options.description: The smallest unit shown, such as DateUtils.MINUTE_IN_MILLIS, so "0 minutes ago" never shows seconds.

states.name: past
states.description: "3 hours ago".

states.name: future
states.description: "In 2 days".

appearance: Plain text in a Monarch type role, usually Caption, in the muted text color, so it reads in every theme.
platformNotes: The web RelativeTime is a component with a tooltip for the absolute time, its own ticking and an absoluteAfter threshold. Android has no hover tooltip on touch, so the absolute time goes in the content description, as on iOS. The ticking is a produceState that updates every minute, and the threshold is an if in the app. java.time is not used because the minimum SDK is 24 without desugaring; times are epoch milliseconds. Monarch's own components write relative times with one rule on every platform, the web formatRelativeTime rule (internal MonarchRelativeTime: seconds to years with the web rollovers, Math.round, "now", "yesterday", "last week", no switch to a date unless a component sets an absolute-after threshold). DateUtils.getRelativeTimeSpanString, suggested here for app code, differs: it never shows seconds and writes a date from a week on.
accessibility: Set the absolute date and time as the content description, so TalkBack reads a time that does not go stale.
The formatters use the user's locale.
The text grows with the font size setting when a Monarch type role is applied.
edgeCases: getRelativeTimeSpanString is worked out when it is composed and does not update by itself; redraw it every minute.
Times more than a week away are written as a date by getRelativeTimeSpanString.
RelativeDateTimeFormatter needs the direction and unit worked out by the app.

examples.title: Relative and absolute
examples.setup:
val now = 1_793_707_200_000L
fun relative(at: Long): String =
    DateUtils.getRelativeTimeSpanString(at, now, DateUtils.MINUTE_IN_MILLIS).toString()
        .replaceFirstChar { it.lowercase() }
fun absolute(at: Long): String =
    DateFormat.getDateInstance(DateFormat.MEDIUM, Locale.forLanguageTag("en-GB"))
        .apply { timeZone = TimeZone.getTimeZone("UTC") }
        .format(Date(at))

examples.title: Kept up to date every minute
examples.code:
MonarchText(
    text = DateUtils.getRelativeTimeSpanString(postedAt, now, DateUtils.MINUTE_IN_MILLIS).toString(),
    style = MonarchTextStyle.Caption,
)

examples.title: Words such as "yesterday"
examples.code:
MonarchText(
    text = RelativeDateTimeFormatter.getInstance().format(
        RelativeDateTimeFormatter.Direction.LAST,
        RelativeDateTimeFormatter.AbsoluteUnit.DAY,
    ),
    style = MonarchTextStyle.Caption,
)

parityExceptions.reason: The web underlines the relative time with a dotted line because hovering it shows the absolute time in a tooltip. Touch has no hover, so the dotted line would suggest a tap target that does not exist; the absolute time is in the content description for TalkBack instead.
parityExceptions.convention: Material guidance: no hover tooltips on touch; do not mark non-interactive text as interactive

whenToUse: When an admin removes someone who may still own open work: issues, tasks, documents or deals that would otherwise be left without an owner.
whenNotToUse: For someone who owns nothing, a confirm dialog (MonarchDialog) is enough. For a member leaving on their own, use the LeaveWorkspaceFlow recipe. For many members at once, use the BulkDestructiveFlow recipe.

states.name: removing

states.name: failed
states.description: A danger MonarchInlineNotice above the buttons; the sheet stays on the confirm step.

states.name: removed

appearance: A Material 3 bottom sheet in the colors Monarch maps to the scheme, holding Monarch parts: headings and body text, assignee pickers, a checkbox row, a member row, a consequence list with its kind colors and a danger button. The snackbar uses MonarchSnackbarHost. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web's RemoveMemberFlow is one component built on WizardDialog with a step-up authentication option, number formatting and a useUndoToast bridge. On Android it is a recipe, as the native-first rule asks for a flow of this kind: a MonarchBottomSheet with two steps instead of a wizard dialog, MonarchAssigneePicker for the hand-over, and the Material 3 snackbar for Undo. The app writes the strings with plurals resources, runs re-authentication (for example BiometricPrompt, which needs androidx.biometric in the app) before the removal, and sends the reassignments to its server. dismissible = false keeps the sheet open while removing. iOS has no entry for this id yet.
accessibility: The title and each step's heading are headings (MonarchTextStyle.Title and Heading).
Each MonarchAssigneePicker is named by its label: Reassign all open work to, or the count and kind of work.
MonarchConsequenceList reads each consequence with its kind, so where the work goes does not depend on color.
Remove member is a danger MonarchButton that reports its busy state while removing.
The Undo snackbar is announced by the system and Undo is reachable by TalkBack.
edgeCases: Skip the reassign step when the member owns nothing: start on the confirm step.
Leave the removed member out of the people offered in the pickers.
Turning on per item copies the all-at-once choice into each picker, so nothing is lost.
Reset the choices each time the sheet opens.
If the removal fails, keep the choices and show the error on the confirm step.

appearance: A MonarchSectionCard: rows in the default and muted text colors separated by subtle dividers, status badges in their tones, the Due soon badge in the warning tone, totals on subtle tiles and the overdue step in the strong danger color. The same in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web RenewalsPanel is a section with a data table that hides columns as the container narrows, a SegmentedControl, ReactNode slots, links and a skeleton. On Android each item is a stacked row at every width, because a six-column table does not fit a phone and the plan named rows; the rows are a Column rather than a LazyColumn so the card can sit inside the screen's verticalScroll. Links (href, renderLink) become onItemClick. The urgent marker is a visible "Due soon" badge, because Monarch bundles no warning icon and the web's visually hidden text would leave the color alone. Dates are epoch milliseconds (UTC) written with android.icu.text.DateFormat; there is no timeZone parameter, and day counts use now or the clock read once, without ticking. The web filterControls and empty slots are not offered; replace the empty strings through labels. The default statuses are MonarchRenewalsPanelDefaults.statuses(), with localised labels. iOS has not built RenewalsPanel yet; the names follow the web.
accessibility: Each row's text is one TalkBack element read in words: name, status, Due soon, description, date and day count, amount, renewal mode, owner, next step, probability and outcome.
With onItemClick the row's text is a button with a 48dp minimum height and a focus ring.
The row action is a separate button read with the item's name: "Update Acme contract"; it keeps a 48dp touch target.
The list is a traversal group named "Renewals" with collection info; each row carries its index.
The filters are Material 3 segmented buttons with the selected state; the group is named "Filter renewals".
The totals are a traversal group named "Totals by currency"; each tile is read as one element.
Urgency and overdue steps are written in words, never shown by color alone.
Text wraps at font scale 2.0; right to left, the lines mirror.
edgeCases: An item's own daysUntil wins over the worked-out count; a missing date shows "Unknown date" and no count.
A past open renewal (negative days) is also marked Due soon.
Amounts are never converted; totals come from the app per currency.
An amount without a currency code is shown as "No price".
Many filters make the segmented row wrap its labels on a narrow phone; keep them few and short.

parityExceptions.reason: The panel writes its dates as plain calendar days in UTC, which is the fixture time zone, so no time zone value is passed; a date at midnight UTC never moves to the previous day.
parityExceptions.convention: day-granular dates are written in UTC, so no zone parameter is needed

parityExceptions.reason: The phone shows each row as a card: the first column is the card title and every other cell carries its column name as a label, so the column header row is not drawn. TalkBack reads each cell with its column name.
parityExceptions.convention: a table is a list of cards on a phone (Material list-detail), not a header row

summary: A list the user reorders by long-pressing and dragging rows, with TalkBack actions, arrow keys and optional move buttons as alternatives, and every step announced.
whenToUse: When the order of a short or medium list is the person's to decide: priorities, pipeline stages, the order of steps or of favourites.
whenNotToUse: For tiles in two dimensions use MonarchSortableGrid. For a list sorted by a field use a sort control instead of manual order. For moving items between lists use Compose drag and drop (dragAndDropSource and dragAndDropTarget).

options.description: A stable, unique key for an item; also the LazyColumn key.

options.name: itemLabel

options.name: onReorder
options.description: Called once per finished move (drop, action, arrow key or button) with the old and the new index. Move the item in items, for example items.add(to, items.removeAt(from)).

options.description: The modifier of the list. Give it a bounded height to make it scroll.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether any row can be moved.

options.name: itemEnabled
options.description: Whether an item can be moved. Other rows can still move past it.

options.name: moveButtons
options.description: Also shows Up and Down buttons on every row, a one-tap alternative to dragging.

options.name: state
options.description: The scroll state of the list.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the handle and button names, the button texts, the four announcements and the handle's action names.

states.name: idle
states.description: Rows on the surface fill with a subtle border, each with an idle drag handle.

states.name: dragged
states.description: The held row follows the finger above the others with the medium shadow, the accent border and a grabbed handle (Picked up); the other rows slide out of its way.

states.name: locked row
states.description: itemEnabled false: the handle is disabled and has no actions, its move buttons are disabled, and a long press does not pick it up.

states.name: disabled
states.description: enabled false: no row can be moved.

states.name: empty
states.description: An empty list draws nothing.

appearance: Each row is the surface fill with a 1dp subtle border and medium corners. The held row has the medium shadow and the accent border; its handle uses the grabbed colors of MonarchDragHandle. Every color comes from the theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow the theme.
platformNotes: The web list picks a row up from its handle with the pointer or with Space, moves it with the arrow keys and drops it with Space, and keeps uncontrolled items itself. On Android a long press anywhere on the row picks it up, as Android lists do, so the rest of the row stays free for scrolling and taps; TalkBack, Switch Access and hardware keyboards use the handle's Move up and Move down actions and arrow keys, which move one place at once and announce the new position. The order is always hoisted: the list reports from and to, and the app moves the item. iOS ships no type and uses the system list's edit mode. If the items change during a drag, the drag continues with the held row's original index and the drop reports from and to against the list as it was when the drag started; keep items stable during a drag.
accessibility: Every row has a MonarchDragHandle named Reorder and the item's label, with the TalkBack actions Move up and Move down; the arrow keys move the row while the handle has focus.
Picking up, moving by an action or a button, dropping and cancelling are announced through a polite live region: "Design review moved to position 2 of 3."
The held row is shown by a border, a shadow and the grabbed handle, not by color alone, and its handle reads Picked up.
The move buttons are named "Move Design review up" and "Move Design review down" and are disabled at the ends.
The handle and the move buttons have 48dp touch targets; the handle comes before the content in both reading directions; row text wraps at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: A drop at the place it started reports nothing to onReorder but still announces the drop.
Move up on the first row and Move down on the last row do nothing.
The list scrolls by at most 16dp a frame while the held row is past its top or bottom edge, and stops at the ends.
Animations are immediate when the person has turned animations off.
Keys must be unique; the same key twice breaks the LazyColumn.

On a phone, as on iOS, it is a recipe: the title, back and download go in the top app bar, the body splits into a Summary tab (scrolling) and a Table tab (MonarchDataTable fills the screen), because a lazy table cannot sit inside a scrolling page. The web's built-in simple table is MonarchDataTable. Times are formatted by the app (minSdk 24, no java.time).

A long title wraps in LargeTopAppBar; use it when titles are long.
Keep the previous result on screen while refreshing instead of the loading state.
Forbidden and not found get no retry.

whenToUse: On a tablet or a large window, for two views people compare or work across: an editor beside its preview, a query above its results. The app keeps the share and restores it.
whenNotToUse: For a list and the detail of the selected item use the Material ListDetailPaneScaffold (see split-layout), which also shows one pane on a phone and has its own drag handle. For a fixed split use a Row with weights.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchResizablePanels(fraction: Float, onFractionChange: (Float) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, axis: MonarchResizablePanelsAxis = MonarchResizablePanelsAxis.Horizontal, range: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Float> = MonarchResizablePanelsDefaults.Range, step: Float = MonarchResizablePanelsDefaults.Step, enabled: Boolean = true, showGrip: Boolean = false, stacksWhenCompact: Boolean = true, handleLabel: String? = null, onResizeFinished: ((Float) -> Unit)? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null, first: @Composable () -> Unit, second: @Composable () -> Unit)
public enum class MonarchResizablePanelsAxis { Horizontal, Vertical }
public object MonarchResizablePanelsDefaults { public val Range: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Float>; public const val Step: Float }

options.name: fraction
options.description: The share of the first panel, from 0 to 1, kept within range. The app owns it; keep it in rememberSaveable or the app's settings to restore the layout.

options.name: onFractionChange
options.description: Called with the new share while the separator moves.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the component.

options.name: axis
options.description: Horizontal: side by side, the first panel at the start. Vertical: stacked, the first panel on top; needs a bounded height.

options.name: range
options.description: The smallest and largest share of the first panel, limited to 0..1.

options.name: step
options.description: The share one arrow key press or one TalkBack adjustment moves the separator.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether people can move the separator.

options.name: showGrip
options.description: Draws a grip in the middle of the separator.

options.name: stacksWhenCompact
options.description: On a compact window (narrower than 600dp) side-by-side panels are stacked at their natural height with a divider and no resizing.

options.name: handleLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in name "Resize panels" read by TalkBack.

options.name: onResizeFinished
options.description: Called with the share when a drag ends and after each key press or TalkBack adjustment. Save the layout here.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The interaction source of the separator, for its dragged and focused states.

options.name: first
options.description: The start or top panel.

options.name: second
options.description: The end or bottom panel.

states.name: resting
states.description: A 1dp line in the default border color in the middle of a 48dp separator.

states.name: dragged or focused
states.description: The line is 2dp and in the accent color; the focus ring surrounds the separator when focused with a keyboard.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The line uses the subtle border color; the separator takes no drag, no key and no adjustment and is announced as disabled.

states.name: stacked
states.description: On a compact window the panels are stacked with a MonarchDivider and there is no separator.

appearance: The line uses the default border color at rest, the accent color while dragged or focused and the subtle border color when disabled; the grip uses the strong border color at rest. The panels draw no surface of their own.
platformNotes: The parity map named a Row with a draggable separator, and ListDetailPaneScaffold where it fits: that scaffold's paneExpansionDragHandle resizes a list and its detail and is documented under split-layout; this component covers any two panels. The web takes any number of panels with alternating handles and sizes in percent; Android, like iOS, takes two panels and one share from 0 to 1, and a third pane is a MonarchResizablePanels nested in a panel. The web keeps the sizes itself (defaultSizes, onLayout); here the app owns the value and onResizeFinished is the moment to save (iOS calls it onResizeEnded; Compose uses "Finished", as in Slider's onValueChangeFinished). Not offered: collapsible panels and a per-handle disabled flag. Stacking on a compact window is the default, as on iOS, because two resizable columns do not fit a phone in portrait. The separator reserves its 48dp touch target between the panels; on iOS the target overlaps the panel edges.
accessibility: The separator is one TalkBack element named "Resize panels" (or handleLabel).
Its state description is the share of the first panel as a whole percentage in the device locale, for example "40%".
It has slider semantics (a progress range with a set-progress action), so TalkBack's adjust gestures move it by step and the value is limited to range.

With a hardware keyboard the separator takes focus and draws the focus ring. The arrow keys along the axis move it by step in the direction they point, so left and right swap in a right-to-left layout; Home and End move it to the ends of range.
Its touch target is 48dp across, reserved in the layout between the panels.
In a right-to-left layout the first panel is on the right and dragging follows the finger.
The active state is a thicker line as well as the accent color.
The panels are not animated while they resize, so there is nothing for reduced motion to turn off.
edgeCases: A fraction outside range is shown at the nearest end of range; a range outside 0..1 is limited to it.
A vertical layout without a bounded height gives each panel its natural height and the share has no effect.
A panel with content wider than its share is clipped by its own content's layout, not by this component; make panel content scroll or wrap.

name: MonarchResponsiveDialog
title: ResponsiveDialog
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.ModalBottomSheet below the breakpoint and androidx.compose.ui.window.Dialog with androidx.compose.material3.Surface at or above it, chosen with androidx.compose.material3.adaptive.currentWindowAdaptiveInfoV2 and androidx.window.core.layout.WindowSizeClass
summary: A dialog that is a bottom sheet on a phone and a centered panel on a large window, from one call, with a title, a description, scrolling content and actions.
whenToUse: For a short task or form that should feel native on both a phone (a sheet within thumb reach) and a tablet or unfolded foldable (a centered dialog), such as renaming, a small settings form or a picker.
whenNotToUse: For a yes or no question, use AlertDialog (see confirm-dialog), which is a dialog at every size. For a long task with several steps, use a full screen. For content that should stay beside the main view on a large screen, use a supporting pane.
api: @Composable fun MonarchResponsiveDialog(onDismissRequest: () -> Unit, title: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, sheetBelow: MonarchResponsiveDialogBreakpoint = MonarchResponsiveDialogBreakpoint.Medium, dismissible: Boolean = true, showHandle: Boolean = true, description: String? = null, actions: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null, content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)
enum class MonarchResponsiveDialogBreakpoint { Medium, Expanded }

options.name: onDismissRequest
options.description: Called when the person dismisses it: back, a tap outside, or a swipe down on the sheet. Not called when not dismissible.

options.name: title
options.description: The heading, also the pane title TalkBack reads when it opens.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the sheet or the dialog panel.

options.name: sheetBelow
options.description: Medium: a sheet on compact windows (narrower than 600dp). Expanded: also on medium windows (narrower than 840dp).

options.name: dismissible
options.description: Whether back, a tap outside and a swipe can dismiss it. When false the actions must close it.

options.name: showHandle
options.description: Whether the sheet shows the Material 3 drag handle. The dialog never does.

options.name: description
options.description: A line under the title in the muted text color.

options.name: actions
options.description: The buttons at the end, such as a ghost Cancel and a primary MonarchButton. They wrap onto another line when there is no room.

options.name: content
options.description: The body, in a column that scrolls when it is taller than the window.

states.name: compact window
states.description: A ModalBottomSheet from the bottom, fully expanded, with the drag handle.

states.name: large window
states.description: A Dialog centered over a scrim, on the Material 3 dialog surface and shape.

states.name: not dismissible
states.description: Back, a tap outside and the swipe do nothing; the sheet cannot be dragged away.

states.name: tall content
states.description: The body scrolls; the title and the actions stay in place.

appearance: Both forms use the raised background, which Monarch maps to the Material surface containers, with the default text color and the large corner radius of the Material sheet or dialog, over the overlay scrim. The title is in the heading style and the description in the muted text color. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ResponsiveDialog switches between Dialog and a bottom sheet with a CSS breakpoint (sheetBelow sm 640px or md 768px) and shows a grab handle. Android decides with the window size classes of the Material guidance (600dp and 840dp) through currentWindowAdaptiveInfoV2, so it follows split screen and foldables. iOS uses the system sheet, which adapts by itself, and ships nothing; Compose has no adaptive sheet, so Android builds this wrapper. The web composes the Dialog parts (header, body, footer); here title, description, content and actions are parameters. When the app removes the sheet by setting its state to false, the sheet leaves without the slide-down animation.
accessibility: Both forms are modal windows: TalkBack stays inside, and back closes them when they are dismissible.
The title is a heading and the pane title, so TalkBack reads it when the window opens.
The sheet's drag handle is the Material 3 handle, which TalkBack offers with its expand and dismiss actions.
The body scrolls at large font sizes instead of being cut, and the actions wrap.
edgeCases: Turning or resizing the window across the breakpoint switches between sheet and dialog; the content keeps rememberSaveable state but not plain remember state.
With dismissible = false, give the person a visible way out in the actions.
The dialog takes the platform's default dialog width; very wide content scrolls inside it.

title: RevokeAccessFlow
wrapsNative: MonarchBottomSheet (dismissible = false keeps it open while revoking) with androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column, MonarchConsequenceList, MonarchTypeToConfirmInput, MonarchInlineNotice, MonarchButton and MonarchStepUpAuthDialog; android.text.format.DateUtils for the last-used time
summary: A recipe, not a component: confirm revoking an API key, an OAuth client, portal access, sessions or devices, listing what is revoked, when it was last used and what happens, with optional type-to-confirm and re-authentication.
whenToUse: Behind every Revoke, Sign out or Remove action on keys, connected apps, sessions, devices or someone's portal access.
whenNotToUse: For a simple sign-out of one session, a MonarchDialog (ConfirmDialog) is enough. For deleting a whole workspace, use the same pattern with the workspace's own wording.
api: MonarchBottomSheet(onDismissRequest = { confirming = false }, title = "Revoke “$keyName”?", description = …, dismissible = !revoking) { … }
DateUtils.getRelativeTimeSpanString(lastUsedMillis, now, DateUtils.MINUTE_IN_MILLIS)
MonarchConsequenceList(items = listOf(MonarchConsequence(MonarchConsequenceKind.Removed, "…"), MonarchConsequence(MonarchConsequenceKind.Warning, "…")), heading = "What happens")
MonarchTypeToConfirmInput(phrase = keyName, value = typed, onValueChange = { typed = it })

MonarchButton(text = "Revoke key", onClick = …, modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(), variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Danger, enabled = MonarchTypeToConfirmInputDefaults.matches(typed, keyName), loading = revoking)
MonarchStepUpAuthDialog(onVerify = …, description = "Revoking access needs you to confirm it’s you.", onVerified = …)

options.name: keyName
options.description: The name of what is revoked, written in the title and typed to confirm.

options.name: lastUsedMillis
options.description: When it was last used, in epoch milliseconds; null reads "Never used".

options.name: typeToConfirm
options.default: true for keys and OAuth clients
options.description: Whether the danger button waits for the name to be typed exactly.

options.name: needsStepUp
options.description: Whether the server requires a recent confirmation; the sheet then shows MonarchStepUpAuthDialog and revokes after it verifies.

options.name: revoking
options.description: The request is running: the danger button shows its progress indicator, Cancel is disabled and the sheet cannot be dismissed.

options.name: failure
options.description: A failed request, shown in a danger MonarchInlineNotice in the sheet.

states.name: confirm
states.description: The question naming what is revoked, a line on what it means, the item with its prefix and last-used time, the consequence list, and the danger and Cancel buttons.

states.name: type to confirm
states.description: For keys and OAuth clients, the danger button stays disabled until the name is typed exactly.

states.name: step-up
states.description: When re-authentication is required, the sheet shows MonarchStepUpAuthDialog; the revocation runs after it verifies.

states.name: revoking
states.description: The danger button shows its progress indicator; Cancel is disabled and the sheet cannot be swiped away.

states.name: failed
states.description: A danger MonarchInlineNotice in the sheet; the person can try again.

appearance: Every part is an existing Monarch component on the sheet's surface: a heading, body text, the consequence list with its marks, the type-to-confirm field and full-width danger and ghost buttons. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web's RevokeAccessFlow is one component with built-in copy for five kinds (api-key, oauth-client, portal-access, session, device) and plural forms. On Android, as on iOS, it is a recipe: the copy is the app's, written for its kind and count, and the step is a MonarchBottomSheet because a MonarchDialog cannot comfortably hold a list, a text field with a match check and a pending state. Danger is right for keys and OAuth clients, which cannot be undone; for sessions, devices and portal access, which can sign in again, use a plain MonarchDialog or the same sheet with warning wording. The web's stepUp prop is MonarchStepUpAuthDialog shown in the same sheet. The last-used time is written with DateUtils.getRelativeTimeSpanString (minSdk 24, no java.time).
accessibility: The title has the heading semantics.
MonarchConsequenceList reads each consequence with its kind.
MonarchTypeToConfirmInput announces when the typed name matches.
The row's Revoke button is named with the item ("Revoke CI deploy key").
Buttons are MonarchButtons with 48dp targets and a loading state while revoking; the sheet cannot be dismissed while revoking, so the result is not lost.
edgeCases: For several items, list each one and put the count in the title and the button ("Revoke 3 keys").
An item never used reads "Never used" instead of a time.
Reset the typed name each time the sheet opens.
After a failure keep the sheet open with the typed name, so the person can try again.
