name: MonarchRichTextEditor
title: RichTextEditor
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.text.BasicTextField with a TextFieldValue and a VisualTransformation that draws AnnotatedString SpanStyles from Monarch's own span model, with MonarchEditorToolbar above it and MonarchMentionPicker below it
summary: A rich-text editor on Compose's BasicTextField: a formatting toolbar for bold, italic, strikethrough, code, links, headings and lists, a prompt, a character count against a limit, @mention suggestions and undo, with the document kept as plain text plus spans.
whenToUse: For descriptions, notes, comments and replies that need inline formatting, links, headings or lists.
whenNotToUse: For plain text, use MonarchTextField or a Material 3 OutlinedTextField with several lines. For block documents with tables, callouts and embeds, compose the block components (MonarchTableBlock, MonarchCalloutBlock).
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable public fun MonarchRichTextEditor(label: String, state: MonarchRichTextEditorState, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, prompt: String? = null, tools: List<List<MonarchEditorTool>> = MonarchRichTextEditorDefaults.Tools, maxLength: Int? = null, showCharacterCount: Boolean? = null, enabled: Boolean = true, readOnly: Boolean = false, invalid: Boolean = false, mentionItems: List<MonarchMentionItem>? = null, mentionStatus: MonarchMentionPickerStatus = MonarchMentionPickerStatus.Ready, icons: Map<MonarchEditorTool, Painter> = emptyMap(), labels: MonarchRichTextEditorLabels = MonarchRichTextEditorLabels(), onMentionSearch: ((MonarchMentionQuery?) -> Unit)? = null, onMention: ((MonarchMentionItem) -> Unit)? = null, onTool: ((MonarchEditorTool) -> Unit)? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)

@Stable public class MonarchRichTextEditorState(text: String = "", spans: List<MonarchRichTextSpan> = emptyList()) { val text: String; val spans: List<MonarchRichTextSpan>; val selection: TextRange; val canUndo: Boolean; val canRedo: Boolean; fun setDocument(text: String, spans: List<MonarchRichTextSpan> = emptyList()); fun undo(); fun redo(); companion object { val Saver: Saver<MonarchRichTextEditorState, Any> } }
@Composable public fun rememberMonarchRichTextEditorState(text: String = "", spans: List<MonarchRichTextSpan> = emptyList()): MonarchRichTextEditorState
public data class MonarchRichTextSpan(mark: MonarchRichTextMark, start: Int, end: Int, url: String? = null)
public enum class MonarchRichTextMark { Bold, Italic, Strikethrough, Code, Link, Heading1, Heading2, Heading3; val isHeading: Boolean }
public object MonarchRichTextEditorDefaults { val Tools: List<List<MonarchEditorTool>>; fun isOverLimit(text: String, maxLength: Int?): Boolean }

public class MonarchRichTextEditorLabels(count: ((Int) -> String)? = null, countOfLimit: ((Int, Int) -> String)? = null, remaining: ((Int) -> String)? = null, over: ((Int) -> String)? = null, toolbar: MonarchEditorToolbarLabels = MonarchEditorToolbarLabels(), mentions: MonarchMentionPickerLabels = MonarchMentionPickerLabels())

options.name: label
options.description: The spoken name of the text area, already localized. Show a visible label nearby, for example with MonarchFormField.

options.name: state
options.description: The document: plain text plus MonarchRichTextSpans, the selection and the undo history. Create it with rememberMonarchRichTextEditorState.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the editor.

options.name: prompt
options.description: Shown in the subtle text color while the document is empty.

options.name: tools
options.description: The toolbar's tools in groups; emptyList() for no toolbar. Undo, redo, body text, headings 1 to 3, bold, italic, strikethrough, code, link and both lists are applied by the editor; custom tools go to onTool; task lists, quotes, code blocks and headings 4 to 6 are left out.

options.name: maxLength
options.description: The most characters. Typing stops there and a paste is cut to fit; the count shows against it. A longer document set by the app shows the danger count and border.

options.name: showCharacterCount
options.description: Shows the count. By default, shown when there is a maxLength.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the text and the toolbar can be used.

options.name: readOnly
options.description: Shows the document as text, without the toolbar or the box; links open on a tap.

options.name: invalid
options.description: Draws the danger border, for a validation error shown nearby.

options.name: mentionItems
options.description: The suggestions for the mention being typed after @ or #; null turns mentions off.

options.name: mentionStatus
options.description: The state of the mention search: loading, ready or failed.

options.name: icons
options.description: The icons of the toolbar's tools. Monarch bundles no icons: a tool without one shows its name.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the count strings, and the toolbar's and mention picker's labels.

options.name: onMentionSearch
options.description: Receives the mention being typed after @ or #, or null when there is none; search and update mentionItems. Also called by the suggestions' retry.

options.name: onMention
options.description: Receives the chosen person or channel after "@Name " is written into the text.

options.name: onTool
options.description: Receives the custom tools of the toolbar.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The interaction source of the text field.

states.name: empty
states.description: The prompt in the subtle text color over the text area.

states.name: focused
states.description: The theme's focus ring around the box while the text or a tool has focus.

states.name: formatting on
states.description: The toolbar toggles of the formats at the caret or over the whole selection are on; the text style menu shows the paragraph's style; a list toggle is on in a list item.

states.name: over the limit
states.description: Only for a longer document set by the app: the count and the border turn the danger color, and the text area's error says how many characters are over.

states.name: invalid
states.description: The danger border.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With enabled = false: the subtle fill and the default border, disabled text, and neither the text nor the toolbar can be used.

states.name: read only
states.description: The document as text, without the box or the toolbar; links are underlined and open on a tap.

states.name: mentioning
states.description: MonarchMentionPicker under the box while @ or # and a name are typed, with its loading, empty and error states.

appearance: A box in the surface color with the input border and medium corners: the toolbar, a subtle divider, then the text in the default text color. Headings use the theme's title, heading and subheading styles, code the code typeface on the muted background, links the link color with an underline. The count is a caption in the muted color, strong danger when over. The roles follow light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web RichTextEditor is built on Tiptap and stores HTML or Tiptap JSON. Compose has no rich-text editor and its styled TextFieldState API sits behind a global foundation flag, so Monarch builds the editor on BasicTextField with a TextFieldValue: the document is plain text plus MonarchRichTextSpans in MonarchRichTextEditorState, which moves the spans with every edit and draws them with a VisualTransformation (the text and offsets are unchanged). iOS binds an AttributedString instead; the Android state is the equivalent, and it stays experimental on both platforms until the interchange format is agreed: no HTML, Markdown or JSON conversion is shipped, and the app stores text and spans. As on iOS: checklists, quotes and code blocks are not offered; lists are text prefixes ("• ", "1. "); headings are levels 1 to 3; a mention is written as plain "@Name " and reported through onMention, where the web inserts a mention node; pasted files are not handled (use MonarchFileUpload beside the editor); the toolbar sits above the text, and the web's toolbarPosition and toolbarEnd are not offered; Markdown typing shortcuts are not offered. Unlike iOS, maxLength stops typing and cuts a paste, as on the web, because the text field reports each change before it is shown. A paste keeps only the plain text, which is the web's safe paste. Undo and redo are the editor's own history of text and formats (100 steps); a hardware keyboard's undo shortcut goes to the text field's own history, which restores text but moves formats only as an edit would. Kotlin-style names: readOnly, invalid and enabled for the iOS isReadOnly, isInvalid and disabled(), showCharacterCount for showsCharacterCount; labels.over is added so the spoken over-the-limit text can be replaced.
accessibility: The text area is a Compose text field whose content description is label, with all system editing actions; past the limit it carries an error, "3 characters over the limit".
The toolbar is MonarchEditorToolbar: a group named "Formatting" whose toggles read their name and on or off state, with 48dp targets; Undo and Redo are disabled when there is nothing to undo or redo.
The count reads "1,988 characters left" or "3 characters over the limit" with a limit, "12 characters" without one, instead of the visible "12 / 2,000".
Mention suggestions are MonarchMentionPicker buttons in a polite live region, so focus can stay in the text.
Formatting is not conveyed by color: bold, italic, strikethrough and headings are type changes, code changes the typeface and links are underlined.
edgeCases: Return at the end of a list item starts the next item (the next number in a numbered list); Return on an empty item ends the list.
Return in a heading splits it into two headings; Return at its end starts body text. Joining a heading to the paragraph before keeps the paragraph's style.

Typing at the end of bold, italic, strikethrough or code continues it; typing after a link does not. A format turned on or off at the caret applies to what is typed next and is dropped when the caret moves.
Characters are counted in UTF-16 units, as String.length, so some emoji count as two.
The undo history is not saved with the state; text, spans and selection are.

parityExceptions.reason: NATIVE GAP: The web document has a heading, bold text, a checklist with one ticked item and a block quote, and the toolbar has the checklist, quote and code block tools. The native editor draws plain text, links and inline marks and the heading mark. A checklist item and the quote are written as lines that start with a check box or a bar glyph, not as real blocks (no check box control, no quote rule, no padding), and the toolbar offers no code block tool. The caret starts at the end of the text, so the quote tool shows as active, where the web has the caret in the heading.
parityExceptions.convention: none: recorded in native-gaps.json

name: MonarchRoadmap
title: Roadmap
wrapsNative: com.rookhq.monarch.components.workflow.gantttimeline.MonarchGanttTimeline (with undated rows, quarter zoom and the roadmap's names), which is built on androidx.compose.ui.layout.SubcomposeLayout and Layout in androidx.compose.foundation.horizontalScroll, androidx.compose.material3.DropdownMenu, SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow and DateRangePicker in DatePickerDialog
summary: Projects over months and quarters, grouped by initiative, with progress, the health last reported in words, milestones and dependencies between projects, on the Gantt timeline.
whenToUse: To give leads a long-range view of projects across teams: when each runs, how far along it is, what was last reported and which projects block others. Pass onChange only where people really replan on this screen.
whenNotToUse: To schedule individual tasks by dragging use MonarchGanttTimeline directly. For a status-only overview without dates use a list of rows with MonarchStatusBadge or a board.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchRoadmap(items: List<MonarchRoadmapItem>, previousIcon: @Composable () -> Unit, nextIcon: @Composable () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, state: MonarchGanttTimelineState = rememberMonarchGanttTimelineState(initialZoom = MonarchGanttTimelineZoom.Year), groups: List<MonarchRoadmapGroup> = emptyList(), dependencies: List<MonarchGanttTimelineDependency> = emptyList(), milestones: List<MonarchGanttTimelineMilestone> = emptyList(), zoomLevels: List<MonarchGanttTimelineZoom> = listOf(MonarchGanttTimelineZoom.Month, MonarchGanttTimelineZoom.Quarter, MonarchGanttTimelineZoom.Year), today: Long? = System.currentTimeMillis(), timeZone: String? = null, toolbar: Boolean = true, onChange: ((MonarchRoadmapItem, MonarchGanttTimelineDates) -> Unit)? = null, onOpen: ((MonarchRoadmapItem) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchRoadmapLabels = MonarchRoadmapLabels(), timelineLabels: MonarchGanttTimelineLabels = MonarchGanttTimelineLabels(), toolbarActions: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null)

class MonarchRoadmapItem(id: String, label: String, start: Long? = null, end: Long? = null, groupId: String? = null, progress: Float? = null, progressText: String? = null, health: MonarchRoadmapHealth? = null, tone: MonarchTone? = null)
class MonarchRoadmapGroup(id: String, label: String, start: Long? = null, end: Long? = null, health: MonarchRoadmapHealth? = null)
enum class MonarchRoadmapHealth { OnTrack, AtRisk, OffTrack, NotReported }
class MonarchRoadmapLabels(health: ((MonarchRoadmapHealth) -> String)? = null, count: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, meta: ((first: String, second: String) -> String)? = null)

options.name: items
options.description: The projects: id, label, start and target day keys (neither makes a row that says "No dates"), groupId, progress from 0 to 1, progressText such as "8/20", health (null writes none, NotReported writes "No health reported") and tone (null takes it from health).

options.name: previousIcon
options.description: The backward chevron of the toolbar. Monarch bundles no icons; the button is named "Earlier" without it.

options.name: nextIcon
options.description: The forward chevron of the toolbar, named "Later".

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the roadmap.

options.name: state
options.description: The first visible day, the zoom, chart or list. The roadmap opens at the quarter zoom (nine months visible).

options.name: groups
options.description: Initiatives, themes or teams as heading rows, in order. Each heading says how many projects it has and its health; a group with dates shows a thin span. Projects without a known group follow the groups.

options.name: dependencies
options.description: Links between projects, drawn as arrows and written as "Depends on" in the list.

options.name: milestones
options.description: Dated checkpoints: on a project's row with itemId, otherwise in a lane under the header.

options.name: zoomLevels
options.description: The zoom levels offered in the toolbar's zoom menu.

options.name: today
options.description: Any time on the day of the today line, read in timeZone; null hides the line and the Today button. Pass a fixed value in tests and previews.

options.name: timeZone
options.description: The zone today is read in. An IANA id such as Europe/Berlin; null, or an id the device does not know, is the device's zone.

options.name: toolbar
options.description: Shows the toolbar: Earlier, Today, Later, the visible range, the zoom menu and the chart or list switch.

options.name: onChange
options.description: Makes dates editable (touch and hold then drag, keyboard, TalkBack actions, the date range picker in the list) and is called with the roadmap project and its new dates. Without it the roadmap is read-only.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Makes each bar and list row a button that calls back with the roadmap project.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the roadmap's own strings: the health words, the group count and the joiner of a heading's second line.

options.name: timelineLabels
options.description: Replacements for the timeline's strings. The chart is named "Roadmap" and the row header says "Project" unless timeline or rowHeader is given here; every other value is passed through.

options.name: toolbarActions
options.description: Extra controls at the end of the toolbar, such as a team filter.

states.name: read only
states.description: The default. Bars have no drag, no key handling and no TalkBack actions; with onOpen they are still buttons that open the project.

states.name: editable
states.description: With onChange, everything the timeline offers to change dates, and onChange receives the roadmap project, not a timeline item.

states.name: health
states.description: On track, at risk, off track or no health reported is written in words on the row heading's second line, after the progress text; at risk tints the bar warning and off track danger.

states.name: no health tracked
states.description: With health null nothing is written about health and the bar keeps the accent color.

states.name: no dates
states.description: A project without dates stays in its group as a row that says "No dates" instead of moving to a separate list.

states.name: out of view
states.description: A project outside the visible window says "Ended …" or "Starts …" on its row.

states.name: list
states.description: The list view writes each project's dates, length, progress, progress text and health and its dependencies.

appearance: As MonarchGanttTimeline: on the surface color with subtle lines, group headings on the subtle background. Bars are a light tint of the accent with the accent's strong fill as outline and progress strip; at-risk bars use the warning tint and off-track bars the danger tint. The second line of each heading (progress text, health, count) is in the muted text color. High-contrast themes swap in their own roles.
platformNotes: There is no iOS Roadmap inventory entry yet, so the names follow the web and the plan (MonarchRoadmap, MonarchRoadmapItem, MonarchRoadmapGroup, MonarchRoadmapHealth, MonarchRoadmapLabels). The web shows health as a Badge with a dot next to the progress text; MonarchGanttTimeline takes its row meta as a plain String, so Android writes the progress text and the health word on one muted line ("8/20 · On track") with no dot or badge color: the words carry the meaning, the bar tint repeats it. The web's no-health dash with hidden text becomes the visible words "No health reported" (MonarchRoadmapHealth.NotReported), and the web's undefined versus null becomes null (nothing written) versus NotReported. Item title is a plain label, not a composable slot. Progress is 0 to 1 instead of 0 to 100, dates are UTC day keys instead of ISO strings, and onChange returns nothing (the web's promise and rollback become the app passing new items back). The web's tone accent is tone = null, because MonarchTone has no accent tone; an app cannot force the accent color on an at-risk or off-track project. defaultZoom becomes the state parameter, which defaults to the quarter zoom. Everything else (sideways-only chart scrolling, touch and hold to drag, the list as the phone and TalkBack alternative) is as described for gantt-timeline. Experimental because MonarchGanttTimeline is experimental and no Rook Android app has adopted it.
accessibility: Each bar is one element read as "<project>, <start> to <end>, <n>% complete"; with onOpen it is a button with a 48dp touch target reserved in the layout.
Health is written as words ("On track", "At risk", "Off track", "No health reported") in the row heading, never shown by the bar color alone.
A group heading is one TalkBack heading that reads its name, its project count and its health.
Without onChange bars have no TalkBack actions; with onChange they offer the timeline's move and resize actions and changes are announced by a polite live region.
The chart and the list are named "Roadmap" for TalkBack, and the row header says "Project", both replaceable.
Project names stay at the start in right to left layouts, and headings wrap at font scale 2.0 without cutting text.
edgeCases: A project without dates stays in its group as a "No dates" row; a project with only one date is a one-day marker.
A group with no projects says "0 projects"; a groupId that matches no group puts the project after the groups.
Without progressText and health a project heading has no second line.
An explicit tone always wins over the health tint.
Callbacks receive the same MonarchRoadmapItem instance the app passed, so the app can match it by identity or id.
Item lists are mapped again only when items, groups, labels or the configuration change.

name: MonarchRolePicker
title: RolePicker
wrapsNative: MonarchRadioCardGroup (androidx.compose.material3.Surface selectable cards with RadioButton) for cards; androidx.compose.material3.ExposedDropdownMenuBox with a read-only OutlinedTextField for compact
summary: Chooses a role for a person, with what each role can do in plain words, as radio cards or a compact menu field. Roles that cannot be chosen stay visible with the reason.
whenToUse: In invite, member and sharing forms, where the person must understand what a role allows before choosing it.
whenNotToUse: For choices without descriptions use a MonarchRadioRow list or a Material 3 ExposedDropdownMenuBox. For several permissions at once use a list of MonarchSwitchRow or MonarchCheckboxRow.
api: @Composable fun <T> MonarchRolePicker(roles: List<MonarchRoleOption<T>>, selected: T?, onSelect: (T) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, layout: MonarchRolePickerLayout = MonarchRolePickerLayout.Cards, enabled: Boolean = true, label: String? = null, helperText: String? = null, errorText: String? = null, placeholder: String? = null)
class MonarchRoleOption<out T>(value: T, title: String, description: String? = null, capabilities: List<String> = emptyList(), enabled: Boolean = true, disabledReason: String? = null)
enum class MonarchRolePickerLayout { Cards, Compact }

options.name: roles
options.description: The roles, from least to most access.

options.name: selected
options.description: The value of the chosen role, or null for no choice yet.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Called with the value of the role the person chooses.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the picker.

options.name: layout
options.description: Cards shows every role with its description and capabilities; Compact is a menu field with the chosen role's description under it.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether any role can be chosen.

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the built-in label "Role".

options.name: helperText
options.description: Help under the control.

options.name: errorText
options.description: An error under the control in the danger strong color; replaces the helper text. The compact field also takes the error semantics.

options.name: placeholder
options.description: Replaces the compact field's built-in "Choose a role", shown while nothing is chosen.

states.name: selected
states.description: Cards: the radio card's filled mark, accent fill and heavier border. Compact: the role's name in the field and its description under it.

states.name: role disabled
states.description: The card in the disabled colors with the reason under the description; in the menu the item cannot be chosen and shows the reason.

states.name: error
states.description: The error text in the danger strong color under the control.

states.name: disabled
states.description: enabled = false disables every role and the compact field.

appearance: The cards layout is MonarchRadioCardGroup and takes its colors. The compact layout is the Material 3 exposed dropdown with the MonarchTextField colors. Helper text uses the muted text role; errors the danger strong role. All roles come from the theme.
platformNotes: The web's compact layout is a custom select with descriptions in each option; Android uses the Material 3 ExposedDropdownMenuBox, whose items show the description and capabilities under the title, with the chosen role's description under the field, as iOS shows it under its menu picker. Capabilities are lines of the card text, because MonarchRadioCardOption takes one description. Selection is hoisted as selected and onSelect, as in MonarchRadioCardGroup, instead of the iOS Binding. The web's required marker and form name have no Android equivalent. The error has no icon because Monarch bundles none; it is text with the error semantics on the compact field.
accessibility: Cards: each role is a radio button with its title and its description, capabilities and reason, selected when chosen, in a selectable group with the label.
Compact: a Material 3 read-only field named by the label that opens a menu; disabled roles cannot be chosen.
The compact field sets the error semantics with the error text; the error is text, not color alone.
Every card and the field are at least 48dp high.
edgeCases: A selection that matches no role shows no card selected and the compact placeholder.
Long descriptions and many capabilities wrap inside the card and the menu item.
A disabled role without a reason shows only its description.

name: MonarchRookBar
title: RookBar
wrapsNative: MonarchIconButton, MonarchButton, MonarchBottomSheet, MonarchMegaMenu
summary: The Rook company bar for the public, signed-out screens of a Rook app: the app's wordmark, the account buttons and a menu button that opens the company menu (products, services, pricing, news) in a full-height bottom sheet. Rook-scoped.
whenToUse: At the top of the signed-out screens of a Rook app that should match the company site.
whenNotToUse: Inside the signed-in app, use the app shell (rook-rail). Outside Rook, use MonarchSiteShell or MonarchMegaMenu in the app's own navigation.
api: @Composable fun MonarchRookBar(brand: String, items: List<MonarchMegaMenuItem>, menuOpen: Boolean, onMenuOpenChange: (Boolean) -> Unit, onNavigate: (String) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, account: MonarchRookBarAccount? = null, onAccountAction: (MonarchRookBarAction) -> Unit = {}, brandMark: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, onBrandClick: (() -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchRookBarLabels = MonarchRookBarLabels())
sealed interface MonarchRookBarAccount { data object SignedOut; data class SignedIn(val name: String) }
enum class MonarchRookBarAction { SignIn, SignUp, Dashboard, Account, SignOut }
class MonarchRookBarLabels(nav: String? = null, openMenu: String? = null, signIn: String? = null, signUp: String? = null, dashboard: String? = null, account: String? = null, signOut: String? = null)

options.name: brand
options.description: The app's name beside its mark.

options.name: items
options.description: The company menu: Products, Services, Pricing and News, with sections, links and featured cards.

options.name: menuOpen
options.description: Whether the menu sheet is shown.

options.name: onMenuOpenChange
options.description: Called with true by the menu button and false when the sheet closes.

options.name: onNavigate
options.description: Called with the link the user taps; the sheet closes first.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the bar.

options.name: account
options.description: SignedOut ("Log in", "Sign up") or SignedIn(name) ("Open dashboard", "Account settings", "Sign out"); null shows none.

options.name: onAccountAction
options.description: Called with the account action the user taps.

options.name: brandMark
options.description: The app's mark before the name.

options.name: onBrandClick
options.description: Called when the brand is tapped, normally to go home; null makes the brand plain text.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for "Rook", "Open menu", "Log in", "Sign up", "Open dashboard", "Account settings" and "Sign out".

states.name: signed out
states.description: The inverse "Sign up" pill sits in the bar from 288dp wide and "Log in" beside it from 448dp, at font scale 1.3 or less; both are always at the end of the menu sheet.

states.name: signed in
states.description: The sheet ends with the person's name, "Open dashboard", "Account settings" and "Sign out".

states.name: menu open
states.description: A full-height bottom sheet with the company menu as a MonarchMegaMenu.

appearance: The bar is the surface with a subtle line under it; the brand uses the default text in the subheading style; "Sign up" is a MonarchButton in the Inverse variant with the full shape, as on the company site. The menu uses MonarchMegaMenu's roles. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web RookBar shows the menus in the bar with hover panels (an app catalog, a featured panel, recent posts) and a full-height sheet on phones. On Android the bar always uses the sheet, as the web does on phones, and the panels are MonarchMegaMenu entries: app categories are sections with their promise as the description, the catalog's "Every app" is the featured card, and recent posts are links with their label and date. The bar never fetches; the app passes the posts. The web's colorScheme, position and cross-app cookie options do not apply.
accessibility: The bar is a traversal group named "Rook"; the menu sheet is a pane with the same name.
The menu button is named "Open menu" and has a 48dp touch target.
The menu entries are MonarchMegaMenu rows: buttons that read their expanded state; external links say they open outside the app.
Account buttons are buttons with touch targets of at least 48dp.
edgeCases: Above font scale 1.3 the account buttons are only in the sheet, so the brand keeps its room.
The sheet closes before onNavigate and onAccountAction are called.

appearance: The Material 3 modal navigation drawer and items in the Monarch theme, with the Monarch switchers and avatar. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from the theme's color scheme.
platformNotes: The web RookRail is a 48dp rail of icons that expands to labels, remembers its state in the rook_rail cookie shared across Rook apps, and becomes a top bar with a drawer below 768px. On a phone Android uses that phone form: a TopAppBar with a navigation icon that opens a ModalNavigationDrawer, which brings focus handling, the scrim, the back gesture and swipe to close. The cookie and the expanded state do not apply: the drawer starts closed, and each app restores its own destination. Links are callbacks: destinations of the app navigate inside it; Rook ID and other products open in a Custom Tab, so the web's "opens in a new tab" becomes a description that says where it opens. Keyboard shortcuts and tooltips of the collapsed rail are not offered; TalkBack reads each item's label. On wide windows a PermanentNavigationDrawer, or the Material 3 WideNavigationRail (an expressive, experimental API in Material 3 1.4), shows the same items beside the content. The theme toggle and notifications slots of the web go into the account menu and the top app bar's actions (the identity-bar recipe). Rook-specific: apps outside Rook use the app-shell recipe. MonarchWorkspaceSwitcher and MonarchSpaceSwitcher are experimental, so the recipe opts in where it uses them. iOS has the same recipe coverage.
accessibility: The menu button is named "Open navigation"; the drawer and its items are Material 3 navigation drawer items with the selected state and 48dp rows.
Icons are decorative; every item is named by its label.
An unread count is a badge hidden from TalkBack and read as the item's state, "3 unread".
A link that leaves the app says so as its state, "Opens in Rook ID".
The account item is named "Account: " and the person's name; the avatar is decorative.
The drawer closes with the back gesture, a tap on the scrim or after choosing a destination.
edgeCases: Long section lists scroll inside the drawer, which has no lazy list, so it may sit in the drawer's column.
Hide the space switcher when the workspace has no spaces (MonarchSpaceSwitcher does this with hidesWhenEmpty).
Keep a large count short in the badge (such as 99+) and give the full number in the state description.

title: RovingFocusGroup
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.focusGroup, androidx.compose.ui.focus.focusRestorer, androidx.compose.ui.focus.FocusRequester
summary: Moving focus inside a toolbar, a set of options or a grid with a hardware keyboard is done by the Compose focus system. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: Nothing is needed for standard controls: Tab moves between focusable elements and the arrow keys move focus in their direction. Wrap a set of controls in focusGroup() so Tab treats it as one stop in the traversal order, add focusRestorer() so focus returns to the last focused item, and use a FocusRequester to move focus in code.
whenNotToUse: Do not make every item of a long list or grid focusable by hand; lazy lists and grids take part in focus search themselves. Do not intercept the arrow keys unless the group has a custom order the layout does not express.
api: fun Modifier.focusGroup(): Modifier
fun Modifier.focusRestorer(fallback: FocusRequester = FocusRequester.Default): Modifier
class FocusRequester { fun requestFocus(): Boolean }
fun Modifier.focusRequester(focusRequester: FocusRequester): Modifier
fun Modifier.focusProperties(scope: FocusProperties.() -> Unit): Modifier

states.name: focused item
states.description: The focused control draws its own focus indication (Monarch controls draw the focus ring).

appearance: No appearance of its own: focus is drawn by each control, and Monarch controls draw the focus ring in the focus-ring color of the theme.
platformNotes: The web needs RovingFocusGroup because a browser puts every control in the Tab order and gives the arrow keys no meaning; it keeps one tabindex=0 item and moves it with the arrows, Home and End. On Android with a hardware keyboard, Compose moves focus with the arrow keys by two-dimensional search, and focusGroup() makes a set of controls one stop for Tab. focusRestorer() returns to the last focused item, which is what the roving tabindex achieves. The web's loop and Home/End have no built-in equivalent; add onPreviewKeyEvent on the group if a toolbar needs them. Only matters with a hardware keyboard or a D-pad. iOS uses its focus engine in the same way.
accessibility: System behavior: Tab and Shift+Tab move between focus groups and focusable elements in layout order; the arrow keys move focus to the nearest element in their direction.
TalkBack does not use keyboard focus: it moves through elements by swiping, so focus groups change nothing for it.
With focusRestorer, Tab back into the group focuses the item that was focused last.
edgeCases: focusRestorer needs the items to have stable identity; in a lazy list give each item a key.
requestFocus() throws when the FocusRequester is not attached to a composed element; call it from an event or after composition.

appearance: A MonarchIconButton with the app's "more" icon in the muted content color, and the Monarch menu in the raised background role; the destructive item takes the strong danger role. The swipe background uses the subtle role of the action's tone. The same mapping in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web RowActionsMenu is a component that sorts danger items to the end and opens a ConfirmDialog for items with confirm. On Android the app lists the items in that order with a MonarchDivider before the destructive ones and shows a MonarchDialog itself, so Monarch adds no type. Android adds SwipeToDismissBox for the primary action, which the web does not have; give the same action to TalkBack as a custom action on the row, because a swipe is not reachable with TalkBack. Monarch bundles no icons, so the "more" icon is the app's. The web shortcut hint has no touch equivalent. iOS documents the same menu as a native SwiftUI Menu with swipe actions.

The MonarchIconButton has a 48dp touch target and each menu item a row at least 48dp high.
The swipe action is also a custom accessibility action on the row, so TalkBack users can run it from the actions menu.
The confirmation MonarchDialog takes focus; the destructive item says what it does, so color is not the only signal.

Allow only one swipe direction (enableDismissFromStartToEnd = false) so the gesture always means the same action.
A destructive action that runs at once after a swipe should offer Undo in a snackbar instead of a confirmation.

whenToUse: When admins create automation or routing rules of the form when this happens, if these hold, do these things, and the product's rule engine takes triggers, conditions and actions as data.
whenNotToUse: For conditions only (show this question when) use MonarchConditionEditor; for a list of steps only use MonarchActionEditor; for a formula keep a dedicated formula editor.

appearance: Section labels as subheadings, Monarch fields, editors and switch rows in the theme, and a danger banner for a blocked save. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web RuleBuilder is one form component with built-in validation, focus moved to the summary, a submit promise, cancel and an options slot. On Android it is a recipe on one scrolling screen, which is the phone pattern for a long form; the Save and Cancel actions can also live in the screen's TopAppBar. The validation is the app's: MonarchCondition.problems and MonarchRuleAction.problems give the incomplete parts. MonarchConditionEditor and MonarchActionEditor are experimental, so the example opts in at each call. Reordering actions uses MonarchActionEditor's move buttons, which TalkBack reaches directly. iOS has no entry yet; its plan is also a recipe.

A blocked save shows a danger banner announced assertively and listing what is missing; each field also shows its own error in words.
Triggers are checkbox rows with the checkbox role; options are switch rows with their state.
The editors name each condition and action by position and move actions with buttons, never only by dragging.

Empty conditions are allowed: the rule then applies whenever it is checked.
Keep the problems list in the order of the form so the banner reads top to bottom.

One row needs the field picker at 120dp, the operator picker at 120dp, the value at 96dp, the remove button at 48dp and three 8dp gaps, 408dp, which does not fit. summary: A running stopwatch for time tracking: a panel with a large clock, Start, Stop, "I stopped earlier" and a confirmed Discard, or a compact indicator for a top bar.
whenToUse: For tracking time on an issue, a task or a project, in a timesheet screen (panel) or in a top bar while the person works elsewhere (indicator).
whenNotToUse: For a countdown or a deadline use MonarchSlaIndicator. For entering time by hand use a form with MonarchNumberInput. For a timer outside the app (an ongoing notification) use the platform's notifications; that stays in the app.
api: @Composable fun MonarchRunningTimer(startedAt: Long?, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchRunningTimerVariant = MonarchRunningTimerVariant.Panel, label: String? = null, warnAfterMillis: Long? = 43_200_000L, startEnabled: Boolean = true, pending: Boolean = false, showWhenStopped: Boolean = false, now: Long? = null, timeZone: String? = null, menuIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchRunningTimerLabels = MonarchRunningTimerLabels(), onStart: (suspend () -> Unit)? = null, onStop: (suspend () -> Unit)? = null, onStopAt: (suspend (Long) -> Unit)? = null, onDiscard: (suspend () -> Unit)? = null, onOpen: (() -> Unit)? = null, fields: (@Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)? = null)
enum class MonarchRunningTimerVariant { Panel, Indicator }

class MonarchRunningTimerLabels(start, stop, stopAndLog, more, moreActions, discard, discardTitle, discardMessage, discardConfirm, stoppedEarlier, stoppedEarlierTitle, stoppedEarlierMessage, started: ((String) -> String)?, workDuration: ((String) -> String)?, save, cancel, stoppedAtFuture, stoppedAtTooEarly, failed, running, stopped, defaultLabel, open, longRunning: ((String) -> String)?), every parameter optional and String? unless noted

options.name: startedAt
options.description: When the running timer started, in epoch milliseconds; null when no timer runs. The app changes it when an action succeeds.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the timer.

options.name: variant
options.description: Panel: a large clock with buttons and fields. Indicator: a compact chip with a stop button and a menu.

options.name: label
options.description: What is being timed, such as an issue key. Shown under the panel's clock and in the indicator ("Timer" when null).

options.name: warnAfterMillis
options.description: Shows a warning once the timer has run this long: a message on the panel, warning colors on the indicator. null turns it off.

options.name: startEnabled
options.description: Whether Start can be pressed, for example only once a required project is chosen.

options.name: pending
options.description: An action runs outside the component: Start shows a spinner and the other buttons are disabled.

options.name: showWhenStopped
options.description: Keeps the indicator visible, at 0:00:00, while no timer runs.

options.name: now
options.description: A fixed reference time, which also stops the clock. For previews, screenshots and tests.

options.name: timeZone
options.description: The zone of the times in the earlier-stop dialog. An IANA id such as Europe/Berlin; null, or an id the device does not know, is the device's zone.

options.name: menuIcon
options.description: The icon of the indicator's menu button. Without it the button reads "More". Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: onStart
options.description: Starts a timer. Adds Start to the stopped panel; the button shows a spinner until it returns.

options.name: onStop
options.description: Stops the timer and logs the time. Adds Stop to the panel and the indicator.

options.name: onStopAt
options.description: Stops the timer at an earlier time. Adds "I stopped earlier", which asks for the time of day.

options.name: onDiscard
options.description: Throws the running time away. Adds Discard (a button on the panel, a menu item on the indicator), confirmed first.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Opens what is being timed. Makes the indicator's clock a button.

options.name: fields
options.description: Fields for the entry being timed, such as a project picker, shown in the panel between the clock and the buttons.

states.name: stopped
states.description: The panel shows 0:00:00 in the muted text color and Start; the indicator is hidden unless showWhenStopped.

states.name: running
states.description: The clock ticks every second in the strong accent color; the panel shows Stop, "I stopped earlier" and Discard; the indicator has the accent surface.

states.name: long running
states.description: After warnAfterMillis the panel shows a warning message; the indicator takes the warning colors.

states.name: busy
states.description: The button of the action in progress shows a spinner and the others are disabled; pending shows the same from outside.

states.name: failed
states.description: A thrown error is shown as text under the buttons (panel) or turns the indicator to the danger colors and is added to its state; it is announced.

states.name: stopping earlier
states.description: A dialog with the start time, a Material 3 TimeInput suggesting an hour after the start, and the length of work that will be saved; Save is disabled for a time in the future or less than a minute after the start.

states.name: discarding
states.description: A dialog asks "Discard the running timer?" with a danger Discard button.

appearance: The panel's clock uses the display style with tabular figures, in the strong accent color while running, the strong warning color when long running and the muted color when stopped. The indicator is a rounded chip on the accent, warning, danger or muted subtle surface with text in the matching strong color. Warnings and errors are caption text in the strong warning and danger colors.
platformNotes: The web's datetime-local input is a Material 3 TimeInput: the chosen time of day is the latest such moment at or before now, which covers timers shorter than a day (a timer that ran longer can still be stopped at a time within the last 24 hours, or discarded). The web's required and invalid errors cannot happen; the future and too-early checks remain. The web's trash, play and stop glyphs are text buttons and the indicator's chevron menu button is an optional icon slot, because Monarch bundles no icons. The web's description hover text is not offered: touch has no hover. The clock uses tabular figures of the text face rather than the monospaced family. The actions suspend instead of returning promises. Showing the timer outside the app stays in the product. iOS builds the same component with the same name.
accessibility: The clock is one element: its content description is the label and the time in words ("ENG-142, 4 minutes, 9 seconds"); its state description is "Timer running" or "Timer stopped", followed by a failure if there is one.
Starting and stopping are announced through a polite live region that is always present, even when the indicator hides; the ticking is not announced.
With onOpen the indicator's clock is a button with the click label "Open" and a 48dp touch target.
The indicator's stop button is named "Stop timer and log time" and its menu button "More timer actions"; each has a 48dp touch target.
Failures and the long-running warning are text in polite live regions, not color alone.
The earlier-stop dialog has a title, the start time, a Material 3 TimeInput and the length of work as text.
edgeCases: A start in the future shows 0:00:00.
Times of 100 hours and more widen the clock (100:00:00).
When startedAt becomes null the discard confirmation and the earlier-stop dialog close.
The dialogs cannot be dismissed while they save.
With now set the clock does not tick.
An error without a message shows "That did not work. Try again."; an error with a message shows the message, as on the web.

name: MonarchSaveStatusIndicator
title: SaveStatusIndicator
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row, androidx.compose.material3.Text, androidx.compose.material3.CircularProgressIndicator, MonarchButton
summary: A small inline status for saving: "Saving…", "Saved · 2 minutes ago" or "Couldn't save" with a Retry button.
whenToUse: In an editor's top bar, next to a form's actions or under a field that saves on its own, so people know whether their edits are safe.
whenNotToUse: For a save the user started with a button and then leaves the screen, confirm with a snackbar. For the age of synced data, use MonarchFreshnessIndicator.
api: @Composable fun MonarchSaveStatusIndicator(status: MonarchSaveStatus, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, announceSaving: Boolean = false, savedAt: Long? = null, errorMessage: String? = null, icon: (@Composable (MonarchSaveStatus) -> Unit)? = null, onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchSaveStatusIndicatorLabels = MonarchSaveStatusIndicatorLabels())
enum class MonarchSaveStatus { Idle, Unsaved, Saving, Saved, Error }
class MonarchSaveStatusIndicatorLabels(unsaved: String? = null, saving: String? = null, saved: String? = null, error: String? = null, retry: String? = null)

options.name: status
options.description: Idle (nothing drawn), Unsaved, Saving, Saved or Error.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the indicator.

options.name: announceSaving
options.description: Also announces "Saving…". Off by default so autosaves stay quiet.

options.name: savedAt
options.description: When the last save finished, in epoch milliseconds (UTC); shown as relative time after "Saved" and redrawn every minute.

options.name: errorMessage
options.description: Replaces "Couldn't save" with the reason.

options.name: icon
options.description: Replaces the dot for Unsaved, Saved and Error, for example a check mark. Tinted with the status color.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Adds a Retry button to the error status.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for monarch_savestatusindicator_unsaved, _saving, _saved, _error and _retry.

states.name: idle
states.description: Nothing is drawn; the live region stays.

states.name: unsaved
states.description: A warning dot and "Unsaved changes".

states.name: saving
states.description: A small progress ring and "Saving…"; a still dot when animations are off.

states.name: saved
states.description: A success dot (or the icon), "Saved" and the relative time. Announced.

states.name: error
states.description: A danger dot, the error in danger text and the Retry button. Announced.

appearance: Caption text in the muted text color; the error text in the strong danger color. The mark takes subtle text while saving and the strong success, warning or danger color for saved, unsaved and error. Retry is a small ghost MonarchButton. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web uses check, warning and dot glyphs; Monarch for Android bundles no icons, so the mark is a dot unless the app passes icon, and the words always carry the status. The web announces through a polite live region, as here; iOS posts an announcement. Times are epoch milliseconds, formatted with DateUtils. iOS shares the name and the statuses.
accessibility: The mark, the status and the time are one TalkBack element read as "Saved, 2 minutes ago"; the mark and the middle dot are hidden.
A change to Saved or Error is announced through a polite live region on a node that is always present; Saving only with announceSaving. The first status is not announced.
The live region is emptied for a frame before each announcement, so a second "Saved" is announced again.
Retry is a separate button with a 48dp touch target.
The progress ring is replaced by a still dot when animations are off.
Long error messages wrap at the largest font size.
edgeCases: savedAt is shown only with Saved.
onRetry without the Error status shows no button.
A save that fails with the same message twice is announced twice.

name: MonarchSavedViews
title: SavedViews
wrapsNative: MonarchButton (androidx.compose.material3.Button) with androidx.compose.material3.DropdownMenu, DropdownMenuItem and RadioButton; androidx.compose.material3.AlertDialog with MonarchTextField for naming and confirming
summary: A menu button that switches between named views of a list (filters, sort and columns), with an Edited marker and actions to save, save as new, discard, rename, set the default and delete.
whenToUse: Above a list, table or board where people save combinations of filters, sort and columns under a name and come back to them.
whenNotToUse: For a fixed set of tabs use a Material 3 TabRow. For a single sort or filter choice use a menu button (DropdownMenu) or MonarchRolePicker.
api: @Composable fun MonarchSavedViews(views: List<MonarchSavedView>, selectedId: String?, onSelect: (String) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, size: MonarchButtonSize = MonarchButtonSize.Md, modified: Boolean = false, enabled: Boolean = true, maxNameLength: Int = 80, trailingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchSavedViewsLabels = MonarchSavedViewsLabels(), onSaveNew: (suspend (String) -> Unit)? = null, onSaveChanges: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, onDiscardChanges: (() -> Unit)? = null, onRename: (suspend (String, String) -> Unit)? = null, onDelete: (suspend (String) -> Unit)? = null, onSetDefault: ((String) -> Unit)? = null)
class MonarchSavedView(id: String, name: String, count: Int? = null, shared: Boolean = false, default: Boolean = false, readOnly: Boolean = false, group: String? = null)

class MonarchSavedViewsLabels(view, noView, modified, shared, defaultView, views, saveChanges: ((String) -> String)?, saveAsNew, discardChanges, rename, setDefault, delete, saveTitle, renameTitle, name, save, cancel, nameRequired, nameTaken, saveFailed, deleteTitle: ((String) -> String)?, deleteMessage, deleteConfirm, deleteFailed), every parameter optional and String? unless noted

options.name: views
options.description: The views in menu order, each with an id, a name and optionally a count, shared, default, readOnly and a group.

options.name: selectedId
options.description: The id of the selected view, or null for none (the button then reads "All items").

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Called with the id of the chosen view; apply its filters, sort and columns.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the button.

options.name: size
options.description: The size of the menu button. The web's xs is Sm; the touch target is 48dp at every size.

options.name: modified
options.description: The list differs from the selected view: shows an Edited badge and offers to save or discard.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the menu can be opened.

options.name: maxNameLength
options.description: The longest name the naming field accepts; longer input is cut while typing.

options.name: trailingIcon
options.description: A decorative icon at the end of the button, such as a down chevron. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string: the button, the menu items, the dialog titles, the validation and failure messages and the delete confirmation.

options.name: onSaveNew
options.description: Stores the current state under the trimmed name and selects it. Offers "Save as new view…". The dialog stays open until it returns.

options.name: onSaveChanges
options.description: Saves the current state into the view with the id. Offered when modified and the view is not read-only.

options.name: onDiscardChanges
options.description: Reapplies the selected view. Offered when modified.

options.name: onRename
options.description: Renames the view with the id to the trimmed name. Offered for a selected view that is not read-only.

options.name: onDelete
options.description: Deletes the view with the id after the person confirms. Offered for a selected view that is not read-only.

options.name: onSetDefault
options.description: Makes the view with the id open by default. Offered for a selected view that is not already the default.

states.name: selected
states.description: The button shows the view's name and count; in the menu the view's radio button is selected.

states.name: edited
states.description: A warning badge reading "Edited" after the name, and Save changes and Discard changes in the menu.

states.name: none selected
states.description: The button reads "All items".

states.name: read-only
states.description: Save changes, Rename and Delete are not offered.

states.name: naming
states.description: A dialog with a Name field; Save shows "Enter a name." or "A view with this name already exists." under the field, and a busy spinner while the callback runs.

states.name: deleting
states.description: A dialog titled "Delete “Open deals”?" with a danger Delete view button and Cancel.

states.name: failed
states.description: A thrown error keeps the dialog open with "The view could not be saved. Try again." or "The view could not be deleted. Try again."

states.name: disabled
states.description: The button takes its disabled colors and the menu does not open.

appearance: The button is a secondary MonarchButton; the count is in the muted text color and Edited is a warning badge. The menu and dialogs take the theme's raised surface; Delete view is in the strong danger color and its confirm button is the danger variant. High contrast themes use their stronger roles.
platformNotes: The web keeps its dialogs open while a returned promise is pending; on Android onSaveNew, onRename and onDelete suspend, so the dialog stays open with a busy button and shows a failure when they throw, as on the web (iOS uses system alerts and synchronous callbacks instead). onSaveChanges, onDiscardChanges and onSetDefault are menu actions that return at once; the app reports their failures. The web's visually hidden "View:" prefix is the button's content description "View". The web's star for the default view is the words "Default view", because Monarch bundles no icons. The web's uncontrolled defaultValue is not offered: state is hoisted. A delete failure has its own message here; the web reuses the save failure. iOS builds the same component with the same name.
accessibility: The menu button is named "View"; its state description is the selected view's name followed by "Edited" when modified.
Edited is a word in a badge, not only a color.
In the menu each view has the selected state and a radio button; its count, Shared and Default view are read as its second line.
Group headings in the menu have heading semantics.
The naming and delete steps are dialogs with a Cancel button; the back gesture cancels them unless a save is running.
The button has a touch target of at least 48 by 48dp and its text scales with the font size setting.
edgeCases: Only actions with a callback are offered; with no callbacks the menu only switches views.
Names are trimmed before they are passed to onSaveNew and onRename, and cut to maxNameLength while typing.
Renaming a view to its own name in another case is allowed.
Choosing the selected view again only closes the menu.
A long view name stays on one line in the button and ends with an ellipsis; the full name is in the menu and in what TalkBack reads.

parityExceptions.reason: The web names this control with one sentence ("View: My open tickets"). On Android TalkBack gets the control name and its current value as the control's name and state description ("View", "My open tickets"), which it speaks as one phrase and announces again when the value changes; the same words are visible in the control.
parityExceptions.convention: a control has a name and a state, not a joined sentence (Android accessibility: contentDescription + stateDescription)

name: MonarchSavingsPanel

whenNotToUse: For all upcoming renewals with owners and actions, use MonarchRenewalsPanel. For a full list of subscriptions, use MonarchSubscriptionsTable.

options.name: modifier

options.name: locale

options.name: loading

options.name: error

options.name: retrying
options.description: The retry of the error state is running.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Try again in the error state.

options.name: onCategoryClick
options.description: Makes each category a button, for example to open the filtered list. Replaces the web href.

options.name: onItemClick

options.name: emptyIcon
options.description: An icon for the empty state. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: actions
options.description: Header actions of the card, such as Review all.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including the headline.

states.name: content
states.description: The headline in the strong body style, category badges with counts, the decision line in the muted color, the savings line in the strong success color, and up to maxItems rows.

states.name: more
states.description: When there are more items than maxItems, "and N more" under the list.

states.name: pressable
states.description: With onCategoryClick or onItemClick, categories and rows are buttons at least 48dp tall with a focus ring.

states.name: loading
states.description: Skeleton rows named "Loading savings".

states.name: error
states.description: "Savings could not be loaded." with the app's message and Try again.

states.name: empty
states.description: unusedCount 0: a success empty state, "Nothing unused".

appearance: A MonarchSectionCard with text in the default and muted colors, status badges in their tones (categories subtle, item categories outline), subtle dividers between rows and the savings line in the strong success color, which is also written in words. The same in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web SavingsPanel is a section with links, ReactNode slots and a skeleton. On Android the hrefs and renderLink become onCategoryClick and onItemClick, amounts are BigDecimal in major units (no minorUnits), and dates are epoch milliseconds (UTC) written with android.icu.text.DateFormat without a timeZone parameter. The web distinguishes amount null ("No price") from undefined (nothing); here that is MonarchSavingsItem.unpriced. The parity map named LazyColumn rows; the panel is a Column inside a MonarchSectionCard so it can sit in the screen's verticalScroll, and the list is capped by maxItems. The parity map listed badge as a dependency; categories and decisions use MonarchStatusBadge with a registry, as on the web. The savings line is in the strong success color; the web leaves it in the default color. iOS has not built SavingsPanel yet; the names follow the web.
accessibility: The headline is plain text that TalkBack reads in full: "3 unused items cost $120.00 + €80.00 to renew (1 without a price).".
The categories are a traversal group named "Unused by reason"; each category is one element read as its label and count, "Parked, 2", and a button with onCategoryClick.
The decision line is read with its prefix: "Decisions: Keep 1 · Review 1".
The item list is a traversal group named "Unused items"; each row is one element read in words: name, category, date, amount or "No price", decision.
Pressable categories and rows keep a 48dp touch target and draw a focus ring.
Statuses and savings are always written in words, never shown by color alone.
Text wraps at font scale 2.0; right to left, the facts of a row mirror.
edgeCases: Costs in several currencies are joined with plus signs, never converted or added.
A category with a count of 0 is left out.
maxItems below 0 counts as 0, so every item is counted as "more".
An unknown status key is neutral with a label made from the key ("no_website" gives "No website").

name: MonarchSchemaDrivenForm
title: SchemaDrivenForm
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn of MonarchFieldRenderer, with MonarchButton, MonarchBanner, MonarchFormActionsBar and MonarchDescriptionList
summary: A form generated from a list of question definitions: the right input for each question, sections and conditional questions, validation, and a submit button that shows progress and errors.
whenToUse: For forms whose questions are data: admin-authored intake forms, settings defined on the server, surveys and applications. The same definitions drive MonarchFieldRenderer and a form builder's preview.
whenNotToUse: For a fixed form known at build time, compose MonarchTextField, MonarchSelect and the other inputs directly, which allows custom layout. For a single question, use MonarchFieldRenderer.
api: @Composable fun MonarchSchemaDrivenForm(fields: List<MonarchFormFieldDefinition>, values: Map<String, MonarchFormFieldValue?>, onValuesChange: (values: Map<String, MonarchFormFieldValue?>, fieldId: String) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, onSubmit: (suspend (values: Map<String, MonarchFormFieldValue?>) -> Unit)? = null, validateOn: MonarchSchemaDrivenFormValidateOn = MonarchSchemaDrivenFormValidateOn.Blur, enabled: Boolean = true, readOnly: Boolean = false, dirty: Boolean? = null, errors: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(), state: LazyListState = rememberLazyListState(), contentPadding: PaddingValues = PaddingValues(), locale: Locale? = null, labels: MonarchSchemaDrivenFormLabels = MonarchSchemaDrivenFormLabels(), onDiscard: (() -> Unit)? = null, secondaryActions: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null)
enum class MonarchSchemaDrivenFormValidateOn { Blur, Submit }

class MonarchSchemaDrivenFormLabels(submit: String? = null, submitFailed: String? = null, empty: String? = null, fields: MonarchFieldRendererLabels = MonarchFieldRendererLabels(), actionsBar: MonarchFormActionsBarLabels = MonarchFormActionsBarLabels())

object MonarchSchemaDrivenFormDefaults { fun visibleFields(fields: List<MonarchFormFieldDefinition>, values: Map<String, MonarchFormFieldValue?>): List<MonarchFormFieldDefinition>; fun problems(fields: List<MonarchFormFieldDefinition>, values: Map<String, MonarchFormFieldValue?>): Map<String, MonarchFormFieldProblem>; fun submittedValues(fields: List<MonarchFormFieldDefinition>, values: Map<String, MonarchFormFieldValue?>): Map<String, MonarchFormFieldValue?> }

options.name: fields
options.description: The questions and section headings, in order. A Section question starts a section that lasts until the next one.

options.name: values
options.description: The answers keyed by question id; a missing key is no answer.

options.name: onValuesChange
options.description: Called with all answers and the id of the question that changed.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the form. Give it a bounded height.

options.name: onSubmit
options.description: Receives the shown answers once valid; shows the submit button. Throw to show the error's message in a danger banner. Without it there is no submit button.

options.name: validateOn
options.description: Blur shows a typed question's error when focus leaves it and a choice's when it is answered; Submit waits for a submit attempt.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the answers can be changed and the form submitted.

options.name: readOnly
options.description: Shows the shown answers as a MonarchDescriptionList instead of inputs.

options.name: dirty
options.description: null puts the submit button after the questions; a value pins a MonarchFormActionsBar under them that offers Save while true.

options.name: errors
options.description: Messages from the app, such as the server's, keyed by question id; shown at once, in place of the question's own error.

options.name: state
options.description: The scroll state of the questions.

options.name: contentPadding
options.description: The padding around the questions.

options.name: locale
options.description: The locale of numbers and dates in the read-only view; null uses the configuration's first locale.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for Save, the failure message and what TalkBack reads for an unanswered question in the read-only view, and the questions' and actions bar's strings.

options.name: onDiscard
options.description: With dirty, offers Discard in the actions bar, confirmed first.

options.name: secondaryActions
options.description: Further buttons after the submit button, such as Cancel.

states.name: editing
states.description: Each shown question with its input, label, help and required mark; no errors until validateOn says.

states.name: invalid
states.description: After a submit attempt, every invalid question shows its message; the form scrolls to the first one and moves focus into it.

states.name: submitting
states.description: The submit button shows progress and the inputs are disabled until onSubmit returns.

states.name: failed
states.description: onSubmit threw: its message, or The form could not be saved. Try again., in an assertive danger MonarchBanner, or in the actions bar with dirty.

states.name: disabled
states.description: enabled = false: inputs and the submit button are disabled.

states.name: read only
states.description: The shown answers as terms and values: option labels, Yes or No, a medium date, a locale number and file names; an unanswered question shows a dash, read as Not set.

appearance: The questions take the roles of the Monarch inputs MonarchFieldRenderer chooses; section headings use the subheading text role. Save is a primary MonarchButton, a failure a danger MonarchBanner, and the read-only view a MonarchDescriptionList. No fill of its own. The same roles adapt to dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web's SchemaDrivenForm has its own field schema (text, textarea, number, select, checkbox, switch, date) with regular-expression patterns, custom validate functions and controlled or uncontrolled values. On Android it renders the MonarchFormFieldDefinition schema that MonarchFieldRenderer and the form builder already use, so it covers more types (email, phone, web address, time, radio, checkboxes, multi-select, yes or no, consent, rating, file) and its rules (required, lengths, ranges, selections, formats); there is no pattern or validate function: the app adds its own checks through errors. Sections are Section questions in the flat list rather than nested groups, and conditions are MonarchConditions. Values are always hoisted. The web's submitLabel = null and form attribute become onSubmit = null, with MonarchSchemaDrivenFormDefaults for apps that submit from elsewhere. The web's blur maps to focus leaving a typed question; choices count as visited when answered, because touch has no blur. The dirty actions bar is Android-only, for edit forms. iOS has no entry for this id yet.
accessibility: Each question keeps the semantics of its Monarch input: the label names the input, the required mark and help are read with it, and a new error is announced by MonarchFormField.
Section headings are headings.
An invalid submit moves focus into the first invalid question after scrolling to it.
A failed submit is an assertive MonarchBanner, so it is announced at once.
Save shows a busy state while submitting and the inputs are disabled.
Save and the secondary actions have 48dp touch targets and wrap at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: Hidden questions, and every question of a hidden section, are neither validated nor submitted; their answers stay in values.
errors win over the question's own message and show before any submit attempt.
A question with readOnly keeps a readable text field; other read-only questions are disabled, as in MonarchFieldRenderer.
onSubmit = null shows no submit button; MonarchSchemaDrivenFormDefaults.problems and submittedValues let the app submit from a top app bar.
The questions are a LazyColumn: give the form a bounded height and do not put it in a vertically scrolling parent.

name: MonarchScopeSelector
title: ScopeSelector
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of outlined group cards, each a MonarchCollapsible (androidx.compose.animation.AnimatedVisibility) holding a MonarchCheckboxGroup (androidx.compose.material3.Checkbox rows), with MonarchButton for Select all, Clear all and Show more
summary: Chooses the scopes (permissions) to grant, grouped by resource, with a count, Select all or Clear all per group and paging for long lists.
whenToUse: When creating or editing an API key, an OAuth app or an integration, to choose what it may access, grouped by API or resource.
whenNotToUse: For a few flat options use MonarchCheckboxGroup. For a person's role in a workspace use a MonarchSelect or radio rows.
api: @Composable fun MonarchScopeSelector(groups: List<MonarchScopeGroup>, value: List<String>, onValueChange: (List<String>) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, showLabel: Boolean = true, defaultExpanded: Set<String> = emptySet(), pageSize: Int = 10, autoSelect: MonarchScopeSelectorAutoSelect? = null, expandIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, emptyContent: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchScopeSelectorLabels = MonarchScopeSelectorLabels())
class MonarchScopeGroup(id: String, label: String, scopes: List<MonarchScopeOption>, description: String? = null, loading: Boolean = false, emptyMessage: String? = null)
class MonarchScopeOption(value: String, label: String? = null, description: String? = null, enabled: Boolean = true)
enum class MonarchScopeSelectorAutoSelect { All, Added }

class MonarchScopeSelectorLabels(label: String? = null, empty: String? = null, loading: String? = null, noScopes: String? = null, count: ((selected: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, selectAll: String? = null, clearAll: String? = null, selectAllIn: ((group: String) -> String)? = null, clearAllIn: ((group: String) -> String)? = null, showMore: ((next: Int, remaining: Int) -> String)? = null)

options.name: groups
options.description: The groups, in display order: id, name, scopes, a description line, a loading flag and a message for a group without scopes.

options.name: value
options.description: The selected scope values.

options.name: onValueChange
options.description: Called with the whole new selection. Scopes of other groups keep their place.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the selector.

options.name: enabled
options.description: When false checkboxes are disabled and Select all is hidden; groups can still be expanded to review.

options.name: showLabel
options.description: Shows the "Scopes" heading. When false the label is the selector's TalkBack name.

options.name: defaultExpanded
options.description: The ids of the groups expanded at first. Pass every id to expand all.

options.name: pageSize
options.description: How many groups show before "Show 10 more of 14", and how many more each press shows.

options.name: autoSelect
options.description: All or Added: a group with nothing selected gets every enabled scope once its scopes load, once per group. Added applies only to groups added after the first composition.

options.name: expandIcon
options.description: An icon after each group's name, such as a chevron pointing down, turned while expanded. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: emptyContent
options.description: Replaces "There are no scopes to choose from."

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

states.name: collapsed
states.description: Each group shows its name, its description, "2 of 5 scopes" and Select all or Clear all.

states.name: expanded
states.description: The group's scopes show as a checklist between the name and the count.

states.name: selected
states.description: A group with any scope selected takes the accent border; the count says the same in words.

states.name: loading
states.description: "Loading scopes…" replaces the count and there is no checklist or Select all.

states.name: no scopes
states.description: The group's emptyMessage or "No scopes available."

states.name: paged
states.description: A ghost "Show 10 more of 14" button under the shown groups.

states.name: empty
states.description: "There are no scopes to choose from." or emptyContent.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Checkboxes are disabled and Select all is hidden; expanding still works.

appearance: Groups are cards on the surface fill with the subtle border, or the accent border while any of their scopes is selected. Group names use the label style of MonarchCollapsible; descriptions and counts use the caption style in the muted text color. Checkboxes take the MonarchCheckboxGroup colors. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those roles.
platformNotes: The web puts the description and the count in the group's header button next to a chevron. On Android the header is MonarchCollapsible, which takes a text label, so the description, the count and Select all sit on a line under the header (under the checklist while expanded). The web shows a scope without a label as monospace code; here it is the plain value. The web's group icon is left out: it was decorative. The web's uncontrolled defaultValue is not offered: the selection is always hoisted. hideLabel becomes showLabel. After Show more the web moves focus to the first new group; Compose leaves focus to the system. Same name as iOS's plan; iOS has not built it yet.
accessibility: Each group header is one button with the state "Expanded" or "Collapsed" and the TalkBack expand and collapse actions, from MonarchCollapsible.
Scopes are checkbox rows read with their label, description and state; disabled scopes are announced as disabled.
Select all and Clear all are named with the group ("Select all in Projects API") and have 48dp touch targets.
The selected state of a group is the count in words, not only the accent border.
Without the visible heading, the selector is named "Scopes" for TalkBack.
edgeCases: Select all skips disabled scopes; Clear all leaves them as they are.
Scopes selected in value that no group lists are kept untouched.
Auto-selection runs once per group id, after its loading flag turns off.
Long group names and scope descriptions wrap.
