name: MonarchScoreRing
title: ScoreRing
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.CircularProgressIndicator (determinate), androidx.compose.material3.Text
summary: A circular score: an arc filled to the value out of the maximum, with the number always written in the center.
whenToUse: For one score on a known scale that people compare against bands, such as a health score out of 100 or an average rating out of 5.
whenNotToUse: For progress of a task, use MonarchProgress. For a value against a target with ranges, use MonarchGauge. For a percentage of a quota, use MonarchUsageMeter.
api: @Composable fun MonarchScoreRing(value: Double?, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, color: MonarchScoreRingColor = MonarchScoreRingColor.Auto, size: MonarchScoreRingSize = MonarchScoreRingSize.Md, max: Double = 100.0, thresholds: List<MonarchScoreRingThreshold> = MonarchScoreRingThreshold.Defaults, showMax: Boolean? = null, label: String? = null, description: String? = null, format: ((Double) -> String)? = null, labels: MonarchScoreRingLabels = MonarchScoreRingLabels())
sealed interface MonarchScoreRingColor { data object Auto; data object Accent; data class Tone(val tone: MonarchTone) }
enum class MonarchScoreRingSize { Sm, Md, Lg }
data class MonarchScoreRingThreshold(val minimum: Double, val tone: MonarchTone) { companion object { val Defaults: List<MonarchScoreRingThreshold> } }
class MonarchScoreRingLabels(name: String? = null, valueText: ((value: String, max: String) -> String)? = null, ofMax: ((max: String) -> String)? = null, noValue: String? = null)

options.name: value
options.description: The score. null or not a number shows an empty ring and a dash. Limited to 0 through max.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the ring and its texts.

options.name: color
options.description: Auto takes the tone of the band; Accent is the brand color for a score with no good or bad meaning; Tone(tone) is fixed.

options.name: size
options.description: Sm 48, Md 80, Lg 120dp at the default font size; the ring grows with the font size setting.

options.name: max
options.description: The top of the scale. Zero, negative or infinite values fall back to 100.

options.name: thresholds
options.description: The bands Auto uses: 80 success, 60 info, 40 warning, below 40 danger.

options.name: showMax
options.description: Shows "/ 100" under the number. null shows it on Md and Lg.

options.name: label
options.description: Shown under the ring and read as its name.

options.name: description
options.description: A second line under the label, read after the name.

options.name: format
options.description: Formats the number in the center and in the spoken value. null writes the whole number in the current locale.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for "Score" (monarch_scorering_name), "78 out of 100" (monarch_scorering_value), "/ 100" (monarch_scorering_of_max) and "No score yet" (monarch_scorering_no_value).

states.name: scored
states.description: The arc is filled to the share of the maximum and the number is written in the center; the arc changes with a short animation, or at once when animations are off.

states.name: no score
states.description: An empty track, a dash in the center and the spoken state "No score yet"; the auto color is neutral.

appearance: The arc takes the solid color of the tone and the number its strong color on the muted background track; the accent color uses the accent solid and strong roles; the neutral tone uses muted text for the arc. The number is semibold, about a third of the diameter; "/ 100" and the description are muted caption text. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web takes the diameter and stroke width in pixels; here three sizes keep the ring on the spacing scale and the ring grows with the font size setting, so the number always fits. The web accent tone is the Accent case of MonarchScoreRingColor, because MonarchTone has no accent tone. The web exposes a meter role; Compose has none, so the range is progress information with the spoken value as the state description. iOS shares the name and the options.
accessibility: The ring, number, label and description are one TalkBack element: the name is the label (or "Score") followed by the description, the state is "78 out of 100".
The range 0 to the maximum and the score are exposed as progress information.
Without a score the state is "No score yet" and there is no range.
The score is always written as a number, so the color of the band is never the only signal.
The ring grows with the font size setting so the number is not cut off at the largest size.
The ring is not interactive.
edgeCases: Values above the maximum or below zero are limited; NaN shows no score.
A custom format that writes long text can be wider than the Sm ring; keep it short.
Empty thresholds give the neutral tone for every score.

examples.title: Bands
A rating out of 5 in the accent color
examples.code:
MonarchScoreRing(
    value = 4.2,
    max = 5.0,
    color = MonarchScoreRingColor.Accent,
    size = MonarchScoreRingSize.Sm,
    label = "Average rating",
    format = { "%.1f".format(it) },
)

examples.title: Not scored yet
examples.code: MonarchScoreRing(value = null, label = "Quality")

name: MonarchScreenShareView
title: ScreenShareView
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.gestures.transformable, androidx.compose.foundation.gestures.detectTapGestures, androidx.compose.ui.graphics.graphicsLayer, with MonarchButton and MonarchDivider
summary: Shows a screen someone shares in a call, with who is presenting, fit and zoom with pan, and buttons for picture in picture and full screen that the app carries out.
whenToUse: In a call or a meeting screen, to show the screen a participant shares.
whenNotToUse: For the camera picture of a participant use a call tile. To capture and share the device's own screen use MediaProjection in the app; this view only shows a shared screen.
api: @Composable fun MonarchScreenShareView(presenterName: String, zoom: Float, onZoomChange: (Float) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, local: Boolean = false, waiting: Boolean = false, pictureInPictureActive: Boolean = false, fullScreen: Boolean = false, showControls: Boolean = true, onPictureInPicture: (() -> Unit)? = null, onFullScreen: (() -> Unit)? = null, onStopSharing: (() -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchScreenShareViewLabels = MonarchScreenShareViewLabels(), video: @Composable () -> Unit)

@Composable fun MonarchScreenShareView(presenterName: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, local: Boolean = false, waiting: Boolean = false, pictureInPictureActive: Boolean = false, fullScreen: Boolean = false, showControls: Boolean = true, onPictureInPicture: (() -> Unit)? = null, onFullScreen: (() -> Unit)? = null, onStopSharing: (() -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchScreenShareViewLabels = MonarchScreenShareViewLabels(), video: @Composable () -> Unit)

options.description: Who is sharing, as it should be read.

options.name: zoom
options.description: The zoom factor, 1 (fit) to 3; values outside are clamped. First overload; the second keeps the zoom itself.

options.name: onZoomChange
options.description: Called with the new zoom from the buttons, gestures and TalkBack actions.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the component.

options.name: local
options.description: The person using the app is sharing: the picture is hidden until asked for, and Stop sharing can be offered.

options.name: waiting
options.description: The shared screen has not arrived: a waiting text replaces the picture.

options.name: pictureInPictureActive
options.description: Switches the picture-in-picture button to its exit form and marks it selected.

options.name: fullScreen
options.description: Switches the full-screen button to its exit form and marks it selected.

options.name: showControls
options.description: Shows the zoom, picture-in-picture and full-screen buttons.

options.name: onPictureInPicture
options.description: Starts or ends picture in picture through the activity. Adds the button.

options.name: onFullScreen
options.description: Enters or leaves full screen. Adds the button.

options.name: onStopSharing
options.description: Stops sharing. Adds the button when local.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

options.name: video
options.description: The picture, from the app's call SDK. It fills the 16 by 9 area.

states.name: fit
states.description: The whole picture fits the 16 by 9 area; Zoom out and Fit to view are disabled.

states.name: zoomed
states.description: The picture is larger than the area and pans by dragging; the level is shown as a percentage.

states.name: waiting
states.description: "Waiting for the shared screen…" on the inverse surface.

states.name: local, preview hidden
states.description: A notice on the subtle background with a "Show preview" button replaces the picture.

states.name: picture in picture active
states.description: The button reads "Exit picture in picture" and is marked selected.

appearance: A surface with the default border and 12dp corners. The bar holds the presenter in the default text color and ghost buttons; Stop sharing is a danger button. The picture area is the inverse surface; the notice is the subtle background with muted text. The same roles are used in every theme.
platformNotes: The web takes a MediaStream and starts browser picture in picture and full screen itself. On Android the picture is a slot for the call SDK's view, and picture in picture (Activity.enterPictureInPictureMode with PictureInPictureParams) and full screen (window insets and orientation) belong to the activity, so the app starts them through onPictureInPicture and onFullScreen; the view shows the buttons and their state, as on iOS. Zoom adds pinch and double tap to the web's buttons and steps through the same levels: 100%, 150%, 200%, 300%. The buttons are text buttons because Monarch bundles no icons. The web names the controls as a group; Compose has no named group, so the buttons are read one by one. The web keyboard shortcuts (+, -, 0) are not offered.
accessibility: The picture is one TalkBack element named "Screen shared by …" with the image role and the zoom level as its state.
TalkBack offers Zoom in and Zoom out as actions on the picture while each is possible.
The zoom level beside the buttons is a polite live region, so a level chosen with a button is announced.
The picture-in-picture and full-screen buttons are marked selected while active.
Every button has a 48dp touch target.
The content of the shared screen is not described.
edgeCases: Pinching keeps the center of the picture, not the point under the fingers.
A zoom outside 1 to 3 is clamped.
At zoom 1 drags are not taken, so the screen around the view still scrolls.
When the controls do not fit one row they wrap below the presenter.
With local and waiting the notice has no "Show preview" button.
TalkBack cannot pan the zoomed picture.

title: ScrollArea
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.verticalScroll, androidx.compose.foundation.horizontalScroll, androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn
summary: A region that scrolls inside a screen is Modifier.verticalScroll or horizontalScroll with a bounded size, or a LazyColumn for long content. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: For a panel, a log, a code block or a row of items that scrolls inside a screen. Bound it with height or heightIn(max =), and use a LazyColumn when the content is long or made of many items.
whenNotToUse: For the screen itself, make the whole content one scrolling container (a LazyColumn or a Column with verticalScroll) instead of nesting scroll areas. Do not nest a scroll area in another of the same direction without a bounded size.
api: fun Modifier.verticalScroll(state: ScrollState, enabled: Boolean = true, flingBehavior: FlingBehavior? = null, reverseScrolling: Boolean = false): Modifier
fun Modifier.horizontalScroll(state: ScrollState, enabled: Boolean = true, flingBehavior: FlingBehavior? = null, reverseScrolling: Boolean = false): Modifier
@Composable fun rememberScrollState(initial: Int = 0): ScrollState
val ScrollState.canScrollForward: Boolean
val ScrollState.scrollIndicatorState: ScrollIndicatorState?

states.name: scrollable
states.description: The content is larger than the area: it scrolls and TalkBack offers the scroll actions.

states.name: fits
states.description: The content fits: nothing scrolls and no scroll action is offered.

appearance: No appearance of its own. The overscroll stretch at the ends is the system's. Compose on Android draws no scrollbar for these containers.
platformNotes: The web ScrollArea draws thin themed scrollbars, adds edge shadows and becomes a labelled, focusable region only when it actually scrolls. By default, the scroll indicators are the system's; in Compose on Android, verticalScroll, horizontalScroll and lazy lists draw no scrollbar at all, so nothing needs theming and there is none to show. ScrollState.scrollIndicatorState exposes the offset, content size and viewport size for an app that wants to draw one, and canScrollForward and canScrollBackward replace the web's onScrollableChange. A scroll container needs no focus stop: TalkBack scrolls as it moves through the content and offers scroll actions, and a hardware keyboard scrolls the focused container. The web's height and maxHeight are height and heightIn(max =). iOS uses ScrollView, whose indicators are the system's.
accessibility: System behavior: TalkBack scrolls the container as it moves to elements outside it and offers scroll forward and backward actions while there is more content.
Content that fits does not expose scroll actions.
edgeCases: A scroll area without a bounded size grows to its content and never scrolls.
A LazyColumn inside verticalScroll throws; give the lazy list a fixed height or use it as the only scroller.

name: MonarchSearchBar
title: SearchInput
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.text.BasicTextField in the Monarch field box, inside androidx.compose.material3.DockedSearchBar for the results area
summary: A search box in Monarch colors over the Material 3 docked search bar, with a debounce before the search runs, a pending state, a clear button and an optional results area.
whenToUse: To search or filter the content of a screen, or to query a server as the user types. Put suggestions or results in the content slot to show them under the field while expanded.
whenNotToUse: For a full-screen search that covers the app bar on a phone, use the Material 3 SearchBar or TopSearchBar directly inside MonarchTheme, which colors it. For a field that only filters a short list in a form, MonarchTextField is enough.
api: @Composable fun MonarchSearchBar(query: String, onQueryChange: (String) -> Unit, onSearch: (String) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, expanded: Boolean = false, onExpandedChange: (Boolean) -> Unit = {}, enabled: Boolean = true, pending: Boolean = false, debounceMillis: Long = 0L, placeholder: String? = null, leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, clearIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, onClear: (() -> Unit)? = null, clearLabel: String? = null, pendingLabel: String? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null, content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit = {})

options.name: query
options.description: The text in the field.

options.name: onQueryChange
options.description: Called with the new text on every keystroke and when the field is cleared.

options.name: onSearch
options.description: Called with the query to run: debounceMillis after the last keystroke (at once when 0), at once on the keyboard's search action, and with "" when the field is cleared.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the component.

options.name: expanded
options.description: Whether the results area under the field is open.

options.name: onExpandedChange
options.description: Called when the field asks to open or close the results area, for example on focus or back.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the user can focus and edit the field.

options.name: pending
options.description: A search is running: the leading icon becomes a circular MonarchProgress and TalkBack reads "Searching" as the field's state.

options.name: debounceMillis
options.description: Milliseconds without typing before onSearch runs. 0 runs it on every keystroke.

options.name: placeholder
options.description: Replaces the built-in placeholder "Search" (monarch_searchbar_placeholder).

options.name: leadingIcon
options.description: Replaces Monarch's own outlined magnifier at the start, for example a MonarchIcon with a null content description.

options.name: clearIcon
options.description: Replaces Monarch's own close mark on the clear button. The clear button is shown while there is text and the field is enabled.

options.name: onClear
options.description: Called after the field was cleared with the clear button.

options.name: clearLabel
options.description: Replaces the name of the clear button, "Clear search" (monarch_searchbar_clear).

options.name: pendingLabel
options.description: Replaces "Searching" (monarch_searchbar_pending).

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the focus and press interactions of the field.

options.name: content
options.description: Results or suggestions, shown under the field while expanded.

states.name: empty
states.description: The leading icon and the placeholder.

states.name: with text
states.description: The clear button at the end, an outlined close mark in a 48dp target.

states.name: pending
states.description: A circular progress indicator replaces the leading icon; the field's state is "Searching".

states.name: expanded
states.description: Material 3 opens the results area under the field with the content slot.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Text, icons and placeholder in the disabled text color; no clear button.

appearance: The Monarch field box: 48dp tall, a 1dp input border with 8dp corners on the surface, an outlined 20dp magnifier and close mark in the muted text color, 14sp default text, the placeholder in the subtle text color, the accent cursor and a 2dp focus ring. While the results area is open it sits on the subtle background with a subtle divider, in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: iOS adopts the system search field (searchable) and ships nothing; Android styles the Material 3 search bar, because it is not themed by MaterialTheme alone (container, divider and elevation) and the web's debounce and pending state are worth keeping in one place. The web's sizes do not apply. The web's keyboard shortcut that focuses the field and its shortcut hint are not offered; put a MonarchKbd beside the field when a hardware keyboard is the point. The web's invalid state is not offered. The full-screen SearchBar is not wrapped: use it inside MonarchTheme. The web's Escape-to-clear is the system back gesture, which closes the results area. Material 3 marks DockedSearchBar experimental; Monarch opts in internally and exposes no Material 3 type.
accessibility: The field keeps the platform text-field role, IME and the keyboard's search action, which runs onSearch at once; its name is the placeholder.
The clear button is a button named "Clear search" with a 48dp target; its visible pad is 28dp, the rest of the target overlaps the field's padding.
While pending, the field's state description is "Searching" and the progress indicator is named "Searching".
The field follows the font size setting.
Announce the number of results after a query in the results (a polite live region), since the list changes without focus moving.
edgeCases: A new keystroke restarts the debounce; the keyboard's search action and the clear button cancel a waiting search and run at once.
With debounceMillis 0 onSearch runs on every keystroke and again on the search action.
Changing query from the app does not call onSearch; only typing, the search action and clearing do.
The field fills the available width, like every Monarch field; pass Modifier.width to narrow it.

A server query with a debounce and a pending state
examples.setup:
var query by remember { mutableStateOf("") }
var searching by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
examples.code:
MonarchSearchBar(
    query = query,
    onQueryChange = { query = it },
    onSearch = { searching = it.isNotEmpty() },
    pending = searching,
    debounceMillis = 300L,
    placeholder = "Search invoices",
)

name: MonarchSearchResultItem
title: SearchResultItem
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.ListItem with an AnnotatedString title and snippet, androidx.compose.foundation.clickable
summary: One search result: a title, a breadcrumb path, a snippet with the matched words highlighted, a leading file icon or tile and trailing meta.
whenToUse: In the results of an in-app search, a command palette or a help search, one row per result. Pass the words typed with monarchQueryTerms, or the match ranges or <mark> markers the search service returns.
whenNotToUse: For a plain list row without a query use the Material 3 ListItem. For a suggestion under a search field use the suggestions of MonarchSearchBar.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchSearchResultItem(title: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, path: List<String> = emptyList(), snippet: String? = null, terms: List<String> = emptyList(), titleRanges: List<TextRange>? = null, snippetRanges: List<TextRange>? = null, snippetMarkTags: Boolean = false, fileName: String? = null, enabled: Boolean = true, onClick: (() -> Unit)? = null, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, meta: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, pathLabel: String? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)
public fun monarchQueryTerms(query: String): List<String>

options.name: title
options.description: The result's title, as plain text.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the row.

options.name: path
options.description: Breadcrumb segments, shown with a slash between them and spoken as Location followed by the segments.

options.name: snippet
options.description: A short excerpt of the matching content, as plain text, at most three lines.

options.name: terms
options.description: Words to highlight in the title and snippet, matched without regard to case, longest first. Use monarchQueryTerms.

options.name: titleRanges
options.description: Exact matches in the title as UTF-16 offsets with an exclusive end, the numbers the web and most search services use. Replaces terms for the title. Overlapping ranges are merged; ranges past the end are clamped.

options.name: snippetRanges
options.description: Exact matches in the snippet. Replaces terms for the snippet.

options.name: snippetMarkTags
options.description: The snippet carries <mark> and </mark> markers, for example from PostgreSQL ts_headline. Only those two markers are read; other markup stays text.

options.name: fileName
options.description: A file name; its MonarchFileTypeIcon fills the leading slot. Takes precedence over icon.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the row responds. A disabled row draws its text in the disabled color.

options.name: onClick
options.description: Called when the row is activated. With it the row is one button and the title takes the link color.

options.name: icon
options.description: A leading icon or avatar on a muted tile. Decorative.

options.name: meta
options.description: Trailing details such as a badge, a date or an owner, in the caption type and the muted color.

options.name: pathLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in Location spoken before the path.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the press, focus and hover interactions of the row.

states.name: interactive
states.description: With onClick: the title is in the link color, the row shows the ripple when pressed and the focus ring when focused.

states.name: plain
states.description: Without onClick: the title is in the default text color and the row is static text.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The title, path, snippet and meta use the disabled text color and the row does not respond.

appearance: The title is in the label type, in the link color (or the default text color); the path is a caption in the muted text color with the slashes in the subtle text color; the snippet is muted body text. Matched words have the subtle warning fill, the default text color and a semibold weight. The leading tile is the muted background with a muted icon. The row has no fill of its own.
platformNotes: The web renders the title as a link (href) or a button, accepts a router link component and a roving tab index. On Android the row runs onClick, and the app navigates from there; roving focus is the list's own keyboard focus. The web's queryTerms is monarchQueryTerms, and ranges are TextRange (start inclusive, end exclusive, UTF-16, as the web). iOS names the action parameter action and the leading SF Symbol systemImage; Android uses onClick and an icon slot, because Monarch bundles no icons. The web moves the meta under the text on narrow screens; the Material ListItem keeps it at the end. The match fill has no padding or rounded corner, which a span background cannot draw.
accessibility: The row is one TalkBack element that reads the title, then Location and the path segments separated by commas, then the snippet, then the meta.
With onClick the row has the button role and one activation; without it the row has no click action.
Matches are also semibold, so they do not depend on the fill color; the highlight itself is not read.
The leading icon or file icon is decorative.
An interactive row has a 48dp touch target; the title wraps whole at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: Terms that are empty or only spaces highlight nothing.
Terms are matched as text, not as patterns: a dot in a term matches only a dot.
Ranges that overlap are merged and ranges past the end of the text are clamped; an empty range is ignored.
Any markup other than <mark> and </mark> in the snippet is shown as text.
A snippet longer than three lines ends with an ellipsis; the title is never shortened.

appearance: The summary is in the caption type and muted text; headings are in the subheading type with the count in muted caption text. Rows, skeletons and the empty and error states are the existing Monarch components, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow the theme roles.
platformNotes: The web results are one Tab stop with arrow keys between them; on Android each result is a ListItem button in a LazyColumn and TalkBack moves through them in order, with heading navigation on group headings. The web's heading level, custom empty node and link component are not offered; href becomes onSelect. The web shows results without groups when given results; here pass one group with a null title. The web's onShowMore on each group is one onShowAll callback. Meta is a string in the caption type, as on iOS, not any node. Monarch bundles no icons, so the empty state's magnifying glass is the emptyIcon slot.
accessibility: The summary is a polite live region that stays in the tree: the result count, Searching…, the empty title or Search failed is announced when it changes.
Group headings have heading semantics and are read with their count, such as "Documents, 24 results"; the icon is decorative.
Each result is one button read as its title, location path, snippet and meta (MonarchSearchResultItem).
Skeleton rows are hidden from TalkBack.
The empty and error states keep their own semantics (heading titles, the Try again button).
Rows and the Show all and Try again buttons have 48dp touch targets; text wraps at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: A total smaller than the results shown is raised to the number shown.
An error wins over results and loading; results win over loading.
A query of only spaces is treated as no query in the summary and the empty title.
Counts use the digits and grouping of the configuration's locale.
The list scrolls itself and takes at most the height it is given: do not put it in another vertical scroll; give it the rest of the screen.

summary: A masked secret such as an API key or a token, with a toggle that shows it as text, an optional copy button and a saved-but-not-shown state.
whenToUse: For API keys, tokens, webhook and signing secrets that people paste, check or copy in a settings or developer screen.
whenNotToUse: For an account password use MonarchPasswordInput, which sets the password autofill type. For a value that is not secret use MonarchCopyField.

options.description: The secret.

options.name: label

options.name: onValueChange

options.name: saved
options.description: A value is saved on the server but not sent to the app. While the field is empty it shows "Saved. Enter a new value to replace it" as the placeholder and "A value is saved and hidden. Leave blank to keep it." below; typing a value replaces it.

options.name: revealable
options.description: Shows the reveal toggle.

options.name: copyable
options.description: Shows a copy button. It copies the current value while it stays masked.

options.name: revealed
options.description: Whether the secret is shown as text. null lets the field keep this itself, starting masked.

options.name: onRevealedChange
options.description: Called with the new state when the user uses the toggle.

options.description: Called with the copied text after each copy.

options.description: Replaces the Show and Hide text of the toggle, for example an eye icon. Decorative.

options.name: copyIcon
options.description: Makes the copy button an icon button with this icon. Without it the button shows Copy.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings: the toggle name and texts, the copy label, the copied label and announcement, and the saved placeholder and description.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the focus and press interactions of the field.

states.name: masked
states.description: Default. One dot per character; the toggle shows Show (or the icon) and is off.

states.name: revealed
states.description: The secret as text; the toggle shows Hide and is on.

states.name: saved, not shown
states.description: Empty, with the saved placeholder and description; reveal and copy are disabled until a new value is typed.

states.name: empty
states.description: Reveal and copy are disabled and drawn in the disabled colors.

states.name: copied
states.description: Below Android 13 the copy button shows Copied for two seconds; on every version TalkBack reads Copied to clipboard. Android 13 and later show their own clipboard confirmation.

states.name: error
states.description: The Material error colors on the outline and label, with the message below the field.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The disabled colors of MonarchTextField; both buttons are disabled.

states.name: read-only
states.description: The secret can be revealed and copied but not edited.

appearance: The same field as MonarchTextField: the surface fill, the input border and medium corners, the text in the body type. The toggle text is in the strong accent color (disabled text color while it cannot act); the copy button is the small ghost Monarch button. Every color comes from the theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow the theme.
platformNotes: The web sets autocomplete new-password and vendor attributes so browser password managers ignore the field. On Android the field uses the password keyboard without autocorrect, which stops the keyboard learning the secret, and sets no autofill content type; the system autofill service may still offer to fill it, as on iOS. The copied clip carries ClipDescription.EXTRA_IS_SENSITIVE, so Android 13 and later hide it in the clipboard preview. Monarch does not set FLAG_SECURE: a screen that shows secrets sets WindowManager.LayoutParams.FLAG_SECURE on its window. iOS names the saved state isSet; Android uses saved, because Compose booleans drop the is prefix and set reads as a verb. The web has sm, md and lg sizes; Android has the one size of MonarchTextField. iOS shows the secret in the monospaced code type; MonarchTextField has one text style, the body type. iOS swaps a SecureField for a TextField; Compose 1.12 keeps the password flag of a text field from its first composition, so TalkBack treats the field as a password field in both states. Monarch bundles no icons, so the toggle and the copy button show words unless icons are passed.
accessibility: The field keeps its label as its name and is a password field for TalkBack.
The reveal toggle is a checkbox named "Show" and the label ("Show API key") in both states; its on or off state says whether the secret is shown.
The copy button is named "Copy" and the label ("Copy API key"), and reads Copied to clipboard as its state after a copy, through a polite live region.
Reveal and copy are disabled while the field is empty, including a saved secret that is not shown.
An error is exposed as the field's error and shown as text, not color alone.
The toggle and the copy button have 48dp touch targets after the field's text in the reading order; the saved description wraps whole at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: An empty error string counts as no error.
Copy works while the secret is masked and never reveals it.
With saved and an empty field, an empty value means keep the saved secret; the app decides that when it saves.
A long secret stays on one line and scrolls inside the field; copy still copies all of it.
Capitalisation and autocorrect are off in both states.

summary: A titled card for one section of a screen or dashboard: a header with actions, the body, an optional footer, built-in loading, empty and error states, and an optional collapsible body.
whenToUse: For the sections of a dashboard or a settings screen that load their own data, such as open tickets, usage or a danger zone, so every section shows loading, empty and error the same way.
whenNotToUse: For a plain surface without a title use MonarchCard. For a title above content that is not boxed use MonarchSectionHeader. For a disclosure inside a form use MonarchCollapsible.

options.name: modifier

options.description: What the body shows: the content, three skeleton rows, the empty state or the error state.

options.name: busy
options.description: Refreshing in place: a progress ring after the title while the content stays.

options.name: retrying
options.description: The error state's retry is running.

options.name: flush
options.description: No body padding, for a list or a table that runs to the edges.

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: The message of the empty state.

options.name: errorMessage
options.description: The message of the error state.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows a retry button in the error state.

options.name: icon
options.description: A decorative icon before the title, tinted in the tone.

options.name: footer
options.description: The footer bar under a line.

options.name: labels

options.name: content
options.description: The body, shown in the ready state.

states.name: ready
states.description: The content.

states.name: loading
states.description: Three skeleton rows from MonarchLoadingState, which announces Loading; the title reads Loading as its state.

states.name: empty
states.description: A small MonarchEmptyState with Nothing here yet and the empty message.

states.name: error
states.description: A small MonarchErrorState with This section didn’t load, the error message and a retry button when onRetry is set.

states.name: busy
states.description: A progress ring after the title (a still ring when animations are off); the content stays; the title reads Loading as its state.

states.name: collapsed

states.name: tone
states.description: A tone other than neutral colors the border and the icon and adds the tone's name to the title's state.

appearance: The MonarchCard surface: the surface fill, a 1dp border in the default border color (the tone's border color for a toned card) and large corners. The header uses the MonarchSectionHeader type and colors; the footer sits under a line in the subtle border color. Every color comes from the theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow the theme.
platformNotes: The parity map names MonarchCard with header and footer slots. MonarchCard pads its content evenly, has no footer and a fixed border color, so the section card draws the same Material Surface with the MonarchCard fill, shape and border width to support flush bodies, a footer and a toned border, as iOS does. The web takes a custom empty node; on Android keep the state Ready and put a MonarchEmptyState with actions in the content, as on iOS. The web's link slot is the actions slot, and headingLevel has no Compose equivalent (the title is a heading). The web's uncontrolled open state is not offered: expanded and onExpandedChange are hoisted, as in MonarchCollapsible; iOS keeps its own state. MonarchSectionHeader draws the title in the default text color, so the tone colors the border and the icon but not the title; the tone's name is spoken. Monarch bundles no icons, so the chevron of a collapsible card is the toggleIcon slot. The danger tone is spoken as "Danger", not the shared "Error", on purpose: the web tone marks a destructive zone ("Danger zone" settings such as delete or transfer), not a failure, so "Error" would tell a TalkBack user that something went wrong. The key monarch_sectioncard_tone_danger is not deprecated.
accessibility: The header is one TalkBack element: the title as a heading, with the description and meta; the actions stay separate elements.
A collapsible header is a button with a 48dp touch target, the state Expanded or Collapsed, and the TalkBack expand and collapse actions.
While loading or busy the title's state adds Loading, and the loading state announces Loading through a polite live region.
A tone other than neutral adds the tone's name to the title's state, so the tone is not color alone.
The title wraps whole at font scale 2.0, and the actions follow the title in the reading order in both directions.
edgeCases: A collapsed card removes the body and the footer from the composition; hoist any state inside them that must survive.
expanded is ignored without onExpandedChange: the body always shows.
The error state shows no retry button without onRetry.
Several state parts are spoken in order, separated by commas: Expanded, Danger, Loading.

whenToUse: To title a section of a screen or a dashboard, or the header row inside a card, when it needs a count, a description or actions such as "View all" beside the title.
whenNotToUse: For the screen title use the TopAppBar title. For a plain group label in a list without actions use a MonarchText with the Label style and heading = true.

options.description: The section title, already localised.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the component.

options.name: description
options.description: A sentence under the title that explains the section.

options.name: meta
options.description: A short secondary line: a count, a date range, "Updated 5 min ago".

options.name: size
options.description: Sm: a 14sp semibold title for dashboard sections and cards. Md: a 16sp semibold title for the sections of a screen.

options.name: busy
options.description: The section's content is loading or refreshing: a small progress ring follows the title.

options.name: busyLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in state "Loading" read on the title while busy.

options.name: actions

options.name: tone

states.description: A progress ring follows the title, still when animations are off, and the title's state description is "Loading".

states.name: actions below
states.description: When the actions would take more than half the width, for example at a large font size, they move below the text, aligned to the start.

appearance: No surface of its own, so it takes the background of the screen, card or pane behind it. The title uses the default text color; the description and the meta line the muted text color. The busy ring uses the accent color on the emphasis track.
platformNotes: The web component can also wrap the section's content (children) in a labelled section element and dims it while busy; on Android, as on iOS, the header is only the header and the content follows it in the app's column or lazy list. The web's headingLevel (h2 to h6) is not offered: Compose has one heading property, which TalkBack's heading navigation uses. The web's separate link slot and SectionHeaderLink are the actions slot here, with a MonarchButton in the Ghost variant. On the web the trailing part wraps under the text when the row is too narrow; here it moves below when it would take more than half the width. Same parameters as iOS (isBusy is busy, following Compose naming).
accessibility: The title is a TalkBack heading.
While busy the title's state description is "Loading" (or busyLabel); the progress ring is hidden from TalkBack, so the state is read once.
The description and the meta line are separate text elements, read after the title.
Each action stays its own element after the text, with its own 48dp touch target.
Every text wraps at font scale 2.0 and nothing is truncated; actions that no longer fit beside the text move below it.
In a right-to-left layout the text is on the right and the actions on the left.
edgeCases: A very long title wraps; the actions stay beside it while they fit in half the width.
Without actions the text takes the full width.
More than two or three actions should move into a menu.

options.description: The alerts, newest first.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the card.

options.name: state
options.description: Ready, Loading or Failed. A ready, empty list shows the empty state.

options.name: retrying
options.description: Whether a retry is in progress, in the failed state.

options.name: now
options.description: The reference time for relative times, in epoch milliseconds. Without it they follow the clock and update every minute.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Retries loading; shows "Try again" in the failed state.

options.name: onAction
options.description: Runs the follow-up of an alert that has an actionLabel, for example opening the session list.

options.name: onMarkRead
options.description: Marks one alert read. Shows "Mark as read" on unread alerts.

options.name: onMarkAllRead
options.description: Marks every alert read. Shows "Mark all as read" while any are unread.

options.name: onDismiss
options.description: Dismisses an alert; remove it from alerts. Shows a dismiss button on every alert.

options.description: An icon before each alert, tinted with the severity's strong color and hidden from TalkBack. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: dismissIcon

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including the title and the line under it.

states.name: unread
states.description: Bold title, a dot in the accent solid color, an unread count badge in the header, and "Unread" read by TalkBack.

states.name: loading
states.description: A circular MonarchProgress with "Loading alerts".

states.name: empty
states.description: A small MonarchEmptyState: "No security alerts".

states.name: failed
states.description: A small MonarchErrorState with a retry when onRetry is given; retrying shows its progress.

appearance: A MonarchCard. Severity badges use the tone of the severity (info, neutral for low, warning for medium, danger for high) and critical is drawn solid; severity icons use the strong role of the tone, muted text for low. The unread mark uses the accent solid role. All colors are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web takes a ReactNode description, a heading level and a header link; on Android the title and description are strings in labels and the title has the heading semantics. The web and iOS open an action URL; Monarch for Android components do not navigate, so a follow-up is an actionLabel with onAction, where the app opens its screen or calls LocalUriHandler. Dates are epoch milliseconds. The web moves keyboard focus and iOS moves VoiceOver focus after a dismissal; on Android focus is left to the system and the dismissal is announced. The web's accent tone for the unread mark is drawn with the accent role directly, because MonarchTone has no accent tone. Severity icons are a slot because Monarch bundles no icons; the severity is always written in the badge.
accessibility: The card title is a heading.
Each alert's text is one TalkBack element: the title and description, with the state "Unread", the severity name and the time, so severity and unread state never depend on color or an icon.
Follow-up, mark-as-read and dismiss are separate buttons with 48dp touch targets.
Each dismiss button is named "Dismiss" and the alert title.
After a dismissal "Dismissed" and the title are announced through a polite live region.
Loading, empty and error states are read by MonarchProgress, MonarchEmptyState and MonarchErrorState.
edgeCases: Long titles and descriptions wrap; the badge and time wrap onto a new row at large font sizes.
An alert with an actionLabel and no onAction shows no follow-up.
An alert without a date shows no time.
Unread alerts only show "Mark as read" when onMarkRead is given.

examples.template:
MonarchSecurityAlertCard(

    onMarkRead = { id -> alerts = alerts.map { if (it.id == id) it.copy(read = true) else it } },
    onMarkAllRead = { alerts = alerts.map { it.copy(read = true) } },
    onDismiss = { id -> alerts = alerts.filterNot { it.id == id } },
)

whenNotToUse: For more than five options, or options with descriptions, use MonarchRadioRow or MonarchRadioCardGroup. For navigation between screens use Material 3 tabs. For an option that is on or off use MonarchSwitchRow.

platformNotes: Replaces SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow and SegmentedButton, whose outlined buttons with a check mark are not the Monarch look. Each segment is selectable with Role.RadioButton inside a selectableGroup, with a 48dp touch target around the pill (the track is 36dp visible at Md). accessibility: Each segment has the RadioButton role and is read as selected or not selected.
Every segment reserves a touch target of at least 48dp by 48dp.
A disabled segment is read as disabled and ignores taps.
The chosen segment shows a check mark as well as a different fill.
Segments follow the layout direction, so the first option is at the right in right-to-left layouts.
edgeCases: Segments share the row width equally, so a long label wraps or is cut at large font sizes; keep labels to one or two words.
With more than five options the segments become too narrow on a phone.

name: MonarchSelect
title: Select
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.ExposedDropdownMenuBox with a read-only androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedTextField anchor, ExposedDropdownMenu and androidx.compose.material3.DropdownMenuItem
summary: A labelled field that picks one value from a short, fixed list through a menu, with group headings, descriptions, disabled options, helper and error text.
whenToUse: For one choice among a handful of known options (a region, a size, a role) where the options do not need to be visible all the time.
whenNotToUse: For a long list or one the person searches use MonarchCombobox. For two to five options that should stay visible use MonarchRadioCardGroup or the Material 3 SegmentedButton. For several values use MonarchCheckboxGroup or MonarchTagInput.
api: @Composable fun <T> MonarchSelect(options: List<MonarchSelectOption<T>>, selected: T?, onSelect: (T) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, label: String? = null, placeholder: String? = null, helperText: String? = null, errorText: String? = null, enabled: Boolean = true, contentDescription: String? = null, initiallyOpen: Boolean = false)
class MonarchSelectOption<out T>(value: T, label: String, description: String? = null, enabled: Boolean = true, group: String? = null)

options.name: options
options.description: The options in order: value, label, description, enabled and group. Consecutive options with the same group share a heading.

options.name: selected
options.description: The value of the chosen option, or null for no choice yet.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Called with the value of the option the person chooses; the menu closes.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the field.

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label, which floats into the outline.

options.name: placeholder
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Choose an option", shown in the muted color while nothing is chosen.

options.name: helperText
options.description: Guidance below the field.

options.name: errorText
options.description: The error message; replaces the helper text and is set as the field's error.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the menu can be opened.

options.name: contentDescription
options.description: The TalkBack name when there is no visible label.

states.name: nothing chosen
states.description: The field shows the placeholder in the muted text color.

states.name: chosen
states.description: The field shows the chosen label in the default text color.

states.name: open
states.description: The Material 3 menu lists the options under their group headings; the chosen one has a filled radio mark and is selected.

states.name: disabled option
states.description: Listed in the disabled color and cannot be chosen.

states.name: error
states.description: The danger outline and label, and the message under the field.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The disabled colors; the menu does not open.

appearance: The field uses MonarchTextField's colors: a surface fill with the input border, the focus ring when focused, the danger strong color in error. The menu is the Material 3 menu on the surface color; group headings and descriptions are muted text; the chosen option's radio mark is the accent strong color and others the input border. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web's Select is a Radix listbox with its own trigger, typeahead and sm, md and lg sizes; iOS uses the system menu Picker and ships no type. Android ships MonarchSelect because Compose has no select control: it is the Material 3 exposed dropdown with a read-only field, which keeps the expand action, menu focus and placement. There is no size option (the field is MonarchTextField's size) and no typeahead in the menu. Separators are replaced by group headings. The web's required mark is not offered; put the field in a form that states it, or use MonarchFormField around another control.
accessibility: The field is the Material 3 exposed dropdown anchor: TalkBack reads the label, the chosen value or placeholder, and the expand state, and double tap opens the menu.
Every option is a menu item read with its label and description; the chosen option is marked selected and also has a filled radio mark, so the choice does not rely on color.
Group headings are headings; disabled options are disabled.
The error is the field's error semantics and is shown as text with a danger outline.
The field is at least 48dp high, the menu items are Material 3 items of 48dp, and text scales and wraps at large font sizes.
edgeCases: A selected value that is not among the options shows the placeholder.
Two options with the same value are both marked selected; give each option a distinct value.
Options with the same group that are not next to each other get two headings.
A long label wraps in the menu; in the field it stays on one line.

title: SequenceBuilder
wrapsNative: MonarchReorderableList (androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn) of MonarchCard rows, each opening an MonarchBottomSheet with MonarchDurationInput, MonarchSelect, MonarchTextField and a preview
summary: A recipe, not a component: a multi-step message sequence as reorderable step rows, each edited in a sheet with its wait, channel, subject, message with variables, and a preview with sample data.
whenToUse: For outreach, onboarding or follow-up sequences: wait, send, wait, send, across channels, with personalised variables.
whenNotToUse: For a single message, use a form with MonarchTextField. For rules that react to events, use MonarchConditionEditor and MonarchActionEditor.
api: MonarchReorderableList(items = steps, key = { it.id }, itemLabel = { … }, onReorder = { from, to -> … }, moveButtons = true) { step, state -> MonarchCard(onClick = { editing = step.id }) { … } }
MonarchBottomSheet(onDismissRequest = { editing = null }) { … }
MonarchDurationInput(minutes = step.waitMinutes, onMinutesChange = { … }, label = "Wait before sending", largestUnit = MonarchDurationInputUnit.Days)
MonarchTextField(value = step.body, onValueChange = { … }, label = "Message", singleLine = false)

options.name: steps
options.type: List of the app's step type
options.description: Each step's id, channel, wait in minutes after the previous step, subject and message, in the app's state.

options.name: channels
options.description: The channels a step can use, in a MonarchSelect; the subject shows for channels that have one, such as email.

options.name: sample
options.description: Sample values of the {{variables}}, used by the preview.

states.name: list
states.description: One card per step with its number, channel, when it is sent and the start of its subject or message; drag handles and move buttons reorder.

states.name: editing
states.description: A bottom sheet with the wait, the channel, the subject, the message with its variables hint, the preview and Done.

states.name: empty
states.description: Only Add step; the app may add a MonarchEmptyState.

appearance: Steps are MonarchCards in a reorderable list with drag handles; the sheet uses the Material 3 sheet surface with Monarch fields. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web's SequenceBuilder is one component with every step's fields open in a long list, inline variable buttons and a details preview. On Android it is a recipe in the list-and-detail pattern: steps are reorderable rows (drag or move buttons, from MonarchReorderableList) and each step is edited in a bottom sheet, because a stack of open editors does not fit a phone. Variables are typed in the message with a hint instead of insert buttons; the preview replaces {{token}} with sample values. Validation (subject, message, length, unknown variables) is the app's, shown as each field's errorText. MonarchReorderableList is lazy, so give it a bounded height or make it the screen's scrolling list. iOS has the same plan: a recipe.
accessibility: MonarchReorderableList gives each row a drag handle with TalkBack actions and announces moves; with moveButtons each row also has Move up and Move down.
Each step card is one button that opens its sheet; the sheet's fields have visible labels.
The preview is plain text, read after its heading.
edgeCases: The first step's wait is from the start of the sequence.
Unknown {{variables}} stay as written in the preview, so they are easy to spot.
Keep step ids stable so a reorder keeps each step's state.

whenNotToUse: For the devices that have accessed the account, with blocking and first-seen times, use MonarchDeviceList. For apps that hold access to the account, use MonarchConnectedAppsList.

class MonarchSession(id: String, label: String, kind: MonarchDeviceKind = MonarchDeviceKind.Desktop, detail: String? = null, signedInMillis: Long? = null, lastActiveMillis: Long? = null, current: Boolean = false)
enum class MonarchSessionListState { Ready, Loading, Failed }

options.name: sessions
options.description: The person's sessions, the current one included, in the order shown.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the list.

options.name: title
options.description: Replaces the built-in title "Where you’re signed in".

options.name: description
options.description: Replaces the line under the title.

options.name: state
options.description: Ready, Loading or Failed. A ready, empty list shows the empty state.

options.name: retrying
options.description: Shows the retry button busy in the failed state.

options.name: confirm
options.description: Asks with an alert dialog before signing out. Set false when the callbacks open the app's own confirmation.

options.name: now
options.description: The reference time for relative times, in epoch milliseconds. Without it they follow the clock, refreshed every minute.

options.name: footnote
options.description: A note in the card's footer, such as how long open apps stay signed in.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Retries loading. Shows Try again in the failed state.

options.name: onSignOut
options.description: Signs one session out, given its id; remove it from sessions when it returns. Shows Sign out on every row; throwing shows the failure.

options.name: onSignOutOthers
options.description: Signs out every session except the current one, given their ids. Shows Sign out other devices in the header while there are other sessions; throwing shows the failure.

options.name: sessionIcon
options.description: An icon for each session's device kind, hidden from TalkBack. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every other built-in string.

states.name: list
states.description: One row per session inside the section card, separated by subtle dividers.

states.name: current
states.description: A success This device badge; the last-active time is left out because the session is in use. Its Sign out confirmation says the person will need to sign in again on this device.

states.name: signing out
states.description: The button that started it shows its progress indicator; every other Sign out button is disabled until it finishes.

states.name: sign-out failed
states.description: A danger MonarchInlineNotice above the list, "Couldn’t sign out Chrome on macOS. Try again.", announced.

states.name: loading
states.description: Skeleton rows from the section card, announced as "Loading sessions".

states.name: empty
states.description: The section card's small empty state, "No active sessions".

states.name: failed
states.description: The section card's error state with Try again when onRetry is given.

appearance: A MonarchSectionCard with rows separated by subtle dividers; labels in the strong body style, the detail and times in the caption style in the muted color, a success This device badge and small ghost Sign out buttons; Sign out other devices is a small secondary button in the header and the confirmation uses a danger button. All are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The parity map names LazyColumn rows; the rows are a plain Column inside MonarchSectionCard instead, because the list sits inside the app's own scrolling settings screen, where a LazyColumn without a fixed height cannot be measured (MonarchDeviceList makes the same choice). The web keeps the confirmation open while the request runs and shows a rejection inside it; the Material 3 AlertDialog closes on confirm, so the progress moves to the button that started it and a failure appears as a notice in the card, as in MonarchDeviceList. The web's detail is a node and its hint is a hover title; here detail is plain text and there is no hint, because a phone has no hover. Monarch bundles no icons, so the device icon is a slot given the kind (MonarchDeviceKind, shared with MonarchDeviceList); the web draws its own. The web's describeUserAgent helper is not offered: an Android app gets the label from its server. The web's headingLevel has no Android equivalent (the title is a heading) and its locale is the device's locale used by DateUtils. iOS has no SessionList yet. The composable is experimental: it is a domain composite that waits for a Rook app to adopt it.
accessibility: The title is a heading, from MonarchSectionCard; the list is a traversal group named "Signed-in sessions".
Each session is one element whose content description is its label and whose state is This device, the detail and the times, built by a tested pure function; This device is a word, not only color.
The device icon is decorative and hidden.
Each Sign out button is a separate MonarchButton with a 48dp touch target, named "Sign out Chrome on macOS".
The confirmations are Material 3 alert dialogs with a danger confirm button and a ghost Cancel; the current session's confirmation says so.
Signing out, signing out the others and failures are announced through a polite live region.
Badges wrap and the description wraps, so nothing is cut off at the largest font size.
edgeCases: Sign out other devices is hidden when the current session is the only one, while loading and when the list failed.
A blank detail is left out; with no times there is no time line.
The app removes signed-out sessions from sessions after the callback returns; the list does not remove them itself.
Only one sign-out runs at a time.
If the app signs out the current session, it usually leaves the screen; the list only reports the request.

title: SettingsPage
wrapsNative: MonarchListRow rows that push a detail screen, androidx.activity.compose.BackHandler, MonarchSectionCard, MonarchFormActionsBar and MonarchUnsavedChangesGuard; androidx.compose.material3.adaptive.navigation.NavigableListDetailPaneScaffold on wide windows
summary: A recipe, not a component: a settings screen as a list of sections, each opening its own detail screen with its settings, a save bar while there are unsaved changes, a guard before leaving them, and the danger zone last.
whenToUse: An app or workspace has several groups of settings (profile, notifications, billing, members) that people change from time to time.
whenNotToUse: For one short group of settings, show a single settings-section recipe on the screen. For settings that save as soon as they change, use MonarchSwitchSettingsList without a save bar.

states.description: The title and one row per section; each row opens its detail screen.

states.name: detail
states.description: The section's settings in a MonarchSectionCard, with a back button and system back to the list.

states.name: unsaved changes
states.description: MonarchFormActionsBar shows Save and Discard; back or the back button opens MonarchUnsavedChangesGuard.

states.name: danger zone
states.description: The last row opens the danger-zone recipe: a danger-toned card with its confirmed actions.

states.name: wide window
states.description: On a tablet or a desktop window NavigableListDetailPaneScaffold shows the list and the open section side by side.

appearance: List rows on the surface color separated by subtle dividers, the danger row's title in the strong danger text color; detail screens use MonarchSectionCard, the save bar and the guard dialog. Every part is an existing component, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web ships SettingsPage: a title, a section navigation (a sticky side list, a scrolling strip on phones), all sections on one long page, a page-wide save bar and a guard on leaving. Android follows the system Settings pattern instead: the screen is a list of sections and each opens its own detail screen, which saves on its own; system back returns to the list. That is why there is no Android component: the list rows, BackHandler, MonarchSectionCard, MonarchFormActionsBar and MonarchUnsavedChangesGuard already cover it, and the app's own navigation (or NavigableListDetailPaneScaffold from the split-layout entry on wide windows) holds the open section. The web's interceptLinks, guardRef and activeSection have no Android equivalent: components do not navigate.
accessibility: Each section row is one TalkBack element with the Button role, its title and summary read together, and a target of at least 48dp from MonarchListRow.
The danger zone is named by its title, not by color alone.
System back returns to the list, and while there are unsaved changes MonarchUnsavedChangesGuard asks first.
The save bar announces unsaved changes and keeps Save and Discard as 48dp buttons, from MonarchFormActionsBar.
edgeCases: Keep each row's summary to one line, such as the current value; long summaries wrap.
Save per section: a change in one section never waits for another.
When the app uses its own navigation library, replace the section state with its back stack and keep the guard on each detail screen.

summary: A recipe, not a component: a titled group of settings in a card, with a save footer that appears while there are unsaved changes, a danger zone, and loading and no-access states.
whenToUse: For each group of an app's settings screen, such as a workspace's general settings or its danger zone.
whenNotToUse: For switches that save one by one, use MonarchSwitchSettingsList. For a bar of Save and Discard pinned to the bottom of a long form, use MonarchFormActionsBar.

options.name: saving

states.name: ready

states.name: dirty

states.name: no access

states.name: danger zone
states.description: A card with the danger tone and MonarchListRow rows whose action is a danger button that opens a confirmation.

appearance: Every part is an existing Monarch or Material 3 component: the section card's surface, border and header, switch and form-field rows, Material 3 list items on the surface color, and small secondary and primary buttons in a footer under a line. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The parity map named a MonarchSettingsSection type; following the native-first rule it is a recipe, because MonarchSectionCard already gives the titled card, its loading and empty states, the busy state, a danger tone and a footer slot, and the rows are existing Monarch rows and the MonarchListRow. The web's SettingsRow is MonarchFormField with the Row layout (or MonarchSwitchRow for a switch), and its SettingsActionRow is a MonarchListRow with a trailing button. The web's stickyFooter is MonarchFormActionsBar, the Android bottom bar for Save and Discard; the web's no-access notice is the card's empty state. iOS plans a MonarchSettingsSectionStyle for its Form sections and has not shipped it yet.
accessibility: The title is a heading and the danger tone is spoken with it, from MonarchSectionCard.
Switch rows are one TalkBack element with the switch role; form-field rows name their control by the label.
The unsaved-changes line is a polite live region, so it is announced when it appears.
Discard and Save changes are MonarchButtons with 48dp targets; Save changes reads "Loading" while saving.
The footer wraps onto more lines at large font sizes.
edgeCases: Keep Save changes enabled only while dirty; Discard restores the saved values the app keeps.
When a save fails, keep the draft and show the error with MonarchInlineNotice in the card.
For a long settings screen with several sections, prefer one MonarchFormActionsBar for the whole screen over a footer per section.

title: ShareButton

summary: A share button opens a small panel with the link, a Copy link button and an Email action; where the app has more to offer it hands the link to the Android Sharesheet (an ACTION_SEND intent wrapped in Intent.createChooser) instead. Monarch ships a MonarchPopover for the panel.
whenToUse: To send a link or text to another app or person. Put the intent in the onClick of a MonarchButton, or of an IconButton with a share icon and a content description, inside MonarchTheme.
whenNotToUse: To copy a value to the clipboard use MonarchCopyButton; the Sharesheet already offers Copy, so do not add a copy fallback next to it.

Context.startActivity(intent: Intent)

appearance: The button follows MonarchTheme like any Monarch button. The Sharesheet is drawn by the system in the system's own colors, not the app theme.
platformNotes: The web component uses the Web Share API where the browser has it and otherwise opens its own panel with the link, a Copy link button and optional targets such as email. Android shows that panel, a MonarchPopover, so the screen reads as on the web; an app that prefers the system chooser puts the ACTION_SEND intent in the onClick of the button instead. iOS uses ShareLink. A web ShareEvent with the chosen target needs a PendingIntent IntentSender on Android; Monarch does not wrap it.
accessibility: System behavior: the Sharesheet is a system screen with its own TalkBack labels and focus order.
The button that opens it is a MonarchButton or an IconButton, so it has the Button role and a touch target of at least 48dp.
An icon-only share button needs a content description such as "Share".
edgeCases: Pass null as the chooser title; a fixed English title would not be translated by the system.
Without Intent.createChooser, Android may open a default app directly; the chooser always shows the Sharesheet.
Share a content:// Uri with FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION and ClipData for files; plain text needs no permission.

title: ShareDialog

summary: A recipe, not a component: sharing one record with people and setting its general access, in a Material 3 bottom sheet: invite people with a role, the people with access and their roles, general access and the link to copy.
whenToUse: When a record (a document, a board, a folder) is shared with people inside the product and their access is managed in place, from a Share button on its screen.
whenNotToUse: To send a link to another app (a message, an email), use the system share sheet (Intent.ACTION_SEND via Intent.createChooser), documented as share-button. To manage the members of a whole workspace, use a screen of MonarchMemberRows.

MonarchEntityPicker(label: String, entities: List<MonarchEntityPickerEntity>, selected: List<String>, onSelectedChange: (List<String>) -> Unit, …)
MonarchRolePicker(roles: List<MonarchRoleOption<T>>, selected: T?, onSelect: (T) -> Unit, layout = MonarchRolePickerLayout.Compact, label: String? = null, …)

MonarchCopyField(value: String, label: String, …)
MonarchButton(text: String, onClick: () -> Unit, variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Primary, enabled: Boolean, …)

states.name: open
states.description: A bottom sheet, fully expanded, that scrolls as one column: the title, Invite people, the role for new people, Invite, People with access, General access and the link.

appearance: The Material 3 bottom sheet on the raised surface with Monarch's large radius and the scrim role, a heading in the heading text style, and the Monarch pickers, rows, copy field and buttons in their own roles. The same roles adapt to dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ships ShareDialog as one component in a dialog, with the people, the access options, password-protected links with expiry, view counts and revoking, and a long list of message overrides. On Android, as on iOS, it is a recipe in a MonarchBottomSheet, the phone pattern for a task that belongs to the current screen, built from the Monarch components that already do each part, so no Monarch type is added. Link management (passwords, expiry, revoking several links) is product-specific: add MonarchTextFields and a list of MonarchMemberRow-like rows inside the same column when the product needs it. Sending the link to another app goes through the system share sheet, not this recipe.
accessibility: The title and People with access are headings, so TalkBack can move between the parts of the sheet.
MonarchEntityPicker names its field Invite people and reads the picked people.
MonarchRolePicker in the compact layout is a menu field with its label; the selected role is read as its value.
Each MonarchMemberRow reads the name, email and role, and offers its role menu and Remove as separate buttons.
MonarchCopyField is a read-only field with a Copy button with a 48dp touch target.
The sheet has the Material 3 drag handle, which TalkBack can expand and dismiss, and closes with the system back gesture.
edgeCases: Many people with access: the column scrolls inside the sheet; do not put a LazyColumn inside it.
Your own row is self = true, so it cannot be removed or have its role changed.
At the largest font scale skipPartiallyExpanded keeps the whole sheet open so nothing is cut off.

name: MonarchBottomSheet
title: Sheet
wrapsNative: MonarchBottomSheet (window, scrim, drag, back, predictive back, motion) with a Monarch surface, handle and header; androidx.compose.material3.ModalNavigationDrawer for a start-side panel
summary: A modal panel from the bottom: MonarchBottomSheet is the MonarchBottomSheet with the Monarch surface, handle and header. The platform keeps dragging, back and the motion.
whenToUse: For a task that belongs to the current screen and needs more room than a dialog: a form with a header and a footer, details of a row, settings for a view. At expanded width, for a panel that sits beside the content, use a supporting pane (see peek-panel).
whenNotToUse: Not for a short question: use MonarchDialog (see dialog). Not for a list of actions: use MonarchMenu. Not for the app's destinations: use a navigation drawer (see sidebar-nav).
api: @Composable fun MonarchBottomSheet(onDismissRequest: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, title: String? = null, description: String? = null, dismissible: Boolean = true, showHandle: Boolean = true, fullyExpanded: Boolean = true, fullWidthContent: Boolean = false, content: @Composable MonarchBottomSheetScope.() -> Unit)
interface MonarchBottomSheetScope : ColumnScope { fun dismiss() }

options.name: onDismissRequest
options.description: Called when the sheet has closed: swipe, back, scrim, the handle or dismiss().

options.name: description

options.description: Whether a swipe, back and the scrim close it; dismiss() always does.

options.name: showHandle
options.description: Whether the handle is shown.

options.name: fullyExpanded
options.description: Opens fully expanded, or half open first when the content is tall.

options.name: fullWidthContent
options.description: The content spans the sheet for list rows with their own 16dp padding; the header then starts at 16dp.

options.name: content
options.description: The content; call dismiss() to slide the sheet away from a button.

states.name: expanded
states.description: With skipPartiallyExpanded = true the sheet opens at the height of its content, up to nearly the full screen.

states.name: partially expanded
states.description: Without it, a tall sheet opens at half the screen and the person drags it up.

states.name: closing
states.description: A drag down, a tap on the scrim or back calls onDismissRequest; hide the sheet with sheetState.hide() before you stop composing it, so it animates out.

states.name: busy
states.description: dismissible = false keeps it open while work runs; dismiss() in the content still closes it.

appearance: The raised background (a lighter step than the screen in a dark theme) with 16dp top corners and no shadow, a 36 by 4dp handle in the subtle text role centred in a 48dp target, the title at 18/600 and the description at 14 in the muted text role, 20dp at the sides and under the content. The scrim is the overlay scrim role.
platformNotes: The web Sheet attaches to any edge (end by default) and has sizes sm to full, a header, body and footer, a close button, a drag handle and a busy state. On Android a modal sheet comes from the bottom: the sizes are the expanded and partially expanded states, the handle is showHandle, busy is dismissible = false, the header is title and description, and the body and footer are ordinary content; dismiss() in the content closes the sheet with its motion. The web's start-side sheet is a ModalNavigationDrawer; there is no end-side modal sheet in Material 3 for Compose, so at expanded width use a supporting pane instead (see peek-panel). iOS uses the system sheet and the inspector.
accessibility: TalkBack reads the title as the pane title and as a heading when the sheet opens.
The handle is a named 48dp button with the Dismiss action (and Expand or Collapse when half open), so closing never needs a drag.
Back dismisses it unless dismissible is false.
The title wraps at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: Call sheetState.hide() and stop composing the sheet in invokeOnCompletion; removing it at once skips the closing animation.
The keyboard pushes the sheet up; keep the confirm button visible by putting it before a long content or making the content scroll.
On a tablet the sheet is limited to sheetMaxWidth (640dp) and centered.
