name: MonarchShiftRoster
title: ShiftRoster
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.PrimaryScrollableTabRow and Tab (one day or one person at a time), androidx.compose.material3.DropdownMenu with DropdownMenuItem and RadioButton (the cell menu), androidx.compose.foundation.horizontalScroll with CollectionInfo semantics (the grid), MonarchEventChip, MonarchAvatar, MonarchBadge, MonarchSkeleton, MonarchBanner, MonarchEmptyState, android.icu.text.DateFormat
summary: Who works which shift on which day: a shift, a day off or nothing for each person and day of a range, with hours per person and the number of people working per day, edited from a menu on each cell.
whenToUse: For a team's weekly or fortnightly rota in a workforce or attendance screen, where a manager assigns shifts and reads coverage per day. Save each MonarchShiftRosterChange as it arrives.
whenNotToUse: For meetings or appointments use MonarchAgendaList or a calendar time grid. For one person's own upcoming shifts use MonarchAgendaList. For bulk rotations or copying a week, build the product's own dialog; the roster edits one cell at a time.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchShiftRoster(members: List<MonarchShiftRosterMember>, shifts: List<MonarchShiftRosterShift>, from: Long, value: Map<String, Map<Long, MonarchShiftRosterAssignment>>, onValueChange: (Map<String, Map<Long, MonarchShiftRosterAssignment>>, MonarchShiftRosterChange) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, days: Int = 7, layout: MonarchShiftRosterLayout = MonarchShiftRosterLayout.Automatic, enabled: Boolean = true, readOnly: Boolean = false, loading: Boolean = false, showTotals: Boolean = true, today: Long? = System.currentTimeMillis(), timeZone: String? = null, is24Hour: Boolean? = null, error: String? = null, onMemberClick: ((MonarchShiftRosterMember) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchShiftRosterLabels = MonarchShiftRosterLabels(), empty: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null)
class MonarchShiftRosterShift(id: String, name: String, start: Int, end: Int, shortName: String? = null, color: Color = Color.Unspecified)
class MonarchShiftRosterMember(id: String, name: String, description: String? = null, image: Painter? = null)
sealed interface MonarchShiftRosterAssignment { class Shift(shiftId: String); data object Off }
class MonarchShiftRosterChange(memberId: String, day: Long, assignment: MonarchShiftRosterAssignment?)
enum class MonarchShiftRosterLayout { Automatic, Grid, ByDay, ByPerson }

class MonarchShiftRosterLabels(roster: String? = null, person: String? = null, day: String? = null, off: String? = null, unassigned: String? = null, clear: String? = null, menuTitle: ((name: String, day: String) -> String)? = null, cell: ((name: String, day: String, assignment: String) -> String)? = null, range: ((start: String, end: String) -> String)? = null, overnight: String? = null, hours: String? = null, hoursValue: ((hours: String) -> String)? = null, working: String? = null, workingValue: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, today: String? = null, emptyTitle: String? = null, emptyDescription: String? = null, loading: String? = null)

options.name: members
options.description: The people in display order, each with an id, a name, an optional description line and an optional picture Painter.

options.name: shifts
options.description: The shifts in menu order: id, name, start and end in minutes from midnight (an end at or before the start ends the next day), an optional short name for the grid and an optional color.

options.name: from
options.description: The first day shown: any time on that date in UTC, as epoch milliseconds (a day key).

options.name: value
options.description: Assignments by member id, then by day key: Shift(shiftId) or Off. A missing day is not assigned.

options.name: onValueChange
options.description: Called with the whole new value and the one change (member, day, new assignment or null when cleared).

options.name: modifier
options.description: Applied to the roster.

options.name: days
options.description: How many days to show from from, 1 to 62.

options.name: layout
options.description: Grid (people by days), ByDay (tabs of days, a row per person), ByPerson (tabs of people, a row per day), or Automatic: the grid when every column fits and the font scale is at most 1.3, otherwise ByDay.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the cells can be used, for example false while saving. Tabs keep working.

options.name: readOnly
options.description: Shows the assignments as text without menus.

options.name: loading
options.description: Shows a skeleton placeholder, read as "Loading roster", instead of the roster.

options.name: showTotals
options.description: Shows each person's hours over the range and the number of people working per day.

options.name: today
options.description: Any time on the day marked Today, read in timeZone; null for no marker. The day layout opens on it when it is in the range.

options.name: timeZone
options.description: The zone today is read in. An IANA id such as Europe/Berlin; null, or an id the device does not know, is the device's zone.

options.name: is24Hour
options.description: Shows shift times on a 24-hour clock. null follows the device's 24-hour setting.

options.name: error
options.description: A message shown in a danger MonarchBanner instead of the roster.

options.name: onMemberClick
options.description: Makes each person a button, for example to open their schedule on a detail screen.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: empty
options.description: Replaces the built-in empty state shown when members is empty.

states.name: shift
states.description: A MonarchEventChip bar in the shift's color with the name (the short name in the grid) and the times.

states.name: off
states.description: A muted fill with the word Off.

states.name: not assigned
states.description: A dashed outline with "Not assigned" (a dash in the narrow grid cells; TalkBack still reads "Not assigned").

states.name: today
states.description: Today's tab reads "Today" above the date, the day heading and grid header use the strong accent and an info badge or the word Today.

states.name: menu open
states.description: A Material 3 DropdownMenu headed by the person and the day, with a radio item per shift, Off, and Clear when the day is assigned.

states.name: read only
states.description: Cells are text without menus.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Cells keep their look but cannot be pressed; TalkBack reads them as disabled.

states.name: loading
states.description: A skeleton placeholder replaces the roster.

states.name: error
states.description: A danger banner with the app's message replaces the roster.

states.name: empty
states.description: With no people, an empty state (or the app's empty slot) replaces the roster.

appearance: Rows are separated by the default divider; names are in the default text color and descriptions, hours and counts in the muted color. A shift cell keeps the event chip's colors (the shift color only as the bar and a light tint), a day off uses the muted background, and an unassigned day a dashed default border. Today uses the strong accent and an info badge. The grid's header and footer rows sit on the subtle background. High contrast themes use their own roles; every state is also written.
platformNotes: The web ShiftRoster is always a table of people by days with a roving-focus keyboard grid and Delete to clear. On a phone that table does not fit, so Android shows one day at a time with Material 3 tabs (or one person at a time) and keeps the table for wide windows (Automatic picks it when every column fits). The web takes ISO dates and a BCP 47 locale and hour cycle; Android takes day keys in epoch milliseconds, the configuration's locale and the device's 24-hour setting. Assignments are a sealed MonarchShiftRosterAssignment (Shift or Off; a missing day is not assigned) because Kotlin cannot tell undefined from null. The value is controlled only (no defaultValue), as for every Monarch component. The plan's drag to assign is not offered: the web has no drag either, and a menu per cell is the touch and TalkBack pattern. There is no iOS ShiftRoster yet, so the names follow the web. Experimental because it is a product pattern not yet adopted by a Rook Android app.
accessibility: Each editable cell is one button with a 48dp touch target, named "<person>, <day>: <assignment>", for example "Alex Kim, Monday, November 2, Today: Morning, 06:00 to 14:00"; an overnight shift adds "overnight" and a grid cell with a short name adds it after the full name.

The cell menu is a Material 3 DropdownMenu headed by a heading with the person and the day; the current choice is marked selected and has a filled radio button, and each shift is read with its spoken time range.
Read-only cells are one text element with the same name and no click action; disabled cells are read as disabled.
Day tabs are Material 3 tabs read as the full date, with "Today" for today; the selected tab is marked selected. The tab rows are named "Day" or "Person".
The day's date is a heading, and the number working is a polite live region, so TalkBack says the new count after an assignment.
Each person is one element read as "name, description, Hours: total"; with onMemberClick it is a button with a 48dp target.
The grid is a collection named "Shift roster"; each cell carries its row and column, day headers are headings read as the full date, and footer counts are read with the date.
Avatars are decorative; no state is shown by color alone.
From font scale 1.5 the cell moves under the person so no text is cut.
edgeCases: Day keys in value may be any time on the date in UTC; they are matched by date, and a change replaces any key of that date.
An assignment to a shift id that is not among shifts reads as not assigned and counts no hours.
A shift whose end equals its start lasts 24 hours.
days is clamped to 1 to 62.
Hours are rounded to one decimal in the locale's number format.
The roster does not scroll vertically; put it in a scrolling screen. The grid scrolls sideways when forced on a narrow window.
Long names and descriptions wrap; nothing is truncated.

examples.title: Editable week
Read only, one person at a time, with a week toolbar
examples.setup:
var week by remember { mutableIntStateOf(0) }
val from = 1_793_577_600_000L + week * 7 * 86_400_000L
examples.code:
Column {
    MonarchCalendarToolbar(
        title = "Week ${week + 1}",
        view = MonarchCalendarToolbarView.Week,
        onToday = { week = 0 },
        onPrevious = { week -= 1 },
        onNext = { week += 1 },
        previousIcon = { Icon(SampleIcons.ChevronLeft, contentDescription = null) },
        nextIcon = { Icon(SampleIcons.ChevronRight, contentDescription = null) },
    )
    @OptIn(ExperimentalMonarchApi::class)
    MonarchShiftRoster(
        members = listOf(MonarchShiftRosterMember("a", "Alex Kim")),
        shifts = listOf(MonarchShiftRosterShift("e", "Evening", start = 14 * 60, end = 22 * 60)),
        from = from,
        value = mapOf("a" to mapOf(from to MonarchShiftRosterAssignment.Shift("e"))),
        onValueChange = { _, _ -> },
        days = 3,
        layout = MonarchShiftRosterLayout.ByPerson,
        readOnly = true,
        today = null,
    )
}

parityExceptions.reason: An unassigned cell is drawn as a dash, and its button is named for TalkBack with the person, the day and "Not assigned" ("Sam Lee, Wednesday 4 November: Not assigned"), not with the dash alone.
parityExceptions.convention: a control is named by what it does and where, not by its glyph (Material accessibility)

title: SidebarNav
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.ModalNavigationDrawer, PermanentNavigationDrawer, ModalDrawerSheet, PermanentDrawerSheet and NavigationDrawerItem; androidx.compose.material3.NavigationRail with NavigationRailItem for the collapsed form
summary: Sections of destinations at the side of the app are the Material 3 navigation drawer: modal on a phone, permanent at expanded width, with NavigationDrawerItem rows, section headings and counts. Its collapsed, icon-only form is NavigationRail. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: For an app with more destinations than fit a bottom bar, grouped in sections: a ModalNavigationDrawer opened from the top app bar on a phone, a PermanentNavigationDrawer on a tablet or desktop window.
whenNotToUse: For three to five top-level destinations use NavigationBar or NavigationSuiteScaffold (see top-nav). For actions use a menu. For a panel of content beside a list use a supporting pane (see peek-panel).
api: @Composable fun ModalNavigationDrawer(drawerContent: @Composable () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, drawerState: DrawerState = rememberDrawerState(DrawerValue.Closed), gesturesEnabled: Boolean = true, scrimColor: Color = DrawerDefaults.scrimColor, content: @Composable () -> Unit)
@Composable fun PermanentNavigationDrawer(drawerContent: @Composable () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, content: @Composable () -> Unit)

@Composable fun ModalDrawerSheet(modifier: Modifier = Modifier, drawerShape: Shape = DrawerDefaults.shape, drawerContainerColor: Color = DrawerDefaults.modalContainerColor, …, content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)

@Composable fun NavigationDrawerItem(label: @Composable () -> Unit, selected: Boolean, onClick: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, icon: @Composable (() -> Unit)? = null, badge: @Composable (() -> Unit)? = null, shape: Shape = NavigationDrawerTokens.ActiveIndicatorShape.value, colors: NavigationDrawerItemColors = NavigationDrawerItemDefaults.colors(), interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)

@Composable fun NavigationRail(modifier: Modifier = Modifier, containerColor: Color = NavigationRailDefaults.ContainerColor, contentColor: Color = contentColorFor(containerColor), header: @Composable (ColumnScope.() -> Unit)? = null, windowInsets: WindowInsets = NavigationRailDefaults.windowInsets, content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)

states.name: current page
states.description: NavigationDrawerItem with selected = true has the subtle accent fill and the selected state.

states.name: with a count
states.description: A MonarchBadge in the badge slot follows the label.

states.name: nested group
states.description: A NavigationDrawerItem that toggles expanded, followed by its children indented with Modifier.padding(start = …).

states.name: collapsed
states.description: NavigationRail shows icons with short labels; the full drawer opens from a menu button.

appearance: The drawer sheet uses the raised background role (Material surfaceContainerLow), selected items the subtle accent role (secondaryContainer) with the strong accent role for text, and other items the muted text role. Section headings are MonarchText in the label style and the muted text role. The high-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colors.
platformNotes: The web SidebarNav renders sections of links with nested groups, count badges with a tone, the current page from the path, an icon-only collapsed mode with tooltips, and a header and footer. On Android the rows are NavigationDrawerItem, which select a destination rather than follow a link; the current page is selected = true; badgeTone is a MonarchBadge in the badge slot; the collapsed mode is NavigationRail (with PlainTooltip on long press for the names); nested groups are rows the app expands; header and footer are ordinary content of the sheet. NavigationSuiteScaffold (see top-nav) chooses between bar, rail and drawer by window size. iOS uses a sidebar List in NavigationSplitView.
accessibility: System behavior: each NavigationDrawerItem is a 56dp-high selectable row with the tab role in a group, read with its label and selected state; the badge is read as part of it.
System behavior: a modal drawer is a pane announced when it opens; back and the scrim close it.
Mark section titles as headings so TalkBack users can jump between sections.
Give the collapsed rail labels, or a contentDescription on each icon; an icon alone is not a name.
The selected row has a fill and a state, not color on text alone.
edgeCases: A long label wraps in the drawer at large font sizes; the drawer is at most 360dp wide.
Drawer content taller than the screen must scroll: wrap it in Modifier.verticalScroll.
In right to left the drawer slides in from the right.

wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column with MonarchSignInWithRookButton, MonarchButton, MonarchDivider, MonarchInlineNotice, MonarchTextField (autofill content type Username and EmailAddress), MonarchPasswordInput (current-password purpose), MonarchLink and MonarchCheckboxRow; the app's androidx.credentials Credential Manager for passkeys
summary: A recipe, not a component: sign in with an email and password, a passkey or single sign-on, with field errors, a form error, Keep me signed in, and links to reset the password and create an account.
whenToUse: For the sign-in screen of an app that has its own accounts.
whenNotToUse: When the app signs in only with Rook ID, show MonarchSignInWithRookButton alone. To reset a password use the PasswordResetForm recipe; to re-confirm a signed-in person use MonarchStepUpAuthDialog.
api: MonarchSignInWithRookButton(onClick = …, fullWidth = true)
MonarchButton(text = "Sign in with a passkey", onClick = …, modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth())

MonarchTextField(value = email, onValueChange = …, modifier = Modifier.semantics { contentType = ContentType.Username + ContentType.EmailAddress }, label = "Email", errorText = emailError, keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(keyboardType = KeyboardType.Email, autoCorrectEnabled = false))

MonarchPasswordInput(value = password, onValueChange = …, label = "Password", errorText = passwordError, purpose = MonarchPasswordInputPurpose.Current, keyboardActions = KeyboardActions(onDone = { signIn() }))
MonarchCheckboxRow(checked = keepSignedIn, onCheckedChange = …, label = "Keep me signed in")
MonarchButton(text = "Sign in", onClick = signIn, modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(), variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Primary, loading = signingIn)

states.description: Single sign-on and passkey buttons, an "or" divider, the email and password fields, Forgot password?, Keep me signed in, Sign in and Create an account.

states.name: field errors
states.description: An empty or malformed email and an empty password show their errors on the fields before anything is sent.

states.description: Sign in shows its progress indicator and reads "Loading".

states.description: A wrong password or a server failure goes in a danger MonarchInlineNotice above the fields.

states.name: passkey
states.description: The passkey button starts the app's Credential Manager request, which shows the system passkey sheet; a cancelled sheet changes nothing.

appearance: Every part is an existing Monarch component: the Rook ID button, a secondary passkey button, a divider with a muted "or", outlined fields with their errors, a checkbox row, links and a full-width primary button. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web's SignInForm is one component with an onSubmit that returns errors and its own messages. On Android, as on iOS, it is a recipe, because the request, the session and navigation belong to the app. Autofill comes from the content types: Username and EmailAddress on the email field and the Password type that MonarchPasswordInput's current purpose sets, so autofill services and Google Password Manager offer saved passwords. Passkey sign-in is the app's Credential Manager call (androidx.credentials GetCredentialRequest with a GetPublicKeyCredentialOption), which shows the system sheet; Monarch does not depend on androidx.credentials. The web's identifier modes (username, email or username) are the field's label, keyboard type and content type.
accessibility: The title has the heading semantics.
Field errors come from MonarchTextField and MonarchPasswordInput, which show them in words and mark the fields as in error.
The "or" divider is decorative and hidden from TalkBack.
Keep me signed in is a MonarchCheckboxRow: one element with the checkbox role and its state.
Forgot password? and Create an account are MonarchLinks; the buttons are MonarchButtons with 48dp targets and a loading state.
The system passkey sheet is the system's.
edgeCases: Do not say whether the email or the password was wrong; use one form error.
Trim spaces around the email but never change the password.
With passkey or single sign-on only, leave out the password field, Forgot password? and Keep me signed in.
Never save the password in the instance state; keep it in remember, not rememberSaveable.

        MonarchLink(
            text = "Create an account",
            onClick = { /* Open sign-up. */ },
            variant = MonarchLinkVariant.Standalone,
        )
    }
}

name: MonarchSignInWithRookButton
title: SignInWithRookButton
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.Button inside a pinned MonarchTheme
summary: The "Sign in with Rook ID" button, in a capsule with fixed light, dark and neutral looks and a loading state. Rook-scoped.
whenToUse: On a sign-in screen of an app that offers Rook ID sign-in. The app runs the sign-in itself, for example in a Custom Tab, from onClick.
whenNotToUse: Outside Rook, or for any other sign-in provider: use MonarchButton. For the main action of a form use MonarchButton with the primary variant.
api: @Composable fun MonarchSignInWithRookButton(onClick: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchSignInWithRookButtonVariant = MonarchSignInWithRookButtonVariant.Light, size: MonarchSignInWithRookButtonSize = MonarchSignInWithRookButtonSize.Md, enabled: Boolean = true, loading: Boolean = false, fullWidth: Boolean = false, mark: Painter? = null, label: String? = null, loadingLabel: String? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)
enum class MonarchSignInWithRookButtonVariant { Light, Dark, Neutral, Auto }
enum class MonarchSignInWithRookButtonSize { Sm, Md, Lg }

options.name: onClick
options.description: Called when the button is activated and not loading.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the button.

options.name: variant
options.description: Light, Dark and Neutral look the same on every screen; Auto follows the theme.

options.name: size
options.description: 32, 40 or 48dp high. The touch target is at least 48dp at every size.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the button can be activated.

options.name: loading
options.description: Shows a progress indicator in place of the mark, reads "Loading" and ignores taps.

options.name: fullWidth
options.description: Fills the available width.

options.name: mark
options.description: The Rook ID mark, drawn before the label at 16, 20 or 24dp without a tint. Decorative.

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Sign in with Rook ID".

options.name: loadingLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Loading" state read while loading.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the press, focus and hover interactions.

states.name: resting
states.description: A capsule on the surface color with the strong border; Neutral is a muted fill without a border.

states.name: pressed
states.description: The muted background; the emphasis background for Neutral, plus the Material 3 ripple.

states.name: loading
states.description: A progress indicator replaces the mark; the colors stay at full contrast.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The subtle background, the disabled text color and the subtle border.

appearance: A capsule. Light and Neutral take their roles from the light theme and Dark from the dark theme, whatever the theme of the screen; when the screen uses a high-contrast theme they use the high-contrast light or dark theme. Auto uses the roles of the screen's theme. Roles: surface or muted fill, default text, strong border.
platformNotes: Rook-scoped: it exists for Rook ID only. The web can render a link (href); on Android it is always a button and the app opens the sign-in, for example in a Custom Tab. Monarch ships no artwork, so the mark is a Painter the app passes; the web's markSrc URL is not offered because Monarch loads no images. iOS also takes a markURL loaded with AsyncImage; Android does not. The web dims a disabled button with opacity; Android uses the disabled color roles. The web's block is fullWidth, as on iOS. The light and dark looks are pinned by drawing the button inside a MonarchTheme with a fixed scheme.
accessibility: A Material 3 button with the Button role, named by its label.
The mark is an Image with a null content description, so TalkBack skips it.
While loading the state description is "Loading", the button is reported as disabled and onClick does not run.
The touch target is at least 48dp high at every size, reserved in the layout.
The label grows with the font size setting and wraps rather than being cut.
edgeCases: Without a mark the button shows the label only.
The mark is drawn as given, without a tint, and is not dimmed when disabled.
A long label wraps inside the capsule and the button grows in height.

title: SignUpForm
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column with MonarchTextField (autofill content types PersonFullName, NewUsername and EmailAddress), MonarchPasswordInput (new-password purpose), MonarchPasswordStrengthMeter, MonarchTermsAcceptance, MonarchInlineNotice, MonarchButton and MonarchLink
summary: A recipe, not a component: create an account with a name, an email and a new password, with the password rules, terms to accept, field errors and a link to sign in.
whenToUse: For the sign-up screen of an app that has its own accounts.
whenNotToUse: When the app signs people up only with Rook ID, show MonarchSignInWithRookButton. To sign in, use the SignInForm recipe; to join from an invitation with a known email, show the email as text instead of a field.
api: MonarchTextField(value = name, onValueChange = …, modifier = Modifier.semantics { contentType = ContentType.PersonFullName }, label = "Full name", errorText = nameError)

MonarchTextField(value = email, onValueChange = …, modifier = Modifier.semantics { contentType = ContentType.NewUsername + ContentType.EmailAddress }, label = "Email", errorText = emailError, keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(keyboardType = KeyboardType.Email, autoCorrectEnabled = false))
MonarchPasswordInput(value = password, onValueChange = …, label = "Password", errorText = passwordError, purpose = MonarchPasswordInputPurpose.New)
MonarchPasswordStrengthMeter(password = password, rules = rules)
MonarchTermsAcceptance(accepted = accepted, onAcceptedChange = …, documents = documents, showRequiredError = tried)
MonarchButton(text = "Create account", onClick = createAccount, modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(), variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Primary, loading = creating)

options.name: nameError
options.description: An empty name, shown on the field after the first attempt.

options.name: emailError
options.description: An empty or malformed email, or the server's "already in use" answer, shown on the field.

options.name: passwordError
options.description: A password that misses a rule of MonarchPasswordRule.defaults(), shown on the field; the meter lists which rule.

options.name: formError
options.description: Any other failure, in a danger MonarchInlineNotice above the fields.

options.name: creating
options.description: Passed to Create account's loading while the request runs.

states.name: ready
states.description: The title, the name, email and password fields, the strength meter with its rules, the terms checkbox, Create account and the link to sign in.

states.name: field errors
states.description: An empty name, an empty or malformed email, a password that misses a rule and unaccepted terms each show their error before anything is sent.

states.name: creating
states.description: Create account shows its progress indicator and reads "Loading".

states.name: email taken
states.description: The server's answer goes on the email field; any other failure goes in a danger MonarchInlineNotice above the fields.

states.name: invitation
states.description: Prefill the email from an invitation and show it as text instead of a field.

appearance: Every part is an existing Monarch component: outlined fields with their errors, the strength meter's segments and rule list, the terms checkbox row, a full-width primary button and a standalone link. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web's SignUpForm is one component with onSubmit, its own messages and an optional confirm-password field. On Android, as on iOS, it is a recipe, because the request and navigation belong to the app. There is no confirm field: the password's reveal button shows typos, and the new-password purpose of MonarchPasswordInput lets autofill services and Google Password Manager suggest a strong password and save it. The email field's NewUsername and EmailAddress content types, and PersonFullName on the name, tell autofill what to offer. Optional single sign-on goes above the fields with MonarchSignInWithRookButton and an "or" divider, as in the SignInForm recipe.
accessibility: The title has the heading semantics.
Field errors come from MonarchTextField and MonarchPasswordInput, which show them in words and mark the fields as in error.
The strength meter reads the strength and each rule as met or not met, in words.
The terms checkbox is one element with the checkbox role; its required error is a visible message.
Create account is a MonarchButton with a 48dp target and a loading state; the sign-in link is a MonarchLink.
edgeCases: Trim spaces around the email and the name but never change the password.
Never save the password in the instance state; keep it in remember, not rememberSaveable.
Show errors only after the first attempt, then update them as the person types.
Send the accepted document versions and the date from MonarchTermsAcceptanceDetails with the request.

name: MonarchSkeleton
title: Skeleton
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Box, androidx.compose.ui.draw.drawBehind, androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Brush.linearGradient, androidx.compose.animation.core.rememberInfiniteTransition
summary: A loading placeholder in the shape of a line of text, a block or a circle, with a shimmer that stands still when animations are off.
whenToUse: While the content of a card, a row or a screen loads and its layout is known: show placeholders in the places the text and pictures will take.
whenNotToUse: For a wait whose layout is unknown, or inside a button, use MonarchProgress or MonarchButton(loading = true). For a failure, use MonarchErrorState or MonarchInlineErrorRetry.
api: @Composable fun MonarchSkeleton(modifier: Modifier = Modifier, shape: MonarchSkeletonShape = MonarchSkeletonShape.Rect)
enum class MonarchSkeletonShape { Text, Rect, Circle }

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the placeholder. Set a width for lines and blocks, and Modifier.size for circles.

options.name: shape
options.description: Text: a line three quarters of the body font size high, 4dp corners. Rect: at least 40dp high, 8dp corners. Circle: 40dp unless Modifier.size sets another size.

states.name: loading
states.description: A lighter band sweeps across the muted fill every 1.6 seconds, from the start edge to the end edge.

states.name: still
states.description: With animations turned off the placeholder is the muted fill and does not move.

appearance: The muted background with a band of the subtle background sweeping across it, in every theme. In the high-contrast themes the two roles are close, so the band is faint and the shape carries the meaning.
platformNotes: The web Skeleton pulses its opacity; Monarch never dims with alpha, so on Android a gradient band sweeps across the fill, as the plan asked. The sweep follows the layout direction. The web width and height props are the modifier here. iOS covers skeletons with the system redaction (redacted(reason: .placeholder)) and ships no type; Compose has no redaction, so Android builds this component.
accessibility: A skeleton is hidden from TalkBack. Give the region that holds the placeholders a content description such as "Loading contact", and say when it has loaded.
The shimmer stands still when the user has turned animations off.
The text line grows with the font size setting, so placeholders match the text that replaces them.
edgeCases: A block or a circle without a size from the modifier takes its 40dp default; a block also fills the width it is given.
A parent that measures with unbounded width, such as a horizontally scrolling row, needs a width on text lines and blocks.

A picture placeholder

name: MonarchSkipLink
title: SkipLink
wrapsNative: MonarchButton, androidx.compose.ui.focus.FocusRequester
summary: An action that moves focus past repeated navigation to the main content of a screen, for keyboard, switch access and TalkBack users, with Modifier.monarchSkipLinkTarget for the element it moves to.
whenToUse: At the top of a screen whose navigation (a long toolbar, a row of filters, a rail of links) comes before the main content in the focus order.
whenNotToUse: On screens where the content comes first or the navigation is a bottom bar; TalkBack users already move by heading there.
api: @Composable fun MonarchSkipLink(target: FocusRequester, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, label: String? = null, onSkip: (() -> Unit)? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)
fun Modifier.monarchSkipLinkTarget(requester: FocusRequester): Modifier

options.name: target
options.description: The requester of the main content, shared with Modifier.monarchSkipLinkTarget.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the button.

options.name: label
options.description: The label. null uses "Skip to main content".

options.name: onSkip
options.description: Called after focus moved, for example to scroll the content into view.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the press and focus interactions.

states.name: resting
states.description: A small secondary button.

states.name: activated
states.description: Focus moves to the element marked with monarchSkipLinkTarget.

appearance: A small secondary MonarchButton: the surface with the default border and the default text. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web SkipLink is hidden until it receives keyboard focus and jumps to an element id. Android has no hidden focus-only element that TalkBack also reaches, so the skip link is a visible small button, read first in its traversal group (traversalIndex -1), and it moves input focus to a FocusRequester instead of an id.
accessibility: It is a button with a touch target of at least 48dp, named "Skip to main content" or the label.
It is read before the other elements of its traversal group.
Activating it requests focus on the target, which monarchSkipLinkTarget makes focusable; the next key press or swipe continues from there.
edgeCases: A target that is not in the composition is not focused; requestFocus has no effect.
Whether TalkBack's accessibility focus follows the input focus was not tried on a device.

name: MonarchSlaIndicator
title: SlaIndicator
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row, androidx.compose.material3.Text, android.icu.text.MeasureFormat
summary: A service-level target at a glance: on track, at risk, breached, paused, met or not applicable, with the time left or overdue, as a chip or as text.
whenToUse: In a ticket row, a ticket header or a side panel, to show whether a response or resolution target will be met and how much time is left.
whenNotToUse: For a status without a deadline use MonarchBadge. For a running timer of elapsed time use MonarchTabularNumber with the app's own clock.
api: @Composable fun MonarchSlaIndicator(state: MonarchSlaIndicatorState, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchSlaIndicatorVariant = MonarchSlaIndicatorVariant.Chip, dueAt: Long? = null, warnBeforeMillis: Long? = null, earlierBreach: Boolean = false, showNotApplicable: Boolean = false, live: Boolean = true, announceChanges: Boolean = false, now: Long? = null, target: String? = null, icon: (@Composable (MonarchSlaIndicatorState) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchSlaIndicatorLabels = MonarchSlaIndicatorLabels(), onStateChange: ((MonarchSlaIndicatorState) -> Unit)? = null)
enum class MonarchSlaIndicatorState { OnTrack, AtRisk, Breached, Paused, Met, NotApplicable }
enum class MonarchSlaIndicatorVariant { Chip, Text }

class MonarchSlaIndicatorLabels(onTrack: String? = null, atRisk: String? = null, breached: String? = null, paused: String? = null, met: String? = null, notApplicable: String? = null, notApplicableMark: String? = null, remaining: ((String) -> String)? = null, overdue: ((String) -> String)? = null, duration: ((Long) -> String)? = null, due: ((String) -> String)? = null, earlierBreach: String? = null, changed: ((String, String?) -> String)? = null)

options.name: state
options.description: The state the server reported. A running state (OnTrack, AtRisk) is derived again from dueAt and the clock.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the component.

options.name: variant
options.description: Chip is a compact rounded rectangle; Text is an icon and text without a surface.

options.name: dueAt
options.description: When the target is due, in epoch milliseconds. It drives the countdown ("2h 15m left") and the overdue time ("Overdue 40m").

options.name: warnBeforeMillis
options.description: Turns an on-track target at risk once it is due within this many milliseconds. By default the state is trusted.

options.name: earlierBreach
options.description: An earlier target of the same item was breached. TalkBack says so.

options.name: showNotApplicable
options.description: Writes a missing target as "No SLA" and not as a dash.

options.name: live
options.description: Whether a running target with a due time follows the clock by itself.

options.name: announceChanges
options.description: Announces a change of the shown state through a polite live region. For one prominent indicator, not for every row of a list.

options.name: now
options.description: A fixed reference time in epoch milliseconds, which also stops the clock.

options.name: target
options.description: The name of the target, such as "First response". Read by TalkBack, not shown.

options.name: icon
options.description: Draws the icon of a state in the content color, for example a clock, an exclamation mark, a pause or a check. Monarch bundles no icons. Not drawn for NotApplicable.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings (monarch_slaindicator_*) and the duration format.

options.name: onStateChange
options.description: Called when the shown state changes after the indicator appeared, such as when a countdown runs out.

states.name: OnTrack
states.description: Muted text, no fill. Shows the time left when dueAt is given.

states.name: AtRisk
states.description: Warning colors; the chip has the warning subtle fill and a warning border. Shows the time left.

states.name: Breached
states.description: The chip is solid danger; the text variant is danger-coloured text. Shows the time overdue when dueAt has passed.

states.name: Paused
states.description: Muted text; the chip has the muted fill. No countdown.

states.name: Met
states.description: Success-coloured text, no fill.

states.name: NotApplicable
states.description: No icon, subtle text in the regular weight: a dash, or "No SLA" with showNotApplicable.

appearance: Text in the caption role with tabular digits. The chip has 6dp corners; at risk uses the warning subtle fill, strong text and border, breached the danger solid fill with its on-solid text, paused the muted background. The text variant only colors the text: muted, warning strong, danger strong, success strong or subtle. All roles follow light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The parity map named MonarchBadge with a countdown. The badge has no border on a tinted fill, no transparent form and a capsule shape, so the indicator draws its own chip from the same roles, as iOS does. The web state none is NotApplicable, as on iOS. The web shows the due date in a tooltip; Android reads it in the state description. The web's icons are built in; Monarch bundles no icons, so the icon is an optional slot that receives the state, and every state has its own text. The web live interval and locale options are not offered: the clock wakes at each whole minute and at the at-risk and due edges, and durations use ICU MeasureFormat in the locale of the configuration. The web file also exports SlaTargetList; on Android that is rows of text and the Text variant (see the last example).
accessibility: One TalkBack element. Its content description is the target name and the time left or overdue in words ("First response, 2 hours, 15 minutes left"), or the state name when there is no countdown.
Its state description is the state name when the description is a countdown, then "due" and the date and time, then a note when an earlier target was breached.
Every state has its own text, so the state does not depend on color or on the icon.
With announceChanges a change of the shown state is announced once through a polite live region, such as "First response: Breached".
The text grows with the font size setting and wraps.
The indicator is not interactive.
edgeCases: A running target whose due time has passed is shown as breached even if the server still reports on track.

Durations are whole minutes rounded down, in at most two units: "<1m", "45m", "2h 15m", "3d 4h". Units come from ICU MeasureFormat in the configuration's locale (narrow for the text, words for TalkBack); only the under-a-minute strings come from the resources.
A breached target without a due time, or with one in the future, shows "Breached".
Paused, Met, Breached and NotApplicable are never changed by the clock, and their indicators do not tick.
With now set, or live false, the text is computed for each composition and does not advance by itself.
onStateChange and the announcement fire for a change of the shown state, whether the clock or a new state value caused it. The first state is not reported.

name: MonarchSlashMenu
title: SlashMenu
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn of MonarchListRow rows under heading texts, in a full-width strip the app places above the text field and the keyboard; androidx.compose.ui.text.input.TextFieldValue for the caret
summary: The / menu of a composer or document editor: a grouped list of blocks to insert, filtered by what is typed after the slash, in a strip above the text field and the keyboard, with helpers that find the command being typed and replace it.
whenToUse: In a notes, document or message composer where people insert headings, lists and other blocks by typing a slash at the start of a line.
whenNotToUse: For @mentions, use MonarchMentionPicker. For a fixed set of formatting actions, use MonarchEditorToolbar. For actions on a selection, use a MonarchMenu.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchSlashMenu(query: MonarchSlashMenuQuery?, items: List<MonarchSlashMenuItem>, onSelect: (MonarchSlashMenuItem) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, groupOrder: List<String> = emptyList(), labels: MonarchSlashMenuLabels = MonarchSlashMenuLabels())
public class MonarchSlashMenuItem(id: String, label: String, description: String? = null, icon: Painter? = null, group: String? = null, keywords: List<String> = emptyList(), enabled: Boolean = true)

public class MonarchSlashMenuQuery(trigger: Char, text: String, start: Int, end: Int) { fun replacing(text: String, replacement: String = ""): String; fun replacing(value: TextFieldValue, replacement: String = ""): TextFieldValue; companion object { const val DEFAULT_MAX_LENGTH: Int = 24; fun find(text: String, caret: Int = text.length, trigger: Char = '/', position: MonarchSlashMenuTriggerPosition = MonarchSlashMenuTriggerPosition.LineStart, maxLength: Int = DEFAULT_MAX_LENGTH): MonarchSlashMenuQuery?; fun find(value: TextFieldValue, trigger: Char = '/', position: MonarchSlashMenuTriggerPosition = MonarchSlashMenuTriggerPosition.LineStart, maxLength: Int = DEFAULT_MAX_LENGTH): MonarchSlashMenuQuery? } }
public enum class MonarchSlashMenuTriggerPosition { LineStart, WordStart }
public class MonarchSlashMenuLabels(label: String? = null, empty: ((String) -> String)? = null, count: ((Int) -> String)? = null)

public object MonarchSlashMenuDefaults { fun filter(items: List<MonarchSlashMenuItem>, query: String): List<MonarchSlashMenuItem>; fun group(items: List<MonarchSlashMenuItem>, groupOrder: List<String> = emptyList()): List<Pair<String?, List<MonarchSlashMenuItem>>> }

options.name: query
options.description: The command being typed, from MonarchSlashMenuQuery.find. Nothing is drawn while it is null.

options.name: items
options.description: Every entry the menu offers. The menu filters them by the query with MonarchSlashMenuDefaults.filter.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Called with the chosen entry. Replace the command with query.replacing(value, replacement); the next find returns null, which closes the menu.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the strip. Place it directly above the text field.

options.name: groupOrder
options.description: Group headings in display order. Groups not listed follow in the order they first appear.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the list's name, the empty text and the count announcement.

states.name: closed
states.description: No query: nothing is drawn.

states.name: results
states.description: The matching entries under their group headings; more than about four rows scroll.

states.name: disabled entry
states.description: Icon and text in the disabled text color; the row cannot be chosen.

states.name: nothing matches
states.description: One line, "Nothing matches “/xyz”", in the muted text color.

appearance: A strip on the surface color with a subtle top border. Group headings are captions in the muted text color; each row has an optional muted icon, the label in the default text color and the description in the muted text color. Disabled rows use the disabled text color. The roles follow light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web SlashMenu is a popover beside the caret, with the highlight moved by arrow keys while focus stays in the field (aria-activedescendant), and hooks that wire it to a textarea or a rich-text editor. Compose gives no caret rectangle, so on Android, as on iOS, the menu is a full-width strip that the app places directly above the text field (and so above the keyboard), the same placement as MonarchMentionPicker, and an entry is chosen by tapping it; there is no highlighted row and no arrow-key handling. The web hooks become MonarchSlashMenuQuery.find and replacing, which read and set the caret through TextFieldValue; the web's filterSlashMenuItems and groupSlashMenuItems are MonarchSlashMenuDefaults.filter and group with the same ranking and order. The menu filters the items itself, where the web takes them already filtered. iOS names a static filter on the menu and an isDisabled flag; Kotlin has no static members on a function, so filter lives on MonarchSlashMenuDefaults, and the flag is enabled, as in Material 3. The icon is a Painter from the app, because Monarch bundles no icons (iOS takes an SF Symbol name). The web's openMenu (a toolbar button that types the slash) is the app inserting "/" into its TextFieldValue.
accessibility: Each entry is a button whose name is its label and description; a disabled entry is marked disabled and cannot be activated.
The strip is a group named "Insert block" and a polite live region whose state is the number of options or "Nothing matches “/xyz”", so the change is announced while focus stays in the text field.
Group headings are headings.
Icons are decorative.
Rows are at least 48dp high (MonarchListRow) and grow with the font size setting; long descriptions wrap.
edgeCases: A slash inside a line (1/2, a path) never opens the menu with the default LineStart position; use WordStart to allow it after white space.
A space, punctuation or more than 24 characters after the slash closes the menu, so typing on continues normally.
While a range of text is selected, find on a TextFieldValue returns null.
A query's range belongs to the text it was found in; replacing in a shorter text leaves it unchanged.
Entry ids must be unique: they are the list keys.

name: MonarchSlider
title: Slider
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.Slider
summary: A slider for one number: a 6dp track, the accent range, an 18dp thumb with a 2dp accent border, a 48dp touch target and an optional label with the value.
whenToUse: For a value where the position matters more than the exact number: volume, brightness, a zoom level.
whenNotToUse: For an exact number use MonarchNumberInput. For a range with two ends use the Material 3 RangeSlider. For a rating use MonarchRatingPicker.
api: @Composable fun MonarchSlider(value: Float, onValueChange: (Float) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, valueRange: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Float> = 0f..1f, steps: Int = 0, onValueChangeFinished: (() -> Unit)? = null, invalid: Boolean = false, label: String? = null, valueLabel: ((Float) -> String)? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)

options.name: value
options.description: The current value.

options.name: onValueChange
options.description: Called while the user drags or presses an arrow key.

options.name: valueRange
options.description: The range of values.

options.name: steps
options.description: Steps between the ends; 0 is continuous.

options.name: onValueChangeFinished
options.description: Called when the user lifts the thumb.

options.name: invalid
options.description: Draws the range and thumb in danger.

options.name: label
options.description: The label above the slider and its TalkBack name.

options.name: valueLabel
options.description: Formats the value shown at the end of the label row and read as the state.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the control.

options.name: enabled
options.description: A disabled control is drawn at half opacity and ignores input.

states.name: value
states.description: The track up to the thumb and the thumb use the accent strong color; the rest of the track the accent subtle color.

states.name: pressed
states.description: Material narrows the thumb while it is dragged.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Material 3 disabled colors; the value does not change by touch.

appearance: MonarchTheme maps the Material 3 scheme so that the thumb and the active track use the accent strong color and the inactive track the accent subtle color. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Built on the Material 3 Slider for its drag, keyboard and TalkBack behaviour (progress range info and the setProgress action), with a Monarch thumb and track. The thumb slot is 48dp high so the slider has a 48dp touch target. Migrating: Slider(value, onValueChange, ...) becomes MonarchSlider(value, onValueChange, ...); drop colors, thumb and track.
accessibility: The slider exposes its range and value; TalkBack reads it as a percentage unless a stateDescription says the value in words.
TalkBack can set the value with its adjust gestures; with steps the value snaps to the nearest step.
With the 48dp thumb, as in every example, the slider is at least 48dp high; the default Material slider is 44dp. SliderTest checks both.
A disabled slider is read as disabled.
The value is not shown by color alone when it is also shown as text beside the track.
edgeCases: steps counts the points between the ends, not the intervals: 0..100 in tens needs 9.
A value outside valueRange is drawn at the nearest end.
In right-to-left layouts the track fills from the right.
In this Material 3 release the set-progress accessibility action of a disabled slider still calls onValueChange, so ignore changes while the slider is disabled if that matters.

name: MonarchSlotPicker
title: SlotPicker
wrapsNative: MonarchMiniMonth and androidx.compose.material3.FilterChip times in an androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow, with MonarchSkeleton, MonarchBanner and MonarchTimezoneSelect
summary: Pick a day on a month calendar, then one of that day's open times, shown in the visitor's time zone with an optional zone picker.
whenToUse: For the booking step of an appointment, meeting or interview, choosing from times the server computed, and for rescheduling to another open time.
whenNotToUse: To pick any date and time use the Material 3 DatePicker and TimePicker (the date-time-picker entry); to compare many people's calendars use MonarchTimeGrid.
api: @Composable fun MonarchSlotPicker(slots: List<MonarchSlotPickerSlot>, selection: Long?, onSelectionChange: (Long?) -> Unit, day: Long?, onDayChange: (Long) -> Unit, timeZone: String, previousMonthIcon: @Composable () -> Unit, nextMonthIcon: @Composable () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, allowDeselect: Boolean = false, visibleMonth: Long? = null, onVisibleMonthChange: ((Long) -> Unit)? = null, availableDays: Set<Long>? = null, isDayDisabled: ((Long) -> Boolean)? = null, minimumDate: Long? = null, maximumDate: Long? = null, today: Long? = null, firstDayOfWeek: Int? = null, is24Hour: Boolean? = null, onTimeZoneChange: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, pinnedTimeZones: List<String> = emptyList(), businessTimeZone: String? = null, loading: Boolean = false, error: String? = null, onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null, onChooseOutside: (() -> Unit)? = null, enabled: Boolean = true, labels: MonarchSlotPickerLabels = MonarchSlotPickerLabels())

options.name: is24Hour
options.description: A 24-hour clock; null follows the device setting.

options.name: onTimeZoneChange

options.name: pinnedTimeZones
options.description: Zones listed first in the picker.

options.name: businessTimeZone
options.description: The zone the business works in; a note says times are converted when it differs.

options.name: loading
options.description: Placeholders instead of the times; announced.

options.name: error / onRetry
options.description: A danger banner instead of the times, with a retry button.

options.name: onChooseOutside
options.description: A way out when no time fits, in the empty state and in the not-open warning.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether days and times can be chosen.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, including the calendar's and the zone picker's.

states.name: no day
states.description: "Choose a day to see available times." under the calendar.

states.name: times
states.description: The day's title and its times as filter chips; the chosen one is selected, taken times are disabled, limited places show "3 left".

states.name: loading
states.description: Six placeholders, hidden from TalkBack, and "Loading available times" announced.

states.name: empty
states.description: "No times are available on this day. Try another day." and the Choose another time button when onChooseOutside is given.

states.name: error
states.description: A danger MonarchBanner with the message and Try again.

states.name: not open
states.description: A warning MonarchBanner when the selection is on the day but is none of its times.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Days and times cannot be chosen.

appearance: The calendar of MonarchMiniMonth, a strong day title, times as Material 3 filter chips in the Monarch theme (the chosen time filled), muted hints and zone notes, and banners in the danger and warning tones. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web places the month beside the times on wide containers; on Android the parts stack, which is the phone pattern, and the picker grows with its content, so put it in a scrolling screen. Days are UTC-midnight epoch milliseconds as in Material 3 DatePickerState and slot starts are epoch milliseconds, where the web uses ISO strings; the zone stays an IANA id string, as in MonarchTimezoneSelect. Times are one TalkBack element each instead of the web's single tab stop with arrow keys; the hour cycle follows is24Hour or the device setting instead of the web's hourCycle. The web's headingLevel, uncontrolled defaults (defaultValue, defaultDay, defaultMonth) and locale prop are not offered: state is hoisted and the locale comes from the configuration. The error is a String instead of a node. iOS has no entry yet.
accessibility: The day's title is a heading.
The times are a selectable group named "Available times on Wednesday, November 4"; the chosen time is selected and taken times are disabled.
Each time is a Material 3 filter chip with a 48dp touch target.
Loading and the number of open times ("2 times on Wednesday, November 4") are announced through a polite live region that is always present.
Days outside availableDays are disabled in the calendar and read with their full date.
The zone is always visible, as text or as a labelled picker, so the times are never ambiguous.
Times and the day title wrap at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: The selection is not cleared when the day changes; clear it in onDayChange if the product wants that.
A selection on the chosen day that is not among the slots shows the not-open warning; a selection on another day shows nothing.
Slot starts are shown in timeZone, so a 09:00 UTC slot reads 4:00 AM in New York in November.
With an unknown zone id the times are shown in UTC.

name: MonarchSortableGrid
title: SortableGrid
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.grid.LazyVerticalGrid with androidx.compose.foundation.gestures.detectDragGesturesAfterLongPress, LazyGridItemScope.animateItem and LazyGridState.scrollBy for auto-scroll; MonarchDragHandle for the TalkBack actions and arrow keys
summary: A grid of tiles the user reorders in two dimensions by long-pressing and dragging, with TalkBack actions and arrow keys in every direction, and every step announced.
whenToUse: For dashboards, launchers, galleries or pinned items where the person arranges tiles in rows and columns.
whenNotToUse: For a single column of rows use MonarchReorderableList. For moving items between containers use Compose drag and drop (dragAndDropSource and dragAndDropTarget).
api: @Composable public fun <T> MonarchSortableGrid(items: List<T>, key: (T) -> Any, itemLabel: (T) -> String, onReorder: (from: Int, to: Int) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, columns: Int? = null, minItemWidth: Dp = 160.dp, enabled: Boolean = true, itemEnabled: (T) -> Boolean = { true }, state: LazyGridState = rememberLazyGridState(), labels: MonarchSortableGridLabels = MonarchSortableGridLabels(), itemContent: @Composable ColumnScope.(item: T, state: MonarchSortableGridItemState) -> Unit)

public class MonarchSortableGridLabels(handle: ((label: String) -> String)? = null, pickedUp: ((label: String, position: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, moved: ((label: String, position: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, dropped: ((label: String, position: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, cancelled: ((label: String, position: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, actions: Map<MonarchDragHandleDirection, String> = emptyMap())

options.name: items
options.description: The items, in order.

options.name: key
options.description: A stable, unique key for an item; also the LazyVerticalGrid key.

options.name: itemLabel
options.description: The plain-text name of an item, used in the handle's name and the announcements.

options.name: onReorder
options.description: Called once per finished move (drop, action or arrow key) with the old and the new index. Move the item in items.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the grid. Give it a bounded height to make it scroll.

options.name: columns
options.description: A fixed number of columns. Without it, as many columns of minItemWidth as fit (GridCells.Adaptive).

options.name: minItemWidth
options.description: The smallest tile width for adaptive columns, multiplied by the font scale, so large text gives fewer, wider tiles.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether any tile can be moved.

options.name: itemEnabled
options.description: Whether an item can be moved. Other tiles can still move past it.

options.name: state
options.description: The scroll state of the grid.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the handle's name, the four announcements and the handle's action names.

options.name: itemContent
options.description: The content of a tile, beside the handle. The state gives the index as shown, whether the tile is dragged and whether it can move.

states.name: idle
states.description: Tiles on the surface fill with a subtle border, each with a small idle drag handle.

states.name: dragged
states.description: The held tile follows the finger above the others with the medium shadow, the accent border and a grabbed handle (Picked up); the other tiles slide out of its way.

states.name: locked tile
states.description: itemEnabled false: the handle is disabled and has no actions, and a long press does not pick it up.

states.name: disabled
states.description: enabled false: no tile can be moved.

states.name: empty
states.description: An empty list draws nothing.

appearance: Each tile is the surface fill with a 1dp subtle border and medium corners, the small drag handle at the start. The held tile has the medium shadow and the accent border; its handle uses the grabbed colors of MonarchDragHandle. Every color comes from the theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow the theme.
platformNotes: The web grid follows the pointer from the handle and slides the other tiles away, and picks a tile up with Space and moves it with the arrow keys. On Android a long press anywhere on the tile picks it up, as Android launchers and grids do, and the tiles slide as on the web; TalkBack, Switch Access and hardware keyboards use the handle's four move actions and the arrow keys, which move one place at once and announce the new position. iOS shows a lifted system drag preview and moves the tile on drop, and marks the drop target with an outline (isDropTarget); Android reorders while dragging, so the item state has dragged instead of a drop target. Same type, labels and default minimum width (160dp) as iOS; the order is hoisted (from and to) instead of a binding. The web's uncontrolled defaultItems is not offered. The grid scrolls vertically only.
accessibility: Every tile has a MonarchDragHandle named Reorder and the item's label, with Move up, Move down, Move backward and Move forward (up and down only in one column); the arrow keys move the tile while the handle has focus.
Picking up, moving by an action, dropping and cancelling are announced through a polite live region: "Revenue moved to position 2 of 4."
Backward and forward follow the reading order, so they are mirrored in right-to-left layouts, and a drag follows the finger in both directions.
The held tile is shown by a border, a shadow and the grabbed handle, not by color alone.
The handle keeps a 48dp touch target; adaptive columns become fewer and wider at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: A move action past the first or last place, or above the first row or below the last, does nothing.
A drop at the place it started reports nothing to onReorder but still announces the drop.
Tiles in the same row take their own height; give the content a minimum height when tiles should line up.
The grid scrolls by at most 16dp a frame while the held tile is past its top or bottom edge.
Keys must be unique; the same key twice breaks the LazyVerticalGrid.

name: MonarchSpaceSwitcher
title: SpaceSwitcher
wrapsNative: MonarchButton (ghost) with androidx.compose.material3.ExposedDropdownMenuDefaults.TrailingIcon opening androidx.compose.material3.ModalBottomSheet with MonarchSearchBar and an androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn of androidx.compose.foundation.selection.selectable rows with androidx.compose.material3.RadioButton; MonarchAvatar for icons
summary: Chooses which Space of the workspace the app shows, All spaces or one Space, from a button that opens a sheet with a searchable list, New Space and Manage Spaces.
whenToUse: In a product's top bar or navigation drawer, when the workspace is divided into Spaces and the person filters the app to one of them.
whenNotToUse: To switch between workspaces, use MonarchWorkspaceSwitcher. For a searchable choice inside a form, use MonarchCombobox.
api: @Composable fun MonarchSpaceSwitcher(spaces: List<MonarchSpaceOption>, selection: String?, onSelectionChange: (String?) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, size: MonarchButtonSize = MonarchButtonSize.Md, enabled: Boolean = true, allowsAll: Boolean = true, loading: Boolean = false, iconOnly: Boolean = false, hidesWhenEmpty: Boolean = true, allIcon: Painter? = null, onCreate: (() -> Unit)? = null, onManage: (() -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchSpaceSwitcherLabels = MonarchSpaceSwitcherLabels())

class MonarchSpaceSwitcherLabels(label: String? = null, all: String? = null, placeholder: String? = null, search: String? = null, empty: String? = null, loading: String? = null, create: String? = null, manage: String? = null, cancel: String? = null)

options.name: spaces
options.description: The Spaces this person can open, in display order.

options.name: selection
options.description: The chosen Space id, null for All spaces.

options.name: onSelectionChange
options.description: Called with the chosen Space id, or null for All spaces. Choosing the current one again does not call it.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the button.

options.name: size
options.description: The height and padding of the button.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the sheet can be opened.

options.name: allowsAll
options.description: Offers All spaces first. Without it a Space must stay chosen and the button reads Choose a Space until one is.

options.name: loading
options.description: The Spaces are still loading; the sheet says Loading spaces… and the search field shows its pending state.

options.name: iconOnly
options.description: Shows only the icon and the arrow, for a narrow bar. TalkBack still reads the name.

options.name: hidesWhenEmpty
options.description: Draws nothing when there are no Spaces and nothing is loading.

options.name: allIcon
options.description: The decorative icon of All spaces; null shows a tinted tile with its initial.

options.name: onCreate
options.description: Adds New Space, which closes the sheet and runs this.

options.name: onManage
options.description: Adds Manage Spaces, which closes the sheet and runs this.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

states.name: all spaces
states.description: Nothing chosen: the button shows All spaces; All spaces is marked in the list.

states.name: one space
states.description: The button shows the Space's icon and name; its row has the radio mark and the selected state.

states.name: no choice
states.description: With allowsAll false and nothing chosen the button reads Choose a Space.

states.name: searching
states.description: The list keeps the Spaces whose name or description contains the text, ignoring case and accents; All spaces is hidden; with no match it reads No spaces match.

states.name: loading
states.description: The list ends with Loading spaces….

states.name: empty
states.description: With no Spaces and nothing loading nothing is drawn, unless hidesWhenEmpty is false.

states.name: disabled
states.description: enabled false gives the ghost button's disabled colors and the sheet cannot open.

appearance: A ghost button with a square MonarchAvatar icon, the caption Space in muted text over the name, and the Material exposed-dropdown arrow. The sheet uses the raised surface, default text for names, muted text for descriptions and messages, and Material radio marks. All are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The parity map lists combobox as a dependency; MonarchCombobox is a labelled form field, so the switcher has its own button and the same sheet, search field and single-choice rows that MonarchCombobox's sheet presentation uses, as on iOS. The web opens a popover listbox (EntityPicker) with arrow keys and type to search; on a phone it is a modal bottom sheet. The web's tooltip on the collapsed trigger is the spoken value here, since a phone has no hover. manageHref, manageExternal and createHref are callbacks (onManage, onCreate): components do not navigate. The web's controlled open state and align are not offered. Space icons are Painters; Monarch bundles no icons. iOS names: selection with a Binding, isIconOnly and manageURL; Android hoists selection with onSelectionChange, drops the is prefix and takes onManage. Experimental: an identity product composite that waits for a Rook app to adopt it.
accessibility: The button is one element named "Space" whose state description is the current Space or All spaces, also when only the icon shows; it keeps a 48dp touch target.

Each row is a radio-button element read as the Space and its description ("Engineering, 18 members"), built by a tested pure function; the chosen row is selected and shows a radio mark, so the choice does not depend on color.
Icons are decorative and hidden.
The title of the sheet is a heading; Loading spaces… and No spaces match. are polite live regions.
Rows, New Space, Manage Spaces and Cancel are at least 48dp high; Cancel and the system back gesture close the sheet without a change.
edgeCases: A selection that is not in spaces reads as All spaces (or Choose a Space without allowsAll).
With allowsAll false the All spaces row is not offered, so the choice cannot be cleared.
Choosing the current Space again closes the sheet without calling onSelectionChange.
The search text is cleared when the sheet closes.
Long names wrap in the sheet; the button grows with the text.

name: MonarchSparkline
title: Sparkline
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.Canvas
summary: A word-sized trend line, area or bar chart for tables, stat cards and lists, with a text alternative.
whenToUse: Beside a figure, to show its recent trend in the space of a word: a stat card, a table cell or a list row.
whenNotToUse: When people need to read individual values or axes, use a full chart. For one change between two periods use MonarchDeltaIndicator.
api: @Composable fun MonarchSparkline(values: List<Double?>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, tone: MonarchTone? = null, variant: MonarchSparklineVariant = MonarchSparklineVariant.Line, range: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Double>? = null, inverted: Boolean = false, showLastPoint: Boolean = true, fullWidth: Boolean = false, label: String? = null, summary: String? = null, formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = null, notEnoughDataLabel: String? = null)
enum class MonarchSparklineVariant { Line, Area, Bar }

options.name: values
options.description: The values in order. null, or a value that is not finite, is a gap.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the sparkline.

options.name: tone
options.description: A color with meaning. null takes the surrounding content color.

options.name: variant
options.description: Line, Area or Bar.

options.name: range
options.description: Fixes the value range, so sparklines in a table share one scale.

options.name: inverted
options.description: Draws smaller values higher, as for a rank.

options.name: showLastPoint
options.description: Puts a dot on the latest point. Lines and areas only.

options.name: fullWidth
options.description: Fills the available width instead of 80dp.

options.name: label
options.description: The spoken name. Without it the sparkline is hidden from TalkBack.

options.name: summary
options.description: Replaces the spoken value "latest 11, low 3, high 11" (monarch_sparkline_summary).

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes the numbers of the spoken value. The default is a number in the current locale.

options.name: notEnoughDataLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in text "Not enough data" (monarch_sparkline_not_enough_data).

states.name: line
states.description: A line that breaks at gaps, with a dot on the latest point and on every point that stands alone.

states.name: area
states.description: The line with a fill down to the baseline.

states.name: bar
states.description: One bar per value, from zero; negative values go down.

states.name: not enough data
states.description: Fewer than two values (one for bars): the text "Not enough data" in the muted color.

appearance: Without a tone the line and bars use the surrounding content color and the area the muted background. With a tone they use the strong color of the tone and its subtle background (the neutral tone uses muted text). The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web sizes are pixels; here the sparkline is 80 by 24dp or fills the width, as on iOS. The web tones current and accent, the series colors, the threshold option that picks a tone from the latest value and markers on all points are not offered: pass the tone you want. The web domain is the range parameter. The chart runs from the start edge, so it is mirrored in right-to-left layouts and the latest value is at the end; the web one is not mirrored. The line is 2dp wide, a little heavier than the web's 1.5px, because it is drawn on dp tokens.
accessibility: With a label the sparkline is one element with the image role: the label is its content description and its state description is "latest 11, low 3, high 11".
The Warning and Danger tones add "Warning" or "Critical" to the spoken value, so they do not depend on color.
Without a label it is hidden from TalkBack, so the numbers must be in text nearby.
The "Not enough data" text is read; with a label it becomes the state description.
It is not interactive and does not animate.
edgeCases: A flat series is drawn in the middle of the height.
A value outside a fixed range is drawn at the edge.
Bars always include zero in their range; a zero value is a one-pixel bar.
A single value between two gaps is drawn as a dot, because a line cannot show it.
The not-enough-data text is not cut off at font scale 2.0; the chart itself keeps its 24dp height.

name: MonarchSpinner

whenToUse: For a short wait in a small area, such as a list row or the center of a loading screen.
whenNotToUse: Inside a button use MonarchButton(loading = true). When the progress is known use a determinate MonarchProgress.

options.description: The modifier of the component.

options.name: size
options.description: Sm 14dp, Md 16dp or Lg 24dp across; the stroke is 2dp.

options.name: color
options.description: The ring; the content color of the surrounding surface by default.

options.name: label
options.description: What is loading, for TalkBack. Null uses "Loading" (monarch_progress_loading); an empty string hides the spinner from TalkBack.

states.name: spinning

states.name: still

accessibility: Announced as an indeterminate progress bar named Loading, or the label.
Not a live region; announce the start of a long wait in text if it matters.

name: MonarchSplitButton
title: SplitButton
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row of two MonarchButtons (androidx.compose.material3.Button) and MonarchMenu anchored to the arrow
summary: A main action joined to an arrow button that opens a menu of related alternatives, such as Save with Save as draft and Save and close.
whenToUse: When one action is the usual choice and a few close variants should stay one tap away without crowding the screen.
whenNotToUse: When there is no main action and the button only opens a menu, use the menu-button recipe (a MonarchButton with a MonarchMenu). For unrelated actions use separate buttons or a MonarchButtonGroup.
