options.name: text
options.description: The main action's label.

options.name: onClick
options.description: Runs the main action. Not called while loading or disabled.

options.name: arrowIcon
options.description: The arrow, for example a MonarchIcon of a chevron that points down with a null content description. Required because Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: variant
options.description: Primary, Secondary, Ghost or Danger, for both buttons.

options.name: size
options.description: Sm, Md or Lg, for both buttons. Each keeps a 48dp touch target.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Disables the main action and the menu together.

options.name: loading
options.description: Shows progress on the main button and disables the arrow.

options.name: menuEnabled
options.description: Disables only the arrow, keeping the main action available.

options.name: leadingIcon
options.description: An icon before the main label.

options.name: moreOptionsLabel
options.description: The TalkBack name of the arrow. Default: "More options for <text>" (monarch_splitbutton_more_options).

options.name: loadingLabel
options.description: The state of the main button while loading. Default: the MonarchButton string "Loading".

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The interactions of the main button.

options.name: menuContent
options.description: The menu items, usually MonarchMenuItems; call close from an item to close the menu.

states.name: idle
states.description: Two buttons of the variant joined by a small gap; the menu is closed.

states.name: open
states.description: The MonarchMenu is shown under the arrow; the arrow's state is "Expanded".

states.name: loading
states.description: The main button shows progress and ignores taps; the arrow is disabled and an open menu closes.

states.name: menu disabled
states.description: The arrow uses the disabled colors; the main action still works.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Both buttons use the disabled colors.

appearance: Both halves are MonarchButtons, so they take the colors of the variant: the accent fill for Primary, the surface with the default border for Secondary, no fill for Ghost, the danger fill for Danger, and the muted fill with the disabled text role when disabled. The menu is the Monarch menu on the raised background role. High-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colors.
platformNotes: The web SplitButton draws the main button and a separate arrow button with its own Tab stop and the name "More options for <label>", with controlled open state and alignment. Android does the same with two MonarchButtons and a MonarchMenu; the open state is kept inside the component and closed with the close callback. The Material 3 SplitButtonLayout is experimental in Material 3 1.4, so Monarch does not use it and joins its own buttons with a small gap, which also keeps the Monarch variants and the loading state. The web items shorthand is replaced by MonarchMenuItems in menuContent. iOS uses the system Menu with a primary action, or a joined pair, as a style recipe.
accessibility: The main button and the arrow are separate TalkBack elements with the Button role; the pair is a traversal group.
The arrow is named "More options for Save" by default and reports "Expanded" or "Collapsed" as its state, with the expand and collapse accessibility actions.
While loading, the main button keeps its place in the focus order and reports "Loading".

title: StackedBarChart
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.Canvas through MonarchBarChart (stacked layout), inside MonarchChartFrame with MonarchChartLegend and MonarchChartTable

whenToUse: To show how a few parts make up each category's total, or, with the 100% offset, how the mix of parts changes from category to category.
whenNotToUse: To compare single values across categories use MonarchBarChart. For the parts of one whole use MonarchDonutChart or MonarchStackedProportionBar.

options.name: title
options.description: The chart's name: the frame heading and the plot's spoken name.

options.name: categories
options.description: The categories in display order, already formatted by the app.

options.name: series
options.description: The parts, each with a key, a label, one value per category and an optional color slot. The first series sits on the baseline.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the frame.

options.name: description
options.description: One line under the title.

options.name: categoryTitle
options.description: The heading of the category column of the table.

options.name: summary
options.description: Replaces the generated spoken summary.

options.name: orientation
options.description: Vertical columns or Horizontal bars.

options.name: layout
options.description: Stacked (one bar of parts per category) or Grouped (the parts side by side).

options.name: offset
options.description: Normal stacks the values; Expand stacks each category's shares so every bar is 100% long. Only applies when stacked.

options.name: status
options.description: Ready, Loading, Empty or Error. Ready with no categories or no series shows Empty.

options.name: hiddenSeries
options.description: The keys of hidden series. null lets the chart keep its own set (rememberSaveable), changed by the legend.

options.name: onHiddenSeriesChange
options.description: Called with the new hidden set when the legend changes it, in both modes.

options.name: highlightedIndex
options.description: A category to emphasise; the bars of the others take the disabled text color and TalkBack reads "Highlighted" on it.

options.name: referenceLines
options.description: Dashed lines at a value. Not drawn with the 100% offset.

options.name: valueRange
options.description: Fixes the value axis. With the 100% offset the axis is always 0.0..1.0 (0% to 100%).

options.name: showValueLabels
options.description: Writes each stack's total at its end (each bar's value when grouped). With the 100% offset the total is 100%.

options.name: legendToggle
options.description: Whether legend entries show and hide their series. The legend appears with two or more series.

options.name: tableToggle
options.description: Whether "View as table" is offered.

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: The message of the empty state.

options.name: footer
options.description: Notes under the chart.

options.name: height
options.description: The plot height: 240dp for columns; 32dp per category plus one, at least 120dp, for bars.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings: the bar chart's (frame, category, total, no data, details, clear, highlighted) and the share summary sentence.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes values with the normal offset. With the 100% offset values are percentages in the current locale with at most one decimal, and this is ignored.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Try again in the error status.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Drill-in: called with the category index (an index into the app's categories, also with the 100% offset) from Details in the inspection row or from the category's TalkBack action.

states.name: ready
states.description: The stacked plot, the legend (two or more series) and "View as table".

states.name: 100% offset
states.description: Every bar is 100% long; the value axis, value labels, inspection row, TalkBack, table and summary show percentages. Reference lines are not drawn.

states.name: inspecting
states.description: After a tap or a drag along columns: the category's band is shaded and a row under the plot reads every part and the stack's total, announced politely, with Details (when onSelect is set) and Clear.

states.name: highlighted
states.description: With highlightedIndex, the other categories' bars take the disabled text color.

states.name: series hidden
states.description: The part leaves the bars and the others keep their colors. With the 100% offset the others keep their shares, so the bar ends short of 100%. The table still lists it.

states.name: grouped
states.description: With layout Grouped the parts stand side by side and the offset is ignored.

states.name: loading
states.description: The frame's skeleton of the plot's height, read as "Loading chart".

states.name: empty
states.description: MonarchEmptyState with "No data yet" and the empty message.

states.name: error
states.description: The frame's error, with Try again when onRetry is set.

appearance: As MonarchBarChart: parts take the theme's data colors 1 to 5 in series order, then the subtle text color, with the far end of each stack rounded. Gridlines use the subtle border color, the zero line the strong border color and labels the muted text color. Every color is a theme role, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes are covered.
platformNotes: The web's StackedBarChart is its BarChart with stacking on and the 100% offset; on Android it is the same composition over MonarchBarChart, drawn with a Compose Canvas (iOS uses Swift Charts). Parts touch, as on iOS: MonarchBarChart has no hairline between stacked parts (the web separates them with the surface color). With the 100% offset the web formats axis ticks with no decimals and other values with one; Android uses one percent formatter with at most one decimal for both, as iOS does. Inspection is a tap or drag with a row under the plot, not a hover tooltip; there is no keyboard arrow navigation and no controlled activeIndex. iOS's hiddenSeries Binding becomes hiddenSeries with onHiddenSeriesChange; iOS's valueTitle is not offered because MonarchBarChart has no value axis for TalkBack to name.
accessibility: The plot is one element with the image role, named by the title, whose state description is the generated summary or the summary parameter: with values, MonarchBarChart's summary (categories, each shown series' total and highest category, reference lines); with the 100% offset, the categories, then each shown series' average share and largest share.
After it, one element per category in category order, read as the category, each shown part's value or share and the stack's total.
With onSelect, each category element has a TalkBack custom action named "Details, <category>" that calls onSelect with the category index.
The legend is MonarchChartLegend: each entry is a filter chip with the state "Shown" or "Hidden"; the last shown series cannot be hidden.
"View as table" shows every value or share as text, with a Total column when stacked.
Parts are told apart by the legend's names, the inspection row, TalkBack and the table, not by color alone.
edgeCases: With the 100% offset, negative values count as zero and a category whose positive total is zero has zero shares everywhere.
Shares are computed over every series, hidden ones included, so hiding a part leaves a gap instead of rescaling the others.
Gaps (null) and values that are not finite draw nothing and are read "No value" and shown "—" in the table.
With the normal offset, negative parts stack down from zero apart from the positive parts.
More than five series: the sixth and later take the neutral color.
TalkBack navigation and the touch gestures were checked with Robolectric semantics tests, not on a device with TalkBack; the share logic and summary are unit-tested.

title: StackedProportionBar

summary: One horizontal bar split into proportions, with a legend that lists each part's value and share.
whenToUse: For the make-up of one total in a small space, such as a pipeline by stage, storage by type with free space, or monitors by state.
whenNotToUse: To compare parts precisely or rank many of them, use MonarchBarList; for one part of a whole, MonarchProgress or MonarchUsageMeter; for a featured share chart, MonarchDonutChart.

options.name: label
options.description: Names the bar and its legend for TalkBack, such as "Lead pipeline".

options.name: segments
options.description: The parts, in display order. Each has a key, a label, a value, and a palette color or a status tone.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the bar and legend.

options.name: total
options.description: The size of the whole, for a capacity. The sum of the parts when null or smaller than the sum; the rest is empty track.

options.name: remainderLabel
options.description: The legend name of the empty rest, such as "Free". Without it the rest is drawn but not listed.

options.name: legendContent
options.description: What each legend entry shows after its label: Both ("1,204 · 34%"), Value, Percent or None.

options.name: size
options.description: The thickness of the bar: Sm 4dp, Md 8dp or Lg 12dp.

options.name: showLegend
options.description: Whether the legend is drawn. Without it TalkBack still reads every part from the bar.

options.name: hideZero
options.description: Whether parts with a value of 0 are left out of the bar and the legend.

options.name: percentDigits
options.description: The decimal places of shares. Shares too small to write read "<1%".

options.name: emptyLabel
options.description: Replaces "No data yet", shown when no part has a value.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes a value. A number in the current locale by default.

states.name: default
states.description: The parts in palette colors, in order from the start edge, each at least 4dp wide with 2dp gaps, in a rounded track; the legend lists every part.

states.name: status mode
states.description: Every segment has a tone: parts and markers take the solid color of their tone, and Neutral the subtle text color.

states.name: remainder
states.description: A total above the sum leaves empty track; with remainderLabel it is listed with an outlined marker.

states.name: legend hidden
states.description: Only the bar is drawn; TalkBack reads the label and every part from it.

states.name: empty
states.description: No part has a value: an empty track and "No data yet".

appearance: Parts take the theme's data colors 1 to 5 in order, later ones the subtle text color, over a track in the muted background color; in status mode the success, warning, danger and info solid colors. Legend markers are squares in the part's color; the remainder's is outlined in the strong border color. Legend text is caption text in the default text color, the value in medium weight. Every color is a theme role, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes are covered.
platformNotes: Drawn with a Compose Canvas (iOS draws shapes in an HStack, the web flex boxes). The web shows a tooltip when the pointer hovers a part; touch has no hover, so, as on iOS, the legend carries every value and there is no tooltip. The web minSegmentWidth option is a fixed 4dp. A mix of tones and palette colors cannot be rejected by the type system as on the web; when not every part has a tone, tones are ignored, as the web does at run time. The web locale and valueFormat options are the current locale and formatValue. The share rule ("<1%", ">99%") is the one MonarchDonutChart uses. The parts run from the start edge, so the bar mirrors in right to left. iOS uses the same names; showsLegend and hidesZero are showLegend and hideZero, in Kotlin style.
accessibility: While the legend is shown the bar is hidden from TalkBack and the legend is a traversal group named by label.
Each legend entry is one element read as the part's name, value and share, such as "Replied 182 · 9%", whatever legendContent shows.
With showLegend off, the bar is one element named by label whose state description lists every part.
With no data, one element reads the label with "No data yet" as its state.
Every part has a text label, so no part is told apart by color alone; the remainder's marker is outlined, not filled.
Legend text scales with the font size and wraps onto more rows.
edgeCases: Negative and non-finite values count as 0.
A share under 1% reads "<1%" and one just under the whole reads ">99%" (with percentDigits, the thresholds move by the same number of places).
Many tiny parts can need more than the bar's width at their minimum; the excess is clipped by the rounded track.
Palette slots follow the segment's position before zeros are hidden, so hiding a zero part never repaints the others. Pin color when a filter can remove parts.
A total smaller than the sum is ignored.
Status mode needs a tone on every segment; a partial set of tones is ignored.

name: MonarchStageJourney
title: StageJourney
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.horizontalScroll Row of drawn stages with androidx.compose.foundation.relocation.BringIntoViewRequester, a Column card with MonarchBadge and MonarchButton in a FlowRow, android.text.format.DateUtils.getRelativeTimeSpanString; MonarchStageHistory as a Column timeline
summary: Where an item is in its pipeline and what can happen next: a strip of stages grouped by phase, a card for the current stage with how long it has been there, and buttons for the moves the product allows; with MonarchStageHistory for the record of past moves.
whenToUse: On the detail screen of an item that moves through a fixed pipeline (an application, a deal, a hire, a claim) where people need to see where it is and move it on.
whenNotToUse: For steps the person completes in a form use MonarchStepper. For a free-form record of activity use MonarchActivityTimeline. For a single status use MonarchStatusBadge.
api: @Composable fun MonarchStageJourney(stages: List<MonarchStageJourneyStage>, currentId: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, terminal: MonarchStageJourneyTerminal? = null, enteredAt: Long? = null, currentMeta: String? = null, variant: MonarchStageJourneyVariant = MonarchStageJourneyVariant.Full, transitions: List<MonarchStageJourneyTransition> = emptyList(), now: Long? = null, labels: MonarchStageJourneyLabels = MonarchStageJourneyLabels(), onTransition: (suspend (MonarchStageJourneyTransition) -> Unit)? = null, content: (@Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)? = null)
class MonarchStageJourneyStage(id: String, label: String, group: String? = null, description: String? = null)

class MonarchStageJourneyTransition(id: String, label: String, kind: MonarchStageJourneyTransitionKind = MonarchStageJourneyTransitionKind.Forward, needsInput: Boolean = false, enabled: Boolean = true)
enum class MonarchStageJourneyTransitionKind { Forward, Exit, Back }
enum class MonarchStageJourneyTerminal { Success, Closed }
enum class MonarchStageJourneyVariant { Full, Strip }

class MonarchStageJourneyLabels(stages: String? = null, now: ((String) -> String)? = null, since: ((String) -> String)? = null, done: String? = null, current: String? = null, success: String? = null, closed: String? = null, nextSteps: String? = null, moveTo: ((String) -> String)? = null, backTo: ((String) -> String)? = null, needsInput: String? = null, moved: ((String) -> String)? = null, failed: String? = null)

@Composable fun MonarchStageHistory(entries: List<MonarchStageHistoryEntry>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, now: Long? = null, emptyMessage: String? = null, labels: MonarchStageHistoryLabels = MonarchStageHistoryLabels())
class MonarchStageHistoryEntry(id: String, to: String, at: Long, from: String? = null, actor: String? = null, meta: String? = null, note: String? = null, backward: Boolean = false)
class MonarchStageHistoryLabels(started: ((String) -> String)? = null, to: String? = null, movedBack: String? = null, empty: String? = null)

options.name: stages
options.description: Every stage in pipeline order, each with an id, a label, an optional group (phase) and an optional description shown while it is current.

options.name: currentId
options.description: The id of the current stage. Stages before it are done. With an unknown id every stage is upcoming and no card is shown.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the journey.

options.name: terminal
options.description: The current stage ends the journey: Success (granted, won, hired) or Closed (withdrawn, lost).

options.name: enteredAt
options.description: When the item entered the current stage, in epoch milliseconds, shown as "since 3 days ago" and updated once a minute.

options.name: currentMeta
options.description: A short note shown as a neutral MonarchBadge next to the current stage.

options.name: variant
options.description: Full: strip, card and moves. Strip: the strip only.

options.name: transitions
options.description: The moves from the current stage: forward (the first is primary), exit (quiet) and one back ("Back to …").

options.name: now
options.description: A fixed reference time for enteredAt and the history, which also stops the minute updates.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: onTransition
options.description: Called with the chosen move; its button shows a spinner until it returns and a thrown error is shown in the card. The app then changes currentId. Without it no moves are shown.

options.name: content
options.description: Extra content at the end of the card, such as a checklist.

options.name: entries
options.description: MonarchStageHistory: the moves, newest or oldest first as the product prefers.

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: MonarchStageHistory: replaces "No stage moves yet.".

states.name: done
states.description: A stage before the current one: accent subtle fill, accent border and a check mark; read as "done".

states.name: current
states.description: The current stage: solid accent fill and semibold; read as "current stage" and selected.

states.name: upcoming
states.description: A stage after the current one: outlined with muted text.

states.name: success
states.description: The current stage ended the journey well: solid success stage with a check mark, success-tinted card; read as "Completed".

states.name: closed
states.description: The journey ended early: emphasis stage with a strong border and a check mark, subtle card; read as "Closed".

states.name: moving
states.description: The chosen move's button shows a spinner and the other moves are disabled.

states.name: failed
states.description: A thrown error is shown in the card in the strong danger color and announced.

appearance: Stages are pills: done on the accent subtle fill with the accent border, current in the solid accent (solid success or the emphasis fill when the journey ended), upcoming outlined in the default border with muted text. The card sits on the surface with a subtle border (success-tinted or subtle when the journey ended). History dots are the accent color (warning for a move back) on a line in the default border color.
platformNotes: The parity map named a horizontal stage strip and a timeline; both are here, the timeline as MonarchStageHistory, which the web exports from the same module (StageHistory). The strip scrolls sideways inside itself and starts scrolled to the current stage. The web's currentMeta and the history's actor, meta and note take any content; here they are strings (currentMeta is a badge); put richer content in the card's content slot. The web's DateInput is epoch milliseconds. Times use DateUtils.getRelativeTimeSpanString instead of the RelativeTime component, because the strip and the spoken entries need plain text and a fixed reference time. The web's undo glyph on the back move is not drawn: Monarch bundles no icons, and the words "Back to …" carry the meaning. The closed outcome uses a check mark like the other ended stages, where the web draws an x; the outcome is in the state description. The web's "Moving…" busy label is the button's built-in loading state. iOS builds the same component with the same name.
accessibility: The strip is a traversal group named "Stages"; each stage is one element read by its name, with "done", "current stage" or the outcome as its state description; the current stage is selected.
Done stages have a check mark as well as their color, so the state is not color alone.
The card's title ("Now: Examination") is a heading and is read with the outcome ("Now: Granted, Completed"); "Next steps" is a heading too.
A move button is read as "Move to Granted" or "Back to Filed", with ", asks for details" when needsInput is true; each has a 48dp touch target.
A change of current stage is announced ("Moved to Granted") through a polite live region that is always present; a failed move is shown in a polite live region.
Each history entry is one element read as the move in words ("Filed to Examination"), "(moved back)", the time, the actor, the facts and the note; the dots and the line are hidden.
Text wraps and scales with the font size setting; move buttons wrap onto new rows.
edgeCases: An unknown currentId shows every stage as upcoming and no card.
Stages without a group are shown without a phase name; a group name repeated later starts a new run.
Only the first back move is shown.
A disabled transition stays disabled; while a move runs the other moves are disabled and a second tap is ignored.
An empty history shows "No stage moves yet." or emptyMessage.
Long stage names do not wrap in the strip; the strip scrolls instead.
The history arrow points left in a right-to-left layout.

name: MonarchStatCard
title: StatCard
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.Surface (clickable with onClick) with androidx.compose.material3.Text, MonarchDeltaIndicator, androidx.compose.material3.TooltipBox and RichTooltip from an androidx.compose.material3.IconButton
summary: One KPI for a dashboard on a card: label, value, change against an earlier period, and an optional hint, help, trend line and drill-down, with loading, empty and error states.
whenToUse: On a dashboard or an overview screen, for a figure people check at a glance and may open for detail. Put several in a FlowRow or a LazyVerticalGrid for a KPI row.
whenNotToUse: For a number inside a row or another card without a surface of its own, use MonarchMetric (or the Plain variant). For a value with a target, use a progress or meter component.
api: @Composable fun MonarchStatCard(label: String, value: Double?, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, format: MonarchMetricFormat = MonarchMetricFormat.Number, compact: Boolean = false, locale: Locale? = null, unit: String? = null, change: MonarchMetricChange? = null, tone: MonarchTone = MonarchTone.Neutral, variant: MonarchStatCardVariant = MonarchStatCardVariant.Card, size: MonarchStatCardSize = MonarchStatCardSize.Md, highlighted: Boolean = false, loading: Boolean = false, caption: String? = null, hint: String? = null, help: String? = null, error: String? = null, onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null, onClick: (() -> Unit)? = null, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, helpIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, sparkline: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, visual: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchStatCardLabels = MonarchStatCardLabels(), interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)

@Composable fun MonarchStatCard(label: String, text: String?, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, spokenText: String? = null, unit: String? = null, change: MonarchMetricChange? = null, tone: MonarchTone = MonarchTone.Neutral, variant: MonarchStatCardVariant = MonarchStatCardVariant.Card, size: MonarchStatCardSize = MonarchStatCardSize.Md, highlighted: Boolean = false, loading: Boolean = false, caption: String? = null, hint: String? = null, help: String? = null, error: String? = null, onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null, onClick: (() -> Unit)? = null, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, helpIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, sparkline: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, visual: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchStatCardLabels = MonarchStatCardLabels(), interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)
enum class MonarchStatCardSize { Sm, Md, Lg }
enum class MonarchStatCardVariant { Card, Plain }
class MonarchStatCardLabels(empty: String? = null, loading: String? = null, help: ((label: String) -> String)? = null)

options.name: label
options.description: What the number measures, for example "Revenue".

options.name: value
options.description: The number, or null when there is none (shown as a dash read as "No data"). Not finite values count as missing.

options.name: text
options.description: Second overload: the value as written by the app, such as "₹12.4L"; spokenText gives what TalkBack reads instead.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the card.

options.name: format
options.description: Number, Percent (a ratio: 0.12 is 12%) or Currency(code), written by android.icu.text.NumberFormat.

options.name: compact
options.description: Writes 12K or €3.4M; TalkBack reads the full value.

options.name: locale
options.description: The locale to write in. null uses the first locale of the configuration.

options.name: unit
options.description: Written smaller and muted after the value, for example "ms". Hidden for a missing value.

options.name: change
options.description: The change against an earlier period, drawn by MonarchDeltaIndicator, from a ratio or from current and previous values, with a good direction.

options.name: tone
options.description: Colors the value for a threshold: Info, Success, Warning or Danger. Say it in hint too: color is not read.

options.name: variant
options.description: Card: surface, border and padding. Plain: none of them, for a figure inside another surface.

options.name: size
options.description: Sm for dense rows, Md, Lg for a hero figure.

options.name: highlighted
options.description: Draws the card in the accent fill and border, to single it out (the web's accent tone).

options.name: loading
options.description: Shows a placeholder for the value; TalkBack reads "Loading".

options.name: caption
options.description: The period, for example "vs last month". It becomes the change's comparison when the change has none, and is shown alone otherwise.

options.name: hint
options.description: A line under the value, for example "38 of 52 people".

options.name: help
options.description: How the metric is defined, in a RichTooltip from a help button next to the label.

options.name: error
options.description: Replaces the value, the change and the hint with this message.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: With error, adds Try again (MonarchInlineErrorRetry).

options.name: onClick
options.description: Makes the whole card a button that drills down into the metric.

options.name: icon
options.description: A decorative icon before the label, tinted muted.

options.name: helpIcon
options.description: The glyph of the help button. Monarch bundles no icons; without it the button shows "?".

options.name: sparkline
options.description: A decorative trend under the value, for example MonarchSparkline.

options.name: visual
options.description: A decorative picture or icon at the end of the card.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces "No data", "Loading" and "About {label}".

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the press, focus and hover interactions of a card with onClick.

states.name: ready
states.description: Label, value, change or caption, hint and sparkline.

states.name: empty
states.description: A missing value is a dash in the subtle text color, read as "No data"; the unit is hidden.

states.name: loading
states.description: A text-shaped MonarchSkeleton replaces the value; the change, hint and sparkline are hidden and TalkBack reads "Loading".

states.name: error
states.description: The message replaces the value, the change and the hint, in the danger color, or as MonarchInlineErrorRetry with Try again when onRetry is given.

states.name: drill-down
states.description: With onClick the whole card is a button with a ripple and a focus ring.

states.name: highlighted
states.description: The accent subtle fill and the accent border.

appearance: The card uses the surface fill, the default border and 12dp corners; highlighted uses the accent subtle fill and the accent border; plain has neither. The label is muted, the value is default text in tabular figures (the strong color of the tone when one is set, the subtle color for a dash), the unit, caption and hint are muted, and an error is in the danger strong color. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Built on MonarchMetricFormat and MonarchMetricChange, so formatting and change follow MonarchMetric. MonarchTone has no accent tone, so the web's accent tone is highlighted = true and uses the accent roles directly. The web's legacy delta, deltaDirection and deltaTone props are not offered: change covers them with a good direction. The web's href and linkComponent become onClick (components do not navigate). The web's help Popover is a Material 3 RichTooltip from an IconButton next to the label; Monarch bundles no icons, so the button shows "?" unless helpIcon is given. The web's description-list semantics have no Android equivalent: the card is one TalkBack element instead. The web's formatOptions are not offered; write the value with the text overload for custom formats. The web's StatCardGroup is a FlowRow or LazyVerticalGrid in the app. There is no iOS equivalent yet; the names follow the plan.
accessibility: The card is one TalkBack element: label, value, change with its comparison, caption and hint.
With onClick the card is a button with a 48dp touch target that TalkBack reads as one element.
The help button is a separate element named "About {label}" with a 48dp touch target; it opens a focusable tooltip.
A compact value is read in full; a missing value is read as "No data".
While loading, TalkBack reads the state "Loading" on the card.
An error without retry is exposed as an error; with onRetry, Try again is its own button.
The icon, the visual and the sparkline are hidden from TalkBack; tone is color only, so the hint must say it.
edgeCases: A long label wraps; the card grows in height at large font sizes.
NaN and infinite values show the dash.
An empty text in the text overload shows the dash.
A tapped help button does not open the drill-down.

name: MonarchStatusBadge
title: StatusBadge
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row, androidx.compose.material3.Text, androidx.compose.runtime.staticCompositionLocalOf
summary: A status shown as words in a tone, such as "Partial outage", looked up by key in a typed registry of statuses.
whenToUse: For the state of a record or a service that comes from data as a key: an incident, a ticket, a deployment. Define the product's statuses once in a MonarchStatusRegistry so every screen shows the same words and tone.
whenNotToUse: For free text or a count, use MonarchBadge. For a live state next to a name, such as online or recording, use MonarchStatusDot.
api: @Composable fun MonarchStatusBadge(status: String?, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchStatusBadgeVariant = MonarchStatusBadgeVariant.Subtle, size: MonarchStatusBadgeSize = MonarchStatusBadgeSize.Md, showIcon: Boolean = true, registry: MonarchStatusRegistry? = null, label: String? = null, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null)

@Composable fun MonarchStatusBadge(definition: MonarchStatusDefinition, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchStatusBadgeVariant = MonarchStatusBadgeVariant.Subtle, size: MonarchStatusBadgeSize = MonarchStatusBadgeSize.Md, showIcon: Boolean = true)
class MonarchStatusDefinition(label: String, tone: MonarchTone, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, description: String? = null)

class MonarchStatusRegistry(definitions: Map<String, MonarchStatusDefinition>) { fun resolve(key: String?): MonarchStatusDefinition?; fun merging(other: MonarchStatusRegistry): MonarchStatusRegistry; companion object { val Empty: MonarchStatusRegistry; fun <K : Enum<K>> of(definitions: Map<K, MonarchStatusDefinition>): MonarchStatusRegistry } }
val LocalMonarchStatusRegistry: ProvidableCompositionLocal<MonarchStatusRegistry>
enum class MonarchStatusBadgeVariant { Subtle, Outline, Solid, Dot }
enum class MonarchStatusBadgeSize { Sm, Md }

options.name: status
options.description: The key: built-in (operational, degraded, partial, down, maintenance, unknown, success, warning, danger, info, neutral) or from a registry. null is unknown.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the badge.

options.name: variant
options.description: Subtle, Outline, Solid or Dot.

options.name: size
options.description: Sm uses caption text, Md label text.

options.name: showIcon
options.description: false hides the icon (and the dot of the dot variant); the label still carries the meaning.

options.name: registry
options.description: Statuses for this badge only, looked up before LocalMonarchStatusRegistry and the built-in set.

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the label of the status, for example a translated string.

options.name: icon
options.description: Replaces the icon of the status; in the dot variant it replaces the dot. Hidden from TalkBack.

appearance: Subtle is the subtle background of the tone with its strong text; Outline has no fill, strong text and the border of the tone; Solid is the solid color of the tone with its on-solid text; Dot is default text after a dot in the solid color of the tone (the neutral tone uses the subtle text color). The pill has fully rounded corners. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web registry also accepts a custom #rrggbb color per status, passed through a contrast guard; here colors come only from the theme by role, so a status picks one of the five MonarchTone values. The web accent tone is not offered, because MonarchTone has no accent tone. The web built-in statuses each have a distinct glyph; Monarch for Android bundles no icons, so the built-in set has none and the app gives icons through MonarchStatusDefinition.icon or the icon parameter. StatusRegistryProvider is LocalMonarchStatusRegistry; nested registries are combined with merging. defineStatuses is MonarchStatusRegistry.of with an enumeration. The parity map lists badge and status-dot as the base; the badge draws its own pill and dot with the same color roles, because MonarchBadge has one text size and MonarchStatusDot reads its dot as part of its own element. iOS shares the name, the variants and the built-in set and uses SF Symbols for the built-in icons.
accessibility: The icon, the dot and the label are one TalkBack element read as the label; the icon and the dot are hidden.
The label is always shown, so the tone is never the only signal.
The badge has no click action and no touch target.
The label wraps at the largest font size instead of being cut off.
edgeCases: A key with no letters, such as "__", reads "Unknown".
The same key in the badge's registry and the provided one: the badge's registry wins.
Statuses of the same tone look alike apart from the label unless the app gives them distinct icons.

whenToUse: For the live state of an item in a list, a table or a header: a service that is running, a person who is online, a job that is deploying.
whenNotToUse: For a label with a filled background use MonarchBadge. For a message about a whole screen or section use MonarchBanner.
api: @Composable fun MonarchStatusDot(label: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, tone: MonarchTone = MonarchTone.Neutral, size: MonarchStatusDotSize = MonarchStatusDotSize.Sm, pulsing: Boolean = false, labelHidden: Boolean = false)
enum class MonarchStatusDotSize { Sm, Md }

options.name: label
options.description: The words for the status. Always required, so color is never the only signal.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the component.

options.name: tone
options.description: Neutral, Info, Success, Warning or Danger.

options.name: size
options.description: Sm: an 8dp dot with caption text. Md: a 10dp dot with label-sized text.

options.name: pulsing

states.name: default
states.description: A dot in the tone color and the label in the default text color.

states.name: pulsing
states.description: A ring of the dot color grows to 2.4 times the dot and fades, every 1.6 seconds. Not drawn when animations are off.

states.name: label hidden
states.description: Only the dot is drawn; TalkBack still reads the label.

appearance: The dot uses the solid color of the tone; the neutral dot uses the subtle text color. The label uses the default text color. The same roles are used in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web StatusDot also has an accent tone; MonarchTone has no accent, so Android offers five tones, as iOS does. The web hides the label with a visually hidden class; Android does not draw it and sets it as the content description. The parameter names follow Android: pulsing and labelHidden for the iOS isPulsing and isLabelHidden. The pulse fades with the alpha of the drawing, as the web animates opacity; no color role is dimmed. The label wraps instead of being ellipsized as on the web, so it is never cut at a large font size.
accessibility: The dot and the label are one TalkBack element, read as the label.
The dot and the pulse are decoration; the meaning is in the words.
With labelHidden the label is the content description of the element.
The pulse is not drawn when the user has turned animations off.
The dot and the text grow with the font size setting.
Not interactive, so it has no touch target.
edgeCases: A long label wraps beside the dot; the dot stays centered on the text.
With labelHidden the sighted user sees only a color: add a visible legend nearby.
The pulse ring is drawn outside the bounds of the dot and is not clipped; leave room around a pulsing dot.

summary: A recipe, not a component: a status page as an in-app screen, with the overall state, each service's state and history, the active incident's updates and a subscribe field.
whenToUse: In an app's help or settings area, to show whether the product works now and what is being done about an incident.
whenNotToUse: For one service's history, use MonarchUptimeBar. For an incident's updates alone, use MonarchIncidentTimeline. For a public status website, use the web component.
api: MonarchCalloutBanner(message = …, tone = MonarchTone.Warning, title = "Partial degradation")
MonarchStatusBadge(definition = MonarchStatusDefinition(label = "Operational", tone = MonarchTone.Success))
MonarchUptimeBar(segments = history, startLabel = "30 days ago", endLabel = "Today", size = MonarchUptimeBarSize.Sm)
MonarchIncidentTimeline(updates = …, live = true)
MonarchTextField(value = email, onValueChange = { … }, label = "Email") and MonarchButton(text = "Subscribe", onClick = { … })

options.name: overall
options.description: The overall state from the app's server: the callout's tone, title and message.

options.name: services
options.type: List of name, MonarchStatusDefinition and List<MonarchUptimeBarSegment>
options.description: Each service with its current state and daily history, oldest first.

options.name: updates
options.description: The active incident's updates; leave the section out when there is none.

options.name: onSubscribe
options.description: The app's call to subscribe an email to updates; leave the section out without one.

states.name: all operational
states.description: A success callout, every service Operational, no incident section.

states.name: degraded or down
states.description: A warning or danger callout, the affected services' badges, and the incident's updates in a live timeline.

states.name: subscribed
states.description: The app replaces the field with a confirmation line.

appearance: Every part is an existing Monarch component: the toned callout, toned status badges with their labels, uptime bars in their status colors with a text summary, and the incident timeline. Section titles use the heading style. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web's StatusPageView is one component with a header, stats, grouped services, maintenance, active and past incidents, a legend and a subscribe form, laid out for a wide page. On Android it is a recipe for one scrolling screen: the overall callout first, then services one per row with a compact uptime bar under each, then the active incident and subscribe. Stats, maintenance windows and past incidents are further sections the app adds with the same components (past incidents in a MonarchCollapsible). iOS has the same plan: a recipe.
accessibility: Section titles use the heading style, which MonarchText marks as a heading.
Each service's state is a status badge with its label in words, never color alone; each uptime bar has a spoken summary.
The incident timeline is live, so new updates are announced.
edgeCases: With many services, group them under headings or in collapsibles.
Times in the timeline follow the time zone the app passes.
A day without checks is a segment without uptime: the bar shows no data.

summary: A menu button that shows and changes the workflow status of an issue, task or ticket, with the team's own statuses grouped under five fixed categories, each with its own glyph and name.
whenToUse: In issue rows, cards and detail screens where the status can be changed. Use MonarchStatusGlyph with the status name where the status is shown but not changed.
whenNotToUse: For a read-only status with a tone, use MonarchStatusBadge. For urgency, use MonarchPriorityPicker. For the steps of a form, use MonarchStepper.

enum class MonarchStatusCategory { Backlog, Unstarted, Started, Completed, Cancelled; val isClosed: Boolean }
class MonarchStatusOption(id: String, name: String, category: MonarchStatusCategory)
enum class MonarchStatusPickerSize { Sm, Md }

class MonarchStatusPickerLabels(trigger: ((String) -> String)? = null, none: String? = null, backlog: String? = null, unstarted: String? = null, started: String? = null, completed: String? = null, cancelled: String? = null)

options.name: statuses
options.description: The statuses to choose from. The menu groups them by category, in category order, and keeps their order within a group.

options.name: value
options.description: The id of the current status; null or an id not in statuses shows No status.

options.name: onValueChange
options.description: Called with the id of the chosen status. Choosing the current status only closes the menu.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the trigger.

options.name: size
options.description: Sm for a dense row or a card, Md for a form. The touch target is 48dp at both sizes.

options.name: showLabel
options.description: Shows the status's name next to its glyph. false gives a glyph-only icon button, still named.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the menu can be opened.

options.name: trailingIcon
options.description: A decorative icon after the name, such as a down chevron. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for "Status: %s", "No status" and the five category headings.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the trigger's press and focus interactions.

options.name: category
options.description: MonarchStatusGlyph: the category whose glyph is drawn, 14dp by default.

states.name: categories
states.description: Backlog: a dashed ring in the subtle text color. Not started: a ring in the muted text color. In progress: a ring with its end half filled in the strong warning color. Completed: a disc with a check mark in the strong success color. Cancelled: a disc with a cross in the subtle text color.

states.name: menu open
states.description: A Material 3 dropdown menu with a heading per category that has statuses, divided by lines; each status shows its category glyph and name, and the current one is selected and has a radio button.

states.name: no status
states.description: The trigger shows the backlog glyph and "No status"; no menu item is selected.

states.name: glyph only
states.description: An icon button with the glyph; the name stays in what TalkBack reads.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The button's disabled colors; the menu does not open.

appearance: The trigger is a secondary MonarchButton with the category glyph and the status name. Glyphs use the subtle text color for backlog and cancelled, the muted text color for not started, the strong warning color for in progress and the strong success color for completed; the check mark and cross are cut out in the surface color. Menu headings are muted caption text. High contrast themes use their stronger roles.
platformNotes: Built like MonarchPriorityPicker: a Material 3 menu takes any composable as an item's icon, so the web's glyphs are drawn on a Canvas from its 14-unit grid instead of an icon set, which Monarch does not bundle. That is why Android builds a type where iOS documents the system menu Picker with SF Symbols and ships none. The web's DropdownMenuLabel group headings are muted caption headings inside the menu, with a divider between groups, because Material 3 menus have no section API. The web's StatusGlyph is MonarchStatusGlyph, STATUS_CATEGORIES is the order of MonarchStatusCategory, and StatusOption is MonarchStatusOption. The web's sm and md sizes map to the MonarchButton sizes. The half fill of the in-progress glyph does not mirror right to left, as on the web.
accessibility: The trigger has the drop-down list role and is read as "Status: In progress".
In the menu each category heading has the heading role, and each status is read by name; the current one has the selected state and a radio button.
The glyphs are hidden from TalkBack; each category has its own shape and each status its own name, so the status never depends on color alone.
The trigger has a touch target of at least 48dp at both sizes, with or without the name.
The name scales with the font size setting without being cut.
edgeCases: A category with no statuses gets no heading.
A value that is not in statuses reads and looks like null: No status.
Long status names wrap in the trigger; the menu wraps them as any Material 3 menu item.
An empty statuses list opens an empty menu; disable the picker instead.

name: MonarchStepUpAuthDialog
title: StepUpAuthDialog
wrapsNative: Content for MonarchBottomSheet: MonarchPasswordInput, MonarchOtpPinInput, androidx.compose.material3.SecondaryScrollableTabRow, MonarchButton and MonarchInlineNotice; androidx.biometric.BiometricPrompt and Credential Manager run by the app through callbacks
summary: Asks a signed-in person to confirm it is still them, with their password, an authenticator code, a passkey or the device's biometrics or screen lock, before a high-risk action.
whenToUse: Before a high-risk action in a signed-in session, such as deleting a workspace, revoking keys or changing the sign-in email, when the server asks for a recent confirmation.
whenNotToUse: To sign in, use the SignInForm recipe. For a confirmation without re-authentication, use a MonarchDialog with a Danger MonarchButton (ConfirmDialog).
api: @Composable fun MonarchStepUpAuthDialog(onVerify: suspend (MonarchStepUpCredential) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, title: String? = null, description: String? = null, methods: List<MonarchStepUpMethod> = listOf(MonarchStepUpMethod.Password), errorMessage: ((Throwable) -> String?)? = null, onRequestBiometric: (suspend () -> Boolean)? = null, onForgot: (() -> Unit)? = null, onCancel: (() -> Unit)? = null, onVerified: (() -> Unit)? = null, onVerifyingChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchStepUpAuthDialogLabels = MonarchStepUpAuthDialogLabels())
enum class MonarchStepUpMethod { Password, Code, Passkey, DeviceOwner }

sealed interface MonarchStepUpCredential { val method: MonarchStepUpMethod; data class Password(val password: String); data class Code(val code: String); data object Passkey; data object DeviceOwner }

class MonarchStepUpAuthDialogLabels(title: String? = null, description: String? = null, methodPicker: String? = null, methodName: ((MonarchStepUpMethod) -> String)? = null, passwordLabel: String? = null, passwordRequired: String? = null, codeLabel: String? = null, codeHelper: String? = null, codeIncomplete: String? = null, passkeyDescription: String? = null, passkeyButton: String? = null, deviceOwnerDescription: String? = null, deviceOwnerButton: String? = null, submit: String? = null, cancel: String? = null, forgot: String? = null, genericError: String? = null)

options.name: onVerify
options.description: Checks the credential with the server. Return when accepted; throw to show the failure. For Passkey run the Credential Manager assertion here. For DeviceOwner the system check has already passed.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the dialog content; give it the sheet's padding.

options.name: title
options.description: Replaces the title "Confirm it’s you".

options.name: description
options.description: Why the person is asked, such as "Deleting a workspace needs your password.". Pass the same text as the BiometricPrompt subtitle.

options.name: methods
options.description: The methods offered, most preferred first. Repeats are dropped; empty means the password; DeviceOwner is offered only with onRequestBiometric. With more than one, tabs switch between them.

options.name: errorMessage
options.description: Turns a thrown error into a message. Without it, or when it returns null, "That did not work. Try again." is shown.

options.name: onRequestBiometric
options.description: Shows BiometricPrompt (the app owns it: it needs androidx.biometric and a FragmentActivity) and returns true when it passed, false when cancelled.

options.name: onForgot
options.description: Starts password recovery. Shows a Forgot your password? ghost button under the password field.

options.name: onCancel
options.description: Shows Cancel, which calls this. Close the sheet in it.

options.name: onVerified
options.description: Called after onVerify succeeds. Close the sheet and run the protected action here.

options.name: onVerifyingChange
options.description: Called with true when a check starts and false when it ends; pass it to the sheet's dismissible so it cannot be swiped away meanwhile.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including the method names and button titles.

states.name: password
states.description: MonarchPasswordInput with show and hide and the current-password autofill purpose; Forgot your password? when onForgot is given. Done on the keyboard submits.

states.name: code
states.description: MonarchOtpPinInput with 6 digit cells in two groups of three; the code submits itself when complete and is cleared after a failure.

states.name: passkey
states.description: A line of text and a Use passkey primary button.

states.name: device owner
states.description: A line of text and a Use screen lock primary button that calls onRequestBiometric, then onVerify when it passed.

states.name: missing entry
states.description: Confirm with an empty password or fewer than 6 digits shows "Enter your password." or "Enter all 6 digits." on the field, announced, without calling onVerify.

states.name: verifying
states.description: The primary button shows its progress indicator; the fields, tabs, Forgot and Cancel are disabled; onVerifyingChange(true) lets the app lock the sheet.

states.name: failed
states.description: The message is shown on the password or code field, or in a danger MonarchInlineNotice for passkey and device owner, and announced. A cancellation shows nothing.

appearance: The title in the heading style, the description in the body style in the muted text color, then the method tabs, the field and full-width primary and ghost buttons, on the sheet's surface. All colors are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: Same names as iOS. The web dialog is the content of a sheet: the app presents it in a MonarchBottomSheet and closes it in onVerified and onCancel, the Android form of the iOS sheet that dismisses itself. iOS's async throws onVerify is a suspend function. iOS runs LocalAuthentication itself; Android's BiometricPrompt needs androidx.biometric, which Monarch does not depend on, and a FragmentActivity, so the app runs it in onRequestBiometric, and the device method is left out without it. For the same reason the passkey sheet is the app's Credential Manager call inside onVerify. The device button reads Use screen lock instead of naming Face ID or Touch ID, because BiometricPrompt chooses the sensor. The web's totp method is called Code; forgotHref is onForgot, because leaving a sheet is the app's navigation. The method picker is a scrollable tab row rather than a segmented control, so the names stay readable at large font sizes.
accessibility: The title has the heading semantics.

The password and code fields are MonarchPasswordInput and MonarchOtpPinInput, so their labels, the show-password toggle, the one-time-code and password autofill types and the field errors come from those components.
Missing entries and failures are written in words and announced through a polite live region on an always-present node.
The method picker is a Material 3 tab row named "Verification method", with the selected state and 48dp tabs.
The primary button names what happens (Confirm, Use passkey, Use screen lock); every button is a MonarchButton with a 48dp target and the primary one reads its loading state while verifying.
With onVerifyingChange wired to the sheet's dismissible the sheet cannot be dismissed while verifying, so an announcement is not lost.
edgeCases: Each presentation starts clean on the first method, because the sheet's content is created anew; the password and code are never saved in the instance state.
Changing the method clears the errors.
Only digits are kept in the code, at most 6.
A cancelled or failed BiometricPrompt leaves the dialog open with no error.
Credential.Password never prints the password in toString.

name: MonarchStepper

wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row and Column of drawn step markers, androidx.compose.foundation.layout.BoxWithConstraints with androidx.compose.ui.text.TextMeasurer for the automatic compact form, Modifier.clickable for reached steps, MonarchProgress (androidx.compose.material3.LinearProgressIndicator) in the compact form
summary: Multi-step progress for wizards, onboarding and setup flows: a row or a column of numbered steps, or a compact "Step 2 of 5" with a progress bar.
whenToUse: At the top of a multi-step flow (horizontal, which becomes compact on a phone) or beside it on a wide screen (vertical). Pass onSelect to let people go back to steps they have reached.
whenNotToUse: Not for the progress of a task that runs by itself; use MonarchProgress. Not for sections the user can visit in any order; use Material 3 tabs (PrimaryTabRow). Not for changing a number; that is a different control.
api: @Composable fun MonarchStepper(steps: List<MonarchStepperStep>, current: Int, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, furthest: Int? = null, orientation: MonarchStepperOrientation = MonarchStepperOrientation.Horizontal, compact: MonarchStepperCompactMode = MonarchStepperCompactMode.Automatic, onSelect: ((step: MonarchStepperStep, index: Int) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchStepperLabels = MonarchStepperLabels(), finished: Boolean = false, busy: Boolean = false)

@Composable fun MonarchStepper(steps: List<MonarchStepperStep>, currentId: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, furthestId: String? = null, orientation: MonarchStepperOrientation = MonarchStepperOrientation.Horizontal, compact: MonarchStepperCompactMode = MonarchStepperCompactMode.Automatic, onSelect: ((step: MonarchStepperStep, index: Int) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchStepperLabels = MonarchStepperLabels(), finished: Boolean = false, busy: Boolean = false)
class MonarchStepperStep(id: String, label: String, description: String? = null, optional: Boolean = false, complete: Boolean = false, error: Boolean = false, enabled: Boolean = true)
enum class MonarchStepperOrientation { Horizontal, Vertical }
enum class MonarchStepperCompactMode { Automatic, Always, Never }

class MonarchStepperLabels(progress: String? = null, stepOf: ((step: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, complete: String? = null, error: String? = null, current: String? = null, optional: String? = null, busy: String? = null)

options.name: steps
options.description: The steps, in order. Each has an id, a label, and optionally a description and the flags optional, complete, error and enabled. No steps draws nothing.

options.name: current / currentId
options.description: The current step, by position from 0 or by identifier. Steps before it are complete. A position outside the steps is moved inside; an unknown identifier selects the first step.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the stepper.

options.name: furthest / furthestId
options.description: The furthest step the user has reached, when they have gone back. Steps up to it stay selectable. By default, and when it is before the current step, the current step.

options.name: orientation
options.description: Horizontal or Vertical.

options.name: compact
options.description: Automatic shows the compact form when the steps of a horizontal stepper do not fit the width with each name on one line; Always and Never fix the form.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Makes reached steps (complete ones and any up to furthest, except the current and disabled ones) buttons. Receives the step and its position.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings: "Progress", "Step 2 of 5", "completed", "needs attention", "current step" and "Optional".

options.name: finished
options.description: Every step is done: all markers show the check mark (an error keeps its mark), no step is current, and the compact summary reads the last step as completed with a full bar.

options.name: busy
options.description: The current step is working: its marker shows a progress ring in place of its number (still when animations are off) and TalkBack adds "in progress" (labels.busy). Ignored when finished.

states.name: complete
states.description: A filled accent marker with a check mark; the line after it is in the accent color.

states.name: current
states.description: An accent-bordered marker with the number and a tinted ring; the name is semibold.

states.name: upcoming
states.description: A bordered marker with the number; the name is muted.

states.name: error
states.description: A danger-tinted marker with an exclamation mark; the name is in the danger color. Takes precedence over every other state.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With onSelect, a step whose enabled is false is not a button, is marked disabled for TalkBack and its name is in the disabled text color.

states.name: pressed
states.description: A selectable step shows the Material ripple, clipped to the medium corner radius, while pressed.

states.name: compact
states.description: "Step 2 of 5", the name of the current step and a progress bar filled up to the current step.

appearance: Markers are circles 28dp across, grown with the font scale. The accent roles color the current and finished steps, the danger roles a step with an error, the strong border and muted text an upcoming step, on the surface background. The lines between steps use the default border color, or the accent solid color after a finished step. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Material 3 has no stepper, so the component is drawn by Monarch. The web switches to the compact form below a width of 36rem; Android, like iOS, measures the names on one line with a TextMeasurer and shows the compact form when the row does not fit the width, which also covers large font scales. The web step status override ('complete' or 'error') is the two flags complete and error; the iOS isOptional, isComplete, hasError and isDisabled are optional, complete, error and enabled, following the Kotlin convention of adjectives without 'is'. currentID and furthestID on iOS are currentId and furthestId. The web step label is any node; here it is a String. Hover underlining does not exist; the Material ripple is the pressed state. MonarchTone has no accent tone, so the accent color roles are used directly. The check mark and the exclamation mark are drawn with Canvas from the web's SVG paths, because Monarch bundles no icon set and the meaning must not depend on an app-supplied icon. Each step carries no interactionSource parameter, because there is one per step.
accessibility: The list of steps has the content description "Progress" (labels.progress), is a traversal group and carries collection info with one entry per step.

Each step is one TalkBack element. Its content description is the position, the name and the description ("Step 2 of 4, Team, Invite people"); its state description is the state ("completed", "needs attention" or "current step") followed by "Optional" for an optional step.
A selectable step has the Button role and a click action, and reserves at least 48dp by 48dp in the layout. The current step, upcoming steps not reached and disabled steps have no click action.
A disabled step in a selectable stepper is marked disabled.
State is shown by a check mark, an exclamation mark or the number, and by the weight of the name, not by color alone. Markers and lines are hidden from TalkBack.
The compact form is one element named "Progress" whose state description is the position and name of the current step; the bar is not read separately.
Names and descriptions wrap at font scale 2.0 and the markers grow with the font scale. Color changes animate with the theme motion and are immediate when animations are removed.
A selectable step draws the Monarch focus ring when focused from a keyboard or D-pad.
edgeCases: No steps draws nothing.
A horizontal stepper with compact Never squeezes the names of many steps into narrow columns, where they wrap; prefer Automatic on a phone.
With Automatic, a long description makes the row too wide and the compact form is shown.
A vertical stepper is never compact unless compact is Always.
furthest before current is ignored: the current step counts as reached.
In an unbounded width (inside a horizontal scroll) the row is never compact and the steps take their natural width.
Step identifiers should be unique; the identifier overload uses the first match.

title: Sticky
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyListScope.stickyHeader, androidx.compose.material3.Scaffold (topBar, bottomBar)
summary: Headers that stay at the top while their section scrolls are LazyColumn's stickyHeader, and bars fixed to an edge are the topBar and bottomBar of a Scaffold. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: stickyHeader for group headers of a long list (letters of a contact list, days of an activity feed). Scaffold's topBar and bottomBar for a filter bar or an action bar that is always at the top or bottom; pass the Scaffold's content padding to the list so nothing is hidden behind them.
whenNotToUse: Do not pin more than one header at a time, and do not pin content in a short screen that does not scroll. For a top app bar that collapses on scroll use TopAppBar with a TopAppBarScrollBehavior.
api: fun LazyListScope.stickyHeader(key: Any? = null, contentType: Any? = null, content: @Composable LazyItemScope.(Int) -> Unit)

@Composable fun Scaffold(modifier: Modifier = Modifier, topBar: @Composable () -> Unit = {}, bottomBar: @Composable () -> Unit = {}, snackbarHost: @Composable () -> Unit = {}, floatingActionButton: @Composable () -> Unit = {}, ..., content: @Composable (PaddingValues) -> Unit)
val LazyListState.firstVisibleItemIndex: Int
val LazyListState.firstVisibleItemScrollOffset: Int

states.name: stuck
states.description: Read from the list state: derivedStateOf { state.firstVisibleItemIndex > 0 || state.firstVisibleItemScrollOffset > 0 } is true once content scrolls under the header; use it to add a divider or a shadow.

appearance: A sticky header needs an opaque background (the surface color) so rows do not show through it. A bar in a Scaffold uses the Material 3 colors mapped from the Monarch theme.
platformNotes: The web Sticky pins any element to the top or bottom with an offset, adds a shadow when stuck (elevateWhenStuck) and reports it (onStuckChange). On Android the two cases are separate APIs: stickyHeader for headers of a lazy list, and the Scaffold's bars for content fixed to an edge. There is no stuck callback; the stuck state is derived from LazyListState, and a top app bar's scroll behavior already changes its color when content scrolls under it. The web's offset is the window insets, which Scaffold applies. iOS uses pinnedViews and safeAreaInset.
accessibility: System behavior: a sticky header is read once, in its place in the list order, not again while it is pinned.
Mark a sticky header as a heading so TalkBack's heading navigation jumps between groups.
Bars in a Scaffold are read before (topBar) or after (bottomBar) the content.
edgeCases: A sticky header with a transparent background lets rows show through it.
Forgetting the Scaffold's content padding puts the first and last rows behind the bars.

name: MonarchSubscriptionsTable

summary: A list of recurring agreements: name and plan, customer, status, price per billing period, the monthly figure and the next renewal, each amount in its own currency.
whenToUse: To show a customer's or a workspace's subscriptions, contracts or licenses, with their status and next renewal, on a phone or a tablet.
whenNotToUse: For upcoming renewals with owners and actions, use MonarchRenewalsPanel. For what unused items cost, use MonarchSavingsPanel. It does not sort, filter or add up; do that in the app.

object MonarchSubscriptionsTableDefaults { @Composable fun statuses(): MonarchStatusRegistry }

class MonarchSubscription(id: String, name: String, status: String, amount: BigDecimal?, currencyCode: String, plan: String? = null, quantity: Int = 1, customer: String? = null, interval: MonarchSubscriptionInterval? = MonarchSubscriptionInterval.Month, intervalCount: Int = 1, monthly: MonarchSubscriptionMonthly? = null, renewalDateMillis: Long? = null, renewsAutomatically: Boolean = true, cancelsAtMillis: Long? = null, changesAtMillis: Long? = null)
enum class MonarchSubscriptionInterval { Day, Week, Month, Year }
sealed interface MonarchSubscriptionMonthly { class Amount(amount: BigDecimal, currencyCode: String); data object NotConverted }

class MonarchSubscriptionsTableLabels(caption: String? = null, subscription: String? = null, customer: String? = null, status: String? = null, price: String? = null, monthly: String? = null, renewal: String? = null, customPrice: String? = null, quantity: ((Int) -> String)? = null, interval: ((MonarchSubscriptionInterval?, Int) -> String)? = null, priceSuffix: ((String) -> String)? = null, spokenPrice: ((String, String) -> String)? = null, spokenOneTimePrice: ((String) -> String)? = null, cancels: ((String) -> String)? = null, changes: ((String) -> String)? = null, renews: ((String) -> String)? = null, ends: ((String) -> String)? = null, evergreen: String? = null, notConverted: String? = null, notConvertedHint: String? = null, noValue: String? = null, emptyTitle: String? = null, emptyMessage: String? = null)

options.name: subscriptions
options.description: The rows, in display order. Empty shows the empty state.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the table.

options.name: registry
options.description: More statuses, or replacements for the built-in draft, trial, active, past_due, paused, cancelled and expired.

options.name: locale
options.description: The locale of amounts and dates. null uses the first locale of the configuration.

options.name: showCustomer
options.description: Shows the customer. Turn it off on a single customer's screen.

options.name: showMonthly
options.description: Shows the monthly figure; null shows it when any subscription has one.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Makes each row a button called with its subscription, for example to open it. Replaces the web href and renderLink.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including the period words and the spoken price.

states.name: compact
states.description: Below 640dp each row has the name, the plan line and customer · renewal at the start, and the status badge, the price with its period and the monthly figure at the end.

states.name: wide
states.description: From 640dp the rows are a table with Subscription, Customer, Status, Price, Monthly and Renewal columns under muted headings.

states.name: selectable
states.description: With onSelect each row is a button at least 48dp tall with a focus ring.

states.name: not converted
states.description: A live (active or past due) subscription whose monthly figure could not be converted shows "Not converted"; TalkBack also reads the explanation.

states.name: evergreen
states.description: No renewal date shows "Evergreen"; a subscription that does not renew shows "Ends …".

states.name: empty
states.description: No subscriptions: a small MonarchEmptyState, "No subscriptions".

appearance: Rows on the surrounding surface separated by subtle dividers, names in the default text color and secondary lines in the muted color; each status badge carries its tone and its words. The same in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web SubscriptionsTable is an HTML table with container queries and links. On Android it is a Column of rows at compact width and a table with weighted columns from 640dp, rather than a LazyColumn, so it can sit inside the screen's verticalScroll with other content; this matches iOS. Links (href, renderLink) become onSelect, which the app uses for navigation. Amounts are BigDecimal in major units; minorUnits is not offered. Dates are epoch milliseconds (UTC) written with android.icu.text.DateFormat; there is no timeZone parameter. The relative-time dependency of the plan is not used: renewal dates are absolute, as on the web. The caption is the table's spoken name only (labels.caption), and the not-converted hint, a hover title on the web, is read by TalkBack. The default statuses are MonarchSubscriptionsTableDefaults.statuses(), with localised labels. iOS ships the same MonarchSubscriptionsTable.
accessibility: Each row is one TalkBack element read in words: name, plan line, customer, status, price "per month", monthly figure and renewal.
The table is a traversal group named "Subscriptions" with collection info; each row carries its row index.
With onSelect each row has the button role, a 48dp minimum height and a focus ring.
The column headings of the wide table and the empty-cell dashes are hidden from TalkBack.
Status is always written in words in its badge, not only by color.
Text wraps at font scale 2.0; right to left, the name and the price mirror.
edgeCases: Amounts are never converted or added; each stays in its own currency.
A quantity of 1 is not written; 3 is written "3 ×" before the plan.
Every 3 months is written "quarter".
A missing price or monthly figure is a dash read as "No value".
An unknown status key is shown in the neutral tone with a label made from the key ("on_hold" gives "On hold").

title: SupportPanel
wrapsNative: MonarchBottomSheet with MonarchTabs and Tab; MonarchMessageRow and MonarchMessageComposer for chat; MonarchSearchResults, MonarchLink and MonarchBadge for help, contacts and status
summary: A recipe, not a component: help and support in a bottom sheet, with a Chat tab (the support conversation and a composer) and a Help tab (articles, other ways to reach the team and the system status).
whenToUse: An app offers in-app support chat, help articles or contact options from a Help entry in its navigation or settings.
whenNotToUse: For a full help center, open it as its own screen or a Custom Tab. For a single contact link, use MonarchLink in place.

@OptIn(ExperimentalMonarchApi::class) MonarchMessageRow(author = MonarchMessageRowAuthor("Support"), time = …, timeStyle = MonarchMessageRowTimeStyle.Clock) { MonarchText(…) }
@OptIn(ExperimentalMonarchApi::class) MonarchMessageComposer(label = "Message", state = rememberTextFieldState(), onSend = { message -> … })
MonarchSearchResults(groups = articles, onSelect = { result, _ -> … }, modifier = Modifier.heightIn(max = …))
MonarchLink(text = "Email support@example.com", onClick = …, variant = MonarchLinkVariant.Standalone)
MonarchBadge(text = "All systems normal", tone = MonarchTone.Success); MonarchLink(text = "System status", onClick = …, external = true)

options.description: The conversation from the app's support chat client; leave the Chat tab out when there is none.

options.name: articles
options.description: Popular or matching help articles, opened in the help center.

options.name: contacts
options.description: Other ways to reach support: email, phone, a contact form.

options.name: status
options.description: The current system status as text with a tone, and a link to the status page.

states.name: chat
states.description: The conversation and the composer; sent messages appear as rows.

states.name: connecting or offline
states.description: The app shows a MonarchInlineNotice above the conversation, such as The team is away. Leave a message and they will reply here.

states.name: help
states.description: Help articles, contact links and the system status.

states.name: closed
states.description: Swiping the sheet down, tapping the scrim or system back closes it, from MonarchBottomSheet.

appearance: A Material 3 bottom sheet on the surface color with a heading, a primary tab row in the accent color, message rows, an outlined composer, result rows, links in the link color and a success badge for the status. Every part is an existing component, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web ships SupportPanel: a side sheet beside the navigation rail with Chat and Help tabs, a built-in client for its Support Chat API (connecting, offline, time-outs, resend) and links that open in new tabs. On a phone it is a bottom sheet, and the parts already exist as Monarch components, so Android keeps it a recipe. The app owns the chat connection and its states (it shows them with MonarchInlineNotice and the message rows' Pending and Failed statuses) because Monarch adds no networking. Links call back: the app opens email with an ACTION_SENDTO intent and web pages in a Custom Tab; there is no target="_blank" and no script-scheme check because no URL is loaded by Monarch. MonarchMessageRow and MonarchMessageComposer are experimental, so the recipe opts in where it uses them.
accessibility: MonarchBottomSheet moves TalkBack focus into the sheet and closes on system back, a swipe down or a tap on the scrim.
The tabs are Material 3 Tabs with the Tab role and the selected state.
Message rows read the author, time and text together, from MonarchMessageRow; the composer is a labelled text field with a Send button, from MonarchMessageComposer.
The system status is text with a tone (All systems normal), never a coloured dot alone.
Links are 48dp targets and say when they open outside the app, from MonarchLink with external.
edgeCases: Keep the sheet's content short enough to fit; the article list scrolls inside a bounded height.
Without a chat client, show only the Help content and no tabs.
While the team is away, keep the composer and say when they will reply.
