whenToUse: For settings that take effect at once and must reach a server, such as notification or privacy settings.
whenNotToUse: For a switch whose value is kept on the device or submitted with a form use MonarchSwitchRow. For a choice saved with a Save button use MonarchCheckboxRow in a form with MonarchFormActionsBar.

@Composable public fun MonarchSwitchSettingsRow(checked: Boolean, onCheckedChange: (Boolean) -> Unit, onSave: suspend (Boolean) -> Unit, label: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, description: String? = null, labels: MonarchSwitchSettingsListLabels? = null, onStatusChange: ((MonarchSwitchSettingsStatus) -> Unit)? = null)
public enum class MonarchSwitchSettingsStatus { Idle, Saving, Saved, Error }

public class MonarchSwitchSettingsListLabels(saving: String? = null, saved: String? = null, error: String? = null, retry: String? = null, retryLabel: ((String) -> String)? = null, errorMessage: ((Throwable) -> String?)? = null)
public object MonarchSwitchSettingsListDefaults { public const val SavedDurationMillis: Long }

options.name: modifier
options.description: List: the modifier of the list.

options.name: title
options.description: List: the heading of the group, a heading for TalkBack.

options.name: description
options.description: List: a sentence under the heading.

options.name: labels
options.description: List: replacements for "Saving", "Saved", "Couldn't save.", "Retry", the spoken retry name and the error message, for every row.

options.name: savedDurationMillis
options.description: List: how long "Saved" stays after a save.

options.name: content
options.description: List: the rows.

options.name: checked
options.description: Row: the saved value.

options.name: onCheckedChange
options.description: Row: called with the new value after onSave returned; update the saved value here.

options.name: onSave
options.description: Row: saves the new value. Throwing rolls the switch back and shows the error with Retry. Cancelled when the row leaves the composition.

options.name: label
options.description: Row: the name of the setting; labels the switch.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Row: whether the user can toggle the row and retry.

options.name: description (row)
options.description: Row: what the setting does, under the label and part of the row's TalkBack text.

options.name: labels (row)
options.description: Row: replacements for this row; null properties keep the list's.

options.name: onStatusChange
options.description: Row: called when the save status changes, for example to disable a Done button while saving.

states.name: idle
states.description: The switch shows the saved value; no status line.

states.name: saving
states.description: The switch already shows the new value; a small spinner named "Saving" and "Saving" in the muted color. Further toggles are ignored.

states.name: saved
states.description: "Saved" in the strong success color for savedDurationMillis, announced.

states.name: error
states.description: The switch returns to the saved value; "Couldn't save." with the reason in the strong danger color and a Retry button that saves the failed value again. Announced, and set as the error of the row. Toggling the row again also saves again.

states.name: disabled
states.description: enabled = false: the row cannot be toggled; label and description take the disabled text color.

appearance: The switch is the Material 3 Switch in the MonarchTheme colors. Status text uses the caption type: muted for saving, strong success for saved, strong danger for an error; the description of the list is muted. The same roles apply in every theme.
platformNotes: The web has SwitchSettingsList and SwitchSettingsItem; Android, as iOS, names the row MonarchSwitchSettingsRow so it can also stand outside the list. The web's onCheckedChange returns a promise; Android splits it into onSave, a suspend function that throws on failure, and onCheckedChange, which receives the value after the save. A save that returns at once still shows "Saved", as on iOS. The web's headingLevel has no Android equivalent (the title is a heading) and the uncontrolled defaultChecked is replaced by the hoisted checked value. The status line sits under the row so it can wrap at large text sizes. The parity map names ListItem rows and lists inline-error-retry: the rows use the same toggleable row as MonarchSwitchRow instead of ListItem, so the whole row is one target, and the error is drawn with a MonarchButton because MonarchInlineErrorRetry cannot give its retry button a per-row TalkBack name and is a live region of its own, which would announce the error twice.
accessibility: Each row is one toggleable TalkBack element with the switch role, read with its label, description and on or off state.
While a save has failed, the error is set as the error of the row, so TalkBack reads it with the switch.
"Saved" and the error are announced through an always-present polite live region per row; "Saving" is not announced, and the spinner is one element named "Saving".
The retry button is a MonarchButton with a 48dp touch target named "Retry" and the row label ("Retry Weekly summary").
Status is written in words, so saved and failed do not depend on color.
The list title is a heading.
edgeCases: An exception without a message shows only "Couldn't save."; pass labels.errorMessage to turn exceptions into text, or return null to show none.
A save that is still running when the row leaves the composition is cancelled, and onCheckedChange is not called.
A new save restarts the "Saved" timer, so a late timer never clears the status of a newer save.
Long labels and descriptions wrap; the error and Retry wrap onto two lines when they do not fit.

name: MonarchTableBlock
title: TableBlock
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.ui.layout.Layout inside androidx.compose.foundation.horizontalScroll; androidx.compose.foundation.text.BasicTextField per editable cell; androidx.compose.material3.DropdownMenu for the controls
summary: A small table of text inside a document: a read-only form that scrolls sideways, and an editable form with a text field per cell and a menu to add and delete rows and columns.
whenToUse: For a short table of text in an article, a note or a document editor: prices, a comparison, a schedule.
whenNotToUse: For a large or sortable data set use a data grid or a lazy list. For a list of key and value pairs use a description list.
api: @Composable fun MonarchTableBlock(data: MonarchTableBlockData, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, caption: String? = null, label: String? = null, labels: MonarchTableBlockLabels = MonarchTableBlockLabels())

@Composable fun MonarchTableBlock(data: MonarchTableBlockData, onDataChange: (MonarchTableBlockData) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, caption: String? = null, label: String? = null, enabled: Boolean = true, labels: MonarchTableBlockLabels = MonarchTableBlockLabels(), onDelete: (() -> Unit)? = null)

class MonarchTableBlockData { val rows: List<List<String>>; val hasHeaderRow: Boolean; val rowCount: Int; val columnCount: Int; val canAddRow: Boolean; val canAddColumn: Boolean; val canDeleteRow: Boolean; val canDeleteColumn: Boolean; operator fun get(row: Int, column: Int): String; fun isHeader(row: Int): Boolean; fun withCell(row: Int, column: Int, text: String): MonarchTableBlockData; fun withHeaderRow(hasHeaderRow: Boolean): MonarchTableBlockData; fun addRow(after: Int): MonarchTableBlockData; fun addColumn(after: Int): MonarchTableBlockData; fun deleteRow(at: Int): MonarchTableBlockData; fun deleteColumn(at: Int): MonarchTableBlockData }

MonarchTableBlockData.Companion: const val MAXIMUM_ROW_COUNT = 50, const val MAXIMUM_COLUMN_COUNT = 20, fun of(rows: List<List<String>>, hasHeaderRow: Boolean = true): MonarchTableBlockData, fun empty(rowCount: Int = 3, columnCount: Int = 3, hasHeaderRow: Boolean = true): MonarchTableBlockData

class MonarchTableBlockLabels(region: String? = null, controls: String? = null, addRow: String? = null, addColumn: String? = null, deleteRow: String? = null, deleteColumn: String? = null, headerRow: String? = null, deleteTable: String? = null, emptyCell: String? = null, cellPosition: ((row: Int, column: Int) -> String)? = null)

options.name: data
options.description: The cells and whether the first row is a header.

options.name: onDataChange
options.description: Editable overload: called with the new table after every change.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the block.

options.name: caption
options.description: Text above the table. Also its spoken name.

options.name: label
options.description: The spoken name of the table when the caption is not the right one.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Editable overload: whether the cells and the menu respond.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings (strings_tableblock.xml).

options.name: onDelete
options.description: Editable overload: adds "Delete table" to the menu. The app removes the table.

states.name: read-only
states.description: Cells are text. Columns are 96dp to 240dp wide at the default font size and the text wraps inside them.

states.name: editable
states.description: Every cell is a text field in a 144dp column, at least 48dp high, and a "Table" button above the table opens the menu.

states.name: header row
states.description: The first row has the subtle background, the strong body style and the heading semantics. Switched in the menu or with withHeaderRow.

states.name: at a limit
states.description: Add row is disabled at 50 rows, add column at 20 columns, delete row and delete column at one.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Editable overload with enabled = false: the text uses the disabled color and the fields and the button do not respond.

appearance: The table has a 1dp border in the default border color with 8dp corners and 1dp lines between cells. Body cells sit on the surface color, header cells on the subtle background; the caption uses the caption style in muted text. Each role has its own value in the dark and high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web component is a scrolling frame for an HTML table and a Tiptap node built on prosemirror-tables. Android has no block editor, so, as on iOS, the editable form is a self-contained composable over a MonarchTableBlockData value that a block editor can host later; the data type has the web's commands (add row below, add column after, delete row and column, header row) and limits (50 by 20). Not offered: selection across several cells, merged cells (colspan and rowspan), rich text inside a cell, and Tab to move between cells (the keyboard's own Next and focus navigation apply). The web shows the controls only while the caret is in the table; here the "Table" button is always above an editable table and acts on the cell that last had focus, or on the last row and column. The data is an immutable value with onDataChange, where iOS takes a Binding. Column widths grow with the font size setting, up to twice.
accessibility: The scrolling frame is a traversal group named by label, else the caption, else "Table"; a caption that is the spoken name is hidden from TalkBack so it is not read twice.
The grid carries collection info (rows and columns) and every cell its row and column, so TalkBack can announce the position.
A read-only cell is read as its text, or "Empty".
Header cells are headings and use the strong body style, so the header does not depend on its fill.
An editable cell is a text field whose content description is its position, "Row 2, column 1".
The controls are a MonarchButton and a Material 3 DropdownMenu; the header row item has the checkbox role and its state; "Delete table" is in the danger text color.
Editable cells are at least 48dp high, the button has a 48dp target, and text grows with the font size setting.
edgeCases: Ragged rows are padded with empty cells; an empty input becomes one empty cell; rows past 50 and columns past 20 are dropped.
Reading a cell outside the table gives an empty string; changing one returns the same value.
After a row or column is added, its cell at the target takes focus; after a delete, the nearest cell does.
At the largest font size the columns are wider and the table scrolls sooner.
The grid is not lazy: it is meant for small tables, which the limits enforce.

name: MonarchTableOfContents
title: TableOfContents
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of entries made with androidx.compose.foundation.clickable and androidx.compose.material3.Text; rememberMonarchTableOfContentsSpy reads androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyListState.layoutInfo in derivedStateOf
summary: In-page navigation built from the page's headings: a list of entries that marks the section being read and asks the app to scroll to the one chosen, with a scroll spy for a LazyColumn.
whenToUse: On long reading screens with several headed sections, such as documentation, policies or reports, usually in a bottom sheet opened from the top app bar on a phone and beside the content on a large screen.
whenNotToUse: For moving between separate screens, use navigation (a bar, a rail or tabs). For a short page that fits on one or two screens, leave it out.
api: @Composable fun MonarchTableOfContents(items: List<MonarchTableOfContentsItem>, selectedId: String?, onSelect: (id: String) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, showTitle: Boolean = true, title: String? = null, currentLabel: String? = null)
class MonarchTableOfContentsItem(title: String, id: String, level: Int = 2)
@Composable fun rememberMonarchTableOfContentsSpy(state: LazyListState, sections: Map<String, Int>, topInset: Dp = MonarchTokens.Space.space0.dp): State<String?>

options.name: items
options.description: The entries in page order, each with a title, the id of its section and a heading level (2 by default).

options.name: selectedId
options.description: The id of the section being read, or null before the first heading. rememberMonarchTableOfContentsSpy keeps it in step with scrolling.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Scrolls to the chosen section, usually LazyListState.animateScrollToItem, and closes the sheet.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the list.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the entries can be chosen. When not, they use the disabled text color.

options.name: showTitle
options.description: Whether the title is shown. When hidden it still names the list for TalkBack.

options.name: title
options.description: Replaces the built-in title "On this page".

options.name: currentLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Current section", read as the state of the current entry.

options.name: sections (spy)
options.description: The id of each section and the index of its heading item in the LazyColumn.

options.name: topInset (spy)
options.description: The height of anything covering the top of the list. A heading counts as scrolled past once it goes under it.

states.name: current
states.description: The entry's text is in the default color and a semibold weight, with an accent line beside it, and reads "Current section".

states.name: other
states.description: Muted text with a subtle line beside it.

states.name: nested
states.description: An entry with a deeper level is indented one step for each level below the shallowest entry.

states.name: no current section
states.description: With selectedId null, no entry is marked, as before the first heading reaches the top.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With enabled = false every entry uses the disabled text color and ignores taps.

appearance: Entries in the body style on whatever surface holds the list, each with a 2dp line at the start: the accent solid color beside the current entry and the subtle border color beside the others. The title is a label in the muted text color. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web TableOfContents reads h2 and h3 elements from the DOM, spies with IntersectionObserver and writes #id to the URL. Compose has no DOM, so the app passes the entries, and rememberMonarchTableOfContentsSpy reads the LazyColumn's layout with the same rule (the first heading in the top 40%, else the last scrolled past). There is no URL hash. The web's activeId and onActiveChange are selectedId and onSelect. The parity map named a LazyColumn for the list; a contents list is short and is usually placed in a sheet or a scrolling column, where a lazy list cannot be nested, so it is a Column. The web moves focus to the heading after scrolling; on Android TalkBack focus stays on the list, and the app can move it with a FocusRequester on the heading. iOS builds the same component with a view modifier spy.
accessibility: The list is one traversal group; the visible title is a heading, and when it is hidden it names the list.
Each entry is a clickable element with its title as the name and a touch target at least 48dp high across the full width.
The current entry reads the state "Current section" and is marked by an accent line and a heavier weight as well as by color.
Entries wrap instead of being cut at large font sizes.
The indent is a start padding, so nesting follows the reading direction right to left.
Each entry draws the Monarch focus ring when it has keyboard focus.
edgeCases: An empty list shows only the title.
A selectedId that matches no entry marks none.
Entries with levels 2 and 4 and nothing at 3 indent the level 4 entries two steps.
The spy returns null until the first heading reaches the top 40% of the list.
When the last section is too short to reach the top, the spy keeps the section scrolled past before it; the app may mark the chosen section itself after onSelect.

name: MonarchTableToolbar
title: TableToolbar
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.ui.layout.Layout, androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow, androidx.compose.foundation.horizontalScroll, MonarchBulkActionBar
summary: The bar above a table or list: a search field, filters, the result count and the app's controls (view switcher, column menu, actions); while rows are selected the search and filters give way to the bulk selection bar.
whenToUse: Above a table, a data grid or a long list that people search, filter, switch between views or select from, such as a list of contacts or invoices.
whenNotToUse: For a screen-wide title and actions, use the top app bar. For actions on selected items without search or filters, use MonarchBulkActionBar on its own.
api: @Composable fun MonarchTableToolbar(modifier: Modifier = Modifier, resultCount: Int? = null, selectedCount: Int = 0, totalCount: Int? = null, bulkActions: List<MonarchBulkAction> = emptyList(), onClearSelection: (() -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchTableToolbarLabels = MonarchTableToolbarLabels(), search: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, filters: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, controls: @Composable () -> Unit = {})
class MonarchTableToolbarLabels(toolbar: String? = null, results: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, bulkActionBar: MonarchBulkActionBarLabels = MonarchBulkActionBarLabels())

options.name: resultCount
options.description: Rows that match the search and filters, shown as "N results" in the locale's digits and announced when it changes. null hides the count.

options.name: selectedCount
options.description: Selected rows. While it is above 0 and onClearSelection is set, MonarchBulkActionBar replaces the search and the filters.

options.name: totalCount
options.description: Rows that could be selected, for "3 of 120 selected".

options.name: bulkActions
options.description: Actions on the selected rows, shown in the bulk selection bar.

options.name: onClearSelection
options.description: Empties the selection. Without it there is no bulk selection bar.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the TalkBack name of the toolbar, the result count text and the strings of the bulk bar.

options.name: search
options.description: A search field, such as MonarchSearchBar, first in the start part. Hidden while rows are selected.

options.name: filters
options.description: Filter controls, such as MonarchChips, in a row that scrolls sideways when it does not fit. Hidden while rows are selected.

options.name: controls
options.description: The trailing controls: a SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow as the view switcher, a Columns MonarchMenu and actions. They wrap onto more lines when they do not fit.

states.name: narrow
states.description: Below 640dp, or when the count and controls need more than half the width: the search and filters (or the bulk bar) take the first line and the count and controls the next, aligned to the end.

states.name: wide
states.description: From 640dp, when the count and the controls take at most half the width: the start part and the end part share one line, vertically centered.

states.name: selecting
states.description: With onClearSelection and a selection, MonarchBulkActionBar with the count, the bulk actions and Clear selection replaces the search and filters; the count and the controls stay.

states.name: no count
states.description: Without resultCount only the controls are in the end part.

appearance: No surface of its own: the controls sit on the screen's background. The result count is caption text in the muted text role; the bulk bar is MonarchBulkActionBar's raised surface. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web toolbar draws its own SearchInput, ViewSwitcher and ColumnMenu from props. On Android these are slots: the app passes MonarchSearchBar, a MonarchSegmentedControl and a Columns MonarchMenu (the view-switcher and column-menu recipes), so their state stays in the app. iOS has no search slot because search belongs to the navigation bar there (searchable); an Android screen has no such place, so search is a slot here. The web's sm and md sizes are not offered: the slotted controls keep their own sizes. The web's bulkChildren and returnFocusRef are not offered; focus after Clear selection follows TalkBack. The web keeps an uncontrolled search mounted while selecting; here search state is hoisted in the app, so the hidden field loses nothing. The layout decision (one line or two) is made from the measured width, not from the window size class, so the toolbar adapts inside panes.
accessibility: The toolbar is a traversal group named "Table controls", so TalkBack reads its controls together.
The result count is a polite live region: a new count is read without moving focus.
While rows are selected the bulk bar announces the count and "Selection cleared" when it empties, through MonarchBulkActionBar.
The controls wrap and the count text wraps at the largest font scale; nothing is cut.
The slotted Material 3 controls keep their own roles and 48dp touch targets.
edgeCases: A selectedCount above 0 without onClearSelection keeps the search and filters: there is no bulk bar to clear it.
Many filters scroll sideways in one line rather than pushing the controls down.
Inside a pane narrower than 640dp the toolbar uses two lines even on a large screen.
The count uses plurals in strings_tabletoolbar.xml with the number formatted for the locale; pass labels.results to write it differently.

name: MonarchTabs
title: Tabs
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.selection.selectable, androidx.compose.foundation.horizontalScroll
summary: Line tabs with an accent underline under the selected tab, counts, and a row that scrolls when the labels do not fit.
whenToUse: To switch between views of related content in the same place: the sections of a record, filtered lists with counts.
whenNotToUse: For the top-level destinations of an app use a NavigationBar or NavigationRail (see top-nav). For two to four short, equal views use MonarchSegmentedControl. For choices that filter without changing the view use a chip.
api: @Composable fun MonarchTabs(selectedIndex: Int, onSelectedIndexChange: (Int) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, panel: (@Composable (selectedIndex: Int) -> Unit)? = null, tabs: MonarchTabsScope.() -> Unit)

interface MonarchTabsScope { fun tab(text: String, enabled: Boolean = true, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, count: String? = null, countTone: MonarchTone = MonarchTone.Neutral, contentDescription: String? = null) }

options.name: selectedIndex

appearance: The label is 14sp medium: default color when selected, muted otherwise. The selected tab has a 2dp underline in the strong accent role with round top corners over a 1dp divider in the default border role. In the high-contrast themes the same roles resolve to stronger colors.
platformNotes: Built from its own layers, not the Material 3 tab rows. A tab is 36dp high with 12dp of touch area above it, so the 48dp target is met and the underline stays against the divider. The web's pill variant is the segmented control; the web's link tabs are navigation and are not offered.
accessibility: Each tab has the tab role, the selected state and its position (2 of 4); the label and the count are read together.
Each tab is at least 48dp high and wide.
A disabled tab is announced as disabled and does not respond.
The selection is marked by the underline and the text color, and announced as selected.
With a keyboard or D-pad the arrow keys move between tabs; Enter or Space chooses one.
The order of the tabs follows the layout direction.
edgeCases: A tab never wraps its label: the row scrolls instead, also at the largest font size.
A count is read as part of the name unless contentDescription is set; keep it a number.

name: MonarchTabularNumberStyle
title: TabularNumber
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.ui.text.TextStyle(fontFeatureSettings = "tnum") with java.text.NumberFormat, drawn by androidx.compose.material3.Text
summary: Fixed-width digits for text, so that columns of figures line up and changing values do not jitter: a text style, and MonarchTabularNumber, which formats a number in the user's locale or shows a dash when there is none.
whenToUse: For figures in tables and lists, totals, counters and timers. Use MonarchTabularNumber(value) for a number that may be missing, MonarchTabularNumber(text) for text that is already formatted, and MonarchTabularNumberStyle.applyTo or spanStyle inside other text.
whenNotToUse: For money with its currency use a currency NumberFormat as format, or the app's money formatting; for a number inside a sentence that is not compared with others, plain MonarchText is enough.
api: object MonarchTabularNumberStyle { const val FONT_FEATURE_SETTINGS: String = "tnum"; fun applyTo(style: TextStyle): TextStyle; fun spanStyle(): SpanStyle }

@Composable fun MonarchTabularNumber(value: Number?, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, style: MonarchTextStyle = MonarchTextStyle.Body, format: NumberFormat? = null, color: Color = Color.Unspecified, textAlign: TextAlign? = null, emptyText: String? = null, emptyLabel: String? = null)
@Composable fun MonarchTabularNumber(text: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, style: MonarchTextStyle = MonarchTextStyle.Body, color: Color = Color.Unspecified, textAlign: TextAlign? = null)

options.name: value
options.description: The number, or null when there is none. A Double or Float that is NaN or infinite counts as missing.

options.name: text
options.description: In the second overload, text that is already formatted.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the component.

options.name: style
options.description: The type role.

options.name: format
options.description: How the number is written: a number, percent or currency instance with its options. null is NumberFormat.getNumberInstance in the locale of the current configuration.

options.name: color
options.description: Unspecified uses the content color of the surrounding surface.

options.name: textAlign
options.description: Align columns of figures to the end.

options.name: emptyText
options.description: Shown in place of a missing number. Built in: an em dash (monarch_tabularnumber_empty).

options.name: emptyLabel
options.description: Read by TalkBack in place of a missing number. Built in: "No value" (monarch_tabularnumber_empty_label).

states.name: value
states.description: The formatted number in fixed-width digits.

states.name: missing
states.description: The value is null, NaN or infinite: an em dash is shown and TalkBack reads "No value".

appearance: The type role and color of the surrounding text; only the digits change to fixed width. Follows light, dark and both high-contrast themes like any MonarchText.
platformNotes: The web TabularNumber formats with Intl.NumberFormat; Android takes a java.text.NumberFormat, so every option of the platform (percent, currency, fraction digits, grouping) is available and nothing is re-implemented. The parity map named MonarchTypography; it has no tabular style, so Monarch ships MonarchTabularNumberStyle (the iOS name) and the MonarchTabularNumber composable in the same folder. The web never breaks a line inside a number; on Android a number that does not fit wraps, and maxLines is the app's choice through a plain Text with applyTo.
accessibility: A formatted number is read by TalkBack as its text.
A missing value is read as "No value" (or emptyLabel), not as a dash.
The text is in a type role in sp and grows with the font size setting.
Number formatting follows the locale of the configuration, including digits, grouping and decimal separators.
edgeCases: NaN and infinity are shown as missing, like null.
Only digits get one width. Separators, signs and currency symbols keep their own widths, so align columns to the end.
A custom font family without tabular digits is not changed by the style.
applyTo replaces other font feature settings of the style, because Compose holds them in one string.
A NumberFormat is mutable and not thread-safe; create it once with remember and do not share it across threads.

name: MonarchTag
title: Tag
wrapsNative: Modifier.selectable, Modifier.clickable
summary: A chip for user data: a read-only label, a label the user can remove, or a filter the user can switch on and off.
whenToUse: For labels people add to a record, recipients, and filters above a list.
whenNotToUse: For a status the system sets, such as Draft or Paid, use MonarchBadge. For one choice among several use radio buttons or a segmented control.
api: @Composable fun MonarchTag(text: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, tone: MonarchTone = MonarchTone.Neutral, size: MonarchTagSize = MonarchTagSize.Md, leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null)

@Composable fun MonarchTag(text: String, selected: Boolean, onSelectedChange: (Boolean) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, size: MonarchTagSize = MonarchTagSize.Md, enabled: Boolean = true, leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, selectedIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)
enum class MonarchTagSize { Sm, Md }

@Composable fun MonarchChip(text: String, selected: Boolean, onSelectedChange: (Boolean) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, size: MonarchTagSize = MonarchTagSize.Md, enabled: Boolean = true, leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, selectedIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)

@Composable fun MonarchChip(text: String, onRemove: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, tone: MonarchTone = MonarchTone.Neutral, size: MonarchTagSize = MonarchTagSize.Md, enabled: Boolean = true, leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, removeIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, removeLabel: String? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)

options.name: text
options.description: The label.

options.name: onRemove
options.description: Called when the user activates a removable tag. Remove the tag from your data here.

options.name: removeIcon
options.description: The close mark after the text. Decorative; Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: selected
options.description: Whether a selectable tag is on.

options.name: onSelectedChange
options.description: Called with the new state when the user toggles the tag.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the tag.

options.name: tone
options.description: Color role of a read-only or removable tag: Neutral, Info, Success, Warning or Danger.

options.name: size
options.description: Sm uses caption text, Md label text. A read-only tag is 24dp or 28dp high; an interactive one is a 32dp chip with a 48dp touch target.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the user can remove or toggle the tag.

options.name: leadingIcon
options.description: A decorative icon before the text.

options.name: selectedIcon
options.description: Shown in place of leadingIcon while selected, for example a check mark.

options.name: removeLabel
options.description: The TalkBack name of a removable tag. null uses monarch_tag_remove, "Remove" and the text.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the press, focus and hover interactions.

states.name: read-only
states.description: A tinted label with no action, read as its text.

states.name: removable
states.description: A Material 3 AssistChip with a trailing close mark; the whole chip removes the tag.

states.name: selected
states.description: Accent fill, accent text and an accent border; selectedIcon replaces the leading icon.

states.name: not selected
states.description: Surface fill, default text and the default border.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Muted fill and muted text; the chip does not respond.

appearance: A read-only or removable tag takes the subtle background, strong text and border of its tone; the neutral tag uses the muted background with default text. A selectable tag is the surface color with the default border when off and the accent subtle background, accent strong text and solid accent border when on. Corners are 8dp in every theme.
platformNotes: Planned as a style entry (MonarchTheme over the Material 3 chips); built as a MonarchTag wrapper instead, because the tones, the sizes, the read-only form and the spoken remove name cannot come from the theme alone. iOS also builds MonarchTag. A removable tag follows Material 3 input chips: the whole chip is the remove action (built on AssistChip, because InputChip is selectable and TalkBack would read it as an unchecked checkbox), where the web and iOS have a separate remove button after the label. For the same reason a tag is either removable or selectable, not both. The selectable form has no tone, as on the web, where selectable tags ignore the tone. The web accent tone is not offered, because MonarchTone has none; a selected tag uses the accent. The web TagGroup (arrow-key movement and focus hand-over after a removal) is not offered. Monarch bundles no icons, so the close mark and the check mark are passed by the app. Interactive tags are 32dp, the Material 3 chip height, at both sizes. The selectable and removable forms are MonarchChip: drawn by Monarch (28dp, 8dp corners, no check icon, a drawn close mark when removeIcon is null) with a 48dp touch target, replacing FilterChip, InputChip and AssistChip. Migrating: FilterChip(selected, onClick, label = { Text(t) }) becomes MonarchChip(text = t, selected, onSelectedChange).
accessibility: A read-only tag is not actionable and is read as its text; its icon is hidden from TalkBack.
A removable tag is a button named "Remove" and the text; removeLabel replaces the name.
Delete or Backspace on a hardware keyboard removes a focused, enabled removable tag.
A selectable tag is a checkbox and reports selected or not selected, so the state does not depend on color.
Removable and selectable tags reserve a 48dp touch target and draw the Monarch focus ring around the visible chip.
The leading icon is before the text in both layout directions; text wraps at the largest font size.
edgeCases: Long text wraps inside the tag and the tag grows taller.
Read-only tags are 24dp or 28dp high and interactive ones reserve 48dp, so a row that mixes them has different heights.
A disabled tag keeps muted, not disabled, text, because the label is still information.
Without selectedIcon a selected tag differs from an unselected one by color only to sighted users; TalkBack still reports the state.

name: MonarchTagInput
title: TagInput
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow of MonarchTag (androidx.compose.material3.AssistChip) and androidx.compose.foundation.text.BasicTextField with ImeAction.Done, MonarchButton suggestions, and a polite liveRegion
summary: A field that edits a list of short values as removable tags, with validation, paste splitting and optional suggestions.
whenToUse: For a short list of free values: skills, labels, keywords, email recipients.
whenNotToUse: For a choice among known options use filter chips (MonarchTag with selected) or a multi-select. For one value use MonarchTextField.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchTagInput(tags: List<String>, onTagsChange: (List<String>) -> Unit, label: String, removeIcon: @Composable () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, readOnly: Boolean = false, placeholder: String? = null, helperText: String? = null, errorText: String? = null, suggestions: List<String> = emptyList(), separators: Set<Char> = setOf(','), maxCount: Int? = null, allowDuplicates: Boolean = false, normalize: ((String) -> String)? = null, validate: ((String, List<String>) -> String?)? = null, suggestionIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, errorIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchTagInputLabels = MonarchTagInputLabels(), interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)

public class MonarchTagInputLabels(duplicate: ((String) -> String)? = null, maximum: ((Int) -> String)? = null, added: ((String) -> String)? = null, removed: ((String) -> String)? = null, remove: ((String) -> String)? = null, addSuggestion: ((String) -> String)? = null)

options.name: tags
options.description: The tags, in order.

options.name: onTagsChange
options.description: Called with the new list when a tag is added or removed.

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label; also the TalkBack name of the text field.

options.name: removeIcon
options.description: The close mark of each tag. Monarch bundles no icons, so the app passes one; it is decorative.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the field.

options.name: enabled
options.description: false shows the tags without remove and disables the text field.

options.name: readOnly
options.description: Shows the tags without remove and without the text field.

options.name: placeholder
options.description: Text in the empty text field.

options.name: helperText
options.description: Help under the box, such as how values are separated.

options.name: errorText
options.description: An error from the app. A refused tag's message replaces it while shown. A blank string is no error.

options.name: suggestions
options.description: Values offered as buttons under the box while the typed text matches them (without case). Added values are left out; at most 8 show.

options.name: separators
options.description: Characters that add the typed text, besides Done. New lines and tabs also split a paste.

options.name: maxCount
options.description: The most tags. Further additions are refused with "You can add up to N."

options.name: allowDuplicates
options.description: Whether the same tag may appear twice. Duplicates are compared without case.

options.name: normalize
options.description: Cleans typed text before it is checked and added. Trims white space by default.

options.name: validate
options.description: Returns a message to refuse a tag, or null to accept it. Runs after the duplicate and maximum checks.

options.name: suggestionIcon
options.description: An icon before each suggestion, such as a plus.

options.name: errorIcon
options.description: An icon before the error message.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the duplicate and maximum messages, the announcements and the TalkBack names of the remove and suggestion buttons.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the focus interactions of the text field.

states.name: empty
states.description: Only the text field, with its placeholder.

states.name: with tags
states.description: Small neutral tags wrap before the text field and the box grows; each tag removes itself when activated.

states.name: focused
states.description: The border takes the focus ring color.

states.name: refused entry
states.description: The refused text stays in the field; the border and the message under the box take the strong danger color; the message is announced and clears when the user types.

states.name: error
states.description: The app's error, shown like a refusal while no tag is refused.

states.name: suggestions
states.description: Matching suggestions appear as ghost buttons under the box while text is typed.

states.name: read only
states.description: Tags without remove; no text field; a subtle fill.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Tags without remove, the text field disabled, the subtle fill and the disabled text color.

appearance: The box has the surface fill with the input border, the focus ring color while focused and the strong danger color with an error; disabled and read-only boxes use the subtle fill and the default border. Tags are MonarchTag in the neutral tone at the small size. The same roles apply in every theme.
platformNotes: The parity map names InputChip; the tags are MonarchTag, which is built on AssistChip because a selectable InputChip is read by TalkBack as an unchecked checkbox. The web's keyboard shortcuts (Backspace in the empty field to reach the last tag, arrow keys between tags) are not offered: every tag is a real button TalkBack reaches. Suggestions are buttons under the box instead of a combobox listbox. The web's sizes, addOnBlur and name for hidden form inputs are not offered. A paste is told apart from typing by the number of characters inserted at once, as on iOS. Monarch bundles no icons, so the close mark of the tags is a required slot. The typed text is kept by the field (rememberSaveable); the tags are hoisted.
accessibility: The text field is named by the label, and carries the refusal or the app's error as its error; the visible label and message are hidden from TalkBack so they are not read twice.
Each removable tag is one button named "Remove" and the tag, with a 48dp touch target, and can be renamed with labels.remove.
Additions ("Added Research."), removals ("Removed Research.") and refusals are announced through an always-present polite live region.
After a tag is removed or a suggestion added, focus returns to the text field.
Suggestion buttons are named "Add" and the suggestion and have 48dp touch targets; the text field is at least 48dp high.
Messages are text (with an optional icon), not color alone.
edgeCases: Pasting "a, b, c" adds three tags; parts that are refused stay in the field joined by commas.
Tags are compared without case for duplicates, so "research" is refused when "Research" is there.
A long tag takes a row of its own in the flow layout.
Tags are identified by position, so duplicate tags (with allowDuplicates) can each be removed.
Typing a separator in the middle of the text adds the part before it and keeps the part after it.

name: MonarchTeamCalendar
title: TeamCalendar
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn with LazyListScope.stickyHeader, androidx.compose.foundation.horizontalScroll with one shared ScrollState, androidx.compose.material3.TooltipBox with PlainTooltip, MonarchAvatar, MonarchEmptyState, MonarchBanner, MonarchSkeleton, android.icu.text.DateFormat
summary: Who is away when: people down the start, the days of a month or a custom range across, absences as bars that span their days, half days as half bars, pending entries outlined, weekends and holidays shaded and today ringed.
whenToUse: For a team's leave or availability overview, where a manager scans who is out on which day and taps an absence to open it or an empty day to add one. Put a MonarchCalendarToolbar above it to move between months.
whenNotToUse: For one person's events day by day use MonarchAgendaList. For choosing a date use MonarchMiniMonth or the Material 3 DatePicker. For meetings with times use an event list or a time grid; this grid has whole and half days only.

class MonarchTeamCalendarHoliday(date: Long, name: String)

class MonarchTeamCalendarLabels(person: String? = null, grid: ((String) -> String)? = null, today: String? = null, holiday: ((String) -> String)? = null, range: ((String, String) -> String)? = null, firstHalf: String? = null, secondHalf: String? = null, pending: String? = null, emptyTitle: String? = null, emptyDescription: String? = null, legend: String? = null, loading: String? = null)

options.name: members
options.description: The rows in display order, each with an id, a name, an optional photo Painter and an optional second line.

options.name: entries
options.description: The absences, each with a member id, a first and last day, a label, a color, a portion, per-day portions and pending. Days outside the range are left out.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the calendar. Give it a bounded height, as for any LazyColumn.

options.name: month
options.description: Any day of the month shown, as epoch milliseconds read in UTC. null is the month of today. Ignored when from and to are both set.

options.name: from
options.description: The first day of a custom range, used with to.

options.name: to
options.description: The last day of a custom range, inclusive. A day before from gives one day; at most 366 days are shown.

options.name: holidays
options.description: Non-working days for everyone: shaded, named in what TalkBack reads and in a tooltip on a long press of the day.

options.name: weekendDays
options.description: The shaded days of the week, Calendar.SUNDAY to Calendar.SATURDAY.

options.name: today
options.description: Today's date, ringed in the header and where the days start scrolled to. null is today on the device; pass a fixed value in tests and previews.

options.name: loading
options.description: Shows a skeleton placeholder, named "Loading team calendar", instead of the grid.

options.name: error
options.description: Shows this message in a danger MonarchBanner, announced politely, instead of the grid.

options.name: showLegend
options.description: Shows the line under the grid that explains shading, half bars and faded bars.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for "Person", the grid name, "Today", the holiday and range phrases, "first half", "second half", "pending", the empty state, the legend and the loading name.

options.name: onEntryClick
options.description: Called when a bar is tapped. Without it bars are read but are not buttons.

options.name: onCellClick
options.description: Called with the member and the day's UTC midnight when an empty day is tapped, for example to add time away. Without it empty days take no taps and are not TalkBack elements.

options.name: empty
options.description: Replaces the built-in empty state shown when there are no members.

states.name: bars
states.description: Consecutive full days of one entry are one bar with the label inside, a solid start stripe in the entry color and a light tint of it; a bar cut by the range has no rounded edge on that side.

states.name: half day
states.description: A half bar at the start (first half) or the end (second half) of the day, without a label; the whole day is still the target.

states.name: pending
states.description: An outlined bar with no fill, and "pending" in what TalkBack reads.

states.name: weekend and holiday
states.description: The day's column is shaded in the muted fill; a holiday's name is read with its day and shown in a tooltip on a long press.

states.name: today
states.description: The day number is bold in the strong accent inside an accent ring, "Today" is read with it, and the days start scrolled to the day before today.

states.name: loading
states.description: A skeleton block instead of the grid.

states.name: error
states.description: A danger banner with the message instead of the grid.

states.name: empty
states.description: MonarchEmptyState "Nobody to show" or the app's empty content when there are no members.

appearance: The grid sits on the surface color inside a default border with large corners; rows are separated by subtle dividers and the header by a default one. Weekend and holiday columns use the muted fill. Bars mix the entry color (the accent by default) into the surface color with a solid stripe at the start; labels keep the default text color, and day names the muted text color. High contrast themes use their stronger text, border and accent roles.
platformNotes: The web TeamCalendar is a table whose cells are squares per day, with the label in a hover title, and a roving tab stop moved with arrow, Home, End and Page keys. On a phone the people column stays fixed while the days scroll sideways in one shared scroll for every row, the day header stays pinned while rows scroll, and the grid opens at the day before today. Consecutive days of an entry are one spanning bar with its label inside, one TalkBack element and one target, so onEntryClick passes the entry and member but not the day (the web passes the day too). The label of a short bar and a holiday's name appear in a Material 3 tooltip on a long press instead of on hover. Pending entries are outlined instead of faded, because Monarch does not dim colors with alpha. Hardware keyboards move focus between the bars and the tappable empty days with Compose's own focus search, not the web's key map. Days are epoch milliseconds in UTC, as in DatePickerState; weekendDays use java.util.Calendar constants, and the locale comes from the configuration. error is a String, not a node. The web's accent color is used through the accent roles directly, because MonarchTone has no accent tone. Marked experimental as a domain composite until a Rook app adopts it. iOS has not built it yet; the planned iOS name is the same.
accessibility: The corner is a heading named for the grid, "Team calendar, November 2026" (or "Team calendar, Nov 2 – Nov 8, 2026" for a custom range).
Each person is one heading element, "Alex Kim, Design", so TalkBack's heading navigation moves from person to person.
Each day header is read as its full date, with "Today" before today's and "Holiday: name" after a holiday's.

Each bar is one element read as "Annual leave, Alex Kim, Monday, November 2 to Thursday, November 5", with "first half" or "second half" for a half day and "pending" for a pending entry; with onEntryClick it is a button.
With onCellClick each empty day is a button read as "Sam Lee, Wednesday, November 4"; without it empty days are not elements.
Days are 48dp wide and rows at least 48dp tall, so bars, half-day bars and empty days have 48dp targets reserved in the layout.
Half days, pending entries, today and holidays are said in words and drawn with shape (half bar, outline, ring), not only with color.
Names and descriptions wrap at the largest font size and the row grows to fit.
The error banner is a polite live region; the loading placeholder is named "Loading team calendar".
Right to left, the people column is at the right and earlier days are further right.
edgeCases: Give the calendar a bounded height; inside a vertically scrolling Column it needs Modifier.height.
One entry per person per day: when two entries cover the same day, the later one in entries is shown, as on the web.
An end before the start is treated as the start; an entry for an unknown member id is ignored.
A one-day or half-day bar has no visible label; it is read by TalkBack and shown in the tooltip.
Very long labels are cut with an ellipsis inside their bar; the full label is read and shown in the tooltip.
A custom range is capped at 366 days.
today defaults to the device's date at composition; pass a fixed value for previews and tests.
Bar colors are the app's: the fill is a tint of the color and the label keeps the default text color, so any color stays readable.

name: MonarchTemplatePicker
title: TemplatePicker

summary: A gallery of templates to start from, with category filters, search and an optional "start from scratch" card first.
whenToUse: When creating a document, project or board can start from one of many ready-made templates, usually on its own screen or in a full-height sheet.
whenNotToUse: For a handful of options with no previews or search, use MonarchRadioCardGroup. For AI prompt templates, use the AI prompt template picker when it exists.
api: @Composable fun MonarchTemplatePicker(label: String, templates: List<MonarchTemplatePickerItem>, selected: String?, onSelect: (String) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, categories: List<MonarchTemplatePickerCategory> = emptyList(), initialCategory: String? = null, query: String = "", onQueryChange: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, blank: MonarchTemplatePickerBlank? = null, enabled: Boolean = true, state: LazyGridState = rememberLazyGridState(), labels: MonarchTemplatePickerLabels = MonarchTemplatePickerLabels())

class MonarchTemplatePickerCategory(id: String, label: String)

class MonarchTemplatePickerLabels(categories: String? = null, allCategories: String? = null, blank: String? = null, search: String? = null, results: ((Int) -> String)? = null, noResults: ((String) -> String)? = null, emptyCategory: String? = null)

options.name: label
options.description: The name of the gallery, read by TalkBack. It is not shown; the screen's title usually says it.

options.name: templates
options.description: The templates in order, each with a name and an optional description, category, badge, keywords, preview slot and enabled flag.

options.name: selected
options.description: The id of the chosen template or of the blank card, or null for none yet.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Called with the id the person chose.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the gallery. Give it a bounded height: the grid scrolls on its own.

options.name: categories
options.description: Category filters, shown as a scrolling row of MonarchTag toggles with "All" first when given.

options.name: initialCategory
options.description: The category filter selected at first. All by default.

options.name: query
options.description: The search text. Every word must appear in the name, description or keywords.

options.name: onQueryChange
options.description: Shows a MonarchSearchBar at the top and is called as the person types. Leave it null when the screen has its own search field and passes query.

options.name: blank
options.description: A "start from scratch" card shown first whatever the filters; its name defaults to "Blank".

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether any card or filter can be used.

options.name: state
options.description: The scroll state of the grid.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the filter names, the blank name, the search placeholder, the announced count and the empty messages.

states.name: selected
states.description: The chosen card has the accent subtle fill, a heavier accent strong border and a filled radio mark.

states.name: pressed
states.description: The Material 3 surface shows its press ripple.

states.name: disabled template
states.description: Subtle fill with disabled text and an empty disabled mark; it cannot be chosen.

states.name: no results
states.description: A filtered MonarchEmptyState saying no templates match the search, with Clear filters, under the blank card.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With enabled false every card, filter and the search field are disabled.

appearance: Cards use the surface color with a default border and 12dp corners; the chosen card the accent subtle fill and a 2dp accent strong border, the same colors as MonarchRadioCardGroup. Previews sit on the subtle background with 8dp corners. Names use the strong body style, descriptions the caption style in the muted color. All are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: Like the web, the picker can show its own search field (MonarchSearchBar, when onQueryChange is given); like iOS, it can instead take the query from the screen's own search field. The category filter is kept by the picker (saved across configuration changes) and starts from initialCategory, as the web's defaultCategory; the selection is hoisted. The web's renderPreview pane is not offered: on a phone the app shows a preview after the choice, for example in the next step. Previews are a composable slot rather than free content. The web's arrow-key grid navigation is replaced by TalkBack and the system's directional focus moving through the cards. The parity map lists radio-card-group: the cards reuse its colors and radio mark, but are laid out in a lazy adaptive grid with previews and badges, which MonarchRadioCardGroup does not offer. When nothing matches, Clear filters resets the category and, when the picker owns the search field, the search.
accessibility: The grid is a traversal group named by label, and a selectable group.
Each card is one element with the radio button role, the selected state, the name, the badge and the description, and is at least 48dp high.
Selection is also shown by the radio mark and a heavier border, not by color alone.
Category filters are MonarchTag toggles in a group named "Categories".
When the category or the search changes, the number of templates shown is announced through a polite live region.
Previews are hidden from TalkBack.
Cards are at least 144dp wide times the font scale, so the largest font size shows one column.
edgeCases: The blank card is never hidden by the filters.
Search ignores case and accents and matches the words in any order.
A selected template hidden by a filter stays selected.
A category with no templates says "No templates in this category."
Template ids are list keys, so they must be unique and differ from the blank card's id.

name: MonarchTermsAcceptance
title: TermsAcceptance
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.Checkbox through MonarchCheckboxRow, with a MonarchLink per document in androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow; androidx.compose.ui.platform.LocalUriHandler opens the documents
summary: The required "I agree to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy" checkbox for sign-up, with a link to each document, reporting the versions that were accepted and when.
whenToUse: On a sign-up or checkout screen where the person must agree to legal documents before continuing, and the app keeps proof of which versions they agreed to.
whenNotToUse: For optional marketing messages, use MonarchMarketingConsentCheckbox. For privacy choices per category, use MonarchConsentPreferences. For a plain yes or no setting, use MonarchCheckboxRow.
api: @Composable fun MonarchTermsAcceptance(accepted: Boolean, onAcceptedChange: (Boolean, MonarchTermsAcceptanceDetails) -> Unit, documents: List<MonarchTermsDocument>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, required: Boolean = true, showRequiredError: Boolean = false, enabled: Boolean = true, onOpenDocument: ((MonarchTermsDocument) -> Unit)? = null, clock: () -> Long = { System.currentTimeMillis() }, labels: MonarchTermsAcceptanceLabels = MonarchTermsAcceptanceLabels())

class MonarchTermsDocument(title: String, url: String, version: String? = null, id: String? = null) { val key: String; companion object { fun versions(documents: List<MonarchTermsDocument>): Map<String, String> } }
class MonarchTermsAcceptanceDetails(versions: Map<String, String>, dateMillis: Long)
class MonarchTermsAcceptanceLabels(label: ((String) -> String)? = null, requiredMessage: String? = null, required: String? = null)

options.name: accepted
options.description: Whether the box is ticked. Start it false for sign-up so the agreement is an active choice.

options.name: onAcceptedChange
options.description: Called when the box changes, with the new state, the version of each document keyed by its key, and the time. Store the details with the account.

options.name: documents
options.description: The documents. Their titles are joined into the sentence and each is a link under it.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the group.

options.name: required
options.description: Whether the box must be ticked to continue. Shows "Required" under the sentence and allows the error.

options.name: showRequiredError
options.description: Shows "Accept the terms to continue" while the box is required and not ticked. Set it when the person tries to continue; the error clears once the box is ticked.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the box and the links can be used.

options.name: onOpenDocument
options.description: Opens a document, for example in an in-app screen. Without it the url opens with LocalUriHandler and the links read as opening in the browser.

options.name: clock
options.description: The current time in epoch milliseconds for the details. Replace it in tests.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the sentence (built from the joined titles), the error and the Required note.

states.name: unticked
states.description: The empty checkbox with the sentence, Required under it and the document links.

states.name: accepted
states.description: The checkbox is filled with a check mark.

states.name: invalid
states.description: With showRequiredError while unticked: "Accept the terms to continue" under the links in the danger strong color, set as the box's error and announced.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The box, the sentence and the links use the disabled text color and cannot be used.

appearance: The Material 3 checkbox in the Monarch accent, the sentence in the body style and Required in the caption style in the muted color, the links in the link color and underlined, and the error in the caption style in the danger strong color. All are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: On the web the document links sit inside the checkbox label. The parity map names a checkbox row with annotated links; on Android a LinkAnnotation inside the sentence would have a touch target the size of its words, far under 48dp, and would sit inside the row's toggle, so, as on iOS, the sentence is plain text and each document is a MonarchLink under it. There is no form submission, so the app sets showRequiredError when the person tries to continue instead of the web's native required attribute, and there are no name, value or versionsName form fields: the app stores the details from onAcceptedChange. The details carry the time as epoch milliseconds instead of the web's ISO string. The web's locale prop is the app's locale: the titles are joined with string resources ("A, B, and C") because android.icu.text.ListFormatter needs API 26 and minSdk is 24. The web's target option is onOpenDocument. Disabling also disables the links, as on iOS. A required box says "Required" in words, because TalkBack has no hint for it.
accessibility: The box is a MonarchCheckboxRow: one TalkBack element with the checkbox role, the sentence as its name and its checked state.
Required is written under the sentence, so it is read with the box and does not depend on color.
Each document is a separate MonarchLink with a 48dp touch target and an underline; links that open the browser say so.
While shown, the error is the box's error semantics and is announced once through a polite live region.
The sentence and the links wrap at the largest font size, and the links follow the layout direction.
edgeCases: One document gives "I agree to the Terms of Service"; three give "A, B, and C".
Documents without a version are left out of the reported versions.
Two documents with the same url need an explicit id, because the key of the versions is the id or the url.
The error never shows for an optional box or a ticked box.

title: TermsUpdateDialog
wrapsNative: MonarchBottomSheet with dismissible = false, holding MonarchText, MonarchLink and MonarchButton; the date formatted with android.icu.text.DateFormat
summary: A recipe, not a component: a bottom sheet that tells people the terms have changed, with a summary, the effective date and links to the documents, which in its blocking form cannot be dismissed until they accept or decline.
whenToUse: When updated terms or a privacy policy need the person's acceptance before they continue (blocking), or need to be shown once (a notice with a Later button).
whenNotToUse: For news about the product, use an announcement bar. For consent to cookies or tracking, use the cookie consent banner.

ModalBottomSheetProperties(shouldDismissOnBackPress: Boolean = true, shouldDismissOnClickOutside: Boolean = true)
android.icu.text.DateFormat.getDateInstance(style: Int): DateFormat

states.name: blocking
states.description: No swipe, back or tap outside closes it: dismissible = false. Only Accept or Decline closes it.

states.name: notice
states.description: The default sheet behavior with a Later button: it can be swiped away and is shown again later.

states.name: accepting
states.description: Pass loading to the Accept button while the acceptance is recorded; show a failure with MonarchInlineNotice in the sheet.

appearance: A Material 3 bottom sheet on the raised surface Monarch maps to it, with the heading, the summary in the default text color, the effective date in the muted text color, standalone links and full-width buttons: Accept primary, Decline ghost. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web TermsUpdateDialog is a component with mode, effectiveDate parsing, documents, version labels, and pending and error props. On Android it composes a MonarchBottomSheet: the date is epoch milliseconds formatted with android.icu.text.DateFormat in the person's locale (in UTC, so the day does not shift), the links open the documents through LocalUriHandler, and blocking turns off every way to dismiss the sheet. iOS uses the same recipe with interactiveDismissDisabled.
accessibility: The heading names the sheet; TalkBack moves into the sheet when it opens.
Each document is a link with a 48dp touch target, named with its title and version.
Decline is named for what it does ("Decline and sign out").
The sheet's content scrolls at large font sizes, so the buttons are always reachable.
edgeCases: In the blocking form there must be a way out: Decline signs the person out.
Record the accepted version, not only a flag, so the next change shows the sheet again.

name: MonarchThemeToggle
title: ThemeToggle
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow with SegmentedButton; androidx.compose.material3.DropdownMenu with DropdownMenuItem and RadioButton for the menu variant
summary: Light, dark or system theme: a segmented control or a menu button that reports the MonarchScheme the app passes to MonarchTheme.
whenToUse: In a settings screen (segmented) or in a toolbar or account menu (menu) when people may choose the appearance of the app instead of following the system.
whenNotToUse: For any other choice between two to five options use SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow directly (segmented-control). Do not add it when the app always follows the system setting.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchThemeToggle(scheme: MonarchScheme, onSchemeChange: (MonarchScheme) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchThemeToggleVariant = MonarchThemeToggleVariant.Segmented, size: MonarchThemeToggleSize = MonarchThemeToggleSize.Md, enabled: Boolean = true, showLabel: Boolean = true, icon: (@Composable (MonarchScheme) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchThemeToggleLabels = MonarchThemeToggleLabels())
public enum class MonarchThemeToggleVariant { Segmented, Menu }
public enum class MonarchThemeToggleSize { Sm, Md }
public class MonarchThemeToggleLabels(title: String? = null, light: String? = null, dark: String? = null, system: String? = null)
public object MonarchThemeToggleStorage { public fun storageValue(scheme: MonarchScheme): String; public fun scheme(value: String?): MonarchScheme? }

options.name: scheme
options.description: The current choice: Light, Dark or System. The app keeps it and passes it to MonarchTheme(scheme = …).

options.name: onSchemeChange
options.description: Called with the choice the user picks. Not called when the current choice is picked again.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the toggle.

options.name: variant
options.description: Segmented shows three segments; Menu shows one ghost button that opens the three choices.

options.name: size
options.description: Segmented: the caption or the label type for the names. Menu: the Sm or Md Monarch button.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the user can change the choice.

options.name: showLabel
options.description: Menu only: whether the button shows the current choice's name beside the icon. The name is always spoken, and shown when there is no icon.

options.name: icon
options.description: An icon for a choice (sun, moon, half-filled circle) on the menu button and in the menu. Decorative; Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings Theme, Light, Dark and System.

states.name: light, dark, system
states.description: The selected segment with the Material check mark, or the menu button's name and the checked radio item in the menu.

states.name: menu open
states.description: A Material 3 dropdown menu with the title Theme and three radio items; picking one closes it.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The segments or the menu button use the disabled colors and do not respond.

appearance: The segmented variant is the Material segmented button row with the Monarch color mapping: the selected segment takes the secondary container color mapped from the accent subtle role, the border is the default border role. The menu button is the ghost Monarch button; the menu is the Material menu on the raised surface. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow the theme roles.
platformNotes: The web toggle reads and writes the shared rook_theme cookie and applies the theme to the html element. In an Android app there is no shared cookie: the toggle only reports the choice; the app stores it (DataStore or SharedPreferences) and passes it to MonarchTheme(scheme = …). MonarchThemeToggleStorage gives the same light, dark and system values as the cookie and the iOS storageValue(for:). The web's controlled and uncontrolled forms become one hoisted value, as Compose state is. The web menu variant's side and align options are not offered: the Material dropdown menu places itself. The web draws sun, moon and system glyphs; Monarch for Android bundles no icons, so the icon slot is empty by default and the names are always shown in the segments. Same names and vocabulary as iOS, with scheme and onSchemeChange instead of a binding.
accessibility: The segment row is named Theme; each segment is a radio button with its name, and the current one is selected.
The menu button is named Theme and its state is the current choice's name, also when only the icon is shown.
The menu has a Theme heading and three radio items, the current one selected and marked with a filled radio button, not color alone.
Each segment and the menu button have a 48dp touch target; the segments follow the reading order in right-to-left layouts.
The names stay whole at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: Picking the current choice again does not call onSchemeChange.
MonarchThemeToggleStorage.scheme returns null for a missing or unknown stored value; use the app's default then.
System follows the system dark theme setting while the app runs, because MonarchTheme reads isSystemInDarkTheme.
In the menu variant with showLabel false and no icon, the name is shown anyway so the button is never empty.
