name: MonarchThreadPanel
title: ThreadPanel
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column with MonarchVirtualMessageList (androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn) for the replies, MonarchChip to follow the thread and MonarchDivider; placed by the app in an MonarchBottomSheet or a supporting pane
summary: The panel of one conversation thread: the message it answers, a reply count divider, the replies pinned to the newest one, a follow chip, and the app's reply box pinned to the bottom.
whenToUse: When someone opens the replies to one message of a chat or channel: in a sheet on a phone, or in a pane beside the conversation at expanded width.
whenNotToUse: For the conversation itself, use MonarchVirtualMessageList with MonarchMessageRow. For discussions anchored to a document passage, use MonarchCommentThread or MonarchCommentsPanel.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun <T> MonarchThreadPanel(replies: List<T>, key: (reply: T) -> Any, time: (reply: T) -> Long, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, replyCount: Int = replies.size, status: MonarchThreadPanelStatus = MonarchThreadPanelStatus.Ready, following: Boolean = false, state: LazyListState = rememberLazyListState(), authorId: (reply: T) -> String? = { null }, notice: String? = null, seenDelayMillis: Long = 400L, now: Long? = null, locale: Locale? = null, timeZone: String? = null, labels: MonarchThreadPanelLabels = MonarchThreadPanelLabels(), onClose: (() -> Unit)? = null, onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null, onFollowingChange: (suspend (Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, onRepliesSeen: ((replyCount: Int) -> Unit)? = null, followIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, headerActions: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null, root: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, typing: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, composer: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, reply: @Composable LazyItemScope.(reply: T, context: MonarchVirtualMessageListContext<T>) -> Unit)
enum class MonarchThreadPanelStatus { Ready, Loading, Error, Deleted }

class MonarchThreadPanelLabels(title: String? = null, close: String? = null, follow: String? = null, following: String? = null, followedNotice: String? = null, unfollowedNotice: String? = null, followFailed: String? = null, replyCount: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, replies: String? = null, loading: String? = null, error: String? = null, deleted: String? = null, list: MonarchVirtualMessageListLabels? = null)

options.name: replies
options.description: The loaded replies, oldest first.

options.name: key
options.description: A stable, unique key per reply.

options.name: time
options.description: When a reply was sent, in epoch milliseconds (UTC), for day separators and grouping.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the panel. Give it a bounded height.

options.name: replyCount
options.description: The number of replies for the divider; can exceed the loaded replies.

options.name: status
options.description: Ready shows the replies; Loading placeholders; Error an error with Try again; Deleted a notice with Close.

options.name: following
options.description: The person follows the thread: the chip is selected and reads Following.

options.name: state
options.description: The scroll state of the replies; index 0 is the bottom row.

options.name: authorId
options.description: The author of a reply, for grouping consecutive replies.

options.name: notice
options.description: A note after the replies, such as Showing the first 500 replies.

options.name: seenDelayMillis
options.description: How long the replies stay on screen before onRepliesSeen.

options.name: now
options.description: The current time for Today and Yesterday; null reads the clock.

options.name: locale
options.description: The locale of the day separators; null uses the configuration's.

options.name: timeZone
options.description: The time zone of the day separators. An IANA id such as Europe/Berlin; null, or an id the device does not know, is the device's zone.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, and optionally the list's.

options.name: onClose
options.description: Shows Close in the header and with a deleted thread.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Try again when the thread could not be loaded.

options.name: onFollowingChange
options.description: Follows or unfollows; shows the follow chip while Ready. Throw to announce a failure.

options.name: onRepliesSeen
options.description: Called with replyCount once the replies have been on screen for seenDelayMillis, and again when the count changes: mark the thread read here.

options.name: followIcon
options.description: The icon of the follow chip.

options.name: headerActions
options.description: Further header controls, before Close.

options.name: root
options.description: The message the thread answers, usually a MonarchMessageRow.

options.name: typing
options.description: Above the reply box, such as a MonarchTypingIndicator.

options.name: composer
options.description: The reply box, usually a MonarchMessageComposer, pinned under the replies.

options.name: reply
options.description: Draws one reply, usually a MonarchMessageRow with grouped = context.grouped.

states.name: ready
states.description: The root message, the reply count divider and the replies, newest at the bottom, with day separators.

states.name: no replies
states.description: The root and 0 replies.

states.name: following
states.description: The chip is selected and reads Following; changing it disables the chip until the app's function returns.

states.name: loading
states.description: A MonarchLoadingState with three rows, read once as Loading thread.

states.name: error
states.description: This thread couldn't be loaded, with Try again (MonarchInlineErrorRetry), or in the strong danger text role without onRetry.

states.name: deleted
states.description: This thread was deleted, announced, with Close.

appearance: No fill of its own, so it takes the sheet's or pane's surface. The heading uses the default text role, the reply count, the notice and the deleted text the muted text role, the dividers the subtle border role, and the follow chip the Material 3 filter chip roles Monarch maps from the theme. The same roles adapt to dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web's ThreadPanel takes the replies as children of a scrolling log; on Android they are items of a MonarchVirtualMessageList, so only the replies on screen are composed, day separators are added and consecutive replies group. The web's follow button with aria-pressed is a MonarchChip here. The web's close icon button is a Close text button because Monarch bundles no icons; a sheet also closes by swiping and with the back gesture. The web reports replies seen while the page is visible; on Android the delay runs while the panel is composed, and the app should not compose it while its screen is stopped. iOS has no entry for this id yet.
accessibility: The title is a heading.
The replies are a list named Replies; new replies are announced by MonarchVirtualMessageList.
The follow chip has the selected state and its text changes between Follow and Following; it is disabled while the change runs.
Following, unfollowing and a failure are announced through a polite live region that is always present.
The deleted notice is a polite live region.
Follow, Close and Try again have 48dp touch targets.
edgeCases: replyCount can be larger than the loaded replies; use notice to say how many are shown.
The root shows only once the replies reach the start of the thread, as the header of MonarchVirtualMessageList.
The follow chip is hidden while loading, after an error and for a deleted thread.
onRepliesSeen is called again when replyCount changes, after the delay.
The replies are a lazy list: give the panel a bounded height and do not put it in a vertically scrolling parent.

name: MonarchTimeGrid
title: TimeGrid
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row and Box columns in androidx.compose.foundation.verticalScroll and a shared androidx.compose.foundation.horizontalScroll, MonarchEventChip blocks and bars, androidx.compose.foundation.gestures.detectDragGesturesAfterLongPress, androidx.compose.ui.semantics.CustomAccessibilityAction and androidx.compose.ui.hapticfeedback.HapticFeedbackType
summary: The day and week view of a calendar: an hour gutter, an all-day row and one column per day, with overlapping events side by side, a now line, working-hours shading, unavailable blocks, tap to create and long press and drag to move.
whenToUse: For a calendar's day or week view, a booking schedule or a rota where the time of day matters. Put MonarchCalendarToolbar above it to change days and views, and open events in MonarchEventPopover or a sheet.
whenNotToUse: For upcoming events listed by day, use MonarchAgendaList, which reads better on a narrow phone; to pick a day, use MonarchMiniMonth or the Material 3 DatePicker. Do not put it inside another vertical scroll: the hours scroll themselves.

class MonarchTimeGridMove(event: MonarchAgendaEvent, start: Long, end: Long)
class MonarchTimeGridUnavailable(id: String, start: Long, end: Long, label: String? = null)
class MonarchTimeGridWorkingHours(weekday: Int, start: Int, end: Int)

class MonarchTimeGridLabels(allDay: String? = null, createEvent: ((String) -> String)? = null, today: String? = null, openDay: ((String) -> String)? = null, range: ((String, String) -> String)? = null, until: ((String) -> String)? = null, moveEarlier: String? = null, moveLater: String? = null, moveToPreviousDay: String? = null, moveToNextDay: String? = null)

options.name: days
options.description: The day columns in order, one for a day view, seven for a week, as day keys: the UTC midnight of each date, as DatePickerState and MonarchMiniMonth give.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the grid. Give it a bounded height.

options.name: events
options.description: The events, the same model as MonarchAgendaList. Timed events are placed by start and end (exclusive); all-day events go in the all-day row of each day they cover.

options.name: now
options.description: The current time for the now line and today's heading; null hides both. Pass a value that changes every minute to move the line.

options.name: startHour
options.description: The first visible hour, 0 to 23.

options.name: endHour
options.description: The end of the visible hours (exclusive), 1 to 24. At least one hour is shown.

options.name: hourHeight
options.description: The height of one hour. Unspecified is 64dp, or 48dp times the font scale when that is more.

options.name: snapMinutes
options.description: Taps, drags and TalkBack moves snap to this many minutes, 1 to 60.

options.name: workingHours
options.description: Working hours per ISO weekday (1 Monday to 7 Sunday) in minutes from midnight; time outside them is shaded. null shades nothing.

options.name: unavailable
options.description: Blocks drawn hatched with an optional label, such as time off or a closure.

options.name: scrollToMinutes
options.description: Minutes from midnight to scroll to when the grid appears and when the first day or the number of days changes. null is an hour before the earliest visible event, else 08:00.

options.name: showAllDayRow
options.description: Shows the all-day row even when no all-day event is visible.

options.name: timeZone
options.description: The zone events are placed and times are written in. An IANA id such as Europe/Berlin; null, or an id the device does not know, is the device's zone.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

options.name: canMoveEvent
options.description: Which events may be moved. null allows all, when onMoveEvent is set.

options.name: onSelectDay
options.description: Makes the headings of a multi-day grid buttons, for example to open the day view. Receives the day key.

options.name: onSelectSlot
options.description: Called when an empty part of a column is tapped, with the time snapped down to snapMinutes. Also makes every hour of every column a TalkBack button.

options.name: onSelectEvent
options.description: Opens an event. Without it events are not buttons.

options.name: onMoveEvent
options.description: Turns on moving events by long press and drag and by TalkBack actions. The grid does not change the events; the app applies or confirms the move.

states.name: week
states.description: Several columns with weekday and date headings; overlapping events share the column width side by side.

states.name: day
states.description: One column; its heading is a heading, not a button.

states.name: today
states.description: Today's date sits on a filled accent circle, its heading is read with "Today", and the now line with its dot crosses its column when now is inside the visible hours.

states.name: all-day row
states.description: Shown when an all-day event is visible or showAllDayRow is on: an "All day" label in the gutter and bar chips per day.

states.name: working hours
states.description: Time outside the working hours of each weekday is shaded.

states.name: unavailable
states.description: A hatched block with its label; taps still reach the slot under it.

states.name: short event
states.description: Events under 45 minutes are one line, start time then title; events of 70 minutes or more also show their detail. A tappable event is drawn at least 48dp tall.

states.name: wide
states.description: When the columns need more room than the width (narrow phone, many days, events side by side), the days scroll sideways together with their headings and all-day row; the hour gutter stays.

states.name: moving
states.description: After a long press the event is picked up with a haptic, a dashed ghost shows the new time and title, scrolling pauses, and each step ticks. Releasing calls onMoveEvent when the start changed.

states.name: read only
states.description: Without callbacks the grid only shows events.

appearance: The grid sits on the surface background with subtle border lines for hours and columns and a default border under the headings. Hour labels, weekdays and the all-day label use the muted text color; today's date is in the accent on-solid color on an accent solid circle; the now line is the danger solid color. Shading is the subtle background, unavailable blocks the muted background with default-border hatching. Events are MonarchEventChip blocks in their own color or the accent. Every role comes from the theme, so the dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web TimeGrid reads ISO days in an IANA zone, drags with a pointer only (touch keeps scrolling), moves focus between hour slots with the arrow keys and takes a renderEvent wrapper. On Android days are day keys in epoch milliseconds and events are placed in the zone of an IANA id; moving is long press then drag, as in Google Calendar, with system haptics; TalkBack gets named move actions instead of keyboard dragging, and hardware keyboards move between slots and events with Compose's focus search, not the web's arrow-key map. There is no renderEvent: onSelectEvent gives the app the event to show in MonarchEventPopover or a sheet. The web's hourCycle and locale come from the configuration's locale. Unlike the web and iOS, a column widens and the days scroll sideways when events side by side would be narrower than 48dp, and tappable events are drawn at least 48dp tall (overlaps are packed by the drawn length), so every target keeps 48dp. Drag to create a range and auto-scrolling while dragging near an edge are not offered. Events reuse MonarchAgendaEvent, as on iOS, whose MonarchTimeGrid has the same parameters (Compose callbacks instead of bindings, timeZone instead of calendar).
accessibility: Each day heading is one element read as "Wednesday, November 4", with ", Today" on today; it is a heading, or a button with the click label "Open Wednesday, November 4" when onSelectDay is set in a multi-day grid, with a 48dp target.
Each event is a MonarchEventChip read as one element: title, time spoken in full ("9:30 AM to 11:00 AM"), status and detail; with onSelectEvent it is a button with a 48dp target.

A movable event has the TalkBack actions Move earlier, Move later (by snapMinutes), Move to previous day and Move to next day, each offered only when the move is possible, so it can be rescheduled without dragging.
With onSelectSlot every hour of every column is a button read as "Create event, Wednesday, November 4, 9:00 AM"; TalkBack and keyboards create at the start of the hour.
Each column is a traversal group named with its long date.
Unavailable blocks are read with their label and times ("Closed, 12:00 PM to 1:00 PM"); shading, the hour gutter, grid lines, the now line and the drag ghost are hidden.
Today is marked by a word and a filled shape, not by color alone; statuses are words read by the event chip.
Hour height grows with the font size, and right to left the first day is at the right.
edgeCases: Daylight-saving days still show 24 rows: events are placed by wall-clock time, so a skipped hour leaves a gap and a repeated hour overlaps; a slot in a skipped hour starts at the next valid time.
An event that ends exactly at midnight does not appear on the next day; a multi-day timed event is clipped on each day it touches.
Events outside startHour to endHour are hidden; events crossing the edges are clipped.
An event with no end, or an end before its start, is drawn snapMinutes long (or 48dp when it can be tapped).
A moved event keeps its duration; a move is clamped so the whole event stays in the visible hours, and a move that would not change the start is not reported.
A week on a narrow phone scrolls sideways; consider three days, or MonarchAgendaList.
Event ids must be unique.

whenNotToUse: For regular weekly working hours use a schedule of time ranges; for one-off bookings use the calendar components; to see who is away on which day use MonarchTeamCalendar.

options.name: entries
options.description: The periods, in display order. All-day entries are days as UTC midnights (end included); timed entries are instants.

options.name: onAdd
options.description: Shows Add time off; the sheet stays busy while it runs and shows the message of what it throws.

options.name: onRemove

options.name: canRemove

options.name: people

options.name: types

options.name: showPast / onShowPastChange

options.name: loading
options.description: Placeholders instead of the list.

options.name: error / onRetry
options.description: A danger banner instead of the list, with Try again.

options.name: timeZone
options.description: The zone timed entries are shown and entered in, and that decides today. An IANA id such as Europe/Berlin; null, or an id the device does not know, is the device's zone.

options.name: now
options.description: The instant that decides which entries are past; pass a fixed value in tests.

options.name: is24Hour

options.name: state
options.description: The scroll state of the list.

options.name: addIcon / removeIcon
options.description: An icon in the add button; the glyph of the remove buttons (null shows them as text).

options.name: notice
options.description: Content above the list, for example a MonarchBanner.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

states.name: list
states.description: One row per entry: who, badges (Closure, the type, the status, Past) and when, with a remove button.

states.name: past hidden
states.description: Entries that ended before now are left out until Include past is on.

states.name: loading
states.description: Three placeholders read as "Loading time off".

states.name: error
states.description: A danger banner with Try again.

states.name: empty
states.description: A small MonarchEmptyState: "No time off planned".

states.name: adding
states.description: A bottom sheet with Who, Type, All day, the dates (and times), Reason and Add time off; the end before the start shows an error; the button shows its loading state while onAdd runs.

states.name: removing
states.description: An alert dialog naming the entry, with a danger Remove button that shows its loading state while onRemove runs.

appearance: A title in the default text color with a muted description, a switch row, rows with a strong name and muted dates, badges in the warning (Closure), neutral (type), info (status) and outline (Past) styles, and Material 3 sheets and dialogs in the Monarch theme. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web opens the add form in a centered dialog with inline date and date-time pickers; on Android it is a bottom sheet whose date and time buttons open the Material 3 DatePickerDialog and TimePickerDialog, the phone pattern. From and Until are two DatePickerDialogs (Until cannot be earlier than From) rather than one DateRangePicker, so all-day and timed entries share the same date field. The web's Include past checkbox is a switch row. Entries and drafts use epoch milliseconds (days as UTC midnights) instead of ISO strings, and the zone is a java.util.TimeZone as in other Monarch scheduling components, so the zone shown in the sheet is its id. onAdd and onRemove are suspend functions where the web returns a promise. The web moves focus to the next remove button after a removal; on Android TalkBack moves on by itself and focus is not moved. The web's headingLevel, locale and uncontrolled defaultShowPast are not offered (the locale comes from the configuration; showPast null keeps it inside). The panel is a LazyColumn, so it takes the screen's height and must not sit in a vertically scrolling parent. iOS has no entry yet.
accessibility: The title is a heading.
Each entry is one TalkBack element read as who, its badges and when; badges are words, so nothing depends on color.
Each remove button is named after the entry, "Remove time off for Alex Kim, Mon, Nov 9, 2026 – Fri, Nov 13, 2026 (all day)", and has a 48dp target.
Include past is a switch row with the switch role and its state.
Removing asks first in an alert dialog; it cannot be dismissed while the removal runs, and a failure is read through an assertive live region.
The add sheet's failure is an assertive banner; the end-before-start problem is shown as the error of the date fields.
Dates and names wrap at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: An all-day entry that ends today is not past; a timed entry is past once its end instant is.
Choosing a From day after Until moves Until to it; Until cannot be before From in its picker.
A timed end equal to its start is refused; an all-day entry may be one day.
A closure has no person: personId is null and it reads Everyone.
A thrown exception with a blank message shows "That did not work. Try again."

whenToUse: For a resubmitted or corrected timesheet, an approval review or an audit view, where the reviewer needs to see what moved and how much time it adds or removes.

options.name: diff
options.description: The entries added, removed and changed, when the product computes the difference itself.

options.name: before, after
options.description: The two versions; entries are matched by id and compared on date, minutes, project, activity, task, billable and note.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the diff.

options.name: title
options.description: The heading. Built in: "What changed".

options.name: subtitle
options.description: Quiet text after the heading, such as "since version 3".

options.name: showTotals
options.description: Shows the totals line.

options.name: showBillable
options.description: Adds the billable change to the totals line. Turn it off when billing does not apply.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, the field names, the delta and totals formats, and the line of an entry (the web's renderEntry, as text).

states.name: added
states.description: A success-tinted line with a success bar at the start edge, an "Added" badge, the time gained and the entry.

states.name: removed
states.description: A danger-tinted line with a "Removed" badge, the time lost and the entry struck through in the muted color.

states.name: changed
states.description: A warning-tinted line with a "Changed time, project" badge, the old line struck through above the new one, and the change of time when there is one.

states.name: empty
states.description: "No changes." in the muted color.

states.name: totals
states.description: "Total +15m · billable +1h" in tabular figures.

appearance: Each line is tinted with its tone's subtle color and has a bar in the tone's solid color at the start edge; the kind is a MonarchBadge in the same tone and the change of time uses the tone's strong color. Entry text is the default text color; struck-through lines use the muted color. High contrast themes use their stronger tone roles.
platformNotes: The parity map named a LazyColumn; the diff is a plain Column so that it can sit inside a card or a scrolling review screen (a lazy list there needs a fixed height), and a review has tens of changes. The web takes ISO date strings; here the day is epoch milliseconds of its UTC midnight, as in the Material 3 date picker, shown in UTC. The web's renderEntry returns any content; here labels.entry returns the line as text, which is also what TalkBack reads. The web's open-ended field names are strings, with MonarchTimesheetDiffFields for the built-in ones. The web's headingLevel is heading semantics. Visible durations ("1h 30m") follow the web's compact form and are not localised; TalkBack reads them in words in the user's locale through ICU MeasureFormat. The kind is a MonarchBadge (the plan's badge dependency); digits use MonarchTabularNumberStyle. iOS builds the same component with the same name.
accessibility: The title has heading semantics.
Each line is one element read in words: "Removed, minus 45 minutes, Mon, Jan 12, 45 minutes, Pulse, non-billable"; a changed entry reads "Before:" and "After:" before its two lines.
Durations and the totals are read in words in the user's locale ("1 hour, 30 minutes", "Total plus 15 minutes · billable plus 1 hour").
The kind is a word in a badge as well as a color; a removed entry and the old line of a changed one are struck through.
Text wraps and scales with the font size setting.
edgeCases: An empty or missing project is shown as "No project".
billable null counts as billable in the totals, as on the web; only false is non-billable.
A changed entry whose time did not change shows no change of time.
A missing value and an empty one are different, so null to "" is a change.
Two dates on the same UTC day are the same date.
Field names neither labels.fields nor the built-in names know are shown by their raw name.
Order: added, then removed, then changed, each in the order of its version.

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: Shown when there are no rows (or no days). Built in: "No time logged for this period."

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, the duration formats and the day formats.

options.name: actionsIcon
options.description: The icon of each row's actions button. Without it the button shows the text "Actions".

options.name: rowActions
options.description: The actions of a row, in a menu beside its name, such as clearing the row. The same type MonarchDataTable uses.

options.name: onDayActivate
options.description: Makes day headings buttons, for example to open a day view.

options.name: onCellActivate
options.description: Makes read-only cells with time buttons, for example to open the entries behind them.

options.name: onCellChange
options.type: (suspend (rowId: String, day: Long, minutes: Int) -> Unit)?
options.description: Saves a typed value: row id, day key and minutes (0 clears). The cell is disabled and read as "Saving" while it runs; a thrown exception's message is shown. Without it, every cell is read-only.

states.name: editable
states.description: Open cells are outlined fields in the grid, or MonarchDurationInput fields in the day layout; the text is read when focus leaves or on the Next key (the Done key in the day layout), and the minutes are passed to onCellChange.

states.name: saving
states.description: The cell is disabled, its text uses the disabled color and it is read as "Saving" (in the day layout its helper text says "Saving") until onCellChange returns.

states.name: error
states.description: Text that cannot be read, a value above the daily maximum or a failed save keeps the typed text, gives the cell the danger border and error semantics, and shows the message under the grid in a polite live region (in the day layout, under the field).

states.name: locked day
states.description: The heading shows the reason, or "Locked"; the column is shaded and its cells are muted, read-only and read with the reason.

states.name: read-only row or grid
states.description: Cells show the time as text, a dash when empty. With onCellActivate, cells with time are Material 3 text buttons in the link color.

states.name: today
states.description: The heading says "Today" in the strong accent color, with an accent bar under it in the grid; the day layout opens on it.

states.name: non-working day
states.description: The column (or the day heading) is shaded; entry is still allowed.

states.name: over the daily limit
states.description: The day total is in the strong danger color with the words "Over limit" under it.

states.name: empty
states.description: Without rows the empty message replaces the rows; without days the day layout shows only the message.

appearance: Headings and the first column use the label style; the header and footer rows use the subtle background, with the muted text color for column headings, descriptions, notes, expected times and summary rows. Locked and non-working columns use the subtle background; today's heading uses the strong accent color with a bar in the solid accent; errors and over-limit totals use the strong danger color with words. Fields use the input border on the surface and the focus ring color when focused, like MonarchTextField. All roles come from the theme, so dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web always renders a table that scrolls sideways; on a phone that is hard to use, so the automatic layout shows one day at a time with a Material 3 PrimaryScrollableTabRow of the days, a MonarchDurationInput (with its − and + steppers) for each editable row and the row's period total under it, as iOS does with its day pages. iOS moves between days with previous and next buttons; Android uses tabs, the Material 3 pattern, so it has no previousDay and nextDay labels. The web keys days and cells by ISO date strings and iOS by Date; here the key is a day key, epoch milliseconds in UTC as in the Material 3 DatePickerState (minSdk 24, no java.time), and any time on the same UTC day matches. The web returns a promise and iOS an async throwing closure from onCellChange; here it is a suspend function, and a thrown exception's message is shown. The web's label, markers and summary cells accept any content; here they are text. The web's row actions slot takes any content; here row actions are MonarchDataTableRowAction values in a Material 3 DropdownMenu beside the row name, with an optional actionsIcon slot because Monarch bundles no icons. The web moves between cells with all four arrow keys; here, with a hardware keyboard, Enter (the Next key) saves and moves down, up and down arrows move between rows, Escape restores the saved value and left and right move the text cursor. The over-limit total says "Over limit" in words where iOS shows a symbol. Locked days have no lock glyph, only the reason or "Locked" in words.
accessibility: The grid is a collection named "Time per row and day" (labels.caption) with its row and column counts; each cell carries its row and column.
Column headings, row names and day headings are headings; a day heading is one element read in full, such as "Mon, Jan 12, Approved" or "Tue, Jan 13, Today".
Each cell is named by its row and day, such as "Atlas, Tue, Jan 13"; a read-only cell's state is the time in words and the lock reason, such as "4 hours, Approved", or "No time" when empty.
An editable grid cell is a text field with that name; it carries error semantics with the message while rejected, and the state "Saving" while it is saved.
Error messages appear under the grid in a polite live region, so TalkBack announces them, and are words, not only the danger color.
Day totals are named "Day total, <day>" and read the time in words, the expected time and "Over limit"; row totals are named "<row>, Total".
In the day layout the day tabs are Material 3 tabs in a row named "Days", each read in full and marked selected; the page opens on today.
Day headings with onDayActivate, cells with onCellActivate and the row actions button are buttons with a 48dp touch target.
Above font scale 1.3 the automatic layout shows one day at a time so no text is cut; long names wrap.
edgeCases: Negative minutes in cells count as 0; two keys on the same UTC day are added together.
Cells keyed by a day that is not in days are ignored in every total.
Empty text clears the cell: onCellChange receives 0.
A value equal to the saved one is not passed to onCellChange.
If onCellChange succeeds but the app does not pass new rows, the typed text stays in the cell until the row's value changes.
A lockReason locks the day even when locked is false.
readOnly wins over onCellChange; without onCellChange every cell is read-only.
The day layout opens on today, else the first day, and stays where the person moved it.
The grid does not scroll vertically: place it in a scrolling screen. It scrolls sideways when the columns do not fit.

parityExceptions.reason: The web shows a row's actions menu only while the pointer is over the row or a control in it has focus, so its still image has none. A touch screen has no hover, so each editable row keeps a visible three dots button (a 48dp touch target) that opens the same Clear row menu.
parityExceptions.convention: no hover on touch: a control that appears on hover on the web is always visible on a phone (Material touch target of 48dp)

name: MonarchTimezoneSelect
title: TimezoneSelect
wrapsNative: MonarchCombobox in its sheet presentation (androidx.compose.material3.ModalBottomSheet with a search field and a LazyColumn) over java.util.TimeZone.getAvailableIDs, collapsed with android.icu.util.TimeZone.getCanonicalID, with java.util.TimeZone.getOffset and getDisplayName
summary: A searchable IANA time zone picker, labelled by UTC offset and city and sorted by offset, with Detected, Pinned and Recent sections.
whenToUse: Wherever a person chooses a time zone: profile settings, a meeting's zone, a workspace's office hours.
whenNotToUse: Not for showing the time in several zones, which is text or MonarchEventChip times. Not for choosing a city or an address, which is a place search with MonarchCombobox.
api: @Composable fun MonarchTimezoneSelect(label: String, selected: String?, onSelectedChange: (String?) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, placeholder: String? = null, helperText: String? = null, errorText: String? = null, zones: List<String>? = null, detectedZone: String? = null, showDetected: Boolean = true, pinned: List<String> = emptyList(), recent: List<String> = emptyList(), now: Long? = null, formatLabel: ((MonarchTimezoneInfo) -> String)? = null, clearIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchTimezoneSelectLabels = MonarchTimezoneSelectLabels())
class MonarchTimezoneInfo(id: String, city: String, region: String, offsetSeconds: Int, offsetLabel: String, longName: String)

class MonarchTimezoneSelectLabels(detected: String? = null, pinned: String? = null, recent: String? = null, all: String? = null, empty: String? = null, combobox: MonarchComboboxLabels = MonarchComboboxLabels())

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label; it names the field and the sheet.

options.name: selected
options.description: The IANA id of the chosen zone, or null. An old id such as Asia/Calcutta selects its current name.

options.name: onSelectedChange
options.description: Called with the current id of the chosen zone, or null when the selection is cleared.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the field.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the list can be opened.

options.name: placeholder
options.description: Shown in the field while nothing is chosen.

options.name: helperText
options.description: Help text under the field.

options.name: errorText
options.description: An error message; the field is in the error state and TalkBack reads it with the field.

options.name: zones
options.description: Limits the list to these zones. Every location zone the system knows when null.

options.name: detectedZone
options.description: The zone under Detected. The device's zone when null.

options.name: showDetected
options.description: Whether the Detected section is shown.

options.name: pinned
options.description: Zones listed under Pinned, such as the workspace's offices.

options.name: recent
options.description: Zones listed under Recent, such as the person's last choices.

options.name: now
options.description: The instant offsets and long names are computed for, daylight saving included. The time the select first appeared when null.

options.name: formatLabel
options.description: Builds an option's label from the zone's information. Built in: "(UTC+05:30) Kolkata".

options.name: clearIcon
options.description: The icon of a clear button in the field while a zone is chosen. Monarch bundles no icons; without it there is no clear button.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the section headings, the empty text and the combobox's own strings.

states.name: closed
states.description: The field shows the chosen zone's label, or the placeholder.

states.name: open
states.description: A bottom sheet with a search field and the Detected, Pinned and Recent sections, then every zone by offset under All time zones.

states.name: searching
states.description: Only the full list is searched, so a zone appears once; every word typed must match.

states.name: empty
states.description: "No time zones match".

states.name: error, disabled
states.description: As MonarchCombobox: the error under the field, a disabled field that cannot open.

appearance: The MonarchCombobox field and sheet: the field uses the text-field roles, the sheet the raised surface, and each row shows its label with the id and long name under it in the muted text color; the chosen zone has a filled radio mark. All colors come from the theme, in every theme.
platformNotes: The web is an inline combobox with a popup list; on Android MonarchCombobox opens a bottom sheet with a search field and a lazy list, which suits touch and TalkBack. The web lists zones with Intl.supportedValuesOf; Android reads java.util.TimeZone's ids for places (Africa to Pacific, leaving out Etc/ offsets and old country aliases), collapses aliases with ICU's canonical id and reads java.util.TimeZone offsets, because java.time needs API 26 and ICU's location-zone list needs API 28. ICU's canonical ids are often the old names, so ids are mapped to their current names as on the web. Long names follow the configuration's locale instead of a locale prop. The web's and iOS's required mark is not offered because MonarchCombobox has none; say it in helperText. The clear button needs clearIcon, since Monarch bundles no icons. iOS builds the same component with the same name; its selection binding is selected with onSelectedChange, and isClearable and prompt are clearIcon and placeholder.
accessibility: The field is MonarchCombobox's field, read with its label and the chosen zone's label, with a 48dp target.
In the sheet each zone is a row read with its label, id and long name; the chosen one is selected and has a radio mark.
Section headings Detected, Pinned, Recent and All time zones are headings.
The error text is read with the field.
Rows and the field are at least 48dp high, and text scales with the font size.
edgeCases: A selected zone missing from zones is still listed and shown.
A zone the system does not know shows an offset of UTC+00:00 and no long name.
Long names that are only an offset, such as GMT+05:30, are left out.
Building every option reads about 420 zones once per instant and locale; pass zones to limit the list.

name: MonarchSnackbarHost
title: Toast
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.SnackbarHost, androidx.compose.material3.Snackbar, androidx.compose.material3.SnackbarHostState
summary: Transient notifications as Material 3 snackbars: a themed host, snackbar content with a tone, and a function that shows one.
whenToUse: For a brief confirmation of something the user just did, such as "Ticket archived", optionally with one action such as Undo.
whenNotToUse: For a message that must stay until it is resolved, use MonarchBanner or MonarchCalloutBanner. For a decision, use AlertDialog. For an error the user must act on, do not rely on a snackbar alone.
api: @Composable fun MonarchSnackbarHost(hostState: SnackbarHostState, modifier: Modifier = Modifier)

class MonarchSnackbarVisuals(override val message: String, val tone: MonarchTone = MonarchTone.Neutral, override val actionLabel: String? = null, override val withDismissAction: Boolean = false, override val duration: SnackbarDuration = …, val icon: ImageVector? = null) : SnackbarVisuals

suspend fun SnackbarHostState.showMonarchSnackbar(message: String, tone: MonarchTone = MonarchTone.Neutral, actionLabel: String? = null, withDismissAction: Boolean = false, duration: SnackbarDuration = …, icon: ImageVector? = null): SnackbarResult

options.name: hostState
options.description: The Material 3 state that shows and queues snackbars.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the host.

options.name: message
options.description: The message of a snackbar. Say the outcome in words.

options.name: tone
options.description: The tone of a snackbar: it colours the status mark at the start; the panel is the raised surface in every tone.

options.name: actionLabel
options.description: The label of the one action, for example "Undo".

options.name: withDismissAction
options.description: Whether a dismiss button is shown.

options.name: duration
options.default: Long with an action or the danger tone, Short otherwise
options.description: How long the snackbar stays. Indefinite keeps it until it is dismissed.

options.name: icon
options.description: An outlined icon at the start in the tone colour; null shows the status mark of the info, success, warning and danger tones.

states.name: shown
states.description: Fades and scales in at the host, one at a time; later snackbars wait in a queue.

states.name: closed
states.description: By its timer, the action, the dismiss button, a swipe, or SnackbarData.dismiss(). showMonarchSnackbar returns ActionPerformed or Dismissed.

appearance: Every tone is the raised background with the default text, a subtle border (strong in high contrast), 12dp corners and one soft shadow in the light themes (none in the dark ones), up to 384dp wide. The tone colours only the status mark at the start (a ring with a check, an exclamation mark or an i, in the strong role of the tone), or the snackbar's own icon. The action is a small ghost MonarchButton; the close button is a MonarchIconButton.
platformNotes: Planned as style: the Material 3 snackbar is the Android answer to a toast, so Monarch supplies the themed host, a SnackbarVisuals with a tone and a show function, and keeps Material 3 behavior. iOS builds MonarchToast with its own center and overlay. The host is placed by the app, normally in the snackbarHost slot of a Scaffold at the bottom; the web's top positions, offsets and hotkey are not offered. Material 3 shows one snackbar at a time, where the web stacks up to three. There is no title and description pair, only one message; the tone shows as a status mark or the snackbar's own icon. The tone is not spoken: write the outcome into the message. The web altText for the action and onDismiss callback are covered by the SnackbarResult returned by showMonarchSnackbar. Durations are the Material 3 Short (4 s) and Long (10 s); the web uses 5 s and 10 s.
accessibility: Material 3 behavior: the snackbar is a polite live region, so TalkBack announces its message when it appears.
The action and the dismiss button are separate buttons with 48dp touch targets; the dismiss button is named by Material 3 ("Dismiss").
Material 3 lengthens the time on screen when an accessibility service asks for longer timeouts.
The tone is color only; the message must say the outcome.
The message wraps at the largest font size.
edgeCases: A plain SnackbarVisuals shown through the host takes the neutral tone.
Snackbars queue: a second showMonarchSnackbar waits until the first one closes.
Inside a bottom sheet or a dialog, give that surface its own host; the Scaffold host is under it.

title: TodayPanel
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column and Row inside MonarchSectionCard, with MonarchAgendaList, MonarchCheckboxRow, MonarchBadge and MonarchText
summary: A person's day on a home screen: MonarchSectionCard titled "Today" with today's agenda (MonarchAgendaList for one day) above the tasks due today, overdue first, each a MonarchCheckboxRow with an "Overdue" badge where it applies.
whenToUse: At the top of a home or dashboard screen that answers "what do I have today?" for one person.
whenNotToUse: For several days of events, use MonarchAgendaList on its own. For a full task list with filters, use a list screen.
api: MonarchSectionCard(title = "Today", meta = date) { MonarchText(text = "Schedule", style = MonarchTextStyle.Label); MonarchAgendaList(events, modifier = Modifier.height(…), from = today, days = 1, today = today); MonarchText(text = "Due today", style = MonarchTextStyle.Label); tasks.sortedByDescending { it.overdue }.forEach { Row { MonarchCheckboxRow(checked, onCheckedChange, label = title, modifier = Modifier.weight(1f), description = detail); if (overdue) MonarchBadge(text = "Overdue", tone = MonarchTone.Danger) } } }

options.name: tasks

options.name: MonarchBadge

states.name: day
states.description: The schedule above the tasks.

states.name: loading
states.description: MonarchSectionCard with state = Loading.

states.name: error
states.description: MonarchSectionCard with state = Error, errorMessage and onRetry.

states.name: nothing today
states.description: MonarchSectionCard with state = Empty and emptyMessage "Nothing scheduled and nothing due today.", or a line of text.

appearance: MonarchSectionCard's surface, MonarchAgendaList's day, checkbox rows in default text with muted descriptions, and the danger badge, all in their own appearance in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web TodayPanel is one component with the agenda beside the tasks on wide screens. On a phone the two stack, so Android composes existing parts in a MonarchSectionCard: the agenda, then the tasks. The web's built-in strings, task links (href), lead and meta slots and maxTasks with a "N more" link are the app's choices here: open a task from its row's own action, and add a MonarchLink to the full list. MonarchAgendaList is lazy, so it gets a fixed height inside a scrolling screen. iOS shares the recipe approach.
accessibility: The card title and the section titles (Schedule, Due today) are headings, so TalkBack users can jump between them.
Each task is one MonarchCheckboxRow: one TalkBack element with the checkbox role, its title and detail, and a 48dp row.
Overdue is a badge in words after the task, not a color.
Events are read by MonarchAgendaList with their times.
edgeCases: Keep the task list short on a home screen and link to the full list.
Overdue tasks come first, then the others in the app's order.
Give MonarchAgendaList a fixed height inside a scrolling screen.

name: MonarchToggleBlock
title: ToggleBlock
wrapsNative: MonarchCollapsible (androidx.compose.foundation.clickable, androidx.compose.animation.AnimatedVisibility), androidx.compose.runtime.saveable.rememberSaveable
summary: A collapsible section of a document: a summary line that shows or hides the content indented under it.
whenToUse: In a document or an article, for details most readers can skip: a long explanation, an appendix, the answer to a question.
whenNotToUse: For a section of a settings screen or a form use MonarchCollapsible. For several sections where one opens at a time use an accordion.

options.name: summary
options.description: The line that stays visible; it is the name of the button.

options.name: expanded
options.description: First overload: whether the content is shown, kept by the app, for example to save it with the document.

options.name: onExpandedChange
options.description: First overload: called with the new state when the user activates the summary or uses the TalkBack expand or collapse action.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the block.

options.name: initiallyExpanded
options.description: Second overload: whether the content shows at first. The block then keeps its own state with rememberSaveable.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the user can activate the summary.

options.name: trailingIcon
options.description: A chevron that points down, after the summary; it turns half a turn while expanded. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: expandedLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Expanded" state of MonarchCollapsible.

options.name: collapsedLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Collapsed" state of MonarchCollapsible.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the press, focus and hover interactions of the summary.

options.name: content
options.description: The content that is shown and hidden.

states.name: collapsed
states.description: Only the summary; the content is not composed.

states.name: expanded
states.description: The content shows under the summary, indented 24dp from the start edge; the chevron points up.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The summary and chevron take the disabled text color and the summary does not respond.

appearance: The summary uses the label type in the default text color and the chevron the muted text color, as MonarchCollapsible; there is no surface, so the block sits on the document background in every theme.
platformNotes: The web ToggleBlock is also a Tiptap editor node with an editable summary and keyboard shortcuts; Android has no Monarch rich-text editor, so only the read view is offered, as on iOS. The web names its button "Show section" or "Hide section" and draws a leading chevron; on Android the summary is the name of the button and the state is spoken as "Expanded" or "Collapsed", and the chevron comes after the summary, because the block is MonarchCollapsible, whose icon slot is trailing. Monarch bundles no icons, so the chevron is optional. The uncontrolled overload replaces the web's defaultOpen.
accessibility: The summary line is one button named by the summary, with the state "Expanded" or "Collapsed" and the TalkBack expand and collapse actions.
Hidden content leaves the composition, so TalkBack does not reach it.
The summary line is at least 48dp high and the whole line responds to touch.
The content appears at once when the user has turned animations off.
edgeCases: A long summary wraps; nothing is cut at font scale 2.0.
State inside the content is lost when it is hidden; hoist it if it must survive closing.
The indent is measured from the start edge, so it is on the right in right-to-left layouts.

name: MonarchTheme
title: ToggleButton
wrapsNative: MonarchIconButton (the checked overload: Modifier.toggleable with the checkbox role) and MonarchChip for a toggle with a text label
summary: A button that stays on or off, such as Bold in a text toolbar or "Show archived" above a list: the checked MonarchIconButton and a selectable MonarchChip.
whenToUse: For an option that is switched in place and shown as a button: the checked MonarchIconButton for an icon, MonarchChip for a short text label.
whenNotToUse: For a setting in a list or a form use MonarchSwitchRow. For one choice out of several use MonarchRadioRow or segmented buttons. For an action that does not stay on use MonarchButton.

@Composable fun MonarchChip(text: String, selected: Boolean, onSelectedChange: (Boolean) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, size: MonarchTagSize = MonarchTagSize.Md, enabled: Boolean = true, leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, selectedIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)

options.name: checked / selected
options.description: Whether the option is on. State is hoisted: the app keeps it.

options.name: onCheckedChange / onSelectedChange
options.description: Called with the new value when the user switches the option.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the control.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the user can switch the option.

options.name: label + icon / text
options.description: The icon toggle takes a label, its TalkBack name, and a MonarchIcon with a null content description; MonarchChip takes its text. The name must not change with the state.

states.name: off
states.description: Icon toggle: no fill and the muted icon color. Chip: a hairline border and no fill.

states.name: on
states.description: Icon toggle: the accent subtle fill with the accent strong icon. Chip: the accent tint with accent text and an accent border.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The disabled text color (an on icon toggle keeps a muted fill); taps are ignored.

appearance: An off icon toggle has no fill and the muted icon color, one surface step on hover and press; an on one has the accent subtle fill and the accent strong icon, like the web's pressed tools. A selected chip has the accent tint, accent text and an accent border. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ToggleButton is a button with aria-pressed and the variants default (borderless until pressed) and outline; iOS ships MonarchToggleButtonStyle for the standard Toggle. On Android an icon toggle is the checked overload of MonarchIconButton (ghost until pressed, then the accent tint with the strong accent icon, like the web default; TalkBack reads the label and whether it is checked), and a toggle with a text label is a selectable MonarchChip. The web outline variant is not offered. The web uncontrolled form (defaultPressed) does not exist: state is hoisted. The icon toggle has the icon button sizes (32, 36 or 40dp) and the chip is 28dp, each inside a 48dp target.
accessibility: The icon toggle has the Checkbox role and is read as checked or not checked with its label; TalkBack says "double-tap to toggle".
MonarchChip exposes a selected state, read as selected or not selected.
Every form reserves a touch target of at least 48dp by 48dp.
A disabled toggle is read as disabled and ignores taps.
On is a change of fill and content color together; the label names the option and does not change with the state.
The chip label scales with the font size setting and is not cut off at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: An icon toggle has no visible text, so its label is required and is the TalkBack name.
A long chip label grows the chip instead of being cut off; keep it to a few words.
There is one icon toggle look; the web outline variant is not offered.

name: MonarchTheme
title: ToggleGroup
wrapsNative: A Row of selectable MonarchChips for any number pressed; MonarchSegmentedControl (Modifier.selectable with the radio button role) for at most one
summary: Related toggle buttons in one row, with any number pressed or at most one: selectable MonarchChips or a MonarchSegmentedControl.
whenToUse: For two to five related options that are each on or off, such as Bold, Italic and Underline, or an optional single choice that can be released, such as a text alignment.
whenNotToUse: For a required single choice that switches views, use the single-choice segmented buttons as in SegmentedControl. For one on or off option use a toggle button or MonarchSwitchRow. For filters with many options use MonarchTag.
api: @Composable fun MonarchChip(text: String, selected: Boolean, onSelectedChange: (Boolean) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, size: MonarchTagSize = MonarchTagSize.Md, enabled: Boolean = true, leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, selectedIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)

@Composable fun MonarchSegmentedControlScope.Segment(selected: Boolean, onClick: () -> Unit, label: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, count: Int? = null, suffix: String? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)

options.name: checked
options.description: Multi-choice (MonarchChip selected): whether this item is pressed. State is hoisted: the app keeps the set of pressed items.

options.name: onSelectedChange
options.description: Multi-choice (MonarchChip): called with the new state of this item.

options.name: selected
options.description: Single choice (Segment): whether this item is the pressed one.

options.name: onClick
options.description: Single choice (Segment): called when the item is pressed. To let the pressed item be released (the web's single type without required), store null when the pressed item is pressed again.

options.name: size
options.description: The height of the segments (Sm, Md, Lg) or of the chips (Sm, Md); the touch target stays 48dp.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Disables one item.

options.name: icon
options.description: An icon before the label: icon on Segment, leadingIcon on MonarchChip. There is no check mark.

options.name: label
options.description: The option's text, with a count when needed (Segment has count, a chip puts it in the text).

options.name: modifier (row)
options.description: Give the row a name with Modifier.semantics { contentDescription = "Text style" }, as the web requires an aria-label.

states.name: pressed
states.description: Chip: the accent tint with accent text and an accent border. Segment: the raised indicator under the item.

states.name: not pressed
states.description: Chip: a hairline border and no fill. Segment: the muted track.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The disabled text color; taps are ignored.

appearance: Pressed chips take the accent tint, accent text and an accent border; the segmented control is a muted track with one raised indicator (the surface with a hairline in light themes, one surface step up in dark ones) that slides to the chosen item. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ToggleGroup is a row of separate toggle buttons with one Tab stop, arrow keys, Home and End, a loop option, variants, sizes and icon-only items; iOS ships a MonarchToggleGroup wrapper. On Android Monarch ships no type: any number pressed is a row of selectable MonarchChips (spaced, each with its selected state), and at most one is a MonarchSegmentedControl (the RadioButton role and selection, one raised indicator), each with a 48dp target. Keyboard focus moves item by item, as in every Compose row; the web's roving tab stop and loop are not offered. The web's single type without required (pressing the pressed item releases it) is written by the app in onClick, as the example shows. The chips are 28dp (24dp small) and the segmented control has Sm, Md and Lg. An icon-only segment uses the icon slot with a content description. The web's default and outline variants are not offered.
accessibility: Chips expose a selected state, read as selected or not selected; segments have the RadioButton role and are selected or not selected.
A pressed chip changes fill, text and border together, and the chosen segment is the raised one, so the state is not color alone.
Every item reserves a touch target of at least 48dp by 48dp.
A disabled item is read as disabled and ignores taps.
Items follow the layout direction, and labels are not cut at font scale 2.0 in a short row.
The row is named by the app with a content description.
edgeCases: Segments share the row width when it is filled; keep labels to one or two words. Chips wrap to the next line in a FlowRow.
More than five options become too narrow for a segmented control on a phone; use chips instead.

states.name: actions
states.description: Icon actions sit at the end of the top app bar; each is a MonarchIconButton with a 48dp target.

states.name: overflow
states.description: Further actions are MonarchMenuItems in a menu opened from a More MonarchIconButton.

states.name: filters
states.description: MonarchChips under the bar show the selected filter with a fill and a check mark slot.

states.name: scrolled
states.description: With a TopAppBarScrollBehavior the bar changes to the scrolled container color or collapses (system behavior).

states.name: disabled
states.description: An MonarchIconButton or MonarchChip with enabled = false uses the disabled colors and is announced as disabled.

appearance: The app bars use the colors Monarch maps to the Material scheme: the canvas or raised background role for the container and the default text role for the title and icons. Filter chips use the outline border, and the accent subtle fill when selected. High-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colors.
platformNotes: The web Toolbar is a role="toolbar" row with search at the start, grouped controls, trailing controls, a filters row and roving arrow-key focus. On Android the app bars are the toolbar: the system places the actions, the app moves extra actions into an overflow menu, and a hardware keyboard moves between them with Tab. Search is a MonarchSearchBar or the Material 3 SearchBar under or in place of the bar. Monarch ships no toolbar type. iOS uses its navigation bar and bottom bar in the same way.
accessibility: Each icon action is a MonarchIconButton with a content description ("Search", "More actions"), read as a button (system behavior).
MonarchIconButtons and MonarchChips have 48dp touch targets (system behavior).
A MonarchChip is read with its label and its selected state.
The title of a TopAppBar is plain text; mark it as a heading with Modifier.semantics { heading() } when the screen has no other heading.
edgeCases: Too many actions crowd the bar on a 320dp phone; keep one to three and move the rest to the overflow menu.
A filter row with many chips scrolls horizontally; it does not wrap.
Inside a Scaffold, pass the bar as topBar or bottomBar so the content is padded by its height.

On Android it also opens on a long press, which is the touch equivalent; the side is TooltipAnchorPosition (Above, Below, Start, End) and the delay is the system's. Shows on a long press, which is the touch equivalent of hover; and on keyboard focus.
Long text wraps at font scale 2.0.

Tooltips on controls inside a scrolling list follow the control while visible and hide when it scrolls away.

title: TransferOwnershipFlow
wrapsNative: MonarchBottomSheet holding MonarchStepper, MonarchEntityPicker, MonarchConsequenceList and MonarchButton, opened from a danger MonarchButton
summary: Hands a workspace to another member in three steps inside a bottom sheet: choose the new owner, review what changes for both sides, then confirm.
whenToUse: In workspace or organization settings, for the owner to transfer ownership to another eligible member.
whenNotToUse: For changing an ordinary member's role use a role picker on the member row; for deleting the workspace use a danger-zone confirmation.
api: MonarchBottomSheet(onDismissRequest = …, title = "Transfer ownership") { Column(Modifier.verticalScroll(rememberScrollState())) { MonarchStepper(steps = steps, current = step); when (step) { 0 -> MonarchEntityPicker(label = "New owner", entities = members, selected = newOwner, onSelectedChange = …); 1 -> MonarchConsequenceList(items = …, heading = "What changes"); else -> MonarchText(…) }; Row { MonarchButton(text = "Back", variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Ghost, …); MonarchButton(text = "Continue" or "Transfer ownership", variant = Primary or Danger, enabled = newOwner != null, …) } } }

options.name: members
options.description: Members who could become the owner, without the current owner; members who cannot (not an admin) are listed with enabled = false and a hint saying why.

options.name: steps
options.description: Choose the new owner, What changes, Confirm.

options.name: consequences
options.description: What changes for you (your new role, what you can no longer do) and for the new owner, with Changed, Removed and Warning kinds.

options.name: your role
options.description: Add on the review step when the owner can choose their role after the transfer.

options.name: re-authentication
options.description: Ask before running the transfer when the product requires it.

options.name: result
options.description: "<name> is now the owner.", or "Waiting for <name> to accept" when the new owner must accept.

states.name: choose
states.description: The entity picker; Continue is disabled until a member is chosen.

states.name: review
states.description: The consequence list for both sides.

states.name: confirm
states.description: A sentence naming the new owner and a danger Transfer ownership button.

states.name: done
states.description: The sheet closes and a success banner names the new owner.

appearance: The Material 3 bottom sheet on the raised surface with its drag handle; inside, MonarchStepper, the entity picker field, the consequence list with its kind marks and the danger button keep their own appearance in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web TransferOwnershipFlow is one component built on WizardDialog, AssigneePicker and ConsequenceList with built-in strings, eligibility by role, a role select, step-up authentication and a pending-acceptance screen. On a phone a multi-step dialog is a bottom sheet, so Android composes a MonarchBottomSheet with MonarchStepper and the same parts; eligibility, the role choice, step-up and acceptance are the app's additions to the recipe (see options). The system back gesture closes the sheet. iOS has no entry yet.
accessibility: The sheet title is a heading and MonarchStepper says which step of three is current.
Members who cannot become the owner are read as disabled, with the reason in their hint.
Each consequence is read with its kind in words.
The final button names the action ("Transfer ownership") and uses the danger variant, not color alone.
Continue is disabled, and read as disabled, until a member is chosen.
edgeCases: Opening the sheet again starts at the first step with nobody chosen.
Dismissing the sheet by dragging or Back cancels without transferring.
With nobody eligible, show a message instead of the picker and keep Continue disabled.

name: MonarchTreeView
title: TreeView
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn, androidx.compose.foundation.clickable, androidx.compose.material3.Text, androidx.compose.material3.CircularProgressIndicator
summary: A hierarchy people can browse and pick from, such as departments, goals and key results or a document outline, drawn as indented rows in a lazy list.
whenToUse: For nested data of unknown depth where people open branches and pick one or more items: an org chart, a folder tree, an outline.
whenNotToUse: For one level of sections that open and close, use MonarchCollapsible or an accordion. For two levels, a list with section headers is easier to scan. For moving between screens, use navigation.

states.description: The expand icon points to the end; the row reads "Collapsed, Level 1".

states.name: expanded parent
states.description: The icon turns a quarter turn and the children follow, indented by one level.

states.name: selected
states.description: The subtle accent fill, a solid accent bar at the start, semibold strong accent text and the selected state.

states.name: current
states.description: Semibold strong accent text.

states.name: loading
states.description: A row with a small progress ring and "Loading" under the parent; the ring is left out when animations are off.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Disabled text; the row and its expand button ignore taps.

appearance: Rows are at least 48dp tall with small rounded corners, indented 20dp per level. Labels are body text in the default text color, descriptions muted caption text, the expand icon muted. The selected row has the subtle accent fill with strong accent text and a solid accent bar at its start edge. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web TreeView implements the WAI-ARIA tree pattern by hand: roving focus, arrow keys, typeahead, single or multiple selection, aria-current, lazy children and row actions. Compose has no tree, so Monarch builds one on a LazyColumn (iOS uses the system List with children instead). Expansion and selection are hoisted; the web's uncontrolled defaultExpanded and defaultSelected are not offered. Lazy children are asked for with onLoadChildren and shown loading through the loading set, where the web awaits a promise; a failed load is the app's to show, for example with MonarchInlineErrorRetry, and to close. With a hardware keyboard the arrow keys towards the end and the start open and close a parent; typeahead, Home and End and the select-all shortcut are not offered, and focus moves with the system's directional focus. The outline variant with indentation guides and the renderActions slot are not offered: put row actions in the screen's top bar or a menu on the selected item. Android has no tree role, so the level is part of the state TalkBack reads. The parity map lists collapsible and checkbox: rows open with their own expand button rather than MonarchCollapsible, because a tree row holds no content of its own, and multiple selection uses the selected state and the start bar rather than a checkbox per row.
accessibility: Each row is one TalkBack element: the label and description, then the state, "Expanded, Level 1", "Collapsed, Level 1" or "Level 2".
Parents offer the TalkBack expand and collapse actions on the row.
The expand icon is a separate button named "Expand Engineering" or "Collapse Engineering", with a 48dp touch target reserved in the layout.
With selection, rows expose the selected state; without selection, rows have the button role.
Selection is shown by the start bar and semibold text as well as the color.
Disabled items are announced as disabled and ignore taps.
The "Loading" row is a polite live region.
Labels wrap at the largest font size instead of being cut off.
edgeCases: A parent with an empty children list opens to nothing.
Expanding an item with hasChildren and no children calls onLoadChildren once per opening; keep the id in loading until the children arrive.
Deep trees indent 20dp per level; past five or six levels at 320dp wide the labels get narrow.
The tree is a lazy list: it cannot sit inside another vertical scroll without a bounded height.

summary: Text cut after a few lines, with a button that shows the rest when the text is longer than that.
whenToUse: For long free text in a list, a card or a detail screen, such as a description or a note, where the first lines are enough most of the time.
whenNotToUse: For a title that must stay on one line without a way to expand, use MonarchText with maxLines = 1 and TextOverflow.Ellipsis. For text that is the main content of a screen, show it whole.

options.name: text
options.description: The text.

options.name: expanded
options.description: Whether the whole text is shown. The first form keeps this state itself, in rememberSaveable, starting cut.

options.name: onExpandedChange
options.description: Called with the new state when the user activates the button.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the text and its button.

options.name: maxLines
options.description: How many lines are shown before the text is cut. Values below 1 count as 1.

options.name: expandable
options.description: Whether a button shows the rest when the text is cut.

options.name: style
options.description: The type role of the text.

options.name: showMoreLabel
options.description: The button label while cut. null uses monarch_truncatedtext_show_more, "Show more".

options.name: showLessLabel

states.name: cut
states.description: The text is longer than maxLines: the last line ends with an ellipsis and a "Show more" button follows.

states.name: expanded
states.description: All lines are shown and the button reads "Show less".

states.name: fits
states.description: The text is within maxLines: no button.

appearance: The text uses the chosen type role in the content color of the surface; the button is a small ghost MonarchButton in the default text color, in every theme.
platformNotes: The web tooltip option is not offered: there is no hover on touch, and TalkBack reads the whole text without it. The web accepts inline elements (links, emphasis); this takes a plain String. The line limit is called maxLines, as on the Compose Text, where iOS calls it lineLimit. Whether the text is cut is read from the text layout (TextLayoutResult.hasVisualOverflow), so no hidden copy of the text is measured. The button is a ghost MonarchButton in the default text color where the web uses the link color, because Monarch for Android has no link-styled button yet.
accessibility: TalkBack reads the whole text whether or not it is cut, because the cut is only a line limit on one Text.
The button is a separate button whose label changes between "Show more" and "Show less"; both labels can be replaced.
The button reserves a 48dp touch target.
The change of height is animated with the Monarch motion spec, which is immediate when animations are turned off.
At the largest font size the expanded text and the button are not cut off.
edgeCases: The button appears after the first layout pass, when the text layout is known.
With expandable = false the cut text has no visible way to expand; use it only where the whole text is one tap away.
An empty string shows nothing and no button.
With expanded = true and text that fits, the button still shows so the state can be turned off.
The button has horizontal padding, so its label is indented from the text by that padding.

title: TwoFactorSetup
wrapsNative: MonarchDialog with a close button and Cancel and Next actions over three steps: an optional androidx.compose.foundation.Image of a QR code the app draws and MonarchCopyField for the setup key; MonarchOtpPinInput; MonarchRecoveryCodes
summary: A recipe, not a component: a dialog that turns on two-step verification in three steps: scan a QR code or enter a key in an authenticator app, enter a code from it, and save the recovery codes.
whenToUse: In account security settings, when a person turns on two-step verification with an authenticator app.
whenNotToUse: To ask for a code at sign-in, use MonarchOtpPinInput alone. To re-confirm a signed-in person, use MonarchStepUpAuthDialog.
api: MonarchDialog(onDismissRequest = { open = false }, title = title, description = description, closeButton = true, actions = { Cancel and Next }, content = { … })
Image(painter = qrCode, contentDescription = "QR code for the authenticator app") — qrCode drawn by the app
MonarchCopyField(value = secret, label = "Setup key")
MonarchOtpPinInput(value = code, onValueChange = …, label = "6-digit code", errorText = codeError)
MonarchRecoveryCodes(codes = codes, onAcknowledge = { … })

options.name: secret / account
options.description: The shared key from the server and the name of the account it belongs to, shown under the QR code.

options.name: qrCode
options.description: A QR code of the otpauth address for scanning, drawn by the app's own generator. Without it only the key is shown.

options.name: step
options.description: The current step, kept with rememberSaveable. The dialog title and the Next button follow it.

states.name: scan
states.description: The QR code when the app provides one, the account, and the setup key with a copy button.

states.name: verify
states.description: A six-cell code field; an incomplete or rejected code shows the field's error.

states.name: recovery
states.description: The recovery codes with copy, save or share, and the "I have saved my recovery codes" acknowledgement, which finishes the setup.

appearance: Existing Monarch components in the theme: the dialog's title, description and footer actions, the copy field's monospaced key, the code cells and the recovery codes panel. A QR code must stay dark on light in every theme so scanners can read it; draw it that way in the app.
platformNotes: The web's TwoFactorSetup is a dialog with a QR code as its first step, and so is this recipe: a centred MonarchDialog with a close button, a step count, Cancel and Next. iOS draws the QR code with Core Image; Android has no first-party QR generator and Monarch adds no dependency, so the recipe shows an app-supplied Painter when there is one (for example from ZXing in the app); the setup key stays as the fallback for entering it in the app by hand.
accessibility: The dialog is named by its title, which follows the step, and the step count is read with it.
The key is copied with a button and spelled out by the copy field; the QR image has a description when shown.
The code field reads its error.
Recovery codes are read character by character, and a missing acknowledgement is announced.
edgeCases: Without a QR painter the step shows the key alone.
Long keys wrap in the copy field; the code field accepts the keyboard's one-time code suggestion.

wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedTextField (through MonarchTextField)
summary: A text field in which the person types a name, such as "acme-site", to confirm an irreversible action.

whenNotToUse: For an action that can be undone, use an undo snackbar (MonarchSnackbarHost) instead. For ordinary text input use MonarchTextField.

options.name: onMatchChange
options.description: Called each time the match state flips, not for the first state.

states.name: mismatch shown

states.name: matching
