states.name: disabled
states.description: The text field's disabled state.

appearance: The same field as MonarchTextField: the input border role, the focus ring role when focused, the danger strong role for the border and message in the error state, in every theme.
platformNotes: The web shows the phrase in a monospaced face inside the label; MonarchTextField takes a plain string label, so the default label puts the phrase in quotation marks, as iOS does. Matching is the web's rule: case-sensitive, ignoring surrounding white space. The web's static phraseMatches is MonarchTypeToConfirmInputDefaults.matches, since a Kotlin function cannot carry a static member. The web announces through a role=status region; Android uses a polite live region on a node that is always present. The value is hoisted (value and onValueChange), so there is no uncontrolled defaultValue.
accessibility: The field is read as a text field whose label names the phrase.
"Text matches" is announced through a polite live region when the typed text starts to match.
The mismatch error is text and the error semantics property, set only when showMismatch is true.
The error never shows while typing unless the app sets showMismatch.
Autocorrection and capitalisation are off, so the keyboard does not change the typed name.
The field is a Material 3 text field with its 48dp minimum height; text grows with the font size setting.
edgeCases: Spaces and line breaks around the typed text and around the phrase are ignored; spaces inside are not.
An empty phrase matches empty text.
onMatchChange is not called for the first state, only for changes.
The component does not disable any button; use onMatchChange or MonarchTypeToConfirmInputDefaults.matches for that.

name: MonarchTypingIndicator
title: TypingIndicator

summary: "Ana is typing…" under a conversation, with three decorative bouncing dots, worded for one, two or several people.
whenToUse: Under a message list or a comment thread, while other people are writing.
whenNotToUse: For the presence of people who are not writing use an avatar stack or a status dot. For the progress of a task use MonarchProgress.
api: @Composable fun MonarchTypingIndicator(names: List<String>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, text: String? = null, reserveSpace: Boolean = true, announceChanges: Boolean = true)

options.name: names
options.description: Who is typing now, as their names should be read, newest last. Leave out the person using the app.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the component.

options.name: text
options.description: Replaces the built-in sentence. Ignored while names is empty.

options.name: reserveSpace
options.description: Keeps the height of one line while nobody is typing.

options.name: announceChanges
options.description: Makes the element a polite live region, so each new sentence is announced.

states.name: nobody
states.description: Nothing is drawn. With reserveSpace the height of one line is kept.

states.name: one
states.description: "Ana is typing…"

states.name: two
states.description: "Ana and Ben are typing…"

states.name: several
states.description: "Several people are typing…"

states.name: animations off
states.description: The dots stand still in the muted text color.

platformNotes: The web takes people with an id and a messages object with three functions; Android takes names and one text override, as iOS does. The built-in wording is three string resources. The web fades the dots with opacity; Android moves between two text color roles instead, because Monarch does not dim colors with alpha. The sentence wraps instead of being ellipsized, so it is never cut at a large font size.

The element is a polite live region, so a new sentence is announced without moving focus, unless announceChanges is false.
The element stays in the layout while nobody is typing, so the first sentence after silence is announced as a change.
While nobody is typing the element has no text and TalkBack skips it.
The dots stand still when the user has turned animations off.
The text and the dots grow with the font size setting.
edgeCases: Long names wrap onto more lines; with reserveSpace only one line is held while nobody is typing.
The built-in strings name at most two people; three or more give "Several people are typing…".
Pass the names in the order they should be read; the first two are used.

title: UndoToast
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.SnackbarHostState.showSnackbar(message, actionLabel, withDismissAction, duration) returning androidx.compose.material3.SnackbarResult
summary: "Note deleted. Undo": a snackbar with an Undo action for a change the app already applied, whose result decides between undoing it and committing it.
whenToUse: For reversible, low-stakes actions the app applies at once, such as deleting or archiving one item, where a confirmation dialog would slow people down.
whenNotToUse: For destructive actions that cannot be reversed, confirm first with a dialog. For a message without an action, use a plain snackbar.
api: suspend fun SnackbarHostState.showSnackbar(message: String, actionLabel: String? = null, withDismissAction: Boolean = false, duration: SnackbarDuration = if (actionLabel == null) SnackbarDuration.Short else SnackbarDuration.Indefinite): SnackbarResult
enum class SnackbarResult { Dismissed, ActionPerformed }
@Composable fun MonarchSnackbarHost(hostState: SnackbarHostState, modifier: Modifier = Modifier)

options.name: message
options.description: What just happened, in the past tense: "Note deleted".

options.name: actionLabel
options.description: "Undo", in the app's strings.

options.name: duration
options.description: Use SnackbarDuration.Long (about 10 seconds) so the snackbar closes and the change commits; Material 3 extends it when an accessibility service needs more time.

states.name: ActionPerformed
states.description: The person pressed Undo: revert the change, then show a short "Restored" snackbar.

states.name: Dismissed
states.description: The snackbar timed out, was swiped away or dismissed: commit, for example run the deferred server delete.

appearance: A Material 3 snackbar in MonarchSnackbarHost: the inverse surface with the Undo action in the accent color for the inverse surface, 8dp corners. The same mapping in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web useUndoToast is a hook that commits when the toast closes for any reason and calls onUndo and onCommit at most once. On Android showSnackbar already suspends until the snackbar closes and says how: ActionPerformed or Dismissed, so the recipe is a when on the result and Monarch ships no API. The web countdown bar and undoAltText are not offered: a Material snackbar has no progress and its action is named by its label. A snackbar queued behind another waits rather than pushing it out; commit before showing the next one when that matters. When the coroutine is cancelled (the screen leaves), showSnackbar throws CancellationException; commit in the view model in that case. iOS composes MonarchToast with its own timer.
accessibility: The snackbar is a polite live region: TalkBack reads the message and the action when it appears.
The Undo action is a button with a 48dp touch target, and TalkBack offers it in the actions menu.
Material 3 keeps the snackbar on screen longer when an accessibility service asks for a longer timeout.
edgeCases: Showing a second undo snackbar while one is open queues it; the first still commits on its own result.
The person can swipe the snackbar away; that is Dismissed and commits.

name: MonarchUnsavedChangesGuard
title: UnsavedChangesGuard
wrapsNative: androidx.activity.compose.BackHandler with androidx.compose.material3.AlertDialog and MonarchButton
summary: Warns before back or the screen's own Close throws away unsaved changes, with Keep editing, Discard changes and an optional Save and leave.
whenToUse: On an edit screen or a sheet with a form, where leaving without saving loses what the person typed.
whenNotToUse: When changes are saved as the person types (show a save status instead), or when the edit is so small that losing it does not matter.

enum class MonarchUnsavedChangesGuardLeaveReason { Discard, Save }
class MonarchUnsavedChangesGuardLabels(title: String? = null, message: String? = null, keepEditing: String? = null, discard: String? = null, save: String? = null, saveFailed: String? = null)

options.name: hasChanges
options.description: Whether there are unsaved changes. While false, back is not intercepted.

options.name: open
options.description: Whether the question is shown. Set it to true from the screen's Close or Cancel when there are changes; back sets it through onOpenChange.

options.name: onOpenChange
options.description: Called with true when back asks, and with false when the person stays (Keep editing, back, a tap outside) and before onLeave.

options.name: onLeave
options.description: Leaves the screen (pops the back stack or closes the sheet), with Discard at once or Save after onSave returned.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the dialog.

options.name: guardsBack
options.description: Whether system back is intercepted while there are changes. Set it to false when the screen handles back itself and opens the guard.

options.name: onSave
options.description: Saves the changes; when given, Save and leave is offered. While it runs the screen cannot be left. Throw to report a failure.

options.name: details
options.description: Extra content under the message, such as the list of unsaved fields.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the question, the message, the three choices and the save failure.

states.name: no changes
states.description: Back works as usual; nothing is shown.

states.name: changes
states.description: Back is intercepted and opens the question instead of leaving.

states.name: asking
states.description: An AlertDialog titled "Discard unsaved changes?" with Keep editing (ghost), Discard changes (danger) and, with onSave, Save and leave (primary).

states.name: saving
states.description: Save and leave shows its progress indicator and reads "Loading"; the other choices are disabled and back and taps outside do nothing.

states.name: save failed
states.description: "Your changes could not be saved. Try again." in the danger strong color inside the dialog, announced; the person stays.

appearance: A Material 3 AlertDialog on the raised background Monarch maps to it, the message in the muted text color, Discard changes as a danger MonarchButton, Save and leave as a primary one and Keep editing as a ghost one. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web UnsavedChangesGuard is a dialog plus a hook that blocks router navigation, intercepts same-origin links and asks the browser to warn before the tab closes. Android has no links or tabs to close: the guard intercepts system back (gesture and button, including predictive back) with BackHandler while there are changes, and the app's own Close opens it through open. Components do not navigate, so onLeave pops the back stack. The web's open and onOpenChange are kept; iOS uses an isPresented binding and a view modifier. Unlike the iOS confirmation dialog, the Android dialog stays open while saving, as on the web, so the busy state and a failure are shown in it. The web's error prop and errorMessage function are not offered: a failure shows labels.saveFailed, because exception messages are not written for people. A ModalBottomSheet's own swipe-to-dismiss is not intercepted: guard it with the sheet state's confirmValueChange while hasChanges is true.
accessibility: System behavior: TalkBack reads the dialog's title and message, and back or a tap outside chooses to stay.
The destructive choice is named "Discard changes", so it does not depend on its danger color.
Each choice is a MonarchButton with a 48dp touch target; Save and leave reads "Loading" while saving and the other choices are disabled.
A failed save is shown as text and announced through a polite live region that is always present in the dialog.
While the save runs, back cannot leave the screen, so a gesture cannot lose the changes.
edgeCases: Setting open to true while hasChanges is false still shows the question; check hasChanges before opening it from the screen's Close.
A save cancelled because the screen left the composition is not shown as a failure.
Place one guard per screen; two enabled BackHandlers compete and the last one composed wins.

examples.title: Leaving with unsaved changes
examples.template:
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space3)) {
    MonarchTextField(value = name, onValueChange = { name = it }, label = {{fieldLabel}})
    Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space2)) {
        MonarchButton(text = {{save}}, onClick = {}, variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Primary)
        MonarchButton(text = {{leave}}, onClick = { asking = true })
    }
    MonarchText(text = "Current page: " + page)
    MonarchUnsavedChangesGuard(
        hasChanges = true,
        open = asking,
        onOpenChange = { asking = it },
        onLeave = { page = {{leftPage}} },
        onSave = { delay(600) },
        labels = MonarchUnsavedChangesGuardLabels(
            title = {{dialog.title}},
            message = {{dialog.message}},
            keepEditing = {{dialog.keepEditing}},
            discard = {{dialog.discard}},
            save = {{dialog.save}},
        ),
    )
}

name: MonarchUploadQueue
title: UploadQueue
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of rows with MonarchFileTypeIcon, MonarchProgress (androidx.compose.material3.LinearProgressIndicator) and MonarchButton (androidx.compose.material3.TextButton), and a polite liveRegion
summary: The files being uploaded: progress and status per file, cancel, retry and remove, and a summary with the total progress.
whenToUse: While the app uploads files the user picked, for example after MonarchFileUpload, so they can follow, cancel and retry each one.
whenNotToUse: For one picture or video field use MonarchMediaUpload. For a single long task use MonarchProgress. For transfers the user does not need to manage, show a notification from WorkManager instead.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchUploadQueue(items: List<MonarchUploadQueueItem>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, showSummary: Boolean = true, labels: MonarchUploadQueueLabels = MonarchUploadQueueLabels(), onCancel: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, onRetry: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, onRemove: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, onClearFinished: (() -> Unit)? = null)

public data class MonarchUploadQueueItem(id: String, name: String, status: MonarchUploadStatus, size: Long? = null, contentType: String? = null, progress: Float? = null, errorMessage: String? = null, retryable: Boolean = true, detail: String? = null)

public data class MonarchUploadQueueCounts(total: Int, queued: Int, uploading: Int, done: Int, failed: Int, cancelled: Int) { public val active: Int; public val finished: Int; public companion object { public fun of(items: List<MonarchUploadQueueItem>): MonarchUploadQueueCounts } }

public class MonarchUploadQueueLabels(title: String? = null, queued: String? = null, uploading: ((Int?) -> String)? = null, done: String? = null, failed: ((String?) -> String)? = null, cancelled: String? = null, retry: String? = null, retryLabel: ((String) -> String)? = null, cancel: String? = null, cancelLabel: ((String) -> String)? = null, remove: String? = null, removeLabel: ((String) -> String)? = null, clearFinished: String? = null, progressLabel: ((String) -> String)? = null, totalProgress: String? = null, summary: ((MonarchUploadQueueCounts) -> String)? = null, announceDone: ((String) -> String)? = null, announceFailed: ((String, String?) -> String)? = null, announceFinished: ((MonarchUploadQueueCounts) -> String)? = null, formatSize: ((Long) -> String)? = null)

options.name: items
options.description: The uploads, in display order. The app passes them again when a status or a progress changes.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the queue.

options.name: showSummary
options.description: Shows the heading, the summary ("2 of 5 uploaded · 1 failed"), the clear button and the total progress.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string and announcement, and the size format.

options.name: onCancel
options.description: Cancels a queued or uploading file by id. Adds cancel buttons.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Retries a failed or cancelled, retryable file by id. Adds retry buttons.

options.name: onRemove
options.description: Removes a file that ended from the list by id. Adds remove buttons.

options.name: onClearFinished
options.description: Removes every file that ended. Adds a header button while there is one.

options.name: MonarchUploadQueueItem.progress
options.description: 0 to 1 while uploading; null shows a moving bar.

options.name: MonarchUploadQueueItem.detail
options.description: Replaces the status line, for example "Checking for viruses".

options.name: MonarchUploadQueueItem.retryable
options.description: false hides Retry for this file.

states.name: queued
states.description: "Waiting" in the muted color and a cancel button.

states.name: uploading
states.description: "Uploading… 40%", a progress bar and a cancel button; without a progress, "Uploading…" and a moving bar.

states.name: done
states.description: "Uploaded" in the strong success color and a remove button.

states.name: failed
states.description: "Upload failed" with the reason in the strong danger color, retry and remove buttons.

states.name: cancelled
states.description: "Cancelled" in the muted color, retry and remove buttons.

states.name: empty
states.description: Only the heading.

appearance: File names use the default text color, sizes and the summary the muted color, and the status the strong success, strong danger or muted color. Progress bars are MonarchProgress in the accent color on the emphasis background. Every theme uses the same roles.
platformNotes: The web shows an image thumbnail when one is given; here each row shows MonarchFileTypeIcon, as on iOS, because Monarch takes no image URLs. The parity map names a LazyColumn; the rows are a Column, because a lazy list cannot sit inside the vertically scrolling screens where a queue usually appears, and a queue holds the uploads of one task. The web's cancel and remove are icon buttons; Monarch bundles no icons, so they are text buttons ("Cancel", "Remove") whose TalkBack names include the file name. The web moves focus to the next row when a row is removed; Android does not move TalkBack focus. Progress is a fraction from 0 to 1 rather than 0 to 100. The web's headingLevel has no Android equivalent. Transfers that must survive the app going to the background belong to WorkManager in the app; the queue only shows them. MonarchUploadStatus is shared with MonarchAttachmentChip and lives in its package.
accessibility: The heading is a heading for TalkBack; the summary is read after it.
Each row's name, size and status are one TalkBack element; status is written in words, so it never depends on color.
Progress bars are named "Upload progress of" and the file name, and the total bar "Total upload progress"; they report their range.
Cancel, retry and remove are separate MonarchButtons with 48dp touch targets, named with the file name ("Retry upload of a.pdf").
Finished and failed files are announced ("a.pdf uploaded."), and when the last active upload of several ends, the result is announced, through an always-present polite live region.
edgeCases: Total progress leaves out failed and cancelled files, and is weighted by size only when every remaining file has a size.
Retry is not offered for items with retryable = false.
Long names wrap to two lines and are then ellipsized.
The summary's English wording is fixed ("1 of 4 uploaded"); pass labels.summary for languages with plural forms.
Nothing is announced on the first composition, only on changes.

examples.title: Mixed statuses
examples.template:
MonarchUploadQueue(

    onCancel = { id -> items = items.map { if (it.id == id) it.copy(status = MonarchUploadStatus.Cancelled) else it } },
    onRetry = { id -> items = items.map { if (it.id == id) it.copy(status = MonarchUploadStatus.Queued, errorMessage = null) else it } },
    onRemove = { id -> items = items.filterNot { it.id == id } },
    onClearFinished = { items = items.filter { it.status.active } },
)

    onClearFinished = { items = items.filter { it.status.active } },

name: MonarchUptimeBar
title: UptimeBar
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.Canvas with pointerInput tap gestures for the segments; androidx.compose.material3.TooltipBox with RichTooltip (a persistent rememberTooltipState and a custom PopupPositionProvider) for the details of a period
summary: A row of per-period status segments, usually one per day, with the details of a period one tap away and the overall uptime under it.
whenToUse: On a status page, a service tile or a monitor row, to show how a service did over the last days or hours, period by period.
whenNotToUse: For a trend of a measured value, use MonarchLineChart or MonarchSparkline; for the share of each state over the whole period, MonarchStackedProportionBar; for one current state, MonarchStatusBadge.
api: @Composable fun MonarchUptimeBar(segments: List<MonarchUptimeBarSegment>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, label: String? = null, description: String? = null, overallUptime: Double? = null, showOverallUptime: Boolean = true, startLabel: String? = null, endLabel: String? = null, thresholds: MonarchUptimeBarThresholds = MonarchUptimeBarThresholds(), size: MonarchUptimeBarSize = MonarchUptimeBarSize.Md, showLegend: Boolean = false, uptimeDigits: Int = 2, activeIndex: Int? = null, onActiveIndexChange: ((Int?) -> Unit)? = null, summary: String? = null, labels: MonarchUptimeBarLabels = MonarchUptimeBarLabels(), onSegmentSelect: ((MonarchUptimeBarSegment) -> Unit)? = null)
class MonarchUptimeBarSegment(id: String, label: String, status: MonarchUptimeBarStatus? = null, uptime: Double? = null, details: List<MonarchUptimeBarDetail> = emptyList(), note: String? = null)
class MonarchUptimeBarDetail(label: String, value: String)
class MonarchUptimeBarThresholds(operational: Double = 99.9, degraded: Double = 99.0)
enum class MonarchUptimeBarStatus { Operational, Degraded, Partial, Down, Maintenance, NoData }
enum class MonarchUptimeBarSize { Sm, Md }

class MonarchUptimeBarLabels(statusNames: Map<MonarchUptimeBarStatus, String> = emptyMap(), uptime: String? = null, overall: ((String) -> String)? = null, legend: String? = null, periods: String? = null, open: String? = null, summary: ((Int, Map<MonarchUptimeBarStatus, Int>, String?) -> String)? = null)

options.name: segments
options.description: The periods, oldest first. Each has an id, a label, and a status or an uptime (or neither, for no data), with optional details and a note.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the whole bar.

options.name: label
options.description: What is monitored, such as a service name: shown above the bar and the bar's spoken name ("Uptime" when null).

options.name: description
options.description: A short line under the label, such as "Last 30 days".

options.name: overallUptime
options.description: The overall uptime in percent. The mean of the measured periods when null.

options.name: showOverallUptime
options.description: Whether the overall uptime is written under the bar.

options.name: startLabel
options.description: Text under the oldest period, such as "30 days ago".

options.name: endLabel
options.description: Text under the newest period, such as "Today".

options.name: thresholds
options.description: The cut points for periods with an uptime but no status: at or above operational is operational, at or above degraded is degraded, below is down.

options.name: size
options.description: The height of the segments: Md 32dp for status pages, Sm 20dp for tiles and rows. The touch area is at least 48dp high either way.

options.name: showLegend
options.description: Lists the names of the colors under the bar. With several bars on a screen, show it on one.

options.name: uptimeDigits
options.description: The decimal places of uptime percentages.

options.name: activeIndex
options.description: The inspected period, used when onActiveIndexChange is set. Give several bars one state to inspect the same period on each. An index outside the periods is ignored.

options.name: onActiveIndexChange
options.description: Makes the inspection controlled: called with the period the user taps, or null when the details close.

options.name: summary
options.description: Replaces the generated spoken summary.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the state names, "Uptime", the overall line, "Legend", "Periods", "Open" and the summary.

options.name: onSegmentSelect
options.description: Opens a period in the app, such as that day's incidents: from the Open button in the details, or from the period's TalkBack action.

states.name: default
states.description: Every segment in its state's color from the start edge, 2dp apart (1dp when segments get narrower than 4dp); no data is a muted, outlined segment.

states.name: inspected
states.description: The inspected segment has a 2dp ring in the default text color, set off by a hairline of the surface color.

states.name: details open
states.description: After a tap, a Material 3 rich tooltip over the segment shows the period as its title, the state with its marker, the uptime, the details and the note, and Open with onSegmentSelect. A tap outside closes it and clears the inspection.

states.name: empty
states.description: No periods: an empty touch area, and a summary of zero periods.

appearance: Operational periods use the success solid color, degraded the warning solid, partial outages the warning strong, down the danger solid and maintenance the info solid; no data is the muted background with a default border. The label is body text, the description, start and end labels muted caption text, and the overall line caption text in the default color. The details take the Material 3 rich tooltip colors of the Monarch theme. Every color is a theme role, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes are covered.
platformNotes: Touch replaces hover: the web shows a tooltip while the pointer moves and keyboard arrows move through the days; here a tap opens the details in a Material 3 RichTooltip placed over the segment, and TalkBack users swipe through one element per period. Unlike iOS, where the bar is one adjustable element, Android follows the Monarch chart pattern of one image element with the summary followed by one element per period, because TalkBack has no adjustable role for custom views in Compose. The parameters start with segments, the only required one, as the Compose guidelines ask; iOS takes the label first. The web dims the other segments while one is inspected; here only the ring marks it, because Monarch does not dim colors with alpha. The web meta slot (a badge in the header) is not offered: put the bar in a Row with the badge. The web exports a separate UptimeLegend; here showLegend draws the same list. The web keeps a hidden data table and iOS a chart descriptor; Android has no chart descriptor, and each period element reads all of its details instead. The parity map named chart-frame as a dependency: the bar does not sit in a MonarchChartFrame card, as on the web and iOS, so it fits in tiles and rows; it has its own label line. Segments run from the start edge, so the oldest day is on the right in right to left.
accessibility: The bar is one element with the image role, named by label (or "Uptime"), whose state description is the summary, such as "Periods: 30. Operational 28, Degraded 1, Down 1. Uptime 99.86%". Only the states present are counted.

After it, one element per period in order (traversal index), placed over the period's segment and read as the period and its details, such as "Mar 2: Degraded, Uptime 99.42%, Checks 1,440, Slow responses".
With onSegmentSelect each period element has a custom action "Open, Mar 2"; without it, the elements have no action.
The touch area of the bar is at least 48dp high in both sizes.
Every state has a name in the details, the legend and the summary, so color never carries it alone; no data is drawn hollow.
The label above the bar and the start, end and overall line under it are hidden from TalkBack, because the bar's name and summary say them.
The legend is a traversal group named "Legend"; each entry is read as its state name.
edgeCases: A segment's own status wins over its uptime.
A segment with neither a status nor a finite uptime has no data.
The overall uptime averages only the measured segments; with none it is not shown.
With 90 segments each can be under 3dp wide; a tap still finds the segment under the finger from its position.
An activeIndex outside the segments is ignored.
Tapping outside the details closes them and clears the inspected segment; the details are not reachable with TalkBack, which reads the same text from each period element.
The tooltip and the touch inspection were checked with Robolectric tests, not on a device.

name: MonarchUsageMeter
title: UsageMeter
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.LinearProgressIndicator, androidx.compose.material3.CircularProgressIndicator
summary: Usage against limits: for each metered item, what was used, the limit and a meter that turns to the warning color near the limit and the danger color over it, with the level written as text.
whenToUse: On a billing or plan screen, to show quotas of requests, storage, seats or minutes for the current period.
whenNotToUse: For the progress of a task use MonarchProgress. For one reading against bands use MonarchGauge. The meter only shows usage; upgrading or buying more goes through the app's own flow and the store's billing rules.
api: @Composable fun MonarchUsageMeter(items: List<MonarchUsageMeterItem>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, title: String? = null, period: String? = null, resetsAtMillis: Long? = null, warningAt: Double = 0.8, loading: Boolean = false, announceChanges: Boolean = false, error: String? = null, onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchUsageMeterLabels = MonarchUsageMeterLabels(), announceThresholds: Boolean = false)
class MonarchUsageMeterItem(label: String, used: Double, limit: Double? = null, unit: String? = null, description: String? = null, id: String = label)

class MonarchUsageMeterLabels(amount: ((used: String, limit: String) -> String)? = null, percent: ((percent: String) -> String)? = null, nearLimit: String? = null, overLimit: String? = null, resets: ((date: String) -> String)? = null, loading: String? = null, retry: String? = null)

options.name: items
options.description: The metered items, in display order. An item without a limit shows the count alone.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the meter.

options.name: title
options.description: The heading, already localised.

options.name: period
options.description: The period measured, such as "This month".

options.name: resetsAtMillis
options.description: When the quota resets, in epoch milliseconds (UTC). Written as a medium date in the current locale and the device time zone.

options.name: warningAt
options.description: The share of the limit at which an item is near the limit.

options.name: loading
options.description: Shows a progress indicator and "Loading usage" instead of the items.

options.name: announceChanges
options.description: Makes every item a polite live region, so TalkBack announces an item whose figures or level change while it is on screen.

options.name: error
options.description: An error message shown instead of the items. It wins over loading.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Adds a "Try again" MonarchButton under the error.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces any of the built-in strings (monarch_usagemeter_*).

options.name: announceThresholds
options.description: Announces once, for the whole meter, the items that have just reached the warning share or gone over their limit ("Storage: Near the limit"), through one polite live region. Nothing is read when the meter first appears.

states.name: normal
states.description: The meter is filled in the accent color and the line under it reads "42% used".

states.name: near the limit
states.description: At or above warningAt: the warning color and "Near the limit · 84% used" in warning text.

states.name: over the limit
states.description: Above the limit: a full meter in the danger color and "Over the limit · 130% used" in danger text.

states.name: unlimited
states.description: No limit, or a limit of zero or less: the count and the unit, with no meter.

states.name: loading
states.description: A circular progress indicator and the loading text replace the items.

states.name: error
states.description: The message in danger text replaces the items, with a retry button when onRetry is given.

appearance: The meter uses the accent solid, warning solid or danger solid color on the emphasis background track. The status line is muted text, or warning strong and danger strong text near and over the limit; the error message is danger strong. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The parity map named MonarchProgress for each item; MonarchProgress has no color or tone parameter, so the meter uses the Material 3 LinearProgressIndicator directly with the level colors. The web lays items out in a grid or a list; on a phone they are one column, as on iOS, so there is no layout option. The web loading state draws skeleton tiles and the error state uses InlineErrorRetry; here loading is a progress indicator with text and the error is a message with a Monarch button. The web shows a warning or error icon next to the level; Monarch bundles no icons, so the level is written as text in the level color. The web announces level changes by default; on Android a component that is on screen from the start makes announcements opt-in, so announceChanges is off by default. The reset date is epoch milliseconds, as in the Material 3 DatePickerState. The eight built-in strings are replaced through MonarchUsageMeterLabels, as on iOS.
accessibility: The title is a heading.
Each item is one TalkBack element that reads its label, its figures and its status line, for example "Storage, 42 of 50 GB, Near the limit · 84% used". The meter itself is hidden.
Near and over the limit are written as text, so they do not depend on the color of the meter.
With announceChanges every item is a polite live region.
The error message is a polite live region, and the retry button is a Monarch button with a 48dp touch target.
The loading indicator and its text are read as one element.
All text scales with the font size and wraps; it is not cut off at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: Used above the limit draws a full meter; the percentage shows the real share, such as 130%.
Exactly at the limit is near the limit, not over it.
A limit of zero, a negative limit or a limit that is not finite is treated as no limit.
The error takes precedence over loading.
The unit is written after the figures with a space, in every locale.
Numbers are written with at most one fraction digit in the current locale.

name: MonarchUsernameAvailabilityInput
title: UsernameAvailabilityInput
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedTextField with LaunchedEffect and kotlinx.coroutines.delay for the debounced check
summary: A text field whose value is checked while the person types, such as a handle or a workspace address, with a status message, an announced result and a retry after a failure.
whenToUse: For a value that must be unique on a service: a handle, a workspace address, a slug. The app supplies the check.
whenNotToUse: For checks that need no service, validate on submit with MonarchTextField and its errorText. For search-as-you-type use the Material 3 SearchBar.
api: @Composable fun MonarchUsernameAvailabilityInput(value: String, label: String, onValueChange: (String) -> Unit, validate: suspend (String) -> MonarchUsernameAvailabilityResult?, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, placeholder: String? = null, helperText: String? = null, prefix: String? = null, debounceMillis: Long = 400L, enabled: Boolean = true, transform: ((String) -> String)? = null, onStatusChange: ((MonarchUsernameAvailabilityStatus, String?) -> Unit)? = null, statusIcon: (@Composable (MonarchUsernameAvailabilityStatus) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchUsernameAvailabilityInputLabels = MonarchUsernameAvailabilityInputLabels(), keyboardActions: KeyboardActions = KeyboardActions.Default, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)
class MonarchUsernameAvailabilityResult(valid: Boolean, message: String? = null)
enum class MonarchUsernameAvailabilityStatus { Idle, Checking, Valid, Invalid, Error }
class MonarchUsernameAvailabilityInputLabels(checking: String? = null, valid: String? = null, invalid: String? = null, error: String? = null, retry: String? = null)

options.name: value
options.description: The text to edit and check.

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label, already localised.

options.name: onValueChange
options.description: Called with the new text, after transform.

options.name: validate
options.description: The check. Return null when there is nothing to check. Throwing sets the Error status. Cancelled when the text changes.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the component.

options.name: placeholder
options.description: An example shown while the field is empty and focused.

options.name: helperText
options.description: Supporting text under the field, shown while there is no status message.

options.name: prefix
options.description: Fixed text before the value, such as a domain.

options.name: debounceMillis
options.description: How long typing must pause before the check runs.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the person can edit the field.

options.name: transform
options.description: Rewrites typed text before it is stored, such as lower-casing.

options.name: onStatusChange
options.description: Called when the status or its message changes, not for the first status.

options.name: statusIcon
options.description: An icon after the text for the settled statuses. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for "Checking availability…", "Available", "Not available", "Couldn’t check availability." and "Try again".

options.name: keyboardActions
options.description: What happens when the person triggers the IME action.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the focus and press interactions of the field.

states.name: idle
states.description: A plain field; the helper text shows.

states.name: checking
states.description: A progress indicator at the end of the field and "Checking availability…" under it, in the muted text color.

states.name: valid
states.description: The success border at rest and the message in the success color.

states.name: invalid
states.description: The field's error state: the danger border, the message in the danger color and the error semantics.

states.name: error
states.description: The message in the warning color and a "Try again" button.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The disabled field; the retry button is disabled too.

appearance: The same field as MonarchTextField: the input border, the focus ring role when focused, the success strong role for the border of a free value and the danger strong role for a taken one. The message under the field uses the muted, success strong, danger strong or warning strong role by status. The prefix is in the muted text role. All roles come from the theme.
platformNotes: The web passes an AbortSignal to the check; on Android the check runs in a LaunchedEffect coroutine that is cancelled when the text changes, which also cancels suspend calls made in it. The web has sm, md and lg sizes; Android has the one size of MonarchTextField, as iOS does. The web reports the first idle status on mount; onStatusChange runs on changes only, as on iOS. The web draws its own status glyphs; Monarch for Android bundles no icons, so statusIcon is a slot and the message carries the meaning. Built-in strings are replaced through one labels value. The Material 3 prefix is shown when the field is focused or has text. It is built on OutlinedTextField with the colors of MonarchTextField rather than on MonarchTextField itself, because that has no prefix slot and no success state. Monarch does no networking.
accessibility: The field is a Material 3 text field named by its label.
Settled results ("Available", "Not available", a failure) are announced through a polite live region; "Checking" is not.
A taken value sets the error semantics with its message.
Each status has its own message in words, not color alone; the progress indicator is hidden from TalkBack.
The "Try again" button is a separate element with a 48dp touch target.
Autocorrection and capitalisation are off. Text grows with the font size setting and the message wraps.
edgeCases: Empty text is idle and is never checked.
A check cancelled by new typing never writes its result, so the status always describes the latest text.
"Try again" runs the check at once, without the wait.
The message returned by the check replaces the built-in and replaced texts.
Changing validate does not start a new check; the next edit does.

name: MonarchVersionHistoryPanel
title: VersionHistoryPanel
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn of androidx.compose.material3.ListItem rows, androidx.compose.material3.SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow, androidx.compose.material3.AlertDialog and androidx.activity.compose.BackHandler, composing MonarchDiffViewer, MonarchTextField, MonarchButton, MonarchAvatar, MonarchBadge, MonarchSkeleton and MonarchEmptyState; android.icu.text.RelativeDateTimeFormatter and DateFormat for the times
summary: The version history of a document or record: the saved versions, what changed between a version and now, its full text, and restore behind a confirmation.
whenToUse: In a full-height ModalBottomSheet or a pane beside a document or record, so people can see earlier versions, compare one with the content now, restore it and save a named version.
whenNotToUse: For the versions an AI model wrote of one artifact, use MonarchAiArtifactVersions. For a log of who did what, use MonarchActivityTimeline. To compare two texts without a history, use MonarchDiffViewer.
api: @Composable fun MonarchVersionHistoryPanel(versions: List<MonarchVersionHistoryPanelVersion>, selection: String?, onSelectionChange: (String?) -> Unit, currentLines: List<String>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, title: String? = null, selectedLines: List<String>? = null, currentId: String? = null, loading: Boolean = false, now: Long? = null, locale: Locale? = null, timeZone: String? = null, onSaveVersion: (suspend (note: String) -> Unit)? = null, onRestore: (suspend (id: String) -> Unit)? = null, onClose: (() -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchVersionHistoryPanelLabels = MonarchVersionHistoryPanelLabels())
data class MonarchVersionHistoryPanelVersion(id: String, date: Long, authorName: String, authorImage: Painter? = null, note: String? = null, automatic: Boolean = false)

class MonarchVersionHistoryPanelLabels(close: String? = null, back: String? = null, versions: String? = null, noteLabel: String? = null, notePlaceholder: String? = null, save: String? = null, saved: String? = null, saveFailed: String? = null, empty: String? = null, current: String? = null, automatic: String? = null, changes: String? = null, fullText: String? = null, now: String? = null, identical: String? = null, restore: String? = null, restoreTitle: String? = null, restoreDescription: String? = null, restoreConfirm: String? = null, cancel: String? = null, restored: String? = null, restoreFailed: String? = null, loading: String? = null, diff: MonarchDiffViewerLabels = MonarchDiffViewerLabels())

options.name: versions
options.description: The saved versions, newest first: id, date (epoch milliseconds), author name and picture, name and whether it was saved automatically.

options.name: selection
options.description: The id of the version on screen, or null for the list. It is the navigation state: the Versions button and the system back gesture call onSelectionChange(null).

options.name: onSelectionChange
options.description: Called with the version to open, or null to return to the list. Load the version's lines here.

options.name: currentLines
options.description: The content now, one entry per block or paragraph.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the panel. Give it a bounded height: the list and the diff are lazy.

options.name: title
options.description: The title of the list. "History" when null.

options.name: selectedLines
options.description: The selected version's content. Placeholders show while it is null.

options.name: currentId
options.description: The version that matches the content now, marked Current and without Restore. The newest when null.

options.name: loading
options.description: Shows placeholder rows while the list loads.

options.name: now
options.description: The reference time for relative times, in epoch milliseconds. null follows the clock, refreshed every minute.

options.name: locale
options.description: The locale of times and dates. null uses the first locale of the configuration.

options.name: timeZone
options.description: The zone of the date written on a version's screen. An IANA id such as Europe/Berlin; null, or an id the device does not know, is the device's zone.

options.name: onSaveVersion
options.description: Shows a name field and Save version above the list. Receives the trimmed name, at most 200 characters. Throw to show the error under the field.

options.name: onRestore
options.description: Shows Restore this version on versions other than the current one, behind a confirmation. Throw to keep the screen with the error; on success the panel returns to the list.

options.name: onClose
options.description: Shows a Close button at the end of the header.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, and the diff's strings in diff.

states.name: list
states.description: The versions, each with an avatar, a relative time, the author and the name; the current one has an info Current badge.

states.name: loading
states.description: Placeholder lines, read once as "Loading".

states.name: empty
states.description: A small empty state: "No versions yet. Save one to mark this moment."

states.name: saving
states.description: Save version shows progress and the name field is disabled; an error shows under the field and is announced.

states.name: version, loading
states.description: The version's screen shows placeholder lines until selectedLines arrives.

states.name: changes
states.description: A MonarchDiffViewer from the version to now, with totals and folded unchanged runs, or "This version is identical to the current one."

states.name: full text
states.description: The version's paragraphs, selectable.

states.name: restoring
states.description: Restore this version shows progress after the confirmation; an error shows above it and is announced.

appearance: No surface of its own: it takes the sheet's or pane's background. The title in the subheading style and default text, rows separated by subtle dividers with the time in the strong body style and the author line in muted caption text, the Current badge in the info tone, ghost buttons for Versions and Close, the Material 3 segmented control in the theme's colors, the diff viewer's added and removed colors with signs, a primary Restore button and errors in the strong danger color. The same roles in dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web is an aside panel that swaps its list for a detail view with tabs. On Android, as on iOS, it is the phone's list and detail pattern: the app presents it in a full-height ModalBottomSheet or a pane, the selection is the navigation state, the system back gesture (BackHandler) and a Versions button return to the list, a Material 3 segmented control switches Changes and Full text, and restore is confirmed in a Material 3 AlertDialog. Names follow iOS; the Binding<String?> selection is selection with onSelectionChange, isLoading is loading, currentID is currentId, onSaveVersion and onRestore are suspending functions (Compose's equivalent of async throws), and the author's picture is authorImage: Painter? because Monarch loads no images (the iOS authorURL is not offered). Monarch bundles no icons, so Back and Close are text buttons. The web's own line diff is MonarchDiffViewer, which word-highlights changed lines; it is lazy, so the panel needs a bounded height. Relative times are written by android.icu.text.RelativeDateTimeFormatter and refresh every minute without now; the absolute date is written on the version's screen instead of a tooltip.
accessibility: The list title and the version's title (its relative time) are headings.
Each version is one button read as the relative time, the author and the version's name or "Saved automatically"; the current one has the state "Current". Rows keep a 48dp touch target.
Avatars are decorative, because the author's name is written beside them.
On the version's screen the author line and the date are read as one element.
The Versions button is named "Back to versions"; the system back gesture does the same.
The diff is read as described for MonarchDiffViewer: each line after "Added" or "Removed".
Placeholders are read once as "Loading".
"Version saved", "Version restored" and the save and restore errors are announced through a polite live region that is always present.
Restore is behind a Material 3 dialog with Restore and Cancel.
edgeCases: A selection that is not one of the versions shows the list.
Without onRestore, and on the current version, there is no Restore.
An empty or blank name saves an unnamed version; names are cut at 200 characters.
A thrown error without a message shows the built-in failure text; a cancellation is not shown as an error.
Times in the future read "now".

options.name: image

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the press and focus interactions of the button.

states.name: poster
states.description: The image crops or fits the frame, with the play mark in the middle.

states.name: placeholder
states.description: While image is null: the inverse fill with a muted play glyph and no round mark.

states.name: button
states.description: With onPlay: one button with a focus ring and the ripple.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The play disc uses the muted background and the triangle the disabled text color; taps do nothing.

appearance: The frame has 12dp corners on the inverse background. The play mark is a 48dp disc in the surface color with the medium shadow and a triangle in the default text color; the badge is the inverse background with inverse text in the caption style with tabular figures. Each role has its own value in the dark and high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web captures a frame from the video in the browser when no thumbnail is given. Here, as on iOS, the view takes a poster by the image convention (a Painter) and frame capture is the separate suspend function captureVideoFrame, built on the platform MediaMetadataRetriever, whose result the app passes as a BitmapPainter; the web's onCaptureError is the exception it throws. The web's translucent play disc and badge are opaque here, because Monarch takes colors by role and does not dim. The length is in milliseconds (durationMillis), as in the Android media APIs, where the web and iOS take seconds. The web's loading pulse is not drawn, because the thumbnail never captures on its own.
accessibility: With onPlay it is one element with the button role named "Play <title>", or playLabel.
Without onPlay it is one element with the image role named by the title.
The length is its state description, in words for the current locale ("1 minute, 5 seconds"); the badge digits are not read.
The thumbnail is as wide as its container, far above 48dp, and draws the Monarch focus ring.
The badge text grows with the font size setting.
edgeCases: A negative length is shown as 0:00; lengths are rounded to whole seconds.
A title of spaces gives the built-in "Video".
captureVideoFrame keeps the time inside the video and returns null when there is no frame there; a URI it cannot open throws.
With showPlayIcon false the poster has no mark, but the button still works.

summary: Long lists are virtualised by the platform: LazyColumn and LazyVerticalGrid compose an item only when it is about to appear. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: For any list or grid that can grow beyond a screen: tickets, contacts, search results, a feed. Give every item a stable key and, where rows differ, a content type.
whenNotToUse: For a handful of rows inside a screen that already scrolls, use a Column; a lazy list cannot be nested in a vertical scroll of the same direction. For a table with columns and sorting, use a data grid.

appearance: No appearance of its own: rows use Monarch components and MonarchDivider, which follow the theme in light, dark and high contrast.
platformNotes: The web VirtualList measures row heights, keeps a window of rows and exposes scrollToIndex; LazyColumn and LazyVerticalGrid do all of that inside Compose. The web getItemKey is the key lambda of items(): use an id that is stable across reloads, so the scroll position and item state follow the data. contentType lets Compose reuse the composition of rows of the same type. Heights are measured by Compose, so there is no estimated height or overscan to set. The web onEndReached is an item at the end whose LaunchedEffect requests the next page. The web scrollToKey is LazyListState.animateScrollToItem with the index of the key. iOS uses List and LazyVStack.
accessibility: System behavior: TalkBack moves through the items in order and scrolls the list as it goes.
Items that have not been composed are not in the accessibility tree until scrolling composes them; TalkBack reports the collection size from the lazy list's collection info.
A trailing loading item should have a content description that says more items are loading.
edgeCases: Without keys, inserting an item at the top moves the state of every row below it, and the scroll position jumps.
A LazyColumn inside verticalScroll throws, because it would be measured with infinite height; give it a bounded height or make the whole screen one LazyColumn.

appearance: The list has no fill of its own. Day separators are muted captions between subtle border lines; the New messages divider uses the strong accent text and accent border roles; the rows, Load more and the jump button keep their own roles. The same roles adapt to dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web measures and positions rows itself (a virtualised scroller with estimated heights, overscan and server-rendered rows); Android uses LazyColumn with reverseLayout, which already composes only the visible rows and keeps the view still when older pages are prepended, so estimatedItemHeight, overscan and initialRenderCount have no equivalent. The web's imperative handle (scrollToBottom, scrollToItem) is replaced by the hoisted LazyListState and scrollToKey. The web's items implement an interface with id, time and authorId; Android takes key, time and authorId selectors so app models need not implement a Monarch type. Thresholds are in rows (loadOlderThreshold), not pixels. highlightedId is not taken: the row slot gets the item and can pass highlighted to MonarchMessageRow. The New messages divider uses the accent tone, as on the web. iOS has no entry for this id yet.
accessibility: The list is named Messages for TalkBack.
Day separators and the New messages divider are headings, so TalkBack can jump between days.
Messages that arrive are announced as N new messages through a polite live region that is always present; rows themselves are not live, so scrolling stays quiet.
The status slot is in a polite live region, so a typing indicator is announced.
The jump button and Load older messages are buttons with a 48dp touch target; the jump button's text says how many messages arrived, not only an icon.
The jump scroll is instant when the user has removed animations.
edgeCases: A message whose key does not change keeps its place; replacing the whole list (a different conversation) is not announced as arrivals.
Grouping needs a known author; it never crosses a day or the New messages divider.
A message timed before the previous one is not grouped with it.
onLoadOlder is not called while loadingOlder or olderFailed is true; after a page arrives it is called again only if the top is still near.
Do not put the list in a vertically scrolling parent.

whenToUse: To name an icon-only control (contentDescription), to add context a sighted person gets from the layout, to replace several texts with one spoken phrase (clearAndSetSemantics), or to hide a decorative image (contentDescription = null).
whenNotToUse: Do not hide information from sighted people that TalkBack users get, or the reverse; if the context matters, show it. Do not replace visible text with a description that does not start with the visible words, which Voice Access uses to find the control.

appearance: Nothing is drawn: the text exists only in the accessibility tree.
platformNotes: The web hides a span off screen so a screen reader still finds it in the document. Android has no document: each composable can carry semantics properties, so the spoken text is set on the element. contentDescription names it, stateDescription describes its state, clearAndSetSemantics replaces what its children would say with one phrase, and hideFromAccessibility() or a null contentDescription hides decoration. iOS uses accessibilityLabel, accessibilityValue and accessibilityHidden in the same way.
accessibility: System behavior: TalkBack reads contentDescription in place of an element's text, then its state description, then its role.
clearAndSetSemantics removes the children's semantics, so their actions must be set again on the parent if they are needed.
An Image or Icon with a null contentDescription is skipped by TalkBack.
edgeCases: Setting contentDescription on a node that merges its children replaces the children's text as well; use stateDescription to add to it instead.

options.description: The time zone of the dates in the details sheet. An IANA id such as Europe/Berlin; null, or an id the device does not know, is the device's zone.

options.name: onRedeliver
options.description: Sends a delivery again. The button shows progress while it runs; the result is announced; throwing announces the failure. Without it there is no Redeliver.

options.name: canRedeliver
options.description: Which deliveries offer Redeliver. null offers it on every one that is not pending or sending.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Opens the app's own detail screen. null opens the built-in details sheet.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

options.name: emptyAction
options.description: Shown in the first-run empty state, such as a Send a test event button.

options.name: actions
options.description: More actions on each row, after Redeliver.

options.name: details
options.description: More content at the end of the details sheet, such as the request and response bodies.

states.name: loading
states.description: Four MonarchSkeleton rows replace the list, read by TalkBack as one polite "Loading deliveries".

states.name: failed
states.description: A MonarchInlineErrorRetry with "Deliveries did not load." and Try again replaces the list; without onRetry the message is danger text in a polite live region.

states.name: empty
states.description: A small first-run MonarchEmptyState, "No deliveries yet", with emptyAction.

states.name: filtered to nothing
states.description: A filtered MonarchEmptyState, "No deliveries match", with Clear filters.

states.name: filtered
states.description: The active filter's menu button becomes primary and reads "Status: Failed"; Clear filters appears next to the menus.

states.name: redelivering
states.description: The row's Redeliver (and the sheet's) shows progress and is read as Loading until onRedeliver returns.

states.name: scheduled retry
states.description: A pending or retrying delivery with nextAttemptMillis shows "Next attempt in 10 minutes" in place of the last attempt's time.

states.name: not attempted
states.description: A delivery with no attempts and no response shows "Not attempted yet".

states.name: more pages
states.description: With onLoadMore, a MonarchLoadMore footer ends the list: Load more, loading, a failure with Retry, or "End of the delivery log".

appearance: A plain list on the surface color with subtle dividers. The event type uses the strong body style in the default text color, the event id the code style; time, response and attempts use the caption style in the muted text color, and an error the strong danger color. Status badges use their tone's subtle fill. The same roles adapt to dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: A domain composite, marked experimental until a Rook app adopts it. The web shows a table with a column per fact; on a phone each delivery is a row of stacked lines and its full details open in a ModalBottomSheet (or the app's own screen through onSelect), the list-and-detail pattern people expect on Android. The copy button of the event id moved into the sheet, where MonarchDescriptionList copies it. The web's status, event type and search filters are a MonarchTextField and two menu buttons that open DropdownMenus with radio items. onRedeliver is a suspend function instead of a returned promise; error is a failed flag with a built-in, overridable message instead of rich content; destination and error are strings. Status icons are not shown because Monarch bundles no icons; the status is always written. There is no iOS entry yet.
accessibility: Each row is one TalkBack element read as status, time, event type, event id, response and attempts, and error; its action is named "View delivery of invoice.paid evt_1".
Redeliver is a separate element named after the event it resends, such as "Redeliver invoice.paid evt_1", and is read as Loading while it runs.
A queued or failed redelivery is announced through a polite live region that is always present.
The counts line is a polite live region, so new totals are read.
The list is named "Webhook deliveries".
Filter menu items are radio buttons marked selected for the current value.
Statuses and errors are words, so nothing relies on color.
Redeliver and the filter buttons have 48dp touch targets.
edgeCases: The search matches the event id exactly, ignoring case, or any part of the event type; blank text is no filter.
Status keys that are neither built in nor in statuses are shown with the key as their name.
The list is lazy: give it a bounded height. Inside a vertically scrolling parent it would get an infinite height and fail.
A delivery that disappears from deliveries while its sheet is open closes the sheet.
Long event types and errors wrap; nothing is cut at font scale 2.0.
Redeliver is ignored while the same delivery is already being redelivered.

summary: Edits weekly availability: each day switched on or off, one or more time intervals per day, copying a day to the whole week, and overlap checks.
whenToUse: Booking availability, business hours, support or on-call hours: any setting that is “these times on these weekdays”.

public data class MonarchWeeklyHoursInterval(day: Int, start: Int, end: Int) { companion object { fun validate(value: List<MonarchWeeklyHoursInterval>): Map<Int, MonarchWeeklyHoursError> } }

public class MonarchWeeklyHoursEditorLabels(title: String? = null, unavailable: String? = null, start: String? = null, end: String? = null, add: String? = null, addItem: ((day: String) -> String)? = null, remove: String? = null, removeItem: ((day: String, position: Int) -> String)? = null, copyToAll: String? = null, copyToAllItem: ((day: String) -> String)? = null, copied: ((day: String) -> String)? = null, range: ((start: String, end: String) -> String)? = null, midnight: String? = null, rangeError: String? = null, orderError: String? = null, overlapError: String? = null)

options.name: value
options.description: The intervals: ISO weekday (1 Monday … 7 Sunday) and minutes from midnight, end exclusive and at most 1440.

options.name: onValueChange
options.description: Called with the whole new value after every change, ordered by weekday; each day's intervals stay in the order arranged.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the editor.

options.name: firstDayOfWeek
options.description: The first day shown, Calendar.SUNDAY to Calendar.SATURDAY. null follows the locale (Monday in Germany, Sunday in the US), as the system calendar does.

options.name: is24Hour
options.description: Shows times on a 24-hour clock; null follows the device setting.

options.name: step
options.description: Minutes between time options, 1 to 60; zero or a negative step falls back to 15.

options.name: defaultStart
options.description: The start of a day switched on for the first time (09:00).

options.name: defaultEnd
options.description: The end of a day switched on for the first time (17:00).

options.name: maxIntervals
options.description: The most intervals per day; the add button is hidden at this count.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the hours can be changed.

options.name: readOnly
options.description: Shows each day's hours as text, without controls.

options.name: timeZoneLabel
options.description: Content under the heading for the zone the hours are in: a text, or the app's MonarchTimezoneSelect.

options.name: removeIcon
options.description: The icon of each remove button; without it the button reads Remove.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

states.name: day on
states.description: The switch is on; each interval shows its start and end menus and a remove button; Add interval and Copy to all follow.

states.name: day off
states.description: The switch is off and the row reads Unavailable in the muted color.

states.name: invalid
states.description: A danger-coloured message under the day says what is wrong: a time outside the day, an interval ending before it starts, or an overlap.

states.name: at the limit
states.description: With maxIntervals intervals the add button is hidden.

states.name: read-only
states.description: Each day is its name and its hours as text, such as 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM, without controls.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Every switch, menu and button is disabled.

appearance: Days are separated by subtle dividers. The day switch is the Material 3 Switch in Monarch colors; the time menus are outlined fields with the input border; the buttons are small ghost MonarchButtons; Unavailable and the read-only hours use the muted text color and errors the strong danger text color. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from the color roles.
platformNotes: Same value shape, validation and defaults as the web, except the first day of the week (`{ day, start, end }` in minutes, ISO weekdays, 09:00 to 17:00, 15-minute steps, six intervals). Differences: firstDayOfWeek takes the java.util.Calendar constants that MonarchMiniMonth and MonarchCalendarMonthView use and, like them, follows the locale when null where the web starts on Monday; and is24Hour replaces the web's hourCycle; onValueChange passes only the value, and MonarchWeeklyHoursInterval.validate gives the errors the web passes beside it. On a phone the start and end menus share one line and the remove button sits under them, with Add interval and Copy to all under the day, instead of the web's one-line row. Times are Monarch menus, not the Material 3 TimePicker, because the TimePicker has no step and no end-of-day 24:00. The menus have the visible labels Start and End; TalkBack reads them inside the day's group after the day switch, where the web uses hidden names such as “Monday interval 1 start”. The web's hidden form input (name) has no meaning in Compose. iOS names the first day firstWeekday.
accessibility: Each day is a switch named by the weekday, with Unavailable read as its description while off; the whole row is the 48dp target.
Each day is a traversal group, so its switch, menus, buttons and error are read together.
Remove, Add interval and Copy to all carry names with the day, such as “Remove Monday interval 1” and “Copy to all days from Monday”, and keep the visible text in the name.
A day's error is text, not only color, and is announced through a polite live region when it appears.
Copying a day is announced through a polite live region (“Monday hours copied to every day.”).
The heading is a heading; the read-only view merges each day's name and hours into one element.
edgeCases: Switching a day off and on again restores its intervals while the editor stays on screen; it starts from the default interval after the editor leaves the composition.
A stored time that is not on the step is kept and offered in the menu.
Intervals with a day outside 1 to 7 are dropped at the next change.
The end of the day is Midnight on a 12-hour clock and 24:00 on a 24-hour clock.
The editor does not scroll on its own: put it in a scrolling screen.

name: MonarchWidget
title: Widget
wrapsNative: MonarchCard (androidx.compose.material3.Surface) with a header of androidx.compose.material3.Text, MonarchButton, MonarchIconButton and MonarchMenu; MonarchSkeleton, MonarchEmptyState, MonarchInlineErrorRetry and MonarchInlineNotice for the states; android.text.format.DateUtils.getRelativeTimeSpanString for the updated line
summary: The frame of a dashboard widget: a title with a period, header actions, an overflow menu, View all, and its own loading, empty and failed states.
whenToUse: For each tile of a dashboard or an overview screen, so every tile has the same header, states and footer.
whenNotToUse: Not for a plain group of fields: use MonarchSectionCard or MonarchCard. Not for a single figure without a frame: use MonarchMetric.
api: @Composable fun MonarchWidget(title: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, description: String? = null, period: String? = null, variant: MonarchWidgetVariant = MonarchWidgetVariant.Card, state: MonarchWidgetState = MonarchWidgetState.Ready, retrying: Boolean = false, updatedAt: Long? = null, now: Long? = null, footer: String? = null, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, menuIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null, onViewAll: (() -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchWidgetLabels = MonarchWidgetLabels(), actions: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null, menu: (@Composable ColumnScope.(close: () -> Unit) -> Unit)? = null, content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)
sealed class MonarchWidgetState { data object Ready; data object Loading; data class Empty(val message: String? = null); data class Failed(val message: String? = null) }
enum class MonarchWidgetVariant { Card, Plain }

class MonarchWidgetLabels(menu: ((title: String) -> String)? = null, more: String? = null, viewAll: String? = null, viewAllLabel: ((title: String) -> String)? = null, loading: ((title: String) -> String)? = null, error: String? = null, empty: String? = null, updated: ((relativeTime: String) -> String)? = null)

options.name: title
options.description: The widget's title. It is a TalkBack heading.

options.name: description
options.description: A caption line under the title.

options.name: period
options.description: The period the figures cover, muted beside the title.

options.name: variant
options.description: Card draws a MonarchCard without a shadow; Plain has no surface, for a widget inside another surface.

options.name: state
options.description: Ready shows the content; Loading three placeholder lines; Empty a small MonarchEmptyState; Failed the message, with Try again when onRetry is set.

options.name: retrying
options.description: With Failed and onRetry: the Try again button is busy.

options.name: updatedAt
options.description: When the data was updated, in epoch milliseconds, shown in the footer as "Updated 5 minutes ago". Hidden while loading.

options.name: now
options.description: The current time for the updated line. null uses the clock and refreshes every minute; pass a value in tests.

options.name: footer
options.description: A note under the body. Hidden while loading.

options.name: icon
options.description: A decorative icon before the title; it is hidden from TalkBack.

options.name: menuIcon
options.description: The icon of the menu button, shown in a MonarchIconButton. Without it the button shows the text "More".

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Adds Try again to the failed state.

options.name: onViewAll
options.description: Adds a View all button to the header; the app navigates.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings (monarch_widget_*).

options.name: actions
options.description: Controls in the header before View all, such as a small segmented button row.

options.name: menu
options.description: The overflow menu's items, usually MonarchMenuItems; call close from an item.

options.name: content
options.description: The body, shown in the ready state.

states.name: ready
states.description: The content is shown under the header.

states.name: loading
states.description: Three MonarchSkeleton lines, one element read as "Loading" and the title. The footer is hidden. The shimmer stops when animations are off.

states.name: empty
states.description: A small MonarchEmptyState with the given title or "Nothing to show yet".

states.name: failed
states.description: A MonarchInlineErrorRetry with Try again when onRetry is set, otherwise a danger MonarchInlineNotice. Both are polite live regions, so the failure is announced.

appearance: Card is a MonarchCard on the surface role with the default border and no shadow; Plain has no surface. The title uses the default text role in the subheading type role; the period, description, icon and footer use the muted text role. The states take the colors of the components they use. High-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colors.
platformNotes: The web Widget is a section landmark with a heading level, a link for View all and an items array for the menu. On Android the title is a TalkBack heading (no landmarks or levels), View all is a button whose callback the app uses to navigate, and the menu takes MonarchMenuItems. The web span belongs to its DashboardGrid and has no equivalent. The web's Try again can wait on a promise; on Android the app sets retrying, as on iOS. Monarch bundles no icons, so the menu button is a text button "More" unless menuIcon is given.
accessibility: The title is a heading, so TalkBack's heading navigation moves between widgets; the icon is hidden.
The menu button is named "More actions for" and the title; View all is named "View all:" and the title.
The loading placeholder is one element named "Loading" and the title.
A failure is a polite live region with its message; Try again is a separate button.
From font scale 1.5 the header controls move under the title instead of squeezing it.
Header buttons keep 48dp touch targets.
edgeCases: Long titles wrap; the header controls keep their size.
The updated line is relative to the current time and refreshes every minute while now is null.
The ready state with empty content shows only the header and the footer.
The menu closes only when an item calls close, on back, or on a tap outside.

whenToUse: For a short task of two to four steps that should not leave the current screen, such as moving a project or setting up an integration.
whenNotToUse: For a long or resumable flow, use full screens with their own back stack. For one question, use a dialog.

@Composable fun MonarchBottomSheet(onDismissRequest: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, title: String? = null, description: String? = null, dismissible: Boolean = true, showHandle: Boolean = true, fullyExpanded: Boolean = true, fullWidthContent: Boolean = false, content: @Composable MonarchBottomSheetScope.() -> Unit)

@Composable fun MonarchButton(text: String, onClick: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchButtonVariant = MonarchButtonVariant.Secondary, …, enabled: Boolean = true, loading: Boolean = false, …)

states.name: first step
states.description: The stepper at step 1, the step's content and Continue; no Back.

states.name: middle step
states.description: Back and Continue.

states.name: last step
states.description: The main action is a danger MonarchButton named for what it does, such as "Move project".

states.name: blocked
states.description: Continue is disabled until the step is valid; say why in the step's content.

states.name: working
states.description: Pass loading to the main action while a step's work runs; show a failure with MonarchInlineNotice and stay on the step.

appearance: A Material 3 bottom sheet on the raised surface Monarch maps to it, with MonarchStepper (accent marks for the current and completed steps), the step title in the heading style, a ghost Back and a primary Continue, or a danger last action. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web WizardDialog is a component that takes steps with content, canContinue, blockedReason, a per-step async onContinue with pending and error states, and a done step. On Android the app holds the step index and composes MonarchStepper and MonarchButton in a MonarchBottomSheet. The web moves focus to the step heading; on Android the step title is a polite live region, so TalkBack announces each new step, and the app can move focus with a FocusRequester. Back within the wizard is the Back button; the system back closes the sheet, or add a BackHandler that goes to the previous step. iOS uses the same recipe.
accessibility: MonarchStepper reads the progress ("Step 2 of 3") and each step's state.
The step title is a polite live region, so TalkBack announces the new step after Continue or Back.
The last action is named for what it does, so it does not depend on its danger color.
Back and Continue have 48dp touch targets; a disabled Continue is announced as disabled.
edgeCases: Keep entered values when going Back.
If the sheet is dismissed half way, decide whether to keep the draft; reset the step when it opens again.
