title: WorkspaceOnboardingForm
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of MonarchTextField, MonarchUsernameAvailabilityInput, MonarchRadioCardGroup and MonarchButton, with rememberSaveable state for values and validation
summary: A recipe, not a component: the form that creates a workspace, with a name, a unique username checked for availability, and a workspace type, with inline validation and a pending submit.
whenToUse: In the first-run flow of a product that needs a workspace or organization before anything else.
whenNotToUse: Not for editing an existing workspace's settings (use a settings screen with sections) and not for signing up a person (that is the account flow).
api: MonarchTextField(value = name, onValueChange = …, label = "Workspace name", errorText = nameError)
MonarchUsernameAvailabilityInput(value = username, label = "Workspace username", onValueChange = …, validate = …, prefix = "@", onStatusChange = …)
MonarchRadioCardGroup(options = …, selected = type, onSelect = …, label = "Type", columns = 2)
MonarchButton(text = "Continue", onClick = …, modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(), variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Primary, loading = creating)

options.name: name
options.description: The workspace name. The example requires 4 to 25 characters; the rule is the app's.

options.name: username
options.description: The unique handle, checked by MonarchUsernameAvailabilityInput. The example allows 5 to 30 letters and digits.

options.name: type
options.description: The chosen workspace type; the example offers Creator and Business.

options.name: submitted
options.description: Set by Continue, so empty fields show their errors only after a submit.

options.name: creating
options.description: Passed to the Continue button's loading while the product creates the workspace.

states.name: invalid name
states.description: MonarchTextField shows the error once the person has typed or submitted: at least 4 and at most 25 characters.

states.name: username checking, available, taken or failed
states.description: MonarchUsernameAvailabilityInput checks the local rules and the product's lookup after typing pauses and reports its status; Continue waits for Valid.

states.name: type missing
states.description: After a submit without a type, an error line in the danger strong color appears under the cards.

states.name: creating
states.description: The Continue button shows its progress indicator and reads "Loading" while the product creates the workspace.

appearance: Each part keeps its own Monarch look: the text field's input border, the username field's status colors, the radio cards' selected border and mark, the primary button. Errors use the danger strong role. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web ships WorkspaceOnboardingForm as one pattern with onSubmit, checkUsername, rules and messages props. On Android it is a recipe, as on iOS: the fields, rules and submit logic stay in the app's composable, so the rules (4 to 25 characters for the name, 5 to 30 letters and digits for the username) and the types (Creator and Business) are shown in the example and are not a Monarch API. The web's form error alert after a failed submit is left to the app, for example a MonarchInlineNotice above the button. The type error has no icon because Monarch bundles none; it is text.
accessibility: Each field keeps its own label, helper and error text, read by TalkBack with the field.
The username status is announced by MonarchUsernameAvailabilityInput through a polite live region.
The type cards are radio buttons in a selectable group with the label.
Errors are text, not color alone.
The Continue button reads "Loading" while creating.
edgeCases: Submitting while the username is still being checked does nothing; tell the person to wait, as the catalogue page does.
At font scales of 1.5 and above, and on windows under 640dp, the two type cards stack in one column.
The values survive rotation through rememberSaveable; the username status is checked again.

name: MonarchWorkspaceSwitcher
title: WorkspaceSwitcher
wrapsNative: MonarchButton (ghost) with MonarchAvatar and androidx.compose.material3.ExposedDropdownMenuDefaults.TrailingIcon; androidx.compose.material3.DropdownMenu with DropdownMenuItem for up to five workspaces, otherwise androidx.compose.material3.ModalBottomSheet with MonarchSearchBar and an androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn of selectable rows with androidx.compose.material3.RadioButton
summary: Switches between the workspaces a person belongs to from a button with the workspace's logo, name and handle, which opens a menu for a short list or a searchable sheet for a long one, with Create workspace and All workspaces.
whenToUse: At the top of a product's navigation drawer or top bar, when a person can belong to several workspaces.
whenNotToUse: To filter the app to a part of one workspace, use MonarchSpaceSwitcher. For a searchable choice inside a form, use MonarchCombobox.
api: @Composable fun MonarchWorkspaceSwitcher(workspaces: List<MonarchWorkspaceOption>, selection: String?, onSelectionChange: (String) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, size: MonarchButtonSize = MonarchButtonSize.Md, enabled: Boolean = true, loading: Boolean = false, iconOnly: Boolean = false, onCreate: (() -> Unit)? = null, onManage: (() -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchWorkspaceSwitcherLabels = MonarchWorkspaceSwitcherLabels())
class MonarchWorkspaceOption(id: String, name: String, handle: String? = null, logo: Painter? = null, keywords: String? = null)

class MonarchWorkspaceSwitcherLabels(label: String? = null, placeholder: String? = null, search: String? = null, empty: String? = null, loading: String? = null, create: String? = null, manage: String? = null, cancel: String? = null)

options.name: workspaces
options.description: The workspaces this person belongs to, in display order.

options.name: selection
options.description: The current workspace id, null when none is chosen.

options.name: onSelectionChange
options.description: Called with the chosen workspace id; the app switches. Choosing the current one again does not call it.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the button.

options.name: size
options.description: The height and padding of the button.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the menu or sheet can be opened.

options.name: loading
options.description: The workspaces are still loading: the button opens the sheet, which says Loading workspaces….

options.name: iconOnly
options.description: Shows only the logo and the arrow. TalkBack still reads the name and handle.

options.name: onCreate
options.description: Adds Create workspace, which closes the menu or sheet and runs this.

options.name: onManage
options.description: Adds All workspaces, which closes the menu or sheet and runs this.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

states.name: menu
states.description: Up to five loaded workspaces: a Material 3 dropdown menu with logos, names and handles, the current one with a radio mark, then a divider and the actions.

states.name: sheet
states.description: More than five workspaces, or loading: a modal bottom sheet with a search field and a list of single-choice rows.

states.name: nothing chosen
states.description: The button shows the initial of Workspace and Choose a workspace.

states.name: searching
states.description: The sheet keeps workspaces whose name, handle or keywords contain the text, ignoring case and accents; with no match it reads No workspaces match.

states.name: loading
states.description: The sheet ends with Loading workspaces….

states.name: disabled
states.description: The ghost button's disabled colors; the menu or sheet cannot open.

appearance: A ghost button with a square MonarchAvatar logo, the name in label text with the handle in muted caption text and the Material exposed-dropdown arrow. The menu and sheet use the raised surface and Material radio marks. All are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The parity map lists combobox as a dependency; MonarchCombobox is a labelled form field without logos, so the switcher has its own button and reuses the sheet of MonarchSpaceSwitcher. As on iOS, the presentation is chosen by count: a Material 3 DropdownMenu for up to five workspaces (unlike the iOS menu it can show logos and handles) and a searchable sheet beyond that, replacing the web's popover listbox. The web's tooltip on the collapsed trigger is the spoken value. manageHref and createHref are callbacks (onManage, onCreate): components do not navigate. The web's controlled open state and align are not offered. Logos are Painters loaded by the app. iOS uses a Binding, isIconOnly and manageURL; Android hoists selection with onSelectionChange, drops the is prefix and takes onManage. Experimental: an identity product composite that waits for a Rook app to adopt it.
accessibility: The button is one element named "Workspace" whose state description is the name and handle ("Acme, @acme"), built by a tested pure function, also when only the logo shows; it keeps a 48dp touch target.
Menu items are read as the name and handle and the current one has the selected state and a radio mark.
Sheet rows are radio-button elements read as the name and handle; the chosen row is selected.
Logos are decorative; messages in the sheet are polite live regions; Cancel and the back gesture close without a change.
Menu items, rows and actions are at least 48dp high.
edgeCases: Choosing the current workspace again closes without calling onSelectionChange.
A selection that is not in workspaces reads as Choose a workspace.
Keywords are matched by search but never shown.
The search text is cleared when the sheet closes.

parityExceptions.reason: The web names this control with one sentence ("Workspace: Acme @acme"). On Android TalkBack gets the control name and its current value as the control's name and state description ("Workspace", "Acme, @acme"), which it speaks as one phrase and announces again when the value changes; the same words are visible in the control.
parityExceptions.convention: a control has a name and a state, not a joined sentence (Android accessibility: contentDescription + stateDescription)

name: MonarchWorldMap
title: WorldMap
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.Canvas with androidx.compose.foundation.gestures.detectTapGestures and androidx.compose.ui.layout.Layout for the TalkBack elements, inside MonarchChartFrame
summary: Values by country on a simplified world map, as a choropleth in one data color with a Less to More legend or as bubbles sized by value, inside a chart frame with a data table.
whenToUse: To show how a measure spreads across countries (signups, workspaces, revenue by country) when the geography matters to the reader.
whenNotToUse: For an exact ranking or fewer than about five countries use MonarchBarList or MonarchBarChart, which compare lengths more precisely than shades. For navigation, addresses or anything below country level use a map SDK; this outline is simplified and not for navigation.
api: @Composable fun MonarchWorldMap(title: String, data: List<MonarchWorldMapDatum>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, description: String? = null, status: MonarchChartFrameStatus = MonarchChartFrameStatus.Ready, variant: MonarchWorldMapVariant = MonarchWorldMapVariant.Choropleth, color: MonarchChartColor = MonarchChartColor.Data1, thresholds: List<Double>? = null, extras: List<MonarchWorldMapExtra> = emptyList(), showLegend: Boolean = true, summary: String? = null, emptyMessage: String? = null, footer: String? = null, countryName: ((String) -> String)? = null, formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = null, onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null, onSelect: ((MonarchWorldMapDatum) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchWorldMapLabels = MonarchWorldMapLabels())
class MonarchWorldMapDatum(country: String, value: Double, details: List<MonarchWorldMapDetail> = emptyList())
class MonarchWorldMapDetail(label: String, value: String)
class MonarchWorldMapExtra(label: String, value: Double, key: String = label)
enum class MonarchWorldMapVariant { Choropleth, Bubble }

class MonarchWorldMapLabels(frame: MonarchChartFrameLabels = MonarchChartFrameLabels(), country: String? = null, value: String? = null, extras: String? = null, less: String? = null, more: String? = null, rangeBelow: String? = null, range: String? = null, rangeAbove: String? = null, select: String? = null, unplaced: ((names: String, total: String) -> String)? = null, summary: ((countries: Int, top: String) -> String)? = null)

options.name: title
options.description: The chart's name, shown as the frame's heading. Already localised.

options.name: data
options.description: One value per ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, with optional detail lines. Codes are trimmed and upper-cased; a later entry for the same code wins; values that are not finite are left out.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the frame.

options.name: description
options.description: One line under the title, such as the period.

options.name: status
options.description: Map, loading skeleton, empty state or error. A ready map without values or extras shows the empty state.

options.name: variant
options.description: Filled countries, or bubbles whose area grows with the value on a neutral map.

options.name: color
options.description: The data color of the steps or bubbles.

options.name: thresholds
options.description: Three ascending values where levels 2, 3 and 4 start. Quarters of the largest value when null.

options.name: extras
options.description: Values that belong to no country ("Global", "EU"), shown as tiles under the map and as table rows.

options.name: showLegend
options.description: Shows the Less to More legend under a choropleth.

options.name: summary
options.description: Replaces the generated summary that names the map for TalkBack.

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: The message of the empty state.

options.name: footer
options.description: Notes under the chart, such as the source.

options.name: countryName
options.description: Names a country from its code. The default is the region's name in the current locale (java.util.Locale.getDisplayCountry), then the code.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes a value. The default is android.icu.text.NumberFormat in the current locale.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Try again in the error status.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Called with a country's cleaned datum when it is tapped or chosen with the TalkBack Select action, for drill-in.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, including the chart frame's.

states.name: choropleth
states.description: Every country with a value is filled with its level: the muted background for zero or less, three mixes of the data color and the color itself; countries without a value stay muted. Countries too small for the outline get a dot in their level's color.

states.name: bubble
states.description: The map stays muted and each country with a value gets a circle whose area grows with the value, filled with a quarter of the data color over the surface and outlined in the data color. No legend.

states.name: country inspected
states.description: A tapped country is outlined (or its dot or bubble is outlined and, for a bubble, filled more strongly) in the default text color, marked selected for TalkBack, and its name, value and details are written under the map and announced politely. A tap on the sea clears it.

states.name: extras and unplaced codes
states.description: Values for no country are tiles under the map; codes the outline does not have are listed in a muted note with their total.

states.name: table
states.description: View as table lists one row per country, largest first, then one per extra, with the value and one column per detail label.

states.name: loading
states.description: The frame's skeleton, read as Loading chart.

states.name: empty
states.description: The frame's empty state, when the map is ready without any value or extra.

states.name: error
states.description: The frame's error message, with Try again when onRetry is given.

appearance: Countries are the muted background separated by thin surface-coloured lines. Choropleth levels mix the chosen data color into the muted background at a quarter, half and three quarters, then use the color itself, as the heatmap does. Bubbles mix a quarter of the data color into the surface with a data-color outline. The inspected country is outlined in the default text color; tiles use the subtle background with a subtle border, muted label and default value. All colors are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes keep five distinct steps.
platformNotes: Uses the same Natural Earth 1:110m outline and centroids as the web's WorldMap, converted into an internal Kotlin source, with the same levels, bubble sizes, summary, legend and table. The web shows a floating tooltip on hover and steps through countries with the arrow keys; on Android a tap inspects a country and writes its details under the map. TalkBack users move through one element per country, largest value first, each with a Select action when onSelect is given; iOS makes the map one adjustable element instead, which Android has no equivalent for that is not a slider. Country elements are smaller than 48dp and overlap in Europe, so they are not buttons; a finger taps the map, and a tap that misses a small country finds the nearest country with a value within 24dp. The controlled activeCountry and onActiveCountryChange props and the web's valueFormat (Intl options) are not offered; use formatValue. The legend reuses the heatmap's Less, More and range strings. The map is never mirrored in right-to-left layouts.
accessibility: The map is a traversal group whose content description is the generated summary (for example "3 countries. Highest: United States 1,200, Germany 300, Singapore 40.") or the summary given, with collection info of the countries.

Every country with a value is its own TalkBack element on the country's center, read as "Germany: 300, Users 90", ordered largest value first by traversal index, with collection item info; the inspected country is marked selected.
With onSelect each country element has a Select custom action that inspects the country and calls onSelect; without it the elements have no action.
The details of the inspected country are a polite live region that is always present, so each new inspection is announced.
The legend is one element read as "Legend" and the range of every step, so the shades are never the only key.
The tiles are a traversal group named "Other values"; each tile is one element read as its label and value.
View as table lists every country, value and detail in rows TalkBack reads one at a time.
The map keeps its geography right to left; the text under it follows the layout direction.
edgeCases: Codes are trimmed and upper-cased; " de" and "DE" are the same country and the later entry wins.
Codes the outline does not know (an invalid code or a territory dropped by the 1:110m set) are listed under the map and still appear in the table and the summary.
Countries with a value but no outline (Singapore, Malta, Bahrain) are drawn as a dot at their centroid; in the bubble variant every country is a bubble.
Negative values are level 0 and the smallest bubble.
Russia and Fiji cross the 180th meridian; the map is clipped to its bounds.
Extras alone (no country values) show the tiles without a map.
The map keeps the 1000 by 394 aspect ratio, so it is short on a phone; small countries are best read through TalkBack, the details line or the table.
